TREs fazem mutirões em escolas para incentivar jovens a participar das eleições — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução As eleições de 2026 serão realizadas no dia 4 de outubro, data para o 1º turno, com a realização do 2º turno em 25 de outubro, caso necessário, para as corridas ao governo e à Presidência da República. Saiba quais cargos estão em disputa. O g1 detalha as atribuições de cada um dos cinco cargos em disputa no pleito de 2026 (inserir link). Na primeira votação, o eleitor terá que escolher os seus representantes para cinco cargos, enumerados aqui na mesma ordem em que aparecerão na urna eletrônica: A quantidade de deputados estaduais eleitos depende da representação dos estados na Câmara dos Deputados, em Brasília. Cada assembleia legislativa terá três vezes o número de deputados estaduais em comparação com os federais. Nos estados com mais de 12 deputados federais, há uma diferença na conta: triplica-se apenas até o 12º representante. Acima disso, cada vaga em Brasília é contabilizada como mais um. Por exemplo: São Paulo tem 70 deputados federais na Câmara. Para calcular o total de deputados estaduais, multiplicam-se os 12 primeiros por 3, o que resulta em 36. Depois, somam-se os 58 deputados federais que excedem esse limite. Assim, São Paulo tem 94 deputados estaduais.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: Vacina do sarampo na cidade de São Paulo. — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil A Prefeitura de São Paulo disponibiliza a plataforma "De Olho na Fila" , conhecida como "Filômetro", para informar a situação das filas nos postos de vacinação contra o sarampo na capital. Desde segunda-feira (3), está ocorrendo uma campanha de reforço da imunização contra a doença em todas as Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs) e nas AMAs/UBSs Integradas da capital. A ação teve início após a confirmação de 15 casos de sarampo no estado neste ano (12 na capital, dois em São Bernardo do Campo e um em Guarulhos). A ferramenta "De Olho na Fila" permite que a população consulte, em tempo real, quais unidades têm menor tempo de espera antes de se deslocar para receber a vacina (veja como funciona abaixo) .

https://www.marinelog.com/news/sci-to-na.text: The Seamen’s Church Institute (SCI) has appointed the Rev. Charles Uhlik as chaplain for its Ministry on the River program serving the Upper Mississippi River region. Based in St. Louis, he will begin the role September 30, providing pastoral care and support to mariners from St. Louis north along the Upper Mississippi River. Uhlik joins SCI’s Ministry on the River team, which includes the Rev. Nancy Simpson in Houston, serving the Gulf Coast and Houston Ship Channel; the Rev. Geoff Davis in New Orleans, serving the Lower Mississippi and Gulf Coast; and the Rev. Grace Pardun in Paducah, Ky., supervisory chaplain for the Upper Mississippi and Ohio River regions. Uhlik currently serves as rector of Grace Episcopal Church in Paducah. His background includes service as a chaplain in the U.S. Army Reserve, parish ministry in the Episcopal Church and nearly a decade as an SCI chaplain associate, a role he has held since 2016. He has also served on committees and trustee bodies within the Diocese of Kentucky and has been involved with community organizations, including the Paducah Warming Center, the Race Unity Organization and local ecumenical clergy initiatives. “I am thrilled that the Rev. Charles Uhlik has accepted the call to serve as our Chaplain for the Upper Mississippi River,” said the Rev. Grace Pardun, Supervisory Chaplain for SCI’s Ministry on the River. “He has been a Chaplain Associate with SCI for many years, knows the industry well, and has been a gracious and collaborative colleague. He will be a wonderful addition to our chaplain team, and I am excited to witness the many ways he will contribute to the well-being of mariners.”

https://petronoticias.com.br/apos-chegar.text: Após estabelecer uma operação no Brasil e garantir seu primeiro contrato no país , a Ocean Installer aposta em um ciclo de forte expansão do mercado subsea brasileiro nos próximos anos. Em entrevista ao Petronotícias, o vice-presidente sênior de desenvolvimento de negócios globais da companhia, Patrick Chapalain , afirma que a carteira de novos projetos offshore deverá sustentar uma elevada demanda por serviços de instalação, especialmente no segmento de SURF. “ Estimamos que o mercado potencial compreenda aproximadamente 15 grandes desenvolvimentos de FPSOs entre agora e 2031, gerando uma demanda contínua por uma ampla gama de serviços subsea ”, declarou. O executivo revelou que o foco imediato da empresa é conquistar contratos de SURF junto a operadoras independentes. Além disso, a companhia também quer participar de futuros desenvolvimentos de grande porte em águas profundas no modelo SURF EPCI, seja de forma independente ou em parceria com aliados estratégicos. Quais foram os principais fatores que levaram a Ocean Installer a estabelecer uma presença local no Brasil neste momento? Nos últimos anos, identificamos uma série de oportunidades atrativas no Brasil. No entanto, conquistar contratos sem uma presença local se mostrava um desafio por diversos motivos. À medida que o mercado continua em expansão, decidimos estabelecer uma empresa no país e formar uma equipe local. Essa iniciativa foi significativamente fortalecida pela disponibilidade de um grupo altamente experiente de profissionais após a decisão da Maersk Supply Service de encerrar seu departamento de projetos. Como resultado, estamos iniciando nossa operação brasileira com uma equipe que já trabalhou em conjunto em diversos projetos subsea no Brasil, o que nos permite estar plenamente operacionais e prontos para executar projetos desde o primeiro dia. Como a empresa avalia o potencial do mercado offshore brasileiro para os próximos anos? O mercado brasileiro de instalações subsea offshore continua em expansão, impulsionado por um sólido portfólio de novos desenvolvimentos de campos e de FPSOs com instalação prevista para os próximos anos. A capacidade dos fornecedores está bastante limitada, o que cria oportunidades significativas para uma empresa de instalação de SURF e sistemas de ancoragem de porte Tier 2, como a Ocean Installer.

https://splash247.com/indian-vessel-sunk.text: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel has been sunk in a suspected Houthi attack in the southern Red Sea, adding another casualty to the growing list of merchant ships caught up in the conflict off Yemen. The mechanised sailing vessel Faize Noore Oliya was struck on Tuesday around 13 nautical miles south of Hodeidah, a port controlled by the Houthis, before capsizing and sinking. India’s shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all 14 people onboard — 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni — were rescued by forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government and taken to Mokha. Maritime security consultancy Windward identified the incident as a bomb-boat attack. The Houthis had not claimed responsibility by Tuesday evening, although Yemeni government-aligned forces blamed the group. The attack is notable because the Houthis have recently said their renewed campaign is focused on Saudi-linked shipping. Four Saudi-flagged vessels have been attacked since last month. Faize Noore Oliya appears to have been operating with its AIS switched off for 44 days before the incident. Its previously recorded calls included ports in the UAE, Oman and Djibouti.

https://splash247.com/black-sea-attacks-.text: Russia has claimed strikes on four vessels and port infrastructure across Ukraine as the Black Sea has become the world’s most dangerous environment for commercial shipping. The Russian defence ministry said its forces hit three vessels in the port of Mykolaiv and another ship at sea off Odesa on Tuesday, alleging all four were being used “in the interests of the Ukrainian military”. Moscow also claimed attacks on a container terminal at Chornomorsk and a warehouse storing drones and drone components. Its assertions could not be independently verified, and the ministry did not identify the ships or provide details of casualties or damage. The attacks come amid an increasingly indiscriminate maritime campaign in which vessels, ports and energy infrastructure on both sides have been struck by aerial, surface and subsea drones. Turkey has urged Russia and Ukraine to protect freedom of navigation after a succession of attacks on Turkish-owned and Turkish-crewed ships. Ankara warned that the conflict’s spread across the Black Sea threatened merchant shipping and could have wider consequences for global food supplies. Turkish maritime union Deniz İşçileri estimates that 35 ships were struck during July, killing 23 seafarers and injuring more than 40.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: Um incêndio de grande magnitude atingiu uma indústria , nesta terça-feira (4), localizada na Estrada do Bonsucesso , no bairro Rio Abaixo, em Itaquaquecetuba , na Região Metropolitana de São Paulo. O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e trabalha no combate às chamas com o suporte de 18 viaturas . Até o momento, não há registro de feridos. De acordo com as autoridades, o fogo concentra-se em uma área que abriga tanques de produtos voláteis . Informações da operação indicam a existência de 24 tanques de solventes no local, o que aumenta a complexidade do controle do fogo devido à inflamabilidade dos materiais. A Defesa Civil de São Paulo está no local. De acordo com as informações iniciais, embora o incêndio envolva compostos químicos, não houve necessidade de evacuar residências na região. Devido à intensidade do incêndio, a unidade fabril foi evacuada preventivamente . Outras indústrias da região também foram evacuadas. As equipes de emergência concentram esforços para conter a propagação do fogo e resfriar as áreas adjacentes aos reservatórios de produtos químicos . O atendimento à ocorrência segue em andamento com o reforço do efetivo, que subiu de 12 para 18 viaturas durante a atualização dos trabalhos.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A Justiça Militar do RJ tornou réu o coronel Lauro César Botto Maia por suposta coação de testemunhas. A decisão ocorreu nesta terça-feira (4). Segundo o MPRJ, o militar enviou mensagens para influenciar depoimentos de 3 sargentos e 1 militar. Ele utilizou um nome falso no aplicativo WhatsApp. A promotoria pediu a prisão preventiva do coronel. O juiz determinou o prazo de 10 dias para a resposta da defesa antes de avaliar o pedido.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/b.text: A Polícia Civil do RJ iniciou nesta quarta-feira (6) nova fase da Operação Contenção. O objetivo é combater roubos de veículos e lavagem de dinheiro. Agentes saíram para cumprir 98 mandados de prisão contra integrantes do grupo criminoso. Os alvos atuam no Complexo do Fallet-Fogueteiro, em Santa Teresa. Ações de roubo de veículos cresceram 58,3% em Santa Teresa e 17,4% no Centro. Os dados comparam períodos de 2025 e 2026. Investigações da DRFA apontam mudança no modelo de atuação da organização. O roubo de veículos virou fonte de financiamento do grupo.

Programa Tolerância Zero entra em uma nova fase nesta quarta-feira (5), com a expansão das ações para ruas do entorno da orla de Copacabana, Leme, Ipanema e Leblon. Cerca de 600 agentes e policiais realizarão blitzes diárias em vias de Copacabana, Ipanema e Leblon. O objetivo é coibir crimes e identificar veículos em situação irregular. A expansão ocorre após episódios de violência. A Polícia Civil prendeu dois suspeitos de atacar uma viatura da Seop com coquetel molotov em Copacabana.

Um grave acidente entre 3 carretas interditou o sentido Rio de Janeiro da Rodovia Presidente Dutra nesta quarta-feira (5). A batida arrancou a cabine de um caminhão. 3 feridos foram levados ao Hospital Geral de Nova Iguaçu após o acidente à 0h13, em Seropédica. Às 8h, o engarrafamento passava de 20 km, com apenas 1 faixa liberada. As 2 carretas que transportavam frutas ainda estavam ocupando a pista. Um grave acidente envolvendo 3 carretas interditou o sentido Rio de Janeiro da Rodovia Presidente Dutra (BR-116 Sul), na altura da Baixada Fluminense, na madrugada desta quarta-feira (5). A batida foi forte que a cabine de um dos caminhões se soltou da carroceria e foi parar na margem

A Polícia Civil prendeu nesta terça-feira (4) Adriano Reis da Cruz. Ele é suspeito de espancar e matar sua companheira, Gabriela Ferreira Reis da Cruz, em Japeri. A vítima morreu na segunda-feira (3) após internação. O crime ocorreu quando Gabriela tentou defender sua filha de uma tentativa de abuso sexual do suspeito. O investigado possuía histórico de violência doméstica e descumpriu medidas protetivas. Ele também manteve a família em cárcere e responderá por feminicídio.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Criminosos do Rio de Janeiro usam fardas e acessórios parecidos com os de forças de segurança para facilitar invasões em áreas de rivais. A Polícia Civil investiga a estratégia. Investigações mostram flagrantes recentes de grupos armados usando roupas camufladas e coletes da Polícia Civil em bairros como Guaratiba e Campo Grande. Desde 2021, uma lei estadual exige cadastro para venda de uniformes. No entanto, especialistas apontam falhas na fiscalização, o que facilita o acesso aos materiais pela internet. Bandidos usam réplicas de fardas das forças de segurança para invadir territórios

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/b.text: Estudo da Firjan aponta que a Baixada Fluminense registrou taxa de roubo de veículos 9 vezes maior que a média nacional em 2025. O levantamento aponta que o estado teve 56.838 mortes violentas em 10 anos. A insegurança gera prejuízo anual de R$ 31 bilhões para a economia fluminense. A Polícia Civil informou que, após criar delegacias especializadas, os roubos de veículos caíram 17% na Baixada Fluminense entre julho de 2025 e junho de 2026. Estudo da Firjan aponta que Baixada tem taxa de roubo de veículos nove vezes maior que a média nacional

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: Quaest mostra empate técnico na avaliação de Lula: 48% aprovam o presidente, 47% desaprovam e 5% não responderam. Os índices ficaram estáveis em relação a julho, com diferença de apenas 1 ponto percentual entre aprovação e desaprovação. Desde março, a aprovação subiu de 44% para 48%, enquanto a desaprovação caiu de 51% para 47%. O governo é avaliado positivamente por 36%, negativamente por 36% e como regular por 26%; outros 2% não responderam. Para 55%, o Brasil segue na direção errada; 38% consideram a direção certa e 7% não responderam.

https://g1.globo.com/pr/parana/noticia/2.text: A juíza Gabriela Hardt continuará recebendo salário durante o afastamento de 2 anos determinado pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça. A decisão ocorreu na terça-feira (4). O afastamento decorre de investigação iniciada em 2024 sobre supostas irregularidades em acordo de R$ 2 bilhões da Operação Lava Jato. A sanção foi aprovada por unanimidade.

https://g1.globo.com/meio-ambiente/notic.text: O Inmet informou nesta terça-feira (4) que monitora a possível formação de um ciclone extratropical entre a Argentina, Uruguai, Sul do Brasil e Oceano Atlântico. O sistema deve começar a se organizar na quinta-feira (6) sobre o norte da Argentina e Paraguai. Depois, avançará rumo ao Rio Grande do Sul. Entre sexta-feira (7) e sábado (8), o ciclone pode ganhar força rapidamente. No Rio Grande do Sul e Santa Catarina, ventos podem passar de 60 km/h. Após o avanço do ciclone para o oceano, uma massa de ar frio provocará queda nas temperaturas do Centro-Sul, Centro-Oeste e Sudeste. Para quarta-feira (5), o Inmet mantém aviso amarelo de tempestades no Sul e Mato Grosso do Sul. Na quinta-feira (6), o alerta sobe para laranja.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/campinas-regiao/.text: O suspeito Gustavo Henrique Ardito foi preso nesta quarta-feira (5). Ele é investigado por atirar contra um motorista de aplicativo na Rodovia Anhanguera. O crime ocorreu na sexta-feira (31) em Americana (SP) após briga de trânsito. Câmeras no veículo da vítima registraram o suspeito, que é CAC, apontando a arma. Segundo depoimento do motorista, foram efetuados 5 disparos no trânsito. A Polícia Civil e a Polícia Científica identificaram inicialmente 3 marcas de tiros no veículo. Durante a Operação Torque Letal, policiais apreenderam 11 armas registradas na casa do suspeito. Uma delas estava pronta para uso dentro de um veículo.

Um CAC foi preso nesta quarta-feira (5) em Americana (SP). Ele é suspeito de tentar matar um motorista de aplicativo após briga de trânsito na Rodovia Anhanguera. O investigado Gustavo Henrique Ardito teria perseguido a vítima e atirado no carro. A polícia apreendeu 11 armas e munições na casa do suspeito. O crime ocorreu na última sexta-feira (31) e foi gravado por câmeras do carro. O delegado Eduardo Salge explicou as regras de transporte de armas de fogo. A prisão ocorreu durante a Operação Torque Letal. A Polícia Civil investiga o caso como tentativa de homicídio qualificado e analisa os materiais apreendidos.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: A Justiça de São Paulo manteve a penhora de 30% do salário do senador Romário. A medida visa pagar indenização por danos morais a Marco Polo Del Nero. A ação começou em setembro de 2013, quando Romário afirmou que Del Nero deveria ser "preso". O ex-dirigente alegou que as declarações extrapolaram a livre manifestação. Nesta terça-feira (4), foi divulgado que Romário recorreu alegando comprometimento de sua subsistência. O Tribunal de Justiça paulista rejeitou o recurso e manteve a retenção mensal. O desconto de cerca de R$ 13,9 mil será depositado pelo Senado em conta judicial. A defesa de Del Nero poderá solicitar a liberação dos valores depositados.

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Argentina, Pablo Quirno, afirma que o país não tomará nenhuma medida contra o Brasil após decisão diplomática. Um dia antes, ele acusou o Brasil de agir por "questões puramente ideológicas", após o governo brasileiro rebaixar o nível das relações diplomáticas. O Itamaraty manterá o embaixador brasileiro no país enquanto Javier Milei mantiver os ataques. A crise diplomática começou após a presença do argentino em evento político em julho. No domingo (2), Milei atacou o presidente Lula, chamando o petista de "ladrão" e "corrupto". Ele também questionou as decisões do STF que anularam condenações de Lula. Inicialmente, o presidente Lula evitou polemizar com o mandatário vizinho. Posteriormente, o petista endureceu o discurso e classificou como "patacoada" a participação de Milei no evento do PL.

https://g1.globo.com/tecnologia/noticia/.text: O modelo de inteligência artificial Claude Mythos 5 , da Anthropic, considerado u m dos modelos de IA mais perigosos do mundo , criou identidades falsas para tentar convencer um desenvolvedor a aprovar alterações maliciosas em um projeto de código aberto durante um teste de segurança cibernética. O caso foi divulgado pelo AI Security Institute e é o mais recente de uma série de incidentes envolvendo os sistemas mais avançados de IA. Segundo o instituto, o comportamento foi identificado durante avaliações rotineiras para medir a capacidade dos modelos de executar ataques cibernéticos. Ao todo, os pesquisadores registraram 17 ações do Mythos 5 e outras duas do GPT-5.6-Sol, da OpenAI, relacionadas a tentativas de burlar mecanismos de segurança utilizando classificadores cibernéticos.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541799-ko.text: KOIL Energy Solutions has entered into a strategic alliance with consultancy Pipeline Network to expand its presence, operational capabilities and customer support across the Eastern Hemisphere. The alliance combines KOIL Energy's subsea technology expertise with Pipeline Network's regional presence and operational capabilities across the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific, providing customers with access to an expanded portfolio of subsea products, rental equipment and field services. Pipeline Network is a consultancy and representation business serving the oil and gas pipeline services sector. The company is led by John Grover, who has more than 40 years of experience in the pipeline and process services industry. "This strategic alliance represents an important milestone in our international growth strategy. By partnering with Pipeline Network, we are significantly expanding our ability to support customers throughout the Eastern Hemisphere, offering an extensive fleet of rental equipment for testing services, supported by an impeccable team of service personnel our customers have come to expect from KOIL Energy,” said Chris Sebesta, Director of Business Development at KOIL Energy. The alliance follows a series of developments announced by KOIL Energy in recent months. In March, the company secured a pre-commissioning project award offshore West Africa, followed in May by $5 million in funding to expand its rental equipment fleet. In June, it announced an award for subsea umbilical handling services, including the acquisition of an additional 3,500-metric-ton mobile offshore carousel. KOIL Energy said these developments support its strategy of expanding geographically, increasing rental capacity and providing integrated subsea solutions to customers worldwide.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541791-va.text: Vantris Energy has secured new offshore engineering and drilling work in Malaysia, including a transportation and installation (T&I) work order from Petronas and a tender-assisted drilling rig (TADR) assignment and contract for offshore development drilling campaigns. Under the engineering and construction segment, VTEB Offshore, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Vantris Energy formerly known as Sapura Offshore, was awarded a work order by Petronas for offshore transportation and installation services under an existing T&I contract for offshore facilities. The work began in the second quarter of calendar year 2026 and is scheduled for completion in the third quarter of 2027. The company's drilling business also received a Notice of Assignment (NOA) from Petronas and a new contract from Vestigo Petroleum to provide tender-assisted drilling rig services. The two awards are expected to commence sequentially during the third quarter of calendar year 2026 and will support offshore development drilling campaigns in Malaysia. Following the awards, Vantris Energy said its order book exceeds $1.4 billion (RM6 billion), reflecting its strategy of expanding work aligned with its core capabilities.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541790-tg.text: TGS has started a 34,000-kilometre 2D seismic reimaging project offshore Egypt in partnership with the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS), aiming to improve subsurface imaging and support future exploration activity in the country's Mediterranean waters. The EGY-2DRE2026 project will combine data from TGS' GeoStreamer 2016, 2018 and 2023 surveys, together with other available conventional 2D seismic data, to create a single regional dataset covering Egypt's offshore basins. The merged dataset will undergo advanced velocity model building and pre-stack depth migration processing, including TGS' proprietary DM-eFWI technology, to improve imaging of the pre-, intra- and post-Messinian salt intervals. TGS said the reprocessed dataset is intended to provide operators with a more consistent basin-wide structural framework to support prospect identification and maturation, helping guide exploration investment ahead of an anticipated future licensing round and supporting activity in the offshore Nile Delta, Herodotus Basin and the wider Eastern Mediterranean Basin. Delivery of the final products for a priority subset of 2D lines is scheduled for the second quarter of 2027, with the full project expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2028. The project is supported by industry funding. "EGY-2DRE2026 will give our customers a modern, regionally consistent view of a basin that has historically been difficult to image beneath its complex Messinian section. By combining our latest imaging technology with the depth and breadth of our existing coverage, we're able to de-risk exploration decisions and support our customers as they evaluate future opportunities in this highly prospective part of the Egyptian offshore,” said David Hajovsky, Executive Vice President, Multi-Client at TGS.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541794-da.text: China-based offshore wind foundations manufacturer Dajin Heavy Industry has delivered KING TWO, the second 40,000 DWT heavy deck carrier in its self-developed and self-built KING series. The delivery represents a step in expanding the company's offshore vessel-building capabilities, marking the transition of the vessel class into standardized batch construction following the commercial deployment of KING ONE. KING TWO has an overall length of 239.8 meters, a beam of 51 meters, a 12,000-square-metre cargo deck, and a range of 16,000 nautical miles. The heavy deck carrier is designed to transport ultra-large offshore structures, including 15-25 MW offshore wind monopiles, jackets and floating foundations, for long-distance heavy-lift operations. According to Dajin Heavy Industry, KING ONE has already completed multiple transoceanic commercial voyages, providing operational validation of the vessel's performance and construction quality. The company has established standardized production processes, an integrated supply chain collaboration system and a quality management framework that enable serial construction of sister ships while supporting scheduled deliveries, construction efficiency and cost control.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541801-fu.text: Fugro Survey India has been awarded a three-year contract by Vantage International Management Company to provide remotely operated vehicle (ROV)-based deepwater drill support services for ONGC's offshore drilling operations in India. Under the contract, Fugro will support drilling and completion activities in water depths of up to 3,000 meters aboard the Platinum Explorer drillship as part of ONGC's deepwater exploration program, which is aimed at developing new offshore energy reserves, strengthening India's energy security and supporting long-term domestic oil and gas production. The scope of work includes subsea installation and intervention, drilling and completion support, blowout preventer (BOP) and well-control monitoring, cementing observation and seabed inspection. Fugro will deploy its FCV3000 ROV system to support the drilling campaign. "This project reflects strong collaboration and trust between Fugro and its partners to support a strategically important deepwater drilling program in India. By bringing specialist ROV expertise and reliable subsea support, Fugro is helping enable safe, efficient operations while contributing to the success of complex offshore developments,” said Sriram Sreenivasan, Business Line Manager for Marine Asset Integrity at Fugro in the Middle East and India.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541796-en.text: EnerMech has secured a multi-year contract to provide topside process and shutdown services across the offshore asset portfolio of a leading North Sea operator, expanding a partnership that has spanned more than a decade. The award is the second major North Sea contract won by EnerMech in recent months for comparable topside process services and expands its role in delivering topside process services and shutdown readiness activities across the operator's offshore assets. Under the contract, EnerMech will provide an integrated delivery model combining embedded engineering expertise, multi-skilled personnel and centralized competency support. From its Aberdeen base, the company will deploy a scalable equipment fleet and its SIMPro engineering software to support shutdown and maintenance projects. The scope of work includes nitrogen purging, nitrogen and helium leak testing, bolt torquing and tensioning, cryogenic pipe freezing, on-site machining, system pressurization and flange management. EnerMech said its delivery approach is intended to minimize rework, reduce downtime and improve planning certainty across a multi-asset program. "This award reflects the confidence our customer places in our people, processes and commitment to continuous improvement. It aligns with our strategy of delivering integrated, technically advanced topside process solutions that improve reliability, reduce complexity and provide operators with greater operational assurance across their asset portfolios,” saod Charles "Chuck" Davison Jr., EnerMech CEO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541793-no.text: Noble Corporation has installed a Stemless Gate Valve (SGV) on its Noble BlackHornet drillship, introducing a dedicated wellbore sealing system designed for managed pressure drilling operations. The technology, developed with Kinetic Pressure Control, provides a dedicated means of sealing the wellbore during managed pressure drilling and was integrated with the rig's blowout preventer (BOP) system following technical evaluation and engineering work involving Noble, Kinetic and other industry specialists. According to Noble, the project included assessments of the technology's reliability, installation requirements, maintenance considerations and compatibility with existing well control systems before offshore deployment. “The result is a new approach that helps preserve the integrity of critical well control equipment while supporting more efficient operations. This project reflects Noble's commitment to advancing offshore drilling through practical innovation and teamwork,” Noble said in a statement. The Noble BlackHornet is a high-specification Gusto P10,000 DW drillship that entered service in 2015. Designed to operate in water depths of up to 12,000 feet (3,658 metres) with a maximum drilling depth of 40,000 feet (12,192 metres), the vessel can accommodate 210 personnel. The drillship is currently working for BP in the U.S. Gulf under contracts running until February 2029, with a one-year priced option.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/eir_still_s.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone on Tuesday, Enverus Intelligence Research (EIR), a subsidiary of Enverus, revealed that it is maintaining its Brent oil price forecast at $100 per barrel across the second half of 2026 and 2027. “EIR finds that global oil markets remain structurally tight despite recent price volatility,” the company said in the statement. “OECD commercial inventories are projected to fall toward a 20 year low in the fourth quarter of 2026, when EIR expects the market to reach its tightest point,” it added. “Balances are forecast to draw sharply through 2026 before shifting to modest builds beginning in the first quarter of 2027,” it continued. EIR noted in its statement that the outlook also reflects recovering Chinese crude demand and continued disruption risk at two critical maritime chokepoints. “China’s crude imports fell to approximately 7.2 million barrels per day in June, down about 41 percent year over year, as the country relied on stockpiles, refinery run cuts, and fuel-export restrictions,” it said.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A VLI passou a receber cargas agrícolas comercializadas na modalidade CIF (tipo de frete em que o vendedor é responsável pelos custos) diretamente em seus terminais por meio de uma plataforma digital desenvolvida pela própria companhia . A solução, denominada CargoCIF , elimina etapas burocráticas na integração entre o transporte rodoviário e ferroviário e já movimentou mais de 280 mil toneladas de soja e milho entre janeiro e junho deste ano . Segundo a empresa, a ferramenta automatiza a troca de documentos fiscais e operacionais entre produtores rurais e clientes, permitindo que cargas comercializadas na modalidade CIF sejam recebidas diretamente nos terminais ferroviários. Até então, entraves relacionados à gestão documental dificultavam esse tipo de operação, levando parte dos embarques a seguir exclusivamente por rodovia até os portos. Atualmente, o sistema conta com 12 clientes ativos. A expectativa da VLI é expandir a solução para todos os seus terminais integradores de grãos até o fim de 2026. "A solução transforma uma dor histórica do mercado em vantagem competitiva para o cliente. Ao conectar, de forma simples, segura e integrada, o produtor à malha ferroviária, eliminamos etapas burocráticas, reduzimos custos logísticos e ampliamos a competitividade das operações", afirma Gabriel Fonseca, gerente-geral de Grãos da VLI. A empresa informa que o CargoCIF opera em ambiente digital com mecanismos de rastreabilidade e conformidade fiscal, proporcionando maior previsibilidade para produtores, embarcadores e operadores logísticos. A plataforma foi desenvolvida no programa de intraempreendedorismo Empreendedores Inova VLI. Segundo Juliano Cota, um dos coordenadores do projeto, o objetivo foi criar uma solução capaz de viabilizar o recebimento de cargas CIF em grande escala. "Assumimos o desafio de criar uma alternativa confiável, rastreável, automatizada e em conformidade com as regras fiscais para o recebimento de cargas na modalidade CIF. Dessa forma, fortalecemos o papel da ferrovia como uma alternativa mais eficiente e estratégica para o escoamento de grãos", afirma.

A TCP , empresa que administra o Terminal de Contêineres de Paranaguá (PR) , publicou seu Relatório de Sustentabilidade 2025 , destacando a conquista da certificação ISO 50001 e a atualização de sua estratégia ESG . O documento, elaborado conforme as diretrizes da Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), confirma a consistência da Matriz de Materialidade definida em 2022 e apresenta avanços em governança corporativa. Segundo a empresa, a revisão da Matriz de Materialidade envolveu benchmarking com outras companhias do setor portuário, entrevistas com lideranças e consultas a públicos internos e externos. O processo resultou na retirada de apenas três temas da matriz - Impactos Econômicos Indiretos, Avaliação Ambiental de Fornecedores e Avaliação Social de Fornecedores -, mantendo inalteradas as principais prioridades estratégicas da companhia. "A atualização da Matriz de Materialidade mostrou que as prioridades definidas pela TCP continuam refletindo tanto os desafios do nosso negócio quanto as expectativas dos públicos com quem nos relacionamos. Isso demonstra que construímos uma estratégia de sustentabilidade sólida, capaz de orientar nossas decisões de longo prazo", afirma Kayo Zaiats, superintendente de Meio Ambiente da TCP. O relatório também destaca a obtenção da certificação ISO 50001, tornando a TCP, segundo a empresa, o primeiro terminal portuário brasileiro certificado na norma internacional de gestão de energia. Na área de governança, a publicação registra mudanças na estrutura organizacional e na alta liderança da companhia, incluindo a primeira mensagem institucional assinada pelo CEO, Jacky Song. O documento reúne ainda indicadores ambientais, sociais e econômicos relacionados à eficiência energética, gestão de resíduos, monitoramento ambiental, preservação da biodiversidade, saúde e segurança ocupacional, diversidade, desenvolvimento de colaboradores e programas de integridade. O Relatório de Sustentabilidade 2025 está disponível para consulta pública no site da TCP.

As empilhadeiras STILL equipadas com o sistema de telemetria FleetManager passaram a ser elegíveis ao financiamento pela linha Finame Máquinas 4.0, do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) . O enquadramento permite financiar até 100% do valor dos equipamentos, com prazo de até 60 meses e condições voltadas à modernização tecnológica da indústria. Segundo a fabricante, o credenciamento foi concedido porque o FleetManager atende aos requisitos da categoria Máquinas 4.0 do Cadastro de Fabricantes Informatizado (CFI) do BNDES, que exige tecnologia embarcada capaz de coletar e monitorar dados operacionais. O sistema registra informações como consumo, produtividade, utilização dos equipamentos e indicadores para manutenção preditiva, permitindo o gerenciamento da frota de empilhadeiras. De acordo com as condições da linha de crédito, empresas com faturamento anual de até R$ 300 milhões podem financiar até 100% do valor do equipamento, com prazo de pagamento de até 60 meses, incluindo até três meses de carência. A taxa de juros da campanha vigente parte de 13% ao ano, composta pelo custo financeiro, pela taxa fixa do BNDES e pela remuneração da instituição financeira credenciada. "O credenciamento das empilhadeiras STILL com FleetManager no Finame representa um avanço importante para ampliar o acesso dos clientes a tecnologias voltadas à eficiência, à segurança e à gestão das operações logísticas. Com condições de financiamento mais atrativas, mais empresas poderão investir na modernização de suas frotas e acelerar sua transformação tecnológica com empilhadeiras STILL", afirma Adriana Firmo, vice-presidente de Sales & Service da KION South America. Segundo a empresa, a contratação do financiamento depende da aprovação de uma instituição financeira credenciada pelo BNDES, responsável pela análise de crédito e pelas condições da operação. A STILL presta suporte na definição técnica dos equipamentos e na indicação de agentes financeiros parceiros, mas não participa da concessão do crédito.

https://safety4sea.com/several-container.text: The Maldives-flagged general cargo vessel MV MSS Graphene lost 17 empty shipping containers overboard on 1 August 2026 after encountering rough weather approximately 17 nautical miles west of the Port of Colombo, Sri Lanka. T he vessel was sailing from Malé, Maldives, to Colombo to collect cargo when strong winds and heavy swells caused the ship to roll heavily, resulting in the deck-stacked containers falling into the sea. No injuries or damage to the remaining cargo were reported. The vessel regained control shortly after the incident and secured the remaining containers. Maldives State Shipping (MSS) said it is working with its Sri Lankan agent and relevant authorities to develop a recovery plan and retrieve the containers once weather conditions allow. Following the incident, the Sri Lankan Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) issued a navigational warning to vessels operating in the area, while the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources warned fishing vessels to remain vigilant due to the risk posed by drifting containers. The Sri Lankan Navy has deployed vessels to monitor the area and assist with locating the containers, which are expected to drift toward the western coastline between Beruwala, Negombo and Puttalam due to prevailing currents.

https://safety4sea.com/imo-expands-globa.text: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez receives Jodi Barrow, Secretary General, Secretariat, Caribbean Memorandum of Understanding, for MoU signing ceremony. Credit: IMO/Flickr The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has signed updated data-exchange agreements with the Black Sea and Caribbean Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) on Port State Control (PSC), aimed at strengthening the global exchange of ship inspection information. T he agreements were signed at the IMO headquarters in London on 21 July by IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez, Black Sea MoU Secretariat Secretary Onur Turhan and Caribbean MoU Secretary General Jodi Munn Barrow. According to the IMO, the updated agreements will expand cooperation between regional PSC regimes by enhancing the exchange of inspection data and supporting the continued development of the Port State Control module within the organization’s Global Integrated Shipping Information System (GISIS). With these agreements, IMO has now concluded updated data-exchange agreements with eight regional PSC regimes. Similar agreements have previously been signed with the Abuja, Indian Ocean, Tokyo, Mediterranean, Paris and Riyadh MoUs, while discussions continue with the Viña del Mar Agreement and the United States Coast Guard. The updated agreements represent another important milestone towards the development of a PSC Overarching Database (ODB), which will enable more comprehensive, harmonized and efficient sharing of PSC inspection data worldwide.

https://safety4sea.com/houthis-claim-new.text: On 5 August, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement claimed it had carried out a ballistic missile attack on the Saudi oil tanker Wafa in the northern Red Sea off the coast of Yanbu. H outhi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the vessel was struck with several ballistic missiles but did not specify when the attack took place. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the claim. Saree said the Wafa was the eighth tanker targeted since the Houthis announced a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia on 22 July. بيان القوات المسلحة اليمنية بشأن تنفيذ عملية عسكرية استهدفت سفينة “وفاء” النفطية السعودية شمالي البحر الأحمر أمام منطقة “ينبع” وذلك بعدد من الصواريخ الباليستية محققة إصابة دقيقة بفضل الله، وذلك في إطار معادلة “الحصار بالحصار”. pic.twitter.com/BGw1NHqBpZ He also claimed that 29 Saudi ships had either been prevented from transiting the Red Sea or forced to turn back, adding that the group would continue and escalate attacks on Saudi oil tankers as part of its “blockade-for-blockade” strategy. On 4 August, the Houthis also claimed responsibility for a drone strike on a “sensitive target” at Najran Airport in southern Saudi Arabia. Saree said the attack was carried out in response to alleged repeated Saudi drone incursions into Yemeni airspace over the provinces of Saada and Hajjah, warning that any future violations would prompt further retaliation.

https://safety4sea.com/indian-cargo-ship.text: An Indian-flagged commercial vessel, MSV Faize Noore Oliya , sank in the Red Sea after coming under attack near Yemeni waters on 4 August, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said. A ll 14 crew members on board, including 13 Indian nationals, were rescued safely, the MEA confirmed. The Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said the vessel was struck by a projectile near Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and eventually sink. An Indian cargo ship, Faize Noore Oliya, sank after an explosive boat attack off Al-Hodeidah, Yemen. All 13 crew members were safely rescued. pic.twitter.com/h5RxkVeR9Q Condemning the attack, the Indian government further said its Embassy in Riyadh is closely monitoring the situation and is coordinating with Yemeni authorities to ensure the safety and security of the rescued crew. The government also expressed gratitude to the Yemeni authorities for their assistance in the rescue operation. The continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. The targeting of commercial shipping in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest. Windward’s Maritime AI analysis indicates the vessel exhibited a pattern of unusual activity in the months leading up to the attack. Between February and June, the vessel made 11 port calls—four at Port Rashid in the UAE, six at Salalah in Oman, and one at Doraleh in Djibouti.

https://safety4sea.com/japanese-companie.text: Hitachi, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), and Japan Airlines (JAL) have signed an MOU to conduct Japan’s first pilot test of Direct Ocean Capture (DOC) technology on Kume Island, Okinawa Prefecture. T he project will use containerized pilot equipment installed on land to extract CO2 dissolved in seawater, with the aim of assessing the technology’s applicability, operational challenges, and environmental impacts for future deployment along Japan’s coastline. DOC technology removes CO2 directly from seawater , encouraging the ocean to absorb additional atmospheric CO2 to restore balance. As seawater contains significantly higher CO2 concentrations than the atmosphere, the technology is being explored as a potential lower-cost and lower-energy carbon removal solution. The initiative aims to advance carbon dioxide removal (CDR) solutions for hard-to-abate sectors such as shipping and aviation, where emissions reductions remain challenging. The three companies have invested in U.S.-based DOC developer Captura Corp. and are exploring the establishment of a domestic carbon removal ecosystem, including the potential use of captured CO2 as a feedstock for synthetic fuels such as e-SAF. Hitachi will focus on monitoring operational and environmental data, improving energy efficiency, and supporting carbon credit verification. MOL will use its partnership with Kumejima Town to coordinate local cooperation and explore regional applications, while JAL will promote awareness of DOC technology and assess its potential role in future e-SAF procurement.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-risk4sea-psi-o.text: The latest RiSK4SEA PSC Stress Index (PSI) Outlook – August 2026, reveals a significant easing in the global Port State Control (PSC) enforcement climate following the broad deterioration observed during the previous months. A fter June marked the first occasion where all four major shipping segments simultaneously entered PSI-9 “Critical Risk Zone” , August PSI Outlook indicates a clear return to a segmented enforcement environment. Commenting on the latest findings, Apo Belokas, Founder & CEO of RiSK4SEA, stated: “ The August PSI Outlook demonstrates exactly why PSC should be monitored as an evolving enforcement climate rather than as isolated inspection statistics. After experiencing broad-based enforcement pressure in June, we are now observing a differentiated recovery across vessel segments. While this is encouraging for much of the industry, bulk carriers continue to exhibit performance deterioration that warrants close operational attention.” The important message for ship managers is that PSC enforcement is becoming increasingly dynamic. Recovery is not occurring uniformly across the industry, making segment-specific intelligence more valuable than ever for allocating resources and prioritizing vessel preparation. Although the Bulker segment improved materially from the PSI-9 conditions observed during June, it remains the only major fleet segment operating outside the “Improving Trend” zone. The August Outlook assigns Bulkers a PSI-6, reflecting continued deterioration in operational performance despite detention activity remaining broadly aligned with historical averages. KPI Performance Stress remains elevated at +10.4%, driven primarily by higher deficiencies per inspection, increasing Ship Structure & Equipment findings and a significant increase in SMS-related deficiencies.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-i.text: CHIRP Maritime draws lessons learned from an incident where a vessel navigating polar ice waters experienced a bridge resource management failure. T he reporter describes a breakdown in bridge resource management (BRM) during navigation in polar waters, highlighting the challenges of maintaining situational awareness in a dynamic ice environment. An expedition vessel had completed daily operations and was proceeding towards open water through an area with 6–7/10 ice concentration, including glacial ice, bergy bits, and icebergs. The bridge team consisted of the Master, who was conning the vessel, and the Chief Officer, who was assisting with a navigational system combining vessel sensor inputs (including GPS and echo sounder data) to provide a real-time 3D representation of the seabed. The Officer of the Watch (OOW) also provided support. The OOW was on their first voyage in polar waters, while the Master and Chief Officer had prior ice experience. There was no dedicated lookout on the bridge, as the assigned lookout was on deck securing expedition workboats. As ice concentration increased, available leads and open water became more limited. The vessel was not following a pre-established passage plan, and no clear route or contingency plan had been agreed upon for the changing conditions.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/yem.text: Yemen’s Houthi group claimed Wednesday that it struck the Saudi oil tanker Wafaa with several ballistic missiles in the northern Red Sea off the coast of Yanbu. The group’s military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said in a statement on X that the missiles hit the tanker “accurately.” Saree said the attack was part of what the group calls its maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and its “blockade for blockade” strategy. The attack brought to eight the number of Saudi oil tankers targeted by the group since the blockade began July 22, he said. Saree also claimed that 29 Saudi oil tankers had either been prevented from passing through the Red Sea and Arabian Sea or forced to turn back. He said Saudi Arabia had redirected its oil tankers to the northern Red Sea after the group succeeded in imposing what it described as a blockade from the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/fes.text: Russian logistics and shipping company FESCO said Tuesday it has stopped accepting new shipment orders through the Black Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack on one of its vessels last week. The move underscores increasing disruption to shipping operations as attacks on vessels by both Russia and Ukraine have intensified, driving wheat prices higher on global markets. Russia’s state nuclear corporation Rosatom, which owns 92.5% of FESCO, said earlier that the vessel Yanina sank in the Black Sea overnight from Friday to Saturday after being damaged by Ukrainian seaborne drones. The ship was carrying frozen food and construction materials. FESCO ranks among Russia’s largest logistics operators, focusing on container shipments by rail and sea. Russia, the world’s largest wheat exporter, has reported multiple attacks on its agricultural export facilities and commercial vessels in the Black Sea in recent weeks. Russia’s main grain lobby group said last week that Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian ships and ports could shut down grain exports via the Black Sea in the near future, potentially pushing prices higher.

https://splash247.com/intermoor-secures-.text: InterMoor, Acteon’s moorings and anchors brand, has been awarded a new contract by Petrobras to provide inspection, preservation, maintenance, and operational readiness services for subsea interconnection, mooring, and anchoring materials. This award marks the third contract secured by InterMoor from Petrobras in less than a year, reinforcing a long-standing partnership. Under the scope of work, InterMoor will deliver integrated services covering a wide range of critical mooring components, including chains, steel wire ropes, anchors, connectors, load collars, anode collars, adapters, and other load handling accessories. These services will support Petrobras’ offshore operations across Brazil’s extensive subsea infrastructure portfolio. The three-year contract includes visual and dimensional inspection of materials and accessories, non-destructive testing, including magnetic particle and liquid penetrant testing, as well as cleaning and surface preparation. The deal will also include surface treatment and painting for preservation purposes, maintenance, repair, replacement, and reconditioning of anchoring components, and handling and transportation where required, with storage and preservation of materials.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: No segundo dia de greve dos funcionários da CPTM (Companhia Paulista de Trens Metropolitanos), as linhas de trem 11-Coral, 12-Safira e 13-Jade continuam operando com impactos nesta quarta-feira (5) . A paralisação parcial continua após assembleia geral realizada na noite desta terça (4). Segundo a companhia, a linha 11, que liga as estações Estudantes e Palmeiras-Barra Funda, atua apenas entre Guaianases e Palmeiras-Barra Funda. Assim como a linha 12, que atende Calmon Viana até o Brás, mas funciona apenas entre as estações Engenheiro Goulart e Brás por conta da greve. As duas linhas atendem a Zona Leste de São Paulo. A linha 13-Jade opera normalmente desde às 6h, mas conta com apoio do sistema Paese (Plano de Apoio entre Empresas em Situação de Emergência) para ajudar na circulação das pessoas. De acordo com a CPTM, os trens operam com intervalo de 30 minutos, maior do que o normal, entre as estações Engenheiro Goulart e Aeroporto-Guarulhos. Para chegar nas estações com operação normalizada, os ônibus do Paese estão distribuídos na frente dos pontos sem funcionamentos. Ao todo, há 95 coletivos de apoio para a linha 11, 90 para a linha 12 e 10 para a linha 13. Caso seja necessário usar uma das linhas com os funcionários em greve, o transporte estará disponível entre as estações Guaianases e Estudantes. O mesmo vale para a linha 12, na qual o serviço está mobilizado entre Engenheiro Goulart e Calmon Viana, e para a linha 13, entre Engenheiro Goulart e Aeroporto-Guarulhos. A população também poderá utilizar as linhas 1-Azul, 2-Verde, 3-Vermelha e 15-Prata do Metrô, que operam desde às 4h com maior quantidade de carros.

A Defesa Civil do Estado do Rio de Janeiro emitiu um alerta "severo" para fortes ventos nas próximas horas na capital fluminense . A mensagem foi recebida por moradores da cidade por volta das 5h05 desta quarta-feira (5). No início da noite desta terça (4), o Rio de Janeiro entrou em Estágio 2 de risco para ocorrências no município , segundo o COR (Centro de Operações Rio). O aviso da corporação pede para os cidadãos evitarem árvores e estruturas metálicas. A previsão, segundo o órgão da Prefeitura, é de ventos moderados a pontualmente fortes, com rajadas de até 76 km/h , entre a manhã e a tarde desta quarta-feira (5/8), principalmente na Zona Oeste e em áreas litorâneas da cidade. Um sistema de alta pressão influenciará o tempo na capital. Segundo o Sistema Alerta Rio, deve haver predomínio de céu parcialmente nublado e não há previsão de chuva. A previsão é de ventos moderados (18,5km/h até 51,9km/h), com rajadas pontualmente fortes (entre 52 a 76 km/h) nos períodos da manhã e tarde. A umidade relativa do ar poderá atingir valores entre 21% e 30% durante a tarde. A temperatura mínima prevista é de 18°C e a máxima de 33°C. O "nível 2", representado pela cor amarela, é um dos cinco Estágios Operacionais da Prefeitura do Rio, que variam de acordo com a previsão e ocorrências de tempestades, calor intenso ou acidentes que possam influenciar a rotina dos cariocas. O Estágio 2 significa que há risco de ocorrências de alto impacto na cidade.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: O Rio Innovation Week apresenta seu primeiro palestrante robô, chamado Tobias. Ele interage com o público e discute o uso social de inteligência artificial. Desenvolvido pela empresa Bolha, o robô possui 1,30 metro de altura. O software levou um ano para ser criado e a estrutura física veio da China. O evento ocorre até sexta-feira (7) no Píer Mauá e deve atrair 200 mil pessoas. A Globo participa da programação com mais de 20 painéis.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/r.text: A Fundação Rio-Águas iniciou nesta quarta-feira (5) a manutenção do Piscinão de Ramos, na Zona Norte do Rio. O lago ficará vazio durante as obras. https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: The Royal Navy's UK Maritime Trade Operations unit (UKMTO) has reported an apparent attempted attack on a tanker in the Gulf of Aden, the first in this area since the start of the Houthi blockade of Saudi ports began last month. At about 1430 hours UTC, the master of a tanker reported hearing an explosion close to the vessel while transiting about 95 nautical miles to the southeast of Aden, well south of the normal shipping lane to and from Bab el-Mandeb. No injuries were reported, and there was no environmental impact. An investigation into the circumstances of the blast is under way. Open source analyst AtlasObserver has tentatively identified the possible subject of the attack as the Dominica-flagged product tanker Daisy (IMO 9516545). The vessel was the only ship on AIS near the reported position at the reported time, other marine traffic being located to the north in the main shipping lane. Immediately after the time of the attack, the Daisy altered course and went AIS-dark. Daisy fits the approximate profile of a vessel that Houthi forces would wish to target: a tanker, Saudi in ownership, inbound towards the direction of Bab el-Mandeb. All other recent attacks have been located in the southern Red Sea, closer to Houthi-controlled shores, but the group has a long history of striking traffic in the Gulf of Aden. If confirmed, the attempt would suggest that the group is willing to take the escalatory step of expanding its targeting into an additional region. The attempt follows shortly after Houthi forces threatened to intensify their strike campaign in order to counter Saudi efforts to avoid the southern Red Sea. Some tankers departing Yanbu have begun heading northwards, through the Suez Canal, in order to evade the Houthi blockade - much to the Houthis' annoyance. The Yemeni militant group said Wednesday it would be “tightening the naval blockade” in response to Saudi efforts to reroute tankers to the north.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Uma baleia franca filmada com filhote nesta terça-feira (4) no Arpoador estava com uma rede de pesca presa na cabeça e na boca. O pesquisador Thiago Ferrari explicou que a espécie está ameaçada e que o salto do animal pode ser uma tentativa de se soltar da rede. O diretor do projeto alertou para que a população não tente ajudar o animal. A costa fluminense também serve de rota migratória para baleias-jubarte. As jubartes viajam até 9 mil quilômetros da Antártida para se reproduzir na Bahia. Atualmente, mais de 30 mil baleias passam pelo litoral brasileiro anualmente.

Por Fernanda Graell, Elis Silvestri, Roberta Pennafort, Gabrielle Malerba, Jornal Hoje A Lei Maria da Penha completa 20 anos com o Brasil registrando 732 feminicídios no primeiro semestre de 2026. O dado representa a maior média da série histórica. Aos 81 anos, Maria da Penha se declarou sobrevivente e disse continuar lutando "para que nós só sejamos reconhecidas como seres humanos que merecem respeito". Sancionada em 2006, a lei foi criada após o Brasil ser responsabilizado pela OEA por negligência e omissão em relação à violência contra as mulheres. A juíza Elen Barbosa explicou que as mulheres denunciam mais atualmente. Contudo, os casos também chegam ao Judiciário com grau maior de violência. Quase 337 mil medidas protetivas de urgência foram concedidas no primeiro semestre deste ano. O volume é o maior registrado desde 2020.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Eight of the world’s leading shipping trade associations, representing elements from containerships to tankers, bulkers, and passenger ships, released a letter submitted to the United Nations warning of the dangers of permitting the imposition of tolls or fees in the Strait of Hormuz. The groups released the letter, which was sent on Monday, August 3, as rumors circulated that Oman and Iran have reached terms for an agreement to manage the Strait, and U.S. officials said a deal is imminent. The groups reiterated their concerns over potential fees in the letter, which is addressed to UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres and IMO Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez. In addition to the direct costs and the threats to supply chains, economic stability, and energy security, the groups, which include the International Chamber of Shipping, ASA, BIMCO, CLIA, ECSA, INTERCARGO, INTERTANKO, and the World Shipping Council, warned of the precedent and potential broader effects on the established international practices for the freedom of navigation. “Introducing compulsory charges for transit, or service fees that are a toll in all but name, through the Strait of Hormuz would represent a significant departure from established international practice,” states the letter. The shipping groups assert that, “Once such a precedent is established, it becomes increasingly difficult to resist similar measures elsewhere, creating uncertainty for international shipping and global commerce.” They warn that it would establish a precedent that could undermine the internationally recognized legal framework governing straits used for international navigation and transit passage. They are calling on the leaders of the UN and the IMO to ensure that internationally recognized rights of navigation are not compromised or “used as part of broader political negotiations.” They assert that it is vital that everyone continue supporting the preservation of the freedom of navigation as “the foundation of international maritime governance.” The Trump administration has wavered throughout the war on exactly what freedom of navigation would look like in an agreement with Iran. CENTCOM is asserting today that the “southern route” remains free and open for all commercial vessels and that over the past three months, “U.S. forces have assisted more than 1,000 vessels in successfully transiting the strait despite unwarranted Iranian aggression.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: The Houthi rebels in Yemen asserted that they are expanding their blockade against Saudi tankers, reporting an attack on a vessel in the northern reaches of the Red Sea. The group said it would be “tightening the naval blockade” in response to Saudi efforts to reroute tankers to the north, avoiding the Houthi threat near Bab al-Mandab. In an unconfirmed report, the Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed on August 5 that they had struck a MR product tanker Wafa (49,990 dwt) outside the Yanbu port complex in the northern Red Sea. Saree always claims “direct hits,” saying the attacks were “precise,” while often the reports turn into near misses or having caused minimal damage. The product tanker, which was built in 2014, was last reported in the Red Sea, although Windward AI speculates the vessel turned around after the Houthis announced their blockade on July 22. The Saudi-flagged vessel controlled by Bahri has been dark since mid-July. Windward AI points out that if the vessel was in fact struck, it would have been “hundreds of kilometers from the declared blockade zone.” The Houthis counted this as their eighth attack on Saudi-linked vessels, although only five have been documented. In addition, Saree asserted that 29 Saudi oil tankers have been “forced to turn back in the Red and Arabian seas.” He said the rebels continue to work on the principle of “a blockade for a blockade,” equating the effort to the U.S. blockade of Iran while saying this was specifically against Saudi Arabia for its aggression in Yemen. Experts believe the Houthis are attempting to pressure Saudi Arabia in peace talks for Yemen. The Houthis on August 4 also claimed an attack on a smaller, regional Saudi airport, Najran, which is located just north of the border with Yemen. Saree asserted the attack was in response to Saudi forces violating Yemen’s airspace with drones. Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, has reemerged as a major oil terminal since the start of hostilities in the Persian Gulf and the closing of the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia accelerated crude oil shipments through its desert pipelines to the terminal and refinery on the Red Sea. Tankers have been loading at the terminal to continue oil shipments to the Far East, and while they can head north to the Suez Canal, it is a longer route, and the large tankers have to transship the oil overland to make the canal transit.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Officials in Ukraine are reporting that they were informed that Sweden’s Supreme Court has upheld a lower court decision to hand over a cargo ship accused of entering the occupied ports of Crimea and exporting grain. It is being called a landmark decision as it represents the first time a foreign court has sided with Ukraine in the seizure of assets that violated international sanctions. Ukraine, in the past, has on several occasions seized vessels locally that it said had been involved in the export of grain and other materials from Crimea. The international community has barred the ports of Crimea and trade from Crimea after the Russian annexation of the region in 2014. Earlier this year, Ukrainian prosecutors appealed to both Sweden and Israel to stop vessels that they accused of illegal exports from Crimea. Swedish authorities had detained the small cargo ship Caffa (4,337 dwt) in March 2026 as it was sailing from Casablanca to St. Petersburg. They reported the ship was suspected of operating under a false flag and had possible maritime safety violations. Further, the Swedish authorities asserted the crew presented false papers when the vessel was inspected. They attempted to prosecute the captain of the Caffa but later dropped the charges. Databases list the vessel as operating under a false flag, claiming registry in Guinea. The ship had its classification withdrawn in June 2025 by the Russian Maritime Register of Ships, but was reported to have a crew of 11, mostly Russians, aboard when it was stopped. Ukraine’s prosecutors approached their Swedish colleagues and requested the seizure of the vessel on the charges of transporting stolen grain. They documented that the ship had entered Sevastopol, where it loaded approximately 3,000 tons of barley that Russia shipped to Syria. They asserted it was the first shipment as Russia was trying to build its relationship with the new government of Syria after the fall of dictator Bashar al-Assad. Swedish prosecutors determined that the courts should decide the situation. The lower courts had ordered that the ship should be turned over to Ukraine, but the decision had been appealed to the Supreme Court.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/541824-op.text: Jeffrey Lewis is a member at Cozen O’Connor and has over 30 years of extensive... A few months ago, I authored an article for Marine News focused on just one of the many successful features of the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 (“OPA 90,” Pub. L. No. 101-380 (1990)) — Alaska’s regional citizen advisory councils (RCACs). The Prince William Sound and Cook Inlet RCACs were established under OPA 90 to work with oil and gas industry interests on behalf of the surrounding communities to ensure safe operations and community buy-in. I was heartened by the positive responses I received from friends, colleagues, and the general readership, which served as a reminder to me that OPA 90 more broadly is one of the best thought out and smartly crafted environmental statutes of our modern era. Accordingly, I think it is fitting here to revisit some of the largely forgotten events that led to the enactment of OPA 90, and to highlight some of the many effective and impactful features of the Act. The TORREY CANYON, Ixtoc I, and the EXXON VALDEZ The 1967 TORREY CANYON disaster marked a significant turning point in public thinking and awareness about oil spills, because of its impacts on coastal communities and the marine environment. It is a classic case of environmental damage. The S.S. TORREY CANYON was a tank ship that was fabricated at Newport News, Virginia, in 1959, and “jumboized” to a dead weight of 120,890 tons at a Japanese shipyard in 1965. In February, 1967, the TORREY CANYON left the Persian Gulf laden with crude oil and destined for Milford Haven, Wales, via the Cape of Good Hope. Most of the voyage was uneventful. At noon on March 17, the tank ship was near the Canary Islands headed on a course that would take it to the west of the Isles of Scilly, which are just off the southwestern tip of Cornwall. During the remainder of the day, the vessel was actually moved to the East, apparently as a result of strong currents. By 6:30 am on March 18, the ship found itself sailing to the East, rather than to the West, of the Isles of Scilly. After a number of maneuvers by master and crew attempting to change course and head off disaster, at 8:50 am on March 18, 1967, at full speed and in broad daylight, the TORREY CANYON ran aground on the rocks of the Scilly Islands. Over the days that followed, all of the ship’s 764,303 barrels, or 32,100,757 gallons, of crude oil leaked from its tanks and covered the coasts of southern England and Normandy. The TORREY CANYON disaster got the world’s attention, and was the beginning of a shift in thinking about marine pollution, which previously had been focused on reducing discharges of oily bilge water and other pollutants that can occur within the scope of a vessel’s routine operations.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos (MPor) publicou nesta quinta-feira (30/07) o Plano Mestre do Complexo Portuário de Paranaguá e Antonina , no Paraná. O documento orienta ações e investimentos de curto, médio e longo prazos nos dois portos, nos acessos ao complexo portuário e na relação porto-cidade, conforme previsto na legislação setorial. O documento foi elaborado pela Infra S.A. , com a participação da Autoridade Portuária de Paranaguá e Antonina (Appa) , sob a coordenação da Secretaria Nacional de Portos (SNP), por meio do Departamento de Gestão e Modernização Portuária (DGMP). O plano contempla medidas relacionadas à integração entre porto-cidade e ao meio ambiente, como ações voltadas à mitigação dos impactos de eventos climáticos adversos e ao fortalecimento da comunicação entre autoridade portuária, terminais, poder público e população. Antes da publicação, o documento foi submetido a consulta pública entre 6 de fevereiro e 23 de março de 2026. O Plano Mestre do Complexo Portuário de Paranaguá e Antonina está organizado em quatro capítulos: Síntese do Complexo Portuário; Projeção de Demanda e Capacidades; Análise Estratégica; e Plano de Ações e Investimentos. O documento também conta com um apêndice que reúne levantamentos de dados e diagnósticos detalhados utilizados como base para as análises apresentadas no plano. A íntegra do documento, os apêndices, o ato administrativo de aprovação e o caderno de respostas às contribuições recebidas durante a consulta pública estão disponíveis no site do MPor .

No primeiro semestre de 2026, portos de diferentes regiões registraram crescimento na movimentação de cargas. Entre os destaques estão complexos como Santos (SP), Suape (PE), Itaqui (MA) e Itajaí (SC) , além dos portos públicos da Bahia e dos portos de Paranaguá e Antonina , no Paraná. O levantamento semestral do Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos reuniu dados de nove portos de diferentes regiões do país de janeiro a junho de 2026, com base em informações enviadas pelas autoridades portuárias. Confira o desempenho da movimentação no período: Considerado o maior porto da América Latina, o Porto de Santos movimentou 92,8 milhões de toneladas no primeiro semestre , um aumento de 5,05% em relação às 88,3 milhões de toneladas do mesmo período de 2025. No primeiro semestre de 2026, 68,71 milhões de toneladas corresponderam a cargas de exportação, enquanto 24,08 milhões de toneladas foram de importação. Nas importações, o maior volume foi registrado em carga geral, com 14,54 milhões de toneladas , puxado principalmente pela carga conteinerizada, que somou 14,10 milhões de toneladas. Em seguida aparecem os granéis sólidos, com 5,71 milhões de toneladas, tendo o adubo como principal carga do grupo, com 3,72 milhões de toneladas. Já os granéis líquidos importados somaram 3,82 milhões de toneladas, com destaque para óleo diesel e gasóleo, que alcançaram 1,56 milhão. Nas exportações, os granéis sólidos lideraram a movimentação, com 41,04 milhões de toneladas , impulsionados principalmente pela soja em grãos, que somou 25,61 milhões de toneladas. A carga geral exportada alcançou 21,35 milhões de toneladas, com predominância da carga conteinerizada, que registrou 16,71 milhões de toneladas. Já os granéis líquidos somaram 6,31 milhões de toneladas, com destaque para óleo combustível, com 2,09 milhões de toneladas, sucos cítricos, com 1,07 milhão, e óleo diesel e gasóleo, com 1,02 milhão. Os portos de Paranaguá e Antonina, administrados pela autoridade portuária Portos do Paraná, movimentaram 34,44 milhões de toneladas de cargas no primeiro semestre de 2026 , entre importações e exportações. O volume representa crescimento de 0,6% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Desse total, 22,30 milhões de toneladas corresponderam a exportações, enquanto as importações somaram 12,1 milhões de toneladas.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-l.text: The Nautical Institute draws lessons learned from an incident where a tug deckhand was fatally injured after a mooring line came under tension during shipyard berthing operations. A cargo vessel in ballast arrived in a port to enter a shipyard under the guidance of a pilot. The pilot and Master agreed on a manoeuvring plan. The two tugs in attendance were to accept two mooring lines each, from the bow and stern central chock of the vessel respectively. The two lines were supposed to be passed to each attending tug together as one. At the arriving vessel’s stern, this was done quickly. At the bow, only one line was given to the attending tug forward. This line was attached to the tug’s towing hook and, unknown to the tug Master, it was made fast on the arriving vessel. While waiting for the second mooring line, the tug passed dangerously close to the port bow of the vessel. The two personnel in the tug’s towing area had to move around to avoid the risks posed by the line that had been secured. The forward tug then manoeuvred to take the second mooring line, which was now suspended from the bow of the vessel. As the tug manoeuvred, the line already secured came under strain, again coming dangerously close to the two seafarers on the stern of the tug. One of them ducked, and the mooring line made a glancing blow on his helmet, knocking it off his head. The deck hand next to him was struck in the chest by the line under tension and seriously injured. The stretched line then pulled the tug towards the vessel and caused the tug to contact the vessel. The uninjured seafarer released the line using the emergency release device on the hook. He also reported the events to the Master at the controls. The tug Master immediately reported the situation to the pilot and the pilot station and requested an ambulance. The victim was quickly transported to the dock, and medical teams were mobilised. The victim was in a serious condition and was taken to the hospital by the paramedics without delay. Despite all efforts the victim succumbed to his injuries. The investigation found, among other things, that the enclosed forecastle deck of the arriving vessel made it difficult for the crew on the fo’c’sle deck to establish effective communication or eye contact with the crew on the stern of the tug. The investigation also found that the tug company should establish procedures for situations where the mooring lines cannot be given at the same time, including precautions to be taken by the tug personnel.

https://safety4sea.com/opportunity-green.text: Climate NGO Opportunity Green has urged IMO Member States to support the Net-Zero Framework (NZF) and reject proposals that could weaken its agreed structure. T he organisation warned that proposed amendments to IMO’s MARPOL Annex VI could undermine investment in zero- and near-zero-emission fuels (ZNZs), weaken emissions reduction incentives and remove a dedicated source of climate finance for developing countries. Opportunity Green concluded that Tuvalu’s proposal is the only option capable of achieving the goals of the IMO’s 2023 GHG Strategy, aligning international shipping with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C goal and complying with states’ legal obligations. However, it noted that the proposal is unlikely to receive sufficient support for adoption, meaning pursuing it alone could risk preventing any agreement. Any suggestion of adopting a weakened proposal is tantamount to abandoning climate vulnerable countries and failing states’ duty to co-operate as the very essence of multilateralism. We expect governments to act with the same integrity and courage they showed when the framework text was first agreed, and to continue pushing for its adoption later this year It warned that failure to reach agreement could lead to multiple regional shipping emissions reduction schemes that may not be compatible and could negatively affect global shipping efficiency. Member States were encouraged to consider the analysis carefully when developing their positions ahead of MEPC.

https://safety4sea.com/eu-shippings-clea.text: European Union member states and the European Commission are calling on the International Maritime Organization (IMO) to ensure that its proposed Net-Zero Framework (NZF) includes stronger incentives for the early production and adoption of zero- and near-zero-emission marine fuels. A joint submission has been filed ahead of the 22nd session of the IMO’s Intersessional Working Group on Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions from Ships (ISWG-GHG 22), scheduled to take place from 1 to 4 September. The proposal is backed by 27 European countries, including major maritime nations such as Greece, Denmark, Germany, Cyprus, Malta and the Netherlands, alongside the European Commission. As explained, the transition of shipping towards fuels, technologies and energy sources capable of delivering net-zero GHG emissions will require significant long-term investment across the maritime value chain. To achieve this transition cost-effectively while ensuring the growing availability of cleaner energy solutions, investors need a clear, predictable and stable regulatory pathway. At the same time, early deployment and the gradual scaling up of zero- and near-zero-emission fuels (ZNZs), supported by appropriate incentives, will help accelerate technological development, increase supply and drive down costs over time. Therefore, any proposals addressing concerns around the IMO Net-Zero Framework should preserve certainty around the direction of the energy transition and provide clear signals of future demand for ZNZs. Such predictability will help reduce investment risks in shipping and related sectors, while preventing stranded assets resulting from fragmented or uncoordinated investment decisions.

https://safety4sea.com/australia-launche.text: Sea containers are a cornerstone of global trade, with millions of units transported across international supply chains each year. However, their movement also creates pathways for the spread of pests and diseases, posing risks to agriculture, biodiversity, food security and international commerce. T o address these risks, the Australian Government has developed a series of capacity-building videos aimed at helping industry participants and global stakeholders reduce pest contamination associated with sea container movements. Pest incursions can have significant environmental and economic consequences, threatening ecosystems, agricultural production and food supplies. Contaminated containers can also disrupt trade by causing shipment delays, increasing compliance costs and requiring additional measures such as cleaning, inspection and outbreak management. Everyone involved in the sea container supply chain has a responsibility to ensure containers and their cargo are free from visible pest contamination. Maintaining pest-free international trade is essential to protecting agriculture, the environment and global ecosystems. However, the growing volume of sea containers and cargo moving between countries has increased the risk of pests spreading through international trade networks.
