https://www.oedigital.com/news/542469-us.text: The U.S. Interior Department is preparing to ease environmental review requirements for some oil and gas exploration activities in Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve as part of the Trump administration's push to speed energy development in the Arctic, an Interior spokesperson said on Wednesday. The agency is working on a proposed "categorical exclusion" that would accelerate permitting for winter oil and gas exploration activities, including seismic surveys and exploratory drilling operations in the reserve, the spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The proposal would be based on findings from dozens of prior environmental reviews showing that winter exploration activities conducted under established operating procedures and mitigation measures have no significant impacts, the spokesperson said. "These efforts are about using decades of experience and analysis to create a more efficient, predictable, and effective process while upholding environmental standards," the spokesperson said. Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to travel to Alaska this week as administration officials continue promoting energy development in the state. A proposed LNG terminal in the state that is a high priority for Trump has recently encountered setbacks, including a stalled bill in the state legislature that would have offered support for the project. The move by Interior was first reported by High Country News, which said the proposed categorical exclusion could allow winter exploration and drilling activities in the reserve to proceed without project-specific environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542468-st.text: Shipping traffic at the Strait of Hormuz rose slightly even as a standoff persisted between the United States and Iran, data showed on Thursday, while the market monitored Iran-Oman talks about the waterway. Visible commodity vessel transits at Hormuz totalled 10 on Wednesday, up slightly from eight on Tuesday, data from Kpler showed. This was below a 10-day moving average of about 15 vessels. Two medium-range fuel tankers, a liquefied petroleum gas carrier, a Panamax-sized tanker, and three handymax-sized tankers entered the strait from the Gulf of Oman. A medium-range fuel tanker, a bitumen tanker and a bulk carrier exited the waterway from the Gulf. Iran and Oman are still working on the details of an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz, a senior Iranian source said on Wednesday, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the two countries had agreed how to share the waterway and its revenue. A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was later extinguished, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said early on Thursday.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542470-to.text: TotalEnergies has completed the transfer of its 10% interest in Russia's Arctic LNG 2 project to NordLine, a subsidiary of Russian gas producer Novatek, and is no longer a shareholder in the project. The transfer follows TotalEnergies' announcement of its second-quarter 2026 results, when it said the transaction with NordLine was being completed. As part of the transfer agreement, TotalEnergies retains the right to be reimbursed by Arctic LNG 2 for its share of loans provided by shareholders to the project, amounting to about $1.3 billion. Any repayment will be subject to applicable sanctions. Arctic LNG 2 is majority-owned by Novatek and is subject to Western sanctions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The project was designed to eventually produce 19.8 million metric tons of LNG per year. Sanctions have clouded the project's prospects and complicated efforts to sell LNG produced by the facility. TotalEnergies had maintained interests in Russian LNG plants following the imposition of Western sanctions but has considered selling its remaining Russian stakes due to sanctions preventing companies from importing the gas.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/kuwait.text: Kuwait and Qatar - two of the Persian Gulf’s smaller oil producers - are sending more crude through the Strait of Hormuz, adding to an increase in shipments that are keeping global prices in check. The two countries, which exported a combined 2 million barrels a day of oil before the outbreak of the Iran war, have managed to get shipments back to 70 percent of pre-conflict levels, according to traders, who asked not to be named as they’re not allowed to speak to media. The United Arab Emirates was the first gulf producer to export large volumes of oil through Hormuz, using ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman in a tactic known as shuttling. It has since been joined by Saudi Arabia, which has been forced to rely more on exporting through the waterway after Houthi militants started targeting tankers in the Red Sea. A total of around 7 to 8 million barrels of oil a day is now exiting Hormuz, up from around 4 million barrels a day in mid-July, the traders said. That’s around three-quarters of pre-war levels. Vortexa said on Monday that the seven-day average of oil flows through the waterway was close to 10 million barrels a day. The increasing volumes come as Washington and Tehran remain in a stalemate over the Iran war, with control of Hormuz the main point of contention. Global benchmark Brent oil is trading near $87 a barrel, down from above $120 in late April. Qatar and Kuwait began shuttling cargoes through Hormuz around June, and have ramped up volumes despite the risk of Iranian attacks. A Kuwait Petroleum Corp. supertanker was struck earlier in August as it was transiting the chokepoint, the country said in representations to the UN’s shipping watchdog.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/hor.text: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz sits near historic lows, even as diplomatic efforts to halt hostilities in the Middle East make progress, media reports said on Wednesday. According to preliminary Kpler data cited by Al Jazeera and CNBC, just five commercial tankers traversed the narrow waterway on Tuesday, compared to a 10-day average of 15. Roughly a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas flowed through the strait prior to the outbreak of the war between the U.S. and Iran in late February. Following the start of the conflict, Tehran moved to effectively shutter activity in the Strait of Hormuz, denting global supply flows and putting upward pressure on oil prices. Still, Brent crude prices have retreated in recent days, sliding below the $90-a-barrel level. Driving the fall was a report from Russia’s RIA Novosti outlet that the U.S. and Iran had agreed to a new ceasefire agreement which would be announced in the coming days. Investing.com could not immediately verify the report, which cited Iranian and Pakistani sources. Meanwhile, a top Iranian official has said Iran and Oman have agreed on a new temporary route through the Strait of Hormuz after diplomats held talks in Tehran, Al Jazeera has reported. But the official stressed that the strait will not reopen completely until the U.S. follows its commitments made in a now-expired framework deal signed in June.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ind.text: Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore reaffirmed their commitment to ensuring the straits of Malacca and Singapore remain free, open and secure for international shipping, as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified attention on global maritime chokepoints. The three littoral states affirmed that the status of the straits of Malacca and Singapore are international navigation waterways where the right of transit passage applies under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, emphasizing that navigational rights and freedoms must be respected “both in principle and practice,” according to a joint statement issued at the 17th Co-operation Forum in Singapore on Aug. 25. “Events in the Middle East this year reminded the world that open sea lanes can never be taken for granted,” Singapore Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow said at the opening of the forum. “In our part of the world, we will endeavor to keep the Straits of Malacca and Singapore free, open, and safe for international shipping.” More than 100,000 vessels transit the straits of Malacca and Singapore each year, carrying almost a quarter of global seaborne trade and nearly a third of the world’s oil and gas supplies, Siow said. In contrast, total crossings through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 23 vessels/day over Aug. 21-23, compared with a daily average of more than 110 vessels prior to the war in the Middle East, according to S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab). At the two-day event held from Aug. 25 to 26 the three littoral states, user states and industry stakeholders are expected to discuss the safe introduction of new technologies and alternative fuels in the straits of Malacca and Singapore, while also reviewing technical projects to improve navigational safety, the joint statement said.

https://splash247.com/knot-takes-modern-.text: KNOT Offshore Partners is adding another young shuttle tanker from its parent in a $113m deal, extending a run of fleet renewal transactions while tackling one of its largest near-term debt maturities. The New York-listed partnership has agreed to acquire the vessel-owning company behind the 2024-built Hedda Knutsen from sponsor Knutsen NYK Offshore Tankers. KNOT will take on $89.4m of outstanding vessel debt and $800,000 of capitalised financing fees, leaving an initial cash cost of about $24.4m, subject to working-capital adjustments. The deal has been approved by the partnership’s board and its independent conflicts committee. The 154,000 dwt DP2 suezmax, built at COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry, is already working in Brazil for Petrobras. Firm employment runs until November 2034, with the Brazilian energy giant holding an option for another five years. The deal was already in the works. Knutsen NYK offered three shuttle tankers to its listed affiliate in June under the dropdown arrangements established when KNOT Offshore Partners floated. The independent committee opted against pursuing two of the ships but continued negotiations on the third. Once completed, the acquisition should take KNOT Offshore Partners’ fleet from 19 to 20 shuttle tankers and continue a steady refresh of its asset base. The fleet averaged 10.5 years of age at the end of the first quarter, when the company had $858m of fixed charter backlog with an average remaining firm duration of about 2.4 years.

https://splash247.com/iran-blacklist-thr.text: The nascent and increasingly vital shuttle tanker trade moving Middle East crude through the Strait of Hormuz for transfer in the Gulf of Oman is under fresh threat after Iran blacklisted some of the vessels at the heart of the operation this week. Broker Braemar warned that 12 VLCCs named by Tehran had carried around 900,000 barrels per day, equivalent to 16% of all crude lifted from inside the Middle East Gulf since the collapse of the memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran in early July. More significantly, the ships accounted for around 750,000 barrels per day, or 24%, of crude subsequently transferred ship-to-ship outside Hormuz. Iran has threatened blacklisted vessels with fines, detention and cargo confiscation and warned that ships conducting STS operations with them could themselves be added to the list. The threat is already having an impact. Reuters reported this week that at least three Indian refiners and a global energy major planned to stop using blacklisted vessels because of security concerns. “If owners begin avoiding these highly active shuttle tankers, the ships yet unnamed by Iran and still willing to transit Hormuz are likely to command higher premiums,” Braemar noted.

https://splash247.com/container-shipping.text: The container shipping industry needs to move fire prevention much further upstream, identifying dangerous cargo risks at booking rather than discovering them after a box has been loaded onboard. That is the central argument of a new report from Thetius and Tigris Systems examining why dangerous goods incidents remain stubbornly difficult to prevent despite established international regulations. The scale of the problem is worsening. There were 250 vessel fires in 2024, up 20% year-on-year and the highest number for a decade, while TT Club estimates a major containership fire occurs roughly every 60 days. Undeclared and misdeclared dangerous goods remain the leading cause, according to the World Shipping Council. The report argues shipping does not primarily suffer from a lack of information. The problem is that declarations, safety data sheets and subsequent corrections often sit in different emails, PDFs and operational systems, leaving carriers, terminals and vessels working from incomplete or outdated versions. “Before loading, you need to know exactly what is in the container,” says dangerous goods safety adviser Paola Staiano. “You cannot feed the system with approximate information.” One proposed solution is much more aggressive digital screening at the booking stage. Dangerous goods declarations, safety data sheets and supporting documents should be automatically compared for conflicting UN numbers, classifications, packaging and quantities. Systems should also extract operational information such as temperature limits, segregation requirements and firefighting instructions.

https://petronoticias.com.br/a-cummins-b.text: A Cummins Brasil inicia uma nova etapa da operação de Osasco (SP), com a produção local de tecnologias em eixos voltadas às aplicações mais exigentes do mercado. Após um amplo ciclo de modernização realizado nos últimos anos, a unidade passa a produzir o primeiro diferencial anterior fabricado no Brasil, destinado às aplicações rodoviárias 6×4, além de iniciar a produção do MT610 para mineração, eixo desenvolvido para suportar até 38 toneladas de carga vertical, o de maior capacidade já produzido pela operação. Os avanços, apresentados no ano em que a operação de eixos em Osasco (SP) celebra 70 anos, reforçam a capacidade da Cummins de desenvolver e produzir localmente tecnologias de maior complexidade para segmentos que demandam elevados níveis de robustez, produtividade e capacidade de carga. Os dois projetos atendem demandas distintas do mercado, mas representam uma mesma estratégia de evolução da capacidade industrial no Brasil. Kleber Assanti, diretor geral da Divisão de Eixos da Cummins, disse que “ A produção local do diferencial anterior do MT160 e do MT610 para mineração visa acompanhar a evolução das aplicações e das necessidades dos mercados em que atuamos. O crescimento do agronegócio, da logística de longa distância e do transporte rodoviário impulsionou a demanda por caminhões 6×4 cada vez mais robustos, enquanto a expansão da mineração passou a exigir eixos com maior capacidade estrutural para operar em condições extremas”. A produção local do diferencial anterior do MT160 representa um importante avanço na capacidade industrial da operação de Osasco. Utilizado em conjuntos tandem destinados às aplicações rodoviárias 6×4, o componente passa a ser fabricado no Brasil após um amplo trabalho de industrialização que envolveu o desenvolvimento de novos processos produtivos, ferramental, linha de montagem e capacitação técnica da equipe. Responsável por transmitir torque às rodas motrizes e também ao eixo traseiro do conjunto tandem, o diferencial anterior possui uma arquitetura mais complexa e exige processos produtivos específicos para sua fabricação. “A nacionalização desse diferencial representa um novo patamar para a nossa operação. Além de incorporar uma tecnologia de maior complexidade ao processo produtivo, esse desenvolvimento amplia nossa capacidade de industrializar futuras plataformas tandem e reforça o papel da engenharia brasileira na evolução do portfólio global da companhia” , afirma Rafael Souza(direita), diretor de Produto e PMO da Divisão de Eixos da Cummins. Desenvolvido para aplicações exclusivamente off-highway, o MT610 amplia o portfólio da Cummins para operações de mineração que exigem elevada capacidade de carga, robustez estrutural e alta disponibilidade operacional. https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A Braskem realizou nesta quarta-feira, 26 de agosto, a cerimônia de batismo do navio Blissful Future, na China, marco que oficializa a incorporação de mais uma embarcação à frota de navios de nafta da Braskem Trading & Shipping (BT&S). Com a nova unidade, a companhia passa a operar três embarcações no segmento de transporte de líquidos: Blooming Future, Beautiful Future e Blissful Future. A frota será ampliada com a entrega do Bold Future, prevista para janeiro de 2027, completando uma série de quatro navios. A Braskem opera ainda os gaseiros Brave Future e Brilliant Future, destinados ao transporte de etano. O batismo integra o projeto Seas of the Future, iniciativa da companhia voltada à expansão e modernização de sua frota marítima. Segundo Hardi Schuck, responsável pelo projeto, a chegada do Blissful Future reforça o compromisso da Braskem com a eficiência logística, o aumento da competitividade e a redução das emissões associadas ao transporte marítimo global. O Blissful Future tem 228 metros de comprimento e capacidade de carga de aproximadamente 89.500 metros cúbicos. As novas embarcações da série foram projetadas para reduzir em cerca de 30% as emissões de CO₂e em comparação à média da frota atualmente operada pela companhia. Entre os recursos que sustentam essa eficiência estão um motor principal de alta eficiência, apto para uso de biocombustíveis, além de sistemas voltados à redução de poluentes: o Scrubber, que reduz emissões de óxidos de enxofre, e o SCR, que mitiga óxidos de nitrogênio. O navio conta ainda com pintura de ultrabaixo atrito no casco, sistemas VFD e soluções de propulsão como o Pre-Swirl Duct e o Twisted Rudder, que contribuem para otimizar o desempenho da navegação e reduzir o consumo de energia. Os navios da classe LR1, categoria à qual pertence o Blissful Future, têm papel estratégico no transporte de nafta para as operações industriais da Braskem, atendendo à rota entre a costa do Golfo dos Estados Unidos e o Brasil. Quando a série de quatro embarcações estiver completa, a expectativa é que ela seja capaz de movimentar entre 40% e 50% da demanda de importação de nafta da companhia.

A Log-In Logística Integrada concluiu a docagem do navio Log-In Endurance, embarcação que integra a frota de cabotagem e Mercosul da companhia e conecta os portos de Manaus, no Amazonas, a Buenos Aires, na Argentina. O processo, realizado ao longo do segundo trimestre, faz parte da estratégia contínua de modernização da frota, reunindo manutenção preventiva, atualização tecnológica, adequações regulatórias e iniciativas voltadas à eficiência energética. O escopo da docagem incluiu uma série de intervenções estruturais e operacionais, como o tratamento e a pintura do casco e das tampas de porão, além da manutenção de motores elétricos, bombas, válvulas e sistemas de propulsão e governo. Como parte do processo, o Log-In Endurance passou a operar com a nova identidade visual da companhia, marcada pela cor verde em destaque no casco e pela aplicação da marca da empresa. A mudança estética acompanha o atual posicionamento institucional da Log-In, voltado a aproximar a logística do cotidiano das pessoas. Mauricio Trompowsky, diretor de Operações da Log-In Logística Integrada, afirma que a modernização do navio integra um plano permanente de fortalecimento da operação da companhia. Segundo ele, a docagem representa um investimento contínuo na confiabilidade e na evolução da frota, incorporando melhorias que contribuem para uma operação mais eficiente e alinhada às demandas atuais da logística brasileira. A embarcação também passou por modernizações nos sistemas de navegação do passadiço, dentro do processo de padronização tecnológica da frota. Entre as iniciativas está a aplicação de pintura com silicone no hélice, tecnologia já utilizada em outras embarcações da companhia, que melhora a hidrodinâmica do propulsor e contribui para uma navegação mais eficiente. O navio recebeu ainda retrofits voltados à eficiência energética e passou pela renovação quinquenal das certificações de classe, etapa necessária para garantir a conformidade regulatória e a segurança das operações.

A Aliança Navegação e Logística passa a operar no APM Terminals Suape a partir de 1º de setembro, ampliando sua presença em Pernambuco e reforçando a conectividade logística entre o Nordeste e os principais centros consumidores e produtores do Brasil. A movimentação chega em um momento de expansão da cabotagem na região. Segundo dados da própria companhia, 49% de toda a carga transportada por cabotagem com destino ao Nordeste parte de portos da região Sul, o que reforça o papel desse corredor marítimo no abastecimento do mercado nordestino. Entre os produtos que chegam à região por esse modal estão cereais, sementes e grãos, com 13% de participação, além de plásticos e papel e celulose, cada um com 11%. Os portos catarinenses de Itapoá, Itajaí, Imbituba e Navegantes concentram sozinhos 20% das cargas destinadas a Suape, enquanto outros 11% seguem para o Porto do Pecém, no Ceará. O fluxo também acontece no sentido inverso. O Nordeste vem se firmando como polo produtor e distribuidor para outras regiões do país, e sal, cimento e plástico já respondem por 45% das cargas que saem da região por cabotagem. Para a Aliança, a chegada ao novo terminal representa um salto de infraestrutura. O APM Terminals Suape é o primeiro terminal 100% eletrificado da América Latina e ocupa posição estratégica para o escoamento e a distribuição de cargas, o que deve trazer mais produtividade, confiabilidade e flexibilidade às operações da companhia na região. Luiza Bublitz, presidente da Aliança Navegação e Logística, destaca o potencial de crescimento da cabotagem no Nordeste e afirma que a chegada ao terminal amplia a capacidade de conectar empresas da região aos principais mercados consumidores do país, com o objetivo de apoiar o desenvolvimento econômico local e o crescimento dos clientes atendidos. A operação em Suape passa a contar com três escalas semanais, integradas aos serviços ALCT 1, nos sentidos Sul-Norte e Norte-Sul, e ALCT 2, conectando Pernambuco às regiões Norte, Sudeste e Sul do país. Entre as cargas estratégicas movimentadas estão alimentos, papel e celulose, plásticos, produtos químicos, máquinas e insumos industriais.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A Polícia Civil investiga a agressão a um estudante dentro do Instituto de Filosofia e Ciências Sociais (IFCS) da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), no Centro do Rio . O caso aconteceu na noite de terça-feira (25). Segundo relatos, o estudante, que seria aluno do curso de História, usava uma camiseta e acessórios com estampas que fariam supostamente alusão ao nazismo. A situação teria provocado a reação de outros alunos. Vídeos que circulam nas redes sociais mostram o estudante sendo agredido com socos e chutes por um grupo de pessoas. O caso é apurado pela 1ª DP (Praça Mauá). Segundo a Polícia Civil, até o momento, não houve registro de ocorrência com essas características na delegacia responsável pela área. Após tomar conhecimento do episódio, a unidade instaurou um procedimento para investigar os fatos. Nesta quinta-feira (27), agentes realizaram diligências para obter mais informações e esclarecer as circunstâncias da agressão. A UFRJ informou que instaurou uma comissão de sindicância para apurar o episódio.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: A Justiça do Rio rejeitou o pedido de Anthony Garotinho para anular parte de sua condenação por improbidade. https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The authorities suspect that an error while transferring fuel aboard the Russian-flagged commercial fishing vessel Alpa Crux caused it to lose stability and sink at its dock in Montevideo, Uruguay. The crew was evacuated without injuries, and the berth has been secured while the investigation begins. The fishing vessel Alpha Crux , built in Spain in 2003, was docked when the emergency call was issued around 7:30 p.m. local time on Tuesday, August 25. The ship, which is 50 meters (164 feet) and 946 gross tons, began listing to port and reported a loss of stability. The authorities report that the ship was transferring fuel between tanks when it developed the list. Personnel from the National Ports Administration (ANP) and the Montevideo Port Prefecture took control at the dock and activated the protocols for these incidents. They carried out an evacuation of the 41 crewmembers aboard the vessel, and the shipping agency Idernol Oriental Shipping contracted the specialized operator Nueva Era Oil Spill Response Organization (OSRO) to implement environmental protection measures. Nueva Era deployed equipment, a boat, specialized personnel, and floating containment booms around the vessel to prevent any impact on the water. An extraction pump was also put into operation to recover the oily liquids observed on the surface, which initially appeared to be bilge water. So far, no spills of liquid fuels have been verified. The shipowner initiated actions with the P&I insurance company for the purpose of salvaging the vessel, a task that will begin in the coming days. The fishing vessel had been operating under the Russian flag since 2023. It was reported to be fishing for the Antarctic toothfish, with a license active until the end of August 2026.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: With attacks in the Black Sea having widened to container shipping, MSC has reportedly suspended bookings for the port of Novorossiysk, Russia. Bloomberg saw a customer alert and received confirmation from MSC’s St. Petersburg office after reports that one of the company’s vessels was struck in the Black Sea. The containership MSC Ulsan III was struck by a drone, reports Martin Kelly, Head of Advisory at EOS Risk Group. He writes that the ship had departed Novorossiysk bound for Turkey when it was struck on August 25. There were no reports of injuries, and the ship was continuing on its voyage. AIS signals show the MSC Ulsan III (39,611 dwt) has reached the Sea of Marmara and is off Tekirdag, Turkey. Built in 2004, the ship has a capacity of 2,700 TEU and has operated for MSC since 2022. MSC is telling customers to contact its Russian agency for information about possible logistical alternatives, including its operations at St. Petersburg. It says it is monitoring the situation but not accepting bookings until conditions allow the resumption of regular weekly service. It follows a series of attacks on containerships as Ukraine widens the war on Novorossiysk. Furthermore, it struck the oil terminal earlier in the month, but reportedly agreed to stop striking international tankers heading to or loading at the Caspian CPC offshore terminal near Novorossiysk. There are also reports that some of the grain terminals in the port suspended operations. The Ukrainian News Agency last week reported a strike on the Turkish shipping company Akkon Lines' vessel RMS Team (12,968 dwt). The vessel, which has a capacity of about 1,100 TEU, was struck by a drone on August 21 while heading to Novorossiysk. A fire broke out, and one seafarer was reported missing.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Iran continues its assertions to be stopping all traffic in the Oman Channel as it seeks a deal over the operation of the Strait of Hormuz. It is claiming to have turned back a tanker while there were reports that a Greek-owned tanker was struck on Tuesday night. The semi-official news agencies Fars and Mehr carried reports asserting the latest actions against vessels. They quoted an IRGC spokesperson who asserted, “No vessel traffic has been observed along the southern route over the previous 24 hours.” The report referenced “an Indian tanker” that attempted to transit the southern route inbound to the Gulf. The IRGC said the vessel “received a warning” and turned back. The tanker was identified as Haana. The Marshall Islands-flagged LPG tanker Haana (54,368 dwt) is showing as anchored off the Port of Ras Laffan in Qatar. The vessel was earlier registered at the Khor Fakkan anchorage off the UAE. Built in 2008, the vessel has, since September 2025, been reported to be managed from India. Tracking showed it entered the Strait of Hormuz and did turn, returning to the anchorage. Reports from India indicate that several of the top refineries, along with major energy companies, are studying Iran’s "blacklist" of tankers issued on Sunday, August 23. They are planning to avoid the listed vessels as well as ship-to-ship transfers while determining how Iran will enforce its edict. It is unclear if that led to the Haana aborting its entry into the Gulf or if it was, in fact, bound for Qatar all along. The AI data intelligence firm Windward also reported that it detected a Panama-flagged product tanker that appeared to attempt and then stop an inbound transit through the Strait of Hormuz on August 26. It said the vessel made a U-turn away from the northern corridor but two hours later appeared to be recommencing its transit.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: Fincantieri and Oceania Cruises, a brand of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, marked the float-out of the first of a new generation of cruise ships as NCLH moves forward with a strategy to align the fleet with the enhanced luxury positioning of the brand. The launch came the same day as the first of the line’s oldest ships prepared to leave the fleet. The new ship, named Oceania Sonata , was christened and floated out at the Fincantieri shipyard in Marghera, Italy. She was moved from the assembly dry dock to the fitting out berth for completion of her interior spaces. She is scheduled to enter service in 2027. "The float out of Oceania Sonata is an incredibly exciting moment as we move one step closer to welcoming our first guests aboard next August," said Jason Montague, Chief Luxury Officer of Oceania Cruises. “As the first ship in our new Sonata Class, she represents the beginning of an exciting new chapter for the brand and a defining milestone in the continued evolution of Oceania Cruises." The line highlights that the ship, at 86,000 gross tons, will be approximately 30 percent larger than the prior class, Allura and Vista (68,000 gross tons), and will increase passenger capacity by just 15 percent from 1,200 to 1,390 passengers with the addition of 90 staterooms. The line says the Sonata class is designed in keeping with the brand positioning to provide more space, elevate accommodations, and enhance the culinary experiences aboard. A third of the accommodations will be suites, including four Owner’s Suites and two new suite categories. Oceania Sonata will feature 13 dining venues. Oceania Sonata is 30 percent larger than the lines' prior cruise ships (Oceania Cruises) Construction began with the steel cutting in June 2025. NCLH has now expanded the order to a total of five ships, with a sistership, Oceania Arietta , starting construction for delivery in 2029. Three more sisters will deliver in 2032, 2035, and 2037.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/d.text: The delay in adoption of the IMO's Net Zero Framework (NZF) has changed the outlook for low-emissions shipping, and DNV's annual Forecast to 2050 report reflects the new reality: fuel efficiency and flexibility are the new watchwords, and green fuels will likely be powering the back burner for years to come. The cost of developing a widely available green fuel supply remains the big challenge. While proposed green-fuel manufacturing projects totaling 270 Mtoe are slated for readiness by 2030, and about five percent of the world's fleet is capable of burning alternative fuels, the cost structure does not appear supportive for demand development in the near term. DNV expects demand for low-GHG fuels in the shipping sector to range from 4-22 Mtoe in the same timeframe, rising to at most 33-185 Mtoe by midcentury - a fraction of the potential pre-FID-status supply on the books today. The upper range of those demand projections also depends upon the adoption of the IMO Net Zero Framework (NZF), which would create financial incentives to buy green fuels. The NZF "remedial" penalty tier would be initially priced at $380 per tonne of CO2 equivalent (about $1,200 per tonne of bunker fuel) for out-of-compliance fuel consumption, high enough to start driving adoption. But the NZF faces stiff political opposition as-written, not least from the United States, and its future is uncertain. If adopted as it is, it could enter into effect as early as 2029. If modified in additional negotiations, or replaced with a different text, entry into force could be delayed as late as 2030-2033 - leaving just 17 years to hit the IMO 2050 target. The uncertainty means that when planning future fleet investments, owners have to take not just the scale of the regulatory transition into consideration, but also the speed at which it happens, DNV says. A delayed (or canceled) NZF is a much different scenario than a rapid-onset NZF, with correspondingly different risk-reward profiles for owning bunker-fueled or dual-fueled ships. In the immediate term, there is still something that owners can do to "green" their operations economically. Many energy efficiency measures (hydrodynamic improvements, wind-assisted propulsion, engine derating) can save money and help meet compliance targets under all of the expected regulatory pathways. DNV estimates that shipping could cut its emissions by 16 percent by 2030 and up to 25 percent by 2050 through efficiency measures and speed reduction alone - achieving half the IMO target for GHG cuts merely by using less fuel, and saving more than $20 billion a year in bunkering costs along the way. https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Por que resgate no Nepal e no Tibete é mais dificil do que em Brumadinho? Entenda Um terremoto de magnitude 5,0 atingiu nesta quinta-feira (27) o Tibete, mas em uma região distante da área atingida na quarta (26) pela avalanche de lama e gelo. De acordo com o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS), o tremor ocorreu dentro do Tibete, região autônoma no sudeste da China, e teve profundidade de 10 quilômetros, considerada rasa. O epicentro, no entanto, foi registrado a mais de 800 km de distância do local da avalanche , que atingiu a zona de fronteira com o Nepal. Não havia indícios, até a última atualização desta reportagem, de que os dois eventos estejam relacionados. O governo chinês também não havia informado, se o terremoto causou danos ou vítimas.

Militares do Nepal resgataram nesta quinta-feira (27) 350 pessoas presas em um túnel após uma avalanche. O número de mortos na região chegou a 392. Quase 1.500 pessoas seguem desaparecidas e as buscas continuam. A suspeita é de que o colapso de uma geleira tenha causado a avalanche. Especialistas alertam para o risco de uma nova inundação por bloqueio de detritos.

As mortes por enchentes e deslizamentos na fronteira Nepal-Tibete chegaram a 392 nesta quinta-feira (27). Quase 1.500 pessoas seguem desaparecidas na região. O desastre aconteceu na quarta-feira (26) após o colapso de uma geleira. O impacto gerou um fluxo de água, lama e detritos. A inundação repentina destruiu casas, pontes e estradas próximas a rios. Equipes de resgate enfrentam dificuldades devido à lama e ao risco de novas inundações.

A avalanche que atingiu na quarta-feira (26) uma região de fronteira entre o Nepal e China foi tão forte que provocou até o rompimento de uma barragem hidrelétrica em construção na área. Um vídeo divulgado nesta quinta-feira (27) registrou o momento em que a avalanche inunda a hidrelétrica, que fica no distrito de Rasuwa, no Nepal. ➡️ Mais de 300 pessoas morreram e outras cerca de 1.500 seguiam desaparecidas no Nepal e na vizinha China depois que uma avalanche de gelo, lama e rochas percorreu um rio na quarta-feira (26), desencadeando uma enxurrada catastrófica .

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A história da formação dos sistemas de transporte na Amazônia é o tema do livro “A História do Transporte da Amazônia”, escrito pela historiadora e escritora Etelvina Garcia e publicado pela Fundação Memória do Transporte (FuMTran) . A obra apresenta um levantamento sobre a evolução dos diferentes modais na região e sua relação com a ocupação territorial , os ciclos econômicos e o desenvolvimento social. Ao percorrer a história amazônica desde o período colonial português, a publicação destaca a importância dos rios como vias de circulação e integração entre comunidades, cidades e atividades econômicas. A navegação ocupa papel central na narrativa, mas o livro também aborda o desenvolvimento da aviação regional, das conexões rodoviárias e de outras soluções criadas para superar as grandes distâncias e as particularidades geográficas da região. Segundo a autora, o transporte esteve diretamente ligado às transformações econômicas, sociais e territoriais da Amazônia. “Fazer a memória do transporte da Amazônia não é simplesmente olhar para o passado, é compreender como essa história foi construída para pensar o futuro”, afirma Etelvina Garcia. A obra também registra a contribuição de povos originários, trabalhadores, empresários e empreendedores para a construção das redes de transporte e abastecimento da região. Para o presidente da FuMTran, Antonio Luiz Leite, o resgate dessa trajetória ajuda a compreender a formação e o desenvolvimento do próprio país. O livro teve seu primeiro lançamento em 27 de maio, durante a TranspoAmazônia, em Manaus, e foi apresentado nacionalmente em 18 de agosto, em São Paulo, durante seminário realizado pela FuMTran. Ao todo, foram impressos 3 mil exemplares, que serão distribuídos a bibliotecas públicas, CEUs de São Paulo, entidades do setor de transporte e autoridades dos poderes Executivo, Legislativo e Judiciário. Criada em 1996 pela Confederação Nacional do Transporte (CNT), a FuMTran atua na preservação e divulgação da memória e da história do transporte brasileiro, abrangendo os modais rodoviário, ferroviário, aquaviário e aeroviário, além da infraestrutura e da logística.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542483-om.text: Subsea services and ROV technology provider Omega Subsea has entered into a long-term agreement to establish operations at Hilleren Navy Supply Park in Mathopen, adjacent to Haakonsvern in Western Norway. The company will become a strategic subsea partner and a key tenant at the site, where it will develop a new operational base comprising workshop, warehouse and office facilities. Omega Subsea provides services and technology within ROV operations, survey and subsea operations. The long-term agreement covers approximately 1,500 square meters of workshop, warehouse and office space, in addition to access to 500 square meters of outdoor space with excellent vehicle access and logistics capabilities. The base is scheduled to be operational by 1 January 2027, and the company plans to recruit between five and seven new employees during the first phase. For Hilleren Navy Supply Park, the establishment marks another step in the development of an environment where the maritime industry, technology providers and emergency preparedness services can work more closely together. “This is a long-term and important investment for Omega Subsea. Hilleren provides the infrastructure and access to port facilities we need to support further growth. It enables us to bring together our people, equipment and operations, creating a stronger platform for delivering our services across Western Norway,” said Trond Berge, CEO of Omega Subsea.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542471-se.text: Sempra Energy's unit Port Arthur LNG has started the federal permitting process for a major expansion of its liquefied natural gas export operations in Southeast Texas, according to a regulatory filing made on Wednesday. The proposed Port Arthur LNG North Project would add four liquefaction trains capable of producing up to 27 million metric tons per annum (mtpa) of LNG, significantly expanding the company's export footprint on the U.S. Gulf Coast, the filing showed. According to the filing, each train would be capable of producing up to 6.73 mtpa of LNG under optimal conditions. The project would also include three LNG storage tanks and marine facilities with up to two LNG berths for loading cargoes onto tankers. If approved and constructed, the project could begin exporting LNG in the second half of 2034, the filing showed. The facilities would be built on land already owned by Port Arthur LNG, the filing said. Sempra is already developing Port Arthur Phase 1 and Phase 2, with a combined capacity of 26 mtpa. The proposal marks the latest effort by U.S. developers to capitalize on growing global demand for LNG as countries seek long-term supplies of the fuel for power generation and industrial use.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542480-to.text: TotalEnergies Gas & Power has entered into a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) for green electricity from Walney I and II, a combined offshore wind farm with a total installed capacity of 367 MW in the Irish Sea. TotalEnergies signed the PPA with Offshore Partners Walney (OPW), which holds a 24.8% ownership stake in Walney I and II, operated by Ørsted. Under the agreement, TotalEnergies will purchase Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin (REGO)-backed electricity annually from OPW's share of generation at Walney I and II through to 2030. The agreement will strengthen TotalEnergies' renewable electricity portfolio and support growing demand from business customers seeking traceable renewable energy solutions. The Walney Offshore Wind Farm is one of the UK's most significant offshore wind assets and plays an important role in supporting the country's transition to a lower-carbon energy system. The agreement further reinforces TotalEnergies' commitment to expanding its renewable power portfolio and providing customers with access to reliable, renewable electricity backed by independently recognised green credentials.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542478-te.text: Technip Energies has been awarded a significant contract by Larsen & Toubro Energy Hydrocarbon (LTEH) to provide detailed engineering services for an ADNOC Offshore project in the United Arab Emirates. The project was awarded by ADNOC Offshore to a consortium led by LTEH and covers the engineering, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning of new offshore facilities, as well as modifications and upgrades to existing infrastructure. Under its contract with LTEH, Technip Energies will provide detailed engineering services, drawing on its local engineering capabilities and experience with offshore projects in the Middle East. Technip Energies classifies a significant award as a contract representing between $58 million and $292 million (€50 million and €250 million) in revenue. https://www.oedigital.com/news/542473-sl.text: SLB has been selected as strategic reservoir partner for the Havstjerne carbon storage project in the Norwegian North Sea, providing technology and engineering services during the concept and front-end engineering and design (FEED) phases. The project, operated by Harbour Energy in consortium with Stella Maris CCS, a Yinson Production company, is intended to provide offshore CO2 storage for industrial emitters across Europe. SLB will coordinate work covering the storage reservoir, injection well design, subsea infrastructure and monitoring of stored CO2 as the project partners develop its technical, cost and schedule basis ahead of a final investment decision. Also, SLB will provide early engineering, subsurface and reservoir maturation and wells services. Its OneSubsea joint venture will deliver the concept and FEED for the subsea injection system, including the template manifold, all-electric trees, control system, umbilical and distribution system. An appraisal well drilled in 2025 confirmed reservoir quality suitable for CO2 injection and storage. The project received €225 million from the EU Innovation Fund in 2025 and has selected a low-pressure floating storage and injection concept.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542482-we.text: Well-Safe Solutions has signed a strategic partnership agreement with NMC Energy to support ongoing operations, including the recently awarded Apache Beryl and Forties decommissioning contracts, and to pursue future project collaboration opportunities. Under the partnership, NMC and Well-Safe will provide operators solutions for critical subsea and platform interface services, including pipeline and flowline flushing, platform integration of decommissioning equipment such as modular platform rig solutions, EDC (Engineering Down and Clean), and topside preparation for heavy lift operations. https://www.oedigital.com/news/542475-se.text: Singapore's Seatrium is preparing for the sailaway of two floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) units for Brazil's Petrobras, with the P-80 and P-82 vessels scheduled to depart within weeks of each other. The two vessels were marked at a christening ceremony at Seatrium's Tuas Boulevard Yard in Singapore and will head to Brazil's Búzios field in the pre-salt Santos Basin. P-80 and P-82 will be the ninth and tenth FPSOs deployed in the Búzios field development, respectively. Each is designed to produce 225,000 barrels of oil per day and process 12 million cubic metres of gas per day. Together, the vessels are expected to add 450,000 barrels per day of oil production capacity to Búzios, representing an increase of about 34% based on the field's current installed production capacity of approximately 1.335 million barrels per day. Each FPSO will also have water injection capacity of about 250,000 barrels per day and oil storage capacity of approximately 2.5 million barrels. The vessels incorporate carbon capture and reinjection capabilities, energy recovery systems and other emissions-reduction technologies, according to Seatrium.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/africa_emer.text: That’s what Enverus Intelligence Research (EIR) said in a statement sent to Rigzone on Wednesday, which noted that the continent has captured nearly half of new upstream country entries globally “as operators broaden exploration portfolios”. EIR, which is a subsidiary of Enverus, highlighted in the statement that it had released a new analysis showing Africa had “emerged as an important focal point of global upstream expansion as companies rebuild exploration portfolios to replenish reserves and pursue future growth”. The company revealed that it had identified 187 country entries, or reentries, that were either completed or under consideration globally during the first half of 2025 and the first half of 2026, “with activity spanning a wide range of companies and geographies”. According to EIR, Africa captured about 50 percent of these new upstream entries. That made it the leading region for current upstream expansion, the statement outlined. EIR said in its statement that interest “has been heavily concentrated in West Africa, led by deepwater activity along the Atlantic Margin”. It added that North African markets “have drawn renewed interest through government efforts to attract international investment, including new bid rounds”. “The acreage rush reflects a broader shift toward organic exploration,” EIR highlighted in its statement. “Dwindling reserve life, subdued exploration spending over the past decade, and a shrinking pool of suitable acquisition targets are placing greater emphasis on finding new resources,” it added.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A ctasmart , especializada em automação e gestão de abastecimento e combustíveis , e a INFLEET , plataforma de telemetria e gestão de frotas , anunciaram uma parceria tecnológica para integrar dados de abastecimento e operação dos veículos. A novidade foi apresentada durante a Concrete Show 2026, que acontece entre os dias 25 e 27 de agosto, em São Paulo. A integração conecta informações que normalmente são gerenciadas em sistemas separados. Dados de telemetria, como odômetro, horímetro e localização do veículo, poderão ser utilizados para validar os abastecimentos, enquanto informações sobre volume, tipo de combustível, data, horário e local da operação serão enviadas para a plataforma de gestão de frotas. A conexão entre os sistemas ocorre por meio de API. Segundo as empresas, a utilização automática de dados como odômetro e horímetro pode reduzir erros de digitação e inconsistências nos registros, enquanto a geolocalização pode ser usada para confirmar se o veículo está em um ponto autorizado antes da liberação do combustível. Com os dados reunidos, a proposta é permitir que gestores relacionem o consumo de combustível à utilização dos veículos e máquinas, acompanhando indicadores como consumo, custo por quilômetro ou por hora trabalhada. A integração também busca facilitar a identificação de desvios de consumo, abastecimentos fora do padrão e outras inconsistências operacionais. A solução é voltada especialmente para empresas dos setores de construção, infraestrutura e logística que operam frotas pesadas e mantêm estruturas próprias de abastecimento, como postos internos e comboios. Nesses casos, a tecnologia pode cruzar informações sobre o veículo, o local da operação, o responsável pelo abastecimento e o volume utilizado. “A integração permite que o abastecimento deixe de ser uma informação isolada e passe a fazer parte da inteligência da operação. Quando conectamos os dados de combustível aos dados reais do veículo, conseguimos entregar muito mais controle, rastreabilidade e segurança para o gestor”, afirma Bárbara Borba, diretora de Marketing da ctasmart.

A Logistique 2026, sétima edição da Feira de Logística, Intralogística, Transporte Multimodal e Comércio Internacional, reuniu mais de 14.200 mil visitantes qualificados . Realizado de 11 a 13 de agosto em Balneário Camboriú, o evento apresentou soluções de ponta de 150 expositores, além de mais de 60 horas de conteúdos, entre apresentações e debates. Dentre os visitantes, a feira registrou 74,7% de representantes de médias e grandes empresas, além de 55,8% de tomadores de decisão ou executivos que influenciam ou recomendam compras, e 45,2% de pessoas em cargos de alta liderança, direção ou gestão. "O que se apurou é que o visitante veio ao evento com objetivos concretos", contou Leonardo Rinaldi, diretor da Logistique . Os dados apurados mostraram que 63,9% dos visitantes procuravam por novas soluções, tecnologias e fornecedores; 49,4% estavam interessados em dados de mercado, de concorrentes e sobre as movimentações do setor; 47,5% buscavam networking profissional e empresarial; e 46,2% procuravam por novos negócios e oportunidades comerciais. Ainda sobre os dados apurados, Rinaldi comentou que os interesses declarados pelos visitantes mostraram demanda por soluções que conectam transporte, comércio internacional, operações internas, tecnologia e infraestrutura. "Para atender a essa expectativa do público, nosso evento reuniu soluções e players especializados em armazenagem, comércio internacional, indústria, distribuição, logística integrada e supply chain", explicou o executivo. Para Gustavo Paschoa, Diretor Comercial da Movecta , estar presente na Logistique é uma oportunidade de acompanhar de perto as discussões e os movimentos do setor na região Sul, onde a empresa tem forte atuação em Itajaí (SC). "No ano passado, estivemos presentes em um dos painéis de debate e, nesta edição, ampliamos nossa participação com um estande, o que nos permitiu apresentar nossas soluções de forma mais próxima ao mercado e fortalecer o relacionamento com clientes e parceiros", comenta. Para o executivo, o resultado foi positivo, com boa repercussão dos painéis, geração de leads e presença de clientes no estande. "Para nós, estar em um evento como a Logistique é uma forma de reforçar nossa presença na região e contribuir para as discussões e o desenvolvimento do setor logístico", completa.

A BYD Indústria de Baterias se juntou ao SENAI para oferecer capacitação a profissionais no interior do Amazonas que vivem longe dos grandes centros. A formação foi feita a bordo de um barco-escola, que capacitou 367 pessoas em Tefé, Coari, Codajás e Parintins , aproximando educação profissional, tecnologia e novas oportunidades de diferentes pontos do estado. A iniciativa conta com apoio da Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (SUFRAMA) e do Centro Internacional de Tecnologia de Software (CITS). O projeto integra um conjunto de investimentos de mais de R$ 1,1 milhão da BYD em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação na região Norte . Iniciativa oferece formação profissional em energia solar, eletrificação e sustentabilidade Durante os cursos, os alunos tiveram contato com conteúdos ligados a sistemas fotovoltaicos, inversores, eletricidade, Indústria 4.0, tecnologia da informação, segurança e sustentabilidade . De acordo com a BYD, os conhecimentos acompanham a transformação do setor de energia e podem abrir novas possibilidades profissionais sem exigir que os alunos deixem suas comunidades. Entre os participantes está a dona de casa Dhierli Gomes dos Santos , de 29 anos, que deixou temporariamente a comunidade onde vive e o filho de 8 anos, para participar da formação em Tefé ao lado do irmão. Os dois chegaram a alugar uma kitnet na cidade durante o período das aulas. "Eu e meu irmão moramos em Caburini a cerca de 45 minutos de lancha de Tefé. Para conseguir fazer o curso, decidimos ficar aqui durante o período das aulas. Não foi uma decisão simples, porque significa ficar longe de casa e assumir um custo que não teríamos normalmente, mas enxergamos nessa formação uma oportunidade que dificilmente chegaria até nós de outra forma. Agora, queremos levar esse conhecimento de volta e poder trabalhar com uma tecnologia que pode melhorar a vida de muita gente na nossa região. Todo esse esforço vale a pena quando a gente pensa no que pode fazer com o que aprendeu", explica a aluna.

A GWM realizou o que classifica como o primeiro transporte de carga da América Latina utilizando um caminhão movido a célula a combustível de hidrogênio . O veículo tracionou uma carreta cegonheira carregada com carros e SUVs eletrificados da marca entre o Laboratório de Hidrogênio do Instituto de Pesquisas Tecnológicas (IPT), na Cidade Universitária da USP, e o Autódromo de Interlagos, em São Paulo . Segundo a empresa, a operação foi a primeira demonstração do caminhão em uma situação real de transporte de carga no Brasil. Os veículos transportados serão utilizados durante o Festival Interlagos, onde o caminhão também ficará disponível para test-drive da imprensa e convidados no dia 26. O modelo é um caminhão elétrico movido por célula a combustível (FCEV). O sistema utiliza o hidrogênio armazenado nos cilindros e o oxigênio do ar para gerar eletricidade, que alimenta o motor elétrico. De acordo com a GWM, o processo gera apenas vapor d'água no escapamento. O caminhão conta com bateria de 105 kWh e cilindros de fibra de carbono com capacidade para armazenar até 40 kg de hidrogênio a uma pressão de até 350 bar. O conjunto entrega até 400 kW (544 cv) de potência e 2.700 Nm de torque, com autonomia de até 500 km e possibilidade de reabastecimento em poucos minutos. Com peso bruto total de 49 toneladas, o veículo pesa 10,8 toneladas vazio. Segundo a companhia, o peso é cerca de 500 kg inferior à média de modelos concorrentes, o que amplia a capacidade útil de transporte. O caminhão também possui sistema de recuperação de energia durante frenagens e desacelerações. A iniciativa faz parte da parceria entre a GWM e o IPT para a realização de testes e estudos relacionados à segurança, ao desempenho e à viabilidade do uso do hidrogênio em veículos pesados. O Laboratório de Hidrogênio do instituto possui duas estações de abastecimento: uma de 700 bar para veículos leves e outra de 350 bar destinada a veículos pesados.

A Eternit , fabricante de materiais de construção, projeta ampliar a participação da EliteMov , sua unidade de negócios voltada a serviços de transporte e soluções logísticas , de cerca de 20% para 50% do volume de cargas da companhia até o fim de 2026 . Criada em 2025, a operação também está sendo avaliada como uma possível plataforma de serviços para outras indústrias. A EliteMov registrou receita líquida de R$ 6,1 milhões no mercado interno no primeiro trimestre de 2026 e de R$ 7,4 milhões no segundo trimestre, totalizando R$ 13,5 milhões no primeiro semestre. Inicialmente implantada na fábrica da Eternit em Hortolândia (SP), onde fica a sede da companhia, a operação foi expandida para as seis unidades produtoras de fibrocimento da empresa. A iniciativa surgiu com o objetivo de ampliar a rastreabilidade das cargas e fortalecer a gestão do transporte. Segundo Rodrigo Inácio, presidente da Eternit, o desenvolvimento do projeto também revelou a possibilidade de avançar sobre uma etapa da cadeia logística anteriormente atendida por transportadoras que atuavam principalmente como agenciadoras de cargas. “Buscávamos maneiras de melhorar o nível de serviço de transporte, com maior rastreabilidade e gestão das cargas. Ao longo do projeto, percebemos que também havia uma oportunidade de avançar na cadeia logística, melhorando o atendimento aos clientes e capturando uma margem que antes ficava com os agenciadores de cargas”, afirma. A EliteMov opera sem frota própria, utilizando uma rede de motoristas autônomos e uma plataforma digital para gerenciar as etapas do transporte, desde a oferta da carga até a confirmação da entrega e o pagamento do frete. De acordo com a Eternit, o modelo permitiu estruturar a operação com menor investimento e flexibilidade para ampliar sua capacidade. Entre os resultados apontados pela companhia estão a redução dos prazos de entrega, a integração da gestão dos pagamentos de frete e uma comunicação mais ágil com os motoristas. A próxima etapa prevista é avaliar a oferta dos serviços logísticos para empresas de outros setores. A estratégia considera, principalmente, o aproveitamento dos fretes de retorno dos veículos que realizam entregas para a Eternit. A proposta é utilizar caminhões que retornariam sem carga para transportar produtos de outros clientes, inicialmente com potencial de atuação junto a empresas da cadeia da construção.

https://safety4sea.com/tanker-hit-by-unk.text: A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on August 25, triggering a fire that was subsequently extinguished, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). T he incident was reported to UKMTO by local authorities at 1730 UTC on August 25 and was issued publicly on August 27. Details about the tanker, including its name, flag, ownership and cargo, have not been disclosed. According to the authorities, the projectile hit the tanker and caused a fire on board. The fire has since been brought under control, while all crew members are reported to be safe and accounted for. There has been no reported environmental impact from the incident. Authorities are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the origin of the projectile. Click here to view the full product⤵️ https://t.co/DlSnmXJTOT #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/GYFdmmjcfY UKMTO advised vessels operating in the area to transit with caution and to report any suspicious activity to the organization. It did not provide further details on the nature of the threat or identify a suspected perpetrator.

https://safety4sea.com/fatal-cargo-grab-.text: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Maritime Administrator has investigated a series of fatal accidents involving cargo grabs aboard RMI-flagged bulk carriers, highlighting the serious risks faced by crews during maintenance and troubleshooting work. A s explained, the incidents underscore the need for greater attention to the hazards associated with cargo-handling equipment, particularly when maintenance activities are being planned and carried out.

https://safety4sea.com/mental-wellbeing-.text: Seafarers are the foundation of global shipping, enabling safe, efficient and sustainable operations every day. Yet despite growing awareness of mental health across the maritime sector, significant challenges remain, notes C apt. Yves Vandenborn, Head of Loss Prevention – Asia Pacific at NorthStandard. L ong periods away from home, isolation, fatigue, operational pressures and multicultural working environments can all influence wellbeing at sea. While the industry has made meaningful progress in recognising these challenges, the latest evidence suggests there is still work to do. The 2025 SEAFiT survey , which gathered responses from more than 20,000 seafarers, showed that mental wellbeing remains one of the weakest areas of crew wellness. Respondents highlighted barriers including limited access to mental health support, a lack of practical information on coping strategies and insufficient opportunities to relax and recharge onboard. Importantly, the findings reinforce a message long shared by crews: mental wellbeing is closely linked to the everyday onboard environment. Access to social interaction, recreation, meaningful rest and supportive relationships all play a vital role in maintaining resilience at sea. This matters not only for individual wellbeing but also for vessel safety, operational performance, crew retention and the long-term sustainability of shipping.

https://safety4sea.com/msc-suspends-novo.text: MSC Mediterranean Shipping Co. has suspended new cargo bookings to and from Russia’s Black Sea port of Novorossiysk following a drone attack on the container ship MSC ULSAN III while it was sailing toward the port. A ccording to Bloomberg, the suspension took effect immediately, with MSC saying it was monitoring the security situation in the region. The company has not disclosed when the attack occurred, who was responsible or whether the vessel sustained damage. MSC has advised customers to contact its Russian agency to arrange alternative logistics solutions for import and export cargo. Regular weekly services through Novorossiysk are expected to resume once security conditions allow. The decision comes amid growing security risks for commercial shipping in the Black Sea , where attacks involving drones have increasingly disrupted maritime operations. MSC continues to serve other Russian ports, including St. Petersburg, while its Novorossiysk operations remain suspended.

https://safety4sea.com/hope-wears-off-fo.text: Indian authorities are continuing air and sea searches for 22 crew members missing after the Panama-flagged bulk carrier MV Ocean Winner sank in the Bay of Bengal on August 22 , while two Chinese crewmembers rescued from a liferaft have been brought ashore in Odisha. I ndian Coast Guard ship Varad brought survivors to Paradip on 27 August after rescuing them from a liferaft on Aug. 22. The two received medical treatment aboard the Coast Guard vessel before being handed over to authorized representatives of the shipping company in the presence of immigration officials and local police. The vessel had 24 crew members, comprising 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi. It sank about 240 nautical miles from the Paradip coast while carrying iron ore. Earlier reports said the vessel was bound for China, while Coast Guard information cited in the latest reports said it was heading toward Singapore. The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy are conducting coordinated sea and air searches, with additional Coast Guard assets and merchant vessels deployed to expand the operation. The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Beijing is also assisting with the search, while the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Sri Vijaya Puram is coordinating the participating agencies. Search aircraft and vessels on Tuesday found an oil slick and two liferafts near the ship’s last known position, but no trace of the vessel or its missing crew. A lifeboat belonging to MV Ocean Winner was located around 7 a.m. on Aug. 25, but a boarding team found no survivors aboard.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/caterpill.text: Caterpillar recently announced receipt of approval in principle (AiP) from DNV for its fuel-blending conversion solution for MaK engines, aligning with a fuel-blending conversion pilot project conducted at a testing facility that allows M 20 to M 43 and legacy engines to lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions up to 20%. In tandem, Caterpillar will debut its dual-fuel conversion option at 2026 Shipbuilding, Machinery and Marine Technology (SMM) September 1 – 4, 2026 in Hamburg, Germany. The dual-fuel conversion enables M 32 and M 43 engines to operate on up to 95% methanol or ethanol by volume which lowers GHG emissions up to 80% based on original carbon intensity of the fuel; tailpipe emissions are the same as with fossil fuels. Enacted last year, 2050 FuelEU Maritime Regulations advance the industry’s GHG emissions reduction ambitions—and operators’ interest in pragmatic pathways to modernize trusted existing assets. Given operators’ substantial investments in current fleets as well as the high cost of newbuild vessels, converting existing ships to operate on lower carbon-intensity fuels enables established vessels to remain in service for decades while aligning with industry requirements. This strategic approach also provides fuel flexibility port to port, ensuring the engines’ inherent ability to run on alcohol-based fuels. Caterpillar Marine will also showcase dedicated energy room configurations for biofuels, hybrid and electric power systems at SMM. Such insights offer operators methodical frameworks for consideration to optimize costs, efficiency and fleetwide GHG emissions levels. “Our extensive dual fuel expertise, advanced diagnostics, digital solutions and global service capabilities empower operators to meet evolving industry requirements in practical ways that help curb OpEx and preserve capital,” commented Andy Law, vice president of Caterpillar Marine. “We’re collaborating with operators worldwide to help them thrive as the industry shifts.” “Keeping pace with FuelEU Maritime requirements is essential to not only ensure vessels remain on the water but also to avoid significant financial penalties,” said Sven Rosenow, global services director for MaK at Caterpillar. “Our fuel conversion solutions give operators options and enable them to modernize their fleets in ways that are ideal for their unique operations.”

https://safety4sea.com/the-safety-parado.text: As shipping accelerates its transition towards lower and zero greenhouse gas fuels, the industry is entering one of the most significant periods of operational change in its history, argues Sunil Krishnakumar, General Manager, Singapore branch, International Chamber of Shipping. M ethanol, ethanol, ammonia, hydrogen and biofuels all have a role to play in helping shipping meet the ambitions set out in the IMO’s greenhouse gas strategy. Yet while these fuels may reduce emissions, they also introduce new and unfamiliar safety risks that must be carefully understood, managed and regulated. This is the safety paradox of decarbonisation. The very fuels and technologies designed to support shipping’s path to net zero can also create new hazards for vessels, crews, ports and supply chains. This should not be seen as a reason to delay progress. Rather, it is a reminder that innovation must be matched by robust safety governance, practical procedures and effective crew training. The uptake of alternative fuels, particularly those with zero or near-zero greenhouse gas emissions, will be critical to achieving international decarbonisation goals. However, with the exception of drop-in options such as some biofuels, these fuels require fundamental changes to ship design, machinery, bunkering infrastructure, and onboard operating procedures.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/master-bo.text: Master Boat Builders has launched Defiant , the third of eight tugboats the Coden, Ala., shipyard is building for Metairie, La.-based Maritime Partners. The 88-foot Defiant is classed as an A1 Escort Tug and Towing Vessel. The tug carries Automated Machinery System (AMS) and Underwater Inspection in Lieu of Drydocking (UWILD) certifications, as well as FFV1 firefighting capability. It is also designated as a Low Emissions Vessel under U.S. standards. “The launch of Defiant reflects what can be accomplished through strong industry partnerships and a shared focus on quality,” said Garrett Rice, president of Master Boat Builders. “Our skilled craftsmen and engineers take great pride in building vessels that meet the highest standards of performance, reliability and safety.” Five additional vessels remain under contract, with deliveries scheduled to continue through completion of the eight-vessel program. Founded in 1979, Master Boat Builders has delivered more than 450 vessels, including tugboats, offshore supply vessels, fishing vessels and dive support vessels. Maritime Partners manages a fleet of more than 1,900 vessels, primarily serving the domestic Jones Act trades.

https://safety4sea.com/dnv-maritime-fore.text: DNV’s latest Maritime Forecast to 2050 depicts a shipping industry moving forward on decarbonization, but in an increasingly uncertain and fragmented landscape. W ith no single fuel or technology pathway yet providing a clear answer, DNV stresses the need to maintain momentum, accelerate energy-efficiency measures and preserve flexibility across fuels and technologies while the regulatory and fuel markets continue to evolve. The report examines four regulatory scenarios, ranging from adoption of the IMO Net-Zero Framework (NZF) in its current form to its outright rejection, which could lead to a period of prolonged regulatory gridlock, and explores the implications of these outcomes for fuel demand, energy efficiency uptake, and long-term fleet fuel and technology strategies. #1 Several regulatory futures remain possible as the IMO continues negotiations on the Net-Zero Framework, with these outcomes shaping investment decisions, low-GHG fuel uptake, and energy-efficiency deployment across the global fleet. #2 With global regulatory incentives in place, the world-fleet could consume 25% less energy by 2050 than under a scenario limited to regional regulations. #3 Energy efficiency can pay off regardless of regulatory outcome – 5,000 TEU container ship case study shows 16% annual fuel savings from hydrodynamic measures retrofit.

https://safety4sea.com/vesselbot-same-ro.text: According to VesselBot’s latest quarterly analysis, emissions intensity rose 1.5% year over year in Q2 2026, but the increase masks efficiency improvements across almost every vessel-size segment. B ased on the Decoding Maritime Emissions Q2 2026: Efficiency Hidden in the Details report, the number of tracked voyages in the second quarter of 2026 was 86,389, 13.4% higher than in the second quarter of 2025. During those voyages, total emissions reached 56,267,630 CO2e (CO2 equivalent) tonnes, a 9.1% year-over-year change, while the total transport work was 736,080,057,307 TEU km, a 16.5% increase year-over-year. The finding points to a broader pattern across the report: fleet-wide and trade-lane averages most shippers and regulators currently rely on can obscure significant differences in the emissions performance of individual voyages and comparable services. On the Northern Europe to North America East Coast trade, for example, three carriers operating comparable services on the same trade lane recorded materially different emissions outcomes despite similar voyage distances and port pairs, highlighting the role of vessel deployment, utilization and voyage execution in determining emissions intensity. On the Northern Europe to North America East Coast trade lane, we observed a 31.3% efficiency gap between the most and least efficient carrier for the route, despite similar voyage distances and port pairs. Distance alone cannot explain that spread. The difference is in how those voyages were executed … said Constantine Komodromos, CEO and Founder of VesselBot, adding that the same pattern appears at fleet level. A fleet-wide number moving 1.5% in the wrong direction suggests the industry lost ground this quarter. But five of the six vessel-size segments actually became more efficient. Feeders moved in the opposite direction and, because they accounted for nearly two-thirds of all voyages, were enough to pull the aggregate number higher.

https://safety4sea.com/port-of-callao-be.text: The Port of Callao has taken a major step towards cleaner port operations with the launch of Latin America’s first shore power system, allowing vessels at berth to switch off their auxiliary engines and connect directly to 100% certified renewable electricity. T he system, launched by DP World at its South Terminal, forms part of the company’s roughly US$1 billion investment in Peru and was integrated into the US$400 million expansion of the Bicentennial Pier. The environmental impact is expected to be significant, as the system could prevent more than 6,300 tonnes of CO₂e emissions each year in Callao, equivalent to around 30 tonnes per vessel call. By allowing ships to shut down their auxiliary engines while alongside, it is also expected to cut fuel consumption and reduce nitrogen oxide, sulfur oxide and particulate matter emissions by more than 90% during connection. Today, from here (the Port of Callao), we are not only moving cargo; we are moving Peru toward the future. We’re talking about a technology that may seem simple but is of enormous importance, since only 3% of the world’s ports have this technology, and we’re proud that Peru is part of this group, serving as an example of environmental protection and modernization. As explained, with a capacity of up to 7.5 MVA, the system can supply enough electricity to meet the power needs of the largest fully loaded container ships calling at Callao.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/seatrium.text: Singapore-based offshore and marine engineering company Seatrium is poised to achieve what it describes as an industry first with the dual sailaway of two giant floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) units, which are slated to depart its Singapore yard within weeks of each other and embark on a journey to Brazil, where they will work for the country’s state-owned energy giant Petrobras. These two FPSOs are said to be among the largest ever built, with a scale capable of lifting Brazil’s national oil production by 10%. Chris Ong , Chief Executive Officer of Seatrium, commented : “Over the last three decades, we have evolved alongside Petrobras’ needs to support its ambitions to be a global energy leader. The sail-away of P-80 and P-82 in close succession is a significant demonstration of that evolution, as we take the learnings to execute strongly for the three remaining P-Series FPSOs in our facilities. “Orchestrating six large, multi-year projects concurrently is incredibly complex. https://petronoticias.com.br/batizadas-n.text: A Petrobrás e a Seatrium realizaram cerimônia de batismo e sailaway das plataformas marítimas P-80 e P-82, nesta quinta-feira (27), no estaleiro Tuas Boulevard Yard, em Singapura. As unidades vão operar no campo de Búzios, no pré-sal da Bacia de Santos, o maior campo em reservas e em produção do Brasil. As unidades estão na fase final de integração dos módulos e navegarão para o Brasil nas próximas semanas. A P-80 (Búzios 9) será a primeira a deixar o estaleiro. O início de produção das duas unidades está previsto para 2027. Cada plataforma tem capacidade de produzir 225 mil barris de petróleo por dia, uma das maiores capacidades da indústria mundial. As unidades também podem processar 12 milhões de metros cúbicos de gás por dia, cada. A presidente da Petrobrás, Magda Chambriard, durante o evento em Singapura, disse que “ São duas plataformas gigantes para nosso campo gigante de Búzios. Elas compõem um novo ciclo de seis unidades de elevada capacidade de produção, iniciado com o FPSO Almirante Tamandaré, que opera em Búzios acima da capacidade de projeto, com produção recorde de 270 mil barris de petróleo por dia. Em seguida da P-80 e da P-82, concluiremos a P-83, a P-84 e a P-85, que vão para os campos de Búzios, Atapu e Sépia, respectivamente. Esperamos alcançar em todas essas unidades produção superior a 225 mil barris por dia .” Além da capacidade de produção recorde, as unidades utilizarão tecnologias e soluções digitais que garantem maior eficiência operacional e energética. A construção das plataformas foi contratada pela Petrobrás pelo modelo EPC ( Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning), no qual a contratada é responsável pela engenharia, suprimentos, construção e comissionamento da unidade até sua entrega para operação no Brasil. Os Módulos de processo da P-80 foram fabricados no Brasil, no estaleiro Seatrium BrasFELS, em Angra dos Reis; e da P-82 no estaleiro Estaleiro Seatrium Aracruz, no Espírito Santo, contribuindo para qualificação de mão de obra e gerando emprego e renda por meio da indústria naval no Brasil. Além disso, houve construções na China, Singapura e Indonésia. Posteriormente, esses módulos foram transportados para Singapura para a integração final, de onde partem para início da produção no Brasil. © 2026 Petronotícias. Todos os direitos reservados.
