https://www.marinelog.com/news/everllenc.text: Everllence announced that the world’s first Everllence B&W G80 ethanol capable engine has been tested and verified at an R&D test at HD Hyundai Heavy Industries Engine and Machinery division in Korea. The engine is bound for the third in a series of 10 × Very Large Ore Carriers ordered by Shandong Shipping for chartering to Brazilian mining and logistics operator, Vale. Vessel delivery is set for early 2027. “This marks a major milestone for the G80 engine platform, transforming it into a fully flexible tri‑fuel engine capable of operating on fuel oil, methanol, ethanol, or any blend of the latter two,” said Bjarne Foldager, head of Two-Stroke Business at Everllence. “The project reflects our shared commitment with Vale regarding pragmatic and scalable decarbonization pathways within the hard-to-abate shipping sector, and positions Vale at the forefront of maritime sustainability. By selecting the G80 tri-fuel engine, Vale is advancing its strategy to reduce emissions across its maritime logistics chain while maintaining operational robustness in what are—currently—demanding conditions for low-carbon fuels.” The new announcement stems from a cooperation agreement signed by Everllence and Vale in February 2026 regarding the development of an advanced, ethanol-powered engine based on the well-proven Everllence B&W ME-LGIM (-Liquid Gas Injection Methanol) platform. “The G80 ethanol engine is based on the proven B&W ME-LGIM platform. It represents the latest evolution of Everllence’s two-stroke dual-fuel engines, designed to enable shipowners to transition seamlessly towards lower-emission fuels without compromising operational efficiency, reliability or safety,” said Christian Ludwig, vice president, head of global sales & promotion, Two-Stroke Business at Everllence. “In general, interest in ethanol as a marine fuel has increased over the past five years as multi-fuel capability increases shipowner flexibility. We foresee the core demand for this engine coming from bulk carriers, tankers and container vessels. With over 250 methanol engine orders under our belt already, of which more than 100 are in service, Everllence is the leading engine designer for methanol and ethanol-fueled engines.” With the order, Everllence continues to expand its footprint across multiple alternative fuel technologies, including methane, methanol, ammonia, ethane, LPG, and now ethanol. As the maritime industry explores new fuel pathways, the company emphasizes the importance of mature, reliable technologies that can be deployed at scale. The G80 ethanol project underscores a shift from early-stage announcements towards tangible implementation, reinforcing Everllence’s role in enabling the next phase of shipping’s energy transition.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/abb-to-po.text: ABB has been selected as the power, propulsion and automation technology partner for two new Ro-Pax ferries, to be named Kupe and Cook , which form part of Cook Strait Ferry Replacement Program, one of New Zealand’s most strategically important infrastructure investments. ABB will supply the integrated systems required to ensure the reliability, efficiency and environmental performance of the two ferries. To be built by Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI) shipyard, the ferries will be delivered to New Zealand Government entity Ferry Holdings Limited in 2029. The 200-meter long (656 feet), 28-meter-wide (92-foot) ferries will operate in the challenging conditions of the Cook Strait at the junction of the Tasman Sea and the South Pacific Ocean, making the 92-kilometer Wellington-Picton crossing between the North and South Islands. They will offer capacity for 63% more passengers (1,530 persons) and 44% more freight (2,400 lane meters) than their predecessors. The ferries are rail-enabled, allowing rail freight to be loaded directly onto the vessels, eliminating multiple cargo handling steps during inter-island transfers. Critical for the national economy, these vessels will also deliver high fuel efficiency, lower emissions and reduced underwater radiated noise (URN) that aligns with the most forward-looking ferry projects in the world. Reducing URN has been prioritized to help protect marine life in the Marlborough Sounds, acknowledged in the DNV SILENT-E class notation. “These ferries represent a key investment in New Zealand’s transport infrastructure,” said Massimo Soprano, Ship Programme director, Ferry Holdings Limited. “Selecting ABB gives us confidence that we will deliver vessels with world-class power, propulsion and automation technology. These systems are designed for the demanding conditions of Cook Strait and built to minimize environmental impact over their entire lifecycle.” “Growing up on the shores of Lyall Bay in Wellington, I watched the ferries push out into Cook Strait in all conditions, wind, swell and everything in between. That image has stayed with me,” said Palemia Field, global segment manager for Ferries, ABB’s Marine & Ports division. “That personal connection makes it even more meaningful to now be part of delivering vessels that will transform that crossing. They are quieter, cleaner, more reliable, and built for the next 30 years of New Zealand’s growth.”

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/new.text: Greek owners provide some of the clearest examples. As reported by Riviera Maritime Media, Navios Maritime Partners has committed $482 million to four scrubber-fitted VLCC newbuildings for delivery in the second half of 2028. Navios also holds options to acquire another two plus two newbuilding VLCCs. In a company announcement in July, TOP Ships said it had agreed to acquire three scrubber-fitted, eco-design MR product tanker newbuildings for delivery in 2029. SAFETY4SEA has meanwhile reported that Aegean Shipping Management has committed to two scrubber-fitted VLCCs and two LR2/aframax tankers. The pattern extends into dry bulk. Splash reported that Seanergy Maritime Holdings’ renewal programme comprised six scrubber-fitted newbuildings in May and has since expanded to include another scrubber-fitted capesize newbuilding for delivery in 2029. Separately, Splash has linked Thenamaris to an order for four scrubber-fitted MR2 product tankers. Look beyond individual companies and the trend is even clearer. Lloyd’s List analysis of Clarksons Research data at the end of June showed scrubbers fitted or planned on 92% of VLCCs on order, compared with 66% of those already trading. For suezmaxes, the comparison was 66% of the orderbook against 40% of the existing fleet. In dry bulk, 74% of capesize newbuildings were due to carry scrubbers, compared with 57% of vessels on the water. For panamaxes, the figures were 46% and 19% respectively. These are not merely investments responding to the 2020 sulphur cap, they concern vessels expected to trade through the 2030s and into the foreseeable future. The value lies in not having to predict 2035 Nobody ordering a ship today can say with confidence which compliant marine fuel will be cheapest or readily available in 2035, what or where alternative fuels will be available at scale, how regional requirements will evolve, or what charterers will be prepared to pay for. Many newbuilds are therefore being provided with basic infrastructure for an alternative future fuel option, e.g. methanol or ammonia, but are also continuing to install EGCS (scrubbers).

https://petronoticias.com.br/eneva-e-dia.text: A Eneva celebrou com a Diamante Geração de Energia e suas afiliadas um acordo para a troca de participações em ativos de geração e infraestrutura de energia. De um lado, a Eneva transferirá 100% das ações da Itaqui Geração de Energia. Enquanto a Diamante repassará os 50% restantes da Porto do Pecém Transportadora de Minérios (PPTM), fazendo com que a Eneva passe a deter a totalidade do capital social da empresa. Além da transferência dos ativos, a Diamante pagará à Eneva R$ 400 milhões em dinheiro, com correção monetária até o fechamento da operação. O acordo prevê ainda um pagamento adicional de até R$ 467 milhões, condicionado à eventual antecipação do início do fornecimento de energia previsto no contrato do Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade (LRCAP) 2026. A Itaqui tem como principal ativo a termelétrica Porto do Itaqui (foto principal), termelétrica a carvão de 360 MW, com contratos de comercialização de energia no ambiente regulado vigentes até 21 de dezembro de 2027. A usina também foi vencedora do LRCAP 2026, no produto 2031, com fornecimento de potência por dez anos a partir de 1º de agosto de 2031. Já a PPTM participará da implantação de um terminal de importação, armazenamento e regaseificação de gás natural liquefeito no Complexo Industrial do Pecém, com capacidade de escoamento de até 14 milhões de m³/dia. Na mesma data, a Eneva foi informada pela Diamante de que a empresa não pretende exercer a opção de compra que permitia adquirir 30% do capital social total e votante das sociedades de propósito específico (SPEs) responsáveis pelos projetos de geração do Hub Ceará. Com isso, a opção foi cancelada sem exercício. A conclusão das operações ainda depende do cumprimento de condições precedentes previstas no contrato, incluindo a aprovação pelo Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade).

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/dan.text: Ukraine’s exports have come under pressure as repeated Russian attacks have disrupted operations at its main Black Sea ports in the Odesa region. The country’s deep-sea ports historically handle most of its grain exports; however, the latest Russian strikes targeted export infrastructure in the region, forcing cargo to be rerouted through lower-capacity Danube ports, including the Port Reni and Izmail. As a result, it is creating massive congestion near the Sulina port, with the current fleet mainly comprising smaller general cargo vessels. Few dry bulk vessels are also caught up in the congestion, putting pressure on vessel availability in the region. As Ukrainian grain exports now rely on the Danube corridor, infrastructure and navigational constraints limit vessel throughput and reduce effective fleet availability, supporting freight markets in the Black Sea. Regional fleet availability under pressure Vessel queues at Sulina remain high, with around 70 vessels, including dry bulk and general cargo, awaiting transit, with limited daily passage capacity to Ukrainian Danube ports. Around 52 (above 2.6 kdwt) general cargo vessels, totalling about 280 kdwt, are currently waiting outside Ukrainian Danube ports. Out of the global fleet of around 30.6 mdwt in this size segment, about 7 mdwt, or 23%, is typically deployed in the Black Sea region, including Russian ports. Although these waiting-zone vessels represent only 4% of the Black Sea fleet (up to 10k dwt), tightening the effective vessel supply, as ongoing delays remove a major portion of the fleet from the active fleet. The congestion can be attributed to several factors rather than a single capacity constraint. Pilot shortages, prioritisation of higher-priority cargoes such as fuel, frequent air-raid alerts and weather-related interruptions have reduced the effective flow of vessels, leading to only three to four vessels transiting per day moving towards Ukraine, which could still take several weeks to clear. According to official data, Ukraine’s grain exports were down almost 70% YoY in August, illustrating the extent to which the disruption is affecting the country’s overall grain flows despite efforts to divert cargo to the Danube. However, it has handled much larger volumes in the past when Russia had blocked Ukraine’s Black Sea ports. Grain export capacity through the Danube reached about 2.5 million tonnes per month during 2022-23. However, current volumes remain well below those levels, highlighting congestion even before the route has returned to its previous peak throughput.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: O deputado federal é o representante da população na Câmara dos Deputados, uma das duas casas do Congresso Nacional. Ele é eleito para um mandato de quatro anos, sem limites para reeleição. criar e votar leis federais; fiscalizar o governo federal; e participar da definição do Orçamento da União . Ao todo, a Câmara dos Deputados tem 513 parlamentares, distribuídos entre os estados e o Distrito Federal de acordo com o tamanho da população de cada unidade da Federação . Veja abaixo o número de deputados federais por estado. A principal atribuição do deputado federal é elaborar e votar leis que valem para todo o país . Os parlamentares podem apresentar projetos de lei, propostas de emenda à Constituição (PECs) e emendas a projetos em tramitação. Também analisam propostas enviadas pelo presidente da República, como medidas provisórias e projetos de iniciativa do Executivo. Outra função é fiscalizar a atuação do governo federal . Os deputados podem convocar ministros para prestar esclarecimentos, solicitar informações sobre ações do Executivo, acompanhar a aplicação de recursos públicos e participar de Comissões Parlamentares de Inquérito (CPIs) para investigar possíveis irregularidades.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/brent_could.text: In an exclusive interview with Rigzone on Wednesday, Art Hogan, Chief Market Strategist at B. Riley Wealth, projected that the Brent crude oil price could hit $100 in the next week “if … there is no resolution to reopening the Strait of Hormuz”. Although Hogan highlighted that WTI crude was $10 lower, he told Rigzone that this commodity “could follow with similar trajectory over the course of the next month”. Hogan pointed out to Rigzone that global strategic petroleum reserves are at historic lows and that oil production capacity was under pressure from attacks across the Middle East. “Key to seeing sustainably lower oil prices comes from a credible and lasting reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said. “Barring that, energy prices have only one way to go - and that significantly higher than they are now,” he warned. In another exclusive interview with Rigzone yesterday, Phil Flynn, a senior market analyst at the PRICE Futures Group, revealed to Rigzone that he didn’t think WTI would hit $100 soon. He did add, however, that Brent has a better chance to get near that figure.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A empresa de software para supply chain nstech anunciou a aquisição da Active Corp , solução de gestão logística e visibilidade que conecta transportadores, embarcadores, indústria e varejo em uma plataforma unificada. A compra marca o retorno das operações de M&A da nstech após quase um ano focando em sua plataforma proprietária, e contribui para a visão da empresa de formar uma rede de logística integrada que conecta empresas, pessoas, dados e soluções ao longo da jornada de transporte. Com a integração, a nstech fortalece sua rede de TNS (Transportation Network System) e amplia sua participação no mercado de intermediárias para transportadores e embarcadores, com foco em frete fracionado para embarcadores com forte presença em bens de consumo, moda e farmacêuticos. Fundada em 1997, a Active Corp possui uma trajetória consolidada de 29 anos no mercado. A empresa promove visibilidade do transporte em todas as etapas, envolvendo embarcadores, transportadores, motoristas e destinatários. Sua plataforma OnSupply conecta cerca de 140 mil empresas a 30 mil transportadores , movimentando um volume total de mercadorias (GMV) de R$ 120 bilhões por ano e gerando 1 milhão de acessos mensais a rastreio de cargas. Além dos embarcadores, a empresa atende mais de 1.000 transportadores com suas soluções de gestão a vista e dashboards integrados ao TMS e emite, mensalmente, cerca de 1 milhão de documentos de transporte. "Essa aquisição representa um marco muito estratégico para a nstech. Após passarmos quase um ano dedicados de forma intensa à nossa plataforma de dados, ao desenvolvimento de soluções de IA e à consolidação da TNS, voltamos ao mercado de M&A trazendo um ativo de peso. A Active Corp reforça a capacidade da TNS de gerar efeitos de rede para toda a cadeia logística, acelerando a nossa jornada de digitalizar a logística brasileira consolidando a liderança no middle market de embarcadores e transportadores", destaca Vasco Oliveira, CEO e fundador da nstech .

https://safety4sea.com/one-dead-and-six-.text: One crew member has died and six remain missing after the tug TNS Catcher capsized while assisting a containership off the coast of Busan on 2 September. A ccording to the Busan maritime police, the tug was assisting a 66,332-ton Liberia-flagged containership, with two tugs towing from either side of the containership’s bow and a third pushing from the stern. Local media report that the tug, TNS Catcher, which was positioned on the starboard side of the containership’s bow, is believed to have capsized while turning to the right, with the hawser potentially contributing to the accident. “It appears to have capsized because the speed and timing did not match during the course change,” an official said, adding that investigators had not yet determined whether the tug became snagged on the towline. The Korea Coast Guard has ruled out a collision between the tug and the containership. It also said the towing operation itself did not appear to have been excessive, taking into account the containership’s engine output and other relevant factors.

https://safety4sea.com/pink-corridor-pro.text: Lloyd’s Register, A.P. Moller – Maersk and the ports of Charleston and Felixstowe are joining forces to examine the security and safeguarding requirements for a potential nuclear-powered containership service linking the UK and US. T he partners will launch a Pink Corridor project to assess the operational, security and regulatory considerations associated with a theoretical nuclear-powered containership operating between the Port of Charleston on the US East Coast and the Port of Felixstowe, the UK’s largest container port. The study will examine the safeguards and security measures that would be required to support such a service, with the findings intended to help inform future regulation and provide a framework for the safe, secure and responsible adoption of nuclear propulsion in trans-Atlantic commercial shipping. The initiative comes as the maritime industry explores alternative propulsion technologies to cut emissions and meet increasingly stringent decarbonisation targets, with nuclear power emerging as a potential option for long-distance commercial shipping. The Pink Corridor joint development programme is an important step for the application of nuclear technology in merchant shipping. By taking a practical, collaborative approach, the project will examine the security and safeguards that would need to be addressed for safe operations. The partnership brings together industry-leading players across shipping, ports and classification, reflecting the growing interest in nuclear technology as a route to more sustainable maritime operations. Centred on a conceptual nuclear-powered container ship, the Pink Corridor will examine the requirements for theoretical port access on the specified route.

https://safety4sea.com/black-sea-drone-a.text: Commercial vessels transiting the Bosphorus are increasingly using improvised measures, including nets, water tanks and tyres, to protect against growing Russian and Ukrainian drone attacks in the Black Sea, according to security experts and video obtained by Reuters. A s explained, the growing risks were highlighted by the abandoned Russian-flagged cargo ship Omskiy-107, whose command deck was burned out before the vessel drifted from Russian waters to a beach north of Istanbul, east of the Bosphorus. Ukraine has intensified attacks on ships and infrastructure linked to Russian oil and grain exports since July, while Russia has increased strikes on Ukraine’s main grain export hubs. Several vessels have since adopted makeshift defences. The Sierra Leone-flagged crude oil tanker Caruzo transited the Bosphorus on August 11 with water tanks suspended around its stern, apparently to help protect the engine room. In addition, the Russian-flagged crude tanker Khrizopraz passed through on August 27 with tyres hanging over its hull, while the crude tankers Brisk and Integrator were fitted with netting known as “cope cages” to protect their superstructures from explosive drones. Corey Ranslem, chief executive of maritime security group Dryad Global, said attacks on commercial vessels and port infrastructure had increased sharply and could escalate further. He said water-filled containers and netting could provide some protection against smaller drones but may be ineffective against larger military drones. Other maritime specialists have also questioned whether such measures can protect vessels from rapid remote-controlled naval drones or airborne weapons carrying large explosive payloads.

https://safety4sea.com/spain-introduces-.text: Spain has introduced new decarbonization requirements for domestic shipping under Royal Decree 611/2026, establishing greenhouse-gas reduction and renewable-fuel targets for cabotage navigation from 2027 to 2040. U nder the decree, obligated fuel suppliers and other specified entities must achieve a 6.5% reduction in greenhouse-gas emissions from fuels supplied for cabotage in 2027, with the target gradually increasing to 33% by 2040. A separate renewable-fuel sub-target will rise from 2% in 2027 to 20% in 2040. Renewable fuels of non-biological origin may contribute to the targets provided they meet applicable sustainability requirements and achieve at least 70% lifecycle greenhouse-gas savings compared with the fossil-fuel comparator. The decree also introduces certification, traceability and reporting requirements for renewable and low-carbon fuels, with supporting documentation generally required to be retained for at least five years. The obligations apply mainly to fuel suppliers, including petroleum and LPG operators, natural-gas marketers and certain direct consumers, rather than being imposed directly on individual vessels. Spain has also amended national rules governing marine fuels, including provisions covering ISO 8217 fuel specifications , sulfur testing and the use of biofuel blends.

https://safety4sea.com/gard-safety-and-c.text: Gard P&I Club has highlighted the risks and commercial considerations for vessels considering southern routes as an alternative to Panama Canal transit restrictions . R ecurring drought and lower-than-expected rainfall have prompted the Panama Canal Authority to impose draft limits, reduce daily transits and adjust auction slots, potentially causing delays and higher voyage costs. Thus, owners are considering the Drake Passage and Strait of Magellan. The Drake Passage offers a more direct route but exposes vessels to severe weather, while the Strait is more sheltered but presents greater navigational complexity and potential pilotage costs. However, Gard’s claims experience shows that routing decisions can lead to disputes over pilotage expenses. Masters retain responsibility for vessel, crew and cargo safety and may choose an alternative route when conditions warrant it. Owners should document such decisions and ensure charterparties clearly address routing and pilotage costs. Southern routes also require consideration of winter conditions, bunker heating, machinery limitations and the challenges of navigating confined waters along the Chilean coast. As a result, Gard has advised that owners and managers should maintain close contact with their local agents to obtain the latest information, as operational restrictions may be amended in response to changing weather and watershed conditions.

https://gcaptain.com/japans-mitsui-osk-s.text: FILE PHOTO: The logo of Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd. (MOL) is displayed at their office in Minato-ku, Tokyo, Japan April 8, 2025. REUTERS/Staff/File Photo (Bloomberg) –The head of Japanese shipping company Mitsui OSK Lines Ltd. expects disruption in the Strait of Hormuz to last longer than previously assumed, with recent attacks elevating the risk for tankers attempting to move oil through the waterway. “Given the current situation, it’s difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year,” Chief Executive Officer Jotaro Tamura said in an interview. “The situation continues to be well beyond the level of risk we can accept.” Clashes between the US and Iran over control of Hormuz have intensified after a period of relative calm, raising the threat for vessels carrying Middle Eastern crude to global markets. After managing to move their ships out of the Gulf after the war began, risk-averse Japanese shipowners have largely avoided the region for safety reasons. The disruption has forced Japan’s oil refiners – which before the war sourced more than 90% of their crude from the Middle East – to seek alternative supplies and routes, including the US, while drawing from the nation’s stockpiles to stave off shortages and price spikes. Mitsui OSK had previously assumed a phased resumption of Hormuz transit from October, followed by a return to normal operations from January. That timeline now appears likely to slip, Tamura said. The resumption of crossings “is likely to be pushed back,” he said, “but at this stage, it’s difficult to say by how much.”

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/oil.text: Oil prices slipped in Asian trading on Thursday after three consecutive sessions of gains, as President Donald Trump said renewed U.S. attacks on Iran would not last long and signs of recovering crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz eased some supply concerns. As of 04:42 ET (08:42 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in November fell 0.2% to $95.43 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) slipped 0.2% to $90.83 a barrel, paring earlier gains after both benchmarks reached five-week highs in the previous three sessions. The rally had been driven by fears that renewed military confrontation between the United States and Iran could further disrupt oil supplies from the Middle East. U.S. forces struck Iran’s southern coast on Wednesday while Tehran retaliated against U.S. positions across the region, in the most intense exchange of fire between the two countries since July. Trump, however, said on Wednesday that the renewed U.S. campaign against Iran would not persist for an extended period, helping to temper some of the market’s immediate supply concerns. He also said the U.S. had targeted Iranian radar, missile systems and capabilities linked to laying mines around the Strait of Hormuz.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/uk-oil-g.text: Edinburgh-headquartered Flotation Energy and London-based Harbour Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on assessing opportunities for powering oil and gas assets in the North Sea with floating offshore wind energy. “The agreement brings together Harbour Energy’s extensive experience as a North Sea operator, with the floating offshore wind and electrification expertise within our project, to explore potential scenarios and build greater understanding of the technical, regulatory and commercial considerations involved”, Flotation Energy said via social media. https://www.offshore-energy.biz/equinor-.text: Norway’s energy company Equinor has awarded Proserv with a contract for the deployment of cable monitoring technology at the 402 MW Dudgeon offshore wind farm in the UK. Proserv’s ECG Business Unit will deploy its advanced monitoring technology to provide continuous visibility of cable and termination health at the project located 32 kilometers off the north Norfolk coast, with deployment scheduled to begin in 2027. The deal will also see the deployment of Proserv’s Distributed Electrical Sensing (DES) technology, which uses existing fiber infrastructure and passive sensing technology and provides high-fidelity current and voltage measurements across the network, delivering enhanced visibility of electrical performance in remote and difficult-to-access environments, the company said. The technology is expected to support earlier identification of developing cable and electrical faults, improved visibility of asset health and network performance and long-term reliability of critical electrical infrastructure, reduced risk of unplanned outages and lost generation, more targeted and proactive maintenance, fewer unnecessary offshore interventions, and a more efficient and data-led O&M strategy. “ECG gives Equinor greater visibility of the condition and performance of its electrical assets, helping identify developing issues before they become costly failures. By combining ECG with DES, we can provide an even richer picture of network performance and give the operator greater confidence in the availability and security of site generation,” said Barry Frost , Director of ECG at Proserv. “Ultimately, this is about moving from reactive maintenance to proactive asset management reducing risk, improving reliability and helping maximise the value of offshore wind assets over their operational life.”

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/ai-power.text: Eco Wave Power’s U.S. subsidiary has entered into an agreement with Germany-based AI engineering to develop an AI-powered digital twin platform for its wave energy technology. The companies have begun Phase 1 of the Eco Wave Power – Digital Twin & Energy-Aware Computing project, combining advanced physics-based simulation with Eco Wave Power’s real-world engineering, wave and operational data. This first phase will focus on digitally modeling how ocean waves interact with Eco Wave Power ‘s proprietary floaters. Using AI engineering’s PAMICS simulation technology, the companies will evaluate floater behavior, structural loads and theoretical energy input under different sea conditions. The plan is to compare simulated results with real-world sensor measurements and begin developing machine-learning capabilities for forecasting energy yield and system loads. “For us, AI is not simply a software layer that we add to our technology—it is an opportunity to fundamentally improve how we understand, design, predict and ultimately operate wave energy systems,” said Inna Braverman , Founder and CEO of Eco Wave Power. “Phase 1 of this collaboration is therefore very practical. We will model wave loading, floater behavior, structural forces and theoretical energy input, while beginning to develop machine-learning capabilities for forecasting loads and energy yield. Importantly, we will also examine how those models can be transferred to new sites with different wave conditions.”

https://splash247.com/what-the-price-cap.text: Simon Lunde and Fredrick Henriksen of BI Norwegian Business School went looking for the G7 price cap in the secondhand market rather than in trade flows. What they found was not a crude-only break, but a broad re-rating of shipping with a sanctions gradient running through it, steepest in the tonnage the shadow trade runs on. On December 5 2022, the G7, the EU and Australia capped the price of seaborne Russian crude at $60 a barrel. The cap did not ban the trade. It withdrew Western insurance, classification and finance from any cargo sold above the threshold, and in doing so split the fleet into a compliant lane and a shadow lane assembled to work outside it. Almost everything written about the cap since has measured it where the money moves: export volumes, the discounts Russian sellers absorbed, the revenue they were left with. We went looking somewhere else – in the price of the ships. There is a reason to look there. A secondhand tanker is a long-lived capital asset: freight rates tell you about this month, but a vessel value is the market’s estimate of what the ship earns over the rest of its life. If the cap made old, route-suitable tonnage the scarce input to a newly valuable trade, that belief should sit in the asset price. It is. Across eighteen years of monthly data from the Clarksons Shipping Intelligence Network (SIN) covering three crude segments, a fifteen-year-old aframax – the size that physically lifts Russian barrels out of the Baltic and the Black Sea – carried a premium of about $17.7m in the 39 months after the cap, above what earnings, oil prices, the freight cycle and recession conditions jointly predict. That is a re-rating of about 123% over its 2018–21 baseline, from a model that explains 89.6% of the variation in that series. These are Clarksons’ assessed values, the industry’s standard series, not recorded sale prices. Now the part most write-ups would leave out. Almost everything floating re-rated after 2022. A 10-year-old LR2 product tanker picked up $16m, on a series too short to lean on. A 10-year-old handysize bulker – no crude exposure of any kind – gained 85% over its own baseline. If the test is “crude tankers jumped and nothing else did,” the data fail it, and we say so in our recently published paper.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/shi.text: BIMCO, European Shipowners | ECSA, the International Chamber of Shipping (ICS), INTERCARGO, INTERTANKO, and World Shipping Council (WSC) welcome the European Commission’s proposal to add two Indian ship recycling facilities to the updated European List of Ship Recycling Facilities. The shipping industry has advocated for the inclusion of compliant non-OECD yards since the entry into force of the EU Ship Recycling Regulation (EU SRR). Beyond its practical significance for shipowners, the proposal sends a strong political signal: non-OECD yards that meet the EU SRR’s safety and environmental requirements can and should be recognised. The inclusion of these two facilities is an important step towards resolving the structural capacity shortage on the European List. With industry estimates pointing to a significant increase in the number of vessels reaching the end of their operational life over the coming decade, the availability of sufficient compliant recycling capacity is essential. A European List that reflects the reality of global recycling capacity is a precondition for the legislation to function as intended: as an incentive for safe and environmentally sound ship recycling worldwide. This proposed update reflects years of substantial investment and effort, following the adoption of the Hong Kong Convention (HKC) in 2009. Inclusion on the European List should be determined solely on whether a facility meets the EU SRR’s safety and environmental requirements, based on objective assessment and inspection. The yards concerned have made considerable capital investments to upgrade their infrastructure, safety systems, and environmental management to meet the HKC and EU SRR standards. These efforts embody the very purpose of the EU SRR: to reduce disparities between operators in the EU, in OECD and in relevant third countries in terms of workplace health and safety and environmental standards, in support of the globally applicable Convention. Other yards in the region followed the same path and are soon expected to meet the EU SRR requirements. https://petronoticias.com.br/el-nino-pro.text: Secas severas estão afetando algumas das principais rotas marítimas do mundo, aumentando a pressão sobre mercados de energia que já enfrentam os impactos das interrupções no Estreito de Ormuz, segundo os dados mais recentes do VesselTracker, da Wood Mackenzie. As condições de seca provocadas pelo El Niño estão restringindo as operações do Canal do Panamá , levando os níveis de água aos menores patamares em comparação tanto com 2025 quanto com a média dos últimos cinco anos. A falta de chuvas obrigou as autoridades a impor restrições de calado que reduzem a capacidade efetiva de transporte das embarcações, com impactos significativos sobre o transporte de GNL em um momento de forte pressão sobre o mercado. Os mercados asiáticos de GNL estão enfrentando os efeitos da interdição do Estreito de Ormuz, que retirou aproximadamente 20% da oferta global de GNL , segundo análise da Wood Mackenzie. A seca no Canal do Panamá acrescenta uma segunda restrição, pressionando os compradores do Pacífico por duas frentes simultaneamente. Os trânsitos diários pelo Canal do Panamá caíram de aproximadamente 325 por dia no início de maio para 271 no fim do mês , antes de uma recuperação parcial para cerca de 308 por dia ao longo de junho, segundo dados de embarcações do Wood Mackenzie VesselTracker. O comportamento indica um corredor cada vez mais restrito, em vez de uma normalização das operações. GNL, GLP e derivados de petróleo estão entre os produtos mais diretamente expostos às restrições do canal. A rota conecta os terminais de exportação da Costa do Golfo dos Estados Unidos aos centros de demanda da bacia do Pacífico. Quando são impostas limitações de calado, os transportadores precisam operar com cargas abaixo da capacidade, disputar vagas de trânsito ou desviar pelo Cabo da Boa Esperança , o que acrescenta aproximadamente 10 a 15 dias ao tempo das viagens. O resultado é um aumento da demanda por tonelada-milha, uma menor disponibilidade de embarcações e fretes mais elevados, mesmo sem alterações nos fundamentos de oferta e demanda. Entre as commodities energéticas, o GNL é o mais sensível devido às margens estreitas de arbitragem, seguido pelo GLP e pelos derivados de petróleo, cujas janelas de negociação podem ser inviabilizadas até mesmo por aumentos modestos nos custos de frete. “ Monitorar as interrupções nas operações do canal provocadas pelo El Niño e a logística da Costa do Golfo será fundamental para antecipar novas desorganizações nos fluxos de commodities ao longo do terceiro e quarto trimestres de 2026 ”, afirmou Ian Solis , associado de dados da Wood Mackenzie. “ Como muitas regiões, especialmente o Pacífico, enfrentam crises de abastecimento de energia, interrupções como essa podem agravar ainda mais mercados que já estão extremamente apertados ”, ac

https://splash247.com/stx-architect-plot.text: One of the most spectacular boom-and-bust figures from shipping’s last great shipbuilding cycle is back. Kang Duk-soo, the architect of South Korea’s former STX empire, is returning to the industry through D-Ocean Asset Management, the consortium acquiring control of SK Oceanplant for around KRW410bn ($298m). SK Oceanplant is the former Samkang M&T, a Goseong-based offshore wind and latterly shipbuilding specialist acquired by SK Ecoplant in 2022 and renamed the following year. Its roots are in heavy steel fabrication, ship blocks and offshore structures, while it also builds special-purpose vessels and undertakes repair and conversion work. The company in a recent release said it has signed for six 115,000 dwt aframax crude tankers, with two additional options. The firm portion is worth about KRW600bn, rising to around KRW800bn ($580m) if the options are exercised. Kang was one of the most high-profile names during shipping’s previous supercycle in the first decade of the 21st century. Starting as an employee at Ssangyong Cement in 1973, he eventually became chief financial officer of Ssangyong Heavy Industries before putting his own money into acquiring the business in 2001 and renaming it STX.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Fighting has intensified on most of the border between Houthi forces in Yemen and the areas held by the internationally recognized government (IRG). The scale of fighting is much worse since an informal ceasefire came into force in March 2022, but has not yet returned to full-scale warfare, largely because the Saudi-led coalition has not fully engaged – although most parties are preparing for the worst. Probably the principal focus of the current fighting is the coastal strip bordering the eastern side of the Red Sea. To the north and south of Hodeida, the coast is held by the Houthis, including Yemen’s second biggest port in Hodeida itself, plus Ras Isa, and Salif further north – through which aid reaches the country, but also the arms and munitions which the Houthis need to arm their war machine. The IRG holds a small stretch of the coastline leading up to the Saudi border, and then the coastline south of Hodeida down to the Bab el Mandeb and the entrance to the Red Sea. Most of the islands in the Red Sea remain in the hands of the IRG, save those close-in to the Houthi-held coastal strip. By hanging on to the coast south of Hodeida, the IRG makes smuggling of arms to the Houthis difficult, and also inhibits attacks on ships where the Red Sea, at its southern end, is at its narrowest. In the current clashes, the Houthis seek to expand their coastal strip – to make it easier to smuggle in goods and attack shipping. The IRG, in contrast, led in this area by the murdered President Ali Saleh’s nephew, Major General Tariq Saleh, is intent on regaining Hodeida, to reduce the Houthis’ access to the outside world. From the number of funerals being held in the Tihama coastal strip from both sides of the conflict, the fighting appears to have been heavy, with large numbers of casualties attributed to the novel use by both sides of camera- and bomb-equipped drones. But as yet, there appears to have been no substantial change to front-line positions or territory held. The importance to the Houthis of gaining ground in this area has been demonstrated in recent days by the Houthi’s firing of at least six high-value Fateh-110 ballistic missiles from the Ibb and Ta’izz areas at targets in the IRG territory being defended by General Tariq and his National Resistance Forces (NRF), most notably at the harbor facilities in Mocha, Khawkah, and on the Hanish Islands, as well as front-line positions further inland. General Tariq’s forces claim to have fended off an attack by five Houthi speedboats that were aiming to make a landing on Zuqar Island off Khawkah. The Emiratis built an airfield on this island before they left earlier this year precisely because Red Sea commercial traffic could be interdicted by any force holding the island, using speedboats, mines or missile

https://safety4sea.com/american-club-key.text: The American P&I Club has published the latest installment of their Good Catch series, highlighting the risks associated with anchoring near pipelines, underwater cables and coral reefs. A ccording to the American Club, as all mariners are aware, there are a lot more than just sharks and fish below the surface of the water. There are pipelines, electrical cables, telecommunications cables for phone and internet, coral reefs, obstructions, debris flushed out by rivers, used fishing gear, and lost anchors. These objects can snag or foul your anchor and make it very difficult to retrieve. In some cases, a fouled anchor can only be retrieved with the assistance of divers or a crane barge, resulting in significant expense and delay. However, those expenses are small compared to the costs and consequences of damaging a pipeline, an electrical cable, a telecommunications cable, or a coral reef. Pipelines and underwater cables may be buried beneath the seabed or laid directly on the seafloor, depending on their purpose. The depth of cover typically varies from 3 to 25 feet (1 to 7.5 meters). However, waves and currents, especially from severe storms, can wash away some of the cover and can cause a pipeline or cable to shift. Also, the anchor’s flukes that dig into the ocean floor may penetrate the cover layer and snag on the pipeline or cable, damaging it. Coral reefs and environmentally sensitive marine life may not be located within anchorage areas but can sometimes be found immediately outside of an anchorage area. That puts them at risk should the vessel swing outside of the anchorage area or drag anchor beyond the anchorage area.

https://safety4sea.com/intertanko-says-m.text: The International Association of Independent Tanker Owners (INTERTANKO) has welcomed the clearance of sea mines from internationally recognised shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz, but warned that the move alone will not be enough to restore normal commercial traffic. U .S. Central Command confirmed that mines had been cleared from the Strait’s Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS), removing a major threat that has disrupted tanker operations for months. However, INTERTANKO said wider security risks remain and could continue to affect vessels transiting the strategic waterway. The association said shipowners will continue to assess whether to use the Strait based on security guidance, vessel-specific risk assessments and the safety of their crews. Operators have also been advised to consider the latest information from maritime authorities before attempting a transit. INTERTANKO said the internationally recognised TSS should ultimately be restored as the primary route for commercial shipping once security conditions stabilise. Until then, the safety of seafarers and secure vessel movements will remain the key considerations for companies operating in the Strait of Hormuz.

https://safety4sea.com/rmi-investigation.text: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Maritime Administrator has issued an investigation report into an incident where a crew member died after collapsing in a cargo-hold access space contaminated by toxic gases released from scrap metal. O n the morning of 19 February 2025, a cargo vessel was underway in the Mediterranean Sea, laden with scrap metal divided over six cargo holds on board. The operator had assessed scrap metal as an oxygen-depleting cargo that could emit toxic gases. Each cargo hold was accessible by means of two booby hatches located on the main deck: one at the forward end and one at the aft end. The booby hatches were locked during the voyage. The forward booby hatch for Cargo Hold No. 1 was located inside a small space beneath the forecastle deck. The space was naturally ventilated and accessible through a weathertight door from the cross deck between the forecastle and Cargo Hold No. 1. Empty pallets and drums containing chemicals were stored inside this space. Based on the definitions contained in IMO Resolution A.1050(27), applicable at the time of the incident, the space was assessed as neither an enclosed space nor an adjacent connected space because of its natural ventilation. At around 0815 hours, following the daily planning and toolbox talk for activities on deck, the Bosun and a deck trainee started to open the four booby hatches of Cargo Holds Nos. 1 and 2 for inspection of the toggle pins and packings of the booby hatch covers by the Chief Officer. At around 0830, they opened the forward booby hatch cover for Cargo Hold No. 1 and two additional hatches before the Bosun was called away. Before leaving, the Bosun instructed the deck trainee to open the forward booby hatch of Cargo Hold No. 2 and then join another crewmember. When the Bosun later passed the entrance to the Cargo Hold No. 1 Access Space, he found the deck trainee collapsed near the entrance. The Bosun alerted other crewmembers working on deck and informed the officer of the watch on the bridge by handheld radio. Two crewmembers were the first to arrive at the access space. One reported a strange smell and difficulty breathing before moving to the vessel’s side to get fresh air. The other entered the space to assist the collapsed crew member but experienced shortness of breath and felt unwell, managing to exit the space unaided. Another crewmember observed his condition and recognised that compressed air would be required to safely enter the space.

https://safety4sea.com/worlds-first-batt.text: On 26 August, CSL and Adbri marked the start of operations of MV Yampu, the world’s first battery-powered self-unloading bulk carrier. T he 125-metre, 11,900-dwt vessel was purpose-built to transport limestone from Adbri’s Klein Point quarry in South Australia to its Birkenhead cement plant in Adelaide. It is expected to carry around 2.7 million tonnes of limestone annually. Yampu can operate on battery power for about 40% of the time, with its batteries recharged while docked at Birkenhead. The vessel is expected to cut diesel consumption by more than 500,000 litres annually compared with the vessel it replaces, while being designed for future operation entirely on battery power. MV Yampu represents a significant step forward in our decarbonisation journey and demonstrates how practical innovation can deliver real environmental benefits while meeting the demands of commercial operations Owned and operated by CSL and crewed by Australian seafarers, the vessel is intended to strengthen the local limestone-to-cement supply chain and support lower-emission cement manufacturing. Every day, the limestone carried by MV Yampu will help produce the cement used to build homes, hospitals, schools, roads and major infrastructure projects across South Australia and Victoria. Being able to do that while further reducing emissions helps Adbri remains at the forefront of lower-carbon cement manufacturing in Australia

https://safety4sea.com/clean-shipping-co.text: As the IMO’s Intersessional Working Group on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships (ISWG-GHG 22) meets in London from 1-4 September, the Clean Shipping Coalition has urged member states to maintain their support for the proposed Net-Zero Framework (NZF), warning against alternative proposals that it says could weaken the shipping sector’s climate commitments. T he coalition said the NZF, while less ambitious than it had hoped, retains broad political support among IMO member states and remains the strongest available mechanism for delivering the goals of the IMO’s Greenhouse Gas Strategy. The NZF’s broad political support from member states means it remains the best tool available to meet the IMO’s Greenhouse Gas Strategy goals on climate, decarbonisation and a just and equitable energy transition for the shipping industry, and must be adopted by the IMO this December “The result of multiple rounds of negotiations, the NZF is already by any measure, an acceptable compromise. Any further weakening would lead to a less effective, slower, and costlier transition,” Leppert further highlighted. The shipping sector makes up 2-3% of global greenhouse gas emissions – comparable to the world’s fifth biggest emitting country, Japan. Approved during MEPC 83 in 2025, the NZF includes a “global fuel standard” (GFS), which requires ship operators to gradually decrease the amount of greenhouse gas emitted by shipping fuels – or pay penalties. The framework also introduces a mechanism that puts a price on a portion of greenhouse gases ships emit, giving the industry a clear financial incentive to reduce emissions in line with the global fuel standard.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A MXP Transportes , especializada no transporte rodoviário de cargas, realizou uma megaoperação para levar duas estações de tratamento de água de Sorocaba (SP) a Manaus , onde os equipamentos serão utilizados nas fábricas de uma empresa multinacional. O projeto exigiu planejamento específico em razão das diferentes condições encontradas ao longo da rota e da necessidade de utilização de transporte por balsa. Por se tratar de uma operação fora da rotina da empresa, a MXP reuniu equipes internas, motoristas, fabricante, fornecedores e parceiros com experiência em operações na Região Norte do Brasil. A estratégia considerou diferentes cenários para definir a rota e antecipar riscos relacionados às condições das rodovias, trechos de estrada de terra e etapas de navegação. “Foi uma operação que exigiu bastante planejamento, flexibilidade e capacidade de adaptação, principalmente porque fomos construindo a solução à medida que as informações eram consolidadas”, afirma Célio Malavasi, diretor executivo da MXP Transportes. Além das condições de rodagem, o planejamento levou em conta tempos de navegação, transporte por balsa, seguro, prazos e segurança da carga. A empresa avaliou essas variáveis de forma integrada para definir os procedimentos de cada etapa do deslocamento. A operação também contou com ferramentas de tecnologia para acompanhamento e controle do transporte. Segundo Malavasi, os recursos tecnológicos foram combinados ao planejamento e à atuação das equipes para permitir o acompanhamento dos cenários e a tomada de decisões durante o percurso. “O grande diferencial está justamente na combinação desses fatores: tecnologia, planejamento, gestão e pessoas. Quando temos as informações corretas, conseguimos analisar os cenários, antecipar possíveis dificuldades e conduzir a operação de forma segura e eficiente”, afirma.

A APM Terminals Suape iniciou as operações comerciais no Complexo Industrial Portuário Governador Eraldo Gueiros, em Pernambuco , com a chegada do navio Maersk Ganges. O empreendimento recebeu investimentos superiores a R$ 2 bilhões e é apresentado pela empresa como o primeiro terminal de contêineres 100% eletrificado da América Latina. A primeira escala comercial foi realizada pelo serviço de cabotagem ALCT2, que também atende os portos de Pecém (CE), Salvador (BA), Santos (SP), Itapoá (SC), Rio Grande e Imbituba (SC). A linha terá duas escalas semanais na APM Terminals Suape. Nesta primeira fase, o terminal terá capacidade inicial para movimentar até 400 mil TEUs por ano. Segundo a empresa, a entrada em operação ampliará em 55% a movimentação de contêineres no Complexo de Suape, contribuindo para a expansão da infraestrutura portuária e para a diversificação dos fluxos logísticos no Nordeste. Um estudo elaborado pela A&M Infra, Navarro Prado Advogados e APM Terminals aponta que o empreendimento tem potencial para acrescentar até R$ 4,8 bilhões às exportações, somar R$ 4,9 bilhões ao Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) e gerar mais de 43 mil empregos diretos e indiretos nas cadeias relacionadas ao comércio exterior. Para Daniel Rose, diretor-superintendente da APM Terminals Suape e Pecém, o início das atividades amplia a capacidade do complexo e cria condições para o crescimento da região. “Trata-se de um investimento estratégico em um mercado com forte potencial de expansão, que reforça a competitividade de Suape e responde à crescente demanda por infraestrutura mais eficiente no Nordeste”, afirma. A operação comercial também marca a conclusão de uma etapa de desenvolvimento, testes e preparação do terminal. De acordo com Herllon Rossato Rossdeutscher, head de Operações da APM Terminals Suape, a primeira escala valida a capacidade operacional instalada e inicia uma fase voltada à eficiência, previsibilidade e confiabilidade para clientes e parceiros.

O Boletim Tracker Fecap , estudo da Fundação Escola de Comércio Álvares Penteado (Fecap) em parceria com o Grupo Tracker, registrou 733 ocorrências de roubos e furtos envolvendo caminhões e outros veículos pesados no Estado de São Paulo entre janeiro e maio de 2026 . O número representa queda de 22,9% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando foram registrados 951 casos. A retração foi concentrada nos roubos, que passaram de 614 para 401 ocorrências, redução de 34,7%. Já os furtos permaneceram praticamente estáveis, com 332 registros em 2026, ante 337 no ano anterior, queda de 1,5%. O comportamento mais recente, porém, acende um ponto de atenção: os furtos cresceram 8,1% em abril e 39,2% em maio. O levantamento analisou, de forma inédita em dez anos de projeto, o comportamento dessas ocorrências entre 2024 e maio de 2026. Em 2024, foram registrados 2.106 eventos no estado. No ano seguinte, o total chegou a 2.141 casos, alta de 1,7%, com crescimento de 2,3% nos roubos e estabilidade nos furtos. “O recuo está concentrado nos roubos, enquanto os furtos permanecem praticamente no mesmo patamar e voltaram a crescer nos dois últimos meses analisados. É importante observar essa mudança porque ela pode representar uma adaptação da atividade criminosa e exige acompanhamento contínuo”, afirma Erivaldo Vieira, pesquisador da Fecap e responsável pelo estudo. A distribuição dos casos ao longo da semana permaneceu semelhante à observada em 2025. Entre janeiro e maio de 2026, 73,3% das ocorrências ocorreram de terça a sexta-feira. A quarta-feira liderou, com 146 registros, seguida por quinta-feira, com 142; terça-feira, com 130; e sexta-feira, com 119. Juntos, os quatro dias somaram 537 ocorrências. A noite e a madrugada também concentraram a maior parte dos registros. Considerando apenas os casos com horário válido, os dois períodos responderam por 60,2% das ocorrências em 2026, ante 58,3% no mesmo intervalo de 2025. A noite teve 172 registros, enquanto a madrugada somou 159.

A Golgi , joint venture de desenvolvimento e gestão de ativos logísticos de alto padrão da canadense Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan e da brasileira Arch Capital, acaba de concluir a entrega da segunda fase do empreendimento Golgi Cajamar . O novo galpão soma 54 mil m² instalados no mesmo terreno do ativo original , entregue em 2025 com 93 mil m², resultando em um total de 148 mil m² de Área Total Locável (ABL) . O ganho de escala transforma o Golgi Cajamar no maior complexo logístico em operação da companhia no Brasil . A expansão está pronta para receber operações logísticas imediatas. O novo estoque chega ao mercado em um momento de alta resiliência e forte absorção do setor, impulsionado pela demanda de grandes e-commerces, varejistas e indústrias por armazéns de alta eficiência logística próximos à capital paulista. De acordo com dados recentes da consultoria JLL, Cajamar, que concentra o maior estoque logístico do Brasil, tem taxa de vacância de apenas 4,8%. No segundo trimestre de 2026, o eixo registrou 112 mil m² de absorção bruta e 27 mil m² de absorção líquida. "Disponibilizar ao mercado 54 mil m² prontos para ocupação, em um dos eixos mais demandados, é uma resposta estratégica ao crescimento e à sofisticação das redes de distribuição e logística no Sudeste", afirma Roberto Miranda, CEO da Arch Capital . O novo galpão da Golgi foi desenvolvido seguindo as diretrizes de padrão construtivo Classe A (Triple A) do mercado global. A estrutura conta com pé-direito livre de 12 metros, capacidade de piso industrial de alta resistência para até 6 toneladas por m², sistema de combate a incêndio com sprinklers instalados, eficiência de armazenagem de 91% e docas com niveladores embutidos automáticos, otimizando a velocidade de carga e descarga de grandes frotas. A localização estratégica do Golgi Cajamar garante acesso rápido e direto às principais rodovias do estado, incluindo a Rodovia Edgar Máximo Zambotto, a Rodovia Anhanguera, a Rodovia dos Bandeirantes e Rodoanel Mario Covas, facilitando o escoamento rápido de mercadorias e o abastecimento de last-mile para a Região Metropolitana de São Paulo.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/keeping-.text: Lloyd’s Register (LR), the UK-based classification society, and the Marine Design and Research Institute of China (MARIC) have unveiled a tri-fuel-ready tanker concept designed to give owners flexibility to pursue liquefied natural gas (LNG), methanol, or ammonia as fuel technologies, infrastructure, and regulations evolve, while uncertainty over future marine fuels continues to shape investment decisions. Lloyd’s Register and MARIC have secured approval in principle (AiP) for a new 114,000 DWT product and crude oil tanker designed to accommodate future conversion to LNG, methanol, or ammonia, giving owners the flexibility to leverage multiple fuel pathways. This tanker concept has been designed as a product and crude oil carrier that can accommodate future conversion to LNG, methanol, or ammonia as technologies, regulations, and fuel supply chains mature. LR emphasizes that the concept aims to reduce future retrofit complexity, providing owners with greater confidence when planning long-term fleet investments, by incorporating conversion readiness at the design stage. Theo Kourmpelis , Global Business Director for Tankers, Lloyd’s Register, commented: “Shipowners are being asked to make major investment decisions today despite continued uncertainty around which fuels will dominate in the decades ahead. “Alternative fuel solutions each offer potential pathways to compliance, but fuel infrastructure, regulation and economics continue to evolve at different speeds around the world. Designs that preserve flexibility will be critical in helping owners manage risk while preparing for multiple future scenarios.”

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/real-tim.text: Offshore operations bring together vessel crews, client representatives, contractors, and project teams. Nobody ever disagrees on the goal of the project. The disagreement happens the moment the question shifts from “what needs to be done?” to “is it safe to do it now?” Someone must make the call. And when conditions are marginal, everyone in that room has a different number in their head. After a weather delay, who decides when to restart? The client representative, pushed by an onshore schedule, may – manually – read the sea state differently to the deck supervisor responsible for the crew at the rail. The project team sees a closing window. The bridge sees wave heights that don’t match the forecast. Everyone is working from the same event, but not from the same facts. Forecasts are useful and no serious offshore operator dismisses them. But a forecast is a probability, not a measurement. It describes potential conditions across a region, across a time window. What it cannot do is tell you, with precision, what the wave height, period, and direction are at your vessel’s exact position right now, as the crew prepares to move. Experience and seamanship matter. But when one qualified person calls conditions acceptable, and another calls them borderline, what follows isn’t a decision, but a negotiation. Pressure enters the room. The people most exposed to consequences may have the least power in that conversation. Across different offshore vessel hazards, this pattern exists across every vessel category, from platform supply vessels and anchor handlers to construction and installation vessels, patrol craft and survey ships. While the specific risks vary, the underlying problem doesn’t. Go or no-go decisions, personnel transfer windows, crane lifts, cargo handling: every one of them requires a judgment call about sea state. Every one of them becomes harder to make well, and harder to defend afterwards, without measured local data.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/woodside.text: Australian energy giant Woodside is forging a path with Mexico’s state-owned petroleum heavyweight Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex) to hunt for potential deepwater hydrocarbon plays in the Gulf of Mexico under a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MOU). This non-binding MOU will allow Woodside and Pemex to analyse potential prospects for hydrocarbon exploration and extraction in the deep waters of the Gulf of Mexico, while facilitating the mutual exchange of technical knowledge, experience, and industry best practices in the oil and gas sector. Liz Westcott , Woodside’s CEO, commented: “This MOU builds on the strong relationship between Woodside and Pemex and our joint efforts to develop oil and gas resources in Mexico’s ultra-deepwater. The agreement strengthens our relationship and opens the door to explore future opportunities to work together in Mexico’s deepwater. “We are grateful to Pemex and Secretary of Energy Luz Elena González Escobar for their continued support and commitment to the development of Mexico’s deepwater resources.” The MOU was signed in Mexico City following a meeting between the two companies’ chief executive officers (CEOs), Woodside’s Westcott and Pemex’s Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso . The two firms are jointly developing the Trion oil project, which is located approximately 180 kilometers off Mexico’s coastline and 30 kilometers south of the U.S.-Mexico maritime border.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/galp-tot.text: French energy giant TotalEnergies and Portugal’s Galp have closed a deal that reshuffles their positions across several offshore Namibian blocks, with the former taking over operatorship of one license, while the latter retains a stake and picks up interests in two others. Galp has completed the deal with TotalEnergies in Namibia, exchanging participation interests in PEL 83, including transfer of operatorship, for positions in PEL 56 and PEL 91. As a result, the Portuguese firm has retained a non-operated 40% participating interest in PEL 83, where the Mopane discovery lies, and assumed a 10% interest in PEL 56, home to the Venus discovery , and a 9.4% interest in PEL 91. According to the company, the completion activates the associated funding agreement, where 50% of all of its investments for a first development in Mopane will be carried. This deal enabled TotalEnergies to acquire a 40% operated interest in PEL 83 license. Galp highlighted: “The transaction closing further supports the operative next steps, with Galp well aligned with partners to support the Venus development upcoming final investment decision (FID) and to continue progressing in the preparations for the next exploration and appraisal campaign at Mopane, targeting drilling in the fourth quarter.” With the closing of the transaction, participating partners in PEL 83 will be Galp (40%), TotalEnergies (40%), NAMCOR (10%), and Custos (10%). Within PEL 56, the ownership structure will become Galp (10%), TotalEnergies (35.25%), QatarEnergy (35.25%), NAMCOR (10%), and Impact (9.5%).

https://petronoticias.com.br/porto-alegr.text: A Be8 vai fazer uma demonstração operacional de estratégias voltadas à redução das emissões de carbono na frota do transporte coletivo de Porto Alegre utilizando o combustível BeVant. A iniciativa integra a estratégia do município de avaliar soluções capazes de contribuir para a descarbonização da mobilidade urbana. A assinatura deste compromisso aconteceu na na Expointer, com a presença do prefeito, Sebastião Melo, do secretário Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana, Adão de Castro Júnior , além do presidente da companhia, Erasmo Carlos Battistella. A operação com o Be8 BeVant seguirá um plano de demonstração com duração de seis meses e envolverá as operadoras do transporte público de Porto Alegre, em linhas que serão definidas em conjunto com a SMMU e a Empresa Pública de Transporte e Circulação (EPTC). Durante o período de testes, as operadoras utilizarão um tanque de armazenamento do biocombustível drop-in fornecido pela Be8. A solução permite fácil integração à frota existente, sem a necessidade de modificações de hardware nos veículos e em conformidade com o arcabouço regulatório vigente. Desenvolvido pela Be8, o BeVant é um biocombustível renovável que pode substituir integralmente o diesel fóssil e reduzir em 99% as emissões de gases de efeito estufa (GEE) no ciclo do combustível. Um dos seus principais diferenciais é ser uma solução que pode ser utilizada nos motores a diesel existentes sem necessidade de alterações técnicas, adaptações ou investimentos adicionais nos veículos e na infraestrutura de abastecimento. “ A transição energética exige diferentes caminhos, e o Brasil tem a vantagem de contar com soluções renováveis que podem gerar resultados agora. O Be8 BeVant permite reduzir significativamente as emissões utilizando os veículos, motores e a infraestrutura já existentes, sem comprometer a performance operacional. A participação de Porto Alegre nesta iniciativa demonstra que é possível avançar na descarbonização do transporte coletivo de forma prática e imediata ”, Battistella. O BeVant já vem sendo utilizado e avaliado em diferentes aplicações, como veículos pesados, ônibus, máquinas e equipamentos. Em janeiro de 2026, a Be8 e a Coleurb anunciaram uma parceria para utilização do combustível em parte da frota do transporte coletivo de Passo Fundo. A solução também já foi aplicada em operação de transporte hidroviário no Rio Grande do Sul. O produto já atende mais de 100 clientes no Brasil, em segmentos como agronegócio, mineração, transporte de passageiros e cargas, geração de energia e operações marítimas e ferroviárias. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Mensagens obtidas pela Polícia Federal revelam canal direto de Cláudio Castro com Ricardo Magro, dono da Refit. O material motivou novas buscas autorizadas pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal. Os diálogos contrariam a versão de Castro de que não tinha relação com Magro. https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: A PGR encaminhou ao STF uma proposta de delação premiada do empresário Antônio Carlos Freixo Júnior, dono da Entre Investimentos, apontada como intermediária de repasses ao filme "Dark Horse". https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Growth in the container segment of the shipping industry has been making headlines for a long time, but it just smashed through a record. Surpassing the 34 million TEU mark, trade group BIMCO says the growth has accelerated and is reshaping the sector. According to BIMCO’s calculations, global container fleet capacity was just 8,000 TEU below the 34 million TEU mark as of the beginning of September. It reported the milestone would be reached after only a few of the 46 ships (totalling 286,000 TEU) scheduled for September delivery enter into service. Indeed, by AlphaLiner’s figures, the industry is there. In its ranking of the Top 100 carriers, AlphaLiner sets the fully cellular capacty is at 34.2 million with 6,822 fully cellular vessels representing 412 million dwt in active service. (Total capacity according to AlphaLiner for all types of vessels is already over 34.6 million TEU.) "When the world’s shipyards deliver just a few more container ships, the global fleet capacity will for the first time reach 34 million TEU,” said Niels Rasmussen, Chief Shipping Analyst at BIMCO. “At that time, the fleet will have grown by 10 million TEU - or 42 percent - in just five and a half years.” BIMCO highlights that the latest addition of 10 million TEU, achieved in just five and a half years, is also a record. In comparison, it says it took the industry 10 and a half years to go from 14 to 24 million TEU. “The growth we have seen reflects a combination of record-high new ship deliveries and remarkably low ship recycling activity,” said Rasmussen. “Less than 300,000 TEU have been recycled over the last five and a half years. The last time recycling activity was this low during the same time frame was between early 2004 and mid-2009, when the fleet was only one-third of its current size.”
