https://gcaptain.com/saudi-pipeline-outa.text: A satellite image shows the Saudi Arabia East-West pipeline, located across the Arabian Peninsula, after a strike that hit it on September 11, 2026, in Saudi Arabia, September 13, 2026. Vantor/Handout via REUTERS LONDON, Sept 13 (Reuters) – Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn’t restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis. Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay off-line. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing. Saudi Arabia’s government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbors. The world’s biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea.But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports. Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypt’s ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said.

Container rates on the transpacific remain at the highest since mid-2022, with prices for containers to the West Coast between $6,585/FEU (40-foot equivalent unit) and $7,750/FEU, and rates to the East Coast are between $8,750/FEU and $11,000/FEU. Rates from supply chain advisors Drewry were up by 2% week on week from Shanghai to Los Angeles and by 1% from Shanghai to New York, as shown in the following chart. Drewry said there have been eight blank sailings announced for next week, up from seven this week, indicating tighter capacity. Rates from online shipping marketplace and platform provider Freightos fell by 1% to the West Coast and by 3% to the East Coast. Judah Levine, head of research at Freightos, said carriers are paying higher costs for fuel as rates have trended higher since the collapse of the ceasefire in July. “Recent escalations as well as an increase in Chinese crude imports have pushed bunker fuel prices back up to levels last seen in June,” Levine said. “Climbing fuel costs are likely setting an elevated floor for container rates, but ocean prices are still largely being driven by demand trends and disruptions to capacity availability.” Levine said he does not expect rates to continue rising after the slight decreases this week but said elevated demand that started in late May has kept prices at peak levels since early July.

https://splash247.com/drowning-in-data-s.text: The next digital race is not about collecting more data. It is about getting the right information to the right decision-maker before the opportunity to act has passed. The latest chapter from SplashTech’s annual report. Engines, generators, fuel-flow meters, navigation equipment, shaft-power meters, cargo systems and countless other pieces of machinery can now produce continuous streams of information. Add AIS, weather, voyage reports, alarms, maintenance histories, photographs, emails and compliance records and the modern vessel can become a formidable data-generating machine. What happens next? Asked what percentage of vessel data is actually translated into operational decisions, SplashTech’s respondents produce estimates ranging from the low single digits to more than 60%. The numbers vary wildly, but the broad conclusion does not: maritime has become considerably better at generating and storing data than using it. Gert-Jan Panken, general manager and vice-president at Inmarsat Maritime, deliberately avoids attaching a neat percentage. “Across the industry, the percentage is still relatively small,” he tells SplashTech, stressing that the figure varies substantially by operator and vessel type. For Panken, the pursuit of a higher percentage risks missing the point entirely.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/w.text: The heavy-lift ship Black Marlin has successfully delivered the world's largest electric ferry, the China Zorrilla. The Australian-made vessel is the world's largest electric vehicle of any kind, and it will operate on a 30-nautical-mile run across the Rio de la Plata between Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay and Buenos Aires, Argentina. China Zorrilla is an aluminum fast-ferry design constructed at the Incat yard in Tasmania. Capable of carrying up to 225 vehicles and 2,100 passengers, it is physically larger and has a larger battery bank than any other battery-electric vessel. It was loaded out on Boskalis' Black Marlin in July for the 40-day eastbound journey to the Rio de la Plata. The ship and its ship-cargo then transited the Pacific and the Strait of Magellan to reach the Atlantic. On arrival at Nueva Palmira, Uruguay, Black Marlin waited for favorable weather, then ballasted down far enough to float the ferry off its deck, reversing the procedure used in Tasmania for loading. "Thousands of people have played a part in bringing this remarkable vessel to life, and they should all be incredibly proud of what has been accomplished." Incat is now engaged in building a series of three 129-meter electric ferries for Denmark's Molslinjen - the largest ferry electrification program (across multiple vessels) in the world. The new vessels will operate in the Kattegat, a high-profile assignment. "China" Zorrilla (originally Concepción Matilde Zorrilla) was a locally-famous actress who made her name in the Uruguayan and Argentinian theater scenes, appearing in countless plays, movies and television shows from the 1950s up through at least 2007. https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: After a serious collision between two bulkers in the Gulf of Kutch, the Indian Coast Guard has launched a major rescue and pollution-response operation to minimize the potential impact of the casualty. On September 11, the bulker KMax Emperor (IMO 9477426) and the True Mariner (IMO 9599822) collided at a crowded anchorage off Mundra Port. AIS data from Pole Star Global shows that the two vessels were anchored next to each other for several days prior to the casualty. The data suggests that at about 0530 hours UTC on September 11, KMax Emperor departed from her anchor circle and moved towards True Mariner, located approximately one kilometer to the northeast. KMax Emperor was making up to four knots prior to making contact, the AIS data shows. After the collision, True Mariner appeared to drift to the west, then went to anchor again a short distance from her initial position. KMax Emperor also anchored again nearby. In a brief statement, the Indian Coast Guard said that it had launched a rescue operation shortly after the collision. KMax Emperor sustained significant damage on the port quarter, and was trimmed by the stern and listing slightly to port. 21 members of her crew were safely evacuated, and three remained aboard to oversee response operations. The Indian Coast Guard also mobilized pollution control resources, working with other agencies to coordinate the response.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) defendeu, em manifestação enviada ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) nesta segunda-feira (14), a retirada do sigilo de mais uma frente de investigação do caso Master. A investigação trata sobre a rede de pagamentos de Daniel Vorcaro e da instituição financeira extinta. O STF já tornou públicos 53 procedimentos de apurações relacionados ao caso Master. A retirada dos sigilos foi concluída após pedido do presidente da Corte, ministro Edson Fachin.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O Supremo Tribunal Federal chega às vésperas da sessão desta terça-feira (15) que pode decidir sobre a abertura de uma apuração contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes por mensagens enviadas por Daniel Vorcaro sem definição do rito e principalmente do quórum que vai analisar o relatório da Polícia Federal. Ministros discutem nos bastidores se os colegas Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça devem participar da sessão que vai decidir sobre a regularidade do relatório. Até agora, o Supremo só confirmou que a sessão será transmitida na TV Justiça e o acesso ao plenário restrito. Alvo do relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou 52 mensagens de Vorcaro , Moraes indicou em conversas internas que ainda não teria decidido se vai ou não pedir para se manifestar e até mesmo votar. Uma ala do Supremo avalia que o ideal seria que Moraes não comparecesse ao plenário para não representar um movimento de pressão sobre os colegas. Já ministros alinhados com Moraes também discutem se vão levantar uma questão de ordem para que o ministro André Mendonça não possa participar da análise do caso.

Segundo informações obtidas pela TV Globo, o deputado federal Cezinha de Madureira (PL-SP) está entre os alvos. A reportagem procurou o deputado, mas ainda não obteve resposta.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542908-ve.text: Baker Hughes has received two orders from Venture Global to supply gas compression systems for the Cloud Connector Pipeline and liquefaction equipment for the expansion of the Plaquemines LNG facility in Louisiana. The Cloud Connector order covers 13 gas compression systems driven by Frame 5/2E gas turbines to transport feed gas through the pipeline to Plaquemines LNG. Baker Hughes described the order as one of the largest deployments for LNG feed gas transportation in the United States. The order is the second for Frame 5/2E gas turbine-driven centrifugal compressor packages for Venture Global's feed gas pipeline, bringing the fleet supporting Plaquemines LNG to 23 systems. For the Plaquemines expansion, Baker Hughes will provide four liquefaction blocks comprising eight liquefaction modules, including Chart cold boxes. Each block will use two electric-motor-driven, single mixed-refrigerant liquefaction modules and associated compression trains featuring Baker Hughes centrifugal compressor technology, alongside cold boxes, air coolers and integrated control systems. "Baker Hughes has been a trusted partner across our LNG developments, both at our LNG facilities and across our pipeline infrastructure," said Mike Sabel, CEO of Venture Global. "As we advance the expansion of Plaquemines LNG, this collaboration not only supports our expansion plans, but also helps ensure we deliver the reliable feed gas transportation necessary to realize our mission of supplying secure LNG to global markets.”

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542899-gr.text: The Greater Sunrise natural gas project has pushed back its earliest possible production start by two years to 2034, East Timor's petroleum minister said, tightening a timeline already plagued by decades of delays. Production at the multi-billion dollar gas field, which has been stalled for decades amid disagreements with Australia, will likely begin in 2034 or 2035, Francisco da Costa Monteiro, East Timor's Minister of Petroleum & Mineral Resources, said at the Gastech conference in Bangkok. East Timor and its Australian partner Woodside ast year forecast the project would produce gas by 2032 to 35, the first time a timeline was announced by both parties. Extraction and subsequent LNG exports from the gas field are crucial for Southeast Asia's poorest nation, also known as Timor-Leste, to prove that bets on LNG in the Timor Sea are viable and attract investors to develop other gas reserves. "Timor-Leste is one of the potential countries that can play quite a role in this region and a role at large," Monteiro said. "We do have several discovered gas resources in the pipeline and the whole idea of putting that in the international market is the challenge at the moment," he said, adding that Sunda GasSNDA.Lhopes to commercialise the Chuditch gas discovery soon.

https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/n.text: O mais recente capítulo da crise inédita no Supremo Tribunal Federal teve início na noite da última quinta-feira (10), quando o presidente da Corte, Edson Fachin, solicitou ao ministro André Mendonça que levantasse o sigilo de todo o Caso Master, do qual Mendonça é relator. Desde então, o que se viu foi uma incessante troca de ofícios entre ministros do Supremo: Mendonça escolheu quais peças seriam abertas; os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e Cristiano Zanin questionaram e pediram abertura total do inquérito; o também ministro Gilmar Mendes pediu a Fachin que mudasse o escopo ou que adiasse a sessão plenária marcada para terça-feira (15) que irá decidir a abertura ou não de investigação sobre Moraes. Por fim, Mendonça liberou o sigilo de novos documentos do Caso Master – documentos que citam os senadores Ciro Nogueira (PL-PI) e Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) e que mostram que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) é investigado pela Polícia Federal em inquérito aberto para apurar a possível prática de crimes relacionados ao financiamento da produção do filme "Dark Horse". Neste episódio, Natuza Nery recebe o jurista Oscar Vilhena para analisar este que é o momento mais tenso de toda a história do STF . Vilhena avalia a gravidade das suspeitas

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Uma reportagem do jornal "Financial Times" , publicada neste domingo (13), afirma que a crise sem precedentes no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) poderá ter um impacto decisivo na eleição presidencial brasileira do próximo mês. O jornal britânico descreve a crise como uma "disputa acirrada" entre os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça , que está "lançando uma sombra sobre a disputa" entre Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) e Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ).

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542903-tp.text: Turkey's state oil company TPAO plans to expand its cooperation with Azerbaijan's SOCAR to explore new offshore areas, including the Karabakh oil and gas field, Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and TPAO CEO Can Ergin said. TPAO-SOCAR cooperation in Azerbaijan, expanded last year through the Shafag-Asiman project, is expected to continue with Karabakh, Bayraktar said. Ergin said TPAO is evaluating opportunities in other prospective structures and new offshore areas with SOCAR. BP acquired a 35% stake in Karabakh from SOCAR in 2025 and became operator, while SOCAR retained 65%.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542906-sa.text: Saipem has been awarded a contract worth about $350 million for subsea work on Azule Energy's West Hub Tails oil project offshore Angola, part of the wider Agogo Integrated West Hub Development. The project is located about 180 kilometers offshore Angola in water depths of up to 1,750 meters. Under the contract awarded by Azule Energy Angola, Saipem will handle engineering, fabrication, transportation and installation of subsea infrastructure, including about 62 kilometers of flowlines, risers and umbilical’s. The infrastructure will be tied back to the Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) unit, with Saipem's work expected to take about two and a half years. Saipem will deploy its FDS and Normand Maximus construction vessels for the offshore installation campaign. Fabrication will be carried out at Saipem's Ambriz yard in Angola, with local companies and workers involved in the activities.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542904-pe.text: Petronas and PTTEP subsidiaries have received approvals from the governments of Malaysia and Thailand for a new 35-year production sharing contract covering Block A-18-01 in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area (MTJDA). PC JDA Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Petronas, and PTTEP JDX Thailand and PTTEP JDX Thailand (JDA) also signed a Gas Sales Agreement with Petronas and PTT Public Company Limited for continued natural gas supply from the block to Malaysia and Thailand. The signed agreements were exchanged on September 14 following collaboration between the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority (MTJA), PC JDA and PTTEP JDX on a new contractual framework for the area. The new PSC has a 35-year term beginning January 1, 2026 and combines the existing Block A-18, whose current PSC expires on April 20, 2029, with an adjacent exploration area offering additional resource potential. Block A-18-01 comprises the Cakerawala, Bumi, Suriya, Bulan, South Bulan, Senja, East Bumi, Samudra and Wira gas fields, as well as an open area. The wider MTJDA spans about 7,250 square kilometers and comprises Blocks A-18-01 and B-17-01. Together, the blocks have natural gas production capacity of about 700 million standard cubic feet per day, distributed equally between Malaysia and Thailand.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542900-sa.text: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East-West pipeline, after the vital oil conduit came under aerial attack in the widening Middle East war, threatening to send energy prices even higher. The world’s largest crude oil exporter said it temporarily closed the pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that both Baghdad and Riyadh said had originated in Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate. Iraq dismissed a military commander on Saturday in response to the attack. The 1,200-km (745-mile) pipeline running across the Arabian Peninsula has served as the main route out for global supplies of Middle East oil for the past six months while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by war. It has been moving 4 million to 5 million barrels per day, amounting to 4% to 5% of global supply, sparing Saudi Arabia the brunt of the disruption that has crippled other Gulf oil and gas exporters. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strikes. Satellite images showed black smoke rising from an area of the pipeline south of Medina. The attack resulted in some injuries and damage that was being assessed, the Saudi Foreign Ministry said without detailing the impact on exports. U.S. President Donald Trump, visiting Ireland to attend a golf tournament at one of his resorts, said Iran was probably to blame. On Saturday, the Saudi Civil Defence said in a statement that a projectile fired by the Houthis had injured two people in Jazan region, along with damaging several buildings, including a mosque.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542901-xr.text: XRG, ADNOC and SEFE have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore wider cooperation across the natural gas and LNG value chain, including supply, infrastructure and shipping opportunities aimed at Germany and the wider European market. The agreement covers potential cooperation in four areas: security of supply, market development and growth, supply chain resilience, and portfolio and shipping optimization. The companies will explore combining ADNOC's UAE-based supply and XRG's international supply sources with SEFE's market presence, trading capabilities, customer relationships and infrastructure access. The partnership could also include investment in and development of energy infrastructure, as well as measures to optimize gas and LNG portfolios and cargo movements. "XRG and ADNOC are committed to Germany for the long term. We have already invested €19 billion, and this week the UAE more widely announced the long-term intention to invest a further €40 billion in the country. This agreement with SEFE combines our capabilities and opens new opportunities across the gas and LNG value chain, strengthening energy security and supporting the competitiveness and growth of German industry," said Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber, ADNOC Managing Director and Group CEO and Executive Chairman of XRG. The MoU was signed during UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan's visit to Germany and builds on an existing relationship between ADNOC and SEFE.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A FedEx prevê investir mais de R$ 75 milhões no Brasil em um projeto de expansão de sua infraestrutura de serviços internacionais e de supply chain . O plano contempla a abertura de novas unidades, ampliação da rede FedEx Ship Center e expansão de centros logísticos em diferentes regiões do país. As novas instalações funcionarão como centros de serviço multifuncionais, integrando as operações de transporte internacional e supply chain. Entre os serviços previstos estão coleta e entrega de remessas internacionais, estoque avançado e distribuição de última milha para equipamentos de ponto de venda (POS) e entregas críticas. Até o fim de setembro, a empresa prevê abrir unidades em Curitiba, Itabuna (BA), João Pessoa, Ribeirão Preto (SP), Aracaju, Goiânia e Rio de Janeiro. O projeto contempla 34 novas unidades, algumas das quais já foram inauguradas em cidades como São Paulo, São Luís, São José dos Campos (SP), Londrina (PR), Joinville (SC), Florianópolis, Campinas (SP) e Pouso Alegre (MG). “Os investimentos reforçam nosso compromisso com a operação da companhia no Brasil e com uma estratégia de crescimento de longo prazo voltada ao fortalecimento dos nossos serviços”, afirma Camila Lima, vice-presidente de Operações da FedEx no Brasil. Segundo a executiva, a expansão busca oferecer soluções mais integradas e flexíveis aos clientes. Além da rede de atendimento, a FedEx está ampliando sua infraestrutura de supply chain. Em Cajamar (SP), a capacidade operacional da unidade está sendo expandida de 55 mil para 90 mil posições-palete. O projeto inclui melhorias de infraestrutura e modernização tecnológica, com a implementação de soluções de automação e classificação de mercadorias. Em Jaboatão dos Guararapes (PE), o armazém atual passará de 16 mil para 26 mil metros quadrados e será modernizado para atender aos padrões Triple A.

A GTS Transportes , empresa de Betim (MG) especializada em logística rodoviária para a indústria, iniciou sua atuação no setor de mineração com uma frota de caminhões extrapesados Mercedes-Benz Axor 2545 6x2 . A companhia já recebeu 26 unidades do modelo, que operam com semirreboques basculantes em sua filial de Nova Lima (MG) , no Quadrilátero Ferrífero. A previsão é chegar a 45 caminhões Axor destinados à operação até o fim de setembro. A entrada na mineração ocorreu em março, como parte da expansão das atividades da empresa, que tem 22 anos de atuação no transporte e na logística rodoviária. Os veículos foram comercializados pela concessionária Minasmáquinas, com financiamento do Banco Mercedes-Benz. “Já são 22 anos da nossa empresa em transporte e logística rodoviária para a indústria. No último mês de março, demos início a um novo capítulo dessa história, com a entrada no segmento de mineração, por meio da implantação de uma filial em Nova Lima”, afirma Rafael Carvalho, CEO da GTS Transportes. Além dos 45 Axor 2545 destinados à mineração, a GTS prevê incorporar mais dois Axor 2545 para operações com prancha de três eixos e três unidades para semirreboques sider. Também estão sendo entregues seis caminhões Axor 2038, para uso com carretas abertas e sider. Com essas aquisições, a empresa deverá atingir 56 caminhões Axor adquiridos em menos de um ano. Segundo Jânio Alves, gerente de Frota da GTS, o movimento faz parte da renovação e expansão da frota, com foco em produtividade, segurança, disponibilidade e eficiência operacional. Os caminhões destinados à mineração operam 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana. De acordo com Alves, o modelo apresentou consumo médio de 2,5 quilômetros por litro na operação e vem atendendo às expectativas da empresa em aspectos como conforto, estabilidade, disponibilidade e economia.

A GH Solucionador Logístico iniciou, neste mês de setembro, as operações de sua nova unidade em Uruguaiana (RS) , criada para ampliar a atuação da empresa no transporte rodoviário internacional. A estrutura terá foco na gestão e no suporte aos fluxos de fronteira , inicialmente com operações destinadas à Argentina, ao Uruguai, ao Chile e ao Paraguai. A unidade conta com equipe própria para acompanhamento das cargas, monitoramento de veículos, suporte aos motoristas, controle das etapas operacionais e interlocução com transportadores e demais parceiros envolvidos nas operações. O escritório tem perfil predominantemente administrativo e operacional e, neste momento, não possui estrutura própria de armazenagem. A operação internacional incorporada à estratégia da companhia reúne um histórico de aproximadamente 2.500 carregamentos anuais, mais de 50 clientes de diferentes segmentos e uma rede de cerca de 300 veículos disponíveis para atendimento das rotas internacionais. A GH realiza operações porta a porta, inbound e outbound, com cargas destinadas principalmente aos setores farmacêutico, têxtil, automotivo, veterinário e outras indústrias de transformação. Entre as atividades realizadas pela equipe em Uruguaiana estão a contratação e gestão de transportes, administração e controle da documentação, atendimento aos motoristas, acompanhamento das cargas e monitoramento das etapas relacionadas aos processos de fronteira. A presença local também busca aumentar a visibilidade sobre as operações e agilizar a resolução de eventuais ocorrências. A GH projeta R$ 60 milhões em faturamento com as operações de transporte rodoviário internacional, considerando fluxos de importação e exportação. Segundo Giovanni Dall Orsoletta, gerente de Expansão Internacional da empresa, a ampliação busca acompanhar o crescimento das operações de comércio exterior e ampliar a capacidade de atendimento nesse mercado. “O Brasil precisa de operadores logísticos cada vez mais preparados para atender o mercado internacional. As importações e exportações crescem a cada ano, acompanhando a abertura de novos mercados. A ampliação da nossa operação internacional fortalece nossa estrutura e aumenta nossa capacidade de atender esse cenário”, afirma.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/brent_oil_p.text: Brent crude spiked to $108.49 per barrel at the Asian opening while WTI reached $106.60 per barrel, before easing back a bit, after Saudi Arabia closed its East-West pipeline following attacks, Saxo Bank noted in a market quick take posted on its site early Monday. The route has been carrying around five million barrels a day of crude bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, Saxo Bank pointed out in the quick take, adding that the closure is estimated to put around four percent of global supply at risk and may force Saudi Arabia to make further output cuts as storage facilities fill. “With no end to the conflict in sight, the risk of further inflationary pressure through higher fuel costs remains a key focus,” Saxo Bank warned in the market quick take. “In Brent, the prompt month spread has jumped to $5.39 while the three-month spread has surged to near $14 highlighting the elevated premiums buyers are prepared to pay for immediate delivery,” it added. In a market analysis sent to Rigzone today, Waleed Said, Technical Analyst at GivTrade, outlined that both Bent and WTI advanced more than three percent “as renewed attacks disrupted critical Middle East energy infrastructure and shipping routes”. “That move reversed part of Friday’s pullback, when Brent settled at $$104.61 and WTI at $100.05 as expectations for possible diplomatic progress temporarily reduced the geopolitical premium,” Said noted.

https://safety4sea.com/atalanta-response.text: On September 10, Operation ATALANTA was alerted to the hijacking of the St. Vincent and Grenadines-flagged merchant vessel Glamor, approximately 38 nautical miles southwest of Balhaf, Yemen. A s stated, the Pirate Action Group (PAG) involved in the incident was reported to comprise six individuals. Prior to the attempted boarding, the crew of the Glamor managed to bring the vessel to a stop and shut down its systems. As a precautionary security measure, the crew then retreated to the vessel’s citadel. Following the alert, ATALANTA redirected assets operating in the area towards the vessel’s reported location. In coordination with the Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), a Japanese reconnaissance aircraft also conducted show-of-force flights over the merchant vessel. The visible presence and approaching response of international maritime forces ultimately prompted the pirates to abandon the Glamor. The ATALANTA Maritime Security Centre – Indian Ocean (MSCIO) subsequently issued security alerts containing relevant information and guidance, enabling vessels operating in the area to take appropriate protective measures in accordance with the Best Management Practices (BMP) for maritime security. Later that day, updated information provided by the vessel’s Company Security Officer confirmed that the incident had been resolved and that all crew members were safe and well. The incident marks the seventh reported piracy case since April 2026, with more than 100 seafarers reportedly having been held captive in connection with piracy incidents during this period. Following the emergence of the latest piracy incidents, ATALANTA’s Maritime Security Centre – Indian Ocean has issued multiple warning alerts to vessels operating in the vicinity, urging crews to maintain heightened vigilance, follow the recommendations set out in the Best Management Practices for Maritime Security, and immediately report any suspicious activity or relevant information to MSCIO and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

https://safety4sea.com/philippine-ferry-.text: Authorities continued recovery operations and the investigation aboard the MV June Aster in Coron, Palawan on 14 September, as teams worked to search the vessel and recover evidence linked to the incident. A s stated on the latest updates from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), the death toll from Philippine ferry fire aboard the MV June Aster has risen to 76, as 41 more bodies have been recovered, with 13 people still missing. The fire engulfed the ferry’s lower decks on evening, just 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) from its destination. Rescuers pulled 43 survivors from the water that night. Furthermore, according to Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab, response teams have completed searches of the vessel’s bridge, crew accommodation areas, economy passenger accommodation and air-conditioned passenger accommodation. “These areas have been 100% penetrated by our response teams. A secondary sweep will be conducted to ensure the recovery of any remaining evidence and other materials relevant to the ongoing investigation,” Cayabyab said. Meanwhile, approximately 65% of the vessel’s cargo hold has been accessed, with operations continuing in the remaining sections. Authorities have also been carrying out water-siphoning operations in the vessel’s engine room since 12 September. The oily water mixture removed from the engine room has so far been transferred into 13 drums for proper handling and disposal.

https://safety4sea.com/mexicos-huachicol.text: P&I Services Mexico has issued an urgent advisory warning of heightened regulatory and law-enforcement risks for chemical and tanker vessels carrying hydrocarbon cargoes to Mexican ports. T he advisory warns that vessels calling at Mexican ports are facing increased inspections, cargo sampling and documentation checks as authorities step up efforts to combat fuel-tax evasion and the illegal trafficking and smuggling of fuel, known locally as “huachicol”. Mexico’s National Customs Agency (ANAM) is now operating under intensified federal directives targeting the illicit fuel trade. As part of the crackdown, customs authorities have significantly increased scrutiny of hydrocarbon and chemical products discharged from vessels, with greater emphasis on physical inspections, cargo sampling and verification of supporting documentation. The heightened enforcement environment means that even relatively minor discrepancies could expose vessels and their operators to significant delays and legal complications. According to P&I Services Mexico, the heightened enforcement measures have also increased the risk of prolonged vessel detentions. Where customs officials identify discrepancies—even relatively minor ones—between the cargo declared in the documentation and the actual physical or chemical characteristics of the shipment, or detect documentation errors, the matter may be referred to Mexico’s Federal Attorney General’s Office (Fiscalía General de la República – FGR).

https://safety4sea.com/first-operational.text: The 5,500 m³ liquefied gas carrier Shenghang Yongle has been converted into a ship-to-ship liquid ammonia bunkering vessel, becoming the world’s first operational ammonia bunker vessel , according to FKAB Marine Design. T he conversion was led by Jiangsu Andefu Energy Development, with FKAB and cargo handling supplier Gloryholder providing the technical drawing documentation. The vessel has also received what FKAB described as the first ammonia bunkering class certificate from China Classification Society. Originally designed as a semi-refrigerated and semi-pressurized liquefied gas carrier, Shenghang Yongle can both transport liquid ammonia and deliver it as a marine fuel through ship-to-ship bunkering. The vessel was designed by FKAB, built by China Merchants Shipbuilding Industry Dingheng shipyard and is managed by Shenghang Shipping. The vessel is capable of carrying several liquefied gases, including ammonia, LPG and vinyl chloride monomer. Its cargo tanks have a minimum design temperature of -48°C and it is equipped with two low-temperature reliquefaction systems, providing the technical foundation for the bunkering conversion. As informed, the conversion included modifications to the bunkering system, operating procedures, risk assessments and safety and emergency-response arrangements. Particular consideration was given to ammonia-related risks, including toxicity, material compatibility, low-temperature operations and leak detection.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-analysis-china.text: The arrival of a Sea Legend containership in the UK via the Northern Sea Route marks another step towards scheduled Arctic container shipping, although safety, environmental, infrastructure and geopolitical constraints continue to limit the route’s wider potential. C hina-Europe container shipping through the Arctic is moving beyond isolated trial voyages, as Chinese carrier Sea Legend seeks to establish a regular seasonal service along Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR). The 1,740-TEU Dubai Tower arrived at Teesport in northeast England on September 9, following a voyage from China through the Russian Arctic. The vessel departed Ningbo-Zhoushan on August 15, subsequently calling at Shanghai, Taicang and Qingdao before leaving China on August 19 for the Northern Sea Route. It carried approximately 1,370 TEU, including energy-storage equipment, batteries and other manufactured goods. The voyage is the first of eight sailings planned by Sea Legend during the 2026 Arctic navigation season and represents a notable step in efforts to move Arctic container shipping from individual demonstration voyages towards a more structured seasonal service. Sea Legend has scheduled eight sailings between China and northern Europe between August and October under its China-Europe Arctic Express (CAX). According to the carrier’s published schedule, seven small and medium-sized containerships are being deployed, with weekly departures originally planned from Ningbo. Cargo can also be consolidated from several other Chinese ports, while European coverage has included the UK, Rotterdam, Hamburg, Wilhelmshaven and Gdynia.

https://safety4sea.com/saudi-pipeline-sh.text: Saudi Arabia has shut its 1,200-km East-West oil pipeline following drone strikes, removing a key alternative route for crude exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted. T he pipeline, which transports crude from oil fields in eastern Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, was attacked on September 11 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. Saudi Arabia said the drones were launched from Iraq, while Baghdad has opened an investigation and condemned the attack. The pipeline had become particularly important during the disruption of Hormuz traffic, providing Saudi Arabia with a means of moving crude to the Red Sea without passing through the strait. It has been transporting around 4 million barrels per day in recent months, equivalent to roughly 4% of global oil supply. According to Reuters, Saudi stocks at Yanbu could support exports for only around five to seven days if the pipeline remains offline. A prolonged outage could therefore place up to 4% of global oil supply at risk, although the actual impact will depend on the duration of the disruption and Saudi Arabia’s ability to use alternative routes and inventories. The pipeline shutdown comes as Saudi Arabia is also facing increasing security risks around the Red Sea. Iran-aligned Houthi forces have captured the Red Sea port of Mokha and the strategic Mayun Island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait , raising further concerns over the security of another route that has been used to bypass Hormuz. The development effectively puts additional pressure on a shipping network already affected by disruptions at both ends of the Arabian Peninsula. Reuters reported that only seven vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on September 9 , while 28 commodity vessels moved through the Bab el-Mandeb during the same period.

https://safety4sea.com/worlds-largest-ba.text: The world’s largest battery-electric ferry , China Zorrilla , has arrived in the Río de la Plata, with operator Buquebus welcoming the vessel to Nueva Palmira, Uruguay. B uquebus said authorities, public and private institutions, strategic partners and media representatives from Argentina, Uruguay and other countries gathered in Nueva Palmira to mark the vessel’s arrival. The China Zorrilla was built by Australian shipbuilder Incat for Buquebus and is designed to operate as a fully battery-electric ferry. The vessel measures 130 meters and is powered by a large battery-electric propulsion system. Among those attending were Uruguay’s Secretary of the Presidency Alejandro Sánchez, Minister of Industry, Energy and Mining Fernanda Cardona, Minister of Environment Edgardo Ortuño, Minister of Tourism Pablo Menoni and Colonia Mayor Guillermo Rodríguez. Representatives of the National Ports Administration, the Uruguayan Navy and other public and private organizations also attended, alongside Robert Clifford, founder and chairman of Incat Group. Its arrival in the Río de la Plata follows its transoceanic transportation aboard the heavy-lift vessel Black Marlin . The ferry is expected to serve Buquebus’ connection between Buenos Aires, Argentina, and Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay. Buquebus described the arrival as the result of a major international effort involving companies, institutions and partners from multiple countries.

https://safety4sea.com/te-warns-eu-ets-r.text: Transport & Environment (T&E) says the European Commission’s proposed 2026 review of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) would expand coverage of smaller ships but could leave significant shipping emissions outside the carbon market. T he proposal would extend the EU ETS to ships between 400 and 5,000 GT from 2031, following their inclusion in the monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) system from 2029. T&E described the expansion as an encouraging first step, but warned that around one-third of emissions from small ships would remain uncovered, including emissions from some highly electrifiable vessel types such as ferries. The organization also criticized the proposed timeline, noting that some small-ship categories, including general cargo and offshore ships, have already been reporting under MRV since 2025. The Commission proposal would extend current exemptions and derogations to 2035. These cover ice-class ships, outermost regions, small islands and services linking Cyprus with Greece. According to T&E, extending these exemptions could result in a revenue loss of €3.5 billion between 2030 and 2035. The Commission is also considering extending the ice-class exemption beyond 2035. The proposal also introduces a new derogation for containerships of 10,000 TEU and above, allowing shipping companies to surrender fewer allowances on certain voyages exceeding 300 nautical miles (555 km) until 2035.

https://safety4sea.com/iacs-new-paris-mo.text: IACS has raised concerns over the Paris MoU’s forthcoming methodology for assessing Recognized Organization performance, warning that the new approach may not accurately reflect an RO’s actual involvement in deficiencies and could have unintended consequences for ships’ PSC risk profiles. T he Paris Memorandum of Understanding (Paris MoU) is set to overhaul the way the performance of Recognized Organisations (ROs) is assessed, with a new methodology coming into force on 6 July 2027. The new system will introduce a fundamental change in how responsibility for detainable deficiencies is assigned. Rather than determining whether an RO caused, contributed to, or could reasonably have prevented a deficiency, the methodology will link the deficiency directly to the RO that issued the relevant statutory certificate. Under the new deterministic approach, the statutory certificate associated with a detainable deficiency will become the key factor in determining which RO is held accountable. Under the new methodology, RO performance will be assessed using a formula based on inspection and detention records over a three-year period, the same as that used for Flag State Administrations, which focuses on the number of inspections and detentions. Performance will be categorised as follows: All recognised organisations (ROs) will be included in the performance lists, regardless of the number of inspections they undergo. The aim is to ensure that each RO can be categorised and that the resulting classification can be used to establish a Ship Risk Profile for targeting vessels for inspection.

https://splash247.com/middle-east-shippi.text: Middle Eastern shipping patterns face another violent reshuffle after fresh vessel attacks around Hormuz, the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline and the Houthis’ advance into the heart of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Two more commercial vessels were attacked on Sunday. The Panama-flagged 47,999 dwt product tanker El Gaia was struck off Oman, leaving one Indian seafarer missing. India said 13 other Indian crewmembers had been rescued. The 2005-built tanker had recently sailed from Sohar and is managed by UAE-based Elsey Ship Management. Separately, an unnamed Iranian containership was hit by a projectile near Qeshm and Hengam islands. Iranian authorities reported one fatality and several injuries. Tehran blamed a “terrorist enemy”, while there was no immediate confirmation of responsibility from Washington. Compounding the disruption, Saudi Arabia shut its 1,200 km East-West pipeline on Friday after a drone attack damaged a pumping station. The route has become Riyadh’s essential escape valve during the six-month Hormuz crisis, moving around 4m barrels per day across the kingdom to Yanbu on the Red Sea — roughly 4% of global oil supply. Industry sources estimate Yanbu has enough crude stocks to maintain exports for only another five to seven days. Repair estimates range from considerably sooner to as long as five or six weeks. TankerTrackers.com noted on Sunday that satellite imagery already showed a new bypass pipeline being assembled south of the damaged pumping station, suggesting Saudi authorities are racing to restore flows.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/saudi-oi.text: Saudi Arabia has shut down its East-West pipeline, after the vital oil conduit came under aerial attack in the widening Middle East war, threatening to send energy prices even higher. The world’s largest crude oil exporter said it temporarily closed the pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that both Baghdad and Riyadh said had originated in Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate. Iraq dismissed a military commander on Saturday in response to the attack. The 1,200-km (745-mile) pipeline running across the Arabian Peninsula has served as the main route out for global supplies of Middle East oil for the past six months while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by war. It has been moving 4 million to 5 million barrels per day, amounting to 4% to 5% of global supply, sparing Saudi Arabia the brunt of the disruption that has crippled other Gulf oil and gas exporters. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strikes. Satellite images showed black smoke rising from an area of the pipeline south of Medina. The attack resulted in some injuries and damage that was being assessed, the Saudi Foreign Ministry said without detailing the impact on exports. U.S. President Donald Trump, visiting Ireland to attend a golf tournament at one of his resorts, said Iran was probably to blame. On Saturday, the Saudi Civil Defence said in a statement that a projectile fired by the Houthis had injured two people in Jazan region, along with damaging several buildings, including a mosque.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/lng.text: The LNG market showed signs of improvement this week, with increased chartering activity and stronger sentiment supporting spot rates across both basins. While vessel availability remains elevated, emerging October requirements and renewed interest in multi-month coverage helped improve market confidence. On the BLNG1 Australia–Japan route, rates increased by $5,300 week-on-week to settle at $26,000/day. The Pacific market strengthened steadily through the week as cargo demand improved and sentiment turned slightly more positive. The BLNG2 US Gulf–Continent route rose by $2,100 to close at $19,100/day. While Atlantic fundamentals remain challenging, increased enquiry and firmer sentiment provided support, allowing rates to recover modestly from recent lows. Similarly, the BLNG3 US Gulf–Japan route gained $8,200 week-on-week to settle at $37,600/day. The route posted the strongest increase of the three assessments, supported by a tighter tonnage list to the backend of the window. In the time charter market, sentiment grew softer. The six-month rate fell by $8,500 to $47,500/day, while the one-year term declined by $2,000 to $52,500/day. Further out the curve, the three-year period eased by $450 to $72,000/day. The LPG market was relatively quiet this week, with many participants focused on industry events. Only one fixture was reported that limited price discovery. Rising tensions in the Middle East remain a key watchpoint and could influence sentiment and freight rates in the weeks ahead.

https://splash247.com/russia-turns-to-sh.text: Russia is stacking shipping containers around oil refineries in the latest improvised attempt to protect an energy system that has been battered by increasingly effective Ukrainian drone attacks. Images carried by Dnipro Osint from the Novoshakhtinsk refinery show containers piled several levels high around tanks and processing equipment, creating walls intended to provide some protection from low-flying drones and flying debris. Russian facilities have also experimented with anti-drone netting and metal frames, although anything exposed from above remains vulnerable and the effectiveness of the container walls has yet to be demonstrated. The increasingly rudimentary defences illustrate the scale of the problem Moscow now faces. Ukrainian drones attacked Russian refineries at least 21 times in August alone, the highest monthly total since the full-scale invasion began. Russian refining runs fell to around 3.8m barrels per day, according to EA Analytics, compared with typical summer processing of 5.3m-5.5m bpd — effectively removing around 30% of normal refining output. Gasoline production fell almost 20% and diesel output more than 23%. The disruption has turned one of the world’s major fuel exporters into an increasingly significant importer. Russia imported 172,000 tonnes of oil products in August, more than seven times the previous monthly high since the invasion and around three times its total imports for all of 2025, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. India supplied 70% of those imports and 94% of Russia’s imported gasoline, much of it coming from the Rosneft-linked Vadinar refinery after processing Russian crude.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fulkrum-.text: Fulkrum, a London-headquartered technical services company providing inspection, expediting, auditing and technical staffing solutions to energy and industrial projects, has landed an inspection services contract with Vår Energi, an independent oil and gas operator on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS). This deal expands the UK firm’s offshore footprint in Norway and enables it to provide inspection and testing support across three subsea developments in the Gjøa area. Fulkrum has secured what it describes as a major inspection services contract across Vår Energi’s project portfolio, supporting quality assurance, operational integrity, and efficient project execution. As part of this framework agreement, the London-based company is currently supporting three subsea developments within the Gjøa area: Ophelia , Gjøa Nord , and Cerisa , providing inspection and testing of equipment and systems both offshore and on-site at the testing facilities. Vår Energi on portfolio reshaping spree: $460M acquisitions, swaps and divestments Fulkrum’s technical expertise will support the Norwegian operator’s commitment to safety through its ongoing investment and initiatives, including hazard identification and risk assessment, legal and regulatory compliance, and continual improvement. The company emphasizes that Vår Energi is one of the largest exporters of gas to Europe from Norway, with equity stakes in half of the producing assets on the NCS and around 1,450 employees. James Dunsford , Senior Key Account Manager at Fulkrum, commented: “This award represents an important step in further establishing Fulkrum’s position within the Norwegian offshore market. Our subsea inspection teams bring extensive technical expertise, operational flexibility, and a strong commitment to quality and safety, enabling us to support critical offshore developments with confidence.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/baker-hu.text: U.S.-headquartered energy technology giant Baker Hughes and Venture Global, an American producer of liquefied natural gas (LNG) sourced from North American basins, are deepening their partnership as the LNG developer moves forward with the next stage of a major U.S. LNG infrastructure buildout. Baker Hughes has secured a substantial order to supply gas compression systems for the Cloud Connector Pipeline project in Louisiana and a major order for a modular liquefaction solution, including cold boxes to support the Plaquemines LNG facility expansion. These awards expand the U.S. firm’s long-standing collaboration with Venture Global to advance critical U.S. gas infrastructure, demonstrating the critical role of integrated natural gas infrastructure in expanding LNG supply and enhancing energy security for global markets. The pipeline deal, which includes 13 gas compression systems driven by Frame 5/2E gas turbines, is said to represent one of the largest deployments for LNG feed gas transportation in the United States, enabling reliable and efficient transportation of feed gas through the Cloud Connector Pipeline to Venture Global’s Plaquemines facility. The Cloud Connector award is the second order of Frame 5/2E gas turbine-driven centrifugal compressor packages for the U.S. LNG developer’s feed gas pipeline, expanding the fleet to 23 Frame 5/2E-driven gas compression systems for the Plaquemines LNG facility. The award supports more than 100 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of existing and planned LNG production capacity. Venture Global’s first three projects, Calcasieu Pass , Plaquemines LNG, and CP2 LNG , are located in Louisiana along the Gulf of America (U.S. Gulf of Mexico).

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Liner shipping sells predictability. Published schedules, fixed rotations, guaranteed port calls—these are the commercial promises that drive shipper decisions. When chokepoint disruptions force carriers to reroute entire service strings, those promises collide with operational reality. The contract is supposed to resolve that collision. Too often, it does not. In a previous article , “When Geography Breaks the Contract,” we examined how chokepoint disruptions—from the Red Sea to the Strait of Hormuz to the Panama Canal—expose fundamental gaps in shipping contracts built on the assumption of geographic stability. That analysis applied broadly across the logistics chain. This article narrows the lens to liner shipping, where the consequences of rerouting are both more acute and more structurally complex. Liner services are network businesses. A single vessel does not operate in isolation. It runs a fixed rotation—a published sequence of port calls repeated on a cycle. When a chokepoint disruption forces rerouting, the impact is not confined to a single voyage. It cascades across an entire service string, affecting every subsequent port call, every transshipment connection, and every shipper whose cargo is loaded anywhere on that rotation. This creates a tension that sits at the heart of liner operations. Carriers need the flexibility to manage their networks in real time—to omit ports, blank sailings, and adjust rotations to preserve the broader schedule. Shippers need predictability—they selected this carrier, on this service, because the published transit time and port sequence matched their supply chain requirements. The question is whether the contractual framework governing liner shipping adequately addresses this tension. In most cases, it does not. In liner shipping, the schedule is the product. Shippers do not typically charter a vessel. They buy space on a service. The decision to book with Carrier A instead of Carrier B is driven by transit time, port coverage, frequency, and connection reliability. All of these derive from the published schedule.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: The Omanis have cancelled a regional conference which they had called for Monday in Salalah, to which all GCC members plus Iraq had been invited. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the Fars News Agency that the business of the meeting in Oman was to have been the joint presentation of a new maritime transit corridor in the Strait of Hormuz, over which Oman and Iran have come to a draft agreement. Oman and Iran have been negotiating for months to try and reconcile differences over future arrangements for navigation in the Strait. Oman insisted that it wished to retain freedom of navigation and the right of innocent passage, as found in the IMO-endorsed arrangement that has been in place since 1968. Iran has been holding out to charge passage fees and to have the right to vet the traffic using the Strait. In the run-up to the conference, Omani leader Sultan Haitham bin Tariq and Oman’s Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Al Busaidi have been keeping fellow GCC members up to date with progress, and also expressed confidence privately that the proposals met with approval from the United States. Separate from the technical arrangements within the Strait itself, Iran is reported to have laid down seven pre-conditions which the United States would have been required to meet before the agreement could come into force, based around its interpretation of the terms of the June 17 US-Iranian Memorandum of Understanding. Most of the concerns that the other GCC states might have about the new arrangements are likely to have been covered by these pre-condition requirements, rather than the technical content of the deal which Oman has hammered out with Iran over navigation in the Strait. Bahrain is known to have refused to attend if Iran’s representatives would be there, since Iran has attacked it with ballistic missiles and drones. Bahrain normally aligns its foreign policy closely with that of Saudi Arabia, and Riyadh is believed to have objected to some of the technical arrangements proposed for the new Strait transit plan. The UAE has not announced that it has refused to attend, but could be expected to have a similar, more robust version of Bahrain’s viewpoint. A well-connected Emirati social media blogger, probably reflecting the official view, chose this particular moment to obliquely criticize Oman’s “never stop negotiating philosophy.” The commentator suggested that diplomacy in foreign policy needed to be matched by deterrence, involving judgement when firmness and robustness in defense of sovereignty and national interest was necessary. If nothing else, the postponement of the conference has revealed the split between the interests of the United States, which seeks to end the war just with some restitution of controls over Iran’s nuclear weapons capabi

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: The Houthis appear to have overextended themselves in their rapid advance in SW Yemen, which saw them capture the Ras Menhali peninsula and Perim Island just offshore in the Bab el-Mandeb. The Houthis were able to advance so quickly down the coastal strip and the Tihama plain for evidently two reasons. They had good intelligence on the disunity within the forces of the Internationally Recognized Government (IRG), which they were able to exploit. It is now apparent that the unity within the IRG had not improved to the extent portrayed, and the Houthis were able to exploit divisions between the semi-autonomous force components, which the IRG had not welded into a sufficiently combined force. The Houthis were also able to exploit the lack of any meaningful threat from the air as they advanced across the open country of the Tihama plain. Battle still fluid, latest indications of positions held in SW Yemen, as of September 14 (Google Earth/CJRC) The balance of advantage is now shifting, and the Houthi force in the newly occupied areas – mostly light infantry - is exposed. It is dangerously dependent on a single supply line to the north, the N2 coastal highway, which is straight, flat, and completely exposed. Houthi movements on the N2 are now being attacked from the air, with civilians having been warned that any movement on the road will be considered to be a legitimate military target. The air attacks are supposedly being carried out by the IRG, although the Yemeni Air Force of late has been presumed to be moribund. Most probably the Royal Saudi Air Force has now become engaged, heavily so, and a large-scale Houthi missile attack on the Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushayt on the morning of September 13 was presumably designed to inhibit such attacks. Being a largely pick-up and motor bike mounted light infantry force, the Houthis in the area are also now exposed to the much better equipped forces of the IRG moving up from Lahj, the neighboring province, where units are still in good order. Southern Giants Forces, displaying the flags of the erstwhile South Yemen, have been seen in coverage of attacks being mounted on the road towards Dhubab, and there have noticeably been no indication of a continuing Houthi presence on Perim or at the Ras Menhali port across the water. Traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb is continuing, but appears to be somewhat reduced based on AIS feeds visible early on September 14 ( VesselFinder )

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Two of the commercial ships hijacked by Somali pirates were recently freed, while four other small tankers remain under the control of the pirates. The situation continues in what is now reported to be the most active period of pirate activity off the Horn of Africa since 2013. The EU monitoring and security operation EU NAVFOR Atalanta reports that a show of force was able to scare off one pirate group that had boarded a bulker off the coast of Yemen last Thursday, September 10. The Glamor (24,000 dwt), a Greek-owned bulker registered in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, was targeted while approximately 98 nautical miles southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen. The vessel appears to have been operating in and out of Djibouti, and the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean (MSCIO) later reported the vessel had been boarded by a pirate action group approximately 38 nautical miles southwest of Balhaf, Yemen. Atalanta reports that the crew of the bulker was able to stop the vessel and shut down all of its systems as they were being overtaken by the pirate group. They fled into the vessel’s citadel before six armed pirates got aboard the vessel. The EU operation redirected naval forces when it was advised of the incident, and it reports a Japanese reconnaissance aircraft carried out show of force flights over the bulker. The Indian Navy, according to additional reports, also sent one of its vessels patrolling the Indian Ocean to the aid of the bulker. Atalanta speculates that the pirates, seeing that international forces were responding, and with the crew locked in a safe area, decided to flee the vessel. The company’s security officer later confirmed to Atalanta that the vessel and its crew were safe and the incident had been resolved. The assault on the Glamor was the 25th incident reported to Atalanta since the start of 2026. It said that it was still monitoring the other vessels that had been boarded and were being held by pirate groups. One of those vessels, the small cargo ship Sward (8,500 dwt), was released on September 11 after 138 days in captivity. The French news agency AFP (Agence France-Presse) confirmed the release, saying that an undisclosed amount of ransom had been paid. The cargo ship, which is registered in St. Kitts and Nevis, was carrying a cargo of fertilizer bound for Mombasa, Kenya, when it was boarded on April 26. It has a crew of 17, made up of 15 Syrians and two Indians.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The police and narcotics units from Turkey’s Ministry of Justice reported a major cocaine seizure recovered by divers examining a sea chest on a bulker docked in the port of Mersin. The port is increasingly becoming a center for drug smuggling, while reports also show that smugglers are increasingly using sea chests to conceal narcotic smuggling. The Mersin Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office and the police reported they were acting on intelligence that a large quantity of narcotics was coming from South America to the port. They were searching vessels coming from South America docked at the port when the divers located the shipment concealed in the sea chest of a bulker docked in Mersin. Justice Minister Akin Gurley told the media that the vessel was the CSPC Pisces (84,500 dwt). Records indicate that the Chinese-owned bulker, which is registered in Liberia, had departed Brazil and made a stop in Tarragona, Spain, before reaching Turkey on September 11. The divers recovered 12 large packages from the sea chest with approximately 350 kg of cocaine. The authorities estimated the value at nearly $31 million. They also recovered diving equipment and an underwater sea scooter. Nine people were taken into custody during the investigation believed to have been aiding in the smuggling. https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Philippine Coast Guard has completed its search of all passenger spaces aboard the burned-out ro/ro ferry June Aster, which caught fire off Palawan last Wednesday and subsequently ran aground. PCG responders have now fully searched the bridge, crew accommodation, economy passenger berthing and air-conditioned passenger accommodation areas, and are about two-thirds of the way through the cargo decks. So far, a total of 76 bodies have been recovered. Escaping passengers awaking to the smoke and fire would have encountered rows of densely-packed, double-height bunk racks on the top deck and interior, photos provided by the PCG show. "These areas have been 100% penetrated by our response teams. A secondary sweep will be conducted to ensure the recovery of any remaining evidence and other materials relevant to the ongoing investigation," PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said in a statement. A body (blurred, left) is visible in this image of June Aster's passenger berthing. Upright pillars show signs of deformation from the fire (PCG) The PCG has issued a letter of demand to the shipowner with instructions to appoint a qualified salvor in short order. The ship is aground, its hull integrity is in unknown condition, and it is taking on small amounts of water in the engine room. The PCG has been dewatering oily waste out of the compartment and storing it in containers, but it wants to conduct the ordinary transfer of responsibility for pollution-abatement and salvage to a qualified private contractor. Damage to the vessel is extensive, and its structural integrity would need to be evaluated. Photos of the interior show that the fire swept through the car deck with intensity, burning off paint and leaving only steel and charred debris behind. Videos obtained by first responders on the night of the fire showed sections of the hull heated to such an intensity that areas glowed dully red, indicating steel temperatures in excess of 1,300 degrees Fahrenheit - consistent with the combustion temperature of burning cars. Steel heated to that temperature can warp and deform; depending upon the circumstances , key physical properties may also be altered by the heating and cooling process, according to DNV, creating an additional factor for salvage planning.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Iran’s so-called Persian Gulf Strait Authority released its second update to its blacklist of shipping while also expanding its past threats to include insurance companies, P&I, and class societies. There’s little evidence that the shipping industry is following these edicts, but confirmed traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains at low levels, more likely due to the persistent attacks. The group, which asserts that it controls transits of the Strait, published online its updated list of ships, which it calls “non-compliant.” It includes the obvious targets, such as vessels operated by Saudi Arabia’s Bahri and the Kuwait Oil Tanker Company. Mostly it focuses on crude oil tankers, but ranges to include LPG, LNG, product tankers, and even bulkers. The list, which started out with 45 vessels at the end of August, has now been increased to 77 vessels identified by name and IMO registration number. The latest iteration adds 21 vessels. In the past, they asserted that some of the information was “voluntarily submitted by the public.” It has also included the tankers that were being used for shuttle operations and ship-to-ship transfers outside the Persian Gulf. It has warned shipowners and operators not to be involved with any of the listed vessels. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority has threatened fines, detention, or confiscation if they attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz. The latest pronouncement, however, expands the threats. “Insurance companies, P&I clubs, and classification societies are warned to refrain from providing services to these vessels to avoid consequences arising from dealing with them,” the group writes without saying what it might do to violators. Tracking data shows, however, that vessel transits of the Strait of Hormuz have been “well below the 10-day average,” reports Reuters, citing preliminary tracking data. It reports that over the weekend, transits fell to “a single digit per day,” this weekend saying that only one LPG carrier and one laden Supermax tanker exited on Saturday and Sunday.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: The salvage team working to remove the wreck of the containership MSC Baltic III from the shore of Newfoundland, Canada, captured in a dramatic video as the bow section was separated from the hull. It is the first section of the hull to be broken apart after the work had stripped away the upper portions of the vessel. The containership was 207 meters (679 feet) in length before the dismantling operation began. There was no indication from the Canadian Coast Guard of how long the section that was severed was, but they reported that 5,700 tonnes, close to 50 percent of the vessel’s total tonnage, have now been removed. The salvage operation in 2025 focused on removing the cargo, fuel, and potential pollutants from the vessel. The second phase of salvage, focusing on removing the ship, began this spring. https://www.oedigital.com/news/542917-ke.text: KERSHIP, a joint venture between PIRIOU and Naval Group, launched the PETAR NJEGOS I, the first of two OPV 60M offshore patrol vessels ordered by Montenegro, at its Lanester shipyard on Friday, September 11, 2026. The construction of the vessels brings together the expertise of KERSHIP and PIRIOU, as well as Naval Group's expertise in combat systems and equipment. Throughout the program, a team from the Montenegrin Navy, supported by the DGA, is monitoring the construction alongside the French industrial teams, ensuring that the vessels fully meet the operational requirements of the Montenegrin Navy.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542913-pe.text: Mexico’s state-run oil firm Pemex has begun repairing an offshore pipeline after a crude oil release about 46 nautical miles off Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche, with the pipeline isolated and no further oil being released. Personnel at the Cantarell Production Asset detected a pressure drop on September 10 in a pipeline collecting hydrocarbons from the Ek-TA, Balam-TA, Balam-A, Balam-TB and Balam-TA2 platforms. The pipeline was depressurized and isolated by closing safety valves at both ends and has since remained without flow or further crude oil releases. Specialized vessels were deployed to the site on the same day for mechanical dispersion and placement of oleophilic containment booms, while divers located the point where containment had been lost and began repair work. Pemex has completed dredging of the seabed and is removing the pipeline's concrete ballast while preparing a metal sleeve that will cover the affected section. Repairs are expected to be completed in the coming days. Vessels equipped for containment, hydrocarbon recovery and mechanical dispersion remain in the area as a precaution.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O estado de São Paulo lidera os investimentos em infraestrutura no Brasil , concentrando R$ 493,7 bilhões em investimentos previstos em infraestrutura de transporte e logística , de acordo com informações da Confederação Nacional do Transporte (CNT). O valor corresponde a 23% da carteira nacional mapeada pela entidade na sétima edição do Plano CNT de Transporte e Logística, reunindo investimentos distribuídos entre intervenções rodoviárias, ferroviárias, metroferroviárias, portuárias, hidroviárias, aeroportuárias e terminais. O estado de Minas Gerais está em segundo lugar, com R$ 289,3 bilhões (13,6% da carteira nacional) em investimentos para infraestrutura logística, seguido pelo Paraná , com R$ 146,4 bilhões (6,9%). O estado do Pará ocupa o quarto lugar, com R$ 137,3 bilhões (6,5%), enquanto o Rio Grande do Sul está na quinta posição, com R$ 125,8 bilhões (5,9%). Desde 2023, São Paulo reforçou investimentos públicos, concessões e parcerias com a iniciativa privada para ampliar e modernizar a infraestrutura paulista. Programas como o São Paulo pra Toda Obra e o SP nos Trilhos , do governo estadual, reúnem obras em execução, projetos contratados e novos empreendimentos de transporte, ao lado de concessões rodoviárias e ferroviárias. A CNT cita 87 projetos de integração nacional e 41 projetos urbanos no estado, distribuídos entre os diferentes modais. O mapeamento inclui projetos em desenvolvimento e novas intervenções. O São Paulo Pra Toda Obra registrou em seu primeiro ano R$ 144,6 bilhões em investimentos públicos e privados . O projeto abrange 61,8 mil quilômetros de rodovias , o equivalente a uma volta e meia na Terra. Ao longo de um ano, o total de intervenções alcançou 4.300 obras públicas e privadas. O programa abrange projetos até 2055, consolidando ações estratégicas de política pública de longo prazo voltadas à modernização da infraestrutura e ao desenvolvimento do Estado. O programa reúne obras de recuperação, pavimentação, duplicação, construção de novos trechos, melhorias de interseções e outras intervenções destinadas à modernização da malha.

Empresas podem esperar consumidores mais exigentes na Black Friday de 2026. A 6ª edição do estudo de Black Friday conduzido pela Gauge, Ecglobal e W3haus, empresas da Stefanini Marketing, aponta que 56% dos consumidores começam a comparar ofertas com mais de 30 dias de antecedência , e 62% dizem identificar facilmente quais promoções são boas . O novo cliente, experiente em pesquisar preços e com a régua pronta para identificar oportunidades, também sente quando a logística não acompanha seu nível de exigência. O frete caro é o principal fator que trava a compra para 47% dos consumidores , à frente de juros altos, para 39% e falta de dinheiro, para 36%. A taxa de desistência chega a 29% quando o consumidor não encontra opção de frete grátis . Esse fator já aparecia em 2025 como o segundo maior gatilho de conversão, e os números atuais mostram que mostrando que a opção de frete gratuito deixou de ser um detalhe operacional e passou a ser uma exigência. De acordo com a pesquisa, a análise do cliente não vai só até a decisão de compra. Fatores ligados ao frete podem levar ao abandono do carrinho na fase de checkout, após a decisão de compra. Mudança de preço no checkout lidera os motivos de abandono de carrinho, com 53% das menções. Prazo de entrega longo aparece em segundo, com 35%, alta de 6 pontos percentuais em relação a 2025. Indisponibilidade de produtos na região do comprador fecha o top três, com 33%, também 3 pontos acima do ano anterior. Para Guilherme Stefanini, CMO Global do Grupo Stefanini e CEO da Stefanini Marketing , a Black Friday deste ano vai encontrar consumidores mais exigentes e cautelosos com ofertas. "O consumidor de 2026 não quer apenas uma promessa de bom preço. Quer evidências de que a oferta é real e de que o que foi prometido vai ser entregue. Para as marcas, conquistar essa confiança pode valer mais do que uma venda em novembro: pode transformá-las em referência para as decisões de compra ao longo de todo o ano", afirma.

Campos maduros e áreas de economicidade marginal não são necessariamente campos sem petróleo. O desafio, além de maior eficiência operacional, é transformar essa percepção em política permanente de recuperação do barril que ainda pode ser produzido O Brasil tem discutido intensamente novas fronteiras exploratórias, grandes descobertas e projetos de elevada escala. Essa agenda é fundamental. Mas existe uma oportunidade menos evidente e potencialmente tão estratégica quanto a abertura de novas fronteiras; produzir melhor o petróleo e o gás que já conhecemos e que permanecem no subsolo de campos maduros e de menor porte. Esse pode ser um dos maiores “barris perdidos” da indústria brasileira de petróleo e gás. Campos maduros e áreas de economicidade marginal não são necessariamente campos sem petróleo. São ativos que entram em uma fase mais complexa de produção: a pressão do reservatório diminui, a produção declina, os custos operacionais aumentam e cada barril adicional exige mais conhecimento, tecnologia, investimento e eficiência. Em muitos casos, ainda há petróleo e gás recuperáveis. O desafio é transformar esse potencial geológico em produção economicamente viável. O desafio é também transformar essa percepção em uma política permanente de recuperação do barril que ainda pode ser produzido. Quando se fala em aumento da produção, é comum imaginar a necessidade de descobrir novos campos. Em muitos casos, porém, existe uma alternativa mais rápida e eficiente: produzir melhor aquilo que já foi descoberto.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 14/09/2026 – Na semana passada, cerca de 180 estudantes do Curso Técnico em Portos do Instituto Federal do Espírito Santo (Ifes/ES), participaram do projeto ANTAQ na Escola. O encontro de iniciativa da Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) ocorreu no auditório da Ifes, e teve como tema “Modernização dos Portos e os Desafios para a Qualificação de Jovens Profissionais”. Os alunos puderam conhecer diferentes aspectos do setor, incluindo a atuação dos órgãos fiscalizadores, as atividades desenvolvidas pelas Unidades Regionais da ANTAQ e as possibilidades profissionais em áreas como operação portuária, navegação, agenciamento marítimo e despacho aduaneiro. Destaque para a palestra que explicou como são realizadas as atividades de fiscalização e, também, a atuação dos drones como ferramenta de trabalho - tecnologia que amplia a capacidade de acompanhamento de terminais e áreas remotas. O encontro reuniu servidores da ANTAQ, da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa), representantes da Vports, Capitania dos Portos do Espírito Santo, Receita Federal, Polícia Federal, além de profissionais do setor privado e de entidades ligadas às atividades portuárias e marítimas. Criado pela Unidade Regional de Fortaleza (UREFT) da Agência, o ANTAQ na Escola aproxima estudantes de cursos técnicos e profissionais da realidade do setor portuário e logístico brasileiro. No Ceará, o projeto já realizou sete edições. A iniciativa busca apresentar aos jovens as oportunidades de um setor em transformação e a importância da qualificação profissional para acompanhar um ambiente cada vez mais moderno e tecnológico. A edição capixaba foi encerrada na sexta-feira (11), com uma visita técnica de 70 alunos do 3º ano às instalações da Vports, no Porto de Vitória.
