https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Arauco abriu as inscrições para o processo seletivo de seu Programa de Formação de Motoristas , em Chapadão do Sul (MS). Realizada em parceria com o Sest Senat, a iniciativa é gratuita e voltada a homens e mulheres habilitados nas categorias B e C que buscam a mudança para a categoria D . Condutores que já possuem a CNH D, e desejam realizar o treinamento de aperfeiçoamento, também podem participar. Esta nova etapa dá continuidade às ações de desenvolvimento social e qualificação profissional da Arauco no Mato Grosso do Sul, preparando a mão de obra regional para atuar nas operações logísticas da companhia em seu Projeto Sucuriú , em Inocência (MS). O projeto marca a entrada da divisão de celulose da Arauco no Brasil. Durante as obras, a Arauco vai oferecer capacitação e gerar mais de 14 mil oportunidades de trabalho. Depois do start up, o Projeto Sucuriú empregará cerca de 6 mil pessoas nas unidades Industrial, Florestal e operações de logística. "O crescimento do setor florestal em Mato Grosso do Sul exige uma infraestrutura logística robusta e, acima de tudo, profissionais preparados. Levar o Programa de Formação de Motoristas a Chapadão do Sul reforça nosso compromisso de gerar oportunidades na região. Queremos capacitar condutores para atuar com alto desempenho e foco na segurança, na eficiência e no respeito às normas socioambientais que regem nossas operações", afirma Rodrigo Sugske, gerente executivo de Logística Florestal da Arauco . A formação tem carga horária de 107 horas , entre aulas teóricas e práticas, com conteúdo sobre Código de Trânsito Brasileiro, condução defensiva, segurança viária e ética profissional. Para concorrer a uma das vagas, os candidatos devem possuir idade mínima de 21 anos e atender aos requisitos de habilitação para o curso pretendido. Focado na promoção da diversidade e valorização dos talentos locais, o programa oferece suporte completo de aprendizado e concederá uma bolsa-bônus no valor de um salário mínimo aos participantes que concluírem o ciclo de capacitação .

A Aliança do Transporte Sustentável , que reúne as três federações do transporte rodoviário do Estado de São Paulo — FETCESP (cargas), FETPESP (passageiros) e FRESP (passageiros por fretamento) — apresenta o Panorama ESG do Transporte Rodoviário no Estado de São Paulo . O estudo é o primeiro do setor a medir o grau de maturidade das empresas de transporte em práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança (ESG) com o rigor da norma técnica ABNT PR 2030. O trabalho foi desenvolvido e operado tecnicamente pela Easy ESG e conta com o patrocínio da Mercedes-Benz e do Despoluir — Programa Ambiental do Transporte, mantido pela CNT e pelo SEST SENAT. A norma ABNT PR 2030 organiza a agenda ESG em eixos, temas e critérios e classifica a maturidade das organizações em cinco níveis, de Elementar a Transformador. As empresas responderam a um questionário e tiveram as respostas auditadas na plataforma da Aliança. Os resultados são apresentados de forma anônima e agregada, sem identificação de qualquer organização. Entre as empresas de São Paulo com auditoria concluída, o setor apresenta score médio de 24,5% , o que corresponde ao nível Não Integrado : nesse estágio, já existem práticas de sustentabilidade, mas ainda desconectadas da estratégia e da rotina de gestão. Por eixo, o desempenho é relativamente equilibrado: Social (26,2%), Ambiental (25,4%) e Governança (22,0%). O achado mais expressivo do estudo está na amplitude: as notas vão de 5,7% a 71,7%, revelando um setor de "duas velocidades" , em que empresas em estágio inicial convivem com organizações que já operam a agenda ESG de forma estruturada. Na distribuição por nível, a maior parte das empresas se concentra no estágio Não Integrado, o que indica um caminho claro de evolução possível a partir de ações práticas do dia a dia. No comparativo por atividade (CNAE), o segmento de cargas apresenta a maior maturidade média , à frente dos segmentos de passageiros e de fretamento — diferença que ajuda a orientar prioridades e trocas de boas práticas entre os diferentes perfis de operação. A Aliança Transporte Sustentável é uma iniciativa conjunta das três federações do transporte rodoviário do Estado de São Paulo (FETCESP, FETPESP e FRESP), voltada a fortalecer a agenda ESG no setor. "O transporte rodoviário de cargas move a economia do Estado de São Paulo, e essa responsabilidade nos obriga a olhar para o futuro. Medir nosso nível de desenvolvimento, com o rigor de uma norma técnica, é o primeiro passo para transformá-lo em competitividade", comenta Carlos Panzan, presidente da FETCESP .

https://brasilenergia.com.br/petroleoega.text: Os efeitos tradicionais decorrentes de choques nos preços do petróleo passam a afetar a economia brasileira de forma contrária. Tal quadro ficou em evidência com a atual crise do petróleo causada pela guerra entre EUA e Israel versus Irã Ao longo do século XX, a história econômica brasileira orbitou em torno do debate sobre os ciclos de commodities que condicionavam os padrões de crescimento econômico internos. Por diferentes formas e razões, o comportamento dos preços do café na primeira metade do século e do petróleo no último terço do século passado afetaram a política econômica interna de forma constante, impondo uma típica restrição externa característica de economias da América Latina em desenvolvimento. No caso do petróleo, os dois choques dos anos 1970 levaram a uma evasão da dependência dos combustíveis fósseis com o começo da pesquisa do etanol, que se consolidou como alternativa crível nos últimos 15 anos e que, se não logrou sucesso na autonomia em relação aos fósseis, obteve ao menos a redução da dependência daqueles. De fato, após os choques dos anos 1970, a economia brasileira respondia de maneira semelhante a crises no mercado de óleo e gás, a saber, uma apreciação do preço internacional do petróleo em um primeiro momento impunha perdas na conta comercial brasileira já que até então a economia do país era importadora líquida de petróleo. Esse efeito provocava imediata depreciação da moeda local em relação às divisas internacionais, o que por sua vez desencadeava um repasse inflacionário que se somava ao efeito posterior de alta dos preços internos dos combustíveis. Um espiral perverso que ainda reduzia as taxas de crescimento econômico já que a indústria local enfrentava restrição para expansão da oferta, um clássico problema estrutural de crescimento. Esse padrão começa a ser alterado quando a economia brasileira alcança a autossuficiência em petróleo, ainda que haja a dependência ao gás importado boliviano. Com isso, os efeitos tradicionais decorrentes de choques nos preços do petróleo passam a afetar a economia brasileira de forma contrária.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 15/09/2026 - A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) vai reforçar a supervisão sobre a cobrança da chamada taxa de seca, ou Low Water Surcharge (LWS), aplicada por companhias de navegação em períodos de restrição hidrológica na Região Amazônica. A partir da nova sistemática, a instituição da sobretaxa ficará condicionada à homologação regulatória da Agência, com análise individualizada das informações apresentadas por cada empresa. A medida foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União (DOU) desta terça-feira (15). Na prática, o simples comunicado da intenção de cobrança não será suficiente para que a sobretaxa passe a ser aplicada aos usuários. As companhias deverão informar previamente a ANTAQ, com antecedência mínima de 30 dias, e apresentar os elementos técnicos, operacionais e econômicos que sustentem a medida, demonstrando a relação entre as condições dos rios, os impactos sobre a operação, eventuais reduções de capacidade ou custos adicionais e o valor proposto para cobrança. A análise poderá resultar em homologação, homologação com condicionantes ou não homologação. A partir daí, a Agência acompanhará a aplicação da sobretaxa e poderá rever sua decisão diante de novas informações ou de mudanças nas condições hidrológicas, além de avaliar posteriormente se os impactos e custos projetados pelas empresas efetivamente se confirmaram. A sistemática também prevê situações de homologação tácita. Ela poderá ocorrer após o prazo decisório de 30 dias, contado a partir de uma comunicação suficientemente instruída e descontadas eventuais suspensões para diligências, ou antes desse prazo, quando atingido nível hidrológico ou situação operacional reconhecida pela ANTAQ. Para 2026, a referência será a cota oficial do Rio Negro, no Porto de Manaus, igual ou inferior a 17,7 metros. Como regra de transição, serão aproveitadas as comunicações e diligências já realizadas, sem reinício da contagem dos prazos, e haverá cinco dias para eventuais complementações. Cobranças já instituídas e vinculadas ao atingimento da cota de 17,7 metros poderão ter homologação preliminar transitória, sujeita à revisão a qualquer momento pela Superintendência de Regulação (SRG) da Agência. A medida não representa proibição da taxa de seca nem tabelamento de preços. O transporte aquaviário opera sob regime de liberdade na formação dos preços e fretes, mas essa liberdade não afasta a competência da ANTAQ para prevenir práticas abusivas e verificar se cobranças extraordinárias possuem fundamento técnico e econômico compatível com os impactos efetivamente provocados pela estiagem.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/santos-b.text: Australia’s energy player Santos is stepping up its liquefied natural gas (LNG) push in Asia through a long-term supply deal with South Korea’s POSCO and a proposed agreement to buy 1 million tonnes per year (mtpa) from an LNG project being developed on Canada’s northwest coast to export lower-carbon LNG to markets in Asia . Santos has struck two new separate non-binding LNG agreements in accordance with its strategy to maximize revenue through portfolio optimization and will leverage high value, long term contracts, complementing its existing contractual commitments. The firm has agreed key commercial terms with POSCO Steel for a ten-year supply of LNG sourced from the Australian player’s diversified global LNG portfolio on a ‘delivered ex ship’ basis, beginning in 2030 or 2031. Execution of the transaction remains subject to the negotiation and execution of an LNG sale and purchase agreement (SPA), and all required corporate approvals. Santos has also entered into a non-binding heads of agreement with Western LNG for the purchase of approximately 1 million tonnes of LNG per annum from the proposed Ksi Lisims LNG project on a ‘free on board’ basis in Canada’s British Columbia for a term of up to 20 years, starting from approximately 2031. The HOA is non-binding and remains subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, including an LNG sale and purchase agreement, satisfaction of customary conditions precedent, and all required corporate approvals. https://gcaptain.com/oman-says-el-gaia-b.text: The tanker El Gaia sits off Oman with smoke and flames visible near the stern following an onboard fire. Photo: Oman Maritime Security Center Omani authorities said Tuesday that the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia is being towed to port after a fire aboard the vessel was brought under control, while two crew members remain missing. Oman’s Maritime Security Center said the tanker was about 103 nautical miles northeast of Musandam Governorate. A Royal Navy of Oman vessel evacuated 23 crew members and provided medical care. Search operations are continuing for two missing crew. The update adds to conflicting accounts over what happened to the tanker. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said El Gaia struck a naval mine while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command rejected that claim , saying the tanker had instead been attacked by Iran twice — first by a missile last month, which left the ship inoperable, and again by a drone over the weekend while it was sitting off Oman. “The IRGC’s false claim is yet another example of their lies and intimidation attempts while they try to impede commercial vessels in the strait,” CENTCOM said.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/maersk-h.text: Shipping group Maersk said on Monday that four more of its joint container services with Germany's Hapag-Lloyd will resume sailings through the Suez Canal, as they gradually return to using the shortcut between Asia and Europe. The Asia-Europe trade corridor through the Suez Canal was abandoned by most shippers earlier this decade after attacks in the Red Sea by Yemen's Houthis, forcing ships to take the much longer trip around Africa. "The Suez Canal is a vital maritime corridor between East and West and a key driver of efficient global supply chains," Denmark's Maersk said in a statement. "By transitioning the AE5, AE11, AE12 and ME2 services to the trans-Suez corridor instead of sailing around the Cape of Good Hope, we will offer more efficient transit times for customers," it added. The two companies will continue to monitor the situation in the Middle East very closely, and any changes to their services within the Gemini cooperation network will depend on the absence of escalation in conflicts in the region, Maersk said. Maersk and Hapag-Lloydin early July and later again in August announced that they would resume some services connecting Asia, the Mediterranean and Europe through the Suez Canal.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: Benchmark Brent crude price resumed its upward climb on Tuesday after news of a pause in the loading program at Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea loading terminal. The terminal's ability to keep exporting crude was already expected to come to a close: recent attacks on the Saudi Aramco East-West Pipeline have brought cross-country oil movement to a halt until repairs can be completed, and full flow may not be restored for three to five weeks, oil industry sources told AP. Satellite imaging intelligence firm Soar Atlas has released imagery that appears to show significant damage to three different pumping stations on the pipeline route, new evidence that extensive repairs may be required. ???? This is starting to look MUCH bigger than a single strike on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline. Satellite imagery has now showed significant damage at Pump Station 9, while possible damage is also visible at Pump Station 8, both along the same critical pipeline system.… pic.twitter.com/GjvNXYJ6i1 In peacetime, Yanbu sees less use and has less strategic importance. Saudi oil production is centered on supergiant fields along its eastern coastline, and most of its cargoes have historically exited through the Strait of Hormuz to reach market. The pipeline to the western Red Sea coast is ordinarily used for cargo deliveries to Europe and points west, and has more recently been used to circumvent Hormuz and offset the impact of the Iranian blockade on GCC tankers. The Yanbu terminal was loading about four million barrels per day on average before the shutdown, equivalent to roughly four percent of world oil supply. Markets will be watching closely to see if Aramco can now increase its (normally higher) Gulf exports enough to offset the temporary loss of its backup pipeline. Recent satellite evidence suggests that this may be possible, or already in progress. https://maritime-executive.com/article/e.text: The EU is providing financing to revamp a cruise terminal at Klaipeda, Lithuania for military uses, adapting its infrastructure to receive NATO ships in time of need. In a statement, the European Investment Bank (EIB) said that it is lending about $115 million to the Klaipeda State Seaport Authority, which manages a strategic port just north of the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The Port of Klaipeda is the largest in Lithuania, supporting about 70 million tonnes of cargo movement per year and about six percent of the small country's GDP. A new cruise ship terminal is under construction at Klaipeda to replace aging, deteriorating quays elsewhere in the port. Two new berths totaling 900 meters in length will give space for two cruise ships at once, located in the heart of the Old Town waterfront. The site master plan includes new mixed-use development, public parks, a yacht harbor and a modern port administration building. Contracts have already been signed for quay reconstruction and the new building. In addition to supporting NATO-standard modifications to make the cruise terminal dual-use, the overall $230 million project includes an array of non-military priorities in line with traditional EU procurement practice. Green improvements include pierside power for ferries, green hydrogen production infrastructure, and better quays for offshore wind vessels, in addition to perennial port necessities like breakwaters and dredging. "Few projects illustrate Europe's priorities as clearly as the Port of Klaip?da," said EIB Vice-President Karl Nehammer. "It is an investment that directly contributes to the missions of supporting European security and cohesion, while aligning with the green transition.” The upgrade at the cruise terminal - while small compared to the civilian scope of the project - reflects a strategic reality for the Baltics. In the event of a Russian ground invasion, a potential NATO Article 5 defense would require rushing troops and equipment from Western Europe into the region. Seaborne transport is a comparatively efficient means of completing that movement - and it would be the only strategic option if the Suwalki Gap is taken, since the Baltics' narrow land bridge to Poland would be shut.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: The Omani Maritime Security Center confirmed on Tuesday, September 15, that it has undertaken a search and rescue effort for the crew of a Panama-flagged product tanker, while saying that two seafarers are missing. UK Maritime Trade Operations is timing it either to late on September 12 or early on September 13, saying there was a distress call followed by reports of a fire in the engine room and an evacuation. Built in 2005, the 48,000-dwt product tanker was registered in Panama and managed from the UAE. The Omanis reported the incident on Tuesday and did not indicate when they evacuated the crew. They said 23 crewmembers had been taken from the vessel and received medical attention. The report said two crewmembers remained missing and that the disabled vessel was being towed to an Omani port. India’s Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attack on Sunday. It said there were 14 Indian crewmembers, and one was missing. Iran’s IRGC Navy issued a statement on Monday claiming the tanker had been attempting to “traverse a restricted zone south of the Strait of Hormuz.” The IRGC Navy called the maritime lane the vessel was using “hazardous“ and "illegal" and said the result was that the vessel struck sea mines. https://maritime-executive.com/article/j.text: The Japanese government is moving forward with its plan designed to encourage investment in the country’s shipbuilding industry. The goal is to dramatically strengthen the country’s shipbuilding capacity as part of an effort to revitalize the industry. The Ministry of Transport confirmed that it approved an additional $635 million in investments on September 11 as part of plans submitted by five of the country’s shipbuilders. This follows three larger grants awarded on September 4, representing a total of $1.4 billion in government investments in projects valued at nearly $3.8 billion. The government plan calls for a total investment of approximately 1 trillion yen ($6.4 billion) coming from a combination of public and private partnerships. The ministry says it will continue to certify plans on an ongoing basis in a program that will run through 2034. The ministry highlights that Japan relies on maritime trade for the transport of essential goods such as energy and food. Calling shipbuilding vital to Japan, the ministry is seeking to encourage large-scale investments such as the installation of labor-saving and automation equipment, dock expansions, and the introduction of new, larger cranes. It is part of an effort to combat Japan’s declining market share along with the challenges of an aging workforce and declining employment in shipbuilding. The industry was calling for government support, and in response, the government formulated the plan in December 2025, calling for a doubling of shipbuilding output by 2035. The Shipbuilding Industry Revitalization Fund reviews plans submitted by the individual companies with a focus on shipbuilding capacity. The Minister of Transport, Yasuyuki Kaneko, announced the first grants, saying the revitalization effort was underway. He called shipbuilding one of 17 priority industries for Japan.

REUTERS/Stringer LONDON/WARSAW, Sept 15 (Reuters) – Saudi Arabia has cut oil shipments to Europe after drone attacks damaged its key export pipeline to the Red Sea, trade sources told Reuters, prompting top customers such as Poland to rush to seek alternatives as cargo prices topped $120 a barrel. The attacks, which Saudi Arabia has blamed on Iraqi militia, forced the kingdom on Friday to shut its East-West desert oil pipeline, which has spared it from the worst of the impact of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz over the last six months. Oil trading and shipping sources said on Tuesday that Saudi Arabia had informed European customers that some September-loading crude cargoes will be canceled and oil loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu had been suspended. The cut in Saudi flows through the Red Sea will prompt Saudi Arabia to try to export more oil via the Strait of Hormuz using so-called dark shipments similar to those already used by the United Arab Emirates and Iraq, trading sources said. Such shipments have allowed Gulf oil producers to export 7 million to 9 million barrels per day, which is 30% to 40% of pre-war volumes.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/lng.text: Rising LNG bunker prices pushed LNG-fueled clean tanker freight rates above conventional rates Sept. 7-11, highlighting the bunker-price sensitivity that alternative-fueled ships face. Platts LNG-fueled Clean tanker freight represents the estimated cost of transporting cargo on a tanker using LNG as primary fuel, with the freight calculation reflecting prevailing LNG bunker prices. As LNG bunker prices change, the fuel cost of operating the ship changes, directly affecting voyage economics. During Sept. 7-11, a sharp rise in LNG bunker prices coincided with higher Worldscale assessments across several clean tanker routes, pushing LNG-equivalent freight materially above conventional rates. The analysis uses an LNG-equivalent freight measure, a normalized calculation that applies the prevailing Worldscale level to the LNG-fueled vessel’s daily freight component, rather than a separate market assessment. The divergence was most pronounced on Persian Gulf-Japan routes, including Jubail-Chiba, Ruwais-Yokkaichi, and Ras Tanura-Yokohama, where LNG-equivalent freight rose about 33%, compared to 25% increase recorded in conventional freight. The daily LNG-fuelled Platts LNG Base Rates (PBR) by S&P Global Energy on the Jubail-Chiba route rose from $36.66/metric ton on Sept. 7 to $38.89/mt on Sept. 11. Over the same period, the applicable Worldscale daily assessment increased from w520 to w650. East of Suez VLCC freight continued to firm Sept. 7, underpinned by a tightening tonnage list in the Gulf of Oman and prompt fixing requirements. Firmer Atlantic rates further strengthened owners’ sentiment, with market participants expecting further upward pressure.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: U.S. Southern Command has intercepted and destroyed a second floating refueling station in the Eastern Pacific, creating more friction for cocaine smugglers on one of the most popular northbound routes. According to CENTCOM, all clues pointed to a connection between a suspicious fishing vessel and the Los Choneros drug gang, a violent organized crime group based in Ecuador. Many South American smuggling voyages begin in Ecuador, and many take advantage of prearranged at-sea refueling for the journey to Central America. In addition to lethal strikes on the drug boats themselves, CENTCOM has recently turned to in-person interdiction of the fuel boats to interfere with the smugglers' logistics. In this instance, U.S. forces intercepted the suspect vessel, searched it, disembarked the crew and destroyed the vessel with explosives. The crew will be handed over to authorities in Ecuador for processing. On Sept. 15, under the direction of #SOUTHCOM , Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTF-WHEM) forces successfully interdicted a floating refueling station supporting illicit at-sea drug trafficking operations in the Eastern Pacific. Intelligence confirmed the vessel's… pic.twitter.com/LEADvwvH9b "We are exerting unrelenting pressure on these narco-terrorists and hurting them where it counts: dismantling their intricate networks, disrupting their sophisticated logistics, and dealing a blow to their finances. This is what total systemic friction looks like," said SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan in a statement. As in the previous interdiction, the presence of a UH-1 helicopter pointed to U.S. Marine Corps involvement.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: [Brief] On Monday morning, three containers fell off the side of a boxship at the Port of Los Angeles, prompting a coordinated response from the Coast Guard and local officials. At about 1120 hours, the Coast Guard base for Los Angeles-Long Beach received notice that several 40-foot boxes had fallen over the side during cargo operations on a CMA CGM boxship at Berth 302. The service dispatched patrol boats to the scene and set up a 400-yard safety zone around the site of the incident. Two of the three boxes sank after entering the water, and their locations have been marked for later retrieval. The remaining container was recovered. All three contained non-hazardous cargo, the service said. Los Angeles City Fire and the Los Angeles Port Police contributed to the response. The root cause of the casualty has not been disclosed yet; the Coast Guard said in a statement that it would issue further announcements as needed. Both sunken containers have been recovered using commercial salvage techniques. Divers found the first sunken container and attached flotation bags to it, then inflated them to increase buoyancy. They raised it to the surface and tug crews towed it off at about 2200 hours Monday night. Salvors returned and retrieved the second sunken container on Tuesday morning without further incident, and the Coast Guard lifted the safety zone around the area.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: A new report consolidating the survey results from seven countries and more than 93,000 cargo inspections highlights an alarming rate of deficiencies. The World Shipping Council published the data showing that one in ten cargo shipments were identified with safety issues and that the rate of deficiencies has increased over the past decade. Problems included incorrect documentation, marking and labelling, improper packing, and inadequate cargo securing, all of which the trade group said can increase the risk of cargo damage, container losses, and ship fires. It comes as the shipping industry continues to struggle with safety issues and after high-profile fires at sea killing and endangering seafarers. WSC points to the latest statistics by insurer Allianz, which indicate that a containership fire occurs every 17 days. “Finding deficiencies in more than one in ten inspected units is far too high,” said Joe Kramek, President and CEO of the World Shipping Council. “Correct declaration, packing, securing and marking are fundamental safety obligations. When these requirements are not met, people’s lives are put at risk.” The group consolidated the reports submitted to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) from 93,079 inspections conducted in 2025 by Chile, Finland, Germany, the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the Republic of Korea, Sweden and the United States. It highlights that deficiencies were identified in 9,645 inspections, a rate of 10.36 percent among the reports. An analysis of the data shows that between 2017 and 2025, the average rate of deficiencies was over 9 percent, but had been as low as 6.5 percent and 7.4 percent in 2020 and 2021. Over the past three years, the rate has ticked upwards to over 11 percent in 2024 and a three-year average of 10.9 percent. The World Shipping Council last week also highlighted lapses in the international dangerous goods rules. It called on the IMO member states to address the gaps, pointing out that containers are currently carrying thousands of undeclared lithium batteries. It said that global lithium-ion battery deployment in 2025 was six times higher than in 2020, according to the International Energy Agency, with battery demand expected to double by 2030.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Malaysia, which has long harbored anti-Israel sentiments, is holding containers that were passing through its busy Port of Tanjung Pelepas bound for Israel. Bloomberg broke the story, and hours later, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed the reports online. Ibrahim, who is currently on an official visit to the Maldives, interrupted his business to post a message on social media in response to the Bloomberg story. It is the second time he has confirmed official actions detaining Israel-bound cargoes, after a similar incident earlier in August. “Malaysia’s position is clear and unequivocal. We will not allow our country to be used as a conduit for any shipment that supports or contributes to Israel’s military capabilities …” wrote Ibrahim. “Any suspicious shipment will be subject to inspection and investigation in accordance with Malaysian law. Where a violation is established, decisive action will be taken.” Bloomberg reported that three containers had been detained at the port on August 19 and, using tracking data from Maersk, wrote that the boxes are still in Malaysia. Bloomberg says it saw manifests that reported the cargo as electric bicycle parts being shipped from China to the Port of Ashdod, Israel. This incident is reported to have taken place nearly two weeks after Malaysia also confirmed that it was holding another container on suspicion that it could contain weapons. The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency was reported to be suspicious of the container because it was going to Elbit Systems, an Israeli defense technology company. Using tracking data from Hapag-Lloyd, Bloomberg reports the first container was detained on August 7. It is also still being held at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas. This first container was reported to be coming from the Philippines. Ibrahim at the time also said he would not permit his nation to be a conduit for trade flow to Israel.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: A fire on the structure of a newly-constructed cruise ship pier caused substantial damage to a moored tour vessel at Whittier, Alaska, according to the operator and local authorities. At about 1100 hours on Monday, the U.S. Coast Guard received notice of a large blaze on the dock at the new north cruise ship terminal. On arrival, first responders found flames consuming the wooden decking of the pier. The year-old facility did not have working fire hydrants, requiring responders to shuttle water by truck over a ten-minute drive to the site, according to the Anchorage Fire Department. The large cruise ship Norwegian Jade was in the vicinity, but departed her berth and was not affected. A local harbor cruise vessel, Klondike Express, sustained damage from the fire, her operator confirmed. Photos from the scene show that her aluminum hull suffered melting damage in a limited area on the port side amidships, where she had been moored. The upper decks also showed signs of flame and smoke damage on the exterior. During the course of the firefighting effort, Klondike Express was released and towed away from the pier, preventing further damage. Operator Phillips Cruises said that it was continuing tour operations with its other vessels, which were unaffected. "Our M/V Klondike Express may be wounded, but she remains strong. There was no fire aboard—or originating from—our vessel. The damage she sustained resulted from the flames, heat, and smoke from the dock fire while she was moored alongside it," the company said.

South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai and Singapore-based BW LNG highlight that they are moving forward with building the world’s first three-tank LNG carriers. The design permits an increased carrying capacity of up to 2,800 cbm (1.6 percent) while avoiding terminal berthing restrictions that could be caused by larger vessels. Designs for the new vessels were developed by HD Hyundai, working in conjunction with French cargo tank technology company GTT, BW as the shipowner, and DNV as a class society. Designs were approved for the 176,800 cbm carriers, and in June BW proceeded with the first order for four of the new design vessels. According to HD Hyundai, it was able to secure an additional 2,800 cubic meters of space by removing one insulated bulkhead from a 174,000 cbm LNG carrier. This allows for the transport of more cargo, lowering the unit freight cost and enabling shipowners to achieve better profits. The conventional design for LNG carriers is a four-tank system. By applying a three-tank system, the space between cargo holds can be reduced while maintaining the vessel's size, thereby increasing loading capacity. The LNG loading capacity of vessels ordered by BW expands from approximately 174,000 cubic meters to approximately 176,800 cubic meters. BW highlights that the design also maintains flexibility, permitting partial loading conditions. The design has other advantages, including a lower boil-off rate. HD Hyundai explains that as the total surface area of the cargo tank decreases, the amount of heat flowing from the outside to the inside is reduced, and thus the daily boil-off rate. The daily boil-off rate of the three tanks was improved by about six percent. One of the key concerns, however, was cargo sloshing. It notes that as the size of the cargo tank increases, the impact load can also increase. It was able to address this concern through precise strength analysis and structural and thermal reinforcement. The vessels will continue to employ the proven Mark III membrane technology.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) , pediu vista na sessão extraordinária desta terça-feira (15), que analisa o relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) sobre relação entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o fundador do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro. 📱Favorite o g1 no Google e acompanhe as principais notícias do dia AO VIVO: Plenário do STF analisa relatório da PF sobre relação entre Moraes e Vorcaro “Eu tenho que interromper esta situação porque nós temos uma questão de ordem. Nós não temos condições de deliberar. O clima é daí para pior, e a sociedade está assistindo a algo diferente do rito que a lei manda”, alegou Dino, após fazer o pedido.

A ministra Cármen Lúcia , do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), disse na sessão plenária desta terça-feira (15) estar em estado de "profunda consternação e tristeza". O julgamento foi covocado para discutir o relatório que aponta a relação entre o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e o ministro Alexandre de Moraes . "Eu não tenho o hábito de antecipar voto quando há um pedido de vista, e por isso eu peço licença ao ministro Flávio Dino . Mas é uma questão de ordem nem é o voto que eu tinha sobre a questão, mas eu me encontro, como talvez muitos de meus colegas, em estado de profunda consternação e tristeza. Hoje um dos colegas me dizia se eu estava contrariada com alguma coisa, não, eu disse eu estou triste não apenas pelo tema que nos traz aqui que você teria sido o aquele ato decidido, mas porque este Supremo Tribunal Federal guarda da Constituição por determinação nela expressa provocou um mal estar cívico em todas as cidadãs e cidadãos brasileiros nesses últimos dias", disse a ministra.

O Conselho Superior do Ministério Público Federal marcou para o dia 25 de setembro a discussão de um procedimento que analisa menções do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro ao procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet. Gonet afirmou nesta terça-feira (15) que não teve relacionamento de proximidade com Vorcaro, disse que a única ligação entre os dois foi "brevíssima e banal" . A fala aconteceu durante sessão do plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) que discutia a validade de um relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) envolvendo o ministro Alexandre de Moraes. Os diálogos que citam o procurador-geral da República estão em mensagens recuperadas do celular de Vorcaro, tornadas públicas após decisão do ministro André Mendonça . O advogado Ciro Soares aparece como principal interlocutor entre os dois. No dia 15 de março de 2025, o advogado envia ao ex-banqueiro uma foto em que aparece ao lado de Paulo Gonet. Em seguida, escreve: "Liga aqui" e "Ele quer falar com você". Segundo a perícia, foram realizadas quatro chamadas consecutivas entre Vorcaro e Ciro na sequência. Para a PF, os registros indicam que o banqueiro conversou com o PGR pelo aparelho do advogado.

https://petronoticias.com.br/petrobras-c.text: A holandesa Strohm foi contratada pela Petrobrás para fornecer, qualificar e realizar testes offshore de tubos compósitos termoplásticos (TCP) para aplicações de injeção de água e gas lift no pós-sal brasileiro. O projeto testará a tecnologia em lâminas d’água de até 1.500 metros. O acordo também inclui testes de qualificação, engenharia de projeto, serviços de campo e suporte aos testes offshore e à instalação. O TCP, que será utilizado em aplicações de injeção de água e gas lift offshore no Brasil, em lâminas d’água de até 1.500 metros, será avaliado em condições reais de operação, incluindo o manuseio e a capacidade de instalação a partir de embarcações típicas de lançamento de dutos da frota da Petrobrás. “ A conquista deste contrato é uma prova da forte colaboração entre nossas duas empresas e demonstra o compromisso da Petrobras em incorporar tecnologias avançadas de dutos às suas operações, com o objetivo de melhorar a eficiência operacional e reduzir os custos de produção ”, declarou Martin van Onna (foto principal), CEO da Strohm. Fabricados com fibras de carbono ou de vidro reforçadas com polietileno ou poliamida, os tubos compósitos termoplásticos são mais leves e fáceis de manusear do que os sistemas convencionais de dutos flexíveis e rígidos. Seu design enrolável e não corrosivo pode proporcionar confiabilidade de longo prazo e eliminar a necessidade de manutenção rotineira, sem comprometer a capacidade de realizar inspeções contínuas de integridade dos dutos. “A conquista deste contrato representa um importante reconhecimento da tecnologia e das capacidades da Strohm, além de ser um marco relevante em nosso roteiro de desenvolvimento, abrindo caminho para novos avanços no país ”, disse Renato Bastos (foto ao lado), vice-presidente da Strohm Brasil. “ Isso demonstra claramente como a Strohm amadureceu e se tornou uma fornecedora profissional de soluções de dutos flexíveis de alto desempenho, com as capacidades e a experiência necessárias para atender à crescente demanda da indústria por produtos avançados e confiáveis ”, acrescentou o executivo. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/economia/se.text: O sorteio especial da Lotofácil da Independência de 2026 , com prêmio estimado em R$ 300 milhões, foi realizado na noite de terça-feira (15), em São Paulo. De acordo com a Caixa Econômica Federal, 72 apostas acertaram os 15 números e levaram R$ R$ 4.488.579 cada. Os números sorteados foram: 01 - 02 - 03 - 04 - 05 - 06 - 07 - 12 - 15 - 16 - 17 - 19 - 21 - 22 - 23. A Lotofácil da Independência é realizada anualmente em setembro e chega, em 2026, à sua 15ª edição. No sorteio especial, o apostador escolhe entre 15 e 20 números, dentre os 25 disponíveis no volante da Lotofácil, e fatura o prêmio se acertar 11, 12, 13, 14 ou 15 números. Pode ainda deixar que o sistema escolha os números por meio da Surpresinha, quando os números são escolhidos aleatoriamente pelo sistema. Quando há mais de um ganhador em uma faixa, o valor do prêmio é dividido entre os vencedores.

https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/n.text: A sessão dessa terça-feira (15) foi marcada pelo presidente do STF , Edson Fachin, para que o plenário da Corte deliberasse sobre a abertura de uma possível investigação contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, no âmbito do Caso Master. Mas a análise do mérito não chegou perto de ser debatida. Logo na abertura da sessão, os ministros Nunes Marques e Dias Toffoli decidiram não participar do julgamento. Na sequência, o clima de animosidade se instalou e os ministros trocaram ironias, acusações e gritos entre si. Na segunda parte da sessão, o presidente do STF pautou a votação de uma questão de ordem que propunha, entre outras coisas, juntar a análise do caso de Moraes aos questionamentos sobre a condução de Mendonça no Caso Master: Gilmar, Zanin e Moraes votaram a favor; Fachin, Mendonça, Fux e Cármen Lúcia, contra. Dino, que havia se declarado favorável, retirou o voto e pediu vista. Assim, a sessão que escancarou a guerra interna do Supremo terminou sem qualquer decisão. Neste episódio, Natuza Nery conversa com o jornalista Reynaldo Turollo Jr, que acompanhou o dia inteiro de atividades no STF. Turollo e Natuza revisam passo a passo do que aconteceu neste dia histórico para o Judiciário.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542984-tu.text: Çan2 Termik's subsidiary Minerosol Group has signed a 20-year operating and production agreement with Venezuela's PDVSA for the CEMA (Petrokariña) oil field, with a planned investment budget of $381.7 million over the contract period. The agreement grants exclusive rights and includes the right to an additional 20-year extension subject to approval. The CEMA field, located in Venezuela's Anzoátegui State, has remaining oil reserves of 104.2 million barrels and remaining gas reserves of 499.3 billion cubic feet, according to the disclosure. Current production is about 400 barrels per day, with a medium- and long-term target of 9,865 bpd. The asset comprises 10 fields covering a total area of 162.4 square kilometers, with oil ranging from 10 to 59 degrees API. Çan2 Termik has also become the majority shareholder of U.S.-incorporated Denarius Holding Group, which is the sole shareholder of Venezuela-based Minerosol Group. Minerosol will carry out the CEMA investment under the agreement with PDVSA. The company had previously become a shareholder in Denarius Pumping Services LLC in 2024. It said the company has about 30 years of experience providing oilfield services in Venezuela and that its activities had been conducted under applicable U.S. sanctions regulations and OFAC authorizations.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542980-pt.text: PTTEP has received Thai government approval to transfer a 40% working interest in two offshore Gulf of Thailand blocks to Valeura Energy under a strategic farm-in agreement between the companies. Thailand's Cabinet granted executive approval for PTTEP Energy Development Company, a subsidiary of PTT Exploration and Production Public Company (PTTEP), to transfer the interest in blocks G1/65 and G3/65. Under the farm-in, Valeura will earn a 40% undivided working interest in the blocks by paying PTTEP 40% of previously incurred costs and funding a 163-square-km 3D seismic survey over the Nong Yao Northeast focus area. Valeura estimated the total amount payable at $25.6 million as of August 31, including a $1.85 million deposit already paid and $2.8 million for the carried 3D seismic acquisition. The costs also include Valeura's share of previously incurred spending on 1,184 square km of 3D seismic over other focus areas, four exploration wells drilled in 2025, geotechnical studies, licence award fees and development planning. PTTEP and Valeura are continuing to share information to support planning for the next phases of exploration and development on the two blocks.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542982-fi.text: Chinese supplier Envision Energy has installed the first turbine at the 128 MW Vinh Long nearshore wind project in Vietnam, marking the first turbine installation for its first international offshore wind project. The project, developed by REE Group, will comprise 16 Envision EN-226/8.X MW turbines, with full-scale installation now underway. The first turbine was installed in less than seven days, with the second in under five days, while the first equipment was delivered five months after the contract was signed. Installation has continued despite heavy rainfall, strong winds and typhoons, as well as limited installation resources. Envision said the EN-226 features a lighter design intended to simplify installation and maintenance in nearshore conditions.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542979-bo.text: Borr Drilling has agreed to sell its 51% stake in two Mexican joint ventures to its local partner, while retaining ownership of three jack-up rigs working for Pemex and continuing to participate in their underlying contracts through bareboat charters. The definitive agreements cover Borr's interests in Perforaciones Estratégicas e Integrales Mexicana and Perforaciones Estratégicas e Integrales Mexicana II, together known as Perfomex. Following completion, Borr's local partner will become the sole owner of Perfomex and take responsibility for managing and operating the Galar, Gersemi and Njord jack-ups. Borr will retain ownership of all three rigs and said the economics from the underlying contracts are expected to remain largely unchanged under the bareboat charter arrangements. Njord is contracted through April 2028, with extension options, while Galar and Gersemi are contracted through May 2030. The sale consideration will be based on the estimated net book value of Borr's equity interest in Perfomex as of July 31, 2026. The transaction is expected to close in September, subject to customary conditions, followed by a transition period for the transfer of operational responsibilities.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542983-eu.text: The European Commission will likely comment within the next 24 hours on a reopening of its antitrust probe of the merger between Norway's Subsea 7 and Italy's Saipem, Subsea 7 CEO Stuart Fitzgerald said on Wednesday. The probe had been halted by the EU while the parties provided additional information. The deal announced in February last year would create a leading global player in offshore energy services, from drilling and engineering to laying subsea infrastructure for offshore oil and gas projects. Both companies operate a fleet of vessels for these services. "We've provided the data (and) now and we expect a restart imminently," Fitzgerald told Reuters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Oslo. "The EU will come out with a timeline, and you can expect that they'll come out probably within the next 24 hours. So we'll let them state the timeline, but it's imminent," he said. The European Commission, which acts as the EU competition enforcer, said in July the deal may have a significant impact on competition in some offshore engineering and construction service markets.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542981-eq.text: The Norwegian Offshore Directorate has granted Equinor a drilling permit for a wildcat well in the North Sea. The permit is for wellbore 25/9-5 S in production license 1042, operated by Equinor with 30% working interest. Its partners are Aker BP with 40% share and Vår Energi with 30% working interest. The drilling operation will be conducted with COSL’s COSLInnovator semi-submersible drilling rig. The rig is able to operate in water depths up to 750 meters and is designed for North Sea, Norwegian Sea and worldwide use in harsh environments.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542978-va.text: Valeura Energy has discovered a new oil accumulation near its Manora field in the Gulf of Thailand, with drilling results prompting the company to move immediately into development planning for a potential satellite facility. The Suraphi discovery was made through the Manora-9 open-water exploration well and associated sidetracks, about 4.5 km northeast of the Manora A platform on Block G1/48, where Valeura holds a 70% operated working interest. Drilling targeted several prospects in separate fault blocks. The E prospect encountered several oil-bearing sandstone intervals within the 600-series lacustrine sands, intersecting a 626-ft gross oil column with 162 ft of net oil pay. The D prospect encountered a similar oil-bearing reservoir section in an adjacent fault block, with an 849-ft gross column and 172 ft of net oil pay. A third sidetrack targeting a shallower, higher-risk play did not encounter hydrocarbons. Valeura said the success in the D and E fault blocks had effectively de-risked the adjacent F fault block, which is visible on 3D seismic. Mapping calibrated with pressure data collected during drilling suggests all three fault blocks could be filled to their spill points. “Our discovery of a new accumulation of oil very nearby our Manora field is a game-changer for Block G1/48. The results for net pay encountered exceed our pre-drill estimates and is likely to justify a new satellite facility development on the block,” said Sean Guest, President and CEO of Valeura.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/542976-ak.text: Aker BP has made a gas discovery in the North Sea, using Saipem’s Scarabeo 8 semi-submersible drilling rig. The discovery was made 25 kilometers north of the Duva field, marking the first exploration well in production license 1153, which was awarded in APA 2021. The license is operated by Aker BP with 40% stake, with its partners Inpex Idemitsu Norge holding 30%, OKEA 20%, and Harbour Energy Norge 10% working interests. Preliminary calculations show that the size is between 0.15 and 2.4 million standard cubic metres of recoverable oil equivalent (Sm3 of o.e.), which corresponds to 1-15 million barrels. The licensees will assess the well results to determine whether the discovery is economically profitable, as well as potential further delineation of the discovery. Scarabeo 8 is a sixth‑generation drilling rig designed to operate in demanding offshore environments. It is equipped with a dynamic positioning system (DP) and an advanced mooring system, fully compliant with the strictest regulatory standards.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Master Cargas Brasil inaugurou, no dia 15 de setembro, uma estrutura de armazenagem refrigerada em Ponta Grossa (PR) , nos Campos Gerais, com 68 mil m² de área construída e investimento superior a R$ 150 milhões desde o início do projeto. Segundo a empresa, trata-se da maior câmara fria instalada no Paraná. A unidade amplia a oferta de armazenagem frigorificada para operações de grande volume na Região Sul, incluindo empresas com operações em Santa Catarina. O complexo conta com seis câmaras refrigeradas, com controle térmico individual por módulo e capacidade de operar em temperaturas de até –25°C. A estrutura foi projetada para atender principalmente empresas dos segmentos de alimentos, bebidas, proteínas e medicamentos, além de operações voltadas a produtos de maior valor agregado. Entre os recursos utilizados estão degelo por recuperação de calor, válvulas de expansão eletrônicas e aproveitamento do calor do condensador para o aquecimento do piso e apoio ao sistema de degelo. A refrigeração utiliza tecnologia baseada em CO₂, com o objetivo de reduzir o consumo de energia em relação a sistemas convencionais. De acordo com Tânia Lopes Anselmo, CEO e fundadora da Master Cargas Brasil, a estrutura foi direcionada principalmente a operações de produtos premium da alta gastronomia, destinados aos mercados nacional e internacional. “Nesse segmento, temperatura é apenas o começo. Estamos falando de qualidade, segurança, rastreabilidade, preservação do produto, disponibilidade de estoque e excelência operacional vinculada às Regras de Ouro, que são nossos parâmetros de qualidade”, afirma. A executiva estima que o hub tenha potencial para movimentar até 400 carretas por dia e 144 mil cargas de carretas por mês. Considerando uma média de R$ 200 mil em mercadorias por carga, o fluxo potencial chegaria a R$ 80 milhões em produtos por dia. A operação também prevê a segregação de SKUs, produtos, clientes e diferentes modelos de atividade por meio da configuração modular das câmaras. Com 480 mil m² de área total, o hub de Ponta Grossa destina cerca de 30% da capacidade a operações refrigeradas. A unidade começou a operar em agosto e integra a estratégia de expansão da Master Cargas Brasil, que inclui investimentos em outras unidades no Paraná e em São Paulo e o avanço de operações relacionadas a comércio exterior e e-commerce.

O Iveco Group inaugurou um novo centro de distribuição de peças em Pouso Alegre (MG) , com investimento de R$ 93 milhões , para ampliar a capacidade de atendimento das operações de pós-venda no Brasil e na América Latina. A estrutura ocupa quase 20 mil metros quadrados e conta com 17 docas , além de capacidade de expansão de 35%. O novo centro aumentou em 40% a capacidade de armazenamento da operação e movimenta cerca de 5,8 milhões de peças por ano das marcas Iveco, Iveco Bus e FPT. A unidade integra recebimento, armazenagem, separação, expedição e distribuição em uma operação dedicada. A mudança também trouxe redução nos tempos de processamento. O prazo de recebimento das peças, ou Inbound, caiu de seis para quatro dias, enquanto o Outbound, que compreende a saída do produto até o cliente, passou de quatro para dois dias. “A competitividade não é definida apenas pela capacidade de fabricar excelentes produtos, mas também pela capacidade de garantir disponibilidade, continuidade e qualidade ao longo de toda a jornada do cliente”, afirma Domenico Nucera, chief Quality & Operations Officer do Iveco Group. Segundo a empresa, a densidade de armazenamento aumentou 37%, enquanto a disponibilidade de inventário para peças de médio e alto giro cresceu 66%. A estrutura também incorpora recursos voltados ao controle de qualidade, como um Quality Lab, quatro Quality Gates e áreas segregadas para ampliar a rastreabilidade dos materiais. “A operação de peças autônoma amplia nossa capacidade de dar o suporte adequado a cada cliente durante toda a vida útil do produto, com respostas mais eficientes e previsíveis”, destaca Karel Novak, head de Quality & Operations do Iveco Group para a América Latina.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/market_expe.text: Market expectations are shifting towards a prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict, as prospects of a rapid return to the previous status quo diminish further. That’s what Standard Chartered Bank Energy Research Head Emily Ashford said in a report sent to Rigzone on Tuesday, adding that “the postponement of planned Hormuz shipping talks rules out de-escalation for now, while damage to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline has impaired a key bypass route for the strait”. “With supply buffers and alternative export capacity already tight, the market is less able to absorb another disruption without a disproportionate price response,” Ashford warned in the report. The Energy Research Head revealed in the report that Standard Chartered Bank expects Brent oil to “remain supported in triple-digits territory” but warned that “geopolitical headlines are likely to continue to drive sharp corrections in both directions”. “The pipeline closure and postponed talks have already helped keep Brent above the $100 per barrel threshold reached last week,” Ashford highlighted. Ashford went on to outline in the report that Standard Chartered Bank’s “core view” on crude oil is that the “continuing U.S.-Iran stalemate and increasing associated physical risks to regional exports should keep oil prices supported above a higher floor”.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-book-review-a-.text: Andrea Barker’s No Quitting: A Memoir of One Young Woman’s Cadetship in the Merchant Navy is a candid and compelling account of entering the British Merchant Navy as a young woman in an industry that is overwhelmingly male dominated. T he memoir follows Barker from her early determination to pursue a life at sea and into the years of demanding cadetship training aboard different vessels. Her goal was to qualify as a deck officer, but achieving it required far more than learning navigation and seamanship. Barker describes the realities of being a woman onboard a ship, including prejudice, isolation, inappropriate behavior and sexual harassment. Some sections are deeply uncomfortable to read, but their inclusion is important. Rather than presenting a sanitized version of life at sea, Barker gives a frank, and explicit account of the attitudes and experiences that could confront women entering the profession. At the same time, No Quitting is not simply a story about discrimination. Barker captures the excitement and rewards of seafaring, from learning the practical skills of the profession to experiencing the unique sights and routines of life at sea. Her descriptions of the ships, voyages and training provide an engaging insight into what a Merchant Navy cadetship actually involved. The book’s greatest strength is its honesty. Her determination is repeatedly tested, yet she continues to pursue the career she had wanted since childhood. The result is both a personal memoir and a valuable record of the barriers faced by women in maritime careers during a period when opportunities for female seafarers were still limited.

https://safety4sea.com/somali-pirates-re.text: Somali pirates have released the Saint Kitts and Nevis-flagged general cargo vessel Sward and its 17-member crew after about 138 days in captivity. T he vessel was released near Garacad, Puntland, on September 11, after being seized off Somalia on April 26 while sailing from the Suez Canal towards Mombasa. The crew comprises 15 Syrian and two Indian nationals and was reported to be in good health. According to Puntland security sources cited by AFP, the pirates received a ransom before leaving the vessel in small boats and travelling ashore, where vehicles were waiting for them. The amount of ransom paid for the Sward remains unclear. Reports have cited figures ranging from about $200,000 to $2.7 million, while an ÆGIR maritime intelligence report estimated approximately $1.7 million. Puntland sources and AFP confirmed that money was paid but did not provide a consistent figure. The vessel, operated by Marshall Islands-based Asena Shipping and belonging to the fleet of Mersin-based Alphamoon Shipping, was carrying about 4,500 tonnes of subsidised fertiliser destined for Kenya’s National Cereals and Produce Board and tea cooperatives. During its captivity, Sward was reportedly used as a mothership to extend the pirates’ operating range and launch attacks against other vessels. Security sources linked the vessel to the seizure of two Iranian fishing vessels and the Cameroon-flagged cargo vessel Lutuf .

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-g.text: Guard vessels play an important role in protecting safety zones and keeping other traffic clear of vessels or activities requiring additional protection. T he Bundesstelle für Seeunfalluntersuchung (BSU) has drawn lessons learned from an investigation of a less serious marine casualty involving a guard tug and a sailing yacht, which showed that the act of enforcing a safety zone can itself introduce risk if the guard vessel’s role is unclear, communication is delayed and the approach leaves little room for an unexpected manoeuvre. However, the case also highlights a wider collision-avoidance lesson: a vessel cannot assume that other traffic understands its intentions simply because its own crew considers them obvious. A tug was performing its normal assisting duties while also monitoring a safety zone established around two tankers anchored in a roadstead. A sailing yacht subsequently entered the safety zone. The tug responded by heading towards the yacht to alert its crew and establish the minimum distance that was required to be maintained. The resulting manoeuvres brought the two vessels into collision. The yacht sustained minor hull damage, while the tug was undamaged. According to the investigation, the yacht’s crew expressed concern about the tug’s manoeuvring because they had not expected the tug to approach them in that manner. The investigation identified several factors behind the casualty. The tug’s role as a guard vessel was not sufficiently apparent to other traffic, meaning it could initially have been perceived simply as a conventional power-driven vessel. At the same time, the approach used to establish contact created a developing collision risk.

https://safety4sea.com/eu-reassesses-arc.text: South Korea is stepping up its Arctic maritime ambitions as the Northern Sea Route (NSR) gains attention as a potential alternative trade corridor between Asia and Europe, while growing Russian military activity and China’s presence in the Arctic are prompting European governments to reassess the region’s strategic importance. O n 16 September 2025, the administration of South Korean President Lee Jae-myung formally adopted Arctic shipping development as a national policy priority. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries subsequently relocated to Busan, with the government seeking to strengthen the city’s role as the country’s maritime hub for Arctic shipping. Now South Korea’s ambitions are moving from policy to operations and the country is expanding its icebreaking capability. On 11 September, Hanwha Ocean, one of the country’s three major shipbuilders, began construction of South Korea’s second icebreaker. The new vessel is expected to be substantially larger than the research icebreaker RV Araon and to offer significantly greater ice-navigation capability. The development comes as European policymakers increasingly view the Arctic through a security lens, as Russia seeks to strengthen its military and commercial presence in the Arctic, while China is expanding its interest in the region and the Northern Sea Route as a potential trade corridor. At the first European Arctic Summit, held in Rovaniemi, Finland, on September 13–14 and hosted by Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, European leaders discussed the implications of Russia’s military activity, China’s growing interest in the region and the opening of new maritime routes.

https://safety4sea.com/amsa-port-welfare.text: The Australian Seafarers’ Welfare Council (ASWC) and the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) have released the findings of a national Seafarer Port Welfare Survey, providing insights into the welfare needs, experiences and challenges of seafarers visiting Australian ports. C onducted between 1 October 2025 and 4 February 2026, the survey received 436 responses from seafarers across a broad range of Australian ports. The findings will inform future work to improve access to welfare services and strengthen support for seafarers while they are in Australia. The survey found that Australia has a strong foundation of seafarer welfare services, but access can be constrained by operational, transport and port access limitations. Reliable internet/Wi-Fi was identified as the highest-priority service, while shore leave and safe ship-to-shore access were also highly valued. Internet/Wi-Fi received 179 rankings as the most important service, making it the highest-priority welfare need identified by respondents. Shore leave was also strongly valued, receiving 168 rankings as the second most important service and a strong overall positive weighting. The findings underline the importance of connectivity for seafarers spending extended periods away from family and social networks. Mental health support was also among the key welfare services assessed.

https://safety4sea.com/seafarer-mental-h.text: Shipping companies are increasingly moving towards earlier intervention and preventative mental health support for seafarers, according to a new report from Global Maritime Forum’s All Aboard Alliance. T he report, Raising the standard at sea: Showcasing what good looks like with the Sustainable Crewing Guidelines , examines how 13 maritime companies are implementing recommendations launched in March 2025 to improve life at sea . While the report covers areas including welfare, inclusion, connectivity and career development, it highlights mental health as an area where companies are adopting different approaches to a shared challenge. As explained in the report, Höegh Autoliners is focusing on training to strengthen mental health awareness and intervention onboard. The company recognises that officers and senior crew members are often among the people best placed to notice changes in a seafarer’s behaviour. Its mental health training aims to equip seafarers to recognise potential signs of distress, start supportive conversations and direct colleagues towards appropriate assistance. This approach places greater emphasis on early identification, rather than waiting until a seafarer’s situation develops into a serious crisis. In another interesting initiative, Synergy has adopted a preventative approach through regular well-being monitoring. Using its in-house Ahoy platform, seafarers provide weekly feedback on how they are feeling. Where responses indicate potential concerns, the company’s relationship team follows up, while more serious cases can be referred directly to professional counsellors. The approach is intended to identify problems at an early stage and ensure that support is available before concerns escalate.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-hamburg-port-a.text: The Port of Hamburg is expanding shore power infrastructure while also strengthening renewable energy generation, storage and grid capacity as it works towards its 2030 decarbonization goals. S peaking with SAFETY4SEA during SMM 2026, held from September 1 to 4 in Hamburg, Hanno Bromeis, Head of Port Energy Solutions at Hamburg Port Authority , highlighted the importance of combining infrastructure development with close collaboration across ports, terminals and shipping companies. Bromeis explained that Hamburg Port Authority’s energy strategy is guided by Fit for 55 requirements, while also taking into account the economic realities of major infrastructure investments. We are guided by the Fit for 55 regulation, so that is basically what leads us, and we want to be compliant and therefore do everything that it takes, Shore power remains a central part of this strategy. Hamburg has already developed facilities for cruise ships and large container vessels, while short-sea shipping is the next area of focus. “We actually continue to build our OPS facilities. We’ve done so for the cruise market and the large container vessels, and now basically short sea is next,” Bromeis explained.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-iridium-naviga.text: As GNSS jamming and spoofing create growing challenges for safe navigation, resilient positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) and communications are becoming increasingly important to maritime safety. S peaking with SAFETY4SEA during SMM 2026, held from September 1 to 4 in Hamburg, Tim Last, Executive Vice President & General Manager at Iridium, and Wouter Deknopper, Vice President & General Manager of Iridium’s Maritime Line of Business, discussed the importance of alternative PNT capabilities, resilient communications and greater choice in maritime safety systems as ships operate in an increasingly complex risk environment. GNSS services have become fundamental to modern navigation, but growing concerns around jamming and spoofing are increasing the need for alternative means of determining a vessel’s position. According to Last, navigational resilience and reliability are particularly important because global commerce depends not only on secure communications but also on reliable positioning services. Global commerce fundamentally relies on safe, secure communications, but also safe and reliable GNSS services, He explained that alternative PNT services can provide another layer of resilience when traditional satellite navigation signals are disrupted or manipulated.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/hou.text: The House of Representatives voted on California’s Ocean-Going Vessels At Berth waiver yesterday. House Joint Resolution 210 attacking the Ocean-Going Vessels At Berth waiver sponsored by Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA-20) passed 216-211. “At a time when the U.S. wants to lead the shipbuilding industry, Congress has just voted to kill American competitiveness of the industry by overturning California’s clean shipping waivers. This congressional attack on California’s At Berth waiver risks turning longstanding investments in cleaner vessels, port infrastructure and maritime innovations into stranded assets. Now all eyes turn to the Senate. We call on the Senate to uphold the waiver to protect the health of communities, state’s rights, and America’s ability to compete in the global economy,” said Teresa Bui, Senior Climate Campaign Director with Pacific Environment. For decades, the precedent set under both Democratic and Republican administrations is that the Clean Air Act waivers are not rules. The dispute has also reached federal court. A federal judge in Washington, D.C., recently granted California an injunction involving four Clean Air Act waivers and has approved California’s request to add the At-Berth and Commercial Harbor Craft authorizations to the litigation. Because the maritime authorizations were transmitted to Congress later, the parties are seeking an express ruling from the court addressing their treatment as well. That means Congress is moving forward with votes on the maritime resolutions while the federal court is still considering the legal status of those same authorizations. The Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth waiver has been active since 2007 and requires ships to plug into shore power or use equivalent emissions controls while docked, reducing harmful pollution at ports by up to 90% and cutting cancer risks by 55% at the port. Businesses, port authorities, and maritime operators have spent years planning and investing millions in shore power, cleaner engines, and alternative fuel systems. America’s largest ports have poured funding into electrification and zero-emissions technologies, California ports alone have collectively invested more than $550 million in shore-power and related electrification infrastructure, including investments at the Ports of Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland and San Diego. Beyond public health benefits, clean shipping investments are strengthening U.S. energy security by reducing fuel consumption, and accelerating deployment of American-made maritime technologies. China and Europe are already moving forward with similar requirements and investing heavily in cleaner ports, vessels, and maritime technologies. Source: Pacific Environment

https://www.marinelink.com/news/strait-h.text: Vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz remained in the single digits at four on Tuesday, down from seven a day earlier, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday, falling well short of the 10-day average of 18. The drop in traffic through the waterway that handled one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supply before the Iran war comes after attacks in the region intensified. Of the total on Tuesday, two ships were exiting and two were entering, according to the data. Some ships may be sailing through the waterway with their transponders turned off and they are therefore not counted. One very large gas carrier, Salute, carrying around 470,000 barrels of liquefied petroleum gas exited via the Iranian route, while Panamax-sized tanker Nautilus, carrying around 510,000 barrels of naphtha, exited via an unknown dark route. The two ships that entered were both laden, with one being a short-range dirty products tanker and the other a dry bulk carrier. Both entered via the Iranian route.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Indian officials are reporting that one of their navy’s patrol ships was hit by a Pakistani warship in an incident in the international waters off Oman. India says it is lodging a "strong protest" while accusing the Pakistani vessel of “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct,” but Pakistan so far has not acknowledged the incident. According to Indian reports, an unidentified “frontline Indian warship on a routine surveillance mission in the north Arabian Sea” was approached by a Pakistani offshore patrol vessel (corvette) on Tuesday evening, September 15. India says the two vessels collided but that there was no significant damage to its ship and it has continued its mission. Media reports say the incident happened approximately 220 km (118 nautical miles) east of Oman. Media reports identify the Pakistani vessel as PNS Hunain (F273), the third ship of the Yarmook-class of offshore patrol vessels, commissioned in July 2024. The vessel, which was built by Damen at its yard in Romania, is approximately 96 meters (315 feet) and 2,600 tons displacement, with a top speed of 22 knots. Unconfirmed reports coming from India said Hunain was spotted coming at a high speed toward the Indian vessels and attempting maneuvers. The Indian captain also attempted to maneuver his vessel after seeing the Pakistani vessel, and it resulted in a glancing blow. The reports vary from "serious damage" to a "big dent" in the Pakistani patrol vessel and that it was returning to port under its own power. India’s Ministry of External Affairs is highlighting a 1991 agreement between the two countries, which are arch rivals, that their warships would maintain a separation of at least three nautical miles at all times. It states that the “Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention” of the agreement, and it summoned the Pakistani Chargé d’Affaires, the highest-ranking Pakistani official in India. “The Chargé d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” writes the ministry. “The Chargé d'Affaires of India in Islamabad has also been instructed to lodge a similar protest with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.”

https://g1.globo.com/pe/pernambuco/eleic.text: Victor Assis, candidato do PCO ao governo de Pernambuco, defendeu o não pagamento da dívida pública e a estatização da saúde e da educação em entrevista à TV Globo. https://www.oedigital.com/news/542985-sa.text: Oil prices settled $3 higher on Tuesday after shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had canceled some cargo deliveries to European customers, deepening concerns that disruptions to a critical oil-export route could persist for weeks. Gains in U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 outpaced Brent on Tuesday, as fears that Saudi Arabia's supply troubles were widening sent investors rushing into U.S. crude as an alternative. Brent finished up $3.07, or 2.9%, at $108.75 a barrel, while WTI closed up $4.44, or 4.38%, at $105.83 a barrel. Both contracts closed at their highest since May 19. The port of Yanbu has taken on outsized importance for global supply since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran caused the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that was the conduit for one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. The war has forced Saudi Arabia to reroute crude westward via the roughly 1,200-kilometer East-West pipeline that carries oil from the east to Yanbu on the west coast, allowing exports to leave through the Red Sea without tankers passing through the strait. Attacks on the East-West Pipeline by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Friday, however, forced the kingdom, the world's largest crude exporter, to shut the key export route.
