https://www.oedigital.com/news/542986-ve.text: Verlume and SubCtech have signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly develop and deliver integrated subsea power systems and pursue opportunities across the offshore energy and defense sectors. The agreement combines Verlume's subsea power platform and systems integration capabilities with SubCtech's battery technology and manufacturing capabilities. The companies are already working together on an active project. A particular focus will be offshore oil and gas applications, including power systems intended to support ageing subsea infrastructure, field-life extensions and more autonomous operations. Under the collaboration, SubCtech's battery systems can be integrated with Verlume's Axonn technology, which manages power, communications and control within a single subsea architecture. SubCtech designs and produces rechargeable lithium-ion battery systems for offshore and subsea applications, including long-duration deployments in demanding operating environments. The companies intend to use the MoU as a framework to identify and pursue further projects where their combined technologies can be deployed, rather than treating subsea energy storage as a standalone component.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/eia_now_see.text: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) predicted a bigger oil market crunch in 2026 and a bigger oil glut in 2027 in its latest short term energy outlook (STEO), compared to its previous August STEO. In its September STEO, the EIA projected that world petroleum and other liquid fuels consumption will outweigh production by 1.97 million barrels per day in 2026 and that world petroleum and other liquid fuels production will outweigh demand by 4.90 million barrels per day in 2027. The EIA’s August STEO saw world petroleum and other liquid fuels consumption outweighing production by 1.91 million barrels per day in 2026 and world petroleum and other liquid fuels production outweighing demand by 4.78 million barrels per day in 2027. For 2026, the EIA’s September STEO sees consumption coming in at 102.59 million barrels per day and production averaging 100.62 million barrels per day. The EIA projects that demand will hit 104.98 million barrels per day next year and that production will come in at 109.88 million barrels per day. In its previous STEO, the EIA projected that consumption would come in at 102.73 million barrels per day and production would average 100.82 million barrels per day in 2026. The EIA saw demand hitting 104.96 million barrels per day and production coming in at 109.74 million barrels per day next year in that STEO. The EIA’s September STEO forecasts that the oil market crunch will come in at 2.96 million barrels per day in the third quarter of 2026 and 1.71 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, before swinging to a glut of 3.01 million barrels per day in the first quarter of next year, 5.05 million barrels per day in the second quarter, 5.23 million barrels per day in the third quarter, and 6.25 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A AGV , operadora logística especializada em cadeias de suprimentos complexas, decidiu desinvestir integralmente de sua operação na Colômbia e concentrar recursos no Brasil . A transação envolve 30 centros de distribuição, que somam mais de 160 mil m² de área operacional técnica . Segundo a companhia, os recursos obtidos com a venda serão direcionados a investimentos em tecnologia, infraestrutura, modernização de processos e aquisições de empresas no mercado brasileiro. A decisão faz parte da estratégia da AGV de ampliar a verticalização dos serviços no país, onde a empresa atua principalmente nos segmentos de Saúde Animal, Saúde Humana e Bens de Consumo. A companhia afirma que pretende concentrar esforços e capital nas operações brasileiras, com foco em soluções logísticas para atividades de maior complexidade. “A decisão pela venda da Colômbia foi estratégica para mantermos o foco do nosso time e dos nossos recursos no mercado brasileiro, fortalecendo a nossa atuação como especialista nos setores em que atuamos”, afirma Mauricio Motta, CEO da AGV. Segundo o executivo, o conhecimento territorial e regulatório desenvolvido no Brasil é um dos diferenciais da empresa e será reforçado com novos investimentos. A estratégia também prevê a realização de aquisições. “Agora iremos aprimorar esses diferenciais investindo ainda mais em tecnologia, pessoas e aquisições de empresas que agreguem valor ao negócio e aos nossos clientes”, completa Motta. A companhia informa que a operação foi estruturada de forma a evitar impactos para clientes binacionais que mantêm atividades com a AGV nos dois países. A operação brasileira permanecerá independente, segundo a empresa, com estrutura financeira fortalecida e foco nos clientes e mercados em que atua. Com 28 anos de atuação, a AGV opera no modelo asset light e oferece serviços de gestão da cadeia de suprimentos, com soluções customizadas para operações de alta complexidade nos segmentos de saúde animal, saúde humana e bens de consumo.

https://safety4sea.com/port-of-los-angel.text: Three 40-foot shipping containers that fell overboard at the Port of Los Angeles have been recovered following an overnight salvage operation, highlighting the importance of secure cargo operations. T he incident occurred on Monday near Berth 302, prompting the U.S. Coast Guard to establish a 400-yard safety zone around the area. One of the containers was recovered shortly after the incident, while two others sank and were marked for recovery. The containers were reported to be carrying non-hazardous cargo, according to the vessel’s manifest. Commercial salvage teams worked through the night to recover the submerged boxes. Divers located the first container and attached flotation bags before it was refloated and towed to a designated holding area at around 10 p.m. Monday. The second submerged container was recovered using the same method on 15 September. The safe recovery of these containers and reopening of the waterway was a direct result of the coordination and professionalism of everyone involved. We appreciate the efforts of our local partners, divers and salvage personnel who worked together to safely resolve the incident and minimize impacts to port operations. With all three containers accounted for, the Coast Guard has now lifted the safety zone and declared the waterway safe for vessel traffic.

https://safety4sea.com/navigator-gas-eth.text: As uncertainty over shipping’s future fuel mix continues, Navigator Gas’ decision to convert two existing vessels to run on ethane highlights the role retrofit and fuel flexibility can play in adapting existing fleets. N avigator Nova and Navigator Prominence will have their Everllence B&W 6S50ME-GI engines converted to ME-GIE ethane-capable configurations, with the first conversion scheduled to begin in March 2027. The project follows the conversion of Navigator Aurora in 2018, giving the company eight years of operational experience with the technology. Kaj Pilemand, Director of Vessel Operations at Navigator Gas, said this experience had given the company “strong confidence in the ME-GIE solution”, adding that retrofitting existing vessels can help reduce emissions while extending their operational relevance. For specialised ethane carriers, the concept offers a particular advantage: cargo can also be used as fuel. Navigator Gas previously reported that Navigator Aurora’s conversion resulted in an approximately 25% reduction in carbon emissions during the first quarter of 2020. However, alternative-fuel conversion involves more than changing an engine. During the original Navigator Aurora project, HAZID assessments identified considerations around gas detection and ventilation, while engine components and control arrangements were modified to accommodate the different properties of ethane. Michael Petersen, Senior Vice President and Head of PrimeServ Denmark at Everllence, highlighted “fuel flexibility” as a key benefit of the company’s retrofit platform.

https://safety4sea.com/un-security-counc.text: The UN Security Council has warned that the Houthi advance towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is increasing the risk of a wider regional conflict, while calling for urgent international efforts to safeguard freedom of navigation through the strategic maritime chokepoint. A t an emergency Security Council meeting on September 15, Khaled Khiari, UN Assistant Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs and Peace Operations, said the situation in and around the Bab el-Mandeb had become “increasingly volatile” in recent days. Fighting has intensified along Yemen’s western coast as the Houthis advance towards the strait and reportedly capture several islands in the southern Red Sea. Windward is tracking 14 Saudi-flagged vessels rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope instead of transiting the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, as Houthi attacks on Saudi-linked shipping in the Red Sea continue. Since July 20, the diversions have added an estimated 140-195 extra… pic.twitter.com/3oQFWmuYa3 Despite the escalation, commercial shipping flows through the Red Sea appear to remain unaffected for the time being, according to maritime tracking data cited by Khiari. The UN nevertheless stressed that developments around the strait could have wider implications for international shipping and maritime security. The Houthis’ advance has been met by a counteroffensive from Yemen’s Government, including extensive air strikes, with localized clashes reported across several front lines. Unconfirmed estimates indicate hundreds of combatant casualties in recent days.

https://safety4sea.com/st-helena-hit-by-.text: The safety risks facing seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz remain acute, after the Djibouti-flagged St Helena was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile on September 14, as vessel traffic through the strategic waterway fell to just four transits the following day. T he incident occurred at around 20:40 UTC on September 14, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). A verified source reported that a vessel had been struck by an unknown projectile. No casualties, vessel damage or environmental impact have been reported, while authorities continue to investigate. UKMTO has advised vessels operating in the area to exercise caution and report any suspicious activity. Click here to view the full product ⤵️ https://t.co/VWOyM2oLdj #MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/Dfppt86s9b Maritime security sources have attributed the incident to Iran, although UKMTO has not identified a perpetrator and has described the object only as an “unknown projectile.” The uncertainty surrounding the incident further highlights the risks faced by crews navigating the Strait, where vessels remain exposed to attacks and other security threats amid the ongoing regional conflict. The approximately 105-metre, 6,800-gt St Helena has been stranded in the Gulf amid the wider disruption to shipping through Hormuz. https://safety4sea.com/study-a-small-sha.text: Not all vessels carry the same level of risk. New research from ShipIn Systems and NorthStandard suggests that a relatively small group of ships is responsible for the majority of reported accidents, with patterns in their operations offering clues long before something goes wrong. T he Maritime Risk Report 2026 found that 29% of vessels accounted for nearly 70% of reported accidents. The finding raises questions about the effectiveness of uniform approaches to fleet safety and points instead toward a more targeted model: identify where risk is concentrated and direct attention there first. The report argues that maritime incidents often begin long before the event itself, emerging through small, repeated deviations in everyday vessel operations. These can include an unattended bridge while at anchor, mobile phone use while on watch, PPE breaches or unsafe deck procedures. Individually, none of these behaviours necessarily appears critical. Their significance emerges through repetition. On the vessels where they occur, such signals can be recorded thousands of times each year. Taken together, they provide a picture of how a vessel is actually being operated and where operational risk may be accumulating. Safety is still too often measured after the fact. What this research shows is that risk is visible much earlier, embedded in everyday operations. When operators can see where those patterns are developing and which vessels they are concentrated on, they can act before they become incidents.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-anschutz-bridg.text: Today’s navigators are dealing with increasingly complex bridge environments, combining higher traffic and congestion with a growing number of systems, sensors and information sources. S peaking with SAFETY4SEA during SMM 2026, held from September 1 to 4 in Hamburg, Ioannis Papaefthymiou, Managing Director (Panama) at Anschütz, stressed that bridge technology should help navigators manage this complexity, reduce workload and support safer decision-making rather than make their role more demanding. Modern bridge teams have access to more information and technology than ever before, but this does not necessarily make navigation simpler. According to Papaefthymiou, navigators increasingly have to manage traffic and congestion while simultaneously working with radar, ECDIS, AIS and multiple other sensors and systems. The navigators of today are requested to face challenges that include increased traffic and increased congestion. They have to deal with more equipment onboard the ship – radar, ECDIS, AIS, different types of sensors. The challenge is not simply having access to information, but being able to interpret it and make appropriate decisions while operating multiple pieces of equipment.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fsru-doc.text: A 294-meter-long floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) has arrived at the new liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal in Stade, marking the start of commissioning preparations and bringing the facility a step closer to operations, with gas feed-in to Germany’s grid expected from November. Deutsche Energy Terminal (DET) , a German state-owned company that operates the federal government’s LNG terminals, has begun preparations to commission its new floating LNG terminal , after the FSRU Energos Force came to the Stade-Bützfleth industrial port. The arrival of the vessel, chartered by DET, marks the start of preparations to commission the Stade floating LNG terminal . Dr. Peter Röttgen , DET’s CEO, remarked: “As promised, the return of the regasification vessel to the Stade jetty marks the start of preparations for the terminal’s commissioning. We expect the first fully loaded LNG tanker to come alongside in early November. From then on, Stade will begin feeding gas into the grid, thereby making the anticipated and important contribution to security of supply. “The road to this point has not always been easy. Shortly after assuming responsibility for completion, we brought all necessary partners on board, who are working together with full commitment toward this common goal. I would like to take this opportunity to express my sincere thanks for ensuring that we can move forward at the necessary pace.” The German LNG operator expects the Stade terminal to feed up to 3.2 billion cubic meters of natural gas into the grid from 2027, which would be sufficient to supply approximately 2.6 million four-person households with heating energy for a full year. Niedersachsen Ports (NPorts) constructed the jetty specifically for the FSRU and the onshore terminal, which is still under construction. Katherina Reiche , Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy, commented: “With the arrival of the Energos Force in Stade, what security of supply means in practice is becoming visible. The FSRU, which is docking at the terminal today, can help ensure a reliable supply of energy to millions of households from November onwards. With an injection capacity of up to 3.2 billion cubic metres of natural gas per year by 2027, Stade will be an important component of Germany’s security of supply.”

https://gcaptain.com/us-coast-guard-and-.text: USCGC Munro shadows MT Marinera (ex Bella 1) in the North Atlantic, January 7, 2026. U.S. Coast Guard Photo Sep 16, 2026 (Bloomberg) –The US is investigating potential cyberattacks on oil and gas tankers, as concerns grow around the threat to maritime safety posed by hackers interfering with vessels’ electronic systems. Personnel from the US Coast Guard and the Federal Bureau of Investigation boarded an unnamed, foreign-flagged vessel on Aug. 21, following indications its network had been compromised by hackers, a Coast Guard spokesperson said in response to questions from Bloomberg News about the VL Prosperity supertanker. The VL Prosperity is currently idling off the Texas coast after arriving in the area in late August, ship-tracking data shows. Iran’s semi-official Mehr News Agency reported late last month that the ship, which had picked up oil in Egypt, had its communications cut for 30 hours following a cyberattack in the Strait of Gibraltar. The tanker has been cleared by the Coast Guard for normal operations, HMM Ocean Service, a South Korea-based company that acts as the safety and technical manager of the ship, said in an emailed response to questions. HMM Ocean Service has rigorous cyber protocols in place to ensure the safety and security of vessels under its care, the company said, adding that it’s awaiting a final investigation report from US authorities. A second vessel, an unidentified liquefied natural gas carrier, was also inspected over a potential cyberattack, according to a Wall Street Journal report that cited an FBI statement. The second boarding occurred on Aug. 24, according to the newspaper.

REUTERS/Stringer A U.S.-contracted vessel carrying American personnel was struck in an Iranian drone and missile attack near the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week, Fox News reported Wednesday, citing two sources familiar with the incident. The attack involved four Iranian drones and at least one missile, according to Fox News Chief Foreign Correspondent Trey Yingst. One of the weapons struck the vessel, causing minor injuries, including smoke inhalation. The injured personnel were taken to an undisclosed Gulf country for treatment, according to the report. Fox said some U.S. personnel were aboard the vessel but did not identify the ship, its operator, flag, exact location or the nature of its contract with the United States. It was also unclear whether the vessel was participating in U.S.-supported commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz .

https://petronoticias.com.br/vallourec-f.text: A Vallourec anunciou hoje (16) que recebeu um contrato de grande porte da Subsea7 para o fornecimento de tubos de linha de aço-carbono sem costura e revestimento de isolamento térmico para o projeto Sépia 2, operado pela Petrobrás no pré-sal da Bacia de Santos. O escopo abrange a entrega de 130 quilômetros de risers rígidos e linhas de escoamento, totalizando mais de 15 mil toneladas de tubos de linha de aço-carbono para serviço em ambientes com presença de gases ácidos (sour service). Os tubos serão produzidos na unidade da Vallourec em Jeceaba, Minas Gerais, enquanto o revestimento de isolamento térmico correspondente será aplicado na planta da Vallourec Coating Solutions, em Serra, no Espírito Santo. “ Este contrato demonstra a força da oferta integrada da Vallourec, que combina tubos de linha premium sem costura e revestimento avançado de isolamento térmico ”, afirmou o presidente do Conselho de Administração e CEO do Grupo Vallourec, Philippe Guillemot . “ Ele confirma nossa posição como parceira de escolha para os projetos mais exigentes do pré-sal e evidencia a excelência de nossa estrutura industrial totalmente integrada no Brasil, desde nossa unidade em Jeceaba até a planta de revestimentos em Serra. Agradeço à Subsea7 e à Petrobras por essa nova demonstração de confiança, que reconhece a dedicação de nossas equipes ”, completou. A contratação ocorre após a Subsea7 conquistar recentemente o contrato de engenharia, suprimentos, construção e instalação (EPCI, na sigla em inglês) junto à Petrobrás para o projeto Sépia 2. A Vallourec garantiu todo o escopo de fornecimento de tubos de linha de aço-carbono e revestimento externo do projeto por meio de uma única oferta integrada. Sépia 2 está localizado a aproximadamente 280 quilômetros da costa brasileira. O empreendimento contempla 15 poços, além de um duto de exportação conectado a uma nova unidade flutuante de produção, armazenamento e transferência de petróleo (FPSO), que será instalada em uma lâmina d’água de aproximadamente 2.170 metros. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://petronoticias.com.br/mdl-conclui.text: A britânica MDL concluiu uma campanha de descomissionamento de SURF utilizando seu sistema WHLS (Wheeled Horizontal Lay System) em águas profundas brasileiras, na Bacia de Campos. Executado a partir de uma embarcação multipropósito, o projeto envolveu o recolhimento de linhas de escoamento flexíveis, umbilicais e jumpers associados a um FPSO descomissionado. O nome do cliente não foi revelado. A MDL forneceu um conjunto completo de equipamentos para o convés de popa, serviços de engenharia e equipe offshore para apoiar as operações de recuperação. O escopo teve como base um estudo de viabilidade realizado anteriormente pela MDL , que avaliou se a embarcação, já afretada pelo operador do campo, poderia ser utilizada nessa campanha de descomissionamento — uma aplicação pioneira desse tipo. O FEED considerou metodologias de recuperação, requisitos de tensão no topo dos produtos, capacidade dos carretéis, disposição do convés e considerações estruturais preliminares da embarcação. Esse trabalho de engenharia orientou a configuração dos equipamentos mais adequada à execução offshore, além de fornecer um cronograma preliminar indicativo do projeto. A MDL forneceu seu sistema de lançamento horizontal sobre rodas (WHLS-02), tensionador de 110 toneladas, sistema de acionamento de carretel de terceira geração (RDS), guincho offshore FRN-150 e carretéis classificados para operações offshore. Segundo a companhia, a utilização do sistema de lançamento ao mar sobre rodas do WHLS reduziu o efeito de cabrestante durante a recuperação de SURF em águas profundas. Isso permitiu que o tensionador único de alta capacidade da MDL suportasse cargas de recuperação de até 105 toneladas. “ Tenho muito orgulho de ver a conclusão bem-sucedida da campanha de recuperação em Campos, que demonstra ainda mais a aplicabilidade e a experiência da MDL no crescente mercado brasileiro de descomissionamento ”, disse o gerente nacional da MDL no Brasil, Yuri Mendes Martins . O executivo explicou que o projeto avançou desde um estudo inicial de viabilidade até a execução offshore, permitindo que a MDL apoiasse o cliente durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto. “O trabalho de engenharia realizado durante a fase de planejamento forneceu uma base sólida para a mobilização e a campanha offshore, além de ajudar a definir o conjunto de equipamentos de recuperação instalado na embarcação do cliente, que normalmente não é utilizada para esse tipo de escopo ”, detalhou.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: Orient Overseas Container Line (OOCL) joined the growing number of container lines returning to the Suez Canal, sending its first ultra-large vessel through the canal as part of Cosco’s strategy to resume some of its normal routes for Cosco and OOCL vessels. It comes as the Suez Canal Authority highlights continued growth despite the latest military moves by the Houthis at the southern terminus of the Red Sea. The OOCL Portugal (225,000 dwt) made the transit on Wednesday, September 16, coming from Belgium and the Mediterranean on its way to China. The vessel, which has a capacity of 24,188 TEU, was in the convoy from the north, representing OOCL’s first return to the Suez Canal and the first for a Cosco-controlled ship since "the tensions in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb," the Suez Canal Authority emphasized. The OOCL Portugal was one of 39 ships making the transit on Wednesday, which remains at levels still well below the Suez Canal’s peak before the start of the attacks by the Houthis. A day earlier, on September 15, the Suez Canal Authority reported that 45 ships transited the canal. OOCL's ultra-large vessel was in the convoy coming from the north toward the Red Sea (SCA) Wednesday’s transits, however, also appear to have included vessels from MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company and CMA CGM. The Suez Canal Authority highlights that both carriers, along with Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, have restored services. While not mentioned by name, pictures also showed a Wan Hai container vessel in the Suez Canal. Cosco is reported to be restoring several routes to the Suez Canal, including shared services with CMA CGM. Well-known industry commentator Lars Jensen, however, points out that the first are mostly on the backhaul and notes that Evergreen, which is also part of the alliance, is not yet returning to the Suez Canal.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: With salvage efforts underway after a cargo hold fire, CMA CGM has informed customers that it is invoking General Average for the incident involving the CMA CGM Petra . The latest fire on a containership adds further emphasis to recent reports from the World Shipping Council on the persistent danger from cargo deficiencies. The 86,715-dwt containership registered in France is currently docked in Port Klang, Malaysia, having reached the berth on September 11. It had been holding offshore while a salvage team from SMIT was managing the situation that had begun on August 22. The LNG-fueled containership is one of the newest in the CMA CGM fleet, having only been delivered by HD Hyundai at the end of 2024, and it is employed on a route from Asia to East Africa. The ship has a rating for 8,048 TEU with 800 reefer plugs. CMA CGM had advised customers that the crew discovered a fire in one of the holds on August 22 while the ship was in the Malacca Strait approximately 45 nautical miles northwest of Penang. The crew was able to contain the fire, with assistance from the team from SMIT and several fireboats. The ship had been sailing toward Kenya but reported it was diverting to Malaysia. There were no reports of injuries to the crew. The ship had made its last port call in Singapore. It was operating on an adjusted schedule due to the typhoons that struck China in August. Scheduled calls at Shanghai and Ningbo had been omitted with alternate stops in Qingdao and Nansha. The reports have not indicated the extent of the damage, but the adjusters were saying that 450 containers were due to be offloaded for inspection in Malaysia. It was also pointed out that because the fire was in one of the holds, the boxes in the area would have been exposed to the heat and smoke, as well as firefighting water or chemicals. CMA CGM signed a Lloyd’s Standard Form of Salvage, which observers said was likely the first step toward General Average. It has also announced the use of a professional salvage team.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Several different developments taking place in recent days indicate that diplomacy and negotiation are not going to bring warfare in the Gulf to an end anytime soon, either in the conflict involving Iran and nor in Yemen. For the maritime community, the scene appears set for a continuation and a worsening of the current pattern of naval action, blockades and of attacks on civilian shipping. This week, the long-running negotiation between Iran and Oman came to a head, with GCC countries unwilling to accept the compromise which Iran and Oman had agreed. When the terms were understood, it appears a set of concessions had been made to Iran which thoroughly compromised the established UNCLOS arrangements governing the Strait of Hormuz itself, but also international standards pertaining to innocent passage through narrows and territorial waters. Under the new arrangements, while the single new channel through the Strait was to pass through both Iranian and Omani territorial waters, the entrances to the channel at both ends were to be in the waters of Iran, giving Iran a veto over who should pass. Oman also appears to have surrendered the right to allow use of its own territorial waters for innocent passage. What is particularly shocking is that the United States was kept abreast of the negotiations and appears to have been ready to agree these arrangements. Unsurprisingly, the remaining GCC states were unwilling to countenance even discussion of such a plan, which would have compromised their ability to trade, export and choose their own security partners, as well as leaving intact Iran’s threatening drone and missile capability and its program of regional expansionism. In effect, the agreement was to have been an endorsement of Iran’s seizure of political suzerainty over the Gulf, as was evident in a description in Mehr News the preceding day of how Iran thought the conference was going to go in Salalah – the GCC representatives were to be ‘informed of the new arrangements’ as a fait accompli, denied an opportunity to discuss or object, and their presence would be advertised to the international community as being ‘tacit non-objection’ to the arrangements. It would have been akin to a surrender ceremony. Having walked away from the Salalah conference, the Gulf States now know that if they want to protect their own national sovereignty, they are going to have to fight for it. In Yemen, the GCC countries have also understood that the Houthi undertaking offered to President Trump not to attack American interests was a means of putting off US intervention – at least until the Houthis had consolidated their military objectives, by which time they would have been in a stronger position to resist any American military counter-move. https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: U.S. officials are confirming an ongoing investigation into an apparent cyberattack on at least one or two tankers bound for the United States last month. The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the U.S. Coast Guard said the vessels’ crews reported the incidents while saying that there was no immediate danger to the crew or the environment. According to a joint statement to The Wall Street Journal, the investigations “were designed to ensure the integrity of the vessel’s operational and information technology systems following indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised by foreign actors ... Currently, there are no reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts.” The Coast Guard did not provide details, but suspicions have quickly centered on Iran after the Iranian media began reporting incidents in early August. The Tasnim agency, which is reported to be associated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, ran a story on August 20 saying the tanker VL Prosperity (IMO 9683697) “was targeted by a major cyberattack in the Strait of Gibraltar, and all of its communications were cut off for 30 hours.” It claimed to have information from a crewmember aboard the Liberian-flagged tanker that “the attackers infiltrated the engine-room systems, reduced the engine’s cooling flow, increased the engine speed, and disabled the ship’s fuel and engine-oil tank.” Similar reports appeared in other Iranian news outlets, including Mehr News Agency. Tasnim followed up with a story entitled “ No American Vessel is Safe Anymore: Will Cannons Give Way to Codes? ” The tanker, which is 319,547 dwt, is managed by HMM Ocean Services and was heading for Galveston, Texas. CBS News reports HMM confirmed its vessel was under investigation. The reports said the vessel experienced the problems while transiting the Strait of Gibraltar. Media reports are also suggesting that a second, so far unnamed, LNG carrier also notified the authorities of a suspected cyberattack.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: With the opening up of the Russian Northern Sea Route, exploiting the reduction in ice in the sea corridor running across Russia’s northern coastline, the way is now open for the movement of oil and LNG along a route firmly under Russian control, with reduced exposure to dark fleet interdictions by others, and with less risk of oil terminal attacks by the long-range Ukrainian sanctions program. This is in keeping with President Putin’s plan to develop the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor in order to better tie together Russia’s Baltic region, the Arctic, and the Far East. In future, Russian use of this route to move both oil and LNG will become more important, as pipelines are extended from the Volkhov region near St. Petersburg, where a number of trans-Russian pipelines already terminate, to Murmansk. But already the Baltic Pipeline System has a terminal in the far north at Varandey, and last month President Putin opened the Sever Bay Terminal, south of Dikson at the mouth of the Yenisei River, which will export output from the Gydan Arctic 2 LNG and Vostok Oil fields. The terminal lies at the end of a newly-constructed 500 mile pipeline built across the Arctic tundra. The lead tanker in the Arc7 LNG class being built at the Zvezda shipyard to ply the Northern Sea Route (NSR), the Aleksey Kosygin (IMO 9904546) made its first journey to Sever Bay in December 2025, and its sister ship Pyotr Stolypin (IMO 9904675) will soon come on line too. But these two ships, plus feeder ships such as the shuttle tanker Akademik Gubnik (IMO 9842190) are already sanctioned, so the protection afforded by the use of the NSR only lasts the length of the corridor; standard dark fleet sanctions evasion procedures and Ship-to-Ship (STS) transfers need to be used thereafter, to protect the origin of the cargoes as they are delivered to China and other importers in SE Asia and further afield. Dark fleet tankers heading East on the NSR from Primorsk, or post an intermediate STS in Murmansk, have hitherto used the relatively protected Nakhodka Bay to conduct STS transfers, with the Fokino base of the Russian Pacific Fleet not far away. The intelligence company SynMax has however spotted four dark fleet tankers, all sanctioned, conducting STS operations 65nm to the east of Chongin in North Korea, in an open area of the Sea of Japan. https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O presidente Lula afirmou nesta quarta-feira (16) que o presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, deve evitar que a crise na Corte atrapalhe as próximas eleições. A declaração ocorreu após o STF suspender, nesta terça-feira (15), o julgamento sobre abrir investigação contra o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, após pedido de vista de Flávio Dino. Lula defendeu investigar as denúncias com direito de defesa. O presidente afirmou que "ninguém está acima da lei, nem eu, nem o Fachin, nem ministro da Suprema Corte". Para o presidente, o momento de desgaste institucional reforça a necessidade de realizar reformas estruturais no Poder Judiciário e também no sistema político brasileiro. Lula elogiou a atuação do ministro Alexandre de Moraes e afirmou: "Acho que o Alexandre de Moraes fez um trabalho extraordinário para garantir a democracia deste país".

O presidente Lula afirmou nesta quarta-feira (16) que não é responsável pelas indicações de ministros ao STF. Ele defendeu a punição de eventuais crimes cometidos. Essa foi a primeira fala de Lula sobre os ministros após o STF suspender, nesta terça-feira (15), o julgamento sobre a abertura de investigação contra Moraes. Antes, Lula evitava se pronunciar para afastar sua campanha da crise na Corte. Alexandre de Moraes foi indicado ao cargo pelo ex-presidente Michel Temer em 2017. O presidente contestou as acusações de seus adversários. Lula afirmou: "Ontem meu adversário disse que eu sou responsável pelo Moraes". Lula elogiou a atuação do ministro na Justiça Eleitoral em 2022. O presidente defendeu a segurança das urnas eletrônicas brasileiras, afirmando que o sistema é confiável.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A XCMG Brasil e a Transportadora Navarini fecharam contrato para a venda de 251 cavalos mecânicos 100% elétricos E7-95T , em uma operação de aproximadamente R$ 500 milhões . Assinado na sede global da fabricante, em Xuzhou, na China, o negócio cria, segundo as empresas, a maior frota de caminhões rodoviários elétricos da América Latina. Com sede em Sorriso (MT), a Navarini atua principalmente no transporte de cargas para o agronegócio e utilizará os veículos no escoamento da produção. Com PBT de 74 toneladas e CMT de 120 toneladas, o E7-95T foi desenvolvido para operações de transporte pesado. A aquisição amplia a aplicação de caminhões elétricos para rotas de longa distância e transporte de grãos, segmento em que a eletrificação ainda tem participação menor que em operações urbanas e de curta distância. O projeto foi desenvolvido ao longo de meses pelas duas empresas, com análise das operações da transportadora, dimensionamento da aplicação, avaliação das características das rotas e do relevo e testes do caminhão em condições reais. Segundo a XCMG, os testes avaliaram aspectos como autonomia, desempenho com carga máxima e custo operacional antes da assinatura do contrato. “Depois de meses de trabalho, estudos da operação, análise de relevo, entendimento das necessidades do cliente e testes em condições reais, chegamos a uma solução capaz de unir produtividade, eficiência operacional e sustentabilidade”, afirma Hilário Matzenbacher, executivo da XCMG Brasil responsável pelo projeto. A Transportadora Navarini iniciou seu projeto de eletrificação em 2024. Segundo Luis Fernando Navarini, fundador da empresa, os testes realizados em condições de operação contribuíram para a decisão de ampliar a frota elétrica. “Nosso objetivo nunca foi apenas comprar caminhões elétricos. É mudar a cultura do transporte no Brasil e provar que a eletrificação funciona onde ninguém acreditava que funcionaria: no pesado, na longa distância, na poeira da safra”, afirma. O E7-95T utiliza propulsão elétrica e não emite gases de efeito estufa durante a operação. A XCMG também destaca redução de ruído e de necessidades de manutenção como características do modelo. Os caminhões elétricos do portfólio da companhia são produzidos e recebem suporte a partir da fábrica de Pouso Alegre (MG).

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/the.text: That may be precisely what makes the present situation more difficult for shipowners. A closed waterway produces a clear decision. An open waterway produces another clear decision. But a passage that remains technically open while traffic collapses, ships are attacked, insurance conditions change rapidly and the political situation can deteriorate between fixture and arrival creates something much harder to manage: commercial ambiguity. On 9 September, preliminary vessel-tracking data showed only seven commodity vessels transiting Hormuz. At the same time, Brent crude was trading above USD 100 per barrel following the latest escalation in the Middle East, including attacks on commercial shipping and Saudi energy infrastructure. Before the present conflict, Hormuz was one of the principal arteries of global energy trade. Today it remains operational — but no prudent owner can treat passage through it as ordinary navigation. This distinction matters because the Middle East crisis is now moving beyond the voyage P&L. For years, when geopolitical risk increased, the shipping conversation often became surprisingly narrow. What is the Additional War Risk Premium? Can Charterers pay it? Can we obtain Kidnap & Ransom cover? Loss of Hire? Can we fix the voyage? Those questions remain important. But they are no longer sufficient. The Extra War Risk cost attached to a voyage is only one visible price within a much larger economic exposure. Public market reporting shows how dramatically the insurance environment has changed. War-risk pricing for Gulf transits has increased sharply, while cargo insurance costs have also become substantial. At the same time, underwriters are increasingly differentiating between vessels according to ownership, chartering relationships, cargo, trading history, nationality nexus and the precise characteristics of the proposed voyage.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: On Wednesday, the House of Representatives passed a measure to overturn California's Commercial Harbor Craft emissions rule. If also passed by the Senate, it would roll back a unique state-level requirement: installation of diesel particulate filters for tugs and workboats in certain big harbors. Since the 1970s, the state of California has had a carve-out in federal law that allows it to create its own motor-vehicle emissions regulations. This unique permission-slip has enabled the California Air Resources Board (CARB) to clean up the infamous smog conditions of the Los Angeles basin. Today, CARB still writes statewide exhaust limits that are more stringent than federal standards, both on-road and off-road - like its recently-revised Commercial Harbor Craft Rule. The 2022 revised rule (in proponents' view, a "waiver" from federal Clean Air Act standards) is intended to cut back on health-hazardous emissions from tugs, workboats and other harbor craft. CARB believes that the rule would reduce early mortality among California residents by about 530 people over the next few decades. In practice, the rule requires tug and harbor craft operators to use an EPA Tier IV engine, the cleanest on the market. In addition, unlike any other regulator, CARB would require local harbor tugs to have a "level 3 Verified Diesel Emission Control Strategy (VDECS)" - a system that reduces particulate emissions by at least 85 percent. Options include switching to a low-emissions newbuild (battery-electric, hydrogen or methanol); or, for existing tugs, to retrofit a diesel particulate filter (DPF) - an emissions control system that has not previously been seen in commercial maritime applications in North America. A marine DPF product exists in the yacht market, where it is used for aesthetic purposes. Commercial DPF technology is common in the market for European inland workboats, providing compliance with stringent EU Stage V particulate matter requirements (the filter is often found as part of a complete OEM-integrated propulsion package). At present, no such system exists in a class-approved form in the United States. But the additional cost, complexity and fire-safety questions that attend the equipment have made California tug operators and the U.S. Coast Guard skeptical. The filters accumulate soot, so they need a cleaning cycle to periodically burn it off. When activated, the cycle runs the filter's internal temperature up to more than 900 degrees F. Because of this heating cycle, DPF exhaust designs get much hotter than non-DPF designs. In the tight confines of a tugboat's engine room, that would add new fire risks, operators say.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: The NTSB has released its annual compendium of prior-year casualty reports, and for 2025, the list includes some of the highest-profile accidents in recent maritime history. NTSB incorporated details and lessons-learned from no fewer than 49 investigations, including the boxship Dali's allision with the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore, the deadly fire on ro/ro Grande Costa D'Avorio, and the implosion of the private submersible Titan - all major marine casualties that grabbed headlines for months. These reports are in the public domain and many have been previously covered, but the annual compendium puts them all in one place, in an accessible, abbreviated format for education and public awareness. Some of the smaller events have previously received little notice. "It is our sincere hope that others will apply the knowledge uncovered by our world-renowned investigators to prevent future marine casualties and save lives," said NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer L. Homendy. "Stakeholders at all levels can voluntarily implement the lessons learned from our investigations to ensure safety." This year, NTSB is highlighting a dozen perennial safety factors that operators and agencies need to consider. All will be familiar to the prudent mariner, but the details in the report lay out when and why these factors matter - and why they arise again every year: • Performing maintenance effectively • Effective voyage planning and management • Detecting and containing vessel fires • Assessing the condition of waterfront infrastructure • Ensuring watertight integrity • Accounting for bank effect • Combating fatigue and distraction • Properly securing and monitoring lithium-ion batteries • Mitigating the risks of a loss of electrical power • Planning and training for emergencies • Operating in strong currents or heavy-weather conditions • Operating equipment and machinery systems as designed. Beyond the big headlines - the cascading power failure aboard Dali, the runaway vehicle fire on Grande Costa D'Avorio, the unique construction and certification practices on the Titan - the report includes dozens of case studies applicable to operators of all kinds. Tug girtings, mistaken steering-control console assignments, undetected gradual flooding events, o-ring failures, engine room fires, parted lines, lithium ion battery cargo fires - casualties on every kind of vessel, all extending for more than 130 pages.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: The contentious negotiations for a new contract for up to 11,000 port workers at Germany’s main seaports have again broken down, with the union, ver.di, reporting it has begun a vote and will seek authorization for an indefinite strike. A representative group polled at the beginning of the week rejected the fourth round proposals from the ZDS, the Central Association of German Seaport Operators. Contract negotiations began in late July with the union demanding an 8.2 percent increase in hourly wages in a 12-month contract. The employers started with a proposed 5.3 percent increase in two stages, plus a one-off payment. The sides reportedly remain far apart, with ZDS offering two new options last week, one for a 3.4 percent increase over 12 months retroactive to August 1 and including a container allowance and more vacation pay. A second option of 5.1 percent plus the allowances and vacation pay for 18-months was immediately rejected by the union and not presented to the members for a vote. The talks cover the workers at Hamburg, Bremen/Bremerhaven, Emden, Brake, and Wilhelmshaven. The members have been without a contract since July 31. ZDS asserts that both of its models were viable options and represented the “top end compared to others in the industry.” It says it deliberately presented two options based on the “impressions and expectations of the employees regarding the duration and structure of a wage agreement.” Ver.di reports that nearly 65 percent of a representative group of over 5,500 employees were surveyed and rejected the 12-month proposal. The union repeated its demands for higher wages on a shorter contract duration. It points to the increasing risks in the workplace, saying that security issues are growing in addition to the economic challenges for members. It highlights the increased number of drone flights over the port facilities, saying that it is “creating additional risks in a work environment already characterized by heavy loads, hazardous materials, and complex technology.” The union opened a vote running until October 1 for the full membership. Ver.di says if at least 75 percent reject the offer and authorize an indefinite strike, it will decide on the failure of the negotiations and initiate the strike.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: With the battle lines forming for the International Maritime Organization to finalize and adopt its Net Zero Framework, a new study is looking at the validity of continuous emissions measurement technology as it applies to the regulation. They are looking at the use of real-time monitoring aboard LNG vessels versus the current modeling used in assessing emissions. The IMO adopted in 2023 its Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) and the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) rating scheme as the first step to cut carbon intensity. The MEPC is set to hold its next session starting at the end of November in an attempt to complete a draft, followed potentially by the next Extraordinary Session to put the Net Zero Framework to a vote for members. “The industry currently relies on default emissions factors and test bed data to estimate environmental performance,” explains Panos Mitrou, SVP Shipping Strategy for Lloyd's Register. “This initiative enables industry stakeholders the opportunity to compare estimated emissions performance against direct measurements from a vessel operating in real-world conditions. The results will generate valuable insights into the role continuous emissions monitoring can play in supporting more accurate reporting as well as an improved operational understanding that can support emissions minimization.” The new joint development project will bring together expertise from across the maritime value chain to provide independent evidence on the accuracy and reliability of continuous emissions monitoring technologies for LNG-fuelled vessels. The initiative will see LR acting as the independent verifier, working with Seapeak, Kongsberg Maritime and Tunable to advance emissions compliance through the deployment and verification of onboard emissions monitoring technology. The project will evaluate measured emissions data from a newly built LNG carrier scheduled for delivery in early 2027, with monitoring and data analysis continuing throughout the year. It will measure the accuracy of Kongsberg Maritime’s Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS), which incorporates Tunable’s gas analysis technology, on board a new LNG carrier. The partners will compare actual CO2 emissions recorded by the vessel’s CEMS against both engine test bed data and default emissions factors, quantifying the resulting differences and assessing the regulatory applicability of direct CO2 measurement against the relevant IMO and EU emissions reporting frameworks. The project will assess the performance of Kongsberg Maritime’s CEMS under real operating conditions and explore how independently verified measurements can help improve confidence in emissions data used by shipowners, charterers, and regulators.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: FIn a surprise announcement, Norway-based 2020 Bulkers reports that it plans to reinvent the company as an owner-operator of large anchor-handler supply ships based on the strong opportunities in the offshore market. The company has entered into a Letter of Intent to purchase a fleet of up to 15 large AHTS vessels and, once completed, will rename itself AHTS. Launched as an investment company in 2017, 2020 Bulkers was focused on the Newcastlemax segment of bulker operations. After a successful track record of returns and dividends for its shareholders, management announced that it intended to sell its fleet of bulkers. With the sale of one vessel in late 2025, the company was down to six vessels, all of which were delivered by April 2026 to new owners. Management had said it would explore new opportunities in the market. AHTS AS commenced operations earlier this year and currently owns seven large anchor handler tug supply vessels. It already has agreements to purchase three additional vessels. The fleet list included in the 2020 Bulkers investor presentation shows vessels built in 2009 and 2010, mostly by Fincantieri in Italy and based on the Moss 242H design. The company highlights in its presentation that its selected segment is a “global workhorse for MODU mooring scope and international in scope.” Under the terms of several parallel agreements, 2020 Bulkers plans to spend a total of $406 million for the acquisition of AHTS and its vessels, including many of them that are coming from United Offshore Support’s fleet. Other vessels are coming from special-purpose companies to create the combined fleet of up to 15 vessels. 2020 Bulker anticipates a total financing of up to $485 million to assemble the new operation and provide for working capital. Management reports that, after the sale of the bulker fleet, it explored various strategic opportunities before selecting the acquisition of AHTS and the anchor handler fleet. It highlights that the segment provides key services in the offshore segment and remains in high demand. Further, it notes that only one large AHTS has been built since 2018 and that there are currently none on order. It notes that the existing industry fleet is aging. It says that the segment is effectively fully utilized, and believes AHTS vessels offer attractive economic returns along with further opportunity for consolidation. Furthermore, it believes the operation will generate strong free cash flows.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Two former crewmembers from the much-discussed carrier USS Abraham Lincoln have admitted to selling deadly narcotics to crewmates. Former Lincoln crewmember Seaman Bailey A. Szramowski, 29, has pleaded guilty of selling cocaine and mislabeled "Percocet" pills to his crewmates, beginning in August 2022 at the latest - about the time period when Lincoln returned to San Diego from a deployment. His fake oxycodone pills were in fact laced with fentanyl, a deadly opiate - a fact which he did not disclose to his clients, with "reckless disregard." His plea agreement shows that he sold these pills to at least two sailors, working in concert with his wife, Seaman Johnnese H. Poomaihealani, 25, who has pleaded guilty to similar charges. One of the buyers, referred to in charging documents as USS Abraham Lincoln crewmember A.N., bought 10 pills from Szramowski on December 30, 2022, in the apparent understanding that they contained oxycodone. A.N. subsequently overdosed and died on January 3, 2023. A coroner determined that A.N. had passed away from ingesting fentanyl. Szramowski attempted to conceal the origin of the drugs by asking the family of A.N. to delete the text messages he had sent to A.N.'s phone, which they declined to do. He attempted to influence them by telling them that the messages could ruin his future or get him criminally charged if they were not deleted. 10 days after A.N.'s demise, Szramowski sold three more pills from the same source to another active-duty sailor, identified as C.L. Shortly after, C.L. suffered an apparent overdose and had to be hospitalized. He survived, and Szramowski reportedly instructed him to tell investigators that he had gotten the pills from A.N., who had recently passed away from the same supply. https://gcaptain.com/container-shipping-.text: OOCL Portugal transits the Suez Canal on September 16, 2026, marking COSCO SHIPPING Lines’ first southbound passage through the canal since the Red Sea crisis began. Photo: Suez Canal Authority Container shipping’s return to the Suez Canal is gathering pace, even as fighting around the southern entrance to the Red Sea is moving in the opposite direction. The 24,188-TEU OOCL Portugal transited the Suez Canal on Wednesday on a voyage from Belgium to China, marking what the Suez Canal Authority described as COSCO SHIPPING Lines’ first southbound passage through the canal since the Red Sea security crisis began. The nearly 400-meter vessel operates on Ocean Alliance’s NEU2 service connecting the Far East and Northwest Europe. For Egypt, the passage is another sign that the container sector is beginning to rebuild its presence on the Suez route after years of diversions around the Cape of Good Hope. The Suez Canal Authority said container ship net tonnage through the canal reached 72.1 million tons during the first eight months of 2026, up 54.2% from 46.7 million tons during the same period last year. The authority said services operated by CMA CGM, Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd and COSCO have all returned to the canal to varying degrees.

https://splash247.com/one-week-to-go-unt.text: With just seven days to go until the inaugural Splash Singapore, shipowners, managers, charterers, technology leaders and investors are preparing to gather at the Fairmont Singapore for a day built around one question: how should shipping operate when the assumptions underpinning the industry are changing faster than ever? Taking place on Thursday, September 24 in the Stamford Ballroom at Raffles City Convention Centre, Splash Singapore builds on eight editions of the Maritime CEO Forum Singapore. The format remains deliberately simple: no presentations, no slides and no selling, just tightly moderated, unscripted discussions between senior industry figures. The opening Big Issues session will put the disruptive environment confronting shipping in 2026 under the microscope. Rather than simply listing geopolitics, regulation, technology and changing trade flows as risks, Splash editor and conference co-founder Sam Chambers will ask what successful shipping organisations have actually changed in response. How much efficiency should companies sacrifice in the pursuit of resilience? How do owners make investments designed to last 20 years when the assumptions behind them can change within six months? How does a company avoid becoming permanently reactive? And what types of people, structures and technology are required when yesterday is becoming an increasingly unreliable guide to tomorrow? Joining Chambers on stage are Bjørn Højgaard, CEO of Anglo-Eastern Univan Group; Hor Weng Yew, managing director and CEO of Pacific Carriers Limited and chairman of the Singapore Maritime Foundation; Jeremy Sutton, CEO of Swire Shipping; John Su, group chairman and CEO of Erasmus Shipinvest Group; Nick Potter, president and CEO of AET; and Shmuel Yoskovitz, CEO of X-Press Feeders.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fore-acc.text: A new liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier design that moves the accommodation block and bridge to the bow to make room for four wind-assisted sails has cleared a key technical milestone, with Lloyd’s Register, a maritime classification society, affirming technical readiness of the HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HHI) and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL) concept, marking a key step toward commercializing large-scale wind-assisted propulsion for LNG transport. Lloyd’s Register has granted design appraisal for HD Hyundai Heavy Industries’ fore-accommodation LNG carrier design featuring the Wind Challenger wind-assisted propulsion system developed by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines. This move confirms compliance with LR’s Wind-Assisted Propulsion Systems (WAPS) notation requirements. Andy McKeran , Chief Growth Officer, Lloyd’s Register, commented: “As LNG carrier designs continue to evolve, the industry needs robust technical frameworks to assess new technologies and configurations. This design appraisal demonstrates how collaborative development and independent technical assurance can support the delivery of larger, more capable and operationally efficient vessel concepts.” The design covers what the project partners describe as the world’s first fore-accommodation LNG carrier equipped with the Wind Challenger hard-sail system and LR’s blessing marks the latest milestone in a joint development project involving the three players and the Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator, following approval in principle (AiP) awarded by Lloyd’s Register in 2025. Hongryeul Ryu , Executive Vice President & CTO, HHI, remarked: “Through close collaboration with MOL and Lloyd’s Register, we have advanced the development of a new LNG carrier concept combining a fore-accommodation arrangement with Wind Challenger in a safe, practical and class-compliant manner. “Achieving design appraisal for compliance with LR WAPS notation demonstrates the technical maturity of the concept and represents an important step toward future commercial application. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries will continue to develop reliable and sustainable LNG carrier solutions for the next generation of shipping.”

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/gtt.text: GTT announces two major developments within GTT Energy, the Group business unit dedicated to containment and energy management systems: the launch of the LNG Performance Centre, a new service ecosystem designed to support ship-owners and charterers in optimising LNG carrier fleet performance and cargo management, as well as the introduction of next-generation LNG as fuel solution for container ships featuring 2 barg[1] technology. An LNG Performance Centre dedicated to LNG carrier fleet management Enhancing the management of LNG operations on board LNG carriers is becoming increasingly strategic, with the potential to improve operational performance and unlock new opportunities for value creation. GTT Energy is therefore launching the LNG Performance Centre, an ecosystem of services specifically designed for LNG carriers to address ship-owners’, charterers’ and crews’ need for greater visibility into vessel operations. The LNG Performance Centre will provide an integrated approach built around three pillars: cargo management, voyage optimisation and containment system performance monitoring. The offering will combine advice from experts and seasoned captains, available 24/7, with a suite of digital solutions underpinned by GTT’s proprietary data and advanced models. These services will foster a more proactive approach to fleet management, helping to preserve and maximise cargo value, improve operating efficiency, support regulatory compliance and reduce their environmental footprint. GTT Energy’s containment technologies currently equip 86% of the LNG carrier fleet in operation worldwide. This installed base represents nearly 20,000 cumulative years of operational experience at sea, together with extensive associated data and proprietary thermodynamic models. This initiative marks a further step in GTT Energy’s development of services covering the entire LNG carrier lifecycle, with increasing integration of data and analytics across the LNG value chain. Next-generation LNG as fuel solution for container ships: maximising cargo capacity and operational flexibility To facilitate LNG fuel tank integration and help shipyards shorten design and construction schedules, GTT Energy is introducing a new LNG as fuel containment solution with standardised cubic geometry for container ships. Designed to enable a higher degree of automation during construction, this solution maximises the space available for cargo, helping improve overall vessel economics.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Navy has awarded contracts for a total of seven Landing Craft Utility (LCU) hulls to a trio of yards on the Gulf Coast, all of them outside of the small circle of traditional defense shipbuilders. In an announcement Tuesday, the Navy said that it would be spending $280 million to build seven "prototype" hulls for the LCU-1700 program at Master Boat Builders, Conrad Shipyard and Saronic's future Brownsville "Port Alpha" shipyard. The first two firms are well-established commercial shipbuilders known for their workboats. The latter has a focus on autonomous vessels, not series-production landing craft, and the order will be its first at its new mega-facility in Texas. "Understanding the urgency of the moment, Saronic is helping address the critical backlog facing America’s shipyards with one of Port Alpha’s first builds. We are tackling the quick production of a vital manned vessel the Navy needs today as we ramp to meet the needs of an autonomous maritime future," said Saronic Co-Founder and CEO Dino Mavrookas. LCU 1700 has been in the works for a long time, and the predecessor LCU 1610 class hulls have now been in service for more than 50 years. It is an upgraded design with more range, more payload capacity, and better berthing arrangements for the small crew. The original LCU 1700 design-build contract was signed in 2018 with Swiftships, a Gulf Coast boatbuilder with a history dating back to the Second World War. The agreement envisioned a series of up to 32 hulls, but the Navy ended the contract in 2024. Swiftships filed for bankrupcy earlier this year. In a separate framework agreement signed in 2023, the Navy awarded Austal USA an order for up to 12 hulls. After exercising options, Austal now has five firm orders, and the first in class - LCU 1710 - began sea trials in February and delivered last month.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: O ex-vereador Milton Leite (União Brasil) recebe, em junho de 2025, o Colar de Honra ao Mérito Legislativo, a maior honraria da Alesp — Foto: Divulgação/Alesp Milton Leite, do União Brasil, é um dos políticos mais tradicionais — e poderosos — de São Paulo. Ocupou uma cadeira na Câmara Municipal da capital por 27 anos, entre 1997 e 2024, e presidiu o Legislativo paulistano por quatro vezes . Com 70 anos, ele começou na política em 1990. Quando jovem, chegou a ser filiado ao PCB, mas pouco depois ingressou no MDB. Ao longo da carreira, construiu sua principal base eleitoral na Zona Sul da capital, especialmente no Grajaú. Nas eleições de 2020, foi o segundo vereador mais votado da cidade, com 132.716 votos . Naquele ano, sua campanha foi a que mais gastou entre os candidatos à Câmara, com despesas de cerca de R$ 2,5 milhões. Segundo o site da Câmara, ele já ocupou o cargo de prefeito em exercício da capital por cerca de cem dias, tornando-se o presidente da Câmara que mais vezes chefiou o Executivo desde a redemocratização. Leite também acumulou influência dentro do Legislativo paulistano. Foi presidente da Câmara pela primeira vez entre 2017 e 2019, durante a gestão de João Doria na prefeitura, e voltou ao comando da Casa por três mandatos consecutivos. Em dezembro de 2022, foi novamente eleito para a presidência, com 47 dos 55 votos dos vereadores. Naquele período, uma mudança na Lei Orgânica do Município permitiu uma segunda reeleição para a presidência da Câmara. A eleição também contou com um acordo de representação entre as bancadas, que garantiu espaço para PT, PL e Republicanos na Mesa Diretora.
