https://safety4sea.com/shipping-groups-u.text: Eight major shipping organisations have called on EU Member States to support the inclusion of two Indian ship recycling facilities on the European List, arguing that yards meeting the bloc’s safety and environmental requirements should be assessed on evidence rather than their non-OECD status. I n an open letter to EU Environment and Transport Ministers, BIMCO, Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA), European Shipowners | ECSA, the International Chamber of Shipping (ICS), INTERCARGO, INTERFERRY, INTERTANKO and the World Shipping Council (WSC) urged Member States to deliver a positive opinion on the European Commission’s proposal. At the centre of the appeal is a broader question for the ship recycling industry: whether facilities outside the OECD should be eligible for the European List when they can demonstrate compliance with the standards established under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation (EU SRR). The organisations said the proposed inclusion of the two Indian facilities follows years of investment since the Hong Kong Convention (HKC) was adopted in 2009. According to the groups, the yards have invested significantly in infrastructure, safety systems and environmental management in order to meet the requirements of both the HKC and EU SRR. They argue that this reflects the objective of the EU regulation itself: reducing differences in workplace health and safety and environmental standards between recycling facilities in the EU, OECD countries and relevant third countries, while supporting the application of internationally recognised standards.

https://safety4sea.com/cruise-fleet-move.text: The cruise industry is continuing to shift away from conventional marine fuels while expanding the technology needed to cut emissions and improve environmental performance, according to the latest annual report from the Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA). T he association’s Environmental Technologies and Practices (ETP) report points to progress across several areas, including greater use of non-HFO fuels, wider shore power readiness, more fuel-flexible ships, improved energy efficiency, advanced wastewater treatment and increased onboard freshwater production. Cruise lines are also testing and piloting biofuels as they prepare for a wider transition towards lower-emission energy sources. CLIA President and CEO Bud Darr said the industry’s progress reflects sustained investment in new technologies and operational capabilities, ranging from more efficient ships and multi-fuel engines to shore power and advanced environmental systems. The latest figures point to a transition that is increasingly moving beyond individual technologies. While cruise lines are expanding what ships can do onboard, the pace and scale of the wider transition will also depend on whether the fuel, port and energy infrastructure needed to support those technologies develops alongside the fleet. The cruise industry is continuing to invest in technologies aimed at reducing emissions and improving resource efficiency, with the latest CLIA data showing growth in multi-fuel capability, shore power connectivity, lower-emission fuels, NOx treatment and onboard water and waste systems. The number of CLIA-member ships equipped with multi-fuel engines capable of switching between conventional fuels and zero- or near-zero-emission fuels has risen from one in 2018 to 30 today.

https://safety4sea.com/tokyo-mou-weighs-.text: Port State Control authorities across the Asia-Pacific are confronting a shipping landscape becoming more complex by the year, from the rise of shadow fleets and fraudulent ship registrations to geopolitical tensions, the energy transition and rapidly developing technologies. T hose challenges were at the centre of discussions as the Tokyo MOU Port State Control Committee held its 37th meeting in Singapore from 7–10 September 2026, bringing together maritime authorities from across the region to discuss how port State control should respond to the industry’s evolving risks. The meeting, chaired by Kenny Crawford, Manager of Maritime Safety Assurance at the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), was officially opened by Ang Wee Keong, Chief Executive of Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority (MPA). Ang highlighted the progress made by the Tokyo MOU over three decades while stressing the need for closer cooperation among maritime stakeholders as new operational, regulatory and security challenges emerge. The discussions followed the 20th meeting of the Tokyo MOU Technical Working Group, held on 3–4 September, which examined issues ranging from PSC procedures and inspection guidelines to concentrated inspection campaigns, information exchange and technical cooperation. The Tokyo MOU is considering stronger measures against under-performing ships after the Port State Control Committee noted with concern that their number has increased over the past three years. The Committee also discussed developing a common framework to support Member Authorities considering national legislation that would prohibit certain ships from entering their ports.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/iam-union.text: The IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers) says that its members at General Dynamics NASSCO have ratified a new three-year collective bargaining agreement covering more than 800 shipbuilders in San Diego. The agreement comes less than a month after IAM Local S6 Members at GD Bath Iron Works ratified a new five-year labor agreement ( see earlier story ). The union says that the agreement with NASSCO delivers a 10% wage increase in the first year, followed by increases of 5% in the second year and 4% in the third year – raising wages by nearly 20% over the life of the contract. The new contract also includes what the union describes as “significant” retirement improvements, including an increase in the 401(k) contribution to 5% and an increase in the pension multiplier to $57. Members also secured an additional floating holiday and stronger language covering attendance, seniority, life insurance, and disability benefits. Additional economic gains include a $2 increase in working preman pay and a $1 increase in leadman pay. The agreement maintains the current employee cost share for the Kaiser HMO/EPO, Kaiser HSA and alternative health plans. Under the SIMNSA plan, the company will pay 95% of the cost, with employees contributing 5%.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/saronic-t.text: The first vessels to be built at Port Alpha — autonomous vessel innovator Saronic Technologies’ next-generation shipyard in Brownsville, Texas —will be Landing Craft Utility (LCU) vessels. Saronic reports has been awarded a contract by the U.S. Navy to construct the LCU vessels under a firm fixed-price agreement executed as an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) award.; LCUs are a core Navy logistics vessel, used to move troops, vehicles, and cargo from ships offshore directly onto a beach or unimproved shoreline without the need for a port or pier. The LCUs have heavy-lift capability with a 170-ton payload capacity, able to carry cargo from amphibious ships across open water, shore-to-shore, and back again, with a range of roughly 1,200 nautical miles. This capability is central to amphibious operations, resupply, and disaster-response missions. The demand for this type of connector is rising from the Marine Corps and Navy, as the existing, aging fleet is actively being replaced. Saronic will now support the delivery of multiple LCUs to address the Navy’s needs under the current program of record, with the OT structure allowing the service to move expeditiously to get the company under contract. “This award reflects the kind of partnership we set out to build with the Navy, where speed, cost discipline, and a modern industrial base reinforce each other,” said Saronic co-founder and CEO, Dino Mavrookas. “Port Alpha is designed to produce large autonomous surface vessels alongside currently manned ships, supporting the Navy’s hybrid fleet strategy while adding surge capacity to the broader U.S. maritime industrial base. “Understanding the urgency of the moment, Saronic is helping address the critical backlog facing America’s shipyards with one of Port Alpha’s first builds. We are tackling the quick production of a vital manned vessel the Navy needs today as we ramp to meet the needs of an autonomous maritime future.”

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/petrobra.text: Brazil’s state-owned energy giant Petrobras has struck a two-decade-long deal with Sempra Infrastructure, a subsidiary of Sempra, for the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from a U.S. project under development in Jefferson County, Texas. Sempra Infrastructure has signed a 20-year sales and purchase agreement (SPA) with Petrobras to supply approximately 0.8 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG, which will be sourced from the developer’s contracted liquefaction capacity at the Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 project, currently under construction in Jefferson County, Texas. Justin Bird , CEO of Sempra Infrastructure, commented: “We are pleased to welcome Petrobras as the first South American company in our LNG customer portfolio, marking an important milestone for Sempra Infrastructure’s growing LNG business. “This long-term agreement establishes a strategic relationship with one of the world’s leading energy companies and underscores the important role Sempra Infrastructure plays in providing reliable and secure U.S. natural gas to a growing list of customers around the world.” With two liquefaction trains capable of producing around 13 mtpa of LNG, which will increase the total liquefaction capacity from about 13 mtpa for Phase 1 to up to approximately 26 mtpa, Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 reached a positive final investment decision in September 2025 . Port Arthur LNG Phase 1, which is also currently under construction , is anticipated to achieve commercial operations at or near the end of 2027 and in 2028 for trains 1 and 2, respectively.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy continues its campaign of attacking vessels and exploiting the incidents to assert that it has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. While it continues to exaggerate the claims in its propaganda warfare, it appears to have an effect, as the confirmed transits through the Strait of Hormuz remain low. In its latest report, it said a Togo-flagged tanker, Trend , was attacked. The IRGC claims the vessel was set ablaze and stopped from its “illegal passage.” It was the third report of a tanker attacked this week. Rear Admiral Ali Ozmaei announced the attack and used it to emphasize his position that Iran “continues to maintain control over the waterway.” He went on to say that any vessel attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz “illegally would face destruction.” He reiterated Iran’s position that vessels should not attempt to transit “without explicit authorization.” The vessel that was identified, Trend , is a small product tanker, 7,119 dwt. Built in 2008, it has been managed for the past few years out of the UAE. Its last AIS position was shown as being anchored off the UAE as of September 15. With most vessels making the transit “dark,” it is harder to verify the claims of attacks. However, UK Maritime Trade Operations did receive information today that a tanker had been hit by a projectile that caused a fire. It was advised, however, that the fire was out and there were no reports of injuries to the crew. The report to UKMTO placed the vessel 16 nautical miles northwest of the Omani coast near Khasab. UKMTO also received a delayed report of another attack on Wednesday, September 16. It said a tanker was reported struck, but had few other details. This has been consistent with most of the recent reports, which are delayed and lacking details. Oman only confirmed on Tuesday that it had helped evacuate the crew from another tanker that appeared to have been attacked several days earlier.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Maersk is moving forward with a large new ship order, equivalent to approximately 10 percent of the carrier’s current total capacity in operation. The news comes after days of speculation in the industry that Maersk was placing large orders and adjusting its strategy, which over the past few years has mostly focused on fleet renewal. “We can confirm that Maersk has ordered 26 large container vessels as part of our ongoing fleet renewal program,” a spokesperson for Maersk told The Maritime Executive on Friday. The carrier has not yet made a public announcement, and so far details are still left to speculation. The company confirmed, however, that the new vessels will have a capacity of 18,600 TEU and will be equipped with dual-fuel engines able to operate on liquefied gas. The vessels are expected to be delivered in 2029 and 2030. The new vessels will be among the largest in the Maersk fleet, as the carrier so far has not followed others in the industry in the jump to ultra-large container vessels with a capacity of 24,000 TEU. Maersk’s largest vessels are the Triple E Class, which was introduced between 2013 and 2019, with a capacity ranging between 18,270 TEU and 20,568 TEU between two groups in the class. Maersk in February 2026 announced its previous large ship order with China’s New Times Shipbuilding Company. That order was for eight large vessels for delivery in 2029 and 2030, as well as possible options that are now being reported. The ships will be equipped with dual-fuel engines for conventional bunker fuel or liquefied gas and have a capacity for 18,600 TEU. Analysts at Linerlytica and Alphaliner had started much of the speculation in recent days about a major new shipbuilding effort. In addition to expanding the order for the 18.600 TEU vessels, Linerlytica wrote that Maersk was in fact making the jump with orders in China for vessels with capacities of 24,000 and 19,000 TEU. Alphaliner also believed that Maersk was negotiating for a class of vessels with a capacity of at least 24,000 TEU. Some of the reports speculated that the total for the next phase of the new ship program was 40 or more vessels valued at upwards of $9 billion.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The Philippine Coast Guard is reporting another incident between one of the country’s supply vessels and a China Coast Guard vessel near the disputed Spratly Islands shoals used by the Philippines for fishing. The Philippine vessel sustained damage to deck railings from the collision but reported no injuries to its crew, while the Chinese quickly issued statements saying the collision was the fault of the Philippine vessel. The incident took place on September 18, approximately 54 nautical miles from Palawan province in the Philippines and a little over six nautical miles from Sabina Shoal. Both the Philippines and China claim the region, while the Philippines points to international decisions in its favor and its long heritage of fishing in this region. The Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat was on one of its regular resupply missions to the fishermen, where it delivers fuel and food supplies. Yesterday, the vessel had briefly gone aground near another portion of the shoals while working to supply 15 to 20 fishing boats. The Philippine Coast Guard said the incident happened during the morning low tide, and one of its vessels assisted in pulling the supply boat free later in the day. The Chinese regularly monitor the operations, and there are frequent interactions between the two countries’ vessels. Yesterday, the Philippine Coast Guard said a China Coast Guard aircraft had challenged them during the refloating operation. Simultaneously, the Coast Guard reported that three China Coast Guard vessels, a warship from the People’s Liberation Army Navy, and three Chinese Maritime Militia vessels were all observed in the area of another Filipino supply vessel, Mamalakaya , as it serviced 35 fishing boats. The Philippine Coast Guard conducted an overflight and said the Chinese issued a radio challenge. To call this unprofessional or bullying would be an understatement. They said the Chinese boat first cut across the stern of the Philippine boat at a distance of only about 10 meters (33 feet). About nine minutes later is says the Chinese vessel made contact with the BFAR vessel while asserting the Philippine vessel was maintaining its course. Later, it says the Chinese vessel made another pass astern of the Philippine vessel at a distance of only about 5 meters (16 feet).

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: O governo da Venezuela e a oposição estão perto de fechar um acordo para transferir as reservas de ouro do banco central venezuelano, avaliadas em cerca de US$ 4 bilhões (cerca de R$ 21,8 bilhões), do Banco da Inglaterra para o Federal Reserve Bank de Nova York , informou o Financial Times nesta quinta-feira. Segundo o jornal britânico, a proposta em discussão prevê que o governo interino liderado por Delcy Rodríguez obtenha o controle legal sobre o ouro, mas sem autorização para vender imediatamente os ativos. De acordo com pessoas familiarizadas com as negociações ouvidas pelo Financial Times, as reservas poderiam ser usadas como garantia para a obtenção de empréstimos destinados a financiar gastos públicos e a reconstrução do país após os terremotos que atingiram a Venezuela em junho.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 18/09/2026 – O novo Sistema de Acompanhamento de Investimentos (SAI) foi divulgado pela Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) nesta quinta-feira (17), no auditório do Departamento Nacional de Infraestrutura de Transportes (DNIT), em Brasília (DF). O workshop foi promovido pela Superintendência de Fiscalização e Coordenação (SFC) da Agência, com o objetivo de apresentar a ferramenta que tornará mais organizado e integrado o acompanhamento dos investimentos previstos em contratos de arrendamento e nos contratos de adesão. A Agência apresentou as funcionalidades do sistema, os perfis de acesso e as etapas do fluxo de acompanhamento. O SAI substitui o envio manual do Relatório de Acompanhamento de Projeto de Investimento Realizado (RAPIR) em PDF por um fluxo digital padronizado. Em um único ambiente, ficam reunidos os contratos e os respectivos acompanhamentos enviados pelos regulados, permitindo o cadastro, o envio, a análise e a aprovação das informações. Segundo o gerente de Planejamento e Inteligência da Fiscalização da ANTAQ, Pedro Soares, a criação do SAI partiu de uma necessidade identificada no acompanhamento dos investimentos. Até então, as empresas preenchiam o RAPIR e encaminhavam o documento à Agência, o que dificultava a consolidação e a comparação das informações. O novo sistema transforma essas informações em uma base estruturada. Para as empresas, a ferramenta oferece um ambiente único, com validações automáticas e notificações a cada etapa. Para a fiscalização, permite acompanhar a carteira de investimentos de forma segura. Entre os recursos apresentados estão o preenchimento de informações financeiras e físicas dos investimentos, notificações automáticas por e-mail, validações realizadas pelo próprio sistema e registro das alterações efetuadas, com informações sobre usuário, data e valores. O fluxo envolve diferentes perfis, como regulado, autoridade portuária, fiscal e outorga. Conforme a etapa, é possível analisar, aprovar ou devolver o acompanhamento para correção, com registro das justificativas e comunicação automática aos responsáveis. Em contratos de adesão, o envio segue diretamente do Regulado para a Fiscalização. A apresentação também mostrou o painel financeiro do SAI, que reúne informações da carteira de investimentos e permite visualizar a evolução dos recursos, a distribuição por região e dados dos contratos monitorados.

https://gcaptain.com/another-tanker-suff.text: (Bloomberg) — A liquefied natural gas tanker bringing fuel from the US to Europe suffered a systems failure that the crew reported as a suspected cyber attack, according to people familiar with the matter. In the latest of a number of potential cybersecurity incidents on tankers, the Vivit Africa LNG was sailing east in the Mediterranean and Adriatic Seas toward Italy early this month when the crew were suddenly unable to access some of the internal control systems, the people said, asking not be identified because the information was not public. Trading giant Vitol Group confirmed that it has the ship under a long-term lease known as a time charter, without commenting further. After idling off the coast of Italy without discharging its cargo, the vessel on Wednesday began sailing away from its intended destination of Rovigo, heading back toward the Spanish port of Algeciras near the entrance to the Mediterranean, according to shipping data compiled by Bloomberg. The crew reported the incident early last week to Korean Register, the organization that acts as the technical and safety adviser to the South Korean-owned vessel, and investigations are ongoing, the people said. There are no indications of who the perpetrator of the suspected attack may be, they said. Korean Register and the owner of the Vivit Africa LNG, South Korea’s H-Line Shipping Co. Ltd., didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

UK Maritime Trade Operations has issued three attack warnings covering incidents in the Strait since September 16, including two tankers struck by projectiles and another security incident near Khasab, Oman. One attack has been claimed by Iran. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said Thursday it struck the Togo-flagged tanker Trend after accusing the vessel of attempting an unauthorized transit through Hormuz. Iran said the ship was hit and stopped after a fire broke out. UKMTO separately reported an attack 16 nautical miles northeast of Khasab on Sept. 17. The crew was reported safe. Two more warnings followed Friday. One tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, causing a fire that was later extinguished. Another tanker was hit by an unknown projectile while outbound through Hormuz on September 16. In both cases, crews were reported safe.

https://gcaptain.com/londons-marine-insu.text: A serviceman of Ukraine's coast guard mans a gun on a patrol boat as a cargo ship passes by in the Black Sea, amid Russia’s attack on Ukraine, February 7, 2024. REUTERS/Thomas Peter//File Photo LONDON, Sept 18 (Reuters) – London’s marine insurance market has widened the area in the Black Sea it deems as ?high risk as the Ukraine-Russia conflict escalates, according to an advisory issued this week. The Black Sea is a vital route for ?shipments of grain, crude oil and refined products. Its waters are shared by Russia and Ukraine as well as Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania and Turkey. Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on each other’s commercial shipping in the past two months, in an escalation of their war, now in its fifth year. The Joint War Committee (JWC) comprises syndicate members from the ?Lloyd’s Market Association and representatives from the London insurance company market and its guidance influences underwriters’ considerations over insurance premiums. “This week, the JWC has expanded the Black Sea reporting requirements to the whole of the Black Sea area. The coastal waters of Russia and Ukraine were already listed,” Neil Roberts, head of marine and aviation at the LMA and secretary of the Joint War Committee, said on Thursday in a note accompanying the advisory.

https://gcaptain.com/shippings-new-norma.text: By Lori-Ann LaRocco – It’s a good time to be an ocean carrier or tanker owner. The slower trade caused by bottlenecks stemming from the U.S. war with Iran, Russia’s war in Ukraine, and the Panama Canal’s El Niño water-mitigation measures has fueled soaring tanker profits and the never-ending surcharges imposed by ocean carriers. “Disruption is no longer the exception,” said Richard Meade, editor-in-chief of Lloyd’s List. “It is becoming the business model over the past week. Shipping’s strongest markets are increasingly being shaped not by economics alone, but by geopolitics, security, and strategic uncertainty.” Cashing in on uncertainty is nothing new in maritime. We have seen soaring profits during previous disruptions. They get larger with each disruption. The $1.10 million per day for a VLCC on the Saudi Arabia/Arabian Gulf-to-China route on September 15 is just one example. “VLCC earnings approaching a million dollars today were almost unthinkable not so long ago,” said Meade. “Yet a combination of business disruption, long-term crew trades, and tightened vessel availability has quickly shown how geopolitics can overwhelm traditional market fundamentals concepts as outdated as supply and demand.” Lloyd’s List senior reporter Greg Miller explained during the company’s weekly webinar that this tanker cycle far exceeds the shipping supercycle of the 2000s.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/lng.text: A liquefied natural gas tanker transporting fuel from the United States to Europe experienced a systems failure early this month that the crew reported as a suspected cyber attack, according to a Bloomberg report Friday. The Vivit Africa LNG was sailing east in the Mediterranean and Adriatic Seas toward Italy when the crew suddenly lost access to some internal control systems, the report added. Trading company Vitol Group reportedly confirmed it has the ship under a long-term lease known as a time charter but did not provide additional comments. After stopping off the coast of Italy without unloading its cargo, the vessel on Wednesday began sailing away from its intended destination of Rovigo. The ship headed back toward the Spanish port of Algeciras near the entrance to the Mediterranean, according to shipping data compiled by Bloomberg. The crew reported the incident early last week to Korean Register, the organization that serves as the technical and safety adviser to the South Korean-owned vessel. Investigations are ongoing. There are no indications of who the perpetrator of the suspected attack may be. The suspected hacking follows other incidents in late August, when two oil and gas tankers off the US coast were boarded by the Coast Guard and Federal Bureau of Investigation due to potential cyberattacks. American officials are monitoring nearly 20 ships around the world for such threats.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/italian-.text: Italy's defence minister on Friday called for a stronger naval presence in the Red Sea to protect merchant shipping amid concerns over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital waterway threatened by the widening Middle East conflict. The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen have made rapid advances in recent weeks along the Red Sea coast, further complicating routes in a region that also includes the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic had already dwindled because of the U.S.-Iran war. Italy, part of the European Union's Aspides mission, launched in 2024 to protect shipping from Houthi attacks, on Thursday said it was preparing a naval mission in the area, saying it could not wait for the EU to respond to the new crisis. "After what I said, something moved within Aspides, but we need more ships," Defence Minister Guido Crosetto, a senior ally of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, told Reuters. "The only nations really supporting (security efforts) are Italy and Greece," he said, declining to estimate how many vessels would be needed to secure the area. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is 18 miles (29 km) wide at its narrowest point and is one of the world's most important maritime routes, carrying goods and commodities from Asia to Europe through the Suez Canal.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/new-cont.text: French provider of tubular solutions Vallourec has won a contract with Subsea7 to supply carbon steel seamless line pipe and thermal insulation coating for Petrobras’ Sepia 2 project in the pre-salt Santos Basin offshore Brazil. The award, described as major, will see Vallourec supply approximately 130 kilometers of rigid risers and flowlines, representing more than 15,000 tons of sour service carbon steel line pipe. The pipes will be produced at the company’s Jeceaba mill in Minas Gerais, Brazil, with the related thermal insulation coating applied at the Vallourec Coating Solutions plant in Serra, Espírito Santo. Philippe Guillemot , Chairman of the Board of Directors and CEO of Vallourec Group, said: “This contract illustrates the strength of Vallourec’s integrated offering, combining premium seamless line pipe and advanced thermal insulation coating. It confirms our position as a partner of choice for the most demanding pre-salt developments and showcases the excellence of our fully integrated industrial footprint in Brazil, from our Jeceaba mill to our Serra coating plant. I thank Subsea7 and Petrobras for this new mark of confidence, which rewards the dedication of our teams.” Sepia 2 is located in ultra-deep waters of the Santos Basin, a pre-salt area approximately 280 kilometers from the Brazilian coast. It comprises 15 wells, as well as an export pipeline connected to a new floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel, to be installed in a water depth of approximately 2,170 meters. Shortly after this announcement, Vallourec reported it was selected by EnEarth, a subsidiary of Energean, to deliver a comprehensive package of premium tubular solutions, including seamless carbon steel and corrosion-resistant alloy (CRA) casing pipes equipped with VAM premium connections for the first phase of the Prinos CO2 carbon storage project offshore Greece, covering approximately 3,000 tons of casing pipes and accessories. The scope also includes CLEANWELL, Vallourec’s dope-free solution.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/hanwha-o.text: The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS), a classification society, has handed out approval in principle (AIP) for a multi-purpose fuel tank and fuel gas supply system design that enables a liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier (LNGC) to shift from LNG to ammonia fuel without replacing the fuel tank or fuel gas supply system (FGSS). Hanwha Ocean has received ABS’ approval in principle that covers the fuel tank and integrated fuel gas supply system for an electrically propelled LNG carrier powered by a gas turbine. According to the classification society, which reviewed the design against relevant class and international requirements, the system is designed to supply either LNG or ammonia to the gas turbine, enabling transition from LNG to ammonia fuel. Gareth Burton , ABS Senior Vice President of Global Engineering, commented: “Fuel flexibility is a practical requirement for owners navigating an evolving regulatory environment, and the engineering challenge of achieving it without tank replacement is significant. “This design addresses that challenge directly, and ABS is pleased to support Hanwha Ocean in verifying the concept’s feasibility against applicable requirements.” ABS describes this approval as the latest development in a series of related projects with Hanwha Ocean, including AiP for an ammonia gas turbine propulsion system in 2023 and gas dispersion study of a 174,000 cbm LNG carrier with an ammonia gas turbine in 2024.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/exmars-f.text: An approval in principle (AiP) from Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore (BV), part of Bureau Veritas Group, is paving the way for Belgian shipping company Exmar to breathe life into its floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) concept, which is based on the conversion of an existing membrane-type LNG carrier. Exmar has been awarded AiP by Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore for its FLNG conversion design, which is created to enable offshore gas processing, liquefaction and LNG storage based on a membrane-type LNG carrier with an effective LNG storage capacity of approximately 170,000 cubic meters (cbm) and a design life of 25 years. David Barrow , SVP for Western Europe and Americas at Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore, commented: “Floating liquefaction solutions already play an important role in unlocking offshore gas resources and supporting the development of energy projects in a flexible and cost-effective manner. “We are pleased to grant approval in principle to Exmar’s FLNG conversion concept, which demonstrates how existing LNG carrier assets can be repurposed to support future offshore developments. This project highlights how collaboration across the industry can drive innovative and practical solutions that combine technical feasibility with project efficiency.” The concept has been assessed against applicable Bureau Veritas requirements for offshore production gas units. The review focused on the hull structure and stability, the existing LNG cargo containment system, and the FLNG mooring arrangement. The AiP demonstrates the potential viability of adapting existing membrane LNG carrier assets into floating liquefaction facilities, providing an alternative pathway to develop offshore gas resources while supporting efficient project execution and diversifying energy supply.

https://petronoticias.com.br/petrobras-b.text: A Petrobrás celebrou nesta semana a cerimônia de batismo da embarcação Starnav Elektra. Construído pelo Estaleiro Detroit, em Itajaí (SC), o navio do tipo PSV (Platform Supply Vessel) recebeu investimentos de aproximadamente R$ 450 milhões e é a primeira embarcação entregue pelo Programa Mar Aberto, iniciativa voltada à renovação e ampliação da frota do Sistema Petrobrás. A embarcação seguirá agora para atuar junto às plataformas das bacias petrolíferas brasileiras. O Starnav realizou a viagem entre Santa Catarina e o Rio de Janeiro com uma tripulação 100% feminina. Sob o comando de Isabela Teixeira Ponce de Leon, a equipe embarcada é formada por 16 mulheres. A cerimônia de batismo aconteceu no Armazém do Porto do Rio, no Píer Mauá. Durante a cerimônia, a presidente da Petrobrás, Magda Chambriard , afirmou que os investimentos realizados pela companhia na indústria naval e offshore contribuem para impulsionar um novo ciclo de negócios e oportunidades para o setor, além de ampliar o retorno sobre o capital da companhia. “ São projetos que nos trazem mais eficiência e lucro. Quando utilizamos nossa própria frota estamos economizando recursos e valorizando o portfólio da Petrobras ”, disse. A executiva também reiterou o compromisso da companhia com a renovação de sua frota, com o objetivo de assegurar segurança e continuidade para a indústria nacional. “ Essa primeira entrega comprova o que nós prometemos e cumprimos. São 48 barcos contratados até o final desse ano. Até o ano que vem, vamos alcançar um total de 96 embarcações, incluindo barcaças e empurradores. As empresas brasileiras estão tendo um desempenho excelente e estão vencendo todas as licitações ”, destacou. © 2026 Petronotícias. Todos os direitos reservados. Montagem e manutenção ECCE.COM.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: One of the few large offshore wind projects proceeding in the United States, Revolution Wind completed the installation of its 65th and final wind turbine. The project began delivering power in March despite repeated opposition from the Trump administration and now expects to complete its commissioning by the end of the year. Revolution Wind is being developed in a 50-50 partnership between Orsted and Global Infrastructure Partners’ Skyborn Renewables. Media reports indicate it represents an investment of $6.2 billion to develop and will become the third large, commercial-scale offshore wind farm in the United States to be completed. It is located in Rhode Island Sound, not too far from the Vineyard Wind and South Fork Wind projects, which have already been completed and commissioned. The project received its final approvals in November 2023 after the companies noted more than nine years of planning and permitting. It has 20-year power purchase agreements to deliver 400 MW to Rhode Island and 304 MW to Connecticut. The project started offshore construction in 2024, and by August 2025 it was reported to be nearly 80 percent complete. The first of its turbines was installed in September 2024, and by August 2025, Revolution Wind said 45 of the 65 Siemens Gamesa turbines were installed. The Trump administration issued its first stop-work order to the project that same month, claiming irregularities in the permitting. The project went to court and, a month later, received a preliminary injunction against the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management from enforcing the order. Revolution Wind, however, was also included in the December 2025 move by the Department of the Interior, which ordered all five of the under-construction wind farms to stop work, this time citing undefined issues for potential interference from the turbines with radar and national security. Revolution Wind won a second injunction early in 2026 that permitted it to resume work again. By March 2026, the project was reporting that it was more than 90 percent complete and that several key construction scopes were finished. By the middle of the month, it had begun delivering power to the grid, but the developers kept a lower profile after their two confrontations with the administration.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Somalia’s fledgling navy is reporting the rescue of seafarers from a bulker in distress. Details of the incident are incomplete, but it is being cited as an example of the government’s efforts to enhance maritime security in a troubled area of the world. The Ministry of Ports and Maritime Transport said on September 17 it was monitoring the grounding of a bulker, which was also taking on water. It said there were 18 crewmembers from India, Syria, and Egypt aboard the vessel but did not provide details on the location of the incident. The ship was identified as the Jacuar (IMO 9181821) sailing under the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Equasis shows the vessel, which was built in 1998, is under Turkish ownership and management. It is 8,556 dwt and 100 meters (328 feet) in length. The ship has a troubled history, showing years of deficiencies in port state inspections. In December 2025, Egyptian authorities cited deck corrosion and problems with the gauges in the engine room. Authorities in Jordan detained the ship in September 2024 and April 2025, citing safety issues. Somalia’s maritime authority did not say what had caused the grounding. It said the ship was carrying 7,007 tonnes of an unidentified cargo sailing from Mozambique to Egypt. The Navy reported the rescue of the crewmembers on September 18. Media reports are saying the vessel capsized. Again, there was no indication of which region of Somalia the ship was located, or confirmation that it had capsized.

South Africa is hoping to boost the fortunes and competitiveness of its East London river port. Port operator Transnet has decided to build a liquefied natural gas (LNG) import terminal at the facility. Located at the mouth of the Buffalo River, the Port of East London is the only commercial river port in South Africa. Though consisting of diversified cargo handling facilities for containers, bulk liquids, dry bulk free-flowing grains, and general breakbulk, the port’s core business has been supporting the region's automotive manufacturing sector as the main export hub. Last year, Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA) completed a $3.6 million project to deepen and strengthen the port’s automotive terminal, allowing two new-generation automotive vessels greater than 200 meters (656 feet) in length to berth simultaneously and increasing the port’s capacity to handle 790,000 units annually. In terms of containers, ongoing investments aim to increase the port’s handling capacity to over 100,000 TEU from roughly 30,000 TEU currently. TNPA wants to further boost the Port of East London’s competitiveness after launching a tender seeking a private operator to invest in a small- to medium-scale LNG terminal. The operator will design, finance, develop, construct, operate, maintain, and transfer the terminal under a 25-year concession agreement. TNPA did not reveal the costs of the project, but stated the facility will be transferred to the state entity upon expiry of the concession. The terminal will be used for receiving and dispatching LNG via vessels, pipelines, and tankers and will incorporate facilities like storage tanks and other terminal infrastructure. It will be built on a greenfield site of approximately 8,900 square hectares located within the port’s West Bank precinct. Currently, the precinct accommodates the automotive terminal, the dry bulk terminal, and a tanker berth. TNPA is highlighting that the LNG terminal forms part of its strategic direction to advance the port’s infrastructure development and support diversification for the future energy demand in the Eastern Cape, where demand for natural gas has been on the rise. Specifically, the terminal is expected to provide a reliable energy solution for niche LNG consumers and industrial users while reinforcing the port’s role in enabling industrial growth, job creation, and economic growth.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: The Houthi takeover of parts of the Red Sea gives the armed group a new platform to challenge global shipping. The group has taken over the port of Mocha, the island of Mayyun, and the Zuqar and Hanish archipelago about 160km north of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. These areas were previously controlled by Yemeni government forces. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is a narrow maritime chokepoint roughly 32km wide. Lying between the Arabian Peninsula to the north-east and the Horn of Africa to the south-west, it directly links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. This geography matters. Mayyun Island, for example, divides a waterway that is used by international shipping. Historically, this passage accounts for about 12% of global trade. The African side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait hasn’t been taken over by the Houthis. But the group’s September 2026 advance has serious economic and security implications for Egypt, Ethiopia, Djibouti and Eritrea, with the potential to escalate existing conflicts in Somalia and Sudan. The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed movement that controls much of Yemen, and has been fighting the country’s internationally recognised government since seizing the capital in 2014. I have studied global maritime geopolitics and security, including issues involving the Red Sea, for more than two decades. In my view, the Houthi threat is not just a logistical one. It also poses a strategic danger to Africa’s Red Sea states. The African shoreline is suddenly much more valuable to outsiders who want to monitor, contain or outflank the waterway opposite them. The Houthis now occupy armed posts around the strait, bringing the threat closer to the critical shipping corridor.

https://g1.globo.com/tecnologia/noticia/.text: O Discord continua permitindo que usuários no Brasil utilizem serviços que possibilitam a transmissão de vídeo em tempo real e o compartilhamento de tela. A brecha foi identificada mais de um mês após a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) determinar a suspensão imediata de todas as transmissões ao vivo na plataforma no Brasil. A GloboNews encontrou pelo menos duas ferramentas disponíveis na seção nativa de "atividades" do Discord que seguem plenamente funcionais para usuários brasileiros, sem qualquer restrição técnica ou bloqueio geográfico aparente. Os recursos permitem o espelhamento de tela e a exibição de imagens em tempo real durante chamadas de voz e em servidores.

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: O presidente americano Donald Trump anunciou nesta sexta-feira (18) um acordo com a Dinamarca. Os EUA controlarão a segurança da Groenlândia "para sempre". A ilha integrou-se à Dinamarca em 1953 e obteve autonomia em 2009. Os EUA tentaram comprar o território estratégico após a Segunda Guerra Mundial por US$ 100 milhões. A Groenlândia é rica em minerais e monitora ameaças navais da Rússia. O aquecimento do Ártico abre rotas marítimas que também atraem o interesse da China. O acordo veta bases militares de adversários dos EUA na ilha. Embora os governos celebrem o tratado, apenas 6% dos habitantes locais apoiam a incorporação aos EUA.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/the.text: Operational Overview Saudi Arabia’s workaround to the partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz came under direct attack last week. Saudi Arabia diverted crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu via the East-West pipeline. On September 10, a pumping station on the pipeline was attacked and preemptively shut down. On the same day, Houthi forces seized Mokha, followed by the Hanish Islands and, by September 11, Perim Island at the center of the Bab el-Mandeb, where the Strait narrows to approximately 20 kilometers. VLCC spot rates to transit Hormuz and load inside the Middle East Gulf crossed $1 million per day, equivalent to approximately $26 per barrel against a normal freight share of 1 to 3%. U.S. forces struck five IRGC-linked tankers on September 8, with Iran responding by attacking a tanker in Iraqi waters with a drone. Windward assesses the operational risk environment across the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, northern Middle East Gulf, and Somali basin as critical. U.S. Forces Strike Five Iranian Tankers, Iran Retaliates On September 5, U.S. Central Command struck three Iranian crude oil carriers after the IRGC launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy warships. M/T DOWNY (IMO 9218480) was permanently disabled off Kharg Island, M/T STARK 1 (IMO 9171450) near Jask, and the unladen M/T KYLO (IMO 9189146), also known as NOXEN, was completely destroyed in the Gulf of Oman and later sank after its crew was directed to abandon ship. Three days later, on September 8, U.S. forces struck five more IRGC-linked oil tankers, bringing confirmed strikes across the two rounds to eight vessels. The vessels struck were M/T DERYA (IMO 9569700), M/T KAVIZ (IMO 9282041), M/T HORIZON 1 (IMO 9130456), M/T CHARMINAR (IMO 9318022), and M/T RIESCO (IMO 9251822). HORIZON 1 is a Palau-flagged 115-meter LPG tanker carrying a high-risk designation. Vortexa data shows it laden with 37,400 barrels in floating storage. The vessel had been anchoring in the Strait of Hormuz East Waiting Area since August 30, transmitting AIS only intermittently. Imagery as of September 9 shows the vessel dark with no damage present, and smoke visible from the funnel.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ira.text: Iran and Oman have almost finalised an agreement on a shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz, but this does not mean the strait will be reopened, said Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesperson for the Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. In August, the Iranian Foreign Ministry said Iran and Oman had agreed to work on establishing a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and jointly clearing mines along the route, while continuing discussions on a permanent shipping corridor through the currently closed strait. “The issue of the agreement with Oman regarding the corridor in the Strait of Hormuz, meaning the vessel traffic system, has been almost fully worked out. We reiterate that the agreement on the corridor in the Strait of Hormuz does not mean it will be opened. The Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States (US) accepts and fulfils Iran’s conditions,” Ghashghavi said. Iranian armed forces will continue to control the Strait of Hormuz until the US fulfils the “conditions defined based on the 14-point Islamabad Memorandum” signed by Tehran and Washington in June, the politician added. On Feb 28, the US and Israel began striking targets in Iran, prompting Tehran to launch retaliatory strikes. In mid-June, Tehran and Washington signed a memorandum to cease hostilities, but resumed exchanging strikes shortly afterwards. At present, the conflict remains unresolved.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ita.text: Italy is preparing to deploy warships to protect its commercial vessels travelling through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, as growing Houthi control over the key Red Sea chokepoint threatens international shipping and has squeezed Saudi Arabia’s ability to use the route as an alternative pathway for oil exports. According to Al Jazeera, Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said Rome would move ahead with measures to safeguard its merchant vessels rather than wait for the European Union to reach a joint decision. He warned that allowing the strategic waterway to become impassable could have serious consequences for the global economy. “We have the capabilities to protect the passage,” said Crosetto, arguing that Italy could not allow bureaucratic delays in decision-making to worsen an already volatile situation. The planned Italian deployment comes as the Iran-backed Houthi movement has expanded its hold over Yemen’s western Red Sea coastline, including strategically important territory and islands around the Bab el-Mandeb. The group’s growing presence has raised concerns over the safety of commercial vessels and the movement of energy supplies through the waterway. For Saudi Arabia, the developments are particularly significant. Riyadh has increasingly relied on the Red Sea as an alternative export corridor after disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, using pipelines to transport crude towards its Red Sea ports before sending tankers through Bab el-Mandeb to international markets. That makes Bab el-Mandeb one of the remaining critical routes for Gulf oil reaching consumers outside the region. Greater Houthi control of the waterway therefore threatens to further restrict Saudi Arabia’s options for moving crude at a time when the kingdom is already facing severe disruption to its traditional export routes. The strait connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and forms an important maritime link between the Indian Ocean, the Suez Canal and European markets. It is one of the world’s key shipping chokepoints, carrying energy shipments, container vessels and other commercial traffic between Asia and Europe. The narrow passage lies between Yemen on one side and Djibouti and Eritrea on the African coast. At its narrowest point, it is only around 30 kilometres wide, making control of the surrounding coastline and islands strategically important for anyone seeking to influence maritime traffic.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/worley-h.text: Australia’s engineering firm Worley has delivered front-end engineering designs (FEEDs) for two critical infrastructure packages related to a multibillion-dollar liquefied natural gas (LNG) and carbon capture and storage (CCS) development project in Indonesia’s Masela block, operated by Inpex Masela, a subsidiary of Japan’s Inpex. Worley is assisting in the development of Inpex’s Abadi LNG project , a planned energy development under Indonesia’s Proyek Strategis Nasional (National Strategic Project) program. The project is expected to contribute to Indonesia’s energy security and support its net zero 2060 goals. The engineering firm’s scope included front-end engineering design for two key offshore infrastructure packages in the Masela Block, covering approximately 150 kilometers of subsea infrastructure, gas export pipelines, and CCS pipelines. Don MacLeod , President of Global Operations – APAC, commented: “We’re pleased to support Inpex to progress this significant development for Indonesia. Our work to successfully deliver the FEEDs demonstrates how Worley brings together deep local knowledge and specialist expertise from across our global business to help advance complex energy developments.” Led by the company’s team in Indonesia, the FEEDs were delivered with specialists from the Subsea Centre of Excellence in Singapore and teams in Perth and Malaysia, developing an integrated infrastructure concept. This brings together subsea facilities, gas export pipelines, and CCS pipelines, supporting a coordinated approach to strengthen energy security while supporting lower-carbon outcomes.​ The Abadi LNG project is expected to produce about 9.5 million tonnes of LNG annually and incorporate CCS to meet regional energy demand while contributing to the country’s emission-reduction goals. Inpex Masela is the operator of the Abadi LNG project with a 65% interest, while its partners are Pertamina (20%) and Petronas (15%), following Shell’s exit in 2023 .

https://petronoticias.com.br/apresentaca.text: A retomada dos investimentos em embarcações e o aumento da atividade offshore no Brasil estão movimentando a cadeia de serviços marítimos e criando novas oportunidades para empresas que atuam no apoio às operações de óleo e gás. É este cenário que a Camorim Serviços Marítimos vai levar à ROG.e 2026, a partir de segunda-feira, no Riocentro, no Rio de Janeiro. A empresa fará sobre os mais de R$ 250 milhões já investidos em 2026 na expansão e modernização de sua frota. O valor contempla investimentos em quatro novos rebocadores azimutais , em um Fast Supply Vessel (FSV) e em uma das maiores cábreas da América Latina. A estratégia acompanha um mercado que volta a demandar novas embarcações e serviços especializados para dar suporte ao crescimento das atividades marítimas. A expectativa é que haja novos investimentos ainda este ano. No segmento offshore, a Camorim opera atualmente 24 embarcações de apoio. A frota inclui platform supply vessels (PSVs), embarcações de resposta a derramamento de óleo (OSRV), line handlers (LHs), uma embarcação de acomodação (MPSV), além de um fast supply vessel (FSV) adquirido recentemente. O movimento da indústria também aparece nos planos da Petrobrás. Em maio deste ano, a companhia assinou contratos de R$ 11 bilhões para a construção, afretamento e operação de quatro embarcações de apoio offshore, com expectativa de geração de cerca de 7 mil empregos diretos e indiretos. O Plano de Negócios 2026-2030 da estatal prevê ainda o afretamento de 40 novas embarcações de apoio para a renovação da frota de suporte às atividades de exploração e produção. Para a Camorim, esse cenário representa uma oportunidade de ampliar sua participação em uma cadeia que passa por um novo ciclo de investimentos. A companhia vem diversificando sua atuação e ampliando sua capacidade para atender às diferentes demandas das operações marítimas. “Estamos acompanhando de perto esse novo momento do mercado e entendemos que é preciso estar preparado para as oportunidades que estão surgindo. Os investimentos que estamos realizando fazem parte de uma estratégia de longo prazo para ampliar nossa capacidade, modernizar nossa estrutura e atender às necessidades dos nossos clientes”, afirma Eduardo Adami, vice-presidente da Camorim Serviços Marítimos. Além da expansão da frota, a companhia vem acompanhando outros desafios estruturais do setor, como a necessidade de profissionais qualificados para atender ao crescimento das atividades marítimas. “ A participação na ROG.e acontece em um momento estratégico para a Camorim. Queremos aproveitar o principal encontro da indústria de óleo e gás no Brasil para estreitar relacionamentos, apresentar nossa estratégia de crescimento e discutir as transformações que estão impactando a cadeia de serviços marítimos” , ressalta

https://www.marinelink.com/news/exmar-fl.text: Exmar has received Approval in Principle (AiP) from Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore for a concept to convert an existing membrane-type LNG carrier into a floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) unit for offshore gas developments. The FLNG concept would use a membrane-type LNG carrier with an effective LNG storage capacity of about 170,000 cubic meters and a design life of 25 years. Designed for operation in mild environments, the converted vessel would provide offshore gas processing, liquefaction and LNG storage and is intended for the development of stranded gas resources. The concept is aimed at projects seeking lower initial capital requirements and shorter timelines between final investment decision and production by converting an existing LNG carrier rather than constructing a new vessel. Bureau Veritas assessed the concept against applicable requirements for offshore production gas units, liquefied gas carriers and position-keeping systems. The review at this stage covered the hull structure and stability, existing LNG cargo containment system and FLNG mooring arrangement. “Floating liquefaction solutions already play an important role in unlocking offshore gas resources and supporting the development of energy projects in a flexible and cost-effective manner. We are pleased to grant Approval in Principle (AiP) to Exmar’s FLNG conversion concept, which demonstrates how existing LNG carrier assets can be repurposed to support future offshore developments,” said David Barrow, SVP for Western Europe and Americas at Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore.

https://gcaptain.com/world-running-short.text: Pipelines run down the deck of Hin Leong's Pu Tuo San VLCC supertanker in the waters off Jurong Island in Singapore July 11, 2019. Picture taken July 11, 2019. REUTERS/Edgar Su Sep 19, 2026 (Bloomberg) –The soaring cost of moving oil around the world is making some long-distance crude trades uneconomical, threatening to disrupt flows at a time when fuel markets have never been tighter. The jump is being driven by a shortage of available supertankers . In some parts of the world, there are barely any of the ships — each the length of three football fields — left for hire. The squeeze is making faraway barrels less attractive and encouraging refiners to snap up supplies closer to home if they can find them. Moving a cargo from Houston to Asia now adds about $26 a barrel — $52 million a cargo — to the cost of supplying the world’s largest crude-importing region. That’s equal to roughly a quarter of the price of West Texas Intermediate futures. Before the war, shipping typically accounted for only a tiny fraction of the cost. The rally is minting fortunes for the small group of shipowners that dominate the tanker market — several industry executives and brokers said the surge would previously have been unimaginable. The value of the world’s largest oil tanker equities soared to a record of almost $70 billion this week. But for oil traders, the risk is that shipping becoming prohibitively expensive. They’re concerned that the higher costs make it unprofitable for some refiners to turn crude into fuels, deterring them from buying cargoes that have to sail over long distances , even when demand to make diesel and gasoline is strong.

https://petronoticias.com.br/arabia-saud.text: A rápida expansão dos terroristas houthis perto do estreito do Mar Vermelho evidencia uma aliança coordenada com o Irã, o Iraque e outros parceiros, que lhes proporciona capacidades militares e apoio estratégico. Há informações de ajuda militar vinda da Rússia e também da China. Nos últimos dias, os terroristas assumiram o controle das ilhas Hanish Maior e Hanish Menor, no sul do Mar Vermelho, dando continuidade ao seu rápido avanço que permitiu à organização controlar efetivamente o estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, de importância estratégica. No início deste mês, suas forças capturaram a estratégica cidade portuária de Mocha, expulsando as forças ligadas ao Conselho de Liderança Presidencial (PLC), grupo com ligações com a Arábia Saudita. Também tomaram a Ilha de Perim, localizada diretamente dentro do estreito, e as ilhas de Zuqar, mais ao norte. As milícias xiitas apoiadas pelo Irã estão agora localizadas no ponto mais estreito do litoral, a apenas 20 km da costa africana. Isso lhes proporciona, e por extensão à aliança regional liderada pelo Irã da qual fazem parte, um controle efetivo sobre o tráfego marítimo que atravessa o Golfo de Aden em direção ao Mar Vermelho. Em declarações feitas durante o avanço, os houthis deixaram claro que pretendem atacar navios sauditas no estreito, em vez de instituir um bloqueio naval geral. O avanço dos houthis foi acompanhado por um ataque de drones de uma milícia xiita iraquiana contra o oleoduto leste-oeste da Arábia Saudita em 10 de setembro. O oleoduto servia como meio de transporte de petróleo para o Mar Vermelho, permitindo que Riad evitasse o Estreito de Ormuz, alvo de ataques iranianos. A previsão é de que fique fora de serviço por três a cinco semanas. O preço do Petróleo Brent futuro está cotado a US$ 103,19 o barril, enquanto o petróleo WTI futuro opera próximo a US$ 99,53. A ação coordenada entre as milícias xiitas iraquianas e os houthis visa claramente ampliar a capacidade da aliança liderada pelo Irã de impor regras ao tráfego marítimo entre o Mar de Ormuz e o Mar Vermelho. O foco na Arábia Saudita (que iniciou a atual rodada de confrontos com o ataque ao aeroporto de Sanaa em julho) evita provocar uma retaliação dos EUA, que um esforço mais amplo para bloquear o Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb poderia desencadear. Os eventos dos últimos dias demonstram a capacidade contínua do bloco regional liderado pelo Irã de agir de forma coordenada em prol de objetivos comuns. Enquanto Israel castigou e enfraqueceu drasticamente (embora não tenha destruído) os aliados do Irã no Levante, mais ao sul, na região do Golfo, Teerã e seus aliados continuam em plena atividade. Os houthis, assim como o Hamas, diferentemente do Hezbollah libanês ou iraquiano, não são uma franquia direta ou um grupo representativo da Guarda Revol

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Às vésperas do primeiro turno das eleições, a ONU Mulheres, braço da Organização das Nações Unidas, publicou um documento com propostas para candidatas, candidatos, partidos políticos, instituições públicas e toda a sociedade. As medidas buscam reduzir a violência e as desigualdades de gênero e incluem temas como participação política, violência contra as mulheres, trabalho, cuidado e crise climática. Segundo a entidade, o documento busca ampliar o debate público e apresentar caminhos para transformar direitos reconhecidos em políticas públicas. https://gcaptain.com/us-tariffs-threaten.text: Sep 19, 2026 (Bloomberg) –The American Century often draws a crowd when the ship pulls into the Port of Duluth-Superior to load Minnesota iron ore. Kids cheer when the captain blasts the fog horn. A voice on the loudspeaker retells the story of how the 1,000-foot-long bulk carrier has sailed the Great Lakes for nearly a half century. It’s a momentary flashback to the waning days of US industrial primacy. The vessel was built in 1981 in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, and runs on four General Motors Co. diesel engines that generate more horsepower than a dozen Formula 1 cars. It set records for coal payloads in the 1990s. The current owner is American Steamship Co., a unit of Mainstay Maritime that’s based in Williamsville, New York, and was founded in Buffalo in 1907. But for all the Made-in-America pride, aging “lakers” like American Century have depended on a regional economy that moved in lockstep with Canada. Coal volumes have hit hard times, and US tariffs have disrupted trade in iron ore. Adding to the uncertainty now is a rift between Ottawa and Washington that threatens lasting damage to supply chains across land and water geared for free-flowing commerce. “Hope isn’t a strategy, but we would expect that this trade war comes to an end at some point and we can get back to regular business,” said Kevin Beardsley, executive director of the Duluth Seaway Port Authority, located less than 200 miles from the Canadian border. “Canada is looking at different supply chains and that type of thing, and that is a risk the longer this goes on.” President Donald Trump has offered mixed messages recently, saying in Ireland last weekend that there may be a deal with Canada “fairly soon” but issued fresh threats when asked this week about Ottawa’s overtures to the European Union. Prime Minister Mark Carney told Bloomberg News on Monday that Canada is “ready to sit down” for talks. That would come as welcome relief to those who depend on waterborne cargo between by both countries.

https://splash247.com/trump-signs-russia.text: President Donald Trump signed sweeping new sanctions legislation on Friday targeting Moscow’s oil trade and the tanker fleet that supports it. The White House confirmed Trump had signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, expanding statutory sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions against Russia while extending existing measures against Iran. For shipping, the most important provisions directly target Russia’s shadow fleet and give Washington powers to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from major buyers of Russian oil and gas. China and India, the two dominant destinations for Russian crude, are consequently at the centre of attention, although the legislation does not mean such tariffs are automatically imposed immediately. Beijing reacted quickly. China’s Ministry of Commerce said it opposed unilateral and secondary sanctions and would closely monitor Washington’s next moves, adding that it reserved the right to take measures to protect Chinese companies and national interests.

https://splash247.com/crew-claims-hacker.text: A US LNG cargo bound for Italy has been diverted after the crew of its carrier reported a systems failure as a suspected cyberattack, adding to growing concerns over attacks on shipboard digital systems. The Liberia-flagged Vivit Africa LNG, owned by South Korea’s H-Line Shipping and on long-term charter to commodities giant Vitol, had loaded at the Cameron LNG export terminal in Louisiana and was approaching the Adriatic earlier this month when crew lost access to some internal control systems. The ship subsequently idled off Italy without discharging before abandoning its planned call at the Adriatic LNG terminal near Rovigo and heading west again towards Algeciras. The crew reported the incident to class society Korean Register, and an investigation is continuing. In an email sent to Splash , members of the crew described a serious sequence of events. “We have determined that the vessel was targeted by cyber attackers prior to berthing at this terminal,” the crew wrote, saying the initial attack was intended to compromise the ship’s control systems.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/denmark-.text: King Frederik X of Denmark has opened the first full-scale CO2 storage site in the EU, led by INEOS Energy, with partners Harbour Energy and the Danish North Sea Fund (Nordsøfonden). Project Greensand was in December 2022 granted an exploration permit for the injection and storage of up to 15,000 tons of CO2 in Nini West over a four-month period. This was followed by a world first on March 8, 2023, with the first-ever injection of CO2 in the North Sea . INEOS, the day-to-day operator, and its partners reached the final investment decision (FID) in December 2024 to invest in the Greensand Future Project, the first commercial phase of the Greensand project. Then, in December 2025, the Danish Energy Agency issued its first-ever approval for a full-scale CO2 storage facility , clearing the Greensand Future project to store CO2. His Majesty King Frederik X of Denmark today, September 18, officially opened the first full-scale facility for the permanent storage of CO2 in the EU, with the ceremony at the Port of Esbjerg, marking Greensand’s move into commercial operation. Mads Gade , CEO of INEOS Energy Europe, said: “Greensand starts with biogenic CO2, but its significance reaches far beyond that first step. We are ready to expand capacity to receive CO2 from industries across Europe. https://gcaptain.com/deluge-of-copper-ar.text: Sep 18, 2026 (Bloomberg) –There’s nothing outwardly remarkable about the journey of the Nord Norfolk, a Liberian-flagged bulk carrier sailing across the Atlantic toward New Orleans. But the boat is loaded with roughly half a billion dollars of African copper, the highest market value for a single commodity shipment ever recorded by analytics firm Kpler. It’s part of a rush of copper to US shores ahead of potential import tariffs, a deluge that’s key ports are struggling to absorb. The Port of New Orleans — a key metals gateway and major hub for CME Group’s Comex copper warehouses — is already largely full, according to people familiar with the matter. And that’s before a total of around 100,000 metric tons more of African and South American copper they say is due to arrive in September and October. “We are seeing serious congestion at marine terminals in the New Orleans area, causing delays for loading copper and other metals and steel to trucks and railcars,” said Anton Posner, chief executive officer of logistics-services provider Mercury Resources. His firm is sending metal up the Mississippi by barge instead. The $500 million boatload and the New Orleans logjam are part of a long drama playing out in the global copper market as traders brace for President Donald Trump to decide whether to expand copper import levies to refined metal. He hasn’t done so months after a decision was expected, and the metal is still pouring in for now. The strength of US copper imports has been the key force behind a record-breaking rally in copper prices, with the global benchmark set on the London Metal Exchange climbing about 50% since Trump first formally proposed tariffs on the metal in February last year. US futures have rallied even more sharply, creating huge arbitrage profits for the traders and producers that have been shipping copper to the US in record volumes.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/vlc.text: The question is particularly timely, as VLCC spot earnings have reached record levels in recent weeks. The Baltic Exchange International Tanker Routes (BITR) Time Charter Equivalent earnings have surpassed $1,000,000 per day for the Middle East to China route assessment, with spot earnings on routes outside of the Middle East earning as much as $400,000 per day. The Suezmax market is following a similar trajectory, with spot market earnings higher than ever before. For owners, the choice between remaining exposed to the very firm spot market and fixing a vessel on a fixed income time charter has therefore become an important strategic decision. Time charters can provide certainty and downside protection, while spot exposure can provide greater upside when markets strengthen. For owners navigating an increasingly volatile market, the challenge is finding the right balance between these competing priorities while retaining enough flexibility to respond to opportunities as they arise. Pooling provides a way for owners to retain access to the spot market while benefiting from the scale, expertise and diversification of a larger fleet. Rather than simply choosing between the certainty of a time charter and the full exposure of operating independently in the spot market, owners can participate in a broader commercial platform designed to navigate changing conditions. The scale of the pool provides revenue stability during volatile market conditions. . A weaker result on one voyage can be balanced by stronger performance elsewhere across the fleet, with participants also gaining access to market intelligence and trading opportunities that may be harder to capture independently. The current market is a reminder of how quickly vessel earnings can change. Predicting exactly when rates will rise or fall is difficult, making flexibility increasingly valuable.

The AIM-listed company operates Q10-A with a 60% interest. The field, about 22 km offshore the Netherlands, started production in January 2019 and currently has six producing wells. Gas is exported from the platform through a 42 km pipeline to TAQA-operated P15-D for processing. The development dates back to a 2018 EPCI award to Heerema Fabrication Group for the unmanned Q10-A platform, then being developed by Tulip Oil, which was subsequently acquired by Kistos.

https://splash247.com/italian-owner-augu.text: Italian product tanker owner Augusta Due has signed for three 40,800 dwt oil and chemical tankers in China as the Mednav Group company pushes ahead with a wider fleet renewal programme. The Rome-based owner has signed the contract with Anhui Port & Shipping Sealand Equipment, part of Tongling Port and Shipping Group. Neither pricing nor delivery dates have been disclosed. The ships will offer about 48,500 cu m of cargo capacity spread across six pairs of cargo tanks, supported by seven independent cargo transfer lines. They have been designed to carry chemicals as well as crude and refined petroleum products covered by MARPOL Annex I. Main and auxiliary engines will be able to burn low-sulphur fuel oil, marine gasoil and biofuel blends, with SCR equipment fitted to meet IMO Tier III requirements. Augusta Due has been active in product and chemical tankers since 1994 and operates both owned and chartered tonnage ranging from about 3,000 dwt to 42,000 dwt, largely serving oil majors and trading houses in the Mediterranean market. The Brullo family-controlled company has already been adding modern Chinese-built tonnage. It took the 18,500 dwt Primo M from Fujian Southeast Shipbuilding in early 2025 and followed with the 18,590 dwt Ginostra M later that year as part of a programme to replace older ships.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/pro.text: US-based startup Demeter Energy plans to build a 100,000 mt/year bio-methanol production plant at the Port of Manatee (SeaPort Manatee) in Florida. SeaPort Manatee is a deepwater port at the entrance to Tampa Bay on the eastern Gulf of Mexico, with access to trade routes through the Panama Canal. The planned facility is expected to produce up to 100,000 mt/year of bio-methanol from woody biomass and other organic waste, targeting demand from the shipping sector as well as other industries. The plant will also include a carbon capture and storage (CCS) system designed to capture around 200,000 mt/year of CO2 generated during the production process. SeaPort Manatee provides the infrastructure, logistics and market access needed to develop the project, Demeter Energy chief executive Tom Walklett said. Demeter Energy has not specified a development or production timeline for the project.

https://splash247.com/henghui-books-up-t.text: China’s Henghui Shipping has signed for up to four 38,000 dwt multipurpose heavylift vessels at Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery, expanding ZPMC’s push into specialised project cargo ships. The deal covers two firm vessels plus two options. Neither pricing nor delivery dates have been disclosed.The ships will carry three 250-tonne cranes giving a combined lifting capacity of 500 tonnes. They will also feature two extended cargo holds, the longest measuring 76.8 m, together with a continuous open deck aimed at oversized machinery and project cargo. The design includes rudder bulbs, wake-equalising ducts and a high-voltage shore power system alongside hull optimisation aimed at cutting fuel consumption. ZPMC only entered the multipurpose heavylift newbuilding market two years ago. Its first order came from Chinese-Polish operator Chipolbrok in August 2024 for two firm plus two optional 38,000 dwt ships, also fitted with three 250-tonne cranes. ZPMC has since moved the Chipolbrok programme into construction, while the Chinese-Polish owner has separately continued expanding its heavy-lift fleet with larger ships at other Chinese yards.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/rus.text: Russia and Ukraine launched major drone attacks against each other over the weekend, killing civilians on both sides and striking a Moscow oil refinery as attacks on energy infrastructure continued, Reuters reported. Russian authorities said two people were killed in the Moscow region during what Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described as one of the biggest Ukrainian drone attacks on the area. Russia said it had downed more than 1,600 drones since Saturday, including 450 headed toward Moscow. Several drones reached the Moscow oil refinery, with Reuters witnesses reporting blasts and plumes of smoke from the facility. The extent of the damage was not immediately clear, and Ukraine had not commented on the attack. The refinery processed 11.6 million metric tons of crude in 2024, producing 2.9 million tons of gasoline and 3.2 million tons of diesel. Ukrainian strikes have already disrupted Russian refining capacity, contributing to fuel shortages and higher prices in parts of the country. The attack came on the final day of Russia’s parliamentary elections. Sobyanin claimed the drone operation was intended to disrupt voting. In the wider Moscow region, authorities evacuated 400 people, including 70 children, from a 21-storey apartment building in Ramenskoye after the attacks. In Ukraine, an overnight Russian drone attack killed four people, including three children, in the Kyiv region. Emergency services said a mother and her two three-year-old children died after a drone struck a private home. Another girl died in hospital following a separate strike.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mar.text: A total of 61 MaritimeONE scholarships were awarded by sponsors from the industry, including maritime companies, unions, associations, and foundations at the MaritimeONE Scholarship Award Ceremony 2026 held last evening by the Singapore Maritime Foundation (SMF). Mr. Murali Pillai, Senior Minister of State, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Transport, was the Guest-of-Honour. This year, more than S$1.5 million was contributed by 45 sponsoring organisations spanning shipping, port operations, maritime services, marine and offshore, associations, classification societies, and foundations (see Annex A).
