https://splash247.com/asyad-sheds-ageing.text: Oman’s Asyad Shipping has agreed to sell three of the oldest tankers in its fleet for a combined OMR68.44m ($178m) as the Muscat-listed owner accelerates the replacement of ageing tonnage with a large slate of newbuildings. The company is selling the 2011-built VLCCs Seeb and Samail for a combined OMR61.7m ($160.5m). A separate transaction covers the 2008-built MR product tanker Al Amerat at OMR6.74m ($17.5m). The 319,439 dwt Seeb was built at South Korea’s DSME, while the 302,845 dwt Samail came from Japan. Al Amerat is a 51,022 dwt STX-built product tanker delivered in December 2008. The VLCC disposals effectively clear out the last of Asyad’s 2011-built crude carriers. The company agreed late last year to sell sister-vintage VLCC Saiq for OMR23m ($60m), with the transaction completed in the first half of 2026. Asyad expected the disposal to generate an approximately OMR8m ($20m) positive earnings impact and said it would continue looking for opportunities to sell older ships and recycle the proceeds into fleet expansion. The latest sales come as Asyad moves quickly in the opposite direction at the younger end of the fleet. Splash reported in January that the company ordered another three 300,000 dwt VLCCs at Hanwha Ocean for about $388.5m, with delivery in 2028 and 2029. The trio added to four VLCCs ordered at the Korean yard in 2024 for roughly $130m each.

https://splash247.com/ate-energy-brings-.text: Taiwanese offshore engineering player ATE Energy International has brought its new cable-laying vessel Oceanus 1 into service, adding another locally based installation asset to the country’s growing offshore energy supply chain. The Taiwan-flagged DPS-2 vessel arrived in Kaohsiung on September 16 following handover from Vietnam’s Pacific Shipbuilding, with Singapore-based Synergy Marine Group taking on technical and crew management. Oceanus 1 is equipped with an 8,000-tonne cable carousel, a 250-tonne hydraulic A-frame, a 40-tonne service crane and jet-plough capability that allows simultaneous cable installation and burial. An SMD Quasar III work-class ROV will support subsea survey and touchdown monitoring. The vessel can accommodate up to 77 crew and project personnel. ATE will oversee deployment and cable-lay operations through its submarine cables division. Mermaid Subsea Services Thailand is also lined up to support project management for cable campaigns, subject to securing the relevant offshore projects and contracts. No initial vessel assignment has been disclosed. The arrival adds to a rapidly expanding Taiwanese offshore construction fleet. Dong Fang Offshore is also building out its cable-laying capability, with another large CLV due in the first quarter of 2027 after the company moved to replace capacity tied up under a long-term DeepOcean charter in Europe.

https://splash247.com/cadeler-expands-of.text: Cadeler’s offshore wind services platform Nexra has signed a memorandum of understanding with Vattenfall to develop new methods for maintaining large offshore turbines. The companies will focus on major component exchanges, including replacing heavy turbine parts such as blades, nacelles, and gearboxes. Their work will examine how specialist vessels, equipment, service procedures and long-term maintenance planning can be combined to reduce downtime and improve execution. The agreement comes as Europe’s offshore wind fleet moves from construction into longer-term operations. As turbines age, operators face more frequent major repairs, and each intervention can require costly vessel campaigns and periods of lost power generation. Nexra and Vattenfall said they will assess solutions that can be applied across different turbine platforms and scaled across multiple wind farms. Safety, maintenance predictability and asset availability will be key areas of the collaboration. “The offshore wind industry is entering a new phase, with a growing installed base and increasingly complex maintenance needs. This collaboration gives us an opportunity to explore new approaches to major component exchange,” said Jacob Christian Gregersen, Cadeler’s chief growth officer. The MoU does not include details of a firm contract, specific vessels or investment commitments. Cadeler has been expanding Nexra’s O&M activity, with its vessels already undertaking maintenance campaigns in Europe and Asia.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: All users of AI are familiar with its tendency to produce false results from time to time, particularly when using older, lower-end chatbots. While more recent frontier models are less likely to feed out made-up results, they are still capable of error, which is why corporate adopters emphasize that accountability for the product remains with the human who delivers it - not the AI agent behind the scenes. The U.S. military also uses AI extensively for data analysis, and nearly got drawn into launching an armed boarding of a Chinese cargo ship because of an AI intel program's hallucination earlier this year, according to CNN. In the wrong circumstances, it was the kind of mistake that could have launched a broader conflict; since it was caught in time, it was merely a misuse of resources. Four sources with knowledge of the episode told CNN that a military intel analyst's report flagged a Chinese cargo ship operating in the Mideast during the height of the Iran conflict. According to this report - formatted like any other - this cargo ship had nuclear weapons components on board. Commanders received and treated the report as though it were accurate, and began preparations to interdict and board the vessel - which, if carried out, would almost certainly spark a significant diplomatic incident with China. The effort got so far along that there were military aircraft aloft and boarding teams getting ready to go for the interdiction. The report, however, was wrong from the start. An analyst had used an AI chatbot to ask about some intelligence data related to the suspect ship's cargo manifest. The chatbot drew on classified data and open-source intelligence, then made up a conclusion: it decided that the vessel was carrying components for a nuclear weapons program, CNN's sources said. This was false, but the analyst did not detect that; instead, they packaged it up for formal use - again using AI for formatting - and sent it up the chain of command. In the run-up to the interdiction operation, officials examined the analyst's intelligence report more closely and determined that AI had been used to come up with the contents. They figured out that the chatbot had misidentified the Chinese vessel's cargo, and halted the operation before any action on the water occurred. The Chinese vessel continued on its commercial voyage, and the AI "hallucination"-inspired intercept effort became a cautionary tale rather than a potential flashpoint in an already tense situation in the Mideast. But CNN's sources said that comparable errors had happened before, and warned that there are no standardized, joint guidelines for catching AI mistakes during one of the military's most consequential data processes - target identification and selection.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/e.text: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has called for a substantial increase in the European commitment to maritime security patrols in the Red Sea. After recent aggression by Yemen's Houthi rebel faction, she suggested, it is time for a 10-warship EU mission in the region. In a letter released over the weekend, Kallas called for EU member states to increase their contributions to the Operation Aspides security mission. The Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and tanker traffic have contributed to the global rise in energy prices, with effects on the European economy and EU shipping interests. Even though the Houthis have repeatedly claimed that they will only attack Saudi vessels, they have hit Western-linked shipping many times in years past - and they have an inconsistent record when it comes to targeting, occasionally striking vessels linked to their own allies. On Monday, Kallas told Reuters that Operation Aspides - the EUNAVFOR security force in the Red Sea - needs "more naval and more air assets to address the increased level of threats in the region." She noted that the original plan for Aspides when it was created in 2024 called for a 10-ship force; it is currently operating with six warships, and the Houthis are now better-positioned than ever to threaten shipping. Kallas' call for more EU involvement complements the messaging from IMO, where Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez has recently appealed to member states to make stronger diplomatic efforts to protect the safety of seafarers. "It falls to you and your capitals, and relevant bodies of the United Nations, to address the root causes [of maritime security risk] and find solutions,” Dominguez said in an address to member state delegates last week.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543143-pt.text: Thai’s state oil firm PTTEP and Valeura Energy have taken a final investment decision on the first phase of the Bussabong gas development in the Gulf of Thailand, targeting first production around the end of 2028 from a 25-well development. Bussabong lies in the eastern part of Block G3/65, where Valeura is set to hold a 40% non-operated working interest and PTTEP Energy Development Company is the operator. The initial development will comprise two wellhead platforms with 24 well slots each, installed in water depths of 75 to 90 metres towards the northern end of the field. The platforms will be connected through a 12-inch, nine-km subsea pipeline to existing gas processing infrastructure at the PTTEP-operated Bongkot field in neighbouring Block G2/61. No additional processing capacity is required to accommodate Bussabong production. The operator plans to drill 25 development wells, with Phase 1 intended to deliver sales gas production of about 30 million cubic feet per day in 2029, rising to around 40 mmcf/d in 2030. Valeura's 40% share would amount to 12 mmcf/d and 16 mmcf/d, respectively. Gas from the field is expected to be relatively dry, based on samples collected during exploration drilling, with about 20 barrels of condensate per million cubic feet of gas.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543138-bo.text: Bounty Oil & Gas has agreed to acquire PetroQuest Liberia Deep Water, giving it a pathway to an interest in deepwater Block LB-32 offshore Liberia, while raising about $2.5 million (A$3.55 million) to advance the acquisition and exploration work. PetroQuest does not currently hold a granted license or executed production sharing contract for LB-32. It holds a letter of engagement with Liberia's National Oil Company, NOCAL, giving it the exclusive right to negotiate a PSC for the block, with PetroQuest acting as the pre-qualified applicant before the Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority. The 2,322-square-kilometre block lies in the Harper Basin in water depths of about 1,500 to 4,200 meters and borders LB-30 and LB-31 to the west. LB-32 is covered by about 656 square kilometers of 3D seismic and 753 line-km of 2D seismic. The 3D coverage forms the eastern portion of TGS's approximately 6,167-square-kilometre Sunfish survey, and Bounty intends to license the LB-32 data as the first step towards due diligence, prospective resource assessment and potential farm-out preparations. The principal exploration target is the Upper Cretaceous basin-floor fan play, including portions of the Jupiter and Zeus fan systems. Bounty said the Jupiter Turonian fan is interpreted in published third-party material to extend into LB-32, while the Cenomanian Zeus fan lies near the LB-31/LB-32 boundary. The company has not yet directly reviewed the 3D seismic and will not report prospective resources for LB-32 until it has acquired the data and commissioned an independent evaluation by a qualified petroleum reserves and resources evaluator.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543137-eu.text: The European Union will maintain its opposition to new oil and gas drilling in the Arctic, a European Commission spokesperson said on Monday, despite Norwegian pressure to drop the EU ban. The EU currently supports a ban on new drilling in the Arctic, over environmental concerns, including the risk posed to sensitive Arctic ecosystems by industrial activities and pollution. It is facing calls from Norway to change this stance in an upcoming revision of the EU's policy on the Arctic. "The EU remains committed to the approach set out in the 2021 Joint Communication on the EU Arctic Policy," a spokesperson for the European Commission told Reuters on Monday, adding that work is ongoing on the revised policy. The document the spokesperson referred to sets out the EU position: it says the bloc supports a ban on further Arctic oil and gas development and will not purchase such hydrocarbons. Norway is Europe's biggest gas supplier. Norway, which is not an EU member, has been pushing Brussels to drop the moratorium. With many ageing fields, Norwegian production is set to decline in the 2030s unless companies such as Equinor (EQNR.OL) make new discoveries outside mature areas.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543139-to.text: Namibia has selected TotalEnergies bidding group to supply the country's bulk diesel and petrol needs for a three-month period from November to January, energy minister Modestus Amutse said late on Monday. The Southern African country earlier in September said it would not renew an exclusive fuel supply agreement with global commodities trader Vitol after extending it through October. The new deal involves the supply of approximately 345 million liters of fuel in total, comprising mainly diesel. The winning bid offered an average discount of 63.85 cents on every liter and a saving of approximately 220.5 million Namibian dollars ($13.57 million), Minister of Industries, Mines and Energy Amutse said. The main fuel suppliers in Namibia are national oil company Namcor, TotalEnergies, Vitol's Vivo Energy, Trafigura's Puma and newcomer Nasan Energies. "The ministry will continue to use open competition to buy the country's fuel on the best possible terms without ever putting security of supply at risk," Amutse said in a recorded video message.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543140-fo.text: Brazilian state-run oil company Petrobras' analysis of oil discovered at the Morpho exploration well in the offshore Foz do Amazonas basin showed it to be "very high quality" crude, an executive told Reuters on Monday. The crude found at the well could prove superior to oil produced from Brazil's prolific pre-salt fields, Petrobras' director of engineering, technology and innovation, Renata Baruzzi, said on the sidelines of an event in Rio de Janeiro. Baruzzi added that Petrobras expects an exploration campaign at nearby wells to begin next year. The area is part of Brazil's Equatorial Margin, which the company considers its most promising exploration frontier. (Reuters - Reporting by Rodrigo Viga Gaier; Writing by Isabel Teles; Editing by Gabriel Araujo)

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT) iniciou os procedimentos para suspensão cautelar do Registro Nacional de Transportadores Rodoviários de Cargas (RNTRC) de empresas que descumprem de forma reiterada a Política Nacional de Pisos Mínimos do Transporte Rodoviário de Cargas. A medida pode ser aplicada a transportadores com mais de quatro autuações, em datas distintas, no período de seis meses, quando houver risco de continuidade da infração, prejuízo à fiscalização ou comprometimento da política de piso mínimo. Os casos serão analisados individualmente e as empresas identificadas serão formalmente notificadas. Os atos de suspensão serão publicados no Diário Oficial da União e passarão a produzir efeitos 72 horas depois. O período da suspensão cautelar será de cinco a 30 dias, conforme os critérios estabelecidos pela regulamentação. A fiscalização é conduzida pela Superintendência de Fiscalização de Serviços de Transporte Rodoviário de Cargas e Passageiros (Sufis) e pela Superintendência de Serviços de Transporte Rodoviário e Multimodal de Cargas (Suroc). A regra foi reforçada pela Medida Provisória nº 1.343/2026 e pela Resolução ANTT nº 6.077/2026. Outro mecanismo adotado em 2026 foi a ampliação da obrigatoriedade do Código Identificador da Operação de Transporte (CIOT), que passou a abranger todas as operações de transporte rodoviário remunerado de cargas. O documento deve ser vinculado ao Manifesto Eletrônico de Documentos Fiscais (MDF-e), aumentando a rastreabilidade das operações. Nas operações de carga lotação, o sistema não permite a geração do CIOT quando o valor informado está abaixo do piso mínimo aplicável. Em caso de reincidência, após decisão administrativa definitiva, a penalidade de suspensão do RNTRC pode chegar a 45 dias. A reincidência na penalidade de suspensão pode levar ao cancelamento do RNTRC e à vedação do exercício da atividade de transporte rodoviário remunerado de cargas por dois anos. A regulamentação também prevê multas majoradas para contratantes que insistirem na prática, podendo chegar a R$ 10 milhões conforme o histórico de infrações.

A Jadlog implantou dois sorters desenvolvidos pela Pitney Bowes Brasil para automatizar a triagem de encomendas na filial do Rio de Janeiro e no hub de Betim (MG). Com tecnologia nacional, os equipamentos têm capacidade para processar até 5 mil pacotes por hora e realizar até 60 classificações simultâneas , direcionando os volumes por cidade e CEP e reduzindo a dependência de etapas manuais de separação. Em Betim, a operação movimenta mais de 30 mil pacotes por dia e está conectada diretamente a cerca de 40 franquias. A unidade conta com aproximadamente 150 colaboradores e recebe parte das encomendas em caminhões procedentes de São Paulo, que são posteriormente redistribuídas para municípios de Minas Gerais e alguns destinos do Rio de Janeiro. A estrutura instalada nas duas unidades possui 20 saídas, com três posições de separação associadas a cada uma, além de módulos de desvio capazes de direcionar os volumes para diferentes destinos. O sistema também utiliza três câmeras e um módulo pré-desviador, que posiciona os pacotes na esteira conforme a localização da rampa de destino. O equipamento conta ainda com mecanismos para evitar o direcionamento de encomendas para rampas que já atingiram sua capacidade. Volumes com inconsistências de rastreamento ou cuja leitura não permita determinar o destino com segurança são encaminhados para uma área de rejeito para nova verificação. O projeto foi adaptado à operação da Jadlog durante o desenvolvimento. A configuração inicialmente previa posições com tecnologia put-to-light, mas a empresa optou pela manutenção dos pallets nas áreas de separação e pela utilização de monitores para indicar os destinos das encomendas. Segundo a Jadlog, a automação já proporcionou redução no tempo de triagem, nos erros de direcionamento e no retrabalho. Para Bruno Tortorello, CEO da companhia, a implantação também muda a rotina das equipes, que passam a concentrar esforços no monitoramento do fluxo, alimentação dos equipamentos, tratamento de exceções e controle de qualidade.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/usa_diesel_.text: U.S. diesel surged again over the last week, GasBuddy highlighted in a blog posted on its website on Monday. The blog revealed that the national average price of diesel rose 30.7 cents in the last week and stood at $6.490 per gallon. The most common U.S. diesel price stood at $6.29 per gallon, “up 30 cents from last week”, according to the blog, which outlined that this was followed by $6.39, $5.99, $6.19, and $6.49. The median U.S. diesel price was $6.39 per gallon, “up 30 cents from last week and about 10 cents lower than the national average”, the blog revealed. Diesel prices at the top 10 percent of stations in the country averaged $7.02 per gallon, while the bottom 10 percent averaged $5.83 per gallon, the blog noted. The states with the lowest average diesel prices comprised Texas, at $5.96 per gallon, Louisiana, at $6.01 per gallon, and Oklahoma, at $6.02 per gallon, and the states with the highest average diesel prices comprised California, at $8.38 per gallon, Washington, at $7.37 per gallon, and Hawaii, at $6.95 per gallon, the blog pointed out. GasBuddy’s blog outlined that the biggest weekly changes were seen in Ohio, which witnessed a 65.3 cent increase, Michigan, which saw a 64.6 cent increase, and Indiana, which saw a 63.6 cent rise. According to the AAA Fuel Prices website, the average price of diesel in the U.S. is $6.5276 per gallon, as of September 22. This is the highest recorded average price of diesel in the U.S., the site showed.

https://safety4sea.com/us-centcom-says-m.text: More than 2,000 commercial vessels have transited the Strait of Hormuz under coordinated protection in recent months, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM), as American forces and regional partners work to maintain the flow of energy and cargo through the strategic waterway. S peaking in a video message on 19 September CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said US forces had supported the movement of more than one billion barrels of crude oil from Gulf producers through the Strait over the past several months. “Primary transit lanes in the Strait are clear of mines,” Cooper said, adding that the number of commercial vessels using the waterway had continued to increase. The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints, connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the wider Indian Ocean. Its security is particularly significant for global energy markets, with large volumes of crude oil, refined products and liquefied natural gas moving through the waterway. According to Cooper, the US military is working with the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), as well as shipping and insurance companies, to facilitate higher volumes of commercial traffic. “Even with this progress, we remain clear-eyed and laser-focused as we work with our teammates … to increase the volume of traffic flow through the Strait of Hormuz,” he said. Cooper said the efforts had contributed to an increase in maritime activity, with volumes of crude oil, cargo and LNG transported through the waterway during the previous two weeks reaching their highest level in six months.

https://safety4sea.com/lng-tanker-divert.text: The LNG tanker Vivit Africa LNG has diverted from its intended destination after its crew lost access to some internal control systems in an incident reported as a suspected cyberattack, Bloomberg reported. T he vessel was sailing east through the Mediterranean and Adriatic seas towards Italy earlier this month when the systems failure disrupted its voyage. The vessel, which had loaded its cargo at the Cameron LNG terminal in Louisiana, was due to deliver the LNG to Rovigo, Italy, but remained off the Italian coast without discharging its cargo. On Wednesday, it began sailing away from its intended destination towards Algeciras, Spain, according to shipping data compiled by Bloomberg. The Italian Coast Guard also assisted after the master reported a malfunction affecting systems used to monitor cargo parameters. There is therefore no official confirmation at this stage that the malfunction was caused by a cyberattack. Bloomberg also reported that there was no indication of who may have been behind the suspected attack. To remind, two energy tankers bound for Texas were hit by cyberattacks in August while underway, prompting US Coast Guard and FBI teams to board both vessels for multi-day investigations.

https://safety4sea.com/esl-announces-dec.text: Emirates Shipping Line (ESL) will stop accepting plastic waste shipments from 1 October 2026, becoming the second major ocean carrier to introduce such a ban following CMA CGM’s decision in 2022 . I n an advisory issued on 15 September, the Dubai-based carrier said it would discontinue bookings for plastic waste cargo under HS Code 3915, citing its commitment to “safeguarding marine ecosystems and preserving biodiversity.” The decision follows engagement between ESL, the Basel Action Network (BAN) and members of the World Shipping Council (WSC), as environmental groups push container lines to restrict the international transport of plastic waste. We believe the decision to ban the carriage of plastic waste is the right step forward and reflects our focus on responsible and compliant shipping practices … said Michael Davies, COO and Regional Managing Director for Middle East at ESL. BAN said hundreds of tonnes of plastic waste are shipped daily from developed to developing countries, often for recycling. However, the organization argues that significant quantities cannot be safely or economically recycled and may instead be dumped, burned or processed under unsafe conditions.

https://safety4sea.com/bulk-carrier-rema.text: The Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Cape Falcon remains aground off Gladstone, Queensland, several days after running aground while attempting to anchor near the port, with two refloating attempts failing to free the vessel. T he 182,066-dwt Capesize bulk carrier grounded at around 15:42 local time on September 18, approximately six nautical miles east of the Port of Gladstone, after departing the Hay Point Terminal south of Mackay. The vessel was attempting to anchor near Gladstone’s bunkering anchorage when the incident occurred. Maritime Safety Queensland is leading the response, with two refloating operations carried out with tugboat assistance. The first involved six vessels, while a second operation involving 10 harbor tugs achieved only minimal movement. With the attempts unsuccessful, the vessel remains aground while authorities and salvors assess further options. There have been no reports of injuries, pollution or hull damage. The vessel is also not obstructing the main shipping channel, although the ongoing recovery operation has affected port operations. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) has opened an investigation into the grounding. Investigators will preserve and examine Cape Falcon ’s voyage data recorder, as well as AIS and other tracking information, weather conditions and relevant crew, operator and maintenance records. They will also board the vessel to interview crew members and collect evidence when conditions allow. The Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) has detained Cape Falcon under the Navigation Act pending an assessment of its seaworthiness. Authorities will carry out inspections before the vessel is permitted to resume its voyage.

https://safety4sea.com/five-year-gcmd-eq.text: Turning maritime decarbonisation technologies from pilot projects into scalable solutions will be the focus of a new five-year partnership between the Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD) and Equinor. T he organisations will work to address technical and operational barriers to the deployment of alternative marine fuels and other emissions-reduction technologies. The partnership aims to combine GCMD’s experience in real-world maritime pilots with Equinor’s expertise as a vessel charterer, energy provider and developer of low-carbon solutions. A key focus will be the safe deployment and assurance of biofuels, ammonia and methanol. GCMD’s work covers operational safety and monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV), including trials aimed at improving bunkering and fuel-handling practices and strengthening confidence in fuel quality, quantity and emissions reductions. The partnership will also examine technologies that can reduce emissions from the existing fleet, including energy-efficiency technologies and onboard carbon capture and storage (OCCS). GCMD CEO Lynn Loo said the shipping industry will need a range of decarbonisation solutions. The challenge now is moving technologies from promising trials into widespread commercial use. Furthermore, Equinor’s Anne Mai Hatlem said the maritime energy transition requires cooperation across different industries and supply chains.

https://safety4sea.com/ocimf-updates-gui.text: The Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF) has published an updated edition of its Safety Critical Equipment and Spare Parts Guidance, urging shipping companies to take a proactive, risk-based approach to identifying and maintaining equipment whose failure could lead to hazardous situations or compromise a vessel’s ability to respond to an emergency. T he guidance is intended to support companies in developing and maintaining their Safety Management Systems (SMS) in accordance with the International Maritime Organization’s International Safety Management (ISM) Code. It replaces OCIMF’s previous edition, published in 2018, and provides a framework for identifying, documenting and maintaining safety-critical equipment and the spare parts required to keep it operational. OCIMF defines safety-critical equipment as an individual piece of equipment, control system or protection device where a single-point failure could result in a hazardous situation, cause an accident or affect the status of duplicated equipment and reduce system redundancy. Safety-critical spare parts, meanwhile, are components required to maintain or repair such equipment. The guidance stresses that identifying the equipment alone is not enough. Companies also need to determine which spare parts are essential to maintaining or restoring the functionality of safety-critical systems. Without the appropriate components readily available, a vessel may be unable to return critical equipment to service when it is needed most. The updated guidance places risk assessment at the centre of the process, encouraging companies to establish clear procedures for determining which equipment and spare parts should be considered safety critical and how they should be managed within the SMS. The approach is particularly relevant to tankers and other vessels where the failure of critical systems can have serious consequences for crew safety, vessel operations or the environment. While the guidance highlights considerations for oil and chemical tankers, OCIMF says its principles can be applied more broadly to companies operating different types of ships and floating structures.

https://safety4sea.com/bulk-carrier-coll.text: The Panamanian-flagged bulk carrier First Margaux collided with the Chinese fishing vessel Luqing Yuanyu 108 in the Singapore Strait on 17 September, with the smaller vessel taking on water but remaining afloat. T he bulk carrier and fishing vessel had departed anchorages east of Singapore and entered the westbound traffic separation scheme. Video circulating online shows First Margaux approaching the fishing vessel from behind before its bow struck the fishing vessel’s starboard side. The impact caused the smaller vessel to heel and seawater to flood across its deck, while crew members were seen holding onto railings. An 82,000-ton cargo ship has ploughed into a Chinese fishing boat in the Singapore Strait. The 750ft-long bulk carrier First Margaux struck the Luqing Yuanyu 108, a 160ft Chinese fishing vessel, at about 8am last Thursday, according to ship-tracking data. According to the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), the fishing vessel took on water during the collision but remained afloat and stable as its crew managed the situation onboard. The vessel was subsequently towed to Raffles Reserved Anchorage for assessment. Essential crew members remained onboard to assist with the tow. The MPA issued navigational safety broadcasts to keep other vessels clear of the tow and escorted the fishing vessel into port. Luqing Yuanyu 108 later continued under its own power and reached a nearby berth, according to reports.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/shi.text: Chinese shipbuilders are enjoying reflective profits as crude oil supply lines are diversified in the aftermath of the war between the U.S. and Iran. After the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, ship owners who want to import crude oil from the Atlantic Ocean and the United States have placed orders for large oil tankers one after another. According to data from the China Ship Industry Association (CANSI) on the 20th, new orders from Chinese shipbuilders in the first half of this year amounted to 1210.6 million tons based on the volume of goods weight tonnage (DWT). This is 2.7 times larger than the same period last year. As a result, China’s share of new orders worldwide increased by 14 percentage points to 82%. In fact, China Ship Group (CSSC), the world’s largest shipbuilder, saw its new orders reach 22.45 million DWT in the first half of this year, more than doubling from the same period last year. Hengli Heavy Industries, a Chinese private shipbuilder, also won 207 orders in the first half of this year alone, far exceeding last year’s annual orders (115 ships).

https://gcaptain.com/kallas-urges-eu-to-.text: FILE PHOTO: EU European Commission Vice-President Kaja Kallas delivers a joint statement with Philippines Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro (not pictured) on the Enhanced Partnership between the Philippines and the European Union, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting at the Philippine International Convention Center on July 24, 2026 in Pasay, Metro Manila, Philippines. Ezra Acayan/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo Sep 22, 2026 (Bloomberg) –The European Union’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, called for member states to send more naval vessels to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea. EU countries, under the aegis of Operation Aspides, have been patrolling the Red Sea since 2024 as increasing threats by the Houthis plague shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. “The operation needs more naval assets and more air assets to address the increased level of threats in the region,” Kallas told reporters in New York after a meeting of EU foreign ministers on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. “The Black Sea, the Strait of Hormuz and the Strait of Bab el-Mandeb are three critical maritime choke points whose disruption spreads far beyond the region.” The mission consists primarily of three ships from Italy and Greece, with occasional back up from other member states. EU members have so far shown no willingness to increase the number of vessels deployed or to adapt the mission’s goals. “When Aspides was put in place, the indication was that it needs at least 10 ships,” Kallas said. “The situation, I think, is even more grave right now.”

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/south-ko.text: Two South Korean companies, GasEntec and Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI), are pooling resources to commercialize small-scale liquefied natural gas (LNG) technology. The two companies have entered into a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for GasEntec to license SHI’s SAMSUNG Enhanced Nitrogen Split Expansion (SENSE) liquefaction technology for small-scale applications between 50,000 and 1 million tons per annum. The MoU enables the duo to pursue the first commercial licensing of SENSE. Brian Yoon , Chief Executive Officer of GasEntec, commented: “As global LNG capacity expands, liquefaction technology is entering a new cycle of innovation and diversification. “Our partnership with SHI brings their proven liquefaction technology to the small-scale segment, backed by our expertise integrating modular LNG systems worldwide, for the first time. Customers will be able to access an integrated platform that enables flexible solutions spanning liquefaction through to downstream delivery.” Canada’s $4B hydro-powered LNG project advances with FLNG launch at Samsung Heavy Industries SHI developed its SENSE technology to achieve efficiencies in excess of standard natural gas liquefaction processes, featuring a gas expansion process that uses nitrogen and methane as single-component refrigerants, with the entire process operating in a gaseous state, thereby increasing stability and operational convenience.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/navitas-.text: Israel’s Navitas Petroleum has brought into its fold a stake in a block off the coast of South Africa through a deal with Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas, an AIM-listed and Canada-headquartered oil and gas company focused on the Atlantic Margin. Navitas has confirmed the completion of the acquisition of a 37.5% working interest in Block 1 CBK offshore South Africa, following receipt of the required regulatory approval. The transaction enables the firm’s subsidiary, Navitas Petroleum Africa, to hold a 37.5% working interest in the block and serve as its operator. Gil Holzman , Eco’s President and CEO, commented: “Completion of the Block 1 CBK farm-down marks another important milestone in our strategic framework with Navitas, extending our partnership into South Africa and demonstrating the value of our growing collaboration across multiple jurisdictions. “Navitas is a highly experienced global operator and producer with an exceptional track record of developing offshore resources. Their expertise, together with South Africa’s growing need to bring new domestic gas supplies online to meet in-country demand for oil & gas, provides strong foundations to progress the development of Block 1 CBK’s sizeable resources.” According to the company, the completion marks another step in the execution of the Navitas 2.0 strategy, expanding exploration portfolio into a new geography while maintaining a selective and disciplined approach to growth. This acquisition also extends the firm’s collaboration with Eco Atlantic Oil & Gas into South Africa, bringing together complementary experience and capabilities as the partners work to advance the exploration potential of Block 1 CBK.

A hipótese que o Guia Marítimo propõe para discussão parte de Roterdã, onde o biodiesel marítimo caiu em setembro para US$ 985 por tonelada, o menor preço já registrado, e depois voltou a cerca de US$ 1.240/t, enquanto o marine gasoil (MGO) chegou a US$ 1.528,50/t. Sem essas regras, a conta muda. Com VLSFO a US$ 710/t em Roterdã e biodiesel a US$ 1.240/t, uma mistura com 24% de biodiesel custaria cerca de US$ 837/t, algo como 18% acima do fóssil. É uma estimativa aproximada da redação. A vantagem europeia depende de custos de carbono que não existem na cabotagem brasileira, e por isso o argumento aqui precisa ser outro. O governo respondeu com a MP 1.391, que prevê R$ 1,00 por litro de diesel A de uso rodoviário por 30 dias, valor que se soma ao programa de R$ 1,12 e chega a R$ 2,12. São afirmações do setor, e os números de capacidade e produção variam entre as fontes. Na cabotagem, o bunker segue cotado em dólar. https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Singapore’s Maritime Rescue Coordination Center is reporting that the crew of an MSC containership was rescued on September 22 after abandoning their vessel. The report indicates there were no injuries to the crew, but no details were provided on the circumstances that caused the crew to abandon ship. The distress call was made around 08:45 local time in Singapore on September 22 from the MSC Hermes III . The 38,193 dwt vessel, which was built in 2006, was acquired by MSC in 2020. It is 212 meters (695 feet) in length with a capacity of 2,490 TEU. The ship had a crew of 25 aboard. The ship had been sailing from Shanghai to Jakarta before returning to Singapore, according to MSC's onlien schedule. It was operating a regional feeder service. The authorities in Singapore broadcast a request for nearby vessels to assist. The MSC Hermes III was in a busy shipping lane, approximately 160 nautical miles (300 km) east of Vietnam in a position north of Ho Chi Minh City. The Singapore MRCC said three vessels responded to the call, and the MSC Ruby , a larger 13,000 TEU vessel, was able to reach the area. The crew of MSC Hermes III had abandoned the vessel to its lifeboat. They were recovered by the MSC Ruby , and the Singapore MRCC says arrangements are being made with the Vietnamese MRCC to land the crew. The MSC Hermes III showed no significant issues on recent Port State inspections. Last year it was cited mostly for paperwork issues during an inspection in Le Havre, but otherwise has not been cited for issues on several recent inspections.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A quantidade de MEI-Caminhoneiro cresceu 86.634 CNPJs em 2025 , alta de 25%, enquanto o número de vínculos formais de motoristas de caminhão aumentou em 6.536 , avanço de 1,22%. Os dados, levantados pelo Instituto Paulista do Transporte de Cargas (IPTC) , ligado ao SETCESP , mostram a expansão do trabalho autônomo formalizado no transporte rodoviário de cargas, embora os dois indicadores representem universos distintos. O levantamento cruzou informações da Relação Anual de Informações Sociais (RAIS), da Receita Federal e do Registro Nacional de Condutores Habilitados (RENACH). Ao final de 2025, o país tinha 541.588 vínculos formais de motoristas de caminhão, enquanto o estoque de MEI-Caminhoneiro passou de 346.558 CNPJs ativos em 2024 para 433.192. Durante o ano, foram abertos 143.014 CNPJs na categoria e 56.380 deixaram de estar ativos, resultando no crescimento líquido de 86.634 registros. Considerando o período entre 2023 e 2025, o estoque de MEI-Caminhoneiro acumulou alta de 47,95%. O crescimento também vem acompanhado de uma taxa relevante de saída. Dos 114.314 CNPJs de MEI-Caminhoneiro abertos em 2024, 90.077 permaneciam ativos um ano depois, uma redução de 21,2%. Para o IPTC, o dado indica um desafio adicional para profissionais que passam a atuar como empreendedores, assumindo responsabilidades relacionadas a custos, tributação, gestão e planejamento. O presidente do SETCESP, Marcelo Rodrigues, afirma que o avanço do modelo representa uma diversificação nas formas de inserção profissional no setor. Segundo ele, a expansão do trabalho autônomo exige preparação para que o motorista, além da atividade de condução, possa administrar de forma sustentável o próprio negócio. O estudo ressalta, porém, que não é possível afirmar que os motoristas estejam migrando de empregos com carteira assinada para o modelo de MEI. Os dados da RAIS e da Receita Federal abrangem universos diferentes e não permitem acompanhar individualmente a trajetória dos profissionais. Uma mesma pessoa também pode manter simultaneamente um vínculo formal e um CNPJ ativo.

A Kothe investiu R$ 40 milhões na implantação de um centro de distribuição em Bom Jesus, no sul do Piauí . Com 11,4 mil m² de área construída, 15.512 posições-palete e 16 docas , a unidade amplia a estrutura logística da empresa no Matopiba (importante região agrícola do Brasil, formada pelos estados do Tocantins, Maranhão, Piauí e Bahia) e foi projetada para operações com sementes, defensivos, produtos biológicos e fertilizantes, incluindo armazenagem climatizada. Instalado em um terreno de 50 mil m², o CD integra o Projeto Raízes, plano de expansão da infraestrutura da Kothe na região. A unidade combina áreas de armazenagem convencional e refrigerada e foi estruturada para aproximar os estoques dos polos produtores do Cerrado piauiense. “Agronegócio trabalha com janelas muito específicas. Não basta transportar um produto de um ponto a outro: é preciso ter o estoque no lugar certo, preservar as condições adequadas de armazenagem e conseguir responder rapidamente às necessidades do cliente. O investimento em Bom Jesus nasce justamente dessa dinâmica e da importância que o MATOPIBA vem assumindo para a nossa operação”, afirma Paulo Kothe, diretor de Logística da Kothe. A operação reúne armazenagem, gestão de estoques, transporte e distribuição. O espaço também conta com uma doca dedicada a operações rápidas e está preparado para entregas expressas e retirada direta de produtos pelos clientes. Para administrar a operação, a Kothe utiliza o sistema SAP EWM, além de recursos de rastreabilidade, controle de estoque e monitoramento. A estrutura climatizada é destinada principalmente a produtos que exigem condições específicas de conservação, como sementes. A companhia espera gerar mais de 50 empregos diretos em Bom Jesus. A implantação também deve movimentar a cadeia local de fornecedores e prestadores de serviços ligados a atividades como transporte, manutenção, segurança, alimentação, limpeza e tecnologia.

https://safety4sea.com/recaap-isc-two-in.text: Over the past week, 15-21 September, two incidents of piracy or armed robbery against ships in Asia were reported to the ReCAAP ISC. A ccording to ReCAAP ISC, both incidents were classified as CAT 3. One occurred onboard a liquefied gas tanker while anchored at Batangas Bay Anchorage, Philippines, on 15 September. Two perpetrators armed with knives and machetes boarded the vessel, with some ship stores reported stolen. The crew were not injured. The second incident occurred onboard a bulk carrier while transiting the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme in the Singapore Strait on 17 September. Four perpetrators armed with knives and gun-like objects boarded the vessel and stole engine spares. The crew were not injured. Ships are advised to intensify vigilance and maintain sharp look-out while transiting the areas of concern or anchoring at ports and anchorages; and to report all incidents immediately to the nearest coastal State. The Centre also urges the coastal States to increase patrols/surveillance in their respective waters, respond promptly to incidents reported to them, strengthen coordination and promote information sharing on incidents and the criminal groups involved to arrest the perpetrators. For a 6th consecutive year, there has been no report of incident of abduction of crew in the Sulu-Celebes Seas and waters off Eastern Sabah. The last incident occurred on 17 Jan 2020. In January 2025, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), coordinated with other stakeholders and counterparts further downgraded the threat level of ‘Abduction of crew for ransom in the Sulu-Celebes Seas’ to ‘LOW’, meaning ‘No information or monitored activities suggest an impending attack; hence incidents are not expected to occur’. The ReCAAP ISC, in its Advisory on 14 Feb 2025 advised ships to “exercise vigilance when transiting the Sulu-Celebes Seas and report incidents to the Operation Centres of the Philippines and Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM)”. Also, to maintain communication with the relevant authorities when transiting the area.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-e.text: A fatal accident involving a chief officer inside a cargo hold resulted in his death after he entered a wood pellet-filled space where oxygen levels were believed to have fallen to an extremely low level. T he incident, highlighted by the Hong Kong Marine Department, shows the potentially fatal consequences of entering an enclosed cargo space without first confirming that its atmosphere is safe. The case also demonstrates how incorrect interpretation of gas readings, inadequate entry controls and weaknesses in the shipboard safety management system can combine to allow a crew member to enter a hazardous space. The Hong Kong-registered bulk carrier was underway in the Atlantic Ocean from the United States to the United Kingdom after all five cargo holds had been loaded with wood pellets. In accordance with the vessel’s safety procedures for transporting wood pellets, the chief officer was responsible for conducting daily atmospheric testing in all cargo holds during the voyage. Gas readings recorded during the first three days were within safe limits. Around lunchtime on the fourth day, the chief officer was reported missing and the crew immediately began searching the vessel. He was subsequently found unconscious on top of the cargo inside No. 1 cargo hold. A walkie-talkie was found hanging from the handle of the watertight door near the hold entrance.

https://safety4sea.com/cytur-finds-94-of.text: A new analysis of more than a dozen marine equipment cyber risk assessments has found that 94% of the systems examined were rated at a level where cyber risk treatment should be considered or is required, with about 60% classified as requiring treatment. T he findings, published by cybersecurity company CYTUR in its September 2026 Threat Brief, highlight the limitations of relying on Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) alone to assess the cyber risk of shipboard equipment. CYTUR said the assessments showed that actual risk was shaped by a combination of vulnerabilities, network exposure, connectivity and the potential operational impact of a compromise. The company stressed that the 94% figure does not mean that 94% of marine equipment is vulnerable, as the systems assessed were commissioned by CYTUR clients and were not a random or representative sample of the wider maritime equipment market. The assessments were reclassified using the risk treatment criteria of IACS Recommendation 171. Under the framework, a Risk Level (RL) below 4 is considered “Optional”, a level of 4 to 12 is “Appropriate”, while a level above 12 means that risk treatment is “Required”. CYTUR found that about 34% of the assessed systems were in the Appropriate category and about 60% were in the Required category, while only 6% fell into the Optional range. The company noted, however, that the risk level is not determined simply by the number of CVEs present. IACS Rec. 171 considers the system’s category, the potential impact of an incident and the likelihood of an attack.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543146-st.text: Petrobras, Shell and Strohm have completed a qualification and offshore field trial program for a thermoplastic composite pipe flowline designed for high-CO2 conditions in Brazil's deepwater pre-salt, clearing the way for a Petrobras pilot installation planned for early 2027. The joint industry program included full-scale qualification and offshore trials of Strohm's corrosion-free TCP technology, designed for a 30-year service life. DNV qualified a six-inch carbon fibre-PA12 TCP for alternating water and gas injection, or WAG, used for enhanced oil recovery, under its DNV-ST-F119 standard. The qualification program involved more than 50,000 testing hours covering materials, sealing and full-scale testing. More than 40 individual full-scale tests were conducted across seven laboratories and certified testing facilities in Europe and Brazil. “The project has great strategic relevance for the subsea sector in Brazil and beyond, as it decisively solves one of the major pipeline integrity challenges identified in recent years: the risk of stress-corrosion cracking in environments with a high CO₂ concentration. By using non-metallic TCP, corrosion is simply eliminated, strengthening system integrity and operational reliability in challenging subsea environments,” said Martin van Onna, Strohm’s CEO. Following the DNV qualification, offshore field trials were completed in July 2026, including deep immersion performance tests and subsea vertical connection tests. The trials were intended to validate the pipe's performance during offshore handling, installation and connection to subsea systems.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543144-on.text: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has struck gas at a deepwater exploration well in India's Mahanadi Offshore Basin, with the well flowing gas at encouraging rates and reservoir pressure. The MN-DW18-1-H-D well, about 43 km off Konark on the Odisha coast, was drilled to a total depth of 1,623 meters and encountered gas in an interval between 1,441 and 1,452 meters. The gas find was recorded on September 18, and ONGC said the well had been flowing gas with encouraging flow and reservoir pressure for three days. It is the first well drilled in the Mahanadi Basin under ONGC's Samudra Manthan exploration campaign. ONGC said the discovery's proximity to the coast could provide potential for early monetization, subject to further appraisal and commercial evaluation. The company added that the find, together with other discoveries in the area, could potentially be developed through shared facilities under India's PNG Rules, 2025.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/qatarene.text: While dismissing alternative pipeline routes as economically unviable, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Qatar’s state-owned oil and gas giant QatarEnergy has highlighted that the country’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) player remains fully committed to maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz, even as facility repairs following recent attacks at Ras Laffan Industrial City face a multi-year timeline. Following Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz , QatarEnergy halted LNG production and associated products at some of its assets and issued a declaration of force majeure to its LNG buyers. A major plot twist came with Iran’s warning about its planned attack on oil and gas facilities across the Gulf region in direct response to Israel’s attack on its giant South Pars gas field, which is known as the North Field on Qatar’s side. Ras Laffan Industrial City was hit by missiles on March 18, 2026. The company’s CEO, who recently rejected the notion that the Strait of Hormuz was obsolete, emphasizing that the waterway handles trade in all products to and from all adjacent countries, has stressed the need for normal movement across the Strait. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi , Qatar’s Minister of State for Energy Affairs, President and CEO of QatarEnergy, said: “We are grateful for our neighbors who have welcomed us to use their territories. However, not everything can be transported via pipelines. The problem is that LNG, our main export commodity, cannot be transported by pipelines. “We will have to transport it by pipelines as gas and then liquify it at receiving terminals wherever that may be. This means we are building redundant facilities to the ones we are already building in Qatar as part of the North Field expansion project. This makes no economic sense.” As a result, the company has decided not to use pipelines as an alternative based on commercial and technical criteria. At the Qatar Economic Forum 2026, which was held in New York, the CEO of the Persian Gulf state’s giant pointed out that the attacks on Ras Laffan resulted in damage to two LNG trains and a GTL plant.

https://petronoticias.com.br/petrobras-u.text: A Petrobras está adotando uma série de medidas para tornar seus projetos de desenvolvimento mais robustos diante do cenário de volatilidade de preços, custos e disponibilidade de equipamentos e serviços. Entre as principais iniciativas estão a simplificação dos projetos de FPSOs, a padronização de equipamentos e linhas, uma nova abordagem nas compras e uma aproximação maior com os fornecedores. A estratégia foi apresentada por Renata Baruz i, diretora da Petrobrás, durante painel realizado hoje (22), na ROG.e, no Riocentro. Entre as medidas adotadas, a Petrobrás colocou a simplificação dos projetos de FPSOs como uma das principais frentes para reduzir custos e melhorar a viabilidade econômica dos empreendimentos. De acordo com Renata, a companhia identificou situações em que projetos tecnicamente avançados acabavam não sendo economicamente viáveis. A partir disso, passou a buscar soluções mais simples para as unidades. Os resultados, segundo ela, já aparecem em projetos em desenvolvimento. No projeto Sergipe Águas Profundas (SEAP), a Petrobrás conseguiu uma redução de 10%, enquanto no projeto Búzios 12 houve uma redução de 17% no peso do topside. O maior ganho citado pela diretora ocorreu no projeto de revitalização de Tupi, no qual a companhia conseguiu reduzir em 51% o peso do topside. Segundo ela, o esforço de simplificação não está restrito às instalações de superfície e também envolve soluções desubsuperfície. A Petrobras também iniciou movimentos de padronização de linhas flexíveis e rígidas, além de mudanças na estratégia de aquisição. Um dos exemplos citados pela diretora envolve as linhas flexíveis. “ Em vez de adquirir uma linha específica para cada poço, sujeita a perder sua utilidade caso o projeto ou a localização do poço seja alterada, a companhia passou a comprar bobinas completas e realizar o corte somente no momento da instalação ”, contou. A outra frente destacada pela diretora é a aproximação com o mercado fornecedor. Renata afirmou que, desde que assumiu a posição, passou a buscar um diálogo mais direto com as empresas para entender quais fatores estão dificultando a apresentação de propostas à Petrobras e contribuindo para a elevação dos preços.

https://petronoticias.com.br/286611-2/.text: Para aproveitar ao máximo a força do vento, os aerogeradores precisam se mover continuamente, ajustando sua posição para que se mantenham de frente para o vento. Desalinhamentos podem reduzir significativamente a geração de energia e aumentar o desgaste mecânico dos componentes do equipamento. Com o objetivo de enfrentar esse desafio, a ENGIE Brasil executou um projeto de Pesquisa, Desenvolvimento e Inovação (PD&I) da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) que aprimorou e validou uma metodologia para ampliar a eficiência de aerogeradores utilizados nos parques eólicos. Iniciado em dezembro de 2025, o projeto recebeu um investimento da ordem de R$ 700 mil. A iniciativa, executada em parceria com a Universidade Federal de Santa Maria (UFSM), é capaz de detectar e estimar perdas de geração causadas pelo desalinhamento do sistema de orientação da turbina em relação à direção do vento a partir de dados operacionais dos próprios aerogeradores. Realizado no Conjunto Eólico Campo Largo, na Bahia, o projeto avaliou o desempenho de um algoritmo desenvolvido pela ENGIE para identificar automaticamente desvios na orientação das turbinas em relação à direção do vento. Para validar os resultados, foi utilizada a tecnologia LiDAR ( Light Detection and Ranging / Detecção e Medição por Luz), técnica de sensoriamento remoto que utiliza pulsos de laser para medir distâncias e mapear objetos ou fenômenos com alta precisão, possibilitando medidas diretas de direção e velocidade do vento. Considerado pioneiro no Brasil, o projeto comparou diferentes tecnologias LiDAR em um ambiente operacional real, superando abordagens baseadas apenas em simulações ou testes laboratoriais. O diretor de Energias Renováveis e Armazenamento da ENGIE Brasil, Guilherme Slovinski Ferrari(dirfeita), disse que “ A iniciativa reforça o papel estratégico da inovação para a competitividade do setor elétrico. A inovação é um dos principais motores para aumentar a eficiência e a sustentabilidade da geração renovável. Projetos de PD&I como este demonstram como a colaboração entre empresas e universidades pode transformar conhecimento científico em soluções práticas, capazes de gerar valor para os negócios e para toda a sociedade. “O desalinhamento do sistema responsável por orientar a rotação da turbina, o yaw, ocorre quando o aerogerador não aponta corretamente para a direção do vento recebido, reduzindo a produção de energia e aumentando o desgaste mecânico dos componentes. A identificação rápida e precisa desse problema permite aumentar a eficiência operacional e reduzir custos de operação e manutenção. De acordo com a gerente do projeto, Camylla Amorim , os resultados demonstram o potencial da solução para gerar ganhos concretos de desempenho nos parques eólicos. “ Além de validar o algoritm

https://g1.globo.com/pop-arte/noticia/20.text: O jornalista Zuenir Ventura morreu aos 95 anos nesta terça-feira (22), em casa, em decorrência de uma pneumonia. https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Last week, Taiwan's coast guard demonstrated its ability to use its coastal patrol vessels to launch locally-built antiship missiles, adding additional heft to its defensive capabilities. In a trial on Friday, the Taiwan Coast Guard patrol vessel Qijin test-launched a Hsiung Feng III supersonic missile at a decommissioned Taiwan Navy frigate in a sinking exercise. The missile traveled about 50 nautical miles - more than half the width of the Taiwan Strait - before striking its target. A coast guard unit followed up with the launch of a subsonic HF-2 antiship missile. The Qijin is one of 12 ships (10 active) in the high-speed catamaran Anping-class, and several sister ships have also test-launched antiship missiles. They are capable of carrying up to 16 box launchers for the purpose and can be readily converted in wartime. Taiwan's Navy has only several dozen vessels capable of launching antiship missiles, and an additional 12 hulls with 16 launchers each would be a meaningful addition. Few other coast guards have taken on a high-end antiship guided missile role, though a military role in time of war is common practice. The U.S. Coast Guard briefly carried the Harpoon antiship missile on some of its largest cutters in the 1980s, but has long since given it up. In time of war, the U.S. Coast Guard has historically been integrated into the U.S. Navy's command structure and assigned to combat missions, like convoy escort and antisubmarine warfare; it is formally a military service and the legal structure for transferring its control to the Navy remains in place. The China Coast Guard operates the world's largest fleet of seagoing cutters - some larger than the largest U.S. Navy destroyers and cruisers - and many are believed to be warships-in-waiting, ready for conversion into surface combatants in time of conflict. It operates under China's military command structure and carries out paramilitary missions in the waters of neighboring states, though it is nominally a "white-hull" law enforcement agency.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: California and a coalition of eight eastern states filed a total of three lawsuits on September 22, each seeking to block deals made by the Trump administration to buy back offshore wind leases in exchange for investments in fossil fuel projects. These suits follow earlier ones, in which they each allege the deals are illegal, violate several federal laws, and redirect renewable energy investments in Democratic-led states to other areas of the country. New York is leading a coalition that includes New Jersey, Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and Vermont, calling the deals with Bluepoint Wind and Invenergy illegal. The federal government committed to reimbursing $1.4 billion in exchange for canceling four wind leases. Bluepoint received $765 million to cancel a project offshore from New York in exchange for investing in LNG projects. Invenergy got a total of $653 million for three offshore wind leases in exchange for investments in natural gas plants in Indiana, Wisconsin, Iowa, Kansas, and Missouri and geothermal projects in the western United States. In addition to the two suits filed today, the eastern states also sued in June, challenging the deal struck by the Department of the Interior to buy back offshore wind leases from TotalEnergies. “Americans are facing increasing energy costs because this administration would rather pay off energy companies than let us build the new power sources we need,” said New York State Attorney General Letitia James, who is a vocal critic of Donald Trump and faced a personal suit by the administration. “These illegal backroom deals take money that should have gone toward lowering New Yorkers' bills and hand it to fossil fuel projects in other states, all while our energy demand continues to grow.” New York argues that the canceled projects were expected to bring more than $16 billion in investments into the state and hamper the state’s efforts to meet energy demands. It cites information from New York’s energy planners that project electricity demand will grow eight percent by 2030 and 24 percent by 2040, driven in part by economic development and new large loads such as data centers. The state alleges that the administration is misusing taxpayer money and sabotaging the state’s ability to meet growing energy needs. “The Trump administration's unlawful pay-to-not-play scheme to pressure companies to forego planned offshore wind projects in America is an outrageous abuse of taxpayer dollars that hurts our ability to meet our energy needs,” said New York State Governor Kathy Hochul.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: In a combined exercise of operational capability mounted jointly by Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, a heavy-weight torpedo has been fired remotely from an unmanned submarine drone cruising in Scottish waters. The weapon used in the trial was jointly developed by Australia and the United States, and has been identified as a Mk 48 Mod 7 Common Broadband Advanced Sonar System (CBASS) heavyweight torpedo, the latest version of a capable weapon with decades of service history. The prime contractor for the Mk 48 Mod 7 is Lockheed Martin. The torpedo is the primary antiship and antisubmarine armament of U.S. Navy attack subs, and can use acoustic homing or wire guidance. In its antiship role, it is designed to detonate under the target's keel, with devastating effects . The launch vehicle was an XV Excalibur, a 12-meter undersea 19-tonne drone, officially described as an Extra-Large Uncrewed Underwater Vehicle, built in Britain by MSubs Ltd. XV Excalibur was formally handed over to the Royal Navy in May 2025, and is mid-way through a two year trials program with the UK’s Submarine Development Agency. ???? https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln , escorted by the Arleigh Burke class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Peterson Jr. , made a brief stop in Guam last weekend. The US Navy acknowledged it was the first return to American soil for the personnel of Carrier Strike Group 3 in nine months without disclosing the plans for the ships. Lincoln has now exceeded 300 days (302 at last count) on deployment after having departed San Diego, California, on November 21, 2025. The official statement from the Navy is that Lincoln and Peterson “returned to the U.S. Pacific Command area of responsibility after nearly seven months operating in the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility.” They said the carrier and destroyer are “conducting routine operations in the U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations.” The ships are just three weeks shy of the mark set by the carrier USS Gerald R. Ford , which was deployed for 326 days before returning to Virginia in May. Ford was said to have set a record for post-Cold War deployments, except for the vessels during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Navy now reports the stop in Guam was a brief logistics call, but the carrier group personnel were afforded on-base liberty. Stars & Stripes reports there was a country music concert for the sailors during the stopover in Guam. The carrier group arrived on September 19, and Stars & Stripes reports they departed the following day. It quotes a spokesperson for the Carrier Strike Group saying the stop at Apra was to load stores, mail, and equipment. It was the second time this deployment the carrier had been in Guam. It made a brief stop in December 2025 just before it was deployed to the Arabian Sea. Lincoln ended up spending 208 consecutive days at sea and 200 days in the combat zone. It made a brief logistics stop in Oman in late July, according to Stars & Stripes. The carrier group then made its first port call in Thailand between September 2 and 6, after leaving the combat zone.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: An Iranian judicial official in a local TV interview said they planned to sell seized commercial ships linked to the Americans and Israelis as a form of compensation. In the past, Iran has sold seized oil cargoes, saying it was compensation, but this would be the first time it attempts to sell the vessels. Hassan Abdollianpour, head of the judiciary’s Center for Lawyers, said he was in Bandar Abbas along with other experts conducting an inspection to assess the damage as the first step in compensation claims. Without naming the specific vessels, he said commercial vessels linked to the United States and Israel seized during the war would be sold, with the proceeds used for compensation. He said the vessels had been stopped in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf for violations and seized under judicial rulings. In April, Iran attacked and stopped two containerships associated with MSC, the MSC Francesca and the Epaminondas . The MSC Francesca , built in 2008, is owned by MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company, which Iran frequently asserts is linked to Israel. The vessel is 174,897 dwt with a capacity for 11,668 TEU. The Epaminondas , however, is Greek-owned and managed by Technomar Shipping and was on charter to MSC. Built in 1998, the 94,769 dwt vessel has a capacity of 6,690 TEU. Both ships are being held near Bandar Abbas, while nearby is the MSC Aries (158,097 dwt) held by Iran since April 2024 and owned by an affiliate of Zodiac Maritime, of which Eyal Ofer is the lead investor. "To file an effective lawsuit and achieve a result, the first step is a detailed assessment and documentation of the damages,” said Abdollianpour in an interview at the fishing pier in Bandar Abbas. He asserts that 537 cases of damages have been documented and are in the legal process in areas ranging from Bandar Abbas to Qeshm, Bandar Lengeh, and Jask. The report says that the assessment process is still ongoing, and that as many as 760 claims have been filed for damage to fishing vessels and boats damaged by the American attacks on the ports. He said a documented and comprehensive report for the injured captains, sailors, and fishermen was prepared so they could pursue claims in the legal framework.

https://g1.globo.com/trabalho-e-carreira.text: O Ministério da Previdência Social e o Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS) prorrogaram por mais 365 dias a regra que amplia o prazo máximo de duração do auxílio por incapacidade temporária concedido por meio de análise documental. A mudança vale para pedidos feitos pelo Atestmed, sistema que permite a concessão do benefício com base apenas em documentos médicos . A medida, publicada nesta segunda-feira (21) no Diário Oficial da União, foi assinada pelo ministro da Previdência Social, Wolney Queiroz Maciel, e pela presidente do INSS, Ana Cristina Viana Silveira. A regra havia sido estabelecida pela Portaria Conjunta MPS/INSS nº 14, de 23 de março de 2026. Com a nova portaria, a ampliação do prazo fica válida por mais um ano.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Lula discursou na abertura da 81ª Assembleia Geral da ONU nesta terça-feira (22). No primeiro ciclo de mandatos do presidente, os pronunciamentos focavam no otimismo da inclusão social. Havia também a expansão do comércio Sul-Sul e críticas ao protecionismo agrícola. Os discursos recentes priorizam o combate à emergência climática e a regulação de plataformas digitais. O presidente também defende a soberania democrática contra o extremismo. Novas pautas ganharam destaque nas apresentações do presidente brasileiro. Entre os temas estão o combate ao crime organizado e a defesa da pauta trabalhista. https://brasilenergia.com.br/petroleoega.text: Hunter Farris, vice-presidente de Águas Profundas da empresa, disse que a petrolífera pode “trazer algo único” para o mercado brasileiro A produção da Exxon na Guiana vai chegar a 1 milhão de barris até o fim do ano, segundo Hunter Farris, vice-presidente de Águas Profundas da empresa. Atualmente, a Exxon mantém quatro projetos em operação no país, que respondem pela produção de 900 mil barris por dia (bpd). “Se você pensar no Brasil, o sucesso que tem feito, o próximo capítulo que será escrito no Brasil, nós queremos ser parte disso. Nós pensamos que poderíamos trazer algo único para essa equação”, afirmou o executivo, em palestra na ROG.e. PUBLICIDADE Farris afirmou ainda que “o capital vai para onde estão as oportunidades”. Em sua opinião, países que atraem investimento têm quatro ingredientes. O primeiro é contar com a presença de hidrocarbonetos. Em seguida surgem fatores sob controle das empresas, como a responsabilidade fiscal. O terceiro ingrediente são os relacionamentos e parcerias. E, por fim, o país interessado em atrair capital precisa contar com estabilidade jurídica. “É preciso ter um arranjo fiscal e regulatório que resista ao tempo, porque haverá desafios à frente. Se tudo isso acontecer, será um lugar atrativo para investimento”, disse Farris. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/sau.text: Saudi Aramco loaded approximately 14 million barrels of crude oil on seven very large crude carriers inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday, according to data from TankerTrackers.com. The increased activity follows an attack that disrupted shipments through the kingdom’s east-west pipeline to the Red Sea. The loadings indicate a partial recovery in Saudi shipments. Expectations of higher volumes contributed to pressure on oil prices on Monday, pushing the Brent benchmark below $100 per barrel for the first time since September 9. Satellite images viewed by Reuters show seven tankers positioned near Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura port on Sunday. Drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its east-west oil pipeline on September 13, halting crude loadings at the Yanbu oil port on the Red Sea. Following the shutdown, Aramco cancelled some crude cargo sales to European clients and increased sales to Asia for crude loaded at its eastern ports inside the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia sold about 60 million barrels of crude from its Ras Tanura port inside the Strait of Hormuz for loading via ship-to-ship transfer at the Omani port of Sohar this month and next, Reuters reported last week. Source: Investing.com

https://gcaptain.com/russias-arctic-port.text: A Russian nuclear-powered icebreaker escorts ships on the Northern Sea Route, July 14 2016. Photo credit: knyazev vasily / Shutterstock MOSCOW, Sept 22 (Reuters) – Russia’s Arctic port of Murmansk will use equipment typically used to load fertilizer when it ships its first grain from southern Russia for export as early as next month, as the Black Sea route remains closed due to Ukrainian drone attacks. Murmansk is located much further away from Ukraine than Russia’s Baltic ports and, unlike them, can be approached through neutral waters. Reuters reported on Monday that Russian companies have been repurposing fertilizer, coal and other cargo terminals at Baltic and Arctic ports, including Murmansk, to handle grain exports. Murmansk commercial port, 2,700 km (1,677 miles) from Novorossiysk, Russia’s main grain export gateway, said on Tuesday it would use a direct-transfer system that moves cargo from railcars straight into ships’ holds, a method normally used for potash exports. The port said it has also been adapting its conveyor systems to handle larger grain volumes.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/gcm.text: The Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD) and Equinor today announced a five-year Impact partnership. The partnership brings together GCMD’s capabilities in conducting real-world maritime pilots with Equinor’s experience as a charterer, energy provider and developer of low-carbon solutions. Together, the organisations will leverage their complementary expertise to help address technical and operational gaps in scaling alternative marine fuels and supporting the development and uptake of other maritime decarbonisation solutions. Advancing the safe deployment and assurance of alternative marine fuels GCMD’s work on alternative fuels, including biofuels, ammonia and methanol, focuses on two critical aspects of deployment: operational safety and robust monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV). Its pilots and studies are generating operational data to support safe bunkering and handling of these fuels. At the same time, its assurance work seeks to strengthen confidence in quantity, quality and GHG emissions abatement. Equinor brings extensive experience as a vessel charterer and marine fuel supplier. This includes chartering dual-fuel LNG, LPG and methanol tankers, testing and using biofuels and supplying methanol to the maritime sector. Equinor is also piloting the use and supply of ammonia as a marine fuel, contributing to the development of associated safety, regulatory and bunkering arrangements. Combining these perspectives can help address practical barriers to alternative fuels deployment while strengthening assurance across emerging marine fuel value chains.

https://petronoticias.com.br/porto-do-ac.text: O Porto do Açu e a operadora Perenco Brasil assinaram nesta terça-feira (22), na ROG.e, uma carta de intenções para o desenvolvimento do primeiro projeto de eletrificação de plataformas offshore na Bacia de Campos. O acordo prevê o fornecimento de energia a partir de terra para as unidades da Perenco dos Polos Pargo e Cherne, localizadas em águas rasas, por meio de um cabo submarino de 80 quilômetros conectado a uma subestação terrestre no Porto do Açu, em São João da Barra (RJ). O complexo portuário disponibilizará uma área para a construção da subestação terrestre de conexão à rede básica de energia da Perenco e o direito de passagem para o cabo, que seguirá da subestação até os polos offshore. O objetivo principal é reduzir as emissões escopo 1 de carbono das operações da Perenco no país. Atualmente, as plataformas da empresa nos Polos Pargo e Cherne utilizam energia gerada localmente por turbogeradores. “ A parceria com a Perenco comprova a vocação do Porto do Açu como um catalisador de soluções de baixo carbono para o setor de óleo e gás. Projetos de eletrificação offshore deste porte ainda são raros no mundo e abrem um caminho promissor para o mercado brasileiro”, ressalta Eugenio Figueiredo, CEO do Porto do Açu. A previsão inicial de consumo de energia do projeto é de 35 MW, podendo expandir para até 60 MW em quatro anos. A expectativa é que o sistema entre em operação até o primeiro trimestre de 2028 e a Perenco também poderá contratar futuramente energia de fontes renováveis no ambiente de contratação livre. “ O projeto de eletrificação une o espírito inovador da Perenco à vocação empreendedora do Porto do Açu. Para o setor de óleo e gás, servirá como referência para iniciativas voltadas à segurança energética via extensão da vida produtiva de ativos com redução dos níveis de emissão “, destaca Damien Szyszka , diretor geral da Perenco Brasil. A Perenco construirá a subestação no complexo portuário para receber a energia do grid. O cabo submarino será conectado à plataforma central do Polo Pargo, que redistribuirá a eletricidade para as demais unidades da operadora por meio de uma rede de interconexão existente. O projeto de eletrificação offshore se integra a outras experiências prévias do complexo portuário do Açu com fornecimento de energia limpa para operações marítimas. Desde 2024, a Vast Infraestrutura, em parceria com a Wilson Sons, já disponibiliza energia de terra para rebocadores e embarcações de apoio atracadas que operam no Terminal 1 (T1) do Porto do Açu. © 2026 Petronotícias.
