https://petronoticias.com.br/a-vallourec.text: À medida que os projetos de óleo e gás avançam para águas profundas e ultraprofundas, crescem também os desafios relacionados à integridade, segurança, sustentabilidade e eficiência das operações. É nesse contexto que tecnologias capazes de atuar em diferentes etapas dos projetos ganham relevância, desde a instalação das tubulações e conexões utilizadas nos poços até o isolamento térmico e anticorrosivo dos sistemas submarinos. A Vallourec esstá apresentando na ROG.e 2026 soluções desenvolvidas para esse cenário desafiador do mercado offshore. Entre os destaques estão os sistemas de resina Proxxima com a tecnologia de isolamento submarino Goldilocks, que passam a integrar o portfólio de revestimentos para line pipe da companhia, e o CLEANWELL, solução livre de graxa aplicada às conexões premium VAM. Com aplicações distintas, as soluções apresentadas na feira demonstram a capacidade da Vallourec de atender aos padrões mais exigentes da indústria de energia. O CLEANWELL é um revestimento multifuncional não poluente aplicado à superfície das conexões VAM. Com propriedades anticorrosivas e de lubrificação, a tecnologia dispensa a utilização de graxas convencionais durante a instalação e o armazenamento das conexões nos tubos. Além de contribuir para a proteção dos componentes, a solução pode acelerar as operações em até 30%, ao mesmo tempo em que amplia a segurança e contribui para a redução de custos ao longo do ciclo de vida dos dutos. A tecnologia também demonstra sua versatilidade em aplicações que extrapolam o óleo e gás convencional. O CLEANWELL já integra soluções da Vallourec destinadas a projetos de captura, utilização e armazenamento de carbono (CCUS), incluindo aplicações desenvolvidas para condições de temperaturas extremas e ambientes corrosivos na região do Mar do Norte. No segmento line pipe, outro destaque serão os sistemas de resina Proxxima com a tecnologia de isolamento submarino Goldilocks, tecnologia de isolamento térmico submarino desenvolvida pela ExxonMobil. A Vallourec é a primeira empresa do mundo licenciada comercialmente para fabricar e comercializar a tecnologia em escala, e iniciou, recentemente, a implantação dos processos necessários para a produção em larga escala e aplicação comercial na unidade de Serra, no Espírito Santo. Os sistemas de resina Proxxima com tecnologia Goldilocks foram desenvolvidos para aplicações submarinas em condições operacionais exigentes. Entre seus diferenciais estão o desempenho térmico aprimorado e o maior tempo de resfriamento (cool-down time), que proporciona aos operadores uma janela maior durante paradas não planejadas antes que possam surgir questões relacionadas à garantia de escoamento. A solução também permite instalação e execução mais rápidas do isolamento. A nova capacidade industria

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: Um helicóptero desapareceu na tarde de segunda-feira (21), em Santa Catarina. Na aeronave estariam o cantor Rick , da dupla com Renner , e o empresário Bruno Avelar, do projeto “O Poder do Network”. Buscas continuam nesta terça-feira (22). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros de Santa Catarina , as buscas pelo helicóptero aconteceram em dois pontos, com cerca de 30km entre eles : o primeiro ponto faz referência ao local da última comunicação da aeronave. De acordo com a corporação, uma equipe foi até o local, mas nada foi encontrado. As equipes que trabalham nas buscas pelo helicóptero concentram os esforços em um ponto de mata , apesar do mau tempo. Inicialmente, a Defesa Civil informou que as buscas ficariam suspensas pela madrugada, mas retificou a informação com o prosseguimento dos trabalhos. Além o primeiro ponto, os bombeiros também receberam a localização do último ponto de sinal de celular de um dos ocupantes da aeronave. Ao todo, cerca 20 bombeiros militares participaram da operação, com apoio de viaturas com tração 4x4, necessárias para acessar o terreno. Os esforços se concentram na região de Urubici. Segundo a Polícia Militar de Santa Catarina, as buscas seguem por terra por causa das condições climáticas e em conjunto com as demais forças de resgate e segurança.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: More than a week after the sinking of the ferry Virgo Transport 8 off the coast of Indonesia, dive teams continue to comb the upside-down wreckage in search of additional victims. Despite rough surface conditions and the risk posed by strong underwater currents, salvage divers from Indonesian coast guard agency Basarnas retrieved an additional three bodies on Tuesday, the agency says. The discovery brings the total number of victims recovered to 18 people, nine of whom have been identified. More than 100 people remain missing and are believed to have gone down with the vessel. Progress at the site has been slow, but Basarnas has committed significant resources to an extended search. Earlier in the week, a dive team found one additional body behind the glass of an exterior window in the side of the hull. Divers broke through the glass to extract the remains. Additional bodies were recovered from an open deck area, where they appeared to have been caught by a railing. The dark interior, the currents around the wreck site, the inverted position of the ship, and the hazards of exploring an enclosed space have so far discouraged the divers from entering deeper into the structure. Tampak tim penyelam Basarnas Special Group (BSG) terus menyisir tiap sudut bangkai kapal untuk menemukan korban KMP Virgo Transport 8. Dari informasi yang dihimpun, saat ditemukan jasad korban ada yang sudah rusak. Selain itu, kondisi arus bawah laut di perairan Masalembo… pic.twitter.com/yVceqxFavX Kondisi bangkai KM Virgo Transport 8 dilihat dari dekat saat tim penyelam Basarnas Special Group (BSG) menyisir tiap sudut kapal untuk menemukan korban. https://t.co/EdYFtJ1tvz pic.twitter.com/BfdWHCMjFp Additional search operations are planned for Wednesday, current and weather conditions permitting.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/w.text: Efficiency was the watchword on the show floor at this year's SMM: the industry's innovators and leaders are focused on reducing use of the bunkers they already have, since every indication suggests that the greenest alternative fuels will only begin to scale up in the 2030s. But suppliers say that when it comes to newbuilds, even comparatively simple efficiency enhancements - a different engine model, custom equipment, a tweak to the hull form - are hard for owners to get right now because big shipyards prefer to build a uniform product. The problem is commercial. Record orderbooks and scarce drydock space have given high-volume shipbuilders a strong incentive to choose the most predictable orders - and in general, that means serial replications of a proven design. If the owner wants customization, the yard may simply wait for a different opportunity. "Shipyards typically build on established standard designs and proven production processes," says Dominik Schneiter, CEO of WinGD. "When new propulsion technologies or hybrid solutions are introduced, they often require additional engineering and integration work. Shipyards need to carefully balance innovation with delivery certainty and operational efficiency. This currently slows the adoption of the latest technologies, and it remains an important challenge for the industry as a whole.” Schneiter is not the only one who sees this as an obstacle to getting innovative technology onto the next generation of ships. "The biggest concern for the shipowners is getting a build slot," says one clean-propulsion supplier, confirming that the biggest shipyards may see innovation as a commercial risk rather than an opportunity right now. There are ways to get around this, like approaching smaller shipyards that see an opportunity in custom orders. During SMM, Norwegian specialist owner Green Maritime Infrastructure (GMI) signed an order for two hydrogen-powered bulkers from India-based Chowgule Shipyard. At about 3,000 dwt, the vessels will only trade on coastal routes, but they are a rare example of high-spec hydrogen propulsion - and a yard in an emerging shipbuilding region was happy to have the order. The other option is to select efficient technologies that make life easier - not harder - for the yard. If it's a simpler product with fewer components, the shipbuilder will be all too happy to use it, says Mattias Gunnarsson, Vice President of Merchant Solutions Division at MacGregor, a leading supplier of electric and hydraulic cranes, hatches and deck equipment.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Saudi Aramco has achieved the technical means for a partial restart on its strategic East-West Pipeline, which was significantly damaged in a drone attack on September 11, according to multiple outlets. The pipeline is now operating at reduced capacity or will be soon, industry sources confirmed to Reuters, Bloomberg and the FT. The interim objective is to achieve a pipeline transfer rate of about four million barrels per day - enough to supply Saudi Arabia's own refineries along the Red Sea, plus a small amount more. One crude export loading has already been scheduled at the key export hub at Yanbu, Reuters reports. New from @hntrbrkmedia : Saudi Arabia appears to be working to assemble a shunt on the critical East-West oil pipeline, bypassing a pumping station damaged in last week's attack. Imagery from Vantor shows workers already laying and welding a pair of new pipelines. pic.twitter.com/HLVG3Zgaxy Fully regaining the pipeline's nameplate capacity of seven million barrels per day could take as long as six weeks because three damaged pumping stations will have to be restored. The remaining eight stations are enough to move crude at a reduced rate with reconnected temporary line sections. For now, the resumption of flow on the line has been enough to bring global benchmark oil prices down - in combination with increasing loading volumes at Ras Tanura, the appearance of a weakening Iranian blockade at the Strait of Hormuz, and the possibility of new diplomatic talks to resolve the Iran conflict. After spiking to $108 per barrel last week, the Brent crude benchmark receded to just $98 on Tuesday, reflecting trader expectations of a better-supplied global energy market.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Ukraine is reporting a new milestone in its campaign, launched during the summer, targeting Russian shipping on the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. Both Ukraine and Russia accelerated their attacks this year on commercial shipping, greatly reducing movement on the Black Sea and leading to protests from Turkey and others. Robert “Magyar” Brovdi, commander of Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Force, released a statement on social media on September 22 asserting that his forces have now disabled 300 vessels supporting Russia. He says the campaign was launched on July 6 and since then they have focused on disabling ships supplying Crimea as well as carrying exports from Russia. Brovdi asserts they have hit and disabled 134 vessels in the Sea of Azov and 166 vessels in the Black Sea. Most of the targets were either tankers moving fuel and energy products or dry bulk carriers. He writes, “The Sea of Azov stands and will stand (still), together with the Kerch Strait. The ‘maybe we’ll slip through’ regime operates in the northern and northeastern part of the Black Sea.” He asserts Ukraine has brought shipping to a standstill, saying the “maybe we’ll slip through mode is in shambles.” The campaign has been controversial, with Russia saying it was worse than piracy, as Ukraine was just attacking, not stealing like pirates. Russia has responded with its own increase in attacks, claiming it is targeting ships moving military supplies for Ukraine. Almost a day doesn’t go by that the Russian Ministry of Defense does not claim hitting a cargo ship in one of Ukraine’s ports or attacking the port infrastructure. Russia reportedly placed a halt on much of the regional shipping, especially in the Sea of Azov. A report by Reuters today, September 22, said that Russia has taken to repurpose fertilizer, coal, and cargo terminals in the Baltic and Arctic and is diverting its grain shipments to those ports. Historically, 90 percent of Russia’s grain exports went through the Black Sea.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Two boaters off the coast of Georgia survived a sinking because of assistance from American mariners - and a bean bag chair. On Saturday, Calvin Roman and Zachary Wade departed shore in their 30-foot boat for an extended fishing trip. Early on Monday morning, at a position about 75 miles off the coast of Brunswick, Georgia, their vessel began rapidly taking on water. The boat began to go down, leaving them clinging to a nonstandard but effective life-saving appliance: a blue-and-white striped bean bag. One of them swam down below the surface to free the EPIRB from the sinking vessel and send a distress signal, and U.S. Coast Guard Southeast District received it at about 0650 hours. In response, the district launched a SAR effort with multiple aircraft. The rescue coordination center also contacted a Jones Act product tanker, the uniquely designed American Phoenix , to request assistance. The crew of the Phoenix arrived on scene and used their rescue boat to retrieve Roman and Wade from the water. Neither sustained serious injuries. A rescue-boat crew from Station Mayport met the American Phoenix at a position about four miles off Mayport and brought them safely ashore.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Royal Caribbean Group, which is one of the largest operators and highest-valued companies in the cruise industry, is reported to be negotiating to buy a hotel chain, Sandals, located in the Caribbean. The Financial Times reported that negotiations are underway and could be concluded in “the coming days.” Sandals, which was established in 1981, is a privately-owned operator with 17 resorts under its brand name, as well as three family resorts, and two private destinations in the Bahamas and Panama. The company was developed as a luxury, couples-only concept, and today has locations in Jamaica, the Bahamas, Saint Lucia, Grenada, Barbados, Antigua, Curacao, and the Turks & Caicos. It started the family resort brand Beaches in 1997 and has locations in Jamaica and Turks & Caicos. The company’s core concept was luxury, all-inclusive resorts, launched by developer Gordon “Butch” Stewart. The Financial Times reports the deal would value the business at more than $6 billion and give Royal Caribbean a majority stake in the company. It sees the motivation as a move by the cruise giant to diversify and create opportunities to cross-sell. While a global company, Royal Caribbean continues to derive the majority of its revenue from North America and has a large presence in the Caribbean. Today it operates the contemporary brand, Royal Caribbean, premium brand, Celebrity Cruises, and luxury brand Silversea Cruises, and is a joint venture partner with TUI Group in Mein Schiff and Hapag-Lloyd Cruises. The company rebounded strongly from the COVID-19 pandemic, but this year lowered its growth forecasts, citing uncertainties in the U.S. economy and slowing demand in its European cruises. Analysts have also speculated that the Caribbean sector will be facing overcapacity due to the rapid construction of giant new cruise ships, which is being led by Royal Caribbean. The cruise line was started in the late 1960s by a U.S. entrepreneur with the backing of Norwegian shipping companies. It has made two large acquisitions, buying Celebrity Cruises from the Chandris family and New York-based Overseas Shipholding Group in 1997 and, more recently, in 2018, buying the majority interest in luxury cruise line Silversea Cruises from Manfredi Lefebvre d’Ovidio. The company currently has 71 cruise ships in service with approximately 175,000 berths and 13 ships on order representing 43,230 berths for delivery between 2027 and 2032. Included in that is its expansion into river cruising under the Celebrity Cruises brand.

As imagens mostram a cabine do avião SC-105 Amazonas, que localizou a aeronave desaparecida. O helicóptero Black Hawk também auxiliou nas buscas. A FAB encontrou destroços de um helicóptero após 13 horas de buscas em Urubici (SC). Foi confirmada a morte de todos os 5 ocupantes, incluindo o cantor Rick. Sinais de celulares dos passageiros ajudaram a identificar a área do acidente. Corpos das cinco vítimas foram resgatados. A aeronave decolou de Porto Belo nesta segunda-feira (21) rumo a São Joaquim. O helicóptero Bell 430 estava com a situação regular na Anac. Investigadores do CENIPA e do SERIPA V apuram as causas da queda do helicóptero. A ação inicial analisa dados e não possui prazo de conclusão.

https://brasilenergia.com.br/petroleoega.text: Presidente Luis Fernando Paroli anunciou a data na ROG.e 2026, após publicação da portaria pelo MME; pré-edital também foi publicado pela empresa e ficará disponível até 28 de setembro A PPSA prevê que o leilão de gás da União deve acontecer até 22 de outubro deste ano. A data foi apresentada pelo presidente da companhia, Luis Fernando Paroli, nesta terça-feira na ROG.e 2026. O anúncio foi feito pouco menos de uma hora após o Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME) publicar a portaria do leilão. PUBLICIDADE Serão leiloados 110 lotes, totalizando 1,1 milhão de m3 por dia, com limite de 16 lotes por comprador. Nesta primeira etapa do leilão, serão priorizados os setores químico e petroquímico (35 lotes), fertilizantes nitrogenados (13 lotes), siderúrgicas, metalúrgicas e mineração (32 lotes), ceramista (20 lotes) e vidreiro (10 lotes). “Se o gás realmente é estruturalmente importante para aquela indústria, se é um insumo muito importante para a formação de preço, também é importante que entre no critério de escolha, para que a gente tenha uma alteração de fato nessa indústria.”

Hunter Farris, vice-presidente de Águas Profundas da empresa, disse que a petrolífera pode “trazer algo único” para o mercado brasileiro A produção da Exxon na Guiana vai chegar a 1 milhão de barris até o fim do ano, segundo Hunter Farris, vice-presidente de Águas Profundas da empresa. Atualmente, a Exxon mantém quatro projetos em operação no país, que respondem pela produção de 900 mil barris por dia (bpd). “Se você pensar no Brasil, o sucesso que tem feito, o próximo capítulo que será escrito no Brasil, nós queremos ser parte disso. Nós pensamos que poderíamos trazer algo único para essa equação”, afirmou o executivo, em palestra na ROG.e. PUBLICIDADE Farris afirmou ainda que “o capital vai para onde estão as oportunidades”. Em sua opinião, países que atraem investimento têm quatro ingredientes. O primeiro é contar com a presença de hidrocarbonetos. Em seguida surgem fatores sob controle das empresas, como a responsabilidade fiscal. O terceiro ingrediente são os relacionamentos e parcerias. E, por fim, o país interessado em atrair capital precisa contar com estabilidade jurídica. “É preciso ter um arranjo fiscal e regulatório que resista ao tempo, porque haverá desafios à frente. Se tudo isso acontecer, será um lugar atrativo para investimento”, disse Farris. https://splash247.com/2020-bulkers-seals.text: 2020 Bulkers has signed the binding deal behind its dramatic move into offshore shipping, setting out to assemble as many as 15 large anchor handlers while launching a private placement of up to $175m. The Oslo-listed company has agreed to acquire all of AHTS AS, which owns seven AHTS vessels and has agreements to buy another three. Those ships have been assigned an aggregate value of $264m on a debt-free, cash-free basis. Based on a preliminary September 30 balance sheet, the equity purchase price for AHTS AS is expected to be about $113m, paid entirely in newly issued 2020 Bulkers shares at $0.299 apiece. AHTS AS has also received acceptances covering all shares in four associated project companies and around 79% of a fifth, bringing another five vessels or vessel purchase contracts into the structure: MH Liberty, Aurora Challenger, Skandi Peregrino, Skandi Emerald and Skandi Launcher. Those project-company assets carry agreed values of another $143m on a debt-free, cash-free basis, taking the total fleet value behind the roll-up to roughly $407m. The equity value of the committed project-company stakes is estimated at about $90m. To fund the enlarged company, 2020 Bulkers has launched a private placement of up to $175m at $0.299 per share, up from the roughly $125m equity raise envisaged when the transaction was first unveiled last week. Total new debt is targeted at around $150m, in addition to existing debt at Anchor Launcher.

https://petronoticias.com.br/a-mol-conse.text: A MOL concluiu as obras na unidade AV3 da Refinaria do Danúbio, que havia sido danificada por um incêndio no ano passado. O projeto foi finalizado dentro do cronograma. Após a remoção dos equipamentos de construção, poderá ser iniciado o reinício gradual da produção. Após o comissionamento e os testes da unidade AV3, a refinaria da MOL, em Százhalombatta, poderá operar novamente em capacidade máxima, reforçando ainda mais a segurança do abastecimento de combustíveis para a Hungria e toda a região. O incêndio ocorrido em outubro de 2025 causou danos significativos à unidade de destilação de petróleo bruto AV3. Ao longo do último ano, a MOL realizou uma restauração completa: a estrutura de concreto armado danificada foi demolida e reconstruída, e os equipamentos afetados, bem como os sistemas elétricos e de controle, foram restaurados. Foram instaladas vinte e sete novas bombas de alta capacidade, substituídos oito quilômetros de tubulações e instalados 100 quilômetros de cabos elétricos. As obras foram concluídas conforme o cronograma preliminar; a próxima etapa será preparar a unidade para uma retomada segura das operações. No próximo período, serão realizados procedimentos de limpeza dos sistemas (flushing), testes de pressão e testes funcionais dos equipamentos de controle de processo e segurança; também serão conectadas as fontes de energia auxiliar necessárias e a operação da AV3 será coordenada com as instalações associadas da Refinaria do Danúbio. Cada etapa do processo é acompanhada por rigorosas inspeções e testes de segurança operacional, após os quais o petróleo bruto poderá ser introduzido. O reinício de uma unidade de refinaria tão complexa é um processo gradual: a produção será retomada passo a passo em outubro. Krisztián Pulay, Vice-Presidente Sênior de Produção e Desenvolvimento de Downstream do Grupo MOL, disse que “ Hoje marca um marco importante: a reconstrução da nossa unidade, atingida por um incêndio em outubro, foi concluída. A partir de agora, podemos iniciar gradualmente os testes e a operação da instalação. A prioridade para a MOL neste momento é que a unidade retome as atividades com segurança e em plena capacidade. Os efeitos da guerra no Irã e da crise energética global já chegaram à nossa região; todos buscam fontes alternativas, o que valoriza ainda mais cada rota de abastecimento confiável e a capacidade de refino europeia. Os últimos meses também demonstraram que podemos consolidar nosso abastecimento de combustíveis por meio de produção própria, diversificação de aquisições e opções de importação. Com o retorno da AV3, recuperamos uma capacidade importante: a Refinaria do Danúbio se tornará mais robusta e flexível, conferindo à MOL maior margem de manobra para atender à demanda doméstica e regional .” © 2026 Petronotí

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: A tropical storm off the Pacific coast of Mexico has exploded into a dangerous Category 5 hurricane in less than 24 hours, according to the National Hurricane Center. It ranks among the most powerful storms ever recorded in the basin, and among the fastest-forming as well - a capstone to an unusually active Pacific cyclone season. On Monday morning, Polo was a common tropical storm with an intensity of about 45 knots. By Tuesday, following a "truly remarkable" stretch of extreme rapid intensification, it had sustained winds of 140 knots. Hurricane Polo hasn't moved much in the past 6-12 hours, and it's doing just fine. The warm water below is deep and contains enough "climate fuel" to sustain a high-end Category 5 for much longer. El Niño 1997 --> El Niño 2026 ... massive hurricanes can't be stopped. pic.twitter.com/92fQXNO2o9 On Tuesday afternoon, a NOAA Hurricane Hunter flight measured an extreme low pressure of 892 mb at the center of the storm and flight-level wind speeds of about 168 knots, with surface-level winds assessed "conservatively" at a powerful 155 knots. It was hovering over one patch of warm water, its drift assessed at just one knot. NHC forecasters predict that the hurricane will retain most of its strength for days, fueled by "extremely warm" El Nino waters and light vertical wind shear. The intensity forecast suggests that its wind speeds will remain above 125 knots through the 25th, and tropical storm warnings extend out as far as Mexico's western coastline. Heavy rainfall will likely have dangerous effects on shore, including flash-flooding and mudslides - and the plume of water vapor spun out by the storm is causing heavy rainfall events as far away as New Mexico, 1,000 miles to the north. Steering forces are expected to move the hurricane to the northwest over the next several days, moving it off the coast of Baja California. The storm may briefly disrupt shipping on the lanes to and from Manzanillo, Mexico's biggest Pacific port, and force vessels on north-south routes along the coast to move further offshore. AIS data provided by Pole Star Global shows the routes that vessels have already adopted to avoid the hurricane's path, and most are giving its winds and waves a wide berth.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: Candidatos à presidência já receberam mais de R$ 10 milhões em doações de pessoas físicas. Cada campanha apresenta um perfil de doador distinto. O empresário Erasmo Carlos Battistella doou R$ 500 mil tanto para Lula quanto para Flávio Bolsonaro. O senador é apoiado principalmente por produtores rurais, enquanto Lula registra doações de acadêmicos e de pessoas próximas ao governo.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Ministros do STF Alexandre de Moraes e André mendonça — Foto: Carlos Moura e Nelson Jr. / SCO / STF Ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) avaliam de forma reservada que o novo pedido de André Mendonça para que Alexandre de Moraes seja investigado por abuso de poder indica que ainda não há disposição para nenhuma composição que possa levar à saída da crise institucional que arrasta a Corte há mais de 20 dias. Nos bastidores, a ala alinhada a Moraes aponta que Mendonça tentou "dar o troco" depois que o colega usou relatórios de inteligência para apontar irregularidades na condução do relator nos casos Master e INSS. Em outra frente, ministros que apoiam Mendonça afirmam que ele conseguiu expor o que vem defendendo de forma pública, que é a instrumentalização da Polícia Federal (PF). Ministros do STF avaliam que crise na Corte pode afetar proposta de código de ética e alterar forças no caso Master Julgamento sobre Moraes deixa questões em aberto no STF; entenda o que ainda precisa ser definido O consenso entre as duas alas é de que o ofício de Mendonça pressionou ainda mais o presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, na crise, e colocou em evidência o estilo que tem adotado para conduzir a tensão na Corte, apostando em conversas individuais e sem articular nos bastidores.

https://g1.globo.com/ce/ceara/noticia/20.text: João Munhoz Neto foi preso nesta terça-feira (22) em Fortaleza. Ele é investigado por relação com a morte da namorada, a estudante de Direito Isabelle Caracristi, de 22 anos. Antes de morrer, Isabelle enviou mensagens a um familiar pedindo para não acreditar na versão do namorado caso algo acontecesse com ela. Ela informou a senha do celular. A morte da universitária ocorreu em 13 de setembro. O caso repercutiu após a mãe de Isabelle cobrar explicações nas redes sociais na sexta-feira (18). A defesa de João criticou a prisão preventiva. Segundo a advogada, o cliente havia se apresentado voluntariamente à polícia no dia anterior e entregue seu aparelho celular. Isabelle foi achada morta em um condomínio. Exames apontaram lesões "compatíveis com o impacto contra o solo" e resultado negativo para substâncias toxicológicas.

Zanin considerou que não ficou comprovada omissão do presidente do Senado. Faltaram esclarecimentos sobre a tramitação de requerimentos do caso. A investigação sobre o Banco Master está no centro de uma disputa política no Congresso entre governistas e a oposição. O Congresso tem 7 iniciativas para criar comissões sobre o banco. A instalação exige que o presidente do Congresso faça a leitura dos requerimentos. Zanin durante julgamento dos acusados de mandar matar Marielle Franco — Foto: Gustavo Moreno/STF

https://g1.globo.com/meio-ambiente/notic.text: A chegada de uma massa de ar frio derruba as temperaturas no Sul nesta quarta-feira (23). O Sudeste registrará chuvas e temporais. Haverá chance de geada no Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina e Paraná. Em Curitiba (PR), a temperatura máxima deve atingir apenas 12°C. No Sudeste, o Rio de Janeiro pode acumular mais de 50 milímetros de chuva. A capital paulista terá mínima de 13°C e chuva no leste do estado. O Centro-Oeste terá tempo abafado e pancadas de chuva. No Norte, a chuva se concentra no oeste, enquanto capitais como Palmas registram calor de até 39°C. No Nordeste, o interior segue com sol, calor e tempo seco. Teresina deve registrar máxima perto de 38°C, enquanto o litoral tem possibilidade de chuva fraca.

https://g1.globo.com/rs/rio-grande-do-su.text: A primavera começou na terça-feira (22) sob influência de um El Niño muito forte. A estação terá chuva frequente no Rio Grande do Sul com volumes acima do normal. Os efeitos do El Niño devem ser mais evidentes na primavera. As condições atmosféricas da estação favorecem a formação de tempestades na Região Sul. A Climatempo alerta que o evento climático poderá atingir nível sem precedentes desde 1950. O pico deve ocorrer no fim da estação. Sinais do fenômeno já foram observados no inverno. No entanto, os reflexos mais significativos e o aumento de chuvas ocorrerão nos próximos meses. A última primavera sob influência do El Niño ocorreu em 2023. O período foi marcado por sucessivos episódios de chuva intensa no estado.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543201-in.text: The 1.1 GW Inch Cape offshore wind project in Scotland has completed installation of its second 85-km offshore export cable, with the two-cable system set to be energized in the coming weeks ahead of first power towards the end of 2026. The second 220 kV three-phase cable was installed in three 28-km sections by Enshore Subsea using the cable-laying vessel CMOS Installer, operating from the Port of Blyth. Two offshore joints were completed by specialists aboard Normand Cutter, while the cable was buried using Enshore's ENS1100 hybrid trenching vehicle. Some final rock placement remains to be completed. Together, the two parallel export cables will carry electricity from Inch Cape's offshore substation to its new onshore substation at Cockenzie, East Lothian, and then into the national grid. A total of 170 km of export cable has now been installed. The 2,000-square-millimetre cable, manufactured by Ningbo Orient Wires & Cables, weighs almost 140 tonnes per kilometre. “The completion of this crucial link between the offshore and onshore substations is another major achievement for the project and testament to the excellent collaboration between the Inch Cape team and our contractors, particularly Orient Cable and Enshore Subsea. The successful finalisation of this scope builds on our solid progress as we now enter the next phases of offshore construction,” said John Hill, Inch Cape Project Director.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543200-ab.text: ABL has been appointed by Allseas as marine warranty surveyor for the single-lift removal of the Statfjord A topside in the North Sea, an operation set to use an upgraded 60,000-tonne lifting system aboard Pioneering Spirit. Allseas is carrying out the engineering, preparation, removal and disposal of the Statfjord A platform, a concrete gravity-base production facility on the Equinor-operated Statfjord field. The entire topside will be removed in a single lift by Pioneering Spirit before being transported to a disposal yard for dismantling and recycling. Allseas has upgraded the vessel's motion-compensated topsides lifting system capacity to 60,000 tonnes from 48,000 tonnes for the project. ABL described the operation as the world's heaviest offshore single lift. ABL's scope includes independent third-party technical reviews of procedural documentation and marine assurance services to verify the operational suitability of the proposed fleet. Its personnel will also attend offshore operations to witness and approve their execution. “We are pleased to continue our long-standing relationship with Allseas in Norway by supporting the safe execution of this trailblazing topside removal and offshore lift operation for Equinor. Statfjord A is a legendary asset, and the project brings significant technical and operational challenges. We look forward to working with Allseas to help deliver this important project,” said Subbi Nookala, ABL Norway country manager.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543198-de.text: DeepOcean and the controlling entity of TFKable Group plan to establish a joint venture offering integrated inter-array cable services for offshore wind projects, including a new purpose-built cable laying vessel (CLV). The venture will combine TFKable Group's subsea cable manufacturing capabilities, including those of Tele-Fonika Kable and JDR Cable Systems, with DeepOcean's offshore engineering, installation and seabed intervention expertise. The planned offering will cover engineering, procurement, construction and installation services across the inter-array cable project lifecycle, including seabed mapping, route surveys, engineering, cable manufacturing and transportation, trenching, installation and cable protection. “Offshore wind developers are increasingly looking for greater collaboration and integration across the supply chain. By combining complementary cable manufacturing and offshore installation capabilities, we intend to create a more efficient delivery model that reduces interfaces, strengthens risk management and supports greater project certainty,” said Øyvind Mikaelsen, DeepOcean’s CEO. The collaboration is planned as a multi-year development program, with capabilities to be introduced progressively and key development milestones planned through 2029. The partners are also progressing plans to construct and operate a dedicated cable-laying vessel for inter-array cable projects.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543195-sa.text: Saudi oil giant Aramco plans to reorganise its business to create a new gas division with an eye on possible listings of business units in the future to raise cash, two sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The move is in line with an existing strategy at Gulf state oil companies of offering outside investors pieces of their businesses while retaining operational control and largely avoiding opening up their main oil-producing divisions. Such deals have included the United Arab Emirates' state oil company ADNOC listing stakes in gas, drilling and retail fuel businesses. Aramco is publicly listed but also has listed subsidiaries such as petrochemicals giant SABIC. Both ADNOC and Aramco have also raised billions of dollars from infrastructure assets such as oil and gas pipelines. The new gas business would allow Aramco to use a focused platform from which to develop its natural gas resources domestically and build a liquefied natural gas (LNG) portfolio abroad. Aramco, long the engine of the economy in the world's largest crude exporter before the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted its main export routes, has been seeking outside capital in its efforts to support the kingdom's drive to reduce its reliance on oil. The reorganisation would move Aramco from two main business segments — upstream and downstream — to three, with each unit having its own president, one of the sources said, adding that the company was also exploring other ways to raise cash, including lease-and-leaseback agreements.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543199-cs.text: CSL OWL has launched the first of two purpose-built subsea rock installation vessels designed for offshore wind construction and maintenance projects. The vessel, named Rock Star, is the first in CSL OWL's two-ship newbuilding program and is designed to carry up to 17,500 tonnes of rock and install material at rates of up to 2,000 tonnes per hour in water depths of up to 100 metres. Measuring 166.8 meters long and 40 meters wide, the vessel has a deadweight of about 21,000 tonnes and will operate under the Netherlands flag with Bureau Veritas classification. “The launch of the first of CSL OWL’s two new subsea rock installation vessels brings us one step closer to delivering a new level of capability to the offshore renewable energy sector,” the company said on social media. It is equipped with DP2 dynamic positioning and a positioning suite comprising Differential Global Positioning System, High Precision Acoustic Positioning and laser-based sensors for precise rock placement. The vessel's dual-fuel engines can operate on marine gas oil or methanol. It has a maximum sailing speed of 12 knots and an economical speed of 10 knots.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543197-sh.text: Shell has completed the sale of its 50% non-operated interest in the Na Kika platform and associated fields in the Gulf of America, along with its wholly-owned Coulomb tieback, receiving about $840 million in cash at closing. The assets were acquired by a subsidiary of Talos Energy and an affiliate of Ridgewood Energy, Shell said. Total consideration announced when the transaction was signed was $1.7 billion before customary adjustments and certain contingent payments. The roughly $840 million received at closing reflects adjustments between the deal's July 1, 2025 effective date and completion. Shell will also receive uncapped upside-linked payments through 2027 and overriding royalty interests on production from new Na Kika tiebacks, subject to certain conditions. The assets accounted for 37,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day of Shell entitlement production in 2025. Shell's proved reserves at the end of that year stood at 4.3 million boe for Na Kika and 7.2 million boe for Coulomb. BP operates Na Kika and holds the remaining 50% working interest. The semi-submersible platform began production in 2003, while production from the Coulomb tieback started in 2005.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543192-ir.text: Iran has restored about 50% of damaged production capacity at the South Pars gas field, Deputy Oil Minister Ahmad Zeraatkar was reported as saying on Wednesday by the semi-official Fars news agency, adding that all planned restoration work would be completed before winter. Zeraatkar said in late August that about 40% of the damaged capacity had been returned to production.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543191-to.text: TotalEnergies and AMNI have taken a final investment decision on the Ima gas development offshore Nigeria, targeting production of 350 million cubic feet per day from 2028 to supply the Nigeria LNG liquefaction plant. TotalEnergies will operate the project with a 40% interest, while Nigerian partner AMNI holds 60%. The Ima field straddles the OML 112 and 117 offshore licenses in shallow waters near Bonny Island. The development will comprise a single offshore platform connected to Nigeria LNG by a 22-km pipeline. At its planned plateau of 350 MMcf/d, equivalent to more than 60,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, Ima is expected to provide about one-third of the gas required for Nigeria LNG's ongoing Train 7 expansion. TotalEnergies holds a 15% interest in Nigeria LNG, whose Train 7 project is set to increase liquefaction capacity to 30 million tonnes per annum from 22 Mtpa. The Ima development will use a simplified platform design and receive electric power from shore. It is planned without flaring and will include permanent methane detection and monitoring.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543194-ch.text: Chevron plans to begin seismic surveys in Greek waters before the end of 2026, covering areas in the Ionian Sea and south of the Peloponnese and Crete, Greece's energy ministry said. The timetable was confirmed during a meeting between Greek Environment and Energy Minister Stavros Papastavrou and Chevron's head for Greece, Beatrice Bienvenu. The two discussed the next steps needed to keep the exploration program on schedule, with the ministry saying work would proceed in accordance with environmental and safety requirements. The planned surveys follow the signing in February of exclusive lease agreements under which a Chevron-led consortium will explore four deep-sea blocks south of the Peloponnese and Crete covering about 47,000 square kilometers. Chevron and Helleniq Energy had won the acreage in an international tender, with Chevron leading the exploration programme. Chevron has also moved to expand its position farther west. Greece in June approved its request to take over a 70% interest from Helleniq Energy in an offshore block southwest of the Ionian Sea and become its operator, with Helleniq retaining 30%.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543193-so.text: South Korea aims to reduce its reliance on crude oil from the Middle East to 50% by 2035, as Asia's fourth-biggest economy seeks to diversify energy supplies following the disruption caused by the Iran war, the Industry Ministry said on Wednesday. In its 10-year natural resources security plan, the ministry said the country needed a "fundamental shift" in its supply chains, citing lessons from the Iran war, which has choked off global energy flows. South Korea relies heavily on oil imports and sourced 70% of its supplies from the Middle East in 2025, most of it delivered through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the ministry. Under the updated strategy, the country adjusted its stockpiling plan for crude oil, targeting an expansion of around 20 million barrels by 2030. South Korea also aims to secure additional supplies of condensate, an ultra-light oil mainly used to produce naphtha, the ministry said. The country has struggled with a shortage of naphtha, the key feedstock for petrochemicals, since the Middle East conflict. South Korea relies on imports to satisfy about 45% of its naphtha demand, with 77% of those supplies typically sourced from the Middle East, according to the ministry.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Velox Soluções Técnicas contratou uma consultoria especializada em expansão internacional para analisar a aderência de seus serviços ao mercado dos Estados Unidos . De acordo com a própria empresa, caso o estudo seja positivo ela pode iniciar atendimentos em território norte-americano já no primeiro semestre de 2027. Especializada na gestão operacional de ocorrências no transporte rodoviário de cargas, a Velox mantém atualmente uma rede de atendimento em oito países além do Brasil: Argentina, Uruguai, Chile, Paraguai, Bolívia, Peru, Venezuela e México. A entrada no mercado norte-americano faz parte da estratégia de internacionalização da empresa, que começou por fluxos rodoviários conectados ao Brasil e agora avalia a possibilidade de avançar para um novo mercado. Para avançar em sua avaliação, a consultoria contratada pela Velox analisará as características do setor nos Estados Unidos com o objetivo de identificar se o modelo de serviços da companhia encontra espaço para operação no país. De acordo com Jeder Ribas, diretor da Velox, a consultoria possui experiência em diferentes regiões do mundo, incluindo Europa, América do Norte, América do Sul e Ásia. A atuação internacional da Velox envolve serviços como pronta resposta, recuperação veicular, sindicância, inteligência e acompanhamento logístico, permitindo atender ocorrências relacionadas também a cargas transportadas entre diferentes países. Na América Latina, Chile, Argentina e Peru vêm ganhando relevância na estratégia da Velox. Segundo Ribas, os dois primeiros países são importantes corredores para cargas como salmão e carne, enquanto o Peru tem registrado aumento da movimentação logística associado ao Porto de Chancay. A empresa já conta com prestadores locais para atender demandas de clientes nesses mercados. O Paraguai também se destaca na operação internacional. No primeiro semestre de 2026, o país concentrou cerca de 80% dos atendimentos realizados pela Velox fora do Brasil. “Esses países são importantes não só para a Velox, mas para toda a cadeia logística brasileira. A movimentação de cargas precisa de suporte onde o cliente estiver, e é aí que entra a nossa atuação”, conclui Ribas.

A ID Logistics ampliou de 10 mil m² para cerca de 20 mil m² o centro de distribuição da Beiersdorf em Extrema (MG) . A expansão amplia a capacidade da operação logística das marcas NIVEA e Eucerin no país e integra a estratégia das empresas para acompanhar o crescimento da demanda nos próximos cinco anos. A parceria entre ID Logistics e Beiersdorf no Brasil começou em 2013 e contempla atualmente a gestão da cadeia de armazenagem nacional. Com a ampliação, o CD passa a contar com uma estrutura maior para as atividades de recebimento, armazenagem, controle de inventário, separação e expedição de pedidos, além de logística reversa, gestão de paletes, inspeção de qualidade e processos documentais relacionados ao transporte alfandegário e de mercadorias classificadas. A operação utiliza tecnologias como inventário com drones, e-cockpit, check-list eletrônico, portaria eletrônica, equipamentos de movimentação com baterias de lítio e telemetria. A expansão também prevê a geração de novos empregos diretos e a realocação de profissionais que já atuavam na operação. “A expansão do centro de distribuição fortalece nossa estratégia de supply chain, combinando tecnologia, eficiência operacional e maior capacidade para acompanhar o crescimento da Beiersdorf no Brasil. Uma operação mais integrada e inteligente nos permite responder com agilidade às demandas do mercado e gerar ainda mais valor para o negócio”, afirma Fátima Ribeiro, diretora de Supply Chain da Beiersdorf - Casa de NIVEA e Eucerin. Segundo a ID Logistics, a operação também conta com iniciativas de sustentabilidade. As unidades de Extrema e Jundiaí têm emissões de carbono zeradas nos escopos 1 e 2. O condomínio logístico possui certificação LEED, além de reutilização de água da chuva, iluminação LED e infraestrutura preparada para mobilidade elétrica. Para a ID Logistics, a ampliação consolida uma parceria de mais de dez anos e reforça a estrutura da empresa para atender à operação da Beiersdorf no mercado brasileiro. “A expansão representa uma operação mais robusta e a consolidação de uma parceria baseada em confiança, inovação e excelência operacional. Seguiremos investindo continuamente em soluções cada vez mais eficientes, sustentáveis e preparadas para o futuro da logística”, afirma Gilberto Lima, CEO da ID Logistics Brasil.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/a_critical_.text: In a report sent to Rigzone on Tuesday by the Macquarie team, Macquarie strategists, including Thierry Wizman, Global FX and Rates Strategist at Macquarie Group, noted that this was a “critical week for oil - and thus for everything else”. “What happens this week may become critical for the direction of crude oil prices over the medium term,” the strategists said in the report. “That’s because the key actors in the U.S.-Iran War will be having meetings in New York, starting today [Tuesday]. And the agreements and accords that come out of those meetings may determine whether the war continues and intensifies or whether an off ramp is found,” they added. In the report, the strategists outlined that they think the discussions can go either way, “including the bad way”. “One reason is that the Iranian side has gotten much more aggressive in its rhetoric already,” they warned. “Officials there have warned that any U.S. attack would make American bases and interests across the region targets of ‘continuous, effective, and painful strikes’, and that U.S. naval forces could be again targeted in the Indian Ocean,” they said.

https://safety4sea.com/all-25-crew-rescu.text: All 25 crew members of the Liberia-flagged containership MSC Hermes III were rescued on September 22 after abandoning the vessel in a lifeboat about 300 km east of Vietnam. T he Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) Singapore received a distress alert from the 212-meter containership at approximately 8:45 a.m. Singapore time. At the time, MSC Hermes III was within Singapore’s Maritime Search and Rescue Region and was reportedly sailing from Shanghai, China, to Jakarta, Indonesia. Following the alert, MRCC Singapore immediately issued a broadcast requesting nearby vessels to assist. Three vessels responded to the request, with the Liberia-flagged containership MSC Ruby subsequently recovering all 25 crew members from their lifeboat after they had abandoned MSC Hermes III. All crew members were reported safe, with no injuries. MRCC Singapore is coordinating with the Vietnamese Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre on arrangements for the rescued seafarers to be safely brought ashore. The circumstances that led to the distress alert and the decision to abandon MSC Hermes III have not yet been disclosed. No further details on the vessel’s condition or any reported pollution have been provided.

https://safety4sea.com/shippings-green-t.text: Credit: Climate action in shipping: Progress towards shipping's 2030 breakthrough The shipping industry is facing a growing risk of missing its 2030 zero-emission fuel target, as regulatory uncertainty and mounting economic and geopolitical pressures threaten to slow the transition, according to a new report. L aunched on 22 September, during New York Climate Week, the fifth edition of Climate Action in Shipping: Progress Towards Shipping’s 2030 Breakthrough assesses the industry’s progress towards a critical 2030 milestone: ensuring that at least 5–10% of the fuel used in international shipping comes from scalable zero-emission fuels (SZEF). The report is a joint effort between the UCL Energy Institute and the Getting to Zero Coalition, in the framework of the Marrakech Partnership. That threshold is considered the level of SZEF uptake needed to put the sector on a credible path towards the ambitions set out in the International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) 2023 Greenhouse Gas Strategy — and, ultimately, its goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. The latest report paints a mixed picture. While some progress has been made, several indicators point to growing headwinds for the transition, including economic and political upheaval, the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, energy-security and supply-chain concerns, and heightened regulatory uncertainty following the failure to adopt the IMO’s proposed Net-Zero Framework (NZF) last year. With the 2030 deadline now rapidly approaching, the report suggests that the disruption of the past year is beginning to translate into tangible risks for the shipping industry’s decarbonisation trajectory.

https://splash247.com/diana-extends-rate.text: Diana Shipping has extended its run of stronger dry bulk fixtures, locking the ultramax DSI Polaris into a new charter with Dai An Ocean Shipping at $18,000 per day, nearly 47% above its current rate. The 2018-built, 60,404 dwt bulker will start its new employment on September 25 at $18,000 per day, less a 5% commission. The charter runs until at least May 1, 2028 and can stretch through June 30 of that year. Diana said it expects the minimum period to generate around $10.37m in gross revenue. The ship is currently earning $12,250 per day with Cargill Ocean Transportation, less a 4.75% commission. That charter started in July last year and was due to end by September 21. The switch to Dai An lifts the headline rate by $5,750 per day, or just under 47%. The latest fixture keeps up the stronger rate trend seen across the Semiramis Paliou-led owner’s fleet. Earlier this month, the 81,513 dwt kamsarmax Astarte moved to Aquavita at $17,000 per day, 36% above its previous employment, while the panamax Leto recently rolled into a $18,000-a-day continuation with Cargill, a 41% increase. Diana currently operates 36 bulkers totalling about 4.1m dwt and has two methanol dual-fuel kamsarmax newbuildings scheduled for delivery in the second half of 2027 and first half of 2028.

https://splash247.com/china-linked-hacke.text: Chinese state-linked hackers are mounting sustained cyberespionage campaigns against maritime organisations across Europe, with shipping emerging as a consistent target for Beijing-linked threat groups, the European Union’s cybersecurity agency has warned. ENISA’s newly published Threat Landscape 2026 says China-nexus groups maintained a particular interest in telecommunications, maritime, semiconductor, manufacturing and government organisations during 2025. Most prominent in shipping was Mustang Panda, also known as Earth Preta, which ENISA says conducted continuous campaigns against maritime-related organisations across at least seven EU member states. The group uses spear-phishing, compromised USB drives and a range of malware including customised versions of the PlugX remote-access tool. The activity was primarily aimed at cyberespionage and strategic intelligence collection rather than immediate operational disruption. Transport accounted for 8% of all cyber events recorded by ENISA across the EU last year, with water transport making up 16.4% of transport-sector incidents. Maritime and railway transport are both classified by the agency as being in a cyber “risk zone”, reflecting their strategic importance and dependence on heterogeneous and increasingly interconnected systems. In 2022, Splash reported that CyberOwl had discovered nation-state malware from the PlugX family aboard seven ships belonging to a major liner fleet. PlugX gives attackers remote access and potentially full administrative control of compromised computers, allowing them to manipulate files, execute commands and spread through local networks.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mae.text: Maersk, the world’s second-largest shipping group, has boosted its use of the shorter Suez Canal route from Asia to Europe amid a very tight global shipping market driven by port congestion and altered trade flows. Speaking on the sidelines of the European Association of Chemical Distributors (Fecc) annual conference, Patrick Hore, global vertical head of chemicals at Maersk, said the global container shipping system has adapted to Middle East disruption, but availability of vessels and uneven trade flows remain major issues. Hore said the system has adapted to ongoing disruption in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz, with more services returning to the Suez Canal because the route cuts transit times and emissions compared with sailing around the Cape of Good Hope. “We’re sending more and more services through the Red Sea and through the Suez Canal with now six major services that we have between Asia and Europe, and our Middle East-Europe-North America service, so there is a return to normal as far as possible, and safe, and of course there are big savings in transit times and in CO2 emissions.” Maersk was one of the earliest container groups to return to the Suez Canal route, which had been out of bounds for most logistics groups since Houthi attacks against shipping began in late 2023. The move by Maersk and others is likely to reduce the cost and transit time for chemical imports to Europe from China and the rest of Asia.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/allseas-.text: Energy and marine consultancy ABL, part of Oslo-listed global consultancy group Aqualis, has been hired by Switzerland-based offshore contractor Allseas to support the lifting of a massive 60,000-ton topside in a single motion as part of a North Sea decommissioning project on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS). ABL has been selected by Allseas as marine warranty surveyor (MWS) for the single-lift removal of Equinor’s Statfjord A topside. The Swiss player is the offshore contractor undertaking the engineering, preparation, removal and disposal (EPRD) of the concrete gravity-base production platform in the North Sea. ABL Norway will lead the MWS project delivery, drawing on the wider expertise of the company’s North Sea decommissioning specialists. The firm’s operations in Norway will work to reduce risks to an acceptable minimum throughout the critical operation, while ensuring delivery in accordance with agreed procedures and in compliance with local regulations. Subbi Nookala , ABL’s Country Manager in Norway, commented : “We are pleased to continue our long-standing relationship with Allseas in Norway by supporting the safe execution of this trailblazing topside removal and offshore lift operation for Equinor. “Statfjord A is a legendary asset, and the project brings significant technical and operational challenges. We look forward to working with Allseas to help deliver this important project.”

https://petronoticias.com.br/castrol-lan.text: A Castrol está trazendo ao mercado brasileiro uma nova solução de monitoramento contínuo da qualidade do óleo lubrificante, com foco na prevenção de falhas e no aumento da confiabilidade de equipamentos de alta criticidade. Batizado de Castrol SmartMonitor, o sistema acompanha em tempo real diversos parâmetros, permitindo identificar alterações na condição dos lubrificantes antes que elas evoluam para problemas mais graves em motores, compressores, turbinas e propulsores marítimos. Em entrevista ao Petronotícias, o gerente de Contas Estratégicas para Energia da Castrol no Brasil, Rafael Clemente , disse que a empresa já iniciou conversas com dois grandes players do setor para testes e parcerias tecnológicas com o SmartMonitor, e tem a expectativa de obter os primeiros resultados de campo ainda este ano. Além do lançamento da ferramenta, a movimentação faz parte de uma estratégia mais ampla da Castrol para ampliar sua presença no mercado brasileiro de energia. A companhia vê oportunidades no crescimento da frota de FPSOs e na atividade de perfuração no país e pretende combinar seu portfólio de lubrificantes com serviços de acompanhamento técnico e soluções digitais voltadas à gestão e à eficiência de ativos. Para começar e contextualizar os nossos leitores, você poderia dar um panorama geral sobre o que é o Castrol SmartMonitor, como ele funciona e qual é o seu objetivo? O Castrol SmartMonitor é uma solução de monitoramento online e contínuo (24/7) da qualidade do óleo lubrificante em uso. O equipamento funciona por meio da gestão e da coleta de dados em tempo real sobre a condição do fluido, enviando essas informações para a plataforma da Castrol, onde são analisadas por nossos especialistas técnicos. Trata-se de uma ferramenta de transformação digital e de evolução no nosso portfólio. Ela traduz a leitura que fazemos do mercado de energia, um setor que exige alta confiabilidade. A ferramenta entrega essa confiabilidade à gestão de ativos, auxiliando na manutenção preventiva, na redução de custos e na antecipação de desafios técnicos e operacionais. Além disso, ela complementa a análise tradicional por amostragem. Hoje, o processo convencional envolve a coleta em embalagens e uma logística complexa, em que o tempo decorrido entre a amostragem e o diagnóstico em laboratório pode ser excessivo. Nesse intervalo, falhas podem ocorrer. O SmartMonitor atua justamente na prevenção dessas intercorrências em motores, propulsores e compressores, combinando monitoramento em tempo real, análise de dados e a expertise técnica da Castrol. A ferramenta coleta os dados e eles são analisados por especialistas humanos, ou existe a utilização de Inteligência Artificial nesse processo?

https://maritime-executive.com/article/d.text: Following a televised discussion between President Donald Trump and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the UN General Assembly in New York, the Diego Garcia surrender deal, which the United Kingdom had negotiated with Mauritius, appears to have been shelved. Trump described the deal as “terrible” and “ridiculous,” while earlier having called it “an act of GREAT STUPIDITY.” Trump’s opinion is critical, as US assent is required under international law to change the existing 1965 UK-US agreement governing the use of the Diego Garcia, which is formally registered as an international treaty. The deal envisioned a transfer of sovereignty of the entire Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius, and then a leaseback of Diego Garcia to the United Kingdom to facilitate the continued operation of the Naval Support Facility, on payment by the UK of an annual rent to Mauritius. The Diego Garcia ramp in May 2025 while the conflict with the Houthis was ongoing (Sentinel-2c) The deal had a number of obvious flaws. The UK was to pay rent, from its heavily stretched defense budget, for a lease to an island that has never been found legally to have been anything but British. With sovereignty surrendered, promises by Mauritius about future constraints on the use of the Chagos could not have been legally enforced, leading to questions about Chinese encroachments and exploitation of what for the moment remains the world’s largest marine reserve. Most importantly, it offered no redress to Chagos islanders, who were neither consulted about the deal nor given any guarantees of a right to return to the islands where many of them had been born. Legally, the lease-back deal agreed between the UK and Mauritius is in effect in suspended animation, as the necessary legislation to ratify the deal failed to pass in the British Houses of Parliament earlier this year. Following the discussions this week in New York, the UK side has agreed that the matter needs to be looked at afresh, and Wes Streeting, the UK Defense Minister, has subsequently described the deal as ‘not good enough’. This all implies that a new deal needs to be negotiated between Mauritius and the UK, one which would need to be acceptable to the United States and guarantee the continued use of Naval Support Facility Diego Garcia. With US bases in the Middle East increasingly vulnerable to newly-developed Iranian missiles and drones, the utility of Diego Garcia – close enough but not too close to the sources of instability in the Middle East – is now probably greater than ever.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543206-st.text: Stillstrom by Maersk has signed a letter of intent (LOI) with Semco Maritime to manufacture and deliver a key part of its offshore vessel charging system, moving the technology into manufacturing following completion of its design phase. Semco Maritime will manufacture the local equipment room, or local equipment room (LER), which controls power, communications and safety functions across Stillstrom's offshore charging infrastructure. The containerized unit houses the transformer and medium-voltage switchgear used to transfer offshore-generated electricity from a wind farm to a vessel, alongside communications equipment, ventilation and fire safety systems. It is designed to be installed on a monopile or hang-off structure at each charging location. Manufacturing is planned at Semco Maritime's facility in Esbjerg, Denmark, with completion targeted for spring 2027. Stillstrom said future units could potentially also be manufactured at Semco Maritime's UK facilities. “Completing the design and now moving into manufacture is a major milestone for us. It controls everything that happens, from how power reaches the vessel to how every safety system talks to each other. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543204-pe.text: Perenco Brazil and Porto do Açu have signed a letter of intent to develop an offshore electrification project that would supply up to 60 MW of shore power to Perenco's platforms in the Campos Basin through an 80 km subsea cable. https://www.rigzone.com/news/usairan_con.text: The U.S.-Iran conflict has changed the definition of an available barrel, Ole Hvalbye, Partner at ABG Sundal Collier, told Rigzone. “Production capacity is of course of limited value if the crude cannot be processed, transported, [and] loaded/delivered to the consumer,” Hvalbye said. “I believe that the market will increasingly distinguish between spare capacity on paper and ‘actual deliverable spare capacity’,” he added. Hvalbye outlined to Rigzone that the conflict may not have caused lasting changes in terms of physical scarcity or permanently higher oil/product prices but warned that he believes it has changed how the market values security of supply and likely also spare capacity. “The oil market is not permanently short, but it is permanently less trusting,” Hvalbye told Rigzone. “The result is unlikely to be one forever high oil price. Yet, it is a higher value placed on secure logistics, inventories, refining flexibility and diversified supply,” he added.

https://safety4sea.com/iran-offers-to-re.text: Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States takes initial steps to ease military pressure on Tehran, according to a senior Iranian government official. T he proposal, which has reportedly been conveyed to Washington through intermediaries, is part of Tehran’s renewed efforts to bring the United States back to negotiations and establish a lasting end to hostilities between the two countries. According to Kyodo news, the Iranian official said Tehran intends to use this week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York to consult with countries acting as intermediaries in the dispute. However, the official ruled out a meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and US President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the gathering. Despite this, Tehran maintains that there is still scope for diplomatic progress, provided Washington demonstrates what the Iranian side described as sufficient “seriousness and commitment” to negotiations. According to the official, Iran is seeking evidence that the United States is prepared to return to talks and take steps toward ending what Tehran describes as a US military blockade of Iranian ports, as well as halting military operations linked to the Strait of Hormuz. If Washington takes those initial measures, Iran would be prepared to reopen the strategic waterway within seven days and return to negotiations, the official said.

https://safety4sea.com/regional-incident.text: Two separate incidents reported in the vicinity of two of the world’s most strategically important maritime chokepoints are once again raising concerns over the security of commercial shipping in the Middle East. Initial reports indicated that the blast appeared to have occurred at sea, with no missile or other projectile reported to have struck the island itself. At the time of the initial reports, there was no confirmed information regarding damage or casualties, while Iranian authorities had yet to provide an official explanation of the cause or precise location of the explosion. Qeshm, the largest island in the Persian Gulf, lies on the northern side of the Strait of Hormuz and occupies a strategically important position along one of the world’s principal maritime energy corridors. Any security incident in or around the strait, even in the absence of confirmed damage, can prompt heightened monitoring by shipowners, operators, insurers and maritime security organizations. Around the same time, Houthi military spokesman Brigadier General Yahya Sari reportedly announced that Houthi forces had shot down a Wing Loong II unmanned aerial vehicle, which he claimed was operated by Saudi Arabia. According to the Houthi statement, the armed reconnaissance drone was conducting what was described as “hostile missions” in the airspace over Mocha, in Yemen’s western Taiz province, when it was engaged with a “suitable weapon.” The statement did not specify the air-defence system used. There was also no immediate official confirmation from Saudi authorities in the initial reporting.

https://safety4sea.com/indonesia-ferry-s.text: The death toll from the capsizing and sinking of the passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 off Indonesia has risen to 28, with rescuers widening underwater search efforts as 107 people remain missing. T he ferry was carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members and an unknown number of vehicles, when it capsized in bad weather early on September 13 while sailing from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan. According to Reuters, Coast guard and Navy personnel recovered 16 bodies from inside the vessel over the past three days, including nine on Wednesday. Two additional bodies were found washed ashore about 253 km from the accident site, according to Mohammad Syafii, head of Indonesia’s National Rescue Agency. As of September 23, authorities had confirmed 28 fatalities, 107 people missing and 108 survivors. The search and rescue operation has been extended until September 27. The latest search efforts are focused on the ferry’s hull, particularly its cabins, where rescuers believe a number of passengers remain trapped. Divers broke the cabin windows on Tuesday but were unable to enter because of poor visibility caused by murky water and strong currents. I Putu Sudayana, head of the Banjarmasin rescue agency, said rescuers were concentrating on the hull after finding multiple passengers inside the cabins. Tim Basarnas Special Group (BSG) menyelam dilokasi tenggelamnya KM Virgo Transport 8, Laut Jawa, pada Minggu (20/9/2026).

https://safety4sea.com/watch-protecting-.text: For thousands of seafarers, the end of a voyage does not always mean a safe return home. With abandonment cases continuing to threaten crews and their families worldwide, The Seafarers’ Charity has released the final films in its “Smart Seafaring. A Safe Return” campaign. R eleased ahead of World Maritime Day on 24 September, the films aim to help seafarers and their families recognise the warning signs of abandonment, take practical steps to protect themselves and understand where to seek help if a situation deteriorates. According to the International Transport Workers’ Federation, 2025 was the worst year on record for seafarer abandonment, with 410 vessels and 6,223 seafarers affected — more than 30% higher than in 2024. Under the IMO/ILO Guidelines, a seafarer is considered abandoned when a shipowner fails to cover the cost of repatriation, provide basic necessities such as food and accommodation, or pay contractual wages for at least two months. The guidelines also refer to the “severance of ties”, including situations where a ship’s master is left without the financial means to operate the vessel. Abandonment can leave seafarers stranded in a foreign port or onboard a vessel with no means of returning home. The Seafarers’ Charity said the films are designed to provide practical and accessible information to seafarers and their families before a situation escalates.

https://gcaptain.com/seafarer-killed-in-.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 31, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer An Indian seafarer has been killed after the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was attacked and abandoned near the Strait of Hormuz, adding to a mounting casualty toll as the United States and Iran reopen diplomatic contacts at the United Nations. The Cape Dao was targeted about 2.5 nautical miles from Oman’s Musandam Governorate on Wednesday, according to Oman’s Maritime Security Center. The attack sparked a fire in the engine room, and a Royal Navy of Oman vessel evacuated 27 surviving crew members and provided medical care. UK Maritime Trade Operations had earlier reported that the cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile at around 0630 UTC while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO said the vessel was on fire and adrift and initially reported two casualties. The Forward Seamen’s Union of India identified the seafarer killed as Suraj Yadav, 26, a wiper from Deoria in Uttar Pradesh. The union said the Cape Dao , IMO 9219020, was sailing from Mina Saqr in the United Arab Emirates toward India with 28 crew members aboard, including 20 Indians. It said the vessel was struck twice on its port side, with one projectile hitting the C-deck accommodation area and another hitting the hull near the engine room.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/perenco-.text: In a bid to strike a balance between maximizing asset longevity and curbing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, Perenco Brasil, a subsidiary of Anglo-French oil and gas player Perenco, is joining forces with Porto do Açu to bring shore power directly to its offshore fields in the Campos Basin off the coast of Brazil. Porto do Açu and Perenco have signed a letter of intent (LOI) to develop what is being described as the first offshore platform electrification project in the Campos Basin. The initiative will link the operator’s shallow-water Pargo and Cherne clusters to shore via an 80-kilometer subsea cable, replacing local turbogenerators with a reliable grid power supply capable of scaling from an initial 35 MW up to 60 MW by early 2028. The port complex will provide an area for the construction of Perenco’s onshore power grid connection, as well as the right-of-way for the cable, which will run from the onshore substation at Porto do Açu in São João da Barra, Rio de Janeiro, to the offshore fields. The primary objective of this agreement, which foresees supplying power from shore to the shallow-water fields, is to reduce scope 1 emissions from Perenco’s operations in Brazil. Currently, the company’s platforms in the Pargo and Cherne clusters rely on power generated locally by turbogenerators. Eugenio Figueiredo , CEO of Porto do Açu, commented: “The partnership with Perenco reinforces Porto do Açu’s position as a catalyst for low-carbon solutions in the oil and gas sector. Offshore electrification projects of this scale are still rare globally and pave a promising way forward for the Brazilian market.” While the project’s initial power consumption forecast is 35 MW, there is potential for expansion to up to 60 MW within four years. The system is expected to become operational by the first quarter of 2028. The operator may also contract power from renewable sources in the open market once it is running.

https://gcaptain.com/trump-takes-aim-at-.text: US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 22, 2026. REUTERS/MIKE SEGAR President Donald Trump used his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday to renew his attack on the International Maritime Organization’s Net-Zero Framework , accusing the UN shipping agency of attempting to impose a global carbon tax that would drive up transportation costs. “Last year, my administration was forced to intervene to stop an obscure U.N. body, the International Maritime Organization, from secretly establishing a first-ever global carbon tax,” Trump said, claiming the measure would raise international shipping costs by “10 to 20% — and maybe more than that.” “There is no global government,” Trump added. “And while I’m president, there will be no global taxes.” The remarks elevate a fight that has been playing out at the IMO for more than a year and come as member states prepare for another attempt to finalize the framework in December. The Trump administration played a major role in last year’s decision to postpone adoption. Ahead of the vote, U.S. officials threatened countries supporting the framework with measures including tariffs, visa restrictions, port fees and sanctions. The extraordinary Marine Environment Protection Committee session ultimately postponed adoption for one year following a 57-49 vote.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/subsea-c.text: Netherlands-headquartered Subsea Cable Assets (SCA) has won its first contract with Saipem for cable transportation and transpooling services in the Caspian region, valued at approximately $20 million. Under the contract secured with Saipem Contracting Netherlands BV, SCA will provide engineering, specific equipment fabrication, installation and operation, demobilization and reinstatement to support an offshore energy project in the Caspian region, described as major. The scope includes the delivery of five cable transport carousels, each with a 1,100 ton capacity and associated cable handling equipment. The cable spooling equipment will be mobilized on a cable transport vessel for cable load-out at JDR Cable Systems in the UK. The loaded cable carousels will then be transported to Southeastern Europe for onward mobilization using self-propelled modular transporters (SPMTs) onto smaller transport barges and to the Caspian region, SCA explained. The company has started the manufacture of cable carousels and related equipment at its facility in Dubai, UAE, with shipment to Europe planned by the end of the year. “This multi-million-dollar contract with Saipem demonstrates the experience our team brings to complex cable transport and handling projects, based on our extensive track record created over recent years,” said Sil de Rijke , SCA’s Chief Operating Officer (COO).
