https://splash247.com/hafnia-closes-in-o.text: Hafnia has raised $300m in fresh equity after making another move on Torm, taking its holding in the Danish product tanker owner to 19.85%. The BW Group-backed tanker giant allocated 35.49m new shares at NOK80 apiece through an accelerated bookbuild, raising the NOK equivalent of approximately $300m. The placement price was about 8% below Hafnia’s NOK86.95 closing price immediately before the deal was launched. Hafnia said the proceeds will strengthen its balance sheet following its accumulation of Torm shares, including repaying debt taken on to fund the purchases. Cash will also be available for potential strategic opportunities and general corporate purposes. The capital raise came as Hafnia agreed to buy another 1.7m Torm A shares at $34 each, spending $57.8m for another 1.66% of the company. The acquisition, funded through cash on hand and available credit lines, lifts Hafnia’s interest to approximately 19.85%. It is Hafnia’s second sizeable Torm top-up in little more than a week. Splash reported last Wednesday that Hafnia had agreed to acquire 4.5m shares at $32.25 apiece for $145.1m, taking its stake above 18% and cementing its position as Torm’s largest shareholder. That followed its initial move last year when Hafnia bought around 14.16m shares from the Oaktree-linked OCM Njord vehicle at $22 each for $311.4m.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/slbs-gra.text: U.S.-headquartered technology player SLB has added more than 450 wells to its job list in one fell swoop by locking down a four-contract quadfecta with Saudi Arabia’s energy giant Aramco. SLB has secured four integrated well construction contracts with Aramco to support oil and gas development across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where it will manage end-to-end well construction services, delivering more than 450 wells during the three-year term, with an optional extension of up to two years for each. Steve Gassen , Executive Vice President of Geographies for SLB, commented: “Delivering hundreds of wells across a multi-year program and in multiple operating environments requires an integrated model that connects planning, execution, and digital workflows to set new industry performance benchmarks. Awarding SLB these advanced well construction programs at scale reflects Aramco’s confidence in our integrated model and capabilities.” The U.S. technology player emphasizes that its integrated well construction model brings together every aspect of well delivery through a technology-enabled operating model, combining digital drilling workflows with automated drilling, evaluation, fluids, cementing, and completions products and services to improve efficiency, consistency, and well performance across diverse, large-scale drilling programs. The latest deal builds on decades of collaboration between the two companies, representing a significant expansion of SLB’s integrated well construction business in Saudi Arabia, while underscoring growing customer adoption of integrated delivery models for large-scale drilling programs and highlighting the model’s ability to improve execution consistency across the well construction lifecycle. The three-year quartet follows weeks after SLB was hired by Brunei Shell Petroleum (BSP), a joint venture between the Brunei government and Shell, to lend a hand in restoring oil and gas production across mature fields off the coast of Brunei.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/go-ahead.text: Norway’s oil and gas player DNO has secured the thumbs-up from the country’s authorities for drilling activities in the North Sea with a semi-submersible rig managed by Odfjell Drilling, an offshore drilling contractor. The Norwegian Ocean Industry Authority (Havtil) has granted DNO Norge consent for exploration drilling in block 25/7 for the Norma Appraisal prospect in the North Sea. This consent covers the 25/7-15 S appraisal well and 25/7-15 A side-track in production license 984 , which is valid from March 1, 2019, until the same date in 2029. DNO Norge (30%) is the operator of this production license, with the remaining licensees being Vår Energi (20%), Equinor (20%), Source Energy (20%), and Aker BP (10%). The water depth at the site is 121 meters, and the drilling activities will be conducted with the Deepsea Yantai semi-submersible rig. The rig is working on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS) on drilling assignments with DNO, Wellesley Petroleum, and Well Expertise.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/chevron-.text: Egypt is putting its foot on the gas pedal in a bid to fast-track its Mediterranean energy hub ambitions by holding high-level talks with the U.S.-headquartered energy giant Chevron to secure an accelerated timeline for its infrastructure to be linked to a gas field off the coast of Cyprus. The new opportunities for Chevron to expand its gas exploration activities in the Mediterranean and acceleration of the frameworks and procedures required to finalize agreements for connecting Aphrodite to Egypt’s infrastructure were among the key topics during a videoconference meeting between Karim Badawi , Egypt’s Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, and Javier La Rosa , President of Chevron’s Base Assets and Emerging Countries, which was also attended by some of the company’s senior executives. Badawi asserted the importance of accelerating the completion of the necessary procedures and agreements to connect the Aphrodite field to the country’s infrastructure, supporting progress in implementing the project and maximizing the available potential for both sides. Aphrodite was discovered with the A-1 well in September 2011 and was followed by the A-2 appraisal well, drilled in 2013, which confirmed approximately 98 billion cubic meters (bcm) of contingent resource with potential for an additional 26 bcm of prospective resources. The plan is to develop a system offshore Egypt for gas transmission to EGAS. Located in the area of Block 12 in Cyprus, the Aphrodite project envisions the production and processing of natural gas from the field through four production wells connected to a floating production unit (FPU) positioned over the field. Egypt’s Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources pointed out that cooperation with Cyprus in the domain of natural gas received high-level political support, providing important momentum for advancing the various technical and commercial tracks related to the project.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/watch-co.text: China Merchants Heavy Industry (CMHI) has started the construction of the first of two Asso.subsea’s trenching support vessels (TSV), described as the most powerful TSV ever built. Asso.subsea reported on September 23 that the steel-cutting ceremony was held for the TSV Avra at the CMHI Shenzhen shipyard, one year after the shipbuilding contract was announced . This March, the partners signed the shipbuilding contract for the construction of the second TSV, named Andromeda, sister to Avra. The vessels will have 24 MW hybrid power and over 180 tons bollard pull, a 4,000-ton under-deck cable carousel capability and twin working decks and will be able to support a wide range of projects including dynamic cable spreads, floating wind installations, inter-array and export cable operations. In the announcement for the first unit, Asso.subsea said it would be methanol- and biofuel-ready, featuring a large battery hybrid system, equipped with cold-ironing capability, and will feature a 150-ton offshore/subsea crane and dual heavy-duty A-frames. Avra is expected to be delivered at the end of 2027, with Andromeda following in the second quarter of 2028.

https://splash247.com/ventura-offshore-a.text: Offshore driller Ventura Offshore has won another contract extension for one of its semisubmersible rigs. Ventura Offshore said Searah West Ganal Limited and Searah Ganal Deepwater Limited, subsidiaries of Searah, a JV between Eni and Petronas, exercised the option for another well. This extension covers the drilling of the JKNE Upside-1 Dir well and a tophole in Indonesia by the semisub drilling rig, SSV Catarina . This well, in addition to the four optional wells exercised previously, further increases Ventura’s firm backlog by approximately $21.7m and is expected to keep the rig utilised into December 2026. The rig started working for Eni in August 2024. Apart from well options in Indonesia, the Italian firm has a fixed-price option for one well in Vietnam. The SSV Catarina became part of the Ventura Offshore fleet in June 2024 when it was bought from Umas 1 for $105m.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: Australian-owned marine engineering firm Birdon has begun building its first "tranche" of Medium Unmanned Surface Vessels for the long-awaited U.S. Navy MUSV program, and at a fast pace of one vessel every two months. After several iterations of its MUSV acquisition strategy, the U.S. Navy has picked out seven different companies to compete for the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel program, including Sea Machines; Leidos; Saronic Technologies; Galliano Marine Services; PacMar Technologies; Birdon; and Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), many in partnership with other firms. Birdon has partnered with autonomous navigation and control firm Mythos AI, based in Florida, for its underlying unmanned-systems technology. For construction, it has an agreement with New Orleans-area shipyard C&C Marine, a modern, high-automation fabrication facility. Birdon provides system integration, design and prime-contractor oversight. The choice of an established shipyard was deliberate, aimed at satisfying the Navy's needs for rapid prototyping and delivery. C&C has been building and repairing working vessels for nearly three decades, and puts a premium on on-time, on-budget performance. It worked with Birdon previously on the Marine Corps' Ancillary Surface Craft (ASC), a prototype 150-foot beach landing vessel for combat logistics. Birdon has put C&C's immediate production-ready capability at front and center in the consortium's plans. "Starting the build moves this effort from planning into execution. It demonstrates our certainty of delivery, founded on in-place - not promised - capacity," said Birdon President Kevin Mooney. "We are pairing production-ready engineering with a trusted serial manufacturer."

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The American Bureau of Shipping, DNV and RINA have agreed to join the Maritime Anti-Corruption Network (MACN), bringing new technical expertise to the global association for integrity in shipping. Historically, MACN's work has centered on combating facilitation payments (gratuities) in seaports, a longtime feature of interaction between ships' officers and local officials in certain port states around the world. Official solicitations for small payments of petty cash, food or cigarettes are common in some regions, and larger demands for bribes are not unheard-of. Seafarers are often at the receiving end, forced to decide whether to pay or to risk a made-up enforcement action that would delay their ship (and cost their company considerable amounts of money). Overall, MACN says that corruption can increase transport cost by 15 percent, and it has a global estimated cost of about $160 million per year - a cost that shipping stakeholders have to pass on to their customers or absorb on their balance sheets. MACN's 200-plus members have banded together to resist these practices by sharing best practices; training seafarers on identifying and reporting corrupt practices; collecting incident reports of corrupt demands; sharing intelligence on port-specific corruption risks; and reporting patterns and problems to local authorities for action. The goal is to put up enough resistance and shed enough light on casual corruption that it gets addressed. Classification societies have expertise, reach and influence that can help MACN's broader goal to increase integrity in shipping, the organization said in a statement. They also have their own exposure to "integrity risks" when it comes to regulatory decisions, especially in high-risk operating environments. MACN's general assembly voted to allow class societies to join the group this April, and ABS, DNV and RINA are the first. "Trust is fundamental to the efficient functioning of global shipping. At ABS, we see integrity as an important part of maintaining confidence in the systems, standards, and relationships that support international trade. Joining MACN provides an opportunity to engage with industry partners, share expertise, and contribute to efforts that strengthen transparency and responsible business practices across the maritime sector," said John McDonald, ABS Chairman and CEO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543264-ld.text: Louis Dreyfus Armateurs ( LD Armateurs) has taken delivery of the DP2 multipurpose support vessel TVO Mariner for its LD TravOcean subsidiary, expanding its capacity for subsea cable installation, repair and protection work. The vessel, delivered to the group in mid-September, will support telecommunications cable installation and repairs, trenching and deepwater ROV operations, as well as offshore wind projects. “The TVO Mariner gives us full ownership on project execution for submarine cable installation and repairs, trenching services and deep water ROV operations. Thanks to this new vessel, we are well positioned to create more added value for our clients in terms of performance, agility and reliability,” said Olivier Le Nagard, LD TravOcean Managing Director. Built in 2011, the TVO Mariner is 88.3 meters long and has a deck capacity of about 2,500 tonnes and a 950-square-metre working deck. The DP2 vessel can accommodate up to 70 people. The vessel will complement LD TravOcean's existing subsea equipment, which includes Rovjets, mechanical trenchers, remotely operated vehicles and deepwater ROVs. TVO Mariner will operate under the French International Register and be crewed by LD Armateurs seafarers. LD Armateurs will oversee technical and ship management, while LD TravOcean's teams will conduct subsea operations.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira (23) mostra Lula com 40% das intenções de voto no 1º turno. Flávio Bolsonaro aparece em 2º com 36%. A diferença de 4 pontos percentuais entre os 2 candidatos líderes está no limite da margem de erro do levantamento. Augusto Cury está em 3º com 5%, seguido por Ronaldo Caiado com 4%, Renan Santos com 3% e Romeu Zema com 1%. O levantamento ouviu 2.002 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 22 e 23 de setembro.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543258-ho.text: Crude oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz reached 33.7 million barrels so far in the week starting September 20, preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler showed on Friday, putting exports roughly on track with the previous week's levels. The traffic comprised 19 tankers, of which 17 are very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that can carry 2 million barrels of oil, the data showed. Most of the tankers are laden with crude from Saudi Arabia, followed by Iraq. For the full previous week, 49.2 million barrels of crude were shipped out via Hormuz, according to Kpler. On Wednesday, some 60 commercial vesselsof all types transited the Strait of Hormuz carrying the highest daily volume of crude oil since early July, a US official told Reuters, speaking on condition of anonymity. State-run Saudi Aramco 2222.SE has boosted its exports via Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline earlier this month halted shipments from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. On Thursday, the number of commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz fell to nine from 14 the day before, Kpler data showed, although an unknown number of ships sail through the waterway with their transponders turned off and are not counted.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543260-en.text: Ventura Offshore has agreed a contract amendment with two subsidiaries of Eni and Petronas joint venture Searah for an additional well offshore Indonesia, adding about $21.7 million to the firm backlog of its SSV Catarina semi-submersible drilling rig. The amendment with Searah West Ganal Limited and Searah Ganal Deepwater Limited covers drilling of the JKNE Upside-1 Dir well and is expected to keep the rig working into December 2026. The new well comes on top of four optional wells previously exercised under the drilling campaign. In July, Searah subsidiary Eni Muara Bakau exercised an option for a fourth well and a tophole for SSV Catarina, adding about $25.1 million to Ventura Offshore's firm backlog and at the time extending the rig's utilization into the fourth quarter of 2026. SSV Catarina is a sixth-generation semisubmersible drilling rig capable of operating in water depths of up to 10,000 feet. Ventura Offshore owns and operates SSV Catarina, semisubmersible rig SSV Victoria and drillship DS Carolina, and manages the drillship Atlantic Zonda. Its rigs are currently operating offshore Brazil and Indonesia.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543259-sa.text: Ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman for Middle Eastern oil from inside the Strait of Hormuz have reached their limits after Saudi Arabia diverted exports from the Red Sea, adding to shipments from other producers, trade sources and analysts said. The increasing amount of Saudi exports this month requires more supertankers to shuttle crude through Hormuz to conduct cargo transfers, they said. That has reduced ship availability, raising shipping costs and increasing the time cargoes are on the water before reaching refineries. State-run Saudi Aramco 2222.SE has sold more than 60 million barrels of crude for STS transfer off Sohar, Oman, this month and next since its East-West Pipeline was attacked on September 13, halting oil exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track to rebound to 3.6 million barrels per day in September, up from about 900,000 bpd in August, data from analytics firm Kpler showed. That nearly 3 million bpd increase in Saudi exports from Hormuz would require between 36 and 40 more very large crude carriers, Kpler analyst Panagiotis Krontiras said. Each VLCC can carry 2 million barrels of oil. Anoop Singh, the head of global shipping research at commodity broker Oil Brokerage, said the number of additional VLCCs required to move the same amount of oil before the war started has risen to 40 this month, versus 24 in August.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543262-ak.text: Aker BP and partners Equinor and DNO have increased the estimated size of the Verdandi and Lillefix discoveries in the North Sea following an appraisal well that encountered both oil and gas. Preliminary estimates following drilling put the discoveries at between 1.3 million and 2.4 million cubic meters of oil equivalent, or 8 million to 15 million barrels, up from a pre-drill estimate of 0.6 million to 1.9 million cubic meters, or 4 million to 12 million barrels. Aker BP has a 50% operating working interest in production license 167, where the 16/1-EA-4 H exploration well was drilled, while partners Equinor and DNO Norge hold 30% and 20% share respectively. The companies are now assessing the commerciality of the discoveries and a potential tieback to the Symra field. The 16/1-EA-4 H horizontal appraisal well encountered a 14-metre gas column and a 44-metre oil column in sandstone layers of the Palaeocene Heimdal Formation. The gas-oil contact was found at 1,776 meters below sea level. A total of 1,515 reservoir meters were drilled horizontally through the oil zone, which had moderate reservoir quality. Fluid samples and pressure data were also collected.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543263-in.text: Inpex has agreed to acquire Jera's 0.735% participating interest in Australia's Ichthys LNG project, increasing its subsidiaries' combined stake in the development to 68.555% from 67.82%. The acquisition covers Jera's interest in blocks WA-50-L and WA-51-L, which include the Ichthys gas-condensate field, as well as shares in Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd, which owns the project's gas export pipeline and downstream liquefaction facilities. Completion remains subject to conditions including approval from Australian government regulatory agencies. The transaction follows Jera's December 2025 decision to sell shares in its Australian project subsidiary holding the 0.735% interest to MidOcean Energy. After Jera notified the other project participants of the proposed sale, Inpex exercised pre-emptive rights under the relevant joint operating and shareholders agreements to acquire the interest. Ichthys LNG liquefies natural gas and conducts LNG marketing activities in addition to owning the project's export pipeline and downstream liquefaction infrastructure.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543266-sl.text: SLB has been awarded four integrated well construction contracts by Aramco covering more than 450 oil and gas wells across Saudi Arabia over an initial three-year period. Each contract includes an option to extend the work by up to two years, potentially extending the multi-year well construction program beyond its initial term. SLB will manage end-to-end well construction services across different operating environments and oil and gas reservoirs in the kingdom. The scope combines digital drilling workflows with automated drilling, evaluation, fluids, cementing and completions products and services under an integrated well delivery model. “Delivering hundreds of wells across a multi-year program and in multiple operating environments requires an integrated model that connects planning, execution, and digital workflows to set new industry performance benchmarks. “Awarding SLB these advanced well construction programs at scale reflects Aramco’s confidence in our integrated model and capabilities,” said Steve Gassen, SLB Executive Vice President of Geographies.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/eleico.text: Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada na quinta-feira (24) aponta que 52% dos eleitores de SP desconhecem o número de urna do seu candidato a governador. Do total de entrevistados, 40% responderam o número corretamente. Outros 8% citaram um número errado para a votação. O levantamento ouviu 1.610 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre 22 e 23 de setembro. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais. Entre os eleitores de Fernando Haddad, 60% sabem o número correto. Já entre os que votam em Tarcísio de Freitas, apenas 34% responderam corretamente.

Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) e Fernando Haddad (PT) em agendas de campanhas ao governo de SP — Foto: Caiuá Maia e Diogo Zacarias Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada na quinta-feira (24) aponta que 71% dos eleitores paulistas afirmam estar totalmente decididos sobre o voto para governador no 1º turno, enquanto 29% dizem que ainda podem mudar de escolha até a eleição, segundo pesquisa Datafolha. O grau de certeza sobre o voto varia de acordo com o perfil do eleitor: entre os homens, 78% dizem estar totalmente decididos, enquanto o índice é de 65% entre as mulheres. Entre os eleitores de 16 a 24 anos, 47% afirmam estar totalmente decididos; O percentual sobe para 74% entre aqueles de 35 a 44 anos; E chega a 86% entre os eleitores com 60 anos ou mais. Entre quem tem renda familiar acima de cinco salários mínimos, 82% dizem estar totalmente decididos; Na faixa de renda de até dois salários mínimos, o índice é de 66%. Entre os eleitores que pretendem votar em Tarcísio, 76% afirmam estar convictos da escolha, já entre os que pretendem votar em Haddad, o percentual é de 77%.

https://g1.globo.com/pi/piaui/eleicoes/2.text: O g1 realiza nesta sexta-feira (25) um debate com candidatos ao Senado pelo Piauí. O evento será transmitido ao vivo, direto de Teresina. https://g1.globo.com/saude/noticia/2026/.text: Seis grandes hospitais dos EUA fecharam acordos com o governo e deixaram de oferecer bloqueadores de puberdade, hormônios e cirurgias de afirmação de gênero a menores de 18 anos. O governo Trump acusa as instituições de usar diagnósticos diferentes para conseguir reembolso de planos de saúde e programas públicos; os hospitais negam irregularidades e não houve decisão judicial sobre responsabilidade. Os acordos preveem multas milionárias e, em alguns casos, recursos para atender pessoas que queiram interromper ou reverter a transição. A ofensiva federal também atingiu o financiamento público e o acesso ao tratamento, enquanto decisões judiciais vêm divergindo sobre até onde o governo pode exigir dados de pacientes e hospitais. O tema divide governo e entidades médicas: associações americanas defendem o acesso a parte desses cuidados, enquanto a gestão Trump questiona as evidências de benefícios; no Brasil, o CFM também restringiu tratamentos para menores.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/dutch_.text: The Netherlands wants to scrap mandatory gas storage targets under a revamp of the European Union's energy supply security rules after spending nearly EUR 1 billion ($1.1 billion) this year to fill the country's reserves. The current EU regulation requires member states to fill storage sites to fixed levels ahead of winter through 2027, with obligations based largely on storage capacity rather than domestic gas consumption. That leaves the Netherlands, which has a relatively large storage system but shrinking demand, with an outsized filling requirement. The European Commission, the bloc's executive arm, isn't planning to extend the mandatory targets beyond the current timeline, according to a draft document seen by Bloomberg News. Instead, it wants to merge some existing laws and create a broader security of supply framework for both gas and electricity. The current gas regulation that includes storage targets would be dropped in the overhaul, which is due to be unveiled later this year. That would be in line with the demands of the Dutch government, which argues that the current EU system forces governments to do a job that the market should be doing. The rules also increasingly clash with market economics. Falling consumption and "large-scale purchases by other European governments" have skewed the economics of storing gas, Climate Minister Stientje van Veldhoven said in a letter to parliament Friday. Gas stockpiling has been particularly difficult this year throughout Europe because the Middle East conflict has driven up near-term prices relative to winter contracts, making summer injections unprofitable. European gas contracts have more than doubled since the start of the war reaching their highest level since late 2022 earlier this month. The result is that the Dutch government has increasingly had to subsidize storage filling to meet its EU obligations. This filling season alone, it committed close to €1 billion to ensure reserves were replenished.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Transnordestina Logística, empresa controlada pelo Grupo CSN e responsável pela implantação e operação da Nova Ferrovia Transnordestina, concluiu neste mês de setembro as obras do lote 6 , com 50 quilômetros entre Quixeramobim e Quixadá (CE). Com a entrega, a fase 1 do projeto, que liga Paes Landim (PI) ao Porto do Pecém (CE), chega a 832 quilômetros executados de um total previsto de 1.053 quilômetros, atingindo 84% de avanço físico. Os 221 quilômetros restantes estão em obras de infraestrutura e superestrutura. A conclusão dessa primeira fase está prevista para o fim de 2027. O avanço das obras aproxima a ferrovia do Complexo do Pecém, no Ceará, que será um dos principais pontos de escoamento e recepção das cargas transportadas pelo modal. O lote concluído envolveu 3,49 milhões de m³ de movimentação de terra, sendo 1,78 milhão de m³ de cortes e 1,71 milhão de m³ de aterros. A implantação do trecho também demandou 6,3 mil toneladas de trilhos, 87,6 mil dormentes de concreto e 129,2 mil m³ de brita. Desde dezembro de 2025, a Transnordestina realiza testes operacionais com trens em fase de operação comissionada. As composições já transportam cargas como milho e sorgo entre o Piauí e o Ceará. A estrutura operacional também recebeu reforço em junho deste ano, quando a companhia concluiu o recebimento de um lote de 100 vagões hopper modelo HTT, em Salgueiro (PE). Fabricados pela Greenbrier Maxion, os equipamentos são destinados ao transporte de grãos e fertilizantes. Uma composição formada pelos 100 vagões tem capacidade equivalente, segundo a Transnordestina, à operação de aproximadamente 357 caminhões graneleiros. A utilização do modal ferroviário busca reduzir o fluxo de veículos pesados nas rodovias e, consequentemente, os impactos associados ao transporte rodoviário de grandes volumes de carga.

A Descartes Systems Group lançou novos recursos de Image Document Management (IDM) baseados em inteligência artificial (IA) para automatizar o processamento de documentos em operações aduaneiras e logísticas. Integradas às soluções de transporte e comércio exterior da companhia, as ferramentas interpretam faturas comerciais, conhecimentos de embarque, packing lists e outros documentos para extrair, validar e preparar dados para uso operacional. Os recursos estão disponíveis por meio da Descartes Global Logistics Network (Descartes GLN) e foram desenvolvidos para uso direto nas aplicações que clientes já utilizam para criar embarques e preparar declarações aduaneiras. A proposta é reduzir a necessidade de redigitação e de transferência de informações entre diferentes sistemas. Segundo a Descartes, os agentes de IA são treinados para operações logísticas e conseguem processar diferentes documentos associados a um mesmo embarque. A tecnologia busca identificar e interpretar as informações no contexto da operação antes de disponibilizá-las para os fluxos de transporte e comércio exterior. A solução é direcionada principalmente a despachantes aduaneiros, freight forwarders e prestadores de serviços logísticos que lidam com grandes volumes de documentos. Entre os efeitos esperados estão a redução de exceções, correções e retrabalho e o aumento da capacidade de processamento sem crescimento proporcional das equipes. “Inserir dados de fatura comercial é uma das atividades que mais consome tempo no processo de importação, especialmente quando os embarques envolvem documentos complexos com centenas de itens de linha”, afirma Scott Sangster, general manager de Logistics Service Providers da Descartes. De acordo com a empresa, a ferramenta pode preparar informações capazes de iniciar diretamente fluxos de trabalho aduaneiros e de transporte, sem a necessidade de entrada manual dos dados. O processamento integrado também busca reduzir a complexidade de implantação em comparação com ferramentas isoladas de processamento de documentos por IA.

https://safety4sea.com/shipping-risks-mo.text: With two of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints under growing security pressure, a Bahrain-led group of 80 countries has called for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, demanding safe and unimpeded passage for commercial vessels without tolls, conditions or additional charges. T he joint statement, delivered at the United Nations, condemned actions affecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and renewed criticism of Houthi attacks around the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab. The countries warned that continued disruption in the two waterways poses a wider threat to maritime security, energy supplies and global trade. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif Al-Zayani said the threat posed by Iran remained serious and was continuing to grow. “I extend my sincere condolences … to all those who have lost innocent lives as a result of this ongoing threat,” Al-Zayani said, referring to casualties from Iranian and Houthi attacks across the region. The joint statement placed maritime access at the centre of its demands, calling on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restore freedom of navigation through the strategic waterway. “Iran’s actions in the Strait of Hormuz continue to threaten international security and navigational rights and freedoms,” the statement highlighted.

https://safety4sea.com/bma-warns-of-dead.text: Based on the preliminary findings of a marine safety investigation, the Bahamas Maritime Authority has issued a safety alert to raise awareness of the serious risk posed by food allergies and share best practice in the immediate recognition and first-line treatment of anaphylaxis on board ships. A s informed, on 23 June 2026, a teenage passenger onboard a Bahamas flagged passenger vessel was mistakenly given cow’s milk. She suffered a severe allergic reaction and, despite extensive medical care onboard and a paramedic-supported helicopter evacuation, later died in hospital. An allergy is the response of the body’s immune system to normally harmless substances, including food. Whilst in most people these substances pose no problem, in allergic individuals their immune system identifies them as a ‘threat’ and produces an inappropriate response. In more severe cases it causes anaphylaxis, which is a life threatening allergic reaction. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that over 220 million people must avoid certain foods because of allergies globally. In 2020, WHO identified a global priority list of food allergens based on their potential to cause anaphylaxis. Many countries have longer lists of allergen that are required to declared by law (9 in The Bahamas and USA, 14 in the UK and European Union, 23 in Australia and New Zealand). Many people have allergies to other foods not listed in the global priority list. Incidence of allergies varies by region. A study published in the British Medical Journal in 2021 identified that cow’s milk had become the most common cause of fatal anaphylaxis in older children across the United Kingdom.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-maib-investiga.text: UK MAIB has issued an investigation report into an incident where a longline fishing vessel capsized and sank after uncontrolled flooding through a line hauling hatch, resulting in 13 fatalities. A t about 1900 on 22 July 2024, the St Helena registered longline fishing vessel capsized and sank while on passage from Port Stanley, Falkland Islands to fishing grounds near South Georgia. Of the 27 people on board, 13 perished and 14 were recovered. At about 1300, while approximately 190 nautical miles east of Port Stanley, the vessel had experienced an uncontrolled ingress of water through the line hauling hatch. Water progressively flooded into the line hauler room then through the vessel via weathertight doors that had been left open, and the vessel took on a starboard list. A crew member raised the alarm via a colleague on a fishing vessel operating in the same region. This alarm was relayed to the authorities in the Falkland Islands and a rescue operation was initiated. As the list of the vessel steadily increased, the crew mustered and donned their immersion suits. At about 1551, the vessel lost propulsion and the vessel drifted in the heavy seas. By about 1600, with the list further increasing, the crew started abandoning ship into two liferafts. One of the liferafts became damaged during the abandonment. The vessel foundered at about 1900. By about 1130 on 23 July 2024, two of the responding vessels had recovered 14 survivors and nine deceased crew members. Four crew members remain missing, presumed dead. The investigation found that the previously closed line hauling hatch opened uncommanded and unexpectedly at the time of the accident. The hatch’s manual securing bolts had likely not been applied before proceeding to sea. The crew were unable to close the hatch once it had opened, probably due to a failure of the hatch’s operating mechanism.

https://safety4sea.com/attack-on-mv-cape.text: A voyage bound for India has ended in tragedy after the cargo vessel MV Cape Dao came under attack off Oman and killing an Indian seafarer, once again putting the safety of merchant crews navigating the waters around the Strait of Hormuz under scrutiny. T he Indian Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said an Indian national was killed when the vessel was attacked while sailing towards India. Of the 20 Indian seafarers on board, 19 were rescued, while one crew member lost his life. The vessel was travelling from Mina Saqr to India via the Oman route when two torpedoes reportedly struck its port side, damaging the accommodation area and part of the engine room. Furthermore, according to Manoj Yadav of the Forward Seamen’s Union of India (FSUI), the deceased seafarer was a wiper from Deoria in Uttar Pradesh. He was reportedly injured in the head during the attack and later succumbed to his wounds. As reported, the wider crew comprised 28 seafarers, including 20 Indian nationals. The crew was evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and taken ashore and the surviving seafarers are, as of the latest update, safe at a jetty in Oman, while the next of kin of the deceased seafarer have been informed. Another Indian seafarer killed. Wiper Suraj Yadav of Deoria, Uttar Pradesh, is dead after MV Cape Dao was attacked today while sailing toward India. 28 crew on board, 20 of them Indian. Two torpedoes: • Port side C-deck (accommodation) • Port side hull (engine room) Assurances… pic.twitter.com/AvrD2p1Cwd

https://safety4sea.com/shifting-regulati.text: Shipping’s decarbonisation drive is entering a decisive investment phase, but shifting regulations are making the path ahead harder to navigate as shipowners must choose today which fuels, technologies and vessels will still make commercial sense tomorrow. T he 2026 edition of DNV’s Maritime Forecast to 2050 highlighted this growing uncertainty, with decisions made today on vessel design, retrofits and fuel capability potentially shaping fleet competitiveness for decades. At the same time, the industry is facing a rapidly changing regulatory landscape, as the IMO continues to develop global measures while the EU and other jurisdictions introduce their own emissions rules and carbon-pricing mechanisms. “Decisions taken today on vessel design, retrofits, and fuel capability will determine competitiveness for decades, while the outcome of ongoing regulatory negotiations could significantly reshape the economics of shipping’s energy transition,” said Øyvind Sekkesæter, Senior Consultant at DNV and lead author of this year’s report. For shipowners, this means that investment decisions must increasingly be assessed against a patchwork of current and emerging requirements — not only in terms of compliance, but also fuel availability, infrastructure and long-term commercial viability. While regulatory uncertainty continues at the IMO, the EU is moving ahead with measures that are reshaping the economics of shipping. Since January 2025, FuelEU Maritime has set increasingly stringent greenhouse-gas intensity requirements for ships over 5,000 GT carrying cargo or passengers in the EU and EEA, including 50% of energy used on voyages to and from the region.

https://safety4sea.com/australia-launche.text: Australia has launched a national Low Carbon Liquid Fuels Knowledge Hub to provide industry, communities and the wider public with evidence-based information on low carbon liquid fuels and support their uptake across the economy. L aunched on September 18, the Hub is intended to provide a single source of information on emerging low carbon liquid fuel technologies, supply chains, sustainability considerations and opportunities for Australia. The initiative comes as demand for alternatives to conventional fossil fuels grows across sectors including transport and shipping. The Hub was delivered in partnership with Queensland University of Technology through the iMOVE Cooperative Research Centre. The Australian Government contributed A$162,500 toward the initiative. Low carbon liquid fuels can be used as alternatives to conventional diesel, jet fuel, petrol and marine fuels. According to the Australian Government, these fuels can be produced from biomass and waste materials, including agricultural and forestry by-products, as well as from renewable hydrogen combined with captured carbon dioxide. It is worth noting that the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA), in its report “New Build Trends in Australia’s Domestic Fleet 2023–2024,” identified the adoption of alternative fuels as an emerging trend , pointing to the domestic fleet’s gradual shift toward lower-carbon operations. The Australian Government said the Hub will bring together information covering the development and deployment of these fuels, helping users better understand their potential applications as well as the challenges associated with their production and supply.

https://safety4sea.com/companies-shake-h.text: Wah Kwong NatPower Limited (WK NatPower) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Aberdeen Restaurant Enterprises Limited (AREL) to explore marine electrification projects in Aberdeen and Shum Wan, Hong Kong. T he collaboration will examine the development of an integrated marine electrification ecosystem covering shore power facilities, vessel charging infrastructure and battery energy storage systems, as well as electric vessels for future transport and tourism services. The initiative comes as the Hong Kong SAR Government advances policies supporting green shipping, smart port development and shore power infrastructure, with the partners aiming to contribute to the development of a cleaner and more sustainable maritime sector. As an initial phase, WK NatPower and AREL will explore the construction of a series of electric and transport vessels. The partnership will also assess the potential deployment of the ApliAbe electric vessel fleet, positioning electric vessels as part of future waterfront mobility and hospitality services in Aberdeen. Vincent Ni, General Manager of WK NatPower, said the MoU would support Hong Kong’s marine energy transition by combining shore power and vessel electrification solutions. Through this collaboration, we look forward to exploring practical ways to introduce cleaner energy, electric vessels and sustainable waterfront experiences, while supporting the revitalization of Jumbo Kingdom for future generations

https://safety4sea.com/mmmczcs-key-quest.text: The Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping (MMMCZCS) said the latest IMO discussions on the proposed Net-Zero Framework (NZF) showed forward momentum, while leaving key questions on targets, compliance, financing and zero- and near-zero-emission fuels unresolved. T he IMO’s recent ISWG-GHG 22 discussions provided greater clarity on the remaining design questions around the proposed Net-Zero Framework, although Member States reached no final decisions. The working group examined target-setting, compliance mechanisms, financing for a just and equitable transition, and incentives for zero and near-zero emission (ZNZ) fuels. The Center for Zero Carbon Shipping, which attended an IMO meeting for the first time as an accredited NGO with consultative status, said discussions showed “forward momentum” despite several issues remaining unresolved. However, according to MMMCZCS, one key question is whether the NZF should establish emissions-reduction targets in advance to drive the development and uptake of low-emission fuels, or whether targets should instead reflect the commercial availability of such fuels. Liberia has proposed linking targets to commercial viability, using criteria including fuel price, market share and availability at ports. Japan has proposed a hybrid approach, with fixed targets through 2035 and later targets determined following reviews of commercial viability. Member States also discussed the stringency of the targets. Brazil and Japan have proposed softer trajectories through 2035/2036 compared with the draft framework approved at MEPC 83. Brazil’s proposal would ultimately reach a 70% base target reduction in 2041, compared with the draft NZF’s 65% target for 2040.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/video-bar.text: Bardex Omni Liftshiplift will be engineered for the specific requirements of the Newport News facility. [Image: Bardex] Goleta, Calif-based Bardex Corporation has been selected to provide a new shiplift system for River Port, LLC, an S23 Holdings company, at its Newport News, Va., facility. The shiplift will be operated by East Coast Repair & Fabrication , LLC (ECR), an affiliated ship repair company, and represents a significant investment in the facility’s future shipbuilding, maintenance, repair, and fleet-support capabilities. With a maximum lifting capacity of just over 25,000 tonnes, the system will increase River Port’s capacity for servicing and repairing ships as well as launching subassembly modules for Navy ships. The Bardex Omni Liftshiplift will be engineered for the specific requirements of the Newport News facility, including forty-eight 640-tonne lift stations and a platform measuring approximately 450 x 110 feet (137m x 33.5 meters). The system will be designed to deliver precise load control, reliability, maintainability, operational flexibility, and life cycle value. Unlike wire rope-based shiplifts, the Bardex OmniLift system uses linear chain jack technology to provide synchronized, controlled lifting without relying on wire ropes as the primary lifting medium. In addition, the system will use motion control technology instead of synchronous motors or variable frequency drives to keep the lift safe, level, and reliable under real-world conditions. The Bardex OmniLift has a perfect safety record: Since the company first installed its linear chain jack system, in 1967, there have been zero catastrophic failures, dropped vessels, or reportable safety incidents.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/worlds-fi.text: NYK completes world's first ship-to-ship ammonia bunkering for ammonia-fueled vessel. (Credit: NYK Line) NYK Line and four Japanese partners have completed what they say is the world’s first ship-to-ship ammonia bunkering operation involving an ammonia-fueled vessel. The operation took place September 17 at Japan Marine United Corp.’s Ariake Shipyard, where ammonia was transferred from the carrier Shoei Maru to an ammonia-fueled medium gas carrier (AFMGC) under construction at the yard. The fuel will be used for the new vessel’s upcoming sea trials ahead of its scheduled delivery in November. NYK carried out the operation in cooperation with Japan Marine United, Nihon Shipyard Co., Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Co. and Kokuka Sangyo Co. Ammonia is being explored as an alternative marine fuel because it produces no carbon dioxide during combustion. However, its toxicity presents significant handling and safety challenges, making the development of reliable bunkering procedures essential to its wider adoption. According to NYK, the companies established safety procedures and operating processes before conducting the transfer, which was completed without incident. The operation provided practical experience in supplying ammonia fuel and represents a step toward developing the infrastructure needed to support ammonia-fueled vessels.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/new-pacif.text: New Pacific Industrial is entering shipbuilding with two Glosten-designed tugboats. [Image: Glosten] Vancouver, Wash. -based heavy industrial fabricator New Pacific Industrial ( NP) has launched its first shipbuilding program with the construction of two 122-foot American Class tugboats for American Marine Corporation (AMC) at its Columbia River waterfront facility. Designed by naval architecture and marine engineering firm Glosten , the vessels also represent American Marine’s first new tugboat construction as the marine services company marks 50 years in business. “As American Marine celebrates half a century in business, our first new-build tug represents an important milestone and an investment in the next generation of our operations,” said Bob Shahnazarian, president and owner of American Marine Corporation. “We wanted a team that could take our operational requirements and carry them all the way through design, construction, and delivery. New Pacific and Glosten give us that continuity throughout the program.” “New Pacific was founded around a straightforward idea: complex projects need experienced people, capable infrastructure, and an operating model that works for the customer,” said Joe Corvelli, CEO of New Pacific. “Starting with a new-build program alongside American Marine and Glosten puts that model into practice from day one.” New Pacific’s first build carries forward the shipbuilding legacy of its Vancouver waterfront. Once part of the historic Kaiser Shipyards, where vessels were constructed during World War II, the site now supports modern shipbuilding and heavy industrial work along the Columbia River. Founded by CEO Joe Corvelli, COO Chris Palmer and CCO Peter Roney, New Pacific’s founders have more than 90 years of combined leadership experience spanning commercial and government shipbuilding, marine operations, advanced manufacturing and complex programs.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/tru.text: US President Donald Trump has signalled that his administration intends to prevent the IMO from adopting a global emissions-pricing mechanism. “Last year, my administration was forced to intervene to stop an obscure UN body, the International Maritime Organization, from secretly establishing a first-ever global carbon tax, very expensive tax, to raise international shipping costs by 10-20% and maybe more than that,” Trump said while addressing the UN General Assembly on 22 September. “There is no global government – and while I am President, there will be no global taxes,” he added. The US delegation walked out of negotiations at the IMO’s 83rd Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC 83) meeting in April 2025. The meeting ended with a draft Net-Zero Framework (NZF) being approved by 63 votes to 16, with 24 abstentions. The draft NZF introduced a two-tiered GHG fuel standard that would require ships to progressively reduce their well-to-wake GHG fuel intensity (GFI) from 2028. Ships that fall short of the direct compliance target would be required to purchase remedial units to cover their emissions deficit through contributions to the IMO Net-Zero Fund. The Tier 1 remedial unit price is set at $100/mtCO2e for 2028-2030. Those that fail to meet both the base and direct compliance targets would also need to cover an additional Tier 2 deficit. This could be done by purchasing surplus units from other ships, using units banked from previous years or buying additional remedial units at a higher price of $380/mtCO2e for 2028-2030.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/hormuz-c.text: Crude oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz reached 33.7 million barrels so far in the week starting September 20, preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler showed on Friday, putting exports roughly on track with the previous week's levels. The traffic comprised 19 tankers, of which 17 are very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that can carry 2 million barrels of oil, the data showed. Most of the tankers are laden with crude from Saudi Arabia, followed by Iraq. For the full previous week, 49.2 million barrels of crude were shipped out via Hormuz, according to Kpler. On Wednesday, some 60 commercial vesselsof all types transited the Strait of Hormuz carrying the highest daily volume of crude oil since early July, a US official told Reuters, speaking on condition of anonymity. State-run Saudi Aramco 2222.SE has boosted its exports via Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline earlier this month halted shipments from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. On Thursday, the number of commodity vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz fell to nine from 14 the day before, Kpler data showed, although an unknown number of ships sail through the waterway with their transponders turned off and are not counted.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ret.text: As some shipping lines begin testing the Suez Canal routing, Indian cargo is reaching the Port of Savannah 10 to 14 days faster. Port officials said improved supply chain velocity means faster inventory fulfillment and lower inventory carrying costs for cargo owners. Maersk has shifted its MECL service from routing around the Cape of Good Hope back to the Suez Canal, cutting the transit time from Nhava Sheva, India, to Savannah to 28 days. The Maersk Denver made the ocean carrier’s first new westbound sailing via the Suez, calling Savannah Aug. 9. With the return to the Red Sea, Maersk also added an eastbound call to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to the MECL service. Ocean carrier CMA CGM is also in the process of returning its INDAMEX service via the Suez Canal. The move will reduce transit time from Nhava Sheva to Savannah by five days and require two fewer vessels to maintain weekly frequency. “Georgia Ports welcomes the transit time improvements as several major carriers return to Suez routings linking Georgia to world markets,” said Kevin Price, President of Georgia Ports. MSC has announced plans to restore some Suez Canal routings in both directions on four major Asia-Europe and Mediterranean services: Tiger, Albatross, Himalaya Express and Jade. By eliminating the Cape of Good Hope detour, MSC expects to operate each service with two fewer vessels, increasing available global container ship capacity.

https://splash247.com/precious-seals-fre.text: Thailand’s Precious Shipping has lined up another index-linked ultramax charter, fixing the Sunisa Naree to Singapore’s PACC Line for up to 13 months. The Bangkok-listed owner told the stock exchange that the charter started on September 23 for 11 to 13 months at a gross variable rate equivalent to 103% of the Baltic Exchange Supramax Index 63K weighted time-charter average over the preceding 15 days. Precious put the current equivalent rate at around $23,000 per day. The 2016-built Sunisa Naree is a roughly 63,000 dwt ultramax delivered by China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering. The latest fixture follows another index-linked deal earlier this month involving the owner’s newly delivered Ratima Naree. That ship went straight from Sanfu into a 12-to-14-month charter with Trafigura Maritime Logistics at 107.5% of the BSI 63K, equivalent to about $22,800 per day when the fixture started. Precious has been shifting the fleet towards larger and younger bulkers while shedding ageing handysize and supramax tonnage. The company has four 63,500 dwt ultramaxes coming from Sanfu under a $133.46m programme, with two already delivered and the remaining pair due through the first quarter of 2027. The Khalid Hashim-led owner has also started diversifying beyond dry bulk this year, adding MR tanker exposure directly and through its 45%-owned Nusantara Maritime venture.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/omega-su.text: Omega Subsea has secured a five-year agreement with NKT to provide a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) system for the newbuild cable-laying vessel (CLV) NKT Eleonora, following the contract for NKT Victoria reported last June. The agreements are part of a wider investment program as part of which Omega Subsea’s total ROV fleet is set to exceed 30 systems by mid-2028. Of the eight new Kystdesign systems scheduled for delivery in 2026, four will be deployed on NKT projects. Mobilization activities for NKT Victoria and NKT Eleonora are currently underway at shipyards in Ulsteinvik and Brattvåg. Operations on NKT Victoria are scheduled to begin before year-end, while mobilization of ROV systems on NKT Eleonora is expected in January. For NKT Victoria, Omega Subsea will also supply two launch and recovery systems (LARS) from Ulmatec, installed in the vessel’s hangar and configured to support operations with the company’s two new ROVs. “NKT is one of the leading players in the cable installation industry, and being selected to support two of their modern cable-laying vessels is a strong vote of confidence. We are expanding both our equipment base and organisation to support long-term operations and multiple projects simultaneously,” said Trond Berge , CEO of Omega Subsea. “Cable installation is a market characterised by long-term demand and significant growth potential. We will continue to be a broad subsea service provider, while strengthening our position in areas where we see sustained activity and long-term opportunities.”

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/ld-armat.text: LD TravOcean, a subsidiary of Louis Dreyfus Armateurs (LD Armateurs) specialized in subsea cable installation and protection, has taken delivery of the DP2 multipurpose support vessel TVO Mariner, previously known as SIDDIS Mariner, following the acquisition announced in April. The 88.3-meter vessel, built in 2011 to Norwegian design standards, features a payload capacity of around 2,500 tons, a 950-square-meter working deck, advanced dynamic positioning, and accommodation for up to 70 personnel. TVO Mariner was delivered to LD Armateurs in mid-September and will support a range of activities, including telecommunications cables, cable repair projects and offshore wind projects. The vessel will operate under the French International Register (RIF) and be crewed by seafarers from LD Armateurs. Technical and ship management activities will be overseen by LD Armateurs, while subsea operations will be conducted by LD TravOcean’s specialist teams. “The TVO Mariner gives us full ownership on project execution for submarine cable installation and repairs, trenching services and deep water ROV operations. Thanks to this new vessel, we are well positioned to create more added value for our clients in terms of performance, agility and reliability,” said Olivier Le Nagard , Managing Director of LD TravOcean. https://www.offshore-energy.biz/inpex-be.text: Japan’s exploration and production (E&P) company Inpex has moved to solidify its foothold in a liquefied natural gas (LNG) project off the northwest coast of Western Australia (WA), with its Australian subsidiaries taking steps to obtain an additional participating interest by exercising pre-emptive rights. Inpex’s Australian subsidiaries have entered into agreements with subsidiaries of JERA to acquire 0.735% in the Ichthys LNG project, which will increase their interests in this project from 67.82% to 68.555%. The completion of the transaction is subject to the fulfilment of certain conditions, including approval by Australian government regulatory agencies. Participating interests entail those in Block WA-50-L and Block WA-51-L, including the Ichthys gas condensate field, and shares of Ichthys LNG downstream company, which owns the gas export pipeline and downstream gas liquefaction facilities, LNG, and conducts LNG marketing and other activities. The deal stems from JERA’s December 2025 decision to sell shares to MidOcean Energy in its Australian project subsidiary, which holds a 0.735% participating interest in the projects. After JERA notified the proposed sale to the project’s participating interest holders, Inpex exercised its pre-emptive rights under the respective joint operating agreements (JOAs) and shareholders agreement (SHA) to acquire the former’s participating interest. The Japanese firm emphasizes that it will “continue to lead efforts to maintain stable operations at the project with the understanding and cooperation of all its stakeholders, including the project’s joint venture participants, the local communities, the Australian federal government and the governments of the Northern Territory and Western Australia.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: A Russian-flagged cargo ship with a history of ties to weapons shipments and sanctioned military cargo vessels has broken away from a convoy that had a naval escort into the port of Tobruk in Libya. It has headed north through the Dardanelles towards the Bosporus and the Black Sea. The Yuriy Arshenevskiy (IMO 8406705) was sailing with the US-sanctioned cargo vessel Anastasiia (IMO 9349291), with an escort provided by the Ropucha Class landing ship Aleksandr Shabalin (L110) when it left the Baltiysk naval base in the Kaliningrad headquarters of Russia’s Baltic Fleet, transited the Strait of Gibraltar in early September, then arrived in the port of Tobruk. Ural trucks and armored vehicles were seen on the quayside in Baltiysk being loaded onto the two cargo vessels. At the other end in Tobruk, social media postings showed tarpaulin-covered military vehicles, including what appeared to be 8-wheeled armored personnel carriers and multiple-barreled rocket launchers, being moved out of the port on low loaders. The Yuriy Arshenevskiy makes its way north through the Dardanelles, September 24 ( VesselFinder ) It is not clear when the Anastasiia and the landing ship Aleksandr Shabalin (L110) left Tobruk. From low-resolution imagery, it appears that the Anastasiia was on the quayside still on September 21, but on September 25 she was cruising westwards between Sicily and Malta. The Yuriy Arshenevskiy left sometime beforehand, and was seen passing through the Dardanelles with its AIS system switched on late on September 24. It was approaching the Bosporus early on September 25, but now appears to have switched course and is heading for the anchorage or port at Tuzla. It was previously incorrectly reported that the Yuriy Arshenevskiy was sanctioned, but this is not the case – not that sanctioned status would have been a bar to transit of the Bosporus, as Turkey – unlike Iran – strictly applies UNCLOS rules regarding innocent passage through narrow channels. The military equipment was unloaded in Tobruk, which is controlled by Field Marshal Haftar’s Libyan National Army, while the Turkish government supports the other side in the Libyan civil war, the UN-recognized government based in Tripoli. A convoy of low-loaders moves military equipment out of Tobruk docks ( Screen grab from Tanasuh TV )

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Donald Trump oferece cerimônia do chá para Xi Jinping na Casa Branca — Foto: Evan Vucci/Reuters O presidente da China, Xi Jinping, disse nesta sexta-feira (25) que a relação entre seu país e os Estados Unidos continuará baseada na reciprocidade. ➡️ O líder chinês voltou a se reunir nesta sexta com o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, seu maior rival geopolítico, em seu último dia de uma visita em Washington marcada pela tentativa de abrandar as tensões entre as duas maiores economias mundiais. https://g1.globo.com/mg/minas-gerais/not.text: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sancionou a lei que transforma os Cefets de Minas Gerais e do Rio de Janeiro em universidades federais nesta sexta-feira (25). Todos os alunos e servidores do Cefet-MG passam automaticamente a integrar a nova instituição. Os estudantes terão transferência automática e sem exigências. A nova universidade manterá o ensino técnico de nível médio. Ela também oferecerá graduação, pós-graduação, pesquisa, extensão e inovação tecnológica. Inicialmente, o reitor e o vice-reitor serão nomeados de forma temporária pelo Ministério da Educação. A instituição terá 180 dias para propor seu estatuto.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Brasfrigo renovou a certificação Halal para 2027 , requisito aplicável às operações de armazenamento de produtos destinados a mercados que exigem ou reconhecem esse padrão, entre eles países do Oriente Médio, como Emirados Árabes Unidos e Arábia Saudita. A relevância da região para as exportações brasileiras de proteína animal aparece nos dados da Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA). Em agosto, os embarques de carne de frango somaram 492,634 mil toneladas, alta de 24,8% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. Os Emirados Árabes Unidos, com 44 mil toneladas, e a Arábia Saudita, com 35 mil toneladas, ficaram entre os cinco principais destinos. Segundo o diretor da Brasfrigo, José Humberto Côrtes, a certificação estabelece requisitos específicos para as instalações, procedimentos e controles das operações de armazenagem de produtos Halal. “Entre eles estão o recebimento e a identificação das mercadorias, limpeza, rastreabilidade, segregação de cargas e medidas para prevenir contaminações e misturas de mercadorias durante a operação”, explica. A atuação da empresa também abrange outros mercados. Em junho, a Brasfrigo registrou o maior volume mensal de exportações, com 52 toneladas. “Estamos habilitados a operar cargas destinadas a mais de 150 países”, afirma Côrtes. A empresa mantém unidades em Itajaí (SC), junto ao complexo portuário da região, e Uberlândia (MG), no Triângulo Mineiro. A localização da unidade catarinense é um dos fatores que sustentam as operações voltadas ao mercado externo. “Estar em Itajaí nos coloca próximos a uma das principais estruturas portuárias utilizadas pelo agronegócio brasileiro para chegar ao mercado internacional”, diz o executivo. A unidade de Itajaí possui capacidade estática para até 42 mil toneladas e conta com câmaras frigorificadas que operam a temperaturas de até -25°C. A estrutura dispõe ainda de 588 tomadas para contêineres refrigerados, movimenta cargas secas e pode realizar até 100 operações de embarque e desembarque por dia.

A Arauco abre uma nova etapa do Programa de Formação de Motoristas , em Três Lagoas (MS), com capacitação profissional gratuita para condutores interessados em obter a habilitação na Categoria E. As inscrições presenciais serão realizadas de 1º a 3 de outubro , na unidade do Sest Senat no município. Em parceria com o Sest Senat , o programa é voltado a motoristas habilitados nas categorias C ou D que desejam se qualificar para a Categoria E , além de profissionais que já atuam no transporte e buscam aperfeiçoamento. Os participantes selecionados também terão direito a uma bolsa-bônus , ao finalizar a formação, conforme as condições do programa. Para participar do processo seletivo, é necessário ter pelo menos 21 anos e possuir CNH nas categorias C ou D há, no mínimo, um ano. Durante as 107 horas de formação teórica e prática, os alunos terão contato com conteúdos como legislação de trânsito, técnicas de direção preventiva, segurança viária, ética profissional e rotina operacional da condução de veículos pesados. A capacitação contribui para a formação de profissionais que poderão atuar nas operações logísticas do Projeto Sucuriú, em Inocência (MS). A oportunidade é aberta a homens e mulheres. A expansão da capacitação reflete a evolução das demandas operacionais da Companhia na região. "À medida que nossas operações avançam, expandimos também o alcance de iniciativas como o Programa de Formação de Motoristas. Incluir a Categoria E nesta nova etapa responde à demanda por capacitação no transporte pesado e florestal, garantindo que os profissionais da região estejam prontos para assumir essas posições estratégicas com foco na direção preventiva, no respeito às normas de trânsito e na excelência operacional", destaca Rodrigo Sugske, gerente executivo de Logística Florestal da Arauco . Além da eficiência logística, a valorização do capital humano e o fortalecimento das comunidades locais guiam a atuação da Companhia. "Mais do que capacitar profissionais, acreditamos no potencial dos talentos locais e na sua capacidade de desenvolvimento, construindo um legado alinhado à cultura da Arauco", complementa Morela Alfonzo, gerente de Gestão de Pessoas da Companhia .

O mercado de logística está trazendo novas oportunidades para quem busca trabalhar com movimentação de cargas, intralogística, transporte e supply chain. Semanalmente, a equipe da Tecnologística registra vagas de emprego e capacitação para profissionais do setor. Nesta semana, nossa equipe registrou vagas para diversas posições e níveis de experiência, com destaque para grandes empresas fazendo contratações fixas e temporárias em preparação para o aumento de demanda das festas de fim de ano. A empresa anunciou a abertura de 850 vagas de emprego no Brasil entre julho e dezembro de 2026, principalmente no centro logístico de Guarulhos (SP). As contratações fazem parte da expansão das operações da empresa no país e incluem oportunidades para profissionais das áreas de armazenagem, logística e liderança. Das oportunidades anunciadas, mais de 800 são destinadas a funções operacionais nos armazéns e na área de logística do centro de Guarulhos. A empresa também prevê a abertura de mais de 50 vagas para cargos de liderança, incluindo supervisores e líderes de equipe. Interessados podem acompanhar a página de carreiras da empresa e o Centro Integrado de Emprego, Trabalho e Qualificação – CIET Guarulhos. O grupo de locação de caminhões, máquinas e equipamentos está com 40 vagas de emprego abertas no estado de São Paulo . As oportunidades são para profissionais com diferentes níveis de experiência e incluem posições efetivas e de aprendizagem.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/trump_.text: President Donald Trump's economic advisers are analyzing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports, underscoring the seriousness of the administration's consideration of the idea. Senator John Hoeven, a Republican from North Dakota, said the study being conducted by National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer aims to inform the administration's decision-making on possible export curbs. "The idea is that you get Bessent and Greer and Hassett to do that analysis and if, on a short-term basis - and we are in harvest season right now - it would show that it would help, then it is something we should consider doing," Hoeven said. Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit foreign sales of US diesel, as conflicts in Russia and the Middle East take supplies offline and spike prices for the fuel right at the peak of the fall harvest season in the US. Diesel is essential for powering farm equipment and is a critical fuel for modern shipping, propelling freight trains, long-haul trucks and delivery vans. And its retail cost - which hit a new high this week and averaged $6.51 per gallon on Wednesday - is adding to voter anxieties about the cost of living ahead of November's midterm elections. A timeline for the government's economic analysis was not immediately available. But the study, described by people familiar with the matter, is expected to forecast a mix of potential consequences - including both lower and higher prices - that could be used by administration officials either to justify or ward off a ban.

https://safety4sea.com/imo-moves-lashing.text: IMO has finalised draft amendments that would formally allow approved lashing software to supplement a containership’s Cargo Securing Manual, bringing digital calculations into the international guidance used to assess container-securing arrangements. T he Sub-Committee on Carriage of Cargoes and Containers completed the revision of the Revised Guidelines for the Preparation of the Cargo Securing Manual (MSC.1/Circ.1353/Rev.2) during CCC 12, held from 14 to 18 September 2026. IMO confirmed at the close of the meeting that the revision had been completed. The amendments are expected to be submitted to the Maritime Safety Committee at MSC 113 in June 2027 for approval. Until then, the revised text remains a draft and does not create an immediate new compliance requirement. Under SOLAS regulation VI/5.6, cargo units and cargo transport units must be loaded, stowed and secured throughout the voyage in accordance with a Cargo Securing Manual (CSM) approved by the flag Administration. The CSM provides the vessel-specific arrangements, limits and instructions needed to secure cargo safely. Lashing software, however, can assess the forces acting on container stacks under a particular loading condition and help crews verify whether the proposed arrangement remains within approved limits. CCC 12 has now finalised an interim harmonised performance standard intended to support consistent approval and use of this software. The draft provisions cover areas including software functionality, calculation methods, tolerances, user interfaces, testing, approval, surveys, data exchange and links with external systems.

https://safety4sea.com/international-gre.text: A new international alliance bringing together shipping lines, ports, energy companies and other maritime stakeholders has been launched in Beijing, aiming to accelerate the industry’s transition towards lower-emission operations. A s shipping moves from decarbonisation targets to the practical challenge of building cleaner trade routes, a new international alliance has been launched to bring maritime players together around the development of green shipping corridors. The International Green Shipping Corridor Alliance will focus on connecting projects, standards, technologies and fuel supply across the maritime value chain to help accelerate the industry’s transition to lower-emission shipping. The initiative is jointly led by the Global Sustainable Transport Innovation and Knowledge Center, COSCO SHIPPING Group, CMA CGM Group, China Energy Engineering Group and Shanghai International Port Group (SIPG), among others. According to China Transport News, the alliance is the first non-governmental international organisation established specifically to promote cooperation around international green shipping corridors. The launch comes as the shipping industry faces growing pressure to develop cleaner vessels, alternative marine fuels and supporting port infrastructure, while international stakeholders seek greater alignment on standards and certification. The alliance held its inaugural general assembly in Beijing alongside its formal establishment. Fu Xuyin, former Vice Minister of Transport of China, was elected as its first chairman, while Li Xinghu, Vice Minister of Transport, attended the meeting and delivered remarks.

https://safety4sea.com/imo-starts-buildi.text: IMO has begun developing goal-based interim safety guidelines for ships fitted with onboard carbon capture and storage systems, marking an important first step towards a common international framework for the technology. T he work was initiated by the Sub-Committee on Carriage of Cargoes and Containers at its 12th session (CCC 12), held from 14 to 18 September 2026. It follows growing interest in onboard carbon capture and storage (OCCS) as a possible way to reduce emissions from vessels that are likely to continue using carbon-based fuels. The outcome moves the issue beyond general recognition of the regulatory gap and into the formal development of safety provisions. However, it does not introduce new requirements for ships at this stage. The planned interim guidelines will establish overarching safety goals and functional requirements rather than prescribe a single technical solution. Detailed provisions for individual OCCS technologies are expected to be added through separate annexes as experience develops. Current planning indicates that chemical absorption could be addressed first, reflecting its more advanced level of maritime application. Other capture methods may be incorporated later as their design and operational characteristics become clearer. This approach is significant because OCCS covers more than the capture unit itself. A complete installation may involve exhaust-gas treatment, chemical solvents, compression or liquefaction equipment, temporary CO₂ storage, ventilation and monitoring arrangements, and systems for transferring captured carbon ashore.

https://safety4sea.com/fire-breaks-out-a.text: A major maritime response operation was launched north of Mykonos, Greece, after a fire broke out aboard the Greek-flagged Ro-Ro vessel Blue Carrier 2 while the ship was underway, prompting the evacuation of all 29 people on board. T he fire reportedly started in a truck inside the vessel’s No. 4 garage and spread through the vehicle deck, with explosions subsequently heard from the garage area. As the blaze could not be brought under control using the ship’s own firefighting systems, assistance was requested and vessels from Syros, Mykonos, Lavrio and Piraeus were deployed to the scene, alongside nearby ships.
