All 29 people were safely evacuated and reported to be in good health. With the evacuation completed, the response has now moved into a second phase focused on the vessel’s technical management and preventing any potential impact on the marine environment.

https://safety4sea.com/fueleu-maritime-t.text: The first year of FuelEU Maritime compliance has provided an early indication of how the regulation is working in practice, with more than 90% of ships using pooling to meet their obligations and biodiesel emerging as the leading renewable and low-carbon fuel used for compliance. T he findings come from a new analysis by Joe Bettles, Climate Policy Manager at the Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping , published as part of the Center’s Countdown series. The analysis was also discussed in the latest episode of the Center’s The Current podcast, featuring Thomas Edelgaard Christensen, Managing Counsel at Gorrissen Federspiel; and Laurids Møhl, Principal at Boston Consulting Group . FuelEU compliance units differ from EU ETS allowances because they are exchanged through pools of ships established for a full year rather than standardized allowances traded through regulated exchanges. Pooling arrangements can be made directly within fleets, between companies or through third-party commercial platforms. The number of third-party FuelEU service platforms has grown since 2024, with the Center identifying at least 16 platforms . These include strategy consultants, pooling brokers and full-service platforms combining brokering, strategic, legal and marketplace functions. At the same time, shipowners and operators can generate surplus through alternative fuel use within their own fleets and market these pools through public platforms.

https://safety4sea.com/xeneta-container-.text: Ocean container freight rates on key US trades are expected to rise in early October, while rates into Europe have continued to decline, according to Xeneta’s latest weekly market update. X eneta Chief Analyst Peter Sand said the sharp rise in spot rates from the Far East to the US West and East coasts could begin to lose momentum in the first half of October. Compared with 1 July, shippers are currently paying an average of $1,280 more per FEU on the US West Coast and $2,691 more on the US East Coast. Meanwhile, short-term rates from the Far East to North Europe and the Mediterranean have fallen significantly since 1 July, declining by 29% and 38%, respectively. Sand expects early October could bring a temporary pause before the downward trend resumes. Sand attributed the current market conditions to the combined impact of several operational disruptions, noting that while individual events had not significantly affected networks, their cumulative effect has created greater disruption. The divergence between US and European trades is also creating uncertainty for shippers preparing to tender for 2027 contract volumes. While contract rates are expected to remain well below current spot levels, Xeneta said shippers cannot assume that the present market conditions will quickly disappear. Sand said the market could see further changes following the Chinese October holidays, as shippers assess how the various disruptive factors affecting global container networks develop.

https://gcaptain.com/qatar-boosts-lng-tr.text: Sep 24, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Qatar has ramped up liquefied natural gas tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz to the highest in more than two months, a sign it’s becoming more comfortable moving ships through the waterway. At least four laden carriers have been sent out through the narrow strait in the last week, while at least two have moved in the opposite direction to enter the Persian Gulf, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. One of the shipments arrived at India’s west coast on Thursday. No signals were detected from five of the vessels when they traversed Hormuz, but jamming and interference is common in the area, complicating efforts to ascertain the exact location of ships. The movements mark the most sustained increase in Qatari LNG tanker activity since early July, when the country largely halted exports through the strait after one of its vessels was attacked. Before the war, Hormuz handled about a fifth of global LNG supply, but transits have become perilous due to numerous strikes on ships. Traffic remains far below pre-war levels of roughly three LNG shipments a day, but any increase could help ease a global gas supply crunch. Prices in Europe and Asia have surged to the highest levels since 2022 over the last few weeks as demand builds in the run-up to winter. Qatar may also be following the strategies of Persian Gulf oil producers, who have been sending significant volumes of crude through Hormuz. They have embraced a tactic known as shuttling , where they send cargoes through the waterway often on their own ships, before loading the shipments to other vessels in the Gulf of Oman. That’s more challenging for LNG, however, due to the technical difficulties of transferring the super-chilled fuel.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/petrobra.text: Brazil’s state-owned energy giant Petrobras has shaken hands with Mozambique’s National Hydrocarbons Company (ENH) on a framework for bilateral cooperation across the oil and gas sector. The two companies have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish the basis for strategic cooperation in the oil and gas sector. While the deal is valid for two years, there is also potential for renewal. ENH is the commercial arm of the Mozambican State for the research, production, processing, commercialization, and distribution of oil and gas, including the development of projects throughout the oil sector’s value chain. The MoU was signed by Sylvia Anjos , Petrobras’ Director of Exploration and Production; Jonilton Pessoa , Petrobras’ Executive Manager of Exploration; Rudêncio Morais , ENH’s Chairman of the Board of Directors; and Alegria Cossa , ENH’s Administrator. Within the objectives of the agreement are joint action in studies, evaluation, development and commercialization, the sharing of knowledge and the exchange of technical experience. This comes shortly after Petrobras inked a 20-year deal with Sempra Infrastructure to buy approximately 0.8 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of LNG from the Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 project, currently under construction in Texas.

https://petronoticias.com.br/transpetro-.text: A Transpetro avalia que a nova legislação que cria uma tipificação penal específica para o furto de combustíveis em dutos representa um reforço no combate a esse tipo de crime no país. Sancionada nesta semana, a Lei nº 15.517 também estabelece penas mais rigorosas para as ocorrências, que, segundo a companhia, representam riscos à segurança das pessoas, ao meio ambiente e à continuidade do abastecimento. Maior operadora dutoviária do país, a Transpetro administra cerca de 8,5 mil quilômetros de dutos utilizados no transporte de petróleo, derivados e biocombustíveis. A companhia afirma investir aproximadamente R$ 100 milhões por ano em ações de prevenção a furtos, além de manter iniciativas de relacionamento com comunidades instaladas no entorno das faixas de dutos e convênios com órgãos estaduais de segurança pública. Na avaliação da empresa, a nova legislação reconhece as particularidades desse tipo de ocorrência. Antes da mudança, os casos de furto de combustíveis em dutos eram enquadrados como furto comum, sem uma classificação penal específica. “E ssa mudança na legislação era aguardada há anos e deixa claro que o furto em dutos não é um crime comum. Além de fortalecer a atuação das autoridades responsáveis, a medida amplia a capacidade de prevenção e proteção de um sistema logístico essencial para o abastecimento do país. A Transpetro é vítima dessas ocorrências e atua permanentemente, em conjunto com órgãos de segurança pública e comunidades vizinhas às faixas de dutos, para reduzir os riscos associados a essa prática criminosa ”, afirma o presidente da Transpetro, Sérgio Bacci. A Transpetro ressalta a importância da participação da sociedade na comunicação de situações suspeitas observadas em faixas de dutos. Para isso, disponibiliza o Canal 168, telefone gratuito que funciona 24 horas por dia, sete dias por semana, com garantia de anonimato e sigilo das informações prestadas. A Transpetro terá agora à sua disposição uma nova desenvolvida pela gigante sueca Nokia e pela empresa brasileira Liderroll, que já atuou algumas vezes proporcionando soluções para as tubulações da Transpetro. o seu presidente, Paulo Fernandes, anunciou que abriu uma divisão de projeto, construção, comissionamento de Big datacenter para atender a exigente demanda de dados para as necessidades de energia da Inteligência Artificial. O suporte da Liderrol nesta empreitada repleta de complexidade vem através de uma parceria com a gigante sueca NOKIA, que é a maior empresa detentora deste conhecimento e fornecedora de todo o sistema, atuando com a Liderroll como a integradora e empresa de engenharia que assume o EPC de todo o projeto.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: O Porto do Açu e a OceanPact assinaram nesta quinta-feira (24) uma Carta de Intenções para ampliar a área ocupada pela empresa no complexo industrial e portuário de São João da Barra, no Rio de Janeiro. O acordo foi firmado durante a feira ROG.e, no Rio de Janeiro, e prevê o reforço da infraestrutura de apoio à cadeia de petróleo e gás na região. Pelo termo, a OceanPact recebe de forma imediata cerca de 27 mil m² adicionais à área atual de 45 mil m² que já ocupa no Açu. O documento também garante à empresa o direito de preferência para incorporar mais 60 mil m², incluindo cerca de 100 metros de acesso ao canal. Com a expansão projetada, a companhia poderá implantar até 300 metros de cais privativo destinado ao atendimento de embarcações de apoio e serviços offshore. A OceanPact está presente no Porto do Açu desde 2014 e utiliza a infraestrutura do complexo como base para operações de resposta a emergências ambientais, suporte marítimo e serviços subsea. Para João Braz, diretor de Terminais e Logística do Porto do Açu, a parceria amplia as possibilidades de desenvolvimento do complexo. Segundo o executivo, a decisão da OceanPact de aumentar sua presença reforça a capacidade do Açu de oferecer infraestrutura e flexibilidade a empresas que precisam crescer conforme a evolução de suas demandas. Erik Cunha, CCO da OceanPact, afirma que a parceria com o Porto do Açu se consolida progressivamente e permite a expansão das atividades da empresa para atender à demanda crescente do setor. Para o executivo, o projeto amplia a capacidade operacional da companhia e reforça a posição do Açu como hub portuário e logístico. Localizado em frente à Bacia de Campos, o Porto do Açu abriga a maior base de apoio offshore do mundo e atende toda a cadeia de óleo e gás, da exploração ao descomissionamento de plataformas. O complexo responde por mais de 30% das exportações brasileiras de petróleo e tem liderado iniciativas de transição energética no setor marítimo, com projetos de eletrificação de atracadouros, testes com combustíveis de baixa emissão e reciclagem sustentável de embarcações.

O Porto de Santos, maior complexo portuário da América Latina, registrou em agosto de 2026 a maior movimentação de contêineres de sua história. Foram transportados 538,2 mil TEU no mês, volume 3,9% superior ao registrado em agosto de 2025. Os dados foram divulgados nesta sexta-feira (25) pela Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS). O desempenho mensal também se reflete no acumulado do ano. Entre janeiro e agosto, o porto movimentou 4 milhões de TEU, novo recorde para os oito primeiros meses de um ano e avanço de 3,9% sobre igual período de 2025. Já a movimentação geral de cargas, que soma todos os tipos de produtos transportados pelo porto, somou 125,9 milhões de toneladas no acumulado do ano, alta de 3,1% ante o período janeiro-agosto de 2025. Os embarques responderam por 93,1 milhões de toneladas, um crescimento de 2,9% na comparação com as 90,5 milhões de toneladas do ano anterior. Os desembarques somaram 32,8 milhões de toneladas, expansão de 3,6% sobre as 31,7 milhões de toneladas de 2025. Na leitura isolada de agosto, o cenário foi de estabilidade com leve recuo. A movimentação geral de cargas no mês totalizou 16,4 milhões de toneladas, queda de 0,5% ante agosto de 2025. Os embarques caíram 0,7%, de 12,1 milhões para 12 milhões de toneladas, enquanto os desembarques tiveram alta marginal de 0,2%, passando de 4,38 milhões para 4,39 milhões de toneladas. Os granéis líquidos foram um dos destaques do mês, com 1,6 milhão de toneladas movimentadas em agosto, aumento de 6,3% sobre o mesmo mês do ano passado. No acumulado de 2026, o segmento somou 13,4 milhões de toneladas, alta de 9,3% e novo recorde histórico para o período. Os granéis sólidos também bateram recorde no acumulado do ano, com 64 milhões de toneladas movimentadas entre janeiro e agosto, avanço de 2,7% sobre 2025. Soja em grãos liderou a pauta de produtos transportados no segmento, com participação de 49,5%, seguida por açúcar, com 19,9%, e soja peletizada, com 11,9%.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: O presidente do TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, anunciou nesta quinta-feira (24) que o aplicativo e-Título poderá ser baixado nos dias de votação das eleições de 2026. https://g1.globo.com/sp/sorocaba-jundiai.text: Um vídeo registrado na segunda-feira (21) mostra pombos comendo a merenda dos alunos na Escola Estadual Antônio Padilha, em Sorocaba (SP). https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: The Philippine Coast Guard is reporting a new standoff between two of its vessels on a resupply mission in the Spratly Islands. While it is part of the long-running dispute over the presence of Filipino forces on a purposefully grounded warship, it is the first time since July that the sides squared off in the area. It also follows another recent bumping incident between a Chinese and Philippine vessel. The Philippines asserts it sent two vessels, BRP Malabrigo and BRP Cabra , on September 24 as part of the regular Rotation and Resupply mission to the BRP Sierra Madre , which has been grounded on the Second Thomas Shoal since 1999. The vessel, built by the United States in the 1940s and operated from the late 1970s until 1999 as an amphibious transport by the Philippine Navy, was grounded to establish a Philippine presence in the Spratly Islands. The Philippines maintains a small crew aboard the ship. During the recent incident, the Philippines asserts there was a large presence of Chinese vessels in the area and that they were "continuously shadowing" its vessels. Chat posted by the Philippine Coast Guard showing the Chinese vessels is says are around the disputed shoal (PCG) “The mission was temporarily suspended after a CCG vessel carried out dangerous maneuvers against M/V Lapu-Lapu that threatened a collision, although no one was injured,” said Jay Tarriela, the spokesperson for the Philippine Coast Guard. The Chinese responded today, calling the incident a “provocation” and saying the Philippines was “attempting to deliver supplies to an illegally ‘grounded’ warship.” Further, they say it happened during a Chinese holiday and that the Filipinos "hyped up" the incident. The statement called on the Philippines to “stop provocations and troublemaking,” asserting that the Philippines is "reneging on its commitments” and disregarding Chinese warnings. It said the Philippines "willfully" dispatched the supply mission.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Authorities in the Puntland region of Somalia are reporting that they freed another vessel being held by pirates. Somali pirates took control of six vessels between April and August this year, with three still believed to be under the control of pirates. The Puntland Navy and Puntland Maritime Police Force only said that the product tanker Sibu 1 had been freed and the pirates were arrested. They reported it was a planned 48-hour operation, and they were continuing to follow up. The local news outlet, the Daily Somalia, however, reports it was a violent clash between the Somali forces and the pirates. The unconfirmed story says the fight took place off the coast of Mudug and that three people were dead and several others injured. It did not specify whether it was all pirates or some of the crew from the ship. The Sibu 1 was transporting oil products when it was boarded on August 20 off the coast of Yemen, approximately 136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla. UK Maritime Trade Operations was informed that six individuals had boarded the ship and directed it to the coast of Somalia. The crew appeared to hastily transmit a final message on AIS reading “PRIRATE ONBOARD HEL,” [sic] as the ship was being seized. The ship was reported to have a crew of 20, including 16 Indian nationals and four Arab crewmembers. The 32,238 dwt product tanker, which was built in 2001 and also operating under the name Seamul , had a murky past and was sanctioned by the United States in December 2025 in an effort targeting an Egyptian businessman. OFAC asserted his companies were associated with multiple shadow fleet vessels, as well as several shipping companies, used to transport Iranian oil products. The Seamul was transferred to UAE management and also started using the name Sibu 1 . It was claiming registry in Eritrea, which is considered false. The rescue of the tanker followed the release of the small cargo ship Sward on September 11 after 138 days in captivity. The 8,500 dwt cargo ship, which is registered in St. Kitts and Nevis, was carrying a cargo of fertilizer bound for Mombasa, Kenya, when it was boarded on April 26. It had a crew of 17, made up of 15 Syrians and two Indians. Reports said an undisclosed amount of ransom had been paid.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/mary-mcal.text: McAllister Towing has taken delivery of its latest high-tech, low-emission tug, Mary McAllister, from East Boothbay, Maine, shipbuilder Washburn & Doughty Associates, Inc. Mary McAllister is the sixth in a seven-tug series of American Bureau of Shipping classed and certified 84-tonne bollard pull, low-emission tractor tugs. Powered by CAT Tier IV engines producing 6,770 horsepower, it is classed with the following ABS certifications and endorsements: +A-1 Towing, +AMS, Fire Fighting (FiFi 1), Escort, Low Emissions Vessel. Its firefighting equipment includes pumps and monitors capable of producing 12,000 gallons of water and foam per minute. “As our customer’s vessels grow larger and services for these behemoths become increasingly demanding,” says the company, “McAllister continues to meet their needs with modern and environmentally conscious equipment.” “The Mary is eventually bound for sunny Florida, but she’ll get a little tour of the U.S. East Coast before she gets there,” says McAllister. “The Mary left Washburn & Doughty just in time to ride out the approaching nor’easter. She will navigate her first North Atlantic storm in Portland before heading south. Joining her sister vessel, Isabel , in Baltimore, Mary will receive her first work order as part of the McAllister fleet. After her Baltimore hitch, the Mary will proceed to her homeport in Port Everglades where she will be a dynamic force for years to come.”

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 25/09/2026 – Ao longo da semana passada, fiscais da Agência percorreram cinco municípios da Região Norte para acompanhar a prestação dos serviços de navegação interior. Pela segunda vez neste ano, a Operação Hora Certa, da Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ), foi realizada até sexta-feira (18), com equipes mobilizadas em Belém (PA), Santarém (PA), Manaus (AM), Porto Velho (RO) e Santana (AP). A ação teve como objetivo fiscalizar 84 embarcações e os serviços prestados por empresas reguladas que operam na região com o transporte longitudinal de passageiros e misto. Para isso, as equipes acompanharam as linhas em operação e verificaram se os serviços estavam de acordo com as diretrizes autorizadas pela ANTAQ. Foram observados aspectos como rotas, horários e frequência das viagens, além das embarcações utilizadas. Também foram verificadas eventuais alterações na operação que pudessem estar em desacordo com o previsto. O nome da Operação Hora Certa tem origem na estratégia adotada pelas equipes. As fiscalizações são realizadas, sempre que possível, próximas aos horários previstos para a saída e a chegada das embarcações. Dessa forma, os fiscais conseguem comparar o serviço encontrado em campo com o que foi autorizado pela ANTAQ e verificar o cumprimento dos horários programados. As informações verificadas foram registradas pelas equipes em campo e os resultados serão divulgados em relatório a ser encaminhado à Gerência de Coordenação das Unidades Regionais (GCOR/SFC) até 23/10.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Iranian officials appearing at the United Nations on Friday, September 25, said they have offered a new proposal for opening the Strait of Hormuz in a week’s time. They said it all depends on the U.S. response to the proposal, which was reportedly conveyed by mediators from Qatar. The core of the proposal appears little changed from the previous interim agreement and terms that have been repeatedly presented and then violated. Iran set as the key conditions the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and embargo on Iranian shipping, waiving the sanctions on Iranian oil sales, and observing a ceasefire with Iran that would also include Lebanon. The reports indicated that, as a “sweetener” or “enticement,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would restart talks with the U.S. on its military program, seven days after the agreement is accepted. Reuters, however, is quoting another “senior Iranian official” who it says indicated on Friday that Iran would show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Today’s message came, Reuters reports, after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the media at the UN on Thursday that he hoped a deal to end the hostilities could be reached before the US midterm elections on November 3. Donald Trump has said in the past that he thinks a deal will be reached after the elections and that Iran was waiting to see the outcome of the vote. There was no immediate response from the White House to the Iranian comments, but it said earlier in the week that U.S. officials had positive and constructive conversations with mediators on the Iran war. The Associated Press is citing Saudi Arabian officials who said they were “skeptical of the latest push for a deal.” Trump had used harsh words after the collapse of the June deal, saying Iran did not respect its agreements and that he accused it of prolonging the discussions and wasting time. He has said he was skeptical that an agreement would be honored and, in his speech to the United Nations this week, threatened Iran with “annihilation.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Speculation is mounting after trackers revealed that three of the tankers stopped by U.S. forces as part of the economic blockade against Iran have been spotted on the move toward the United States. The U.S. has a history of pursuing forfeiture complaints, and the Trump administration has hinted at it as a step in the ongoing efforts to punish Iran. The discussions began when TankerTrackers.com posted a brief message on Wednesday saying, “Nearly six million barrels (valued at nearly $600M) of seized Iranian crude oil are quietly crossing the Atlantic Ocean towards the United States of America.” It did not provide further details. The ships, however, have now been identified using data from Kpler and others. Two of the VLCCs are the Tifani (IMO 9273337), a 300,000 dwt tanker falsely claiming registry in Botswana, stopped in April in the Indian Ocean, and the Majestic X (IMO 9198317), a 281,500 dwt tanker falsely claiming registry in Guyana, which was stopped two days after the first tanker, also in the Indian Ocean. Both of these vessels were detected sailing north along the coast of Brazil. Both were laden with Iranian crude and made it out of the Persian Gulf, likely heading for China, before the blockade was first imposed in April 2026. The Pentagon asserted the vessels were stopped under the right of visit, inspecting sanctioned stateless vessels. The Department of Homeland Security later inspected the vessel, and reports said the US would seek seizure orders. The third tanker drew some more speculation before it was identified as Davina (300,976 dwt), although most databases list the vessel as Lenore. It was claiming a false registry in Curacao and, before that, had also falsely claimed it was sailing under the flag of Palau. It was stopped in June off Sri Lanka. Kpler’s data said the vessel had sailed past Africa’s Cape of Good Hope, recently entering the Atlantic. Combined, the three ships would be laden with approximately six million barrels of Iranian crude. That would be a value of roughly $600 million based on current market prices. Only the Majestic X , briefly in late July, showed a destination of the United States, according to Kpler’s data. Observers, however, are confident the ships are headed toward the United States, likely Texas, where the U.S. will enforce its forfeiture.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: Japanese shipping major NYK is moving to strengthen its business in the offshore wind power segment. The group, best known for its operations in dry bulk and tankers, has said it views the offshore sector as a strong growth opportunity. In its latest move, the company has ordered a newbuild service operation vessel (SOV) to support its operations in the Asia-Pacific region. The new 89-meter (292-foot) vessel will be built by PaxOcean Group, a member of Kuok Maritime Group, and will support the construction, operation, and maintenance of offshore wind farms. It will serve as an offshore base for personnel accommodation and logistical support. The company did not reveal the cost of the new vessel. In recent years, NYK has been pushing to deepen its interests in the offshore wind sector. Last year, the company entered the European market by investing in Northern Offshore Group (NOG), a crew transfer vessel operator with over 60 vessels in the global offshore wind industry. According to NYK, the investment in NOG in February last year was partially designed to ensure the company gains important operational experience in preparation for future expansion of offshore wind in waters closer to Japan. With the SOV order, the company reports that the newbuild project is leveraging the expertise and experience accumulated in Europe, a move that will enable it to further develop its offshore wind business in the Asia-Pacific region where the market is recording significant growth. Data show that last year, investments in the region’s offshore wind exceeded $50 billion. NYK says the new vessel will have a capacity of 120 persons and is designed to support logistics needs associated with offshore wind farm construction projects. The vessel will be equipped with a dynamic positioning system that can automatically calculate external forces such as wind and currents and uses thrusters and other propulsion devices to maintain its position at sea.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Florida-based American Roll-On/Roll-Off Carrier Group (ARC Group) is highlighting its recent addition of a large vehicle carrier to its U.S.-flagged fleet. The ship, which moved from the Swedish flag, will support commercial and government customers while adding further capacity to the Maritime Administration’s Maritime Security Program. Built in 2011 at Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering in South Korea, the vessel had been operating for Wallenius Marine as the Figaro . Data show her ownership was transferred to ARC Group in June, and she entered the American register. ARC, which is a subsidiary of Norway’s Wallenius Wilhelmsen Group, supports the U.S. Government with a fleet of 10 vessels. The addition of the new vehicle carrier, which was renamed ARC Freedom , expands the company’s capacity and adds a large new carrier. The ship is 231 meters (757 feet) and 31,143 dwt with a capacity of nearly 8,000 units. It has 13 vehicle decks, including five hoistable decks that will provide flexibility for various sizes and configurations of cargo. ARC’s president and CEO Eric Ebeling said the name ARC Freedom was a fitting name for a vessel carrying the U.S. flag as America marked its 250th anniversary. Large stern ramp gives the vessel good flexibility for cargo including helicopters (ARC Group) “Adding the ARC Freedom to the U.S.-flag fleet is a major win for America’s national security,” said Captain Stephen M. Carmel, Administrator of the Maritime Administration (MARAD) at the U.S. Department of Transportation. “As a member of the Maritime Security Program, this vessel will deliver the rapid response our military depends on to keep America safe.”

A third interdicted ship was observed heading west into the Atlantic after rounding the Cape of Good Hope. The seizures captivated the market at the time as the US imposed a strict blockade on Iran’s oil exports. The ships initially changed direction multiple times in the Indian Ocean, with it unclear where they would eventually go. In April, Bloomberg News reported that the Justice Department had initiated a forfeiture process against the Tifani and Majestic X , which is also known as Phonix. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/the.text: The energy sector is developing zero-emission bunker fuel supply and infrastructure to meet the IMO’s 2030 target of 5-10% uptake. But vessel orders and commercial demand are struggling to keep pace. The IMO wants zero- or near-zero-emission energy to account for at least 5% of international shipping’s energy consumption by 2030, striving for 10%. But the shipping industry still has a long way to go to meet this ambition, probably even further than two years ago. In September 2024, researchers at the UCL Energy Institute and the Getting to Zero Coalition, run by the Global Maritime Forum (GMF), found that fuel supply was partially on track but demand was lagging. Two years later, their September 2026 report suggests little has changed. “In several cases, progress has not only slowed relative to previous years but regressed,” the 2026 report said. The assessment focuses on e-methanol and e-ammonia as scalable zero-emission fuels (SZEF) with a well-to-wake GHG intensity below 19 gCO2e/MJ. It excludes e-methane because of its methane slip, as well as blue fuels produced from fossil feedstocks with carbon capture and storage.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fit-out-.text: Fit-out works are currently underway on the converter stations in Germany and the UK for NeuConnect, a high-voltage submarine cable that will create the first direct energy transmission link between the two countries. The construction of the 24-meter-high, 70-meter-wide converter hall buildings reached full height earlier this year, allowing main contractor Siemens Energy to start the internal and external fit-out phase that will see key mechanical and electrical systems being installed. At the UK converter station, the transformers, each being 7 meters long, 5 meters tall and weighing over 200 tons, have been moved into position, while at both the UK and German sites work is underway to fit the transformers with equipment and accessories. As for the internal works on the converter stations, they include cable trays, ladders and heating ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) ducting being installed throughout, while external works are continuing with cladding works underway in Germany and nearing completion in the UK. Other external works include installing guttering and drainage equipment, and preparing site roads for tarmacking to help form access routes across all parts of the converter station sites. Furthermore, in Germany, the AC switchyard has seen a number of trellis-type support towers constructed that will hold key overhead equipment. NeuConnect CEO Arnaud Grévoz said: “NeuConnect’s construction is moving into an important new phase as we start to install the key systems and equipment that will help to power this vital new UK-German energy link. With our onshore Converter Stations taking shape and offshore cabling works also well over halfway, we are making good progress and remain firmly on track.”

https://gcaptain.com/how-europes-intensi.text: An octopus on a rock at Porthkerris reef, Cornwall, Britain, August 2025. Kirsty Andrews/Handout via REUTERS LONDON, Sept 26 (Reuters) – As drought spread and wildfires raged across Europe this summer, the extraordinary heat didn’t stop at the shoreline. European waters notched their hottest summer months since satellite sensors began providing reliable data in 1982, according to a Reuters analysis of temperatures recorded at the seas’ surface. Records fell from the English Channel to the Mediterranean Sea. An offshore buoy near Mallorca recorded a temperature of 33.02 degrees Celsius (91.44 degrees Fahrenheit) on August ?5, the highest ever registered in the Spanish port authority’s buoy network. Scientists warn that events like this year’s marine heatwaves are becoming more frequent, more intense and more widespread as greenhouse-gas emissions drive up atmospheric temperatures around the globe. The world’s oceans absorb the majority of the excess heat and retain it longer than the land or atmosphere. That’s transforming marine ecosystems , with catastrophic consequences for some European fisheries and the people who rely on them, according to a review of the scientific literature and interviews with more than a dozen researchers, fishing industry sources and analysts. Species that have sustained some coastal communities in Spain and southern England for generations are disappearing, as unfamiliar arrivals surge into newly hospitable waters.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/new.text: Shipping’s energy transition has entered a new phase. The technology options are increasingly well understood. LNG, methanol, biofuels, wind-assisted propulsion, and emerging ammonia solutions are no longer concepts but commercial realities. Yet despite this progress, shipowners face a more difficult challenge than ever: making investment decisions amid unprecedented regulatory uncertainty. The 2026 edition of DNV’s Maritime Forecast to 2050 argues that uncertainty itself is now becoming one of the most important drivers of fleet strategy. “Decisions taken today on vessel design, retrofits, and fuel capability will determine competitiveness for decades, while the outcome of ongoing regulatory negotiations could significantly reshape the economics of shipping’s energy transition,” says Øyvind Sekkesæter, Senior Consultant at DNV and lead author of this year’s report. “Maritime Forecast to 2050 aims to assist that decision-making with our latest core insights and case study examples.” Four regulatory scenarios could shape shipping very differently This year’s Maritime Forecast takes a scenario-based approach, presenting four possible regulatory futures for shipping. These range from the full adoption of IMO’s initially approved Net-Zero Framework (NZF) to its rejection and prolonged political gridlock, while also exploring several intermediate outcomes, including a delayed or revised NZF and scenarios where regional regulations play a more prominent role in driving decarbonization. Rather than predicting which outcome is most likely, the scenarios illustrate how different regulatory futures could affect fuel demand, energy-efficiency uptake, investment signals, and fleet competitiveness. Stronger global regulation accelerates demand for low-GHG fuels and increases the attractiveness of energy-efficiency measures, while the absence of such regulation slows market development. The result is a transition whose pace may vary significantly depending on future policy decisions. “For shipowners, this means the challenge is no longer identifying a single fuel pathway that fits the operational profile of their fleet. Instead, it is preparing fleets that remain competitive across multiple possible futures,” Sekkesæter concludes. Tapping the fleet’s efficiency potential Fully realizing the fleet’s energy-saving potential requires improvements not only to newbuilds but also to existing ships through retrofits.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/acc.text: The transition to zero-emission short-sea shipping has reached a pivotal milestone as the EU-funded HyShip project welcomes the SeaShuttle container vessels as its new real-world demonstrators. Supported by the Clean Hydrogen Partnership, the project is tackling one of the maritime industry’s most persistent challenges: creating an end-to-end liquid hydrogen ecosystem that connects fuel production, port infrastructure and vessel operations. By linking advanced onboard hydrogen storage systems with quayside bunkering infrastructure, HyShip is moving beyond isolated trials to establish a fully operational corridor between Oslo and Rotterdam. This integration paves the way for the wider adoption of hydrogen-powered shipping across the continent. From concept to commercial deployment At the heart of this initiative are two hydrogen-powered SeaShuttle vessels currently being built by HyShip partner Samskip, the Netherlands. The first is scheduled to enter service in the second quarter of 2027. Unlike many research prototypes, these ships are designed from the outset for commercial freight operations, transporting containerised cargo while eliminating carbon emissions. In total, the two vessels will be powered by 32 Ballard FCwaveTM 200 kW fuel cell engines, delivering a combined 6.4 MW of zero-emission power. When operating on green hydrogen, each ship is expected to reduce CO2 emissions by approximately 25 000 tonnes annually. The project aims to accumulate over 3 000 hours of real-world operational data during an 18-month commercial demonstration. It will provide invaluable insights into sailing performance, port manoeuvring and bunkering procedures. This data will be used to inform future vessel projects, regulatory pathways and investment decisions. A critical component of the HyShip mission is the development of safe, scalable infrastructure to support these vessels. Consortium partner LH2 Shipping, Norway, is leading the design, construction and operation of the port bunkering system, ensuring that liquid hydrogen can be transferred safely and efficiently from shore to ship. Building a scalable hydrogen ecosystem The significance of this project extends far beyond the success of two individual ships. HyShip is generating the operational knowledge and safety standards required to replicate this model across European short-sea routes. The project brings together a diverse consortium of shipowners, technology providers, researchers, classification societies and infrastructure specialists to validate the entire liquid hydrogen value chain. https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/economia/mo.text: A proibição das bets e do jogo do "tigrinho" por meio de Medida Provisória gerou críticas contundentes no mercado financeiro. Ao CNN Prime Time , Luiz Fernando Figueiredo, ex-diretor de Política Monetária do BC, avaliou que esse tipo de decisão transmite uma perigosa sensação de insegurança jurídica aos investidores, independentemente do porte de seus negócios. Segundo ele, o que se observa é um conjunto de incoerências: o governo liberou as bets, depois vetou a participação de beneficiários de programas sociais nos jogos e, agora, às vésperas das eleições municipais, promulgou a proibição total . Figueiredo destacou que o principal efeito desse tipo de decisão sobre o mercado é a perda de confiança nas instituições e no cumprimento de contratos. "Qualquer investidor, qualquer empresário pequeno, médio, grande, quando olha esse tipo de coisa, fala: tudo pode acontecer. Quando tudo pode acontecer, a decisão a seguir é parar para olhar", explicou. Segundo ele, um contrato firmado pode ser alterado a qualquer momento por uma nova medida provisória , o que torna inviável qualquer planejamento de investimento de longo prazo — seja de três, cinco ou dez anos. O especialista também alertou para o impacto direto na confiança dos agentes econômicos. Ele apontou que esse índice já vinha caindo e tende a recuar ainda mais diante de um cenário de incertezas sobre o futuro. Figueiredo acrescentou que o Brasil precisaria de um nível de investimento superior a 20% do PIB, mas atualmente opera entre 14% e 15%, o que, segundo ele, representa um processo de deterioração da economia.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Chinese criticism of Japan’s growing defense budget appears to have been one of the most consequential developments coming out of the days President Xi Jinping spent in Washington for his state visit, which otherwise seems to have done little to move forward Sino-US relations. In advance of the meeting, Chinese Ambassador to Washington Xie Feng had warned that President Xi should not be challenged over Taiwan, democracy and human rights, nor restrictions to China’s growing development influence in the world, so the agenda between the two presidents was limited. Japan’s Sanae Takaichi was in New York at the same time to make her first appearance as Prime Minister at the UN General Assembly, and held bilateral meetings with President Trump in New York. Chinese state media chose the moment of the Sino-US summit to launch a stinging attack on Prime Minister Takaichi’s radical plans to increase Japanese defense spending, and in particular to strengthen naval and air defense forces defending Japan’s isolated southern islands, specifically the Nansei Chain islands of Miyako, Ishigaki and Yonaguni. Japan’s possession of these islands, and others to the east and north-east of Taiwan, would prove an obstacle to any Chinese plan to invade Taiwan. If long-range anti-aircraft and anti-shipping missiles are stationed on these islands, they would be able to disrupt the deployment of the PLA Navy to encircle Taiwan and cut it off from external reinforcement. Prime Minister Takaichi has already made it clear that a Chinese invasion of Taiwan would be a causus belli for Japan, and a strategic threat to Japan’s national security. Her approach has been endorsed in this year’s general election in Japan, which gave her an unprecedented supermajority in the Japanese Diet, sufficient to change the constitution and to support a doubling of the percentage of GDP devoted to defense. Besides a significant expansion of the Japan Maritime Self Defense Force, in particular enhancements to its Mogami Class frigates and submarine fleet, the Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Minister Koizumi has already announced that infrastructure to support a permanent presence of Chu-SAM (Type-03) medium-range air defense missiles on the Japanese island of Yonaguni will be in place by 2030. Field-deployed Chu-SAM systems are probably there already, with sufficient range to cover the eastern approaches to Taiwan. These systems will thicken up air defense cover for the Okinawa-based 12th Marine Littoral Regiment, which is tasked alongside the JGSDF with defending Japan’s outlying islands, and which has recently been re-equipped with the Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction Systems (NMESIS) and Marine Air Defense Integrated Systems (MADIS). Ziara tem melanoma uveal, câncer raro no olho, que está em metástase pelo corpo — Foto: Arquivo pessoal Durante anos, Ziara Abud foi uma advogada bem sucedida com o sonho de se aposentar cedo para viver a vida que sempre quis: viajar, mergulhar com tubarões e saltar de paraquedas, esporte em que competiu pelo país e acumulou recordes. Em 2013, vendeu para uma multinacional americana a empresa que fundou e se aposentou antes dos 50 anos, para se dedicar ao que mais gostava. Foi em uma das sonhadas viagens, para mergulhar na Indonésia, que a visão de um dos olhos começou a embaçar. Em janeiro de 2020, veio o diagnóstico: melanoma uveal , um câncer que nasce dentro do olho e atinge cerca de 5 pessoas a cada milhão. Mesmo dentro dessa doença rara, Ziara está em um grupo sem tratamento específico aprovado no país. Seis anos, várias cirurgias e sucessivas linhas de tratamento depois, o tumor chegou ao fígado, aos pulmões, ao cérebro, aos ossos e a uma região próxima ao coração. O prognóstico é difícil, mas ela não pensa em desistir. “Eu amo viver, eu quero continuar vivendo. Eu tenho só 59 anos, sabe? Ainda tem muita vida”, conta. Quando Ziara esteve em grupo que bateu recorde em salto na Tailândia — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/north-se.text: Three Norwegian oil and gas players – Aker BP, Equinor, and DNO – have carried out appraisal drilling activities on two hydrocarbon discoveries in the North Sea off the coast of Norway, raising the estimated size of these finds. Aker BP and its partners, Equinor and DNO, have drilled the 16/1-EA-4 H appraisal well on the Verdandi and Lillefix discoveries in the North Sea, which has increased the projected discovery size, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate. The well 16/1-EA-4 H was drilled about 200 kilometers west of Stavanger by Odfjell Drilling’s Deepsea Nordkapp rig from the subsea template on the Symra field as a horizontal appraisal wellbore. This was the 11th exploration well in production license 167 , which was awarded in the 13th licensing round. The well was drilled to a vertical depth of 1,864 meters below sea level and terminated in the Heimdal Formation from the Palaeocene, with the objective of proving reservoir rocks from the Palaeocene in the Heimdal Formation and confirming the extent of the reservoir and presumed oil-water contact. The well encountered a 14-meter gas column and a 44-meter oil column in sandstone layers in the Heimdal Formation. The gas-oil contact was encountered at 1,776 meters below sea level. A total of 1,515 reservoir meters were drilled horizontally through the oil zone in the Heimdal Formation with moderate reservoir quality. Data acquisition has been carried out, which included obtaining fluid samples and pressure points.

https://www.offshore-energy.biz/cnooc-ke.text: Australia’s engineering firm Worley has picked up a multi-year renewal of its assignment in the North Sea with CNOOC International, a subsidiary of China’s CNOOC, supporting the operator’s offshore operations on the UK Continental Shelf (UKCS). Worley has obtained a five-year renewal of its engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) framework agreement with CNOOC International’s UK business , including the Scott , Buzzard , and Golden Eagle fields. The Australian firm’s scope includes engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, completions and decommissioning services, from like-for-like replacements through to complex brownfield modifications and larger project scopes. The company stated: “Over the past 12 years, Worley has delivered more than 1,100 scopes of work under the previous framework agreement, helping CNOOC maintain the integrity and performance of its offshore assets. “This proven delivery record, combined with deep asset knowledge, enables Worley to provide efficient solutions that minimise operational disruption and maximise value. Safety remains central to the partnership, having executed more than five million work hours without a lost time incident in 12 years.” While extending a long-standing partnership between the two companies, the award reinforces Worley’s long-term commitment to the North Sea and the Aberdeen area, and supports the continued development of the regional energy supply chain.

https://gcaptain.com/gulf-of-oman-ship-t.text: A satellite image of side-by-side ships at sea, off the coast of Sohar, Oman, June 9, 2026. SPOT © CNES 2026, Distribution Airbus DS/Handout via REUTERS SINGAPORE, Sept 25 (Reuters) – Ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman for Middle Eastern oil from inside the Strait of Hormuz have reached their limits after Saudi Arabia diverted exports from the Red Sea, adding to shipments from other producers, trade sources and analysts said. The increasing amount of Saudi exports this month requires more supertankers to shuttle crude through Hormuz to conduct cargo transfers, they said. That has reduced ship availability, raising shipping costs and increasing the time cargoes are on the water before reaching refineries. State-run Saudi Aramco 2222.SE has sold more than 60 million barrels of crude for STS transfer off Sohar, Oman, this month and next since its East-West Pipeline was attacked on September 13, halting oil exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track to rebound to 3.6 million barrels per day in September, up from about 900,000 bpd in August, data from analytics firm Kpler showed. That nearly 3 million bpd increase in Saudi exports from Hormuz would require between 36 and 40 more very large crude carriers, Kpler analyst Panagiotis Krontiras said. Each VLCC can carry 2 million barrels of oil.

https://petronoticias.com.br/porto-sudes.text: O Porto Sudeste, terminal portuário privado localizado em Itaguaí (RJ), está ampliando sua infraestrutura para acompanhar o crescimento da movimentação de petróleo e derivados no Brasil. Com conclusão prevista para o primeiro semestre de 2027, o projeto permitirá a realização de até 144 operações com granéis líquidos por ano. Atualmente, as operações envolvendo granéis sólidos e líquidos utilizam a mesma infraestrutura portuária. A entrada em funcionamento dos novos dolfins — estruturas marítimas destinadas à atracação e amarração de embarcações — permitirá a criação de uma área exclusiva para petróleo e derivados, aumentando a previsibilidade na programação dos navios. A expansão ocorre em meio ao avanço da produção brasileira de petróleo, especialmente nas áreas do pré-sal. Com a entrada de novos volumes no mercado, cresce também a demanda por infraestrutura portuária, embarcações e alternativas de transbordo capazes de dar maior eficiência ao escoamento da produção. “ Esse avanço aumenta a demanda por estruturas capazes de dar maior eficiência ao escoamento e atender ao aumento dos fluxos de carga. A ampliação da capacidade do Porto Sudeste contribuirá para reduzir restrições logísticas e oferecer maior flexibilidade às empresas que atuam na produção, no transporte marítimo e na comercialização de petróleo e derivados ”, afirma Jayme Nicolato , CEO do Porto Sudeste. Instalado em águas abrigadas da Baía de Sepetiba, região caracterizada pela baixa variação de maré, o terminal possui condições favoráveis para operações de transbordo atracado, conhecidas como Double Banking. A localização próxima à Bacia de Santos, principal área produtora do pré-sal brasileiro, também coloca o Porto Sudeste como uma alternativa para o escoamento da produção offshore. A expansão contribui ainda para fortalecer a posição de Itaguaí como polo portuário e logístico. O movimento ocorre paralelamente a mudanças no ambiente regulatório do setor. A Resolução nº 1.007/2026 da Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) atualizou as regras para a distribuição de royalties relacionados às operações de embarque e desembarque de petróleo e gás, acrescentando novos elementos ao debate sobre a repartição das receitas geradas por essas atividades e seus impactos sobre os municípios.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: New Zealand has made further progress in restarting domestic gas production with a new round of funding targeting offshore exploration projects. Resources Minister Shane Jones and Associate Finance Minister Chris Bishop this week announced $21 million financing for two offshore gas projects. The financing will be made through the Gas Security Fund (GSF), a $113 million state-owned investment facility to ramp up gas production in New Zealand. One of the projects considered for funding in this round is EnZed Energy’s Kaheru offshore gas exploration in Taranaki Basin. The project will receive $12.19 million for a time-limited equity arrangement. The project has a total cost of $40.2 million with EnZed Energy seeking to raise the remaining $28.1 million from other investors. Initially, the project will prospect the Kaheru field to determine whether commercially recoverable gas is present. The Australian explorer EnZed Energy was awarded gas exploration permit by New Zealand in July. It was the first such rights to be issued by the country after reversing the 2018 ban on offshore oil and gas exploration. The 12-year exploration permit covers about 546 square kilometers in the offshore Taranaki Basin, east of the producing Kupe field. “This project targets an estimated 182 petajoules(pj) of additional gas reserve in the Kaheru permit. That’s equivalent of nearly 25 percent of New Zealand’s January 2026 proven and probable gas reserves,” said Minister Shane Jones. According to government petroleum data, New Zealand’s natural gas proven plus probable reserves as of 1 January 2026 was 731 pj, a decline of 23 percent from last year. The Ministry of Business noted that this was the lowest level of natural gas reserves since recording began 20 years ago. Jones added that projects such as Kaheru could be a significant new source of domestic gas supply, helping meet New Zealand’s energy needs in the coming years. The other project to receive the funding is led by the oil services company Schlumberger New Zealand (SLB). The company was awarded $8.2 million to provide industry players with free access for two years to its proprietary seismic data, spanning New Zealand’s key exploration provinces. Over the years, SLB has assembled an extensive seismic library, comprising over 28,000 km2 of 3D data and 5,000 km2 of 2D seismic coverage across both the Taranaki and East Coast basins. As part of the funding, the government wants SLB to combine this fragmented subsurface exploration information into a single, basin-scale, AI-enabled dataset, to be delivered in industry standard format.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/tra.text: The OECD’s September 2026 interim economic outlook projects world GDP growth of 2.9% this year and 3.0% in 2027. While private-sector resilience has given the economy more momentum than previously anticipated, the organisation warns that the commodity-price shock is proving more persistent than assumed. Its central forecast is for growth to encounter headwinds through the end of 2026 and into early 2027 before recovering gradually. “Global growth has held up better than expected, but the buffers that absorbed the energy shock are being depleted,” OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann said. “Growth is weaker than last year and inflation is rising again. “Governments need to target support where it is most needed and get public spending on a sustainable track. They also need to build long term growth foundations, with stronger skills, more diversified energy supplies and faster AI adoption.” Purchasing power is expected to be squeezed as commodity prices bite and policy rates increase, although the OECD assumes an eventual resolution of the Middle East conflict will help activity recover. At the same time, artificial intelligence investment is emerging as an increasingly important pillar of global trade demand, with AI-related spending and production forecast to continue outweighing relatively weak investment elsewhere in the business sector in many G20 economies. The projections rest on some substantial assumptions about commodity markets. The OECD uses futures pricing as of September 14, under which Brent crude reaches an average $105 a barrel in the fourth quarter of 2026 and European TTF gas €82 per megawatt hour. Prices then decline steadily, with Brent averaging $85 a barrel and TTF gas €60/MWh in 2027. Food commodity prices, however, are assumed to keep climbing into the second quarter of next year, peaking about 11% above their third-quarter 2026 level.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mac.text: At its General Assembly on 30 April 2026, members of the Maritime Anti-Corruption Network (MACN) voted in favor of opening MACN membership to classification societies. Following this decision, MACN is pleased to welcome ABS, DNV, and RINA as the first classification societies to join the network. Strengthening integrity across the maritime value chain The maritime industry is facing growing complexity driven by geopolitical developments, changing trade patterns, and evolving vessel ownership and operating structures. These trends underline the importance of maintaining integrity across the maritime value chain and ensuring all relevant actors contribute to practical, coordinated solutions. Classification societies play an essential role throughout a vessel’s lifecycle, including design, construction, maintenance, surveys, and certification. Their work directly supports safety, compliance, and trust in international shipping, while also placing them close to technical, commercial, and regulatory decisions where integrity risks can arise, particularly in complex or high-risk operating environments. By opening membership to classification societies, MACN further strengthens representation across different parts of the maritime ecosystem. Their technical expertise, global reach, and influence can help improve information sharing, strengthen collective responses to corruption risks, and support greater consistency in standards and practices across the industry. The expanded membership also reflects the increasingly interconnected nature of global shipping and the need for collaboration across the maritime value chain. “Classification societies play an essential role in safeguarding standards, safety, and trust across global shipping. Welcoming them into MACN brings vital technical expertise and a wider perspective to our network. Our Collective Action initiatives will be stronger when classification societies stand alongside shipowners, operators, and other maritime stakeholders in addressing corruption risks and advancing integrity across the industry.” – Cecilia Müller Torbrand, CEO, MACN ABS, DNV, and RINA become MACN’s first classification society members The admission of ABS, DNV and RINA marks an important milestone in MACN’s development and puts the General Assembly decision into practice. As three of the world’s leading classification societies, these organisations bring extensive technical expertise, global reach, and deep engagement across the maritime industry.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ind.text: India will honor its overseas commitments for petroleum products, including diesel, Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said Sept. 24, assuring global markets that the country would maintain supplies despite geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. “We will continue with product exports and honor our export commitments,” Puri said at an industry event in New Delhi. India, the world’s fourth-largest refining nation, is a major supplier of refined petroleum products to European and African markets, according to the oil ministry. India’s petroleum product exports fell 40% year over year to 2.7 million metric tons in August, according to the ministry. Exports declined 46.7% year over year to 11.2 million mt during April-August, while exports for fiscal 2025-26 (April-March) fell 9.2% to 46.2 million mt. Concerns about tight diesel supplies come after US President Donald Trump and US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said their administration was considering fully or partially restricting diesel exports amid surging pump prices, following days of increasing political pressure from fellow Republicans to implement an export ban, Platts reported Sept. 22. On Sept. 23, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told a Dow Jones Energy event in New York that the US was unlikely to impose a full ban on diesel exports, though the government is considering a range of options to keep more US-produced diesel in the country in the coming weeks.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/yem.text: Yemen’s internationally recognized government pressed world leaders anew for help defeating the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, saying that their new perch along one of the world’s busiest waterways presents an international economic risk. The Houthis — who have controlled Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, and much of the country’s north for over a decade — stormed down Yemen’s coast this month and seized the crucial port city of Mokha and key Red Sea islands. That gives them better surveillance of ships passing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, at the sea’s southern end. About 12% of the world’s trade usually passes through the waterway. The rebels have declared a blockade on Saudi shipping. While asserting there’s no other threat to commercial shipping on the Red Sea, they have warned other nations not to get involved. But the vice president of the internationally recognized government council urged world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly not to trust the Houthis’ assurances — and to see a bigger picture in the strife around the strait. “The Houthi militias’ use of the safety of navigation as a tool for blackmail threatens not only Yemen. It is taking hostage the entire global economy,” said the vice president, Abdullah Abdulkader al Alimi-Bawzer. Yemeni VP says weapons, technology should be kept from rebels’ hands Arguing that protecting the strait “is the responsibility of every economy that depends on secure supply chains, energy security and freedom of navigation,” he urged the international community to keep weapons and technology from getting into the rebels’ hands.

https://petronoticias.com.br/sbm-offshor.text: A SBM Offshore firmou durante a ROG.e 2026 um acordo de cooperação com o Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas (Sebrae/SE) e o Instituto Euvaldo Lodi de Sergipe (IEL/SE) para avaliar iniciativas de identificação, qualificação e desenvolvimento de fornecedores locais para o projeto Sergipe Águas Profundas (SEAP), desenvolvido em parceria com a Petrobras. A assinatura contou ainda com representantes do Fórum Empresarial de Sergipe, da Associação É de Sergipe, da Associação das Empresas de Petróleo, Gás e Energias de Sergipe e da Rede Petrogas de Sergipe, que participaram como testemunhas e representaram diferentes segmentos da cadeia de fornecedores do estado. A parceria integra a estratégia da SBM Offshore para preparar empresas sergipanas para as oportunidades relacionadas ao SEAP e ampliar a capacidade local de atendimento às futuras demandas da indústria de petróleo e gás. O acordo prevê a análise de ações destinadas a aumentar a participação de empresas do estado na cadeia de suprimentos dos setores de petróleo, gás e energia. Entre as frentes previstas estão o mapeamento de potenciais fornecedores, o desenvolvimento de iniciativas de capacitação e qualificação e a produção de informações estratégicas para apoiar o fortalecimento da cadeia produtiva sergipana. “ A assinatura desse acordo representa um passo importante na preparação de Sergipe para as oportunidades que poderão surgir com o desenvolvimento do SEAP. Nosso objetivo é trabalhar em conjunto com instituições que conhecem a realidade local para identificar oportunidades e desenvolver fornecedores, considerando as necessidades técnicas e operacionais da indústria. A iniciativa também reflete o compromisso da SBM Offshore de contribuir para o desenvolvimento local e deixar um legado positivo nas regiões onde atua, por meio da geração de oportunidades e do fortalecimento da cadeia produtiva ”, afirma Jonas Lobo , Country Manager da SBM Offshore no Brasil. O acordo faz parte do planejamento de entrada da SBM Offshore em Sergipe e amplia o relacionamento da companhia com instituições e lideranças locais. A empresa já mantém uma presença consolidada na cadeia de fornecedores brasileira. Mais de 80 fornecedores nacionais participaram dos três projetos mais recentes de FPSOs da companhia, que atualmente conta com uma rede de mais de 1.000 fornecedores brasileiros qualificados.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Europe’s decision to intensify its crackdown and detentions of the shadow fleet transporting Russia’s crude is achieving results following a drastic decline in the number of vessels flying false flags and a growing number of sanctioned vessels seeking refuge in the Russian flag registry. A report by nonprofit think tank Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) shows that due to detentions, the number of shadow vessels flying false flags has declined from a peak of 101 in October last year to 45 by the end of June. In the first half of this year, authorities boarded and detained some 13 tankers in European or UK coastal waters. Among the shadow fleet vessels detained in European waters is the 2009-built Smyrtos , a crude oil tanker seized by British forces in the English Channel in June for violating Russian sanctions. In May, French troops boarded the Tagor (114,809 dwt) as she was sailing in the Mediterranean. The CREA report shows that due to the increasing detentions and boarding, a growing number of the shadow fleet vessels are seeking refuge in the Russian flag registry. Over the period from January 2025 to the end of June this year, some 107 vessels were added to the Russian flag registry. This resulted in the number of ships now sailing under the Russian flag increasing by 36 percent from 280 vessels to 382. Notably, 87 percent of the vessels that joined the Russian ship registry over that period were already under sanctions. The authors of the report highlight that December last year was the most active month in terms of shadow fleet reflagging. During the month, the Russian registry recorded an influx of 25 vessels. Since then, monthly additions have fallen on a monthly basis from 17 in January to just three in June, an indication that the initial surge of sanctioned vessels seeking refuge under the Russian registry has largely subsided mainly due to a draft presidential decree proposing to cap the age of vessels the registry accepts. Notably, some 93 of the 107 vessels that joined the Russian registry were already under sanctions. 72 of them had transported Russian fossil fuels worth €7.5 billion ($8.5 billion) globally as of the end of June. After being sanctioned, the 72 vessels changed flags roughly three times more frequently, registering under a new flag every three to four months on average before settling under the Russian flag.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/imo.text: Participants at an International Maritime Organization (IMO) forum have called for greater cooperation to address gaps in spill-response preparedness as shipping expands its use of alternative bunker fuels. The IMO’s two-day research and development forum, held in Singapore on 21–22 September, examined how the different properties of LNG, LPG, methanol, ammonia, hydrogen and biofuels could affect marine pollution incidents and emergency response operations. Participants stressed that spill-response measures need to keep up with the shift to alternative bunker fuels, and that procedures should be in place for each fuel before major incidents occur. The participants also examined how the behaviour of each fuel in a spill could change the way responders handle an incident. They called for closer cooperation between governments, industry and researchers to ensure that ongoing research and operational experience inform future spill-response protocols. The forum was hosted by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA), with support from China. Source: By Konica Bhatt, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/asi.text: Rates for shipping containers from east Asia and China to the US rose this week on resilient demand and persistent, weather-driven congestion at Asian ports, while rates for liquid chemical tankers ex-US Gulf were flat to slightly higher. CONTAINER RATES Container rates to the US West Coast are between $7,400-8,300/FEU (40-foot equivalent unit) while rates to the East Coast are between $9,600-11,500/FEU, remaining near the highs seen in mid-2022 for both trade lanes. The following image shows rates from China to the US West Coast from ocean and freight rates and analytics firm Xeneta. Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta, said the trend of rising rates from Asia to the US could be nearing an end. “For the high-flying spot rates from Far East to US East and West coasts, we may just begin to see the end of that rising trend as we get into the first half of October,” Sand said. “When comparing today’s spot rates to the level experienced on 1 July, shippers are paying on average $2,691/FEU (+31%) and $1,280/FEU (+18%) more.” Sand said shippers who are about to start tendering for 2027 contract volumes find themselves in an uneasy position. “While the contracted rates they aim for are a far cry from the currently red-hot spot market, they cannot fully dismiss the market conditions as something that will go away soon,” Sand said. “They need to assess the disruptive elements individually, set them up against their transportation needs and consider what it means to them at a company level.” Rates from supply chain advisors Drewry rose by 2% from Shanghai to Los Angeles and were flat from Shanghai to New York. Drewry said carriers continue to manage capacity with blank sailings, with 15 announced for next week after nine in the current week. Despite capacity reductions, Drewry expects rates to decrease next week ahead of the upcoming Golden Week holiday in China from 1-7 October. Rates from online shipping marketplace and platform provider Freightos rose by 4% to the West Coast and fell by 1% to the East Coast. The following chart shows rates from the Far East to the West Coast. Judah Levine, head of research at Freightos, said that despite the early start to east-west ocean peak season back in May, which pushed container rates up sharply into early July, transpacific rates remain at about peak levels. “Resilient transpacific demand – possibly helped by the lack of a tariff hike in late July, and now including a last push to get containers moved before the Golden Week holiday – alongside persistent, weather-driven, Far East port congestion and blanked sailings, are keeping container rates at year highs,” Levine said.

As China’s automobile export volumes surge and Chinese shipbuilders absorb the carrier demand, European shipping companies that had assigned work to Korea and others are also said to have recently placed large-scale orders in China. According to Clarksons Research, a British shipbuilding and shipping market analysis firm, 58 new PCTCs were ordered worldwide from the start of the year through last month. China won orders for 56 of them. In 2023 and 2024, PCTC orders were 83 and 73 ships, respectively, but amid concerns about oversupply last year, orders plunged to nine. However, this year, as China’s automobile exports increased, projections grew that there were not enough ships to transport them, expanding PCTC demand again. According to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM), in the first half of this year China exported 5,096,000 vehicles, up 65.3% from the same period a year earlier. In June alone, auto exports reached 1,037,000, surpassing 1 million for the first time. While China’s automobile export volumes have surged, PCTC supply is short, and demand for secondhand vessels has also increased sharply. In July, a 26-year-old 4,310 CEU-class PCTC in China sold for about $42 million, three times the minimum bid price of about $14 million. One CEU is space for one car, and the ship was a mid-sized PCTC capable of carrying about 4,300 passenger cars. China’s auto industry has remarked on a shortage of carriers. According to Reuters and other foreign media, executives at Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD said on this month’s first-half earnings conference call that “overseas exports were hampered by transport constraints this year,” adding, “if transport had been smooth, exports would have been higher.”

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/how.text: Ethanol is beginning to gain momentum as a viable option for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in shipping. A growing number of projects and technical developments are helping to move the fuel from regional discussions to global considerations. For years, ethanol sat on the periphery of the maritime fuel debate. Whilst the orderbook shows that LNG and, more recently, methanol have seen growing uptake in the global fleet, ethanol has remained largely confined to regional discussions despite being the world’s most widely produced liquid biofuel. Why interest is growing in ethanol as marine fuel Part of ethanol’s appeal is its maturity outside shipping. Decades of use in road transport have created extensive production capacity, established supply chains, and well-developed fuel logistics. At the same time, increasing focus on lifecycle emissions and regulations such as FuelEU Maritime are directing attention towards fuels capable of delivering meaningful well-to-wake greenhouse gas reductions. However, production scale and emissions performance alone do not explain the growing interest. Ethanol is entering the maritime conversation at a time when the industry is searching for practical pathways that can support decarbonization without locking companies into a single long-term fuel choice. Why cargo owners are investing in ethanol-powered ships Among those exploring ethanol’s potential is VALE, a mining company and cargo owner which sees the fuel as part of its broader decarbonization strategy. That commitment is already translating into projects. VALE has partnered with Shandong Shipping to build at least two Guaibamax vessels equipped with rotor sails and powered by ethanol, with delivery expected in 2029, and is evaluating the conversion of methanol-fuelled vessels into tri-fuel ships capable of operating on methanol, ethanol, and conventional fuel.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/new.text: More than 90 per cent of the estimated oil pollution in the oceans occurs within national waters – including in protected areas. Oil slicks cover an estimated 1.58 million square kilometres of the world’s oceans each year, according to a new satellite analysis that exposes the scale of pollution at sea. That amounts to an area about three times the size of Spain. Yet, unlike headline-grabbing spills such as the Deepwater Horizon crisis, much of the pollution appears as smaller oil slicks that draw little public attention. The analysis by conservation technology nonprofit SkyTruth found that ships were linked to around 81 per cent of the oil slicks whose likely source could be identified. Oil tankers and cargo ships were the most common culprits, while offshore oil and gas infrastructure accounted for another 18 per cent of them. “Oil pollution is a constant, global issue that happens far more often than the spills that make headlines,” says Karl Wuster, chief technology officer at SkyTruth. Where is ocean oil pollution the worst? Released on 23 September during Climate Week NYC, the analysis used satellite observations collected between 2023 and 2025 and data from SkyTruth’s Cerulean oil pollution monitoring system.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Published Sep 27, 2026 11:00 PM by Shad Blidberg Hallam, Wolfgang Lehmacher and Mikael Lind Consider a vessel arriving late at a port. Its revised arrival time is useful to the cargo owner only if the terminal, inland carrier and receiver can act on it. Who may share that information, who must respond, and who settles a disagreement about what happened? These are the questions behind what we call corridor sovereignty: the capacity to coordinate trade across borders without surrendering control over how sensitive information is used. We argue for federation: participants remain independent and retain control of their data, while agreeing what they need to achieve together, how information is exchanged and how decisions are coordinated. The test is not who owns the platform, but whether the arrangements work for the parties at both ends. A trade corridor crosses borders. Within it, cargo owners and their transport partners use recurring lanes whose performance depends on contributions from multiple independent actors. A lane connects nodes and infrastructure shared by many shipments, while each shipment has its own end-to-end itinerary, including the first and last mile. Follow one such shipment. It starts at an origin specific to one cargo owner and ends at its particular destination, but along the way it may pass through nodes, transport services and infrastructure shared with shipments from many other cargo owners. It may travel by road, rail, air or sea, and pass through intermediate nodes and jurisdictions before reaching its receiver. Components moving from a supplier in Asia to a receiver in northern Europe may be collected by road, loaded at an origin port onto a vessel carrying cargo for many other owners, transferred at an intermediate node, then moved inland by rail and delivered by truck: three jurisdictions, seven or more independent organizations, one end-to-end movement. The shipment is end-to-end; much of the infrastructure and many of the services it relies on are shared. Figure 1. End-to-end shipments from multiple cargo owners co-utilize recurring lanes, shared nodes and infrastructure across jurisdictions.

The Marines sustained smoke inhalation injuries, along with possible traumatic brain injury symptoms (concussion and headaches). All eight have since returned to duty, the officials said. According to the Pentagon's internal database, more than 800 American servicemembers have been injured during the conflict with Iran over the course of the year to date. The strike occurred on the 14th, the officials told NBC. They declined to identify the name or the type of the vessel, except that it was not a U.S. Navy ship. Private maritime security sources have previously identified a Western-operated vessel that was hit in the same region on the same day. U.S. forces are engaged in a concerted effort to maintain the flow of commercial marine traffic through the southern end of the Strait of Hormuz, and have achieved a high degree of success in moving supertankers through the waterway. At this point, more than 10 million barrels per day of crude are moving through the Strait, a meaningful degree of recovery after months of low traffic. U.S. Central Command has declined to comment in detail on its methods, but they do not appear to involve direct U.S. Navy convoy escorts. In addition to attacks on American assets in the region, Iran has also proven intent on capturing U.S. Navy drones in the vicinity of Hormuz. The latest claim, released Sunday, appeared to show the seizure of a Remus 600 drone, a standard U.S. Navy intelligence-gathering drone. Iran previously seized an Anduril Dive-LD, a larger and more capable unmanned submersible. U.S. Central Command said at the time that it was disabled and adrift, and claimed that was an outdated model.
