https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The growth of the cruise industry in the post-COVID-19 pandemic era has created increased awareness of maintaining a healthy environment for travelers. The trade group Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) predicts that close to 40 million people will take a cruise in 2027. Keeping those folks safe from environmental health issues while onboard has emerged as a major business opportunity for SGS Marine Services. SGS (General Society of Surveillance), founded in 1878 by Henri Goldstuck, is a global company based in Geneva, Switzerland. It offers a multitude of testing, inspection, and certification services for industries such as agriculture, forestry, building infrastructure, consumer products and retail, cosmetics, cybersecurity, and technology. Marine services for the rapidly growing cruise industry are one of its newest additions. Robert Goldring, SGS’s Manager of Global Sales, said he started the company’s move into the cruise sector in 2000 when more industry regulations started coming into effect. SGS now works with approximately 85 percent of the world’s cruise lines. “It is a huge program,” said Goldring. “It started with one cruise line, Norwegian Cruise Line, in 2000. They had an inkling that regulations were coming, and they did, so we started with one company, and I brought it into the SGS world, and we call it SGS Marine Services. “The things we focus on are regulations from the general vessel permit, which is a set of regulations that came from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) specifically for large ships to control their discharges, and that includes ballast water testing and water treatment plants on board the ship. We also do public health testing such as Legionella testing. Actually, Legionnaires' disease (a serious lung infection) propelled it (testing), and a lot of the cruise lines are doing it now.” Goldring said SGS has expanded its program for Legionella testing “because we now have our labs on a global scale. They are certified by the CDC (Centers for Disease Control),” for an elite testing program.

After 20 years and being a pioneer in Asia and the Chinese cruise market, Costa Cruises has operated its final Asian cruise as it prepares to reposition its last ship in Asia back to the western markets. For her finale, Costa Serena is operating an unusual charter as the first cruise ship used to accommodate athletes at the Asian Games. The charter, which had been planned by the organizers of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Organizing Committee as far back as 2024, however, drew attention during the final rush to the games. Organizers had anticipated around 11,000 participants, but in the final rush, it turned out that more than 17,000 were registered, raising concerns about whether they would have sufficient housing. The cruise ship is housing about 4,000 athletes and officials from up to 43 nations. She is moored at the Kinjo Pier at the Port of Nagoya, operating as a floating hotel and residential facility. Media reports indicate that the charter deal worth approximately $30 million was negotiated by JTB’s Nagoya Business Division and was signed in September last year. She will remain in Nagoya until October 6. Costa highlights that it made special preparations for the event. The fitness areas were expanded and re-equipped, and the pools, thermal areas, and quiet zones were repurposed as recovery spaces. The onboard medical center is coordinating with the games’ medical services. Operations aboard were also adjusted, such as the dining hours, and menus were adapted to meet the athletes’ needs. Costa Serena was built in 2007 by Fincantieri as one of five ships in the class that included the ill-fated Costa Concordia . The 114,000 gross ton cruise ship, which is 289.5 meters (950 feet) in length, is now the oldest member of the Costa fleet. Her role as a floating accommodation facility continues through the end of the games, with the ship scheduled to leave Tokyo on October 18 for a 65-night voyage to Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is the end of Costa’s Asian deployments, which included becoming, in 2006, the first international cruise line to homeport a cruise ship, Costa Allegra (28,430 gross tons), in mainland China.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: A small line that started focused on the UK market, Ambassador Cruise Line is growing as a niche operation beyond the big lines that dominate the industry. It emerged last week that Ambassador is the previously unnamed buyer of Oceania Cruises’ Sirena , and it will be used to develop the German market following Ambassador’s expansion into France. Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings had reported earlier the sale of the 30,000 gross ton cruise ship Sirena as part of a broader fleet modernization program and upgrades to Oceania Cruises. Built in 1999 as part of the ships for the now-defunct company Renaissance Cruises, Oceania was launched with two ships from the class and ultimately acquired four, with Sirena being the last to join the line in 2016. Sirena will continue to sail with Oceania through the spring of 2028 to complete previously published cruises. In the earlier days of the passenger shipping and cruise industry, there was a group of companies that survived on secondhand vessels. The competition from the major lines and financial pressures, however, put many of these lines out of business. Indeed, Ambassador Cruise Line was started in 2021 as a successor to another firm, Cruise & Maritime Voyages (CMV), that had been following the strategy of smaller, second-hand cruise ships, but collapsed financially during the COVID-19 pandemic. “When we launched Ambassador in 2021, we identified a clear gap in the market for an affordable quality cruise experience that was authentic, welcoming and accessible,” says CEO Christian Verhounig. “We set out to combine the traditions of classic cruising with the standards and expectations of today’s guests, and that philosophy remains fundamental to our success.” Ambassador took some time to develop its niche in the UK, but today it highlights its operation as offering affordable, no-fly cruises. The line recently shifted to adult-only and says it is focused on the “silver market” (i.e. 50-plus). It launched with one ship, a 70,000 gross ton vessel built in 1991 by Fincantieri for Princess Cruises, and, after several different operators had been in Australia for P&O before the COVID-19 pandemic. Today known as Ambience , she accommodates about 1,400 passengers and operates from London’s Tilbury Port. Ambassador added a second ship, a 1999-built vessel that started sailing for the line in 2023 as Ambition . It is 48,000 gross tons with accommodations for up to 1,200 passengers and sails from seven different UK ports.

As buscas contaram com equipes oficiais e voluntários. Voluntários a cavalo iniciaram buscas na segunda-feira (21). https://g1.globo.com/fantastico/noticia/.text: Acidente com Rick: perícia usa drone especial e scanner 3D para mapear local da queda Equipes do Fantástico refizeram o trajeto do resgate até o ponto do acidente que matou o cantor Rick e outras quatro pessoas. Imagens exclusivas revelam a busca por indícios que ajudem a desvendar os últimos momentos do voo. Cada peça espalhada pela mata pode ajudar a esclarecer uma pergunta ainda sem resposta: como um voo de menos de uma hora terminou com a morte de cinco pessoas na Serra Catarinense? Novas imagens mostram os destroços retorcidos da aeronave na mata fechada. Com o auxílio de drones e de um scanner tridimensional, a Polícia Científica reconstrói a cena da colisão do Bell 430, prefixo PP-MGR. É como se os peritos pudessem voltar virtualmente ao local da tragédia, com os vestígios preservados. "Nós vamos conseguir testar e simular, por exemplo, como se deu a entrada da aeronave na área de mata fechada. Com as medidas da aeronave, diâmetro de rotor, comprimento de fuselagem a gente consegue fazer uma análise muito detalhada e chegar a conclusões importantes", explicou o perito criminal Fernando Henrique Ponzetti. As imagens revelam a violência do impacto. Dos mais de quinze metros de comprimento do helicóptero, sobraram pouco mais de três. Cada fragmento agora pode ajudar a reconstruir os últimos momentos do voo.

https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/n.text: O IBGE informou que a inflação oficial do país registrou queda de 0,32% nos preços no mês de agosto. Já a pesquisa Quaest mais recente mostra que 2 em cada 3 eleitores afirmam que os preços no mercado subiram ao longo deste mesmo mês. Números como estes mostram parte das contradições da economia brasileira. Por um lado: o país vem crescendo ano a ano em ritmo mais forte do que apontam os analistas de mercado; a renda do trabalhador chegou a nível recorde e o desemprego está na mínima histórica; e a inflação está dentro do teto da meta. Por outro: a dívida pública rompeu o patamar dos R$ 10 trilhões e custa mais de 82% do PIB; o endividamento aflige 82% das famílias brasileiras, índice recorde; e o país ostenta hoje o maior juro real do mundo. Neste episódio, Natuza Nery recebe o jornalista Léo Arcoverde para explicar os principais aspectos da economia brasileira. Ele também apresenta o que os candidatos à Presidência propõem para enfrentar a dívida pública, os juros altos e o endividamento privado. Também neste episódio você ouvirá trechos das entrevistas que o produtor Carlos Catelan conduziu com os economistas Armínio Fraga, André Roncaglia, Carla Beni, Felipe Salto, Marcos Mendes e Monica de Bolle.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543295-ac.text: ACUA Ocean and Forssea Robotics have completed trials combining an uncrewed surface vessel (USV) with a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) for fully remote subsea inspection and light intervention operations off Plymouth in the UK. The three-week campaign paired Forssea's 170-kg ARGOS ROV with ACUA's USV Pioneer, completing more than 40 deployments with launches, dives and recoveries commanded remotely from shore. The integration, carried out under a contract with the European Space Agency, included operations in two-meter waves south of the Plymouth breakwater, with no impact on the ROV, according to the companies. Over six days at sea, the partners completed as many as eight launch-and-recovery cycles in a single day. The ROV reached and inspected the seabed in more than 20 meters of water and operated with up to 35 meters of tether deployed. Testing included an inspection of the Poulmic wreck, a seabed feature and a concrete target block in Cawsand Bay. Operations were also conducted in one-meter waves with winds averaging 18 knots and gusting between 20 and 30 knots. Sonardyne's Mini-Ranger 2 USBL system installed on Pioneer tracked a WSM6+ transponder on ARGOS, while manual and dynamic-positioning station keeping were used to hold the ROV on task.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543287-sh.text: Shearwater Geoservices has been awarded a three-year ocean bottom node (OBN) seismic acquisition contract by an undisclosed oil and gas company for work offshore South America, with operations set to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026. The contract includes firm scopes in the first and third years of the award period, as well as a framework for potential additional projects during the three-year term. Shearwater will deploy the SW Tasman using its internally developed Pearl node technology, while the SW Gallien will carry out source operations. Both vessels are expected to work on the campaign through 2027 following the fourth-quarter start. A subsequent firm scope is expected to begin in late 2028 and continue for about 10 months. “This award marks a milestone for Shearwater’s OBN platform consisting of our internally developed Pearl technology and our one-of-a-kind Tasman vessel design. We are proud to have secured this position in South America and look forward to continuing our contribution into the successful development of one of the world’s most important offshore basins” said Irene Waage Basili, Shearwater’s CEO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543294-da.text: Dajin Heavy Industry has selected Ulstein's ULSTEIN HX122 design for an offshore installation vessel capable of installing future 4XL monopiles, expanding the offshore wind foundation supplier's activities into offshore installation. The vessel, designed by Ulstein Design & Solutions in the Netherlands, is intended to install monopiles, jacket foundations and offshore substations. It will also be capable of supporting oil and gas construction and decommissioning work. The project will expand Dajin's capabilities beyond manufacturing, logistics and transportation, allowing it to add installation to its offshore wind offering. The ULSTEIN HX122 will feature a large working deck, lifting capabilities and dynamic positioning, as well as Ulstein's U-STERN and X-BOW hull solutions. The U-STERN configuration enables monopiles to be stored longitudinally and upended along the vessel's centerline at the stern, allowing installation with the vessel heading into prevailing seas. Combined with the X-BOW, the design is intended to improve vessel motions and increase the available weather window for offshore installation work. "Offshore wind has entered a new development phase, and installation capacity is the core bottleneck for project delivery. The ULSTEIN HX122 with U-STERN® project represents Dajin’s strategic layout to close the final link in offshore wind foundation delivery.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543291-me.text: Mermaid Maritime has established a joint venture with Nigerian oilfield services company Marine Platforms Limited to pursue subsea work for TotalEnergies Nigeria and other oil and gas operators in the country. The new company, Mermaid Subsea Services Limited, will be 49% owned by Mermaid Subsea Oil and Gas Services, a wholly owned subsidiary of Mermaid Maritime, while Marine Platforms will hold 51%. The venture is intended to allow direct operational engagement with TotalEnergies Nigeria and other oil and gas companies while meeting Nigerian local content, regulatory and contracting requirements. Marine Platforms, established in 2001, provides subsea engineering, procurement, installation and construction services and solutions, as well as ROV support, well services and vessel chartering. Mermaid Subsea Services has issued and paid-up capital of 100 million naira, equivalent to about $72,000. Mermaid Maritime will fund its investment from internal resources. The company said the transaction was not expected to have a material impact on its net tangible assets or earnings per share for the current financial year.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543290-qa.text: More QatarEnergy-linked liquefied natural gas vessels, laden and in ballast, have transited the Strait of Hormuz in the last week despite the US-Iran conflict. In August, Kpler data showed no visible transits by Qatar-linked LNG vessels or vessels carrying cargoes from the Ras Laffan gas terminal, amid fears of attack by Iran, which has tried to throttle traffic through the Strait. Some may have got through undetected if they kept their transponders off, but this month, visible transits of LNG tankers have begun to pick up. The latest LNG vessel to reappear outside the strait is the GasLog Skagen, which showed up off Sri Lanka on September 27 with a cargo from Ras Laffan, LSEG and Kpler data showed. The vessel, managed by Greece's GasLog LNG Services, had been inside the Gulf from the start of the war, ferrying cargoes from Qatar to the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, until it was last seen there on September 20. Another LNG vessel carrying a Qatar-origin cargo, Al Shamal, was last seen inside the strait on September 19 and reappeared outside Hormuz around September 24-25. Managed by Seapeak Maritime, it is currently skirting southern India.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543289-fi.text: Finder Energy has secured the principal environmental approval for its Kuda Tasi and Jahal (KTJ) oil development in Timor-Leste, clearing a key regulatory hurdle as the project moves towards a final investment decision. Timor-Leste's Autoridade Nacional do Petróleo (ANP) approved the Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the KTJ project, establishing the environmental framework covering its development, construction, installation, operations and eventual decommissioning. The approval follows the previously approved Field Development Plan (FDP), putting the key regulatory foundations for the development in place, according to Finder. Finder Energy is now progressing joint venture processes, project agreements and debt financing ahead of a potential FID. “With both the FDP and EIS now approved, the key regulatory foundations for development are in place. We continue to work with our joint venture partner and other stakeholders to complete the remaining commercial and financial activities to achieve FID,” said Damon Neaves, Finder Energy’s CEO. The environmental framework also sets management and monitoring requirements throughout the project's lifecycle. The assessment was prepared by MCC Sustainable Futures in partnership with Timor-Leste advisory group Halona Serena and included consultation with regulators, government stakeholders, local communities and the public.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543292-fu.text: Fugro has completed an ultra-deepwater geohazard site survey for Petronas Carigali's Megah and Limbayong fields off Sabah, East Malaysia, using autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) technology. The offshore campaign ran from June to August 2026 and collected seabed and shallow subsurface data to identify geohazards and support engineering design and field development planning. Fugro deployed its Echo Surveyor 8 AUV from the Fugro Equator, with the AUV operating close to the seabed to acquire high-resolution bathymetric, geophysical and shallow subsurface data. The project marked the application of AUV technology for Petronas Carigali's ultra-deepwater geohazard site survey supporting development activities. Fugro's Kuala Lumpur Remote Operations Centre supported the campaign with continuous data quality control and processing. “Our collaboration with Petronas Carigali allows us to push the boundaries of how offshore projects are delivered. By integrating advanced technologies with real-time remote operations, we are enabling faster insights and more efficient execution. This project highlights Fugro’s continued innovation and our ability to deliver high-impact solutions through our strong footprint in Asia Pacific,” said Safri Drahman, Fugro's Regional Business Line Director, Marine Site Characterization APAC.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543286-tu.text: Noble Corporation has secured a contract by Tullow Oil for the Noble Faye Kozack drillship for a drilling campaign offshore Ghana. The work will include up to 10 wells off Ghana, with the campaign expected to start in mid-2027. “This award reflects the strong working relationship between Tullow and Noble and the performance our crews continue to deliver offshore Ghana. The Noble Faye Kozack is well positioned to support this campaign, and we look forward to getting started,” Noble Senior Vice President of Marketing & Contracts Blake Denton said. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543285-to.text: TotalEnergies, SOCAR and XRG have taken a final investment decision (FID) on the full-field development of Azerbaijan's Absheron gas and condensate field, targeting an increase in gas production to 6 billion cubic meters per year from 2029. TotalEnergies operates the Caspian Sea development with a 35% interest, alongside SOCAR with 35% and XRG with 30%. The full-field development will also increase condensate production to 47,000 barrels per day. Gas will supply Azerbaijan's domestic market and be exported to Turkey through existing infrastructure connecting the country to the European gas market. Absheron, located about 100 km southeast of Baku, holds approximately 140 billion cubic meters of recoverable gas reserves. The project's first development phase started production in 2023 and has capacity to produce 1.5 billion cubic meters of gas annually and 12,000 barrels per day of condensate.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543284-bi.text: The world's biggest energy companies are poised to deliver another quarter of bumper profits, fuelled by record refining margins. Flush with cash, Big Oil now needs to chart a course for future growth in a world reshaped by the Middle East crisis. Big Oil has seen its cash coffers balloon this year. The five largest Western oil companies — BP, Chevron, Exxon Mobil, Shell and TotalEnergies - are expected to report combined third-quarter profits of around $53 billion, according to RBC Capital Markets estimates, up from $48 billion in the second quarter and more than double year-earlier levels. Yet since the start of the Iran war in late February, oil majors have largely reacted cautiously to this windfall, directing billions toward debt reduction rather than major new investments. Combined debt is set to drop to $150 billion in the third quarter from $200 billion in the first quarter, according to LSEG estimates. That approach made sense in the early months of the conflict, when energy markets were swinging wildly on every headline and investors largely accepted US President Donald Trump's prediction that the war would be short-lived. What began as a confrontation between the US, Israel and Iran has evolved into a protracted, low-intensity regional conflict characterized by attacks on energy infrastructure, refineries and shipping lanes. Many of the consequences for global energy markets – including a higher geopolitical risk premium, altered supply lines and greater energy nationalism – are likely to linger long after the fighting ends. That changes the calculus for an industry that makes multibillion-dollar investment decisions with time horizons measured in decades.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A integração de RFID, inteligência artificial e ferramentas de gestão em tempo real em um hub tecnológico próprio elevou em 80% a produtividade da operação de armazenagem e distribuição do Grupo Asia Shipping . Desenvolvida pela Hórus Logística , adquirida pelo grupo em 2024, a plataforma acompanha o fluxo desde o lançamento do pedido até a expedição e permite aos clientes consultar estoques, movimentações e indicadores operacionais em tempo real. Um dos resultados registrados foi a redução do tempo de conferência de cargas, que passou de cerca de duas horas para cinco a dez minutos com o uso de RFID. O inventário, que podia levar de sete a 14 dias, também passou a ser realizado em aproximadamente 30 minutos, dependendo do tamanho e das características da operação. O hub reúne informações como plano de embarque, ordens de montagem, listas de separação, dimensionais de produtos, histórico de estoque, acompanhamento de pedidos, consolidação de pallets e gestão da entrada e saída de veículos. A plataforma também concentra dados financeiros e operacionais e está integrada ao WMS utilizado nos armazéns. “Investir em tecnologia própria permite crescer sem perder controle, previsibilidade ou capacidade de resposta. À medida que aumentamos o número de clientes e a complexidade das operações, precisamos garantir que cada nova demanda possa ser absorvida com o mesmo nível de serviço”, afirma Alexandre Pimenta, CEO da Asia Shipping. Segundo o executivo, o hub dá suporte à expansão e à integração entre armazenagem, distribuição e demais etapas conduzidas pelo grupo. A solução também incorporou um assistente de inteligência artificial capaz de responder, por texto ou comando de voz, a consultas sobre o andamento da operação. Entre as informações disponíveis estão o número de pedidos separados no dia, a quantidade de veículos nas docas e o cumprimento de metas operacionais. A tecnologia está presente nas unidades de armazenagem e distribuição do grupo e foi desenvolvida para ser replicada em futuros centros sem a necessidade de criação de um novo sistema. Segundo a companhia, a integração das ferramentas permite que uma pessoa realize, no mesmo intervalo de tempo, atividades que anteriormente demandavam até quatro profissionais.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/energy_grou.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone recently, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers (AFPM) announced that more than 30 U.S. business, energy, and manufacturing groups from around the country have issued a letter to U.S. President Donald Trump “urging him to reject calls to ban or limit the export of diesel and other fuels from the United States”. The letter - which accompanied the statement and was signed by groups including the AFPM, the American Exploration & Production Council (AEPC), the American Petroleum Institute (API), the Independent Petroleum Association of America (IPAA), the Texas Oil & Gas Association (TXOGA), the International Liquid Terminals Association (LTA), and the Liquid Energy Pipeline Association (LEPA) - thanked Trump for his “continuing commitment to an unsurpassed U.S. energy industry” but urged him “to reject calls to ban or otherwise limit the exports of diesel and other products that have made the U.S. energy industry so strong”. “Export bans would lead to less fuel production, tighter supplies, and rising costs for American families, farmers, and truckers,” the letter warned. “With 10 percent of global refining capacity offline, U.S. refiners are running at full capacity to supply the U.S. and to help stabilize global fuel markets,” it added. “The U.S. produces more diesel than it consumes, allowing us to meet domestic demand and to supply our allies in Latin America and Europe. U.S. crude oil exports have likewise helped keep refineries running in other parts of the world as disruptions occurred through the Strait of Hormuz,” it continued. “Exports allow U.S. refineries to balance their systems and maximize production. An export ban would require refineries to throttle utilization to reduce diesel production to equal domestic demand,” it noted.

https://safety4sea.com/new-zealand-joins.text: A Royal New Zealand Navy task group has joined international efforts to enforce United Nations sanctions on North Korea, conducting maritime patrols in international waters in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea to monitor vessels suspected of sanctions evasion. N ew Zealand is a member of the Pacific Security Maritime Exchange, a multinational partnership focused on identifying and reporting activities intended to circumvent UN Security Council measures targeting North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. The task group is deployed to the Indo-Pacific for three months, carrying out a range of maritime operations, exercises and regional engagements. The deployment marks the first time the frigate Te Mana has taken part in UN sanctions monitoring operations. The patrols involve monitoring vessels suspected of transporting refined petroleum to North Korea or exporting commodities including coal, iron ore and sand, which can provide revenue linked to the country’s weapons programmes. During the operation, the Royal New Zealand Navy’s tanker Aotearoa also operated in the area, conducting six at-sea replenishments for Te Mana and vessels from partner nations. Over the course of the deployment, Te Mana covered approximately 180,000 square nautical miles, monitored seven vessels of interest and broadcast 60 maritime radio messages as part of efforts to deter and identify potential sanctions-evasion activity.

https://safety4sea.com/black-sea-ais-ano.text: Worldwide AIS Network has reported a series of anomalous AIS position reports that it says indicate GNSS interference affecting ships in the Black Sea and Gulf region. A ccording to the company, four vessels off the Bulgarian coast recently transmitted 27 AIS positions showing the ships located within a single 1 km area in central Lima, Peru, approximately 12,129 km from their actual location. Worldwide AIS Network said the incident was detected directly at its terrestrial AIS receivers, rather than through an aggregated maritime data feed. The company argued that this distinction can help identify GNSS interference in near real time, before anomalous data are filtered or treated as erroneous positions by data platforms. The company also reported significant positioning anomalies in the Gulf between 2 and 9 September. During this period, it recorded 1,702 “impossible position jumps” involving 379 vessels. In addition, at midnight UTC on 9 September, nearly one-third of all position reports received by the network indicated that the vessels’ own positioning systems were flagged as inoperative. Worldwide AIS Network said such data are often treated as “noise” and removed during the cleaning and aggregation of maritime datasets. However, it considers these anomalies potentially useful indicators of GNSS disruption.

https://safety4sea.com/msc-hermes-iii-re.text: The container ship MSC Hermes III, which was abandoned by its crew in the South China Sea on 22 September, appears to be under tow towards Vietnam, according to AIS tracking data. T he vessel issued a distress call at around 08:45 Singapore time on September 22, which was subsequently relayed by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). The ship’s 25 crew members abandoned the vessel and boarded a lifeboat after the incident. As reported, they were later rescued by the MSC Ruby, which responded to the distress call. Two other MSC vessels, MSC Florentina and MSC Turin III, also diverted towards the area. At the time, MSC Hermes III was reported to be drifting around 300 km east of Vietnam. The circumstances that prompted the crew to abandon the vessel have not been disclosed. AIS data from Pole Star Global now indicates that the container ship may be under tow by the anchor-handling tug TC Mercury and tug Boka Guard, both of which departed from Vietnam and are reporting Vung Tau as their destination. The vessel had been sailing from Hong Kong to Jakarta when the incident occurred. The condition of MSC Hermes III, as well as the nature of the incident that led to its abandonment, remains unclear.

https://safety4sea.com/sanctions-pressur.text: Unmarked oil or gas tanker, concept of Shadow Fleet / Image Credit: Shutterstock Russia’s ship registry expanded by 36% between January 2025 and June 2026, as growing international pressure on vessels linked to sanctions appears to have encouraged part of the so-called shadow fleet to move under the Russian flag. A ccording to a new analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), 107 vessels were added to Russia’s registry during the period, with the increase reaching a peak in December 2025, when 25 vessels were registered in a single month. The growth comes as governments and maritime authorities tighten scrutiny of open registries and vessels suspected of being used to circumvent sanctions. Some registries have removed sanctioned tonnage altogether, while others have significantly reduced the number of such vessels they carry. Barbados and Palau, for example, have cleared their registries of sanctioned vessels, while Panama has cut its number by almost two-thirds from a peak recorded in May 2025. Meanwhile, the world’s largest ship registries have established the Registry Information Sharing Compact (RISC), aimed at improving information sharing and addressing practices such as flag hopping and sanctions evasion.

https://safety4sea.com/hydrogen-powered-.text: The transition to zero-emission short-sea shipping is entering a new phase as the EU-funded HyShip project prepares to use two hydrogen-powered container vessels as real-world demonstrators on a planned green shipping corridor between Oslo and Rotterdam. T wo hydrogen-powered container ships built by Samskip are set to move from concept to commercial operation as part of a European project testing whether liquid hydrogen can provide a practical zero-emission solution for short-sea shipping. The vessels will form part of a planned green shipping corridor between Oslo and Rotterdam, where the project will put both the ships and the infrastructure needed to fuel them through real-world operations. Supported by the Clean Hydrogen Partnership, the project is focused on testing the full liquid hydrogen supply chain for commercial shipping, linking fuel storage and port bunkering infrastructure with vessel operations. The first vessel is expected to enter service in the second quarter of 2027, with both ships designed for commercial freight operations rather than as research prototypes. The project aims to gather more than 3,000 hours of operational data during an 18-month commercial demonstration. As stated, the data will cover vessel performance, port manoeuvring and hydrogen bunkering, providing practical experience that could inform future ship designs, regulatory requirements and investment decisions.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-ets-skuld-warn.text: The UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) was extended to domestic maritime activity on 1 July 2026, creating new contractual and cost considerations for charterers and traders, according to Skuld. I n his analysis, Ivan Serracin, Vice President, Claims, Lawyer, Skuld, said charterers should keep the UK ETS separate from the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime when planning fixtures and drafting contracts, as the regimes have different scopes, compliance mechanisms and settlement requirements. While charterers will not normally be directly responsible to UK regulators, the commercial costs of compliance may be passed down through the charter chain. The UK ETS initially applies to ships of 5,000 GT and above operating on voyages between UK ports, including return voyages, as well as relevant UK port activity. Skuld noted that a UK-foreign voyage is not covered in its entirety, with the scheme instead applying to the relevant UK port emissions. Domestic UK voyages and UK port emissions are subject to a 100% surrender obligation, while UK-Northern Ireland voyages are fully monitored and reported but receive a 50% surrender deduction. The scheme covers CO2, methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) on a tank-to-wake basis. Treatment of anchorage emissions depends on their location and the applicable port boundary, meaning charterers should not assume that all anchorage periods will be treated in the same way. The regulated person is normally the maritime operator, generally the registered owner. Where the registered owner does not perform the duties of the ISM company, the UK ETS responsibilities can be delegated to the ISM company through a legally binding arrangement.

https://safety4sea.com/vesselbot-eu-ets-.text: The EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) generated an estimated €572.4 million in allowance exposure across more than 20,000 EU/EEA-linked containership voyages during Q2 2026, according to a VesselBot case study. T he analysis found that the underlying carbon cost of transporting a container can vary significantly depending on the voyage and routing, while carriers’ standardized per-TEU surcharges do not necessarily reflect the EU ETS exposure generated by each shipment. During Q2 2026, more than 20,000 containership voyages departing from or arriving at EU/EEA ports generated over 11.8 million tonnes of CO₂e. Of this, 7.15 million tonnes, or 60%, were estimated to fall within the EU ETS allowance-surrender requirement. Using an EU Allowance (EUA) price of approximately €80 per tonne at the end of the quarter, VesselBot estimated the associated carbon cost at €572.4 million. On a fleet-wide basis, the exposure equated to approximately €13.4 per TEU. However, VesselBot noted that this is a directional benchmark rather than a shipment-level figure, because voyage-level TEU data can count the same container multiple times as it moves through different legs of a carrier’s network. Under the EU ETS, shipping companies must surrender allowances for 100% of emissions on voyages between EU/EEA ports and 50% of emissions on voyages between EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA ports.

https://safety4sea.com/fuel-oil-pumping-.text: Russian authorities have confirmed the completion of fuel oil pumping from the sunken sections of the tankers Volgoneft-212 and Volgoneft-239 in the Kerch Strait, almost two years after the vessels were severely damaged during a storm and triggered a major fuel oil spill in the Black Sea. T he completion of the operation was confirmed on September 25 by a specially established commission comprising representatives of Russia’s environmental regulator Rosprirodnadzor, the Ministry of Emergency Situations and the Marine Rescue Service, following a meeting of the government commission chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Savelyev. The authorities said the remaining wreck sections will subsequently be recovered by the relevant services and agencies as part of their ongoing work. According to reports citing the Russian government, the affected waters and coastline in Krasnodar Territory, Crimea and Sevastopol have also been cleaned. More than 185,000 tons of contaminated sand and soil have reportedly been disposed of or put into economic use. Clean sand has also been placed on affected beaches in Anapa, while 115 beaches received permits from Rospotrebnadzor for the 2026 season. Savelyev said the response had eliminated the environmental consequences and risks associated with the casualty, while highlighting the contribution of rescue services, federal and regional authorities, scientific organizations and volunteers. The latest confirmation follows an earlier announcement on August 21 that fuel oil pumping from the submerged tanker sections had been completed. However, subsequent satellite monitoring raised questions about whether petroleum products were still escaping from the wreck sites. On August 26, satellite imagery reportedly showed oil films around the submerged stern of Volgoneft-212 and bow of Volgoneft-239. The Sky Eye monitoring project said the images indicated that completion of the pumping operation did not necessarily mean that oil-product leakage had stopped.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/qatarlin.text: More QatarEnergy-linked liquefied natural gas vessels, laden and in ballast, have transited the Strait of Hormuz in the last week despite the US-Iran conflict. In August, Kpler data showed no visible transits by Qatar-linked LNG vessels or vessels carrying cargoes from the Ras Laffan gas terminal, amid fears of attack by Iran, which has tried to throttle traffic through the Strait. Some may have got through undetected if they kept their transponders off, but this month, visible transits of LNG tankers have begun to pick up. The latest LNG vessel to reappear outside the strait is the GasLog Skagen, which showed up off Sri Lanka on September 27 with a cargo from Ras Laffan, LSEG and Kpler data showed. The vessel, managed by Greece's GasLog LNG Services, had been inside the Gulf from the start of the war, ferrying cargoes from Qatar to the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, until it was last seen there on September 20. Another LNG vessel carrying a Qatar-origin cargo, Al Shamal, was last seen inside the strait on September 19 and reappeared outside Hormuz around September 24-25. Managed by Seapeak Maritime, it is currently skirting southern India.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/lng.text: LNG carrier rates strengthened throughout the week, with all three Baltic LNG benchmark routes ending higher as improving chartering activity and seasonal demand expectations supported sentiment. The strongest gains were recorded on the US Gulf export routes, reflecting firmer freight demand and tightening vessel availability. BLNG1 increased from $28,050/day at the start of the week to $33,200/day by Friday, while BLNG2 rose from $24,700/day to $32,400/day. BLNG3 posted the largest gain, climbing from $51,900/day to $66,000/day over the same period. Market sentiment improved with activity most noticeable in the Atlantic Basin. Winter gas demand continues to provide support as Europe and Asia compete for LNG supplies ahead of the heating season. Strong US flows and healthy production levels from alternative export regions are also helping to maintain cargo availability and trading opportunities. Period assessments were mixed. The six-month assessment softened to $42,500/day, suggesting some caution over short-term market prospects, while the one-year and three-year assessments increased to $55,167/day and $73,000/day, respectively, reflecting continued confidence in longer-term LNG shipping fundamentals. The LPG market strengthened this week, with freight rates most notably in the US Gulf climbing as available tonnage was reported to be thinning out, bolstered by short-term charters proving lucrative in the Middle East region keeping vessels there. On the BLPG1 Ras Tanura–Chiba route, rate remained stable this week at $242, with corresponding TCE earnings rising from $231,500/day to $234,700/day. The BLPG2 Houston–Flushing route increased by $2.17 week-on-week to settle at $174.00. The corresponding TCE increased by $5,300/day to $202,700/day.

https://splash247.com/siemens-gamesa-tap.text: Spain-based wind turbine manufacturer Siemens Gamesa has taken Purus’ service operation vessel Purus Horizon on a long-term charter for offshore wind maintenance in the North Sea. Purus has not identified the wind farms involved or disclosed the charter length or value. However, it said the vessel would start work early in 2027. The agreement marks the vessel’s second long-term assignment. Formerly named Edda Passat , it was among the first generation of purpose-built offshore wind SOVs and began a five-year contract at Ørsted’s Race Bank wind farm off the UK in 2018. Purus bought and renamed the ship in 2024. Earlier this year, the company won a five-year charter for the construction service operation vessel (CSOV) Purus Power at the OranjeWind offshore wind farm in the Netherlands.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/oil.text: Oil prices rose more than 2% on Monday after Iran said it would not soften its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, after President Donald Trump rejected Tehran’s proposal, keeping uncertainty high over when traffic through the crucial oil shipping route will return to normal. As of 04:31 ET (08:31 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in November rose 2.7% to $107.08 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained 2.4% to $94.66 per barrel. Brent futures were up about 18% for the month, including Monday’s gains. Iran’s proposal would allow the Strait of Hormuz to reopen within seven days while broader negotiations resume, provided Washington lifts its naval blockade, eases military pressure, removes sanctions on Iranian oil sales and agrees to a ceasefire. Iran has said it remains committed to those conditions despite Trump’s rejection. Trump has nevertheless said he expects negotiations with Iran to resume this week, according to an Axios report. Qatar has been shuttling between the two sides in an effort to revive talks. The Strait, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies moved before the conflict began, has seen a sharp reduction in shipping activity.

https://petronoticias.com.br/aveva-apont.text: A transformação digital da indústria de óleo e gás deverá avançar para além dos sistemas internos das companhias e alcançar as relações entre os diferentes elos da cadeia. Essa é a avaliação do líder do setor de O&G da AVEVA, Joachim Boese , nosso entrevistado desta segunda-feira (28). Segundo ele, a capacidade de produtores, refinarias, fornecedores, operadores logísticos e parceiros tecnológicos compartilharem dados e indicadores será cada vez mais determinante para a resiliência e a agilidade do setor. “E u acredito que o próximo passo será o da digitalização das relações. A resiliência está deixando de ser uma capacidade exclusivamente interna para se tornar uma característica de toda a rede ”, afirmou. Boese também destacou que sistemas operacionais conectados ajudam a preparar melhor as organizações ao estabelecerem uma visão comum dos dados e do desempenho. Como exemplo, citou a ADNOC, que utiliza tecnologias da AVEVA em um centro de visualização de dados em tempo real e totalmente integrado. A estrutura permite obter insights, gerar ganhos de eficiência e identificar novas oportunidades para otimizar as operações. A indústria do petróleo enfrenta um cenário marcado interrupções nas cadeias de abastecimento que estão gerando oscilações de preços e mudanças na demanda. O que torna o momento atual particularmente desafiador? A indústria de petróleo está acostumada a lidar com cadeias globais de suprimentos complexas, mas o cenário atual acrescenta um novo grau de imprevisibilidade. Desde o início da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã, o fornecimento passou a ser afetado em duas frentes importantes: o Estreito de Ormuz e o Mar Vermelho. Ao mesmo tempo, refinarias e produtores enfrentam gargalos logísticos, custos mais elevados de transporte e sinais de enfraquecimento da demanda, porque preços de energia elevados por períodos prolongados acabam reduzindo o consumo. Isso significa que, hoje, tanto a oferta quanto a demanda podem mudar rapidamente. Uma decisão política, um ataque militar ou uma nova sanção pode alterar, em poucas horas, a disponibilidade de petróleo, as rotas marítimas e as condições comerciais. Como a tecnologia pode ajudar as empresas a tomarem decisões mais seguras em ambiente tão voláteis? Trata-se de uma questão estratégica na qual cada dado conta. Isso significa que informações de fornecedores, operadores logísticos, equipes operacionais, mercados e clientes precisam ser analisadas de forma integrada. Caso a empresa tenha uma visão operacional completa e atualizada continuamente, ela será capaz de prever, avaliar e responder com maior precisão às mudanças do mercado.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/economia/mo.text: A ANJL (Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias) rompeu o acordo com a Sportradar, plataforma que monitora manipulações de resultados esportivos, para a preveção das atividades no Brasil, segundo nota publicada neste domingo (27). A decisão ocorre após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) assinar uma MP (medida provisória) proibindo o funcionamento de bets no país, em ato realizado na sexta-feira (25) . De acordo coma ANJL, o contrato com a Sportradar foi firmado em fevereiro deste ano, em consequência de outro tratado feito com o Ministério do Esporte, em 2025 O contrato previa a manutenção de duas plataformas educacionais para agentes do esporte e autoridades que atuam no monitoramento, detecção e recebimento de denúncias. "Esta é a primeira das muitas consequências, infelizmente, da Medida Provisória do governo federal. As plataformas mantidas pela ANJL ofertavam módulos dedicados, entre outros temas, aos riscos das apostas, ao monitoramento e à detecção, às regras e regulamentos e aos canais de denúncia. Perdem o esporte, os atletas e também os apostadores, que migrarão para plataformas ilegais e ainda estarão sujeitos a resultados manipulados nas apostas”, disse Plínio Lemos Jorge, presidente da ANJL. A ANJL aponta que o fim do mercado regulamentado no país levará os usuários às plataformas ilegais, "e também seguirão existindo os casos de cooptação de atletas, em diversos esportes, mas principalmente no futebol, por esquemas de manipulação".

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The crew of the Australia-flagged boat Tai Tam (51 feet) has a whale of a tale to tell, for real. According to the New Zealand Defense Force, four sailors spent several hours in a life raft after they were forced to abandon their boat after colliding with a whale. They were sailing approximately 250 nautical miles north of Norfolk Island, a small, remote volcanic island in the South Pacific Ocean that is an external territory of Australia. It was around 1:00 pm Saturday when the four sailors activated their EPIRB as they were abandoning their boat. Maritime New Zealand’s Rescue Coordination Center received the alert and launched the rescue operation. It dispatched a Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8A plane to begin the search for the four individuals. The plane crew was able to establish two-way communication with the four sailors in the raft. At the same time, the Rescue Center alerted vessels in the area, requesting assistance. The containership Sofrana Surville (12,500 dwt) responded to the call and diverted to the area to aid in the rescue. The Malta-flagged vessel operates for ANL Singapore. “This was a well-coordinated and executed rescue,” said Rescue Coordination Centre Operations Manager Mike Clulow. “The crew of the yacht did all the right things, and it was unfortunate to have struck a whale in open water. They were well prepared and the early activation of their EPIRB was key to helping get them to safety.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The US naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports appears to be nearly 100 percent effective, cutting the flow of goods through Bandar Abbas and other Gulf and southern coast ports which used to handle 80 percent of Iran’s trade before the current conflict. Within the last week, air traffic to the outside world has also largely been cut. Some flights will still be leaving and entering, perhaps some military aircraft flying with disabled transponders, and perhaps a few to Russia and China, but in total carrying very little cargo. Road routes across the land borders from and to Iraq, Turkey, Azerbaijan and Armenia have significant capacity issues, with Al Jazeera reporting recently that at the Norduz crossing into Armenia, as many as 1,800 trucks are queuing, some trucks taking as long as 10 days to pass through the border checkpoint. Neither Turkey nor Iraq will wish to face US wrath by increasing traffic flows, and poor Azeri-Iranian diplomatic relations will be a hindrance to traffic flows. In other conflicts in the region, enterprising truck drivers have taken to delivering crude by truck when pipelines and tankers are unavailable, but that will not be happening at any scale from Iran, given the route and border restrictions. A snapshot of the Caspian Sea, September 27, with cargo vessels marked in yellow ( VesselFinder ) To get around the strictures of the US naval blockade, the Iranians have only two viable options for moving heavy cargo. One of these could be the railway connections through Turkmenistan, from Sarakhs in the northeast to China, and through Incheh Borun to Kazakhstan and Russia. Cruise missiles hit the Aq Tekeh Khan railway bridge on the latter route on July 9, although traffic on the route was quickly restored. Turkmenistan has declared itself neutral in the conflict, so it will be anxious not to be seen to be providing a back door for Iran to move heavy volumes of additional traffic. But no doubt the specialist smugglers of the IRGC’s Unit 190 will be getting high-value cargo through on this route, and this route will also be used to ship Chinese-manufactured dual-use sodium perchlorate, historically for processing into ammonium perchlorate rocket fuel at Parchin south of Tehran and Khojir. Ammonium perchlorate makes up 70 percent of the standard fuel load of most of Iran’s solid-fueled ballistic missiles, such as medium-range Khybar-Shikan and Fattah missiles, and the shorter-range Fateh-110 and Zolfaghar missiles. This then leaves the cargo routes across the Caspian Sea, principally to Russia. Before the war, the Iranian ports on the southern coast of the Caspian handled about 10 percent of Iran’s trade. The governor of the northern Iranian province of Gilan has said that from March to August this year volumes had increased by 50

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Ukraine filed papers in court at the end of last week seeking to prosecute another Russian captain on charges of transporting grain from the closed port of Sevastopol to Syria. According to the court papers, the captain, Mykola Telagin, age 54, was in command between 2022 and 2024 of a Russian-flagged bulker, Matros Pozynich, notorious for transporting grain that Ukraine asserts is being stolen from Crimea and shipped from the closed port of Sevastopol. The Security Service of Ukraine assembled the indictment after a long investigation into the actions of the captain and the bulker. They charge that the captain organized and managed the movement of the cargo while being aware of the hostilities between Russia and Ukraine. The European Union placed an embargo on the ports of Crimea after the Russian annexation of the region. The bulker Matros Pozynich (28,351 dwt) was built in 2010 and has been sailing under the Russian flag and ownership since 2022. Tracking operations have spotted the bulker in Sevastopol, Syria, Egypt, and Turkey. The charges are related to a shipment of 27,000 metric tons of wheat grown in the Donetsk region, currently occupied by Russia, to the Syrian port of Latakia in November 2022. There was a second shipment of 27,300 tons documented in January 2023. Ukraine asserts the captain managed the entry of the vessel into Sevastopol on these occasions. He also controlled the acceptance of the cargo and managed its transport. They accuse him of representing the cargo as being of Russian origin. In addition, they assert the bulker turned off its AIS transmissions, and at times also displayed “unreliable” or false route information. While the court papers only highlight these two specific instances, observers report the vessel has continued in this operation. In April of this year, it loaded 27,500 tons of wheat at the Avlita grain terminal in Crimea and proceeded to Latakia. The AIS transmission disguised the shipment as coming from Iskenderun, Turkey.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Another one of the few remaining classic passenger ships is facing an uncertain future as Funchal is currently being auctioned as part of the insolvency of her owner. Built in the days when passenger ships conducted liner service, the now 65-year-old ship retains her classic silhouette and her original name even though she was converted to cruising and has changed ownership multiple times. Shipping aficionados and members of the Portuguese community are rallying with last-minute hope to save the classic ship even though her age and condition likely mean her prospects are limited. The Madeira Judicial Court has ordered Funchal (IMO 5124162) to be sold in a sealed-bid auction as part of the liquidation of a company called Teamson, her last owners, which the media links to Brock Pierce. A child actor who appeared in Disney movies, Pierce is an American cryptocurrency entrepreneur who acquired the ship in 2021 for a reported price of approximately 1.6 million euros. The court and insolvency administrator opened the Funchal on September 18 for inspection by potential bidders. Interested parties have until September 30 to submit sealed bids. They will be opened on October 9, with the administrator highlighting that the buyer gets the ship free of debts and encumbrances but takes over the expenses immediately. Minimum bids are set at 802,354 euros ($921,000), putting Funchal in the scrap market. It is not the first time Funchal has faced the auction block in her long career. Emblematic of the long-ago Portuguese passenger fleet, people argue she deserves to be saved yet one more time. The insolvency administrator highlights that before the current owners stopped work, the interiors had been stripped and are free of asbestos and other hazardous products. They also obtained a license for her to operate as a hotel on Portugal’s Tagus River. Funchal was conceived in the late 1950s as a replacement for another ship built in 1907 that was operating carrying passengers, cargo, and mail from Portugal to Madeira, the Azores, and the Canary Islands. Funchal was ordered by the privately-owned Empresa Insulana de Navegacao, a Portuguese shipping company with a long heritage of sailing both to the islands and South America. The ship was built at the Elsinore shipyard and, despite only being 9,842 gross tons and 501 feet (155 meters) in length, was at the time the largest ship built in Denmark. She was launched in February 1961 and entered service in November of the same year with accommodations for 80 First Class and a total of 320 Tourist Class passengers.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The UK Government announced two new projects it will be undertaking that will be bid out only to the national shipbuilding industry. The Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey, said they would herald a “new age of industrialization” for the UK while contributing to national security. The government said it would back two major projects, the building of new dry docks for the Royal Navy’s submarine service and the building of a new marine research vessel to be deployed by the government. It will limit the bidding for the projects to UK-based companies only to ensure that they provide critical work for the shipbuilding industry. “Britain has a proud shipbuilding heritage, and every pound of this strategic investment in a critical sector is backing British jobs on the Clyde and businesses across the UK, supporting growth” in every part of the UK, said Healey. He pledged it would become a “new age of industrialization.” One of the projects calls for the building of three new floating docks for the submarine service. The BBC reports that the last floating dry dock built in the UK is believed to be the Admiralty Dock 60, built in the 1960s and used by the government until the late 1990s at Faslane. It was later sold for commercial use. Currently, the submarine base at Faslane, the BBC reports, has only one shiplift available for submarine maintenance. Healey called building new dry docks a program of importance for national security and one that could be used to ensure the sovereign British industry. The project, known as Programme Euston, calls for three large dry docks for HM Naval Base Clyde. They will be built in the UK and used to provide critical maintenance work for current and future nuclear submarines. They will carry out inspections, upgrades, and repair work.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Iran is continuing to assert that it controls the Strait of Hormuz and has issued a new warning to the charters of vessels to follow its restrictions. It came after Iran made overtures through mediators for terms to reopen the waterway, which were quickly rejected by Donald Trump. The so-called Persian Gulf Strait Authority issued the threat to charterers, purporting it had received a letter from a shipowner citing its charter agreement. The letter they released says the unnamed vessel was required to make an illegal transit because of the charter and that the PGSA should not hold the shipowner or master responsible. “Some charterers are forcing vessels to use illegal routes,” posted the PGSA. “This risks financial and life losses for the vessel, owner, master, and crew, and seriously restricts its future Strait of Hormuz passage.” The message warns that shipowners must “be vigilant.” It further threatens that the charterers will be added to the non-compliant list and all their vessels’ passage through the Strait of Hormuz will be restricted. It is the latest threat from the agency, which claims to control all passages and has increased its non-compliant list to 81 vessels as of last week. Donald Trump, however, quickly rejected Iran's terms, which were largely a repetition of its earlier demands. He asserted that the Strait is moving, saying 29 ships had made the transit Friday night and a record amount of oil was flowing out of the Gulf. He did not mention the four vessels that were attacked last week while saying the war would end quickly and that Iran was losing. One of the rear admirals of the Iranian Army Navy took to the media, then repeating the claim that Iran has full control of the Strait. He said the Army Navy controls the eastern part of the Strait extending into the northern Indian Ocean, while the IRGC Navy has "full control" over the western side of the Strait and the Strait of Hormuz.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Panama Canal Authority is easing some of the restrictions it began imposing over the summer to manage water levels in anticipation of a prolonged drought due to the large El Niño in the Pacific. While the El Niño phenomenon continues, the authority is citing “close to average precipitation in the watershed” and the effectiveness of water-saving measures implemented at the locks. The number of daily transits will increase by one in the Neopanamax locks, which are used by the largest vessels that transit the canal. Beginning October 15, it will return to 10 daily transits in the Neopanamax locks after having removed one slot at the beginning of September. Based on present and projected water levels in Gatun Lake, the canal will be handling a total of 33 transits per day. The authority had reduced the number of daily transits in the older Panamax locks from 25 to 23 as of September 15. It is maintaining that level for those locks along with a 39.5-foot maximum draft. Equally important for the big ships, the maximum draft in the Neopanamax locks is being increased by one foot effective immediately. It returns to 49 feet, which is especially significant for LNG carriers and the larger containerships. The canal had lowered the draft to 48 feet, but delayed in September a planned further reduction to 47.5 feet. The current conditions at the canal show a limited backlog because nearly all the vessels are booking reservations for the transit. The authority has warned that vessels without reservations would be delayed, and it has prompted some ships to divert to other routes. There were also a few reports of record-high prices paid at the auction for transit slots. “While the water deficit continues in the canal watershed, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only way to guarantee a transit date. Vessels without a reservation may therefore face indefinite delays,” warns the Panama Canal Authority in its most recent advisory.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: A specialized damage control team from the Indian Coast Guard was able to arrest the flooding endangering a product tanker off the northeastern coast of India in the Bay of Bengal. The Chinese-owned vessel was being taken in tow to a secure anchorage off Paradip, India, for additional repairs. The Coast Guard received a distress call from the tanker Sea Gull 9 (11,131 dwt) early on Saturday morning, September 27. The vessel was approximately 37 nautical miles east-southeast of Paradip and reported uncontrolled flooding. Built in 1998, the tanker is registered in Belize and has a crew of 23 aboard. It is 127 meters (417 feet) in length. The tanker was coming from Malaysia bound for Paradip with a cargo of 9,000 metric tons of palm oil. The crew reported a main engine failure. Pictures released by the Coast Guard show the vessel listing to port and low in the water. The Indian Coast Guard patrol boat ICGS Vishwast responded and deployed a damage control team to the tanker. The team deployed submersible de-flooding pumps, stopped the leak, blanked two damaged seawater pipelines, and contained a third fractured line. They were able to eliminate the immediate threat of the vessel sinking. A pollution control vessel and an additional patrol boat were deployed, and a Coast Guard aircraft surveyed the area. They reported locating an oil sheen and trail from the vessel in the water. It was believed to be a leak of the palm oil cargo. Further surveys on September 28 confirmed the sheen had dissipated.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The pace of construction on the next generation of ultra-large cruise ships is gaining momentum. The ships are being floated out of their assembly docks and going on sea trials, while steel cutting and block assembly are already underway for even more of the giants. For years, Royal Caribbean International’s two Oasis-class ships at 225,000 gross tons were the outliers, with none of the large, contemporary segment cruise lines willing to jump the 200,000 gross ton milestone. Imaginative concepts were presented, such as Kloster’s World City (proposed at 250,000 GT), but the lines continued to build ships in the 150,000 to 180,000 gross ton range. Changing economics and the need to make space for even more amenities, however, are changing that. Currently, there are a dozen ships exceeding the 200,000 GT milestone, as MSC Cruises surpassed the mark and now Disney Cruise Line, which acquired and completed Genting Hong Kong’s partially built Global Dream . Collectively, these ships represent approximately 68,000 berths (roughly 3.8 million passengers annually), a relatively small fraction of the total industry, which the trade group Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) projects is nearing 40 million passengers per year. Fully a quarter of the new ships in the orderbooks, however, are set to exceed 200,000 gross tons, a total of 19 ships due to enter service in the next decade between November 2026 and 2037. Collectively, they represent more than 40 percent (4.3 million GT) of the total gross tonnage on order in the cruise industry, and more than 105,000 berths, or nearly half the capacity on order. Yet, while the ships are coming in classes, Royal’s Oasis and Icon, MSC’s World, Carnival’s Ace, and Norwegian's so far unnamed class, the lines are working to differentiate the ships. They are learning from the designs and continuing to add new amenities, giving the giants individual personalities. https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: A.P. Moller Capital, a global fund manager focused on infrastructure, transportation, and energy, entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a majority stake in Euroports Group, a leading port terminal operator and provider of logistics solutions. It is the latest in a series of investor moves based on the perceived opportunities in ports, supply chains, and logistics. Started in 2006, Euroports has grown through a series of acquisitions, consolidating operations in the breakbulk sector of the industry. It now operates more than 50 deep-sea and inland port terminals across 10 European countries and China. The company handles more than 70 million tonnes of bulk, breakbulk, and liquid bulk cargo each year, including fertilizers, agribulk, sugar, fruit, forest products, metals, and minerals. The company also operates and manages Manuport Logistics, an independent freight forwarding business active in more than 20 countries. “In a changing world, resilient supply chains and secure trade flows are increasingly essential to economic stability and growth,” said Kim Fejfer, Managing Partner and CEO at A.P. Moller Capital. “We see significant long-term value in combining Euroports’ strong operational platform with A.P. Moller Capital’s industrial expertise and long-term investment approach. Together with SFPIM, PMV, and the management team, we look forward to developing Euroports’ position as a leading provider of critical logistics infrastructure and helping ensure that important trade flows remain efficient, reliable, and resilient.” The new consortium will be led by A.P. Moller Capital’s majority ownership. Two other investment funds, SFPIM and PMV, will remain shareholders, saying they are committed to supporting the company’s long-term development. R-LOGITECH, an international logistics services provider focused mainly on essential commodities, had been an investor in Euroports, but will be exiting as part of this transaction. The investors said they would preserve the company’s existing management structure, governance framework, and strategic direction. The current management team, they commented, has successfully achieved stable growth over the years and will continue under the new ownership structure. “The shareholders will support management’s plans to expand Euroports’ activities, broaden its footprint, and help attract additional customers and volumes, while maintaining high standards of service and a strong commitment to responsible growth and long-term value creation for all stakeholders,” they said in announcing the transaction.

Após o recurso, o ministro Flávio Dino enviou sua decisão para aprovação no plenário. Nos últimos dias, cresceu nas redes sociais uma acusação de que movimento teria intenção de tirar de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil. Postagens relacionavam a ação a Flávio, que desmentiu. Flávio Bolsonaro afirmou que o PT criou fake news com a ajuda da CNBB. A decisão de Dino reverteu determinação anterior do ministro André Mendonça. Dino argumentou que a postagem não cita Flávio e protege a liberdade de expressão. A defesa pede que o ministro Luiz Fux suspenda a decisão.

O governo brasileiro decidiu mover uma ação nesta segunda-feira (28) no valor de R$ 1 bilhão contra 17 operadoras de apostas online — as bets — para cobrar ressarcimento de despesas do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) atribuídas aos danos causados pelo jogo e danos morais coletivos. A ação foi ajuizada pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) na Justiça Federal em Pernambuco e pede ainda a restituição em dobro dos valores apostados por pessoas diagnosticadas por ludopatia (transtorno do jogo patológico). Segundo a ação, cerca de 28 milhões de brasileiros apostam atualmente, e 10,9 milhões apresentam padrão de risco ou problemático de jogo. Entre janeiro de 2018 e dezembro de 2025, os atendimentos do SUS ligados aos diagnósticos de jogo patológico e comportamento de jogo excessivo cresceram aproximadamente 140%.

Os candidatos ao Senado por SP Marina Silva, Simone Tebet, Guilherme Derrite e André do Prado — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM Candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo reagiram nesta segunda-feira (28) à desistência de Ricardo Salles (Novo) da disputa , anunciada a seis dias do primeiro turno das eleições. Salles deixou a corrida para apoiar Guilherme Derrite (PP) e André do Prado (PL), os dois candidatos ao Senado apoiados pelo governador Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). A decisão busca concentrar os votos da direita nos dois nomes na reta final da eleição. Marina Silva (Rede) classificou a movimentação como um "vale-tudo" e afirmou que a desistência de Salles desrespeita os eleitores que pretendiam votar no ex-ministro. "A desistência da candidatura do Ricardo Salles ao Senado desrespeita seus eleitores ao abandoná-los às vésperas da votação, num vale-tudo do grupo da direita para conter o avanço das duas candidatas mulheres do campo progressista", afirmou Marina. A candidata disse ainda que São Paulo tem a oportunidade de eleger duas mulheres para o Senado — numa referência a ela e a Simone Tebet (PSB) — e afirmou que a reta final da campanha exige "coerência".

Nenhum país foi citado nominalmente. A medida ocorre a pouco mais de 1 mês das eleições legislativas. O pleito de meio de mandato definirá 435 deputados e parte dos senadores. O resultado pode alterar o controle do Congresso, atualmente com os republicanos. Donald Trump incentivou redesenhar mapas eleitorais, o que foi contestado na Justiça.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Por Márcio Falcão , Luiz Felipe Barbiéri , Mariana Laboissière , g1 e TV Globo — Brasília Gilmar Mendes ajustou voto para suspender o julgamento de Alexandre de Moraes no caso Master até a identificação de todos os magistrados mencionados nas investigações. https://g1.globo.com/pa/para/noticia/202.text: A PF realizou no domingo (27) uma operação contra o deputado federal Antonio Doido (MDB) no Pará. A ação apreendeu R$ 87 mil e um celular no esgoto. Foram cumpridos 4 mandados de busca sobre possíveis crimes nas Eleições 2026. Uma pessoa foi presa em flagrante por corrupção eleitoral. Parte do dinheiro estava em envelopes com nomes de pessoas e assinaturas de recebimento. O celular foi localizado perto de 2 sacolas com dinheiro. Todo o material recolhido será analisado para mapear a origem e o destino do dinheiro. O inquérito continua para identificar outros possíveis participantes.

O deputado federal Antonio Doido foi alvo de operação da PF contra crimes eleitorais neste domingo (27). A ação cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão em endereços do parlamentar. Na ação, os agentes apreenderam R$ 87,4 mil em espécie e documentos. O político já havia sido alvo de outra investigação da PF em dezembro de 2025. Antonio Doido também é citado em inquérito do STF sobre suposto esquema em licitação da COP 30. Ele declarou patrimônio de R$ 2,23 milhões em 2026.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O Mercado Livre lançou uma nova modalidade de entrega em até 60 minutos em São Paulo e também ampliou sua atuação com o início da venda de medicamentos que exigem receita médica. As novidades foram anunciadas durante o Mercado Livre Experience, realizado na quinta e sexta-feira passados (24 e 25/09), em São Paulo. O serviço Envios Agora está em fase de testes em bairros de São Paulo deve ser ampliado em breve em toda a capital, e posteriormente em outras cidades. O serviço funciona conecta o consumidor a vendedores próximos, e aceita mercadorias de até 15 kg em diferentes categorias. A entrega é feita pela rede de entregadores do Mercado Livre, que retiram os produtos no estabelecimento do vendedor e os levam ao cliente em até 60 minutos, podendo usar diferentes meios de transporte. A disponibilidade deve variar de acordo com a localização do comprador e dos produtos oferecidos nas proximidades. No caso dos medicamentos, a operação começa pela farmácia própria do Mercado Livre na Zona Sul, adquirida pela empresa no ano passado . A unidade passou a oferecer, a partir de 25 de setembro, medicamentos que exigem prescrição, como antibióticos, canetas para controle de peso e diabetes, dentre outros. Para fazer a compra, o paciente precisa anexar a receita médica antes do checkout. O documento deve ser analisado pelo vendedor e aprovado antes de seguir para separação e envio. Caso o documento seja recusado, a compra é cancelada. De acordo com a documentação do serviço pelo Mercado Livre, o vendedor fica responsável pelo armazenamento das receitas em seus próprios sistemas quando necessário. Já a cópia disponível na plataforma é excluída após dois meses.

O Porto de Santos (SP) r egistrou, em agosto de 2026, a maior movimentação mensal de contêineres de sua história, com 538,2 mil TEUs, alta de 3,9% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. No acumulado dos oito primeiros meses do ano , o terminal também alcançou um recorde, com 4 milhões de TEUs movimentados, volume 3,9% superior ao registrado no mesmo período do ano passado. De acordo com dados divulgados pela Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS) em 25 de setembro, a movimentação total de cargas entre janeiro e agosto chegou a 125,9 milhões de toneladas, crescimento de 3,1% na comparação anual. Os embarques somaram 93,1 milhões de toneladas, avanço de 2,9%, enquanto os desembarques totalizaram 32,8 milhões de toneladas, alta de 3,6%. Considerando apenas agosto, a movimentação geral de cargas foi de 16,4 milhões de toneladas, uma ligeira retração de 0,5% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. Os embarques recuaram 0,7%, para 12 milhões de toneladas, enquanto os desembarques cresceram 0,2%, alcançando 4,39 milhões de toneladas. A movimentação de granéis líquidos somou 1,6 milhão de toneladas em agosto, crescimento de 6,3% na comparação anual. No acumulado de janeiro a agosto, o volume chegou a 13,4 milhões de toneladas, alta de 9,3% e recorde para o período. Já os granéis sólidos totalizaram 64 milhões de toneladas nos oito primeiros meses de 2026, avanço de 2,7% e também recorde histórico para o período. Soja em grãos, açúcar e soja peletizada foram os principais produtos movimentados, com participações de 49,5%, 19,9% e 11,9%, respectivamente. No comércio exterior, o Porto de Santos respondeu por 28% da corrente comercial brasileira nos oito primeiros meses do ano. A China permaneceu como principal parceira comercial, sendo origem ou destino de 31,8% das transações com o exterior realizadas por meio do complexo portuário.

A Tópico , fabricante e locadora de galpões modulares, transferiu sua unidade de Contagem (MG) para uma estrutura maior na cidade, localizada na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, com o objetivo de aumentar o suporte às operações no estado. A empresa projeta faturar cerca de R$ 30 milhões em Minas Gerais em 2026 e prevê crescimento de 25% nos negócios na região em 2027 , impulsionada principalmente pela demanda do setor de mineração. Segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração (Ibram), Minas Gerais concentra 25,6% dos investimentos previstos para a mineração brasileira até 2030. A demanda por galpões modulares no segmento mineral do estado cresceu aproximadamente 18% em 2025 e deve avançar mais 25% até o fim de 2026. A flexibilidade das estruturas é um dos fatores que impulsionam a procura. Fabricados em aço e cobertos com lona reciclável, os galpões podem ser desmontados e transferidos para outras áreas de uma operação conforme o avanço das atividades de mineração, sem necessidade de demolição. “Minas Gerais concentra uma das atividades minerais mais complexas do Brasil, com projetos que exigem respostas rápidas e infraestrutura adaptável. O galpão modular acompanha o avanço das lavras e, quando uma área é esgotada, a estrutura é desinstalada e transferida para outro ponto da operação”, afirma Sergio Gallucci, diretor Comercial e de Marketing da Tópico. A mudança da filial para Contagem também busca ampliar a capacidade de atendimento às equipes em campo e de armazenagem de materiais destinados às obras na região. “Investimos nessa nova unidade para oferecer um maior suporte às equipes em campo e ampliar nossa capacidade de armazenagem de materiais destinados às obras da região. É um reflexo direto do aumento de demanda que vivemos em Minas Gerais”, acrescenta Gallucci. Com 47 anos de atuação e mais de 50% de participação no mercado nacional de galpões flexíveis, a Tópico mantém entre 150 mil e 200 mil metros quadrados de estruturas em estoque para pronto atendimento. O prazo entre o pedido e o início da obra varia de três a 15 dias.
