https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 28/09/2026 – A fiscalização do transporte aquaviário exige o acompanhamento recorrente de estruturas, operações e áreas de grandes dimensões ou com acesso limitado. Para apoiar esse trabalho, desde 2019, os drones integram as ferramentas utilizadas pela Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) para reunir informações e auxiliar nas atividades de fiscalização e no acompanhamento da infraestrutura portuária. Na Agência, o uso de Aeronaves Remotamente Pilotadas (RPAs) começou a ser testado em 2016, na Unidade Regional de Porto Velho (UREPV), a partir de uma iniciativa do Especialista em Regulação Wescley Sousa. Com um drone de uso particular, ele propôs testar a ferramenta nas ações de fiscalização, e a experiência abriu caminho para a adoção da tecnologia pela ANTAQ. Em 2019, a utilização das RPAs foi oficializada com a realização de um curso para treinamento de pilotos, voltado à correta operação dos equipamentos. Segundo Sousa, as imagens aéreas trouxeram “um salto qualitativo para atividades fiscalizatórias”. A ferramenta facilita a observação de estruturas de difícil acesso, como o topo de armazéns e equipamentos portuários, sem expor fisicamente os fiscais. Os registros também podem auxiliar na medição de áreas, no cálculo de volumetria e na elaboração de modelos tridimensionais das instalações. Os drones também são utilizados para acompanhar o fluxo de veículos nas vias de acesso aos portos, a ocupação de pátios e a movimentação nos terminais. As imagens produzidas durante os voos integram e subsidiam relatórios e análises elaborados pelos servidores. A tecnologia não se restringe às atividades de fiscalização. A Agência também utiliza as aeronaves em outras áreas, como no acompanhamento e na validação do avanço físico de obras de infraestrutura previstas. E a capacitação para operação dos equipamentos também favorece a integração entre órgãos: nos cursos realizados pela Agência, são reservadas vagas para servidores de instituições parceiras, como a Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT), a Anatel, a Marinha do Brasil e autoridades portuárias. A cooperação também ocorre em outras frentes: a Polícia Federal, por exemplo, eventualmente oferece aos servidores da ANTAQ treinamentos em fotogrametria, mapeamento aéreo e processamento de dados geoespaciais.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/maersk-in.text: The world’s largest bioethanol producers, Sioux Falls, S.D.-headquartered POET reports that it supplied the plant-based bioethanol for the first 100% bioethanol marine bunkering operation in the United States., marking a significant milestone in the development of bioethanol as a marine fuel. The successful trial with Tangier Maers k, the first in a new series of six 9,000 TEU vessels ordered by Maersk, took place in Houston and builds on Maersk’s successful testing of bioethanol in its dual-fuel fleet. “Seeing American-made bioethanol move from the farm to a containership in one of the nation’s largest ports is an exciting moment for our industry,” said Jeff Broin, founder and CEO of POET. “Bioethanol is an abundant, affordable, and clean option for the marine sector. It demonstrates what is possible when partners across the value chain work together to open new markets for American agriculture.” The successful operation was made possible through collaboration across the maritime and biofuels industries. Maersk provided the vessel and has championed bioethanol as a marine fuel. Kirby Corporation supported the marine bunkering operation and transportation of the fuel. Port of Houston provided critical port coordination and infrastructure, while the U.S. Coast Guard supported the regulatory requirements necessary to conduct the first U.S.-based 100% bioethanol bunkering operation. “Bioethanol has the potential to contribute meaningfully to the future energy mix for shipping,” said Emma Mazhari, Maersk’s vice president energy markets. “[Bioethanol] can offer another scalable, lower-emission fuel option and greater flexibility in how the maritime industry approaches its transition to lower-carbon fuels. This operation with POET is an important step in exploring how bioethanol can be incorporated into marine-fuel supply chains in the United States.” The Houston operation also highlights the connection between American agriculture and global commerce. As the 11th-largest U.S. container exporter, POET connects the value chain from American farms to international markets — helping feed the world with high-quality feed ingredients that are a coproduct of the bioethanol process.

REUTERS/Stringer Eight U.S. Marines were injured when an Iranian cruise missile struck a vessel they were operating aboard in the Strait of Hormuz earlier this month, according to a previously unreported incident disclosed by NBC News. The Sept. 14 attack injured seven enlisted Marines and one officer, NBC News reported , citing three U.S. officials. The Marines suffered smoke inhalation and possible traumatic brain injuries after showing concussion symptoms, including headaches. None was seriously injured, and all eight returned to duty shortly afterward. The Marines were serving as part of a battalion landing team, a Marine infantry formation capable of conducting amphibious and maritime operations. Officials said the vessel hit by the missile was not a U.S. Navy ship but declined to identify it, describing it only as a “maritime vessel.” The eight Marines were added roughly 10 days later to the Pentagon’s casualty database, which as of Wednesday listed 861 U.S. service members wounded since the war with Iran began. The increase also included 29 Navy sailors whose injuries were added to the tally this week. U.S. Central Command declined to comment on the Sept. 14 incident, according to NBC.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/80-.text: A group of 80 countries has called for shipping access through the Strait of Hormuz to be fully restored, arguing that continued disruption is affecting trade and energy markets. Bahrain’s foreign minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani presented the joint statement urging the implementation of Security Council Resolution 2817 during a UN Security Council media stakeout on maritime security. The resolution, adopted on 11 March 2026, condemns Iran’s attacks against Gulf countries and Jordan and addresses threats to maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. It was adopted with 13 votes in favour and two abstentions, from China and Russia. The signatories called for all vessels to be able to use the strait safely and exercise their navigational rights under international law. They also opposed the imposition of tolls or other restrictions on transit. The statement condemned Iran’s attacks on countries in the region and its interference with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. It also criticised renewed Houthi hostilities in Yemen and attacks targeting Saudi Arabia and shipping in the Red Sea.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/bra.text: The negotiations around the IMO Net-Zero Framework have moved into an interesting phase. Following the decision not to adopt the draft amendments to MARPOL Annex VI in October 2025, IMO Member States have spent much of 2026 considering how the framework could be adjusted without reopening the entire package negotiated at MEPC 83. Brazil’s contribution ISWG-GHG 22/2/12, submitted ahead of the September 2026 intersessional working group meeting (ISWG-GHG 22), is particularly relevant in this context because it attempts to address several of the concerns that have prevented agreement while preserving most of the underlying compliance architecture. The IMO ISWG-GHG 22 Brazil proposal’s starting point is relatively conservative. Its stated preference remains adoption of the IMO Net-Zero Framework as negotiated, with changes only where they are considered necessary to achieve agreement. The alternatives contained in its submission are therefore presented as compromise options. The global GHG Fuel Intensity standard would remain, as would ship-level compliance balances, Surplus Units, Remedial Units and financial support for zero- and near-zero fuels. Changes concern the initial stringency of the targets, the presentation of the economic element, and the institutional structure through which compliance contributions would be collected and redistributed. Similar to the initial proposal, Brazil wants the framework to operate explicitly as a flexible compliance system. A ship that reaches the required GHG intensity through its own fuels or technologies would comply directly and would not make a compliance payment. A ship that performs even better could create transferable surplus. Only where physical performance is insufficient would the company need to balance the remaining deficit through compliance units. At the same time, the first year of FuelEU Maritime gives the industry a useful real-world example of how such flexibility can develop once a compliance market becomes operational. FuelEU has shown that surplus markets can facilitate compliance very effectively, but it has also exposed a more complicated question: the cheapest way of producing compliance is not necessarily the fuel pathway that policymakers ultimately may want to see scale in the long term. The current European experience therefore provides a useful lens through which to assess both the strengths and the remaining weaknesses of the Brazilian proposal. The framework would remain built around GHG Intensity The basic technical architecture remains unchanged. Ships would be measured against an annual GHG Intensity calculated on a well-to-wake basis and expressed in gCO₂eq/MJ. https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Maersk reports it recently completed the first ship-to-ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a container vessel in the United States. It was a 100 percent bioethanol blend from U.S. producer Poet as part of an ongoing trial by Maersk of ethanol and alternative fuels. The bunkering took place aboard the Tangier Maersk , a recently delivered mid-size vessel built in China and delivered in February this year. The ship, which is 270 meters (900 feet) in length, has a capacity of 9,000 TEU and is equipped with a dual-fuel engine able to operate on methanol. Maersk previously explained that, because ethanol and methanol are both alcohols, they share similar properties, and it was testing interoperability, or swapping ethanol onto its dual-fuel vessels. POET, which is headquartered in South Dakota and bills itself as the world’s largest bioethanol producer, supplied plant-based bioethanol for the first 100 percent bioethanol bunkering operation in the United States. The company points out that it was a cooperation that also involved Kirby Corporation, which supported the marine bunkering operation and transportation of the fuel. Port of Houston provided critical port coordination and infrastructure, while the U.S. Coast Guard supported the regulatory requirements necessary to conduct the bunkering operation. Maersk reported that the operation was providing valuable real-world experience. It said it would provide valuable insight into the operational, infrastructure, sourcing, and supply chain considerations for using ethanol as a marine fuel. While ethanol benefits from an established production base, Maersk said that existing infrastructure and compatibility with alcohol-enabled vessel technology, scalable future fuel pathways would also depend on fuel availability, regulation, and operational readiness across the maritime value chain. The operation builds on previous ethanol trials aboard Laura Maersk and Antonia Maersk and reflects Maersk’s continued commitment to exploring and advancing credible pathways to drive progress within the shipping industry’s energy transition. The company announced in December 2025 that it had conducted the initial test using E10 (10 percent ethanol) in an ethanol-methanol blend to confirm safe integration and performance. They reported they would be looking at issues including ignition quality, how the fuel burned, potential corrosion issues, and testing the emissions to see if there were differences. Building on a successful initial trial, the company planned to blend 50 percent ethanol with 50 percent methanol in a test onboard the vessel Laura Maersk . It said it was also aiming for a 100 percent ethanol test.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The US Navy’s Sixth Fleet and the UK Royal Navy teamed up for two weeks of joint training called Atlantic Thunder 26, which included a live-fire exercise. Full details on the program have not been released, but as U.S. European Command reported, the exercise concluded on September 25 with “a very bad day” for the decommissioned frigate USS Klakring . The program, which had been delayed for four months from May to September, kicked off a pre-sail conference at Faslane in the UK on September 10. It was a joint force multi-domain exercise. It included multi-axis and long-range maritime training, concluding with the SINEX. According to U.S. commanders, it was designed to increase U.S. and UK interoperability and strengthen the strategic partnership. The U.S. Navy participation included USS Paul Ignatius , an Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, along with the submarine USS Massachusetts . HMS Portland was also participating along with the Royal Air Force and U.S. Air Force. The exercise was underway from September 14 to 25. A full report on the exercise is still pending, but it was said to include tests of weapons systems and targeting networks, with a focus on interoperability and information sharing. The U.S. Navy also reported that the two forces would be testing unmanned underwater vehicles from the Royal Navy. It was the first time in four years the two navies trained together with a live-fire SINKEX element. In 2022, they sank the Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigate, the ex-USS Boone . The target for the 2026 exercise was the decommissioned frigate USS Klakring . The 4,100-ton displacement frigate was built at Bath Iron Works and commissioned in 1983. The vessel was 453 feet (138 meters) in length. After an active service career, she was decommissioned in 2013 and was laid up in Philadelphia before being towed to Scotland for this exercise.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: Greenpeace activists in New Zealand are intensifying their opposition to deep-sea mining. They boarded a state-owned research vessel that was returning from an exploration mission in the Pacific on behalf of a U.S. company. On September 26, the activists boarded the RV Tangaroa , New Zealand’s only ice-strengthened and dynamically positioned deep-water research vessel, to protest the country’s role in facilitating U.S. company Glomar Minerals’ plans to start deep-sea mining in the Pacific Ocean. The 1991-built Tangaroa , which is 70 meters (230 feet) in length, had just returned to Wellington Harbor after completing exploration work for Glomar. An activist dressed like U.S. President Donald Trump flew an American flag from the vessel while another held a banner reading “Don’t Mine the Moana.” The activists occupied the vessel for about seven hours before they were removed by the police. Operated by Earth Sciences NZ (formerly NIWA), Tangaroa is equipped for ocean science, exploration, and marine engineering and has carried out environmental survey and ocean science research missions across the South Pacific, Southern Ocean, and Antarctic waters. The vessel is equipped with a range of modern and sophisticated equipment that enables the sampling and measurement of ocean environments. Greenpeace highlighted that its activists boarded the vessel following her return from the Clarion- Clipperton Zone (CCZ) in the international waters of the Pacific, where the ship surveyed deep-sea minerals. The research was carried out on behalf of UK Seabed Resources Ltd (UKSR), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Glomar Minerals. According to Glomar Minerals, Tangaroa had departed Tahiti in late July for the CCZ to survey its license area for polymetallic nodules rich in critical minerals. The campaign was the first comprehensive geological and biological survey of the UK2 license area in more than 40 years. UKSR’s license areas cover approximately 133,000 square kilometers of deep seafloor, an area covered in polymetallic nodules containing manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, and rare earths in a single ore.

Nas eleições de 2026, o eleitor não pode votar em candidatos a governador, senador ou deputado que disputem a eleição por outro estado . Para esses cargos, a escolha fica restrita aos candidatos que concorrem pelo estado onde o eleitor tem domicílio eleitoral. Já para presidente, é possível votar em qualquer candidato do país. Governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual: o eleitor pode votar em qualquer candidato que concorra pelo seu estado, independentemente da cidade. Presidente: o eleitor pode votar em qualquer candidato do país, independentemente do estado. Exemplo: um eleitor do Paraná pode votar em um candidato a deputado federal que concorra pelo Paraná, seja ele de Curitiba, Londrina ou qualquer outra cidade paranaense. Mas não pode votar em um candidato que concorra por Santa Catarina. É possível votar fora da cidade onde o eleitor tem seu título por meio do voto em trânsito , desde que a pessoa tenha feito a solicitação dentro do prazo estabelecido pela Justiça Eleitoral.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/qatar-ex.text: QatarEnergy has extended force majeure notices and will not be able to deliver liquefied natural gas cargoes to Italian utility Edison or some Asian clients as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, Edison and trading sources said on Monday. Edison, one of the company's biggest customers in Europe, will not receive LNG cargoes until the beginning of December, the Italian group said on Monday, in the latest extension under a force majeure notification first issued in April following disruptions caused by the US-Iran war. Clients in Asia, including in Bangladesh and Pakistan, were also informed that force majeure notices had been extended until November, two trading sources said. Qatar is among the Iran conflict's biggest economic casualties, with its liquefied natural gas exports slashed by 96%, Reuters calculated at the end of August. While neighbouring Gulf exporters have managed to ship oil secretly out of the Strait of Hormuz, Qatar had exported just 18 LNG cargoes until end-August, down from 509 in the same period last year, according to data intelligence firm ICIS. With the winter heating season starting within days, buyers in Europe will have to look elsewhere to refill gas storage inventories ahead of the coldest months of the year.

https://gcaptain.com/europe-draws-more-l.text: (Bloomberg) — European imports of liquefied natural gas are rising ahead of the Northern Hemisphere winter, as prolonged disruptions to flows through the Strait of Hormuz threaten to intensify global competition for the fuel. Deliveries to the European Union and UK are about 4% lower than a year ago on a 30-day moving average, but have increased since early August, when imports were 30% below last year’s levels, ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg show. Over the same period, LNG flows to Northeast Asia fell. The price arbitrage for US LNG currently favors Europe over Asia, according to traders, providing an incentive for Atlantic cargoes to remain in the region into October. Europe is projected to absorb about a quarter of global LNG supplies in September, up from less than 19% in July, according to Kpler. The persistent lack of LNG from the Persian Gulf, which provided about a fifth of global supply before the Iran war, sent prices to the highest level since late-2022 earlier this month. The tighter market means greater competition between Europe and Asia, home to the world’s top buyers, for the same flexible supply from the US and elsewhere. One source of competition for Europe is India, where LNG demand is rising as dry weather curbs hydropower generation and fertilizer plants require more gas. Imports are set to climb 10% in September from a year earlier, according to Kpler. Indian buyers are continuing to snap up spot cargoes, even at prices above their typical purchasing threshold. Europe has boosted LNG imports since 2022 to refill inventories and meet higher winter demand after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine forced buyers to replace pipeline supplies from Moscow.

https://gcaptain.com/at-sea-confined-spa.text: On a laid-up mobile offshore drilling unit (MODU), a worker descended alone into the leg to check on a diesel pump being used for dewatering operations. When he didn’t return, an electrician went down and found him collapsed near the pump. The electrician was nearly overcome by exhaust fumes but made it back on deck and raised the alarm. Another crew member immediately descended to help. Then the captain, superintendent, and a fitter entered the leg to attempt a rescue. They found the second crew member, who had collapsed one level above the first worker. Without proper safety equipment, however, they too began to suffer the effects of the vapor in the confined space. By the time a sixth crew member, the rigging master, entered the leg outfitted with a breathing apparatus, the fitter had collapsed. The rigging master managed to help the captain and superintendent escape, but it was too late for the first three crew members who had entered the leg. They lost their lives in what the U.S. Coast Guard later described as a preventable tragedy marked by a lack of training and the absence of safety gear. This was not an isolated occurrence. According to data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics , more than 100 workers die in confined space accidents each year. In the maritime industry, these incidents may occur in cargo holds, ballast tanks, fuel tanks, pump rooms, and engine compartments, which exist on every vessel and platform. Confined spaces are unavoidable in maritime operations. They’re also among the deadliest work environments in the industry. A space becomes a “permit-required confined space” when it contains or has the potential to contain a hazardous atmosphere, materials that could engulf an entrant, walls that converge inward or floors that slope downward and taper into smaller areas, or any other recognized safety or health hazard.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543328-ha.text: Norwegian offshore safety regulator Havtil has identified four non-conformities at Equinor's Hammerfest LNG facility following an investigation into chemical exposure incidents, while finding that measured exposure levels were relatively low. Havtil launched the investigation after receiving reports of numerous exposure incidents at the onshore facility between June 2024 and April 2025. The regulator also became aware through media coverage of incidents that had not been reported and had resulted in more serious consequences than indicated through normal reporting channels. The investigation found instances of chemical exposure linked to the Snøhvit Future project and other activities at Hammerfest LNG. However, measurements and documentation indicated that exposure levels had consistently been relatively low. Havtil subsequently examined other factors that could help explain the consequences of the incidents. Interviews, document reviews and previously known whistleblowing reports contained accounts of a culture of fear, lack of trust in management and perceptions of discrimination based on nationality. The regulator identified four non-conformities covering compliance with internal requirements and conditions specified in the PDO/PIO, arrangements for the physical and psychosocial working environment, oversight of exposure sources and support for decision-making. Havtil also found that a subcontractor with limited experience working on oil and gas facilities had been selected for Hammerfest LNG without a corresponding strengthening of the project organization.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543326-un.text: Well integrity and decom specialist Unity has launched an ultra-compact blowout preventer valve designed to enable well intervention in space-constrained offshore environments where conventional Blowout Preventer (BOP) systems cannot be deployed. The new Unity Qb valve is one-third the width of conventional systems and rated to 10,000 psi, twice the pressure rating of Unity's existing compact shear valve, while maintaining the same weight. Backed by around $675,000 (£500,000) of research and development investment, the recently patented system is aimed at wireline, slickline and coil tubing operations, with potential future drilling applications. Unlike conventional BOPs, which use rams that move in a straight line from opposite sides of the wellbore, the Unity Qb uses rams that rotate around a central cartridge within its housing. Unity describes the design as a hybrid between a conventional BOP and a ball valve. The configuration allows the valve to perform conventional BOP functions within a smaller footprint and potentially be installed in locations where previously only a Shear-Seal Ball Valve could fit. The system can also be stacked in single, dual or triple configurations, while its 10,000 psi rating allows deployment on higher-pressure wells that cannot be serviced by lower-rated equipment.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/oil_risk_pr.text: In a report sent to Rigzone by the Standard Chartered Bank team late Monday, the company’s Energy Research Head, Emily Ashford, outlined that there will be no return to normal for the oil market, warning that the “oil risk premium is becoming structural”. The Energy Research Head highlighted in the report that Standard Chartered Bank’s call rests on three “key developments”. The first of these is that the conflict is “regional rather than bilateral”, the second is that “diplomacy is increasingly likely to produce an imperfect and gradual de-escalation, rather than a clean reset”, and the third is that the energy system “is moving from optimization around efficiency towards resilience, redundancy, and optionality,” Ashford pointed out. The report revealed that Standard Chartered Bank has raised its average Brent crude forecast for 2026 to $92.00 per barrel, from $85.50 per barrel, and its 2027 Brent crude forecast to $89.50 per barrel, from $77.50 per barrel. Standard Chartered Bank’s average WTI forecast for 2026 is now $86.00 per barrel, from $80.25 per barrel, and its 2027 WTI forecast has risen to $82.75 per barrel, from $72.50 per barrel, the report showed. “The energy market is confronting a more persistent deterioration in the Middle East security environment,” Ashford said in the report. “We see little prospect of a return to the pre-conflict status quo. No credible pathway to a durable settlement is yet visible and the conflict has now broadened to a regional security problem with the Houthi/Saudi escalation adding a second front,” Ashford added.

https://safety4sea.com/dutch-safety-boar.text: The Dutch Safety Board has opened an investigation into the death of an engine-room crew member aboard a Dutch merchant vessel in the English Channel on September 11, 2026. T he vessel, which was carrying zinc concentrate, was sailing through the English Channel on the afternoon of September 11 when an engine-room crew member was reported missing. The Dutch Safety Board launched its investigation on September 14, three days after the incident. The Board said the investigation is intended to establish the circumstances surrounding the fatal incident and identify factors that may have contributed to what happened. The investigation will also seek to draw lessons that can contribute to improved safety on board seagoing vessels. The Board’s work is therefore focused not only on establishing the sequence of events, but also on identifying potential safety lessons from the incident.

https://safety4sea.com/gard-club-warns-o.text: Loss of bridge control is not always the result of a mechanical or electrical failure. Even when a vessel’s steering and control systems are operating normally, incorrect settings entered by the crew can trigger a loss of control and, in some cases, lead to serious accidents. A s modern bridges become increasingly automated and integrated, the interaction between crew and control systems is becoming a critical area of maritime safety, Gard Club explains in a recent article. When control is unexpectedly lost, bridge teams may have only seconds or minutes to identify the cause and respond. Under pressure, an incorrect intervention can compound the problem rather than restore control. An analysis of accident cases by Gard has highlighted how quickly such situations can escalate, including cases involving highly sophisticated bridge-control systems. The lessons are relevant not only to advanced vessels but also to conventional steering arrangements, which are themselves evolving towards greater levels of automation and integration. As maritime technology develops, the potential consequences of failures involving critical bridge systems remain significant.

https://safety4sea.com/maersk-completes-.text: A.P. Moller – Maersk has completed the first ship-to-ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep-sea container vessel in the United States, as it continues to assess alternative fuel pathways for shipping. T he operation involved Tangier Maersk, a dual-fuel alcohol-enabled container vessel, which was bunkered with 100% U.S.-produced corn ethanol. According to Maersk, the operation provided practical experience on the operational, infrastructure, sourcing and supply chain requirements associated with using ethanol as a marine fuel. While ethanol benefits from an established production base and existing infrastructure, Maersk noted that the scalability of future marine fuel pathways will also depend on fuel availability, regulatory frameworks and operational readiness across the maritime value chain. This bunkering operation aboard Tangier Maersk provides valuable real-world experience with alternative fuels in commercial shipping. The insights gained will help drive the development of more sustainable supply chains The operation follows previous ethanol trials aboard Laura Maersk and Antonia Maersk, and forms part of Maersk’s broader efforts to evaluate multiple fuel options for shipping’s energy transition. The company said the latest bunkering will help build operational knowledge around ethanol while highlighting the wider requirements that need to be addressed before alternative fuels can be deployed at scale across the maritime sector.

https://safety4sea.com/hd-hyundai-tests-.text: Image hereabove is being used for illustration purposes only/ Credit: Shutterstock HD Hyundai is moving to integrate physical AI into shipyard operations, with a new demonstration at HD Hyundai Samho’s shipyard in Yeongam, South Jeolla Province, combining 5G and GPU-based AI computing to enable autonomous welding and painting. T he demonstration, led by KT, forms part of South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT initiative to develop high-performance AI network infrastructure. It will apply 5G standalone (SA), network slicing, AI-RAN and autonomous network technologies, allowing robots to process video and sensor data in real time and carry out operations with greater autonomy. The project will establish a high-performance AI network across welding and painting facilities and test two types of industrial robots. By bringing computing resources closer to the robots through the communications network, the system is intended to overcome limitations associated with onboard computing capacity while reducing the latency associated with sending data to distant cloud infrastructure. The initiative seeks to automate existing semi-automatic welding and painting processes, with the ministry targeting productivity and safety improvements. A separate SK Telecom-led consortium is conducting physical AI demonstrations involving autonomous patrol and transport at SK Incheon Petrochem and KG Mobility facilities. The ministry plans to validate physical AI applications across the shipbuilding, petrochemical and automotive sectors before expanding the technology to other manufacturing industries.

https://safety4sea.com/northstandard-hig.text: Vessels calling at Turkish ports, regardless of flag, are required under Turkish Customs Regulations to declare the quantity of bunkers remaining on board through the Ship’s Stores List submitted to customs authorities. T he requirement places a particular emphasis on accurate fuel reporting, with discrepancies potentially exposing shipowners and crew to significant consequences. According to NorthStandard guidance, the bunker quantity declared on arrival should be consistent with the vessel’s records and supported by reliable measurements. Crews calling at Turkish ports should accurately verify and declare bunker quantities, using physical soundings and regularly checking tank measurement systems. Any discrepancies with customs figures can lead to onboard inspections, fines for owners and crew, and potentially criminal proceedings. As explained by Kaan Erdi, Claims Executive – Middle East, India & Africa at NorthStandard and Nazli Selek and Nisanur Kopuz of NSN Law Firm; and Ismail Aydin of Aydin & Partners, who contributed their assistance to the guidance, accurate bunker measurement and careful record-keeping are therefore essential for vessels calling at Turkish ports, helping operators avoid unnecessary customs disputes and potential penalties. Customs fines for excess bunkers are divided into two categories and customs authorities can apply one of the following: Shipowners may benefit from a deduction of ¼ of the total amount of the fine if the payment in respect of a fine for irregularities is made within one month and in respect of a fine for tax losses within 15 days following the service of written notification.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/shi.text: One Tanker Met Fifteen Counterparts in Ninety Days Between May 27 and August 27, 2026, Windward tracked a Barbados-flagged product tanker of roughly 40,000 deadweight tonnes across two anchorage clusters at opposite ends of the Strait of Hormuz. Inside the Gulf, it worked the Basrah and Kuwait anchorages. Outside, it worked Fujairah and Shinas. Across the window, it recorded 15 distinct meeting partners, more than any other vessel in the reviewed set, and four transfers corroborated by cargo model. The Relay Splits One Cargo Movement Into Two Legs The pattern is consistent enough to describe as a structure. Feeder and port tankers hand cargo to the intermediary at the Basrah and Kuwait anchorage, inside the Gulf. The intermediary then transits the strait and hands that cargo onward to different tankers waiting at Fujairah and Shinas, on the Gulf of Oman side. Neither leg is unusual on its own. Ship-to-ship transfer at anchorage is routine commercial practice across both clusters. What the 90-day view shows is the same vessel performing both roles repeatedly, receiving inside and delivering outside, rather than carrying a cargo on its own bill of lading from load port to discharge port. For a counterparty screening a fixture, that structure matters. The vessel named on the documentation for either leg is real, and its behavior is unremarkable. The movement of the cargo across the chokepoint sits in the gap between the two.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/tan.text: As Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues, more tankers are crossing the strait with their automatic identification system (AIS) turned off, helping crude supplies recover and international oil prices remain relatively stable. According to European commodities analytics firm Kpler on the 28th, the volume of crude that passed through the Strait of Hormuz this month averaged 9.36 million barrels a day, up 3.56 million barrels from August. That is the highest since the U.S.-Iran military clashes began at the end of February and has recovered to about 60% of the roughly 15 million barrels a day that passed through before the clashes. Nihon Keizai Shimbun (Nikkei) reported that observers say the recovery of crude supply through the Strait of Hormuz to about 60% of the level before the U.S.-Iran military clashes is partly due to an increase in tankers transiting the strait with AIS turned off. In fact, Kpler’s estimate of crude volumes through the Strait of Hormuz included oil carried by tankers with AIS turned off. Turning off AIS makes it harder to track a ship’s position, reducing the risk of Iranian drone attacks or seizure. Recently, Saudi Arabia and Iraq have been increasing crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia boosted oil exports rerouted toward the Red Sea immediately after the U.S.-Iran clashes, but after a pipeline was hit by a drone attack, it is said to be expanding exports through the Strait of Hormuz again. According to U.K.-based commodity price agency Argus Media, Saudi state oil company Aramco has launched a spot tender to supply crude delivered in September–November via ship-to-ship transfer off Oman. This is unusual given that Saudi Arabia has typically sold crude based on long-term contracts and its monthly official selling price (OSP).

https://splash247.com/great-eastern-adds.text: India’s Great Eastern Shipping has contracted to acquire a 157,000 dwt newbuilding suezmax, adding a yard-built ship to a fleet renewal drive that has so far been dominated by secondhand transactions. The Mumbai-listed owner disclosed the deal late on Monday, saying the tanker will be constructed by an unnamed leading shipbuilder in the Far East and delivered in the second half of fiscal 2028-29, putting handover between October 2028 and March 2029. No purchase price, propulsion details or shipyard have been disclosed. Great Eastern said the acquisition will be financed from internal accruals. Shipbroking sources said the crude carrier is being built in Vietnam under Samsung Heavy Industries’ programme for Eyal Ofer’s Zodiac Maritime and booked for about $85m. The company currently owns 40 ships totalling about 3.24m dwt, comprising 25 tankers and 15 bulkers. Its tanker fleet consists of five crude carriers, 16 product tankers and four LPG carriers, while the dry bulk side includes two capesizes, 10 kamsarmaxes, one ultramax and two supramaxes. Great Eastern also has two secondhand kamsarmaxes under contract for delivery during the October-December quarter. The suezmax contract marks a change of gear after a particularly busy year in the secondhand market. Splash reported earlier this month that Great Eastern’s 2026 spending on used tonnage had passed $200m, including several kamsarmax acquisitions, the $35.5m purchase of the MR2 Ardmore Engineer and a $72m deal for the LR2 Seriana .

https://splash247.com/tufton-scores-81-u.text: London-listed Tufton Assets has capitalised on the strong tanker market, fixing one of its MR product tankers at $39,000 per day, an 81% increase on the vessel’s existing employment. The Mia Grace has been fixed for 12 to 14 months, up from its current rate of $21,500 per day. The new charter is expected to start around September 30 and equates to an annualised yield of about 29% based on the ship’s June valuation. Tufton has also secured fresh employment for handysize bulker Amilyn , fixing the ship for nine to 11 months at more than $15,000 per day. The rate is around 20% above the $12,750 per day secured in February for sistership Whitby . Elsewhere in the bulker portfolio, Tufton has exercised an option to convert the index-linked charter of the Staithes to a fixed $19,000 per day for the fourth quarter. The vessel will revert to floating-rate employment at the end of the year, with Tufton retaining an option to fix the first quarter of 2027. The tanker fixture comes during an exceptional spell for the sector. Tufton linked the tightening market to sanctions and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, which it said had reduced the pool of compliant tonnage and fed through from crude into product tankers. The wider market has remained extremely tight through September, with product tanker rates also benefiting from altered Gulf trading patterns. Tufton Assets currently counts 21 ships across the handysize bulker and product tanker sectors. Earlier this year, the fund agreed a $33m en bloc purchase of two Japanese-built handysizes as it stepped up its exposure to dry bulk.

https://navaltoday.com/2026/09/29/decomm.text: The decommissioned US Navy frigate, ex-USS Klakring (FFG 42), was sunk in the North Atlantic during Exercise Atlantic Thunder 2026, a US-UK multi-domain sinking exercise led by the US 6th Fleet. The Oliver Hazard Perry-class guided-missile frigate was used as the surface target during the exercise, which concluded on September 25. US and UK forces conducted live-fire engagements against the ship to train in maritime strike, targeting and battle damage assessment. The US Navy guided-missile destroyer USS Paul Ignatius (DDG 117) employed an anti-surface variant of the Standard Missile-6 (SM-6), while the Virginia-class attack submarine USS Massachusetts (SSN 798) engaged the target with a Mk 48 Advanced Capability torpedo. The torpedo strike resulted in the final hit that sank ex-USS Klakring. Royal Navy frigate HMS Portland (F 79) also participated in the exercise, with the Royal Navy confirming the firing of the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) and Sea Venom. US Navy and Royal Air Force P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, a Royal Navy Wildcat helicopter and US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagles also took part. “The successful firing of NSM marks a significant milestone for the Royal Navy, demonstrating our ability to deliver credible, modern maritime strike capability,” said Royal Navy Lt. Cmdr. Louise Kirkaldy , HMS Portland’s Principal Warfare. “This achievement reflects the professionalism, dedication and teamwork of all those involved, whose hard work has ensured we remain ready to meet the challenges of today and tomorrow.”

https://petronoticias.com.br/camorim-ve-.text: A Camorim está ampliando sua atuação no setor de serviços marítimos diante de um cenário de demanda aquecida no mercado offshore e portuário. Segundo Plínio Salles , diretor estratégico da empresa, os R$ 250 milhões já investidos neste ano fazem parte de um ciclo de expansão que contempla novos rebocadores azimutais, navios do tipo FSV e na Super Cábrea, dentro de um movimento de ampliação da capacidade operacional da companhia. A estratégia acompanha um mercado que volta a demandar novas embarcações e serviços especializados para dar suporte ao crescimento das atividades marítimas. A empresa também acompanha os possíveis desdobramentos da exploração na Margem Equatorial, que poderá exigir novas configurações de embarcações para atender às características operacionais da região. Para começar, você poderia detalhar os R$ 250 milhões investidos este ano pela empresa, explicando onde esses recursos foram aplicados e qual o objetivo por trás desses investimentos? Nós construímos cinco embarcações de apoio portuário. São cinco rebocadores azimutais que já estão em operação nos portos. Essas cinco embarcações foram concluídas e entregues até o final do ano passado. Trata-se de um pedido inicial de cinco unidades e, no início de 2026, assinamos um contrato com o estaleiro para a construção de mais quatro. No total, somam-se nove embarcações. O primeiro rebocador dessa segunda série de quatro ficará pronto em meados de 2027, e o último tem previsão de entrega entre agosto e setembro de 2028, concluindo assim este ciclo. Além dos rebocadores, a Camorim tem planos para expandir outros tipos de embarcações na frota? Sim. Recentemente, assinamos o contrato para a construção de um guindaste sobre balsa (Super Cábrea). Compramos na China um guindaste com capacidade para 750 toneladas, que já está em processo de embarque, enquanto a balsa está sendo construída na Bahia. Esse é um investimento voltado para operações de içamento de cargas. Na área offshore, também realizamos aquisições recentes: compramos no México a embarcação Susan, do tipo Fast Supply Vessel (FSV) — um navio de apoio menor, construído em alumínio e com maior velocidade —, que já está operando no Brasil. Além disso, adquirimos o Ilha das Flechas, que possui características semelhantes de menor capacidade e alta velocidade. Nosso foco prioritário de investimento é o apoio portuário, mas estamos aproveitando as oportunidades que surgem tanto no mercado offshore quanto no setor de movimentação de cargas para obras marítimas.

https://splash247.com/mermaid-teams-with.text: Thailand’s Mermaid Maritime has teamed up with Nigerian offshore services player Marine Platforms to establish a local subsea joint venture targeting work with TotalEnergies and other oil and gas majors. The Singapore-listed offshore contractor has taken a 49% stake in Mermaid Subsea Services through wholly owned Mermaid Subsea Oil and Gas Services, with Marine Platforms holding the remaining 51%. Mermaid said the new company will give it a platform for direct operational engagement with TotalEnergies Nigeria and other operators while meeting Nigerian local content, regulatory and contracting requirements. No contract award was announced alongside the establishment of the venture. Marine Platforms, founded in 2001, provides subsea engineering, ROV support, well services and vessel chartering. Its current asset and operating footprint includes more than 300 employees, five OIMR vessels and 13 ROVs. The Nigeria move is the latest in a series of steps by Mermaid to widen its geographical reach. In August, the company established a Delaware subsidiary as a platform to pursue offshore oil and gas, subsea and decommissioning work in the US Gulf. That followed a June deal with DS Global Offshore Engineering to establish a 50:50 Singapore joint venture to reactivate and commercialise the laid-up diving support vessel Mermaid Commander .

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Low water levels on Germany’s sections of the Rhine have been challenging inland cargo vessels since the height of the summer, but now a vessel loaded with Mercedes Sprinter vans has stranded in Düsseldorf. German authorities are reporting the Rhine is effectively cut in two, reducing the movement of cargo from ports, including Düsseldorf, out to the ocean ports. The Dutch-flagged barge Terra 2 (135 meters – 443 feet in length) had loaded a cargo of 168 Mercedes vans and was set to depart on Monday. According to the police, the vessel only got a short distance off the dock when it stranded on a sandbar. It made several attempts to free itself, but was stuck overnight. Reports said it is not common for vessels to have trouble or stand in the basin in low water conditions. The Terra 2 was not blocking traffic, and the port was functioning, as onlookers gawked at the stranded vessel. Im #Hafen in #Düsseldorf hat sich ein #Frachtschiff festgefahren. Auch am Dienstagmorgen (29.09.) ist es noch nicht wieder frei. Der Frachter hat Transporter geladen. Am Montag wollte er den Hafen verlassen - blieb aber stecken. Grund ist der extrem niedrige #Pegelstand des… pic.twitter.com/kJv4CKfQEI Low water levels, however, were complicating the efforts. The water police reported water levels were too low for their vessel to navigate out to the stranded barge. They depended on the fire department to reach the ship so they could begin the investigation. They also said it was too dangerous for tugs to attempt to reach the Terra 2 , so it would have to free itself or wait for the water levels to improve. Authorities are reporting the water level on the Rhine has fallen so low that captains are refusing to navigate the river. At one critical juncture, the water level was officially recorded at just one meter (3.3 feet). Cargo ships have already been required to sail with partial loads, with reports that highways are clogged by trucks trying to make up for the lack of river capacity. Special low-draft vessels are required for parts of the river. The Rhine typically carries up to two-thirds of Germany's inland freight.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: After growing speculation that opposition was mounting in Israel to Hapag-Lloyd’s proposed acquisition of Zim along with the investment fund FIMI, the Israeli media outlet Calcalist is reporting Tuesday night that Israel formally closed the review of the original deal. According to the report, the Government Companies Authority closed the review of the original proposal but left the door open for Hapag and FIMI to submit a new proposal and restart the review. The rejection of the original terms comes after Hapag and FIMI reportedly presented the framework to revise the original proposal. While not increasing the financial offer, it reportedly proposed adding an Asian trade route to the surviving company and strengthening government control of the Israeli company. Reuters reported on Tuesday that Hapag was still urging the Israeli government to review the revised terms, which were developed in response to earlier objections to the deal. Hapag and FIMI were proposing to acquire Zim and create a new domestic shipping company that would manage the routes to Israel and meet the obligations of the government’s Golden Share. It reportedly added the Asia route, increased the number of ships and reefer capacity, and improved the training and job provisions in the revised offer. Hapag was to assume Zim’s current international service and chartered fleet of ships. The Israeli media was reporting on Monday that the Finance Ministry had provided a paper that officially rejected the deal, citing concerns over national security, maritime independence, and the viability of the new Zim. It reportedly raised concerns that Zim would be dependent on Hapag and referenced the investments in the German company by Qatar’s and Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth funds. It also questioned the structure of the deal for FIMI, the long-term financial stability of the new company, while pointing out Zim would retain older ships. The Finance Ministry expressed its opposition, saying the material risks were not adequately addressed, and it recommended not approving the deal. This came after reports that the Economic Ministry had softened its position. Initially, it also opposed the deal but said it believed concerns were being addressed. It proposed an additional meeting with Hapag to address the remaining concerns. Earlier reports had said other ministries and factions within Israel also opposed the deal, including the union. The Defense Ministry was also opposing the deal based on security concerns and saying Israel needed a strong, independent shipping company.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Following successful completion of acceptance trials in August, the U.S. Navy on Tuesday, September 29, took “preliminary acceptance” of the nation’s next aircraft carrier, the future USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), from Newport News Shipbuilding, a division of HII. According to the Navy, preliminary acceptance will allow the ship and its crew to conduct at-sea testing and build underway proficiency while the shipbuilder completes final ship systems testing before formal delivery of the new carrier. Preliminary acceptance allows CVN 79 to be delivered to the U.S. Navy on the fastest path possible to achieve combat readiness. The Navy is expected to take formal delivery of the carrier in March. “Achieving preliminary acceptance marks a new phase for the ship and her crew, allowing them to get more water under the keel as they test and train underway, said Captain Mark Johnson, the Navy’s Program Manager for Gerald R. Ford-Class New Construction. "This milestone is a testament to the shared commitment of our sailors and our combined Navy-industry team, who remain laser-focused on completing the final stages of construction and test with precision and efficiency to deliver combat-ready lethality to the fleet." John F. Kennedy is reported to be approximately 99 percent complete. All major systems are complete. The shipbuilder is currently completing final ship systems testing, including testing of the remaining four Advanced Weapons Elevators. After years of delays, the multi-billion-dollar carrier went to sea for the first time on its builder’s sea trials, which were completed in early February. The second member of the Ford class completed acceptance sea trials in mid-August. USNI News reports the Navy said the carrier has now departed the Newport News shipyard, moving over to a berth at Naval Station Norfolk, where the final elements will be completed. The carrier still faces extensive trials and training before it will be deployed for the first time. However, with the lessons learned from the commissioning of Gerald R. Ford, the Navy is confident it can accelerate the process with fewer problems along the way.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/l.text: A landing mishap aboard aircraft carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower (CVN 69) caused injuries to four personnel on September 28, the U.S. Navy reported. The Navy said in a statement that the mishap occurred during aircraft recovery operations off the coast of Virginia. In the incident, two Navy aviators assigned to Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 3 ejected from their aircraft and were promptly recovered by search-and-rescue personnel. The statement on X added that both aviators were safely returned to the ship for medical evaluation. “Four shipboard personnel were also injured during the mishap and are receiving medical care. One sailor is being transported to a Norfolk-area hospital for treatment of non-life-threatening injuries,” added the brief statement. According to the USNI News, the aircraft carrier is in the midst of early carrier qualifications after completing its most recent repair period in July. Commissioned in 1977, Eisenhower currently serves as the flagship of Carrier Strike Group 2. Having been in operation for close to five decades, a period in which the ship has undergone numerous overhauls, the Navy intends to replace her with the new USS Enterprise (CVN-80). Construction of Enterprise commenced in 2017, but delivery, which was originally slated for 2028, has been pushed back several times. Current projections indicate the warship will enter service in 2031.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Frustrated by the 2016 ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, which found that Beijing’s claims to historic rights within the Nine-Dash Line in the South China Sea had no legal basis under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), China has been further annoyed by events in the area in recent weeks, in which other claimants have stood their ground. There has been a noticeable escalation of tension in the last month involving the Philippines, with clashes reported at sea between Chinese Coast Guard vessels and fishing boats supported by Filipino maritime agencies in the areas of the Scarborough Shoal and the Second Thomas Shoal, where the Philippines has been attempting to resupply its presence aboard the grounded ship BRP Sierra Madre (LT-57). The situation was worsened by the very public rebuff of the Chinese made by the Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jnr at the Defense Dialogue conference in Seoul on September 8. These tensions have prompted a Chinese counter-offensive. The LST-542 Class landing ship BRP Sierra Madre (LT-57) aground in the 2nd Thomas Shoal (USN file photo) In the wake of the Hague ruling in 2016, China started – sparingly at first - to use the term Nanhai Zhudao to describe the area of the South China Sea where it claimed four separate groups of islands: Pratas Island, the Paracels, Scarborough Shoal, and the Spratly Islands. Alongside Nanhai Zhudao, it has also used the descriptor Four Sha (or Four Sands). In recent pronouncements, the Chinese have begun referring to these islands as one collective, politically administered as Sansha City, and implying that the four separate island groups are an archipelago, one geographic entity, and part of China’s internal seas and territorial waters. China will be adopting this single collective identity to try to strengthen its claims. However, The Hague judgment specifically dismissed historical background as irrelevant to adjudications made under UNCLOS, and in any case, Nanhai Zhudao is a recent invention, and the first known mention of the invented term Four Sha is dated etymologically to 2017. Claims that the four island groups form a single archipelago are also geographically incorrect, and again are irrelevant to the case adjudicated under UNCLOS by the Hague Arbitration Tribunal. Nonetheless, the Chinese Military Bugle newspaper somewhat optimistically claimed on September 27 that “Nanhai Zhudao have long been widely recognized by the international community as part of China's territory.” Disputed South China Sea islands occupied by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, and the Philippines (Google Earth/Copernicus/CJRC)

https://maritime-executive.com/article/k.text: A new incident has been confirmed in the Strait of Hormuz, with reports that a tanker was struck after a lull of nearly a week. It comes after Donald Trump rejected overtures from Iran through the mediators, and IRGC leaders continue to assert that they control transits in the Strait. The IMO lists the latest attack as striking the Kuwaiti tanker Al Funtas (316,648 dwt). The vessel, which was built in 2014 and operates for Kuwait Oil Tankers, was not on the Iranian “non-compliant list” published by the so-called Persian Gulf Strait Authority. The Iranians, however, have threatened Kuwait’s tanker operations and listed several of its vessels. The tanker was making the transit “dark” and did not directly report the attack to UK Marine Trade Operations or MSCIO. The security services received the information "late" from a third party that the tanker was struck on Monday evening, September 28, while transiting the Strait. A fire resulted, but reports are that it was extinguished and the tanker was again underway. The extent of damage is not known. The strike came as Iran continues to attempt to assert that it still has total control and randomly targets vessels among the 10 to 20 a day believed to be transiting the Strait. U.S. officials deny Iran controls the Strait, but yesterday’s strike comes after at least four vessels were struck a week ago. The IMO is now setting the confirmed number of incidents involving vessels in the Persian Gulf area at 86. It says the confirmed death toll is 24 fatalities, although additional reports continue to come in. The Indian media is now confirming the death of two seafarers last week on the tanker El Gaia (IMO still lists them as missing), while the IMO also reports another death aboard the Cape Dao on September 23. Iran yesterday claimed it had turned back a total of 19 tankers on Friday and Saturday, saying that control of the region was split between its Army Navy and the IRGC Navy. The U.S. asserted it has sunk Iran’s Navy, but it has not been able to stop all the drone and missile attacks.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/eleico.text: Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) mostra o governador Tarcísio de Freitas ( Republicanos ), candidato à reeleição em São Paulo, com 44%, e Fernando Haddad ( PT ) com 24%.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: The Puntland Maritime Police Forces are reporting that they freed the product tanker Honour 25 , which had been held by pirates for over five months off the coast of Somalia. Unconfirmed reports from the local media indicate there may have been deaths among the crew and possibly the captain, although the official report only mentions injuries among the pirates. It is the second aggressive action by the police forces used to free vessels held by pirates in recent days and follows a similar operation led by Turkish forces to free a vessel transporting military equipment. It comes after the president of the semi-autonomous region of Puntland, Saeed Abdullahi Deni, said the government would “fight the pirates without mercy.” Local media reports are saying that two of the pirates were wounded in the operation to free the Honour 25 . An unspecified number were also reported to have been detained and arrested. The Honour 25 (3,089 dwt) was transporting oil products to Mogadishu when it was seized by the pirates on April 21 and taken into Somali coastal waters. EU NAVFOR Atalanta reported the day before that a fishing boat had been seized and believed it was used to stage the attack on the tanker. A Japanese Maritime Patrol aircraft was used to locate the vessel, but it was in Somali waters, so Atalanta forces, which reached the ship on April 25, were only observing, with the authority over the incident lying with the forces in Puntland. The ship had a crew of 17, mostly from Pakistan, as well as Sri Lanka and Indonesia, and Pakistan had attempted diplomatic efforts to release the crew. Unconfirmed media reports said the pirates were demanding $3 million for the ship and its crew. The authorities in Puntland announced on September 25 that they had freed another cargo ship, Sibu 1, during a 48-hour maritime operation. The vessel had been held since August 20. The Puntland forces said all the pirates were "apprehended," while media said some had been killed or wounded. The media also said as many as 47 people were arrested during the operation, but unconfirmed reports later said at least 19 pirates had escaped from a convoy that was to take them to Mogadishu.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543335-td.text: TDI-Brooks, in partnership with Taka Hydrocore Indonesia (THI), has been selected by the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources (MPRM) to execute a light geotechnical and environmental baseline survey program offshore Timor-Leste in support of the planned TLNG development. The program will provide data to support the routing of the Gas Export Pipeline from the Greater Sunrise field to Natarbora on the south coast of Timor-Leste, as well as the Bayu-Undan Pipeline Highway to Natarbora. The survey will utilize TDI-Brooks’ DP2 research vessel, R/V Nautilus . The geotechnical scope will include approximately 508 seabed tests, consisting of gravity CPTs (gCPT), piston cores (PC), box cores (BC), and cyclic T-bar measurements. In parallel, the environmental baseline study (EBS) will cover 16 provisional stations, including the collection of 40 sediment samples and 40 water samples. Field operations for both the geotechnical and environmental scopes are scheduled to commence in mid-January 2027. With over 30 years of experience, TDI-Brooks has successfully executed numerous offshore programs throughout Indonesia, including 15 multi-client seep-hunting campaigns. This survey will deliver critical geotechnical data to support pipeline routing, engineering design, and geohazard assessment for offshore development activities.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Kothe iniciou a operação de dois novos armazéns em Cajamar (SP) , que somam 64 mil m² de área e capacidade para 120 mil posições-palete . O complexo, formado por uma unidade de 44 mil m² e outra de 20 mil m², amplia a infraestrutura da companhia em São Paulo e integra armazenagem, transporte e distribuição em uma das principais regiões logísticas do país. A nova estrutura passa a fazer parte de uma rede nacional composta por 33 filiais e 18 armazéns, com mais de 450 mil posições-palete e frota própria superior a 1.500 veículos. A empresa conta ainda com mais de 3.150 colaboradores e presença em todo o Brasil. Segundo Paulo Kothe, diretor de Logística da companhia, a expansão em Cajamar faz parte da estratégia de ampliar a capacidade de atendimento e integrar as operações. “Mais do que aumentar espaço físico, estamos ampliando nossa capacidade de oferecer soluções integradas e atender operações cada vez mais complexas em escala nacional”, afirma. A localização foi um dos fatores considerados para a instalação do complexo. Cajamar tem acesso às rodovias Anhanguera, Bandeirantes, Rodoanel Mário Covas e Castello Branco, além de estar a aproximadamente 57 km do Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos, 64 km de Viracopos e 114 km do Porto de Santos. A estrutura também está conectada à rede de transporte da Kothe, que utiliza veículos equipados com tecnologia embarcada. A integração permite atender desde demandas regionais até operações que envolvem diferentes etapas da cadeia logística em escala nacional. Além de transporte, armazenagem e distribuição, a companhia oferece operações multiclientes, dedicadas e in house, além de serviços de cross-docking e paletização. Os processos são apoiados por sistemas de gestão, rastreabilidade e segurança, que permitem acompanhar a movimentação dos produtos.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A LATAM Cargo completou o primeiro ano da rota cargueira direta entre Miami, nos EUA, e Belo Horizonte/Confins , celebrando 829 toneladas de carga transportadas em 46 semanas. A operação, que ampliou a conectividade logística internacional de Minas Gerais, deve superar 900 toneladas movimentadas ao completar as 52 semanas do primeiro ano de operação. Operada uma vez por semana , aos sábados, a rota utiliza aeronaves Boeing 767-300F , com capacidade para transportar até 50 toneladas por voo . Entre as principais cargas movimentadas no período, estão equipamentos, componentes, peças e outros embarques destinados especialmente aos setores de mineração, ferroviário e industrial. A ligação direta com Miami, um dos principais centros de distribuição de cargas da rede da LATAM Cargo, oferece às empresas de Minas Gerais uma alternativa regular para seus fluxos internacionais, com ganhos de agilidade e previsibilidade logística. Para Andres Varela, diretor Comercial da LATAM Cargo para Estados Unidos e Ásia , a consolidação da rota neste primeiro ano reforça a importância de uma conexão cargueira direta entre Miami e Minas Gerais. "A rota atende setores relevantes para a economia mineira, como mineração, ferroviário e industrial, apoiando o transporte de equipamentos, componentes e peças com mais agilidade e previsibilidade. Seguimos comprometidos com uma operação sustentável no longo prazo e atentos à evolução da demanda para acompanhar as necessidades dos nossos clientes", afirma Andres. Uma das principais metas da BH Airport, concessionária do Aeroporto de Confins, é consolidar Minas Gerais como uma plataforma logística cada vez mais conectada ao mercado global. Como o único terminal alfandegado primário do estado, o aeroporto se destaca como um hub logístico multimodal, integrando os modais aéreo, marítimo e rodoviário. O complexo conta com mais de 15 mil metros quadrados dedicados à operação de cargas internacionais, e atende setores estratégicos da economia, como saúde, automotivo e mineração. O aeroporto tem conexões internacionais diretas como Miami, Orlando, Lisboa, Cidade do Panamá, Santiago e Buenos Aires.

https://safety4sea.com/psychological-tra.text: A new systematic review has highlighted psychological trauma as an under-recognised occupational health and safety risk for seafarers, with piracy, accidents, violence, deaths onboard, armed conflict and prolonged isolation among the experiences that can have lasting psychological consequences. P ublished on September 24, 2026, in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health , the review by Maria Carrera-Arce, Raphael Baumler and Charles Watkins examined the existing evidence on the causes, impacts and interventions related to psychological trauma among seafarers. The researchers identified 28 original studies for their final analysis. The authors note that seafaring combines exposure to acute traumatic events with chronic conditions that can make recovery particularly difficult. Unlike many shore-based workers, seafarers may remain onboard for months after a traumatic incident, with limited access to healthcare, psychological services, family networks or opportunities to leave the environment in which the event occurred. The review identifies piracy, serious occupational incidents, maritime disasters, violence, sexual harassment, suicide and deaths onboard as important sources of trauma. Extreme weather and other hazardous operating conditions can also contribute, while the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated how prolonged uncertainty and confinement can create additional psychological pressure. However, the researchers stress that trauma should not be understood only as the result of a single dramatic event. Chronic conditions can also become “traumatogenic”, particularly when individuals have limited ability to escape them. These conditions can include excessive working hours, chronic fatigue, prolonged separation from family, difficult onboard social environments, precarious employment conditions and continuous exposure to environmental and operational stressors such as noise, vibration and vessel movement.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/photon-ma.text: An electric workboat powered by Photon Marine outboards docked on the Erie Canal. [Photo: Photon Marine]An electric workboat powered by Photon Marine outboards docked on the Erie Canal. [Photo: Photon Marine] The NSF Energy Storage Engine in Upstate New York has selected Portland, Oregon-based electric marine innovator Photon Marine t o receive its inaugural $1 million MegaBoost award. It will put a production-grade electric workboat, a marine fast charger and a first-of-its-kind floating energy storage platform into service in New York State. It follows a pilot in which a small leased workboat, fitted with electric outboards from Photon Marine has been quietly doing ordinary things on the New York State Canal System, including pulling buoys, towing dredge pipe and carrying crews out to job sites. All without burning fuel. That boat, a leased hull fitted with electric outboards from Photon Marine, was a pilot project with the New York Power Authority and the New York State Canal Corporation. The crews wanted to know something practical. Not whether an electric workboat could exist, but whether it could get through a Tuesday. The NSF Energy Storage Engine says that the next chapter is considerably more ambitious. Building on real-world operating experience from the pilot, Photon Marine will develop something American waterways have not yet had: a complete marine electrification ecosystem, with the boat, the charger and the energy storage all designed to work together.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 29/09/2026 – Atenção à nova data: o webinário sobre o Tema 2.6 – “Sobrestadia de contêiner - Resolução ANTAQ nº 62/2021”, integrante da Agenda Regulatória 2025/2028, foi remarcado para o dia 08/10, às 15h. O encontro será realizado pela Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) para apresentar e debater o assunto com os interessados e esclarecer aspectos relacionados ao relatório de Análise de Impacto Regulatório (AIR) Preliminar. O prazo para participação na Tomada de Subsídios Pública SRG nº 03/2026 permanece inalterado. Até as 23h59 do dia 20/10, usuários e agentes do setor aquaviário nacional, além dos demais interessados, poderão encaminhar contribuições, subsídios e sugestões sobre o relatório de AIR Preliminar exclusivamente por meio de formulário eletrônico disponibilizado pela Agência. A tomada de subsídios é um mecanismo de participação que permite reunir informações e contribuições para subsidiar a construção de conhecimento e o desenvolvimento de propostas sobre determinada matéria. Na ANTAQ, o instrumento possibilita que os interessados colaborem por escrito. Como participar As contribuições deverão ser encaminhadas exclusivamente pelo formulário eletrônico da Tomada de Subsídios SRG nº 03/2026 até as 23h59 de 20/10. Não serão aceitas manifestações enviadas por outros meios. É possível encaminhar imagens digitais, como mapas, plantas e fotos, pelo e-mail srg@antaq.gov.br, desde que o participante esteja identificado e respeite o prazo. O conteúdo da contribuição, no entanto, deverá ser obrigatoriamente preenchido nos campos específicos do formulário eletrônico. As contribuições recebidas serão disponibilizadas no site da ANTAQ. A transmissão ocorrerá no dia 08/10, a partir das 15h, no canal oficial da Agência no YouTube. Os participantes que desejarem tirar dúvidas durante a videoconferência poderão escrever para o número de WhatsApp (61) 2029-6515.

https://gcaptain.com/cheniere-signs-22-y.text: Loading of the first commissioning cargo on board the Asia Vision at Cheniere's Sabine Pass LNG Terminal in February 2016. File photo: Cheniere Energy Cheniere Energy has signed a 22-year agreement to supply Brazil’s Petrobras with U.S. liquefied natural gas, adding another long-term customer as the company looks to support further expansion of its Gulf Coast export business. Under the sale and purchase agreement , Petrobras will purchase approximately 800,000 tonnes of LNG per year from Cheniere Marketing on a free-on-board basis. Cheniere did not disclose when deliveries will begin or the pricing formula for the contract. The free-on-board structure generally leaves the buyer responsible for arranging ocean transportation after the LNG is loaded, giving Petrobras flexibility over where it sends the cargoes. “We are pleased to enter into this multi-decade agreement with Petrobras, one of the largest energy companies in the world,” said Jack Fusco, Cheniere’s chairman, president and CEO.

https://gcaptain.com/fog-of-war-deepens-.text: File Photo: Oil tanker Al Shaffiah sails at the sea near the Omani coast, as seen from Musandam, Oman, June 26, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer The maritime picture in the Strait of Hormuz is becoming harder to verify, with another delayed report of a vessel strike raising questions over how much of the fighting is making it into the public record. UK Maritime Trade Operations said Monday it had received a “time-late” third-party report of a vessel struck by a suspected unknown projectile while transiting the strait Sunday evening. The impact caused a fire, which was later extinguished. The vessel remained underway and its crew was safe. Notably, UKMTO classified Warning 143-26 as “suspicious activity,” rather than an attack, despite reporting that the vessel had been struck by a projectile. The warning came after Iran claimed over the weekend that its forces had targeted or intercepted 19 vessels operating outside Tehran-designated routes through Hormuz — 12 on Friday and seven on Saturday. Iran has not identified the ships or produced evidence showing that 19 vessels were struck.

https://petronoticias.com.br/a-argentina.text: O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, afirmou que seu governo buscará arbitragem internacional contra o Reino Unido devido a um projeto petrolífero próximo às Ilhas Malvinas. O gabinete de Milei afirmou ter dado ao Reino Unido duas semanas para interromper os trabalhos no Sea Lion , um campo petrolífero offshore que está sendo desenvolvido pela Petroleum e pela empresa britânica Rockhopper Exploration. Caso isso não aconteça, a Argentina afirma que solicitará ao Tribunal Internacional do Direito do Mar, um tribunal marítimo com sede em Hamburgo, que ordene a suspensão temporária do projeto. “A Argentina não ficará de braços cruzados” , afirmou o comunicado presidencial, acusando o Reino Unido de causar danos “ irreversíveis e irreparáveis”. O tribunal, um órgão independente estabelecido pela Convenção das Nações Unidas sobre o Direito do Mar de 1982, pode emitir ordens de emergência juridicamente vinculativas. Mas mesmo que ordenasse ao Reino Unido a suspensão do projeto, não teria meios de obrigar o governo a cumprir a ordem. O Reino Unido rejeita a reivindicação de soberania da Argentina sobre as Ilhas Malvinas, argumentando que os habitantes das ilhas têm o direito de determinar seu próprio futuro e desenvolver seus recursos naturais. Em um referendo realizado em 2013, os residentes das Ilhas Malvinas votaram esmagadoramente a favor da permanência como território ultramarino britânico, embora a Argentina alegue que as ilhas foram povoadas ilegalmente. A disputa representa um conflito crescente por recursos que podem transformar a economia do arquipélago pouco povoado do Atlântico Sul. O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Argentina, Pablo Quirno , elogiou a iniciativa de Milei como “ um passo histórico e sem precedentes ” na campanha de quase dois séculos do país para garantir a soberania sobre o arquipélago. “ Quem explorar ou explorar nossos recursos naturais nas Malvinas sem autorização argentina deverá arcar com as consequências”, escreveu ele no X, usando o nome argentino para as ilhas. Milei , que se autodenominava “ anarcocapitalista”, inicialmente atraiu o desprezo de seus oponentes nacionalistas por sua postura conciliatória em relação à Grã-Bretanha e professava admiração por Margaret Thatcher, a primeira-ministra em tempos de guerra odiada na Argentina por ordenar a recaptura das ilhas. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, um aliado próximo do líder argentino, sugere que poderia reconsiderar a neutralidade de longa data de Washington na disputa. Na semana passada, Um míssil de fabricação francesa, Exocet, lançado pela Argentina, afundou uma fragata inglesa durante a guerra Milei dedicou grande parte de seu discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU à reivindicação de soberania da Argentina, acusando o organismo internacional de negligenciar
