https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Demonstrating the strength in the cruise industry and its ability to navigate global challenges, Carnival Corporation reported quarterly results with all-time highs in revenues, net income, and yields, while presenting a strong outlook. Indeed, management said accelerating demand and even stronger cost discipline drove “results ahead of our expectations.” CEO Josh Weinstein pointed to accelerated bookings that had started in June and carried through the quarter. Despite concerns over the economy and geopolitical disturbances, he believes consumers are placing a high value on vacation experiences. He emphasized the value for the dollar that the company’s brands provide while reporting they are already half booked for 2027. “Looking further ahead, 2028 is also off to an excellent start at higher occupancy and prices than last year.” He also pointed to volumes that were “meaningfully ahead of last year,” while critically highlighting that it is far outpacing capacity growth. Carnival Corporation is taking a pause this year in new ship deliveries as an aftereffect of the COVID-19 pandemic. It is scheduled to resume deliveries next year, but only has five ships on order, all for its Carnival Cruise Line brand. Weinstein has said going forward the company will have a more measured pace for newbuilds. The company reported a $150 million impact from fuel costs, but said it had been able to overcome that through strong cost controls along with improvements in net yields. This was also despite a close-in 2025 decision to redeploy capacity away from the previously planned first quarter 2026 Arabian Gulf voyages. The corporation achieved an all-time high net income in the third quarter of $1.9 billion on revenues of more than $8.4 billion. Analysts noted that some of the strongest growth appeared to be coming from Carnival’s “Onboard & Other” segment, likely demonstrating passengers' willingness to spend for extras aboard the ships and the revenues coming from the new Celebration Key destination on Grand Bahama and the completed renovations at both the newly named RelaxAway destination, Half Moon Cay in the Bahamas, and Isla Tropicale at Roatán in Honduras. The company reported almost 2.5 million guests at Celebration Key in its first year, and more than 250,000 guests each at the other private destinations. As an indicator of the strong outlook, the company said consumer deposits for future cruises were at record levels in the third quarter, up nearly seven percent compared to the prior year. Deposits reached $7.6 billion, setting a new record, up by $0.5 billion despite the corporation’s flat capacity growth over the next 12 months.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Japan’s first Arctic research vessel with full icebreaking capabilities is nearing completion. In preparation for the delivery of the vessel later this year and its first research trip in the summer of 2027, the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) contracted with Mitsui O.S.K. Lines for the operation of the vessel named Mirai II. Under the terms of the unique agreement, the shipping company will provide operational services and related work for Mirai II. Under the agreement, MOL will be responsible for operating the ship, which will serve as an international research platform MOL reports it has been preparing to establish the operational framework for the Mirai II since it was provisionally selected in 2023 for the role as operator. As part of these preparations, in February, MOL conducted polar survival training for the seafarers scheduled to serve aboard the vessel. The training simulated emergency situations in extremely cold environments and included cold-water swimming exercises using immersion suits, drills for escaping from the sea onto ice, and outdoor activities on ice. The naming and launching ceremony was held in March 2025 at the Japan Marine United (JMU) Corporation's Yokohama Works. Currently, outfitting work, including the installation of living quarters, observation equipment, electrical systems, and the engine room, is ongoing. The vessel has completed its first sea trials in preparation for the vessel's delivery on December 18, 2026. JAMSTEC highlights that the 13,000 gross ton vessel is larger and more capable than the original Mirai, which was retired in December. The new ship is an icebreaker capable of continuously breaking flat, one-year ice up to a 1.2-meter thickness at a speed of 3 knots. The previous vessel was able to enter the Arctic Sea, making its northernmost transit in 2010. The new ship is 128 meters (420 feet) in length. It has accommodations for up to 97 crew and scientists.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Ukraine’s Defense Forces are being accused of an attack on a Turkish-owned bulker that has left one seafarer missing. There has been no official comment on the incident, but the family of the missing sailor posted online, and independent watchdog organizations pieced together some of the details. The vessel Aroyat (18,315 dwt) was reported to have been in the vicinity of Novorossiysk, Russia, when it was struck on September 27. The vessel’s AIS signal shows its last port call in Georgia, but it is unclear if it had loaded in Russia or was approaching the port. The vessel was hit by what it believed to be an aerial drone, which started a large fire in the accommodation block of the ship. Media reports say the ship had seven Egyptian, six Syrian, and three Turkish crewmembers. Pictures posted online show extensive damage to the ship. The reports said it was disabled and towed back to Turkey. The ship is registered in Palau and has been operated for Turkish companies since 2022. Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the dry bulk carrier Aroyat on Sept. 27 while it was heading to a Russian port, causing a fire in the stern. The vessel carried a crew of 7 Egyptian, 6 Syrian and 3 Turkish sailors, with casualties reported among them. In 2023, nearly three years… pic.twitter.com/wvmuMjUGNQ The family of the vessel’s Turkish second engineer posted online that he is missing and has not been heard from. They said he was not among the rescued crewmembers, but they held out hope he might be somewhere in Russia. They were asked if anyone knows anything or has seen the engineer. Furthermore, they said the authorities were promising a complete search of the vessel now that it is in Turkey.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: The mystery continues around the circumstances around the MSC Hermes III containership after Vietnamese authorities reported an emergency evacuation of a crewmember from the vessel on Tuesday, September 29. Last week, on September 22, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore reported it had coordinated the evacuation of the vessel, which later appeared to be under tow. The Vietnam Maritime Search and Rescue Coordination Center reported it received an urgent call for aid on September 28 while the vessel was south of Vietnam. According to the statement, the captain advised that a 30-year-old crewmember had suffered a “work-related accident” that had resulted in a severe head injury from a fall. The crewmember had been experiencing from “unusual symptoms, vomiting, and unconsciousness.” The victim's condition was assessed as serious and potentially life-threatening, requiring urgent medical assistance. Medical evacuation for a crewmember who fell unconscious and suffered a severe head injury (VMSRCC) At the time, the ship was reported to be located approximately 30 nautical miles northeast of Vung Tau Ward (Ho Chi Minh City). The Vietnam Maritime Administration dispatched a specialized search and rescue vessel, SAR 272, along with two medical officers. The rescue boat departed at 9:15 PM on September 28, reaching the containership at 1:30 AM on September 29. After providing initial medical assistance, the victim was removed and landed in Ho Chi Minh City at 6:30 AM and transferred to a hospital. Media reports are saying it is suspected the individual might have inhaled toxic gas. The authorities in Singapore did not report why the 25 crewmembers had initially abandoned the ship while it was approximately 300 km (186 miles) east of Vietnam. Reports said they had entered the lifeboats and were taken aboard another MSC vessel. The MSC Hermes III was drifting before tugs took it in tow to Vietnam. Pictures released by the Vietnamese authorities of yesterday’s rescue appear to show crewmembers aboard the vessel. There are no visible signs of damage, such as from a fire, and the freefall lifeboat is in place.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Fires on vessels present serious dangers to passengers, crew, and firefighters; can have significant environmental impact; and can affect billion-dollar commerce in busy ports. Marine fires present unique hazards that are incredibly dangerous and challenging incidents for firefighters to respond to, including vessel instability, tight onboard spaces, and the need for specialized resources that are not typically available in many ports. The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), the non-partisan, fact-based arm of Congress, recently published a report highlighting the prevalence of these fires and the Coast Guard’s efforts address them. According to Coast Guard data, 886 nearshore marine fires occurred between 2015 and 2025. About a quarter of these were classified as serious because they resulted in either death, injury, over $200,000 in damage, or a total loss of the vessel. The figure below shows the locations of these marine fires, including incidents where fire departments responded. Fifty-five people died in serious marine fires from 2015 through 2025. These included the deaths of land-based firefighters, such as a 2023 incident where two Newark firefighters died while responding to a fire on a large vehicle cargo vessel. Following the Newark fire, the Coast Guard established a task force to identify and address marine firefighting challenges. The task force took several steps to address these challenges, including developing guidance for standardizing marine firefighting plans and a tool to quickly collect and share information during a marine fire. But some gaps persist: Training for firefighters. The Coast Guard, the National Transportation Safety Board, and fire chiefs have found that available training on preparing for and responding to marine fires for land-based firefighters is limited. In response, the Coast Guard partnered with an emergency response organization to develop online training videos on marine fires for firefighters. But Coast Guard officials and fire chiefs told us that ensuring firefighters have hands-on training, like vessel tours and exercises with “boots on boats,” will better prepares firefighters for complex marine fires, instead of virtual or classroom training alone.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/wti_discoun.text: In a report sent to Rigzone late Tuesday, Standard Chartered Bank Energy Research Head Emily Ashford highlighted that West Texas Intermediate’s (WTI) discount to Brent continued to deepen and was sitting at over $12 per barrel, “its widest since early May”. “The spread is not just the result of Brent acquiring more geopolitical premium, but also WTI-specific weakness,” Ashford noted in the report. “There is explicit evidence that the market is pricing in the risk of a not-immaterial cut to U.S. refinery runs. This is being compounded by high freight rates preventing the usual Brent-WTI arbitrage from closing the spread,” Ashford added. “Given the escalation in VLCC freight costs, WTI needs a steeper discount to Brent to compensate for these costs. If Washington were to step decisively away from the risk of export restrictions, we could see WTI’s discount narrow rapidly,” Ashford continued. In the report, Ashford went on to note that diesel has moved from a market problem to a policy problem. “The next few weeks could clarify how far Washington is prepared to intervene in U.S. product markets as the U.S. midterm elections approach,” Ashford said.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543359-ch.text: China Three Gorges Corporation has connected the first batch of turbines at its Yangjiang Qingzhou V and VII offshore wind project to the grid, enabling the transfer of clean power from the site located offshore Guangdong Province. The connection is using a ±500 kV direct-current transmission system to carry power from around 70 kilometers offshore mainland China. The project comprises 163 turbines, each rated at more than 12 MW, giving the development a combined capacity of more than 1.95 GW. Power from the turbines is collected through 30 circuits of 66 kV subsea array cables and transmitted to the offshore converter station, where it is stepped up and converted from 66 kV alternating current to ±500 kV direct current for transmission to shore. The system uses two DC subsea cables forming a single transmission circuit capable of carrying up to 2 million kWh of electricity per hour. China Three Gorges described the project as the world's first integrated offshore wind flexible DC transmission project and said its transmission system has the world's highest voltage level and largest transmission capacity of its type. It also uses what the company described as the world's first ±500 kV DC submarine cable for offshore wind.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543352-ka.text: Kazakhstan has restarted enforcement action to collect a 2.3 trillion tenge ($5.22 billion) fine from the international consortium operating the Kashagan oilfield, Interfax reported on Wednesday, citing the Ministry of Justice. https://safety4sea.com/marine-fires-rema.text: A vessel fire can turn a routine voyage into a race against time within minutes, with confined spaces, complex systems and hazardous cargo making every blaze potentially catastrophic. U .S. Coast Guard data show that 886 nearshore marine fires were reported between 2015 and 2025, highlighting the persistent risks faced by seafarers, passengers, firefighters and vessels operating in U.S. waters. According to the “Additional Action Needed to Address Marine Firefighting Challenges” study conducted by the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), while many incidents were contained, roughly one-quarter—206 fires—qualified as serious marine incidents, resulting in death, injury requiring professional medical treatment, more than $200,000 in property damage or the total loss of a vessel. The figures underscore the distinctive nature of marine firefighting. Seven fire chiefs interviewed across the United States described vessel fires as generally low-frequency, high-consequence events, where limited opportunities for intervention can quickly give way to life-threatening conditions. The risks came sharply into focus following a 2023 marine fire that claimed the lives of two firefighters. In response, the Coast Guard established a task force to examine the challenges surrounding marine firefighting and identify measures to strengthen preparedness and response capabilities. While the task force has taken several steps, significant gaps remain. Coast Guard data indicate that marine fires frequently originate in vessel galleys and engine rooms, areas where heat, electrical systems, fuel and machinery can create a particularly dangerous combination. Investigations by the National Transportation Safety Board have identified a range of contributing factors, including inadequate maintenance, damaged vessel components, poor oversight during fueling or cargo operations, and hazardous equipment or materials.

https://safety4sea.com/seafarer-rescued-.text: A seafarer aboard the Liberian-flagged MSC HERMES III was rescued after developing severe symptoms and losing consciousness in an incident suspected to involve toxic gas exposure off Vietnam. T he Vietnam Maritime Search and Rescue Coordination Centre (Vietnam MRCC) received an urgent medical assistance request from MSC Vietnam Co., Ltd. on September 28 after the seafarer developed abnormal symptoms, including vomiting, before becoming unconscious. His condition was assessed as serious and potentially life-threatening. At the time, MSC HERMES III was sailing toward Buoy No. 0 in Vung Tau ward, Ho Chi Minh City, where it was scheduled to undergo repair and maintenance work. Following the request, Vietnam MRCC provided initial medical advice and coordinated the rescue response. At 9:15 pm on September 28, it deployed the specialised SAR 272 search and rescue vessel from its standby berth in Phuoc Thang ward. Two medics from the Ho Chi Minh City Border Guard also joined the operation to provide emergency medical care to the seafarer. The rescue team maintained communication with MSC HERMES III and coordinated with relevant authorities to determine the fastest way to evacuate the seafarer.

https://safety4sea.com/seafarer-reported.text: A Turkish seafarer is reportedly missing following a drone strike on the bulk carrier Aroyat as the vessel approached the Russian port of Novorossiysk on 27 September. T he vessel was sailing from Poti, Georgia, to Novorossiysk when it was reportedly struck by an aerial drone. The impact sparked a significant fire in the accommodation block and stern area, leaving the bulk carrier disabled. An official casualty list has not been released. However, Turkish media reports say the family of the vessel’s second engineer has reported him missing since the incident. The family said they have been unable to establish contact with him, while continuing to hope that he may be somewhere in Russia or could still be aboard the vessel. Following the attack, Aroyat was towed to Turkey, where it is expected to undergo further inspection, searches and repairs. The circumstances surrounding the reported disappearance of the second engineer remain unclear, and there has been no official confirmation of his whereabouts. Ukrainian authorities have not claimed responsibility for the attack. The incident comes amid continued concerns over the safety of commercial shipping and seafarers operating in the Black Sea, where merchant vessels have increasingly been exposed to the wider risks associated with the war.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-maib-annual-re.text: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published its Annual Report 2025, setting out accident activity, investigations and safety recommendations while identifying several areas of continuing concern across the maritime sector. T he UK MAIB received 1,585 reports during 2025 , compared with 1,515 in 2024. It started 16 new investigations during the year, seven of which involved loss of life, and published 17 accident investigation reports. For merchant shipping, MAIB identifies the standard of watchkeeping, lookout and application of the Collision Regulations as continuing areas of concern. The report cites the March 2025 collision between the containership Solong and the tanker Stena Immaculate as an example of how departure from established seafaring practice can result in loss of life, pollution and vessel loss. The Solong/Stena Immaculate investigation remained underway when the annual report was prepared. MAIB also places renewed emphasis on the effective use of safety management systems and the ISM Code , stressing the importance of applying basic risk controls in practice.

https://safety4sea.com/recent-jotuns-pro.text: The application of a new hull coating to the Handysize bulk carrier MAAS CONFIDENCE highlights the role of coating selection and application quality in maintaining hull performance under changing trading conditions. J otun’s SeaQuest Endura II coating was applied to the vessel during dry-docking at ONEX Syros Shipyards in July 2026. The ship is managed by Hellas Confidence Shipmanagement S.A., and Jotun coating advisers supported and monitored the application process, according to the company’s announcement. Commenting on the application, Raoul de Troije, Director of Hellas Confidence Shipmanagement S.A ., said: “The finish achieved with SeaQuest Endura II has exceeded our expectations.” Giannis Vamvakousis, General Manager of ONEX Syros Shipyards, highlighted the delivery schedule and application conditions: “O ur teams in Syros delivered the vessel on schedule and to the standard our partners expect, providing the right environment for Jotun’s application team to achieve this result.” Jotun describes SeaQuest Endura II as a ”tin-free biocidal foul-release coating, developed as part of its Tailored to Trade™ approach and included in its Hull Performance Solutions (HPS) 2.0 offering.” Designed for vessels with unpredictable trading patterns, the coating incorporates Flexcure™ technology, which Jotun says supports adhesion and levelling, optimised curing speed, humidity tolerance and extended repairability.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/somali-p.text: Somali pirates killed five crew members of the hijacked MT Honour 25 petroleum products tanker before it was rescued by security forces, Somalia's semi-autonomous state of Puntland said on Tuesday. Puntland's authorities said they also rescued a second vessel on Tuesday that had been hijacked in May. The deaths aboard the Palau-flagged ship appear to be the first at the hands of Somali pirates in over a decade. The ship with 17 crew members was seized by pirates in April during a resurgence of Somali piracy that experts have attributed, in part, to impacts of the Iran war, including elevated oil prices that make tankers ⁠more attractive targets. Puntland's information ministry said in a statement that a rescue mission had successfully freed the ship and captured 16 pirates. https://splash247.com/first-somali-pirac.text: Five seafarers were killed by Somali pirates before Puntland security forces recaptured the hijacked product tanker Honour 25, marking what appear to be the first crew deaths at the hands of Somali pirates in more than a decade. Puntland’s information ministry said three Pakistanis, one Indian and one Myanmar national were killed before forces boarded the Palau-flagged vessel. Four other crew — three Pakistanis and an Indian — were injured, while 16 suspected pirates were captured. The Honour 25, carrying 17 crew and around 18,500 barrels of oil, was seized on April 21 roughly 30 nautical miles off Puntland. Splash reported at the time that its hijacking formed part of four attacks in four days, prompting regional security authorities to raise the Somali coast threat level. By July, conditions aboard the tanker had deteriorated severely, with food reduced largely to rice, unsafe drinking water and several crewmembers suffering health problems. Splash also reported gunfire between rival pirate groups around the vessel. Puntland forces also freed the hijacked tanker Eureka on Tuesday after its captors fled ashore. Together with last week’s rescue of the US-sanctioned Sibu 1, five of the six vessels held by Somali pirates in late August have now been released. The revival of Somali piracy has accelerated through 2026. Splash reported eight successful hijackings since April by mid-September, with groups increasingly using captured fishing vessels and dhows as motherships to extend operations far offshore.

https://splash247.com/90m-for-near-17-ye.text: The tanker S&P market continues to deliver eye-catching prices. A sale has raised eyebrows among brokers who report a non-eco suezmax selling for $90m — a price difficult to imagine only weeks ago. The deal involves Greek shipping heavyweight George Procopiou’s Dynacom Tankers, selling the 150,000 dwt Karolos (built December 2009 at New Times Shipbuilding in China) for around $90m. The price is striking; a nine-year-old, Korean-built suezmax was reported sold for just under $100m only a few weeks ago. A suezmax positioned in the Mediterranean can be fixed at $372,600 per day, according to the latest rate indications from Arrow. The reported Karolos transaction follows the August sale of the Sonangol Namibe (158,425 dwt, built 2007 at Daewoo), which changed hands for just under $50m despite being 19 years old and firmly within the age bracket commonly associated with shadow fleet trading.

https://splash247.com/gulf-crude-exports.text: Middle Eastern crude exports have staged a dramatic recovery in September, with tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz rebounding while Saudi Arabia simultaneously restarts its alternative Red Sea export route. Updated Kpler data cited by Reuters put crude exports from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait and Iran at 16.33m barrels per day this month, the highest since the war with Iran began in late February and just under 80% of pre-conflict levels. February exports stood at 19.51m barrels per day. Hormuz flows have recovered particularly sharply. Kpler estimates September crude movements through the strait at around 9.72m barrels per day, including ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, compared with levels as low as 2.2m barrels per day in late July. Saudi Arabia has driven much of the rebound, with exports expected at around 5.4m barrels per day in September, more than double August’s 2.45m barrels per day. Ras Tanura has returned to the centre of Saudi export activity following the September attack on the kingdom’s East-West Pipeline. Shipments from the Gulf terminal have climbed to around 3.25m barrels per day this month from 929,000 barrels per day in August. Kpler counted 19 VLCCs, each carrying roughly 2m barrels of Saudi crude, exiting Hormuz in a single week. At the same time, Saudi Arabia has restarted tanker loadings at Yanbu after repairing the East-West Pipeline, restoring another outlet that bypasses Hormuz.

https://splash247.com/cosco-shipping-spe.text: COSCO Shipping Specialized Carriers is pressing ahead with another major fleet expansion, lining up 14 more 60,000 dwt multipurpose heavylift ships through a mix of owned newbuildings and long-term bareboat charters. The Shanghai-listed unit of COSCO Shipping Group has approved eight vessels at COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry’s Dalian yard for up to RMB2.624bn ($392m), or a maximum of $49m per ship. Deliveries are slated across 2029 and 2030. The related-party deal will be placed through COSCO Shipping (Hong Kong) Investment and Development or affiliated companies and still requires shareholder approval before contracts are signed. A separate filing revealed another six 60,000 dwt heavylifters. COSCO’s Xiamen-based specialized transport subsidiary will bareboat charter the ships for around 20 years, with the vessels planned for construction at Huanghai Shipbuilding. The lessors will be selected from CITIC Financial Leasing, ICBC Financial Leasing, CMB Financial Leasing and CZBank Financial Leasing. Charter hire has been set at around $9,100 per vessel per day, including tax, putting annual payments across the six ships at about $20m. COSCO will be responsible for managing the vessels. No delivery schedule for the Huanghai series was disclosed. The move comes just two months after COSCO Specialized lined up eight 60,000 dwt heavylifters at CSSC’s Chengxi Shipyard in a deal worth up to $392m, with a similar delivery schedule. Industry sources suggest that this deal has now shifted to the Dalian yard. Earlier this year, the company also contracted four 40,000 dwt multipurpose heavylift ships at Chengxi for about $213m, due from mid-2028 through early 2029.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The nuclear aircraft carrier Harry S. Truman (CVN 75) has shifted from Naval Station Norfolk to HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding to officially begin its multi-year Refueling and Complex Overhaul. It comes after the Navy confirmed the awarding of a contract valued at $5.1 billion for what becomes the eighth Nimitz-class aircraft carrier to undergo the long-term renovation. The carrier, which was commissioned in 1998, has been at its homeport in Norfolk since returning from the Middle East in June 2025, after leading the response to the Houthis in Yemen. It completed a 251-day deployment, during which the Navy reported the strike group completed more than 13,000 sorties and 25,000 flight hours. It included the strike group delivering 124,000 pounds of ordnance on a single day, which was reported to be the single largest strike from a carrier. However, it also included a collision with a merchant ship near the Suez Canal and the loss of two F/A-18 Super Hornets overboard and a third shot down in a friendly-fire incident. The Navy had considered in 2019 possibly mothballing the carrier instead of proceeding with the life extension. It now emphasizes that it is using an innovative Fixed Ceiling Incentive structure for the refueling and complex overhaul, which appropriately shares risk and incentivizes improved shipbuilder performance to achieve required delivery dates. HII reports Newport News has been awarded a $5,099,973,132 contract for the refueling and complex overhaul (RCOH). The contract includes options that, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of the contract to $5,183,380,744. It comes as Newport News is completing a similar project for USS John C. Stennis (CVN 74), which has been at the yard since 2021. Reports indicate it is a year behind schedule but is expected to return to the Navy in October. Work is already visible from the "Smart Start" that began in November 2025 to prepare for the RCOH (USN) Truman began its formal RCOH “Smart Start” period in November 2025, preparing the ship and crew for the multi-year maintenance and modernization effort. Pictures released by the Navy show tugboats assisting the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier departing Naval Station Norfolk for the relocation to Newport News Shipbuilding. Work was already visible on the vessel.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump unveiled a $54 billion commitment from Korean investors to build the Alaska LNG pipeline and liquefaction project, a unique energy export initiative that has been under discussion for years. "Today we're thrilled to announce one of the largest energy infrastructure investments in American history," Trump said. "Thanks to the agreements my administration has secured with the Republic of Korea, they will invest up to $200 billion to build a six gigawatt power generation facility in Texas, . . . eight new large scale nuclear power plants, and at long last, the Alaska liquefied natural gas pipeline [Alaska LNG]." Alaska LNG is a megaproject that would pipe gas all the way from the North Slope to a liquefaction plant on the Gulf of Alaska, and if built, it would be among the most ambitious infrastructure development projects in recent U.S. history. The 3.5 billion cubic foot-per-day pipeline would traverse the permafrost of the North Slope, the rugged mountains of central Alaska, and wend its way southwards to Cook Inlet, covering a distance equal to a transit from Missouri to New York. On arrival, the gas would be liquefied at a multibillion-dollar plant and shipped to Asian customers. Alaska LNG was first conceived of as a commercial project with big-name private investors, including BP, ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips. All three oil majors backed out by 2016, leaving the investment company Glenfarne Group and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation in charge of moving it forward. The consortium has been gradually advancing through permitting ever since, with backing from state leaders: it secured its FERC export permit in 2020 and received a key approval from the Department of Energy in 2023, derisking investment. Climate activists oppose the project because of its carbon footprint, and it would undoubtedly face legal challenges ahead of construction, but it is locally popular. It has at least two early commercial commitments: two Japanese LNG buyers have agreed to buy about 10 percent of production if it is built. In a statement, a White House spokesperson said that investments in Alaska's infrastructure fulfill "day one promises to unleash American energy, unlock Alaska’s extraordinary resource potential, and accelerate America’s nuclear energy renaissance."

https://maritime-executive.com/article/l.text: In a development which has surprised even traders in the London LNG commodities market, prices for LNG have been falling and come off year-long peaks in recent days, despite there being no agreement on a return to normality in the Strait of Hormuz. With vessels navigating with AIS transponders off, and all operators maintaining tight operational security over movements, it is difficult to give an accurate picture of traffic flows through the Strait. But commodity brokers and ship brokers guess that the lift of LNG through the Strait is at about 20% of pre-war levels, with shuttle tankers conducting ship-to-ship transfer of LNG once safely out of the danger zone. LNGCs moving UAE-loaded LNG appear to be taking the Omani coastal route. LNG carriers which have loaded at Ras Laffan and appear slated to unload in Pakistan appear also to be taking the southern route, with the possibility that the IRGC are holding fire. The shortfall between what is getting through the Strait in recent weeks and what normally does, looks as if it is being filled by a cutback in demand consequent upon higher prices, but primarily from increased production in Canada, the United Sates and Malaysia, and to a lesser degree from Australia and Oman. That the market has achieved balance is suggested by storage levels in India, where facilities are nearly reaching capacity, and indeed with some stock now being sold on. Whilst the global shortage of diesel is well-advertised, and is reflected in very high prices at pumps in the United States, shortages of supply are not being felt in every product category. LNG prices have fallen, and crude prices are settling after the scare cause by Houthi disruptions to the Saudi East-West pipeline, now coming back on stream. 10 million barrels were loaded at Yanbu on September 28, and Kpler reports that Saudi crude loadings over the last week averaged 8.5mbd, well above pre-war levels. Crude exports from Gulf countries are now running at about 80% of pre-war levels. Prices have certainly risen during the crisis, but not perhaps to the levels which analysts expected, and suggesting that supply and demand mechanisms have been able to handle the shocks to the system. In large part, the maritime community has shown a high degree of agility, switching rapidly from previously established trading routes to alternatives – and commanding premium rates for doing so. Two particular problems need to be addressed with some urgency: the lack of alternative strategic trade routes along with identification of potential choke points against which contingency plans must be in place, and the failure of some nations to have adequate reserves and to preserve domestic production of critical petrochemical products such as diesel and jet fuel.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: The authorities in the semi-autonomous region of Puntland within Somalia confirmed the earlier reports that five seafarers were killed on Tuesday, September 29, as they proceeded with a crackdown on the pirates operating along the coast. The reports are now indicating that all the vessels being held in the Puntland region have been freed, although one remains held in a neighboring state. The details on the death of the five seafarers vary by report, but they were all crew aboard the tanker Honour 25 , which had been held since April 21. The Puntland Maritime Police Force said the five killed included three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar, and one from India. In its version of the incident, it says the pirates killed the crewmembers before the government operation began. Local reports claim the crew was killed after an exchange of gunfire between the pirates and the Puntland forces. One report says the pirates were preparing to flee the vessel and that they had offered to surrender. The unconfirmed reports indicate that among the dead are the tanker’s chief engineer, second officer, and third engineer. An Indian seafarers union said the Indian dead were the ship's cook and the fifth person was a sailor. In addition, four crewmembers were also wounded among the total of 17 aboard. Three are Pakistani, and one is Indian. The Puntland Maritime Police Force said that a total of 16 pirates were apprehended and turned over to the authorities. It reports that others fled to shore and inland and that they were being pursued.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: The Indian Coast Guard reported a large-scale drug seizure, which it says was completed after a “hot pursuit” of an Iranian dhow. A search of the apprehended vessel found 526 kg of high-grade heroin and methamphetamine valued at approximately $312 million. The authorities were working on intelligence and a “hot tip” and formed a joint effort between the Coast Guard and the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad. They mounted a coordinated air and sea surveillance operation. The effort located a “suspicious Iranian dhow” in the Arabian Sea west of Lakshadweep in the southwestern area of the subcontinent. The Coast Guard reports they maintained sustained tracking of the suspicious vessel before launching the interdiction. The vessel was boarded and searched, and the narcotics were seized. They also arrested five Pakistani nationals who were aboard the dhow. The Coast Guard escorted the vessel to Mumbai. A multi-agency investigation is underway and will be followed by prosecution. They believe their effort neutralized a major transnational narco-smuggling operation.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Three vessels reported being struck on Tuesday, September 29, in the area around the Strait of Hormuz as Iran appears to be lashing out to demonstrate that it is still threatening vessels. While it brings the total number of vessels struck to four so far this week, observers point to increasing oil flows and vessel traffic in the region. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported the incidents, although few details were provided. It said that the information had come from verified sources but was delayed in being transmitted. It was unclear when the strikes took place. It identified all three incidents as involving tankers without details on the extent of the damage, while an unconfirmed report said one of the vessels was an LNG carrier. Two of the vessels were identified in the tracking by the International Maritime Organization, with both being crude oil tankers flying the Liberian flag and sustaining damage. One VLCC, the Mersin Prosperity (299,319 dwt), is operated by ADNOC. The other tanker appeared to be a smaller vessel, possibly involved in the shuttle operations that have arisen to get oil from the Gulf states to tankers waiting south of the Strait in the Arabian Sea. This tanker was identified as Sinbad (115,949 dwt), and it was last reported at Fujairah. Both tankers appeared to be making the transit dark. Iran’s Fars News Agency reported that warning shots were fired on Tuesday at vessels violating the Strait of Hormuz. It did not provide details on the incidents but said they accounted for the reports of explosions near Qeshm Island and other points along the coast. At the same time, an IRGC spokesperson, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, repeated the refrain that Iran controls the Strait. The Wana News Agency quotes him saying vessels attempting to transit the Strait without permission either will be targeted or will hit a mine. Iran continues to make these claims while evidence builds that oil volumes are rising from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq. “Windward MIOC assesses that Iran is less able to constrain southern-corridor traffic than it was in mid-summer, as rising crude flows continue despite the threat to individual vessels,” writes Windward’s Zane Amundsen, MIOC Middle East Desk Lead. He cites 55 AIS-visible transits from September 16 to 23, while also concluding “the true number of transits is almost certainly higher.”

Pesquisas Quaest de setembro mostram que o voto útil já começou em 5 estados. O movimento esvazia a terceira via e beneficia quem lidera a disputa. A migração de votos amplia a liderança de Lula em Pernambuco e a de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio de Janeiro, em São Paulo e no Distrito Federal. Minas Gerais é a exceção por ser o estado mais equilibrado. O fenômeno segue a teoria da "deserção estratégica", que se acelera com a proximidade do pleito. Em 1997, o cientista político Gary Cox publicou "Making Votes Count", o livro que se tornou a referência sobre como as regras eleitorais moldam o comportamento do eleitor. A ideia central é simples: o voto útil não é um ato de traição às convicções, mas um cálculo. O eleitor abandona o candidato de sua preferência quando percebe que ele não tem chance de vencer e que insistir nele pode facilitar a vitória justamente daquele que mais rejeita. Para esse cálculo acontecer, Cox mostra que três condições precisam estar presentes: o eleitor se importa com o resultado (não vota apenas para expressar uma identidade), sabe quem é viável e quem não é, e essa informação é compartilhada por todos — o que, nas democracias modernas, é o papel das pesquisas. Quando os três ingredientes se combinam, a disputa converge para os dois nomes com chances reais, e os demais encolhem. Cox chama isso de "deserção estratégica". As últimas três rodadas da Quaest em São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Pernambuco e Distrito Federal mostram esse mecanismo em funci

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543377-wi.text: Windward Offshore celebrated the official naming of its Commissioning Service Operation Vessel (CSOV), Windward Munich, in Hamburg on September 22, bringing together customers, partners and representatives from the Offshore Wind and Maritime Industries at the dawn of WindEnergy Hamburg. The ‘Windward Munich’ is the third vessel in the Windward offshore fleet. Built by VARD Vung Tau in Vietnam, she is the first of two vessels in the fleet to feature a helicopter landing deck. She follows the ‘Windward Athens,’ delivered in September 2025, and the ‘Windward Paris,’ delivered in January 2026. All three vessels commenced their charters shortly after delivery. With the delivery of the fourth sister vessel, ‘Windward Hamburg,’ in August, Windward Offshore has taken delivery of four CSOVs within twelve months. ‘Windward Hamburg,’ is now on her way to Europe and will enter service shortly after arrival. The christening and naming ceremony took place at the Überseebrücke against the backdrop of the Elbphilharmonie. It featured addresses by Dr. Melanie Leonhard, Hamburg's Minister for Economy, Labour and Innovation, Sven Utermöhlen, CEO of RWE Offshore Wind and Windward Offshore representatives. The godmother Claudia Haindl then officially christened the ‘Windward Munich.’ Following the ceremony, Windward Offshore hosted a reception on board, attended by approximately 200 guests. That afternoon and the day after, guided tours of the vessel gave investors, clients, suppliers and other interested groups an insight into the technical equipment as well as the working and living areas on board.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543369-in.text: India's federal Ministry of Mines said on Wednesday it would launch the auction of offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea on Thursday, reviving a push to develop domestic deep - sea mining after an earlier attempt failed to draw bids. The auction will cover two blocks in the Andaman Sea for the grant of a composite licence, the ministry said, adding that the move followed changes to the law in 2023 that allowed it to auction offshore mineral blocks. India announced its first offshore mineral auction in November 2024, offering 13 blocks, but cancelled that sale in December 2025 after repeated deadline extensions failed to attract enough interest. The ministry said offshore minerals including cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements were important for electric mobility, renewable energy systems and electronics.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A unidade da CAP Logística em Paranaguá (PR) recebeu habilitação para armazenar carne de aves destinada à exportação ao México. Segundo a empresa, a aprovação foi anunciada em 19 de agosto de 2026, após avaliação que incluiu uma auditoria presencial de autoridades mexicanas. A inspeção ocorreu em outubro de 2024, com a participação de duas fiscais mexicanas, um auditor fiscal federal agropecuário de Brasília e o fiscal responsável pela unidade no Brasil. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543368-rs.text: Ørsted’s 90 MW Barrow Offshore Wind Farm has marked 20 years of commercial operations, a milestone that also represents two decades since the company began generating power in the UK. Located 7 km southwest of Walney Island in the East Irish Sea, Barrow comprises 30 turbines of 3 MW each and entered commercial operation in 2006. The project was Ørsted’s first UK offshore wind farm and was originally developed as a joint venture between Centrica and DONG Energy, which later became Ørsted. DONG Energy acquired Centrica’s remaining 50% stake in 2014 and Ørsted now owns the project outright. Since Barrow started operating, Ørsted’s UK wind farms have generated more than 180 TWh of electricity. The company now has a portfolio of 12 offshore wind farms around the UK with combined capacity of 5.7 GW. “Twenty years ago, Barrow was part of a pioneering generation of offshore wind projects that showed what could be achieved by taking turbines out to sea and harnessing the UK's abundant wind resource. “Today, offshore wind is a fundamental part of the UK's energy system, but Barrow remains special to us. It was Ørsted's first UK project and has been the foundation for two decades of learning, innovation, and operational excellence,” said Godson Njoku, Chief Generation Officer at Ørsted.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543363-v-.text: Vår Energi has completed the acquisition of selected assets and licenses from Pandion Energy, adding stakes in the producing Nova field, the Ofelia development and the Sierra Solberg discovery. The transaction gives Vår Energi a 10% interest in Nova, a 20% stake in Ofelia and a 49% interest in Sierra Solberg, as well as a portfolio of exploration licences in the Gjøa area. The acquisition, first announced on June 18 for a cash consideration of $110 million, strengthens Vår Energi's position around the Gjøa and Åsgard areas and increases its ownership across producing assets and development projects. The exploration portfolio includes Annabelle, which Vår Energi said when announcing the transaction was planned to be drilled later this year. Nova provides the company with additional near-term production and, prior to the acquisition, was the only producing asset tied to the Gjøa infrastructure in which Vår Energi did not have an ownership interest. The deal is part of Vår Energi's strategy of concentrating ownership around key operated hubs to support long-term production and extend the use of existing infrastructure.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: Os investimentos em tecnologia de gestão de transportes ganharam importância estratégica para as empresas na última década , mas a adoção de inteligência artificial (IA) ainda está em estágio inicial na maioria das organizações . É o que aponta a 10ª Pesquisa Anual Global de Benchmark de Gestão de Transportes, realizada pela Descartes Systems Group e pela SAPIO Research , que identificou um aumento de 53% para 78%, entre 2017 e 2026, na proporção de empresas norte-americanas que planejam ampliar os aportes em tecnologia para o setor. O levantamento também mostra que 85% das organizações pesquisadas consideram o transporte um diferencial competitivo ou de atendimento ao cliente, ante 65% em 2017. O crescimento dos negócios é o principal fator para a adoção de sistemas de gerenciamento de transportes (TMS), citado por 53% dos embarcadores e 48% dos provedores de serviços logísticos (LSPs). Apesar do avanço dos investimentos, apenas 19% dos embarcadores e 15% dos LSPs afirmam utilizar IA em escala. A maioria ainda está em fase de exploração, projetos-piloto ou implementação parcial. Entre os principais obstáculos para ampliar o uso da tecnologia estão a qualidade dos dados, apontada por 33% dos embarcadores e 45% dos LSPs, e a complexidade de integração, mencionada por 39% e 38%, respectivamente. “Dez anos de pesquisas de benchmark mostram que a discussão sobre tecnologia para transportes mudou fundamentalmente. As organizações já não precisam ser convencidas de que a tecnologia de transportes gera valor, mas estão cada vez mais concentradas em como maximizar esse valor”, afirma Alan Dunkerley, vice-presidente sênior de Gestão de Produtos da Descartes. Para o executivo, conectar redes de transporte, automatizar processos e garantir dados de qualidade serão fatores importantes para ampliar a aplicação da IA. O estudo também identificou expectativas de crescimento para os próximos dois anos. Entre os embarcadores, 79% esperam expansão anual de pelo menos 5%, enquanto, entre os LSPs, o percentual chega a 84%. Nesse cenário, o custo do frete permanece como o principal desafio relacionado ao transporte, citado por 35% dos embarcadores e 25% dos provedores logísticos. A visibilidade das operações de carga completa (full truckload) também aparece entre os pontos de atenção. O modal foi apontado como aquele que mais necessita de melhorias no acompanhamento em tempo real por 57% dos embarcadores e 43% dos LSPs. Os índices representam aumentos de 14 e 19 pontos percentuais, respectivamente, em relação a 2025.

A Shopee anunciou ontem (29/09) a expansão do programa "Plataforma Internacional Shopee" para mais de 150 mil vendedores brasileiros. O serviço permite que lojistas anunciem e vendam produtos para Argentina e México a partir do Brasil, usando a estrutura logística da varejista. Com a novidade, a Shopee assume todas as etapas do transporte internacional e oferece suporte no desembaraço aduaneiro e atendimento ao cliente, sem custo adicional para os vendedores. O vendedor brasileiro precisa apenas preparar o pedido para a coleta, enquanto o marketplace fica responsável pela retirada do produto e toda a jornada de entrega por meio de parceiros logísticos. Durante a fase piloto, mais de 19 mil vendedores selecionados aderiram ao programa no país e anunciaram mais de 1,4 milhão de produtos no exterior. A expansão da Plataforma permite que PMEs brasileiras participem do e-commerce regional e desenvolvam seus negócios, enquanto consumidores na Argentina e no México ganham acesso a uma variedade maior de produtos de vendedores brasileiros. A iniciativa faz parte de um conjunto de esforços da Shopee para apoiar a internacionalização de pquenas e médias empresas que participam de sua plataforma. Para Felipe Lima, diretor de desenvolvimento de negócios e operações de fulfillment da Shopee , o programa busca facilitar a expansão internacional, que muitas vezes exige do empreendedor novas capacidades e gerenciar processos desconhecidos. "A Plataforma Internacional Shopee oferece às pequenas e médias empresas brasileiras uma maneira de aproveitar a presença online e a experiência que já desenvolveram com a Shopee para explorar o e-commerce regional. Isso torna o comércio internacional mais acessível para negócios em diferentes estágios de maturidade", afirma. A iniciativa se soma a outros esforços da Shopee focados em promover a internacionalização dos empreendedores brasileiros, como a parceria firmada em 2025 com a ApexBrasil (Agência Brasileira de Promoção de Exportações e Investimentos), que reúne iniciativas de capacitação, conteúdo estratégico e suporte técnico para empresas interessadas em se expandir para o exterior.

A Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT) reajustou a tabela de pisos mínimos de frete do transporte rodoviário de cargas. A mudança foi encadeada pelo aumento do preço médio nacional do diesel S10, que chegou a R$ 7,33 por litro. O reajuste foi publicado na Portaria SUROC nº 22 , no dia 28 de setembro de 2026, e passa a valer hoje (30/09). Os novos valores devem ser considerados em todas as operações de transporte rodoviário de cargas sujeitas à tabela de frete mínimo. As transportadoras e contratantes precisam consultar a tabela atualizada antes de contratar novas viagens. A atualização utiliza R$ 7,33 por litro como novo preço médio de referência para o Diesel S10 , conforme registrado pela Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP). O valor substitui os R$ 6,97 utilizados na atualização de julho. Na prática, a mudança afeta os coeficientes empregados no cálculo do valor mínimo de transporte, conforme as características de cada viagem. Os pisos variam de acordo com tipo de carga, número de eixos carregados e modalidade de contratação. O reajuste contempla diferentes mercadorias, incluindo cargas gerais, frigorificadas, conteinerizadas, granéis sólidos e líquidos, produtos perigosos e cargas a granel pressurizadas. Tabela A: transporte de carga lotação com contratação do caminhão completo ou da composição veicular.

A VAMOS está utilizando um caminhão semiautônomo Agronomous na operação de transbordo de cana-de-açúcar da Adecoagro durante a safra 2026–2027. Desenvolvido pela BMB Mode Center , empresa do Grupo VAMOS especializada na customização de veículos, o equipamento segue rotas predefinidas por meio de georreferenciamento , com o objetivo de reduzir o pisoteio de brotos e aumentar a eficiência da colheita mecanizada. A tecnologia permite que o caminhão acompanhe a linha de colheita com maior precisão, reduzindo desvios que podem danificar os brotos e comprometer o desenvolvimento futuro do canavial. A preservação da soqueira contribui para prolongar a vida útil da lavoura e manter seu potencial produtivo ao longo das safras. “O diferencial do Agronomous está em transformar tecnologia em resultado. Ao eliminar desvios no transbordo e reduzir danos aos brotos, a solução contribui para aumentar a longevidade do canavial e preservar o investimento ao longo das safras”, afirma Bernardo Balbinot, diretor de Operações da BMB Mode Center. O modelo é baseado em uma plataforma 8x4, preparada para operações severas, e conta com sistema de georreferenciamento para manter o alinhamento durante o transbordo. Também utiliza pneus de alta flutuação, que reduzem a compactação do solo e aumentam a estabilidade em terrenos agrícolas. Para a VAMOS, a iniciativa faz parte da estratégia de ampliar sua atuação no agronegócio por meio da locação e venda de veículos e equipamentos pesados. Segundo a empresa, o modelo de locação pode proporcionar redução média de até 30% nos custos operacionais em comparação à aquisição direta, além de permitir o acesso a tecnologias sem a necessidade de imobilizar capital na compra dos ativos. “Não estamos apenas alugando caminhões; estamos entregando precisão dentro do canavial. O Agronomous na safra da Adecoagro prova que a automação no campo não é mais futuro, é o padrão de eficiência para quem quer escala com sustentabilidade”, afirma José Geraldo Júnior, vice-presidente da VAMOS.

https://safety4sea.com/liberia-improper-.text: The Liberian Maritime Authority has warned operators that statutory certificate extensions used contrary to applicable Convention or Code requirements could result in vessel detention in Australia. I n a Marine Advisory dated 23 September 2026, Liberia highlighted the Australian Maritime Safety Authority’s (AMSA) position on certificate extensions, following an AMSA Marine Notice in late August. The advisory applies to Liberian-flagged vessels trading to or intending to trade to Australian ports while relying on an extension of statutory certification. Under SOLAS Chapter I , regulation 14, extensions are permitted only in specific circumstances and subject to the conditions set out in the relevant Convention or Code. Liberia stressed that the maximum period permitted by a Convention does not automatically allow a vessel to continue normal commercial trading throughout that period. AMSA has reportedly encountered vessels whose certificates were extended under SOLAS regulation 14(e) or 14(f), but which continued or planned to continue commercial trading instead of proceeding directly to the agreed cargo discharge and/or survey port. AMSA has also identified cases where extensions exceeded the minimum period required to complete a survey, including situations where dry-docking was still outstanding. Where AMSA considers an extension to have been granted or used contrary to Convention or Code requirements, the vessel may be detained. Where an extension was issued by a flag State’s Recognized Organization, AMSA may also hold that organization responsible for the detention.

https://safety4sea.com/msc-and-chinas-wt.text: Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) is expanding its cooperation with China’s maritime sector, with a new agreement focused on strengthening seafarer assessment, training and career development. M SC and China’s Waterborne Transport Research Institute (WTI) signed an agreement on 21 September covering the assessment and development of seafarers’ overall competencies. The agreement represents one of the first projects to emerge from a broader cooperation agreement reached between the two sides in May during the 10th Maritime Silk Road Port Cooperation Forum. The latest agreement focuses on developing a comprehensive model for assessing seafarer competencies, alongside an intelligent digital system designed to support the recruitment, training and career development of seafarers. WTI Director Liu Peng said the two sides had continued to deepen their cooperation since 2025, working across areas including carbon-footprint accounting, the electrification of port equipment and the supply of green marine fuels. He further noted that the agreement would strengthen technological cooperation, joint standards and resource sharing, supporting closer collaboration between industry, academia and research institutions across the maritime and port sectors. For MSC, the partnership forms part of its broader focus on seafarer development. Marie-Caroline Laurent, Senior Vice President of Shipping Policy and Government Relations at MSC, said the company regards seafarers as a core strategic resource and plans to deepen cooperation with WTI on competency development and training, while also expanding seafarer recruitment in China.

https://safety4sea.com/saudi-arabia-resu.text: Saudi Arabia has resumed oil tanker loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu, reopening a crucial outlet for crude exports after the restart of the kingdom’s East-West Pipeline. A s stated, the move offers some relief to global oil markets, but renewed attacks around the Red Sea are keeping pressure on one of the region’s most important energy corridors. Saudi Aramco notified customers of its October loading programme from Yanbu, according to Reuters, while tankers have already returned to the terminal. Satellite imagery also indicated that nearly 10 million barrels of crude were being loaded at Yanbu and the nearby Al Muajjiz terminal. R Reuters The resumption follows the September 11 drone attack that forced Saudi Arabia to shut the East-West Pipeline, disrupting crude flows to Yanbu. Pipeline operations resumed on September 22, although throughput remains well below its full capacity of 7 million barrels per day. Kpler estimates flows could rise to 3 million-4 million bpd in the coming days, with a full recovery to pre-attack levels of around 5.5 million bpd potentially taking another month. The return of Yanbu loadings has already been reflected in oil markets. Brent crude fell 2.6% on September 29 as traders focused on signs that Middle Eastern exports were recovering. Regional crude exports reached 16.328 million bpd in September, their highest level since the US-Israeli war on Iran began, although flows remain below pre-conflict levels.

https://safety4sea.com/iacs-cyber-resili.text: The delivery of a new MR product tanker in China illustrates a broader shift underway in maritime cybersecurity: requirements that once sat largely within policy and management frameworks are increasingly finding their way into the design and integration of the ship itself. F or shipowners and shipyards, that signals a change in how cyber requirements are encountered throughout a vessel’s lifecycle. Cyber resilience increasingly has to be considered at the design stage — from equipment selection and system interfaces to the architecture of onboard automation, communications and operational technology — rather than treated as an issue to address after a vessel has entered service. The 50,000 dw t Zhi Neng Yun Fan, built by Dalian COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry, was named and handed over in Dalian with compliance with IACS Unified Requirement UR E26 among its stated features. Furthermore, its cargo system is designed to handle three grades simultaneously, while the vessel is also equipped to support biofuel use. Liaoning provincial authorities described the vessel as the first Chinese MR tanker of its size to combine a full smart-ship package with UR E26 cyber-resilience compliance and a China Classification Society cyber-security notation. IACS UR E26, together with the related UR E27 requirement covering the cyber resilience of onboard systems and equipment, reflects a broader shift in how maritime cybersecurity is being addressed. Rather than treating cyber risk primarily as a company-level or shoreside IT issue, the requirements bring cyber resilience into the design, construction and integration of the ship and its operational technology. The Zhi Neng Yun Fan provides a practical example of what that shift means on a vessel. Its onboard systems include remote monitoring, voyage and operational management and predictive maintenance functions, alongside the systems supporting cargo handling, propulsion and other core shipboard operations.

https://safety4sea.com/dcsa-expands-trac.text: DCSA has released Track & Trace 3.0.0, extending its container visibility standard to include IoT and reefer events, while introducing changes that existing users will need to address when migrating from the previous version. T he Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) has published Track & Trace 3.0.0, expanding the standard beyond shipment, transport and equipment events to include data generated by connected containers and refrigerated cargo. The update introduces two new event types covering IoT and reefer operations, bringing information on container location and condition into the same standardised framework used to exchange conventional shipment visibility data. Track & Trace is intended to provide common definitions for container-shipping events so that information can be exchanged more consistently between carriers, terminals, inland operators, shippers, freight forwarders and technology providers. DCSA first introduced its common Track & Trace standards in 2020, establishing common processes, data definitions and interface standards to support cross-carrier shipment tracking. Under the new version, IoT events can include information generated by connected containers and devices, such as geolocation, geofence crossings and door status.

Pete Ciaramitaro , a 2,600-horsepower inland towboat, to Southern Devall in Memphis, Tenn. The vessel is the first delivery from C&C Marine’s six-vessel spec towboat program and was delivered just over two months after the contract was signed July 20, 2026. The five remaining vessels are scheduled for delivery beginning in November at approximately two-month intervals. Because the vessel was built on spec, Southern Devall was able to acquire it on an accelerated schedule while making adjustments to the final design to suit its operations. “The Capt. Pete Ciaramitaro was available when we needed to add horsepower to our fleet, and its size and 2,600 horsepower are well suited to our operations,” said Brandon Devall, vice president of engineering at Southern Devall. “The vessel gives us the versatility to support both our river and coastal operations.” The M/V Capt. Pete Ciaramitaro measures 87 feet by 33 feet, 8 inches by 11 feet, 3 inches and is outfitted for Subchapter M service on inland rivers, canals and intracoastal waterways. Two EPA Tier 4 Mitsubishi S12R main engines power the vessel through Reintjes WAF 665 reduction gears supplied by Karl Senner LLC. Laborde Products supplied the main engines and generator sets.

https://safety4sea.com/maritime-companie.text: New research from Thetius and Marcura shows that artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in maritime workflows, even as companies struggle to establish the governance, accountability and human oversight needed to use it effectively. N early two-thirds (63%) of maritime professionals now use AI every day, yet only 8% describe their organisation as mature and governed in its use of the technology, according to the “Earning Trust: AI in Maritime” report from Thetius and Marcura. The gap is also evident in the time professionals spend checking AI-generated work. More than half (55%) spend at least an hour a week reviewing or correcting AI outputs, while almost one in five spend five hours or more on verification. Despite this additional workload, 85% say AI still saves them time overall after verification is taken into account. The report draws on survey responses and in-depth interviews with maritime professionals to examine where human oversight is essential to sound decision-making, where it reflects uncertainty, and how leading companies are turning the need for verification from a cost into an opportunity for learning and improvement. 60 maritime professionals responded to the 2026 survey, representing technology providers, shipowners, ship managers and asset-light operators.

https://gcaptain.com/three-more-tanker-a.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, August 3, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer Three more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have surfaced through delayed reports from UK Maritime Trade Operations, adding to growing uncertainty over how quickly incidents in the water are making it into the public record. UKMTO issued three separate warnings Wednesday — 144-26, 145-26 and 146-26 — covering incidents reported on Sept. 29 but not published until Sept. 30. In the first case, UKMTO said a crude oil tanker was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile. A second warning said a tanker transiting inbound through the strait had also been hit by an unknown projectile. The third provided even fewer details, saying only that a tanker had been struck.

https://splash247.com/bomesc-wins-fpso-t.text: Chinese offshore engineering contractor BOMESC has secured a contract worth between RMB1.6bn and RMB2.1bn ($225m and $295m) from SBM Offshore for work on an FPSO destined for South America. BOMESC said its wholly owned subsidiary Tianjin BOMESC Offshore Engineering had signed the contract with Single Buoy Moorings, SBM Offshore’s operating subsidiary. The scope covers the design, procurement, and construction of topside modules for the FPSO, with fabrication to be carried out at BOMESC’s offshore engineering base in Tianjin. The contract is scheduled to be completed in the second half of 2028. BOMESC said the final contract value will depend on the actual workload carried out under the agreement. The contract includes a fixed portion and a variable component, so the final amount will be determined once the work is completed. The company did not identify the FPSO or the project it will serve, saying only that the unit is destined for operations in South America. The award represents a significant contract for BOMESC, with the upper end of the estimated value exceeding the company’s reported 2025 revenue. BOMESC has previously worked with SBM Offshore on several FPSO projects and has supplied topside modules for units deployed offshore Brazil.

https://petronoticias.com.br/periodo-de-.text: A Operação Codajás adota, desde a segunda quinzena de setembro, medidas preventivas para garantir o abastecimento de combustíveis, em especial do Gás Liquefeito de Petróleo (GLP), durante o período de seca dos rios na Região Norte. Realizada pela Transpetro e Petrobrás, com o apoio da Marinha do Brasil, a operação reúne ações logísticas voltadas a mitigar os impactos da vazante no transporte de produtos. A iniciativa também contribui para a continuidade do escoamento da produção de petróleo e gás natural proveniente do Polo de Urucu, garantindo a segurança energética local. Realizada anualmente, entre setembro e dezembro, a Operação Codajás é acionada este ano em um cenário de tendência de redução dos níveis dos rios e de maior restrição à navegação nas próximas semanas. O Comitê da Vazante Amazônica monitora semanalmente condições climáticas, níveis dos rios e planejamento operacional e, de forma preventiva, avalia medidas para preservar a segurança e garantir a continuidade do transporte de produtos durante a vazante. O plano de contingência logístico prevê ações como a mobilização antecipada de recursos e o posicionamento estratégico de embarcações. O diretor de Transporte Marítimo da Transpetro, Jones Soares, disse que “Os sinais observados pelo comitê multidisciplinar reforçam a importância do planejamento antecipado. Por isso, iniciamos as avaliações técnicas e operacionais necessárias para ampliar nossa prontidão logística. A Operação Codajás é um exemplo de como conhecimento do território, monitoramento contínuo e integração entre instituições são fundamentais para garantir que o gás de cozinha chegue à população do Norte de forma contínua, mesmo em cenários desafiadores. ” Para a Operação Codajás de 2026, estarão disponíveis dois navios com dedicação exclusiva, os gaseiros Gilberto Freyre e Jorge Amado, além dos gaseiros Oscar Niemeyer, Barbosa Lima Sobrinho , Darcy Ribeiro e Lucio Costa e os petroleiros Sergio Buarque de Holanda , Romulo Almeida e José Alencar. Além deles, o navio-tanque Epic Baluan será posicionado em Coari, para atuar como tancagem estendida, complementando a capacidade de armazenamento dos terminais da região. A estratégia contempla ainda o uso do convênio com a Marinha do Brasil para o acompanhamento dos navios e a sondagem dos trechos críticos durante o período de vazante. Criada em 1995, a Operação Codajás completa 31 anos em 2026 como uma das principais ações logísticas voltadas à manutenção do abastecimento da Região Norte. Ao longo desse período, a iniciativa permitiu superar sucessivos desafios impostos pela dinâmica dos rios amazônicos. https://petronoticias.com.br/o-submarino.text: O Submarino “ Almirante Karam” concluiu sua primeira imersão estática na área marítima de Itacuruçá, próximo ao Complexo Naval de Itaguaí, no Rio de Janeiro. O procedimento avaliou o comportamento do submarino na água e permitiu a verificação de parâmetros importantes para a continuidade dos testes. Sem utilizar a propulsão, o “Karam” foi levado à condição de imersão de maneira controlada. Durante a atividade, militares, engenheiros e técnicos acompanharam a estanqueidade do casco, o funcionamento dos sistemas de bordo e a resposta do submarino às variações de peso e inclinação. O Comandante do Submarino “Almirante Karam” , Capitão de Corveta Leandro Amaral, explicou que na imersão estática, a água do mar preenche os tanques de lastros por meio da abertura dos suspiros dos tanques até que o submarino alcance a condição prevista para o teste. Os pesos posicionados ao longo da embarcação também podem ser movimentados para observar as inclinações transversais e longitudinais. Os dados obtidos ajudam a determinar o deslocamento e as condições de equilíbrio da embarcação. O procedimento permitiu avaliar o comportamento do “ Karam” na água e verificar parâmetros relacionados ao equilíbrio e à estabilidade da embarcação. Mais do que verificar se o submarino é capaz de mergulhar, a atividade possibilita conferir como ele se comporta na água. É nessa fase que os resultados calculados durante o projeto são comparados às respostas apresentadas pela embarcação. Antes de um submarino mergulhar, os engenheiros estimam como ele deverá flutuar, inclinar e reagir às mudanças na distribuição de peso. Esses cálculos consideram o peso do casco, dos equipamentos, das baterias, tanques e demais sistemas instalados, bem como sua distribuição a bordo. O Encarregado da Seção da Fiscalização da Construção dos S-BR no Estaleiro de Construção, Capitão-Tenente (Engenheiro) Amós Rodrigues , da Coordenadoria-Geral do Programa de Desenvolvimento de Submarino com Propulsão Nuclear, ressaltou que a imersão estática mostra como essas previsões se confirmam na prática. Mesmo submarinos de uma mesma classe, construídos a partir de um mesmo projeto, podem apresentar pequenas diferenças na distribuição de peso. Por isso, cada unidade precisa passar por avaliações próprias. Militares, engenheiros e técnicos acompanham os parâmetros registrados durante a imersão estática do Submarino. Para a tripulação, o teste também representa um contato mais próximo com o comportamento do novo meio. É quando passam a conhecer, na prática, o comportamento do submarino na água. Os dados obtidos nesta etapa aumentam a familiaridade com o meio e contribuem para a preparação para os próximos testes.
