https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Philippine Coast Guard has filed its first criminal complaint in connection with the tragic fire aboard the ferry June Aster, which killed at least 77 people and left eight others missing. On September 9, the ferry June Aster left Manila and got under way for the port of Coron, Busuanga Island. At about 1845 hours that night, the Aster caught fire at a position about one nautical mile off the east side of Busuanga. Passengers who escaped reported a blast followed by an intense fire. First responders pulled 43 people from the water, then turned to the grim task of search and recovery. After the fire, the wreck went hard aground off the coast of Busuanga Island, just south of Mindoro, enabling boarding and search operations. 77 bodies have been recovered, and eight people remain missing. The process of identification of the remains will take longer: some of the bodies were so charred by the intense heat that forensic specialists have had to look for usable DNA material in dental pulp, inside of the victims' teeth. Aerial search operations continue for the eight missing people off Palawan and Southern Tagalog. The shipowner has retained a salvor, and discussions are under way on the prospect of salvaging the wreck. Meanwhile, in Manila, the PCG has filed a complaint with the Philippines' justice department against the June Aster's captain, Roel Sarmiento. The captain survived the fire and voluntarily met with investigators on September 14, the week after the casualty. He now stands accused of "falsification of public documents" in connection with his Master's Declaration of Safe Departure process - the unique Philippine regulation requiring a documented safety check at the outset of every voyage. The specific allegation has to do with the number of people listed on the vessel's manifest. "We had six passengers who were initially listed on the ticket manifest but did not board the ship," a PCG spokesperson told local radio station dzBB. "We also found a duplicate entry for one passenger's name, while another entry listed a crew member who did not actually board the ship."

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: Canada LNG, the country’s first LNG export operation, reports that, along with its investment partners, the decision has been made to proceed with Phase 2 of the operation. It comes just about 15 months after the project began exports, and according to the group, it builds on Phase 1 with a new project that represents one of the largest private sector investments in Canada. Located in Kitimat, British Columbia, the partners highlight that it is ideally located to serve the growing Asian market for LNG. It has access to an ice-free deepwater harbor and is fed by a pipeline. In its first year of operation, it shipped more than 100 cargoes. Shell owns 40 percent of the project along with Petronas (25 percent), PetroChina (15 percent), Mitsubishi Corporation (15 percent), and Korea Gas (5 percent). It began exports in June 2025 with its first train and completed the second train in October, with an annual capacity of 14 million tonnes per annum. “LNG Canada Phase 2 is another nation-building investment that demonstrates Canada can build big things when governments, First Nations partners, local communities, skilled trades, contractors, and investors work together with shared purpose. With FID secured, Phase 2 will double LNG Canada’s capacity from 14 to 28 million tonnes a year, putting LNG Canada on a trajectory to become one of the largest LNG facilities in the world and helping move Canada toward becoming one of the world’s top five LNG exporting nations,” said Chris Cooper, President and CEO, LNG Canada. The partners highlight that global demand for LNG is expected to increase from 422 mtpa in 2025 to nearly 700 mtpa by 2050. According to Shell's LNG Outlook 2026, global LNG demand is expected to rise by around 60 percent by 2040 and around 65 percent by 2050, driven by growing energy demand and the need for secure, flexible, and reliable energy supplies. “At a time when our country must build a stronger economy that allows us to be an energy superpower for the long term, this is exactly the kind of investment Canada needs,” said the Honourable Tim Hodgson, Canada’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), Galliano Marine Services and Saronic have each secured a contract to build 10 small autonomous warships for the Navy's Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) competition, giving the Navy a pipeline for 30 of the long-awaited vessels - a meaningful mass for operational implementation. Other competitors - Leidos, PAC MAR, and Sea Machines - received $15 million completion awards for their work and will be listed on the Drones.mil "Maritime Marketplace" for future authorized orders. HII celebrated the contract award in a statement. “HII has made deliberate, early investments in the development of autonomous systems, advancing capabilities essential to the Navy’s hedge strategy,” said Chris Kastner, HII president and CEO. HII's Romulus MUSV entrant is a midsize unmanned vessel with a speed of 25 knots and a range of 2,500 miles. It has a familiar crewboat layout with a long aft deck, suitable for modular payloads. HII envisions a wide variety of roles for Romulus, including ISR, counter-drone, mine countermeasures, strike, and the launch and recovery of unmanned platforms - likely to include HII's own Remus submersible survey drone, a standard tool that exists in quantity in the Navy inventory. To build the first Romulus prototype, HII turned to Breaux Brothers, a commercial yard on the Gulf Coast with a long and successful history of building commercial aluminum working vessels. HII builds it subs, carriers, surface combatants and amphibs out of steel; Breaux has decades of knowledge in building with aluminum and had input on the design to ensure its manufacturability in a commercial setting. Competing startup Saronic is pursuing the same program but plans to keep production in-house through the construction of a mega-shipyard in Brownsville, Texas - a $3 billion plant that could become the largest in the U.S. if fully built out. It broke ground at its "Port Alpha" facility on Wednesday in a ceremony attended by Vice President JD Vance, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and other dignitaries.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: Global marine solutions provider Resolve Marine released photos showing the work underway to remove the masts from the historic wreck of the SS Richard Montgomery , a World War II Liberty ship that sank in 1944 in the Thames Estuary while carrying Allied munitions. After six years of planning and annual surveys of the wreck site, the UK Department for Transport (DfT) appointed Resolve Marine in April 2026 to undertake the carefully planned engineering operation. The vessel went down in a storm in August 1944 in a position approximately 50 miles east of London. A salvage operation began but was suspended after the wreck cracked and was deemed too dangerous. The wreck still contains approximately 1,400 tons of munitions and has been regularly surveyed by the UK authorities. It has also become a local tourist attraction as the mast tops rise above the water. Concerns were raised a few years ago that as the vessel was decaying, the masts were becoming unstable. Engineers warned that the masts would likely fall and could cause further damage, while the media speculated about the dangers from the munitions. The Department of Transportation decided to proceed with the removal project . "The removal of the SS Richard Montgomery 's masts is a unique and highly specialized marine engineering project that requires meticulous planning, rigorous risk management, and exceptional technical expertise,” said Resolve Marine Director of Projects Sam Adams. Working under strict safety and engineering protocols, Resolve Marine engineers and divers are carefully cutting and lifting the vessel's three steel masts. The operation has been developed following extensive technical assessments and independent expert review to ensure the continued stability of the wreck and the safety of personnel, local communities, and maritime traffic. "The SS Richard Montgomery is one of the most extraordinary wrecks in the world - a piece of wartime history that has rested in the Thames Estuary for over 80 years," said UK Maritime Minister Keir Mather. "Beginning the careful removal of its masts is a hugely significant moment.” The project supports the UK government's long-term strategy for managing the SS Richard Montgomery wreck site and preserves an important chapter of maritime history while maintaining public safety. The government has committed to placing the masts on display once they are safely removed from the wreck.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Salvors have successfully towed the burned-out fishing vessel Triumf into port at Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky in the Russian Far East, and a search operation has uncovered four victims' bodies within the interior of the vessel. The seiner Triumf was under way off the southern end of Kamchatka on September 25 when she caught fire. 29 crewmembers were aboard the vessel at the time of the casualty, and 25 were evacuated by a nearby good Samaritan vessel. Of the survivors, seven were injured, including two in critical condition. A salvage tug, the Suvorovets, managed to tow the Triumf into port at Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky to enable firefighting operations, arriving on Tuesday. Shoreside fire teams came aboard and began their work, but the mass of the firefighting water began to endanger the vessel's stability and the effort was suspended. Instead, the hatches were all sealed and the fire was allowed to burn itself out, Interfax reports. On Wednesday, responders found that the conditions were improved enough to resume operations, and firefighters began extinguishing the blaze in the interior. During this operation, they recovered the bodies of the four missing members of the crew. The damage inside the ship is extensive, the Ministry of Emergency Situations said in a statement. A criminal inquiry has been opened into the case with a focus on possible safety violations. Early lines of investigation include a possible fault in the ship's electrical system or an error by the crew.

https://splash247.com/tdi-brooks-adds-ti.text: US-based offshore surveyor TDI-Brooks, in partnership with Taka Hydrocore Indonesia, has been selected to execute a light geotechnical and environmental baseline survey programme offshore Timor-Leste in support of the planned TLNG development. The programme, awarded by the country’s Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, will provide data to support the routing of the gas export pipeline from the Greater Sunrise field to Natarbora on the south coast of Timor-Leste, as well as the Bayu-Undan Pipeline Highway to Natarbora. The survey will utilise TDI-Brooks’ DP2 research vessel, Nautilus . The geotechnical scope will include approximately 508 seabed tests, consisting of gravity CPTs, piston cores, box cores, and cyclic T-bar measurements. The project will deliver critical geotechnical data to support pipeline routing, engineering design, and geohazard assessment for offshore development activities. In parallel, the environmental baseline study will cover 16 provisional stations, including collecting 40 sediment samples and 40 water samples. Field operations for both the geotechnical and environmental scopes are scheduled to commence in mid-January 2027. Last week, Dutch surveyor Fugro signed a contract for a pipeline survey on the same two fields. Under the contract, Fugro will undertake an extensive offshore site characterisation programme, including geophysical, seismic, and AUV surveys. The survey area includes deepwater areas with water depths exceeding 3,000 m.

https://splash247.com/norden-the-capital.text: Jan Rindbo says today’s fragmented shipping markets demand flexibility, with tanker exposure being reduced as dry bulk offers a more attractive balance of risk and reward. Shipping’s fragmented markets are moving through very different stages of the cycle, and for Norden chief executive Jan Rindbo, that is increasingly shaping where the Danish shipping group puts its money. Tankers remain exceptionally strong, but a growing orderbook and a geopolitically driven market have prompted Norden to take a more cautious approach. At the same time, the company is paying more attention and capital towards dry bulk, where Rindbo sees a more attractive balance between risk and reward. “In shipping we have many different markets, and most of them are at different levels in terms of where they are in that cycle,” Rindbo says in this week’s big Maritime CEO interview. For Norden, which operates across tankers and dry cargo, the contrast is becoming clearer. Tanker earnings remain strong, but newbuilding activity has accelerated, and the orderbook has expanded significantly.

https://splash247.com/transocean-valaris.text: Transocean’s $5.8bn takeover of offshore driller Valaris has cleared a key regulatory hurdle in the US, and the companies now expect to complete the transaction in the final quarter of the year. Valaris and Transocean have been notified by the Antitrust Division of the US Department of Justice that it has closed its investigation into the proposed business combination under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act. The clearance removes one of the main regulatory conditions hanging over the all-stock combination. The DOJ had stepped up its review of the transaction in May by issuing both companies with requests for additional information and documentary materials. Transocean and Valaris now expect the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to satisfying or waiving the remaining closing conditions. Under the agreement signed in early February , Switzerland-based Transocean will acquire all outstanding Valaris shares, and Valaris shareholders will receive 15.235 Transocean shares for each share they hold. The deal will leave Transocean shareholders with approximately 53% of the enlarged company on a fully diluted basis, while Valaris shareholders will own about 47%.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: Despite Iran's attempts to close off the Strait of Hormuz, oil exports out of the Gulf states have steadily climbed back to the point where they are approximately the same as prewar volumes, though Iran's barrels continue to be locked in by the U.S. blockade. Kpler assesses that oil volumes exiting the Gulf - via both tanker and pipeline - reached 16.5 million barrels per day on average in September. (JPMorgan concurs, assessing current Gulf export volumes at 98% of prewar levels). The water-side movement is heavily assisted by a shuttle-tanker system set up to carry crude through the dangerous waters of the strait and then transfer the oil to other vessels for the long haul to market. More than 70 percent of the oil that moves through the strait ends up in an STS transfer at the other end, according to Kpler's analysts - a statistic backed up by independent assessments of the busy transfer activity at the Fujairah anchorage. Saudi crude export volume hit 6.4 million bpd last week, according to Kpler analyst Amena Bakr - higher than average levels seen before the war, and a big part of the reason why total Gulf volumes have recovered. But these shipments come at a cost. Bloomberg reports that Iraqi exporters are getting their crude out of the strait by selling it at up to $37 per barrel below benchmark pricing, thereby absorbing the extreme cost of shipping in order to get it to market. Though oil exports have substantially recovered, the bounceback has yet to come for other major commodities - LNG, urea, ammonia, sulfur and refined products. None are getting through the strait and out to market at prewar levels. Distillates are a particularly pinched segment of the market. U.S. pricing for bulk diesel soared to record levels this week, driven up by the timing of physical delivery contracts and by a persistent shortage. Ukrainian attacks have temporarily eliminated Russia's diesel export trade; Gulf refinery exports are constrained by the security situation at Hormuz; and Saudi Arabia's Red Sea refineries have been hampered by militia attacks (both Houthi and Iraqi, per Saudi officials). Given the factors hemming in refinery capacity, the increased flow of Gulf oil may not immediately relieve supply-side pressure on fuel pricing at the pump. In the U.S., the average retail price for diesel - needed for trucking, construction, agriculture and delivery service - hit a new record of $6.53 per gallon last week, up from $3.70 a year ago.

Segundo os advogados dela, Pike recebeu duas doses de pentobarbital, um barbitúrico que, em doses altas, provoca coma e, em seguida, a parada da respiração e do coração. O pentobarbital pertence aos barbitúricos, classe de medicamentos inventada no fim do século 19. Ele funciona como um sedativo de ação curta e, por décadas, foi usado como anestésico, para induzir o sono e para controlar convulsões. Seu uso terminou proibido e ele foi trocado pelos benzodiazepínicos por causa do risco, inclusive de vício.

Morgan report sent to Rigzone by Kaneva late Tuesday. “With flows through the Saudi East-West pipeline restored, regional exports are now just 11 percent below pre-war levels - a remarkable recovery for a region still at war,” the analysts stated in the report. “Over the past five days, the 10‑day average for total oil exports has held at 20.5 million barrels per day, or 89 percent of 2025 levels,” they added. “Crude flows have rebounded to 17.5 million barrels per day or 98 percent of pre-war levels, while product exports remain at just three million barrels per day, or 58 percent, underscoring that the crude market has largely normalized even as refined product supplies remain constrained,” they said. The J.P. Morgan analysts revealed in the report that early signs of rising exports are already visible in India, which they described as “the largest nearby buyer”. “In September, India’s imports from the Middle East and ‘unknown origins’ rose to 2.8 million barrels per day, up 1.2 million barrels per day from August, and exceeding 2025 levels,” they noted.

https://safety4sea.com/west-pi-highlight.text: The West of England P&I Club is highlighting a recurring pollution risk involving overboard piping routed through fuel oil tanks, following two further incidents involving a similar arrangement. I n both recent cases, Oil Discharge Monitoring Equipment (ODME) overboard discharge pipes passed through bunker fuel tanks before terminating at the ship’s side, allowing fuel to escape overboard after the pipe sections failed. The incidents follow an earlier case in which a deck scupper drain pipe routed through a fuel oil tank developed a defect, allowing bunkering fuel to enter the damaged pipe and discharge into the sea. Although all three incidents involved tankers, the recurrence of this failure mode across unrelated vessels highlights a broader risk. These incidents demonstrate how seemingly isolated overboard piping can create a direct pathway between an oil-containing tank and the sea if the pipe loses its integrity. According to Dmitry Kisil, Senior Loss Prevention Office, West, in both recent cases, the section of ODME overboard discharge piping located within a bunker tank failed. Bunker fuel entered the damaged pipe and escaped directly into the sea. Importantly, the discharge occurred despite the ODME overboard valve being closed and the removable spool piece having been removed inside the vessel.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-c.text: A routine task on board can become a serious accident when incompatible chemicals are brought together. I n a case investigated by Germany’s Federal Bureau of Maritime Casualty Investigation (BSU), a motorman intending to refill a sewage treatment plant dosing tank inadvertently selected sodium bisulphite instead of sodium hypochlorite. The resulting chemical reaction caused the tank to burst, releasing hazardous substances and injuring the crew member. The incident highlights how labelling, equipment design, training and risk assessment must work together to prevent a simple selection error from becoming an accident. The motorman noticed that the sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) dosing tank serving the vessel’s sewage treatment plant was running low and set out to refill it. Instead of taking sodium hypochlorite from the chemical store, he inadvertently selected a 38–40% sodium bisulphite (NaHSO₃) solution. The error went unnoticed as the chemical was transferred into the dosing tank, which still contained sodium hypochlorite. When the two substances came into contact, an exothermic reaction occurred. The resulting reaction released toxic gases and generated sufficient force to rupture the plastic dosing tank.

https://safety4sea.com/nuclear-powered-l.text: A joint study involving ABS, Blossom Energy and a global shipping company has assessed the economic case for nuclear propulsion on LNG carriers, finding that a nuclear-powered vessel could significantly reduce fuel costs despite a substantially higher initial investment. P resented at Gastech 2026, the study examined a 174,000-cbm LNG carrier fitted with a 20–25 MWe high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) being developed by Blossom Energy. The analysis compared the vessel’s arrangement, propulsion system and operating conditions with those of a conventional LNG-fueled newbuild. It also assessed the economics under a range of potential regulatory penalty scenarios. According to the study, the initial investment for the nuclear-powered LNG carrier would be approximately 2.5 times that of a conventional LNG carrier. However, the nuclear design could deliver substantially lower fuel costs over the vessel’s operating life. ABS said the findings provide a quantitative basis for assessing the potential economic implications of nuclear propulsion in commercial shipping. Nuclear energy has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of commercial shipping, from vessel design to long-term operating costs … commented Patrick Ryan, ABS Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer.

https://safety4sea.com/the-logbook-comes.text: NAVTOR's Digital Logbooks are driving new competitive advantages for users worldwide / Image Credit: NAVTOR In the following article, NAVTOR’s Amitabh Sankranti argues that digital logbooks are evolving from a compliance tool into a source of operational and commercial value. Paper logbook entries die on the page. The same entries in digital format live across a fleet, every day, adding up to a picture of situational awareness no single ship ever had – and a picture can be read, compared and acted on. That is not a compliance improvement. That is a competitive advantage sitting in a book we already fill in. It is worth remembering this is how the logbook started. For three centuries it was the most valuable data product afloat – soundings, tracks, currents and coastal sketches, extracted ashore, engraved on copperplate and reprinted for the whole fleet. It was also how money moved: naval logs were filed before pay was issued, and courts, underwriters and charterers settled on what the book said. The logbook was never an archive. It was the instrument that redrew the map. Somewhere in the last century we forgot that, and the log became something you produced for an inspector. That era is now ending, for financial reasons.

https://safety4sea.com/us-coast-guard-pr.text: The US Coast Guard is proposing to remove six training and competency requirements attached to certain merchant mariner endorsements, arguing that the requirements go beyond what is required under the international STCW Convention and, in some cases, impose additional burdens without providing corresponding safety benefits. T he proposal would affect a range of deck and engineering personnel, including Masters and Officers in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OICNW) serving on vessels of less than 500 GT in near-coastal waters, as well as engineering officers, Designated Duty Engineers (DDEs) and Electro-technical Ratings (ETRs) serving on vessels with propulsion machinery of 750 kW/1,000 HP or more. The US Coast Guard (USCG) says the changes form part of a broader review of its regulations aimed at eliminating requirements considered duplicative, outdated or more restrictive than international standards. The Coast Guard is also proposing technical amendments to remove outdated or duplicative language from the regulations, including correcting an instance where the Radar Observer requirement was inadvertently listed twice. The central argument is that some of these requirements go beyond the competency standards established by the STCW Convention and STCW Code. For smaller near-coastal vessels, the Coast Guard points to the relatively small size of the bridge team. In many cases, a single credentialed mariner serves as the watchstander while also performing the functions of helmsman and lookout.

https://safety4sea.com/american-club-spo.text: Not all hazards are obvious at first glance. Conditions such as limited lighting and compromised footing can increase risk and make hazards more difficult to recognise, the American Club highlights in the latest instalment of its Good Catch series. T aking a few moments to assess the work environment before starting a task can help prevent injuries, falls overboard and other incidents that may have lasting consequences for seafarers. Identifying potential hazards early and addressing them before work begins can make a critical difference in keeping everyone on board safe. Against this backdrop, the American Club highlights a case in which a deckhand on an inland towing vessel fell overboard while working in a barge fleeting area. In a barge fleeting area while the crew was building a tow of 20 barges, a deckhand on an inland towing vessel slipped from a barge and fell overboard. Fortunately, he was rescued by other crew members using a ring buoy with an attached lifeline. Several hopper barges recently loaded with sand were being added to the tow. While walking along the side of one of the barges and carrying a ratchet, the deckhand fell overboard. He later explained that his right foot likely caught the edge of a void hatch cover that he didn’t see, and then, when attempting to catch his balance, his left foot slipped on the sand that had accumulated on the deck. He fell hard and went directly overboard along with the ratchet. The incident happened just after midnight. Of additional note, the deckhand had only seven months of industry experience, all of which had been onboard this towing vessel on a 28-day rotation.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543394-de.text: DEME has installed the 68th and final monopile at Vattenfall's 980 MW Nordlicht I offshore wind farm in the German North Sea, completing the project's monopile installation campaign. The milestone follows installation of the first monopile in July and the first transition piece in August. DEME carried out the monopile campaign using its offshore installation vessel Orion. Nordlicht I is located about 85 kilometers north of the German island of Borkum and is set to become Germany's largest offshore wind farm once completed. The work forms part of contracts awarded to DEME for the transport and installation of 112 foundations across the Nordlicht I and II projects, as well as scour protection. Under the contracts, DEME is responsible for 68 foundations at Nordlicht I and another 44 at the 630 MW Nordlicht II project. Its scope involves several vessels, including Orion, a jack-up vessel and a fallpipe vessel for scour protection. Vattenfall is developing the Nordlicht offshore wind cluster, with BASF holding a 49% interest in the projects.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543392-iw.text: Integrated Wind Solutions (IWS) subsidiary IWS Fleet has ordered four Skywalker-class commissioning service operation vessels (CSOVs) for a combined firm yard price of around $301 million (€260 million), expanding its owned fleet from six to 10 CSOVs. The four vessels, priced at around $75 million (€65 million) each, will be built by Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment and delivered in 2029 and 2030 under fixed-price turnkey contracts. IWS Fleet has also secured options for another four vessels at the same firm prices, with deliveries scheduled for 2030 and 2031, subject to certain adjustments for foreign exchange rates and key sub-suppliers. The newbuilds will be based on a Kongsberg Maritime design and equipped with three-dimensional motion-compensated cranes and gangway systems supplied by MacGregor Norway. IWS plans to finance the four firm vessels through a combination of operating cash flow and additional debt, without raising new equity, while maintaining its ordinary quarterly dividend in line with its dividend policy. Payments will be made in instalments during construction, with the remaining 50% due on delivery. The final financing structure will depend on market conditions, liquidity, operating cash flow and debt capacity.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543389-in.text: Inpex, Japan’s largest exploration and production (E&P) company, has acquired 50% participating interests in the Agung I and Agung II exploration blocks offshore Eastern Java, Indonesia, from BP’s subsidiaries. The interests were acquired through wholly owned subsidiaries INPEX WEST AGUNG and INPEX EAST AGUNG from BP Agung I Limited and BP Agung II Limited, respectively. Following the transaction, Inpex and BP will each hold 50% of both blocks, with the BP subsidiaries remaining operators. Agung I covers 6,656 square kilometers in water depths ranging from 100 to 2,000 meters, while Agung II spans 7,969 square kilometers across the same water-depth range. The blocks are located near the Barong and Serpang blocks, where Inpex already holds participating interests, allowing the company to pursue exploration across a wider area offshore Eastern Java. According to Inpex, multiple oil and gas fields have been discovered in the region and that the area offers a range of potential exploration plays.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543391-bo.text: Borr Drilling has announced new commitments for three premium jack-up rigs, including a three-well award in West Africa, an exercised Shell option in Nigeria and an accommodation contract in the UK. The Norve rig has received a binding letter of award from an undisclosed operator in West Africa for three wells with an estimated firm duration of 245 days. The commitment is expected to start in mid-December 2026 and keep the rig working into August 2027. It also includes priced options covering an estimated additional 175 days. In Nigeria, Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company (SNEPCo) has exercised a one-well option for the Natt rig. Based on the current well program, Borr expects the rig to remain contracted with Shell into early August 2027. The Joro rig has meanwhile been awarded a contract by an undisclosed operator for accommodation activities in the UK. The UK contract is expected to start in mid-October 2026 and has an estimated firm duration of 60 days, keeping the Joro committed into December. It also includes priced options covering an estimated 56 days.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543388-se.text: Serica Energy has completed the acquisition of a portfolio of Southern North Sea assets from Spirit Energy, adding around 10,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day of production and 18.7 million boe of proved and probable reserves. Serica made a net payment of $43 million (£33 million) to Spirit Energy at completion, comprising upfront consideration of $75 million (£57 million), reduced by post-tax cash flows generated between the transaction's effective economic date of January 1, 2025 and completion on October 1, 2026. The acquired assets are now forecast to generate more than $200 million of free cash flow by the end of 2028, more than double Serica's expectation when the transaction was announced in December 2025. The company attributed the increase primarily to a stronger gas price outlook, robust production expectations and the rephasing of some production and cash flows into the post-completion period. The portfolio includes a 15% non-operated interest in the Cygnus gas field, a 25% non-operated interest in Clipper South and operated positions across assets in the Greater Markham Area, alongside other operated and non-operated Southern North Sea gas interests. The assets also contain 3.4 million boe of 2C resources as of the January 1, 2025 effective economic date.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543386-bo.text: Boskalis has secured a contract to transport and install inter-array cables for the first phase of the Zeevonk Offshore Wind Farm in the Dutch North Sea. The contract, awarded by Zeevonk, a joint venture between Vattenfall and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), covers the transport and installation of about 149 kilometers of 66 kV inter-array cables connecting 69 wind turbines. Boskalis will also carry out cable testing and termination, install cable protection systems and perform survey and seabed intervention work. The cables will be transported from a manufacturing facility in Eemshaven, the Netherlands, to the wind farm and installed using Boskalis' cable-laying vessel BOKA Ocean. One of the company's subsea rock installation vessels will be deployed for seabed intervention work. Engineering is expected to begin shortly, while the offshore installation campaign is planned for 2029. Boskalis said the contract is worth between $58 million and $174 million (€50 million and €150 million).

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543390-no.text: Northern Lights joint venture and Swedish energy company Öresundskraft Kraft & Värme have signed an agreement for the transport and permanent storage of up to 200,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide per year from a waste-to-energy plant in Helsingborg. The agreement targets a start in the fourth quarter of 2029 and will use available capacity across Northern Lights' CO2 shipping portfolio under a shared logistics model. The deal remains subject to certain agreed requirements. CO2 will be captured and liquefied at Öresundskraft's Filbornaverket waste-to-energy plant before being transported by truck to the Port of Halland in Halmstad. Northern Lights will then ship the CO2 to its receiving terminal in Øygarden, Norway, before it is transported offshore for injection and permanent storage in a reservoir 2,600 meters below the North Sea seabed. “The agreement with Öresundskraft is an important milestone for Northern Lights and it further strengthens the Nordics as a leading CCS region. Öresundskraft’s project contributes to the development of a portfolio approach with shared infrastructure. This will be an enabler of further growth of the CCS industry “, said Tim Heijn, managing director of Northern Lights JV. Öresundskraft aims to capture both biogenic and fossil CO2 emissions from Filbornaverket, which processes household and industrial waste and produces district heating and electricity.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543385-tg.text: TGS has launched a 3D seismic reprocessing project covering about 514 square kilometers over Petronas’ Megah discovery in Block SB-3K offshore Sabah, Malaysia, with final products expected in April 2027. The project will apply TGS' Elastic Multi-Parameter Full Waveform Inversion and depth imaging technologies to its legacy Geostreamer Sabah multi-client 3D Phase 2 dataset, which was acquired in 2017. Processing began in July 2026 and will use a high-resolution velocity model and diffraction imaging across the Megah field. Petronas made the Megah discovery in 2025. The reprocessed data is intended to improve geological interpretation and prospect evaluation and support planning for future appraisal wells. "The Megah discovery has reinforced the exploration potential of this area, and advanced reprocessing can play an important role in reducing subsurface uncertainty. This project highlights TGS' ability to apply leading imaging workflows where improved subsurface definition can directly support exploration and appraisal decisions,” said David Hajovsky, EVP Multi-Client.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543383-th.text: Malaysia's state energy firm PETRONAS said on Thursday that Trans Thai-Malaysia (Thailand), its joint venture with Thailand's, had temporarily shut the Songkhla Export Pipeline after identifying an issue during a routine inspection. The Songkhla Export Pipeline is part of the Trans Thailand-Malaysia gas system linking offshore gas production in the Gulf of Thailand with processing and gas markets in Thailand and Malaysia.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543384-h-.text: Höegh Evi and Petroleum Sarawak (PETROS) have agreed to jointly develop, own and operate a proposed LNG import terminal in Kuching, Malaysia, targeting first gas by the end of 2029. The Kuching LNG Terminal will comprise a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), mooring infrastructure, subsea and onshore pipelines and onshore receiving facilities. The project will form part of the Kuching Low-Carbon development in Sarawak and supply natural gas for power generation in Kuching. The partners are also assessing opportunities to accelerate its delivery in response to growing demand. The terminal is planned to provide additional services including small-scale LNG distribution, truck loading, LNG bunkering, storage and reloading. “Höegh Evi is proud to work with PETROS as development partner in the Kuching LNG Terminal, a testament to our proven track record delivering floating LNG infrastructure projects. We are committed to supporting Sarawak’s evolving infrastructure needs and enabling long-term growth in the region,” said Erik Nyheim, CEO in Höegh Evi. PETROS is the master developer of the wider Kuching Low-Carbon development. The companies also plan to explore knowledge sharing, training and skills development as part of the project.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543382-so.text: US President Donald Trump unveiled plans on Wednesday for South Korea to invest some $200 billion in US projects, but Seoul quickly suggested one key element, a $54 billion pipeline for an LNG project in Alaska, was not yet set in stone. The announcement from the White House amounted to the first set of major projects under a broader $350 billion strategic investment package South Korea made as part of a trade agreement with Washington last year. The package included $150 billion for shipbuilding and $200 billion for strategic investments. "Thanks to the agreements my administration has secured with the Republic of Korea, they will invest up to $200 billion," Trump said from the Oval Office. He said the investment would include the construction of eight large-scale nuclear power plants, a natural gas pipeline and a 6-gigawatt power generation facility in Texas. The announcement is the latest in a series of economic and investment deals Trump is highlighting ahead of November's midterm elections, as he seeks to reinforce his economic record amid voter concerns over the Iran war and high gasoline prices. The pipeline project could carry political significance in Alaska, where Republican Senator Dan Sullivan faces a competitive reelection race against Democrat Mary Peltola. Sullivan attended Wednesday's announcement.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/three-oi.text: Three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles when transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, shipping intelligence service Marisks said. The vessels had been moving through the strait with their Automatic Identification System transponders turned off to avoid detection, Marisks said in a report late on Wednesday. Oil products tanker Al Ruwais was last seen as having conducted a ship-to-ship transfer off Sohar, Oman, in late September to discharge its diesel cargo, data from analytics firm Kpler showed. Very large crude carrier Mersin Prosperity also made a ship-to-ship transfer off Sohar in mid-September to move 2 million barrels of Iraqi Basrah crude onto another vessel, Kpler data showed. Aframax-sized tanker Sinbad loaded refined products at Saudi Arabia's Jubail industrial port in early September, the data showed. ADNOC Logistics & Services ADNOCLS.AD, which manages Al Ruwais and Mersin Prosperity, declined to comment.

https://splash247.com/transpetrol-trims-.text: Belgian tanker owner Transpetrol Maritime Services has offloaded its 2016-built aframax in a $73m deal with Turkish buyers. VesselsValue data identified Transpetrol as the seller of the Hyundai Samho-built 114,070 dwt TP Affinity and put the ship’s current market value at $80.72m. Transpetrol’s own fleet records show it was delivered in July 2016 and completed a scheduled drydock in Singapore in July. The reported disposal comes as Transpetrol pours capital into younger tonnage. Splash covered the company’s most recent order of two 75,000 dwt LR1 product tankers at Yangzijiang Shipbuilding for delivery in 2030, its first newbuildings in the segment. Earlier this year, it also booked two 90,000 cu m dual-fuel VLGCs at HD Hyundai Samho and has been taking delivery of a series of LR2s. Transpetrol currently lists TP Affinity and TP Spirit as its two aframaxes. Completion of the sale would therefore leave the company with a single ship in the segment while its LR1, LR2 and gas carrier fleets expand. The privately held outfit has also recently been linked to a sale of two 2011 Japanese-built MR2s, Turmoil and Luctor .

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/eas.text: Singapore-based shipowner Eastern Pacific Shipping (EPS) has taken delivery of a new LNG dual-fuel pure car and truck carrier (PCTC) that Spain’s Suardiaz Group will operate under a charter. The 5,500 CEU vessel RS Atlantico was built at the Xiamen shipyard which is a part of China’s Fujian Chuanzheng Shipbuilding group. The vessel was developed as a collaboration between EPS and Suardiaz. The vessel has left the shipyard for Europe, Suardiaz said. During the launch of the vessel in June, Suardiaz said it will operate on the company’s Atlantic routes. It is the first PCTC newbuilding EPS has chartered to Suardiaz, and the first LNG dual-fuel PCTC to join Suardiaz’s operations. Source: By Nachiket Tekawade, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

https://gcaptain.com/tanker-congestion-s.text: Stock Photo: Tankers carrying out a ship-to-ship (STS) transfer at sea. Photo: Shutterstock/Vallehr Oct 1, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Persian Gulf oil producers are shifting critical cargo transfer operations even farther out of the war-hit region as waters just outside the Strait of Hormuz become congested with tankers. It’s another illustration of the maritime convulsions caused by the war, with delayed or diverted shipments helping to drive the cost of hiring a supertanker to above $1 million a day, adding to price pressures on crude and refined fuels. The Gulf of Kutch, off the coast of Gujarat in western India, is emerging as an alternative waypoint for transferring Persian Gulf cargoes onto vessels that will deliver them to buyers around the world, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg and consultant Vortexa. Two supertankers recently conducted ship-to-ship transfers — also known as STS — onto other very large crude carriers in the Gulf of Kutch, the data show. The receiving vessels are now headed to East Asia, signaling Singapore and South Korea. These are the first eastbound Gulf crude cargo transfers observed in the area since the Iran war began. At least two more VLCCs are currently performing STS transfers in the region, the data show.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/sea.text: New AI-powered assistant helps maritime professionals find answers to contract queries, surface risk and make more confident fixing decisions — built directly into Sea’s Contract Management. Sea, the intelligent marketplace for fixing freight, today announced the launch of Cora, its new AIpowered assistant built into Contract Management, the industry standard for charter party and recap management. A fixture can turn on a single clause. But that clause might be buried in an amendment, worded differently to a company’s standard position, or missing entirely – and finding out can often mean hours spent cross-checking documents while a deal is moving. Cora has been created to close that gap: chartering, legal and operating teams can now ask a question in natural language -“Which contracts are missing a sanctions clause?”, “What was our last agreed position with this counterparty?” – and get an answer grounded in their own contract portfolio, in seconds, catching what would otherwise take significant time and manual review to find. Unlike general-purpose AI tools, Cora is trained specifically on maritime language, charter party structures and clause logic – understanding niche shipping concepts in a way general models can’t. It also sits within Sea’s own security environment, a protection general-purpose chatbots don’t necessarily offer, always keeping sensitive contract data safe within a customer’s own ring-fenced space at all times. With Cora, users can: • Find any answer in seconds – laytime, demurrage, trading limits and more — without digging through folders or chasing colleagues for the latest version • Catch what’s missing before it becomes exposure – spot inconsistent or absent clauses across an entire portfolio, not just the contract in front of them • Negotiate from a position of strength – see instantly how terms have been agreed with a counterparty before, and benchmark new positions against a company’s own fixture history • Make fixing decisions with the full picture, not a partial one pieced together under time pressure -commercial terms, clause history and risk, together in one place • Stay consistent with approved positions, comparing new wording against a company’s own standard clauses or BIMCO’s industry-standard library Cora is designed to support decision-making, not replace it. Contractual and legal assessments, and the final commercial call on any fixture, remain firmly with the team making it.

https://splash247.com/akrotiri-tankers-d.text: Greek tanker newcomer Akrotiri Tankers has returned to New Times Shipbuilding for a second suezmax, continuing a rapid expansion of its Chinese newbuilding programme. Shipbroking sources place the latest order at $84.4m for a 157,000 dwt crude tanker scheduled for delivery in June 2029. The contract takes Akrotiri’s suezmax orderbook to two ships. The Marielena Procopiou and Konstantinos Lampsias-led company made its first move into the segment earlier this year, booking a ship of the same size at New Times for around $82m, also with delivery in 2029. That order marked Akrotiri’s expansion beyond the LR1 product tanker segment on which it initially built its fleet. New Times has quickly become Akrotiri’s main newbuilding partner. The owner started out with two LR1s at the yard late last year before moving into larger crude tonnage, and earlier this month added two 93,000 cu m VLACs for 2029 delivery in its first venture into gas shipping.

https://splash247.com/imperial-petroleum.text: Harry Vafias-led Imperial Petroleum has reportedly sold its remaining suezmax, the 2008-built Suez Protopia , for $82m. VesselsValue identified Imperial Petroleum as the seller in its September 30 transaction data. The buyer has not been disclosed. VesselsValue estimates the Samsung Heavy Industries-built 160,391 dwt tanker at $74.34m, putting the reported transaction about $7.7m above its valuation. The deal would take Imperial Petroleum completely out of the suezmax segment. Its September 10 fleet update listed Suez Protopia as its sole remaining suezmax after the company sold the 2007-built Suez Enchanted in August. Imperial said that disposal generated a net gain of approximately $32m. Imperial bought Suez Protopia and Suez Enchanted together in 2022 for just $46.8m in total, taking delivery of both on June 3 that year. The reported $82m price for Suez Protopia alone is therefore substantially higher than the original aggregate purchase price of the two ships, although their individual acquisition costs were never disclosed. Imperial has not been shrinking overall. The Nasdaq-listed owner recently said it had 21 ships on the water and four acquisitions lined up, taking the fleet towards 25 vessels. Its tanker exposure following the reported suezmax sale would be concentrated in MR product carriers, alongside a growing dry bulk fleet.

https://petronoticias.com.br/navemestra-.text: A Navemestra, empresa de bunkering do Grupo Bravante, deve iniciar ainda neste ano a construção de uma série de seis novos rebocadores portuários. As obras das embarcações acontecerão no Estaleiro São Miguel, em São Gonçalo (RJ), também integrante do Grupo Bravante, retomando novos investimentos após mais de cinco anos. O projeto conta com financiamento aprovado pelo Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e é mais um passo para o renascimento da indústria naval brasileira. O diretor de Novos Negócios do Grupo Bravante, Thiago Lemgruber , explica que a companhia pretende manter os investimentos em renovação e expansão de frota, além de investir na melhoria contínua dos negócios. “ O mercado tem alto potencial com as perspectivas da expansão em diversas frentes, desde a Margem Equatorial até Pelotas, passando por Sergipe e a expansão continua no pré-sal ”, avaliou. Poderia começar explicando quais foram os motivos que permitiram a retomada de novos investimentos do grupo para a construção das embarcações? O Grupo Bravante acessou o Fundo de Marinha Mercante que oferece condições competitivas para financiamento de construção naval. Dessa forma foi possível resgatar o relacionamento com o BNDES para financiar a renovação da frota marítima do Grupo Bravante, iniciando com o projeto de construção de rebocadores portuários para atuar no mercado de bunkering. https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: Priscilla Bueno assume hoje, dia 1º de outubro, como CEO global da Craft. A nomeação sucede uma transição planejada com Marcellus Hansford e Marcio Dias e dá continuidade à estratégia de crescimento da companhia, que completará 30 anos em 2027. Ao longo de quase 21 anos na Craft, Priscilla construiu uma trajetória da operação ao Conselho de Administração. Liderou a criação e o desenvolvimento de linhas de negócio, começando pelo produto aéreo e ampliando sua atuação para FCL Importação e procurement, além de participar da expansão internacional da companhia. Fundou também a Craft U, plataforma de educação voltada a todo o mercado. Mais recentemente, como Chief Transformation Officer (CTO), conduziu as agendas de transformação em tecnologia e pessoas e compartilhou a condução da empresa com Marcio. À frente de uma diretoria experiente, Priscilla terá como foco a integração dos negócios e dos países, o desenvolvimento das verticais de produtos e tecnologia para sustentar a expansão da Craft junto a seus clientes e parceiros. “Nosso próximo ciclo parte de uma base construída ao longo de quase três décadas. Vamos preservar a visão empreendedora de Marcellus, que deu origem à Craft e segue orientando sua evolução. Temos conhecimento de mercado, negócios especializados e equipes com capacidade de realização. Meu papel é seguir dando direção, conectar as competências dos nossos times e garantir que nossa escala se traduza em valor para que clientes, parceiros e equipes prosperem junto com a Craft”, afirma Priscilla. Após 13 anos na Craft, Marcio Dias encerrou sua atuação executiva em 30 de setembro para se dedicar a um empreendimento próprio. Sua liderança contribuiu para a expansão da companhia, o fortalecimento da cultura comercial, a formação de lideranças e a construção de relações duradouras com clientes e parceiros. Para Marcellus Hansford, fundador da Craft, a escolha reúne conhecimento profundo do negócio e capacidade de transformação. “Priscilla liderou a construção de negócios que fazem parte do que a Craft é hoje. Sua experiência conecta operação, mercado, pessoas e estratégia. Poucas pessoas reúnem uma visão tão completa da companhia e, ao mesmo tempo, tanta capacidade de conduzir sua evolução.”

Durante anos, a transição energética esteve associada principalmente aos carros, à expansão das fontes renováveis e à transformação da matriz energética. Pouco se falava, porém, sobre um mercado que pode movimentar centenas de bilhões de dólares nas próximas décadas: a descarbonização do transporte marítimo, responsável por cerca de 90% do comércio mundial e aproximadamente 3% das emissões globais de CO₂. A combinação entre novas regulações internacionais, precificação das emissões e crescente preocupação com segurança energética está mudando a lógica de um setor que movimenta a economia global. Reduzir emissões deixa de ser apenas uma agenda ambiental para se tornar uma questão de competitividade, em um setor com imensa sensibilidade a custo e efeito em cadeia nos preços, principalmente de alimentos. Essa transformação abre espaço para combustíveis capazes de reunir atributos que raramente coexistem: baixa intensidade de carbono, disponibilidade em escala, infraestrutura consolidada e viabilidade econômica. É nesse contexto que o etanol passa a ocupar uma posição de destaque. Hoje, a evolução dos motores marítimos e as primeiras operações comerciais demonstram que seu potencial é realidade. Os principais fabricantes de motores navais já desenvolvem plataformas multicombustível capazes de operar com diferentes alternativas. Além de seus benefícios ambientais, o etanol oferece outras vantagens relevantes. É isento de enxofre, apresenta menor toxicidade e requer procedimentos de segurança menos complexos para armazenamento, transporte e abastecimento, fatores que contribuem para ampliar sua viabilidade em escala comercial. O primeiro abastecimento de um navio porta-contêineres transoceânico com etanol em território brasileiro, realizado recentemente no Porto de Santos, pela Copersucar e parceiros, simboliza essa mudança. Mais do que uma operação pioneira, ela comprova que a transição energética da navegação já começou. A operação realizada no maior porto da América Latina demonstra que existe um caminho tecnicamente viável para inserir o etanol na matriz energética da navegação internacional.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: O Rio de Janeiro não terá lei seca nas eleições de 2026. A venda e o consumo de bebidas alcoólicas estarão permitidos no dia de votação. A restrição à comercialização e ao consumo de bebidas alcoólicas nas eleições não é aplicada desde 1996. Essa decisão cabe às autoridades de cada estado. O primeiro turno ocorre no domingo (4) de outubro. Os eleitores escolhem o presidente da República, o governador, dois senadores, um deputado federal e um deputado estadual.

O candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro, Coronel Busnello, propôs nesta quinta-feira (1) medidas contra o crime organizado. Suas propostas focam em investigação e transformação de favelas. O candidato criticou o prefeito de São Gonçalo, Capitão Nelson, e seu filho, Douglas Ruas. Ruas também disputa o cargo de governador do Estado. Busnello apontou que São Gonçalo é a cidade com mais barricadas. Ele declarou que o prefeito e seu filho são policiais e não solucionaram a questão. O plano de desfavelização consiste em transformar favelas em bairros normais. O candidato planeja incluir as pessoas na sociedade formal por meio de títulos de propriedade. Busnello participou de um ato em Niterói, na Região Metropolitana do Rio. O evento contou com a presença de Renan Santos, candidato à presidência pelo Missão.

Neste domingo (4), o transporte público estadual do Rio de Janeiro terá serviço gratuito das 6h às 20h. A medida visa facilitar o deslocamento de eleitores. A gratuidade vale para barcas, trens, metrô e ônibus intermunicipais urbanos. O benefício também será oferecido no dia 25 de outubro, se houver 2º turno. O benefício não se aplica a ônibus executivos ou rodoviários. A gratuidade atende às resoluções do TSE e TRE-RJ para os dias de votação.

O candidato Douglas Ruas (PL) fez campanha nesta quinta-feira (1º) no Mercadão de Madureira, Zona Norte do Rio. Ele prometeu reforçar a segurança na região. Ruas propôs implementar o Segurança Presente no polo comercial. O objetivo é reduzir roubos de rua e apoiar os negócios locais. Se eleito, o candidato promete convocar concursados da segurança. Ele planeja investir R$ 1,6 bilhão para aumentar o efetivo da Polícia Militar.

O candidato Eduardo Paes prometeu construir um hospital com emergência 24 horas em Mesquita, na Baixada Fluminense. Ele realizou uma caminhada no município nesta quinta-feira (1). Paes visitou o terreno de uma antiga fábrica fechada há mais de 10 anos. O espaço foi o local escolhido para receber o novo hospital. O candidato planeja expandir a rede básica para evitar a transferência de pacientes. Ele também pretende aumentar o orçamento geral da saúde.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: Observers have noted that a large vessel backlog appears to be building in the Baltic and the Gulf of Finland as vessels wait to reach Russian ports. The Finnish newspaper Helsingin Sanomat calculated that as of the end of September, there were as many as 150 vessels bound for Russia holding in the region. The newspaper’s analysis shows that most of the vessels are trying to reach the ports in the Ust-Luga region, including the oil terminal as well as the neighboring bulk port at Laukaansuu. Some of the others are holding for Primorsk and St. Petersburg. It reports that the congestion grew through all of September and is now termed as “an exceptionally large number of ships queuing for Russian ports.” Officials at the Gulf of Finland Coast Guard confirmed the paper said that there was a larger than normal number of vessels and a large number of ships waiting for the Russian ports. It noted the number varies and sometimes clears quickly. Helsingin Sanomat, however, says the backlog appears to be continuing to build. By its calculation, there were 65 tankers and 85 cargo ships waiting on September 30. It spotted two large groupings, one near Laukaansuu and the other further out to sea. This included 16 tankers and 30 general cargo ships in the area around the port complex near Ust-Luga and Laukaansuu. A line of vessels stretches across the Gulf of Finland and into the Baltic, with two large groupings of ships waiting to get into Russian ports (courtesy of Marine Traffic ) It also pointed out that there was a line stretching for more than 30 miles across the Gulf of Finland and into the Baltic. As of September 30, it said there were 46 vessels making up the lineup.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Police in Indonesia are formally investigating the master of the Virgo Transport 8, the ferry that capsized in the Java Sea last month with the loss of dozens of lives. Local police in South Kalimantan initially handled the case, and the captain remains in detention in their care. Responsibility for the criminal investigation has been passed up to the National Police's Water Police Directorate for further work. At this stage, the inquiry is still preliminary - involving interviews and event sequence reconstruction - and the police are determining who (if anyone) may be accused of wrongdoing, an officer told Jakarta Globe. On Sept. 30, the 18th day of search operations, divers and shoreside beach teams recovered another four bodies, bringing the total number of confirmed fatalities to 78 people. Many have been retrieved from inside the wreck in difficult conditions, including five who were found on the 17th day of the search (Sept. 29). 57 remain missing and the effort to locate them continues. Of the recovered victims, 27 have yet to be identified. As the search period extends into weeks, not just days, the condition of the recovered bodies is deteriorating, making the operation more challenging. The wreck is itself upside down, creating a disorienting environment, and there are powerful prevailing currents at the wreck site - an inherent hazard for diving. https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: On Wednesday night, the U.S. Coast Guard launched a high-priority effort to try to find a missing individual from a medical-flight helicopter that crashed shortly after taking off from Catalina Island. Two people were killed in the crash, including the pilot, per the Oceanside Fire Department. Two occupants of the flight were saved and hospitalized in stable condition. The last individual aboard the helicopter remained missing as of Thursday. Initial reports indicated a total of three people aboard the aircraft, but this was incorrect and later revised upwards. The aircraft's operator acknowledged the incident in a statement and confirmed that it is working with the authorities. It added that it could not currently provide further comments. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has joined the investigation. The Coast Guard initially deployed an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter aircrew and a response boat out of LA/Long Beach. LA County's fire department joined the effort with assets from multiple locations. The USCG said in a statement Thursday that the search has expanded to include a subsurface examination of the helicopter's wreckage, performed via ROV. The wreck sits in 240 feet of water, according to local media, a depth that adds risk and requires more skill for human divers to perform safely. NTSB said in an emailed statement to local KTLA that there are plans in motion to recover the wreckage of the helicopter from the bottom for the purposes of the investigation.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: A small cargo ship sailing from Sweden to Estonia was briefly detained by the Russian authorities for an inspection late on Wednesday, September 30, into Thursday, October 1. The Estonian Broadcasting Corporation (ERR) reported the situation and received confirmation from the Estonian Police and Border Guard Board. The Västerbotten (6,800 dwt) has been owned and operated by a German company since 2013, and according to its AIS track, it was sailing from Monsteras, Sweden, bound for Sillamäe, Estonia, when it was intercepted and stopped for an inspection. The tracking shows the ship making sharp turns and changing course. The ship, which was built in 2008, is registered in Cyprus. The Estonian Transport Administration told ERR that it had not received an explanation from the Russian authorities. It can only speculate as to why the vessel was detained and inspected. Route of the past 24 hours showing turns as the vessel was stopped for an inspection by Russian authorities ( Vessel Finder ) The ship’s route is along an internationally recognized corridor and one that Russia, Estonia, and Finland agreed to. It is used by ships to avoid some of the dangers of the coastal waters in Estonia, but in places it skirts and enters the Russian zone. Sillamäe, the authorities noted, is a rarely used port, and it is located close to Russia. The interception appears to have happened as the vessel approached or entered Russian waters. The news outlet EA Daily speculates the ship was taking the shortest available route. It would have saved about 4.5 miles and 40 minutes of sailing time, they write. Instead, it reports the ship was detained about six miles from the Estonian border.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office announced a further round of sanctions on Russia, which it said were meant to increase pressure in response to the recent increase in attacks in Ukraine and ahead of the coming winter season. Among the new targets are Russia’s new fleet of ARC7 LNG carriers currently being delivered from the Zvezda Shipbuilding Complex. In announcing the new sanctions, the Minister for Europe, Lord Wood, noted that Russia increased its aggression against Ukraine in recent months, firing over 3,100 jet-powered drones in September, which outstripped the record level in August. He also pointed to the sham elections in the occupied areas and the continued propaganda efforts from Russia. The UK asserts that international sanctions have already cost Russia nearly $500 billion in funding while saying the pressure must be maintained. It notes that the UK has been among the most aggressive with sanctions on vessels, having listed approximately 600 tankers and other vessels from the Russian fleet or used by Russia in the shadow fleet. The UK and EU continue to vie for the most ships sanctioned, with the EU having reached 673 as of the 21st package. The latest UK listing includes three of Russia’s newest large ice-class LNG carriers. Two of the vessels were delivered this year and last year, while the third is still outfitting at the Zvezda Shipbuilding Complex. Included are Aleksey Kosygin (IMO 9904546), Konstantin Posiet (IMO 9904704), and Pyotr Stolypin (IMO 9904675). Zvezda, and Sovcomflot, which owns the vessels, as well as Novatek, highlight the LNG carriers, which each hold over 172,000 cubic meters of liquefied natural gas, as among the most advanced in the fleet. They are 81,000 dwt and 300 meters (984 feet) in length, with a capability of handling ice at over two meters (6.5 feet) thickness. The United States has already sanctioned the vessels, as has the EU, for the two that were delivered. The new UK package also includes three older LNG carriers. It also adds a small product tanker used for support and bunkering, which appears to have recently been delivered to Turkey for recycling. It also lists a crew offshore support vessel registered in Sri Lanka. With the primary target being the LNG operations, the UK also extended the sanctions to Novatek Gas and Power Asia. It is a chartering arm of the Russian company based in Singapore.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The Philippine Coast Guard is still on the scene of a fire aboard a tanker carrying molasses that was docked in Calaca, south of Manila. The vessel was alongside the Balayan Distillery when the fire broke out. The Coast Guard reports that the city disaster management office and the local fire teams responded to the fire, which was thought to have begun in the engine room of the tanker Gindara . Pictures from the scene show the fire spread into the accommodation block and reached the bridge of the vessel. There were 22 crewmembers aboard the ship when the fire began. The Coast Guard said 20 were accounted for and reported safe, while two sustained injuries and were taken to local hospitals. There was no update on their conditions. The Coast Guard dispatched its 144-foot multi-role response vessel BRP Malapascua to the scene to assist with the firefighting. As of Thursday during the day, the Coast Guard was reporting that no additional fire was visible on the bridge or in the superstructure of the vessel, although smoke remained visible. There was no indication of what caused the fire. The Coast Guard was planning to conduct an investigation once the firefighting efforts were completed.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Nautika Coberturas concluiu a instalação de nove galpões que totalizam 55 mil m² para uma montadora instalada no polo automotivo de Camaçari (BA). Contratadas por meio de locação, as estruturas foram entregues em diferentes etapas, sendo que a primeira, com 33,4 mil m², foi concluída em aproximadamente 30 dias. A empresa não divulgou o nome da montadora. Os galpões, 100% entregues e operacionais, são utilizados como pátio coberto para armazenagem de itens de alto valor agregado, protegendo os materiais contra intempéries. O projeto exigiu estruturas com grandes vãos livres, sem pilares centrais, para facilitar a movimentação de empilhadeiras e rebocadores e permitir a instalação de porta-paletes. Segundo a Nautika, a execução em prazo reduzido foi viabilizada pela disponibilidade imediata de componentes em estoque, pelo uso de estruturas pré-fabricadas com sistemas de engate rápido e pela mobilização simultânea de várias equipes de montagem. A operação também envolveu desafios logísticos, como o transporte de centenas de toneladas de perfis metálicos e lonas até a Bahia. A montagem foi realizada por equipes que trabalharam em paralelo, com o uso de guindastes e plataformas elevatórias e protocolos de segurança exigidos pela indústria automotiva. A empresa também precisou adequar os sistemas de fixação às condições do solo e prever possíveis variações climáticas durante o içamento das estruturas. De acordo com Carlos Pela, presidente da Nautika, o projeto demonstra a capacidade da empresa de atender a grandes demandas com planejamento e agilidade. Os galpões contam com estruturas metálicas galvanizadas, dimensionadas para resistir a rajadas de vento, e coberturas de lona vinílica com proteção contra raios ultravioleta, tratamento antimofo e propriedades antichamas. O projeto também prevê recursos para aproveitamento da iluminação natural e ventilação, considerando as condições climáticas da região.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A DP World recebeu, em setembro, dois portêineres e seis guindastes de pátio sobre pneus (RTGs) para seu terminal no Porto de Santos (SP) . A entrega integra um plano de investimentos superior a R$ 2 bilhões voltado à modernização e à ampliação da infraestrutura da companhia no Brasil. O lote faz parte da aquisição de quatro portêineres e 15 RTGs . Com os primeiros equipamentos e a otimização das estruturas já licenciadas, a empresa prevê elevar a capacidade anual do terminal, atualmente de 1,4 milhão, para 1,7 milhão de TEUs até o fim de 2026 . TEU é a unidade equivalente a um contêiner de 20 pés. A segunda entrega está prevista para o início de 2027. A incorporação de todos os equipamentos, combinada com novas intervenções estruturais, deverá ampliar a capacidade para 2,1 milhões de TEUs nos próximos anos , segundo a companhia. "Estamos ampliando nossa capacidade operacional para atender ao crescimento do comércio exterior brasileiro com mais eficiência, produtividade e sustentabilidade", afirma o CEO da DP World Brasil, Fabio Siccherino . Fabricados pela chinesa ZPMC , os portêineres movimentam contêineres entre os navios e o cais. Os novos modelos possuem 72 metros de alcance , sete metros a mais que os equipamentos atualmente em operação no terminal, e 56 metros de altura do cais à lança, permitindo atender embarcações de maior porte. Com tecnologia Siemens, os portêineres têm capacidade para movimentar até 65 toneladas na operação com dois contêineres de 20 pés, 50 toneladas com um único contêiner e 80 toneladas com gancho para cargas especiais e não conteinerizadas.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543398-si.text: Siemens Energy has contracted EST-Floattech to supply a battery system of more than 1 MWh for Marco Polo Marine's new CSOV Plus, a vessel designed to work in both offshore wind and oil and gas operations. The Octopus High Energy battery system will support hybrid and dynamic positioning operations aboard the vessel, which is being built by Marco Polo Marine at its shipyard in Batam, Indonesia. Siemens Energy is the system integrator for the hybrid power plant. During dynamic positioning, the batteries will provide spinning reserve and absorb variations in power demand, allowing fewer generator sets to operate and enabling those in use to run closer to their optimal load. The vessel has also been designed to allow its battery capacity to be expanded to 20 MWh in the future, which would enable fully electric sailing. Space for the additional modules has been incorporated into the design. Designed by Salt Ship Design, the CSOV Plus will feature a 100-tonne active heave-compensated crane and a motion-compensated gangway capable of walk-to-work transfers in significant wave heights of up to 3 meters. Construction started in the second quarter of 2026, with delivery scheduled for the second quarter of 2028.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A fabricante de móveis gaúcha Madesa ampliou a capacidade de armazenagem e expedição de seu centro de distribuição em Bom Princípio (RS) com um investimento adicional de R$ 4 milhões . A expansão acontece menos de um ano após a inauguração da estrutura, que custou R$ 51 milhões. Com 31 mil m² e operação plena alcançada em 2026, o empreendimento foi criado para centralizar a operação logística da empresa, integrando os processos de armazenagem, separação e expedição de pedidos. A estrutura opera desde 2025, e contribuiu para o faturamento de R$ 1 bilhão da Madesa no ano passado . "Essa nova estrutura ampliou a capacidade operacional da empresa, reduziu movimentações internas e criou as condições necessárias para sustentar o crescimento da empresa nos próximos anos", afirma Pedro Cini, CEO da Madesa . De acordo com o executivo, o investimento representa uma etapa estratégica para acompanhar a evolução do negócio e ampliar a integração dos processos internos. "Agora temos uma capacidade de armazenagem significativamente maior, com uma operação logística mais integrada e preparada para atender ao crescimento da demanda. Para o cliente, o principal benefício é uma experiência de compra mais ágil, desde o processamento do pedido até a expedição do produto", destaca o executivo. O novo centro de distribuição foi projetado para integrar indústria e logística em um único fluxo operacional. De acordo com a empresa, o modelo reduz deslocamentos internos, melhora a organização dos estoques e aumenta a eficiência na separação dos pedidos. A operação de armazenagem foi estruturada de acordo com as características do portfólio da Madesa, formado por produtos com elevada cubagem e embalagens de diferentes dimensões. Por essa razão, a companhia adotou um modelo logístico flexivel, com movimentação mecanizada e a preparação desse tipo de mercadoria. O formato permite adaptar a operação à variedade de produtos e otimizar o uso do espaço disponível.

A Emergent Cold LatAm , operadora de logística de alimentos com temperatura controlada, divulgou o Panorama de Sustentabilidade 2025 , que reúne indicadores ambientais, sociais e de gestão referentes ao ano passado. Segundo o documento, a companhia registrou redução de 23% nas emissões totais de gases de efeito estufa , em um período no qual sua capacidade operacional cresceu 52%. Na frente energética, as fontes renováveis representaram 65% da matriz da empresa . O consumo de energia solar aumentou 394%, enquanto a capacidade instalada de geração solar passou de 11,9 MW para 19,9 MW, avanço de 67%. As emissões diretas das operações caíram 53%, de acordo com o balanço. “Para uma empresa que opera uma infraestrutura com alta demanda de energia, sustentabilidade significa assumir a responsabilidade de crescer reduzindo o impacto de nossas operações”, afirma Moises Ventocilla, diretor de Engenharia da Emergent Cold LatAm . O relatório também aponta redução de 23% no consumo total de água e volume de reúso 16 vezes maior que o registrado em 2024. A quantidade de resíduos destinada a aterros caiu 43%, e o percentual de reaproveitamento de materiais passou de 71% para 83%. Em relação às instalações, a empresa obteve 16 novas certificações EDGE em 2025 e encerrou o período com 22 armazéns certificados em diferentes níveis LEED ou EDGE , incluindo oito classificados como carbono zero. Os indicadores acompanham a expansão da companhia, cuja rede chegou a 110 armazéns em 11 países em 2025. No Brasil, a aquisição da Comfrio ampliou sua presença no mercado. O número de colaboradores passou de 3.757 para 7.034 ao longo do ano.

Este artigo examina as possíveis trajetórias da produção, a dimensão e o aspecto crítico das reservas, os novos acordos de investimentos e os riscos jurídicos e políticos associados ao tratamento desses recursos pelo governo interino, sob a vigilância do governo norte-americano Mesmo com as dificuldades impostas pela extração de petróleo predominante pesado (até 21 API), a Venezuela vinha apresentando crescimento contínuo desde a década de 1940, tendo alcançado seu máximo histórico de 3,71 milhões de barris/dia em 1970. Após a nacionalização da indústria do petróleo no país, em 1976, e a criação da estatal PDVSA, a produção declinou bastante até 1985. No período entre 1985 e 1998, a produção voltou a crescer com a contribuição de iniciativas, como os Convênios Operacionais e os Convênios/Alianças Estratégicas, com o aporte de investimentos estrangeiros, chegando a ultrapassar os 3 milhões de barris/dia. Em 2 de fevereiro de 1999, quando Hugo Chávez assumiu o poder, a PDVSA já estava bem posicionada como geradora de valor. Mas a partir deste momento passou por turbulências e iniciou seu declínio da produção. Um fato marcante ocorrido entre 2002 e 2003 foi a demissão de 18 mil trabalhadores - recursos humanos de alto nível técnico e gerencial da PDVSA – ordenada por Chavez porque se opunham às suas ideias. Após 2007, a indústria sofreu outro revés. Expropriações, via cancelamento unilateral dos Convênios Operacionais e dos Convênios/Alianças Estratégicas, converteu as empresas no país em “empresas mistas” controladas e operadas pela PDVSA que, assim, assumiu o controle total e monopolista de toda a indústria petrolífera venezuelana. O gráfico publicado em artigo da Reuters “How Venezuela pulled its oil production out of a tailspin”, por Parraga, M., de 27/12/2021, mostra o histórico da evolução da produção de petróleo do país, incluindo altos e baixos e o declínio da produção. Os recentes eventos na Venezuela, após a captura de Nicolás Maduro por forças americanas, em janeiro, acarretaram muitas mudanças na indústria petroleira do país. Aos poucos vai acontecendo a retomada das atividades e, fato relevante, a redução das vendas do petróleo para alguns países, entre estes China e Cuba. O governo venezuelano vem adotando outras medidas em relação a indústria de petróleo, não se sabe se por convicção ou por orientação emanada pelos Estados Unidos. Daí há o risco de uma possível ilegitimidade das novas regras e de possíveis conflitos futuros com outros governos que venham a suceder o atual ou mesmo com organizações civis ainda bem atuantes.
