https://www.marinelog.com/news/more-uscg.text: A new report from the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) says that the U.S. Coast Guard needs to take more action to address marine firefighting challenges. The watchdog agency notes that fires on vessels are among the most dangerous and challenging incidents to which firefighters can respond. Vessels may also carry hazardous cargo, like lithium-ion batteries, further complicating marine firefighting responses. According to U.S. Coast Guard data, there were 886 nearshore marine fires that occurred between 2015 and 2025. About one quarter (206) of these resulted in either death, injury, over $200,000 in damage, or a total loss of the vessel. The U.S. Coast Guard is the principal federal agency responsible for overseeing marine safety. For marine firefighting, the Coast Guard plays a coordinating role while land-based fire departments extinguish fires. Following a marine fire that resulted in two firefighter deaths in 2023, the Coast Guard established a task force to address various marine firefighting challenges. The task force has taken several steps to address them but gaps remain. Designating consistent Coast Guard field personnel to lead coordination before marine fires occur, facilitating more hands-on training for firefighters on vessels, and establishing an information sharing mechanism would help ensure firefighters have the knowledge and skills necessary to safely and effectively extinguish vessel fires, says GAO. Further, developing guidance on what warrants vessel response plan activation would help ensure resources are quickly mobilized and better ensure the safety of firefighters.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 1º/10/2026 – A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) realizou, entre os dias 21 e 25 de setembro, o Encontro Nacional de Fiscalização (Enafis 2026), em Curitiba e Paranaguá (PR). Organizado pela Superintendência de Fiscalização e Coordenação das Unidades Regionais (SFC), o evento reuniu cerca de 80 fiscais presencialmente em uma programação com debates, palestras, apresentações e visitas técnicas voltadas ao aprimoramento das atividades de fiscalização do setor aquaviário. O Enafis é um espaço de integração técnica e reciclagem profissional dos servidores que atuam na fiscalização. A programação teve como objetivo promover a atualização sobre normas e procedimentos, contribuir para a padronização das atividades operacionais e fortalecer conhecimentos aplicados à regulação e ao controle do setor. A programação teórica, realizada nos quatro primeiros dias do encontro, contou com transmissão ao vivo e foi aberta a todos os servidores e colaboradores da ANTAQ, independentemente da área de atuação. Entre os temas abordados estiveram logística de contêineres e Direito Marítimo, inteligência artificial, dados abertos para análise técnica, fiscalização portuária, navegação interior, acompanhamento de investimentos e procedimentos fiscalizatórios e sancionadores. O diretor-geral da ANTAQ, Frederico Dias, participou da programação do primeiro dia e falou aos fiscais sobre aspectos relacionados à atuação das equipes, como foco na resolução de problemas e em resultados, trabalho colaborativo, flexibilidade e inovação. Ao longo do encontro, os participantes acompanharam discussões sobre gestão e fiscalização portuária, acessos aquaviários, dragagem, sinalização e balizamento, além de conhecerem o Sistema de Acompanhamento de Investimentos (SAI), desenvolvido pela SFC para otimizar, padronizar e automatizar o monitoramento dos investimentos previstos nos contratos de arrendamento portuário e nos contratos de adesão.

https://splash247.com/tankers-enter-the-.text: Like climbers entering the death zone above 8,000 metres en route to the summit of Everest, VLCCs have entered their own peak: the moment where prices for secondhand tonnage surpass newbuild prices, and sell signs flash hard. These moments tend to be fleeting and have historically been associated with the hottest stages of shipping cycles. The question is how often the market has reached this altitude before, and how long it can survive there. The numbers today are extraordinary. VesselsValue, a Veson Nautical solution, puts a five-year-old VLCC at $207.6m, almost 49% more than the $139.6m value of a newbuilding. A 10-year-old ship is assessed at $182m, while a 15-year-old VLCC has just edged above the newbuild benchmark at $140.1m. A prompt resale is valued at $226.4m. The explanation is delivery time. Owners can earn today’s spectacular freight rates with an existing ship, whereas a newbuilding ordered now will generally not appear until r 2029, by which time the market could look very different. That immediacy has rarely been worth more. Clarksons Research said this week that global VLCC earnings were running at around $600,000 a day, 17 times their 10-year average, as recovering Middle Eastern export volumes collide with severe disruption to normal tanker trading patterns. The precise historical frequency of the secondhand-over-newbuild phenomenon depends heavily on what is measured. Rebecca Galanopoulos at Veson Nautical uses a five-year-old VLCC as the benchmark, arguing that a zero-year-old resale frequently commands a premium to a yard contract and is therefore less meaningful as a cycle indicator. On that measure, five-year-old VLCC values have sustainably exceeded newbuild prices only five times this century: June 2000 to February 2001, May to July 2004, October to December 2004, November 2007 to October 2008, and the current run, which started on February 20 this year. The four completed periods averaged roughly six months, ranging from around two months to 11 months. The present inversion is therefore already longer than both 2004 episodes. More strikingly, it is considerably more extreme.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/j.text: Japan completed what it is calling a world’s first as it successfully demonstrated a coastal tanker using a hydrogen-fired 4-stroke high-speed engine. It is part of an ongoing research and demonstration project sponsored by The Nippon Foundation to contribute to the decarbonization of shipping. The project called for designing and demonstrating a 4,800-dwt tanker specifically designed for hydrogen propulsion. The coastal tanker Kikou Maro (IMO: 1015595) was launched on February 14, 2025, at the Nagasaki Yard of Fukuoka Shipbuilding Co., which was one of the members in the coalition for this project. The ship measures approximately 105 meters (344 feet) and was outfitted with two electric propulsion engines on two shafts. It was delivered in October 2025 to Uyeno TransTec. When sailing, the tanker is driven by electricity generated by a hydrogen fuel engine in a container mounted on deck. It is also equipped with a hybrid generator and uses lithium-ion batteries to smooth the load and optimize fuel consumption. The demonstration voyage lasted for about two hours on September 25. The tanker sailed approximately 20 miles in Osaka Bay using its hydrogen-fired engine as a carbon-neutral demonstration. The Nippon Foundation says it equated to a reduction of approximately 1.2 tons of CO2 emissions compared to conventional fossil fuels. The vessel uses an engine designed by Yanmar Power Solutions. The first bench tests for the engine were completed in October 2024, during which it successfully operated at a rated output of approximately 500 kW. During the first tests, it used a small amount of diesel oil as a pilot ignition source to burn a pre-mixed mixture of hydrogen and air. Later testing was working to transition the engine to using HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) for its pilot ignition. The project called for developing the engine, fuel supply system, and the hull design to achieve an AiP from ClassNK. It also developed the training and manual for the operation of hydrogen-fueled vessels.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: A rescue operation off the southern coast of South Africa’s Western Cape region went horribly wrong on Wednesday, September 30, with three of the rescuers having been killed and two others missing, presumed drowned. The operator of the rescue boat, AMSOL, and the South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA) both said investigations have been launched while they are working to support the families of the lost crewmembers. The tug Umkhuseli (5,400 gross tons) was dispatched on September 30 to an emergency off the coast. The vessel, which was built in 2013 and is 83 meters (272 feet) in length, is contracted to South Africa’s Department of Transportation as an emergency towing and response vessel. The vessel was operating near an offshore platform approximately 47 nautical miles south of Mossel Bay and the southern coast of South Africa. According to the report from SAMSA, one of the crewmembers working on deck fell overboard. AMSOL reports emergency protocols were immediately started, and the crew was responding to the situation. A Fast Rescue Boat (FRB) was launched with a crew to start the search and recovery of the overboard crewmember. They did not detail what caused it, but the FRB capsized, throwing its four crewmembers into the ocean. The Maritime Rescue Coordination Center in Cape was alerted and activated a search and rescue operation. The National Sea Rescue Institute and the South African Police Service responded and started a search for the now five missing crewmembers. Rescuers located three of the crewmembers, and they were recovered, but confirmed to have died. The other two individuals remained missing. The search was suspended Wednesday night but resumed on Thursday at daylight. Helicopters and boats were searching, and the tug Umkhuseli remained on the scene. The company’s tug Inkanyezi also joined the search.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The government of Pakistan has agreed to work with the country’s manufacturers and shippers to explore obtaining a dedicated containership. Like other nations, it cites the growing challenges and rising costs of shipping, while the manufacturers urge that they are at a growing disadvantage due to the problems in shipping. The Minister of Maritime Affairs hosted a meeting in Islamabad on October 1 to discuss the challenges with the shipping industry. Adidas Pakistan led the discussion along with a local manufacturer, Style Textile, and the Pakistan National Shipping Corporation. Adidas has large manufacturing capabilities in Pakistan and is also a major retailer in the country. The manufacturers and exporters emphasized the growing challenges, in part due to the disruption from the US-Iran war and the problems in the Red Sea. They highlighted the disruptions to shipping due to the rerouting of vessels away from the Gulf region and diverting around Africa to avoid the dangers from the Houthis in the Red Sea. They also cited changes in the shipping industry and the routing of the large containerships to main routes and relegating smaller ports to more limited feeder services. They emphasized that the longer shipping distances are making it more difficult to move goods and driving up the cost of shipping. Furthermore, they said it is disadvantaging Pakistani exporters compared to regional competitors who have more direct access to major markets. The Pakistan National Shipping Corporation told the meeting that it would be willing to charter or purchase a container vessel to facilitate the exporters' needs. However, they said it would have to ensure sufficient cargo volumes to make the operation commercially viable. The ministry, along with the shipping corporation and the exporters, agreed to form a working group to examine the steps available to improve shipping connectivity and access to international markets. They are also asking for other measures aimed at reducing transportation costs and improving connectivity.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Navy has signed a five-plus-two year deal with Raytheon for up to $25 billion worth of SM-6 multipurpose interceptor missiles. This SM-series variant is designed for long range anti-air warfare and has proven capability for shooting down cruise missiles, drones, and ballistic missiles, plus a secondary application as an antiship missile - all at lower cost than an SM-3. During the high-intensity phase of the war with Iran this year, the U.S. military's global stockpiles of all high-end interceptors (Patriot, THAAD, SM-3, SM-6) substantially declined, according to the Congressional Budget Office. The office estimates that "the United States has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of those munitions since June 2025." The size and multiyear structure of the new contract is is intended to correct that deficit, providing the long-term visibility that defense contractors need in order to scale up production. As of yet, Congress still has to agree to fund the contract (and others like it) with appropriations. A continuing resolution environment is expected to extend through at least early December, without a full FY2027 defense budget. Pricing from the FY2025 budget request puts the value of one SM-6 at roughly $6 million for procurement only (CBO estimates the price to be lower, at $4 million). Assuming a comparable cost structure going forward, the award would yield a production rate many times higher than the previous 125-unit-per-year contracts. “Combat credibility depends on having enough weapons, produced at the speed and scale the Fleet requires,” said Adm. Daryl Caudle, Chief of Naval Operations in a statement. “This SM-6 award gives industry the demand signal and stability to expand production, strengthen the munitions industrial base, and build the magazine depth our Fleet needs." In a parallel but far larger deal, the U.S. Army has committed to pay up to $59 billion for additional Patriot interceptors, the standard go-to ballistic missile defense munition for shoreside applications.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: Recruitment is going so well for the U.S. Coast Guard this year that it is going to be able to reopen six stations that had previously been shuttered for lack of manpower, the service said Thursday. The announcement is the start of a phased reversal of its 2023-24 adaptation strategy, which helped the Coast Guard keep core functions running with fewer people. The turnaround has been remarkable. Last year, the Coast Guard brought in 5,200 new enlisteds, beating its goal by 110 percent. It was the largest incoming cohort of recruits since 1991. Numbers remain strong this year. “Record recruiting is giving us the people we need to strengthen frontline operations,” said Adm. Kevin E. Lunday, commandant of the Coast Guard. “Returning these stations to full operations means more Coast Guard men and women serving in our communities and greater capacity to respond when the American people need us. This is an important step, and more stations will follow.” The soon-to-be-reactivated outposts are spread around the country, and include Stations Castle Hill, Rhode Island; Milford Haven, Virginia; and Saginaw River, Michigan. On the West Coast, the Coast Guard wants to bring back Stations Vallejo, Golden Gate and Rio Vista, all located in the greater Bay Area. These reopenings depend upon Congressional appropriations in the FY2027 budget - currently in a holding pattern, as the government is operating in continuing resolution status. If adopted, the FY2027 president's budget request for the Coast Guard - the service's own proposal - would add another $2.1 billion for operations and bring total personnel to nearly 55,000 FTE, an increase of more than 3,000 FTE from last year. It would be a stepping-stone on the path to raising USCG military headcount by another 15,000 servicemembers within the next few years.

Voto branco e voto nulo não são a mesma coisa na forma como são registrados na urna, mas têm o mesmo efeito na apuração das eleições: os dois são desconsiderados na contagem dos votos válidos e não são destinados a nenhum candidato ou partido. A principal diferença está na maneira como o eleitor escolhe não votar em uma candidatura. Antes da adoção das urnas eletrônicas, a votação era feita em cédulas de papel. O voto em branco acontecia quando o eleitor deixava a cédula sem marcar nenhuma opção. Com a urna eletrônica, o papel em branco foi substituído pelo botão branco. Para votar em branco, basta apertar a tecla correspondente e, em seguida, a tecla verde, de confirmação.
O eleitorado brasileiro no exterior cresceu 31,8% desde 2022, passando de 697,1 mil para cerca de 918,9 mil pessoas.
O voto é um direito, e também uma obrigação para a maior parte da população brasileira. Pessoas alfabetizadas com mais de 18 anos e menos de 70 anos precisam votar nas eleições.

Desde 2022, o horário da votação é sincronizado com o horário de Brasília. Então, oficialmente, a votação começa às 8h e termina às 17h, no horário de Brasília. Mas, nos estados em que o fuso horário é diferente, como o Amazonas, Rondônia e Mato Grosso, por exemplo, existem locais onde a votação começa às 7h e termina às 16h – no horário local. E em partes do Amazonas, o relógio vai marcar ainda mais cedo: a votação vai das 6h às 15h – no horário local.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/cru.text: Crude oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz have basically returned to levels normal before the Iran war, as U.S. military escorts have boosted shipments and pipelines have redirected flows. Crude transiting Hormuz reached a seven-day average of 13.5 million barrels per day as of Monday, which matches a prewar baseline for shipments through the strait, according to data published Wednesday by Kpler, a firm that tracks tankers and global trade flows. Iran has claimed throughout the war that it controls Hormuz and has declared the closure of the strait multiple times. But Tehran is losing its influence as strong volumes pass through Hormuz, said Matt Smith, director of commodity research at Kpler. Crude oil shipments from the Middle East region, including the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, are sometimes higher than prewar levels. The region reached a seven-day average of 19.5 million bpd as of Monday, surpassing a prewar baseline of about 17 million bpd, the Kpler data showed. But the recovery is uneven, said Natasha Kaneva, head of global commodities strategy at JPMorgan. The “crude market has largely normalized even as refined product supplies remain constrained,” Kaneva said. The world faces a global fuel crisis as supplies from the Middle East are constrained and Ukraine pounds Russian refineries. Refined products shipped through Hormuz are at a seven-day average of 677,000 bpd as of Monday compared with 3.6 million bpd before the war, according to Kpler.

https://splash247.com/precious-adds-asya.text: Thai dry bulk owner Precious Shipping has fixed its recently delivered ultramax Rossarin Naree to Asyad Shipping for up to 14 months in the latest index-linked deal for its larger bulker fleet. The Khalid Hashim-led company said the 63,500 dwt ship started a 12-to-14-month charter with Asyad on October 1 at a gross variable rate equivalent to 108% of the Baltic Exchange Supramax Index 63K weighted time-charter average over the preceding 15 days. Precious put the current equivalent rate at around $24,000 per day. The Rossarin Naree joined the fleet from China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering at the end of May as the first in a four-ship ultramax series ordered in 2024 for a combined $133.46m, or about $33.36m apiece. The latest fixture extends a string of index-linked deals for Precious. Newly delivered sistership Ratima Naree went straight to Trafigura Maritime Logistics last month for 12 to 14 months at 107.5% of the BSI 63K, equivalent to around $22,800 per day when the charter started. A couple of weeks later, the 2016-built ultramax Sunisa Naree was fixed to Singapore’s PACC Line for 11 to 13 months at 103% of the same index, then equivalent to about $23,000 per day. Asyad’s Singapore operation has built up a sizeable chartered dry bulk book of its own. The Oman-based group said its Singapore desk managed an average of 25 dry bulk ships in 2024, with a strategy weighted towards medium- and long-term chartering.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Philippine Coast Guard reported Monday that it had "disrupted" and chased off a Chinese vessel that was conducting unauthorized research within the Philippine EEZ, a breach of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. The vessel in question, Jia Hai Ke 7 (or Jiahai Ke 7 ), was spotted loitering northwest of Itbayat in the Strait of Luzon on September 28, the PCG said. The area is strategic, providing a key passage from the open Pacific into the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait, and it is home to telecom cables connecting the Philippines with Taiwan. AIS data provided by Pole Star Global appears to confirm Jia Hai Ke 7's voyage to the area from mainland China. On Thursday morning, the Philippine vessels BRP Teresa Magbanua and PCG Islander 251 were dispatched to intercept the Chinese research vessel and "drive" it out of the Philippine EEZ. After "sustained pressure" from the two Philippine vessels, the Jia Hai Ke 7 left its "loitering position" and withdrew, the PCG said. The pressure tactics included an approach to within 50 yards, a rare example of Philippine ships employing assertive maneuvering against a Chinese vessel - a tactic often used by the China Coast Guard against Philippine vessels in regional maritime disputes. AIS data shows that it has not left the area entirely, and the PCG confirmed that BRP Teresa Magbanua continues to shadow Jia Hai Ke 7. A China Coast Guard cutter has escorted the survey vessel throughout and has attempted to fend off the Magbanua's close approaches, the PCG said. Jia Hai Ke 7 does not broadcast an IMO number or appear in international registry databases. Chinese media sources report that it is privately owned, DP2 equipped, and less than two years old. It is fitted out as a "comprehensive survey vessel," its state-owned builder told Chinese outlet iMarine last year. https://maritime-executive.com/article/e.text: The main Saudi oil export terminal on the Red Sea, located at Yanbu, appears to have been hit by an unidentified projectile on Thursday. The port has become a critical vulnerability in the European oil supply chain, and last week French President Emanuel Macron pledged to protect Yanbu with France's air defense capabilities. Bystander videos from the scene show one isolated fire in the vicinity of a tank farm; security consultancy Vanguard Tech confirms that the projectile landed within the port area and caused a fire. The terminal temporarily suspended operations due to the attack, Vanguard said. Unconfirmed footage showcasing fires earlier today at Saudi ARAMCO Yanbu North Crude Terminal, Al Madinah Province, Saudi Arabia. https://t.co/oMK6Y8eCVP pic.twitter.com/sV0ItNBSZa Saudi forces reported shooting down a small number of attempted drone and ballistic missile strikes at Jazan and the inland city of Khamis Mushait on the same day. The new strike at Yanbu follows shortly after Saudi Aramco had successfully restored loadings at the terminal. Yanbu ceased operations temporarily last month due to a major strike on the East-West Pipeline, which feeds the terminal with crude from Saudi fields along the Arabian Gulf. The attack damaged three pumping stations on the line, and Yanbu - at the far western end - was shut down for 17 days while Aramco's repair teams worked to restore flow. The terminal resumed loadings on Monday; by Wednesday, it was loading 11 tankers simultaneously, according to Bloomberg's Javier Blas. Saudi officials have attributed last month's long-distance drone attack on the East-West Pipeline to Iraqi militias. No one has publicly claimed Thursday's strike on Yanbu, but past attacks have been linked to Yemen's Houthi rebels, who are actively fighting the Saudi-backed internationally-recognized government of Yemen.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Decarbonisation, digitalisation, shifting patterns of global trade and an increasing level of influence from Asia are continuing to reshape the shipping, logistics and trading sectors. With this year’s WISTA International AGM and Conference taking place in Kuala Lumpur, the association’s president, Elpi Petraki, explains why there are important lessons to learn from the region as the challenges facing the industry demand more than new technologies and innovation. As the world’s largest maritime market, Asia offers an extraordinary degree of maritime capabilities and specialities. It is home to the world’s leading shipbuilding nations, some of its largest ports, many major shipowners and a multitude of maritime service providers. Its financial centres are globally significant, while regional governments are powerhouse investors in decarbonisation, digitalisation and emerging technologies. According to Clarkson’s Research and United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD), China, the Republic of Korea and Japan accounted for 91% of ships completed globally in 2025. Meanwhile, Singapore retained its position as the world’s leading maritime centre for the 13th year running in the 2026 Xinhua-Baltic International Shipping Centre Development Index (ISCDI). And the Philippines remains the world’s largest supplier of STCW-certified seafarers, with approximately 460,147 active Filipino seafarers according to the 2026 BIMCO and International Chamber of Shipping (ICS) Seafarer Workforce Report. As such, Asia’s influence on international shipping is growing. Across the region, new technologies and operating models are being developed, tested and deployed, with innovation seen in digital twins, AI and autonomous vessels, and in alternative fuels and smart-port infrastructure. China, Japan, South Korea, and hubs such as Singapore, are also providing real-world environments for developers to move from concept to reality. While Hong Kong, Malaysia and other maritime centres contribute critical expertise across finance, professional services, ports and logistics. But the scale of maritime operations and willingness to invest in new technology offer only part of the explanation for Asia’s success. Across the region, governments, industry and educational institutions are also coming together to form highly integrated clusters that invest not only in technology and infrastructure, but also in people.

https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/n.text: A dois dias da eleição, o país acompanha uma corrida para o Palácio do Planalto entre dois candidatos que disputam a liderança cabeça a cabeça. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543427-ne.text: Ocean Breeze Energy has agreed to acquire the 60 MW Alpha Ventus offshore wind farm from EWE, RWE and Vattenfall, with plans to operate Germany's first offshore wind farm beyond its originally planned 20-year service life. Located about 45 kilometers north of Borkum, Alpha Ventus was commissioned in 2010 and comprises 12 wind turbines. In doing so, we want to continue the success story of Alpha Ventus and make maximum use of the potential of this pioneering project to make a positive contribution to the energy transition and climate neutrality,” said Jean Huby, Managing Director of Ocean Breeze Energy. Ocean Breeze Energy owns and operates the 400 MW BARD Offshore 1 wind farm, which comprises 80 offshore wind turbines. The company is wholly owned by funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543429-ec.text: Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas has received final ministerial approval to transfer a 60% participating interest in three exploration licenses offshore Namibia to BP, clearing the final governmental consent required for the transaction. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543425-dn.text: BW Offshore's blue ammonia floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) concept, jointly developed with McDermott, has received Approval in Principle (AiP) from DNV, advancing the proposed offshore low-carbon ammonia production solution towards further design development. The AiP provides an independent, risk-based assessment of the concept at an early stage and establishes a basis for further design development, certification and classification. Unveiled in February, the FPSO concept is designed to process up to 3 million cubic meters of natural gas per day and produce more than 1 million tonnes of ammonia annually. The unit would convert natural gas supplied from offshore fields into hydrogen and then ammonia, while carbon capture technology is designed to capture and compress up to 99% of the CO2 generated during production. The captured CO2 could then be exported for geological sequestration or other approved uses. The concept has an estimated carbon intensity of around 0.5 tonnes of CO2 per tonne of ammonia, with options to further reduce emissions from onboard power generation systems. Locating the production facility near offshore gas resources and CO2 storage sites is intended to reduce reliance on the land, permitting and infrastructure required for large onshore facilities. Liquefied ammonia would be stored in refrigerated tanks in the FPSO hull and offloaded directly to gas carriers, avoiding the need for pipeline or port infrastructure.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543423-ln.text: The number of liquefied natural gas cargoes exiting the Strait of Hormuz rose in September to its highest monthly level since the US-Israeli war on Iran began, data from analytics firms show, despite persistent security worries and uncertainty. A total of 19 LNG cargoes were shipped through the key waterway in September, made up of 13 from Qatar and six from the United Arab Emirates, S&P Global Energy said. That compares with the June figure of 15, when a pact between the US and Iran had started to take effect, said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at S&P. "LNG transits through the Strait of Hormuz accelerated in the second half of September and if this is maintained into October, we could see full-month transits recover to 25% of pre-war levels." Data from Kpler shows a total of 21 LNG cargoes exiting the Strait of Hormuz in September, up from 15 in June. More QatarEnergy-linked liquefied natural gas vessels, laden and in ballast, have transited the strait in recent weeks, despite the conflict.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/oil_prices_.text: In a report sent to Rigzone by the Fitch Group on Friday, analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, noted that oil prices have “come under pressure” heading into the fourth quarter, pointing out that Brent futures were down around five percent week on week. “This is largely due to the rollover from November to December expiry in the front month contract in a steeply backwardated market,” the analysts said in the report. “Bearish news flow around rising exports from the Middle East Gulf and the restart of the East-West pipeline, and some optimism over the potential for a U.S.-Iran deal has also played a part,” they added. The analysts warned, however, that other market indicators showed continued signs of strain. “The term spread remains deep in backwardation and physical barrels are holding sizeable premiums to paper barrels, both typically a marker of fundamental tightness,” they said. “In the downstream market for fuels, price pressures remain even more acute, in particular for diesel,” they added.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-c.text: A hidden chemical interaction in a vessel’s bilge system can turn routine cargo and cleaning operations into a serious toxic-gas hazard. A ccording to an IMCA Safety Flash published on 1 October 2026, hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) was detected by portable gas detectors in an open area of the main deck during a vessel’s transit back to port. The gas was traced to certain bilge vents, with the suspected source linked to mud loaded for a rig. No personnel were injured or suffered ill health, but the incident exposed gaps in bilge-system cleaning, chemical compatibility assessment and H₂S monitoring. During the vessel’s return to port, portable gas detectors detected H₂S in an open area on the main deck, specifically around certain bilge vents. The affected area was isolated and continuously monitored, while personnel working on the main deck and in the engine room were equipped with portable gas detectors. Sludge and bilge disposal services were arranged for the vessel’s arrival in port. The suspected source of the H₂S was the mud that had been loaded for the rig. However, the incident was not attributed simply to the presence of the mud. Several residues and conditions within the bilge system had created an environment in which H₂S could form during the voyage.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-expands-russia.text: The UK has announced a new package of 31 sanctions targeting Russia, including eight vessels, as it steps up economic pressure on Moscow and intensifies efforts to disrupt the financing and maritime networks supporting the war in Ukraine. T he package covers 23 individuals and entities and eight ships. Those targeted by the sanctions will face asset freezes, while certain entities will also be subject to trust-services restrictions and director-disqualification measures. Sanctioned individuals will additionally be subject to travel bans. The eight vessels will face shipping and trade restrictions and include three vessels identified as part of Russia’s so-called shadow fleet, two ships providing bunkering services to the shadow fleet and three Russian-owned ice-class vessels. Furthermore, the measures target individuals and entities accused of contributing to Russia’s war effort, spreading disinformation and participating in human rights abuses, including the torture of Ukrainian civilians and the deportation of Ukrainian children. The latest sanctions also follow what the UK described as sham elections held earlier this month in Russia-occupied Ukrainian territories. London said it was taking action against individuals and entities it considers responsible for undermining Ukraine’s territorial integrity and facilitating abuses in the occupied territories. The latest measures come as maritime organisations continue to warn about the growing risks facing commercial shipping across several strategically important waterways.

https://safety4sea.com/two-crew-injured-.text: Two crewmembers were injured after a fire broke out aboard the motor tanker Gindara while the vessel was berthed at Balayan Distillery Inc. in Calaca City, Batangas, Philippines, on September 30, according to the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG). T he fire started in the vessel’s engine room while the tanker was carrying molasses and had 22 crewmembers on board. Twenty crew were accounted for and reported safe, while two sustained injuries and were taken to medical facilities. One was admitted to Metro Lemery Medical Center, while the other suffered an inhalational injury and was treated at Metro Calaca Hospital before being discharged against medical advice. PCG personnel, local firefighters, volunteers and tugboats responded to the incident, while the 44-meter multi-role response vessel BRP Malapascua was deployed to reinforce firefighting operations. The PCG said no visible fire was observed on the vessel’s bridge or superstructure, although smoke remained visible.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-g.text: CHIRP presents a reported incident where a tender became trapped against a vessel’s rail during towing operations in high swell, highlighting the risks of degraded communication, monitoring and loss of positive control. D uring operations to place the tender on tow, damage occurred to the vessel’s rail while the tender was alongside being prepared. Sea conditions included a high swell, causing significant tender movement. The tender was being held off the vessel by a fender. The bosun was on the tender while the deck hand disconnected the towing hook. The chief officer remained on the vessel and used a fender to keep the tender away from the vessel’s side. The chief officer requested the captain via VHF radio to “bump ahead”. The response was delayed by interruptions in communication. The vessel’s cameras also froze and displayed delayed images, limiting the captain’s ability to assess the tender’s position and apply the appropriate propulsion. As the tender continued to move unpredictably amid high surge and heaving, it became trapped against the vessel’s rail. The rail was bent before the situation could be corrected. No injuries were reported. This incident highlights the importance of recognizing when the controls supporting an operation are no longer effective. Strong surge, unpredictable tender movement and degraded communication and monitoring reduced the team’s ability to maintain positive control. Temporary measures, such as using a fender to control a tender, may work in benign conditions but can quickly become inadequate as environmental forces increase. Risk assessments should identify these limitations and establish clear criteria for stopping the operation.

https://safety4sea.com/dnv-september-mar.text: Orders for alternative-fuelled vessels surged in September, with 69 new orders recorded during the month, according to Kristian Hammer, Product Manager AFI at DNV. T he September total made it the strongest month for alternative-fuelled vessel orders since October 2024 and lifted the third-quarter 2026 total to 168 vessels, the highest quarterly figure since Q3 2024. DNV Product Manager AFI Kristian Hammer shared the latest figures on LinkedIn on October 1, noting that the strong third-quarter performance followed a slower start to the year. LNG continued to account for the largest share of new alternative-fuelled vessel orders in September, with 48 vessels ordered. The container and car carrier segments accounted for most of these LNG orders, with 26 and 18 vessels respectively. The trend has also been evident across the year. DNV recorded 200 LNG-fuelled vessel orders in the first nine months of 2026, representing a 52% increase compared with the same period in 2025. DNV’s AFI platform tracks alternative-fuel uptake across vessel types, fuels and infrastructure, providing data on the industry’s transition toward alternative energy pathways.

https://splash247.com/fresh-attacks-hit-.text: Kuwait Oil Tanker Company has suffered its second VLCC strike in four days, while a separate projectile attack at Saudi Arabia’s Yanbu port briefly disrupted loading operations, piling fresh security pressure on two of the Middle East’s key oil export routes. Maritime security firm Vanguard Tech identified the latest Hormuz casualty as the Kuwait-flagged Kazimah III , which was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. UK Maritime Trade Operations, which did not name the vessel, said it received a third-party report that a tanker had been hit, triggering a fire onboard. The crew was reported safe, while the extent of the damage and any environmental impact remained unknown. The 333 m long 2006-built Kazimah III is a 317,250 dwt VLCC operated by Kuwait Oil Tanker Company. The strike comes just four days after another KOTC VLCC, the 316,648 dwt Al Funtas , was hit while passing through Hormuz on September 28. A fire broke out onboard but was extinguished, with the ship subsequently continuing its voyage. All crew were safe and no pollution was reported. Three more tankers were struck the following day. Maritime security sources identified them as ADNOC-operated VLCC Mersin Prosperity , the 115,949 dwt Sinbad and product tanker Al Ruwais . All three had been transiting Hormuz with their AIS switched off.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/hou.text: Purported arms sales, military training and growing contacts between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Somalia’s Al-Qaeda-affiliated Al-Shabab are raising alarm over a partnership that could strengthen both groups and widen the threat to international shipping. US Africa Command has warned that the relationship poses an escalating danger to regional stability, potentially increasing Al-Shabab’s ability to carry out attacks in the Horn of Africa. And giving the Houthis greater access to maritime corridors in the Red Sea and western Indian Ocean, according to Financial Times reporting carried by regional news outlets. The warning brings into focus a threat that extends beyond individual weapons shipments: the possibility that the two armed groups could combine technical expertise, smuggling routes and coastal access to undermine security across the Gulf of Aden. Daniele Garofalo, an intelligence and terrorism analyst and security consultant, told Arab News that the reported exchanges point to an increasingly consequential relationship. “The simple discovery of Yemeni-origin weapons in Somalia does not by itself demonstrate Houthi-Al-Shabab cooperation. What is more significant is the accumulation of evidence since 2024 indicating direct contacts, training arrangements and the movement of Al-Shabab personnel to Yemen.” The Financial Times reported alleged Houthi weapons sales and training for Al-Shabab members. Somalia specialist Matt Bryden, a former head of the UN Panel of Experts on Somalia, estimated that as many as 1,500 fighters from Al-Shabab and other Somali factions had trained with the Houthis in Yemen.

https://splash247.com/mol-lands-vale-cha.text: Japanese shipping giant Mitsui OSK Lines (MOL) will operate two 210,000-dwt ore carriers for Vale under a 25-year contract, introducing tri-fuel propulsion to the long-haul iron ore trade. MOL Ocean Bulk, the group’s Singapore-based capesize bulker operator, signed the agreement with Vale International for vessels scheduled to enter service in 2030. The ships will primarily transport Brazilian iron ore to China and other global destinations. The newbuildings can run on ethanol, methanol, or conventional heavy fuel oil. MOL described the project as the first involving 210,000-dwt ore carriers with this three-fuel configuration. The vessels will also be built with provisions for future LNG or ammonia operation, giving the owner and charterer scope to change fuel pathways as availability, regulation, and economics develop. Their design includes energy-saving equipment intended to reduce fuel consumption. Each vessel will measure 299.95 m long with a beam of 50 m. The 210,000-dwt size places the ships in the newcastlemax segment, widely used on the Brazil–Asia iron ore route. MOL said ethanol could reduce lifecycle carbon emissions by up to 90% against heavy fuel oil, depending on the fuel’s production pathway. Unlike some emerging fuels, ethanol is liquid at ambient conditions, which could make handling and bunkering less complex.

https://splash247.com/splash-wrap-when-n.text: For an industry that has spent much of the 2020s making extraordinary money from things going wrong, this week brought an unfamiliar threat: things starting to go right. Some of shipping’s most important pressure points showed signs of easing. At the Panama Canal, for instance, improving rainfall allowed the authorities to announce this week an increase in drafts and more daily transit capacity from October 15. Half a world away, the return to Suez is gathering momentum . The Premier Alliance will send its FE1 Asia-Europe service back through the canal this month, joining Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, MSC and others in gradually abandoning Cape of Good Hope diversions. More than 140 containerships representing over 2m teu have returned to Suez routings since May. Normality is relative. Merchant ships are still queuing for EU naval escorts through the southern Red Sea , with Brussels admitting it lacks sufficient warships to satisfy demand. The same tentative recovery is evident at Hormuz despite a host of attacks in recent days. Middle Eastern crude exports rebounded sharply in September and traffic through the strait has recovered dramatically from July’s lows. Even Washington and Beijing managed a temporary outbreak of cooperation . Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump extended the suspension of reciprocal port fees until January and agreed new commodity trade commitments, providing shipping with some breathing space from a dispute that had briefly turned vessels themselves into weapons of trade policy.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Multiple sources are confirming that two more tankers reported strikes, bringing the total to six ships in one week and 110 incidents directly related to the US-Iran conflict, says UK Maritime Trade Operations. The latest wave comes as analysts report Iran’s oil industry appears to have been effectively choked off and oil income is running dry. The first of the two reports used third-party data to UKMTO but has also been widely reported by security consultants. The Kuwait Oil Tanker Co. crude oil tanker Kazimah III (317,250 dwt) was struck while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, October 1. The Iranian news agency Fars reported the incident, saying it was about five miles off the coast of Oman. It did not name the tanker but said it was burning. Late on Friday, UKMTO received information from the master of an unnamed tanker that was struck while outbound. A fire was extinguished, but there were also reports of a blackout onboard. Security consultancy Ambrey reported it was a Panama-flagged crude oil tanker located about 5.3 nautical miles off the coast of Oman. It said plumes of smoke were coming from the rear of the vessel. Iran’s so-called Persian Gulf Strait Authority told Iranian media that the ships being targeted included those on its non-compliant list. The reports noted that at least three of the tankers were controlled by the UAE, Al Ruwais, Sinbad, and Mersin Prosperity, and that they had made several unauthorized transits in the past two months. As of Friday, the list stands at 82 vessels. Iran, however, also targeted at least two tankers controlled by Kuwait this week that are not on the non-compliant list. All the tankers, however, appeared to be in the southern channel of the Strait near the coast of Oman. The Al Ruwais was a small LR2 product tanker. The attacks escalated as mediators reported no progress on the talks between the United States and Iran that took place around the United Nations General Assembly.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: The District Court in Gothenburg, Sweden, found both the captain of the cargo vessel Misje Verde and the pilot who was aboard guilty of negligence in the summer boating accident that killed a mother and daughter and injured the father and son aboard a small pleasure boat. Prosecutors argued it was a failure to keep a proper watch while the captain and pilot disagreed over their roles and responsibilities. The 5,310 dwt vessel was navigating in an archipelago area on the western coast of Sweden on July 28 when it hit and sank the 7-8 meter long pleasure craft with the family of four aboard. The father testified in court that he only saw the 90-meter (295-foot) dry cargo ship when it was a few meters behind his boat. He tried to swerve, but the pleasure boat was sucked under the bulb. While the weather was not good at the time of the accident, the Swedish Accident Investigation Board found that the pleasure boat was visible on radar. Under the navigation rules, the larger cargo ship overtaking the small pleasure boat had the obligation to give way to the small boat. The authorities asserted that the vessel did not see the boat because it failed to keep a proper lookout and did not stop after hitting the boat. It was only when the authorities informed the captain later, as the cargo ship was stopping to disembark the pilot. Another private boat rescued the father and his son, and the mother and daughter were later found deceased in a search of the area the following day. The authorities believe the Russian master of the vessel had at one point left the bridge to do paperwork. They said the Swedish pilot had assumed greater responsibilities beyond necessary in a pilotage assignment. Since he was navigating the vessel, they said he also had a responsibility to maintain a lookout, which he did not. Further, because it was an archipelago environment during the summer, they said there was a greater importance to maintaining a lookout. During the trial, the captain admitted ultimate responsibility as the master of the vessel but said he thought the pilot was maintaining the lookout while navigating. The pilot said the captain had misunderstood his role as officer of the watch.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company released a statement on the incident aboard its vessel MSC Hermes III a week and a half ago off Vietnam. The company stated that the evacuation of the vessel was a precautionary response to water ingress that happened on September 22. The Singapore Maritime and Ports Authority had reported that the crew abandoned the vessel, which was built in 2006, on the morning of September 22 while it was about 186 miles east of Vietnam. The 25 crewmembers were taken aboard another MSC container vessel while tugs were dispatched to help the drifting containership. MSC says the master of the vessel had ordered the crew to abandon the vessel as a precaution after MSC Hermes III (38,193 dwt) experienced water ingress in the engine room. After an assessment of the vessel, the crew returned to the ship on an unspecified date. The Vietnamese authorities reported that they conducted a medical evacuation after one of the crewmembers fell and sustained a head injury on September 28 as the vessel was approaching the Vung Tau port. MSC, in its statement, says the crewmember is “recovering well.” The ship remains berthed in Vung Tau, where MSC reports an incident investigation and subsequent repairs are being completed, as well as cargo discharge. The company’s online system showed the vessel scheduled to depart on October 3 and proceeding to proceed to Singapore and then Hong Kong. The MSC Hermes III has been sailing for MSC since 2020 and is registered in Liberia. The 212-meter (695-foot) vessel has a capacity of 2,490 TEU. The container vessel operates on a regional service that connects China, Vietnam, Thailand, and Malaysia.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: US officials in Washington have briefed the press that a third US Carrier Strike Group, led by the USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), is on its way to the Central Command area. The USS Theodore Roosevelt, homeported in San Diego, departed quietly on September 27. Also seen deploying from San Diego on September 28 was the Amphibious Ready Group led by the Wasp Class amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8), accompanied by the USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and the USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26). The ARG has the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit embarked. Central Command has intimated that these deploying formations will rotate with forces currently manning the blockade line in the Arabian Sea, with the USS Theodore Roosevelt CSG relieving the USS George Washington CSG. Presumably the USS Makin Island ARG is relieving the USS Boxer ARG and the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit, while leaving the second aircraft carrier USS George HW Bush on the line. The USS George HW Bush has been in the Arabian Sea since April, and by the end of November will have been at sea for about 200 days. The rotation of forces looks as if it is scheduled for the end of November. This will be after the results of the mid-term elections are in, before which President Trump has said decisions will not be made regarding Iran – whether to agree to a negotiated settlement or, as Trump puts it, to “annihilate Iran.” Even if the rotations still go ahead as conjectured, there will be a period of weeks in which US naval and marine forces will be at nearly double strength, with outgoing and inbound formations both still present in theatre. Force planners may consider that with US Air Force bases within the region vulnerable to Chinese and Russian surveillance and Iranian missile attack, it would be useful to have additional airpower afloat and onboard US aircraft carriers instead, in case offensive operations are to be resumed against Iran. The current movement of forces therefore gives US Central Command some useful options should Trump forsake negotiations and opt instead to resume a wider war. This window of opportunity should occur at about the same time as the last revenues from the dwindling Iranian stock of oil held afloat in Asia are being banked, exacerbating Iran’s financial crisis further.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: The Taiwan Coast Guard used a water cannon on a Chinese fishing boat that it reports illegally entered Taiwan’s waters and refused to respond to commands on October 1. It was one of the more dramatic encounters over the ongoing disputes about Chinese fishing vessels approaching Taiwan. Over the past few days alone, the Taiwan Coast Guard reported seizing a Chinese fishing vessel on September 26 that was operating illegally in the waters near Mudouyu, the northernmost island in the Taiwan Strait. Four days later, on September 30, it boarded and searched another Chinese fishing vessel, which was 22 nautical miles northwest of Huayu Island in the Penghu archipelago. It found 5,000 kg of fish aboard and escorted the vessel into port. The Coast Guard reports it detected an unidentified boat around 1100 on October 1 about 15.5 nautical miles northeast of Dongsha, part of the Pratas Island atoll southwest of Taiwan. The Taiwanese patrol boat Yunlin was sent to investigate. The patrol boat found two Chinese fishing vessels operating in the area about 27 nautical miles east of the island. It broadcast instructions for the vessels to leave the area, and according to reports, one vessel, the Yue Hui Dong Yu 75066 , followed the instructions. The second vessel, Jin Sha , did not respond to three radio warnings from the Taiwan patrol boat. It then moved into a position about 200 meters (656 feet) and fired its water cannon for approximately 30 seconds. The vessel still failed to respond, so the patrol boat moved closer. The second time, it fired its water cannon for 90 seconds. The Taiwan Coast Guard then approached the Chinese fishing vessel and instructed the crew to leave or face arrest. They said the fishing vessel would also be seized, but the standoff ended without arrests.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that it has been stopping vessels transporting oil to Cuba, with two ships stopped earlier in the summer. It has resumed the enforcement of the Trump administration’s imposed embargo on fuel shipments to the Caribbean island after the U.S. permitted some emergency oil shipments earlier this year. “Illicit fuel shipments violate international law and pose severe environmental threats in the Caribbean Sea," said Vice Adm. Nate Moore, deputy commandant for operations, in a Coast Guard statement. “As the Coast Guard leverages our unique authorities and capabilities on the high seas, coordinated efforts are vital to stopping illegal fuel shipments and upholding international law.” The statement confirmed that a small container vessel, Grace , had been stopped in early September and was taken to Progreso, Mexico, where the Mexican Navy searched the vessel. They reported finding “large quantities of fuel in the vessel’s ballast tanks” and additional containers on deck believed to be transporting illicit fuel. “The unsafe stowage of fuel in ballast tanks represents an inherent hazard to the marine environment. The actions of the United States and Mexico prevented an unregulated fuel transfer in the Caribbean Sea, where deceptive shipping practices, unsafe vessel conditions, and concealed cargoes can increase the risk of oil spills and other pollution incidents that threaten coastal communities, fish stocks, and sensitive marine ecosystems,” the Coast Guard said in its statement. It asserts the vessel was “employing tactics common amongst the ‘dark fleet,’" without providing further details. The cutters Alert and Charles Sexton were involved in the interdiction, which The New York Times reports took place between Mexico and Cuba on September 5. The vessel’s AIS was showing its previous port as Colón, Panama, on August 31. The action also involved USCG aircraft and a law enforcement team.

O presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, fixou nesta sexta-feira (2) um filtro para evitar o direcionamento de pedidos a ministros específicos. A medida visa barrar conflitos internos. A mudança ocorreu após questionamentos do ministro Kassio Nunes Marques. Ele criticou a sobreposição de competências entre o STF e o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral. Agora, novas petições apresentadas em ações existentes passarão por análise prévia de vínculo. Se não houver relação suficiente, o pedido vira um processo independente redistribuído. A validação técnica do vínculo será feita pela Secretaria Judiciária e pela Presidência da Corte. A norma não altera manifestações normais das partes do processo. Em setembro, o tribunal enfrentou decisões individuais conflitantes de ministros. Fachin precisou intervir após determinações divergentes de André Mendonça e Flávio Dino sobre a Polícia Federal.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: Maria Eduarda Santana Nascimento, de 24 anos, morreu baleada nesta quinta-feira (1) durante uma tentativa de assalto na Zona Sul de São Paulo. A polícia investiga se o tiro que atingiu a jovem partiu do assaltante, que também morreu, ou de um investigador da Polícia Civil. O pai da jovem desabafou: "Minha filha estava a caminho do trabalho e, infelizmente, encontrou esse sei lá o quê despreparado que achou que estava num faroeste.".

Maria Eduarda, de 24 anos, morreu após ser baleada durante troca de tiros entre um assaltante e um policial civil que interveio no roubo. O assaltante também foi baleado e morreu. A Corregedoria da Polícia Civil instaurou inquérito para investigar o caso.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Total Express registrou crescimento de 40% na receita gerada por pequenas e médias empresas (PMEs) em julho de 2026 , na comparação com o mesmo mês do ano anterior. No período, a base de clientes desse segmento aumentou 6,5% e ultrapassou 5,8 mil empresas . A operadora logística recebe, em média, mais de 350 novos clientes PME por mês e prevê superar 6 mil até o fim do ano. O crescimento da receita acima da expansão da carteira de clientes acompanha o aumento dos volumes e a maior complexidade das operações das PMEs. Com a ampliação dos negócios e a entrada em novos mercados, essas empresas passam a demandar serviços como integração de pedidos, fulfillment e logística reversa, além de maior controle sobre as entregas. Segundo Marcus Tadim, head comercial da Total Express, a expansão das PMEs exige estruturas logísticas capazes de acompanhar o aumento dos volumes e a diversificação das necessidades de entrega. Para atender a essa demanda, a companhia tem ampliado sua estrutura e seu portfólio de soluções, que inclui integração de pedidos, transporte, distribuição, retirada, armazenagem e logística reversa. A Total Express atua nos mercados B2C e B2B e realiza mais de 100 milhões de entregas por ano para uma carteira superior a 30 mil clientes. Sua estrutura inclui dois centros automatizados de cross-docking, em Jundiaí e Barueri (SP), mais de 25 hubs regionais e 120 unidades de última milha. A empresa tem capacidade para processar mais de 1 milhão de volumes por dia e oferece serviços de transporte e distribuição de encomendas, armazenagem e suporte a processos de importação de cargas internacionais, entre outras soluções.

A Imediato Nexway completa 49 anos com uma estrutura que reúne 74 unidades, mais de 7 mil colaboradores e operações em nove estados. A transportadora, fundada em 1977, em Ribeirão Preto (SP), inicia uma nova etapa de sua trajetória com um planejamento estratégico voltado ao crescimento sustentável, à excelência operacional e à inovação e tecnologia. A mudança na liderança faz parte dessa transição (leia mais aqui ). Essa estrutura separa a definição das prioridades estratégicas, sob responsabilidade do conselho, da gestão executiva, concentrada na implementação do planejamento e na busca por resultados. A história da empresa começou com dois caminhões utilizados no transporte de equipamentos para a montagem de usinas de álcool, em um período marcado pelo Proálcool, programa federal criado em 1975 para estimular a produção de combustível a partir da cana-de-açúcar. Posteriormente, a companhia ampliou sua atuação para o transporte de produtos acabados e estabeleceu uma relação comercial com a Brahma, hoje Ambev, da qual é atualmente a maior transportadora do país. A partir das operações de transporte, a Imediato Nexway avançou para serviços dedicados de distribuição, ampliando sua participação na cadeia logística dos clientes. Ao longo das décadas, diversificou sua atuação para os setores de alimentos e bebidas, agronegócio, comércio eletrônico, bens duráveis, varejo, farmacêutico e papel e celulose. Entre seus clientes estão, além da Ambev, Raízen, Mercado Livre, PepsiCo, C&A, Metalfrio e Suzano. Atualmente, a estrutura da empresa inclui serviços de transporte, armazenagem e distribuição, com mais de 4.800 equipamentos e cerca de mil veículos de agregados dedicados. Para o próximo ciclo, a estratégia prevê a conquista de novos clientes, a ampliação dos serviços prestados à carteira atual e a integração de estruturas e operações. O desenvolvimento de pessoas também integra o planejamento. A Academia de Liderança Imediato Nexway (ALIN) e os programas de formação de talentos são utilizados para preparar profissionais para novas responsabilidades e aproveitar competências já existentes na companhia. A empresa pretende manter essa estratégia de valorização interna enquanto amplia sua atuação e se aproxima do cinquentenário.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O Brasil manteve a liderança mundial nas exportações de algodão , com crescimento de 28,6% nos embarques em contêineres entre janeiro e julho de 2026 , na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. Segundo levantamento da Datamar, foram exportados 152.581 TEUs no período, com a China assumindo a posição de principal destino da fibra brasileira, seguida por Bangladesh. A liderança brasileira foi alcançada no ano comercial 2023/24, quando o país ultrapassou os Estados Unidos, de acordo com o Departamento de Agricultura Norte-Americano (USDA). O avanço é atribuído a investimentos em produção sustentável, ganhos de produtividade e melhorias logísticas, fatores que contribuíram para ampliar a competitividade do algodão nacional no mercado internacional. A China recebeu 29.193 TEUs de algodão brasileiro nos sete primeiros meses de 2026, um aumento de 232,1% em relação ao mesmo intervalo de 2025. Bangladesh também ampliou as compras, com crescimento de 43,9% nos embarques, consolidando-se como um dos principais destinos da produção nacional. O desempenho ocorre em um cenário de mudanças na oferta e na demanda global. Projeções do USDA divulgadas em agosto de 2026 indicam que, no ano comercial 2026/27, o consumo industrial mundial deverá superar a produção pela primeira vez em três anos. A expectativa também é de redução dos estoques finais globais ao menor nível desde 2011/12. Para Andrew Lorimer, CEO da Datamar, esse contexto aumenta a importância da regularidade de fornecimento e da capacidade logística dos exportadores. Segundo ele, a disponibilidade, o preço e a confiabilidade das entregas ganham peso nas decisões dos compradores internacionais, ao lado da qualidade da fibra. O Conselho Consultivo Internacional do Algodão (ICAC) atribui o avanço brasileiro à produção recorde, aos preços competitivos, ao maior acesso a mercados e à menor disponibilidade de algodão norte-americano no comércio internacional. Além desses fatores, a rastreabilidade e a comprovação de práticas sustentáveis também vêm ganhando importância nas decisões de compra de marcas, varejistas e indústrias têxteis, de acordo com a Datamar.

A CIONET Awards Brasil 2026 , encerrou sua segunda edição nesta quinta-feira, 1º de outubro, no edifício Bisutti Cardoso de Melo, na Vila Olímpia, em São Paulo. A premiação reconhece líderes e projetos de tecnologia que geram impacto estratégico e transformação digital nas organizações. A iniciativa internacional foi criada para celebrar excelência, inovação e resultados que ajudam a estabelecer novos referenciais para o mercado. Aqui estão algumas das empresas de logística brasileiras que foram destaque no evento: A empresa de logística e transporte para e-commerce Jadlog foi vencedora na categoria Growth com o projeto Nexus 87 , o novo e maior hub logístico da empresa em Perus, na zona noroeste de São Paulo. Liderado pelo CIO Alexandro Strack, o trabalho uniu automação, tecnologia e inteligência operacional para otimizar os processos logísticos do hub, projetado para garantir maior escala, previsibilidade e velocidade à malha de distribuição da companhia. "O Nexus 87 representa uma transformação na forma como operamos. O projeto combina automação, tecnologia e inteligência operacional para dar mais escala, velocidade e previsibilidade à nossa malha. O reconhecimento da CIONET reforça a importância desse investimento para sustentar o crescimento da Jadlog e acompanhar a evolução do mercado", afirma Bruno Tortorello, CEO da Jadlog . A MRS Logística foi uma das finalistas na categoria de infraestrutura com a Plataforma Datacenter 360 , projeto desenvolvido pelas áreas de Infraestrutura de TI e de Tecnologia da informação, que modernizaram o ambiente tecnológico da empresa. A iniciativa envolveu a modernização completa da infraestrutura de Datacenter da MRS , incluindo a migração de mais de 600 servidores para uma nova arquitetura tecnológica, ampliando os níveis de disponibilidade, resiliência e escalabilidade necessários para sustentar a evolução digital da MRS. O impacto também pode ser visto na estrutura tecnológica solidificada para a expansão de ambientes multicloud e de aplicações de inteligência artificial.

O mercado de logística está trazendo novas oportunidades para quem busca trabalhar com movimentação de cargas, intralogística, transporte e supply chain. Semanalmente, a equipe da Tecnologística registra vagas de emprego e capacitação para profissionais do setor. Nesta semana, nossa equipe registrou vagas para diversas posições e níveis de experiência, com destaque para grandes empresas fazendo contratações fixas e temporárias em preparação para o aumento de demanda das festas de fim de ano. A empresa de infraestrutura de mobilidade está com mais de 300 vagas de emprego abertas para suas operações de trilhos em São Paulo. Os novos contratados atuarão nas linhas 4-Amarela e 5-Lilás, de metrô, e 8-Diamante e 9-Esmeralda, de trens. Algumas das funções não exigem experiência e os candidatos escolhidos terão toda a capacitação técnica oferecida pela concessionária antes de serem efetivamente contratados. São oportunidades para aprendiz, oficial de manutenção, técnico de manutenção, agente de atendimento e segurança (AAS) e operador de trem . Todas as vagas são afirmativas para mulheres. Para agente de atendimento e segurança (AAS) , os interessados devem ter ensino médio completo e atingir a pontuação determinada no teste de aptidão física (TAF) promovido pela empresa. Sendo aprovados nas etapas, são contratados e iniciam a formação técnica de vigilante, requisito obrigatório para exercer a função. Após a conclusão e certificação, são inseridos no efetivo que atua diariamente nas estações. Caso o inscrito já tenha o certificado de vigilante, ele segue direto para as capacitações ministradas pela própria empresa e inicia suas atividades com supervisão dos formadores. Outra função que não exige experiência é a de operador de trem . Para concorrer a ela, basta ter ensino médio completo e CNH de categoria B. Passando pelas etapas do processo seletivo, o candidato será inscrito na formação realizada em parceria com o Senai. Todos os que forem certificados serão contratados.

https://safety4sea.com/msc-hermes-iii-re.text: MSC has confirmed that the container ship MSC Hermes III experienced water ingress in its engine room on 22 September, prompting the Master to order the 25-member crew to abandon the vessel. I n a statement issued on 2 October, MSC said the incident occurred while the vessel was at sea, and that the abandonment was ordered as a precautionary measure. All crew members safely embarked on another MSC vessel before subsequently returning to MSC Hermes III after an assessment of the vessel’s condition. One crew member sustained a head injury during the incident and was taken into medical care . According to MSC, the seafarer is recovering well. The incident had initially been reported on 22 September, when MSC Hermes III issued a distress alert at around 08:45 Singapore time while sailing approximately 300 km east of Vietnam. The Singapore Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) requested assistance from vessels in the vicinity, and three vessels responded. MSC Ruby recovered all 25 crew members after they abandoned the containership in a lifeboat. At the time, authorities had not disclosed what had prompted the crew to abandon the vessel. The ship subsequently remained afloat and was reported to be drifting in the South China Sea. MSC has now confirmed that water ingress in the engine room was the reason for the precautionary evacuation. Following tug assistance, MSC Hermes III reached Vung Tau, Vietnam, on 24 September, where it berthed for cargo discharge, an investigation into the incident and subsequent repairs.

https://brasilenergia.com.br/petroleoega.text: Ainda não chegamos ao “ponto de não retorno”. O resultado da regulação do Gas Release, do SIE e do SIP e a adoção do método RCM na revisão das tarifas de transporte podem redefinir os rumos da abertura do mercado de gás O mercado brasileiro de gás vive um momento decisivo, no qual as decisões a serem tomadas pela Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) nos próximos meses poderão moldar a estrutura do setor pela próxima década. Agendas como o Programa de Redução da Concentração no Mercado de Gás Natural (Gas Release), a regulação do acesso e da remuneração dos Sistemas Integrado de Escoamento e de Processamento (SIE e SIP), a revisão das tarifas de transporte e a aplicação da Receita Máxima Permitida com o Método do Capital Recuperado (RCM) aos contratos legados finalizados não são temas isolados. Juntas, essas medidas atingem diretamente os principais componentes do preço e da competitividade do setor. Por essa razão, todos os caminhos conduzem atualmente à ANP, tornando mais fundamental do que nunca a preservação de sua independência regulatória. Essa independência, contudo, enfrenta desafios concretos. No 2º Workshop sobre o Gas Release, promovido no final de setembro na FGV Energia, o diretor da ANP Pietro Mendes relatou publicamente uma tentativa de cerceamento da agência e criticou o que classificou como argumentos "maniqueístas". O desabafo está no contexto dos debates da Consulta Pública CP 16/2026, que trata justamente da desconcentração do mercado de gás. Paralelamente, informações da imprensa apontaram que representantes da Petrobras se reuniram com autoridades do governo, em 28 de setembro, para tratar do programa. Embora seja legítimo que a Petrobras, como empresa diretamente afetada, defenda seus interesses, é imperativo preservar a separação entre a defesa empresarial e a decisão regulatória.

https://safety4sea.com/imo-updates-guida.text: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has updated its guidance on the validity of radiocommunications equipment installed and used on ships, noting that some coastal stations may implement new VHF channel arrangements before the 2028 deadline. A s explained by Lloyd’s Register (LR), MSC.1/Circ.1460/Rev.5 replaces the previous Rev.4 and retains the requirement for VHF radiocommunication equipment to comply with the new channel arrangements by the first radio survey after 1 January 2028 . However, the revised circular acknowledges that some VHF coastal stations may already have moved to the new arrangements and no longer support legacy VHF channels. The circular states that ships should be capable of transmitting and receiving VHF radiotelephony with shore facilities in their area of operation, noting that some administrations may implement the new channels before 1 January 2028. Where this applies, ships’ VHF GMDSS equipment must be compatible with the frequencies and channel arrangements specified in Appendix 18 of the ITU Radio Regulations (RR) . The revised Appendix 18 introduces four-digit channel designations, replacing the previous two-digit format. For newer VHF equipment, compliance may be achieved through a software update, while older equipment may require replacement. Shipowners and operators are advised to check whether coastal stations in their areas of operation have already implemented the new channel arrangements and determine whether equipment updates are needed ahead of 2028, LR notes.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-maritime-secur.text: Maritime security has entered a period in which traditional and emerging threats increasingly overlap. Merchant vessels continue to face piracy, armed robbery, unauthorized boarding, stowaways and the risk of drugs or contraband being placed onboard. At the same time, ships may operate close to armed conflicts, military activity and areas affected by missile, drone or mine threats. R ecent incidents have shown how quickly the operating environment can change. Commercial vessels have been exposed to attacks or heightened security risks in strategically important waterways, while renewed piracy activity off Somalia and in the Gulf of Aden has underlined that threats once considered largely contained can quickly return. This creates a more unpredictable security environment for Masters, crews and shore-based teams. One of the most significant developments is the growing exposure of merchant shipping to geopolitical instability . A vessel does not need to be the intended target of military activity to be placed at risk. Its route, cargo, ownership, flag or simply its presence in a strategic area may increase its exposure. Missiles, drones, mines and other hostile activity can turn what would normally be a commercial voyage into a security operation requiring continuous reassessment. In such conditions, voyage planning cannot rely solely on information available before departure. Threat levels may change within hours, making timely intelligence, communication between ship and shore and the ability to adjust plans increasingly important. The renewed focus on geopolitical risk should not distract from more familiar maritime security challenges. Piracy and armed robbery remain present in several regions, while incidents involving vessels at anchor or underway continue to demonstrate the importance of effective access control and watchkeeping arrangements.
