https://www.oedigital.com/news/543451-ad.text: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) has signed a multi-year agreement to supply about 2 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Thailand's Gulf Group starting in 2027. Under the sales and purchase agreement, ADNOC Trading will deliver the LNG to Gulf Group, extending a supply relationship established through the companies' first LNG agreement in 2025. “This agreement builds on our first LNG supply agreement with Gulf Group and reinforces ADNOC’s commitment to ensuring reliable energy supplies to Thailand and our Asian customers. It marks another milestone in ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform, enhancing the scale, flexibility and optionality of our LNG solutions to meet growing global demand,” said Nasser Al Muhairi, Acting CEO of ADNOC Downstream Industry, Marketing & Trading. The agreement comes after ADNOC launched a global LNG marketing and trading platform at Abu Dhabi Global Market in July 2026, consolidating its LNG marketing and trading activities into a single commercial platform. ADNOC is targeting 47 million tonnes per annum of marketable LNG beyond 2030, with ADNOC Trading serving as the counterparty for LNG trading activities and connecting its portfolio with customers in international markets. ADNOC Trading has built a third-party LNG portfolio over the past four years and operates from offices in Abu Dhabi, Singapore and Geneva.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543450-ba.text: Baker Hughes has signed two agreements aimed at developing Venezuela's natural gas and energy infrastructure, including a partnership with state oil company PDVSA targeting gas production, processing, transportation and potential LNG exports. The company signed a strategic alliance agreement with PDVSA, Lindsayca and Fulcrum LNG to restore and expand Venezuela's natural gas infrastructure, while a separate memorandum of understanding with New Stratus Energy covers support for future oil and gas developments in the country. The PDVSA alliance will focus initially on identifying and carrying out infrastructure developments and upgrades needed to meet the state company's internal gas requirements and supply the domestic market, including gas for power generation. Over the medium and longer term, the partners plan to evaluate the development and financing of new open-access midstream and LNG infrastructure, potentially allowing PDVSA and other upstream operators to commercialize their gas and opening a route to Venezuela's first LNG exports. “A central objective of these partnerships is the development of an integrated gas value chain capable of transforming Venezuela's substantial natural gas resources into reliable domestic supply and future export opportunities, including the potential to export the first LNG molecules produced in Venezuela,” said Lorenzo Simonelli, Baker Hughes CEO. Under the alliance, Baker Hughes will contribute technologies for oil and gas field development, gas infrastructure and LNG, while Lindsayca will provide engineering, procurement, construction and operational capabilities. Fulcrum will contribute midstream and LNG project development, financing and market access.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543447-re.text: Reach Subsea has exercised a one-year option to extend the charter for Deep Cygnus subsea vessel from Havila Subsea & Renewables, keeping the vessel in its fleet through March 2028. The original charter, announced in July 2022, covered a four-year period with an option for an additional year. Deep Cygnus has been part of Reach Subsea's fleet since 2023. The vessel is equipped for inspection, maintenance and repair (IMR), survey and light construction work across the offshore energy and renewables sectors. Deep Cygnus is a subsea construction, IMR and walk-to-work vessel equipped with a 150-tonne active heave-compensated crane and 1,400 square meters of deck space. Its subsea equipment includes one Kystdesign Constructor ROV and one Kystdesign Supporter ROV, while the vessel can accommodate 92 people.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543446-ha.text: Halliburton has ruled out working on the Sea Lion oil project near the Falkland Islands after Argentine federal authorities raised questions over potential criminal and civil enforcement related to hydrocarbon activities around the disputed territory. The U.S. oilfield services provider said it had been in contact with Argentine federal authorities regarding any potential involvement in Sea Lion and confirmed that neither it nor its subsidiaries would conduct work on the project. Halliburton also said it does not participate in hydrocarbon exploration or production activities in or around the Falkland Islands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas. The statement comes as Argentine President Javier Milei's government steps up its response to hydrocarbon development around the islands, which are controlled by Britain but claimed by Argentina. In September, Milei ordered a regulatory decree and proposed new legislation in response to the Sea Lion development. Argentine authorities subsequently opened sanction proceedings against 45 individuals and legal entities suspected of involvement in hydrocarbon exploration and production around the islands. Halliburton said Argentine authorities had raised questions about criminal and civil enforcement of existing legislation, pending new criminal and civil legislation and existing right-to-contract certification regulations.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543454-en.text: Yinson Production has signed a contract amendment with Eni for a major gas capacity upgrade of the John Agyekum Kufuor floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) unit offshore Ghana. Under the amendment, signed on October 2, Yinson will carry out topside modifications to increase the FPSO's gas export capacity to 355 million standard cubic feet per day from about 210-220 MMscf/d. The non-associated gas modification project will install additional gas compression to address expected declines in reservoir pressure and expand the vessel's gas handling and processing capabilities. The work will include the fabrication and integration of two topside modules. The MG2 module will house two gas turbine-driven compressors, while the MC4 auxiliary gas treatment module will be designed to handle the increased gas volumes. As part of the amendment, the FPSO's firm lease period has been extended by four years to 2036. Once the modifications are completed, Yinson will also receive an incremental day rate through 2036. The additional day rate and lease extension together add about $600 million to its firm backlog. “The signing of this contract amendment for the NAG Modification Project on FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor marks a milestone in our partnership with Eni, our joint venture partners, and in Ghana’s energy sector. By increasing gas export capacity, we are strengthening reliable offshore energy infrastructure, supporting Ghana’s domestic energy needs, and helping extend the field’s economic life,” said Flemming Guiducci Grønnegaard, Yinson Production’s CEO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543448-va.text: Norwegian shipbuilder Vard, part of Fincantieri, has opened a new design and engineering office in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and plans to grow its workforce there to more than 40 engineers in the coming years. The new Vard Design and Engineering Vietnam center brings together engineers working across structural design, piping and machinery, HVAC, naval architecture, hydrostatics, stability and marine electrical disciplines. The office expands Vard's ship design and engineering capacity in Vietnam and will work as part of the company's international design network, sharing engineering knowledge, standards and practices across its teams. Vard said the new center would also create additional roles for engineers in Vietnam working on the design of advanced vessels.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543449-se.text: Seatrium has been awarded the conversion of Karpowership's LNGT Akdeniz into a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), marking the ninth FSRU conversion project between the companies. Work on LNGT Akdeniz is scheduled to start in the first quarter of 2027, with Seatrium responsible for engineering, conversion, integration, installation and commissioning of the vessel's regasification equipment and associated systems. The converted vessel will have regasification capacity of up to 600 million standard cubic feet per day and will join the LNG fleet of Kinetics, Karpowership's energy transition initiative. LNGT Akdeniz is the second project to materialize under a previously announced letter of intent between Seatrium and Karpowership, following the award of the LNGT Karadeniz conversion. The LOI covered three potential FSRU conversions as well as the potential integration of up to six new-generation Powerships. Seatrium has delivered seven FSRUs to Karpowership since the companies began working together in 2018. LNGT Karadeniz, their eighth FSRU project, is currently undergoing conversion.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543445-pe.text: Petrobras has made a new oil discovery in block FZA-M-59 in ultra-deep waters off Brazil's Amapá state after finding another oil-bearing interval while drilling deeper at its Morpho exploration well. The discovery was made at the 1-BRSA-1405-APS well in a water depth of 2,886 meters and follows an earlier discovery at the same well announced in August. Petrobras continued drilling Morpho after the August discovery to evaluate deeper exploration targets, leading to the identification of the new oil-bearing interval through electrical logs, indications in rock samples and fluid samples obtained during operations. The company is progressing with the analysis of the new discovery, with collected samples to undergo laboratory testing and the results to be integrated with other data acquired during drilling. Analyses of the oil encountered in the interval announced in August have meanwhile confirmed its good quality, Petrobras said. The latest discovery provides additional information for evaluating the petroleum systems and resource potential of the Foz do Amazonas Sedimentary Basin.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543440-ir.text: The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven Iranian conditions set out in a June interim agreement with the US are met, state media reported Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as saying on Sunday. Iran presented a proposal during the UN General Assembly under which the Strait of Hormuz waterway could be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days if the conditions were met, with the US replying to this proposal last week via Qatari intermediaries. "The position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, was quoted as saying. He said Washington "must understand that the period of dragging out the (diplomatic) process and dictating one-sided demands is over". A Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had clarified its broad positions via mediators to the US response but that additional points remained to be communicated to Washington. "The Americans' propositions are more or less in line with their previous positions, specifically on the nuclear issue. We told them our focus in this stage is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz and the return to security in this waterway requires clear steps from the US," spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543442-ap.text: More than 160 offshore workers at Apache have backed strike action in a pay dispute that could disrupt operations at seven North Sea assets and potentially affect the Forties Pipeline System, trade union Unite said. The industrial action, which could begin in October, involves workers on seven Apache assets associated with the Forties and Beryl oil fields and follows the rejection of a pay offer that Unite said ranged from a pay freeze to below-inflation increases. The union said disruption could bring Apache's Charlie platform to a standstill, potentially reducing pressure sufficiently to shut down the Forties Pipeline System. The Ineos-operated system handles about 29% of UK oil and 30% of its gas, according to Unite, which said any shutdown could also affect operators including Neo Next+, Harbour Energy, Serica Energy, CNOOC, Adura and BP. The workers involved include electrical, instrument, mechanical and production technicians, as well as telecoms technicians and radio operators. Unite also said Apache had set deadlines for reaching an agreement over back pay and indicated that payments could be withheld.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543443-it.text: Ithaca Energy has agreed to acquire Suncor Energy's interests in the Terra Nova and White Rose oil assets offshore eastern Canada for $860 million in cash, marking its first international acquisition outside the UK. The deal includes a 48% operated interest in Terra Nova, a 40% non-operated interest in the White Rose Existing Lands and a 38.6% non-operated interest in the White Rose Growth Lands, including the West White Rose Extension. Ithaca could pay Suncor up to an additional $250 million depending on Brent crude prices over a 27-month period beginning July 1, 2026. The assets are expected to contribute average 2P production of about 30,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day between 2027 and 2031, rising to 35,000-40,000 boepd in 2029 as production grows from the West White Rose development. First production from West White Rose, which is operated by Cenovus Energy, is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The acquisition adds 103 million barrels of oil equivalent of 2P reserves, with an estimated reserve life of about 17 years, as well as around 200 million boe of additional resources. Ithaca said several of those resources are progressing towards final investment decisions.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543444-or.text: Orcadian Energy and an unnamed U.S. offshore data center developer have terminated an agreement to jointly develop an offshore energy-to-compute project using gas resources from Orcadian's Earlham and Orwell discoveries in UK waters. The companies ended the agreement because the development scope and timeline for Earlham did not align with the U.S. developer's near-term deployment priorities, Orcadian said. The Earlham Gigagrid concept envisages using gas resources within Orcadian's P2680 license to provide power and infrastructure for offshore computing capacity, disconnected from the UK electricity grid and designed to minimize Scope 3 emissions. Orcadian previously said the proposed scheme was intended to enable development of an offshore data center ‘of real scale in UK waters’, with the potential partner acting as the offshore compute platform developer, owner or financier of the computing hardware and seller of contracted computing capacity. Earlham and Orwell have estimated combined 2C contingent resources of 145 billion cubic feet of gas as of January 1, 2026, comprising 114 Bcf at Earlham and 31 Bcf at Orwell. The estimates were internally generated and have not been independently verified. The joint development agreement, signed on September 2, established a 90-day process for due diligence, commercial validation and negotiation of a definitive Earlham and Orwell energy-to-compute transaction.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/usa_continu.text: In a statement posted on its X page recently, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced that it had issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR). The move continues the DOE’s execution of the 172 million barrel release previously announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, in coordination with the International Energy Agency (IEA) member nations’ overall 400 million barrel commitment, the statement highlighted. This action builds on the DOE’s five previous solicitations that collectively awarded more than 133 million barrels across four completed exchanges, the DOE noted. “DOE’s earlier exchanges demonstrated the SPR’s ability to rapidly deliver crude under emergency authorities while achieving a 25 percent premium in returned barrels - expanding the reserve and saving taxpayers billions of dollars,” the DOE said in its statement. The DOE pointed out in its statement that deliveries under awarded exchanges are scheduled for November and December 2026. For its latest exchange, crude oil will originate from the SPR’s Big Hill and Bryan Mound site, the DOE revealed. “Under DOE’s exchange authority, participating companies will return the 40 million borrowed barrels with additional premium barrels, ensuring immediate market supply while increasing the SPR’s long-term inventory at no cost to taxpayers,” the DOE said.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-e.text: A missing flooring panel beneath a 415V bow thruster electrical motor cabinet created a potential electrical and personnel safety hazard during vessel operations. A ccording to IMCA, during a vessel inspection, a missing flooring panel was identified beneath a 415V bow thruster electrical motor cabinet. The panel had been removed to facilitate maintenance work but had not been reinstated after the work was completed. It was also observed that water piping located directly beneath the cabinet lacked adequate splash protection. The condition created a potential risk of water ingress into the electrical equipment, increasing the likelihood of electrical failure, short circuit or personnel injury. There was inadequate coordination between maintenance personnel, contractors and supervisors, which allowed the unsafe condition to remain unaddressed after the work was completed. Post-maintenance inspections and housekeeping checks failed to identify that the flooring panel was still missing. Work planning and risk assessment did not adequately consider the exposure of electrical equipment to potential fluid hazards once the flooring had been removed.

https://safety4sea.com/the-hidden-danger.text: Steam and hot-water systems are an essential part of shipboard operations, but they can also conceal a serious danger long after a system has been isolated. Stored heat and pressure can remain within equipment and pipework, turning routine maintenance into a potentially hazardous task. T he Bahamas Maritime Authority (BMA) has issued an alert urging greater awareness of the risks associated with working on or near hot-water and steam systems. The warning underlines a critical point for crews: isolating a system does not necessarily mean that all stored energy has been removed. The alert follows two recent steam-related casualties involving vessels in the Bahamas-flagged fleet. In one of the incidents, a crew member required hospital treatment. While the circumstances of the two cases differ, both highlight the potentially severe consequences of residual heat and pressure and, importantly, provide lessons that can be shared across the wider maritime community. The engine room day team were tasked to rectify a leak on the #1 Exhaust Gas Boiler circulation pump. The plan was to replace the circulation pump entirely with a spare pump and repair it in a controlled environment. In preparation for the task, the second engineer completed the ‘works requiring lockout and tagout’ checklist which included a preparation and risk analysis as per the company’s safety management system. The second engineer stopped the EGB circulation pump, switched off the main breaker, and closed the suction and delivery valves for the pump. The staff chief engineer countersigned the checklist at 09:50, authorising the work to begin. Around 10:30, a 1st repairman removed insulation from the delivery side flange and began slackening the bolts. Another 1st repairman began slackening bolts on the suction side flange. There was no water or steam draining so they continued slackening the bolts simultaneously until the flange faces were unsealed, which effectively vented the system.

https://safety4sea.com/new-digital-appro.text: ABS, HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE) and Siemens are joining forces to develop a digital twin-based approach to assessing the safety of ammonia-fuelled vessels, as the shipping industry moves towards alternative fuels while grappling with the safety challenges they present. T he companies signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) at Gastech 2026 to combine computational fluid dynamics (CFD), artificial intelligence and digital twin technologies to model how ammonia could disperse following a leak. The aim is to enable ship designers to assess a wide range of leakage and accident scenarios earlier in the design process, helping identify and address potential safety risks before a vessel reaches the construction stage. The partnership comes as ammonia gains momentum as a potential zero-carbon marine fuel. However, its toxicity and the potentially serious consequences of an onboard leak make safety assessment a critical part of its development and deployment. Under the agreement, HD KSOE will lead the development of ammonia safety systems and related experimental research, while Siemens will provide simulation and digital twin technologies. ABS will contribute a safety assessment methodology built around digital twins. The collaboration also reflects the growing role of AI and digital technologies in shipbuilding, allowing complex safety scenarios to be tested and analysed virtually before they occur in real-world operations.

https://safety4sea.com/cargo-vessels-cau.text: Commercial shipping in the Black Sea is once again facing mounting danger, as Russia intensifies strikes on cargo vessels and port infrastructure around Ukraine’s Odesa region. A ccording to Russia’s Defence Ministry, four dry cargo vessels were targeted in separate incidents involving Chornomorsk Port, the Bug Estuary and the wider northwestern Black Sea. The attacks also extended to logistics facilities in Chornomorsk, with further strikes reported overnight on October 5. Industrial and port infrastructure across the region was hit, triggering several fires that were later brought under control by emergency crews. No casualties were reported in those attacks. Russia also said it had targeted the port of Vylkove, fuel storage facilities in Chornomorsk and additional cargo vessels operating in the area. The Defence Ministry claimed the vessels were carrying military equipment and supplies, but did not provide their names or other identifying details. The latest strikes came just days after a Liberian-flagged civilian cargo vessel was hit at a port in the Odesa region on October 3. The attack killed one motorman and injured three other crew members, while a further 13 seafarers were evacuated from the vessel. The scale of the damage to Ukraine’s maritime sector has continued to grow since the start of the full-scale invasion. The Ukrainian government said last month that Russian attacks had damaged or partially destroyed 1,173 port infrastructure facilities and 274 civilian vessels.

https://safety4sea.com/engine-room-fire-.text: An engine room fire broke out aboard the cargo ship Seacon Oceania off Gothenburg, Sweden, late on October 1, with all 21 crew members confirmed safe and no injuries reported. T he vessel, which was ballasting from Gdansk to Narvik with 21 crew on board, was anchored off Vinga island, west of Gothenburg’s southern archipelago, when the fire was reported at around 9:35 p.m. The vessel was also reported to have been at Donsö in the southern Gothenburg archipelago to refuel. The Swedish Maritime Administration coordinated the emergency response, deploying a large number of resources, including Coast Guard vessels KBV 001 and KBV 316, a pilot boat, Swedish Sea Rescue Society units from Hovås and Rörö, an ambulance boat, marine police and commercial vessels. Maritime Incident Response Group (MIRG) teams were also alerted, while a Danish ambulance boat arrived at the scene at around 11 p.m. The Gothenburg-based search and rescue helicopter was initially unavailable as it was conducting a medical evacuation from another vessel. The Gothenburg MIRG team therefore prepared to reach Seacon Oceania by boat. The crew had evacuated the engine room, closed it off and activated the vessel’s own fixed firefighting systems. They also cooled the engine room’s exterior side with water, preventing the responding emergency services from having to conduct active firefighting. According to Swedish rescue authorities, all 21 crew members had been located and there were no reports of injuries or missing persons.

https://safety4sea.com/portsmouth-warns-.text: Portsmouth International Port has taken a major step towards maritime electrification with the launch of the UK’s first high-voltage, multi-berth, multi-user shore power system. But with the infrastructure now operational, the port faces a more difficult question: can ships afford to use it? M ike Sellers, Port Director at Portsmouth International Port, says the port’s ambition is to become a net-zero facility while helping enable the wider decarbonisation of shipping. Shore power is central to that strategy, allowing vessels to connect to the electricity grid while alongside and switch off their engines. Yet the economics remain challenging. Electricity currently accounts for around 80–85% of the total cost paid by a vessel using shore power, with port charges making up only 15–20%. With electricity prices remaining high, connecting to shore power can therefore be more expensive than generating electricity onboard. The pressure is compounded by rising grid-related costs. Portsmouth is facing an estimated 10% year-on-year increase in Transmission Network Use of System (TNUoS) charges over the next five years, adding further costs to an already expensive system. The challenge extends beyond electricity prices. Securing sufficient grid capacity remains a significant obstacle for ports looking to electrify. Portsmouth required a 15MVA grid upgrade to enable two ferries and a cruise ship to connect simultaneously, highlighting the scale of infrastructure needed to support high-voltage shore power. For Sellers, the experience demonstrates that government support remains essential. While public funding can help ports overcome the substantial upfront cost of installing shore-power infrastructure, the business case becomes much harder to sustain if vessels face high electricity costs once the system is operational.

https://splash247.com/reach-subsea-exten.text: Norwegian subsea services specialist Reach Subsea has exercised the one-year extension option under the charter agreement for the subsea vessel Deep Cygnus . The charter agreement was originally announced in July 2022 as a four-year agreement with an option to extend for an additional year. Exercising the option extends the agreement through March 2028. The 2009-built Deep Cygnus MPSV is owned by Volstad Maritime and has been an important part of Reach’s fleet since 2023. The extension secures continued access to a vessel with ROV capability, crane capacity, and deck space well suited for inspection, maintenance and repair, survey, and light construction projects across the offshore energy and renewables sectors.

https://gcaptain.com/shadow-fleet-traffi.text: Nuclear icebreaker Vaygach escorting a convoy of crude oil and oil product tankers along the Northern Sea Route in July 2024. (Source: Atomflot) The number of shadow-fleet vessels carrying Russian oil and LNG through the Northern Sea Route has surged this summer, according to a new analysis by Bellona’s Environmental Transparency Center, raising concerns about the ability to respond to accidents in one of the world’s most remote shipping environments. Bellona has identified more sanctioned oil tankers and LNG carriers on Russia’s Northern Sea Route in the first two months of the 2026 navigation season than during the whole of 2025, with many vessels lacking meaningful ice capability and information about accidents increasingly difficult to obtain. The organization counted 50 shadow-fleet oil tankers and 18 shadow-fleet LNG carriers on the NSR between the start of the summer-autumn navigation season and mid-September. That compares with 38 oil tankers and 13 LNG carriers identified during the entire 2025 season. The increase is particularly striking because the 2026 figures cover only about two months of navigation. Bellona said the number of shadow-fleet vessels using the route has increased for three consecutive years. Sanctioned vessels accounted for about three-quarters of all oil tankers and almost 40% of LNG carriers observed on the route during the period, according to Bellona’s monitoring.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/val.text: Brazilian miner Vale will charter two ethanol-capable vessels from MOL Ocean Bulk, a subsidiary of Japanese shipping firm Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, under a 25-year agreement. The two 210,000-DWT ore carriers will be capable of running on ethanol, methanol and conventional fuels. The design will also include an option for future conversion to LNG or ammonia, MOL said, without specifying their level of readiness. The vessels are scheduled for delivery in 2030 and will mainly be deployed to transport iron ore from Brazil to China and other global markets. Earlier this year, Vale signed a separate 25-year charter agreement with China’s Shandong Shipping for two ethanol-capable ships from 2029. Engine makers such as Everllence and Winterthur Gas & Diesel (WinGD) are working on triple-fuel-capable engines that can run on both ethanol and methanol alongside conventional fuels.

https://splash247.com/seatrium-bags-nint.text: Singapore shipyard group Seatrium has secured a contract from Karpowership to convert an LNG carrier into the FSRU LNGT Akdeniz , extending a partnership that has produced seven delivered units since 2018. The work is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027. LNGT Akdeniz will be the ninth FSRU conversion awarded by Karpowership to the Singapore yard group and the second to materialise under a 2025 letter of intent covering three LNG-carrier conversions and potential powership integration work. Seatrium will carry out engineering, conversion, integration, installation and commissioning of the vessel’s regasification plant and supporting systems. The completed unit is designed to deliver up to 600m standard cubic feet per day of regasification capacity. The FSRU will join Kinetics, Karpowership’s LNG infrastructure and energy-transition business, expanding its fleet to 12 LNG vessels. The group operates a 45-vessel powership fleet and pairs floating generation units with LNG import infrastructure in markets requiring rapid-deployment power supply. The award follows the September delivery and sailaway of LNGT Türkiye , the final vessel in a seven-unit FSRU conversion programme that began in 2018. Seatrium is also converting LNGT Karadeniz , the partnership’s eighth project and the first under the later LOI. Conversion work on that vessel began at Seatrium’s Tuas Boulevard yard in the third quarter of 2026. “The successful delivery of LNGT Türkiye and the award of LNGT Akdeniz are important milestones in the continued growth of Karpowership’s LNG-to-power business,” said Gokhan Kocak, Karpowership CTO.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/war.text: Shipping companies operating in contested waters are facing higher requirements for war coverage and legal complications, as attacks spread across multiple military conflicts and sanctions threaten to delay casualty response, according to Neil Roberts, head of marine and aviation at the Lloyd’s Market Association. The Joint War Committee of LMA, which represents insurers in the world’s largest marine market, has expanded the “listed areas” — where they see heightened operational risks — in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf, and the Arabian Sea this year. With a rising number of ship attacks in the Iran-US, Houthis-Saudi and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, Roberts, who chairs the committee, told Platts in a recent interview that the revisions to London market war-risk zones reflected a changing threat environment. “There have been quite a significant number of attacks that have fallen outside of the [earlier] listed area,” said Roberts, referring to intensifying attacks of Russia and Ukraine on commercial ships linked to each other’s trades before nearly all of the Black Sea was listed last month. Higher insurance expenses The move exposes a wider range of voyages to additional insurance procedures and costs, as marine insurers would charge additional war risk premiums in the high-risk waters. Higher insurance costs have ultimately affected the delivered cost of energy and commodity cargoes. The additional war risk premium (AWRP) for crude oil shipments from the Black Sea rose from $2 per barrel on July 17 to $3.7/b on July 29, the highest in recent years, before easing to $2.9/b on Sept. 30, according to Platts assessments.

https://splash247.com/grace-energy-nearl.text: Dubai-based Grace Energy Shipping-linked interests are cashing in on the surge in tanker asset values, with brokers reporting the sale of the 2011-built suezmax Vendavel for $94.5m, close to double its acquisition price a little over two years ago. S&P sources list the 149,999 dwt New Times Shipbuilding-built tanker with the buyer undisclosed. Brokers note that the ship was acquired for $50m in May 2024. The vessel was formerly George Procopiou-controlled Dynacom Tankers’ Demetrios, initially renamed Grace Noel. Vessel records show it subsequently became Vendavel, with Vendavel Shipping as registered owner and Grace Energy Shipping as manager. Against the $50m acquisition figure, the reported resale would represent a gross uplift of about $44.5m, or 89%, before ownership and transaction costs. Grace Energy has been steadily building its presence in the suezmax sector. Splash noted last year that the UAE-based outfit acquired Frontline’s Front Thor for about $48m, while in March it was linked to the $40.5m purchase of Tsakos Energy Navigation’s 2009-built Pentathlon. The deal lands in an exceptionally strong suezmax market. Brokers’ latest assessments put five-year-old secondhand values at $130m, up 19% over three months.

https://petronoticias.com.br/cladtek-ass.text: A multinacional Cladtek está levando sua nova tecnologia de conexão mecânica RapidPipe para o mercado offshore com o objetivo de enfrentar alguns dos principais gargalos que atualmente afetam a instalação de dutos rígidos. A empresa assinou recentemente um contrato com uma grande operadora do pré-sal para avançar com a tecnologia, já qualificada pela DNV, para a etapa de qualificação em campo em condições de pré-sal. Segundo Eduardo Menezes, diretor de Operações e vice-presidente da região das Américas, a solução pode aumentar de menos de dez para mais de 100 o número de embarcações capazes de instalar dutos MLP (Mechanically Lined Pipe), além de reduzir significativamente a duração das campanhas offshore. De acordo com as análises da Cladtek, a instalação de um duto de 60 quilômetros poderia ser concluída em 27 dias, em vez de 150. A empresa também prevê novos investimentos no Brasil. Segundo o CEO do Grupo Cladtek, Lee Wilson (foto principal), a companhia investirá entre US$ 4 milhões e US$ 5 milhões em sua fábrica brasileira neste ano, além de ampliar sua capacidade de armazenamento, avaliar novas expansões e fortalecer sua fábrica local, em Santa Cruz (RJ), que emprega mais de 800 pessoas. Atualmente, o MLP enfrenta um grande desafio no mercado de águas ultraprofundas especificamente relacionado à instalação, devido à disponibilidade limitada de embarcações capazes de lançar esses dutos. Existem menos de dez embarcações no mundo capazes de instalar essa tecnologia. https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: The South African government is continuing efforts to move forward with its pledge to improve the operations of its beleaguered commercial ports. The cabinet last week approved a measure that sets the stage for separating the administration of the country’s eight commercial ports into a stand-alone government-owned company. The vote approved a plan to begin exploring the structure for the stand-alone company. While it still requires further development, it is part of a program of reforms for the country’s ports. Currently, the government-owned Transnet Group is responsible for port administration as well as the operation of terminals. The cabinet approved separating the Transnet National Ports Authority into an independent company. It also provided a provision that would permit the stand-alone company to bring in a minority investor from among South Africa’s development finance institutions. Reports point out that this could provide critical financing for additional modernization of the operation and administration of the ports, while the government has committed to maintaining current employment. The government said Transnet Group, which manages the ports, rails, and pipelines in South Africa, would be compensated but also gain a greater focus on its operations. The government has indicated in the past it would be open to having competing operators in the ports, and it has also pushed Transnet to privatize operations. Transnet has already entered into a long-term concession with Philippines-based International Container Terminal Services (ICTS) for the operation of the Durban Container Terminal. It has also launched tenders for other key terminals, including in the Port of Ngqura and Cape Town. The government says the reforms are working to improve the reliability, efficiency, and competitiveness of South Africa’s freight operations and supply chain. Critics, however, called the move to create a stand-alone company “largely cosmetic,” saying it does not get at the underlying issues that have plagued the port operations for years.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: The U.S. Navy is facing a formidable task to rebuild its aging and overstretched shipyards, a mission that could cost a staggering $200 billion and take five decades to complete, according to the Government Accountability Office (GAO). In a report assessing the Navy’s plans to undertake its largest-ever construction and restoration effort to improve poor conditions and outdated infrastructure at its four shipyards, GAO is highlighting that the Navy could have greatly underestimated the task ahead. In its Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP), unveiled in 2018 and whose core objective was to address infrastructure deficiencies and modernize shipyards to meet the needs of a 21st-century Navy, the U.S. put the cost of the task at $21 billion and the period required at 20 years. SIOP was established with the aim of rebuilding the four naval shipyards, namely Norfolk, Pearl Harbor, Portsmouth, and Puget Sound. The yards provide essential maintenance and modernization projects for the fleet of aircraft carriers and nuclear-powered submarines to ensure they are battle-ready. In coming up with the program, the Navy intended to address both the poor physical condition of the shipyards and capability gaps affecting ship maintenance operations. Part of the specific gaps included insufficient dry-dock capacity to support the new and larger classes of aircraft carriers and submarines. To tackle the gaps, the Navy’s plan included expanding and updating dry docks and piers, recapitalizing shipyard facilities and optimizing workflows, and modernizing capital equipment and technology. To carry out the task, the Navy had put the costs at $21 billion over a 20-year period. GAO, however, is highlighting that the Navy could have greatly underestimated the task ahead, reckoning that rebuilding and modernizing the yards will take much longer and cost much more than originally anticipated due to multiple challenges and changes involved in the program. Environmental issues, for instance, have led to additional projects and more extensive work affecting project plans and costs. Realistically, a whopping $200 billion is required for the task that will be completed in 2080. While the Navy unveiled SIOP in 2018, it only hoped to submit a proposed program plan and cost estimate for approval by September this year, which is eight years down the line. New realities now indicate the program will cost substantially more and will take multiple decades to complete. A case in point is Portsmouth Shipyard, whose modernization cost is estimated at $41.6 billion, the lowest of the three completed shipyard cost analyses. GAO contends that the Navy is far from embarking on the actual modernizing of the yards because the planning activities and project development for each shipy

https://maritime-executive.com/article/l.text: The insurer and the owner of the lost ferry Virgo Transport 8 have reached an agreement to raise the wreck of the sunken vessel, potentially enabling the recovery of up to 55 additional missing passengers and crewmembers. If raised intact to preserve human remains, the procedure would be an exception to the norm for salvage. Whole-ship raising is costly and technically challenging, and is rarely attempted. The location and state of Virgo Transport 8 will present significant additional complications for any salvor: the site has strong currents, which limit diver access, and the wreck is fully inverted, resting on its superstructure. On the favorable side, it came to rest in shallow water, putting it within reach for commercial divers without special techniques. A spokesperson from the shipowner, PT Virgo Karya Shipping, told local media that it has been involved in extensive discussions with its P&I insurer, which is based abroad. The owner has also secured significant backing from Indonesian government agencies in pressing for the timely appointment of a salvor. As of yet a contract has not been signed, but a final agreement with an international salvage partner is expected soon. The spokesperson told Tempo that the objective is to have the salvage team on scene by the end of the month. Kemana korban 55 lagi? Infonya Sejak 2 hari lalu sudah tidak ditemukan lagi korban baru. SC : Basarnas https://t.co/XHtjtRTyAC Regional port authority KSOP Banjarmasin has been pushing Virgo Karya Shipping to complete the raising in short order because of the number of victims remaining within the wreck. Dozens of salvage divers have been working to retrieve remains from within the vessel, but the work is hazardous: in addition to the currents, the interior compartments are narrow, dark, and cluttered with debris - and are all inverted because of the ship's position. If raised to the surface, an interior search would be straightforward.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: On May 6, 2025, following a weeks-long bombardment on Houthi targets in Yemen, US President Donald Trump declared the fight to be over. The Houthis, “a band of individuals with advanced weaponry that were threatening global shipping”, had – according to the US president – “capitulated” and agreed to halt their attacks on maritime traffic in the Red Sea. In one of the first “America-First” deals of the second Trump administration, the United States had extracted itself from one regional conflict, not fixed it. Despite being threatened with annihilation, the Houthis had suffered limited military degradation. They could also continue fighting Israel, which had been excluded from the agreement. As Trump headed to Saudi Arabia for his first major international trip a week later, observers concluded that Israel had been sidelined and left to confront the Houthi threat alone. Fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia has reignited in recent weeks, unravelling an informal ceasefire that had been in place since 2022. Recent Houthi attacks have targeted Riyadh and Mecca, as well as critical infrastructure sites, including the East-West oil pipeline and facilities at Yanbu port. The Houthis have also declared a blockade on Saudi-linked vessels in the Red Sea and launched attacks on Saudi ships. Saudi Arabia, for its part, has sought to disrupt Houthi operations and reinforcement efforts on the Red Sea coast that offer the group strategic control over the Bab-el-Mandab Strait. Alongside Saudi-backed government-aligned forces, Saudi Arabia has conducted hundreds of airstrikes on Houthi positions in south-western Yemen, exacerbating an already-dire humanitarian situation in Yemen. The escalation on Saudi Arabia’s southern border comes amid heightened pressure on Riyadh. The ongoing US war with Iran, and the latter’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, has restricted Saudi Arabia’s oil exports, leading Saudi Arabia to shift some oil exports to a Red Sea bypass – a route that is now being threatened by the Houthis.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Romanian officials are reporting a complex rescue operation in the Black Sea while also condemning the attacks on civilian ships. It reported that a total of 11 seafarers were saved on Monday from a Turkish vessel carrying grain that later sank and that it retrieved the bodies of two other crewmembers who died in the attack. ARSVOM (the Romanian Agency for Rescue of Human Life at Sea) identified the vessel as the Turkish-owned cargo ship Royad Mammadov (6,933 dwt). Built in 2006 and registered in St. Kitts and Nevis, the ship had a crew of 13 aboard when it issued a distress call at 10:37 a.m. (Romanian time) on October 5. The crew were reported to be Turkish and Azerbaijani citizens. Romanian authorities are emphasizing that the vessel was in their EEZ, approximately 20 miles offshore and near their offshore oil platforms. They are not reporting the circumstances of the attack, but Ukraine asserts the vessel was struck by two drones. ARSVOM’s pictures show scorch marks on one side of the deckhouse and the vessel listing at the stern. ARSVOM sent rescue vessels, and was joined by the deployment of military helicopters and the border police. The authorities reported that several injured crewmembers were hoisted to the helicopter for transfer to shore. Ukrainian reports say the vessel had loaded a cargo of corn in Izmail and was bound for Italy when it was struck. They said the captain had been killed, and one other seafarer was missing, while three were injured. Romanian authorities later said the two deceased individuals had been identified without providing details. “Romania supports an immediate moratorium on attacks against merchant ships and port infrastructure,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement. It emphasized that it has repeatedly raised the issue, including at the UN General Assembly. It highlighted that between 20 and 30 percent of globally traded wheat and grain transits through this corridor and that the ports manage 50 percent of global sunflower seed oil exports.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/j.text: The Japanese government announced a package of sanctions at the end of last week designed to target Russian trade, which included its first-ever vessel sanctions. According to the government, it was imposed for the purpose of contributing to the international effort for achieving peace. The move was seen as an effort by the Japanese government to further align with the West. The package included 35 vessels as well as 33 entities and nine individuals. Japanese companies are required to obtain permission for payments to the individuals or entities and for capital transactions. In addition to specific restrictions on exports to the Russian Federation and Belarus, Japan targeted several other companies seen as supporting the Russian war efforts. It included four companies in Turkey and the UAE. The vessel sanctions targeted a network based in Oman by including 13 crude oil tankers registered in Oman. It also targeted 17 vessels flagged in Russia, mostly crude oil tankers, but also a product tanker and four RoRos or cargo vessels. The vessel sanctions also included five tankers that are identified as having a false flag or no known registry. Japan provided a temporary exclusion for contracts that had been entered into before October 2. It, however, only gave the companies a month, until November 1, to complete previous contracts. The sanctions include elements such as services or repairs to the vessel as well as a prohibition against providing insurance or any other supporting services. The sanctions, however, did not extend to Russia’s gas operation. Japan has been an importer of Russian gas, although the government reports it is working to transition to other sources. Last week, the UK, while extending sanctions to Russia’s newest gas carriers, noted that it was maintaining an exclusion for Japan as well as Korea. It said that Japan had committed to $20 billion in financial aid to Ukraine to be used to rebuild infrastructure, along with a recent $100 million aid package for Ukraine from Korea.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Philippine military says that a Chinese fighter made an unsafe close approach to a patrol aircraft near Scarborough Shoal, a contested reef west of Luzon in the South China Sea. According to the AFP, a Philippine C-208 light patrol aircraft was conducting a flight near Scarborough on Saturday when it was approached by two Chinese military aircraft. One of the Chinese planes, a J-16 jet fighter, approached repeatedly and moved in too close for safe operation, the AFP claimed - including maneuvers in front and in back of the Philippine plane. The C-208 is a small, unarmed prop plane used for maritime patrols in Philippine service. The Shenyang J-16 is a fourth-generation strike fighter derived from the design of the Soviet-era Su-27. "This incident is part of a recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behavior against Philippine government vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations," the AFP said in a statement. "The AFP will continue to conduct routine maritime and air patrols in the [western Philippine EEZ]." The C-208 aircrew completed the mission and returned to base without incident, according to the AFP. China claims the vast majority of the South China Sea as its own - including a large swathe of the Philippine EEZ - under its historically-derived "Nine Dash Line" claim and its more recent, geographically-based "Four Sha" straight-baseline theory. It seized control of Scarborough Shoal from Philippine forces in 2012 and has held it ever since. The Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in 2016 that these claims in the Philippine EEZ have no basis in the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea; China refused to recognize the ruling and has continued to expand its presence in the region.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: Residents of a Norwegian coastal town reported being awoken early Monday morning to a loud boom that turned out to have been a collision between three short sea vessels navigating in one of the coastal fjords on Norway’s west coast. The authorities are trying to sort out the circumstances of the unusual collision between the three ships, which left one taking on water and all three damaged. The collision took place just after 01:30 a.m. October 5, near Alesund. Two of the vessels were sailing to the north through Valderhaugfjorden, and the third was sailing to the south. The police report poor visibility and darkness, but a video obtained by Norwegian broadcaster NRK appears to show normal nighttime conditions. The loud bang can clearly be heard as the vessels collide. Media reports on Monday said that three crewmembers had been placed under suspicion of careless navigation. However, the authorities would only say that the investigation was still underway. It is unclear from the reports which vessels collided first or how three vessels could have become involved in one collision. The reports said there were approximately 30 crewmembers between the three ships, and while the crews were uninjured, all three vessels have sustained significant damage. The emergency call came into the rescue authority, which dispatched one of its boats. The Navy sent the frigate Fridtjof Nansen, and a rescue helicopter was seen overhead using its spotlight. Local emergency services from shore also responded, but no evacuations were required. The Norwegian Safety Authority reported that two of the vessels, Bergfjord and Hav Frakt, have been detained and will require repairs before they are permitted to sail. The third vessel, a small tanker, Xanthia, sustained damage, but inspectors from DNV told the authorities the hull was sound and it was permitted to resume its trip to Finland, where it will undergo further inspections.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Iran has added to a rapidly-expanding list of strikes on energy shipping in the Strait of Hormuz with another attack on a tanker off the Musandam Peninsula. On Monday evening at about 1637 UTC, the master of a tanker informed UKMTO that the vessel was hit by an unknown projectile, sparking a fire in the engine room. The crew was still fighting the fire at the time of the report. No injuries were reported, nor any environmental damage. UKMTO advised shipping to remain cautious when transiting the area. Eurasia Group analyst Gregory Brew assesses that Iran has hit 11 ships since last Wednesday - a new, intense campaign to stop GCC oil producers from getting their crude to market. With extensive American assistance, UAE, Saudi, Kuwaiti (and more recently Iraqi) shipping interests have begun moving oil through the southern waters of the strait via "shuttle" convoys. Instead of exposing a large number of chartered tankers to high risk and high insurance rates, these producers are using a smaller number of risk-tolerant tankers to make round trips between loading piers in the Gulf and the busy anchorage off Fujairah, where these ships offload their cargoes onto more risk-averse vessels for long-haul delivery. The shuttle method has succeeded beyond expectations, and objective counts based on satellite data showed that it had largely restored net Gulf exports to prewar volumes by the end of September. It remains to be seen whether recent Iranian attacks can dent the system's productivity, whether by physically disabling the tonnage involved or by deterring tanker owners and crewmembers from participating.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: Yemen’s Internationally Recognized Government (IRG) has launched Operation Dawn of Yemen across all fronts, with apparently substantial support from allies. The IRG counterattack comes after Houthi forces made a breakthrough down the Tihama coast last month, capturing Mocha, Dhubab and finally Perim Island and the Ras Menhali peninsula, and thus potentially overextending themselves. The IRG’s president, Rashad Al-Alimi, has announced that the objective of Operation Dawn of Yemen is to recapture the capital Sana’a and to end the Houthi insurgency. In recent days, forces of the IRG have faced heavy attacks by Houthi forces trying to tighten their siege on Taiz, having failed for years to capture the city. IRG sources admit that the Houthis have captured some ground. But they have failed to cut the road linking Taiz to Aden, and have faced fierce resistance not just from IRG formed units, but also from local militias and residents, who have no tribal or religious affiliation with the Houthis. Local resistance should not be underestimated in Yemen, where every household, as a matter of routine, even in peacetime, holds a substantial armory of automatic weapons. The Houthis have not been able to consolidate their gains around Taiz, nor have they made much progress on other fronts. The IRG counterattack on the Tihama coast has so far recaptured the airstrip at Dhubab and has reached the coastal N2 highway, thereby cutting off Houthi forces farther south occupying Perim Island and any remaining presence on the Ras Menhali peninsula. IRG sources say their next immediate objective is the recapture of the harbor town of Dhubab. But in keeping with the objective President Al-Alimi has set out, the IRG will be aiming to recapture first Mocha and then Hodeida – a move that would cut off the Houthis' ability to ship in imports. Houthi and Yemeni Government positions in SW Yemen as noted in reporting on October 5; the situation on the ground is likely to change quickly (Google Earth/CJRC) A key component of success on the Tihama coastal front will be airpower, as the ground is low-lying scrubland and exposed, and there is only one substantial north-south communications route – the flat and straight N2 highway, which is a close air support pilot’s dream target. Social media has already shown IRG forces near Dhubab on the N20 and motoring north toward Mocha.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543475-dn.text: Oil platforms, gas production facilities, offshore wind farms, port facilities and ship cranes all depend on energy and data supply that keeps working while waves, weather and constant movement do their worst. That's why igus® partnered with DNV to certify chainflex® cables for dynamic use on ships and offshore installations. Classification societies like DNV typically approve cables against international standards for fire behavior and similar properties. None of those standards addressed cables flexing continuously inside an energy chain, so igus and DNV developed a new test procedure together. After more than three years of investigation, chainflex cables became the first cables ever designated for use in energy chains on ships and offshore. In 2020, igus and DNV upgraded and renewed that jointly developed standard. The result: you can run chainflex cables in moving maritime applications without pursuing expensive special approvals. The DNV-certified range includes more than 370 control, servo, motor and robot cables, plus bus, data, encoder and fiber optic cables. Power, signal and communication for an entire offshore application can come from one certified source. NEK 606 is the Norwegian standard for cables used in offshore applications. 301 chainflex cables are mud resistant according to its requirements, which is critical for equipment working around drilling fluids. Every chainflex cable is engineered specifically for motion in energy chains, and the DNV-certified range is no exception. These cables carry the same 4-year guarantee as the rest of the chainflex line. Pair them with e-chain® cable carriers to source your complete moving energy supply from a single supplier.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: Em um centro de distribuição de 60 mil m², a operação convivia com um cenário em que o papel ainda orientava parte relevante do turno. O WMS funcionava em modo básico, a separação era conduzida por lotes impressos, os apontamentos aconteciam depois da execução das tarefas e o estoque era atualizado ao fim do turno. Ao mesmo tempo, a movimentação interna dependia da disponibilidade de equipamentos e operadores, enquanto colisões e condições de uso da frota não tinham o mesmo nível de rastreabilidade. A resposta foi estruturada em três frentes integradas: WMS GARDEM, AGVs e Telemetria SMART. Mais do que automatizar etapas isoladas, o projeto buscou fazer com que a informação acompanhasse o fluxo físico dos materiais e orientasse a operação em tempo real. A partir das regras do processo, CSI Cargo e Dinamik Rental conectaram gestão, movimentação autônoma e controle de equipamentos em uma arquitetura de tecnologias próprias. A primeira transformação aconteceu na gestão do armazém. Com o WMS GARDEM, coletores de dados, ring scanners, impressoras portáteis e tablets passaram a registrar as atividades no próprio ponto de execução. Recebimento, armazenagem, picking, packing, inventário e expedição foram incorporados a um fluxo digital, com confirmação de endereço, item e quantidade, tratamento de divergências dentro do sistema e direcionamento das tarefas conforme as necessidades da operação. O WMS GARDEM também ampliou a capacidade de decisão sobre o estoque. Recursos como mapa de calor, RFID, roteirização, algoritmos aplicados à definição de percursos e ao posicionamento dos materiais, integrações via API e acompanhamento de indicadores passaram a apoiar a rotina. No recebimento, o case registra redução de 99,95% nos erros de conferência. Na expedição, a acuracidade chegou a 100%, com a carga conferida contra a demanda que originou a coleta. Os resultados consolidados mostram a dimensão da mudança. A acuracidade de inventário evoluiu de 97,1% para 99,68% e o índice de reclamações caiu de 19,21 para 1,78 a cada 10 mil pedidos, na comparação de 24 meses apresentada no case. O consumo de papel passou de sete resmas por dia para 0,33, equivalente a 2.081 resmas poupadas por ano. A digitalização reduziu controles paralelos e permitiu que divergências fossem identificadas e tratadas enquanto a operação acontecia, e não apenas ao final do turno. A Dafiti passou a oferecer entregas até o dia seguinte para pedidos realizados na cidade de São Paulo (SP). A nova modalidade, chamada Next Day, inclui produtos vendidos e entregues pela própria varejista e por vendedores que utilizam o serviço de fulfillment da companhia, o Dafiti Full. No momento, o prazo reduzido é válido apenas para pedidos realizados de segunda a quinta-feira até as 17 horas na capital paulistana. De acordo com a empresa, o serviço foi viabilizado pela incorporação de um novo parceiro de transporte e de uma frota dedicada à operação. A implementação ocorre de forma gradual e atenderá todas as zonas da capital paulista. A Dafiti ainda planeja levar o serviço para as regiões do ABC Paulista, Grande São Paulo, Campinas e, posteriormente, para o Rio de Janeiro (RJ). "O lançamento da entrega no dia seguinte representa um avanço importante na nossa estratégia de oferecer uma experiência de compra cada vez mais eficiente. Investimos em uma operação logística dedicada para reduzir o tempo de entrega sem abrir mão da qualidade e da confiabilidade do serviço", afirma Helder Lameirinha, gerente de Transportes Sênior da Dafiti . A mudança reduz o prazo de entrega em parte da operação da Dafiti e amplia a participação do marketplace na gestão logística dos pedidos de terceiros, já que os sellers integrados ao Dafiti Full também poderão utilizar a modalidade. Com a inclusão dos itens do sevirço Dafiti Full no Next Day, vendedores que utilizam a estrutura de fulfillment , em que a Dafiti se responsabiliza pela armazenagem, separação, embalagem e expedição de pedidos, passam a ter acesso ao novo prazo sem precisar realizar qualquer mudança. A modalidade seguirá a política padrão de frete da Dafiti.

Começaram nesta terça-feira (29/09) as convocações dos candidatos selecionados para o programa Mais Motoristas , iniciativa do SEST SENAT que oferece a mudança de categoria da Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) para C, D ou E e formação especializada para quem deseja atuar no transporte profissional. O programa é gratuito e busca ampliar a oferta de motoristas qualificados no país, gerar oportunidades de emprego e renda e contribuir para um trânsito mais seguro. O SEST SENAT custeia integralmente tanto a mudança de categoria da CNH quanto a formação na Escola de Motoristas Profissionais ou em cursos homologados pela instituição. Nesta primeira chamada, 16.136 candidatos foram convocados para assinar o Termo de Adesão ao programa e iniciar o processo para obtenção da CNH (Carteira Nacional de Habilitação) nas categorias C, D e E, além da qualificação profissional. Motoristas com habilitação AB ou B podem fazer a mudança para a categoria C. Já quem possui CNH nas categorias AB, B, AC ou C pode solicitar a mudança para D. Para a categoria E, são contemplados condutores habilitados nas categorias AC, C, AD ou D. Após a mudança de categoria, o participante fará a Escola de Motoristas Profissionais , com formação especializada em uma das seguintes áreas: Também poderão ser realizados cursos homologados e o Curso de Condução Segura e Responsável. Após a assinatura do termo, os candidatos serão encaminhados para a realização dos exames toxicológico, médico e psicológico, das aulas práticas em CFC (Centro de Formação de Condutores) e da prova prática no Detran.

A Super Terminais iniciou a transferência de uma estrutura flutuante de aproximadamente 4 mil toneladas de Manaus para Itacoatiara (AM) , como parte da Operação Seca 2026. A infraestrutura, que transporta três guindastes elétricos Konecranes ESP10 , integra uma base de transbordo temporária que recebeu investimento de R$ 70 milhões para manter o fluxo de mercadorias e o abastecimento do Polo Industrial de Manaus durante o período de estiagem. A estrutura será instalada em uma área própria de 300 mil metros quadrados na margem esquerda do Rio Amazonas, a 1,4 quilômetro do porto público de Itacoatiara e com acesso rodoviário asfaltado pela estrada do Aeroporto. O píer flutuante tem 240 metros de comprimento e 24 metros de largura e ficará posicionado a 100 metros da margem, com 34 metros de calado, permitindo a atracação e o atendimento a navios de diferentes portes. A operação em Itacoatiara funcionará 24 horas por dia, em três turnos. A estrutura será utilizada para descarregar as cargas dos navios e transferi-las por balsas até Manaus, em um percurso de 108 milhas náuticas, cerca de 200 quilômetros. O tempo estimado de navegação é de 18 horas no trajeto de ida e 12 horas na volta. Além do píer, a base contará com serviços de fornecimento de combustíveis e óleo diesel, apoio para atracação de navios, equipes de mergulho e reparos portuários. A infraestrutura também terá segurança permanente, suporte médico de emergência, coleta de resíduos, sistema de combate a incêndios, conectividade para monitoramento em tempo real e uma base terrestre para alimentação e abastecimento de água potável. “Mobilizar uma estrutura dessa magnitude exige inteligência logística de ponta, mas garante a estabilidade econômica e o fornecimento contínuo de suprimentos para a população e para as indústrias da região no momento em que os rios atingem seus níveis mais baixos”, afirma Marcello Di Gregorio, diretor-geral do Super Terminais. Segundo o executivo, a iniciativa busca reduzir os impactos da estiagem sobre a cadeia produtiva e dar previsibilidade às operações do Polo Industrial de Manaus. A estratégia retoma a experiência da empresa durante a seca de 2023/2024, quando o Super Terminais ficou 32 dias sem movimentar cargas em Manaus. Na ocasião, a companhia investiu R$ 60 milhões na implantação da Operação Itacoatiara. A estrutura atendeu 27 navios e movimentou mais de 33 mil contêineres, contribuindo para evitar interrupções industriais na Zona Franca.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/boksa-mar.text: Boksa Marine Design (BMD), Tampa, Fla., a naval architecture and marine engineering firm, recently announced the addition of shoreside electrical engineering services to its portfolio. This new practice expands BMD’s core capabilities to include shoreside electrical design and power systems, to help accelerate vessel electrification, shore-power integration, and climate-resilience upgrades for U.S. maritime facilities. BMD’s new service offers complete, end-to-end engineering solutions, from shipboard systems to high-voltage shoreside utilities, and flood-resilient electrical design. By combining deep vessel design heritage with dedicated shore-power expertise, BMD offers port operators, fleet owners, and facility managers a single, highly technical partner capable of modernizing marine operations for a sustainable future. “As naval architects and vessel engineers, we intimately understand the power demands of modern fleets,” said Jeff Kuenning, president of BMD. “By bringing that same technical rigor to shore-based power distribution, we ensure every dock and terminal upgrade is built for next-generation operations. We eliminate the guesswork by engineering both sides of the water’s edge.” • Ferry Terminals and Operators: High-frequency, high-capacity hybrid or electric ferry operations require massive power transfers. BMD provides the critical utility load evaluations, and electrical layout designs required for fast-charging infrastructures that keep fleets on schedule. • Ports and Shipyards: Modern vessels demand significantly more shore power during construction, refit, and maintenance. BMD modernizes aging port and shipyard distribution networks to boost capacity, enhance reliability, and deliver flood- and storm-resilient electrical infrastructure built for the next generation of fleets. • Industrial and Cargo Terminals: BMD upgrades shoreside power to support heavy terminal machinery and floating assets. The firm converts legacy diesel equipment to efficient electric systems and upgrades grid capacity, delivering lower operating costs, reduced emissions, and reliable power where needed.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 05/10/2026 – A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) realizou, nos dias 24 e 25 de setembro, o 33º Encontro do Sistema de Desempenho Portuário (SDP). Organizado pela Gerência de Estatística e Avaliação de Desempenho (GEA), o evento aconteceu em Santa Catarina, com o apoio do Porto Itapoá, e reuniu cerca de 130 participantes, representando 60 instalações portuárias. Realizado anualmente, o encontro promove a troca de experiências entre as instalações portuárias, especialmente sobre a utilização do Sistema de Desempenho Portuário. Por meio do SDP, as instalações enviam dados relativos à movimentação de cargas, que servem de insumo para as informações disponibilizadas no Estatístico Aquaviário da ANTAQ. A cada edição, uma instalação portuária diferente recebe o evento, permitindo aos participantes conhecer diferentes realidades, experiências e práticas adotadas pelo setor portuário brasileiro. Nesta edição, um dos principais temas da programação foi a apresentação do novo Sistema de Desempenho Portuário. Os participantes conheceram a nova disposição e organização das funcionalidades do SDP, além de recursos relacionados à gestão de usuários e ao envio de dados, que poderá ser realizado por meio do preenchimento no próprio sistema ou pelo envio de arquivo XML. A programação também abordou o Módulo de Acompanhamento de Preços Portuários (Módulo APP). Durante o encontro, foi apresentada uma planilha voltada à aplicação dos conceitos fundamentais do módulo pelos terminais.

The latest reports add to a surge in attacks against commercial shipping in the Strait, although the use of delayed reporting makes the precise number of individual incidents difficult to establish. UKMTO on Sunday issued three new “time-late” warnings involving tankers struck by unknown projectiles. One involved an LPG tanker transiting inbound through the Strait that was reportedly struck at 1716 UTC on October 4. A second involved a crude oil tanker struck at 1907 UTC the same day. https://gcaptain.com/five-hormuz-inciden.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, August 3, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer UK Maritime Trade Operations reported five separate incidents involving commercial shipping in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, including four tanker attacks and an incident in which Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened another vessel with attack. Three of the four attack notices were time-late reports covering incidents from October 3 and 4, while the latest strike occurred Monday afternoon. The concentration of reports underscores both the intensity of the recent violence and the difficulty of establishing what is happening in the Strait in real time. The latest incident, UKMTO 156-26, occurred at 1637 UTC Monday when the master of a tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The strike caused a fire in the vessel’s engine room, which the crew was fighting when UKMTO issued its warning. No casualties or environmental impact had been reported. Two were time-late reports from October 4. UKMTO said an inbound LPG tanker was struck by an unknown projectile at 1716 UTC, followed less than two hours later by a crude oil tanker struck at 1907 UTC.

REUTERS/Norlys Perez (Bloomberg) –FBI and US Coast Guard investigators have found evidence that hackers accessed the propulsion system of an oil supertanker as it was approaching the Texas coast this summer, according to US officials familiar with the matter, an extraordinary breach that highlights the growing physical risks from cyberattacks . The cyberattack resulted in outsiders gaining temporary access to the digital system on the ship, said the people, who asked not to be identified because they weren’t authorized to discuss the matter. Officials are still examining how the breach occurred and who was responsible. It wasn’t immediately clear how long the hackers had access and what they could’ve controlled aboard the ship with it. The breach of the tanker’s propulsion system, a rare and particularly invasive hack into a ship’s operations, underscores the urgency that led US authorities to board the VL Prosperity in August. The carrier — which is longer than the Chrysler Building is tall and as wide as an American football field — was fully-laden and bound for Galveston. The Coast Guard declined to comment. The FBI declined to answer questions beyond providing a statement the two agencies previously released about their joint boarding of the VL Prosperity and another ship “to ensure integrity of the vessel’s operational and information technology systems following indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised.” “Currently, there are no reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts,” the FBI said in the emailed statement.

https://gcaptain.com/opinion-oils-new-pr.text: A ship off the port of Aden, where traffic remained steady after the Iran-aligned Houthis said their forces had carried out missile and drone strikes on Saudi oil tankers, in Aden, Yemen, July 23, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer LONDON, Oct 5 (Reuters) – Middle East crude exports recently climbed to their highest levels since the start of the Iran war as more Gulf producers resume transit through the Strait of Hormuz – despite the continued threat of Iranian attacks. Yet oil prices remain stubbornly elevated, suggesting logistical problems are proving as disruptive as outright supply losses. Crude flows through the embattled waterway reached 14.2 million barrels per day on a seven-day average on Sept. 26, nearly 80% of pre-war levels, according to analytics firm Kpler. While volumes have declined since, they will likely be revised higher because ships often disable satellite tracking systems while traversing the strait and for several days thereafter. Either way, the trend is clear: a lot more crude is getting through the strait. So why is Brent still trading above $100 per barrel? For decades, the global oil industry functioned as a finely tuned system designed to move enormous volumes of crude and fuels over long distances at the lowest possible cost. The conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe have fractured that model, as a combination of record-high tanker rates, soaring insurance costs and a severe shortage of refining capacity has created bottlenecks across the energy supply chain. Those problems may take months, if not years, to unwind, leaving consumers facing persistently high energy bills – even if the crude supply squeeze continues to ease.

REUTERS/Mohammed Aty SINGAPORE, Oct 5 (Reuters) – Gulf oil exporters topped pre-war levels for about half of September, shipping data showed on Monday, though attacks on tankers and logistical constraints cloud the outlook for sustained higher flows. Ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz face a “heightened and increasingly unpredictable kinetic threat” given the recent sharp increase in traffic, Marisks, a shipping intelligence service, said on Saturday. The seven-day moving average for crude exports from the region was 18.3 million barrels per day on September 30, provisional data from Kpler showed, with volumes topping pre-war levels on 14 days in September. That included Gulf oil sent Hormuz, via the Red Sea, and from terminals and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman. Shipments had earlier matched or exceeded pre-war levels on a handful of days in June and July, Kpler data showed, after Washington and Tehran reached a memorandum of understanding that has since lapsed.

The country is producing about 2 million barrels a day, compared with about 2.6 million before the conflict began at the end of February, Sheikh Nawaf Al-Sabah, chief executive officer of Kuwait Petroleum Corp., said in an interview. In the opening months of the conflict, Kuwait’s output fell below 1 million barrels a day as Iran blocked shipping through the waterway. While Tehran continues to threaten shipping in the strait, a growing number of tankers are risking transits anyway, he said. “More ships are getting through because people recognize there’s no alternative to the Strait of Hormuz,” he said. “Everything you do, every pipeline you build, storage facility, all of that cannot replace the vital importance of the Strait of Hormuz to international commerce.” His comments are the latest sign of rising oil exports from the Middle East, with some Wall Street banks estimating shipments are approaching prewar levels. Gulf producers including Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia have been sending cargoes out through Hormuz even though ships transiting the contested waterway continue to be attacked.

https://gcaptain.com/lng-trade-through-h.text: Oct 5, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Shipments of liquefied natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz extended a rebound that began in September, as the region’s producers seek to restore supplies to energy-starved customers. At least three LNG shipments have exited the key waterway since late last week, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg and Kpler. While outbound traffic in September climbed to the highest level since the Iran conflict began in late February, flows remain more than 75% below pre-war levels. The market is closely watching LNG shipments through Hormuz for signs of relief from a supply crunch that last month pushed prices in Europe and Asia to the highest since late 2022. A sustained recovery could help ease prices just before the Northern Hemisphere winter, when heating demand typically surges. The increase in traffic comes as risks to shipping remain acute following a flurry of incidents in recent days. UK Maritime Trade Operations said it received a report of a tanker being hit by an unknown projectile within Hormuz on Oct 4.
