https://petronoticias.com.br/yinson-fech.text: Diante da queda das pressões dos reservatórios e da necessidade de reforçar a segurança energética regional, a malaia Yinson e a italiana Eni decidiram avançar com um importante projeto de modificação do topside para ampliar a capacidade de exportação de gás do FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor (JAK), que opera offshore de Gana. O acordo permitirá estender por quatro anos o período de afretamento do FPSO JAK, até 2036. Somada à extensão de quatro anos do contrato, a operação elevará o backlog firme da subsidiária Yinson Production em aproximadamente US$ 600 milhões. O principal objetivo do projeto de modificação é instalar um sistema de compressão para compensar a esperada redução das pressões dos reservatórios e aumentar a capacidade de exportação de gás da unidade de aproximadamente 210 milhões a 220 milhões de pés cúbicos padrão por dia (scf/d) para 355 milhões de scf/d. A previsão é que o projeto seja concluído no primeiro trimestre de 2028. Os trabalhos incluirão a fabricação e integração de dois módulos principais de topside destinados a ampliar a capacidade de processamento de gás do FPSO JAK. O módulo MG2 será equipado com dois compressores acionados por turbinas a gás, enquanto o módulo MC4 funcionará como uma unidade auxiliar de tratamento de gás, projetada para processar volumes maiores. “ A assinatura deste aditivo contratual para o Projeto de Modificação NAG no FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor representa um marco em nossa parceria com a Eni, nossos parceiros de joint venture e no setor energético de Gana ”, afirmou o CEO da Yinson Production, Flemming Guiducci Grønnegaard . “ Ao aumentar a capacidade de exportação de gás, estamos fortalecendo uma infraestrutura energética offshore confiável, apoiando as necessidades domésticas de energia de Gana e contribuindo para prolongar a vida econômica do campo ”, acrescentou. O FPSO JAK é propriedade de uma joint venture liderada pela Yinson Production, que detém uma participação de controle de 74%. Os 26% restantes pertencem a um consórcio japonês formado por Sumitomo Corporation, Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K Line), JGC Holdings Corporation e Development Bank of Japan (DBJ). O FPSO opera no bloco Offshore Cape Three Points (OCTP), em Gana, onde processa petróleo e gás não associado dos campos Sankofa Gye Nyame.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mid.text: Middle East oil exports, excluding Iran, surpassed the pre-war average of 18 million barrels per day last week, despite attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, according to data from the maritime tracking firm Kpler. Crude oil exports reached pre-war levels in September, with at least 16.5 million barrels leaving the region excluding Iran, Kpler said on Wednesday. “Forty percent now bypass Hormuz, and most crude crossing the strait changes tankers offshore,” Kpler said, adding that most of the oil flowed through Saudi and United Arab Emirates pipelines. These figures include flows via the Red Sea, a route increasingly used to bypass the blockade Iran is attempting to impose on Hormuz, where around a fifth of the world’s petroleum supplies crossed before the war. Iran still claims control over the strait, and ships without its authorization risk coming under attack, but more and more are making it out, and alternative routes meant to bypass the waterway are operating at full capacity. Despite the rebound, experts stressed that the situation was far from normal, and Iran remains deprived of a large share of its own exports by a U.S. counterblockade of its ports.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Any deep-ocean seabed operation is an expensive proposition, as research vessel operators and offshore drilling companies are well aware. Deep-sea mining for manganese nodules would be no exception, demanding specialized tonnage, robotics, processing equipment and R&D. In a new report, some of the budding industry's opponents suggest that the overhead of industrial-scale subsea operations could make deep sea mining a loss-making proposition - even before accounting for environmental factors. Drawing on an investment prospectus for two projects belonging to The Metals Company, one of the biggest deep sea mining firms, the environmental consultancy Koinon conducted "stress-tests" to see if TMC's business model would hold up under various scenarios. The study was sponsored by five NGOs and foundations that are opposed to rapid commercialization of the practice. Koinon's analysts looked at typical cost overruns for megaprojects and ran 10,000 simulations on various outcomes, finding that the median outcome would result in no meaningful return. "In 60% of iterations, the collector’s net cash flow is negative in every year, with the consequence that no internal rate of return exists," Koinon's analysts wrote. "Among the minority of runs that do generate a positive return profile, the median IRR stands at 4%." The report concludes that the project has an 83 percent probability of returning a loss, with a median net present value of -$5 billion, assuming a discount rate of 8 percent. By comparison, under TMC's own projected scenario, the two projects would make $23 billion. The consultancy's analysis found that the up-front capex cost of the collection system was the primary driver of profitability, and the only variable capable of moving the project's margins into the zone of positive returns. Koinon estimated that - based on typical cost overruns for a frontier industry - the average simulated cost of the collection system would likely be about 1.9 times TMC's expected cost, based on typical overruns in past reference cases in offshore oil and gas, frontier technology and mega-scale mining projects. In its sensitivity analysis, changes in capex alone could vary the size of the return by more than $8 billion, making capex alone determinative of project profit or loss. The discount rate is a key element in this analysis. Koinon noted that the regulatory and environmental risk associated with deep sea mining has prompted dozens of bankers, insurers and industrial-metals buyers to publicly vow not to do business with deep-sea minerals producers - potentially making project financing more expensive (and thereby driving up the discount rate).

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Neste domingo (4), brasileiros foram às urnas em diferentes partes do mundo para escolher quem ocupará a Presidência da República pelos próximos quatro anos. A disputa foi marcada — mais uma vez — pela polarização entre Lula (PT) e um candidato do Partido Liberal (PL), desta vez Flávio Bolsonaro . No entanto, apesar da disputa acirrada entre os dois candidatos, que resultou em um 2º turno, houve uma única cidade no exterior em que um candidato diferente figurou entre a primeiras colocações: Mumbai, na Índia. Por lá, Lula ficou em primeiro com 5 votos, porém a segunda a colocação ficou com Renan Santos (Missão), com 3 votos. Flávio Bolsonaro, por sua vez, recebeu apenas um voto. Ao todo, 57 pessoas estavam aptas a votar para presidente na metrópole indiana, porém apenas 11 eleitores compareceram às urnas. Somando todas as seções eleitorais da Índia, Lula teve 29 votos (47,54%), contra 27 votos (44,26%) de Flávio e 3 votos (4,92%) de Renan Santos. Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro não aparecerem entre os dois primeiros colocados é algo raro. A única cidade em que a situaçã se repetiu foi em Guarani de Goiás, onde Ronaldo Caiado ficou em segundo lugar, com 32,26% dos votos, enquanto Flávio terminou na terceira colocação, com 26,64%.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: Just days after President Donald Trump unveiled a multi-billion-dollar South Korean investment in the Alaska LNG pipeline megaproject, officials in Seoul and the United States are walking back the timing and review status of the commitment. On Monday, Vice President JD Vance acknowledged to Reuters that there are still "details" to work out on the agreement. Alaska LNG is among the most ambitious infrastructure proposals in the United States, an 800-mile line connecting gas fields on the Artic tundra of the North Slope with a liquefaction plant on the Gulf of Alaska. It would be a big boost for Alaska's economy and state budget, but it would also be a major commitment of capital. At inception, the proposal had big-name backing, at one time boasting involvement from BP, ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips. All three oil majors backed out by 2016. At present, the investment company Glenfarne Group and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation are in charge of pursuing permits, investors and customers, with considerable assistance from the state and the White House. If built, the project would deliver 20 million tonnes per annum of LNG to buyers in Asian markets, but at considerable financial cost and risk. The pipeline route has to traverse remote, rugged areas of central Alaska, where logistics are difficult and seasonal weather is harsh. With the need to construct a treatment plant at the North Slope side of the project, then build an overland supply pipeline, the megaproject is expected to cost $45-55 billion. This works out to as much as $2.7 billion per mtpa - approaching three times the capex required for Gulf Coast LNG projects, according to Reuters. So far, the sponsors have preliminary commitments for offtake totaling about 13 mtpa - but no binding sales contracts. Accordingly, energy analysts and South Korean regulators are looking closely at the financial details. Korea's energy ministry says that it will need a complete commecial feasibility study before it can commit to an investment decision. Multiple analysts predict that the LNG will have be more expensive at the pier because of the capex of the treatment and pipeline system, so other factors will have to determine the decision - like the short shipping distance, the available alternatives in British Columbia, and the strategic benefits of having a new U.S. supplier. "Currently, there is no evidence that any entity is willing to fund this project, nor is there any evidence that customers have stepped forward to purchase the gas," one former senior State of Alaska official with experience on Alaska LNG told Chosun Ilbo. https://g1.globo.com/ciencia/noticia/202.text: Durante mais de duas décadas, o físico belga Francis Halzen defendeu uma ideia que muitos colegas consideravam improvável: transformar um quilômetro cúbico de gelo antártico em instrumento científico, capaz de registrar partículas que atravessam planetas inteiros sem deixar rastro. Nesta terça-feira (6), a aposta lhe rendeu o Prêmio Nobel de Física de 2026, anunciado pela Academia Real das C
Francis Halzen levou o Nobel de Física de 2026 por contribuições decisivas para o Observatório de Neutrinos IceCube e pela descoberta de neutrinos de alta energia de origem astrofísica .

O Nobel de Física de 2026 foi para o belga Francis Halzen, da Universidade de Wisconsin-Madison (EUA), que transformou o gelo do Polo Sul em um detector de partículas vindas do espaço profundo. O anúncio foi feito nesta terça-feira (6) pela Academia Real das Ciências da Suécia.

O físico belga Francis Halzen quebrou nesta terça-feira (6) uma marca que se mantinha havia mais de 30 anos: tornou-se o primeiro cientista em décadas a ganhar sozinho o Nobel de Física. Desde 1992, o prêmio vinha sendo sempre dividido entre dois ou três pesquisadores. Professor da Universidade de Wisconsin-Madison (EUA), Halzen foi premiado pela Academia Real das Ciências da Suécia por suas contribuições decisivas ao Observatório de Neutrinos IceCube, no Polo Sul. O último a receber a láurea sem dividi-la foi o francês Georges Charpak, que, assim como o belga, foi reconhecido por um instrumento capaz de revelar partículas invisíveis. A invenção de Charpak, de 1968, é uma caixa com gás atravessada por fios metálicos eletrizados. Quando uma partícula passa por ela, arranca elétrons do gás e gera uma pequena corrente no fio mais próximo. Computadores registram esses sinais e reconstroem o caminho da partícula. A câmara de Charpak tornou a coleta de dados mil vezes mais rápida do que os métodos fotográficos usados até então. Com ela, os físicos passaram a conseguir flagrar interações raríssimas, às vezes uma em um bilhão, que revelam o interior da matéria. Hoje, quase todo experimento de física de partículas usa algum detector derivado dela, que também chegou à medicina, na detecção de raios X.

Flávio Bolsonaro ficou em segundo lugar, sendo o mais votado em 36 nações. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543493-eq.text: Failure to secure approval for the Rosebank and Jackdaw projects would be a major setback for Equinor's Adura joint venture with Shell in the North Sea, Equinor CEO Anders Opedal said on Tuesday. "Not approving Rosebank would be contradictory to energy security, to job creation," Opedal told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London. He added that a rejection would prompt Equinor and other investors to question whether Britain remained an attractive place to invest. Rosebank and Jackdaw have become focal points for climate activists in Britain. Greenpeace and Uplift successfully challenged the projects in court over their treatment of downstream emissions, overturning the original approvals and forcing fresh applications in 2025. Britain approved Rosebank in 2023 and Jackdaw in 2022 under the previous Conservative government. A decision on Jackdaw could come within days after media reports said an announcement had been delayed until after an October 8 by-election. Much of the infrastructure needed for Jackdaw is already in place, meaning the gas field could begin production this winter if approved. Rosebank could deliver first oil in the first half of 2027.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543491-mi.text: MISC has named Th’ailib, the first of three new 174,000-cubic-metre liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers secured under long-term charter agreements with QatarEnergy, at Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI) in South Korea. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543490-kb.text: KBR has been awarded a contract by Saudi Aramco to provide engineering and project execution services for upgrades to offshore facilities at the Marjan oil and gas field in the Arabian Gulf. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543486-ll.text: Lloyd's Register (LR) has awarded Approval in Principle (AiP) to GasEntec for a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) concept capable of delivering up to 1 billion cubic feet of gas per day, placing it among the highest-capacity FSRU designs currently under development. The approval, presented during Gastech 2026 in Bangkok, followed LR's independent assessment of the design's technical and safety fundamentals. The FSRU features a multi-mode regasification system capable of operating in open, closed and combined-loop configurations, allowing its operation to be adapted to different environmental conditions, regulatory requirements and project needs. GasEntec has designed the unit around a modular architecture that can be configured for different capacities, pressures and operating requirements. If built, the unit would rank among the world's largest FSRUs by send-out capacity. “This FSRU delivers a common modular platform that can be configured for different capacities, pressures and operating conditions, enabling efficient project specific engineering and faster deployment. “As energy demand accelerates around the world, from grid growth to AI data center driven power needs, the constraint isn't supply; it's how quickly and reliably you can get gas to where it's needed,” said TG Kim, GasEntec Co-Chief Operating Officer.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543494-no.text: Solstad Offshore has exercised an option to purchase the construction support vessel (CSV) Normand Maximus for $125 million, with the acquisition scheduled to be completed in October 2027. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543492-tw.text: Drilling waste management specialist TWMA has secured a multi-million-dollar contract from an unnamed North Sea operator to provide offshore drilling waste management services for a multi-well campaign in the UK North Sea. The contract, awarded under an existing agreement, covers deployment of TWMA's RotoMill technology and associated equipment, with mobilization scheduled for the third quarter of 2026 and operations starting in the fourth quarter. TWMA expects to process about 2,000 metric tonnes of drill cuttings per well during the campaign, with the project to be delivered by its Aberdeen-based team. The RotoMill system treats drilling waste offshore at source rather than transporting it to shore for processing. TWMA said the approach can reduce vessel movements and associated emissions by up to 50% compared with onshore processing. “We’ve been working in the North Sea for more than two decades and securing new work like this is a strong endorsement of our UK business and our team in Aberdeen. It reflects the confidence operators continue to place in our technology, our people and our ability to deliver safely and efficiently in challenging offshore environments,” said John Robertson, TWMA UK General Manager. TWMA has been active in the North Sea for more than two decades and said the latest award adds to its existing portfolio in the region.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543478-oi.text: Shipping bottlenecks, deep cuts in refinery output and inventory draws that could take years to replace will keep global oil prices high beyond this year, industry executives said at a conference in London on Monday. Following the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran at the end of February, Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, choking exports through one of the world's most crucial shipping bottlenecks. The impact has been compounded by attacks on oil and gas infrastructure, hampering production and adding to the disruption of exports of crude oil and refined fuels. "I think it is going to be bedlam for the bulk of the end of the year and maybe 2027," Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said. In his first conference address since the start of the Iran war, Amin Nasser, chief executive of the world's biggest oil company Saudi Aramco, told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London it could take up to two years to refill global stockpiles drawn on as an emergency measure. "Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify. Even then, replenishing inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," he said. Both ends of the barrel refers to unrefined crude and refined products, such as diesel and jet fuel

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543477-ne.text: New Fortress Energy's Fast LNG unit offshore Altamira, Mexico, has gone offline following a mechanical problem with its gas turbine, with the company expecting the facility to return to service during the fourth quarter. https://www.rigzone.com/news/brent_once_.text: The price of the global crude benchmark, Brent, is once again toiling around $100 per barrel as its reasons for trading much beyond the psychological three-digit mark are being eroded. That’s what John Evans, an analyst at PVM Oil Associates, which is part of the IP ICAP Group, said in a market analysis sent to Rigzone on Tuesday. “It is … very hard to complete a picture on how many oil tankers are making passage through Hormuz for the data is retrospective rather than live,” Evans noted in the analysis. “With the attacks on shipping increased, there is little doubt that the reported return to export volumes from the Middle East to pre-war levels will be adjusted accordingly to the downside, but for now the assumption of more crude getting through has dampened price fervor,” he added. Evans also highlighted in the analysis that Saudi Arabia “unexpectedly” cut its official selling price (OSP) for November delivery into Asia. “Through a mixture of ship-to-ship (STS) transfers and alternative delivery routes, the OPEC kingpin has increased exports to six million barrels per day, the monthly average of 2025, according to Kpler,” Evans pointed out.

https://safety4sea.com/amsa-psc-inspecti.text: The Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) has reminded operators that seafarers visiting Australian ports must be provided with access to shore leave , stressing that the possibility of a Port State Control (PSC) inspection is not a valid reason to delay, restrict or deny it. I n Marine Notice 2026/02, published in late September, the authority has specifically clarified that if crew members are ashore while AMSA conducts a PSC inspection, their absence will not, in itself, result in adverse action against the vessel. Under the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 (MLC), seafarers must be granted shore leave “to benefit their health and well-being and consistent with the operational requirements of their positions.” The requirement is implemented in Australia through the Navigation Act 2012 and Marine Order 11, covering living and working conditions on vessels. AMSA emphasized that companies have responsibilities for the health, safety and wellbeing of seafarers, with shore leave and access to shore-based welfare facilities playing an important role in supporting physical and mental health and reducing fatigue. The authority expects companies to give significant consideration to the wellbeing and recovery benefits of shore leave when assessing associated risks. It also stressed that financial considerations should not be used as the basis for deciding whether to grant shore leave. AMSA acknowledged that shore leave can involve risks, including exposure to communicable diseases, but said these risks cannot be eliminated entirely and can be managed through “suitable and acceptable controls” that allow seafarers to go ashore safely.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-h.text: A fatal accident aboard a tanker at anchor off Ningbo has highlighted a familiar but serious maritime safety risk: sending crew onto an exposed deck when sea conditions make even routine tasks potentially life-threatening. A Hong Kong Merchant Shipping Information Note found that failures to follow heavy-weather procedures, ineffective risk assessment and inadequate safety awareness contributed to the incident. The case also raises questions about whether onboard controls are genuinely changing behaviour when conditions deteriorate. The tanker was awaiting a berth at an open-sea anchorage east of Ningbo when it encountered gale-force winds, rough seas and heavy swell. On the morning of the accident, the bosun and pumpman went onto the main deck to cover equipment with tarpaulins and prevent seawater ingress. They subsequently discovered that a foam hose box and mooring rope on the forward mooring deck had been damaged and displaced by the heavy seas. The two crew members collected the foam hose and nozzle that had been scattered from the box and then attempted to tidy the mooring rope.

https://safety4sea.com/wellbeing-ripple-.text: “What if the secret to better wellbeing was not one big change, but a series of small ones?” questions Stavrie Kleanthous, Wellbeing Services Manager and Lead Clinical Dietitian (RD, MSc) at Oceanic. M any of us look for dramatic solutions when it comes to health, yet some of the most powerful improvements come from simple daily habits. Choosing a healthier meal, getting enough sleep whenever schedules allow, staying active, or taking time to connect with others can each create positive effects that extend into many areas of life. Like ripples spreading across water, these small actions often have a greater impact than we realise. In turn, feeling more energised may encourage healthier food choices, greater productivity, and more positive interactions with others. One small action can create many positive outcomes, illustrating how wellbeing habits often extend far beyond the moment they begin. The reason these small habits matter so much is that wellbeing is interconnected. The food we eat, the rest we get, how active we are, and the relationships we build all play a role in our health. When one area improves, others often benefit too. Together, these daily choices help create a positive cycle that supports wellbeing, resilience, and quality of life.

https://safety4sea.com/new-project-explo.text: Liberty Global Logistics LLC (LGL) and Hyundai Glovis Co., Ltd. are exploring the potential development of a small modular reactor (SMR)-powered Pure Car and Truck Carrier (PCTC), under a new agreement focused initially on trade between the United States and South Korea. S MR technology is attracting growing interest as the maritime industry searches for ways to cut greenhouse gas emissions without compromising the range and cargo capacity needed for global trade. To that end, the companies signed on 30 September a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to assess the commercial, technical and regulatory requirements for developing and operating the vessel, as the shipping industry looks for alternatives to conventional marine fuels. Under the agreement, LGL will examine the US regulatory and operating environment, initially focusing on ports on the US West Coast. The assessment will cover federal and state approvals, port infrastructure and other operational requirements. Hyundai Glovis will carry out a corresponding review in South Korea. The two companies will also assess the feasibility of building the vessel, including potential shipyards, flag-state requirements, classification and other technical and commercial considerations.

https://safety4sea.com/recaap-isc-one-in.text: Over the past week, 29 September to 5 October, one incident of piracy or armed robbery against ships in Asia was reported to the ReCAAP ISC. A ccording to ReCAAP ISC, οne CAT 4 incident of armed robbery against ships2 in Asia was reported to the ReCAAP ISC. The incident occurred onboard a bulk carrier while underway in the eastbound lane of the Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) in Singapore Strait (SS) on 1 Oct. 2026. The crew were not injured, and nothing was stolen from the vessel. Ships are advised to intensify vigilance and maintain sharp look-out while transiting the areas of concern or anchoring at ports and anchorages; and to report all incidents immediately to the nearest coastal State. The Centre also urges the coastal States to increase patrols/surveillance in their respective waters, respond promptly to incidents reported to them, strengthen coordination and promote information sharing on incidents and the criminal groups involved to arrest the perpetrators. For a 6th consecutive year, there has been no report of incident of abduction of crew in the Sulu-Celebes Seas and waters off Eastern Sabah. The last incident occurred on 17 Jan 2020. In January 2025, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), coordinated with other stakeholders and counterparts further downgraded the threat level of ‘Abduction of crew for ransom in the Sulu-Celebes Seas’ to ‘LOW’, meaning ‘No information or monitored activities suggest an impending attack; hence incidents are not expected to occur’. The ReCAAP ISC, in its Advisory on 14 Feb 2025 advised ships to “exercise vigilance when transiting the Sulu-Celebes Seas and report incidents to the Operation Centres of the Philippines and Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM)”. Also, to maintain communication with the relevant authorities when transiting the area. Ship master and crew are to report all incidents of piracy and armed robbery against ships to the nearest coastal State and flag State, referring to the Poster on the Contact Details for Reporting of Incidents of Piracy and Armed Robbery against Ships in Asia, exercise vigilance and adopt appropriate preventive measures taking reference from the Regional Guide 2 to Counter Piracy and Armed Robbery Against Ships in Asia; both produced by the ReCAAP ISC.

https://safety4sea.com/yemeni-forces-adv.text: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have rapidly advanced along the Red Sea coast toward Mocha, seeking to retake territory around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Iran-backed Houthi forces, amid renewed fighting that is raising fresh risks for commercial shipping through the strategic waterway. T he Yemeni government said its forces, backed by heavy Saudi air strikes, had secured key positions in the Dhubab area at the mouth of the strait, including an airstrip, and reached the outskirts of Mocha late on October 5. Yemen’s Defence Ministry said Mocha had fallen, although Reuters could not independently verify the extent of the government’s gains. According to Reuters, government sources said Houthi fighters were retreating toward the highlands, while another source said fighting was continuing around a military base near the strait. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the government forces had secured effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and cut off remaining Houthi forces in the area. The Houthis, however, rejected the claims as “completely untrue.” The advance follows the seizure of key positions around Bab el-Mandeb by the Houthis last month, an escalation that sent shockwaves through energy markets as Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz has already disrupted a major oil export route. The Bab el-Mandeb is a critical maritime chokepoint connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean , making developments around the strait a significant concern for vessel operators.

https://safety4sea.com/togo-introduces-n.text: Togo has introduced a new Environmental Compensation Fee (Droit à Compensation Environnementale – DCE) that applies to several economic sectors, including maritime transport. T he legal framework for the fee was established under Law No. 2026-007, adopted on March 23, 2026, which amended the country’s environmental legislation. Procedures for calculating and collecting the fee were later set out in Order No. 105/MERPCCC/MFB/2026, issued on August 7, NorthStandard has informed. According to McLEANS-WAMS and BUDD Group, the fee applies to maritime operations involving Togo and is based on the carbon footprint of a voyage. The calculation takes into account factors such as the mode of transport, voyage distance, vessel type and, where available, actual fuel consumption. Under the scheme, 50% of the calculated carbon footprint is attributed to Togo. Certain shipments may qualify for additional reductions. The reported rate is €15 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent, plus applicable taxes. Africa Blue Economy and Traffic Management (ABETM) has been appointed as the independent body responsible for verifying emissions and collecting the fee. Once payment is made, a DCE Certificate is issued, which the decree identifies as a mandatory document for maritime operations in Togo. Companies seeking an exemption must apply to ABETM and obtain an official exemption certificate if they meet the relevant criteria.

https://safety4sea.com/west-club-bunker-.text: Several major bunkering hubs recorded elevated levels of technically off-specification fuel results between April and September 2026, according to an update from West P&I Club’s Neptune Bunker Information service. T he update, prepared by Dmitry Kisil, Senior Loss Prevention Officer at West P&I Club, provides bunker quality data covering the six-month period and highlights regional trends across residual and low-sulphur fuels. West P&I encouraged Members to continue applying established bunker testing and fuel management practices and to use bunker quality data when assessing supply risks and planning bunkering operations. For heavy fuel oil (HFO), the highest technical off-specification rates were recorded in Antwerp at 46.2%, followed by Norfolk at 41.4%, the Panama Canal at 38.0% and Rotterdam at 35.5%. The reported issues varied between locations but commonly involved density, viscosity, water content, catalytic fines and ash-related exceedances. West P&I noted that these levels were significantly higher than those recorded at other major bunkering hubs, highlighting potential risks associated with fuel quality and subsequent onboard handling and machinery performance. In the very low sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO) category, particular attention was drawn to sulphur compliance in Europe. Rotterdam recorded a 68.6% sulphur off-specification rate, while Antwerp reached 58.9%, representing the highest levels in the dataset. The insurer cautioned that the number of samples from these locations was substantially smaller than at some other major bunkering ports, but said the results nevertheless underline the importance of robust bunker procurement, testing and fuel management procedures, particularly in relation to emissions-control requirements. For ultra-low sulphur fuel oil (ULSFO), the highest technical off-specification rates were reported in Barcelona at 70.3% and Genoa at 51.0%. In both cases, the results were primarily linked to pour point non-compliances.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-risk4sea-psi-o.text: RiSK4SEA’s PSC Stress Index (PSI) Outlook for October 2026 indicates a normalization of the global Port State Control (PSC) enforcement climate following the broad-based improvement recorded in September. Bulkers, Containers and General Cargo have all moved from PSI-2 “Improving Trend” to PSI-5 “Normal Conditions”, while Tankers remain at PSI-2 and continue to experience a comparatively favourable enforcement environment. T he October Outlook marks another shift in the PSC enforcement cycle observed over recent months. September saw all four major shipping segments converge at PSI-2, supported by detention activity materially below their respective 36-month baselines. Entering October, detention activity for Bulkers, Containers and General Cargo has returned close to historical norms, while Tankers continue to record lower-than-baseline detention pressure. At the same time, the underlying performance picture remains mixed, with technical and SMS-related indicators continuing to deteriorate across several segments. Commenting on the October findings, Apo Belokas, CEO & Founder of RiSK4SEA, said: October should be viewed as a normalization rather than a deterioration of the PSC enforcement climate. After the unusually favourable conditions recorded in the previous Outlook, detention activity across three of the four major segments has moved back towards historical levels. Tankers remain the exception, continuing to operate within an improving PSI environment. “The important signal is underneath the headline PSI. Normal enforcement conditions do not necessarily mean normal vessel performance. SMS and technical indicators remain elevated across several segments, reinforcing the need for ship managers to maintain preparation discipline even when the overall PSC climate appears stable.” Bulk carriers move from PSI-2 in the September Outlook to PSI-5 “Normal Conditions”, reflecting a return of detention activity towards its long-term baseline rather than a move into an unusually adverse enforcement environment.

https://safety4sea.com/europes-methane-p.text: The European Union’s efforts to curb methane emissions could inadvertently add further pressure to an energy system already facing supply and affordability concerns, according to Wood Mackenzie. S imon Flowers, Chairman and Chief Analyst, and Valentina Kretzschmar, Vice President of Consulting, Energy Transition Strategy at Wood Mackenzie, argue in a recent article that the timing of the EU’s methane regulation could prove particularly challenging given the bloc’s continued dependence on imported oil and gas. With concerns growing over energy security ahead of winter, the European Commission is now considering whether the regulation’s implementation should be delayed. Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen indicated this week that a postponement of up to 12 months could be considered. For Europe, the debate highlights a growing tension between environmental ambitions and energy security. While tighter controls on methane emissions are intended to accelerate decarbonisation and reduce one of the most potent greenhouse gases, imposing additional requirements on imported energy at a time of supply uncertainty could have wider consequences for the market. Tackling methane emissions is an increasingly urgent aspect of decarbonisation globally. The EU proposals aim to bring importers of oil and gas produced outside the EU in line with methane emissions regulation already in place for indigenous oil and gas producers from 1 January 2027. Penalties for non-compliance are severe at up to 20% of the importer’s global annual revenues. As ever with regulation, the devil is in the detail, detail that is necessarily dense. To wit, implementation of Article 28 of the EU MER requires importers to comply with the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) equivalence of EU crude oil, gas and coal for import contracts effective from 4 August 2024.

https://splash247.com/tanker-attacks-aro.text: Commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz is enduring its most intense spell of attacks since the US-Iran war began on February 28, with four tankers struck and another directly threatened in incidents disclosed by UK Maritime Trade Operations on Monday. The latest attack came at 1637 UTC yesterday when a tanker transiting Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile, starting a fire in the engine room. The crew was fighting the blaze when UKMTO issued its warning, with no casualties or pollution initially reported. Three other attacks disclosed on Monday were time-late reports from the previous two days. An inbound LPG carrier was struck on Saturday afternoon, followed less than two hours later by a crude tanker. A further crude carrier was hit above the waterline on Friday. Separately, an inbound tanker around 11 nautical miles north of Khasab was hailed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and ordered to turn around or face attack. The master complied. One of the more worrying incidents involved a drone entering a tanker’s funnel and falling into the engine room The disclosures follow an already violent run through the narrow waterway. UKMTO has registered repeated projectile strikes since late September, while the Joint Maritime Information Center has documented attacks concentrated along the Omani side of Hormuz. One of the more worrying incidents involved a drone entering a tanker’s funnel and falling into the engine room, starting a small fire and temporarily knocking out power. Other vessels have been struck around the stern and engine spaces, with several temporarily losing propulsion before either continuing independently or requiring tug assistance.

https://splash247.com/grain-carrier-sink.text: Commercial shipping in the western Black Sea has come under a fresh wave of attacks, with another general cargoship sinking and a second catching fire off Bulgaria barely a day after the loss of the Royad Mammadov off Romania. According to UK maritime security specialist Vanguard Tech, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and Palau-flagged Able issued distress signals around 70–80 nautical miles east of Byala and Cape St Atanas, inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. Bulgarian sources state that both vessels had been struck by drones. Alfa Watan reportedly suffered critical structural damage and subsequently sank, prompting a search and rescue operation for its crew, whose status remains unclear. The Able sustained a major fire, forcing all 18 crew members to abandon ship. All were subsequently rescued by the Bulgarian-flagged ferry Dioscuria. The circumstances remain under investigation. Vanguard notes that an earlier Turkish source suggested the two vessels had collided near the entrance to Romania’s Sulina Canal, while no responsibility for any alleged drone strike has yet been officially attributed. The incidents follow Monday’s sinking of the 6,933 dwt Royad Mammadov (pictured) in Romania’s exclusive economic zone. The Turkish-owned, St Kitts and Nevis-flagged vessel was carrying corn from Izmail to Italy when it caught fire and sank around 30 nautical miles south of Sfantu Gheorghe. Two seafarers were killed and 11 rescued. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the ship was struck by two Russian drones.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/shi.text: Merchant shipping companies are increasing their fleets’ defenses against drones following attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea and Middle East. Counter-drone specialists including Marss, Drone Defence and D-fend said they received more inquiries from shipowners. Interest was particularly strong among companies that handle oil and gas cargoes and those working around offshore energy infrastructure. Commercial ships are being targeted in the Gulf and the Black Sea as parties in conflicts seek to disrupt critical commodity supply chains. Shipowners willing to operate in dangerous waters are commanding record freight rates for their vessels. Jeffrey Starr, chief marketing officer at D-fend Solutions, said the business had seen “huge demand” from the shipping sector. The company was founded by Israeli cyber experts and specializes in taking over the controls of hostile drones before safely landing them. “What we are finding is that shipowners, shippers and naval forces are facing an asymmetric threat that is causing a big inbound uptick in enquiries about our technology,” he said. “This drone threat is no longer just limited to high-intensity war zones.” Richard Gill, chief executive at Drone Defence, said the company had more inquiries from oil tanker and liquefied natural gas carriers. He said that if shipowners could protect their vessels “they can do the more risky routes”.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/thr.text: At least two tankers have been struck in the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Monday, adding that a third vessel avoided being hit after complying with instructions from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The British navy monitor said it received “a time-late report of an incident within the Strait of Hormuz” in which a “verified source” reported that “a crude oil tanker has been struck by unknown projectiles,” adding that “authorities are investigating.” In a second statement published minutes later, UKMTO said it had received another delayed report, citing a “verified source” as saying that a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker “transiting inbound has been struck by an unknown projectile.” “Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO,” the agency said. https://splash247.com/exmar-confirms-luc.text: Belgium’s Exmar has confirmed the sale of the first suezmax in its four-ship newbuilding programme at South Korea’s DH Shipbuilding, crystallising a profit of around $22m on the transaction. The Antwerp-listed company said it has signed an agreement to sell the first tanker under construction, with the vessel to pass to its buyer simultaneously with delivery from the yard in the third quarter of 2027. Exmar did not disclose either the buyer or sale price. Greek shipping and financial sources previously identified Evangelos Marinakis-led Capital Group as the buyer of the 157,000 dwt hull HN5112, with the resale priced at more than $106m. The $22m gain disclosed by Exmar is broadly consistent with those market numbers. Exmar ordered four scrubber-fitted, 157,200 dwt suezmaxes at DH Shipbuilding in September 2025 in the Belgian gas shipping specialist’s first move into crude tanker ownership. The vessels are designed to carry around 1m barrels of crude each. Market reports at the time valued the original four-ship package at around $339m, or roughly $85m per vessel. Exmar’s 2025 accounts subsequently showed $309.4m of remaining capital commitments attached to the suezmax programme at year-end.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/misc-nam.text: MISC has named Th’ailib, the first of three new 174,000-cubic-metre liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers secured under long-term charter agreements with QatarEnergy, at Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI) in South Korea. Th’ailib will enter a firm 15-year charter with QatarEnergy starting in 2026, with two additional vessels scheduled for delivery as part of MISC's participation in the energy company's LNG fleet expansion programme. The three vessels form part of the second phase of the program. MISC previously participated in its first phase through a consortium arrangement involving 12 LNG carriers, bringing its involvement across the two phases to 15 vessels. Th’ailib is equipped with dual-fuel engines, a reliquefaction system, high-performance anti-fouling hull coating and an air lubrication system aimed at improving fuel efficiency and energy use and reducing emissions intensity. The vessel's name is derived from Jabal Thuaileb in Qatar's Fox Hills district and from the Arabic word for ‘fox’.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/no.text: A Justiça do Piauí condenou o cantor Gusttavo Lima e a empresa Marina de Iracema Park S.A. a pagarem, de forma solidária, R$ 5 mil por danos morais a uma espectadora que foi repreendida e exposta publicamente durante um show de Réveillon. https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: The Royal Marines have released video footage of an unusual boarding method their units can use to embark a submarine at the completion of a covert mission: driving over the propeller and up the slope of the stern, at speed. The demonstration was part of a large scale NATO-member exercise across Scotland with 2,000 personnel. The commando mission in question was an insertion of forward observers to direct naval artillery at inland targets. Members of 148 Battery - a joint Navy/Army unit - deployed aboard a German attack submarine and used inflatable rubber raiding boats to reach the beach at Cape Wrath. From there, they infiltrated up into the cliffs and provided forward observation for the 76-mm deck gun of a Portuguese frigate, NRP Dom Francisco de Almeida. "This level of complexity and coordination of live assets has not been achieved by 148 Battery for nearly 30 years," commented the unit's unnamed operations officer. The drill included dramatic float-on/float-off evolutions with rubber raiding boats in rough surface conditions. With the submarine pitching in heavy swells, the Royal Marine boat teams drove over the submerged propeller and between the Type-212A submarine's upper two X-rudders in order to hit the sloping aft deck of the submarine, driving up and out of the water to land on top. A team of crewmates - tethered to the deck for safety - were on hand to grab the boat and pull it aboard. Commandos x submarine. A powerful combination. Commandos emerged from the depths of the North Atlantic on a German U-boat to carry out a daring operation as part of the largest test of all arms of the @Commando_Ops in 15 years. Read more: https://t.co/WOIYXxpWx2 https://t.co/Y9E0ix3FuQ Earlier in the exercise series, 148 Battery provided naval gunfire control for Dutch frigate HNLMS Van Amstel and Royal Canadian Navy frigate HMCS St. John’s for additional live-fire drills. A separate Royal Marines unit also deployed to the Faroe Islands to demonstrate presence.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: A large tanker has caught fire off the coast of the resort city of Sochi, Russia, according to local media accounts and satellite sensing data. The vessel is readily visible from shore, and multiple videos depicting the fire have appeard on Russian social media channels. The bystander-image sequence begins with a substantial fire centered on cargo tanks amidships, followed by obvious signs of burning oil spreading aft down the starboard side. Later videos and photos show a large pool of burning oil on the water aft of the vessel and a towering column of smoke. Initial reports indicate that the vessel is likely the Aframax Rio, previously sanctioned by Ukraine for alleged involvement in Russian oil exports. Marine traffic tracking sites last spotted Aframax Rio on Monday at a position just off the coast of Sirius, a small coastal town to the southeast of Sochi. https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: As part of the U.S. Navy’s push to expand shipbuilding capacity and accelerate construction, it has awarded a $2.9 billion contract to defense contractor Anduril Industries. The company reports it will invest an additional $3.7 billion in private capital to create a new submarine industrial base to be located at Maryland’s historic Sparrows Point, once the home of American shipbuilding. Anduril describes the planned new facility as a “software-defined shipyard.” The project, which Maryland officials said would be the largest private investment in the state in over a decade, is targeted to begin production by 2030 and is expected to provide more than 3,100 new jobs. To be known as Arsenal-2, it will be built at Tradepoint Atlantic in Baltimore County, which is the redevelopment of the former Sparrows Point shipyard, which built military vessels deployed in the First and Second World Wars as well as commercial ships. The Sparrows Point Shipyard stopped new ship construction in 1986, and the legacy site finally closed completely in 2003. During a briefing hosted by the White House, they asserted that the new facility will play a critical role in the production capacity the Navy needs to continue to build the Virginia-class submarines. Reports said that component manufacturing, such as that for torpedo tubes, is currently delaying the submarine construction programs. The White House asserted that the yard, when fully operational, would add about 9 million labor hours of production capacity each year, a 15 percent increase for the submarine program. The new yard will be located on 187 acres at Sparrows Point and cover more than 2 million square feet. It will have fabrication and assembly areas, production lines, and a 1,200-foot graving dock. Arsenal-2 will manufacture components and later large-scale blocks for the submarines. The blocks will be transferred to General Dynamics Electric Boat and HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding, which are assembling the submarines. Anduril, which is known for its drones and AI-powered software tools, highlights that the new yard will be built around a digital backbone. It says it will connect fabrication workflows, outfitting sequences, material movement, inspection protocols, and documentation requirements in a single system that creates real-time visibility into the state of production.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Cruise ships will be moving among three of Carnival Corporation’s brands as the company continues efforts to maximize the financial strength of its operations. Holland America Line and P&O Cruises will be increasing capacity by receiving newer ships, while Cunard will be giving up one ship, with the changes taking place in 20029. The changes will begin in the spring of 2029 when Cunard’s Queen Anne will be transferred to P&O after completing her previously announced world cruise. The ship will be “reimagined and renamed,” according to the announcement, before joining the UK-based operation in May 2029. P&O, however, will also be conducting a farewell season for its 20-plus-year-old cruise ship Arcadia , which will retire from the fleet on August 21, 2029. She will then transfer to Holland America Line as part of its ongoing fleet evolution. She will be refitted and renamed to join the US-based operation. “These decisions reflect a careful, long-term view of our portfolio and where the individual strengths of each ship can best support guest demand and the future direction of our two cruise lines,” said Paul Ludlow, president of Carnival UK, P&O Cruises, and Cunard, announcing the changes. “This decision does not change our commitment to Cunard or its future.” Queen Anne had been heralded with her launch in May 2024 as the first new ship added to Cunard since 2010, and the first time the venerated British brand would be operating four Queens. At 114,188 gross tons and 1,058 feet (323 meters) in length, the ship is based on the platform used for Holland America’s newest class of ships. She was a large addition for Cunard, with a 2,956-passenger capacity, but incorporated what the company calls “a bold and contemporary expression of Cunard,” which also drew criticism among the loyal clientele. Ludlow said the changes would provide Cunard “a more closely unified fleet.” The ship will continue in service for the planned Four Queens celebration in Liverpool in May 2028 and then her final world cruise. Carnival Corporation is also investing in an upgrade and modernization of Queen Mary 2 in April 2027, which will add suites and redo the wellness area, shops, and some public spaces.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: The latest update from the Canadian Coast Guard, which is monitoring the removal operation for the wreck of the MSC Baltic III containership, shows strong progress. The effort being led by Resolve Marine has passed the halfway mark based on the tonnage of the vessel, while images show the hull stripped down and broken apart. On September 27, the bow and midship sections of the MSC Baltic III were successfully pulled an additional 42 meters (approximately 138 feet) to shore. The vessel had measured 207 meters (679 feet) when it was in operation and 33,767 dwt. The dismantling operation accelerated during the summer with the removal of the deckhouse, machinery, and upper portions of the vessel. A large portion of the bow section was removed from the MSC Baltic III on September 9 and pulled onto shore. Since then, the hull has been split near where the vessel cracked after it was driven ashore in 2025. The Coast Guard highlights that pulling the forward section toward the shoreline is making it accessible from the scrap pad. A large crane was positioned on the pad for lifting sections of the hull, which are being trucked away for recycling. While the cutting and removal operations are ongoing, the Coast Guard reports that as of the beginning of October, the total tonnage removed from the wreck is approximately 6,086 tonnes. It is close to 55 percent of the vessel's total tonnage. The stern section of the wreck remains in the water and is being prepared for pulling operations. Comparison showing the hull at the beginning of September (Canadian Coast Guard)

https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: Bulgarian officials are denouncing the attack on two small cargo ships in the Black Sea while reporting that the crew of one vessel is missing. The reports said the two ships were attacked overnight, with 18 seafarers rescued and a search and rescue operation continuing. Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev convened a special meeting of the government, and he called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and a “gross violation of international law.” He declined to officially state who had attacked the ships, but reports are widely attributing the strikes to Russia, a charge repeated by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a posting on social media. “If this war is not ended in time, it will continue to expand its spatial scope and increase the risk of even a global conflict,” said Radev. He pointed out that Bulgaria does not border Ukraine or Russia and lies at a critical point in the Black Sea, more than 140 nautical miles from Ukraine. According to the reports, the Bulgarian ferry Dioscuria was in the area approximately 70 nautical miles east of Byala in the eastern part of Bulgaria when the attacks took place. Bulgarian officials said the strikes were attacks by air and sea drones. The ferry’s crew saw an explosion and headed to the area, which officials emphasized was in Bulgaria’s EEZ. The Navy, Air Force, and Border Police also responded. The ferry crew reported seeing an overturned lifeboat, three rafts, and life jackets in the water but was unable to locate any crewmembers. The ship, which is being identified as the Turkish-owned Alfa Watan (3,160 dwt), is believed to have sunk. Built in 1976, it is registered in Togo. The ship was sailing from Egypt and bound for Sulina, Romania, according to its AIS transmission.

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Um navio comercial afundou nesta terça-feira (6) no Mar Negro, na costa da Bulgária, após ser atingido por drones. A tripulação está desaparecida. O incidente ocorreu a 112 km de Byala. Este pode ter sido o primeiro ataque registrado na zona econômica exclusiva da Bulgária. Ao todo, 2 navios foram atingidos. O que afundou tinha bandeira do Togo, enquanto o outro transportava grãos e teve a tripulação salva. O primeiro-ministro búlgaro relacionou o ataque à guerra. A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, também condenou o episódio.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O ex-presidente da República, Jair Messias Bolsonaro (PL), fez uma aparição de cerca de 20 minutos no quintal da casa onde ele cumpria prisão domiciliar em 9 de setembro de 2025 — Foto: Wilton Junior/Estadão Conteúdo A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) se manifestou nesta terça-feira (6) sobre o pedido da defesa de Jair Bolsonaro para receber a vista de Flávio Bolsonaro. "Considerando a ausência de fatos supervenientes indicativos de descumprimento das condições fixadas ou da necessidade de prorrogação da medida restritiva anteriormente determinada, a Procuradoria-Geral da República não opõe óbice ao deferimento do pleito formulado", diz trecho da manifestação da PGR. Os advogados de Jair Bolsonaro (PL) solicitaram na segunda-feira (5) ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes, relator do caso da trama golpista no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), autorização para que o ex-presidente receba uma visita do filho. Moraes enviou o pedido para manifestação da PGR antes de decidir se aprova a visita. A defesa de Bolsonaro também pede que o regime normal de visitas do ex-presidente seja restabelecido.

O ministro Nunes Marques deve liberar para julgamento, após o segundo turno, os pedidos de Bolsonaro para anular sua condenação a 27 anos e 3 meses de prisão. Antes de liberar o caso, Nunes Marques pedirá manifestação da PGR sobre a nova revisão. A expectativa é de um parecer contrário ao ex-presidente. Há a expectativa de que Alexandre de Moraes devolva para julgamento ações sobre o cálculo das penas dos condenados pelos atos golpistas de 8 de janeiro. Apresentada em 25 de setembro, a nova revisão criminal contesta a cadeia de custódia. A defesa alega limitações para verificar integralmente as provas digitais do processo.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543507-su.text: Sumitomo Corporation Global Metals Co., Ltd. (SCGM) and TFI Marine Limited have formed a partnership to introduce innovation into mooring solutions for floating offshore wind and offshore energy projects. The partnership enables and accelerates the deployment of floating offshore wind in Japan and globally, contributing to decarbonization and energy security. Mooring systems are among the principal cost and risk drivers in floating offshore wind. As projects move into deeper water and towards commercial scale, developers need mooring solutions that reduce loads, extend component life and lower cost without introducing new project risk. Both companies are working together to bring the SeaSpring, a load and fatigue reduction component, to projects in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, and to support the wider adoption of next generation mooring solutions internationally. TFI Marine has developed the SeaSpring, a load and fatigue reduction component delivering next generation mooring solutions, together with the modeling and design expertise to engineer them. SeaSpring is incorporated into the mooring line to reduce peak loads and improve fatigue performance, enabling the use of smaller mooring chain and synthetic fiber rope, anchors and components. This reduces installation time and vessel requirements. The impact is a reduction in project CAPEX and OPEX, directly reducing the levelized cost of energy. The SeaSpring has achieved DNV and ClassNK certification. Sumitomo Corporation Global Metals serves as the core entity responsible for the global execution of the Group's steel-related businesses. Equipment and materials for offshore wind facilities is a growth area for the company's Plate & Construction Steel Products business, and SCGM works with companies across the industry to ensure that Japan has access offshore energy technology. In this partnership, SCGM, as a leading Japanese corporation, delivers supply chain expertise and resilience, established relationships across the energy sector, and the industrial network that enables the establishment of Japanese manufacture and component supply globally. The two companies will jointly engage project developers, EPCI contractors and all floating offshore wind stakeholders to accelerate early adoption of innovative mooring solutions. The companies have also agreed to explore the manufacture of SeaSpring components in Japan, supporting local supply chain development and local content for Japanese floating offshore wind projects.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543495-ch.text: Chevron Technical Center has joined a long-term digital subsurface collaboration between SLB and TotalEnergies to co-develop technologies for reservoir engineering and geoscience. The collaboration, known as Arena, was established by SLB and TotalEnergies in 2024 and will now include Chevron as its second global operator. Chevron will contribute investment, intellectual property and technical expertise, including capabilities in uncertainty analysis, optimization and field development planning, to help shape the development of scalable digital subsurface technologies. Arena is focused on technologies designed to improve decision-making across reservoir engineering and geoscience workflows as operators manage increasingly complex reservoirs and growing volumes of subsurface data. “This collaboration brings SLB’s digital and subsurface expertise together with operator knowledge to help develop technologies for reservoir engineering and geoscience. Chevron adds valuable experience and perspectives that will help strengthen how we address complex subsurface workflows and field development decisions,” said Rakesh Jaggi, president of SLB’s digital business. Subject matter experts from Chevron and TotalEnergies will work within SLB technology centers, bringing operator experience directly into technology development and shortening feedback loops between product development teams and operators.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543497-fe.text: Forum Energy Technologies (FET) has appointed Amariko Co., Ltd. as its local representative for the Dynacon product family in Japan. Under the partnership, Amariko will provide business development, technical and administrative support to Dynacon customers throughout Japan. FET’s Dynacon family specializes in the custom design and manufacture of winches and launch and recovery systems (LARS). Dynacon LARS can be configured to meet a range of ROV launch and recovery specifications for customers. Headquartered in Yokohama, Amariko is a specialist distributor and service provider in marine and ocean-monitoring technologies. Amariko will combine its expertise and collaborate with FET to support customers across Japan.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/100_oil_exe.text: More than 100 oil and gas firm executives revealed where they expect the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil price to be at various points in the future in the third quarter Dallas Fed Energy Survey, which was released recently. The survey asked participants what they expect WTI prices to be in six months, one year, two years, and five years. Executives from 106 oil and gas firms answered this question and gave a mean response of $88 per barrel for the six month mark, $82 per barrel for the year mark, $79 per barrel for the two year mark, and $82 per barrel for the five year mark, the survey showed. Executives from 120 oil and gas firms answered this question in the second quarter Dallas Fed Energy Survey and gave a mean response of $68 per barrel for the six month and year marks, $72 per barrel for the two year mark, and $77 per barrel for the five year mark, that survey showed. In the first quarter Dallas Fed Energy Survey, executives from 116 oil and gas firms answered the question and gave a mean response of $78 per barrel for the six month mark, $73 per barrel for the year and two year marks, and $79 per barrel for the five year mark, that survey showed. The third quarter 2026 Dallas Fed Energy Survey also asked participants what they expect the WTI crude oil price to be at the end of the year. Executives from 125 oil and gas firms answered this question and gave an average response of $88.38 per barrel, the survey outlined. The low forecast was $70 per barrel, the high forecast was $126.00 per barrel, and the average daily spot price during the survey was $98.70 per barrel, the survey pointed out. The second quarter 2026 survey also asked participants what they expect the WTI crude oil price to be at the end of the year. Executives from 124 oil and gas firms answered this question and gave an average response of $80.55 per barrel, that survey highlighted. The low forecast in this survey was $60 per barrel, the high forecast was $150.00 per barrel, and the average daily spot price during that survey was $87.27 per barrel, the survey revealed. In the first quarter Dallas Fed Energy Survey, executives from 131 oil and gas firms answered this question and gave an average response of $74.04 per barrel, that survey highlighted. The low forecast was $50 per barrel, the high forecast was $135.00 per barrel, and the average daily spot price during the survey was $94.65 per barrel, the first quarter survey pointed out.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A substituição de isotanks por flexitanks vem ganhando espaço no transporte internacional de líquidos a granel , especialmente entre empresas dos setores químico, alimentício e do agronegócio . Segundo a DHL , a mudança é impulsionada pela combinação entre exigências de sustentabilidade, auditorias internacionais e pressão de investidores por métricas de consumo de recursos e geração de resíduos . Os flexitanks são equipamentos de polipropileno instalados dentro de contêineres convencionais. Em comparação com os modelos tradicionais, a solução permite eliminar a etapa de higienização do equipamento após a descarga, processo que demanda água tratada e pode gerar efluentes industriais de difícil gerenciamento. De acordo com Eric Brenner, CEO da DHL Global Forwarding no Brasil, questões ambientais relacionadas aos ativos logísticos passaram a integrar as decisões estratégicas das empresas. “A discussão sobre sustentabilidade na cadeia de suprimentos subiu para o C-level. O consumo de água na higienização de um ativo ou o risco de contaminação cruzada são tratados como fatores de risco financeiro e de imagem”, afirma. Além da redução do consumo de recursos, a adoção dos flexitanks está relacionada à busca por maior segurança sanitária e rastreabilidade, principalmente em mercados regulados, como a América do Norte. Em determinadas operações, os embarcadores optam por equipamentos de primeiro uso a cada envio, reduzindo o risco de contaminação cruzada de produtos. A mudança também envolve a integração de processos logísticos. A DHL passou a acompanhar etapas que incluem a produção dos flexitanks e o rastreamento individual dos equipamentos por lote e número de série durante o transporte internacional. A estratégia busca ampliar o controle sobre as cargas e atender às exigências de compliance dos embarcadores. Com isso, critérios relacionados ao consumo de recursos naturais e à segurança operacional passam a complementar o custo do frete na avaliação das alternativas de transporte. Para a DHL, o movimento indica uma mudança na forma como a eficiência logística é avaliada no comércio exterior, incorporando aspectos ambientais e de rastreabilidade à tomada de decisão.

A FedEx concluiu a venda de sua subsidiária FedEx Supply Chain para o CMA CGM Group . A transação, anunciada em julho deste ano, foi realizada por US$ 1,4 bilhão na última quinta-feira (01/10). O braço de logística contratual com foco em cadeia de suprimentos representava menos de 2% da receita anual consolidada da FedEx, que agora concentra seus esforços no transporte de cargas e entrega de encomendas. Conforme o acordo entre as empresas, a CMA CGM se tornará a transportadora marítima preferencial para a FedEx ao longo de múltiplos anos. Com a aquisição, a CEVA Logistics, braço logístico do CMA CGM , praticamente triplicará sua operação na região . A empresa incorporará os ativos da FedEx Supply Chain e cerca de 10 mil colaboradores, passando a operar aproximadamente 150 armazéns. Somadas às estruturas já existentes, as operações da CEVA na América do Norte alcançarão mais de 240 unidades e um quadro de aproximadamente 20 mil funcionários.

A Penske Logistics Brasil registrou turnover médio mensal de 2% no primeiro semestre de 2026, abaixo dos cerca de 4% observados no setor no mesmo período, segundo dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged), do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego. Com cerca de 1.500 colaboradores, a empresa vem apostando na capacitação e na promoção interna para reduzir a rotatividade e atender à demanda por profissionais em funções operacionais e de maior exigência técnica. A estratégia ganha relevância em um cenário de disputa por mão de obra impulsionada pelo crescimento do comércio eletrônico e pela concentração de centros de distribuição em polos logísticos, como Cajamar (SP), onde a Penske está presente há mais de 15 anos. Segundo estudo da Confederação Nacional do Transporte (CNT), a taxa de rotatividade no setor apresenta trajetória crescente desde 2020 e chegou a 48,4% em 2025, próxima à média de 53,7% do mercado de trabalho celetista. De acordo com o levantamento da CNT, algumas funções operacionais apresentam índices ainda mais elevados. O turnover entre auxiliares de logística chegou a 108,9% em 2025, enquanto ajudantes de motorista registraram 66,1% e motoristas de caminhão, 56,6%. No mesmo ano, o segmento de transporte, armazenagem e correio teve alta de 3,36% no volume de empregos, segundo dados do Departamento Intersindical de Estatística e Estudos Socioeconômicos (DIEESE), acima do crescimento de 2,71% do mercado formal brasileiro. Na Penske, uma das iniciativas para suprir a demanda por profissionais qualificados é o programa interno "Dirigindo para o Futuro", voltado à formação de operadores de empilhadeira a partir da capacitação de auxiliares e conferentes. A iniciativa formou 17 profissionais em 2025 e outros 22 em 2026. Entre 2025 e agosto deste ano, a companhia contabilizou ainda 257 promoções em posições operacionais e 47 progressões para cargos de liderança. "A estabilidade das equipes tem impacto direto na eficiência e na segurança das operações dos nossos clientes. Em um mercado com alta rotatividade, priorizar a promoção interna e capacitar profissionais que já conhecem a cultura da empresa reduz os prazos de recrutamento e garante a continuidade dos níveis de serviço", afirma Andrea Molina, diretora de Recursos Humanos da Penske Logistics Brasil. A estratégia de desenvolvimento interno aparece na trajetória de Peterson Evangelista, que ingressou na companhia em 2017 como conferente na unidade paulista. Depois de participar de treinamentos internos, ele passou por quatro promoções, atuando como operador de empilhadeira, líder de turno e analista, até chegar ao cargo de líder de operações.

A Brasil Cold Storage (BCS) recebeu autorização da Receita Federal para operar como Recinto Especial para Despacho Aduaneiro de Exportação (Redex) em São Vicente (SP) , em uma área de quase 20.000 m² . O reconhecimento foi publicado no Diário Oficial da União em 5 de outubro, e se refere ao estabelecimento localizado na Rodovia Padre Manoel da Nóbrega , no município litorâneo de São Paulo. A unidade de São Vicente é a estrutura mais recente da BCS e opera com mercadorias conteinerizáveis de exportação e cabotagem. Com a nova habilitação, a empresa passa a contar com dois terminais Redex na Baixada Santista. A companhia já contava com um Redex próprio em Cubatão, implantado em 2024. A área total da estrutura de São Vicente é de mais de 70 mil m², sendo mais de 10 mil m² de armazém. O local apresenta capacidade estática superior a 2.200 TEUs, 200 tomadas para contêineres refrigerados e três balanças rodoviárias. A unidade também dispõe de estrutura para estufagem e pré-stacking de contêineres e monitoramento por mais de 200 câmeras. A operação integra um complexo voltado a diferentes tipos de cargas e serviços. Entre as mercadorias listadas pela BCS estão açúcar, algodão, líquidos, grãos, congelados, couro, produtos do setor automotivo e cerâmica. A unidade está situada no Parque Industrial Imigrantes, próxima ao Porto de Santos. Segundo a empresa, a proximidade portuária e os acessos rodoviários fazem parte da estratégia de posicionamento de seus terminais na Baixada Santista. Com mais de 100 mil m² de operações entre terminais e armazéns, a BCS conta mais de 400 funcionários e mais de 70 clientes ativos.

https://gcaptain.com/a-dozen-seafarers-i.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, August 3, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer Twelve seafarers were injured after a Panama-flagged oil tanker was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to India’s Ministry of External Affairs, marking one of the most serious crew casualty incidents in the latest wave of attacks on commercial shipping. The vessel was identified as the On Peace (IMO 9893204), an Aframax tanker carrying a crew of 19, including 17 Indian nationals. Eleven of the 12 injured crew members are Indian. The injured seafarers were evacuated with assistance from Omani authorities and taken to Khasab for medical treatment, India’s foreign ministry said Tuesday. “The continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a cause of deep concern for India,” the ministry said, calling for an immediate end to attacks targeting commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure. The incident appears to be connected to an attack reported Monday by United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, although the link has not been formally confirmed.

https://gcaptain.com/imo-chief-decries-r.text: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez opens the IMO Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) 84th Session at IMO Headquarters in London, April 27, 2026. Photo courtesy IMO Five seafarers were killed during the rescue of a hijacked ship off Somalia last week, prompting International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez to issue yet another statement mourning merchant mariners killed amid piracy, conflict and attacks on commercial shipping. “It is troubling to have to make these statements so often, and even more difficult to convey in words how distressing it is continuously hear that seafarers are losing their lives simply for doing their jobs,” Dominguez said. The five crew members were reportedly killed September 29 during the rescue of the HONOUR 25 in Somali waters. Several others were seriously injured, according to the IMO. The statement was only the latest in a series from Dominguez this year as seafarers have been killed, injured, stranded or taken captive across the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Black Sea and waters off Somalia. His message has been consistent: seafarers are civilians, they are doing their jobs, and they should not be the ones paying for conflicts beyond their control.

https://gcaptain.com/gulf-oil-flows-rise.text: File Photo: Oil tanker Al Shaffiah sails at the sea near the Omani coast, as seen from Musandam, Oman, June 26, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer LONDON, Oct 6 – Gulf oil flows excluding Iran surged to over 81% of pre- war levels in September, data showed, led by a recovery in Saudi exports despite attacks on the kingdom’s oil infrastructure and escalating Iranian attacks on regional shipping, while Iranian exports fell to zero due to a US blockade. The blockade has all but choked off Iranian exports, while other Gulf producers have adapted to attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping by relying on so-called dark transits — switching off tankers’ tracking systems to evade detection — to protect the oil flows that underpin their economies. Flows of crude, condensate and refined fuels including LPG averaged 19.2 million barrels per day (bpd) from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Iraq and the UAE, Vortexa data showed, compared with an average of about 23.6 million bpd in the year that preceded the outbreak of the Iran war on February 28. Crude and condensate flows recovered to 91% of their pre-war levels of 16.3 million bpd, Vortexa data showed. But exports of refined fuels, including LPG, remain at 60% of their pre-war levels of 7.3 million bpd. The decline in fuel exports has exacerbated global shortages of diesel and jet fuel, contributing to record or near-record prices in several markets. The Middle East is a key supplier of such fuels, making regional disruptions particularly significant for global consumers.

https://petronoticias.com.br/seatrium-fa.text: A Seatrium foi contratada pela Karpowership para realizar o nono projeto de conversão de uma unidade flutuante de armazenamento e regaseificação (FSRU).
