O novo contrato ocorre após a entrega de sete FSRUs desde 2018 e a conversão em andamento do LNGT Karadeniz, oitavo projeto de FSRU da parceria. O projeto LNGT Akdeniz envolve a conversão de um navio transportador de GNL em uma FSRU, com início dos trabalhos previsto para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. O escopo da Seatrium inclui engenharia, conversão, integração, instalação e comissionamento dos equipamentos de regaseificação e sistemas associados. Após a conclusão, a unidade ampliará a capacidade de importação e regaseificação de GNL em seu mercado-alvo, contribuindo para a segurança energética e para o fornecimento confiável de uma fonte de energia mais limpa. “ A entrega bem-sucedida do LNGT Türkiye e a contratação do LNGT Akdeniz são marcos importantes no crescimento contínuo dos negócios de GNL para geração de energia da Karpowership. Juntas, essas FSRUs fortalecem nossa capacidade de oferecer soluções energéticas confiáveis e flexíveis a mercados onde a segurança energética é fundamental ”, afirmou o diretor de Operações Técnicas da Karpowership, Gokhan Kocak . Após a contratação do LNGT Karadeniz, o LNGT Akdeniz é o segundo projeto a ser concretizado no âmbito da carta de intenções (LOI) anunciada anteriormente entre as duas empresas. Além de três conversões de FSRUs, o acordo também previa a possível integração de até seis powerships de nova geração, criando oportunidades para que as duas companhias atendam às necessidades energéticas globais em evolução por meio de soluções integradas de energia flutuante. “ A contratação do LNGT Akdeniz, nosso nono projeto de FSRU com a Karpowership e a segunda unidade da nova geração de FSRUs da companhia, demonstra a força dessa colaboração e reforça ainda mais a posição da Seatrium como líder global em soluções de infraestrutura flutuante de GNL ”, disse Alvin Gan , vice-presidente executivo de Reparos e Modernizações da Seatrium. “ Com capacidade de regaseificação de até 600 milhões de pés cúbicos por dia (MMscfd), o LNGT Akdeniz desempenhará um papel importante no fornecimento confiável e flexível de energia. Agradecemos à Karpowership pela confiança contínua na Seatrium e esperamos ampliar essa parceria bem-sucedida para desenvolver soluções energéticas inovadoras para o futuro ”, acrescentou. © 2026 Petronotícias. As autoridades responsáveis divulgaram uma nota dizendo que “ O material apresenta baixa atividade, e o Ac-225 é emissor de radiação alfa, que possui pequeno poder de penetração. Considerando a quantidade envolvida e as características do radionuclídeo, a ocorrência representa baixo risco radiológico para a população. Ainda assim, por precaução, caso o material seja encontrado, não abra, recomenda-se que não manipule nem ingira seu conteúdo. ” A ANSN alertou para que caso o material fosse encontrado, não fosse aberto, manipulado ou ingerido, devendo as autoridades serem imediatamente comunicadas pelos telefones: (21) 99304-9453 ou (21) 99299-2620. https://petronoticias.com.br/propoe-meta.text: O Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME) apresentou nesta semana uma proposta para redução de 1% das emissões no próximo ano, a ser alcançada por meio da participação do biometano no consumo de gás natural. O tema entrou em consulta pública que ficará aberta por 30 dias no portal do ministério . A proposta estabelece ainda percentuais indicativos da presença do biometano para os anos seguintes: 3% em 2028, 4% em 2029 e 5% em 2030. Para 2027, a meta de 1% corresponde à utilização de 363,2 milhões de metros cúbicos de biometano ao longo do ano, ou aproximadamente 995,2 mil metros cúbicos por dia. O volume equivale a 3.632.492 Certificados de Garantia de Origem de Biometano (CGOBs). A minuta submetida à participação social também define os valores de intensidade de carbono que serão considerados no cálculo da meta. Para o gás natural veicular (GNV), o parâmetro proposto é de 76,85 gCO₂eq/MJ. Para o gás natural utilizado em combustão estacionária, o valor é de 73,52 gCO₂eq/MJ, enquanto o biometano apresenta intensidade de carbono de 9,36 gCO₂eq/MJ. A definição das metas está prevista na Lei nº 14.993/2024, que criou o Programa Nacional de Descarbonização do Produtor e Importador de Gás Natural e de Incentivo ao Biometano. O mecanismo estabelece metas anuais de redução de emissões de GEE no mercado de gás natural, vinculando seu cumprimento à participação do biometano e ao uso dos CGOBs. Em 2026, a meta de redução estabelecida foi de 0,5%. Com a proposta apresentada pelo MME, o percentual seria elevado para 1% em 2027, dando continuidade à trajetória de aumento gradual da participação do biometano como instrumento de descarbonização do mercado de gás natural. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/sec.text: A Greek-flagged LNG carrier controlled by the Angelicoussis Shipping Group was struck by an unidentified projectile while leaving the Strait of Hormuz, in the latest incident to hit commercial shipping along one of the world’s most important energy routes. The Maran Gas Mystras, operated by Maran Gas Maritime, was hit around the waterline on Sunday, according to initial reports from Greece. Smoke was subsequently seen coming from the vessel, although the ship remained operational and continued under its own power. Maran Gas later said the vessel and its crew were safe, adding that the LNG carrier was fully operational and continuing its voyage normally. No damage affecting its operation has been reported and there has been no report of pollution. As of Monday morning, the incident had not appeared on the International Maritime Organisation’s (IMO) list of confirmed Middle East incidents, which was last updated on October 5. The IMO list recorded 93 confirmed incidents in the region, including the October 4 strike on the Lipsi, managed by George Prokopiou’s Dynacom, but did not yet list the Maran Gas Mystras. The latest incident comes only a day after the Dynacom tanker Lipsi, delivered just six weeks earlier, was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. That attack damaged the vessel’s engine room, leaving it disabled and adrift, although its crew was reported safe and no pollution was recorded. UK Maritime Trade Operations issued a warning following the incident.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Shipowners aren't the only ones making a fortune from million-dollar day rates for Hormuz transits. Far from being coerced or tricked into sailing into harm's way, seafarers are reportedly able to earn a small fortune if they agree to brave the short but dangerous run through the strait. According to the Financial Times, tanker captains are making base salaries of up to $100,000 per month plus a $50,000 per-trip bonus aboard ships that make the Hormuz run. The rest of the crew can make four to six times their normal salaries - an incentive which does not ordinarily figure into the public discourse on seafarer rights and safety. The Wall Street Journal puts the cost of a single Strait of Hormuz "shuttle" run at $40 million per trip. Even after paying sky-high war risk insurance premia, this leaves abundant margins to compensate the crew and the owner. The Journal found one Chinese crewing agency that is offering a $25,000 per-trip bonus for oilers and ordinary seamen. The risks to crewmembers are real, but rarely fatal. Iran has yet to sink a tanker during the Hormuz crisis. Right now, there are about 30-40 vessels that regularly transit the waterway. Most do not get hit, and most hits do not injure crewmembers or disable the vessel. A recent uptick in serious incidents may change the calculus, but for now, the majority of vessel transits pass unhindered - though not all. On Monday or Tuesday, an LR2 was hit off the Omani coast during an outbound transit, injuring 12 seafarers and prompting a medevac. The hazard pay is far less than the owners' share, but it is far more than the average salaries in seafarer-supplying regions. “Given the millions being made at the moment, [bonuses are] absolutely nothing to the shipowners,” E.A. Gibson consulting director Richard Matthews told the WSJ.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: South Korean shipbuilding group HD Hyundai is reporting the delivery of its first container vessel using the company’s newly developed "Lashing-Free" system that eliminates the need for workers to manually secure containers on board. It highlights benefits of increased capacity and ease of handling while also reporting that the system will be able to handle heavy weather and provide other benefits to the ships. The system was installed on a new containership built for CMA CGM, which underwent sea trials in September. The ship has a capacity of 13,000 TEU while using HD Hyundai’s hybrid-type Lashing-Free Technology. The ship is methanol-fueled and otherwise appears to use a conventional layout for the placement of containers above deck. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries reports it independently developed and validated all key components of the Lashing-Free technology. HD Hyundai Samho was responsible for the detailed design and construction of the vessel incorporating the system. The vessel extends the cell guides, which support containers stacked vertically in alignment inside the cargo hold, above deck. HD Hyundai says that it also incorporates technologies designed to prevent cargo loss and maximize logistics efficiency. The technology the shipbuilder says is expected to play a key role in accelerating automation and unmanned operations across the broader logistics network connecting land and sea, including container terminals. The Lashing-Free containership removes the need for manual container lashing, which traditionally is carried out by workers using lashing equipment on large container vessels. Improperly attached containers and failures of the locking system have often been cited as a concern and one of the potential contributors to stack collapse or overboard containers. The conventional large hatch covers used on container vessels currently would obstruct the extended cell guides, preventing them from reaching above deck. To overcome this structural limitation, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries developed a standardized “portable bench" that can be installed between the cell guides. The portable bench is built to the same dimensions as a 40-foot container, allowing it to be handled using the same port cranes used to load and unload containers.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/q.text: The harbor master and local emergency services are reporting that a quick, coordinated action on Monday evening prevented a Spanish-flagged offshore support vessel from sinking at the dock in Eemshaven in the Netherlands. The vessel Nautilus reported that it was taking on water as it was returning to the Dutch port around 18:30 on October 5. The local emergency service, Veiligheidsregio Groningen, scaled the incident to a Level 1 emergency, reporting the vessel was clearly sinking with the forward section sitting lower in the water. It believed the ship was in danger of going under at its dock. The police and fire departments responded, with the harbor master organizing a rescue. Grootste gevaar voorbij: 'Gat is gedicht, het schip komt omhoog' (update) https://t.co/Zw65UVYJP4 Built in 2001, the Nautilus is a 73-meter (239-foot) OSV used to support the offshore wind energy industry. Dutch broadcaster RTV Nord quoted the local authorities saying the water was entering the ship through the engine room. They believed it was a leak from a valve. It did not specify how much water had entered the ship or the rate of flooding. However, the ship was ordered evacuated, and two crewmembers were checked by an ambulance for minor injuries. The Dutch national waterways authority responded, placing an oil containment barrier around the vessel as a precaution in case it sank at the pier. Within less than an hour after the first report, a follow-up said an emergency team from a private salvage company was aboard the vessel. In addition, two tugs were positioned alongside to further secure the vessel.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Local media in North Carolina are reporting that concerns about potential so-called “forever chemicals” are causing the North Carolina State Ports Authority to delay consideration of a long-planned dredging project for the Port of Wilmington and its channel. WilmingtonBiz first reported that the Ports Authority had sent a letter to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers asking that consideration of the project be suspended for further consideration. Located on the U.S. Southeast Coast, Wilmington highlights that it is one of the few regional ports with readily available berth and storage areas for containers and general cargo. It had a strong year in FY26, having “moved a total of 4.4 million short tons of bulk and breakbulk cargo, finishing the year consistent with budget expectations and slightly ahead of last year’s performance,” the authority reported in July. Containers are currently a modest part of the port’s overall operation, with a capacity of 600,000 TEU, but it is stronger in reefer containers, especially moving tropical fruit. It has seven container cranes and a total of nine berths and also handles Ro-Ro operations. The Port of Wilmington sits 26 miles inland, reached by transiting the Cape Fear River. It maintains a 42-foot channel, but advocates have long called for deepening it to 47 feet. The reports point out that neighboring and competing ports such as Norfolk, Charleston, and Savannah have deepened their channels to handle larger vessels. The US Army Corps of Engineers has been studying the project for the Port of Wilmington and in June released its environmental impact statement. News reports said it acknowledged contaminants in the river upstream from the port but said it was unclear if there was silt containing chemicals in the harbor or downstream that would be dangerous from the dredging. It left it to the state to determine those concerns. The Corps concluded dredging would not impact drinking water contaminant concentrations. Environmentalists have long argued against the project, saying it would release harmful chemicals. Business North Carolina also writes that the state’s governor, Josh Stein, is “not keen on the project.” One concern could be the estimated $1.4 billion cost, of which the state would pay $344 million, Business North Carolina reports. It says that there were calls to get the federal government to pay up to 75 percent of the cost.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: The administration of French President Emmanuel Macron is putting new emphasis on France's nuclear deterrent, and specifically on its nuclear ballistic missile submarine fleet. In March, Macron used a launch ceremony at the L'Île Longue submarine base to announce that France would expand its arsenal and cooperate with other European countries on a broader nuclear deterrence system. On Tuesday, he made an unannounced trip to a frigate off Brittany for the first seagoing test-launch of an M51.3 ballistic missile - and he reiterated that message. "To be free, one must be feared. And to be feared, one must be powerful," Macron said in a ship-wide PA address to the crew. "Our nuclear deterrence protects us and will continue to protect us. Long live the Republic, and long live France." The launch was a post-drydocking test shot for Le Vigilant, one of France's four Le Triomphant-class ballistic missile submarines, as well as the first sub-launched test of the third variant of France's M51 sub-launched ballistic missile. Macron's attendance was not expected at the routine test, according to Le Monde, but the launch provided a powerful and somber visual to accompany his message: that France can respond to nuclear threats. The rationale for Macron's newly-serious focus on nuclear arms can be found in Russia's increasingly aggressive stance towards NATO. Last month, the Russian government sent a diplomatic note to NATO (later shared with Reuters) that threatened "Russian strikes against decision-making centers" in Europe at the very start of any conflict. Exercises near the Baltic Sea exclave of Kaliningrad are of particular concern, Moscow suggested. "Russia will be ready to use the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, in order to defend its territory should NATO countries undertake any attempt aimed at isolating the Kaliningrad Region from the ?rest of the country," the Kremlin warned in the note. France has been upgrading its ballistic missile inventory to account for increasingly capable air defense technology. U.S. and Israeli systems managed a 90-percent interception rate against Iranian ballistic missiles in 2024, and sustained a high success rate throughout the more recent Mideast conflict from March 2026 onwards. According to Sidharth Kaushal of the Royal United Services Institute, Russia's investments in similar air defense systems could render the French deterrent - reliant upon the nuclear missiles fielded by its subs and strike fighters - somewhat less effective. ArianeGroup is developing a fourth generation variant of the missile with "enhanced range, precision and penetration capabilities" to counteract these developments.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: The Federal Maritime Commission filed a Show Cause order at the end of last week against the Chinese-flagged carrier COSCO, which threatens the potential for "substantial" civil penalties for delaying for more than seven months the payment of a small award. The Commission notes that the action of the carrier “raises questions about whether these potential violations of statutes were knowing and willful,” while hinting at a concern that a failure to act undermines the authority of the Commission. The action stems from what appears to be a minor dispute related to demurrage and detention invoices sent in 2025 to a company called Agribusiness Holdings. While the award was for a relatively small amount, $24,328.80 in reparations plus interest, the FMC states COSCO did not make payment despite repeated contacts from the complainant and eventually from the FMC itself. Notice of the award was served requiring payment by January 20, 2026, after the FMC found that COSCO had failed to properly issue invoices to the complainant for the D&D fees. The carrier failed to make payment for a total of 223 days. The FMC highlights that, under the regulations, a common carrier such as COSCO may not retaliate or resort to any other unfair action because a shipper took action, including filing a complaint. The FMC is also empowered to impose civil penalties for violating its order. At issue, and highlighted in the Show Cause notice , are broader issues about the authority and powers of the FMC. It notes that a U.S. Court of Appeals recently recognized in another matter that the FMC has a strong interest in preserving the integrity of its procedures. The court recognized that a “respondent’s disregard of binding FMC orders can undermine its authority.” Under the statutes, the FMC is currently empowered to impose inflation-adjusted penalties of $14,988 with each day considered a separate violation. If the violation is found to be “willful and knowing,” the penalty jumps to $74,943, and again each day is a separate violation. COSCO’s violation could, under those rules, result in civil penalties of between $3.345 million and $16.725 million.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Operations at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea loading terminals have rebounded more swiftly than expected, according to a new analysis from Kpler. The consultancy found that with the East-West Pipeline restored to service, loadings from the two main Aramco terminals on the Red Sea came in at about 45 million barrels in total from September 17 through October 4 - an average of about 2.5 million barrels per day over the period. Tstrong showing reflects Aramco's ability to rapidly circumvent or repair damaged pumping stations on the pipeline route. Three stations were hit in a suspected Iraqi militia strike on September 11, temporarily disabling the line. But the line was reactivated in less than a week, and flows are already back up to 5.8 million barrels per day, Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an audience at the Energy Intelligence Forum, per Kpler Mideast chief Amena Bakr. This volume approaches the 7 million bpd average that Aramco sustained in the months prior to the attack, and it would be sufficient to supply Saudi Red Sea refineries and export terminals alike. The rebound at Yanbu is key to Saudi Arabia's success in restoring its oil trade, despite the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. According to Standard Chartered, Saudi oil exports hit nearly 7 million barrels per day in September, up from 2.5 million bpd the month before. In addition to the volume shipped through the pipeline, Aramco substantially increased tanker loadings at its core Arabian Gulf terminals, dispatching more crude through the strait despite security concerns. Iran has substantially accelerated its campaign of attacks on energy shipping in the strait, and has hit 12 tankers and gas carriers in the last seven days alone. Still, despite the deteriorating security environment, tanker operators have been moving about 10-14 million bpd of petroleum out of the Strait of Hormuz alone in recent days, Vitol CEO Russell Hardy said at the EI Forum on Tuesday. That supply is critical for pricing, he said. "Without it, you do have that $200 per barrel scenario," he told Reuters.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543528-yi.text: Yinson Production has priced $1.458 billion of senior secured notes to refinance debt linked to its Agogo floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) unit operating offshore Angola, in what the company said was the largest FPSO project bond to date. The notes were issued by Yinson Azalea Production, which owns the Agogo FPSO, and have a scheduled maturity of 13.3 years. Priced at 98.164% of their principal amount, the notes carry a fixed annual coupon of 6.517%, payable semi-annually. Settlement is expected on October 21, 2026. Proceeds will primarily be used to refinance existing debt related to the FPSO, as well as fund required reserve accounts, cover transaction costs and make equity distributions from excess proceeds. The Agogo is leased to Azule Energy Angola and operates at Block 15/06 offshore Angola under a 15-year firm bareboat charter, with extension options of up to five years. “We are very pleased with the strong support from institutional investors for this offering, which is our third FPSO project bond in three years and sets a new benchmark as the largest FPSO project bond to date. It also represents an important milestone for the asset class as a whole, as this is the first FPSO project bond outside Brazil, broadening and diversifying the investable universe for investors seeking exposure to infrastructure assets backed by highly visible cash flows and strong counterparties,” said Markus Wenker, Yinson Production Chief Financial Officer.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543521-co.text: The cost of Aker BP's major ongoing oil and gas development projects, Yggdrasil and Valhall-Fenris, has risen by 9.8% and 23%, respectively, from nominal estimates a year ago, data from the government's fiscal budget showed on Wednesday. The increase was in line with projections made by Aker BP in July, a company spokesperson said. The Yggdrasil project, the largest project under development off Norway since 2019, is now expected to cost 195 billion Norwegian crowns ($20.41 billion) up from a nominal estimate of 177.6 billion crowns one year ago. The project to build a new processing platform for Aker BP's Valhall field, combined with the development of the nearby Fenris gas discovery, is now expected to cost 93.4 billion crowns, up from a previous estimate of 75.9 billion crowns. Yggdrasil and Valhall-Fenris were originally projected to cost 120.8 billion crowns and 52.9 billion crowns, respectively, when they were approved by the government in 2023. Aker BP flagged a cost rise in July citing updated estimates for construction of offshore installations and extra resources needed to meet the 2027 completion deadline.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543525-ca.text: Danish contractor Cadeler has completed installation of all 76 wind turbines at the 1.2 GW Baltic Power project, Poland's first offshore wind farm, using its jack-up vessels Wind Osprey and Wind Mover. The completion of the turbine campaign moves Baltic Power into the final stages of preparation for full commissioning and operation after the project delivered first power to Poland's national grid in July 2026. Cadeler installed 76 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines at the Baltic Sea project. Each turbine has a total height of more than 260 meters and a swept area exceeding 43,700 square meters. Baltic Power is a joint venture between Polish energy group ORLEN and Canadian developer Northland Power. “We are pleased to have completed the installation of all 76 turbines at Baltic Power – Poland’s first offshore wind farm. This is an important milestone for the project and for the development of offshore wind in Poland. Projects of this scale require highly capable vessels, experienced teams and close collaboration across the project. “We are proud to have supported our client in reaching this milestone and look forward to building on our partnerships in Poland as the country's offshore wind industry continues to develop,” said Mikkel Gleerup, Cadeler’s CEO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543520-ve.text: Verlume has completed hyperbaric testing of the enclosure for its Orah subsea energy storage system, clearing a qualification milestone ahead of its planned deployment at the OranjeWind offshore wind farm in the Dutch North Sea. The testing was carried out at JFD's hyperbaric facility in Aberdeen and subjected the enclosure to a controlled pressure profile representative of its intended subsea operating environment. The 10-tonne enclosure, measuring 7.2 meters long, 2.4 meters wide and 2.4 meters high, was the largest vessel tested at JFD's hyperbaric center to date. Testing covered pressure and depth qualification, enclosure integrity and functional performance under pressure. It demonstrated the enclosure's ability to withstand external loads associated with its intended operating depth and maintain its pressure boundary under representative subsea conditions. Orah is a 500-kWh modular subsea energy storage system designed to provide autonomous grid support for offshore wind farms. The system uses Verlume's Axonn power management platform to manage power generation, storage and demand. The complete Orah system will weigh 85 tonnes and is planned for deployment at the OranjeWind offshore wind farm being developed by RWE and TotalEnergies.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543527-dn.text: Buchan Offshore Wind has secured DNV Basic Design Certification for the BW Ideol-designed concrete Damping Pool floating foundation planned for its nearly 1 GW project off Scotland, marking a further engineering milestone ahead of commercial-scale development. The certification provides independent validation of the project-specific foundation design selected for Buchan, which is being developed around 75 km northeast of Fraserburgh in the North Sea. “Achieving DNV Basic Design Certification is a significant milestone for the Buchan project, reflecting the expertise, commitment and hard work of the team and is an important step towards the industrialisation of floating offshore wind in Scotland,” Clare Lavelle, Buchan Offshore Wind Project Director. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543523-ni.text: Nigeria has launched its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 blocks spanning onshore, shallow-water and deepwater areas as the country seeks new investment and higher production. Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) Chief Executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan announced the round following approval from President Bola Tinubu, with Nigerian and international investors eligible to compete for the acreage. “The round offers 40 blocks across land, shallow water and deep water terrains. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543516-ch.text: Chevron and the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS) have signed an agreement covering at least $88 million of investment in natural gas and crude oil exploration and production in the Lotus offshore area in the Mediterranean Sea. Chevron currently invests in six offshore exploration areas in Egypt's Mediterranean waters - Nargis, North Dabaa, Lotus, Northwest Atoll, North Simian and North Cleopatra, where it participates alongside Shell. Its exploration activities have included the Nargis gas discovery, while drilling of the Velox well in the North Cleopatra offshore area more recently showed indications of crude oil.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543507-su.text: Sumitomo Corporation Global Metals Co., Ltd. (SCGM) and TFI Marine Limited have formed a partnership to introduce innovation into mooring solutions for floating offshore wind and offshore energy projects. The partnership enables and accelerates the deployment of floating offshore wind in Japan and globally, contributing to decarbonization and energy security. Mooring systems are among the principal cost and risk drivers in floating offshore wind. As projects move into deeper water and towards commercial scale, developers need mooring solutions that reduce loads, extend component life and lower cost without introducing new project risk. Both companies are working together to bring the SeaSpring, a load and fatigue reduction component, to projects in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, and to support the wider adoption of next generation mooring solutions internationally. TFI Marine has developed the SeaSpring, a load and fatigue reduction component delivering next generation mooring solutions, together with the modeling and design expertise to engineer them. SeaSpring is incorporated into the mooring line to reduce peak loads and improve fatigue performance, enabling the use of smaller mooring chain and synthetic fiber rope, anchors and components. This reduces installation time and vessel requirements. The impact is a reduction in project CAPEX and OPEX, directly reducing the levelized cost of energy. The SeaSpring has achieved DNV and ClassNK certification. Sumitomo Corporation Global Metals serves as the core entity responsible for the global execution of the Group's steel-related businesses. Equipment and materials for offshore wind facilities is a growth area for the company's Plate & Construction Steel Products business, and SCGM works with companies across the industry to ensure that Japan has access offshore energy technology. In this partnership, SCGM, as a leading Japanese corporation, delivers supply chain expertise and resilience, established relationships across the energy sector, and the industrial network that enables the establishment of Japanese manufacture and component supply globally. The two companies will jointly engage project developers, EPCI contractors and all floating offshore wind stakeholders to accelerate early adoption of innovative mooring solutions. The companies have also agreed to explore the manufacture of SeaSpring components in Japan, supporting local supply chain development and local content for Japanese floating offshore wind projects.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543509-oi.text: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of Middle East crude. The offshore areas in the Gulf in the storm's path produce 15% of US crude oil and 5% of the country's natural gas. KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said the storm was an "unwelcome complication for crude, raising the prospect of production and refining disruptions at a time when the market already has enough supply-side headaches". The storm could affect six refineries. Refineries in US Gulf states account for about 50% of the national capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).

https://safety4sea.com/drone-strikes-put.text: Commercial shipping in the Black Sea is facing a widening security threat, with drone attacks increasingly reaching beyond the immediate approaches to Ukrainian and Russian ports and into established merchant shipping routes. R ecent incidents involving crude oil tankers and cargo vessels have highlighted the risks facing civilian crews, raising fresh concerns over seafarer safety, voyage planning and the continuity of trade through one of the world’s most important maritime regions. The latest incident involved the Liberian-flagged crude oil tanker Aframax Rio, which caught fire after being struck by a Ukrainian drone off Russia’s southern coast on the evening of 6 October. The vessel was near Sochi in Russia’s Krasnodar region while sailing from Novorossiysk to India. It was carrying a nearly full cargo of crude oil when an unmanned naval drone struck the tanker, triggering a major fire that spread to the vessel’s cargo. All 23 crew members aboard the Aframax Rio were Indian nationals and were safely rescued following the attack. The tanker continued to burn in the Black Sea, with the intensity of the blaze initially preventing emergency responders from approaching. Russia’s Transport Ministry later said firefighting operations began after the fire had subsided sufficiently for responders to reach the vessel.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-e.text: A scaffolding kickboard weighing 2.4 kg was accidentally dropped from a height of 6.5 metres to the main deck during installation work on a vessel in dry dock. A ccording to IMCA, a vessel in dry dock was undergoing installation activities, with a scaffolding team completing final adjustments to scaffolding erected around a new crane pedestal. During the final adjustments, a scaffolding kickboard weighing 2.4 kg was accidentally dropped from the upper platform. The kickboard fell approximately 6.5 metres to the main deck, creating a significant dropped-object hazard for personnel working in the area. The incident occurred while the scaffolding team was carrying out the final laydown and adjustment of materials, highlighting how routine activities can create serious risks when materials are not properly controlled. The scaffolders were using unsafe methods during the laydown process of materials. The work also took place alongside other simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) , but the interaction between the different activities had not been fully considered.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-mca-urges-ship.text: The UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) is urging shipowners, operators, ports and maritime service providers to strengthen their preparedness for GNSS disruption, warning that jamming, spoofing or signal loss could affect navigation, communications, vessel tracking and other critical systems. W ith maritime operations increasingly dependent on GPS and other satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services, the MCA says operators should not assume GNSS will always be available. Instead, vessels should be able to maintain safe operations using alternative navigation methods when satellite-derived information becomes unreliable or unavailable. The first step is to identify how heavily a vessel or operation depends on GNSS. GNSS inputs can feed a wide range of bridge systems, including ECDIS, AIS, radar, integrated bridge systems, autopilots, track-control systems, dynamic positioning and GMDSS equipment. The impact can also extend beyond the bridge to communications, timing systems, vessel tracking, port operations and logistics. The MCA therefore recommends reviewing system architecture and data flows to identify equipment that could be affected if GNSS-derived PNT is disrupted. GNSS loss should be treated as an operational risk rather than simply a technical problem. Ship operators should review existing risk assessments to determine what happens if positioning or timing information becomes unreliable.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-rightship-vett.text: RightShip has introduced Revision 4.0 of its Dry Bulk Vessel Vetting Baseline Criteria, effective 1 October 2026 , bringing a substantial revision of the framework used to support vetting recommendations for dry bulk and general cargo vessels. T his is more than a periodic update of individual thresholds. RightShip’s own Revision Log states that Version 4 has been extensively reformatted and rewritten , with the stated objective of providing clearer baseline criteria, review thresholds, acceptability expectations and closure requirements. Among the most important developments are a comprehensive revision of the Port State Control criteria, restructuring of incident assessment, expansion of Flag, Class and regulatory compliance requirements, stronger provisions on ownership transparency and sanctions, enhanced technical and operational requirements, and changes to RightShip Inspection and Management of Change requirements. The scope has also been expressly expanded to include general cargo vessels alongside dry bulk vessels. Against this background, SAFETY4SEA reviewed the new criteria and their Revision Log to identify what has changed and, more importantly, what those changes mean in practice for ship operators. The following assessment uses four levels of practical significance: Limited, Moderate, Significant and Major. The significance ratings are SAFETY4SEA’s assessment of the operational impact of each change and are not ratings assigned by RightShip.

https://gcaptain.com/qatar-brings-empty-.text: A man looks as the LNG tanker DUHAIL crosses through the Suez Canal April 1, 2008. REUTERS/Stringer/File Photo Oct 7, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Qatar has amassed a fleet of empty liquefied natural gas tankers in the Persian Gulf, a sign that one of the world’s biggest exporters of the fuel may be preparing to boost shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. At least 12 ballast LNG carriers owned or chartered by QatarEnergy are waiting in waters near the country, according to a Bloomberg News analysis of satellite images and ship-tracking data. Together, the vessels can hold about 1.1 million tons of LNG, or roughly 2% of the carrying capacity of the entire global tanker fleet. There’s no guarantee the vessels will sail through Hormuz once loaded, particularly as Iranian attacks on ships have intensified. A Greek-owned LNG carrier was hit by an unidentified object while sailing near the waterway, Athens News Agency reported on Tuesday, citing Greece’s shipping ministry. Still, the prospect of additional flows could help to temper global gas prices, which rallied to the highest level since late-2022 in Asia and Europe last month. LNG traffic through Hormuz rose in September to the highest level since the war began, but shipments remain about 75% below levels in February, before the US and Israel attacked Iran. The recent increase in flows has caught some buyers off guard. India, for example, has been forced to scale back some spot purchases to make room for the return of Qatari cargoes.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/hormuz-o.text: Twelve crew members were injured after an unknown projectile struck Panama-flagged oil tanker On Peace while it was passing through the Strait of Hormuz, India's foreign ministry said on Tuesday. Eleven of the 12 injured crew members are Indian nationals, it said, adding there was a crew of 19 onboard the Aframax-sized tanker. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ira.text: Iran has stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days as oil shipments through the waterway near prewar levels. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported nine attacks in the waterway this month, matching half the total reported for September across both the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf. Last month’s figure included four assaults in the final two days, showing the recent increase in activity. Vessels in Hormuz have faced attacks throughout the Iran war, with varying levels of intensity. Earlier strikes led to brief drops in shipments, though higher volumes in following days often offset these reductions. Maritime security officials and shipping executives said it remains unclear whether the latest escalation will reduce Hormuz shipments. The effect on seaborne gas flows, which also rose in recent weeks, is also uncertain. Several consuming nations announced plans last week to release millions of barrels of emergency stockpiles to ease market pressure. US President Donald Trump has been examining options to lower domestic fuel prices before midterm elections. Most tankers passing through Hormuz use a corridor near the Oman coast. They typically cross with their digital signals turned off, forcing traders and analysts to rely on satellite images and shipping data to track supply movements.

https://splash247.com/aframax-rio-blaze-.text: The Aframax Rio was ablaze off Sochi on Tuesday after being struck by unmanned surface vessels, adding another tanker casualty to a rapidly worsening Black Sea security picture. All 23 crew, all Indian nationals, were rescued and no injuries were reported. Images from the coast showed a large column of black smoke rising from the tanker and burning oil on the water. The Aframax Rio is a tanker linked to Russian oil exports and listed under Ukrainian sanctions. https://splash247.com/pyxis-lifts-mr-ear.text: Nasdaq-listed Pyxis Tankers has locked one of its MR product tankers into a two-year charter with CITGO Petroleum at $31,000 per day, securing about $21.8m in net charter revenue. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/kor.text: The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced on Oct. 5 that a Korean tanker has passed through the Suez Canal, located on the northern side of the Red Sea, and is transporting crude oil to the country. According to the ministry, as of 10 a.m. that day, the vessel had safely navigated through the Suez Canal and was en route to Korea. This marks the first time a Korean tanker has passed through the Suez Canal in about one and a half months since Aug. 19. Following the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz at the end of February, Korean tankers had been using the Red Sea as an alternative route. The route involved loading crude oil at the port of Yanbu in Saudi Arabia and passing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on the southern end of the Red Sea. However, as the military conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi rebels heightened the danger in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, tankers began using the northern Suez Canal route starting in mid-August. This route requires passing through the Mediterranean Sea and rounding the southern tip of Africa, which extends the sailing distance and increases the cost burden. The tanker that passed through the Suez Canal on this occasion is the 18th vessel to transport crude oil to the country via the Red Sea since the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. It is the third vessel to pass through the Suez Canal. The ministry stated that “the decision to pass through the Suez Canal on the northern side, rather than the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on the southern side of the Red Sea, was made by shipping companies and cargo owners.” Source: Business Korea

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: Germany’s federal government made official the decision to block the acquisition of a domestic freight forwarder and logistics company by the Chinese state-controlled COSCO Group. Political opposition had been mounting against the deal, with reports saying it demonstrates an emerging hardline against Chinese investments in Germany and Europe. COSCO had announced in January 2026 plans to acquire an 80 percent stake in the German freight company Konrad Zippel. A domestic freight and logistics company that dates back to 1876, reports said it plays a key role in moving cargo between the Port of Hamburg and inland, especially into the eastern regions of Germany. It has a fleet of more than 200 trucks and also handles a range of intermodal transport, including by rail. The two managing directors of Zippel had agreed to sell 80 percent of the company to a COSCO affiliate. One managing director was to retain 20 percent ownership and continue in a management role, while the other was selling all his shares and leaving the company. The Federal Cartel Office cleared the deal weeks later, reporting that it did not find concerns based on competition law. It said there was no risk of a dominant market position being established in freight transport, but it does not oversee the broader issues of foreign investment. Concerns began to emerge over the acquisition after the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution voiced fears about foreign investments. By September, however, it became clear that the Ministry for Economic Affairs, the Foreign Office, and the Ministry of Defense were all expressing economic and security concerns over the sale of Zippel to a Chinese state company. It was highlighted that Zippel provides logistical support to NATO and the German Armed Forces. The Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs announced on Wednesday, October 7, that the Bundestag (the federal parliament) had officially voted to reject the sale. The Ministry reported the decision, saying concerns had been raised about security and dangers to German and European supply chains.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: There were reports of a new incident in the southern Red Sea early on Wednesday, October 7, although the details are unclear and there were no claims of responsibility. It comes as fighting is intensifying along the coast of Yemen as Saudi and government forces are clashing with the Houthis while attempting to reclaim areas lost in the recent fighting. MSCIO, the EU-sponsored Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean, received reports of a small boat harassing a passing containership. The vessel said that shots had been fired by a small craft while it was transiting the southern Red Sea in the area north of the Bab el-Mandeb. The small craft was reported to have subsequently moved away from the area, and the containership was continuing its northbound passage through the Red Sea. The crew was uninjured. The ship is being identified by security consultants as the Singapore-flagged CUL Klang (35,300 dwt). Delivered in 2024, the ship is operated by the Chinese CUL Lines, which maintains routes to the Mediterranean, Middle East, and intra-Asia. The vessel has a container capacity of 2,433 TEU and is displaying a message on its AIS that reads “China owned&CHN crew.” In the past, reports have indicated that some of the small boats might be fishing boats in the region and simply acting to protect their boats and fishing nets. The Houthis have said they would be only targeting ships linked to Saudi Arabia, further raising doubts that they would target a Chinese container vessel. Their forces are also engaged in a series of clashes with Saudi-backed forces and those aligned to the internationally recognized government of Yemen. Yemen’s Homeland Shield Forces, a pro-government military faction, had announced that it was part of a “large-scale offensive” in the area around al-Waziya in the mountainous Taiz region. Other reports of fighting were along the coast south of Mocha. There were reports of strong fighting around Dhubab, located to the south of Mocha and near the Bab al-Mandeb. The Sudi forces reported on Tuesday they had retaken Mocha and key parts of the coastline. They claimed to once again be in control of the Bab el-Mandeb, but today there are conflicting reports, with both sides claiming to have retaken strategic parts of the coastline.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/d.text: Spanish authorities became suspicious when they detected a jet ski moving near the containerships in the Port of Algeciras. They reported that the operation caught three individuals in the act of attempting to offload 50 kilos of cocaine while disguised as port workers. European law enforcement agencies have warned that the smuggling operations were attempting to infiltrate port operations. Sometimes they plant individuals who are legitimate employees or bribe port workers, but in this case they attempted to disguise themselves as port workers. Officers from Guardia Civil, Customs Surveillance, and the Tax Agency were working together to monitor activity in the port and began to track the movements of the jet ski. It was observed approaching the dock where an unnamed containership was alongside, carrying out container loading. Two individuals got off the jet ski wearing clothing similar to the dockworkers in an apparent effort to blend in with the operations. They were successful in approaching and boarding the containership while being watched by the officers. The police decided to move in and took the two individuals into custody while they were still aboard the vessel. They began a search of the ship and discovered two backpacks that they believed were removed from a container and which the smugglers were preparing to carry off the ship. The smugglers apparently detected the officers and attempted to hide the backpacks before they were apprehended. A search of the backpacks revealed 50 packages, each with 1 kilo of cocaine. The police set the total value of the drugs at more than €1.5 million.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: [Breaking] The Royal Navy's maritime security tracking office, UK Maritime Trade Operations, has released a report of a significant vessel attack in the middle of the Arabian Gulf - hundreds of miles from the Strait of Hormuz, the region affected most by the U.S.-Iran conflict. At about 1900 hours UTC, the master of a tanker reported that the vessel was "struck by multiple projectiles" at a position about 50 nm to the north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar. The name of the vessel has not yet been released, as is UKMTO's practice in initial reports. Casualties have been reported in the incident and the authorities are currently investigation, UKMTO said. Consultancy Vanguard Tech has identified the vessel in question as the tanker Acers , corroborated by AIS data on the vessel's position. The 50,000 dwt Acers is flagged in Antigua and managed in Greece. It is the first reported tanker attack in the western half of the Arabian Gulf in weeks. U.S. military airborne security patrols have been active in the southern reaches of the Strait of Hormuz, defending a narrow maritime corridor around the Musandam Peninsula, but American forces have only a limited presence to the west of the waterway - rendering tankers transiting off Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Qatar comparatively vulnerable. The U.S. Navy no longer maintains an operationally significant presence in Manama, Bahrain, former home of U.S. Fifth Fleet, and there are no U.S. surface combatants operating west of Hormuz. On land, U.S. air and ground forces have been drawn down at bases around the region due to the threat of Iranian drones and ballistic missiles - though this could change quickly if the Trump administration orders a renewed buildup, as reported by Axios on Wednesday.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Uma fábrica de velas em Cordovil, na Zona Norte do Rio, foi atingida por um incêndio nesta quarta-feira (7). O caso ocorreu na Rua Capitão Cruz. Bombeiros de Parada de Lucas e Irajá foram acionados por volta das 17h50. As equipes combatem as chamas. Até o momento, não há informações sobre feridos ou imóveis atingidos. As causas do incêndio ainda não foram informadas.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: The crew of a small Turkish cargo ship struck early Tuesday morning, October 6, off the coast of Bulgaria has not been located, and based on the results of the search, Bulgaria ended the search. Officials told the media in a briefing on Wednesday about the two attacks , that they believe the cargo ship Alfa Watan (3,200 dwt), registered in Tonga, sank in a matter of minutes, and that they were continuing to monitor the second vessel, Able (7,400 dwt), which has been abandoned in the Black Sea. Multiple agencies from Bulgaria, aided by Romanian aircraft, searched the Black Sea approximately 70 miles east of the Bulgarian coast. Another cargo ship, Mercy , flagged in St. Kitts and Nevis, also diverted to the area to aid in the search. The authorities said they had received a signal from the Alfa Watan ’s distress beacon at around 02:30 local time. Initial reports said they had located an overturned lifeboat, three rafts, and various debris. There was no sign of the crew, and the search was unable to locate any traces of the crew. Bulgarian authorities have declined to comment on the specific number of seafarers who were lost, but media reports are saying there were between 10 and 12 crew, likely all from Syria. The ship, which was built in 1976, was owned by a Turkish company and was sailing into the Black Sea. The second ship that was hit yesterday, another Turkish-owned general cargo ship, Able , registered in Palau, continues to draft after the evacuation. The Chief Director of Bulgaria’s Maritime Administration Agency, Rumen Nikolov, reported that the ship had issued a distress call around 03:30, with the crew reporting they were preparing to evacuate the ship. Nikolov reported the ship was struck in the stern and that a large fire had resulted. The captain suffered a head injury but was released from the hospital. The chief engineer was severely burned and is in a hospital. The other crewmembers received a medical check and are in a hotel in Varna.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: U.S. maritime conglomerate TOTE has accepted a contract with MARAD to manage the Missile Range Instrumentation Vessel (MRIV) project, a three-ship series for the Missile Defense Agency (MDA), and immediately awarded a subcontract to Hanwha Philly for the construction of the first hull plus two options. In July, MARAD announced that it had awarded Hanwha Philly and TOTE Services the bid to build the MRIVs (not to be confused with MIRVs , the munition class underlying MDA's primary mission). Outfitted with house-sized radar units, the MRIVs will be used to track and analyze missile flights during testing. They will be deployed to MDA's missile testing ranges for R&D work in support of the Trump administration's Golden Dome project. They will replace two aging vessels, Pacific Tracker and Pacific Collector, which are both over 50 years old. The design for the MRIV is derived from the previous Hanwha Philly / TOTE design for the National Security Multi-Mission Vessel (NSMV), the school-ship series built for America's state maritime academies. The selection of an existing design as the basis for the MDA's ships should produce efficiencies, as the Hanwha / TOTE team and their suppliers are already familiar with it. TOTE and Hanwha believe that having a vessel construction manager between the shipyard and the government contracting authority will itself save about 50 percent of the construction cost of a typical federal shipbuilding program. Illustrations released by TOTE show two giant radomes on the new vessel's foredeck and one box-shaped radar array mounted on the stern. The graphics also suggest that the NSMV's characteristic double-level wheelhouse - designed for training many cadets simultaneously - has been reduced to a single level. The accommodations block has also been shortened, leaving more space for the gigantic aft radar, and the number of life boats has been reduced. The design of the NSMV was always intended for a naval auxiliary role when and if required, and is just seeing its first action in that application. SUNY Maritime's NSMV is now preparing to deploy in support of U.S. forces overseas, demonstrating the design's secondary capability in a national-security mission.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A PF e o MPRJ deflagraram nesta quarta-feira (7) a Operação Magen. Ao todo, 5 pessoas foram presas sob acusação de negociar armas para uma facção. Marcel Rodrigues Fernandes, um dos detidos, movimentou mais de R$ 33 milhões em 5 anos. Ele recebia R$ 8 mil em cargo comissionado na Alerj. A investigação indica que o grupo negociou ao menos 22 armas, incluindo 13 fuzis. A quadrilha também fornecia informações sigilosas para a organização criminosa. Entre os alvos está o policial civil Carlos Barnabé Santos Souza, investigado por fornecer informações. Ele e o chefe da facção, Peixão, são considerados foragidos. Policiais e ex-policiais militares investigados por vender fuzis ao tráfico de drogas no Rio de Janeiro também negociavam investigações clandestinas para ganhar dinheiro e utilizavam informações sigilosas das forças de segurança para ajudar criminosos, segundo uma investigação da Polícia Federal e do Ministério Público do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ). De acordo com a apuração, o grupo chegou a tentar obter imagens de câmeras de segurança do estado para beneficiar um miliciano acusado de homicídio .

Dois emus, incluindo o que correu em viaduto de Campo Grande na terça-feira (6), serão levados para o BioParque do Rio. Eles passarão por avaliação clínica. O emu foi filmado na pista por motoristas e colocado em um carro por pessoas não identificadas. A Delegacia de Proteção ao Meio-Ambiente iniciou diligências para apurar o caso. A Patrulha Ambiental realizou fiscalização nesta quarta-feira (7) para investigar as circunstâncias.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: Douglas Ruas (PL), candidato ao governo do Rio, afirmou nesta quarta-feira (7) confiar na Justiça na análise do recurso sobre a candidatura de Anthony Garotinho. Ruas declarou que não vê conflito na situação. Ele espera a confirmação de uma decisão anterior que determinou a anulação dos votos do candidato. O candidato relembrou que Eduardo Paes pediu a anulação e o Ministério Público foi favorável. Ruas disse crer que a decisão seguirá a legislação vigente.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: China’s People’s Liberation Army (Navy) (PLAN) released pictures of the Type-071 amphibious dock landing ship Yimengshan (Hull 988) launching a Type-726 landing hovercraft while at sea. The Type-726 Wild Horse Class landing hovercraft has been in service with the PLAN since 2007, with probably more than 40 now in service. The 150-ton hovercraft can move either a single Type 96 or Type 99 main battle tank or, as can be seen in the photos of the exercise published by the PLAN, four small wheeled armored vehicles. The configuration, capability, and its developmental timeline suggest that the Type-726 design was strongly influenced by the Bell Aerospace LCAC, in service with the US Navy and Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force since the late 1980s. Unfortunately, no video of the operation was published. But the East Sea Fleet exercise was carried out in late September on a flat calm sea, and the ship Yimengshan appears to be stationary whilst the exercise was carried out. From the pictorial evidence, it also appears that the ship Yimengshan is equipped with an azimuth positioning system to help keep the landing ship steady and stable as the launch operation proceeds, but it also suggests that such an operation could be a challenge to mount in a heavy swell. It also appears that the ship Yimengshan may have launched a second hovercraft, which is visible in other pictures speeding away from the mother ship. The Type-071 landing ships are believed to be able to hold four Type-726 hovercraft. The ship also has a hangar capable of housing up to four Z-8 helicopters, a licensed production variant of the French SA 321 Super Frelon capable of airlifting 25 troops. Taken together, the Yimengshan appears capable of landing a force sufficient in size to seize a reef, for example, or a small island. The Type-071 amphibious ship fleet, with associated Type-726 hovercraft, is split between the East and South Seas Fleets, with most exercise activity involving these craft being noted in the South Seas Fleet area adjacent to the South China Sea and the Chinese-claimed Land of Nanhai Zhudao.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O presidente Lula divulgou um vídeo nesta quarta-feira (7) cobrando o posicionamento do senador Flávio Bolsonaro sobre o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1. No vídeo, Lula questionou a orientação de voto de Flávio Bolsonaro e de seu partido, o PL. A publicação visa aumentar a presença digital do petista. Lula explicou que a proposta altera a jornada para 5 dias de trabalho e 2 de folga. Ele afirmou querer ver a redução sair do papel. A PEC estabelece jornada máxima de 40 horas semanais. O Senado começou a debater o texto nesta terça-feira (6) e a primeira votação pode ocorrer na próxima semana.

O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) afirmou nesta quarta-feira (7) que, se eleito, pretende usar o “capital político de presidente” para tentar aprovar uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que acabe com a reeleição. Flávio também reafirmou que, caso vença o segundo turno, não pretende disputar um novo mandato em 2030. “Quando eu falo que eu sou a favor do fim da reeleição e é assim que eu vou fazer, eu vou usar o capital político de um presidente recém-eleito para aprovar essa PEC, para redemocratizar o nosso país nesse sentido. É para dar o exemplo”, afirmou Flávio. A eventual aprovação do fim da reeleição poderia ter impacto direto na próxima disputa presidencial. Sem Flávio concorrendo a um segundo mandato, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) seria um dos nomes da direita com caminho aberto para disputar a Presidência em

A ex-candidata Clariana Barão (DC) declarou apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nesta quarta-feira (7). O candidato disputa o segundo turno contra Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Clariana afirmou ter "compromisso irrestrito" com Flávio Bolsonaro. No entanto, ela cobrou maior atenção às pautas de mulheres e crianças no segundo turno. Durante a campanha, Clariana encabeçou uma chapa feminina com Fabiana Torquato. O foco principal foi o combate à violência doméstica. O apoio soma-se aos de ACM Neto, Michel Temer, Romeu Zema, Ronaldo Caiado e da federação União Brasil e PP, declarada nesta terça-feira (6). O segundo turno ocorrerá em 25 de outubro. Flávio Bolsonaro obteve 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula no primeiro turno.

https://g1.globo.com/economia/blog/ana-f.text: A Polícia Federal decidiu arquivar uma investigação sobre suposta interferência do governo de Donald Trump nas eleições brasileiras. O pedido, feito pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), falava sobre o eventual uso de dinheiro público dos Estados Unidos no financiamento de organizações e grupos que operam em território brasileiro. O pedido de investigação foi encaminhado na última quinta-feira (1) ao diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, e ao procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet. No domingo (4), dia do primeiro turno das eleições, Andrei Rodrigues afirmou que a PF estava realizando uma apuração preliminar sobre o caso, sem instauração formal de inquérito.

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Em carta enviada nesta terça-feira (6), 12 deputados democratas norte-americanos acusaram o governo de Donald Trump de tentar influenciar as eleições do Brasil. No documento, os parlamentares citam a revogação do visto da embaixadora brasileira e planos para enviar 2 autoridades para questionar o sistema brasileiro. Os deputados exigem que o Departamento de Estado apresente justificativas para as ações até 20 de outubro, antes do 2º turno brasileiro. Esta é a 3ª cobrança em menos de 1 mês. Cartas anteriores foram enviadas em 24 de setembro e 5 dias depois por congressistas.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/eleico.text: A federação PSOL/Rede conquistou direito a 9 vagas na Câmara por São Paulo, mas preencherá apenas 6 pois parte dos candidatos não atingiu a votação mínima de 10% do quociente. Erika Hilton recebeu mais de 1,5 milhão de votos, mas só outros 5 candidatos do grupo alcançaram o piso de 33,8 mil votos exigido em São Paulo. As 3 vagas restantes não herdadas pelo PSOL serão distribuídas no cálculo das sobras eleitorais.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Transpetro assinou contrato com a Petrobras para prestar serviços de transporte rodoviário de bunker e óleo combustível entre refinarias e terminais , ampliando sua atuação multimodal. Para atender à demanda, a companhia investiu cerca de R$ 43 milhões na aquisição de 33 caminhões-tanque , que serão movidos a Diesel R, biocombustível desenvolvido pela Petrobras com conteúdo renovável de óleos vegetais e/ou gordura animal. O contrato contempla inicialmente duas rotas: entre a Refinaria Presidente Getúlio Vargas (Repar), em Araucária (PR), e o Terminal de Paranaguá (Tepar), em Paranaguá (PR); e entre a Refinaria Alberto Pasqualini (Refap) e o Terminal de Niterói (Tenit), ambos em Canoas (RS). Para a operação, a Transpetro também firmou parceria com a Budel Transportes, especializada na gestão operacional de cargas de combustíveis. O início dos serviços está previsto para janeiro de 2027, com foco em deslocamentos de curta distância e na conexão entre ativos logísticos do Sistema Petrobras. “O novo modal será utilizado especialmente em operações de conexão entre ativos logísticos do Sistema Petrobras e atendimento da chamada última milha. A iniciativa integra a estratégia de multimodalidade da companhia e tem início de operação previsto para janeiro de 2027. As primeiras rotas serão implantadas na Região Sul, com previsão de movimentação superior a 50 mil toneladas de combustíveis por mês”, afirma Sergio Bacci, presidente da Transpetro. Na rota entre a Repar e o Tepar, a previsão é movimentar 36 mil toneladas de produtos por mês. Já no trecho entre a Refap e o Tenit, a estimativa é de 18 mil toneladas mensais. O contrato atende exclusivamente à demanda da Petrobras, e uma eventual expansão para outras operações dependerá de avaliações de viabilidade técnica, operacional e econômico-financeira. A entrada no transporte rodoviário faz parte da estratégia da Transpetro de ampliar seu portfólio de serviços. Ainda em 2026, a companhia prevê iniciar operações de navegação interior com barcaças adquiridas para o transporte de bunker em portos brasileiros. O serviço terá início no Rio de Janeiro e também será ofertado em Santos (SP), Belém, Paranaguá e Rio Grande (RS).

A Movecta anunciou uma parceria estratégica utilizando o sistema de rastreamento de veículos em tempo real da Raster . A iniciativa faz parte do plano de modernização da frota da companhia e garante maior visibilidade sobre cargas, rotas e deslocamentos em todo o território nacional. A tecnologia já foi instalada integralmente na frota recentemente incorporada em julho à unidade da Movecta em Guarujá (SP) . Além de fornecer o acompanhamento dos trajetos em tempo real, a plataforma ainda permite analisar dados logísticos e enviar alertas automatizados diretamente aos motoristas. A tecnologia pode antecipar desvios de rota, paradas não programadas e incidentes antes que afetem o nível de serviço, usando Inteligência Artificial para prever comportamentos de risco. De acordo com a empresa, a solução já gerou uma queda de 50% nos indicadores de ocorrências monitorados. A integração está alinhada às metas de expansão do Plano Movecta 2030 e se soma a outros esforços já consolidados da empresa em tecnologia, como a implementação de seu Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO), em dezembro de 2024. A empresa relata 15% de redução nos custos de transporte, aumento de 20% na produtividade da equipe de gestão e satisfação 25% maior dos clientes corporativos desde o início da operação do CCO.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543531-pe.text: TechnipFMC has been awarded a subsea contract worth between $75 million and $250 million by Petrobras to supply flexible pipe systems for multiple pre-salt developments offshore Brazil. The contract, awarded following a competitive bidding process, covers the design, engineering and manufacture of flexible flowlines for use across several pre-salt fields. TechnipFMC said the work will draw on engineering, manufacturing and supply chain capabilities in Brazil. “This award highlights the confidence Petrobras continues to place in TechnipFMC's execution capabilities. Our industry-leading flexible solutions and ongoing industrialization efforts enable us to deliver greater efficiency, consistency, and predictability as we support Petrobras’ offshore developments and help ensure project timing and performance,” said Jonathan Landes, President, Subsea at TechnipFMC.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543530-fr.text: Framo has signed a four-year agreement with Petrobras to inspect and maintain pumping systems across the Brazilian energy company's fleet of about 30 floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) units, in what the Norwegian pump manufacturer said was its largest service contract of its kind to date. The agreement covers inspection, maintenance and training for Framo pumps installed across the fleet, including seawater lift, firewater, cargo and water injection systems. Work under the agreement will be carried out by Framo's local team in Rio de Janeiro. The contract comes as Framo expects its installed base in Brazil to exceed 1,500 pumps by 2028, driven by new FPSOs entering the market. Framo is also expanding its service capacity in Rio with a new maintenance facility at Galeão, which will support inspection, maintenance and training activities. “This agreement represents a significant step in how we support Petrobras across the lifecycle of its equipment. Rather than looking at individual service requirements in isolation, we will be working across a large fleet under a structured programme covering inspection, maintenance and training,” said Morten Sivertsen, Director, Framo Services Offshore.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/ferries-2.text: Small and mid-sized shipyards play an outsized role in keeping U.S. ferry fleets moving—and at Marine Log ’s FERRIES 2026 conference, taking place November 10-11 in Seattle, a panel of industry leaders will examine how these regional yards are supporting fleet growth, modernization and the maritime workforce. The panel, “How Small-to-Mid-Sized Shipyards Are Driving Ferry Growth and Modernization Across the U.S.,” will explore how local and regional shipyards are providing ferry operators with critical construction, modernization, repair and maintenance capacity, particularly in markets where access to larger shipyards may be limited. Moderated by Jeffery Brault, vice president of global public affairs at Hornblower Group, the discussion will feature Shull Autin, chief maritime officer at Hornblower Group; Erik Derecktor, operations | new construction at Derecktor Shipyards; Lance Lemcool, vice president, sales and marketing at Eastern Shipbuilding Group; and Gerona Goethe, general manager at Bay Ship & Yacht Co. Beyond vessel construction and maintenance, the panel will look at the role these yards play in building local maritime job pipelines and supporting skilled trades in their communities. Panelists will also discuss how federal funding and proposed legislation could help strengthen and expand smaller shipyards, increasing capacity for ferry operators while supporting long-term maritime workforce growth. As ferry systems across the country face growing demands for fleet renewal, modernization and reliable maintenance capacity, small and mid-sized shipyards are increasingly serving as a critical backstop for the industry—and a foundation for its future growth. The session is part of Marine Log ’s FERRIES 2026, bringing ferry operators, shipbuilders, naval architects, technology providers and other maritime stakeholders together in Seattle to discuss the challenges and opportunities shaping the next generation of passenger and vehicle ferry operations.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/framo-si.text: Framo has signed a four-year agreement with Petrobras to inspect and maintain pumping systems across the Brazilian energy company's fleet of about 30 floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) units, in what the Norwegian pump manufacturer said was its largest service contract of its kind to date. The agreement covers inspection, maintenance and training for Framo pumps installed across the fleet, including seawater lift, firewater, cargo and water injection systems. Work under the agreement will be carried out by Framo's local team in Rio de Janeiro. The contract comes as Framo expects its installed base in Brazil to exceed 1,500 pumps by 2028, driven by new FPSOs entering the market. Framo is also expanding its service capacity in Rio with a new maintenance facility at Galeão, which will support inspection, maintenance and training activities. “This agreement represents a significant step in how we support Petrobras across the lifecycle of its equipment. Rather than looking at individual service requirements in isolation, we will be working across a large fleet under a structured programme covering inspection, maintenance and training,” said Morten Sivertsen, Director, Framo Services Offshore.

https://gcaptain.com/attacks-on-tankers-.text: A still image from handout video released on September 15, 2026, said to show a damaged Panamanian-flagged oil tanker "El Gaia" following an incident in Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the tanker was hit by sea mines as it passed through a prohibited zone south of the Strait of Hormuz, a claim the U.S. military disputed, saying the vessel was struck by an Iranian missile "last month and rendered inoperable." IRIB/Handout via REUTERS. LONDON, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest last week of any week since the Iran war began, according to maritime security sources tracking incidents, amid a bigger export push by Gulf producers. Attacks, attempted attacks and harassment activity including drone overflights, surveillance and hailing using VHF radio by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have persisted in the strait, the US Navy-led Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) said in a note on Sunday. “These actions continue to demonstrate Iran’s intent to assert presence along key transit lanes and maintain pressure on transiting vessels,” the JMIC said. In the week of September 28-October 5, there had been at least 12 attacks on oil, liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas tankers around the Strait of Hormuz, according to data from three maritime security sources who analyzed incidents based on information received from the area. That was the highest number of attacks in a single week since the US war with Iran began on February 28, the sources said.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/reb.text: Iran has stepped up its attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a fragile rebound of crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf. Nearly 20 commercial ships, mostly tankers, have come under attack over the past month while sailing through Hormuz, the Persian Gulf or off the coast of Oman, according to the Joint Maritime Information Center, a group of U.S.-allied militaries that provide security updates to merchant vessels. Iran attacked roughly two ships for every 100 vessels that crossed the strait in the third quarter, said Michelle Wiese Bockmann, senior maritime intelligence analyst at Windward, which tracks ships for defense departments and governments. Oil flows through Hormuz now depend on a major U.S. military commitment to protect tankers transiting along a southern route along the coast of Oman. With the security situation in Hormuz still dangerous, it is unclear how long the rebound in crude exports can be sustained in the absence of a negotiated settlement or capitulation by Tehran. Shuttle system In many cases, tankers are bringing crude through Hormuz and then transferring the oil onto ships in the Gulf of Oman that haul it to Asia. This shuttle system reduces the exposure to attack from Iran but also requires more vessels to move the oil.

https://splash247.com/eidesvik-fixes-psv.text: Norwegian offshore vessel owner Eidesvik Offshore has secured fresh work for the platform supply vessel Viking Queen , taking the ship out of the spot market for a drilling campaign starting early next year. The contract covers one well and has an estimated firm duration of about 290 days, with further extension options attached. The customer has not been disclosed. “We are very pleased to announce this contract in a positive market,” Eidesvik chief executive Helga Cotgrove said. The award provides forward cover for a vessel that has been trading spot since coming off its previous term employment with Harbour Energy in October 2025. The 2008-built Viking Queen is a 6,200 dwt LNG dual-fuel PSV with 1,000 sq m of deck space. The 92-m ship also carries a 652 kWh battery system.Its return to term work comes as Eidesvik has been steadily rebuilding its PSV backlog. Splash reported in June that the Bømlo-based owner signed a fresh four-year frame agreement with Aker BP, including two further two-year options, while securing a three-year firm charter for the Viking Prince . Equinor has meanwhile exercised the remaining options on the Viking Avant , keeping the long-serving PSV employed through the end of this year.

https://petronoticias.com.br/prio-ve-pot.text: A PRIO vê potencial para desenvolver os recursos prospectivos dos blocos Magnetita e Hematita, arrematados nesta quarta-feira (7) no leilão do 4º Ciclo de Oferta Permanente sob o regime de partilha, por meio de tieback ao FPSO Valente, instalado no Campo de Frade, na Bacia de Campos. Em comunicado divulgado após o leilão, a petroleira informou que os dois blocos estão localizados ao norte da Bacia de Campos, próximos aos campos de Wahoo e Frade. A companhia ofereceu um percentual de excedente em óleo de 32,80% pelo bloco Magnetita e de 7,18% por Hematita. Segundo a PRIO, a empresa ainda irá avaliar os recursos prospectivos das duas áreas. Em caso de sucesso exploratório, os blocos poderão ser desenvolvidos por meio de tieback ao FPSO Valente, localizado no Campo de Frade. A estratégia de tieback consiste na conexão de uma nova descoberta a uma unidade de produção e à infraestrutura já existente, permitindo o aproveitamento de instalações que já estão em operação. No caso dos novos blocos adquiridos pela PRIO, a proximidade com os campos de Wahoo e Frade abre a possibilidade de integração com a estrutura já utilizada pela companhia na região. © 2026 Petronotícias.
