https://maritime-executive.com/article/k.text: Japanese conglomerate Kawasaki Heavy Industries is among the country's largest shipbuilders, and it also happens to have rare access to its own internal robotics division. It is putting a long legacy of robotics expertise to the test with a new emphasis on "physical AI" in every domain, including out in the yard. On Tuesday, it released an initial look at an AI-enabled, magnet-footed drone robot that can climb bulkheads and navigate small spaces. The prototype model is small, just two feet long, but the objective is to field a fully-developed version that can weld or perform weld inspections on vertical surfaces, without need for high-reach equipment or human workers. A robot that could work aloft on contoured surfaces would have substantial advantages in a drydock, removing the need for access equipment and staging for human workers. Japanese shipyards have a strong business need to increase their efficiency: The labor supply in Japan is restricted by an aging, steadily declining population. Guest-worker programs have helped to plug the gap, but the national government is instituting ever-tighter restrictions on work visas. In this environment, a front-line labor position replaced with technology is a job filled rather than a job lost. South Korean yards face similar constraints and have taken a leading role in developing robotic welding robots for block construction. More broadly, Kawasaki wants to accelerate its efforts with the introduction of AI in day-to-day operations. That includes robotics and "physical AI," a fusion of hardware and AI that creates systems that interact with the physical environment. It plans to invest $3.5 billion on the upgrade effort across all its manufacturing divisions over the next four years, including early testing at the Sakaide shipyard in Kagawa Prefecture. "Physical AI . . . reaches out from the screen into the real, physical world. Think of self-driving cars, or robots — physical AI can recognize what's happening around it, make decisions, and move things in the real world. As it spreads, we can expect the machines around us to move more flexibly, making our daily lives more convenient," said Jun Yamaguchi, lead co-creation manager at Kawasaki's new physical AI R&D lab in San Jose, California. By 2030, Kawasaki Heavy Industries wants to have an AI-enabled humanoid robot in general service, bringing the advantages of robotics to a broad range of human tasks.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: Por Kleber Tomaz , William Santos, Leonardo Pinheiro , g1 SP e TV Globo — São Paulo A Polícia Civil de São Paulo investiga ao menos 9 mortes com características de execução. O secretário de Segurança descartou a hipótese de um "serial killer" na capital. Os crimes ocorreram de setembro a outubro em diferentes regiões. O DHPP investiga as ocorrências de forma individualizada por não haver indícios de ligação entre elas. Das 9 vítimas, 8 foram identificadas e parte tinha passagens criminais. A polícia apura se as mortes foram motivadas por vingança ou ação de facções.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Tropical Storm Isaias is strengthening swiftly as it heads towards the U.S. Gulf Coast, and is expected to reach hurricane strength by the time it makes landfall near the Florida Panhandle. The storm's probable path will take it near to U.S. offshore oil and gas infrastructure, with near-term effects in the form of evacuations and well shut-ins. In its Wednesday afternoon update, NOAA's National Hurricane Center said that Isaias' intensity was about 55 knots, expected to rise to 95 knots before landfall on Friday. Strong upper-level wind shear is expected to limit its strength. A hurricane watch has been issued between Bay St. Louis, Mississippi and Indian Pass in the Florida Panhandle; NHC warned of the possibility of damaging winds, dangerous storm surge and extended power outages for residents in this region. Storm surge levels could reach up to seven feet in some coastal areas of Mississippi and Alabama, and up to five feet in the Florida Panhandle. The affected warning area covers a large segment of the U.S. shipbuilding industrial base: Ingalls Shipbuilding and Bollinger in Pascagoula, Birdon and Metal Shark in Bayou La Batre, Austal USA and Alabama Shipyard in Mobile, and Eastern Shipbuilding in Panama City and Port St. Joe, among others. The storm is expected to continue to bring heavy rainfall along the Gulf Coast and inland areas until Saturday, potentially leading to isolated areas of flash flooding. The storm's path is expected to run near the eastern edge of the Gulf oil patch, and some offshore infrastructure is within the NHC's warning cone for probable storm path. Risk of elevated winds and waves is prompting a small number of rig operators along the easternmost edge to curtail work and evacuate personnel. The newly-unified Marine Minerals Administration - formerly the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management and the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement - said in a statement that as of Wednesday, eight production platforms and two non-DP rigs have been evacuated. One DP rig has temporarily moved off-location to get further away from the storm's path. As a precautionary measure, offshore wells totaling about 25 percent of all Gulf oil production and 16 percent of the region's gas production have been shut in. Industry operators will bring these wells back online after a post-storm inspection, usually with a fast turnaround time.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: The number of ships choosing to reroute around South America has skyrocketed, according to a new report from the analysts at Bloomberg. Using data from the Chilean Navy on the number of pilot requests for the Strait of Magellan, Bloomberg reports a strong year-over-year increase in shipping volume. It reports the diversions began in July and increased 70 percent year-over-year in both August and September. The Chilean Navy did not provide Bloomberg with data on the types of ships making the transit, but the analysts said the increase came primarily in the 60,000 to 65,000 gross ton size of vessel. The timing of the increase coincides with the Panama Canal’s efforts, which began both lowering the number of daily transits and, more importantly, restricting maximum draft for the transit. Large gas carriers and containerships were expected to be impacted by the restriction. Containerships, for example, are required to restrict their cargo loads or offload and tranship boxes across the isthmus to meet the draft restriction. Industry analysts have also cited examples of LNG carriers diverting around South America. The Panama Canal typically maintains a level of around 38 daily transits, but it had begun restricting the number as part of its water conservation methods. Currently, the largest vessels, which use the Neopanamax locks, are restricted to a total of nine daily transits, although the Panama Canal Authority was adding one back based on current water levels. The older Panamax locks currently have a maximum of 23 ships per day. The Panama Canal Authority strongly emphasized that vessels were advised to make reservations to manage the reduced number of transits. Even with that, there are currently 45 booked vessels waiting for transit, and the northbound delay is again rising, with the average over the past 28 days now up to 5.5 days waiting time. There are, however, only three ships currently waiting that do not have a booked transit slot. Operators had the option of entering the bidding for slots, but there too the prices skyrocketed, especially ahead of the restrictions starting in September. Record prices exceeding $4 million and then $5 million were reported to obtain slots and jump the wait at the Panama Canal.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai is working to accelerate its efforts to commercialize Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) through a new agreement partnering with the nuclear industry and academia. The plan is to combine the design and construction capabilities of the shipbuilding industry with the expertise of the nuclear industry and universities to serve as a catalyst for accelerating commercialization. The new SMR Marine Technology Demonstration Center includes the participation of the Korean Register as well as the nuclear industry and Korean universities. The 12 participating organizations plan to jointly utilize their existing testing facilities and research infrastructure to reduce redundant investments and enhance the efficiency of technology verification for SMR technology. They will jointly develop core technologies required for marine SMR applications and work together to identify and plan large-scale national projects. They will also seek to participate in government R&D opportunities. By linking the various segments of expertise and technology, HD Hyundai says it will contribute to the development, testing, verification, and demonstration of SMR technology. It is the next step in the efforts to develop SMR technology to power a new generation of vessels. Last year, HD Hyundai’s HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE) revealed its first model of a 15,000 TEU containership employing SMR technology for propulsion power. The company noted that it had already obtained Approval in Principle from ABS (American Bureau of Shipping) for its design for the SMR-powered containership. It said it had advanced the designs while highlighting the enhanced economic efficiency and safety of the design by incorporating actual equipment and safety design concepts. HD KSOE highlights that the SMR technology does not require engine exhaust systems or fuel tanks. In its design, it optimizes the space used by a large engine room on a conventional containership to accommodate additional containers. In addition to the inherent benefit of SMR technology, HD Hyundai also applied a marine radiation shielding system using a double-tank method with stainless-steel and light water containment. The shipbuilder HD KSOE announced last year that it planned to establish a marine nuclear demonstration facility. It said it would open the center at its Future Technology Center in Yongin, South Korea, to verify the safety of SMR designs.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: O Grupo CMA CGM concluiu a aquisição da FedEx Supply Chain, subsidiária da FedEx Corp., em uma transação avaliada em US$ 1,4 bilhão. Com a integração, a CEVA Logistics passa a ter cerca de 150 armazéns na região, mais de 240 localidades e aproximadamente 20.000 profissionais na América do Norte. A operação adiciona cerca de 34 milhões de pés quadrados de área de armazenagem (aproximadamente 3,2 milhões de metros quadrados) à estrutura da CEVA e incorpora quase 10.000 profissionais da FedEx Supply Chain. Com isso, a empresa triplica sua presença logística no continente e se posiciona entre os principais operadores de logística contratual da região. A compra também reforça o histórico de investimentos do grupo francês nos Estados Unidos, mercado em que a CMA CGM atua há mais de 25 anos. Para a companhia, o movimento avança na estratégia de oferecer soluções logísticas completas, que combinam transporte marítimo, terminais, transporte terrestre, armazenagem e serviços logísticos de valor agregado. Além da escala física, a integração une capacidades digitais e operacionais das duas empresas. A expectativa é acelerar a adoção de automação e robótica na rede norte-americana. A CEVA também amplia sua experiência em setores como saúde, tecnologia, bens de consumo e varejo, o que fortalece a gestão de cadeias de suprimentos complexas nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá. Paralelamente ao fechamento, CMA CGM e FedEx firmaram acordos comerciais de múltiplos anos nas áreas de frete aéreo e marítimo. No modal marítimo, a CMA CGM será uma das transportadoras preferenciais da FedEx, em contrato sem exclusividade. No transporte aéreo, as empresas planejam um acordo de capacidade de carga em rotas estratégicas, entre elas Ásia e Europa. A proposta é melhorar o aproveitamento das aeronaves e dar mais flexibilidade às operações de longa distância. Para a CMA CGM, o arranjo também amplia a atuação como provedora integrada de soluções logísticas nos modais marítimo, aéreo e terrestre.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 07/10/2026 – O transporte aquaviário brasileiro alcançou, em 2025, a maior produção dos últimos cinco anos. Foram aproximadamente 374,6 bilhões de toneladas-quilômetros úteis (TKU), crescimento de 9,81% em relação a 2024. O resultado faz parte do estudo Produção de Transporte Aquaviário: Toneladas por Quilômetro Útil – TKU no Setor Aquaviário – Exercício 2025, aprovado pela Diretoria Colegiada na Reunião Ordinária de Diretoria nº 619, em 24 de setembro. Realizado a cada dois anos pela Agência, o levantamento acompanha a evolução da produção do transporte de cargas e identifica os principais corredores hidroviários, perfis de carga e rotas comerciais do país. O TKU considera a quantidade de carga transportada e a distância percorrida: uma tonelada transportada por um quilômetro corresponde a um TKU. O estudo integra a Agenda Plurianual de Estudos da ANTAQ 2025-2028 e atualiza os dados referentes ao exercício de 2023. Os resultados mostram crescimento nas diferentes modalidades analisadas. A navegação interior chegou a 42,70 bilhões de TKU, avanço de 21,06% em relação a 2024. O longo curso realizado em vias interiores cresceu 23,46%, alcançando 44,98 bilhões de TKU. Já a cabotagem atingiu 286,92 bilhões de TKU, alta de 6,49%. Relator da matéria, o diretor Wilson Lima Filho destacou em seu voto que o estudo amplia o conhecimento sobre o setor e fornece informações para subsidiar as atividades de planejamento, acompanhamento e regulação desenvolvidas pela Agência. “Na prática, o estudo sobre a produção do transporte aquaviário em Tonelada-Quilômetro Útil (TKU) permite comparar modais de transporte, avaliar a capacidade e a eficiência, além de contribuir para o planejamento de infraestruturas e para a regulação do setor. Ao associar a quantidade de carga útil transportada à distância percorrida, o indicador também oferece elementos para compreender a intensidade de utilização dos corredores hidroviários e as ligações entre as origens e os destinos das cargas", analisa o diretor. Considerando a navegação interior, a cabotagem em vias interiores e o longo curso em vias interiores, a produção realizada nas hidrovias brasileiras chegou a 114,59 bilhões de TKU em 2025, crescimento de 19,06% em relação ao ano anterior. A Hidrovia do Baixo Amazonas respondeu por 63,95% desse total. Já na navegação interior, Madeira e Baixo Amazonas concentraram, juntas, cerca de 59,6% do TKU.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: A series of reported diesel shipments from Ulsan to Vladivostok have added fuel to a growing diplomatic dispute between South Korea and the Ukrainian government. According to a recent analysis by The Guardian, Korean exporters shipped about 1.3 million barrels of diesel and other fuels to Russia in July and August. Three of the ships involved were sanctioned by the EU, and two of these vessels appear to have called directly in Ulsan to take on cargo before delivering it to Russia - without apparent difficulty with the local authorities over their sanctions status, according to the report. The Guardian found that on some of these voyages, the tanker crews initially declared a destination in Japan or Singapore before diverting to Vladivostok to deliver their fuel. The report's findings were echoed by Ukrainian presidential adviser Vladyslav Vlasiuk this week, drawing strong pushback from Seoul. "That a Ukrainian presidential official cited a Guardian article to publicly portray Korea as helping ease Russia's fuel crisis and loss of refining capabilities . . . is different from the truth and inappropriate," a spokesperson for the Blue House said Wednesday. But by Thursday, South Korea's foreign ministry reversed course and said that it would review whether any Korean diesel was exported to Russia. Some energy commodities, including diesel and jet fuel, are not currently covered by South Korean export controls on sales to Russian commercial buyers, the ministry noted - but it pledged to take legal steps if irregularities are discovered. Relations between Kyiv and Seoul were already strained before the tanker dust-up. North Korea supplies manpower and arms for the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine, and Ukrainian soldiers occasionally capture a small number of North Korean nationals on the battlefield. In a recent prisoner transfer, Ukraine sent two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea; this sensitive deal was agreed in advance, but the two sides differ on whether it was supposed to be kept secret. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed the transfer in public during a meeting of the UN General Assembly on September 24, using it to illustrate North Korea's arms and personnel trade with Russia. "Kim Jong Un uses them like currency and gets [military technology] in return," Zelensky said in his address.

https://g1.globo.com/pop-arte/noticia/20.text: A escritora canadense Anne Carson venceu o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio foi feito pela Academia Sueca nesta quinta-feira (8). Nascida em 1950, Carson combina poesia, tradução e docência. Sua obra destaca-se por atualizar a tradição clássica em produções como "Autobiography of Red". Historicamente, a premiação soma 123 laureados desde 1901. O vencedor anterior da láurea, em 2025, foi o escritor húngaro László Krasznahorkai.

Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio da premiação foi feito nesta quinta-feira (8). Segundo a Academia Sueca, a canadense Carson foi escolhida “por sua obra ousada e inventiva que, em diálogo lúdico com a tradição clássica, criou novas formas para a literatura contemporânea”. Ao longo de toda a carreira, combinou a escrita de poesia com o trabalho de tradução e o ensino em diferentes universidades. A década de 1990 marcou a publicação de uma obra frequentemente apontada como a maior de Carson: "Autobiography of Red: A Novel in Verse (1998)". O livro demonstra sua notável capacidade de atualizar a tradição literária clássica. Com um olhar preciso para os modos de falar e as experiências contemporâneas, Carson parte de fragmentos de poemas do poeta grego Estesícoro, do século VI a.C., sobre o monstro vermelho alado Gerião. Suas colaborações com artistas visuais, coreógrafos e diretores de ópera e teatro demonstram a liberdade com que ela se relaciona com as expectativas literárias e os sistemas de regras. É essa liberdade que está por trás da importância que sua obra, desde os anos 1990, adquiriu para o cenário internacional da arte e da literatura.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543559-en.text: Eni CCUS Holding, jointly owned by Eni and BlackRock’s Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), has completed the installation of the Douglas CCS platform in Liverpool Bay, off UK, describing it as the world's first purpose-built offshore platform dedicated to carbon capture and storage (CCS) for industrial decarbonization. The platform will serve as the offshore hub of the Liverpool Bay CO2 transportation and storage system, which forms the backbone of the UK's HyNet industrial decarbonization cluster. Douglas CCS will receive CO2 captured from industrial facilities across North West England and North Wales before directing it through a network of repurposed offshore pipelines to depleted natural gas reservoirs for permanent storage. The platform comprises a 1,885-tonne topside, a 1,755-tonne supporting jacket and eight foundation piles weighing a combined 730 tonnes. The facility was delivered in less than 18 months from contract award under an accelerated engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning program. The installation forms part of the wider Liverpool Bay CCS development, which is approximately 50% complete.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543553-tr.text: Shell and Chevron said on Wednesday they were curtailing offshore operations in the Gulf of Mexico as Tropical Storm Isaias approached the region. Shell said it was evacuating all personnel and shutting in production at its Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox assets. The company added that it had already moved non-essential personnel from its Stones asset. Separately, Chevron said it had initiated shut-in procedures for production at four Chevron-operated Gulf of Mexico facilities in preparation for the storm. Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern US coast early on Saturday, bringing heavy rains, storm surges, and possible tornadoes across several states, the National Hurricane Center said. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543557-te.text: TenneT Germany has joined DEME and Subsea Cable Assets (SCA) as a development sponsor of Frequensea's subsea cable decommissioning tool, which is being developed to recover buried offshore cables while reducing seabed disturbance. The technology uses patented vibration-induced fluidisation to reduce soil resistance around buried subsea infrastructure, allowing cables, umbilicals and pipelines to be recovered with potentially smaller vessels and lower energy consumption. TenneT Germany will contribute its experience as an offshore transmission system operator, particularly in subsea power cable infrastructure, to the tool's development. Following the successful completion of a testing programme at Deltares, TenneT Germany plans to evaluate the technology's potential for future offshore cable decommissioning in the North Sea. The company joins existing sponsors DEME, an offshore energy contractor, and SCA, a specialist in cable handling systems. The development programme aims to qualify the Frequensea Decommissioning Tool for offshore deployment, with potential applications in recovering subsea power cables as offshore wind farms reach the end of their operational lives.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543549-us.text: The US Environmental Protection Agency said on Wednesday it would soon propose scrapping a Biden-era rule aimed at curbing large leaks of methane from oil and gas operations. The move is part of a broad Trump administration effort to slash regulations that it says burden US businesses as it seeks to boost fossil fuel production. "Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work. They can’t do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a statement after making the announcement at a meeting with oil and gas industry representatives in New Mexico. EPA's "super emitter" program requires companies to react when third parties report suspected methane leaks using remote sensing. The Trump administration, after taking office last year, had delayed implementation of the policy until next year. Methane is the second-biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide, and the oil and gas industry is a major source of the gas "This giveaway to fossil fuel executives is foolish and short-sighted, and reveals who the Trump administration really works for - its political donors,” Mahyar Sorour, director of the Sierra Club's Beyond Fossil Fuels campaign, said in a statement.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-s.text: A hydraulic oil leak below the moonpool of a pipelay/construction vessel resulted in an estimated 185 litres of oil being released, with around 150 litres ultimately lost to sea. T he incident, detailed by the International Marine Contractors Association (IMCA), highlights a less obvious safety challenge: critical pressure-retaining components can fall outside established lifecycle controls, while restricted access and limited visibility can delay confirmation of an alarm. The case raises wider questions about how vessels identify, inspect and respond to seemingly minor hydraulic-system abnormalities. During operations, the vessel’s moonpool doors were opened and a hydraulic oil leak was identified below the moonpool. Operations were stopped immediately, and the main hydraulic power unit was shut down and isolated. The subsequent investigation traced the leak to a failed “minimess” monitoring hose, specifically at its termination/crimp fitting inside the aft worktable door hydraulic control cabinet. Review of the vessel’s SCADA data showed that a minor low-pressure alarm had activated earlier. However, the area below the moonpool doors could not be visually inspected at that point because of the system configuration.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-analysis-the-s.text: A ship designed to use a new fuel represents a significant investment. It does not, by itself, establish that the fuel can be bunkered safely on its route, handled confidently by its crew or used routinely in service. Those conditions have to be built around the vessel. T hat distinction deserves more attention as shipping measures progress towards lower emissions. The UCL Energy Institute and Getting to Zero Coalition’s 2026 Climate Action in Shipping report records advances in fuel-capable vessels, trials and bunkering. It also finds that technology and supply are only partially on track against its 2030 breakthrough goal. Its assessment of civil society, which includes workforce and training developments, is likewise partially on track. The report’s wider finding is that progress remains uneven across the organisations needed to make the transition work. For safety leaders, the question is immediate: what must be ready before a capable vessel begins using a different fuel as a normal part of its operation? The answer extends beyond the ship’s design. It includes the bunkering location and supplier, agreed procedures at the ship–shore interface, personnel familiar with the particular installation, and an emergency response that has been understood and practised. Bunkering is a useful test of whether technical capability has become operational capability. A vessel may have suitable tanks and fuel systems, but fuel transfer brings the ship, supplier and port into a single operation. Their equipment and procedures must work together, and the people involved need a common understanding of their responsibilities.

https://safety4sea.com/india-eu-green-sh.text: India and the European Union have launched a new industry coalition aimed at developing a green shipping corridor between the two markets, linking India’s growing renewable-fuel potential with Europe’s demand for lower-emission maritime fuels. T he India–EU Green Shipping Corridor Coalition was launched during the third edition of Sagar Manthan in New Delhi, where a Letter of Intent was signed to advance cooperation on cleaner maritime transport and strengthen green-fuel supply chains between India and Europe. The initiative will bring together industry stakeholders to assess the commercial and infrastructure requirements needed to establish viable green shipping routes. Green ammonia and methanol are expected to be among the key fuels considered under the initiative. The coalition is intended to examine the full supply chain required for green maritime corridors, including fuel production and demand, port infrastructure, transport networks and potential commercial models. India’s expanding renewable-energy capacity provides an opportunity to develop a larger supply base for alternative marine fuels, while European ports and industrial users represent potential receiving markets and offtakers. The initiative will also involve V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority and technical partner Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI), with the participants expected to explore cooperation with European receiving ports and industrial customers.

https://safety4sea.com/south-korea-advan.text: Twelve South Korean shipbuilding, nuclear industry, research and academic organizations have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish an offshore small modular reactor (SMR) technology demonstration center in Ulsan. T he agreement was signed on October 6 at the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST). The participating industry organizations include HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering, KEPCO Engineering & Construction, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, the Korean Register, Hyundai Heavy Industries Turbomachinery and Clad Korea. Research and education institutions include Ulsan Technopark, UNIST, Seoul National University, KAIST and Hanyang University. The center will coordinate the verification and demonstration of offshore SMR technologies by connecting the participating organizations’ specialized personnel, testing facilities and research infrastructure. The partners also plan to share existing facilities to reduce duplicate investment and improve testing and verification efficiency. Alongside technology demonstrations, the organizations will jointly develop core technologies, link university research with industry requirements and identify large-scale government-funded research projects. By combining shipbuilding capabilities with nuclear design and operational expertise, the partners aim to establish a full-cycle foundation covering SMR development, demonstration and eventual commercialization in South Korea. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries said the center is expected to strengthen cooperation between the country’s shipbuilding and nuclear sectors and help bring forward the commercialization of offshore SMRs.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-drugs-and-cont.text: Drug trafficking presents a particular maritime security challenge because a vessel does not need to be attacked or hijacked to become part of a criminal operation. S hips, cargoes and legitimate supply chains may be exploited without the knowledge of the company, Master or crew, while in other cases criminals may seek assistance from individuals who already have authorized access onboard. Drugs and other contraband may be concealed inside containers or cargo, placed in stores or ship spaces, or attached externally to the hull or underwater fittings. Criminals may also gain unauthorized access while the vessel is in port, placing packages onboard for recovery at another location. The consequences can be serious. Discovery of illicit substances may result in vessel detention, investigation, operational disruption and potential legal consequences for seafarers, including those with no involvement in the trafficking operation. One of the factors that makes drug trafficking particularly difficult to prevent is that not every case involves an unknown intruder. Crew members, contractors, stevedores or other individuals with legitimate access to the vessel may be approached, bribed, threatened or, in some cases, knowingly involved. The security threat may therefore come from someone who is authorized to be onboard. For companies, Masters and Ship Security Officers, this makes awareness of local trafficking patterns and port-specific risks particularly important. Crew members should also understand that unusual approaches, requests, behaviour or attempts to gain access to restricted areas should be reported without hesitation. These risks should be addressed through the vessel’s Ship Security Plan and appropriate port-specific security measures.

https://safety4sea.com/european-ports-pu.text: Europe’s ports are entering a new phase of the environmental transition: the emphasis is shifting from adopting sustainability policies to delivering measurable reductions in emissions, improving resilience and providing the infrastructure needed for cleaner shipping. T hat is the central message of the ESPO Environmental Report 2026 – EcoPortsinSights, which assesses environmental management, monitoring and green services across 73 European ports in 17 countries. The report finds that environmental management remains deeply embedded in the sector, even as ports face growing pressure from climate change, energy transition, regulation, competitiveness and geopolitical uncertainty. The report also cautions that year-on-year comparisons need to be treated carefully because the participating-port sample changes. Nevertheless, the longer-term direction is clear: European ports have moved substantially beyond simply establishing environmental policies and are increasingly being asked to demonstrate results. Climate change has retained its position as the number-one environmental priority for the fifth consecutive year, selected by 59 of the participating ports. Air quality and energy efficiency follow, underlining how closely climate policy is now tied to the day-to-day operational concerns of ports. Noise has risen to fourth place, while relations with local communities climbed from seventh to fifth. Land-related port development fell to sixth, although ESPO stresses that this does not necessarily mean land pressure is becoming less important. Ports increasingly need space not only for cargo and logistics, but also for renewable energy, alternative fuels and other infrastructure associated with the energy transition. The changing ranking reflects a broader transformation in the port environmental agenda. Traditional concerns such as dredging, waste, water quality and land use remain, but they now sit alongside climate mitigation, energy transition, resilience and community relations.

https://safety4sea.com/eu-shipping-faces.text: Europe’s shipping industry is entering another important phase of regulatory change, with lawmakers moving ahead with reforms to the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) while also seeking to simplify reporting requirements under the bloc’s maritime climate rules. M eanwhile, the European Parliament is considering tougher measures to prevent companies from avoiding carbon costs, while new initiatives on cybersecurity, shipbuilding, industrial competitiveness and funding are beginning to take shape. The developments, highlighted in the Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore’s September 2026 European Affairs Report , point to a broader shift in EU policy – that shipping is increasingly being treated not only as a sector that must decarbonise. The EU’s ETS reform is currently one of the most significant issues for shipping. Following the European Commission’s proposal in July, the European Parliament is now working towards its negotiating position. The lead European Parliament Rapporteur, Peter Liese, has proposed several changes, including directing a larger share of ETS revenues towards industrial decarbonisation. Under the proposal, the share of ETS revenues allocated to industrial decarbonisation would rise to 75%, compared with 50% in the Commission’s proposal. The draft also proposes changes to the pace at which emissions allowances are reduced between 2030 and 2040. For shipping, another important element is the proposed strengthening of anti-evasion measures.

https://safety4sea.com/ai-automation-and.text: Artificial intelligence may have dominated the technology conversation in recent years, but the next phase of the transformation is moving beyond the screen. T he next wave of change in shipping will likely come not from a single breakthrough, but from the convergence of AI, autonomy, connectivity, robotics and new energy technologies. That is one of the broader messages emerging from McKinsey’s Technology Trends Outlook 2026, which identifies major technology trends and highlights how AI is increasingly moving beyond software and into the physical world. For maritime transport, that shift could prove particularly significant. Ships, ports and logistics networks are already becoming more connected and automated, but the technologies highlighted by McKinsey suggest that the next stage could bring greater autonomy, more intelligent vessels and increasingly automated operations across the maritime supply chain. “Mobility is becoming a software-defined system where value comes as much from data, software, and fleet operations as from the vehicle itself. The winners will be those that integrate electrification, autonomy, and digital infrastructure into a seamless customer and operating experience,” highlighted Andreas Breiter, partner, Bay Area. McKinsey argues that the next frontier is increasingly physical. AI is being combined with sensors, robotics and connected machines to allow systems to perceive their surroundings, make decisions and act on them. A vessel equipped with increasingly sophisticated sensors and AI systems could process information about traffic, weather, navigation and its surroundings much faster than traditional systems. Over time, this could support more automated navigation and allow crews to focus on higher-level decisions rather than constantly managing individual tasks.

https://safety4sea.com/world-shipping-co.text: The World Shipping Council (WSC), in partnership with HUB Ocean, has launched a digital version of its Whale Chart, giving the global maritime industry easier access to information on measures designed to reduce the risk of ship strikes and other impacts on whales. F irst launched in 2023, the WSC Whale Chart was the first global compilation of mandatory and voluntary government measures aimed at protecting whales from vessels. The chart covers a range of measures, including speed restrictions, routing requirements, areas to be avoided and rules intended to reduce underwater radiated noise. The new digital version brings this information into a searchable, regularly updated format that can be integrated into digital tools and operational systems used by shipowners, operators and crews. Mariners operate across many different jurisdictions, and the measures in place to protect whales vary from country to country and region to region. Bringing this information together digitally and making it available to mariners on the bridges of the ships they are navigating makes it easier to use in voyage planning and helps crews see where changing course or slowing down can make a real difference. The launch also coincides with the release of the fourth edition of the WSC Whale Chart handbook, which provides a concise regional overview of whale-protection measures. The need for such information is particularly relevant as whales routinely cross national boundaries and migrate through some of the world’s busiest shipping routes.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/is-.text: Middle East oil exports have climbed back above levels seen before the US-Israel war on Iran began in February, despite Tehran’s attempts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz and attack vessels. Crude exports from the region exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September, reaching between 19.5 and 22.5 million barrels per day (bpd), according to provisional data from maritime tracking firm Kpler. Before the war, exports averaged about 18 million bpd. This surge in oil exports from the region has so far largely been attributed to US ships shepherding tankers out of the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with increasing ship-to-ship transfers that reduce the risks of being targeted by Iranian missiles and drones. Meanwhile, the fact that oil prices have remained high has been explained by analysts as the result of still-elevated insurance rates — driven by fears of Iranian attacks — and a market factoring in the possibility of a return to a hot war. But a senior Kpler analyst last week offered a different explanation for the rise in oil exports at high prices. Gulf countries, she suggested, may be paying Iran to allow their oil through – potentially handing Tehran a significant portion of the value of the cargo. Before the war, one-fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz. Does this explanation hold up, and what does it mean for the war and oil prices?

Upon completion, the vessel will become the 13th FSRU in our fleet and will expand the reach and capabilities of our LNG infrastructure platform,” said David Liner, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of Excelerate Energy.

https://splash247.com/tanker-attack-off-.text: The war on merchant shipping in the Middle East has taken a worrying geographical turn, with casualties reported aboard a tanker attacked off Qatar, hundreds of miles west of the Strait of Hormuz, while a containership has also come under fire in the Red Sea. The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged oil/chemical tanker Acers (IMO: 9301902) was struck by multiple projectiles on Wednesday evening, approximately 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, according to maritime security firm Vanguard. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) confirmed the attack at around 1900 UTC, reporting casualties but providing no details on their number or severity. Most attacks since Iranian strikes on commercial shipping resumed on September 28 have been concentrated around the Strait of Hormuz. Wednesday’s incident, deep inside the Arabian Gulf, marks the first reported attack outside the strait during the latest escalation. It raises the prospect of a much larger area of the Gulf becoming a maritime combat zone, threatening ships serving oil and gas terminals in Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq. The attack also comes amid an increasingly intense campaign against merchant shipping, with at least a dozen tankers and gas carriers reportedly targeted around Hormuz between September 28 and October 5. Reports are also emerging of another possible strike, with the Marshall Islands-flagged VLCC Dhalkut reporting a fire approximately 22 nautical miles east of Fujairah. The ship is operated by Asyad, and is on charter to Trafigura.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/dre.text: With regional security changing rapidly, Drewry’s Red Sea Diversion Tracker delivers timely intelligence to shippers, carriers, ports and other stakeholders on the evolving structure of carrier networks. Transits via Suez up 154% year-on-year During the week ended 4 Oct, the number of containership transiting via the Suez Canal (in either direction) reached a one-year high of 61, up 154% when compared with the number in the same week of 2025, as carriers continued their gradual policy of returning to the Suez route. The average number of transits was 52 in the latest 3 weeks, up 15% from the average in the previous three weeks. Source: Drewry

https://splash247.com/seatrium-bags-firs.text: Singapore shipyard group Seatrium has secured an EPCIC contract from New York-listed floating regasification specialist Excelerate Energy to convert an LNG carrier into an FSRU, with an option for a second unit. The project is Seatrium’s first FSRU conversion for Excelerate. Financial terms were not disclosed. Engineering work is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026, with delivery scheduled for 2028. Once completed, the vessel will join Excelerate’s fleet as the 13th FSRU. Seatrium’s scope includes installing and integrating regasification equipment, LNG transfer and cargo-handling systems, utility and offloading facilities, electrical and automation systems, marine modifications, and related infrastructure. The converted unit will have 170,000 cu m of LNG storage capacity. It will also retain tri-fuel diesel-electric power generation and reliquefaction equipment. Excelerate purchased the LNG carrier Methane Patricia Camila for about $79m as the conversion candidate. The company has said the vessel’s existing power and reliquefaction systems would simplify the project and reduce execution risk.

https://splash247.com/yinson-production-.text: Singapore-based Yinson Production has priced $1.458bn of senior secured notes backed by the Agogo FPSO, marking what the company says is the largest FPSO project bond to date and the first of its kind outside Brazil. Yinson Azalea Production, which owns the Agogo FPSO, is issuing the notes, which will be used primarily to refinance existing debt linked to the vessel. The notes have a scheduled maturity of 13.3 years and carry a fixed coupon of 6.517% per annum, payable semi-annually. They were priced at 98.164% of principal and are expected to settle on October 21. Part of the proceeds will also fund reserve accounts, transaction costs, and potential equity distributions from excess proceeds. The Agogo FPSO is leased to Azule Energy Angola and operates on block 15/06 offshore Angola under a 15-year firm bareboat charter, with options that could extend the contract by up to five years. Yinson chief financial officer Markus Wenker said the transaction is the company’s third FPSO project bond in three years.

https://splash247.com/almi-marine-founde.text: Greek shipowner Evgenia Daskalopoulou, founder and president of dry bulk outfit Almi Marine Management, has died. Almi announced her death on Wednesday, saying she passed away surrounded by her family. Daskalopoulou was born in 1958 and founded the Athens-based company in 1992. She built Almi from a small dry bulk operation into a modern supramax and ultramax owner and manager. Greek shipping records show the company started out with two 1970-built handysize bulkers. “More than that, she shaped its character,” Almi said in announcing her death, highlighting her emphasis on integrity and respect for staff both ashore and at sea. The company said operations would continue as normal and that the Daskalopoulou family and management team remained committed to carrying on the business. Almi currently manages six bulkers totalling 365,140 dwt — three supramaxes and three 64,000 dwt ultramaxes. Its fleet includes the 2024-built Mea Mare, Spike and Subra, alongside the older Altus, Anima and Sole.

https://splash247.com/pif-energy-launche.text: US energy trader PIF Energy has unveiled plans to spend $2bn acquiring up to 15 crude tankers, with purchases already underway as the company moves to secure shipping capacity through the Strait of Hormuz. The Dallas-based company, founded and led by chief executive Ben Morrow, specialises in crude oil and refined products trading, supply and logistics, with operations spanning the US Gulf, Europe and the Middle East. PIF, which stands for Pay It Forward, trades crude and products including diesel and jet fuel, supplying refineries, governments and industrial customers. The privately held business has also been pursuing opportunities in Iraq, where it has held discussions with the country’s oil ministry over cooperation in the upstream sector. PIF is targeting secondhand VLCCs, with the new fleet intended to transport oil from Iraq and other Gulf producers to markets in Asia and Europe. “Our investment is focused on a practical contribution: owning and operating the transportation capacity to connect crude supply with refinery demand and support sustained deliveries,” PIF stated in a recent social media post. The company expects to complete its initial acquisition programme within three to four weeks, subject to vessel availability and due diligence.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: There is some debate about exactly how much oil and LNG is being shipped out of the Gulf from the GCC producers on its southern shores, but little disagreement about how much Iran is managing to export: none. With the Iranian oil reserve held afloat off Malaysia and China likely to run out this month, and the last revenues from these sales all coming in by the year’s end, Iran faces a drastic curtailment on government revenues - probably amounting to 40% of what had previously been expected in the annual budget. There will still be enough money to fund national security priorities – rebuilding the nuclear program, manufacturing ballistic and air defense missile stocks to replace wartime attrition, and paying the wages and running cost of the Basij internal security apparatus. But the money devoted to the general population will be in very short supply. Iran since the revolution has lived through many crises, and out of adversity has demonstrated hardiness and resilience. In particular, it has honed its sanctions evasion skills and stratagems. It should be expected that with no oil or LNG flowing out of Iran on traditional routes, alternative export routes will be sought to help prop up the nation’s finances. There are a number of potential plans which might be under consideration. Iran has two railway connections which might be of value, of which the route through Sarakhs, across Turkmenistan to China, might have some potential. Moving oil by rail car is not optimal, and is obviously more expensive than doing so by ship. Nonetheless, Canada managed to ship 175,000 bpd from Alberta to refineries in the United States in 2014, equivalent to about 20% of Iran’s oil exports to China. But the challenges of setting up such a transport system are enormous. Infrastructure has to be built, and rail cars procured. The rail route and its bridges have been bombed by the United States before, and probably would be so again if any traffic was observed. The rail journey to China would take between 10-15 days – and then the rail cars need to be returned. Moreover, the rail path has a number of track gauge changes en route, adding cost, time and complexity. Such a solution would take years to deliver, and Iran’s need is immediate. Shipping oil across the Caspian is another non-starter. The Iranian national oil transmission network has a pipeline link to Zaghmarz on the Caspian Sea, but this was built as an import conduit for Russian oil being imported for refining to meet domestic fuel needs in northern Iran. Tankers on the Caspian are shallow draft and carry low volumes. Neither Azerbaijan nor Kazakhstan are on friendly terms with Iran, so would not be prepared to insert Iranian oil into their oil transmission systems, either from Kazakhstan through the Caspian Pipel

https://g1.globo.com/df/distrito-federal.text: O candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o candidato a vice-presidente na chapa, Alfredo Gaspar (PL), fizeram uma "visita institucional" nesta quinta-feira (8) ao Arcebispo Metropolitano de Brasília, cardeal Paulo Cezar Costa. "O encontro transcorreu em clima de cordialidade e diálogo, constituindo uma oportunidade para a reflexão sobre questões de interesse da Igreja e da sociedade brasileira", afirmou a arquidiocese em uma rede social. https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The US aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returned to her home port of San Diego, California, on October 8, concluding what became the second-longest deployment in the modern era, except for extended tours during the COVID-19 pandemic. The carrier also set a new record for the longest number of consecutive days at sea, 264 days, beating the 206 days for USS Dwight D. Eisenhower during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. It was the close of one of the longest, most challenging combat periods for the carrier. According to the Navy, Abraham Lincoln was engaged in 40 straight days of combat when the war with Iran began on February 28, followed by participation in the follow-on efforts and the blockade of Iranian shipping and ports. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew to the carrier on Wednesday to recognize the efforts of the approximately 5,000 sailors. The air wing had already departed the carrier for its return to base. He issued the Presidential Unit Citation to the carrier group. The Navy reports the strike group conducted 3,693 combat sorties and delivered 1.37 million pounds of ordnance during the campaign. It also launched 450 cruise missiles. A total of 77 one-way attack drones fired by Iran were reported to have been shot down, along with 21 anti-ship cruise missiles that were destroyed. The strike group sank 64 Iranian warships according to the Navy and defended against four fast-attack boats and explosive-carrying wooden dhows. The carrier had deployed on November 21, 2025, and made a port stop in Guam as it was crossing the Pacific. It would not arrive in Thailand until September 2 and, after a brief stop, proceeded to Guam before its return to California. At 321 days, it is just five days shy of the mark set by USS Gerald R. Ford, which was deployed for 326 days, the longest in the post-Vietnam War era, before returning to Virginia in May. USS Abraham Lincoln was replaced in the Middle East by USS George Washington , which is operating alongside USS George H.W. Bush . USS Theodore Roosevelt is expected in the region at the end of this month.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Although there have not been any formal updates covering progress, it appears that the salvage activity on the wrecked Aframax tanker Caroline Bezengi (IMO 9224439) is continuing off Yemen’s southeastern coast. The Caroline Bezengi remains firmly stuck on the rocks off the southwest tip of Jazirat Al Qibliyyah. The tanker is sanctioned by the EU, UK and US (OFAC), and has a past association with Russian state shipowner Sovcomflot. The tanker had completed a transit of the Suez Canal on May 30 and had left the Maritime Security Transit Corridor when a suspected limpet-mine blast occurred on June 8. The tanker was laden with oil taken on board at Novorossiysk and was destined for Gujarat. The crew was taken off without injury some four days later, reportedly by another sanctioned and Russian-connected dark fleet tanker, the Noble Walker (IMO 9292981), which was also en route to India with Russian oil aboard. Caroline Bezengi continued to drift northeast with the monsoon winds until running aground on June 30. Post-monsoon season weather appears to have started, with wind speeds on October 8 reported as a comparatively light 11 knots. Swells on October 8 were less than one meter and are expected to remain so for the following week. These mild surface conditions will enable operations on the deck of the tanker, and may enable the next phase of the salvage plan: maneuvering a small tanker close in to the lee of the island to start the offloading process. As of October 8, there is no sign yet of an offload operation in progress. On satellite imagery and showing up on AIS on October 8 is the offshore vessel EDT Kennedy (IMO 9671400). There are three other vessels in the vicinity seen in the imagery. With the return of calmer seas, fishing boat activity in the area has now resumed. The Caroline Bezengi is still leaking oil, and the sheen of a plume can be seen flowing towards the northeast, as seen previously. In the changed and calmer weather conditions, it now also appears to be spreading southeast.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/l.text: Bulgaria’s military reports it is monitoring the movements of an abandoned bulker that is drifting in the Black Sea. A month after the vessel was struck near Ukraine, it reappeared earlier this week off the coast of Bulgaria, raising concerns over its movement. The German-owned bulker Emil (175,463 dwt) has been adrift since August 5, when the crew abandoned the ship approximately 21 nautical miles from the Greater Odesa area. The vessel, which was built in 2012 and is 292 meters (958 feet) in length, was registered in Liberia. It was struck by a Russian drone , which caused a fire and the failure of technical systems. The crew abandoned the vessel, with reports that Russia again struck the ship, but it has remained afloat. The bulker has been drifting in a southwesterly direction, with reports indicating it had been in Romania’s region of the Black Sea. On October 4, Bulgaria determined it had drifted into its EEZ. The Air Force and Navy conducted reconnaissance. The report placed the ship approximately 40 nautical miles east of Cape Shabla in northeast Bulgaria just south of the Romanian border. Pictures confirmed the vessel was struck in the stern. Fire damage is visible on the stern as well as to the accommodation block. The bridge of the bulker appears burnt out. The Bulgarian Navy issued a warning to shipping, and they are charting the movement of the ship. Bulgaria said it would continue to monitor the drifting vessel and that it is ready to take any necessary action if the situation changes. It is not the first time Bulgaria has had to deal with a war casualty. In December, the shadow tanker Kairos washed up in Bulgaria days after it was attacked by Ukraine off Turkey after it entered the Black Sea. A tug appeared to move the hulk from Turkish waters but released it off Bulgaria, and it then drifted to the coastline. Bulgaria provided support for the crew that was on the burnt-out tanker and removed the vessel to a sheltered anchorage. It later said it had been reimbursed for the costs by the owners of the vessel and had sold the ship.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Sanctions remain one of the primary tools used by the West to increase pressure on both Russia and Iran. The UK launched its second package of sanctions in a week, going after Russia’s oil and financial interests, while the United States added sanctions targeting Iran’s petrochemical industry as part of the economic campaign launched in August. The latest move by the United States was a coordinated action by the State Department and Treasury, with each taking aim at the shadow tanker fleet and petrochemical industry. The State Department said it was participating to further isolate the Iranian regime, including targeting a broad network of petrochemical traders based in Turkey and the UAE, as well as Iran. The Treasury Department said it was part of the program it dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, with its focus on more of the tanker fleet. Treasury asserted that with the U.S. blockade of Iran’s ports and shipping, along with dwindling Iranian oil shipments outside the blockade, and its economic pressures, “the regime is running out of options to stabilize Iran’s failing economy.” The operation is “taking action against remaining shadow fleet vessels that are continuing to evade U.S. sanctions by transporting Iranian petroleum and petrochemicals.” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent asserted that the effort “effectively neutralizes the vast majority of Iran’s remaining shadow fleet.” The action lists 17 additional tankers, with Treasury highlighting that the vessels involved are registered in more than a dozen jurisdictions and operate by an intricate web of international front companies. The vessels, which are mostly product tankers and LPG carriers, as well as two crude oil tankers, have flags including Comoros, Panama, the Bahamas, Mongolia, Palau, Cameroon, Zanzibar, Sierra Leone, Vanuatu, Hong Kong, San Marino, and Gambia. While the U.S. asserted that the action targets “the vast majority of Iran’s remaining shadow tanker fleet,” the analysts at TankerTrackers.com wrote, “The only issue is: There are still 173 Iran-linked tankers which are not under US sanctions.” They pointed out that it was the first action in six weeks.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: The Philippine Coast Guard has reported another dust-up at Second Thomas Shoal, where the Philippine Navy maintains an outpost aboard a deteriorating shipwreck in order to deter Chinese expansion within Manila's exclusive economic zone. Second Thomas Shoal has been an on-again, off-again flashpoint for tensions between Philippine and Chinese forces in the Spratly Islands since at least 1999, when the Philippine Navy intentionally grounded the WWII-era landing ship BRP Sierra Madre on the reef to serve as a base. The service has maintained a small detachment of marines on board the wreck ever since, and the periodic resupply and rotation missions to and from the shoal are a recurring source of friction. In times of heightened diplomatic tension, the China Coast Guard has often attempted to prevent PCG personnel from reaching the station, periodically adopting forcible methods like aggressive maneuvering and water-cannoning. The latest encounter occurred on October 8, according to PCG spokesman Jay Tarriela. A Navy servicemember aboard BRP Sierra Madre was in need of medical attention and required evacuation from the station, and the PCG was tasked with mounting a medevac mission. On Thursday morning, the patrol vessel BRP Cabra departed Lawak and got under way for Second Thomas Shoal. At about 0730 hours, Cabra arrived at a position about nine nautical miles away from the reef, where it encountered a familiar presence: China Coast Guard cutter CCG 5306. The CCG crew turned on their water cannon and closed the distance to Cabra, approaching to within 400 yards, Cabra's crew reported. The Chinese cutter's maneuvering prevented further progress towards the Philippine base. In order to avoid getting hit by the water cannon, BRP Cabra stayed about 13 miles offshore and waited. The crew had hoped to conduct a rendezvous and transfer closer to the patient, but this was not possible because of the Chinese presence, Tarriela said. By early afternoon, the situation had not changed. To adapt, Cabra's crew launched a team in its RIB boat, and the BRP Sierra Madre station dispatched two inflatable rubber boats with the patient and escort personnel. They met up about four nautical miles off the reef and transferred the patient between boats. Throughout the evolution, CCG small boats and cutters harassed the PCG boat crews, Tarriela said, using "dangerous" maneuvers. Other Chinese vessels involved or in the area included CCG cutters 5009 and 21585, plus the PLA Navy frigate Yongzhou (628) and one maritime militia fishing vessel. After bringing the patient safely aboard, the Cabra's crew provided him with a checkup and with IV fluids, then got under way to deliver him to shore for a higher level of care.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/y.text: Fighting in Yemen is intensifying and spreading to Saudi Arabia as the Houthis seek to deter further Saudi support for Yemen’s Internationally Recognized Government (IRG). But conversely, the broadening of Houthi attacks appears to have strengthened the resolve of both the Saudis and the Yemeni populations of areas that the Houthis are trying to seize – which largely fall outside the traditional areas where the Houthis have commanded support from those with whom they share religious and tribal affinities. Trustworthy information about what is happening on the ground in Yemen is difficult to find, the airwaves being dominated by propagandists and fake news. The most reliable source is @BashaReport, which has excellent access to local sources, checks reports out carefully, and only publishes verified information. Houthi and Yemeni Government positions in SW Yemen as noted in reporting on October 8; the situation on the ground is settling into a stalemate and a prolonged war. (Google Earth/CJRC) The IRG appears to have consolidated its hold on the SW coastal strip of Yemen, having retaken Perim Island and the Ras Menhali peninsula, overlooking the narrowest part of the southern Red Sea at its narrowest point, the Bab el Mandeb. This in itself is a major recovery gain for the IRG - and for the global maritime community, as it reduces the potential threat to shipping seen in the past from short-range weapons and from small craft. But whereas the IRG had briefed several days ago that the goal of the IRG was to advance north to seize Hodeida, the Houthis’ principal trade window to the outside world, progress northwards appears to have ground to a halt. It is still not clear if the IRG has fully secured the port of Mocha, halfway to Hodeida, and instead the IRG is trying to secure more of the hilly territory to the east, which overlooks and dominates the coast and the Tihama Plain. The situation on the coastal strip is still far from settled. Elsewhere, the Houthis are pressing hard to isolate and then capture Taiz, which, before the war, the Houthis had already surrounded on three sides. So far the Houthis have faced stiff resistance from a population with whom they have a long-standing adversarial relationship, both on tribal and religious grounds. But the Houthis have tightened their grip and may be able to impose a siege; again, the situation is very fluid, and the outcome is uncertain.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: New data suggests that the volume of ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz has again fallen off, despite the consistent assertions from U.S. Central Command that flows are increasing and “building momentum for freedom of navigation.” The latest reversal followed an increased pace of attacks on tankers, and after reports had indicated oil flows were back to pre-war levels. The volume of crude oil transiting the Strait of Hormuz has reportedly fallen by a quarter (27 percent), Reuters reports, citing data from Kpler. It says that the number of vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz is at its lowest point since July 23. Kpler cited a total of seven commodity vessels, i.e., tankers and others, on Tuesday, October 6, while LSEG data showed eight vessels on Tuesday, including five tankers. LSEG shows that 14 vessels had made the transit on Monday, and it is well below the average of more than 20 per day earlier in the month. Exact numbers are difficult to determine because of the proportion of vessels making a dark transit, i.e., without AIS transmissions, which continues to be high. Still, all the experts agree the volume of transits has again fallen. Kpler reports the largest portion of the decrease in oil shipments is from vessels involved in the ship-to-ship transfers. Iran appeared to be targeting these vessels based on the statements of its Persian Gulf Strait Authority and the vessels it added to its “non-compliant list.” Further, Kpler says an increase in exports from the Gulf of Oman coast and the Red Sea is, however, making up for some of the shortfalls of crude being shipped through the Strait of Hormuz. These reports contrast with U.S. Central Command, which released new statements refuting Iranian claims that the Strait of Hormuz is closed and under Iran’s control. CENTCOM cites 20 million barrels of crude that transited through the Strait without citing a timeframe. Further, it asserts, “In recent months, U.S. forces have supported the shipment of over 1.25 billion barrels of crude oil from Gulf partners and through the Strait of Hormuz.” The increase in the number of attacks on tankers is believed to be having the greatest impact on transits this week. Iranian media asserted that over the past week, 14 vessels have come under attack and that more than six have been warned to turn back.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: A coligação de Eduardo Paes (PSD) anunciou nesta quinta-feira (8) que recorrerá ao STF contra decisão do TSE que anulou os votos de Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos). O grupo de Paes também apresentará medida cautelar para tentar garantir a realização do 2º turno na eleição de governador do Rio de Janeiro. A anulação dos 274.411 votos de Garotinho altera o cálculo dos votos válidos e abre caminho para que Douglas Ruas (PL) vença a eleição no 1º turno.

Douglas Ruas (PL) liderou o primeiro turno para o governo do RJ com 49,27% dos votos. Ele pode ser eleito após o TSE confirmar a nulidade dos votos de Anthony Garotinho. Policial civil e advogado, Ruas foi eleito deputado estadual em 2022 com 175.977 votos. Ele presidiu a Alerj e comandou a Secretaria Estadual das Cidades. Seu plano de governo prioriza a segurança pública com o programa Escudo Fluminense. A proposta prevê ações em saúde, educação, habitação e transporte no estado.

https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: O deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, que está nos EUA — Foto: Wilton Junior/Estadão Conteúdo O ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), determinou o início do cumprimento da pena do ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP), condenado a 4 anos e 2 meses de prisão, em regime inicial semiaberto, pelo crime de coação no curso do processo. Eduardo Bolsonaro vive nos Estados Unidos . Em julho, o ex-deputado obteve o chamado "green card", documento que concede a estrangeiros o direito de viver e trabalhar legalmente no país por tempo indeterminado . 🔎 O green card é um documento emitido pelo governo dos EUA que concede a estrangeiros o direito de residir e trabalhar legalmente no país por tempo indeterminado. Na prática, o "green card" transforma o brasileiro em residente permanente nos EUA, mas não altera sua cidadania brasileira nem encerra os processos judiciais que ele responde no Brasil . Nesta quinta, Moraes também mandou expedir um mandado de prisão contra o ex-parlamentar, que seja destinado à Polícia Federal, e também incluí-lo no banco de mandados de prisão.
