https://www.oedigital.com/news/543570-le.text: Subsea Equipment specialists Legasea have launched a new basket rental service for decommissioning and seabed clearance projects, offering credit against rental costs when recovered equipment can be reused. The service uses a fleet of five subsea baskets, sourced surplus from a major oil and gas operator, and fully refurbished and rectified by Legasea. Each basket is rated for a 5,000 kg maximum payload (7,500 kg maximum gross weight) and carries a unique ALBA identification number for traceability. When baskets are returned carrying recovered subsea equipment, Legasea assesses the items at its permitted Westhill facility. Equipment that can be cleaned, refurbished and recertified is credited against the client's rental. Depending on the equipment recovered, this can significantly reduce the net cost of the baskets. Credit depends on equipment type, condition and assessment outcome, and is subject to agreed terms. NORM-contaminated items are not accepted, but permitted sub-contractors can manage these items if required.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543560-la.text: Lamprell has signed an agreement with International Maritime Industries (IMI) to fabricate several offshore structures, including a production platform and jackets, at IMI's Ras Al-Khair facility in Saudi Arabia. The fabrication work forms part of an offshore engineering, procurement, construction and installation (EPCI) project being delivered by Lamprell. The agreement marks the first offshore production platform and jacket fabrication scope undertaken at IMI's Ras Al-Khair yard, expanding the facility's activities beyond shipbuilding. IMI is a joint venture between Aramco, Lamprell, Bahri and Hyundai Heavy Industries, with Lamprell among its founding shareholders. “This agreement is a defining step in IMI’s journey beyond shipbuilding. By taking on the fabrication of offshore structures for the first time, we are demonstrating the depth and versatility of our capabilities and reinforcing our role as a diversified, world-class industrial partner to Saudi Arabia’s energy sector,” said Abdullah Al-Ghamdi, IMI’s Chief Executive. The agreement will draw on Lamprell's offshore EPCI and fabrication experience while supporting the development of IMI's offshore construction capabilities and local industrial capacity in Saudi Arabia.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A VLI iniciou a movimentação ferroviária de sorgo para exportação em três corredores logísticos , com operações pela Ferrovia Centro-Atlântica (FCA) e pelo tramo norte da Ferrovia Norte-Sul (FNS) . O primeiro embarque ocorreu em setembro, pelo Porto de Tubarão (ES), com destino à China, e a companhia estima transportar mais de 800 mil toneladas da commodity até o final de 2026. A empresa já movimentou mais de 250 mil toneladas de sorgo até setembro. Desse volume, 90 mil toneladas seguiram pelo Corredor Sudeste, de Uberaba (MG) ao Porto de Santos (SP), enquanto mais de 160 mil toneladas foram transportadas pelo Corredor Leste, de Araguari (MG) ao Espírito Santo. As duas operações tiveram a China como destino. Em setembro, a VLI também iniciou a movimentação do grão pelo Corredor Norte, que atende a região do Matopiba. A primeira carga seguiu para o Porto do Itaqui, em São Luís, e os primeiros embarques para exportação estão previstos para outubro, com destinos no norte da África e novamente na China. Para viabilizar a operação, a companhia realizou capacitações técnicas e ajustes nos processos e na infraestrutura existente. No Sudeste e Centro-Oeste, a malha ferroviária atende regiões produtoras como Goiás e Minas Gerais, responsáveis, respectivamente, por 26% e 19% da produção nacional, segundo dados da Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento (Conab). No Corredor Norte, a operação contempla produtores da Bahia, Maranhão e Tocantins. "Alguns segmentos da economia brasileira dependem da infraestrutura para atingir seu pleno potencial de desenvolvimento, e a VLI é parceira nesta jornada. A inclusão do sorgo em nosso portfólio reflete a capacidade da companhia de desenvolver soluções logísticas ágeis e aderentes às necessidades do mercado", afirma Carolina Hernandez, diretora-executiva Comercial, de Projetos e Planejamento Estratégico da VLI. Segundo a executiva, a diversificação das cargas movimentadas permite ampliar o uso da infraestrutura ferroviária e criar novas alternativas logísticas para os clientes. A operação também acompanha a expansão do mercado de sorgo, utilizado tanto na alimentação humana quanto na produção de ração animal, silagem, biomassa, bioenergia e etanol.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/eia_boosts_.text: In its latest short term energy outlook (STEO), the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) raised its 2026 Brent crude oil spot price forecast by more than $5 per barrel and its 2027 Brent price forecast by $10 per barrel, compared to its previous STEO. The EIA’s latest STEO, which was released on October 6, sees the Brent crude spot price averaging $96.32 per barrel this year and $83.74 per barrel next year. These projections mark a third consecutive EIA Brent price projection increase for both 2026 and 2027. In its previous STEO, which was released in September, the EIA saw the Brent spot price averaging $91.01 per barrel this year and $73.74 per barrel next year. The EIA’s August STEO projected that the Brent price would come in at $86.81 per barrel in 2026 and $69.39 per barrel in 2027, and its July STEO saw the Brent price averaging $81.91 per barrel this year and $64.76 per barrel next year. In its June STEO, the EIA expected the Brent crude oil spot price to come in at $95.39 per barrel in 2026 and $79.39 per barrel in 2027. The EIA highlighted in its October STEO that the Brent crude oil spot price increased to an average of $114 per barrel in September, which it pointed out was $23 per barrel higher than in August. “Prices rose following increased attacks on oil infrastructure and tankers around the Middle East,” the EIA noted in its latest STEO. “The most notable among these developments were attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, which temporarily halted flows on a crucial bypass used to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz,” it added.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: L'Oréal, Santos Brasil, Maersk, Voith e Rodonaves estão com inscrições abertas para cursos gratuitos de qualificação profissional em Santos, Guarujá, Ribeirão Preto e na capital paulista. São 87 vagas disponíveis para jovens residentes próximos às unidades das empresas e que tenham renda per capita de até um salário mínimo por pessoa. A iniciativa é fruto de um convênio firmado entre as empresas e o Formare, programa de qualificação profissional para jovens em situação de desvantagem socioeconômica, da Fundação Iochpe . A fundação mantém há 36 anos o programa, que já qualificou mais de 28 mil jovens, em parceria com empresas de médio e grande portes. O índice de formalização no mercado de trabalho chega a 89% dos egressos nos últimos dez anos, de acordo com uma pesquisa realizada pelo Plano CDE em 2023. As aulas acontecem dentro das unidades das companhias, com uma metodologia que combina teoria e prática, em um ambiente real de trabalho. O diferencial está no formato: os educadores são os próprios profissionais da empresa, que atuam de forma voluntária, oferecendo aos alunos uma formação conectada com as exigências do mercado. Os cursos são certificados pela Universidade Tecnológica Federal do Paraná (UTFPR), agregando reconhecimento à formação profissional oferecida pelo programa. Requisitos: Ter nascido entre 01/01/2009 e 31/12/2009 e ter 18 até dia 31/12/2027; estar cursando ou ter concluído o ensino médio em rede pública de ensino; ter renda familiar per capita* (por pessoa) de até um salário mínimo; ter interesse pela área do curso (preferencialmente); não ter frequentado cursos profissionalizantes. Benefícios: Bolsa-auxílio de estudos, alimentação, uniforme, auxílio transporte, material didático para uso durante o curso, seguro de vida em grupo, assistência médica ambulatorial, equipamento de proteção individual e coletivo (para aulas teóricas e práticas, quando necessário).

A Total Express ampliou sua cobertura direta para 5.165 municípios brasileiros , com a incorporação de 4.500 novos CEPs à rede logística. A expansão, que alcança 16 estados, inclui localidades como Parintins (AM), Cururupu (MA), Buritis (MG) e Fernando de Noronha (PE) e faz parte da estratégia da companhia de ampliar a capilaridade e oferecer alternativas de recebimento de encomendas. Desde 2018, a rede de atendimento direto da empresa cresceu quase três vezes, passando de 1.480 para 5.165 municípios. A ampliação também incorpora novas modalidades de atendimento, incluindo pontos de retirada de mercadorias para consumidores que estejam em endereços fora da área de cobertura direta dos entregadores. "Expandir nossa cobertura significa criar novas possibilidades de conexão entre sellers e consumidores em diferentes regiões do país, dada a revolução comercial que estamos vivenciando no varejo e indústria brasileiros. Esse movimento é resultado de uma estratégia contínua de crescimento da malha, que busca acompanhar as características de cada localidade e ampliar as possibilidades de atendimento", afirma Fernando Magnoler, diretor de Estratégia Comercial da Total Express. Para esses endereços, a companhia disponibiliza a rede de PUDOs (Pick-Up & Drop-Off) Total Points, permitindo que o consumidor escolha um local para retirar a encomenda. Segundo a Total Express, o modelo amplia as possibilidades de conclusão das entregas e pode reduzir custos associados a devoluções e cancelamentos, além de oferecer uma alternativa para regiões nas quais a entrega domiciliar apresenta limitações operacionais. A rede de Total Points chegará a mais de 2 mil unidades. Cinco novas cidades passarão a ser atendidas integralmente por meio dos pontos de retirada. Nos últimos 12 meses, a estrutura cresceu 21%, alcançando 18 estados e 391 municípios. No mesmo período, mais de 4 milhões de pacotes foram movimentados pela rede, entre operações de coleta, entrega e devolução. "Não estamos falando apenas de abrir pontos parceiros. Estamos construindo uma malha logística de coleta e entrega conectando esses pontos com a malha da Total Express capaz de competir onde a logística tradicional não consegue operar com eficiência", destaca Greisieli Uesugui, gerente de Produtos da Total Express.

A CMA CGM e a DSV firmaram um acordo para ampliar o uso de combustíveis de baixo carbono no transporte marítimo , com meta de reduzir em 12 mil toneladas as emissões de CO₂ associadas às operações da DSV ao longo de dois anos . A parceria prevê a utilização da solução ACT+ , desenvolvida pela CMA CGM para apoiar clientes na redução das emissões de suas cadeias de transporte. O ACT+ utiliza combustíveis de menor intensidade de carbono, incluindo biocombustíveis de segunda geração produzidos a partir de UCOME (Used Cooking Oil Methyl Ester), um tipo de biodiesel avançado produzido a partir da reciclagem de óleos de fritura e de cozinha usados e BioLNG (biometano liquefeito). Segundo a CMA CGM, a solução pode proporcionar redução de até 83% nas emissões de CO₂ em comparação com o uso de combustíveis marítimos convencionais. O acordo amplia uma parceria de longa data entre as duas empresas e está alinhado às metas de descarbonização da DSV, que pretende alcançar emissões líquidas zero em suas próprias operações e em sua cadeia de valor até 2050. Para a CMA CGM, a iniciativa também integra a estratégia de atingir o Net Zero Carbon no mesmo horizonte. "Na DSV, reduzir as emissões nas cadeias de suprimentos globais exige forte colaboração e soluções escaláveis. Por meio da parceria com a CMA CGM e do uso da solução ACT+, estamos ampliando o acesso a opções de transporte marítimo com menores emissões para nossos clientes", afirma Michael Hollstein, SVP Global Ocean Product da DSV. Segundo a companhia, a contratação do ACT+ pela DSV acompanha um movimento de empresas que vêm adotando ou renovando compromissos com a solução como parte de suas estratégias de descarbonização. A CMA CGM lançou o ACT+ como parte de sua estratégia de transição energética. A companhia iniciou em 2017 um programa de larga escala para adoção de propulsão a GNL em navios porta-contêineres de grande porte, que levou à entrada em operação, em 2020, do CMA CGM Jacques Saadé, primeiro porta-contêineres de 23 mil TEUs movido a GNL.

A LATAM Cargo relatou que o transporte de produtos farmacêuticos entre a Europa e o Brasil cresceu aproximadamente 150% de janeiro a julho de 2026 na companhia, na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. O avanço foi impulsionado principalmente pelo transporte de medicamentos à base de GLP-1, classe utilizada em tratamentos para diabetes tipo 2. Nos primeiros sete meses do ano, os medicamentos à base de GLP-1 representaram cerca de 15% do volume total transportado pela companhia entre Europa e Brasil. Considerando todos os tipos de carga, a LATAM Cargo movimentou quase 32 mil toneladas entre os dois mercados no período , crescimento de 27% em relação aos primeiros sete meses de 2025. Cerca de 75% desse volume correspondeu a cargas gerais e consolidadas, entre elas produtos de automação, máquinas para mineração, itens têxteis e commodities. "O crescimento do transporte de produtos farmacêuticos mostra como a demanda por soluções logísticas especializadas vem ganhando relevância entre Europa e Brasil. Nossa prioridade é acompanhar essa evolução com uma operação segura, eficiente e preparada para as necessidades específicas de cada tipo de carga. Ao mesmo tempo, o crescimento de 27% no volume total reforça a importância da conectividade entre os dois mercados e a capacidade da nossa rede de atender diferentes setores da economia", afirma Jorge Carretero, gerente de Vendas de Carga na Europa do LATAM Airlines Group . Para atender aos requisitos específicos da indústria farmacêutica, a LATAM Cargo oferece soluções que incluem monitoramento de temperatura, salas climatizadas, segregação de cargas, coberturas térmicas e redução do tempo de exposição no pátio. No caso de cargas transportadas em contêineres ativos, os procedimentos incluem conexão à fonte de energia, monitoramento periódico e acompanhamento dos níveis de bateria e temperatura. A companhia possui ainda o CEIV Pharma Hub em Miami, que dispõe de câmaras para diferentes faixas de temperatura e espaço dedicado ao carregamento e armazenamento de contêineres farmacêuticos ativos.

A MRS Logística firmou uma parceria com a Cosco para realizar operações de transporte ferroviário de contêineres entre Minas Gerais e o Rio de Janeiro , integrando a malha da companhia aos terminais do Grupo Tora e às rotas marítimas da armadora chinesa . O modelo permite conectar a origem da carga ao navio e inclui a possibilidade de utilização do Redex do Grupo Tora em Contagem (MG) para etapas do despacho aduaneiro. Na operação, os terminais do Grupo Tora em Contagem e Arará atuam na consolidação, armazenagem e movimentação das cargas. O Redex de Contagem permite realizar determinadas etapas do despacho aduaneiro antes da chegada da carga ao porto, incluindo inspeções da Receita Federal quando aplicáveis. A primeira operação da parceria envolve a exportação de ferro-gusa. O fluxo começa com o transporte ferroviário de contêineres vazios do Rio de Janeiro até o terminal do Grupo Tora em Contagem. No local, os contêineres são carregados com o ferro-gusa e seguem novamente por ferrovia até o Porto do Rio de Janeiro, onde a carga é embarcada em navios da Cosco. O modelo permite que as diferentes etapas da operação nacional sejam integradas antes do transporte internacional. Além do ferro-gusa, a estrutura poderá atender cargas industrializadas, paletizadas, em bags e a granel que possam ser acondicionadas em contêineres nos terminais parceiros. Segundo as empresas, a integração entre os modais pode oferecer uma alternativa ao transporte rodoviário direto, com potenciais ganhos de custo, segurança da carga, previsibilidade e confiabilidade operacional. A utilização do Redex também permite antecipar determinadas etapas dos processos aduaneiros, contribuindo para organizar o fluxo antes da chegada ao porto. A Cosco, além da operação marítima, oferece soluções logísticas terrestres aos embarcadores. No modelo desenvolvido com a MRS e o Grupo Tora, a ferrovia funciona como elo entre a origem das cargas e o porto de embarque, onde a armadora mantém rotas marítimas e escalas semanais.

https://safety4sea.com/attacks-piracy-an.text: Global shipping faced one of its most dangerous quarters in recent history during Q3 2026, as attacks on merchant vessels increased across the Middle East and Black Sea, piracy returned to the Gulf of Aden and the use of false flags and dark-fleet tactics expanded, according to Windward’s latest analysis. T he Windward Q3 2026 Maritime Risk Report identifies a sharp deterioration in the maritime security environment, with Iran, Russia, Ukraine and the United States all carrying out strikes affecting commercial shipping during the quarter. The Strait of Hormuz emerged as one of the most acute areas of risk . Windward recorded 45 attacks on ships in the Middle East Gulf between July and September, compared with 25 in Q2 and 22 during February and March. The nature of the attacks also changed. Tankers accounted for 87% of vessels targeted, up from 28% in Q2, while 93% of attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz. Almost half of the vessels attacked belonged to national fleets of Gulf energy companies. Despite the attacks, shipping through the strait gradually recovered. UKMTO-recorded traffic increased from about 16 transits per day in the second half of July to around 31 in the final week of September, although this remained well below the pre-war average of 138. Much of the recovery came from U.S.-facilitated southern-corridor convoys operating with AIS switched off. Windward estimates that dark convoy passages accounted for 47% of Hormuz traffic in August and 52% in September.

https://safety4sea.com/three-arrested-af.text: Spanish authorities have arrested three people at the Port of Algeciras after two of them allegedly boarded a container vessel disguised as port workers in an attempt to retrieve a shipment of cocaine. T he arrests followed a joint operation involving the Spanish Tax Agency and the Guardia Civil, after officers detected suspicious activity around the vessel while it was alongside the quay and cargo operations were underway. According to the authorities, Guardia Civil officers initially observed a personal watercraft behaving suspiciously near the containership. The craft subsequently approached the quay with three people on board. Two of the occupants reportedly disembarked and boarded the vessel, allegedly wearing clothing intended to make them appear as port personnel. Officers intervened and searched the ship, where they discovered two backpacks containing packages of a substance later identified as cocaine. The suspects are alleged to have removed the backpacks from a shipping container and concealed them after becoming aware of the presence of law enforcement officers. Meanwhile, a Guardia Civil patrol vessel intercepted the third suspect, who was piloting the personal watercraft used to transport the other two individuals to the containership. Authorities later established that the watercraft had been reported stolen in La Línea de la Concepción.

https://safety4sea.com/tanker-attack-off.text: A crude oil tanker caught fire off Russia’s Black Sea coast after an attack involving an unmanned vessel, prompting pollution concerns following the incident. T he Greek-owned, Liberian-flagged Aframax Rio was attacked off Sochi on October 6, according to Russian authorities and Reuters. All 23 crew members, who were Indian nationals, were safely evacuated and no injuries were reported. Meanwhile, the incident has raised particular concern because of the vessel’s role as an oil tanker. Greenpeace warned that an oil spill from the damaged tanker could have serious consequences for the Black Sea marine environment. Russian authorities, however, said no pollution had been detected. Sochi authorities closed nearby beaches as a precaution and continued monitoring air and water quality following the incident. The cargo aboard the Aframax Rio at the time of the attack has not been officially confirmed. Shipping data show that the tanker had been operating from Russian oil terminals, but its specific cargo and voyage at the time of the incident remain unclear. The tanker incident was one of several serious attacks involving merchant vessels in the Black Sea in recent days. On October 6, two commercial vessels were struck in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. The Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank, while the Palau-flagged Able was damaged and caught fire. The Able ‘s crew was rescued, while the search for the missing crew of the Alfa Watan was subsequently halted.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-maib-investiga.text: UK MAIB has issued an investigation report into an incident where a crew member was fatally injured after a passenger lift reactivated while he was inside the lift shaft during an inspection. A t about 0552 on 26 October 2025, the crew member on board a Bermuda registered passenger vessel was fatally injured. The vessel was on passage from Southampton, UK, to Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. The lift had been returned to normal operation for testing before the inspection and moved in response to a stored call signal while the crew member was inside the lift shaft. The investigation found that the inspection was not supported by a clearly communicated and mutually understood plan. Positive control of the lift had not been established before the crew member entered the lift shaft, and the work relied on self-resetting door interlocks that did not provide an effective barrier against lift movement. Following the accident, the vessel’s managers have taken action to reinforce lift maintenance procedures, communication arrangements and training requirements across their fleet. A recommendation has been made to the vessel’s managers to review the use of self-resetting lift door interlocks as a safety barrier during lift maintenance and inspection. The transport team had completed their troubleshooting and testing of the lift when the senior electrical technical officer (SETO) decided to test the lift and inspect the travelling cable L-bracket. At that stage, the lift had been returned to normal operating mode and remained capable of responding to lift calls.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 08/10/2026 – O Sistema de Desempenho Portuário (SDP) da Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) está de volta em uma nova plataforma tecnológica. A partir desta quinta-feira (8), as instalações portuárias já podem acessar o sistema reformulado, que ganhou layout modernizado e interface desenvolvida para tornar a navegação mais intuitiva e eficiente. O SDP reúne dados que permitem acompanhar o desempenho operacional dos portos organizados e das instalações portuárias autorizadas do país. A retomada do sistema é coordenada pela Gerência de Estatística e Avaliação de Desempenho (GEA), responsável pela gestão do SDP. Com a reativação da plataforma, as instalações portuárias deverão acessá-la para enviar as informações referentes às atracações e cargas. Os novos prazos para envio das informações referentes às desatracações ocorridas em cada mês foram apresentados durante o 33º Encontro do Sistema de Desempenho Portuário, realizado nos dias 24 e 25 de setembro, em Santa Catarina. Outra novidade é que o SDP passa a incorporar a função de gerenciamento de usuários, anteriormente realizada por meio do Sistema de Gestão de Usuários (SGU). Com a mudança, todas as instalações portuárias deverão possuir, até 20 de janeiro de 2027, um usuário máster cadastrado. Esse perfil será responsável pela inclusão e exclusão de usuários vinculados a cada instalação. Instalações que já possuem usuário máster: o usuário deverá acessar o SDP e gerenciar os colaboradores cadastrados;

Brasília, 8/10/2026 – A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) realizou, nesta quarta-feira (7), em Rio Grande (RS), a segunda sessão da Audiência Pública nº 06/2026 , que discute o processo de concessão do Sistema Aquaviário Integrado do Sul e Lagoa Mirim (SAIP Sul-Mirim). Realizado presencialmente, o encontro buscou aproximar as discussões da realidade local e ampliar a participação da comunidade, de representantes do setor aquaviário e de demais interessados na infraestrutura que será concedida. O projeto contempla as infraestruturas de acesso aquaviário aos portos de Rio Grande, Pelotas e Porto Alegre, além de trechos das hidrovias da Lagoa dos Patos, do Lago Guaíba e dos rios Jacuí, Caí, dos Sinos e Gravataí. Ao todo, a proposta abrange cerca de 510 quilômetros de vias navegáveis e prevê a estruturação do primeiro modelo de concessão hidroviária integrada do país. Durante a audiência, 68 participantes se inscreveram para apresentar subsídios à proposta. Desse total, 35 compareceram presencialmente e fizeram contribuições, com questionamentos e esclarecimento de dúvidas. As manifestações serão analisadas pela Agência e poderão contribuir para o aperfeiçoamento do projeto, incorporando diferentes perspectivas de usuários, operadores e demais atores envolvidos com o sistema aquaviário gaúcho. O contrato de concessão terá prazo inicial de 25 anos e prevê investimentos em obras de dragagem, monitoramento e modernização da infraestrutura de canais e hidrovias do Rio Grande do Sul. A iniciativa busca estruturar, de forma integrada, a gestão e a manutenção das vias navegáveis incluídas na concessão. A consulta pública permanece aberta até 14 de outubro para o recebimento de subsídios. Os interessados podem encaminhar suas contribuições exclusivamente por meio de formulário eletrônico.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/iran-clo.text: Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorized , sources said. Last week already saw the biggest number of attacks on tankers in the key waterway since the Iran war began - cutting the number of vessels trying to get through to the lowest in more than two months. Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Tehran told Reuters. It was part of a plan agreed by both Iran's political leaders and its Revolutionary Guards, the official added. "Iran has absolutely no intention of allowing control of the Strait of Hormuz to slip from its hands, and has plans ready to block routes that some regional countries have for exporting oil," a senior diplomat in the region briefed by Tehran told Reuters separately. "This could involve missile and drone attacks on ships, or sending boats to scare ships away," the diplomat added. "It plans to continue this policy of fear and threats," he said.

https://gcaptain.com/tanker-attack-off-q.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 31, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer A chemical tanker was struck by multiple projectiles off the coast of Qatar on Wednesday, with casualties reported among its crew, in the latest attack on commercial shipping as violence spreads beyond the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred at approximately 1900 UTC on October 7, about 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) . In its warning, UKMTO said the tanker had been hit by multiple projectiles and that casualties had been reported. The agency did not specify how many seafarers were injured or killed, the extent of the damage, or the type of weapons involved. The vessel has since been identified as the Acers , an Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical and oil tanker. The location of the strike is particularly concerning. While most recent attacks have been concentrated in or near the Strait of Hormuz, Wednesday’s incident occurred farther west in the Persian Gulf, raising questions about the risks facing tankers operating well beyond the contested waterway. The attack comes amid a sharp escalation in violence against commercial shipping. At least 12 oil and gas tankers were attacked between September 28 and October 5, according to Reuters, making it the most intense week of tanker attacks since the war with Iran began in February.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/syria-ca.text: Syria called on the International Maritime Organization and Bulgarian authorities on Thursday to conduct an independent investigation into the sinking of a cargo ship in the Black Sea, whose 10 crew members including 9 Syrians were missing. The investigation should look into why search and rescue operations stopped before the fate of the missing crew was determined, said Mazen Aloush, director for international relations of the Syrian General Authority for Ports and Customs. Bulgaria said on Wednesday it had halted its search for the crew of a ship that sank after being hit by a drone about 70 nautical miles (130 km) off its coast. Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov said no trace of the sailors had been found and that the rescue operation would not resume. The ship, the Alfa Watan, was attacked early on Tuesday in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, Aloush said. Aloush added the authority was closely monitoring the incident and condemned the targeting of a civilian commercial vessel, saying it represented a serious violation of maritime safety and a direct threat to sailors' lives, as well as international trade routes. He urged authorities to use all available technical means to locate and inspect the wreckage to help establish the cause of the incident, and said the case should not be closed before all available avenues had been exhausted to determine the crew's fate.

https://petronoticias.com.br/technipfmc-.text: A TechnipFMC fechou um contrato com a Petrobrás para o fornecimento de sistemas de dutos flexíveis destinados a projetos offshore no Brasil. O acordo, conquistado após processo de concorrência, contempla o desenvolvimento de soluções para diferentes campos do pré-sal. Classificado pela TechnipFMC como “significativo”, o contrato tem valor entre US$ 75 milhões e US$ 250 milhões. O pedido foi contabilizado pela companhia na carteira de encomendas do terceiro trimestre de 2026. Pelo acordo, a TechnipFMC será responsável pelo projeto, engenharia e fabricação de linhas de fluxo flexíveis que serão utilizadas nas operações da Petrobrás. A execução contará com capacidades locais de engenharia, fabricação e cadeia de suprimentos, reforçando a participação da indústria brasileira nos projetos de produção offshore. “ Este contrato destaca a confiança que a Petrobras continua depositando na capacidade de execução da TechnipFMC. Nossas soluções flexíveis e os esforços contínuos de industrialização nos permitem oferecer maior eficiência, consistência e previsibilidade ”, afirmou Jonathan Landes , presidente da área Subsea da TechnipFMC. Segundo o executivo, a empresa pretende apoiar o desenvolvimento dos projetos offshore da Petrobrás, contribuindo para o cumprimento dos cronogramas e para o desempenho das operações. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://petronoticias.com.br/a-transpetr.text: A Transpetro assinou um contrato com a Petrobrás para a prestação de serviços de transporte rodoviário de combustíveis entre refinarias e terminais. O objetivo é ampliar a eficiência logística entre essas infraestruturas. Com a frota própria de 33 veículos, que serão movidos a diesel renovável, a Transpetro amplia sua atuação multimodal. O contrato prevê a atuação da Transpetro no transporte de bunker e óleo combustível em duas rotas inicialmente, entre a Refinaria Presidente Getúlio Vargas (Repar), em Araucária (PR), e o Terminal de Paranaguá (Tepar), em Paranaguá (PR), e entre a Refinaria Alberto Pasqualini (Refap) e o Terminal de Niterói (Tenit), ambos em Canoas (RS). Para atender a essa demanda, a Transpetro investiu cerca de R$ 43 milhões na aquisição de 33 caminhões-tanque e firmou uma parceria com a Budel Transportes, empresa especializada na gestão operacional de cargas de combustíveis. O presidente da Transpetro, Sergio Bacci, disse que “ O novo modal será utilizado especialmente em operações de conexão entre ativos logísticos do Sistema Petrobras e atendimento da chamada última milha. A iniciativa integra a estratégia de multimodalidade da companhia e tem início de operação previsto para janeiro de 2027. As primeiras rotas serão implantadas na Região Sul, com previsão de movimentação superior a 50 mil toneladas de combustíveis por mês.” Nos últimos anos, a Transpetro tem investido para ampliar seu portifólio de serviços. Ainda neste ano, a companhia inicia a operação no modal de navegação interior (em águas protegidas, como rios, lagos, canais, baías e lagoas) com barcaças adquiridas para o transporte de bunker nos principais portos do país. A estreia desse modal será no Rio de Janeiro, mas a Transpetro também ofertará esse serviço em Santos (SP), Belém (PA), Paranaguá (PR) e Rio Grande (RS). Desde o final de 2025, a Transpetro também atua no apoio marítimo e no controle de emergências em áreas de exploração de petróleo operadas por consórcios liderados pela Petrobras. Os caminhões dessa frota serão movidos à Diesel R, biocombustível desenvolvido pela Petrobras e que tem conteúdo renovável de óleos vegetais e/ou gordura animal. As primeiras operações ocorrem a partir de janeiro de 2027 e são focadas no transporte de pequenas distâncias, onde o transporte rodoviário se torna um modal mais eficiente. Na rota paranaense, a Transpetro estima uma movimentação mensal de 36 mil toneladas de produtos e na rota gaúcha a previsão é de uma carga de 18 mil toneladas por mês. O contrato prevê o transporte de óleo combustível e bunker e atende a demanda exclusiva da Petrobrás. A expansão para outras operações dependerá de avaliações de viabilidade técnica, operacional e econômico-financeira. © 2026 Petronotícias. Todos os direitos reservados. Montagem e

https://petronoticias.com.br/a-constella.text: A Constellation, maior empresa de perfuração offshore do Brasil, recebeu da American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) o certificado Approval in Principle ( AiP ) para o projeto Fuel Processor (Processador de Combustível), uma tecnologia inovadora desenvolvida para aumentar a eficiência energética e reduzir emissões em motores diesel utilizados em unidades offshore. O AiP valida a segurança e a fundamentação técnica de soluções disruptivas para as quais a regulamentação convencional ainda está em desenvolvimento, ajudando a viabilizar o avanço seguro para a fase operacional. O projeto, contratado no final de 2025 e com vigência prevista até 2028, é desenvolvido em parceria com a Petrobrás, com recursos da cláusula de Pesquisa, Desenvolvimento e Inovação (PDI) da Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP). A iniciativa conta ainda com a participação da Clean Energy Power Systems (CEPS) e da PUC-Rio como terceira parte independente para validação dos resultados. Atualmente, a tecnologia está em fase de implementação e testes a bordo do navio-sonda Laguna Star. Em fase piloto, o Fuel Processor busca aumentar a eficiência da combustão dos motores diesel, contribuindo para a redução do consumo de combustível e das emissões associadas às operações offshore. “ A Constellation aposta em tecnologias disruptivas como ferramenta para acelerar a descarbonização de suas operações. O reconhecimento da ABS reforça a consistência técnica dessas iniciativas e sua contribuição para os compromissos estabelecidos em nosso Plano ESG 2030 “, destaca Leonardo Guimarães , Diretor Técnico da Constellation. Além da entrega do AiP , a Constellation e a ABS assinaram um Memorando de Entendimento voltado ao avanço de novas tecnologias de descarbonização para o setor offshore. O acordo estabelece bases para o desenvolvimento de discussões técnicas, diretrizes e futuras iniciativas de certificação relacionadas à hibridização por meio de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias e às operações em barramento fechado (closed bus), soluções consideradas promissoras para ampliar a eficiência operacional e reduzir emissões nas atividades offshore. Enquanto o Fuel Processor e o projeto de Gêmeo Digital, desenvolvido em parceria com a Petrobras e a Universidade de São Paulo (USP), avançam em implementação, a nova cooperação com a ABS amplia o portfólio de iniciativas da Constellation voltadas à inovação tecnológica, eficiência operacional e descarbonização de suas operações. © 2026 Petronotícias. Todos os direitos reservados. Montagem e manutenção ECCE.COM.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A CMA CGM e a DSV assinaram um acordo sob o qual a DSV utilizará a solução de transporte marítimo de baixo carbono ACT+ da CMA CGM para apoiar uma meta de redução de 12.000 toneladas de emissões de CO₂ ao longo de dois anos. Essas reduções de emissões serão alcançadas por meio do uso de combustíveis de baixo carbono, especificamente biocombustíveis de segunda geração baseados em UCOME (óleo de cozinha usado). Como parte de seu compromisso de atingir o Zero Carbono Líquido (Net Zero Carbon) até 2050, a CMA CGM desenvolveu a ACT+, sua linha de soluções de transporte de baixo carbono projetada para ajudar os clientes a reduzirem suas emissões de CO₂. Por meio deste acordo, a DSV se beneficiará da ACT+, que pode ajudar a reduzir as emissões de CO₂ em 83% em comparação ao combustível marítimo convencional, mediante o uso de combustíveis de baixo carbono. Esta parceria reforça o relacionamento de longa data entre a CMA CGM e a DSV e apoia o compromisso da DSV em alcançar emissões líquidas zero em todas as suas operações e cadeia de valor até 2050. Também reflete uma tendência crescente de mercado, com a DSV se juntando a um número cada vez maior de empresas líderes que escolhem ou renovam seu compromisso com a ACT+ como parte de suas estratégias de descarbonização. Pioneira na descarbonização do transporte marítimo, a CMA CGM foi a primeira empresa de navegação a assumir um compromisso em grande escala com a propulsão a GNL (Gás Natural Liquefeito) para navios porta-contêineres de grande porte, após uma decisão estratégica tomada pelo Presidente e CEO Rodolphe Saadé em 2017. Esse compromisso levou à entrega, em 2020, do CMA CGM Jacques Saadé, o primeiro porta-contêineres de 23.000 TEUs movido a GNL do mundo. Desde então, a CMA CGM continuou a acelerar sua transição, lançando a ACT com a CMA CGM+ em 2020 e, em 2026, o CMA CGM NOTRE DAME, o maior porta-contêineres atualmente operando sob a bandeira francesa e o primeiro de uma série de dez navios movidos a GNL de nova geração com capacidade de 24.212 TEUs. Até 2031, a CMA CGM prevê operar cerca de 200 navios de combustível duplo (GNL e metanol) capazes de usar energias de baixo carbono. Essas iniciativas fazem parte da estratégia mais ampla de descarbonização da CMA CGM, que visa alcançar o Zero Carbono Líquido até 2050 por meio da melhoria da eficiência energética, da adoção acelerada de energias de baixo carbono e da colaboração próxima com clientes, fornecedores e partes interessadas do setor. "Na DSV, reduzir as emissões nas cadeias de suprimentos globais exige uma forte colaboração e soluções escaláveis. Por meio de nossa parceria com a CMA CGM e do uso da solução ACT+, estamos expandindo o acesso a opções de transporte marítimo de menor emissão de carbono para nossos clientes. Este acordo reflete nosso

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: Imports into the U.S. continue to defy predictions with a strong series of months through the summer, but are now projected to level off. The National Retail Federation reports that after a “drawn-out peak shipping season,” it believes retailers are mostly stocked for the remainder of the year and imports will slow, in part reflecting a cautious consumer outlook. “Most holiday merchandise has arrived, and the remainder of the year is just a matter of last-minute replenishment and preparation for early 2027,” said NRF Vice President for Supply Chain and Customs Policy Jonathan Gold. “The truth is that the peak season started early and was stretched out through the summer and early fall, with the difference from month to month often amounting to little more than a rounding error.” Total imports for September, however, appear to have defied expectations and continued a string of strong months. Technology provider Descartes Systems expects U.S. container exports reached 2.55 million TEU. It represented a better-than-10 percent increase versus last year, and Descartes says it is likely a new record month. Driving the strong volumes, Descartes says, were imports of retail goods, such as plastic goods, furniture, bedding, toys, and sporting goods. It points to more than 924,000 TEU coming from China. Chinese volumes, it says, were a third of total U.S. volumes (36 percent). It was likely in part driven by the potential expiration of the trade tariff truce between the U.S. and China, which was extended during the summit in Washington, D.C. The NRF reports 2.28 million TEU for retail imports coming through the top U.S. ports. It believes the volumes were likely off slightly from August, when 2.3 million TEU were imported. Volumes, it notes, were up between July and August but down slightly from last year. The retail trade association expects strong increases over last year’s volumes, but the import volumes will level off with October at a forecasted 2.25 million TEU. It predicts November and December will fall to around 2 million TEU per month. It sees a slight rebound in January 2027 at 2.07 million TEU and a decline in February to 1.92 million TEU, in part due to a shorter month and Chinese holidays.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: Following yesterday's tanker attack in the central Arabian Gulf, Brent oil futures climbed to $104 per barrel, Dated Brent hit $136, and benchmark Gulf-East Asia tanker rates passed the $1.4 million per day mark - all reflecting expectations of a heightened risk of Iranian attack for energy shipping in and out of the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel hit in the central Gulf on Wednesday has now been identified as the Antigua-flagged product tanker Acers (IMO 9301902), according to multiple maritime security sources. EOS Risk Group's Martin Kelly reports that Acers was hit by three drones, damaging the funnel and the upper decks of the superstructure while also sparking a fire in the engine room. The blaze has since been put out, he reports. Additionally, UKMTO reported another attack on an unnamed crude oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a rapidly growing series. On Wednesday evening, shortly after 1700 hours UTC, a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile off the Musandam Peninsula. No casualties were reported, and the agency had no further informtion on the damage assessment. It was the 13th strike of the month, according to UKMTO's public tally. Privately, officials told the New York Times on Thursday that the count is closer to 20 ships affected. A limited body of evidence suggests that another tanker may have been hit Wednesday in the Gulf of Oman, on the eastern side of the strait. NASA FIRMS infrared sensing data corroborates Iranian-source claims of an attack on a vessel off Fujairah, east of the port's busy tanker anchorage. "If confirmed, [this] would indicate Iran is targeting feeders and shuttle runners outside of [Hormuz]," said Kelly. If Iran expands its anti-tanker campaign beyond the narrow waters of the strait, the threat to shipping would extend beyond the protection of the U.S. military's heavy patrol presence around the Musandam Peninsula - and out into areas where defensive assets are more thinly spread. U.S. forces are not going to be responding to the concerted campaign of Iranian attacks with escalation, at least before the U.S. midterm elections are over, President Donald Trump said on Thursday. "While Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and while the blockade will remain in full force and effect . . . we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3," Trump said in a statement.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: As Hurricane Isaias closes in on the Gulf coast, the National Hurricane Center is warning residents from eastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle to get ready for a "life-threatening storm surge." Isaias intensified as expected overnight Wednesday, and the latest Hurricane Hunters flight into the storm suggest surface wind speeds in the range of 85 knots. The system is moving swiftly at about 10 knots to the northeast, and is expected to turn to the north, putting it on track to make landfall somewhere in the vicinity of the Panhandle late Friday night. Isaias is moving over warm waters in the northern Gulf, conditions that would normally favor intensification. However, intensifying vertical wind shear will likely offset the effect as the storm gets closer to shore. The relative impact of these two competing factors remains to be seen, but in all events, "Isaias is expected to remain a dangerous hurricane through landfall," the center warned. The worst of the storm's winds will be concentrated along the coasts of Mississippi, Alabama and the Panhandle, home to the heart of the Gulf shipbuilding industry. But the storm surge - often the most dangerous element of a hurricane - will extend further, from the mouth of the Mississippi eastwards to Suwannee, Florida. To prepare, the U.S. Coast Guard Heartland is getting ready to reconstitute its forces for post-storm recovery, and it warned on Thursday that this process typically means that its ability to perform SAR operations will be reduced in the run-up to the hurricane's arrival. It advised boaters to secure their craft, ensure that EPIRBs can't come loose and activate, and monitor the National Hurricane Center's alerts. Coast Guard Sector Mobile has set Condition Yankee and advised commercial shipping to prepare to depart port or contact the Captain of the Port for alternatives. Long before it makes landfall, the storm will sweep past offshore oil and gas infrastucture at the eastern edge of the Gulf oil patch. According to the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement - recently folded into the new Marine Minerals Administration - fully 121 production platforms have been evacuated in the Gulf as a precautionary measure, about one third of the offshore production footprint. Another five non-DP rigs have been evacuated, and four DP rigs have repositioned off location to avoid the worst of the wind and waves.

Goltens Worldwide, long recognized as a leader in planning and performance maintenance and repair work, has agreed to be acquired by HD Hyundai Marine Solution (HMS). With HMS, Goltens says it sees considerable scope to invest, grow, and develop capabilities, while for HD Hyundai, it provides a critical opportunity to expand its aftermarket support globally. The proposed acquisition, the companies explained, offers opportunities to expand technical capabilities, strengthen its global service coverage, and support investment in people, facilities, and technologies. Together, Goltens and HMS see significant potential to help customers meet increasingly complex maintenance, operational efficiency, and decarbonization requirements across the marine, energy, and industrial sectors. Goltens, which describes itself as the only independent repair specialist to offer all-inclusive worldwide service, says the deal will bring together its global engineering and service capabilities with the complementary strengths of HMS. Goltens says its global network of service centers and field engineering teams will create strong synergies with HMS, enabling the combined organization to better serve the growing aftermarket customer base, including the large fleet of vessels and engines built by HD Hyundai. The company says it works with over 3,000 shipowners, shipyards, industrial plants, and power stations annually. Established in 1940, Goltens currently has 28 locations in 15 countries. HD Hyundai highlights Goltens' strong expertise in maintenance, repair, and overhaul for 2-stroke and 4-stroke engines used in ships and land-based power plants, from a broad range of manufacturers. The South Korean company has been working to expand its role in the aftermarket. According to reports in the Korean media, HMS will acquire all the shares of Goltens for approximately $247 million. The transaction is anticipated to be completed in the late fourth quarter of 2026 or early first quarter of 2027. Following completion, Goltens will continue to operate as an independent service provider, maintaining the service approach, customer relationships, and technical expertise.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: The Galveston Wharves Board of Trustees has approved a lease and development agreement with Power LNG, which paves the way for the first LNG bunkering facility on the Gulf Coast. Power LNG plans to develop a small-scale, modular liquefied natural gas production, storage, and fuel bunkering facility on Pelican Island, with port officials highlighting that the project will position Galveston to serve the growing demand for LNG as a marine fuel both in the port and the region. The board approved the agreement that provides for a 30-acre greenfield development, which will be located on the east side of an approximately 82-acre, port-owned tract on the deep-water Galveston Harbor. It will be part of the port’s plan for the development of what it highlighted as one of Texas’ few underdeveloped large-scale deepwater port sites. The port owns 357 acres of prime waterfront acreage, including 100 acres on Galveston Harbor adjacent to the Gulf Cooper shipyard, which Davie Defense is developing into a shipbuilding facility for the Arctic icebreakers and other projects. Power LNG plans to develop an LNG facility capable of producing approximately 400,000 gallons per day. The facility will use two parallel liquefaction trains, each capable of producing about 200,000 gallons per day, with the potential to expand production at this site to 800,000 gallons per day using modular liquefaction technology. Power LNG also proposes to build an underground natural gas pipeline to provide feedstock to the facility, a 3-million-gallon LNG storage tank, and a shore-to-ship pier to fuel both ships and bunker vessels. Austin Terry, Power LNG CEO, highlighted that the company will develop a fully integrated LNG fueling solution, including liquefaction, storage, bunkering, vessel loading, and export capabilities. The facility is projected to begin commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2028, following completion of required approvals and agreements. Galveston highlights that Power LNG’s strategic partners and customers are expected to coordinate LNG bunkering operations, which may provide LNG fuel to ships calling at the Port of Galveston and other locations in the Galveston, Houston, and Texas City ship channels. “As more LNG-powered ships are built, demand for LNG marine fuel is reaching a tipping point,” said Rodger Rees, Galveston Wharves port director and CEO. “This facility will give Galveston an opportunity to support this growing market while further diversifying our port’s operations,” Rees said, predicting this development will pave the way for the Port of Galveston to play a leading role in providing cleaner marine fuels to the region.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/op-ed-por.text: Material handling hubs are seeing record throughput, with U.S. containerized imports reaching 2,603,709 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in August 2026—the third-highest monthly volume on record. Next year also promises tighter sustainability mandates, with upcoming EPA regulations sharply reducing allowable nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions by more than 80% and lowering particulate matter under real-world conditions. The combination of extreme weather conditions and heightened demand for power is already straining the electrical grid and is set to create long interconnection times for operations that simply can’t wait. And perhaps most prevalent, diesel prices are skyrocketing and predicted to continue to climb in 2027. The U.S. is experiencing record highs in diesel prices , and the Department of Energy predicts the average retail price will increase by 8.4%, or 33 cents per gallon, next year. The reality of supply chain and logistics today is that everything is going to keep increasing: throughput, strictness of sustainability mandates, grid demand, and diesel prices. Amid these challenges, there’s a solution that ports can adopt to alleviate all three pain points—a resilient, reliable, and renewable energy strategy built around alternative fuels like propane. Propane’s edge lies in its ability to deploy immediately on-site while hedging against economic volatility and dependence on the electrical grid, all while meeting the stringent requirements of sustainability mandates: The operational viability of propane as an enterprise-grade solution is already proven at major maritime hubs. At the West Basin Container Terminal (WBCT) at the Port of Los Angeles, the first U.S. port terminal to power its entire yard tractor fleet with propane—operators achieve an estimated $1 million in annual savings. Operating a fleet of 80 ultra-low NOx propane terminal tractors, WBCT benefits from fuel costs running at $6.17 per hour compared to $8.14 for diesel, all while realizing a 99.9% decrease in tailpipe nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions and a 75% reduction in total hydrocarbons. Material handling operations can’t halt when the next extreme weather event hits or when diesel prices are simply too high to work into budgets. Renewable energy, independent of the grid, is key to ensuring supply chains stay continuous and resilient, as cargo volumes continue to skyrocket. Alternative fuels give ports an advantage over sole diesel and electric power, and can seamlessly be integrated into energy strategies today.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/lr2.text: LR2 product tankers loaded on average 2.1 million barrels per day (mbpd) of clean products during the first three quarters of 2026, 0.8 mbpd less than in the same period of 2025. In 2025, more than 40% of clean product volumes carried by LR2s were loaded in the Persian Gulf, equivalent to 1.2 mbpd. Following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, this fell to 0.4 mbpd in 2026, accounting for just 18% of all clean product volumes loaded on LR2s. However, the decline in clean products has been more than offset by increased crude oil and heavy product volumes carried by LR2s. During the first nine months of 2026, these averaged 5.1 mbpd, up 1.8 mbpd year-on-year. “As a result, LR2s loaded 1.0 mbpd more during the first nine months of 2026 than in the same period of 2025, an increase of 15%,” says Rasmussen. Despite the increase in volumes, total tonne-mile demand rose by only 2% year-on-year in the same period. The average sailing distance fell 12% as volumes lost from the Persian Gulf were on longer-than-average trades, while new volumes were generally carried over shorter distances. Higher volumes from the Mediterranean and the Americas accounted for 80% of the increase in crude oil and heavy product volumes, although LR2s gained volumes in almost all loading regions. In the US and Canada, the increase in crude oil and heavy product volumes loaded on LR2s exceeded the overall increase in exports from both countries. LR2s also captured nearly 30% of the increase in Venezuela’s crude oil and heavy product exports.

https://gcaptain.com/supertankers-racing.text: Supertankers are racing to the Middle East to cash in on soaring fees for carrying oil through the Strait of Hormuz , exacerbating a global shortage of vessels that has spiked freight rates. Crude flows through the waterway, which connects the Persian Gulf to international markets, have recovered to near pre-war levels in recent weeks despite continued attacks on ships. But the perils of the trade have prompted tanker fees to skyrocket: Moving oil from the gulf to East Asia costs more than six times as much as it did prior to the conflict. More than 40% of the world’s fleet of about 850 very large crude carriers are now either in the Persian Gulf or within a couple of days sailing time from it, according to Signal Ocean, a shipping data provider. The concentration of vessels in the area is being exacerbated by the so-called shuttling trade where crude is transferred to other ships — which aren’t willing to take the risk of crossing Hormuz — in the Gulf of Oman or at new transshipment points, such as off the west coast of India. “The recent months have been have been the best of all time for crude tankers,” said Georgios Sakellariou, a freight analyst at Signal Ocean. “The major issue is that the ship-to-ship system outside Hormuz is inefficient and that’s really stretching vessel supply there and elsewhere.” The number of empty VLCCs heading to Atlantic Ocean ports has halved from a month ago, the Signal Ocean data show. The dearth of supertankers is also changing the composition of the oil fleet elsewhere, driving an increase in the amount of smaller vessels that don’t benefit from economies of scale like the larger carriers do.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/the.text: European ports are being remade. Long established as cargo-handling facilities, they are becoming multi-functional nodes at the intersection of the energy transition, digitalisation and infrastructure resilience: gateways for conventional trade, industrial platforms for renewable energy and sustainable fuels, receiving terminals for hydrogen, ammonia and captured CO2, and marshalling hubs for offshore wind. The transformation is not voluntary. It is driven by a prescriptive body of EU legislation spanning climate, transport, energy, competition, security, waste and industrial policy, binding on port authorities, terminal operators, shipping lines, fuel suppliers, service providers and Member States. The principal instruments are the FuelEU Maritime Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1805), the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804), the extension of the EU Emissions Trading System to maritime transport (Directive 2003/87/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/959), the revised TEN-T Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1679), the reformed State aid framework, the NIS2 and Critical Entities Resilience Directives, the Seveso III Directive, the Port Reception Facilities Directive and the EU Taxonomy. The first is the IMO’s Net-Zero Framework. Approved at MEPC 83 in April 2025, its adoption was adjourned at an extraordinary session in October 2025 by 57 votes to 49, and the session reconvenes in the autumn of 2026. Whether a global fuel intensity standard and carbon pricing mechanism is adopted, and in what form, determines whether the EU’s regional measures remain the operative constraint on shipping calling at European ports or become one layer of a two-tier system. The July 2026 EU ETS review proposal expressly anticipates the question. The second is the closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the outbreak of hostilities in the Gulf on 28 February 2026. Roughly a fifth of seaborne LNG and a third of seaborne crude normally transits the strait, and Europe draws 12% to 14% of its LNG from Qatar through it. Brent moved from below $60 at the start of 2026 to above $100, European gas prices rose by between 40% and 67%, and the Commission’s spring 2026 forecast revised its Brent assumption upwards by 46%. The consequences run through this analysis: the economics of LNG import terminals, the price assumptions underlying power purchase agreements, the political appetite for energy sovereignty investment, and the State aid framework itself, amended in April 2026 to accommodate the shock. They also explain why the EU Ports Strategy of March 2026 gives as much weight to security, dual-use capability and foreign ownership as to decarbonisation. https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: O juiz de direito Gustavo de Castro Campos , do TJSP (Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo) , foi encontrado parcialmente carbonizado dentro de um carro na Fazenda Aliança, em São João da Boa Vista, no interior de São Paulo, na noite desta quarta-feira (7). Nascido em Mogi das Cruzes, na região metropolitana de São Paulo, Gustavo tinha 45 anos e era formado em Direito pelo Centro Universitário Braz Cubas. Campos ingressou na magistratura paulista em 2014, como juiz substituto da 14ª Circunscrição Judiciária (CJ), em Barretos. Ao longo da carreira, também atuou na comarca de Tambaú. Atualmente, era titular da 2ª Vara da Comarca de Mococa . Em nota, o TJSP lamentou a morte de Gustavo e agradeceu a dedicação e as contribuições prestadas ao longo da carreira. O magistrado deixa uma filha de nove anos. O juiz Gustavo de Castro Campos, do TJSP (Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo), foi encontrado morto dentro de um carro na Fazenda Aliança, em São João da Boa Vista, no interior do estado, na noite desta quarta-feira. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, ao qual a CNN Brasil teve acesso, o veículo do magistrado foi encontrado em chamas na Estrada de Terra Euclides Dotta, na zona rural do município. Equipes da Polícia Militar e do Corpo de Bombeiros foram acionados e, no local, identificaram um corpo no banco do motorista, parcialmente carbonizado .

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Navy's carrier force has been carrying an unusually heavy load in the Mideast for years, and has been setting records with extended carrier deployments. Extensions come with well-known consequences: deferred maintenance causes unexpected issues, which cause delays during the next yard period, which can then cascade into delays for the yard itself and for other carriers in the fleet. The Navy is very good at performing on an extended deployment when asked, the service's second-in-command told a blue-ribbon panel on navy reform on Thursday - but its willingness to jump when ordered by a combatant commander comes at a cost, and that cost only becomes clearer down the line. "We're seeing artificially high combat surge ready rates because those ships are over there [in the Mideast], and they haven't been introduced back into maintenance," Vice Chief of Naval Operations Adm. James Kilby told the National Commission on the Future of the Navy in an unclassified hearing. "The problem will come when eventually they do come home. The industrial base will not be able to swallow that pill." To get a worn-down and late-returning carrier into the yard and back out again, Kilby said, the Navy has to triage the workload. Some maintenance has to be deferred, and necessary modernization work gets skipped in the interest of conserving time and shipyard capacity. "That's the piece that I think we need to be better at articulating and demonstrating: what the cost of this extension will be two years from now, so that [decisionmakers] see that and sign that bill," he said. Kilby also emphasized the impact of long operational deployments on Military Sealift Command, both on maintenance and on mariners. MSC's ships are civilian-crewed, and the command has long struggled with finding and keeping enough people to man its full fleet of naval auxiliaries - the oilers and dry stores ships that keep carriers running. Congress has recently provided MSC with legislative changes to provide mariners with more competitive pay and timely relief - a significant step forward - but the long deployments to the Mideast are offsetting that progress, Kilby said. "Relief of mariners on time is key to building their trust and having them want to work for [MSC], and now we're pulling that rubber band in the other direction now with the conflict we're in," he said. "More than just the material part, there's a human part that I think we've got to be thoughtful about." The Navy hopes that its future unmanned capabilities will be able to alleviate some of the burden on the carrier force, along with the destroyers, naval auxiliaries and thousands of crewmembers who provide support while under way. https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: On Wednesday, the U.S. Coast Guard arranged a medevac for a crewmember of the Ocean Gladiator, a U.S.-flagged tweendecker. On Tuesday morning, Ocean Gladiator was passing south of Hawaii on a long voyage from Baltimore to Manila when a crewmember developed a medical issue. The Ocean Gladiator requested a medevac from the Coast Guard, but was still too far out at sea for immediate assistance. At the time, the ship was operating about 540 miles to the southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii. The Coast Guard's SAR center in Honolulu made plans to arrange for a helicopter medevac once the ship got within flight range. In the meantime, the crew of Ocean Gladiator monitored the patient's condition and reported back on his status. On Wednesday morning, Ocean Gladiator approached to within 90 miles of the Big Island's shores. An MH-65 Dolphin helicopter aircrew flew out to meet the ship, and lowered their rescue swimmer carefully onto the vessel's starboard bridge wing. With assistance, the patient was loaded into a litter and hoisted up for transfer back to shore. The Coast Guard's video footage of the hoist shows that Ocean Gladiator had unusual deck cargo for the voyage: two 87-foot Marine Protector-class U.S. Coast Guard cutters, approved for tranfer and repainted for the Philippine Coast Guard, along with a fuel barge. The USCG has been decommissioning the Marine Protector-class gradually as newer Fast Response Cuters enter the fleet, and some have been set aside for transfer to the Philippines. Ocean Gladiator was built in 2010 and flagged into the U.S. registry in 2020. She is a tweendecker with twin 400-tonne heavy lift cranes, plus a third smaller crane forward. She has a capacity of 17,000 dwt or 1,000 TEU. The vessel is ice-classed, and is regularly chartered to Military Sealift Command for the annual Operation Deep Freeze supply mission to McMurdo Station, Antarctica. AIS data shows that the ship has resumed her commercial voyage.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543593-sh.text: Equinor has signed an agreement to sell a 30% interest in its Bay du Nord offshore oil project in Canada to Shell, bringing in a new partner as the companies work towards a final investment decision in early 2027. Under the agreement, Equinor will retain a 70% stake and remain operator of the project, located approximately 500 kilometers offshore Newfoundland and Labrador in the Flemish Pass basin. The development, estimated to require an investment of around $9.8 billion (C$14 billion), is expected to produce its first oil in 2031, subject to regulatory approvals, market conditions and the companies' investment decisions. Bay du Nord is planned as a phased subsea development connected to a floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel, with estimated recoverable resources exceeding 400 million barrels of oil in its initial phase. In April 2026, BW Offshore has signed a front-end engineering and design (FEED) agreement with Equinor for the Bay du Nord development offshore Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. The agreement follows BW Offshore’s selection as preferred bidder for the FPSO and marks the next phase of the project ahead of a potential final investment decision in 2027.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543589-tr.text: Offshore drilling contractor Transocean has added approximately $1.1 billion to its firm contract backlog following final approval of a previously announced agreement with Equinor and a new drilling contract with Shell offshore Norway. The company received final approval from Equinor in late September for an agreement covering three harsh-environment semisubmersible drilling rigs, converting approximately $1 billion in previously announced contract value into firm backlog. The agreement covers semi-submersible rigs Transocean Enabler, Transocean Encourage and Transocean Endurance, all operating in Norway. Separately, Transocean has been awarded a two-well drilling contract by Norske Shell for the Transocean Norge semi-submersible rig. The contract is expected to generate approximately $62 million in firm backlog, excluding additional services, and covers an estimated 120 days of drilling operations. Work is scheduled to begin immediately after the rig completes its previously awarded drilling programs in Norway. The agreement also includes an option for one additional well.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543586-va.text: Valeura Energy has started offshore installation work at its Wassana oil field redevelopment project in the Gulf of Thailand, marking a milestone in the development of a new central processing platform (CPP). The company confirmed the start of offshore installation in an October 9 update, following the early completion of onshore construction of the CPP earlier in the month. The platform and its supporting jacket were subsequently loaded onto vessels for transportation to the Wassana field, located in Block G10/48, where Valeura holds a 100% operated interest. The installation follows the completion of an oil export pipeline in September, which will connect the new CPP to a floating storage and offloading vessel. Valeura is targeting first oil from the new platform around the beginning of the second quarter of 2027, approximately two months earlier than originally planned. Development drilling is expected to begin in late 2026, with the company having arranged for the Shelf Enterprise drilling rig to start its charter on November 1.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543584-eq.text: Energy services company Weatherford International has secured a two-year extension of several strategic framework agreements with Equinor and been selected as the primary provider of completion systems for the Statfjord and Oseberg licenses on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. The agreements expand Weatherford's involvement in Equinor's offshore development and production operations in the North Sea. Under the extended contracts, Weatherford will provide integrated well completion technologies and services aimed at improving operational efficiency, well performance and production throughout the well lifecycle. The selection as primary completion systems provider for Statfjord and Oseberg adds to the companies' existing collaboration in offshore well construction and production operations. “We are pleased to continue expanding our collaboration with Equinor through these agreement extensions and the award of this important completions scope,” said Girish Saligram, Weatherford's President and Chief Executive Officer.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543585-vi.text: Azane Fuel Solutions has received approval from Norway's Directorate for Civil Protection (DSB) to conduct a test bunkering of up to 73 tonnes of ammonia aboard the Viking Energy platform supply vessel (PSV), marking a milestone in its conversion to ammonia propulsion. The operation is scheduled for October or November 2026 at Stord, Norway, as part of the commissioning of ammonia fuel systems being installed under the Apollo project. Ammonia will be transferred to the vessel from up to three tank trailers, allowing project partners to test the bunkering arrangements and onboard safety systems before the vessel enters ammonia-fueled offshore service. The Viking Energy PSV is owned and operated by Eidesvik Offshore, which aims to make it the world's first ammonia-powered platform supply vessel and demonstrate the technology during operations for Equinor in the North Sea. The Apollo project has received $5.6 million (€5 million) in EU funding to install a dual-fuel ammonia engine and associated fuel supply system aboard the vessel. An order for the Wärtsilä 25 engine and complete fuel supply system was placed in July 2024. Azane has reviewed safety plans for the operation with the local fire and rescue service.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: A proposta defendida pelo candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) de acabar com a reeleição e ampliar a duração do mandato presidencial depende de uma mudança na Constituição Federal para entrar em vigor. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543582-us.text: US producers in the Gulf of Mexico shut in about 1.3 million barrels per day of oil production and 1.1 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas as Hurricane Isaias blew through the corridor ahead of an expected landfall somewhere between southern Alabama and the Florida Panhandle later this week. The shut-ins represent roughly 63% and 57% of US oil and natural gas production in the Gulf, respectively, according to the Marine Minerals Administration. Oil prices rose 4% on Thursday, partly due to mounting supply disruptions as the hurricane approached. O/R Personnel have been evacuated from 121 production platforms, representing 33% of the 371 manned platforms in the Gulf, and workers had been removed from five of 11 non-dynamically positioned rigs, it said. Four of the Gulf's 17 dynamically positioned rigs moved off location as a precaution to avoid the hurricane's path, the agency said. On Wednesday, 25% of oil production and 16% of natural gas output had been shut in.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543587-ge.text: The topsides and jackets for two offshore substations serving Germany's 927 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm have departed the Netherlands for installation in the Baltic Sea as part of the OST-6-1 offshore grid connection project. The OSS Zingst and OSS Darß substations are being delivered by the HSI joint venture, comprising Smulders HSM and Iv, under an engineering, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning (EPCIC) contract. The substations, each with a capacity of approximately 450 MW, will form part of the infrastructure connecting Skyborn Renewables' Gennaker offshore wind farm to transmission system operator 50Hertz's onshore grid. The topside and jacket for OSS Zingst departed from Schiedam, while the corresponding structures for OSS Darß sailed from Vlissingen. Their departure follows the completion of engineering, procurement, fabrication, assembly and systems integration activities across the two Dutch yards. The HSI joint venture is responsible for the full EPCIC scope of both substations, including transportation, offshore installation and commissioning.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A indústria de implementos rodoviários registrou 109.715 emplacamentos de janeiro a setembro de 2026, queda de 1,47% em relação às 111.355 unidades do mesmo período de 2025. Já o segmento de Carroceria sobre chassis somou 55.941 unidades no acumulado de 2026, contra 57.698 no mesmo intervalo do ano passado, uma retração de 3,05%. Para José Carlos Spricigo, presidente da Associação Nacional Fabricantes de Implementos Rodoviários (ANFIR), o desempenho dos Reboques e Semirreboques indica uma possível consolidação da recuperação do mercado. “O desempenho do setor de Reboques e Semirreboques pode ser um sinal de que estamos a caminho do equilíbrio, indicando que a recuperação está se consolidando”, afirma. Segundo o executivo, a realização da Fenatran, em novembro, também pode contribuir para os resultados dos meses seguintes. “Como teremos a Fenatran em novembro, com reflexos positivos nos negócios ao longo de pelo menos os quatro meses seguintes podemos estar diante da possibilidade de realizamos um resultado pouco acima de 2025”, completa.
