A GEE (Gestão Eficiente de Embalagens) , operadora de pool de paletes reutilizáveis , estima que seu modelo de recuperação, manutenção e reutilização de ativos evitou potencialmente 6.959,8 toneladas de CO₂ equivalente (CO₂e) em 2025 . O cálculo considera um cenário alternativo no qual novos paletes precisariam ser fabricados continuamente e descartados após o uso. No mesmo ano, o inventário de emissões da empresa contabilizou 856,85 toneladas de CO₂e emitidas pela operação. Os números fazem parte do primeiro relatório de sustentabilidade da companhia, que reúne indicadores ambientais, sociais e de governança. Em 2025, a GEE movimentou mais de 1,8 milhão de paletes, encerrou o ano com 162 clientes ativos e destinou 135,8 toneladas de resíduos de madeira à reciclagem e ao reaproveitamento energético, sem envio para aterros. Cada palete pode completar até 20 ciclos de reutilização. O inventário foi elaborado com base na metodologia do Programa Brasileiro GHG Protocol e alinhado à ISO 14064. O levantamento abrange as emissões diretas e indiretas dos Escopos 1, 2 e 3 da unidade de Cabreúva, na região metropolitana de São Paulo. Do total contabilizado, 99,1% correspondem ao Escopo 3, concentrado principalmente no transporte realizado por terceiros, apontado como o principal desafio para a redução das emissões da cadeia de valor. A estimativa de emissões potencialmente evitadas considera os efeitos da recuperação, manutenção, rastreamento e reutilização dos paletes. Segundo a empresa, os benefícios ambientais estão relacionados sobretudo à menor necessidade de fabricar novos ativos e ao desvio de resíduos de madeira dos aterros. “Cada palete que retorna ao nosso Centro de Serviços representa madeira preservada, resíduos evitados e emissões que deixam de ser geradas. Este relatório marca um passo importante na nossa jornada de transparência e reflete os números que temos, os compromissos que assumimos e a consciência de que ainda há muito a evoluir”, afirma Augusto Canozo, sócio-gerente da GEE. A operação é monitorada pelo GEEnet, sistema que gerencia pedidos, coletas, estoque, inventário e faturamento. Em 2025, a plataforma passou a se conectar diretamente à Secretaria da Fazenda para capturar automaticamente arquivos XML de notas fiscais, reduzindo o retrabalho e ampliando a segurança das informações. Para 2026 a 2030, a empresa prevê aumentar as movimentações anuais de 1,8 milhão para 4 milhões de paletes, expandir a malha logística, incorporar inteligência artificial ao GEEnet 2.0 e aprimorar os dados do inventário de carbono, além de desenvolver iniciativas para reduzir as emissões da cadeia de valor. Na área de gestão de pessoas, as mulheres representam 41% do quadro de colaboradores. A companhia também implementou ações voltadas ao clima organizacion

O Supernorte , varejista alimentar da Região Norte do país, reduziu em 43% o estoque total e diminuiu a ruptura de produtos de aproximadamente 17% para 11% em 12 meses , após implementar o sistema de planejamento de distribuição e reposição de estoques DRP (Distribution and Requirements Planning), da Neogrid . No mesmo período, o tempo necessário para o fechamento dos pedidos caiu 80%. O projeto teve início em fevereiro de 2025 e envolveu a qualificação da base de dados e a revisão dos parâmetros de planejamento, considerando características dos produtos, das lojas e o comportamento da demanda. A ferramenta passou a apoiar a operação com previsões e recomendações de compra, inclusive em situações nas quais havia pouco ou nenhum histórico de vendas. Antes da implementação, parte do processo de abastecimento dependia de atividades manuais e da intervenção das equipes para definir os pedidos. Com a adoção do DRP, o Supernorte passou a utilizar indicadores de ruptura, cobertura de estoque e aderência dos pedidos, além de capacitar as equipes para incorporar as recomendações à rotina. "O DRP trouxe mais segurança para nossas decisões de abastecimento. Hoje conseguimos trabalhar com mais previsibilidade, reduzir estoques e, ao mesmo tempo, evoluir a disponibilidade e a agilidade da operação", afirma Helio Pompeu, gerente do Supernorte. Além da redução dos estoques e da queda na ruptura, o projeto alcançou 98,5% de aderência aos pedidos, indicador que, segundo a empresa, demonstra a incorporação das recomendações de abastecimento à rotina operacional. A mudança buscou equilibrar dois fatores da operação do varejo alimentar: a necessidade de manter os produtos disponíveis nas lojas e o controle do capital imobilizado em estoque. A partir da combinação de dados, revisão de processos e capacitação das equipes, a empresa passou a estruturar as decisões sobre quanto, quando e onde abastecer.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/121_gulf_pl.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone late Thursday, the Marine Minerals Administration (MMA) revealed that personnel had been evacuated from a total of 121 production platforms in the Gulf, based on data from offshore operator reports submitted as of 11am CDT yesterday. That represents 32.61 percent of the 371 manned platforms in the Gulf of America, the MMA highlighted, noting that production platforms are the offshore structures from which oil and natural gas are produced and transported to shore. The MMA pointed out in the statement that, unlike drilling rigs, which typically move from location to location, production facilities remain in the same location throughout a project’s duration. The statement also revealed that personnel had been evacuated from five non-dynamically positioned rigs, which it noted was equivalent to 45.45 percent of the 11 rigs of this type currently operating in the Gulf. Rigs can include several types of offshore drilling facilities including jack up rigs, platform rigs, all submersibles, and moored semisubmersibles, the statement highlighted. Four of the 17 dynamically positioned rigs in the Gulf have moved off location out of the storm’s path as a precaution, according to the MMA, which noted that dynamically positioned rigs maintain their location while conducting well operations by using thrusters and propellers. These rigs are not moored to the seafloor, so they can move out of harm’s way in a relatively short time frame, the MMA stated, adding that personnel remain on board and return to the original location once the storm has passed. In its statement, the MMA outlined that, from operator reports, it estimates that approximately 62.89 percent of the current daily oil production and 57.35 percent of the current daily natural gas production in the Gulf of America has been shut in. The production percentages are calculated using information submitted by offshore operators in daily reports, the MMA noted. Shut-in production information included in these reports is based on the amount of oil and gas the operator expected to produce that day, the MMA said, adding that the shut-in production figures are estimates that the MMA compares to historical production reports to ensure the estimates follow a logical pattern.

https://safety4sea.com/worlds-first-ammo.text: The world’s first ammonia-powered dry bulk carrier, Mineral Europa , has successfully completed its sea trials and is preparing for its maiden voyage to Australia, marking a significant milestone in the development of alternative-fuel propulsion for deep-sea shipping. T he vessel, operated by CMB.TECH, demonstrates the potential of ammonia-powered engines to propel large ocean-going ships and represents the first step in the company’s planned expansion of ammonia-fuelled vessels across its fleet. CMB.TECH describes Mineral Europa as the beginning of a new phase in maritime propulsion, with ammonia emerging as a potential pathway towards reducing shipping’s carbon emissions. The company plans to introduce 21 ammonia-powered vessels between now and 2029, comprising 18 dry bulk carriers, one container ship and two chemical tankers. Green ammonia is produced using renewable electricity, water and nitrogen extracted from the air, offering a potential alternative to conventional marine fuels. When used in an engine, ammonia contains no carbon and therefore does not produce CO₂ directly from fuel combustion. Its wider environmental benefits, however, depend on how the fuel is produced and supplied, as well as the emissions associated with its use onboard.

https://safety4sea.com/armed-small-boat-.text: An armed small boat opened fire on a containership transiting the Southern Red Sea on 7 October, prompting renewed security concerns in the strategically important shipping corridor. A s reported, all crew members were reported safe following the incident, according to the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean (MSCIO), which operates as part of the EU Naval Force. The incident occurred at approximately 06:15 UTC, when the small boat fired at the vessel as it sailed north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The attackers subsequently moved away from the containership, although the circumstances surrounding their withdrawal remain unclear. Maritime security consultants identified the vessel as CUL Klang, operated by China United Lines (CULines). No immediate claim of responsibility was reported, and further details about the circumstances of the attack were not immediately available. The vessel was sailing from Port Klang, Malaysia, at the time of the incident. The ship’s Automatic Identification System (AIS) was displaying the message “China owned & CHN crew” following the incident. The attack adds to security concerns surrounding commercial shipping in the Red Sea, a key maritime route connecting the Indian Ocean with the Suez Canal and the Mediterranean.

https://safety4sea.com/mbf-battery-hybri.text: The global fleet of battery-powered commercial vessels has surpassed 2,000 ships, marking a significant milestone in the maritime industry’s transition towards lower-emission propulsion and energy systems. A ccording to the Maritime Battery Forum’s (MBF) Ship Registry, more than 2,000 commercial vessels equipped with batteries have either been delivered or are currently on order. Together, these ships represent approximately 2.4 GWh of installed battery capacity, highlighting the growing role of energy storage in maritime operations. The milestone reflects advances in battery technology and falling costs, which are helping expand electrification beyond smaller vessels operating on short routes. Syb ten Cate Hoedemaker, managing director of the Maritime Battery Forum, said the industry was approaching a turning point as battery-powered propulsion becomes increasingly viable for larger vessels. “Reaching 2,000+ ships marks a significant moment for marine electrification,” Hoedemaker said, noting that installations with capacities of up to 100 MWh per vessel could become a reality in the coming years. The MBF registry shows that hybrid propulsion remains the most common configuration among battery-equipped commercial vessels. Around 68% operate with batteries alongside another energy source, such as a diesel engine or hydrogen fuel cell. Plug-in hybrids account for a further 13%, while 18% of the fleet is fully electric.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-o.text: Heavy seas during a voyage from a supply base to an oil field caused approximately 15 containers to shift around one metre from port to starboard, despite being secured with tightened tugger wires. A ccording to the Marine Safety Forum, the movement also damaged an electrical cable on a refrigerated container, resulting in power loss and compromising the food cargo. The incident highlights the challenges of securing deck cargo for adverse weather, particularly when operational requirements influence cargo distribution and securing arrangements. It also raises wider questions about how vessels assess changing weather conditions, account for uneven cargo distribution and determine whether existing securing measures are adequate for the planned voyage. During transit from the supply base to the oil field, the vessel encountered heavy seas, with waves reaching approximately 7 metres and south-southeasterly winds of 40 knots. Despite the cargo being secured with tightened tugger wires, around 15 containers shifted approximately one metre from port to starboard. Additional cargo had been loaded on the port side to meet rig requirements and accommodate the positioning of the crane offshore. This uneven distribution increased the potential for cargo movement under the prevailing conditions.

https://safety4sea.com/dnv-energy-transi.text: The global energy transition is advancing, but not at the pace required to meet climate targets , with shipping among the hard-to-abate sectors facing the greatest challenge in moving away from fossil fuels, according to DNV’s Energy Transition Outlook 2026. D NV’s latest forecast points to a transition increasingly driven not simply by climate policy, but by energy security, industrial competitiveness and the strategic interests of individual countries. For shipping, that shift could prove as important as the development of new fuels themselves. The report forecasts that fossil fuels will still account for 51% of global primary energy in 2050, down from about 80% today. Oil demand is expected to recover from 163 EJ in 2026 to around 170 EJ in 2028 before entering a prolonged decline, reaching 83 EJ by 2060. Gas demand is expected to peak around 2035 at 191 EJ, although its subsequent decline will be slower than previously forecast. DNV says the expansion of hydrogen is proving more expensive than anticipated, while gas continues to displace coal in parts of manufacturing. For shipping, the implications are significant. The maritime sector remains heavily dependent on liquid fuels, while the alternatives needed to decarbonise long-distance transport — including advanced biofuels, hydrogen and hydrogen-derived fuels — are still scaling from relatively small bases. DNV identifies shipping, together with aviation and heavy industry, as sectors that continue to struggle to reduce emissions through cleaner fuels.

https://safety4sea.com/death-toll-rises-.text: The death toll from an explosion aboard an engineering vessel in Guigang, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China, has risen to three after two missing workers were found dead, local authorities said on 8 October. A ccording to China Daily, the two bodies were recovered at 04:20 and 09:08 local time on 8 October, respectively. Both workers were confirmed dead in a statement issued by the local emergency management bureau. The explosion occurred on Tuesday, 6 October, during spray-painting operations aboard the vessel. One worker was killed in the initial blast, while two others were reported missing. The recovery of their bodies brings the confirmed death toll to three. Two additional workers sustained minor injuries in the incident, according to the authorities. An investigation into the cause of the explosion is underway, while local authorities continue to manage the aftermath of the incident. Further details regarding the circumstances of the blast have not yet been released.

https://safety4sea.com/tokyo-mou-to-revi.text: The Tokyo Memorandum of Understanding (Tokyo MOU) will introduce a new method for calculating flag State and recognized organization (RO) performance, changing how these are assessed in its Annual Report and used to determine ship risk profiles under the New Inspection Regime (NIR). U nder the revised methodology, flags and ROs will be classified as high, medium or low performance according to their detention rates compared with the regional average. The classification will depend on whether each detention rate falls below the regional average, reaches or exceeds that average but remains below twice its level, or is equal to or greater than twice the regional average. The Tokyo MOU’s planned changes follow a similar move by the Paris MOU, which is revising its recognized organization (RO) performance methodology ahead of the amended EU Port State Control Directive, due to take effect on 6 July 2027. Both approaches compare detention rates with a regional or overall average and link detainable deficiencies to the RO that issued or endorsed the relevant statutory certificate. The International Association of Classification Societies (IACS) has raised concerns about the Paris MOU’s approach, warning that detention rates may not accurately reflect an RO’s actual involvement in deficiencies . It argues that operational, maintenance and crew-related issues can fall outside an RO’s direct control, potentially leading to misleading performance classifications and increased port State control (PSC) inspections for ships. IACS has called for further validation, appropriate statistical safeguards and open discussions with maritime stakeholders, while exploring possible appeal mechanisms and proposals to strengthen port State control officer training and oversight. Performance calculations will generally use detention data from the latest three calendar years. However, transitional arrangements will apply to RO performance calculations : Only one detention will be counted for each flag or RO per inspection, regardless of the number of detainable deficiencies attributed to it.

https://safety4sea.com/bimco-adopts-fram.text: BIMCO has adopted the Energy Saving Device Retrofit Addendum 2026, a new contractual framework aimed at facilitating investments in energy-saving technologies installed during a time charter. T he addendum is designed to help owners and charterers agree on how the costs, time implications and fuel-saving benefits of retrofit projects should be allocated. It comes as the shipping industry faces increasing pressure to improve fuel efficiency, comply with decarbonisation regulations and manage rising operational costs. BIMCO said retrofit investments have often been complicated by a misalignment of commercial interests. While shipowners may fund the purchase and installation of energy-saving equipment, charterers can receive some or all of the operational benefits through lower fuel consumption during the charter period. This has reduced the incentive for parties to implement retrofit projects, even when such projects could generate significant fuel savings and environmental benefits To remind, approximately 2.4 trillion dollars were invested in the energy transition in 2024 – a record high and a 20% increase from the average annual levels of 2022/23, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Stinne Taiger Ivø, Deputy Secretary General and Director of Contractual Affairs at BIMCO, explained that the addendum addresses this “long-standing commercial challenge” by providing a mechanism for parties to structure retrofit investments more effectively.

https://splash247.com/bimco-moves-to-bre.text: Shipping association BIMCO has adopted a new contractual framework designed to settle one of the industry’s longstanding commercial disputes: who pays for energy-saving upgrades when the charterer receives much of the financial benefit. The Copenhagen-based organisation announced that its Documentary Committee had approved the Energy Saving Device Retrofit Addendum 2026, giving shipowners and charterers a standard framework for negotiating retrofit projects during existing time charters. The addendum covers how the two parties share installation costs, time implications and the financial gains generated by lower fuel consumption. Rather than setting fixed percentages, it allows the parties to negotiate arrangements for individual projects. The framework addresses a mismatch in traditional time charter agreements. Shipowners typically fund equipment installed on their vessels, while charterers may capture much of the resulting fuel savings during the employment period. That division has complicated investment decisions even where upgrades offer measurable efficiency improvements. BIMCO said the addendum is technology-neutral and can accommodate different energy-saving systems, as well as the financial implications of existing and future environmental regulations.

https://gcaptain.com/eu-imports-record-1.text: Europe’s estimated bill reaches €7.88 billion through September as U.S. sanctions deadline adds uncertainty for Yamal’s specialized tanker fleet. The European Union imported a record 12.18 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas from Russia’s Yamal Arctic project in the first nine months of 2026, paying an estimated €7.88 billion, according to an analysis by German environmental group Urgewald. Shipments rose 9.5% compared with the same period last year, even as Yamal’s worldwide deliveries fell 1.3%. Europe received 167 cargoes, accounting for 85% of the project’s recorded deliveries by volume, according to Urgewald’s analysis of Kpler shipping data. The figures highlight Europe’s continuing importance to Russia’s Arctic gas trade despite the EU’s planned phaseout of Russian LNG imports. The bloc’s estimated bill included €2.88 billion in the first quarter, €3.08 billion in the second and €1.92 billion in the third. Third-quarter deliveries fell 13.6% year-over-year to 2.21 million tons. September shipments, however, reached 792,440 tons, slightly above the same month last year, with an estimated value of €818 million. The figures come ahead of an Oct. 18 deadline for the Trump administration to implement provisions of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, signed into law on Sept. 18.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/nyk-simu.text: Japanese shipping company NYK has conducted a maritime emergency response drill simulating the grounding of a large bulk carrier and a subsequent fuel oil spill in Japan's Seto Inland Sea. The full-day exercise, held on September 30, involved a simulated accident aboard an NYK-owned and operated bulk carrier managed by NYK Bulkship Partners (NBSP), an NYK Group company. The scenario involved a vessel approximately 300 meters long and measuring about 100,000 gross tons suffering steering failure while navigating waters off Kagawa Prefecture. The simulated steering failure caused the vessel to run aground in shallow waters, damaging a fuel oil tank and releasing oil into the sea. The exercise involved Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism's Maritime Bureau, the sixth Regional Coast Guard Headquarters and the Japanese Shipowners' Association. After receiving the initial accident report from NBSP, NYK activated its emergency response procedures, established communication channels with relevant parties and set up an accident response headquarters.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/viking-e.text: Azane Fuel Solutions has received approval from Norway's Directorate for Civil Protection (DSB) to conduct a test bunkering of up to 73 tonnes of ammonia aboard the Viking Energy platform supply vessel (PSV), marking a milestone in its conversion to ammonia propulsion. The operation is scheduled for October or November 2026 at Stord, Norway, as part of the commissioning of ammonia fuel systems being installed under the Apollo project. Ammonia will be transferred to the vessel from up to three tank trailers, allowing project partners to test the bunkering arrangements and onboard safety systems before the vessel enters ammonia-fueled offshore service. The Viking Energy PSV is owned and operated by Eidesvik Offshore, which aims to make it the world's first ammonia-powered platform supply vessel and demonstrate the technology during operations for Equinor in the North Sea. The Apollo project has received $5.6 million (€5 million) in EU funding to install a dual-fuel ammonia engine and associated fuel supply system aboard the vessel. An order for the Wärtsilä 25 engine and complete fuel supply system was placed in July 2024. Azane has reviewed safety plans for the operation with the local fire and rescue service.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/worlds-f.text: CMB.TECH's Mineral Europa, described by the company as the world's first ammonia-powered dry bulk vessel, has embarked on its maiden voyage to Australia, signalling a significant step forward for alternative-fuel shipping. The 210,000-deadweight-tonne vessel, built in 2026, is the first of 21 ammonia-powered ships scheduled to join CMB.TECH's fleet by 2029. The company's ammonia-powered newbuilding program comprises 18 dry bulk carriers, one container ship and two chemical tankers, with most of the vessels expected to be delivered within the next nine months. “Today marks a defining moment for CMB.TECH and for the shipping industry. After almost a decade of hard work, we are proving that decarbonising shipping is no longer a distant ambition. It is happening today,” said Alexander Saverys, Chief Executive Officer of CMB.TECH. Ammonia can be used as a marine fuel without producing carbon dioxide during combustion, although its overall emissions depend on how the fuel is produced and other emissions associated with its use. CMB.TECH is also investing in ammonia storage infrastructure and bunkering barges to support fuel supply to ocean-going vessels.

https://splash247.com/black-sea-grain-ex.text: Black Sea wheat exports are plunging at the height of the traditional shipping season as escalating attacks on commercial vessels and port infrastructure leave both Russia and Ukraine struggling to get their harvests to international markets. Fresh vessel-tracking data compiled by AXSMarine and published by Greek shipbroker Ursa show wheat loadings across the Black Sea slumped to just 1.6m tonnes in September, 77.8% below the 7.3m tonnes recorded in the same month last year. September volumes were also down 45.6% from August, with shipments falling to their lowest September level since 2017. The collapse is particularly striking given that August and September are normally among the busiest months for Black Sea grain exports as the new harvest comes to market. Across the first nine months of 2026, Black Sea wheat loadings reached 36.3m tonnes, down 12.2% year-on-year and the second-lowest January-to-September total since 2017. The deterioration comes as the maritime war spreads well beyond the immediate approaches to Russian and Ukrainian ports, increasingly threatening alternative grain export corridors. Earlier this week, the Turkish-owned general cargo ship Royad Mammadov, carrying corn from Ukraine’s Danube port of Izmail to Italy, sank following a drone attack in Romania’s exclusive economic zone, killing two seafarers.

https://splash247.com/splash-wrap-drones.text: Maritime war spread far and wide in the Black Sea and the Middle East this week, attacks increasing both in number and geographical scope. This week’s Maritime CEO interview was Bing Hou, who after four decades at sea and ashore, has developed ShipGod AI , which he described as an offline-first workspace giving each vessel its own digital environment and AI assistant. “The turning point for me was watching how much time good officers spend managing documents instead of being officers, and how much of what they know is never captured for the next crew,” Hou said. Over at Splash Ports , this week’s CEO interview was with Beth Branch, president and chief executive of the Port New Orleans . “We cannot predict every geopolitical development, but we can build capacity, strengthen partnerships and give customers more flexibility,” she told the new, fast-growing ports title. Also of interest in this week’s ports coverage, while driverless trucks are becoming a common sight at terminals around the world, there’s also a growing band of pioneers developing autonomous freight trains to move containers beyond a port’s perimeter, something Splash Ports took an in-depth look into yesterday. Meanwhile, SplashTech ’s lead feature this week tried to identify how to tell whether seafarers genuinely value the systems being introduced onboard . “If six months after introducing your platform the crew still maintains the same spreadsheet beside it, you haven’t really digitised anything. You’ve given them another system to update,” quipped Aristos Philis, chief executive of KeelX. And in big tech news for the container sector, HD Hyundai has just delivered what it says is the world’s first containership designed to eliminate manual lashing . The 13,000 teu vessel, which is methanol dual-fuelled, has been handed over to France’s CMA CGM after being built using HD Hyundai’s proprietary hybrid lashing-free system.HD Hyundai’s new arrangement extends cell guides above deck, allowing containers to be held in place without traditional lashing. The breakthrough centres on what HD Hyundai calls a portable bench, a standardised structure fitted between cell guides. The unit is the same size as a 40 ft container, meaning terminal cranes can handle it as part of normal cargo operations. Containers positioned outside the cell guides are secured directly to the hull using a newly developed twist-lock routing system.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A Polícia Civil prendeu nesta sexta-feira (9) o pastor Rafael Átila Teles. Ele é suspeito de abusar de ao menos 9 crianças na Baixada Fluminense. Uma vítima de 18 anos relatou ter sofrido abusos desde os 6 anos de idade. Ela decidiu denunciar após manter silêncio por 10 anos. A mãe da jovem soube dos abusos no ano passado. Na ocasião, a filha adotiva do pastor revelou que também teria sido vítima dele. Em gravações, Rafael Átila Teles menciona um erro cometido no passado. Ele afirma: "Eu vou me entregar, vou pagar pelo erro que eu cometi".

Transportes, saúde, comércio e bancos têm horários alterados na Região Metropolitana do Rio nesta segunda-feira (12). A mudança ocorre pelo feriado nacional de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. O Metrô Rio funciona das 7h às 23h na segunda-feira (12), e as UPAs municipais operam sem interrupção. Postos de atenção primária estarão fechados. Agências bancárias e postos do INSS fecham na segunda, mas canais digitais funcionam. Rodovias do estado projetam aumento na circulação de veículos. Com o feriado nacional de Nossa Senhora Aparecida e o Dia das Crianças, o g1 reuniu os horários de funcionamento dos serviços na Região Metropolitana do Rio nesta segunda-feira (12). https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Belgium’s CMB.TECH is highlighting that its nearly decade-long effort to develop and launch large ammonia-fueled ships is coming to fruition. It is highlighting that Mineral Europa (210,000 dwt) is entering service as one of 12 vessels it is chartering to Fortescue and as part of a larger fleet of 21 ammonia-powered ships due to enter service by 2029. The Saverys family and CMB.TECH have been at the forefront of advocacy for the development of ammonia as a marine fuel to achieve decarbonization of shipping. Alexander Saverys, CEO of CMB.TECH, is calling the vessels the beginning of the “propulsion revolution.” As Mineral Europa embarks on its maiden voyage to Australia, Saverys says it “proves that large ocean-going ships can be powered by ammonia.” Built by CSSC Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding Co., the vessel is equipped with a dual-fuel engine capable of using ammonia or conventional marine fuel. The engine was developed in a partnership with WinGD. The ship is 300 meters (984 feet) in length with a reported speed of 14 knots. It will operate under charter to Fortescue, transporting iron ore from Western Australia’s Pilbara region to China and other international markets. The vessel is being managed by Anglo-Eastern and owned by Bocimar, the dry bulk line within CMB.TECH. The ammonia is stored in liquid form in independent tanks that are located on the deck of the vessel, at a safe distance from the sides of the ship, reports CMB.TECH. Safety protocols were established, and all the crew must undergo training before boarding the vessel. CMB.TECH highlights that it is building a new fuel ecosystem needed to support the transition to clean shipping. It says the vessel will operate on “green ammonia,” which combines renewable power, water, and air to produce the fuel. It did not comment on the current availability of the fuel for the vessels. Mineral Europa joins Mineral Latvia , with the ships registered in Belgium. CMB.TECH reported in June 2026 that Fortescue would charter 12 Newcastlemax vessels, wth up to three being delivered with dual-fuel ammonia engines and due to enter service in 2026. It said the other nine would be built ammonia-ready and could be converted to operate on ammonia.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: For nearly a decade, the Outlaw Ocean Project, the non-profit journalistic organization that I founded, has produced high-impact investigative stories about lawlessness at sea and the variety of threats posed to the people and biodiversity of a space that covers two thirds of our planet. The oceans bear a heavy and largely invisible burden. The public usually takes it for granted, a forever self-replenishing resource that we use to fill our stomachs or line our wallets. Our journalism intends to stoke urgency and to help the public reimagine the oceans, less a grocery store than a library or a cathedral, a protected common. Aquaculture was meant to ease pressure on the oceans. By raising fish, fewer would need to be taken from the wild—or so the logic went. In practice, the opposite has occurred. More than a fifth of all marine life removed from the oceans is used for feed, primarily for farmed fish. And demand for farm-raised fish is increasing. More than half of the seafood eaten globally comes from aquaculture, which is a $313-billion industry and the fastest-growing segment of global food production. Over the past 5 years, an international team of journalists at The Outlaw Ocean Project examined the largely unaccounted-for toll of using food for feed. We focused on one of the world’s most important feed ingredients: fishmeal. Consisting of two dozen stories and documentary films, the Food for Feed investigation offers a sobering picture of what fish-farming really entails, including forced labor, avoidable worker deaths, rampant stench, lost livelihoods, civil unrest, illegal fishing, food insecurity and species disappearance. Obscured behind aquaculture’s well-marketed reputation for sustainability and clever, eco-friendly adaptation, most of these ills have remained invisible to the consumers of farmed fish. Until now. The reporting began by identifying the locations of more than 1,400 fishmeal factories across 64 countries—facilities responsible for nearly the entire global supply of this lucrative, protein-rich, dark-yellow powder and its oil counterpart. We assessed more than 2,400 ships tied to fishmeal production, operating in the waters of at least 30 countries.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps Navy issued a statement on Friday, taking credit for a series of recent attacks on tankers, saying it was increasing enforcement on non-compliant vessels and the range of strikes. This came as one new strike was confirmed, with several other incidents reported, and the International Maritime Organization showed that incidents related to the war have now passed the 100 mark. Concern is rising in the shipping community as Iran has escalated the rate of attacks during October. Kpler is reporting that crude exports are “sharply lower” this week. As of October 7, it says the level is down by approximately a third to just under 10 million barrels per day versus around 15.5 million barrels per day in September. Increasing the fears is the confirmed report of a tanker struck while anchored off the UAE on Friday morning. UK Maritime Trade Operations said multiple sources placed the vessel 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, with reports of a fire caused by the strike. It came just days after Iran struck another tanker off Qatar, the first strikes in the broader Gulf region in at least six weeks. Several of the security consultancies are reporting today’s strike was on a Chinese-owned VLCC, Gem No. 2 (302,783 dwt), registered in Panama and operating under charter to Trafigura. The reports said the fire had been extinguished, but the level of damage is unclear. The IRGC Navy did not take credit for this attack, but in its statement said “From now on, encounters with offending vessels will not be limited to the Strait of Hormuz, and any vessel that passes through an unauthorized passage anywhere in the region will be pursued and its punishment will be certain.” UKMTO has reported 15 or 16 incidents believed to have taken place since September, with a dozen in recent days. Further, it reports that since July, there have been 59 incidents, of which 41 involved commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The IMO, in its listing, shows that confirmed incidents since the start of the war passed 100 with the strike on the tanker ST1 (IMO 9256999) off Oman on Wednesday.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The guided-missile destroyer USS Arleigh Burke , namesake for her class, entered dry dock in Spain on Wednesday, October 7. The U.S. 6th Fleet is highlighting that it is the first time it has sent a forward-deployed vessel to a shipyard in Europe for maintenance. The U.S. Navy set up its Forward Deployed Regional Maintenance Center as part of a program that calls for more vessels to remain overseas in the deployed region while receiving maintenance. It has already carried out maintenance in the Pacific region and also sent several support ships to dry dock and to undergo overhauls at yards in South Korea and even India. “The dry docking of Arleigh Burke is a major milestone in expanding U.S. Navy forward-deployed maintenance capabilities in Europe,” said Vice Adm. J.T. Anderson, commander, U.S. 6th Fleet. “By integrating dry docking into planned maintenance periods overseas, the Navy is increasing material readiness for our forward-deployed warships.” The 9,000-ton displacement destroyer was commissioned in 1991 and, of late, is based in Rota, Spain. She arrived at the Navantia shipyard in Cadiz and entered dry dock this week for her maintenance. Previously, in 2022, she had completed the largest maintenance availability ever conducted at the base in Rota. According to the Navy, facilitating this current work locally maximizes operational readiness and availability, and expands forward-deployed maintenance capability. Throughout the project, Forward Deployed Regional Maintenance Center U.S. military and civilian maintenance personnel and ship’s crew are working alongside Navantia to execute planned maintenance and modernization.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: The long-running battle over the future of Romania’s Mangalia Shipyard was settled with the court-appointed liquidator confirmed a deal to sell the yard, with the goal of quickly resuming work. Germany’s Rheinmetall has agreed to acquire the yard for €138 million ($154 million) as part of an effort to build four ships for the Romanian Navy. Once one of the largest shipyards in Europe and a major employer in Romania, the yard of late had been in a joint venture with the Damen Group. Reports said the yard had, at its peak a decade ago, employed between 2,000 and 2,500 people. Damen entered into a joint venture with the Romanian government in 2018 to operate the yard as part of its Eastern European operations in addition to the Gala?i shipyard, which has been operating in Romania since 1999. Damen owned 49 percent of the joint venture for Mangalia, with the government holding the other 51 percent. However, according to media reports, the troubles began in 2023 when Romania changed the rules for the management of private enterprises, and Damen asserted it was a breach of contract for Mangalia. Damen filed in 2024 to put the yard into insolvency, citing the large loans it had made to the joint venture for the modernization and operation of the yard. A plan to reorganize the operations was rejected by the creditors, of which Damen is the largest, and the courts declared the company bankrupt in April 2026. The court-appointed liquidator set the value of the assets at €84 million, and the creditors agreed to a series of auctions starting at €184 million. By August, it was reported that the first three auctions had received no bidders, and the administrators were proposing to the court to begin lowering the price for the subsequent auctions. Under the rules, there were to have been six auctions at the full price, and then they were going to step down the price first to 75 percent and then potentially 50 percent. The yard was reported to have debts totalling €190 million. Rheinmetall acquired the yard at 75 percent of the originally agreed auction price. Romania’s former Minister of Economy and now the Minister of Defense called it a major step forward in the promise to revitalize the operation and restore employment at Mangalia. He asserted the ministry had been offered just €10 million for the yard when the process began, and he rejected it despite criticism from opponents.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: On August 21, 2026, U.S. Coast Guard law enforcement, USCG Cyber Protection Team (CPT), a vessel inspector and FBI Cyber Action Team (CAT) boarded a 333-meter crude oil tanker in the Atlantic. The ship, later identified through Iranian and open-source reporting as the VL Prosperity, was three weeks out from Egypt’s Sidi Kerir terminal, headed for Galveston with roughly 2.3 million barrels of crude. Its network showed signs of compromise by a foreign cyber actor. Investigators spent four days aboard, working with the crew and the operator to assess the vessel’s systems before it reached a U.S. port. A second 227-meter liquefied petroleum gas tanker, the Kohaku , was boarded three days later in the Gulf of Mexico, on August 24, after a suspected, related attack. Two tankers, days apart, both Texas-bound as they had earlier transited the Strait of Gibraltar. Both vessels transited a chokepoint that’s seeing heavier traffic because Hormuz access has been disrupted by the Iran War. Separate reporting also alleged that Vivt Africa LNG experienced cyber-related disruption affecting navigation, communications, and cargo-operation systems on 9 September 2026. What’s confirmed so far is limited: USCG and FBI found malicious cyber activity and performed incident response, noting no physical damage, environment impacts or crew injuries at the time. Unconfirmed claims, that the attacker reached propulsion, navigation, and cargo systems directly, come only from Iranian state media. Ships and ports have an attack surface that’s absorbed versions of this exposure for years. The U.S. Maritime Transportation Security Act (MTSA) has been around since 2002, with cyber only recently being accounted for as an addition to the regulation effective July 2025. The regulatory timing is not a coincidence and echoes the importance of asset owner and operator readiness against high-consequence cyber incidents impacting extended operational technology (xOT). That pattern isn’t specific to this incident; roughly 90% of global trade moves by ship, which alone makes maritime transportation a prime target. Commercial vessels carry a real attack surface, with systems that move a 333-tanker controlled by computers dependent on electronic charting and GPS to know where they are. Some prior examples include:

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A remadora Rie Nagasako, de 48 anos, morreu nesta sexta-feira (9). Ela sofreu um acidente de canoa na última quinta-feira (8) no Rio de Janeiro. Rie foi campeã pan-americana de Va'a em 2025. Ela também conquistou medalha de bronze na categoria sprint no Campeonato Mundial da categoria. No momento do acidente, ela dava aula e tentou salvar seus alunos. A atleta foi levada pela correnteza, resgatada e encaminhada ao Hospital Miguel Couto.

Uma mulher de 63 anos é investigada por maus-tratos após ser filmada agredindo a cunhada de 73 anos em Rocha Miranda, no Rio. Segundo a polícia, a investigada se reconheceu nas filmagens e admitiu as agressões. Ela vive em união estável com o irmão da vítima. Uma auditoria do governo do Rio de Janeiro apontou indícios de desvios superiores a R$ 400 milhões na Cedae Saúde. O relatório identificou irregularidades e favorecimento de empresas. Segundo o documento, 4 firmas ligadas a uma offshore do ex-presidente da Cedae Saúde, Eric Frederik Gualberto, receberam R$ 95 milhões em sua gestão. A investigação começou após a exoneração de Gualberto, em 23 de junho de 2026. A nova diretoria recuperou arquivos apagados contendo dados de fornecedores e registros contábeis. A atual gestão apontou discrepâncias nos repasses à Cedae Saúde. O valor mensal caiu de R$ 20 milhões na antiga gestão para cerca de R$ 6 milhões atualmente.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/129_gulf_pl.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone on Friday, the Marine Minerals Administration (MMA) revealed that personnel had been evacuated from a total of 129 production platforms in the Gulf, based on data from offshore operator reports submitted as of 11am CDT today. That represents 34.77 percent of the 371 manned platforms in the Gulf of America, the MMA highlighted, noting that production platforms are the offshore structures from which oil and natural gas are produced and transported to shore. The MMA pointed out in the statement that, unlike drilling rigs, which typically move from location to location, production facilities remain in the same location throughout a project’s duration. The statement also revealed that personnel had been evacuated from eight non-dynamically positioned rigs, which it noted was equivalent to 72.73 percent of the 11 rigs of this type currently operating in the Gulf. Rigs can include several types of offshore drilling facilities including jack up rigs, platform rigs, all submersibles, and moored semisubmersibles, the statement highlighted. Two of the 17 dynamically positioned rigs in the Gulf have moved off location out of the storm’s path as a precaution, according to the MMA, which noted that dynamically positioned rigs maintain their location while conducting well operations by using thrusters and propellers. These rigs are not moored to the seafloor, so they can move out of harm’s way in a relatively short time frame, the MMA stated, adding that personnel remain on board and return to the original location once the storm has passed. In its statement, the MMA outlined that, from operator reports, it estimates that approximately 71.51 percent of the current daily oil production and 58.84 percent of the current daily natural gas production in the Gulf of America has been shut in. The production percentages are calculated using information submitted by offshore operators in daily reports, the MMA noted. Shut-in production information included in these reports is based on the amount of oil and gas the operator expected to produce that day, the MMA said, adding that the shut-in production figures are estimates that the MMA compares to historical production reports to ensure the estimates follow a logical pattern.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A TransJordano inaugurou, nesta quarta-feira (07/10), em Sumaré (SP), a primeira parte de seu Corredor Verde , rota de 450 km que passa pelas cidades de Ribeirão Preto, Sumaré e Cubatão, em São Paulo, usando biometano como combustível. O eixo conta com pontos de abastecimento planejados ao longo do trajeto e prevê 100 caminhões movidos a biometano operando na rota até dezembro deste ano. O primeiro ponto de abastecimento começa a operar em Sumaré neste mês, seguido pelas unidades de Ribeirão Preto, em novembro, e Cubatão, em dezembro. De acordo com a empresa, os caminhões Scania G 460 6×4 receberam cilindros adicionais para ampliar a autonomia, chegando a até 700 quilômetros. A alteração permite ampliar o alcance das operações a partir das três bases. Com a frota completa, o Corredor Verde pode evitar aproximadamente 6.486 toneladas de CO₂ equivalente por ano , de acordo com estimativa da TransJordano verificada pelo Bureau Veritas. A substituição do diesel por biometano também pode contribuir para as metas de redução de emissões de Escopo 3 de embarcadores, que contabilizam impactos associados à cadeia de valor, incluindo o transporte contratado. O projeto tem financiamento do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), por meio do Fundo Clima. Os pontos de abastecimento do Corredor Verde estão disponíveis para uso por outras transportadoras. A estrutura será operada pela GarageLog , empresa do Grupo TransJordano, enquanto o biometano será fornecido pela Ultragaz . A WLM Quinta Roda anunciou a instalação de um ponto de manutenção na GarageLog e o suporte aos veículos ao longo das rotas por meio da rede de concessionárias Scania. De acordo com dados da operação da TransJordano em Cubatão, a unidade recebe mais de 300 veículos por dia e movimenta mais de 360 mil litros de combustível por mês. A empresa avaliou a falta de locais para abastecimento como um dos principais entraves para a expansão do uso de biometano, situação que busca remediar com o Corredor.

O mercado de logística está trazendo novas oportunidades para quem busca trabalhar com movimentação de cargas, intralogística, transporte e supply chain. Semanalmente, a equipe da Tecnologística registra vagas de emprego e capacitação para profissionais do setor. Nesta semana, nossa equipe registrou vagas para diversas posições e níveis de experiência, com destaque para grandes empresas fazendo contratações fixas e temporárias em preparação para o aumento de demanda das festas de fim de ano. A empresa de infraestrutura de mobilidade está com mais de 300 vagas de emprego abertas para suas operações de trilhos em São Paulo. Os novos contratados atuarão nas linhas 4-Amarela e 5-Lilás, de metrô, e 8-Diamante e 9-Esmeralda, de trens. Algumas das funções não exigem experiência e os candidatos escolhidos terão toda a capacitação técnica oferecida pela concessionária antes de serem efetivamente contratados. São oportunidades para aprendiz, oficial de manutenção, técnico de manutenção, agente de atendimento e segurança (AAS) e operador de trem . Todas as vagas são afirmativas para mulheres. Para agente de atendimento e segurança (AAS) , os interessados devem ter ensino médio completo e atingir a pontuação determinada no teste de aptidão física (TAF) promovido pela empresa. Sendo aprovados nas etapas, são contratados e iniciam a formação técnica de vigilante, requisito obrigatório para exercer a função. Após a conclusão e certificação, são inseridos no efetivo que atua diariamente nas estações. Caso o inscrito já tenha o certificado de vigilante, ele segue direto para as capacitações ministradas pela própria empresa e inicia suas atividades com supervisão dos formadores. Outra função que não exige experiência é a de operador de trem . Para concorrer a ela, basta ter ensino médio completo e CNH de categoria B. Passando pelas etapas do processo seletivo, o candidato será inscrito na formação realizada em parceria com o Senai. Todos os que forem certificados serão contratados.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/new-safes.text: As ports prepare for ships fueled by methanol, ammonia, and hydrogen, they face a common challenge: how to introduce new fuels safely while keeping daily operations steady. A new guidance from Denmark’s SafeSBU (Safe Storage, Bunkering and Usage of Green Fuels) project is designed to provide ports, operators, emergency services and authorities with a practical framework for managing the transition. The guidance is the final output from the SafeSBU project, and covers the entire safety chain from fuel storage and bunkering to onboard use within a single risk-based framework. Rather than prescribing one-size-fits-all solutions, it is designed to helps organizations understand hazards, assess risks, and implement appropriate safety measures for their specific operations. The SafeSBU guideline brings together contributions from DBI (Danish Institute of Fire and Security Technology), Denmark-based independent research and technology organization FORCE Technology, Aalborg University, Port of Rønne, Complete Solutions, DFDS and MHO-Co. “The maritime industry is turning towards low-carbon fuels, and many ports are asking the same questions: What are the risks? How do we demonstrate that operations are safe? And how do we coordinate across the many organizations involved? This guideline provides a common language and a structured approach to answering those questions,” says Nicklas Sjøgren Koch, team leader at DBI. SafeSBU is part of MissionGreenFuels, a Danish partnership working to accelerate the development and deployment of sustainable green fuels in sectors such as shipping and aviation. “Green fuels are essential to decarbonizing shipping, but large-scale deployment requires confidence that new solutions can be introduced safely,” says Carina Jensen, partnership director at MissionGreenFuels. “By turning shared knowledge into practical guidelines for stakeholders across the value chain, SafeSBU helps the maritime sector move from ambition to adoption and accelerates the deployment of green fuels.” Ports are increasingly becoming a preferred hub for the production, storage and distribution of green fuels. Unlike conventional marine fuels, methanol, ammonia and hydrogen introduce very different hazard profiles, requiring new approaches to risk assessment, emergency preparedness, operational procedures and competence development.

The strike caused a fire that has since been extinguished. The condition of the crew, extent of damage and any environmental impact remain unknown, according to UKMTO Warning 160-26. Authorities are investigating the incident. UKMTO has not identified the vessel or publicly established responsibility for the attack. The incident follows an October 7 attack on a tanker near the coast of Qatar, marking the second time in three days that a vessel has been struck inside the Persian Gulf rather than while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/the.text: The recent decision in Olam International Ltd v Pacific Basin Supramax Ltd (The Grande Island) [2026] EWHC 2136 (Comm) concerned a familiar feature of charter party negotiations where standard wording had been incorporated but parts of it deliberately deleted. The question was what those deletions meant for the provisions left behind. Background The Grande Island was chartered under an amended NYPE form for a trip from Ghent to Nigeria. The charter party incorporated the BIMCO Piracy Clause for Time Charter Parties 2013, but sub-clauses 81(a) and (b) were expressly deleted. Had it remained, Clause 81(a) would have given Owners a broad right, based on the reasonable judgement of Owners or the Master, to refuse to proceed to or through an area considered dangerous because of piracy, or to leave such an area. Clause 81 (b) dealt with the alternative orders to be given by Charterers following the exercise of that right. Furthermore, Clause 81(c) was retained, and it allowed Owners, where the vessel proceeded to or through an area exposed to piracy risk, to take reasonable preventative measures to protect the vessel, crew and cargo. The clause gave examples of such measures, including re-routing, proceeding in convoy and adjusting speed or course, but this list was not exhaustive. After arriving off Warri, the vessel was unable to berth. Considering the background of piracy risk in the area, she left Warri and returned towards Lagos, before returning to Warri around three days later. The dispute was whether that temporary departure was permitted under Clause 81(c) and therefore whether the vessel remained on hire. Charterers’ case Charterers’ position centred on the parties’ decision to delete Clause 81(a) and (b). In their view, this was important because Clause 81(a) contained their express right for Owners to leave an area on account of piracy risk. Having specifically removed that right, Charterers argued that the more general wording of Clause 81(c) should not be interpreted as giving it back.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/uk-.text: The UK and Japan are tightening the net around vessels linked to Sovcomflot: London through new LNG carriers and Tokyo through oil tankers. UK sanctions on Russian LNG shipping are also arriving earlier in a vessel’s life. The 1 October package listed PYOTR STOLYPIN (IMO 9904675) before Kpler recorded any cargo, and KONSTANTIN POSIET (IMO 9904704) before any direct international export. Arctic LNG 2 has exported 0.95 million tonnes (mt) so far in 2026, all since July and almost double the 2025 total. Sanctions authorities are therefore targeting the fleet while it is still being built up. • A vessel can now be sanctioned before trading starts. The UK listed PYOTR STOLYPIN (IMO 9904675) as “likely to be involved” in Russian LNG trade before it had carried a cargo. This suggests that a vessel’s intended role in a Russian LNG project, rather than its trading history alone, can be enough to trigger a listing. • Enforcement is moving from the company to individual vessels. Sovcomflot has been on the UK sanctions list since 2022, but the UK and Japan are now designating its ships one by one: LNG carriers in London and oil tankers in Tokyo. This makes it harder to separate vessels held through different registered owners from the wider sanctioned group, particularly ahead of the 1 January 2027 UK and EU LNG restrictions. On 1 October, the UK added 31 entries to its Russia sanctions list, including eight vessels and Novatek Gas and Power Asia, the Singapore-based chartering arm of Novatek. The UK listed the eight ships because they carry, or are likely to carry, Russian-origin LNG to third countries. Among them are three new Russian-built Arc7 ice-class carriers, ALEKSEY KOSYGIN (IMO 9904546), KONSTANTIN POSIET (IMO 9904704) and PYOTR STOLYPIN (IMO 9904675), and three older conventional carriers, CHAIVO (IMO 9331048), PORTOVYY (IMO 9246621) and AVACHA (IMO 9319404).

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/bac.text: This is an extract from the Container Forecaster Issue 3 2026, released 30 September. The apparent eagerness of container lines to return to the Suez Canal is difficult to explain if the calculation is reduced to a simple voyage-cost comparison between Suez and the Cape. Drewry’s slot cost comparison shows only a marginal economic benefit to using Suez (see Table 1) with a saving of approximately $1 million per round-voyage, or $43 per slot, when comparing two services deploying ships of 24,000 teu that use either Suez or the Cape in both directions. However, our calculations do not factor in war-risk premiums, as this information is not readily available, nor the fact that the Suez Canal is known to commonly offer discounts to carriers to tempt them back. Both line items are highly dynamic; war-risk insurance is often negotiated voyage by voyage, while any canal discounts are discretionary. With limited information to hand, we had no alternative but to exclude both items from our formal analysis. We can, however, give a broad overview of how much war-risk premiums and canal discounts could change the economic calculus.

https://petronoticias.com.br/ceo-da-sca-.text: O transporte marítimo pode se transformar em uma nova e relevante fronteira para o etanol brasileiro. A avaliação é de Martinho Seiiti Ono, CEO da SCA Brasil, que vê no processo de descarbonização da navegação uma oportunidade para o país ampliar os mercados consumidores do biocombustível. Segundo Ono , a vocação agrícola brasileira, a extensão territorial e, principalmente, o avanço da produção de etanol de milho colocam o país em posição favorável para atender a esse novo mercado. A diversificação das fontes de consumo também ganha importância diante das transformações no setor automotivo, com o avanço dos veículos híbridos e elétricos. “O Brasil está diante de uma nova fronteira para o etanol com o uso do biocombustível na navegação e seu potencial para reduzir a pegada de carbono do setor marítimo. Temos enorme capacidade de produção, especialmente com o crescimento do etanol de milho” , afirma Ono. Na avaliação do CEO da SCA Brasil, o uso do biocombustível no transporte marítimo pode evoluir em ritmo mais acelerado do que outros mercados emergentes, como o de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF). “O biobunker parece ser um mercado bastante promissor e pode avançar mais rapidamente até mesmo do que o SAF. Na aviação, existem diferentes feedstocks para a produção do combustível sustentável e uma trajetória gradual de aumento da mistura. Na navegação, já existem testes com diferentes proporções de etanol, chegando inclusive ao E100, com resultados positivos ”, explica. Para Ono , a possibilidade de utilização de diferentes percentuais de etanol nas embarcações amplia as perspectivas para o produto brasileiro. “Os testes têm mostrado boa aceitação das misturas, o que abre uma oportunidade muito grande para o etanol brasileiro ”, acrescenta. A perspectiva ganha relevância com o desenvolvimento de uma nova geração de embarcações preparadas para operar com combustíveis alternativos. Parte desses navios deverá entrar em operação até 2030, abrindo espaço para que grandes produtores de biocombustíveis se posicionem como fornecedores. Para aproveitar esse mercado emergente, Ono considera necessário que o Brasil comece a preparar sua estrutura produtiva e logística.“ Precisamos olhar para esses novos navios que estão sendo fabricados para utilizar biocombustíveis e que estarão no mercado até 2030. O Brasil precisa preparar sua capacidade produtiva e de infraestrutura, e os portos também terão que estar estruturados para abastecer essas embarcações. É um cenário desafiador ”, afirma. A estimativa mais recente da Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento (Conab) aponta que o Brasil deve produzir 41,88 bilhões de litros de etanol na safra 2026/27. O transporte marítimo mundial, por sua vez, consome aproximadamente entre 250 e 298 bilhões de litros de combustívei

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A MSC e a Ocean Network Express (ONE) seguirão operando juntas o serviço Ipanema, que liga a Ásia à costa leste da América do Sul, após o fim do atual acordo de compartilhamento de navios (VSA) com a Hapag-Lloyd. A primeira saída sob o novo formato está prevista para 3 de abril de 2027, partindo de Xangai. A MSC informou aos clientes que o VSA do serviço Ipanema, hoje operado em conjunto por MSC, ONE e Hapag-Lloyd, será encerrado na configuração atual. A rota, no entanto, não será descontinuada. As duas primeiras empresas continuarão com a operação semanal, mantendo as conexões entre diversas origens asiáticas e os portos sul-americanos. Com a mudança, a MSC vai alocar navios adicionais ao serviço. Segundo a companhia, o reforço busca ampliar a presença em uma rota que ela classifica como estável e confiável, além de ajustar a capacidade ao crescimento da demanda dos clientes. O Ipanema mantém escalas diretas em Santos (SP), Paranaguá (PR) e Navegantes (SC), no Brasil, e em Montevidéu, no Uruguai, e Buenos Aires, na Argentina. A MSC afirma que a cobertura e os tempos de trânsito continuam competitivos para o comércio entre as duas regiões. A rotação completa do serviço é a seguinte: Xangai, Ningbo, Shekou, Hong Kong, Singapura, Santos, Paranaguá, Navegantes, Montevidéu, Buenos Aires, Rio Grande, Paranaguá, Navegantes, Santos, Singapura, Hong Kong e Xangai. A reconfiguração acontece em um momento em que os armadores revisam parcerias e redes de serviços para ajustar oferta e cobertura nas principais rotas. Para importadores e exportadores brasileiros que usam o Ipanema, o ponto de atenção é o calendário de transição, já que a primeira saída da nova formação, em abril de 2027, definirá o início efetivo do arranjo entre MSC e ONE.

A descarbonização da navegação pode abrir um novo mercado para o etanol brasileiro. A avaliação é de Martinho Seiiti Ono, CEO da SCA Brasil, que aponta o biocombustível como alternativa para reduzir a pegada de carbono do transporte marítimo e, ao mesmo tempo, ampliar os destinos da produção nacional. Segundo Ono, a vocação agrícola do país, a extensão territorial e o crescimento do etanol de milho colocam o Brasil em posição favorável para abastecer esse mercado. Ele também lembra que a diversificação da demanda ganha importância diante do avanço dos veículos híbridos e elétricos no setor automotivo. Na visão do executivo, o chamado biobunker, como é conhecido o biocombustível usado em embarcações, pode evoluir mais rapidamente do que o combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF). Ele argumenta que, na aviação, há diferentes matérias-primas e uma trajetória gradual de aumento da mistura. Na navegação, já existem testes com diversas proporções de etanol, incluindo o E100, com resultados positivos. Esse movimento coincide com o desenvolvimento de uma nova geração de navios preparados para combustíveis alternativos. Parte dessas embarcações deve entrar em operação até 2030, o que abre espaço para grandes produtores de biocombustíveis se posicionarem como fornecedores. De acordo com Ono, Vale e Maersk já realizam testes e adaptações em embarcações para uso de biocombustíveis, com resultados positivos. A estimativa mais recente da Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento (Conab) indica produção de 41,88 bilhões de litros de etanol no Brasil na safra 2026/27. O transporte marítimo mundial, por sua vez, consome entre 250 e 298 bilhões de litros de combustíveis por ano. Para dimensionar o potencial, Ono faz um exercício: se o setor adotasse apenas 10% de etanol na mistura, o consumo poderia chegar a cerca de 30 bilhões de litros ou mais. O número é uma projeção do executivo, e não uma meta oficial.

Em sua primeira palestra internacional, especialista do PORTa levou ao debate global os impactos da seca na Amazônia, a resiliência das hidrovias e os desafios para a governança logística O Instituto PORTa esteve representado no 21st GreenPort Congress, realizado de 7 a 9 de outubro de 2026, em Portsmouth, no Reino Unido, por Maria Eduarda Medeiros, Analista de Inspeção Naval do Instituto PORTa, que participou como palestrante da programação internacional do evento. Considerado um importante encontro internacional dedicado à sustentabilidade, inovação e resiliência no setor portuário, o GreenPort Congress 2026 reuniu representantes de autoridades portuárias, terminais, empresas de navegação e organizações especializadas para discutir os desafios ambientais e operacionais que estão transformando os portos. A edição deste ano teve como eixo central o equilíbrio entre os desafios ambientais e as demandas econômicas, com debates sobre qualidade da água, redução de emissões, resiliência climática, inovação e adaptação. Maria Eduarda participou da Session 7 – “Spotlighting practical action to address climate resilience, water scarcity & adaptation”, dedicada a ações concretas para enfrentar os impactos das mudanças climáticas, a escassez hídrica e os desafios de adaptação dos portos e sistemas logísticos. Às 11h40, Maria apresentou a palestra “Dredging and Predictability: Waterway Resilience and Logistical Governance in Response to the 2026 Amazon Drought”, abordando a relação entre dragagem, previsibilidade, resiliência das hidrovias e governança logística diante dos impactos da seca de 2026 na Amazônia. A apresentação colocou em perspectiva internacional um tema de grande relevância para o Brasil: a necessidade de compreender as hidrovias como infraestruturas estratégicas e de desenvolver mecanismos de planejamento e governança capazes de responder a eventos climáticos extremos, garantindo maior previsibilidade para a logística e para as operações portuárias.

Bulgaria’s Minister of Defense said without evidence they would not speculate on the origins of the drone. He noted that both Ukraine and Russia have denied attacking the two vessels early on October 6. Initially, Bulgaria had said it would not continue the search after declaring the 10 crewmembers from the cargo ship Alfa Watan missing. However, reports are that Syria, which had nine crewmembers aboard the missing vessel, has called for an independent investigation involving both Bulgaria and the International Maritime Organization. Bulgarian media also reported that officials in the European Union told the country that it had to do more if it wants to push for sanctions as a result of the attacks. The frigate Verni was sent to the site on Thursday to locate the Able and determine the condition of the vessel. The Palau-flagged ship, which is 114 meters (approximately 374 feet) in length and 7,400 dwt, is reported stable. It is down by the stern after taking water through a breach in the hull. https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Port of Los Angeles reported on Friday that it has just completed the strongest month in the port’s history, with container volumes dramatically ahead of last year and the port’s five-year average. It capped the strongest four-month stretch in the port’s history with expectations that volumes will continue strong as the fourth quarter begins. “September was a month for the record books, and it was part of an extraordinary run for the Port of Los Angeles,” said Port Executive Director Gene Seroka. “Consumer demand remains resilient, importers are replenishing inventories, and more cargo is being allocated to Los Angeles as shippers navigate continued challenges along other global trade routes.” The port handled a total of 1,042,652 TEU, which was a record, topping the prior record set in July 2025. Seroka highlighted that the volume was the highest ever to pass through any port in the Western Hemisphere. He said the increase of 23,000 TEU over July 2025’s volume was equal to two more full ship loads. It was also the strongest quarter in the history of the Port of Los Angeles, handling nearly 3 million TEU. Adding June, the port handled nearly 4 million TEU over the four-month span. The strong performance was driven by import volumes, which reached 545,696 TEU in September. Seroka highlighted that it was 19 percent ahead of September 2025 and 26 percent above the port’s five-year average for the month. He noted it was only the tenth time in the history of the port that it has handled that volume of imports, while noting no other U.S. port has ever reached those import volumes. Exports, however, remained soft. They were up 10 percent, but Seroka feels exporters such as farmers are still facing a headwind.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The United Kingdom is marking a historic achievement as the world’s last seagoing paddle steamer celebrates the 80th anniversary of her launch. The Waverley , a steamer that was launched in Scotland in 1946 and which continues to be an iconic symbol of UK shipbuilding, is this week celebrating a major milestone as the last steamer that is still in operation. The Waverley boasts a rich history, having been named and launched at the Pointhouse Yard of A.&J. Inglis in Glasgow on October 2, 1946. The steamer entered service the following year in June, beginning what would become a remarkable career that would see her become one of the most recognizable historic vessels in the world. As the last paddle steamer to be built in Scotland, construction of the historic ship began in 1945, but due to post-World War II material shortages, she was not launched until 1946. Her boilers were finally installed in 1947, enabling her to enter service that summer. The Waverley went on to operate until the early 1970s as a commercial ferry in western Scotland and then briefly was in service, offering a combination of excursion cruises along with her ferry service. Waverley measures 240 feet (73 meters) and has a displacement of 1,524,600 lbs. (691 meter tons). She has a historic 2100 horsepower diagonal triple expansion steam engine turning two 216-foot diameter paddle wheels, and each paddle float is 36 feet deep. Originally fitted with a double-ended Scotch boiler, it was replaced in 1981 with a Babcock Steambloc boiler. She was originally certified for 1,350 passengers but today carries a maximum of 860 people. In 1974, she was gifted for £1 to the Paddle Steamer Preservation Society, and she spent the next decade operating cruises. The steamer was rebuilt in the early 2000s, restoring her to her 1940s style and once again returning her to service as an excursion steamer. In May 2019, her career was again threatened by a boiler failure but was saved by a public appeal that raised over $3 million to replace her forty-year-old boilers. The refit project saw new boilers and electrical systems installed, along with other areas of the vessel being refurbished. She entered drydock in the spring of 2020, and after delays, including due to COVID-19 restrictions, she completed sea trials in mid-August. This week, the Waverley is celebrating her remarkable achievement of being the world’s last paddle steamer in service. Part of the celebrations saw the steamer make a spectacular passage through London’s Tower Bridge as part of a special anniversary sailing on the River Thames.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: The maritime industry entered 2026 with less regulatory certainty than it had a year earlier, not more. The most consequential piece of global shipping regulation of the decade, the International Maritime Organization’s Net-Zero Framework, was agreed in principle in 2025: a global fuel standard that lowers the permitted greenhouse gas intensity of marine energy over time, backed by a mechanism that prices emissions and rewards cleaner ships. Its formal adoption then stalled. The decision was pushed back a year, and the framework returns to the table at the end of 2026 with its eventual shape, timing and geographic reach all still in play. If it is adopted in something close to its current form, the first obligations would begin to bite from 2028. That uncertainty sits on top of a regional picture that is already in force and already diverging. The European Union’s Emissions Trading System reached full coverage of shipping in January 2026, and FuelEU Maritime is tightening the permitted carbon intensity of marine fuel with each compliance period. National authorities, port states and major charterers are adding conditions of their own. An owner ordering a vessel today has to satisfy one set of rules that is binding now, another that is still being drafted in London, and a patchwork of regional and commercial requirements that neither align with one another nor show much sign of converging. The temptation, understandably, is to wait. To order conventional tonnage, defer the harder choices, and hope the picture clarifies before the penalties become unmanageable. The temptation should be resisted, because the picture is unlikely to clarify in the way the cautious approach assumes. Regulatory fragmentation shows every sign of being a permanent condition rather than a transitional phase on the way to a single global standard. Owners waiting for certainty are waiting for something that will not arrive. Even if the IMO adopts its framework at the end of the year, the European regime is already binding and already shaping trade; and if the global measure is diluted or delayed again, the regional rules will carry even more of the weight. There is no single regulatory outcome to design for, and no safe year to begin. The alternative is to design for the fragmentation itself, building and refitting vessels that stay compliant across a range of outcomes rather than being optimized for any single one. This is the logic of designing a vessel once to comply across jurisdictions, and it changes what a sound specification looks like. It means treating lower energy demand and lower carbon intensity as a baseline, building in fuel flexibility and the space to adopt new systems later, and being able to prove performance with verified data. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/rus.text: Russia increased crude exports in September by relying more heavily on non-G7 tankers, particularly those operated by domestic companies, whose shipments reached their highest level since Western nations imposed a price cap. Tankers flagged, owned and operated by companies not based in G7 countries and their allies, and not insured by Western protection and indemnity clubs, lifted nearly 2.89 million barrels/day in September, compared with 2.7 million b/d in August, according to S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab) and Maritime Intelligence Risk Suite data. The increase came as overall Russian seaborne exports rose to 4.09 million b/d from 3.82 million b/d in the same period. While the overall share of Russian crude exports on non-G7 tankers, mainly from the shadow flee established to bypass Western sanctions, showed little change month on month, Russian tanker operators were shouldering more responsibilities for their home country’s overseas sales. Continuing the upward trajectory seen in recent months, shipments rose from 18.6 million barrels in August to 20.6 million barrels in September — the highest since the G7 and EU began banning maritime service firms from participating in Russian crude exports unless the barrels were sold below a certain threshold in December 2022. State carrier Sovcomflot’s tankers loaded 6.4 million barrels in September, while the remainder were generally lifted by tankers owned by small, little-known companies, according to the CAS and MIRS data. All of the ships were flagged in Russia.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/iea_members.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone late Wednesday by the International Energy Agency (IEA), IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol revealed that, in a meeting this week, IEA member governments “expressed support for accelerating the oil stock releases announced in the Collective Action of March 2026, with a view to completing them as soon as possible”. A statement posted on the IEA’s website on March 11 announced that the 32 member countries of the organization unanimously agreed to make 400 million barrels of oil from their emergency reserves available to the market “to address disruptions in oil markets stemming from the war in the Middle East”. Birol highlighted in the IEA’s latest statement that, at the IEA meeting this week, IEA members also supported the “prioritization of the release of diesel stocks, to the extent possible, given the current tightness in diesel markets”. “Participants in the meeting expressed strong appreciation for the IEA’s response to the energy impacts of the Strait of Hormuz crisis,” Birol noted. “They emphasized their commitment to delivering on the March 2026 Collective Action and the importance of the IEA Secretariat’s role in continuing to monitor progress towards the completion of the action and providing up to date market analysis,” he added. Birol also said participants welcomed the recent statement by G7 Leaders on global energy security and market stability, “including its emphasis on the importance of free flow of energy trade”.
