https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/economia/mo.text: Ministros da Opep (Organização dos Países Exportadores de Petróleo) e países não membros da Opep participantes da DoC (Declaração de Cooperação) se reuniram nesta segunda-feira (12), em Riad, para reafirmar a importância de proteger as rotas marítimas internacionais para garantir o fluxo ininterrupto de energia. Em comunicado, eles também observaram que a interrupção atual dos fluxos elevou o custo de transporte e de seguro, que atingiram níveis sem precedentes de mais de um terço do valor da mercadoria, dificultando o movimento oportuno e eficiente de petróleo bruto e derivados e colocando pressões inflacionárias adicionais na economia global. Os ministros também revisaram as condições de mercado e concordaram em continuar as consultas com todos os países da Opep+ para alcançar e manter um mercado de petróleo estável. "Os ministros continuarão monitorando a situação e se envolverão com governos, partes interessadas da indústria e organizações internacionais, como a AIE (Agência Internacional de Energia), para melhorar as condições de transporte global", acrescentou a nota.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: Work is proceeding on three new large container ships being built for Matson as part of what the company reports is a $1 billion investment in fleet expansion and modernization. The Makua was christened at the Hanwha Philly Shipyard on October 10. At nearly 51,000 dwt, Matson's three new Jones Act-compliant vessels are being built to match the size and speed of Matson's two existing Aloha Class ships, Daniel K. Inouye and Kaimana Hila , which were also built in Philadelphia and introduced in 2018 and 2019. The ships are each 850 feet long with a capacity of 3,600 TEU, with 408 reefer slots. Like their sisterships, the new vessels will be equipped with dual-fuel engines designed to operate on either conventional marine fuels or liquefied natural gas (LNG). They are being delivered LNG-ready to join the older ships, which were recently converted to LNG operations. They will have a top speed of 24 knots. Other "green ship technology" features include a fuel-efficient hull design, environmentally safe double hull fuel tanks, and freshwater ballast systems. "We're excited that adding three new Aloha Class ships to Matson's fleet over the next 18 months will improve operating efficiencies and reliability, and increase capacity in our core Hawaii service, as well as our China-Long Beach Express service,” said Matt Cox, chairman and chief executive officer of Matson. Matson board member Jenai Wall officially christened the vessel Makua in front of an audience of approximately 300 invited guests, including U.S. Maritime Administration Deputy Administrator Mark Johnson, Matson and Hanwha executives, shipyard workers, and union leaders. The new ship is scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 2027. Assembly of the ship began with the first grand block being placed in the dry dock in August 2025. The second vessel began assembly in May 2026, and steel cutting is underway for the third vessel. Matson plans to name the other two new containerships Malama and Makena , with delivery scheduled for the third quarter of 2027 and the second quarter of 2028. The three new ships will replace three vessels currently deployed in Matson's Hawaii and China-Long Beach Express services. In turn, those vessels will replace three older vessels currently deployed in Alaska service, introducing bigger and faster vessels into that trade lane.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: South Korea celebrated the completion of its first Arctic round trip using a containership. Government officials said it demonstrated the potential of the Northern Sea Route (NSR) while saying it would play a critical role in the country's economy and committed to expanding the demonstration program next year. The containership Panstar Acro arrived back in Busan on Sunday, October 11, completing a 50-day round trip through the Arctic to Europe and back along Russia’s Northern Sea Route. While the voyage was not a commercial success, it is being hailed by Korean officials as an achievement that is a “springboard” for the development of their planned service. Panstar Acro (45,500 dwt) was acquired from HMM at the beginning of August and prepared for the demonstration voyage, which had been organized with the support of the South Korean government and the shipping association. Built in 2011, the ship has a capacity of 2,758 TEU, and the hull was ice-strengthened before the voyage. The captain and crew received Arctic training, and the first officer was transferred from South Korea’s icebreaker research ship to provide specific experience for the challenges of the trip. The ship docked in Busan Sunday morning, after having departed Gdansk, Poland, on September 18. It had set off from Busan on August 22 and entered the Arctic on August 31. It reached Felixstowe in the UK on September 12 and Rotterdam the following day. While the ship was five days behind schedule on its return, the trip was pronounced a success, with reports of no major incidents during the voyage. Panstar Acro completed a 50-day round trip to Europe and back along the Northern Sea Route (President Lee on X) South Korean President Lee Jae-myung hailed the return in a message on social media. He noted the trip took about 10 fewer days than the normal route via the Suez Canal. He wrote that it “allowed us to accumulate polar navigation experience and voyage data for our containerships. Based on this achievement, we will steadily prepare for the Arctic route era.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: [Breaking] A fire has been reported aboard the seismic survey ship Rem Andes off the coast of Grande Isle, Louisiana, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. 46 people were on board at the time of the incident, and abandon-ship operations were initiated, the Coast Guard said in a statement. An unspecified number of those on board disembarked into life rafts and transferred to nearby Good Samaritan vessels. The agency's SAR aircrews were dispatched to the scene to ensure that all of the survivors who departed the vessel were properly accounted for. AIS data provided by Pole Star Global suggests that the ship slowed and began to drift to the north of its normal racetrack survey route at about 0955 hours on Monday morning. According to local media, the fire was out by about 1445 hours. The effort to retrieve crewmembers from lifeboats that had already cast off from the stricken ship was still underway as of mid-afternoon. Eight crewmembers remained behind aboard the ship to fight the fire and conduct damage assessment, the Coast Guard told the local Fox News affiliate, and would be evacuated at a later point. The ship continued to broadcast AIS through the day, drifting slowly northeast at a position some 90 nautical miles south of Whiskey Island, Louisiana. Rem Andes is a Norwegian-operated ship that entered service in 2012. The vessel is classed and equipped as a seismic ship, and AIS records show that it has been engaged in running survey tracklines on the deepwater U.S. continental shelf for at least the past year, operating out of Gulfport and Port Fourchon. It passed its last U.S. Coast Guard port state control inspection in late 2025 with no issues recorded.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: Russians near the city of Kaliningrad on the Baltic were rushing to the beaches over the weekend to view a large cargo ship that had been driven aground during a fierce storm. Officials were even posting directions on how best to reach the ship as the tourist crowds grew. According to the report, the Bahamas-flagged general cargo ship Sunny Faith (17,221 dwt) was holding off Kaliningrad on a trip from Skikda, Algeria. The officials said they believed the crew misjudged the strength and direction of the hurricane-force winds as a storm moved through the area on Friday, October 9. There was no distress call from the vessel, but instead residents found the vessel firmly aground near the tourist town of Yantarny. The vessel, which is 130 meters (426 feet) in length, had a crew of 19 aboard. It is listed as being Chinese-owned and managed. Winds across the region reportedly reached 60 mph during the storm. In addition to the cargo ship, the officials were reporting that a jack-up platform had broken free and was adrift in the high surf. The Marine Rescue Service contacted Sunny Faith , and the captain said they did not need to evacuate. He said the conditions were fine, and they would contact the authorities if they required assistance. They were awaiting the storm and high seas to calm down so that tugs could begin to explore pulling the vessel off the shoreline. There were limited concerns about pollution, according to the officials. They reported the ship was on a ballast voyage. They said there appears to be no hull damage or breaches.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: The French military has boarded the sanctioned shadow fleet tanker DF Peak on the high seas of the Indian Ocean, hundreds of miles from land. It is perhaps the most remote, far-removed interdiction of a Russia-linked tanker since the beginning of the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. French President Emmanuel Macron announced Monday that the Marine Nationale had boarded the tanker at a position about 450 nautical miles to the south of the department of Réunion, the French island territory east of Madagascar. Macron said that the ship was suspected of flying a false flag and conducting "illicit fuel transportation activities." "This action, carried out in accordance with international maritime law, demonstrates our determination to uphold the rule of law and combat all illicit trafficking, wherever it occurs," Macron said in a statement. La France est déterminée à lutter contre la flotte fantôme, partout dans le monde. Ce matin, à plus de 450 nautiques au sud de La Réunion, notre Marine nationale a arraisonné le pétrolier DF Peak, suspecté de naviguer sous un faux pavillon et impliqué dans des activités illicites de transport de carburants. Cette action, conduite conformément au droit international de la mer, témoigne de notre détermination à faire respecter le droit et à lutter contre tous les trafics illicites, où qu’ils se produisent. DF Peak has a long history in Russian service. Built in 2006, the 110,000 dwt tanker served in the state-owned Sovcomflot fleet as the NS Captain until 2024, when it was renamed Kaliningrad. It took on its current name in 2025. It became part of the SCF-linked, Dubai-based Sun Ship fleet in early 2022, and is currently managed by a company in Hong Kong. The vessel's Equasis record suggests that it is falsely flagged in Benin, a national register once known as a haven for the Russia-linked shadow fleet. Benin has taken steps to deregister noncompliant tonnage and push back against the fraudulent, unauthorized use of its flag, a persistent pattern for sanctioned vessels.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: [Updated] UK Maritime Trade Operations, a division of the Royal Navy, has recorded four more previously-unreported attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz occurring Sunday. The news adds to the two strikes previously reported, bringing the total for October 11 to six attacks - an unprecedented rate during the current conflict, if accurate. The third strike hit an outbound tanker of undefined type at a position northeast of the Musandam Peninsula. The crew was unharmed, UKMTO reported. The fifth strike hit a tanker in the general vicinity of the north end of the Musandam Peninsula. The crew has been confirmed as safe. The sixth strike hit a product tanker at an unknown time on Sunday at a position to the northwest of the Peninsula. No further information was released. The new reports did not come with specific times, locations or vessel names. They bring the total number of known incidents to four strikes on October 11 alone, in addition to three prior attacks on October 9-10. At about the same time as UKMTO's lastest report, Iran's Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy released video footage purporting to show an attack on a tanker that was "ignoring warnings and switching off its navigation system," according to state media. Unverified footage of the stern displays the name of the UAE-owned tanker Al Maqam (IMO 9732577).

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: The Hellenic Coast Guard released the details of a miraculous rescue of a passenger who had jumped overboard from a cruise ship in the Ionian Sea west of Piraeus. The reports say the woman was in the water for up to 20 hours, but was found conscious and suffering from a mild case of hypothermia. Passengers aboard Royal Caribbean International’s Odyssey of the Seas (167,704 GT) were informed of the incident early on Saturday, October 10. The cruise ship had departed Mykonos and was traveling to Naples when the incident occurred. The female passenger, who was identified as a 44-year-old woman from El Salvador, appears to have jumped around 0600 on October 9. The Bahamas-flagged cruise ship, which is 1,138 feet (347 meters) in length, carries approximately 4,200 passengers. It was approximately 72 nautical miles southwest of Zakynthos. The circumstances of the overboard incident have not been reported. However, the woman had a life preserver from the cruise ship. Unconfirmed reports said she grabbed the life preserver and apparently went over the side of the cruise ship at around 0600. The cruise ship commenced a search, circling the area. The Hellenic Coast Guard dispatched two patrol boats and a helicopter, while the Hellenic Air Force also deployed a plane for the search. The Coast Guard also altered vessels in the area. The MSC Rossella III (38,771 dwt) spotted the flashing light attached to a lifering early on Saturday morning. The 2,700 TEU containership was sailing from Piraeus to Giola Tauro, Italy, when it spotted what it believed could be the individual in the water. It immediately alerted the Coast Guard.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: The HMM containership HMM Platinum is displaying a message of “restricted manoeuvrability” on its AIS transmission as the vessel approaches South Africa. The insurance claims consultants are reporting that the vessel suffered a container fire while crossing the Indian Ocean and is currently heading to a port of refuge. The extent of the damage is unknown, but the reports indicate the vessel, which has a capacity of 5,023 TEU, is seeking to make a stop in South Africa. Its AIS shows a destination of Durban with an ETA of October 11, but both WE Claims Group and Dolphin Maritime & Aviation Services are reporting that alternates are being explored. The reports suggest the vessel might proceed to Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), possibly due to the congestion and delays at Durban. The 63,000 dwt ship departed Kattupalli International Container Terminal in India on September 27 and was scheduled to proceed on a month-long crossing to Santos, Brazil. WE Cox, is reporting that there are 2,300 TEU aboard, with all the consultants warning that there could be heat, smoke, or water damage to containers located near the source of the fire. The vessel was built in 2013 and is registered in Liberia. Its AIS signal shows it moving at a speed of 6.5 knots on October 12 as it approaches South Africa. SMIT has reportedly been appointed to organize the salvage operation, and the ship appears to be traveling accompanied by a tug. It is unclear if the fire has been totally extinguished. Based on the reports, the fire began while the ship was south of Lavanono, Madagascar, around the beginning of the month. The reports again highlight the persistent danger to vessels from container fires. Data from commercial insurer Allianz in June shows a containership fire occurred every 17 days on average in 2025. The World Shipping Council said the information underscored the persistent risk that misdeclared and undeclared dangerous goods pose to seafarers, shipping, and global supply chains.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: The Swedish Transport Agency confirmed that it has lifted the ban on a Chinese-owned tanker that had been detained since March during a crackdown on false flag and potentially dangerous vessels entering the Baltic. The tanker Sea Owl 1 (75,000 dwt) was held until it could confirm a valid registration and seaworthiness.l The tanker, which was built in 2007, was inbound from Santos, Brazil, when Swedish forces boarded the vessel on March 12 on suspicion that it was traveling under a false flag and concerns over its seaworthiness. The Russian master presented papers showing the vessel was registered in Comoros, although records showed it was operating falsely under the flag since July 2025. Swedish authorities said a preliminary investigation was addressing suspected violations regarding a lack of seaworthiness for the tanker. It was ordered to anchor off Trelleborg in southern Sweden. It came days after Sweden stopped another small cargo ship, Caffa , on similar suspicions. The first captain was arrested in March on charges that he presented false papers, but was later released because prosecutors said it was difficult to prove the captain had knowingly presented false papers. However, a replacement captain presented papers claiming the vessel had been registered in Cameroon, which, according to the Swedish authorities, also turned out to be false. He was also detained in May for presenting false papers . The Swedish Coast Guard reports that the Sea Owl 1 is listed under EU sanctions, but it was not suspected of any sanctions violations. The vessel reported that it was heading to the Russian port of Primorsky when it was detained. The detention order was lifted as of October 12 after the Swedish authorities confirmed the vessel had been registered in Equatorial Guinea. It is still showing at anchor off Sweden, awaiting orders.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: Um ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reuniu eleitores em Copacabana nesta segunda-feira (12). O evento ocorreu na Avenida Atlântica. https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Elon Musk gastou cerca de US$ 366 milhões nas eleições de 2026 nos EUA, conhecida como midterms . O objetivo foi ajudar republicanos a manter o controle do Congresso. A doação, revelada pelo New York Times, torna Musk provavelmente o doador político individual nas eleições. Desse total, US$ 276 milhões foram doados desde julho. A imprensa internacional interpreta o ato como ofensiva contra democratas que pedem investigações sobre contratos da SpaceX e sua atuação no governo de Donald Trump. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543619-do.text: DOF Group ASA announced the award of a significant contract with a North Sea operator for a subsea decommissioning campaign. The contract scope includes project management, engineering, offshore execution and disposal services for the removal of subsea infrastructure and seabed clearance across multiple offshore fields. The offshore campaign is scheduled for execution during the first quarter of 2027. DOF will utilize its integrated decommissioning capabilities, combining in-house engineering, project management, marine operations, ROV services, survey and offshore execution. Offshore operations will be performed by one of DOF's Construction Support Vessels (CSVs).

https://www.rigzone.com/news/usa_oil_gas.text: The number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry hit a post pandemic September low, data on the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) website showed. According to preliminary figures included in the BLS data page, the number of employees in the sector stood at 114,100 last month. That was the lowest September figure since 2021, when it came in at 111,400, and the second lowest September figure in the data set, which spanned from January 2026 to September 2026, the data page outlined. The number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry came in at 160,800 in September 2026, 143,600 in September 2017, 141,400 in September 2018, 144,000 in September 2019, 126,800 in September 2020, 115,300 in September 2022, 119,600 in September 2023, 120,900 in September 2024, and 115,900 in September 2025, the data page revealed. September’s preliminary figure of 114,100 was also the lowest figure so far this year, according to the data page, which outlined that the number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry came in at 114,700 in August, 114,600 in July, 115,100 in June, 115,400 in May, 115,200 in April, 115,900 in March, 116,200 in February, and 115,500 in January. August’s figure is still preliminary, the data page highlighted. Including the 2026 figure, the number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry has decreased from August to September in five out of the last 11 years. Looking at September to October figures, the number of employees in this sector has decreased in seven of the last 10 years. The number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry came in at 158,600 in October 2016, 142,200 in October 2017, 141,100 in October 2018, 143,400 in October 2019, 127,000 in October 2020, 111,300 in October 2021, 115,900 in October 2022, 120,100 in October 2023, 120,500 in October 2024, and 115,700 in October 2025, the BLS data showed.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/rus.text: Black Sea tanker economics strengthened sharply in late September and early October as attacks on commercial shipping, disruption to Russian energy flows and tighter scrutiny of Russia-linked tonnage increased the cost and complexity of moving cargoes. Baltic routes moved in the opposite direction: Aframax spreads fell further into discount territory against global benchmarks even as outright earnings rose. The divergence reflects a growing segmentation in Russian seaborne trade. Vessels operating from the Black Sea are attracting higher compensation for security, insurance and voyage-execution risks, while Baltic routes continue to trade below their relevant benchmarks amid the operational and commercial constraints associated with Russia-linked tonnage. The UK added 12 tankers to its sanctions list on Oct. 8, alongside measures against Russian oil companies Zarubezhneft and INK Capital. The move followed the Joint War Committee’s decision on Sept. 16 to add the Black Sea to its Listed Areas, increasing war-risk insurance considerations for vessels operating in the region. Sanctions and attacks have not removed Russian oil from global trade, but they have changed the vessels, routes, counterparties and risk premiums required to move it. More than 1,600 vessels linked to Russian trade over the past two years accounted for 73% of the total shadow fleet at the end of August, according to S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab) data. The size of the Russia-linked fleet, combined with the latest designations, highlights the widening separation between tonnage active in Russian trade and vessels readily accepted by mainstream charterers, insurers, banks and terminals. The latest pricing reflects that shift. Black Sea Suezmaxes command the strongest relative returns as owners seek compensation for elevated security and execution risks. Baltic Aframaxes remain at the deepest discount to their relevant benchmark, while clean MR economics continue to vary sharply by loading region and destination.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/e.text: The European Union has released its largest-ever sanctions package on Russian defense-industry companies, a counterpoint to the Trump administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel fuel. The 930-page list is exhaustive, covering nearly 1,600 businesses and individuals across the defense industrial base, and there are dozens of shipyards, ship repair plants, design bureaus and equipment suppliers among the designees. Taken in total, it covers the majority of Russian shipbuilding activity. "This is the strongest package of listings we have adopted so far," said the EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, at a press conference Monday. "It is clear that at this time we need more pressure on Russia and not sending signals that we are easing up somehow, because they are actually killing more civilians than they have ever done. They are really escalating on the ground, and that is why it is time for no concessions." Shipyards are inherently dual-use infrastructure, and the EU drew on Russia's own list of militarily-relevant companies to determine whether or not the selected facilities were part of the Russian military-industrial complex. Many of the firms are known subsidiaries of United Shipbuilding Corporation, a conglomerate which accounts for about 80 percent of all Russian newbuild tonnage and is already heavily sanctioned. Among many others, the 23 listed shipyards and ship repair plants include: - Admiralty Shipyard, one of the best-known yards in Russia and a division of already-sanctioned United Shipbuilding Corporation (USC). - Sevmash, the primary builder of Russia's nuclear submarine fleet, also a division of USC. - Almaz Shipbuilding Company, a commercial and government shipbuilding contractor located in St. Petersburg. It has built icebreakers, amphibious craft and assault hovercraft (LCACs) for the Russian Navy.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: O subtenente do Bope Glaucio Marcelo Fonseca da Silva, de 54 anos, morreu neste domingo (11) em um tiroteio entre policiais militares na Gardênia Azul. https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: Early Tuesday, two more vessels were hit by suspected Russian drone strikes off the coast of Bulgaria, injuring five and sinking one ship. The attacks were the latest in a long string of strikes on Black Sea merchant shipping, dating back to early 2022 and increasingly employed by both sides of the conflict. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced the news of the latest attacks in a statement Tuesday. The vessels were hit outside of the nation's territorial seas, he claimed. At about 0130 hours local time, the Ukrainian-operated coastal freighter Chelsea 3 made a distress call, reporting that it had been hit three times by aerial drones. The 15 crewmembers were evacuated and taken to the port of Varna, Radev said. Five of the seafarers were injured and needed medical care. Additionally, Radev said that his ministers had been informed of a second vessel strike at a position about 17 nautical miles off Krapets. The as-yet-unnamed ship was sunk, he said. Only one crewmember from this vessel had been rescued at the time of his announcement early Tuesday. Just last week, a suspected Russian drone strike sank a merchant ship off the Bulgarian coast, leaving all 12 crewmembers lost at sea. Another ship sustained serious damage but remained afloat. Russia has denied involvement in these earlier attacks. While Bulgaria has denounced the kinetic strikes and has called for a cessation of the violence, its leaders have stopped short of naming a suspect just yet. "We do not have clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either side. However, as I have already stated, the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation. I will therefore summon the Russian Ambassador for a meeting today," said Radev on Tuesday.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: On Sunday, an inland vessel laden with a cargo of hydrogen went aground on the Rhine, restricting traffic on the upper stretches of the river. It is the latest in a string of groundings of varying severity on the drought-stricken waterway, which has been unable to carry typical volumes of industrial traffic due to months of persistent low water levels. At about 0700 hours on Sunday morning, the cargo vessel was downbound on the Rhine near the village of Ludwigshohe when it became stranded, the local water police reported. It was the fourth such instance of the weekend, three other ships having grounded nearby on Saturday and Sunday. All of the incidents have reportedly resolved without difficulty and the vessels were able to refloat. To prevent a recurrence, a vessel size restriction was put into effect on the Rhine near Mainz. The low water levels on the Rhine have set new records this year and have disrupted German industry. In Cologne, levels fell to just 40 centimeters at a key river gage, a historic low, according to NTV. The situation is not expected to improve until significant volumes of rain return to the entire region at the end of the season. Augmented train and truck transport networks are filling the gap for industrial commodities like coal, coke, iron ore and scrap metal, according to trading news outlet Eurometal. Specially-constructed shallow draft inland vessels also can carry more cargo and operate at lower river gage levels than conventional peers, but availability of this newer tonnage is limited. For most commercial vessels, the water near Mainz is so low that the Rhine is divided in two, unnavigable in the middle when laden with cargo. "At the moment, the Rhine is fed – roughly speaking – only by sewage treatment plants, glacial ice and a little groundwater inflow," Rhine Waterways and Shipping Office expert Florian Krekel told DPA. Overall, the Rhine's low water restrictions are expected to trim nearly half a percentage point off of Germany' GDP for 2026, according to a forecast by the German Economic Institute (IW). The losses are concentrated in the industrial enterprises that line the Rhine corridor, the historic cradle of German manufacturing.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543640-ci.text: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) has acquired a 25% stake in the 1.1 GW Five Estuaries offshore wind farm project in the UK from a Macquarie-led consortium, following RWE's exit from the development. The acquisition was made through CIP's fifth flagship fund, Copenhagen Infrastructure V (CI V), making the company a partner alongside EDF power solutions, ESB and Sumitomo Corporation. Under the updated ownership structure, EDF power solutions holds 33.33%, CIP 25%, ESB 20.83% and Sumitomo Corporation 20.83%. The transaction follows RWE's completed sale of its 33.33% stake to EDF power solutions UK and Ireland, announced on October 12, with EDF assuming responsibility for leading the project's development on behalf of the joint venture partners. Five Estuaries is planned approximately 40 kilometres off the north Essex and south Suffolk coast in the southern North Sea, across two seabed areas covering approximately 128 square kilometres. The project is an extension of the operational Galloper offshore wind farm and received development consent from the UK's Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero on December 17, 2025.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543629-tg.text: TGS and SLB have announced the second phase of their Pelotas Sul multi-client 3D seismic survey offshore southern Brazil, covering approximately 11,200 square kilometers in the Pelotas Basin. A Ramform Titan-class vessel is scheduled to begin data acquisition in October 2026, with the survey expected to be completed in the second or third quarter of 2027. The project follows Pelotas Sul Phase 1, which was acquired earlier this year, and will expand 3D seismic coverage across the southern part of the basin. The new survey will cover both held and open acreage, providing subsurface data for companies evaluating existing exploration positions and potential opportunities associated with future licensing rounds and farm-in activity. According to TGS, the Pelotas Basin contains several underexplored geological play concepts, including turbidite systems, deep-water channels, and stratigraphic and structural traps. The company also pointed to geological similarities along the conjugate margin and discoveries in Namibia as factors supporting exploration interest in the basin.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543632-to.text: Vallourec has been awarded a contract by TotalEnergies to supply more than 16,000 tonnes of tubular products for the development of the Absheron gas field in Azerbaijan's sector of the Caspian Sea. The contract covers oil country tubular goods (OCTG) and line pipe solutions, including approximately 159 kilometers of anticorrosion-coated line pipe for onshore and offshore applications. For the OCTG portion, Vallourec will supply premium pipes equipped with its VAM connections, including the VAM SLIJ-3 semi-flush connection designed for offshore environments. The package also includes accessories manufactured across Vallourec's global facilities and its CLEANWELL dope-free technology. Vallourec will also be able to provide local operational support through its VAM Caspian entity. The Absheron field is located approximately 100 kilometers southeast of Baku, in water depths of around 500 meters.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543631-ha.text: Hampidjan Advant has signed an agreement with Cadeler to manufacture and supply heavy-duty lifting slings for the East Anglia TWO offshore wind farm project in the North Sea off the east coast of England. The equipment will be used aboard Cadeler's new wind turbine installation vessel (WTIV), Wind Ace, during construction of the wind farm, which is owned by ScottishPower Renewables. The slings will be manufactured by Hampidjan Baltic in Lithuania using high-modulus polyethylene (HMPE) fiber and designed for heavy-lifting operations involving offshore wind turbine foundations and turbines. The largest slings supplied for the project will measure 190 millimetres in diameter and 64 meters in length, with a breaking strength of 4,000 tonnes. Their design is based on engineering assessments of load requirements, dimensions and operating conditions specific to the project. East Anglia TWO will be located in the southern North Sea, more than 30 kilometers off the Suffolk coast, and is expected to have a capacity of up to 960 MW, comprising up to 75 wind turbines.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543633-se.text: Offshore drilling contractor Seadrill has secured new drilling contracts and extensions covering four rigs offshore Indonesia, Malaysia, Angola and in the U.S. Gulf. In Indonesia, West Carina drillship has been awarded a contract with an undisclosed operator for an estimated firm duration of 880 days, with operations expected to begin in the first half of 2027. The contract is valued at approximately $420 million for the firm period, including a mobilization fee and excluding additional services, and includes priced options for up to another 880 days. In Malaysia, Seadrill said all remaining priced options for West Capella drillship had been exercised, extending operations by 120 days and adding approximately $41 million in contract value. A further 120 days of unpriced options have also been exercised, adding approximately $53 million. Both amounts exclude additional services. The drillship is now expected to continue working without interruption through February 2028.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543636-iw.text: Kongsberg Maritime has secured a contract with IWS Fleet, a subsidiary of Integrated Wind Solutions (IWS), to provide vessel design and integrated technology systems for four new commissioning service operation vessels (CSOVs) intended for offshore wind operations. Kongsberg Maritime's scope includes electrical power systems, navigation and bridge systems, propulsion, deck machinery, dynamic positioning systems and overall system integration. Each vessel will feature a double-ended design with four rim-drive azimuth thrusters, two forward and two aft, enabling symmetrical operations and manoeuvring between offshore wind turbines. The thrusters use permanent magnet motor technology and will operate alongside Kongsberg Maritime's dynamic positioning system to provide station-keeping capabilities during offshore operations. The vessels will be built by Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment and will be based on Kongsberg Maritime's latest UT 5519 DEx design, representing the next generation of the Skywalker Class. The order will expand the Skywalker Class series to ten vessels, following the delivery of six vessels since 2023.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543630-ja.text: Conrad Asia Energy has confirmed the arrival of the Valaris 104 jack-up rig at PaxOcean's shipyard in Batam in Indonesia, where it will be converted into a mobile offshore production unit (MOPU) for the Mako gas project in the West Natuna Sea. The arrival marks a key milestone for the development in the Duyung Production Sharing Contract (PSC), which remains on budget and on schedule to achieve first gas in the fourth quarter of 2027. The donor rig reached Batam after completing its transit through the Strait of Hormuz in September, following planning and coordination involving maritime authorities, naval task forces, classification bodies and marine warranty surveyors. The transit was managed by GAC Logistics, engaged by MOPU contractor PT Duta Marine/PT Pakarti Tirtoagung. Fabrication of the MOPU topside modules has commenced, with a formal first-cut ceremony targeted for early November. The arrival of Valaris 104 allows the project to advance into the next phase of physical conversion and integration. Engineering and procurement activities for the conductor support frame (CSF) and subsea umbilical, riser and flowline (SURF) packages are also progressing on schedule.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543628-mu.text: Murphy Oil Corporation has reported a successful appraisal well offshore Côte d'Ivoire and an oil discovery offshore Vietnam, alongside the start of production from two offshore developments in Vietnam and the Gulf of America. In Côte d'Ivoire, the Bubale West-1X appraisal well in Block CI-103 encountered approximately 88 feet (27 meters) of net oil pay in the Turonian reservoir, along with additional hydrocarbons in the deeper Albian reservoir. The well was drilled to a total measured depth of 19,357 feet (5,900 meters) in water depths of 9,039 feet (2,755 meters). Preliminary analysis of well logs and fluid samples indicated high-quality oil, with the results to be incorporated into the remaining appraisal program at Bubale. Murphy operates Block CI-103 through its subsidiary Murphy CI-103 Oil Co., holding an 85% working interest, while Côte d'Ivoire's PETROCI holds the remaining 15%. In Vietnam, Murphy reported an oil discovery at the Lac Da Trang North-1X exploration well in Block 15-1/05, which encountered 131 feet (40 meters) of net oil pay.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543626-eq.text: Equinor and Dutch energy company Eneco have signed a five-year agreement for natural gas deliveries from the Norwegian continental shelf to the Netherlands, covering approximately 9 TWh of gas annually and including verified greenhouse gas emissions data. The agreement covers around 0.9 billion cubic meters of natural gas per year, with deliveries to the Dutch gas grid having started on October 1, 2026. Under the agreement, Equinor will also transfer verified environmental attributes to Eneco through a digital platform operated by Attributes SA, providing information on the gas's origin and upstream greenhouse gas footprint. According to Equinor, the gas supplied under the contract has a lifecycle greenhouse gas footprint 11.8% lower than the average gas supplied through the Dutch grid, based on a comparison using 2025 data. The calculation covers emissions from extraction, transport and combustion, with the difference attributable to extraction and transport rather than gas consumption. The comparison uses emission factors from CO2-emissiefactoren.nl, the Dutch standard for CO2 calculations, with underlying lifecycle calculations for natural gas performed by Royal Haskoning.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543627-eu.text: The European Union is examining a bloc-wide windfall profit tax on oil and gas companies, the EU's tax chief told Reuters on Monday, as governments scramble for funds to help citizens with soaring energy bills. Oil and gas companies have reaped bumper profits this year, as energy prices have surged during the US-Israeli war with Iran, amid disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian attacks on Gulf neighbours. Wopke Hoekstra, the European Commissioner responsible for climate and taxation, said the Commission was setting up a working group to examine the merits and drawbacks of a levy and assess whether such a measure would be viable. "Citizens, and particularly vulnerable citizens, are confronted with dramatic increases in their energy bills. And some companies are reaping truly excessive benefits without delivering any additional service or any additional products. They're reaping the benefits from the world being in turmoil," Hoekstra said in an interview. "To many citizens and many politicians, that feels off... I think we all have sympathy for the underlying logic, regardless of where we exactly take the conversation," he said. Benchmark Brent crude futures prices climbed to multi‑year highs near $120 a barrel in late April and remain more than 70% above their level at the start of the year, boosting profits for oil refiners and producers.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543625-bp.text: BP expects to report $3 billion to $4.5 billion of impairments in its third quarter results, relating to its gas and low-carbon energy segment, the oil major said on Tuesday. This is the second time in a year that the British firm has booked large write-downs in its low-carbon business, previously flagging $4 billion to $5 billion in impairments in January. The refining indicator margin for the quarter is due to be $46.7 per barrel, versus $29.6 per barrel in the second quarter. Realised refining margins are expected to be in the range of $1.9 billion to $2.1 billion. The US-Israeli war on Iran has disrupted global oil supplies, driving up prices and helping majors book stronger profits. BP expects its gas marketing and trading result to be significantly higher in the third quarter compared with the previous quarter. It expects its upstream production to be 2.19 million to 2.24 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, versus about 2.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the previous quarter.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A AliançaBiodiesel , formada pela Associação dos Produtores de Biocombustíveis do Brasil (APROBIO) e pela Associação Brasileira das Indústrias de Óleos Vegetais (ABIOVE), apoia a decisão da Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) de restabelecer, por 24 meses, a proibição da comercialização de biodiesel entre distribuidores de combustíveis líquidos . A medida busca combater as chamadas bionotas, operações documentais sem movimentação física do produto e sem a efetiva mistura ao diesel A. Segundo a entidade, essas operações prejudicam empresas que atuam regularmente, favorecem a concorrência desleal e comprometem a transparência do mercado e a arrecadação pública. “Essas práticas prejudicam as empresas que atuam regularmente, geram concorrência desleal, reduzem a transparência do mercado e comprometem a arrecadação pública”, afirma Jerônimo Goergen, presidente da APROBIO. Para André Nassar, presidente executivo da ABIOVE, a decisão da agência contribui para dar previsibilidade ao setor. “A decisão da agência traz a segurança jurídica e a previsibilidade regulatória necessárias para o desenvolvimento estruturado do setor”, diz. Ele também defende que o combate às irregularidades é importante para preservar a integridade da cadeia produtiva e o papel do biodiesel na descarbonização da matriz de transportes. A restrição também busca reforçar a rastreabilidade do combustível, assegurando que o biodiesel destinado à mistura obrigatória seja efetivamente produzido, comercializado e entregue de acordo com as regras da ANP. A AliançaBiodiesel defende que a vedação se torne permanente após a conclusão do processo de análise de impacto regulatório, consulta pública e audiência pública. Para a entidade, a continuidade da medida é necessária para garantir condições equitativas de concorrência e impedir operações baseadas apenas em registros documentais. “A indústria brasileira tem capacidade, tecnologia e condições para ampliar sua participação na matriz energética nacional. Para isso, é fundamental que todos os agentes concorram em igualdade de condições e que o produto físico prevaleça sobre operações puramente documentais”, completa Goergen.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/gasbuddy_fl.text: In a blog posted on its website on Monday, GasBuddy flagged a “fragile calm at the pump” in the United States. According to GasBuddy data, the nation’s average price of gasoline fell 0.4 cents over the last week and stood at $4.29 per gallon, the blog highlighted, noting that the national average was up 0.4 cents from a month ago and $1.28 per gallon higher than a year ago. The national average price of diesel fell 5.9 cents in the last week and stood at $6.248 per gallon, the blog pointed out. “More states saw average gasoline prices decline than rise over the last week, with diesel falling approximately five cents per gallon nationally,” Patrick De Haan, Head of Petroleum Analysis at GasBuddy, said in the blog. “On the policy front, the Trump administration’s proposed diesel deal raises more questions than it answers, and I remain skeptical that it will deliver significant relief to the trucking industry and consumers who depend on diesel,” he added. “Meanwhile, Hurricane Isaias has passed, but we are awaiting updates on two refineries that were in its path, the outcome of which could impact the supply picture in the days ahead,” he warned. “For now, the trend is cautiously in the right direction for motorists, but between hurricane season and continued geopolitical uncertainty, it is far too early to declare the pressure on fuel prices resolved,” De Haan went on to state.

https://safety4sea.com/hydrogen-laden-ve.text: Inland shipping on the Rhine is facing renewed disruption as persistently low water levels continue to hamper navigation along one of Europe’s most important commercial waterways. O n 11 October, an inland vessel reportedly carrying 250 tonnes of hydrogen ran aground near Ludwigshöhe in Germany, becoming the latest in a series of incidents linked to the river’s drought-stricken conditions. According to local water police, the vessel was travelling downstream at approximately 07:00 when it became stranded. The incident marked the fourth grounding reported in the area over the weekend, following three similar cases on Saturday and Sunday. All four incidents were resolved without major difficulty, with the vessels eventually refloating. Nevertheless, the repeated groundings prompted authorities to introduce a restriction on vessel size on the Rhine near Mainz, aiming to reduce the risk of further incidents as navigational conditions deteriorate. The latest incidents highlight the growing operational challenges facing vessels navigating the Rhine, where prolonged dry weather has driven water levels to exceptionally low levels. The river is a critical transport corridor for Germany and the wider European economy, carrying industrial raw materials, chemicals, fuels and other essential commodities between inland ports and major industrial centres. The resulting loss of carrying capacity can increase transport costs and place additional pressure on supply chains that depend on reliable inland waterway connections. Groundings and restrictions on vessel dimensions add another layer of uncertainty for operators already navigating constrained conditions.

https://safety4sea.com/eleven-missing-af.text: Eleven sailors are missing after a cargo ship sank following a drone attack off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast on October 13, while another vessel was hit and its crew rescued, Bulgarian officials said. T he incidents prompted Sofia to summon Russia’s ambassador amid growing concerns over attacks on commercial shipping in the region. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the sunken vessel went down approximately 17 nautical miles east of Krapets. Five crew members were initially reported rescued, while 11 remained missing. The latest attack on a commercial vessel in the immediate vicinity of Bulgaria’s territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable. At 01:30, a distress call was received from a vessel 18 nautical miles east of Byala. According to the crew, the Chelsea 3—sailing under the Maltese flag, registered in Odesa and Ukrainian-owned—was struck on its deck and side by three aerial drones. All 15 crew members—seven Ukrainian and eight Azerbaijani nationals—were safely transported to the port of Varna. Five are receiving medical assistance. Our Permanent Representatives to NATO and the EU have been informed. Bulgaria continues to seek support for an investigation into the attacks to determine the country of origin of the drones. We are also seeking assistance to strengthen surveillance of the air and maritime domains and enhance our response capabilities. We do not have clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either side. However, as I have already stated, the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation. I will therefore summon the Russian Ambassador for a meeting today. At an extraordinary meeting of the Security Council under the Council of Ministers, we also received information about another vessel, struck 17 nautical miles east of Krapets. It sank, and one crew member was rescued. Bulgarian media identified the vessel as the Azov Concord , although further details about its ownership and management were not immediately available. The second vessel, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 , was struck by three aerial drones approximately 18 nautical miles from Byala. All 15 crew members, comprising seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, were rescued. Some crew members reportedly sustained minor injuries. Radev condemned the incidents as “absolutely unacceptable,” saying the attacks occurred in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters. He convened an emergency meeting with security officials and summoned Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova.

https://safety4sea.com/french-navy-board.text: The French Navy intercepted and boarded the oil tanker DF Peak in the Indian Ocean on October 12 over suspicions that it was sailing under a false flag and involved in illegal fuel trafficking, French President Emmanuel Macron announced. T he operation took place more than 450 nautical miles south of Réunion Island, a French overseas territory in the Indian Ocean. Macron said the boarding was conducted in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and international maritime law. La France est déterminée à lutter contre la flotte fantôme, partout dans le monde. Ce matin, à plus de 450 nautiques au sud de La Réunion, notre Marine nationale a arraisonné le pétrolier DF Peak, suspecté de naviguer sous un faux pavillon et impliqué dans des activités illicites de transport de carburants. Cette action, conduite conformément au droit international de la mer, témoigne de notre détermination à faire respecter le droit et à lutter contre tous les trafics illicites, où qu’ils se produisent. France’s Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin confirmed that the tanker was under French Navy escort following the interception. She emphasized that international law must be enforced and said French armed forces remained mobilized to combat illegal activities at sea. Je félicite les militaires des Forces Armées dans la zone Sud de l’océan Indien, mobilisés ce matin à près de 450 nautiques au sud de l’île de la Réunion. Leur intervention a permis d’intercepter un pétrolier suspecté de naviguer sous faux pavillon. Le navire est désormais escorté par nos forces pour la poursuite des vérifications, sous l’autorité du préfet de la Réunion. Le droit international n’est pas une option. Nos armées sont pleinement mobilisées pour le faire respecter et lutter contre les activités illicites en mer. The tanker is suspected of transporting sanctioned Russian oil as part of the so-called shadow fleet, a network of vessels used to move Russian petroleum and circumvent international restrictions. Such vessels have raised concerns over sanctions compliance, opaque ownership structures, insurance coverage and potential environmental risks.

https://safety4sea.com/lng-trade-faces-a.text: The International Gas Union’s latest report highlights the growing importance of emissions verification, cargo traceability and cross-border regulatory alignment, with implications for LNG exporters, importers and the maritime industry. A s highlighted in the Global State of the Methane Regulation Report from the International Gas Union (IGU), methane regulation is emerging as an increasingly important factor in global natural gas trade, placing new emphasis on how emissions data are measured, verified and linked to traded cargoes. For the maritime industry, where LNG moves through an interconnected network of liquefaction terminals, carriers, floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) and import terminals, the challenge extends beyond emissions reduction to the documentation and traceability underpinning international energy shipments. The report examines how differing national and regional rules are reshaping the natural gas industry. One of the key findings of the analysis, finds that jurisdictions accounting for approximately 67% of global natural gas production have adopted or proposed operational rules addressing methane emissions. It also highlights a 10% decline in global average upstream methane intensity since 2019, reflecting progress in industry abatement programmes and measurement, reporting and verification practices. However, as regulation expands, the lack of consistent requirements across jurisdictions risks creating a more complex compliance environment for internationally traded gas.

I n warnings, UKMTO reported that three vessels were struck while sailing outbound through the strait, while the container ship was hit during an inbound transit. The incidents involved a product tanker, a crude oil tanker and two other vessels described in the reports as tankers. Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for striking the ADNOC Logistics and Services-operated VLCC Al Maqam. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency published footage showing the Liberian-flagged tanker on fire around its funnel and engine-room area, with a tug providing assistance. https://safety4sea.com/south-korea-compl.text: South Korea has taken a significant step towards expanding its presence in Arctic shipping after the container vessel PanStar Acro completed the country’s first commercial round trip to Europe via the Northern Sea Route on 11 October, arriving at the port of Busan 50 days after departing on 22 August. A s reported by Reuters, the voyage forms part of Seoul’s broader ambition to establish regular Arctic shipping services by 2030 and strengthen Busan’s position as a global maritime hub. The Northern Sea Route, which runs along Russia’s Arctic coastline, offers the potential to shorten transit times between Asia and Europe by approximately one-third compared with conventional routes. Against a backdrop of geopolitical uncertainty and disruption across major maritime corridors, the route is attracting renewed interest as shipping companies and governments explore alternative options for international trade. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a strategic priority, with authorities looking to build the country’s operational capabilities and develop the infrastructure needed to support future services. However, the PanStar Acro voyage also highlighted the commercial, logistical and geopolitical challenges that must be addressed before regular operations become viable.

https://safety4sea.com/wallenius-marine-.text: Wallenius Marine has launched a research project with KTH, RISE and AlfaWall Oceanbird to investigate how vessel design can improve the efficiency of wind propulsion systems and help reduce shipping emissions. T he project, named WinPrOVeDD (Wind Propulsion Oriented Vessel Deck Design), will examine how ship design affects the performance of wing sails and other wind propulsion technologies. Supported by the Swedish Energy Agency, it aims to identify design improvements that enable vessels to harness more wind energy. Previous research indicates that conventional vessel designs can limit wind propulsion performance, while more aerodynamic designs could deliver significant efficiency gains. The project will run from September 2026 to December 2029, combining advanced simulations with wind tunnel testing. Its findings will be published as open-access design guidelines for ship designers, shipyards and shipowners worldwide. We need to design the ships of the future around the wind, rather than simply adding wind technology to vessels developed for a fossil-fuel era … said Urban Lishajko, Head of Ship Design, Newbuilding & Innovation at Wallenius Marine.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/coa.text: Coal futures traded just below $150 per ton, hovering near a three-year high as elevated LNG prices, driven by supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict, continued to encourage a shift toward coal-fired power generation. With coal costing roughly 80% less than LNG, buyers in Asia and Europe have increased imports ahead of the winter season. The International Energy Agency also projected in September that global coal demand would reach a record high this year, despite ongoing efforts to transition to cleaner energy sources and the closure of numerous coal-fired power plants across Europe and North America. Meanwhile, Indonesia, the world’s leading coal exporter, tightened export restrictions, contributing to a 23% drop in shipments in August. The IEA expects Indonesian coal production to decline by more than 12 million tons this year, citing lower production quotas and policy uncertainty. Source: Trading Economics

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/rsg.text: Following the signing of an agreement with DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the government has initiated the process of appointing Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Gateway Terminal (RSGT) as the operator of the Chittagong Container Terminal (CCT). The Ministry of Shipping and the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) are currently processing the appointment, according to sources. The Ministry of Shipping has directed the CPA to process an appointment letter for the proposed CCT operator, according to an official letter issued by the ministry’s Development-1 Branch on September 28. The letter, signed by Farzana Hossain, senior assistant secretary of the ministry, said Red Sea Gateway Terminal International, a private investment company, has expressed interest in implementing the Chittagong port’s CCT and General Cargo Jetty and Bay Port-Multipurpose Terminal projects under the public-private partnership (PPP) model. Against this backdrop, the ministry directed the CPA to process the appointment letter for the company to operate the CCT. The letter referred to a communication dated August 19, 2016, from the Public-Private Partnership Authority. Copies of the letter were forwarded to the CPA chairman, a relevant official of the Ministry of Shipping and the chairman of the Invest Bangladesh Authority for information.

https://splash247.com/saverys-keeps-cash.text: Belgian shipping group CMB.TECH has continued to cash in on elevated tanker values, selling its fifth suezmax this year and locking in another $59.6m capital gain. The Alexander Saverys-led company said it has already delivered the 2011-built, 165,000 dwt Stella to its new owner and will book the gain in the fourth quarter. CMB.TECH did not disclose either the buyer or sale price, but market sources have estimated the deal at at least $80m. The numbers in CMB.TECH’s own accounts point to a similar level. Stella and the 2007-built Sienna had a combined carrying value of $32.9m at the end of 2025. Sienna subsequently sold for $41.9m, producing a $29.2m gain, implying a carrying value of around $12.7m and leaving roughly $20.2m attributable to Stella. Adding the latest $59.6m gain suggests a net sale price close to $80m. Market reports have also linked Stella to a one-year charter with Trafigura at around $120,000 per day following the sale, highlighting the earnings backdrop behind the sharp increase in secondhand values. SEB analysts described the disposal as another positive step in CMB.TECH’s tanker divestment programme.

https://petronoticias.com.br/carlos-mast.text: Considerado um dos pioneiros na disseminação mundial do uso de plataformas do tipo FPSO, Carlos Mastrangelo escreveu, em parceria com o também experiente executivo Jorge Mitidieri , o livro “ FPSO: Legado Offshore” . A obra aborda desde as escolhas técnicas que moldaram o mercado de navios-plataformas até os atuais desafios operacionais e as tendências futuras. Em entrevista ao Petronotícias, Mastrangelo analisou os fatores que pressionam o mercado de unidades de produção offshore, como a disputa por equipamentos com setores como os de data centers e aviação, e as incertezas que afetam as decisões de investimento em projetos de petróleo e gás. O executivo também discutiu os impactos da adoção de novas tecnologias, como a inteligência artificial, e defendeu o planejamento de longo prazo e a atuação do governo para evitar sobrecargas na cadeia brasileira de fornecedores e ampliar a participação nacional nos projetos. Qual foi a proposta da obra e por que considera importante olhar para o passado ao pensar no futuro da indústria? O título FPSO: Legado Offshore pode dar a impressão de que se trata de um livro de história, voltado ao passado. No entanto, essa não é a proposta. A obra busca compreender o presente com base nos acontecimentos anteriores, de modo a projetar o futuro. A palavra “legado” está relacionada justamente ao que deixamos para as próximas gerações, oferecendo referências para que possam pensar no futuro. Para projetar o futuro, seja na vida pessoal ou nas empresas, é preciso conhecer o passado. As histórias se repetem e, infelizmente, os erros também. O livro aborda diversos aspectos dessa relação, incluindo a influência da inteligência artificial nos projetos. Por exemplo: existe um discurso politicamente alinhado de que a IA contribuirá para reduzir o número de pessoas a bordo e substituir atividades realizadas no mar. Essa redução de pessoal se concretizou em outras etapas da evolução tecnológica? No livro, fazemos um regaste histórico do que aconteceu na indústria ao longo dos anos. No início da década de 1990, surgiram as primeiras unidades com sistemas digitais no Brasil, enquanto essa transformação também começava a ocorrer em outras partes do mundo. Os computadores passaram a permitir a substituição dos sinais mecânicos de pressão por sinais elétricos, por exemplo.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL) assinou, por meio da MOL Ocean Bulk, contrato de 25 anos com a Vale International, subsidiária da Vale, para o transporte de minério de ferro em dois navios com motor tricombustível. A propulsão pode operar com etanol, metanol e óleo combustível pesado. Segundo a empresa, serão os primeiros minereiros de 210 mil toneladas do mundo com essa configuração, com entrega prevista para 2030. A MOL Ocean Bulk, com sede em Singapura, é a empresa que opera o negócio de graneleiros Capesize do grupo fora do Japão. Os dois navios atuarão principalmente no transporte transoceânico do minério da Vale, dentro da estratégia de descarbonização da frota que a mineradora mantém para o seu transporte marítimo. Além do motor tricombustível, as embarcações terão projeto preparado para uso futuro de GNL ou amônia e contarão com tecnologias de eficiência energética disponíveis para a nova geração de navios. A ideia, segundo a MOL, é dar flexibilidade na escolha do combustível conforme a disponibilidade, o ganho de descarbonização e a viabilidade econômica de cada alternativa. Sobre o etanol, a MOL afirma que ele pode reduzir as emissões de carbono em até cerca de 90% em relação ao óleo combustível pesado, considerando o ciclo de vida completo, da produção ao consumo. A companhia também destaca que a facilidade de manuseio do combustível tende a favorecer sua adoção mais ampla no uso marítimo. O contrato também tem efeito sobre o chamado escopo 3 da Vale, que reúne as emissões geradas na cadeia de valor e não nas operações diretas da empresa. Para a MOL, a operação dos navios ajuda a reduzir esse indicador no transporte marítimo da mineradora e contribui para as metas do grupo, que busca emissões líquidas zero de gases de efeito estufa até 2050, dentro da visão ambiental BLUE ACTION 2035 Phase 2. Fora da operação dos navios, o grupo diz que trabalhará com clientes e parceiros ao longo de toda a cadeia de suprimento de etanol e metanol, da compra ao fornecimento e ao abastecimento. O comunicado não informa de onde virá o combustível, em quais portos o abastecimento será feito, nem detalha estaleiro, fabricante do motor ou valor do contrato.

A Zilor conquistou a certificação internacional ISCC EU para a Unidade São José, em Macatuba, no interior de São Paulo. O reconhecimento amplia as oportunidades de fornecimento de etanol ao mercado de biocombustíveis da União Europeia e ao segmento de navegação, em um cenário de pressão crescente por combustíveis com menor intensidade de carbono. A certificação atesta que a unidade atende a critérios internacionais de sustentabilidade, rastreabilidade da cadeia produtiva e redução de emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Na prática, o selo é um dos instrumentos usados para comprovar que o biocombustível cumpre os requisitos necessários para ser contabilizado nas metas de energia renovável do bloco europeu. Segundo a companhia, o resultado foi construído a partir do trabalho integrado de diferentes equipes, com revisão de processos, treinamentos e auditorias ao longo da preparação. Os números ajudam a dimensionar a base envolvida. A Zilor informa que mais de 50 mil hectares estão certificados e que cerca de 3 milhões de toneladas de cana estão aptas ao processo. A empresa não detalhou, no comunicado, volumes de etanol previstos para exportação nem contratos já firmados. Para o transporte marítimo, o tema é particularmente relevante. A regulamentação europeia FuelEU Maritime, em vigor desde janeiro de 2025, estabelece redução gradual da intensidade de emissões da energia utilizada a bordo de navios que escalam em portos da região. Nesse contexto, combustíveis de origem renovável e com cadeia certificada ganham espaço entre as alternativas em avaliação por armadores e operadores. A certificação também se soma ao movimento de posicionamento do etanol brasileiro em mercados estratégicos da transição energética global. Para o setor, os próximos passos a observar são a conversão do selo em contratos e volumes embarcados, além de uma eventual extensão do processo a outras unidades da companhia.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/b.text: Moradores do Andaraí, na Zona Norte do Rio, reclamam de água parada em obra na Rua Barão de São Francisco nesta terça-feira (13). O local abrigava um prédio do Banco do Brasil. O imóvel está sendo demolido para a construção de um condomínio. Os moradores procuraram a construtora responsável pela obra, mas não receberam resposta. A vizinhança relata o aumento de mosquitos.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Criminosos vendem cadastros falsos para motoristas de aplicativos por até R$ 350 em grupos de mensagens, prometendo burlar sistemas de reconhecimento facial. Em Niterói, a polícia investiga a morte de Maycon Batista da Silva. O motorista do aplicativo envolvido no acidente usava uma conta falsa e não tinha habilitação. A Polícia Civil monitora as vendas ilegais em aplicativos de mensagens. A associação das empresas afirma que o uso de contas falsas é proibido e gera punições.

Uma operação realizada nesta terça-feira (13) investiga policiais ligados ao Comando Vermelho. A ação baseia-se na análise de dados do celular do sargento Yuri Ribeiro. Investigações apontam que Yuri ostentava luxos, mas pedia dinheiro para o traficante Manoel Pereira, o Paulista. O policial enviava alertas sobre operações policiais para a facção. O sargento foi assassinado em julho com 23 tiros, sob suspeita de autoria da facção. A polícia também procura o cabo Erick Lobato, que está foragido.

Um PM de folga matou o comerciante Willyan Curado da Silva, de 28 anos, nesta segunda-feira (12) no Cachambi. Ele disse que a vítima apontou uma arma falsa. O policial militar permaneceu no local após o crime. O caso aconteceu no cruzamento das ruas Baldraco e Ferreira de Andrade, onde fica o bar da vítima. A Delegacia de Homicídios da Capital investiga o caso. A área do bar foi isolada para perícia e o policiamento na região foi reforçado.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/e.text: Em sua primeira visita à Alerj após vitória confirmada no 1º turno, o governador eleito Douglas Ruas (PL) anunciou que pautará assuntos econômicos na próxima semana. O político afirmou que permanecerá na Alerj até 5 de janeiro de 2027. Ele garantiu que deputados de todos os partidos terão "portas abertas" em sua gestão. Ele descartou antecipar sua posse para este ano. O governador eleito também relembrou que o déficit estimado do Estado é de R$ 13 bilhões para o próximo ano.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration has agreed to buy autonomous surface vessels from the American boatbuilder Maritime Tactical Systems (MARTAC), maker of the Devil Ray T24, a 28-foot unmanned boat that can hit 50 knots. It has seen action with U.S. forces in a variety of roles for years. According to MARTAC, Taiwan's purchase is one of the most important foreign sales deals for a U.S. manufacturer of USVs on record. The deal began with an agreement that MARTAC made with Taiwan's state-owned defense R&D institute back in 2025. Under the terms, the T24s for Taiwan will be built in two locations: by MARTAC at its facility in Florida and by a local partner, Confucian Co., in Taiwan. The localization model gives Taiwan an opportunity to build its own domestic capabilities, and was key to getting government buy-in, Confucian said in a statement. The scale of the acquisition was not disclosed, but MARTAC has described it as significant for both the company and for USVs as a technology. “This pursuit by the Taiwan Coast Guard represents a landmark moment for MARTAC and for the adoption of unmanned surface vessels in the Indo-Pacific region,” said Seamus Flatley, Chief Growth Officer of MARTAC. Notably, Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration is a civilian law enforcement bureau with a civilian parent agency, the Ocean Affairs Council; it is not part of the formal Taiwanese military. The Trump administration has yet to approve a pending $14 billion military sales package for Taiwan, which is politically sensitive for China and for the U.S.-China trade relationship.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: On 10 October, the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS) reported that 22 vessels from the Chinese maritime militia had been deployed near Kota Island, a Philippine-held area in Palawan. The task force also confirmed that Chinese Maritime Militia Vessel 9622, along with 22 small boats, returned to the area after two weeks, where they engaged in unauthorised fishing and dumping waste at sea. A few days prior, on 8 October, a China Coast Guard (CCG) vessel used water cannons on a Philippine medical mission to evacuate a Filipino soldier from the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal. The BRP Sierra Madre is the Philippine vessel purposely grounded in Ayungin in 1999, in response to China’s militarisation of a nearby reef (Mischief Reef). The Philippines and China signed a “provisional understanding” in 2024 to provide both sides with a predictable process and reduce the risk of miscalculation. Despite this, the Philippines confirmed on 25 September that the CCG and the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) obstructed a rotation-and-resupply mission to the BRP Sierra Madre. Another Philippine vessel, the BRP Datu Magat Salamat, sustained damage on 18 September after a CCG ship rammed it while en route to deliver fuel to Filipino fisherfolk. These incidents support the Philippines’ observation that China’s military and coast guard presence in the West Philippine Sea doubled in the last month. The Philippines monitored 101 PLAN and CCG ships around Pag-Asa Island, Ayungin Shoal, Escoda Shoal, and Chinese-controlled Scarborough Shoal. That number is almost double the 56 vessels recorded in August 2026. Repeated intrusions and coercive action at sea are practically a staple in China’s tool chest in the South China Sea. Beyond these, however, widespread malign information campaigns on maritime issues in the West Philippine Sea challenge national security narratives and public trust in democratic institutions. Chinese messaging includes rewriting history, undermining the Philippines’ independence, and projecting a positive image through development projects. This approach gives China access to economic channels through elite influence and capture. At the recent Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said that the country is “resigned” to managing tensions with China and avoiding escalation. The stance is far from that of acquiescence. Indeed, the Philippines’ transparency approach replaces the previous policy of quiet diplomacy with public documentation and exposure of coercive maritime actions. Under the initiative, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the NTF-WPS actively publicise videos, photos, and reports of Chinese activities in the West Philippine Sea.
