https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Navy is moving towards the selection of a contractor for its massive Bremerton naval shipyard overhaul, one of the largest maritime infrastructure projects in the Northwest in a generation. The $15 billion project includes the construction of a massive new drydock for aircraft carriers at Naval Base Kitsap, plus related improvements to the adjacent waterfront. Most of the existing shipyard at the Bremerton base dates back to the turn of the 20th century and is now well over 100 years old. The newest drydock was built during the Cold War. All of it was laid out for an earlier era of shipbuilding and an earlier generation of Navy tonnage; modern supercarriers are far bigger than the vessels in service in the 1890s. The multi-award contract will offer up to five prime contractors the opportunity to split up the project into sections, each allocation valued at $1 billion minimum. Various phases of design and construction will be awarded to the selected contractors as the project progresses, generally in tranches of several billion dollars at a time. "This project is a massive engineering undertaking that will require the highest levels of industry expertise," said Capt. Troy Brown, the project officer for Multi-Mission Dry Dock, in a statement earlier this year. "We encourage companies of all sizes, including our local and regional small businesses, to review the Sources Sought notice . . . Partnering with us means joining the team directly responsible for delivering the foundation of fleet readiness." The objective of the overhaul is to give the Bremerton yard - the heart of the area's local economy - the capacity it needs to keep overhauling the nuclear-powered carrier and submarine fleet. It is the only West Coast yard certified to do nuclear carrier refueling, a deep, multi-year overhaul process. The scope of work for installing a new carrier-sized drydock at an existing yard is massive. The site will need demolition of existing facilities, installation of new tunnels, substations, rail systems, crane tracks, flooding and dewatering systems, and new off-site facilities for relocating some existing functions.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/b.text: With the security situation deteriorating in the Black Sea, Bulgarian officials are calling for the European Union and NATO to support the efforts to enhance security, while Bulgaria says it is also working with Turkey and Romania for increased regional security. The action came after the report of two more vessels struck early on Tuesday off the coast of Bulgaria, with 11 seafarers feared killed, bringing the death toll to over 20 seafarers after four ships were attacked in less than a week. Bulgaria’s Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the attacks in the vicinity of Bulgaria’s territorial waters were “absolutely unacceptable.” He called an emergency meeting of the Security Council while also initiating calls to the President of the European Commission and the Secretary General of NATO. He also reported that the Defense Minister was contacting his colleagues in Turkey and Romania while saying they would also raise the issue at the European Council meeting on October 15 and 16. “We do not have clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either side. However, as I have already stated, the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation. I will therefore summon the Russian Ambassador for a meeting today,” said Radev. Reporting the still-developing situation, the Prime Minister’s office added, “There’s no logic for Ukraine destroying its own ships.” It said the strikes work to Russia’s advantage. This came after Bulgarian officials last week refused to assign responsibility after the first two ships were struck, sinking one and leaving 10 seafarers missing. Bulgaria’s Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov added that the “situation in the Black Sea is becoming increasingly complex.” He said it would require coordination with the neighboring countries and the support of NATO. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen responded, also calling the situation “unacceptable,” while saying, “The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine.” She called for those responsible to be held accountable.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Iran filed a formal protest at the International Maritime Organization, asserting that U.S. military forces are misusing VHF Channel 16, turning it into “an instrument of military intimidation and psychological pressure against civilian crews.” It is the latest in the efforts by Iran to pressure the United States in hopes of loosening the blockade of Iranian shipping and its ports. In a letter filed with the IMO at the end of last week, Iran’s ambassador and permanent representative to the IMO said the government instructed them to raise the serious concern affecting maritime security, distress communications, and the safety of seafarers in the Persian Gulf. It says it has received reports from commercial vessels, shipping companies, and maritime operators that VHF Channel 16 is being misused by the U.S. military. It points out that, under the IMO resolution, the channel is reserved for distress, urgency, and very brief safety communications. “Iranian seafarers have been addressed in Persian with threatening, abusive, and provocative language and, in certain instances, urged to abandon their vessels. Such conduct has disrupted the proper availability of this essential maritime safety channel and caused serious stress and psychological pressure upon civilian crews,” Iran writes in its protest letter. Iran declares to the IMO that the misuse by the military forces of a channel designed for maritime distress and safety communications for hostile and intimidating communications further violates SOLAS regulations. It says the U.S. is obstructing the effective discharge of obligations in safety and distress situations. It, however, does not make mention of the attacks conducted by Iran, which, according to the IMO’s calculations, numbered 15 so far in October. These are, of course, creating the safety situations that Iran references. The IMO calculates that since the start of the conflict, there have been 106 incidents with 24 fatalities, including two sailors missing in October and 12 others injured. “Neither armed conflict nor a naval blockade can justify turning an internationally protected maritime safety channel into an instrument of military intimidation and psychological pressure against civilian crews,” Iran asserts in its letter to the IMO.

https://g1.globo.com/saude/noticia/2026/.text: Papa Francisco antes de cirurgia para retirada de tumor do pulmão. — Foto: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters O papa Leão XIV foi diagnosticado com adenocarcinoma pulmonar, um tipo de câncer no pulmão, após exames de um nódulo removido durante uma cirurgia nesta terça-feira (13), informou o Vaticano. Durante o procedimento, os médicos retiraram o tumor do pulmão direito do pontífice. Segundo o boletim médico, a cirurgia durou cerca de 90 minutos, foi concluída com sucesso e não teve complicações. Leão XIV acordou normalmente e voltou ao quarto do hospital, onde se recupera. Segundo a agência de notícias Associated Press, médicos tiveram de aplicar uma anestesia geral e realizaram uma biópsia na lesão após a remoção. A AP afirmou que cirurgia teve início após profissionais de saúde, Stefano Margaritora e Luigi Carbone , rezarem o terço na capela do hospital.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O ministro André Mendonça, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), determinou nesta terça-feira (13) a suspensão de peça de propaganda eleitoral do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que associa a política fiscal de um eventual governo de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a cortes em programas e benefícios sociais. Na decisão, o ministro disse que as medidas do plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro “preveem expressamente a manutenção e o aperfeiçoamento dessas políticas, com aprimoramento da gestão, correção de distorções e combate a fraudes, assegurando que os beneficiários não perderão o auxílio estatal”. Mendonça afirmou ainda que a expressão “tesouraço”, utilizada por Flávio Bolsonaro, refere-se "exclusivamente à redução da estrutura administrativa estatal, mediante corte de ministérios, cargos comissionados, despesas administrativas, penduricalhos e supersalários com o objetivo de equilibrar as contas públicas e reduzir a carga tributária, não havendo qualquer previsão de supressão ou redução de programas sociais". As publicações mencionadas alvo da decisão de Mendonça foram feitas em 6 de outubro e relacionaram a política fiscal de um eventual governo de Flávio Bolsonaro a cortes em programas como Farmácia Popular, Minha Casa, Minha Vida e Mais Médicos, além de possíveis prejuízos a ações de combate ao câncer, de prevenção de desastres e à merenda escolar. Mendonça avaliou ainda que "é certo que programas de governo não constituem garantia absoluta de implementação futura das medidas anunciadas" e que "também é legítimo que adversários políticos questionem a viabilidade dessas propostas ou apontem eventuais contradições entre promessas eleitorais e posições anteriormente defendidas". "O que não se mostra admissível, contudo, é converter a mera possibilidade de divergência entre promessas e futuras ações governamentais em afirmação categórica de que direitos e benefícios determinados serão suprimidos, sem a indicação de elemento concreto que sustente semelhante conclusão", diz o ministro na decisão.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: Andros Garcia Maldaner, de 40 anos, mora desde 2018 nos Estados Unidos e está preso num centro de detenção de imigrantes ilegais da Flórida. — Foto: Montagem/g1/Acervo pessoal "Não consigo entender como a terra da liberdade se transformou nisso", afirma o executivo brasileiro Andros Garcia Maldaner, de 40 anos. Nos Estados Unidos desde 2018, ele viveu o sonho americano de construir carreira fora do Brasil durante oito anos. Mas viu esse sonho se tornar um pesadelo em 30 de julho , quando foi parado em uma blitz de trânsito em uma rodovia da Flórida . O executivo conta que saía do banco de investimentos Morgan Stanley , onde trabalha como assistente de vice-presidente, e seguia para casa para ver o filho de 8 anos. Mas Andros não voltou para casa e há está preso há dois meses em um Centro de Detenção para imigrantes ilegais com mais de 1.200 pessoas de nacionalidades diferentes. Embora não estivesse ilegalmente no país, ele foi acusado por um policial de trânsito de dirigir bêbado e foi entregue diretamente ao Serviço de Imigração e Controle de Alfândegas dos Estados Unidos ( U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement ), o ICE.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543625-bp.text: BP estimated on Tuesday its third-quarter refining margins tripled from last year as the Iran war boosts profits for oil majors, but also flagged $3 billion to $4.5 billion in impairments relating to its gas and low-carbon energy segment. This is the second time in a year that the British firm has booked large write-downs in its low-carbon business after writing down over $4 billion related to its solar, biogas and offshore wind businesses. Impairments in BP's transition businesses over the last year have added up to around $10 billion, or about 10% of BP's equity before the COVID pandemic earlier this decade, which "showcases the damage BP's previous adventures have caused," RBC analysts said in a note, referring to the foray into renewable energy the group abandoned last year. "We would imagine the house is now clean, but we also thought that last quarter," RBC said. BP estimated its refining indicator margin for the July-September quarter at $46.70 per barrel, up from $29.60 per barrel in the second quarter and $15.80 per barrel a year ago. The Iran war has disrupted global oil supplies, driving up prices and oil majors' margins. A boost to refining margins will lift BP's profit in the products segments by $1.9 billion to $2.1 billion versus the previous quarter, the group said in a trading statement ahead of results due on October 30.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/bp_slashes_.text: BP expects net debt to have declined by as much as $7.8 billion to $13.5-14.5 billion as of the end of the third quarter (Q3) from $22.3 billion at the end of Q2. The reduction partly reflects the redemption of $1 billion in hybrid securities, now expected to have fallen to around $12 billion entering the last quarter. "As a result, we expect the total of net debt, hybrid bonds, leases and Gulf of America settlement liabilities to reduce by around $9-10 billion compared with the second quarter", BP said in its quarterly trading statement. The statement previews results for the July-September period, scheduled for release October 30. On the other hand BP expects $3-4.5 billion in impairments for Q3. "These charges are primarily attributable to transition businesses in the gas and low-carbon energy segment and are excluded from underlying replacement cost profit [adjusted net income]", it said. BP had reported $6.04 billion in net impairments and losses from the sale of businesses and fixed assets for 2025. The company's annual report attributed the bulk of the figure to Lightsource BP and Archaea Energy, with charges also stemming from offshore wind assets. On December 16, 2025 state-owned Petróleo Brasileiro SA (Petrobras) and BP solar company Lightsource BP said they had penned a deal under which Petrobras would acquire 49.99 percent of Lightsource BP's subsidiaries in Brazil. Lightsource BP's Brazilian portfolio included 1-1.5 gigawatts (GW) in different stages of development, according to a joint online statement.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional (CSN) reduziu em R$ 75 milhões o capital imobilizado em estoques após reestruturar a governança de suprimentos e implementar ferramentas de análise da GTPLAN , empresa de tecnologia para gestão de supply chain. O projeto envolveu a revisão de quase 300 políticas de estoque que operavam sem padronização , com o objetivo de equilibrar a disponibilidade de materiais e a redução de recursos parados. Antes da iniciativa, as decisões de compra eram influenciadas pela percepção de risco e por regras pouco uniformes de reposição. A insegurança sobre as quantidades necessárias levava à formação de estoques preventivos, sem eliminar a ocorrência de falta de itens essenciais. O trabalho abrangeu materiais como equipamentos de proteção individual (EPIs), uniformes e outros itens considerados críticos para a operação industrial. Segundo Thiago Fialho, cofundador da GTPLAN, o excesso de estoque pode estar relacionado à ausência de critérios consistentes para orientar as compras. “Em grandes indústrias, o excesso de estoque raramente é um problema de volume de compras; em sua maioria, é de como as políticas de reposição estão desenhadas. Quando existem centenas de regras dispersas, a percepção subjetiva de risco passa a comandar os pedidos, gerando compras por proteção que pesam no caixa e não evitam rupturas”, afirma. Para estruturar o novo modelo, foram implementados dois módulos da plataforma: o SIO (Service and Inventory Optimization), voltado à otimização dos parâmetros de reposição e à calibração das políticas de estoque, e o MRP (Planejamento de Reposição por Compras), destinado à organização e à antecipação dos pedidos. O projeto também incluiu suporte técnico para revisar premissas e fundamentar as decisões das equipes internas. Além da redução do capital imobilizado, a metodologia contribuiu para diminuir os dias de cobertura dos estoques e elevar a taxa de atendimento das demandas. De acordo com Fialho, a combinação entre tecnologia e revisão contínua das regras de reposição permite reduzir recursos parados sem comprometer a disponibilidade de materiais necessários à operação. A GTPLAN atua no desenvolvimento de soluções SaaS para gestão da cadeia de abastecimento e informa atender mais de 800 clientes no Brasil. A empresa tem presença em setores como saúde e indústria, incluindo companhias como Gerdau, Suzano, CSN e Usiminas.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/video-u-s.text: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) reports that its forces disabled the commercial cargo vessel Ocean Molica [IMO: 9139270] in the Gulf of Oman, Oct. 10, after the ship’s crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran. A U.S. military fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica with a precision munition, fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew. The 70,296 DWT bulk carrier was attempting to transit regional waters after having previously departed an Iranian port, says CENTCOM. According to reports, the Ocean Molica’s registered owner, manager and operator is Western Bulk Shipping Co. Ltd., which is registered in Hong Kong. CENTCOM forces resumed the U.S. blockade against all ships entering or departing Iranian ports on July 14. Four commercial vessels have been disabled and 135 ships have been turned around during three months of strict enforcement. Additionally, U.S. forces have destroyed 10 tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ multibillion-dollar shadow network over the same period. CENTCOM warns that all mariners are advised to heed blockade warnings from CENTCOM forces. Crews should also continue to monitor Notice to Mariners broadcasts and contact U.S. naval forces on bridge-to-bridge channel 16 when operating in the Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz approaches.

https://gcaptain.com/fire-forces-crew-to.text: A U.S. Coast Guard Air Station New Orleans helicopter aircrew lowers a rescue swimmer to assist mariners aboard a life raft 100 miles south of Grand Isle, Louisiana, Oct. 12, 2026. U.S. Coast Guard image A fire aboard a seismic research vessel in the Gulf of Mexico forced dozens of crew members to abandon ship Monday, with nearby offshore supply vessels helping bring the evacuees safely ashore. The Cyprus-flagged Rem Andes was operating approximately 100 nautical miles south of Grand Isle, Louisiana, when the fire broke out on October 12, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. A Coast Guard C-27 Spartan aircraft from Air Station Clearwater intercepted the vessel’s mayday call and diverted to assist. Crew members who had evacuated into life rafts were picked up by responding offshore supply vessels and transported to Port Fourchon, Louisiana. Local reports indicated that 46 people were aboard the vessel, including 38 who evacuated into life rafts and eight who remained aboard to fight the fire and assess the damage. The Coast Guard had initially reported 42 people aboard. No injuries were reported. The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the vessel was coordinating commercial salvage operations, the Coast Guard said.

https://gcaptain.com/supertankers-turn-f.text: A file image from March 2, 2024, shows the Chinese-flagged VLCC supertanker Cosnew Lake, which exited the Red Sea via the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on July 23, 2026. VLADIMIR TONIC/Handout via REUTERS A growing number of empty supertankers have been turning away from the Persian Gulf as escalating Iranian attacks threaten a critical transfer hub for wartime oil shipments. At least 10 very large crude carriers and several Suezmax vessels approaching the port of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates have stopped or reversed course in recent days, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. While other vessels are still continuing on their journeys into the region, the retreat of these tankers amid near-daily attacks around the Strait of Hormuz — some near Fujairah itself — raises fresh concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the waterway. Fujairah is commonly signaled as an interim destination by vessels ultimately sailing to the Gulf of Oman — where they can collect cargoes via ship-to-ship transfer — or onward into the Persian Gulf. That makes the number of ships heading toward the port a broader indicator of tanker operators’ appetite for approaching the waterway. The shift threatens a key workaround that has helped Persian Gulf oil exports recover to near prewar levels. Large crude carriers can wait off Fujairah and in Omani waters outside Hormuz while shuttle tankers make the riskier transit through the strait, bringing out crude and transferring it for onward shipment to buyers.

https://gcaptain.com/saudi-arabia-strike.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, August 3, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer RIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) – Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis said Saudi Arabia was attacking the Yemeni capital Sanaa on Tuesday after a Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city’s outskirts, part of a rapidly escalating war between the sides. The Houthis have for a week been targeting Saudi airports, including a strike on Riyadh on Saturday that killed 13 people, in retaliation for the kingdom’s backing of government forces against the Houthis in Yemen’s reignited civil war. Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that the Saudi-led coalition had targeted the Yemen Petroleum Company’s Sabah central station, a fuel depot on the outskirts of Sanaa. The coalition said in a statement on Tuesday evening that it attacked the station and other sites in an operation aimed at “neutralizing the capabilities of Houthis” to threaten the kingdom, Yemen and international waterways. It said the Iran-aligned group was using the sites in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Dhamar to “supply its arsenal of missiles and drones” to attack Saudi Arabia and commercial vessels in the Red Sea.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/rec.text: At the same time, demand for tanker capacity has surged as traders seek alternative routes and sources of supply, including increased shipments from the US. The opening of a protected corridor through Omani waters has enabled additional crude exports and vessel movements, but has also placed further strain on an already stretched market. Shuttle services now operate around the Strait of Hormuz, with under the radar activity and ship-to-ship transfers taking place outside the chokepoint. The conflict and tanker seizures in the Persian Gulf erupted at a time when the market was already facing a shortage of capacity. New deliveries of crude carriers slowed sharply following a record-low order book in 2022-23, while an increasing number of older and smaller vessels joined Russia’s shadow fleet, further reducing the pool of compliant tankers available to the wider market. Crude tanker earnings rose tenfold on rush for capacity The capacity squeeze, combined with operating in risky war zones and facing highly elevated insurance premiums, has sent tanker rates soaring. We have seen previous surges in this volatile market, such as in 2022 after sanctions were placed on Russia, but this spike is beyond levels ever seen before. Average global crude vessel earnings exceeded an unprecedented level of $500,000 per day, 10 times the 2025 average, in early October. For Suezmax tankers and very large crude carriers (VLCCs, with a maximum capacity of 2m barrels) alone, rates surged even beyond that. Crude shipments from Ras Tanura in Saudi Arabia to Rotterdam made up about $2/bbl in 2025; in September, this surged beyond $35. Combined with high refinery margins (the current crack spread of diesel in Europe is about 2.5 times the 2025 average), this could add over $0.50 to the base price of a litre of diesel at the gas station. Earnings of product tankers have also tripled compared to the 2025 average. Nevertheless, these have responded much more moderately. This is mainly because of the key importance of the Middle East region for crude oil. And when it comes to the supertankers, the VLCCs, these are designated to transport crude and traditionally are intensively deployed on the Middle East trade routes. Crude tanker orders pick up after a prolonged downturn Tanker markets are cyclical by nature, and there’s a clear connection with freight rates. Over the pandemic years of 2020-21, tanker earnings hit lows due to lower oil consumption and shipments. This resulted in an order book of just 4% of global crude carrier capacity, the lowest on record since the 1990s.

https://petronoticias.com.br/aumentar-a-.text: A publicação do edital do primeiro Leilão de Gás Natural da União abre uma nova frente para ampliar o acesso da indústria brasileira ao insumo e fortalecer a competitividade de setores intensivos em energia e matérias-primas. A avaliação é da Associação Brasileira da Indústria Química (Abiquim), que defende medidas complementares para estimular a concorrência, aprimorar a infraestrutura e garantir condições econômicas e regulatórias adequadas ao aproveitamento industrial do gás natural. O edital prevê a oferta de até 1,1 milhão de metros cúbicos por dia, distribuídos em 110 lotes de 10 mil m³/dia, com fornecimento entre 1º de março e 31 de dezembro de 2027. O leilão será realizado em 22 de outubro, por meio da plataforma eletrônica da Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), e é destinado exclusivamente a empresas brasileiras enquadradas como indústria de base. Do total ofertado, 35 lotes são destinados aos setores químico e petroquímico, que utilizam o gás natural tanto como fonte de energia quanto como matéria-prima para a produção de fertilizantes nitrogenados, metanol, resinas termoplásticas, gases industriais e intermediários químicos. Em 2025, o consumo de gás natural da indústria química brasileira se aproximou de 7,1 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia, equivalente a aproximadamente um quarto do consumo industrial nacional, segundo dados reunidos pela Abiquim. “ O leilão é uma oportunidade importante para ampliar as alternativas de suprimento da indústria e avançar na abertura do mercado de gás natural. Mas a competitividade depende de uma agenda mais ampla, que envolva oferta efetiva, concorrência, infraestrutura e condições regulatórias capazes de permitir que o gás chegue à indústria a preços competitivos”, afirma André Passos Cordeiro, presidente-executivo da Abiquim. Para a entidade, a iniciativa deve ser acompanhada de avanços estruturais no mercado. Entre as prioridades estão a ampliação e a diversificação da oferta, o acesso aberto e não discriminatório às infraestruturas essenciais, a expansão da capacidade de escoamento, processamento, transporte e armazenagem, além de regras tarifárias mais eficientes. A Abiquim também defende o aproveitamento econômico do gás atualmente reinjetado, a comercialização competitiva do gás natural pertencente à União e o desenvolvimento de mecanismos que ampliem a concorrência entre fornecedores. Outro ponto é a valorização dos líquidos do gás natural, como etano, propano e butano, relevantes para a cadeia petroquímica. “ O Brasil precisa transformar sua disponibilidade de recursos naturais em produção industrial e valor agregado. Isso exige integrar a oferta de gás à infraestrutura e à demanda produtiva, com regras previsíveis e condições que estimulem investimentos no país, em vez de limit

https://petronoticias.com.br/o-instituto.text: O desenvolvimento de uma embarcação movida a hidrogênio contará com o apoio técnico do Instituto de Pesquisas Tecnológicas (IPT). O projeto JAQ H2 foi apresentado durante o São Paulo Boat Show 2026, realizado na capital paulista, e prevê uma embarcação capaz de produzir parte da energia necessária à própria navegação. O JAQ H2 é uma evolução do modelo JAQ H1, apresentado durante a COP30, conforme explicou Hernani Passiornic, fundador do Grupo Náutica. A iniciativa envolve diferentes parceiros estratégicos, entre eles o IPT, que deverá contribuir com sua infraestrutura e conhecimento técnico na área de hidrogênio. Intitulado “Arquitetura Nacional de Propulsão Naval Híbrida Inteligente para Embarcações de Baixa Emissão de Carbono (JAQ-H2)”, o projeto contempla o desenvolvimento de um sistema híbrido de propulsão que combina duas rotas complementares de geração de energia. “Nisto, o Laboratório de Hidrogênio do IPT poderá ter um papel fundamental “, afirma João Carlos Cordeiro, superintendente técnico da unidade Energia do Instituto. O uso do hidrogênio na embarcação busca contribuir para a descarbonização do transporte aquaviário. Segundo Cordeiro, a tecnologia pode proporcionar maior eficiência energética, reduzir o consumo de combustíveis fósseis e diminuir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa e de poluentes atmosféricos. O projeto prevê uma parceria institucional envolvendo o Laboratório de Hidrogênio (LabH2) do IPT e as empresas MWM, Quanthus, MAN e WEG. Inaugurado em 2025, o Laboratório de Hidrogênio (LabH2) amplia a capacidade do IPT de apoiar o desenvolvimento de tecnologias voltadas à transição energética e à descarbonização da economia. “O hidrogênio é um vetor energético eficiente para a transição para uma economia com menor emissão de gases de efeito estufa. Pode substituir combustíveis fósseis com eficiência e de maneira limpa. Sua produção pode envolver processos que utilizam exclusivamente energia renovável ou também alternativas de baixa emissão, como o aproveitamento de resíduos “, explica Cordeiro . A infraestrutura do LabH2 permite atuar em diferentes etapas da cadeia tecnológica do hidrogênio, incluindo produção, compressão, armazenamento e fornecimento, em condições controladas de segurança. Na inauguração do laboratório, Cordeiro já destacava o potencial da estrutura para apoiar projetos inovadores e ampliar a capacidade tecnológica do País . “Não dá para ser menos ousado se queremos conquistas importantes para nossa pesquisa e sociedade.Temos uma estrutura ímpar para produção, compressão, armazenamento e fornecimento de hidrogênio com segurança. Todo o laboratório e cada um dos seus componentes estarão disponíveis para apoiar a indústria nacional, a cadeia do hidrogênio e a sociedade.” Projetos como o JAQ H2 aproximam essa infrae

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: On Tuesday, strikes on merchant shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued with two reported attacks, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. UKMTO reported an attack on a tanker and another strike on a container ship in the strait on Tuesday, both to the north of the Musandam Peninsula. Both involved an "unknown projectile." UKMTO did not provide times, vessel names, damage, crew status or salvage details. Six attacks were reported Sunday - the most damage yet recorded in one day since the start of the conflict. None were reported on Monday. All stakeholders have been tight-lipped about tactics in the Strait of Hormuz standoff, but two Iranian officials told Reuters on Tuesday that their approach has changed, resulting in an increased hit rate in attacks on merchant shipping. Both the method of the attack and the pace of the operation have been changed, they told the news service, without providing exact details. The officials explicitly stated that the goal of the operation was to impede U.S.-sponsored oil exports through the strait, keeping global oil prices high and putting economic pressure on American voters ahead of the U.S. midterm election. They said that the strategy has support at the highest levels of Iranian leadership. Some of the vessels struck in recent attacks have suffered serious fires or disabling damage, indicating heavier hits than previously seen with UAV strikes. The nonpartisan Institute for the Study of War assesses that Iran may be "developing its anti-ship missile capabilities to improve its ability to target vessels." Drawing on recent Iranian state media statements, ISW infers that Iran may have developed an antiship variant of its inexpensive and plentiful Kheibar Shekan ballistic missile, then used it in an attempt to target American naval forces on September 5.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: The Suez Canal Authority reports it hit a new milestone in rebuilding volumes following the disruptions due to Red Sea security concerns. Despite the persistent concerns, volume continues to build with more carriers switching vessels back to their planned routes. Transits of containerships increased dramatically during the third quarter of 2026 versus 2025. The Suez Canal Authority released data reporting that 166 medium (over 130,000 net tons) and ultra-large container vessels made the transit between July and September. That is versus just 16 container vessels in that size range in the third quarter of 2025. Tonnage figures showed an equally large increase. The total for large container vessels reached 29 million net tons during the most recent quarter. That compared to just a total of 2.4 million net tons a year ago. "The Suez Canal holds a strategic significance for containerized trade due to the operational savings it achieves and its promotion of the concept of economies of scale,” said SCA Chairman Admiral Ossama Rabiee. He noted the mounting pressure on container lines, citing increasing fuel prices, while shippers have to contend with rising freight rates. He highlighted the Suez Canal for its ability to provide reduced transit times and shorter voyage distances, saying it contributes to enhancing economies of scale for container vessels. The authority continues its efforts to attract more vessels, and it expects to continue to see volumes rise. CMA CGM was at the forefront, but Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company, and OOCL have returned vessels to the routes through the Suez Canal and the Red Sea. COSCO has also restored some of its vessels, and the Premier Alliance, including Ocean Network Express (ONE), HMM, and Yang Ming, are set to return to the Suez Canal routes in the coming days. Today, October 13, two large CMA CGM vessels were making the transit, as the Suez Canal Authority reported its results. The brand- new CMA CGM Pantheon (233,559 dwt), which entered service in July, was part of the convoy coming from the north. The vessel, which has a capacity of 24,212 TEU and is registered in France, was making her first-ever transit while traveling between Tangier Med and Port Klang, Malaysia.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Since the February 2026 commencement of the military operations in Iran, the issue of maritime shipping chokepoints has dominated headlines, with the focus on the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, linking the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea (respectively) to the Indian Ocean and global shipping lanes more broadly. Even before this, the Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) initiated a broad-based fact-finding proceeding titled “Investigation Into Transit Constraints at International Maritime Chokepoints” focusing on seven key passages that have an outsized effect on global oceangoing trade: the Northern Sea Passage, the English Channel, the Malacca Strait, the Singapore Strait, the Strait of Gibraltar, the Panama Canal, and the Suez Canal. The FMC’s inquiry noted the 2021 grounding of the EVER GIVEN in the Suez Canal, which blocked that crucial maritime artery for six days, resulting in cascading backups for the following traffic. War and accidents are not the only causes of maritime chokepoints. Many of the bottlenecks identified in the FMC investigation, including the Suez and Panama canals, are susceptible to weather-related restrictions (and in fact, the EVER GIVEN incident was caused in part by an uncommonly strong sandstorm with high-velocity winds). With the advent of an unprecedented and historic El Nino phenomenon in 2026, the issue of maritime bottlenecks is becoming a problem well beyond the Middle Eastern war theater due to effects on the water levels in Gatun Lake, the manmade body of water that controls the passage draft for vessels transiting the Panama Canal. Due to the extreme drought conditions brought on by this year’s “Super El Nino” event, the water level in Gatun Lake has been trending well below historic levels, leading to increasing levels of passage restrictions by the Panama Canal Authority (PCA). These conditions led to both draft restrictions and per-day transit restrictions in September 2026, the latter of which included a cap for daily vessel transits at 34 as of September 4, with a further reduction to 32 transits starting September 15. There had been anticipation of even further reductions to 29.5 in October, but the PCA recently indicated these additional cuts would not be necessary — at least through December — due to meagerly higher rain levels in August/September. However, the previous restrictions led to PCA auctions for transit slots, resulting in a record-breaking $5.3 million bid (for a liquefied natural gas tanker) for transit on September 1, which “exceeded the previous record of $4.6 million set earlier in August and was nearly 100 times the median auction price of about $55,000 recorded before February.” The unanticipated delays, and potentially unanticipated costs, of navigating maritime chokepoints

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: The Panama Maritime Authority is highlighting that it is moving quickly to expel three tankers that were sanctioned days ago by the United States in the ongoing efforts to pressure Iran. While saying that it regularly monitors its registry for violators, the authority is also saying it had already dealt with the vessels included in the recent UK sanctions package. In the past, Panama has been criticized for harboring sanctions violators or being slow to react. The authority highlights that it must follow a prescribed procedure to notify vessels and revoke their registry while also saying it has increased its efforts and enacted new legislation to expedite the removal process. It cites a 2024 Executive Decree, which simplified the process and accelerated the time required to remove a ship from Panama’s rolls. In the first six months after the Executive Decree was invoked, Panama reports a total of 107 sanctioned vessels were removed from its registry. Three more were in the process. As the largest registry by number of ships, Panama has historically noted the challenges of monitoring all the vessels under its flag. Currently, it has approximately 7,700 flag vessels representing more than 196 million gross registry tons. The U.S. Treasury reported its latest efforts on October 8 as part of what it is calling Operation Economic Outcast. It said a total of 17 tankers were being listed as part of the efforts to further tighten the restrictions on the fleet of shadow tankers supporting Iran’s oil operations. The U.S. effort included vessels operating under a broad range of flags, including Comoros, Bahamas, Palau, Mongolia, Cameroon, Zanzibar, Sierra Leone, Vanuatu, Hong Kong, San Marino, Gambia, and notably three tankers registered in Panama. Panamanian officials noted that they have already restricted the three vessels listed by the United States and, according to databases, one of the ships has already changed its flag. AMP officials said the full removal of the vessels is in process. The product tanker Starway (46,000 dwt) is listed in the databases as having moved its flag in September to Barbados after sailing under the Panama flag for approximately two years. The ship is listed as being Chinese-managed and owned by a corporation registered in the Marshall Islands. The U.S. Treasury accused the vessel of having transported over three million barrels of Iranian naphtha since 2025.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: A cocaine-smuggling suspect was killed and two others were injured during a high-speed boat chase off the coast of Portugal on Sunday, according to the country's Judicial Police. Portugal and Spain are top transit countries for the wave of cheap, abundant Colombian cocaine flooding onto European shores. The trade starts in South America with cargoes loaded onto boats and ships for transatlantic transport to waters off the Canary Islands and the Strait of Gibraltar. The carrying vessel will drop off the drugs at a rendezvous point, and smugglers in powerful high-speed boats will pick up the goods for the final-mile delivery to the littorals west of Gibraltar. Their boats are too fast for most police interceptors, and they are often carrying arms. In the latest interaction, a suspicious high speed vessel - previously known to the authorities - was spotted on the high seas at a position about 80 nautical miles to the south of Faro. The boat's three-person crew attempted to resist arrest, using their four-outboard, 1,400-horsepower speedboat to attempt to flee. They suffered a serious collision with a pursuit boat during the chase. One suspect sustained severe injuries and was medically evacuated by helicopter; despite attempts at on-site first aid, he was declared dead on board the aircraft. The law enforcement team recovered 3.7 tonnes of cocaine at the scene. The two survivors were arrested and brought to shore in Portugal for trial. Cocaine flows adapt to enforcement pressure rapidly, shifting to routes where enforcement is lower and profits are higher. A combination of American pressure off Central America and strengthening pierside enforcement in European ports have pushed more volume onto the smuggling networks of Spain's southwestern shores. Availability, price and purity of cocaine have all reportedly improved at the street level in Europe - and at least some parts of the United States, despite U.S. Southern Command's lethal-force campaign targeting smuggling craft.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The Trump administration is renewing its challenges to Ørsted’s offshore wind farm, Revolution Wind, located off the coast of Rhode Island. The Department of Justice is asking a District Court in the District of Columbia to remand its prior approval of the construction and operations plan (“COP”) for further review on a project that has completed construction and is in the final stages of commissioning. It marks the third time the Trump administration has challenged the 704 MW wind farm project, which is contracted to supply power to Connecticut and Rhode Island. In August 2025, it sought to stop construction while the project was approximately 80 percent complete, but it was rejected by the courts. In December 2025, the administration included Revolution Wind in its stop-work orders, this time contending the operations posed a risk to national security due to the potential for radar interference. The courts again rejected the stop-work order and let the project resume construction in January 2026. The Department of Justice made its new filing in a case being pursued by an environmental group that has been challenging the project in the courts for years. Green Ocean has been suing the Department of the Interior and Revolution Wind, contending the project would cause harm to the environment. The new filing made on October 9 asked the court to grant Green Ocean a summary judgment on its claims against the National Marine Fisheries Service and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, related to the approval of the project. Further, it says the Department of the Interior agrees that remand of its prior approval of the construction and operations plan (COP) for the Revolution Wind Project is warranted so that the agency can reevaluate its compliance with the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act. The project gained its approval in 2023 during the closing days of the Biden administration. The Trump administration is alleging the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management issued the approval after it found that its preferred alternative was “expected to have major impacts on commercial fisheries and for-hire recreational fishing; cultural resources; other marine uses: scientific research and surveys; and visual resources.” The federal government is asking the court to send the approval of the COP back to the Department of Interior for further review. It would create a state of uncertainty for the project after years of review.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: Pessoas que estavam no Zig Festival, realizado na madrugada do último domingo (11), em São Paulo, relataram calor intenso e falta de ventilação na pista fechada do evento. O jovem Pedro Higa de 28 anos morreu após passar mal durante o festival , realizado em uma casa noturna, na Zona Oeste da capital paulista. O caso foi registrado como morte suspeita no 2º DP (Bom Retiro). Segundo uma pessoa presente no evento, que relatou à CNN Brasil , a temperatura no local teria chegado a 40°C, após medição com o celular . A testemunha que estava na plateia também afirmou que, por volta das 3h15, o público já estava sem camisa e não havia mais espaço nem junto às paredes do fundo . Ainda segundo a pessoa que preferiu não se identificar, após apenas 15 minutos de show , os espelhos dos dois únicos banheiros disponíveis já estavam cobertos de vapor . Para tentar aliviar a sensação, frequentadores colocavam a cabeça nas pias ou lavavam o rosto. “Muitos desistiram de voltar à pista e assistiram ao show da porta do banheiro”, relatou testemunha à CNN Brasil. O espectador que estava acompanhado de uma amiga, também afirmou que viu pessoas saírem carregadas do local . Uma das principais reclamações, segundo ele, era a demora da abertura das portas de emergência na lateral direita do palco, o que poderia ter ajudado a melhorar a ventilação . “Uns sentavam no chão e outros iam embora direto para fora. A equipe da produção demorou pelo menos 20 minutos até distribuir garrafas de água para o público”, relembra a pessoa presente no festival.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: American ambitions to bring nuclear power back to the waterfront are gathering steam: Bluecore Energy, the Long Beach-based floating nuclear power startup, has bought its first supply of low-enriched uranium, a 4.95-percent blend of U-235 suitable for a commercial nuclear power installation. Floating nuclear power has a long history, beginning with the USS Sturgis, a WWII-era Liberty Ship converted into a moored powerplant in the 1960s. Rosatom reinvigorated the concept with the construction of the moored nuclear power barge Akademic Lomonosov in the 2010s, and the idea has seen a resurgence in the United States in recent years. The concept has strong support from the U.S. Maritime Administration, including both sea-going and permanently-moored applications (like Bluecore's). The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) has been closely involved in an advisory and R&D capacity for years, and is providing Bluecore with class services, starting with an AIP issued in June 2026. Bluecore's BC-15 reactor is traditional: a conventional pressurized-water reactor using a commercial, standardized fuel assembly. According to its regulatory application with the Department of Energy, Bluecore picked well-known and approved reactor technology in order to focus the regulatory review on the maritime aspects - mounting a reactor on a barge and operating it at a port. That part of the regulatory process will involve both the Department of Energy and the U.S. Coast Guard, within their respective areas of expertise. Bluecore is headquartered within the Port of Long Beach, with which it has a strong partnership - but the fuel will not be coming to California. It is currently stored in the form of uranium hexafluoride (UF6), an intermediate stage before conversion to the uranium dioxide (UO2) used in fuel pellets. The supplier, Dutch commodity firm WMC, has America's largest commercial nuclear fuel facility. "Having access to the expertise and infrastructure at the largest commercial nuclear fuel facility in the U.S. allows us to approach this next phase with the rigor it requires. Our goal is not simply to move fast. It is to create and deliver zero-emission energy as safely and quickly as possible," said Megan Moyette, a former nuclear-sub officer who now serves as Bluecore's Licensing & Safety Lead. The purchase follows shortly after Bluecore's announcement of a successful $50 million seed round.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543673-pe.text: Petrobras has signed cost and volume balancing agreements with Shell, TotalEnergies and Petrogal covering the Berbigão and Sururu shared reservoirs in Brazil's offshore Santos Basin, under which it will receive a net payment of approximately $859 million. The agreements follow the implementation of production individualization agreements (AIPs) for the two reservoirs, which established revised ownership interests among the partners following approval by Brazil's National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP). Petrobras said the payment from its partners in the BM-S-11A consortium is expected to be settled by November 2026. Under the approved production individualization arrangements, Petrobras holds a 45.394% interest in the Sururu shared reservoir, alongside Shell with 23.742%, TotalEnergies with 21.367% and Petrogal with 9.497%. In the Berbigão shared reservoir, Petrobras holds a 62.913% interest, while Shell has 16.125%, TotalEnergies 14.512% and Petrogal 6.450%. The shared reservoirs span the BM-S-11A concession and the Transfer of Rights agreement, both operated by Petrobras.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543672-fu.text: Fugro has secured a $169 million (€150 million) unsecured financing facility from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to support the development and deployment of its uncrewed surface vessel (USV) technology and expansion of remote maritime operations. The financing will support a phased expansion of Fugro's remote operations capabilities, including the continued development and deployment of USV technology as part of the company's transformation program. The facility covers eligible costs incurred between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2031, with individual drawings carrying maturities of up to 10 years. The EIB financing ranks equally with Fugro's existing senior debt and is intended to provide long-term funding for the company's technology development and deployment plans. Separately, Fugro has secured a two-year extension of its existing senior unsecured debt facilities, moving their maturity to December 2031. The facilities comprise a $448 million (€400 million) revolving credit facility and a $112 million (€100 million) term loan, with the extension agreed on the same terms as those secured in December 2024.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543669-bw.text: BW Energy has secured $208 million in long-term lease financing for the Akoum wellhead platform (WHP) planned for its Bourdon oil field development offshore Gabon, alongside an 18-month extension of its $250 million corporate revolving credit facility. The project-level lease agreement with Minsheng Financial Leasing (MSFL) covers the full capital expenditure of the platform, which is being converted from the Akoum drilling rig into a 12-slot wellhead facility for installation at Bourdon. The agreement replaces previously announced short-term financing and has a firm term of eight years, with an option to extend for another four years, giving it a potential duration of 12 years. Lease costs will be shared among the partners in the BW Energy-operated Dussafu licence according to their participating interests, with BW Energy accounting for 73.5%. Ownership of the platform will transfer to the license at the end of the lease. BW Energy said the conversion of the Akoum rig is progressing according to plan, with first oil from Bourdon targeted for the first quarter of 2028. The company sanctioned the Bourdon Phase 1 development in May 2026, approximately 14 months after the discovery, targeting gross proved and probable (2P) reserves of 25 million barrels of oil equivalent, almost entirely oil.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543674-do.text: Norwegian offshore vessel owner DOF Group has secured a contract extension for its construction support vessel (CSV) Skandi Nomad. The 12-month extension will keep the vessel on firm contract until November 2027. The company classified the value of the option period as limited, representing a contract worth less than $15 million under its contract value reporting system. Skandi Nomad, built in 2010, is designed for subsea operations across a range of water depths and environmental conditions.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543666-ar.text: Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands. The request aims to prevent the United Kingdom from exploiting hydrocarbon resources on the continental shelf of the Northern Falklands Basin, the government added in a statement. The filing "seeks to preserve Argentina's sovereign rights over its continental shelf and prevent activities authorized unilaterally and illegally by the United Kingdom," the government added. Addressing Britain's parliament after Argentina's move, Uma Kumaran, parliamentary under-secretary for the foreign office, said that "legitimate commercial activity in the Falkland Islands remains lawful, and the British government stands behind those engaged in it." Kumaran added that the UK would engage with the tribunal process but would not provide a running commentary on the proceedings. "The notification does not constitute a judgment by an international court or tribunal. It does not invalidate licenses issued by the Falkland Islands government, alter the islands' regulatory authority, or require lawful hydrocarbon development activities to cease," Kumaran said. Britain also announced it was taking legal measures to protect businesses from pressure to comply with Argentine domestic measures.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543665-ir.text: Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. Tehran has tried to exert control over the Strait of Hormuz since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28. It has restricted passage through the waterway, which carried about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade before the war, in an effort to gain leverage over Washington. Its threats and attacks have severely curtailed traffic through the strait, driving up oil prices, though some oil has continued to transit. The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships. The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said. "The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices," one of the two officials said.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543664-gu.text: ExxonMobil has told Guyana it will need more offshore gas to maximize oil production than the government had expected, potentially leaving less for liquefied natural gas production and exports, two people close to the talks said. Guyanese officials are now weighing whether to shrink a planned LNG project or skip exports altogether and use the gas for domestic power and petrochemical facilities only. It would deal a blow to the South American nation's ambitions to become a regional energy powerhouse as it continues to grow oil and gas output. Guyana has been pushing a consortium led by Exxon, which controls all of the country's crude and gas production, to deliver as much gas as possible so that the nation can monetize its reserves, which rank among the largest in the region. But the Exxon group, which also includes Chevron CVX.N and China's CNOOC 600938.SS, is forecasting it will need about 2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) of gas for reinjection into oilfields so it can meet crude output targets at its government-approved projects, the people said. That required volume would constrain supplies for any gas export projects, including a floating LNG facility proposed by Fulcrum LNG, the US developer the government chose in 2024 to build and operate gas infrastructure in the country. Instead of the 6 million metric tons per annum (mtpa) of capacity initially planned, the project may now have to start with up to 3 mtpa and expand later, the people said.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543671-av.text: Aventa has acquired Irish Sea Contractors (ISC), an Ireland-based marine contractor specializing in subsea cable projects, commercial diving and marine civil engineering, as part of its strategy to expand offshore operations and installation capabilities. The acquisition combines Aventa's engineering, consulting and offshore installation activities with ISC's experience in subsea cable landfalls, nearshore installation, marine infrastructure construction and underwater inspection, repair and maintenance. ISC, based in County Wexford, has more than 40 years of experience in marine contracting, including fibre-optic and power cable projects across Ireland, the UK and mainland Europe. Its activities cover cable landfalls, pull-ins, nearshore installation, burial, protection and remedial works, alongside port and harbour construction and maintenance. The acquisition also brings ISC's AERSUB subsea cable repair solution, which has received DNV qualification, into Aventa's service portfolio. Aventa said the transaction would strengthen its ability to combine engineering and planning with offshore execution, particularly for offshore wind, interconnector and other marine energy and transmission projects.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543663-ge.text: A Ukrainian ex-military officer goes on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas. The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert to mount one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case will provide the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the crime. Prosecutors have alleged that Serhii K., who was arrested under an international warrant in Italy last year, worked with other members of the military to plan the clandestine operation on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities. Serhii K. has denied any involvement in the blasts that ruptured the 1,200-km (750-mile)-long Baltic Sea pipeline. The government in Kyiv has also denied any involvement, a sensitive point in its relations with Germany, Ukraine's largest European supplier of military aid. The Russian government said on Monday it expected a "just verdict" that would reveal the names of the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543662-eq.text: Equinor and its partners Petoro and TotalEnergies have made an oil and gas discovery near the Oseberg field in the Norwegian North Sea, with preliminary estimates indicating between 19 million and 50 million barrels of recoverable oil equivalent. The discovery was made in exploration well 30/8-7 S Grimsnes, drilled by the Deepsea Bergen rig in production license PL 190, approximately 15 kilometres southwest of the Oseberg Sør platform and 145 kilometers west of Bergen. Equinor said the partnership is planning a fast, cost-effective development by connecting the discovery to existing subsea infrastructure and producing the hydrocarbons through the Oseberg Sør platform. The Grimsnes discovery is planned to be tied back to the Stjerne subsea installation, which is already connected to Oseberg Sør. “This confirms that the area around the Oseberg field remains very attractive. We plan to quickly tie the discovery back to existing subsea facilities and produce the volumes through the Oseberg Sør platform. By making use of already paid for infrastructure we achieve good resource utilization and competitive barrels”, said Frode Skarstein, senior vice president for Exploration and Production West at Equinor. The well was drilled in water depths of 96 meters, with preliminary recoverable volumes estimated at between 3 million and 8 million standard cubic metres of oil equivalent.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A VLI economizou mais de 4 milhões de litros de diesel e evitou a emissão de 9,3 mil toneladas de CO₂ equivalente (CO₂e) com o uso do sistema Leader , tecnologia de condução semiautônoma de trens. Os resultados foram registrados entre o início da implementação, em maio de 2024, e julho de 2026. Atualmente, a ferramenta é utilizada em cerca de 60% das viagens ferroviárias realizadas pela companhia . O sistema analisa em tempo real dados da via e da composição para calcular um plano de condução otimizado. A partir dessas informações, ajusta aceleração, frenagem e velocidade do trem para reduzir o consumo de combustível, respeitando as restrições operacionais, os tempos de percurso e a integridade dos ativos. Nos corredores logísticos de maior movimentação da empresa, a tecnologia proporcionou economia média de combustível de aproximadamente 8%. Entre as áreas atendidas estão o Corredor Norte, que conecta o Tocantins ao Porto do Itaqui (MA) pelo tramo norte da Ferrovia Norte-Sul, e os Corredores Leste e Sudeste, que ligam regiões produtoras aos sistemas portuários do Espírito Santo e de Santos (SP), respectivamente, por meio da Ferrovia Centro-Atlântica. “A agenda de descarbonização é um fator de competitividade nas operações logísticas. O transporte ferroviário já emite cerca de seis vezes menos CO₂ que o rodoviário, quando comparado o uso de diesel em ambos os modais, e o uso de tecnologias como o sistema Leader nos permitem potencializar os resultados positivos, ao converter ganhos de produtividade em benefícios ambientais concretos e tornar nossa operação ferroviária ainda mais eficiente no consumo de combustível”, afirma Alessandro Gama, diretor-executivo de Planejamento, Engenharia e Tecnologia da VLI. A companhia também informou ter reduzido em 12,5% as emissões de gases de efeito estufa provenientes do diesel de locomotivas por tonelada transportada em 2025, em comparação com o ano-base de 2020. A meta é alcançar uma redução de 15% até 2030. Os inventários de emissões da VLI são públicos desde 2020 e passam por auditoria independente. A empresa possui o Selo Ouro do Programa Brasileiro GHG Protocol, nível máximo de qualificação da iniciativa, que reconhece a transparência e a conformidade dos dados reportados sobre emissões de gases de efeito estufa.

https://safety4sea.com/iran-accuses-us-f.text: Tehran has reportedly lodged a formal complaint with the IMO, alleging that US military forces have occupied VHF Channel 16 with threatening transmissions to Iranian seafarers, as fresh attacks on commercial vessels were reported near the Strait of Hormuz. I ran has accused US military forces operating in the Persian Gulf of misusing VHF Channel 16, the internationally recognised maritime distress, safety and calling frequency, warning that the alleged interference could jeopardise communications between vessels in an emergency. In a letter dated 9 October 2026, Iran’s ambassador and permanent representative to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) said Tehran had received reports in recent weeks from commercial vessels, shipping companies and maritime operators concerning the alleged use of the channel by US forces. According to the letter, US military personnel had repeatedly occupied VHF Channel 16 for prolonged periods, addressing Iranian seafarers in Persian with what Tehran described as threatening, abusive and provocative language. In some instances, the transmissions allegedly urged crews to abandon their vessels. Iran argued that the reported conduct had disrupted the availability of an essential maritime safety channel, causing significant stress and psychological pressure among civilian crews. The complaint cited IMO Assembly Resolution A.954(23), entitled Proper Use of VHF Channels at Sea, which addresses the appropriate use of VHF radio communications. Tehran warned that using the channel for purposes unrelated to maritime safety could obstruct or delay genuine distress, urgency and safety traffic, potentially placing ships and seafarers at risk.

https://safety4sea.com/etf-issues-appeal.text: The European Transport Workers’ Federation (ETF) has called on European Union leaders to take immediate action to protect seafarers and dock workers following continued attacks on merchant vessels and maritime infrastructure. I n an appeal issued on October 13 ahead of the European Council meeting on October 15-16, ETF urged EU leaders, the European Commission, Member States and relevant national and international authorities to prioritize the safety of civilian maritime workers and restore safe navigation in the Black Sea. According to Ukrainian government figures published in September 2026, 1,173 port infrastructure facilities and 274 civilian vessels have been damaged or partially destroyed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The federation emphasized that seafarers of many nationalities, including Ukrainian and Russian nationals, work aboard merchant vessels operating in European waters and worldwide, often alongside one another. It stressed that no seafarer should be held responsible for the actions of their government or exposed to danger because of their nationality. Seafarers and dock workers are civilians, not combatants. They must never be targets … ETF stated, adding that merchant vessels, ports and civilian maritime infrastructure must be protected in accordance with international law.

https://safety4sea.com/guangzhou-port-co.text: Guangzhou Port has completed its first green methanol bunkering operation alongside a terminal, marking a further step in the expansion of alternative-fuel supply infrastructure in China. A s more dual-fuel vessels enter service, access to reliable bunkering infrastructure will be essential to enabling operators to incorporate alternative fuels into their trading patterns. As stated, the operation marks a milestone in the port’s efforts to expand its alternative-fuel capabilities as the shipping industry accelerates its search for lower-emission energy solutions. The bunkering, carried out on 28 September at the Nansha port area, saw 281.6 metric tonnes of green methanol supplied to the COSCO Shipping Carnation. The fuel was delivered by the Da Qing 268, a methanol dual-fuel oil and chemical bunkering vessel operated by China Shipping & Sinopec Suppliers (Sinobunker). The vessel is described as China’s first bunkering ship of its kind and has a total tank capacity of 10,362 cubic metres. The receiving vessel, COSCO Shipping Carnation, is among COSCO Shipping’s first series of 16,000-TEU methanol dual-fuel container ships. Measuring 366 metres in length and 51 metres in width, the vessel is equipped with an 11,000-cubic-metre methanol fuel tank and operates on the US West Coast trade route. According to Guangzhou Port Group, the port has already carried out anchorage-based green methanol bunkering, as well as terminal-based LNG bunkering for international roll-on/roll-off (ro-ro) vessels and bulk carriers since the beginning of the year.

https://safety4sea.com/emsa-annual-overv.text: The European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) has published its Annual Overview of Marine Casualties and Incidents 2026, providing a decade-long assessment of maritime safety based on data recorded between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2025. A ccording to EMSA, a total of 26,802 marine casualties and incidents were recorded during the 2016–2025 period. In 2025, the number of reported occurrences stood at 2,630, approximately 2% below the ten-year annual average. These included 52 very serious casualties, among the lowest annual totals recorded over the period. The incidents reported in 2025 resulted in 29 fatalities, 813 injuries, five missing persons and the loss of 16 ships. While the number of lives lost fell to its lowest annual level in the decade under review, the number of injured persons remained comparatively high, highlighting the continued human impact of maritime accidents. The report draws on occurrences recorded in the European Marine Casualty Information Platform (EMCIP) by the safety investigation authorities of the 27 EU Member States, Iceland and Norway. It places the figures for 2025 in the context of trends observed over the preceding ten years. Cargo ships accounted for the largest share of marine casualties and incidents recorded over the 2016–2025 period, followed by passenger ships. At subtype level, solid-cargo ships represented approximately 38% of all occurrences, while conventional passenger ships and passenger/Ro-Ro cargo ships combined accounted for around 23%. The age profile of ships involved in reported occurrences was distributed across several age groups. Vessels aged 15–29 years formed the largest group among ships of known age, accounting for approximately 39% of occurrences over the 2016–2025 period. Their share rose to 45.5% in 2025.

https://safety4sea.com/abs-and-u-s-doe-p.text: The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to advance commercial nuclear technology for maritime applications. T he agreement, announced on 12 October, focuses on concept and feasibility studies for floating nuclear power and nuclear transportation corridors, alongside efforts to develop a U.S. shipbuilding sector capable of safely building and operating nuclear-powered maritime assets. Under the MoU, ABS will co-manage the Maritime Nuclear Applications Group (MNAG) and provide technical, regulatory, economic and policy support for concept development and feasibility studies. The organization will also work with DOE to strengthen coordination across U.S. government agencies and support the development of a viable domestic maritime nuclear sector. ABS will coordinate related activities through the U.S. Center for Maritime Innovation (USCMI), an initiative of the U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD), for which ABS serves as Secretariat. Previously, MARAD and CORE POWER had signed a Memorandum of Cooperation aimed at developing the commercial, regulatory and industrial framework needed for a future fleet of U.S.-flagged nuclear-powered merchant ships. ABS Chairman and CEO John McDonald said the agreement provides a framework to build on existing work and advance nuclear energy as a practical option for commercial maritime applications, with safety remaining a key consideration.

https://safety4sea.com/cm-available-does.text: Seafarer welfare is often measured by what is provided: shore leave, connectivity, welfare centres, transport, medical support and recreational facilities. But recent evidence from Australia exposes a more fundamental question. Can seafarers actually use what is supposedly available to them? T he distinction between provision and effective access may be one of the most important gaps in how maritime welfare is currently assessed. The Seafarer Port Welfare Survey, conducted by ASWC and released by the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) , collected 436 responses from seafarers visiting Australian ports. Despite the country’s established network of welfare services and Port Welfare Committees, respondents identified several barriers to accessing support. Of the 202 seafarers who answered the relevant question, 55, approximately 27%, reported being unable to go ashore. Fast cargo operations, short port stays, inspections and onboard responsibilities were among the main obstacles. Limited transport options, long distances between terminals and port gates, and associated costs created further difficulties. The findings illustrate how shore leave may be permitted in principle but remain difficult to arrange in practice.

https://safety4sea.com/bulgaria-summons-.text: Bulgaria has summoned Russia’s ambassador after drone attacks struck two merchant ships in the Black Sea, sinking one vessel and leaving crew members missing, as concerns grow over the conflict’s expanding impact on commercial shipping. B ulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev convened an emergency meeting on October 13, 2026, and summoned Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova following the overnight attacks. While Bulgaria has stopped short of directly blaming Moscow, Radev said the outcome of the incidents “benefits the Russian Federation.” The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity sank approximately 17 nautical miles (31 km) east of the village of Krapets , near the Romanian border, after issuing a distress signal. Bulgarian officials reported that six crew members were rescued, while 10 remained missing, with search and rescue operations ongoing. Earlier reports put the number of missing crew at 11, but the latest figures from the Bulgarian authorities indicated 10 missing. The second vessel, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea-3 , was struck by three drones approximately 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala. All 15 crew members, including seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, were rescued. Five sustained minor injuries, but none were reported to be seriously injured. Both vessels were struck in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ), outside its territorial waters. This is absolutely unacceptable, another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters

https://safety4sea.com/cmes-and-rina-to-.text: China Merchants Energy Shipping (CMES) and RINA have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore cooperation in maritime safety, digitalization, operational efficiency and emerging shipping technologies. T he agreement establishes a framework for long-term collaboration, building on the existing relationship between the two organizations and combining their expertise to support innovation and address the maritime sector’s evolving needs. Under the MoU, the companies will explore initiatives covering fleet safety and risk management, carbon emissions management, regulatory compliance, and data-driven vessel operations. They will also examine applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive maintenance, energy efficiency and operational decision-making. During the 2023 SMART4SEA Athens Forum, Mr. Themistoklis Sardis, IT Manager, Costamare Shipping Company S.A. explained that, among other things, AI can be used to predict when equipment and vehicles will need maintenance, this will help to reduce downtime and save costs. The cooperation will further cover research into alternative fuels, smart shipping technologies, automation and other innovations relevant to the industry’s future development. In addition, CMES and RINA will promote technical exchanges, research activities and knowledge sharing to support operational excellence and help address the maritime sector’s changing regulatory and technological requirements.
