https://splash247.com/japan-prepares-to-.text: Japan is preparing to subsidise the additional cost of importing oil from suppliers outside the Strait of Hormuz, in a significant government intervention aimed at reducing the country’s dependence on the increasingly dangerous waterway. The Japanese cabinet approved three bills yesterday designed to diversify energy imports, support tanker insurance and finance alternative oil transport infrastructure. The proposed legislation would establish a grant scheme compensating refiners, trading houses and petrochemical companies for part of the additional cost of sourcing crude and petroleum products from alternative suppliers. Japan sourced 94% of its crude oil imports from the Middle East last year, with government figures putting its dependence on the Strait of Hormuz at 93%, although the latter measure is based on countries of origin rather than actual tanker movements. Diversifying towards suppliers such as the US would substantially increase tonne-miles and shipping costs. Diversifying towards American crude would substantially increase tonne-miles. Tanker voyages from the US Gulf Coast to Japan via the Cape of Good Hope can take 45 to 60 days, or 35 days via the Panama Canal, compared with roughly 20 to 30 days from the Middle East. The funding scheme would be administered by state-backed Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC), using contributions collected from oil importers.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/suez-can.text: "During the first two weeks of October, weekly container ship capacity transiting the Suez Canal averaged 753k TEU, according to Clarksons Research, compared with 1,457k TEU during the same period in 2023. Since the Houthi attacks began in the Red Sea, this is the first time that transits have exceeded 50% of pre-disruption levels,” says Niels Rasmussen, Chief Shipping Analyst at BIMCO. In November 2023, the Houthis announced that they would target Israeli ships in the Red Sea in response to Israeli attacks in Gaza. They later broadened their criteria to include attacks on other ships, which created uncertainty. To avoid attacks, container lines began diverting ships away from the Suez Canal and the Red Sea in December 2023 and started sailing via the Cape of Good Hope. By the last week of 2023, weekly container ship capacity transiting the Suez Canal had fallen to 330k TEU, compared with the year-to-date average of 1,290k TEU. “From early February 2024 to mid-2026, container ship capacity transiting the Suez Canal averaged 141k TEU per week, equal to on average 11% of the capacity recorded during the same weeks of 2023,” says Rasmussen. Since the Gemini Alliance (Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd) announced on 6 July 2026 that its AE15/SE3 Asia–Mediterranean service would return to the Suez Canal, the move back to normal routings has gathered pace. The Gemini Alliance has since announced the return of five more services to their normal routings, including its remaining three Asia–Mediterranean services. Members of the Ocean Alliance and Premier Alliance, as well as MSC, have also announced routing changes. In total, changes to 16 services have been announced since early July.

https://splash247.com/the-floating-conta.text: Every so often a ship comes along that makes even seasoned shipping watchers look twice. Meet the Fan Zhou 8, an extraordinary floating container platform that has just carried more than 3,000 teu out of China. According to Alphaliner, German independent carrier Carrier53′ Shipping chartered the 2024-built, 58,405 dwt heavy-load deckship from China’s Jiangsu Fanzhou Shipping for a September loading at Taicang, near Shanghai. The vessel loaded 1,558 40 ft high-cube containers, equivalent to 3,116 teu, stacked across an enormous open deck measuring 256 m long and 51 m wide. Its vast, unobstructed deck covers an area equivalent to almost two football pitches. The boxes were arranged in 17 bays and 20 rows, stacked five tiers high, with just two tiers on the outer rows. Alphaliner describes the ship as one of the world’s largest heavy-load deckships, a vessel type rarely seen carrying containers on this scale. The voyage was arranged in cooperation with container trader Lotus Containers. Carrier53′ specialises in unconventional cargo movements, including oversized 53 ft containers manufactured in China for the North American market. Such boxes can prove awkward for conventional liner operators, particularly when capacity is tight.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: O Grupo CMA CGM e o Grupo ENGIE anunciaram uma parceria para desenvolver uma unidade de produção de biometano na zona industrial-portuária de Le Havre, na França, área do HAROPA PORT e um dos principais polos logísticos da Europa. A usina deverá começar a operar entre 2029 e 2030 e produzir cerca de 7 mil toneladas de biometano por ano, volume destinado à frota da armadora. A ENGIE será responsável por liderar o projeto, incluindo o desenho técnico e o processo de licenciamento. Se houver decisão final de investimento, a companhia também assumirá a construção e a operação da planta. A CMA CGM entrará como acionista minoritária, com aporte feito pelo PULSE, fundo de energia do grupo voltado a tecnologias inovadoras e infraestruturas que apoiem a descarbonização de suas atividades de transporte e logística. A unidade vai converter resíduos de pecuária, biorresíduos domésticos e resíduos agrícolas em biometano. O combustível será entregue aos navios da CMA CGM pela rede de gás europeia, sob um sistema certificado de balanço de massa. Nesse modelo, o biometano injetado na rede é contabilizado e atribuído ao consumidor, sem que as moléculas cheguem fisicamente ao tanque do navio. O processo também gerará 100 mil toneladas de digestato, material orgânico rico em nutrientes que pode ser usado como fertilizante natural por agricultores locais. Além disso, 13 mil toneladas de CO₂ biogênico serão recuperadas para comercialização, o que melhora o desempenho do projeto em redução de emissões. Quando estiver em operação, a unidade deve evitar cerca de 23 mil toneladas de emissões de CO₂ por ano, segundo a CMA CGM. Todo o biometano produzido será dedicado ao abastecimento da frota de navios dual fuel do grupo. O investimento se soma à parceria iniciada pelos dois grupos em 2021 para acelerar a transição energética. Para a CMA CGM, garantir acesso a combustíveis renováveis é condição para descarbonizar a frota. https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy released images on Wednesday morning, October 14, claiming that a containership had struck a mine while traveling on an “illegal and dangerous” route through the Strait of Hormuz. The cause of the incident has not been confirmed, but the sinking of the vessel is being widely reported after Iran struck a total of four vessels in the past hours. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that it had received information that two container vessels had been struck, but both reports said there was minor damage to the ships. The vessels were not identified, but one was said to be a 50,000-tonne containership and the second was identified as a 19,000-tonne containership, with the reports saying both were struck by unidentified projectiles. The vessel seen with containers strewn in the water in the Iranian images is being identified as the GFS Pride (39,446 dwt), built in 2008, and operated by a company based in Dubai. The vessel was registered in Singapore with a capacity of 2,824 TEU. According to the Iranian statement, the vessel “exploded and caught fire” after striking a mine. They made no mention of the crew or any rescue efforts. It is one of two containerships from the same company that were reported to have been struck. The other, GFS Giselle (54,117 dwt), was built in 2015 and also registered in Singapore. It has a capacity of 4,370 TEU. Both vessels’ last registered position on GPS was in the Fujairah Anchorage nearly two weeks ago. Singapore's Maritime and Ports Authority issued a statement confirming the attack on both vessels and that the GFS Pride has sunk. It said all 21 crew members were safely evacuated while calling the attacks "unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law." It said the GFS Giselle had been able to proceed to a safe anchorage and that all 22 crewmembers were safe.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543678-gu.text: Guardian Decommissioning and Wild Well Control have signed an agreement for the decommissioning of the Bullwinkle offshore platform in Green Canyon Block 65 in the U.S. Gulf, with well abandonment activities scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026. Under the agreement, Guardian will assume operatorship as agent of the wells and, subsequently, the pipelines and platform, overseeing the project through final decommissioning. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543676-su.text: Sunda Energy has advanced to the exclusive phase of its application for an offshore petroleum exploration permit covering the Awakino gas condensate discovery in New Zealand's Taranaki Basin, following the conclusion of a three-month competitive bidding period. The application covers approximately 645 square kilometers offshore the west coast of New Zealand's North Island, including the Awakino-1 and Awakino South-1/ST1 gas condensate field, originally discovered in 1985. Sunda submitted its application on July 14, 2026, under New Zealand's open market competitive process for petroleum exploration permits. The three-month period during which competing applications could be submitted ended on October 14, leaving Sunda's application exclusive. New Zealand Petroleum and Minerals (NZPAM) will now undertake a detailed assessment of the proposal before deciding whether to grant the permit. Sunda cautioned that neither the award of the permit nor its timing is guaranteed.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Fulwood anunciou a ampliação de seu condomínio logístico em Extrema (MG), o Infinity Business Park. As obras começam neste bimestre e devem adicionar cerca de 40 mil m² de área bruta locável ao empreendimento. De acordo com a empresa, a expansão deve gerar 860 empregos diretos e indiretos, além dos 120 postos de trabalho diretos atuais. O condomínio próximo à Rodovia Fernão Dias conta com quatro módulos e 37 mil m² de área construída, atualmente ocupados por uma única empresa da área de eletrodomésticos e eletroportáteis. Os galpões são padrão triple A, com pé-direito livre de 12 metros, iluminação LED e zenital, sistema de reaproveitamento de águas pluviais, infraestrutura para recarga de veículos elétricos e áreas de apoio a motoristas e equipes administrativas. “Além de entregar infraestrutura adequada às demandas de operações cada vez mais complexas, os empreendimentos logísticos têm um papel importante na geração de oportunidades e no fortalecimento da economia dos municípios onde estão inseridos. O Infinity Business Park traduz essa visão ao combinar uma localização estratégica, padrão construtivo elevado e potencial de crescimento em uma região de grande relevância para o setor”, afirma Fernando Schilis, diretor comercial da Fulwood . Em Minas Gerais, a Fulwood já investiu mais de R$ 1,5 bilhão no desenvolvimento de condomínios logísticos ao longo da última década. Com o Infinity Business Park, a companhia soma sete parques logísticos em Extrema. A companhia conta ainda com empreendimentos em Pouso Alegre e Betim, consolidando sua atuação em regiões estratégicas para a logística nacional.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/mma_propose.text: The Marine Minerals Administration (MMA) announced, in a statement posted on the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management’s (BOEM) website recently, the availability of a Proposed Notice of Sale for Big Beautiful Cook Inlet 2, or BBC2. This is the second offshore oil and gas lease sale in Alaska’s Cook Inlet required by the Working Families Tax Cut Act of 2025, the statement noted, adding that the proposed sale would make approximately 1.05 million acres available for leasing in the northern portion of the Cook Inlet Planning Area. This is the same area offered in the Big Beautiful Cook Inlet 1 sale, held in March 2026, the statement pointed out. The proposed lease area includes 224 blocks stretching roughly from Kalgin Island in the north to Augustine Island in the south, the MMA statement revealed. The MMA outlined in its statement that, on Tuesday, it sent the Proposed Notice of Sale to the governor of Alaska and published a Notice of Availability in the Federal Register. This step began a 60-day regulatory review period for the state and affected local governments to submit comments and recommendations on the proposed sale’s size, timing, and location, the statement revealed, noting that the MMA will consider those comments and recommendations before issuing a Final Notice of Sale. The Proposed Notice of Sale includes the proposed size, timing, and location of the sale, as well as lease stipulations, terms and conditions, minimum bids, royalty rates, and rental rates, the statement said. “To encourage strong industry participation and support investment in domestic energy production, the proposed terms include a 12.5 percent royalty rate,” the MMA highlighted.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 14/10/2026 - A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ) publicou, nesta terça-feira (13), o edital do Leilão nº 04/2026, referente ao arrendamento da área IQI16, localizada no Porto do Itaqui, em São Luís (MA). A capacidade dinâmica anual estimada é de 1,008 milhão de toneladas. O Porto do Itaqui é um importante corredor logístico para o transporte de cargas no Maranhão e em outros estados, especialmente das regiões Norte e Nordeste. A área IQI16 tem relevância para a movimentação e a armazenagem de insumos como fertilizantes, utilizados na produção agrícola. A exploração do terminal contribui para a estruturação da capacidade portuária e para a integração entre transporte aquaviário e as cadeias de abastecimento.

https://gcaptain.com/containership-sinks.text: An image purportedly shows the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS PRIDE listing heavily and emitting thick black smoke following an attack in the Strait of Hormuz on October 13, 2026. The vessel subsequently sank, with all 21 crew members safely evacuated. The image has not been independently verified. A Singapore-flagged containership has sunk after being struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, as a widening series of attacks on merchant shipping raises fresh questions about U.S. claims of control over the strategic waterway. The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) confirmed Wednesday that the container ship GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire following an attack on October 13 and subsequently sank. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated, with no injuries reported. A second Singapore-registered container ship, GFS GISELLE , was struck on October 14, Singapore time, sustaining hull damage. The vessel subsequently reached a safe anchorage under its own power. All 22 crew members were reported safe. The loss of GFS PRIDE appears to mark the second confirmed sinking of a large, ocean-going ship during the conflict, following the loss of the Safeen Prestige . The latest sinking comes amid a sharp escalation in attacks on commercial shipping. At least six vessels were struck in a single day on Sunday, October 11, and UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has since issued four additional verified attack warnings covering incidents on October 13.

https://petronoticias.com.br/murphy-oil-.text: A petrolífera americana Murphy Oil, sediada em Houston, anunciou que conseguiu resultados positivos de exploração e avaliação de poços offshore na Costa do Marfim e no Vietnã, além do início de operações de novos ativos em águas vietnamitas e no Golfo dos Estados Unidos. Na Costa do Marfim, o poço Bubale West-1X, situado no bloco CI-103, foi perfurado até uma profundidade medida total de aproximadamente 19.357 pés (5.900 metros), em uma lâmina d’água de 9.039 pés (2.755 metros). A perfuração identificou cerca de 27 metros de espessura líquida de petróleo no reservatório Turoniano. A empresa destacou que também foram encontrados hidrocarbonetos em um reservatório mais profundo, do período Albiano. As análises preliminares dos perfis de poço e das amostras de fluidos indicam a presença de petróleo de alta qualidade. Segundo a companhia, as informações obtidas com a perfuração serão integradas aos dados geológicos já existentes para otimizar o restante do programa de avaliação da descoberta de Bubale. Enquanto isso, no Vietnã, a companhia americana divulgou mais detalhes sobre o resultado exploratório do poço Lac Da Trang North-1X, localizado no bloco offshore 15-1/05. O poço identificou 40 metros de espessura líquida de petróleo e foi perfurado até uma profundidade medida total de aproximadamente 12.579 pés (3.834 metros), em uma lâmina d’água de 45 metros. A Murphy e suas parceiras avaliarão os dados obtidos no poço Lac Da Trang North-1X para analisar as possibilidades de novas atividades de avaliação e desenvolvimento. O campo de Lac Da Vang, localizado nas proximidades, oferece infraestrutura que poderá ser utilizada para conectar a descoberta de Lac Da Trang North às instalações existentes, abrindo caminho para um desenvolvimento com menor necessidade de capital e prazo mais curto até o início da produção. A Murphy também anunciou o início da produção de petróleo no campo de Lac Da Vang (Golden Camel), offshore do Vietnã, e a entrada em operação do poço de desenvolvimento Chinook #8, no Golfo dos Estados Unidos, na região do Golfo do México.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: O Inmet (Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia) emitiu um alerta laranja de "perigo" para tempestade, nesta quarta-feira (14), em seis estados do Centro-Sul do país. Áreas do Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul e do Paraná devem ser afetadas. A previsão é de precipitação de 60 mm/h ou 100 mm ao longo do dia, ventos intensos de até 100 km/h e queda de granizo . Segundo o Instituto, há risco de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de árvores e de alagamentos. O aviso tem início à 00h de quarta (14), e é válido até o final do dia às 23h59. Quase todo o estado de São Paulo está sob alerta. Os municípios de Presidente Prudente, São José do Rio Preto, Campinas, Bauru, Piracicaba, Assis, Araraquara, Marília, Itapetininga, Ribeirão Preto, Araçatuba devem ser atingidos pelo temporal. As regiões do Litoral Sul Paulista, Vale do Paraíba Paulista, Metropolitana de São Paulo e Macro Metropolitana Paulista também devem sofrer com as fortes chuvas. https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A A.P. Moller – Maersk concluiu o abastecimento do Tangier Maersk, porta-contêineres dual fuel preparado para operar com álcoois, usando etanol de milho 100% produzido nos Estados Unidos. Segundo a companhia, a operação foi o primeiro abastecimento comercial ship-to-ship de etanol realizado em um navio de longo curso no país. O abastecimento ocorreu em 28 de setembro e faz parte do esforço da Maersk para explorar múltiplos caminhos de combustível para o futuro do transporte marítimo. A empresa afirma que a operação trouxe aprendizados sobre aspectos operacionais, de infraestrutura, de suprimento e de cadeia logística associados ao uso do etanol como combustível marítimo. A Maersk destaca que o etanol conta com uma base de produção já estabelecida, infraestrutura existente e compatibilidade com a tecnologia de navios preparados para álcoois. Esses fatores ajudam a explicar o interesse do setor pelo combustível. Ao mesmo tempo, a companhia pondera que a escalabilidade de rotas futuras de combustível dependerá também da disponibilidade do produto, da regulamentação e da prontidão operacional ao longo de toda a cadeia de valor marítima. Em outras palavras, a viabilidade do etanol em larga escala passa por fatores que vão além do navio e do motor. Ditlev Blicher, presidente regional da Maersk para a América do Norte, afirmou que alcançar uma logística de menor emissão exige transformar novas tecnologias em soluções práticas e escaláveis. Segundo ele, o abastecimento do Tangier Maersk oferece experiência real com combustíveis alternativos no transporte marítimo comercial, e os aprendizados devem contribuir para o desenvolvimento de cadeias de suprimento mais sustentáveis. A operação se apoia em testes anteriores com etanol realizados nos navios Laura Maersk e Antonia Maersk. Para a companhia, o conjunto de iniciativas reflete o compromisso de explorar e fazer avançar caminhos considerados críveis para a transição energética do setor.

Kennedy is the second in the class and the first to deliver with all of the special features required to support the F-35C fighter on deployment. The ship completed acceptance trials in August and received "preliminary acceptance" on September 29. The service says that this status will open up the fastest path possible to get the carrier up to full combat readiness after years of delays. As of September, the Kennedy team was still completing testing of four of the ship's Advanced Weapons Elevators, the electromagnetically-actuated platforms that carry munitions between the stores on the lower deck levels, the hangar bay and the main deck. The AWE system was designed to be faster than previous designs, but it proved to be a multi-year reliability challenge during commissioning of first-in-class USS Gerald R. Ford. The Navy believes that lessons learned from the experience with Ford will make Kennedy's commissioning go faster. The third Ford class carrier, the future USS Enterprise (CVN-80), is also experiencing delays and is now on track to deliver in 2030. The timing of the fourth hull, CVN-81, is uncertain and depends in part on an executive decision. The White House has ordered a study on installing steam catapults and hydraulic elevators on CVN-81. Steel has already been cut and the change would likely cause delays, according to America's sole carrier shipbuilder, Huntington Ingalls Industries. "It's a significant effort [to change the design for steam catapults]. It would delay the ship schedule significantly and there'd be a pretty significant cost related to it that we'd have to figure out with the Navy," HII CEO Christ Kastner said on the Mission Critical podcast last week.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: Austal confirmed in a stock exchange filing on Wednesday, October 14, that it has commenced commercial negotiations with Hanwha Defense USA while also extending the due diligence process following the earlier indication of interest in acquiring the US operations of the Australian company. At the same time, it reports there is an ongoing dialogue with a US-based investment firm that also indicated interest in bidding for the shipbuilding operations. The companies went public in early August, reporting that Hanwha Defense USA had made a non-binding offer of between $1.0 and $1.2 billion for the U.S. operation while calling for a due diligence review. Hanwha says the substantive issues have been completed but that it is also extending the due diligence period to complete “lower materiality data requests” from Hanwha that remain outstanding. The goal was to permit Hanwha to review the data in order to firm up its indicative, non-binding, conditional offer, which was announced on August 10. Austal expects Hanwha to produce a binding offer and reports that negotiations have begun with Hanwha regarding a potential transaction. Austal reports it is also seeking professional advice on various tax implications for a potential deal. A month after the initial announcement, U.S.-based Wildcat Infrastructure also came forward with a separate “non-binding indication of interest” for the U.S. operations of Austal. It proposed a higher valuation of $1.25 to 1.35 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis. However, it is said it was conditional on being able to conduct four weeks of due diligence. Ausutal says it “remains in ongoing dialogue with Windcat Infrastructure.” It did not indicate if the proposed due diligence would proceed or if it could be setting the stage for a bidding war. The continuing discussions represent a change in posture for Austal, which a little over a year ago rejected overtures from Hanwha to acquire the whole company. At the time, Austal questioned the ability of Hanwha to gain the necessary approvals in the United States and Australia. Since then, Austal has finalized its strategic shipbuilding partnership and position as a prime contractor for the Australian Defence Force, leading analysts to believe the company has decided to focus on its Australian shipbuilding.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Speculation has recently mounted that Iran is managing to export its crude oil using routes over the Caspian Sea. Given the Iranian regime’s sanctions-breaking expertise, developed over nearly 50 years, one might expect the Iranians capable of putting such diversions in place. But as yet there is little public evidence that they have managed to do so in any appreciable quantity. Iranian oil is produced onshore in the southwestern province of Khuzestan (from the Ahvaz, Gachsaran, Marun and Aghajari oilfields) and offshore in the Gulf from the Abuzar, Doroud, Foroozan and Salman fields. Iran’s domestic oil is largely refined in Gulf coastal areas close to the producing fields, in part because pipelines headed northwards have to go through the Zagros Mountains. There is however the Ahwaz-Ray Oil Pipeline, which can deliver 300,000 bpd of crude from the Dezful oilfield to Tehran refineries. This supplements a small 100,00 bpd capacity pipeline from Yeke Tut on the Caspian coast to Tehran and thence to Tabriz, which is fed by crude purchased from Russia, shipped south across the Caspian. These two crude pipelines therefore enable refineries to produce petroleum products for Tehran and north-western Iran. There is also a petroleum product pipeline delivering 204,000 bpd of petrol and diesel direct to Tehran from the south as well. But for the moment there is no means of getting Iranian crude in bulk from the main producing fields in the southwest past Tehran to the Caspian. It might be possible to switch the flow of the Tehran to Yeke Tut pipeline, and make it an export rather than an import pipeline – and to convert it even to carry petroleum products such as diesel. It should also be feasible to expand the terminal at Yeke Tut to handle greater volumes. The Caspian coast oil pipeline terminal at Yeke Tut north of Zaghmarz (Google Earth/Airbus/CJRC) From Yeke Tut, Iran would need a tanker fleet to move the crude north across the Caspian. Russia does have a fleet of shallow-draft tankers which can navigate both the Caspian and Volga-Don Canal system, but Russia is already facing difficulties exporting what it produces itself. Even Iranian ingenuity is unlikely to deliver a quick technical or infrastructure solution to these gaps in the network.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Cybersecurity firms are alerting the maritime community to what appears to be a massive data breach possibly exposing 38 organizations ranging from shipping lines to ports, terminal operators, and agencies. According to the information, a newly emerged, shadowy “data-theft extortion operation,” n0n Group, posted the names of the 38 organizations on October 12 and gave them one week to pay millions in ransom or have their data released. The list of companies includes the offices of major shipping lines, including Ocean Network Express (ONE) in Singapore, CULines, T.S. Lines, and companies in South Korea, Japan, and Indonesia. It also includes ports and terminals ranging from South Korea to India, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Brazil, and Vietnam. In addition to agencies supporting shipping operations, it also reaches into related businesses, including Chinese crane manufacturer ZPMC. Not a lot is known about the group, which first emerged on the scene in September and, prior to this, has appeared to make broad opportunistic strikes according to the security firm SOCRadar. Before this, it believes the group, which is likely located in Russia, had hit a total of 21 organizations ranging from investment firms to telecommunications, retail, education, and the pharmaceutical industry in a total of 17 countries. None of the shipping companies and others among the 38 organizations that were listed on a dark web site have publicly confirmed the attack. SOCRadar says the companies have until October 19 to make payments with Bitcoin, or their data will be published. The ransom amounts vary by the amount of data n0n claims to have, with SOCRadar saying it is between $2.4 million and $14 million, although the group indicates a willingness to negotiate with at least some of the organizations. SOCRadar analyzed the information and believes the exposure likely came out of one shared system. It notes that n0n appears to avoid traditional ransomware development and instead manipulates a victim’s data with administration tools. The current attack seems to be centered on firms in Asia. The breach appears to involve a narrow group of categories, reports SOCRadar, such as EDI messages, manifests, gate and equipment interchange records, terminal system configuration, release documents, and deployment material. It notes that the attack resembles other unrelated mass-exploitation extortion campaigns in 2023 and 2024, where a flaw in one widely deployed fire transfer product in a single application created the exposure.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: Turkish authorities are once again dealing with an abandoned tanker that washed up on its shores as a casualty of the ongoing war in the Black Sea. In the latest instance, which happened on Monday, the hulk of an abandoned product tanker was driven ashore as fierce storms overtook the region. Media reports said the area in the Black Sea near Istanbul was experiencing winds up to 50 mph. Sea conditions were very rough, and rainfall was causing flooding in parts of the city. The tug Athletic (571 dwt), registered in Cameroon, was moving the hulk when the storm made it impossible to manage. High seas and wind caused the tow line to break, and the tug was unable to maneuver to regain control of the abandoned tanker. The tug ultimately sought shelter in the port of Igneada. The product tanker, Grace Romavictor (49,990 dwt), was caught in the waves and winds and ended up ashore in the Cilingoz Nature Park, northwest of Istanbul. It is unclear what the plan had been and if the vessel was possibly being towed to Turkish recyclers. The tanker had reportedly been struck by a Ukrainian drone on August 31 while it was off Novorossiysk in the Black Sea. The crew was reportedly uninjured but was evacuated from the vessel. The ship, which was built in 2012, was managed from Dubai. The tanker is 183 meters (about 600 feet) in length. Media reports have shown several vessels, mostly the smaller ones from the Sea of Azov attacks, that washed up abandoned in Turkey. The Istanbul Regional Port Authority is reported to be working on organizing a salvage operation to remove the tanker. Initial surveys showed no oil leaks, and the hulk is believed to be mostly empty.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Deputado federal Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL - RJ) — Foto: Bruno Spada/Câmara dos Deputados O líder do PL na Câmara dos Deputados, Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ), afirmou nesta quarta-feira (14) que o senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), vai insistir na aprovação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) das horas trabalhadas, mesmo se o fim da escala 6x1 for aprovado. O texto é de autoria do senador e coordenador de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência, Rogério Marinho (PL), e cria um regime alternativo à Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) em que empregador e trabalhador negociam o valor do trabalho por "hora trabalhada". "Na nossa mentalidade, nós nunca vamos mudar o conceito, a melhor relação é hora trabalhada, hora recebida", disse Sóstenes. "Essa outra PEC é opcional ao trabalhador, se ele quiser uma nova modalidade de trabalho que nós entendemos que é melhor". Segundo o deputado, a proposta não prevê um salário mínimo ou um mínimo de horas que o trabalhador teria direito a trabalhar semanalmente. Ainda de acordo com Sóstenes, o texto permite a redução de salário, a depender dos termos do acordo com o trabalhador. Ao ser questionado sobre direitos como o décimo terceiro salário e férias remuneradas, Sóstenes disse que a proposta do PL não prevê esses direitos. "A PEC não é CLT, você tem que mudar o chip", disse o deputado.

A oposição no Senado apresentou emenda para incluir a redução da maioridade penal na PEC da Segurança Pública. O texto pode ser votado nesta quarta-feira (14). A emenda foi proposta pelo senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) e assinada por Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Flávio afirmou que a medida serve para "aprimorar" o projeto. A proposta original do governo, elaborada pelo ex-ministro Ricardo Lewandowski, institui o Sistema Único de Segurança Pública. O objetivo é integrar as forças policiais do país. O projeto original também prevê prisão em presídios de segurança máxima para facções criminosas. Além disso, proíbe a progressão de regime e as saídas temporárias.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543689-eq.text: US oil major Chevron is on track to deliver the first gas from its offshore Aseng gas project in Equatorial Guinea in 2028, a senior company executive said on Wednesday. Equatorial Guinea is aiming to bolster its dwindling gas production, which threatened its LNG exports. Chevron took a final investment decision on the $690 million project earlier this year and was "happy with its progress", Jim Swartz, managing director for Chevron Nigeria and the Mid-Africa region, told reporters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Cape Town The company plans to bring in a drilling rig, likely early next year, to drill a development well at Aseng and complete a tie-back to existing infrastructure, Swartz said. "Probably the first gas that we expect is in 2028," he said The company is also considering data from other prospective Equatorial Guinea blocks, he said In February, Chevron renewed its commitment to develop the Yoyo-Yolanda gas project which contains an estimated 2.5 trillion cubic feet of gas and straddles the maritime border between Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon

https://www.marinelog.com/news/fmc-seeks.text: After investigating reports of restrictive port practices by the Government of Spain, the Federal Maritime Commission ( FMC) has determined that Spain has created unfavorable shipping conditions against U.S.-flagged vessels. In order to address these unfavorable conditions, the FMC proposes two sets of remedies: (1) a per-voyage fee on all Spanish-flagged vessels entering U.S. ports of $200,000 and (2) restrictions on the import of certain Spanish goods into the United States. The trade categories possibly facing restrictions include perfumery and cosmetics, oils and fats, ceramics, articles of stone, and sugar and confectionaries. The FMC initiated an investigation in December 2024 to determine whether Spain is creating general or special conditions unfavorable to shipping in U.S. foreign trade by barring certain vessels from its ports, including vessels transporting cargo under the United States Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Security Program. The FMC’s investigation found conclusive evidence that Spain denied U.S.-flagged vessels access to its ports, and that these actions created unfavorable shipping conditions in the foreign trade. These unfavorable conditions have grave consequences for the efficiency and reliability of the international ocean shipping supply chain, as well as the ability of the FMC to promote the growth and development of U.S. exports, encourage the development of a liner fleet of U.S. vessels capable of meeting national security needs and supporting commerce, and supporting the U.S. merchant marine. The FMC is seeking public comment on all aspects of these proposed actions to help it decide the appropriate remedy to counter the unfavorable shipping conditions created by Spain. The FMC encourages the public to weigh in on the potential impacts of these proposed actions by filing written comments.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/rafaela-c.text: With maritime disputes increasingly demanding counsel who can navigate both complex litigation and international arbitration, law firm Jones Walker has named Rafaela Castells a partner in its Miami maritime practice group, strengthening the firm’s capabilities in maritime litigation, cruise industry disputes, and domestic and foreign arbitration. An experienced maritime litigator, Castells’ practice focuses on domestic and international maritime law claims. “As we continue to expand our maritime capabilities in key markets, Rafaela brings a valuable combination of litigation experience, international perspective, and detailed client service,” said Bill Hines , the firm’s managing partner. “Her maritime litigation background and worldwide legal experience make her a natural fit for our firm and will further strengthen our ability to serve clients across the United States, Latin America, and beyond.” Castells represents ship owners, cruise lines, resort operators, and other travel and hospitality industry clients in federal and state courts as well as domestic and foreign arbitrations, including matters involving the enforceability of arbitration agreements and forum selection clauses. She has regularly handled pre-litigation investigations, litigation, appellate, and arbitration matters for companies operating in the maritime, travel, and hospitality sectors. She has also successfully defended clients against class action claims and matters involving novel communicable diseases, catastrophic injury, and death. “As international commerce and transportation continue to evolve, clients need counsel who can navigate disputes across borders efficiently and strategically,” Castells said. “Jones Walker’s combination of maritime industry knowledge, established cruise line practice, and international arbitration experience offers a unique platform for serving those clients. I am excited to join a firm that shares my commitment to providing sophisticated, practical solutions in complex international matters.” Originally from Spain and raised in Puerto Rico, Castells brings an international perspective to cross-border matters.Drawing on experience across multiple jurisdictions, she helps clients navigate disputes efficiently while managing legal and business risk.

https://www.marinelog.com/news/op-ed-leg.text: A great deal has been made of late in news coverage and the court of public opinion regarding data centers—popularly understood as the physical facilities and operating systems needed to collect, store, and process large amounts of digital data. These functions are needed to support our ever growing demand for, among other things: digital and consumer services like texting and email, online banking, and e-commerce; public health and safety systems such as health records and telehealth and emergency response systems and their security; and entertainment media, including content streaming and online gaming. The possibility of these data centers being sited in and around local communities has resulted an understandable and classic NIMBY (“Not in my back yard!”) reaction from much of the American public. Beyond just citizens’ own communities, this sentiment has even extended to concerns about unsightly and potentially environmentally harmful facilities being located in low population density rural areas throughout the American South and wide-open spaces of the American West. The reaction has been so pronounced that the data center issue has easily found its way into the nation’s political discourse in the midst of the 2026 midterm congressional election cycle. One way to address the sweeping public concerns about data centers may be to fully “embrace the NIMBY”—that is to say, to site them not on land at all but, rather, thoughtfully and strategically on and under our oceans. The old proverb, “Out of sight, out of mind,” certainly is apropos here. While the currently ebbing push for offshore wind facilities in recent years also carried with it some NIMBY baggage, that pushback centered largely on the undesirable eyesore of towering offshore windmills that would spoil the ocean views of residents, tourists, and beachgoers. Ocean data centers (ODCs), by contrast, could be low- or no-profile, positioned just over the ocean horizon or submerged and completely out of view. An ODC, broadly conceived, could take at least three different forms: it could be a structure that floats on the ocean surface, either anchored in place or mobile; it could be a fixed structure on the ocean surface that is permanently attached to the subsea floor; or it could be a completely submerged structure, either floating in the water column—perhaps anchored, perhaps mobile—or built on the subsea floor. The form of an ODC (“status”) and its location in the ocean (“situs”) will both have a bearing on the statutory and regulatory regime that applies to it. A floating ODC could have vessel status, in which case it would likely be deemed a commercial vessel by the U.S. Coast Guard and regulated as such. This, of course, assumes that it would meet U.S. ownership and other legal requirement

https://gcaptain.com/bulk-carrier-sinks-.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz near the beach of Bandar Abbas, Iran, June 17, 2026. Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA/via WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Handout via REUTERS LONDON, Oct 14 (Reuters) – A container ship and a dry bulk carrier have both sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride , a small container vessel with a capacity of 2,824 20-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait , according to maritime security sources. “GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported,” the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday. In a separate incident, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Cape Dao sank close to the strait, weeks after being struck by a projectile on September 23, data from UN shipping agency the International Maritime Organization showed on Wednesday.

https://gcaptain.com/qatar-rewrites-its-.text: By Stephen Stapczynski, Priscila Azevedo Rocha, Salma El Wardany and Sing Yee Ong (Bloomberg) — Six months into a war that sowed upheaval in the Persian Gulf, Qatar found itself stuck. By late August, even limited shipments from the gas heavyweight had all but stopped following a projectile attack on one of its tankers outside the Strait of Hormuz. Pressure was growing, not only from energy-starved clients but also from inside an economy built on regular deliveries. Then senior executives at QatarEnergy saw a potential fix — Al Rayyan, one of the oldest vessels in the fleet. Out in the calm waters of the Gulf, a few hours from the country’s coast, Al Rayyan’s captain had been idling for days when the order came through. With security assurances from the US Navy in hand, he was given the green light, but was told to sail out quietly, without transponders or lights. At the helm of a 29-year-old gas tanker — a dinosaur in a flotilla that includes some of the most expensive vessels in the world — the shipmaster would be testing a vital workaround. It worked. The tanker slipped through and headed toward the port of Sohar in Oman on Sept. 10. A few days later, it was met by another Qatar-controlled vessel, the Al Mas’habiyyah, a state-of-the-art carrier built in 2025. The second ship would now carry the cargo of liquefied natural gas on to its final destination: China. Bloomberg News interviewed more than two dozen traders and officials to piece together Qatar’s efforts to steadily restore its position as a leading LNG exporter — until the war began, it was second only to the United States — even without a clear end in sight for the conflict between the US and Iran that has destabilized the region. Their accounts, provided under condition of anonymity given the sensitive nature of the issue, offer a glimpse into how a gas powerhouse has begun to adapt to a new and uncertain reality.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/singapor.text: A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile, while a dry bulk carrier damaged in an earlier attack is also reported to be sinking, maritime security sources said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, a small container vessel with capacity for 2,824 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait, the sources said. "GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported," the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said in a statement on Wednesday, adding that the vessel had been sailing through the strait on Tuesday. The loss of the GFS Pride marks the second vessel to sink since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to data from the UN shipping agency, the International Maritime Organization. "MPA is deeply concerned about the continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz," the Singapore authority said. "Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable, and a breach of international law."

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: On Wednesday, North Korean forces tested two different types of missiles that can be launched from underwater, according to Pyongyang's state-owned media. If effective in operation, the submarine-launched missiles would give the North a way to conduct attacks with less notice, and would provide a strike or counterstrike capability that is harder to target and eliminate. "The test-fire aimed to examine the current mobilized posture of the underwater combat systems and contributed to getting the Navy skilled in performing its strategic missions and showcasing high reliability, trustworthiness and ability of the war deterrents of the DPRK," state outlet KCNA said in a statement. KCNA's phrasing is official language, and the inclusion of the word "strategic" in the event description suggests to analysts that the missiles may be nuclear-capable. The outlet described the devices as "strategic cruise missiles," and official photos depicted the missiles on a horizontal flight path. While KCNA published an accompanying image of a submarine, it is not known whether the North possesses an operational sub with the capability to launch missiles of this type. North Korea has been known to conduct submerged missile launch testing with a purpose-built submersible launch platform. North Korea has previously tested one type of submarine-launched cruise missile, the Pulhwasal-3-31 , last seen in January 2024. It unclear how closely the two devices tested this week were related to the previously-disclosed model. In a statement Monday, U.S. Pacific Command confirmed that North Korea had test-launched two ballistic missiles and said that the event did not pose a threat. The command has not yet commented on the claimed cruise missile launch.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: The U.S.-based division of Fincantieri reports it is moving forward with $10 million in new U.S. Navy and U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) funding. The investment is for advanced manufacturing and workforce investments across its Wisconsin shipyards. The investment consists of approximately $8.3 million in Navy Shipbuilding Capability Industrial Base (SCIB) funding and a $1.3 million MARAD Small Shipyard Grant. The company says it is part of its long-standing investments in its U.S. shipyards to expand and modernize American shipbuilding. Since establishing its presence in the United States two decades ago, Fincantieri reports it has invested more than $800 million in its U.S. shipyards, which include three Wisconsin shipyards and a repair and sustainment facility in Jacksonville, Florida. “This investment is an important demonstration of the Navy’s confidence in Fincantieri, our people and our ability to be a partner in strengthening American shipbuilding,” said George Moutafis, CEO of Fincantieri Marine Group. “It also complements our efforts to put proven advanced manufacturing technologies into the hands of our employees so that we can deliver at speed. Together, these investments are helping create the industrial capabilities, skilled workforce and modern infrastructure needed to support the Navy’s future fleet requirements.” The company said the investments will accelerate ongoing modernization of Fincantieri’s Wisconsin System of Shipyards, adding advanced cutting, forming, welding, and automation capabilities that will improve production efficiency and strengthen the shipyards’ ability to execute the Landing Ship Medium (LSM) program and other current and future shipbuilding requirements. The Navy agreement also enables Fincantieri to continue to offer its Employee Dependent Care Contribution Program through 2027. The annual tax-free $5,000 payment has helped employees offset childcare and elder care costs. In addition to the federal funding, Wisconsin's governor Tony Evers recently announced state support, which will include $232,788 to train Fincantieri workers to operate and program advanced robotic welding systems.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. military claims that Iran has been using scouts embedded in the boat traffic in and around Hormuz for spotting and targeting vessels, including American warships. Human spotters help offset the loss of Iran's coastal radars, which U.S. forces have targeted and destroyed on multiple occasions, a military official confirmed to Reuters. According to CENTCOM, U.S. forces intercepted and destroyed an Iranian-linked dhow on October 6. The vessel had been watching U.S. Navy ships in the Gulf of Oman, the command said. Two U.S. Marine Corps Apaches used missiles to damage the boat and set it on fire. Prior to destroying the vessel, Navy servicemembers retrieved the crew, and Central Command is working on repatriating the evacuees. An American military official confirmed to Reuters that Iran is using spotters on smaller craft to assist its targeting at sea. Countless dhows and small craft use the waters of the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman for commerce, smuggling and fishing - providing plenty of civilian traffic in which IRGC-affiliated personnel can hide. The destruction of the dhow on October 6 does not appear to have slowed the pace of the Iranian attacks on shipping in and around the strait. Six merchant ships were attacked on Sunday alone, and four more on Tuesday, including a small container ship that was hit and sunk within the strait. Separately, a bulker that was hit on September 23 succumbed to flooding and sank on Tuesday.

After a nearly two-year investigation, the Federal Maritime Commission says it found “conclusive evidence” of restrictive port practices by Spain that were creating unfavorable shipping conditions in foreign trade. The FMC is proposing fines for Spanish-flagged vessels and restrictions on the importation of certain Spanish goods. The investigation stems from incidents in November 2024, which saw vessels operating for the U.S.-flagged Maersk Line, Ltd. divert from Algeciras to Morocco. It started with a series of protests by activists in Spain, which pressured the government to deny the port calls. They asserted that the Maersk ships were carrying military supplies to Israel, supporting the war in Gaza, which violated Spain’s ban on the transshipment of arms to Israel through its ports. The activists said that the ships had been regularly transporting these cargoes since at least September 2023. A Maersk spokesperson at the time said the company understood that it is Spain’s discretion to change its criteria while emphasizing that the cargo it was carrying was all legal. Further, they said that “cargo to be transshipped through the port does not include any military weapons or ammunition.” Maersk Line, Ltd. participates in MARAD’s Maritime Security Program, and a large share of the cargoes are government-owned goods and equipment, including military cargoes. The investigation was launched in December 2024, with the FMC citing a report from The Maritime Executive about the diversions. In December 2025, the FMC said it was seeking input while highlighting that it could impose fines of up to approximately $2.3 million per voyage on Spanish-flagged vessels. The FMC is saying that three ships were diverted and that since then carriers have been substituting port calls in Tangier instead of Algeciras. It says the investigation determined that Spain “has created unfavorable shipping conditions against U.S. flagged vessels.” In announcing its findings, the FMC writes, “These unfavorable conditions have grave consequences for the efficiency and reliability of the international ocean shipping supply chain, as well as the ability of the FMC to promote the growth and development of U.S. exports, encourage the development of a liner fleet of U.S. vessels capable of meeting national security needs and supporting commerce, and supporting the U.S. merchant marine.”

UK media is speculating that the Royal Navy may be facing a significant problem after its only polar icebreaker, HMS Protector , appears to have suffered a significant failure. Reports are indicating that the now 25-year-old survey and scientific vessel used as a demonstration of sovereignty in the polar regions has experienced a potentially serious mechanical failure without plans for a replacement. The publication Naval Lookout and local newspapers are reporting that HMS Protector was towed into her homeport at Davenport on October 13. A Royal Navy spokesperson would only say that it was to permit “investigations into a defect” aboard the vessel. There is no official word on the scope of the problem, but the daily newspaper The Telegraph is reporting that the vessel experienced a “double-engine defect” while at sea, requiring a tow to return to port. The latest incident comes after the vessel, which was originally built in Norway in 2001 as Polarbjorn , had just undergone her five-year drydocking in 2025. She was given a significant overhaul, which was designed to extend her operations. The vessel, which has a DNV Ice Class 05 rating with a capability of maneuver through first-year ice up to 20 inches (0.5 meters), was built as a commercial polar research and subsea support vessel by GTC Rieber Shipping. The Royal Navy took her on an emergency charter in 2011 for three years, designed to fill a gap after the prior polar vessel, HMS Endurance, also experienced a catastrophic failure that resulted in flooding on the vessel. The Royal Navy acquired HMS Protector in 2013 and completed her outfitting for its polar missions. Between 2015 and 2019, she was deployed full-time to the Southern Hemisphere at sea for as much as 330 days and based in South Africa. The ship has a displacement of 5,000 tons and has an overall length of 89 meters (292 feet). She has a normal complement of 88 and is also capable of embarking a Royal Marine detachment. Her primary mission has officially been to carry out observations, fishery inspections, and hydrographic surveys. However, she was mostly seen as a demonstration of British sovereignty and spent the past few seasons splitting her time between the Arctic and Antarctic. Supply missions to the UK’s Antarctic station are carried out by the British Antarctic Survey, which commissioned its vessel RRS Sir David Attenborough in 2021 after construction delays.

Lula (PT) registra 44%. Os candidatos estão em empate técnico. A margem de erro do levantamento é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. O fim da escala 6x1 e a proibição das bets são prioridades do governo Lula nesta reta final de mandato. Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14) mostra que 43% dos brasileiros têm medo da reeleição de Lula e 43% temem a volta da família Bolsonaro. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pelo jornal O Globo. A pesquisa mapeou os motivos de receio dos eleitores em cada cenário avaliado. No cenário simulado de 2º turno para a disputa presidencial, os candidatos apresentam empate técnico dentro da margem de erro. O instituto entrevistou 2.154 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais. A margem de erro do levantamento é de 2 pontos percentuais. Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) durante propaganda eleitoral gratuita nesta quarta-feira (14). — Foto: Reprodução Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14) mostra que 43% dos brasileiros têm medo da volta da família Bolsonaro com a possível vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), ao mesmo tempo em que outros 43% têm medo da reeleição de Lula (PT). O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pelo jornal O Globo.

A primeira pesquisa Quaest do segundo turno divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14) mostra Flávio Bolsonaro com 46% das intenções de voto e Lula com 44%. Os candidatos estão em empate técnico dentro da margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais. Para 91% dos entrevistados, a escolha do voto é definitiva. Na pesquisa espontânea, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 43% e Lula tem 42%. Foram entrevistadas 2.154 pessoas entre os dias 10 e 13 de outubro. No primeiro turno, Flávio Bolsonaro terminou à frente com 47,03% dos votos, contra 45,16% de Lula. A diferença foi de cerca de 2,2 milhões de votos.

Flávio e Lula aparecem tecnicamente empatados na primeira pesquisa Quaest para o segundo turno presidencial de 2026. Flávio tem entre 44% e 48%, e Lula, de 42% a 46%. Eleitores que se abstiveram ou votaram em branco no primeiro turno dividem-se na segunda etapa. Desse grupo, 43% declaram voto em Lula e 38% apoiam Flávio. Na margem de erro, a rejeição também aponta empate, registrando 53% para Lula e 54% para Flávio. O levantamento ouviu 2.154 pessoas entre sábado (10) e terça-feira (13).

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (14) mostra Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) com 46% e Lula (PT) com 44% no 2º turno. Eles estão em empate técnico. O levantamento aponta que 10% dos eleitores de Flávio Bolsonaro decidiram o voto no dia da eleição. Entre os votantes de Lula, o índice foi de 5%. Além disso, 84% dos eleitores de Lula escolheram o petista antes do início da campanha, enquanto isso aconteceu com 66% dos eleitores de Flávio.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/sue.text: In November 2023, the Houthis announced that they would target Israeli ships in the Red Sea in response to Israeli attacks in Gaza. They later broadened their criteria to include attacks on other ships, which created uncertainty. To avoid attacks, container lines began diverting ships away from the Suez Canal and the Red Sea in December 2023 and started sailing via the Cape of Good Hope. By the last week of 2023, weekly container ship capacity transiting the Suez Canal had fallen to 330k TEU, compared with the year-to-date average of 1,290k TEU. “From early February 2024 to mid-2026, container ship capacity transiting the Suez Canal averaged 141k TEU per week, equal to on average 11% of the capacity recorded during the same weeks of 2023,” says Rasmussen. Since the Gemini Alliance (Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd) announced on 6 July 2026 that its AE15/SE3 Asia–Mediterranean service would return to the Suez Canal, the move back to normal routings has gathered pace. The Gemini Alliance has since announced the return of five more services to their normal routings, including its remaining three Asia–Mediterranean services. Members of the Ocean Alliance and Premier Alliance, as well as MSC, have also announced routing changes. In total, changes to 16 services have been announced since early July. This meant that during the first two weeks of October, 36% of the total container ship capacity routed via either the canal or the cape transited the canal. This was up from an average of 8% between 2024 and mid-2026 but still a long way below the 80% recorded before the attacks began.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: On Wednesday, the U.S. Coast Guard cutter Tampa delivered nearly 30,000 pounds of cocaine to a pier in Port Everglades Florida. The crew of the 42-year-old medium endurance cutter captured all of the haul themselves in a series of six interdictions in the Eastern Pacific. "By honing their maritime skills, standing the watch and working together, they intercepted over $226 million in illicit narcotics. Their resounding teamwork during complex operations is astounding. I commend them on their tremendous tenacity and true camaraderie as they worked through long days and nights to successfully complete difficult cases and continue the disruption of transnational criminal organizations," said Capt. Joshua DiPietro, commanding officer of Tampa, in a statement Wednesday. The delivery is a capstone for Tampa's successes last month. In just six days in September, Tampa's crew caught four smuggling vessels in back-to-back busts. The first suspect boat was carrying 6,800 pounds of cocaine; four days later, Tampa caught two boats with a combined 15,000 pounds; and the next day, a fourth boat with another 3,400 pounds. It was far from easy, DiPietro said. "The vessels we saw this patrol were much more powerful than what I’ve seen the rest of my career. Most of them averaged around 1,000 horsepower, three to four high-power outboard engines, 35 feet minimum, 45 feet maximum, and each of them held much larger loads than we’ve seen in the past," DiPietro told Miami's WSVN News. USCGC Tampa (WMEC-902) was built in 1984 in Tacoma, Washington. The vessel was the first in her class to undergo a deep overhaul, entering drydock in 2005 for a life extension refit to carry her through 2015-2020. From her home port in Portsmouth, Virginia, she still serves along the East Coast and conducts counter-trafficking missions in waters south of the United States. The WMEC fleet is due for eventual replacement by the future Offshore Patrol Cutter (OPC), currently being constructed by Austal. The earliest hulls in the class are now more than 60 years old. While awaiting the arrival of the new Offshore Patrol Cutters, the efforts of WMEC crewmembers are essential for maintaining the existing fleet.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: On Wednesday, Taiwan's government confirmed that it currently plans to buy six million tonnes per annum of LNG from the Alaska LNG megaproject, and it intends to make a $4.4 billion investment in the construction of the system, subject to further negotiations. In a statement on his social media platform on Wednesday, President Donald Trump confirmed that Taiwan had agreed to an "offtake commitment" equaling 30 percent of the plant's output "because this is now a U.S. federal government project." New York-based investment company Glenfarne Group and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation are the project's sole owners, holding equity stakes of 75 percent and 25 percent respectively. Taiwan's energy ministry couched its commitment in terms of an ongoing negotiating process, pledging "an estimated maximum" investment amount only after further study and budgeting. "Specific investment arrangements, shareholding ratios, and related conditions will be handled according to subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures," the ministry said. Alaska LNG is a longstanding proposal for an infrastructure network to pipe abundant North Slope gas resources across the state to Cook Inlet for liquefaction and export. It would require construction of an 800-mile line connecting gas fields on the Artic tundra to an LNG plant rated at 20 million tonnes per annum. At one time, Alaska LNG had support from BP, ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips and was advancing steadily as a private-sector venture. All three oil majors backed out in 2016 following an independent assessment of the project's economics . At present, a New York-based investment company and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation own the equity in Alaska LNG. With the need to construct a $9 billion gas treatment plant at the Arctic northern side, then build an 800-mile overland supply pipeline through rugged wilderness, the megaproject is expected to cost $45-55 billion for 20 mtpa of capacity. This works out to as much as $2.7 billion per mtpa, much higher than the $1.6 billion per mtpa capex cost for the LNG Canada Phase 2 project in Kitimat, British Columbia. About 900 nautical miles apart, the two sites are natural competitors: they target the same East Asian market, and at similar scale. Two weeks ago, LNG Canada got the green light from private investors for its $23 billion Phase 2 expansion, which will double its capacity to 28 mtpa.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543704-an.text: Angola intends to implement faster exploration concessions from next year as part of a new long-term hydrocarbon strategy that aims to attract investment and stimulate oil and gas production, a senior government official said on the sidelines of an energy conference in Cape Town. The 25-year plan seeks to build on regulatory reforms that have seen oil companies, including TotalEnergies and Eni, recently commit billions of dollars to projects in Sub-Saharan Africa's second-largest oil producer after Nigeria. Angola intends to drop its multi-year oil and gas auction rounds and will open up more than 100 blocks, mainly onshore, as soon as the plan is passed later this year, said Alcides Andrade, a board member at the National Agency for Petroleum, Gas and Biofuels (ANPG), late on Wednesday. He said ANPG wanted to reduce the time taken to award concessions, aiming for a three-month process versus the current six months. On exploration, it will not be a "one-size-fits-all" approach on terms and conditions, but rather a risk-profile-based model that distinguishes between marginal or mature fields and onshore versus deep-water blocks, for example. Drilling more exploration wells will hopefully lead to higher crude production over the long term, Andrade said, as Angola aims to grow its current oil output of around 1 million barrels per day.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543696-oi.text: Oil markets initially treated the Iran war as a brief bullish disruption in a long-term bearish trend. But traders are now betting that oil prices will remain elevated through 2028, forcing a rethink of the global inflation outlook. Eight months into the war, the buffers that helped absorb the initial energy shock – most notably onshore crude oil stockpiles – are wearing dangerously thin. At the same time, the recovery in crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz remains fragile, global refining capacity has been eroded and credible diplomatic pathways to end the conflict appear narrower than ever. Global benchmark Brent crude futures tell the story. Contracts for delivery in December 2027 LCOZ7 have climbed more than 13% since the start of September to $86 a barrel, the highest level for the contract, while December 2026 contracts LCOZ6 have gained around 12%. The Brent forward curve is not a price forecast, of course. But it reflects the willingness of refiners, airlines, commodity traders and asset managers to lock in elevated prices months and even years into the future. In effect, market participants are paying a premium against the possibility that today's disruptions will become tomorrow's normal. This market positioning stands in stark contrast to widely held industry expectations of a recovery in global oil supplies next year. The International Energy Agency projects global supply will rise to 108.3 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2027 from 100.7 million bpd this year as Middle Eastern exports recover.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543703-se.text: Seascape Energy has signed a letter of agreement with Petronas for a 547-square-kilometre extension of its Temaris Cluster Small Field Asset production sharing contract (PSC) offshore Malaysia, potentially doubling the gas resources identified in the area. The extension, located north and east of the existing acreage, will increase the Temaris PSC area by approximately 45% to around 1,770 square kilometers, subject to the execution of final documentation. Seascape holds a 100% interest in the PSC, which lies in approximately 70 meters of water on the western flank of the Malay Basin. The expanded acreage covers a continuation of the Miocene sandstone system associated with the Tembakau and Mengkuang gas discoveries, allowing Seascape to pursue the wider gas play under a single PSC. The company's previous technical work, including 3D seismic reprocessing using Full Waveform Inversion techniques, identified extensions of gas-bearing sandstone channels across the surrounding area. An earlier independent competent person's report (CPR) identified approximately 950 billion cubic feet (bcf) of gross mean prospective resources within the original Temaris PSC.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543697-bw.text: BW Energy has confirmed commercial oil volumes in two appraisal wells at the Dussafu field offshore Gabon, identifying approximately 8 million to 9 million barrels of gross recoverable oil and paving the way for two additional production wells. The company said the results from the 10P2 and 10P1 appraisal wells support an expansion of its drilling program, with the first additional production well to be drilled during the ongoing MaBoMo Phase 2 campaign. The 10P2 appraisal well encountered a 30-metre oil column in the Gamba reservoir, with formation evaluation confirming good porosity and permeability. Wireline logging and pressure testing indicate that a production well at the location could initially deliver more than 5,000 barrels of oil per day (bopd) gross, comparable to recent MaBoMo Phase 1 wells. BW Energy estimates incremental recovery from the 10P2 location at approximately 6 million barrels gross, with the planned production well expected to achieve a payback period of less than one year. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543694-ir.text: TotalEnergies expects its refining margins to have nearly quadrupled in the third quarter compared to last year, as the Iran war continues to lift energy prices and boost profits for oil majors, the French company said in a trading update on Thursday. https://www.rigzone.com/news/north_sea_p.text: The North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) announced, in a statement posted on its website this week, that emissions in the North Sea have fallen for a sixth consecutive year, “demonstrating real effort and achievement on behalf of the oil and gas industry”. According to the statement, “robust regulation and industry action” saw production emissions fall by an estimated seven percent in 2025. This contributed to an overall estimated reduction of 37 percent since 2018, according to the latest Emissions Monitoring Report from the NSTA, the statement outlined. More than half of last year’s emissions reductions were attributable to active measures implemented on installations that remain operational, rather than just assets that have stopped producing, the NSTA’s statement noted. The statement highlighted that the NSTA’s report also showed the UK’s production emissions intensity was “well below the global average”, according to Rystad data, “mainly due to very strong performance on methane emissions”. “While this is impressive, CO 2 intensity compares less favorably globally, and with UK production forecast to decline in future years, continued industry effort on decarbonization will be needed to prevent sharp increases in emissions intensity, and loss of global position,” the NSTA said. The North Sea Transition Deal interim targets of reducing emissions by 10 percent by 2025 and by 25 percent by 2027 have been surpassed, the NSTA highlighted in its statement. It added that the goal of halving emissions by 2030 is achievable, “based on the current trajectory”.

https://safety4sea.com/bimco-flags-persi.text: BIMCO has highlighted persistent safety risks involving scrap metal fires, fumigation and enclosed-space fatalities in dry bulk shipping. A t its eighth meeting on 8 October 2026, the BIMCO Dry Bulk Cargo Network discussed these three challenges, focusing on the need for clearer cargo information, stronger charter party provisions and practical measures to protect crews. Members examined concerns about contaminated scrap metal cargoes and the limitations of existing safety provisions, the transfer of fumigation responsibilities from specialist contractors to ships’ crews, and the continued occurrence of enclosed-space accidents despite greater awareness of the hazards. Self-heating and oxidation can increase the risk of fire , particularly when scrap is moved from outdoor storage, where drainage and ventilation are possible, into a cargo hold, where compaction can restrict both. As informed, BIMCO continues to receive member enquiries about scrap cargoes, including questions about the meaning of “as dry as possible,” the presence of plastics, tyres, oils and other flammable materials beyond declared impurity percentages, and the implications of lithium batteries being present, including whether this introduces dangerous goods considerations under Class 9 of the IMDG Code. When asked whether changes were needed to better address the risks associated with scrap cargoes, members responded as follows: Some members commented that the schedule itself is clear, but that problems arise at scrap yards and among shippers. These include confusion about the distinction between different scrap metal cargoes and how they should be described and classified, and a general lack of understanding of the hazards.

https://safety4sea.com/saudi-strikes-hit.text: Saudi Arabia has intensified its campaign against Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen, striking oil storage facilities near Sana’a and the port of Hodeidah, while intercepting missiles targeting the area around Saudi Aramco’s headquarters. The attacks were followed by a missile interception near Dharan, home to the headquarters of Saudi state-owned energy giant Saudi Aramco, according to reports. https://safety4sea.com/es-ecsa-smap-must.text: European Shipowners | ECSA has called for a significant increase in the proposed allowance reserve under the EU’s Shipping Maritime Allowance Pool (SMAP) mechanism, arguing that the European Commission’s current proposal would fall short of providing the market signal needed to accelerate the uptake of sustainable maritime fuels and technologies. I n the new analysis, “Creating a Market for Sustainable Maritime Fuels and Technologies: How Can ETS Revenues Contribute?” , ES | ECSA estimates that at least 330 million EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) allowances would be required to establish a credible market for sustainable fuels and technologies. This is three times the 110 million allowances proposed by the European Commission, which the association says would cover only around one-third of the amount needed to achieve the mechanism’s objectives. Introduced as part of the revision of the EU ETS, SMAP is intended to help bridge the cost gap between conventional marine fuels and sustainable alternatives, while encouraging investment in cleaner propulsion technologies and energy-efficiency measures. Rather than providing direct financial payments, the mechanism would allocate EU ETS allowances to shipping companies adopting eligible fuels and technologies, with the monetary value of the allowances covering part of the additional cost. Under the Commission’s proposal, support would cover 55% of the remaining price differential for biogas and advanced biofuels, 80% for low-carbon hydrogen and low-carbon fuels, and 90% for renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBOs). The mechanism would also cover 90% of the additional cost of eligible technologies.

https://safety4sea.com/industry-calls-fo.text: The European Union’s proposed Shipping Maritime Allowance Pool (SMAP) should prioritise long-term investment in e-fuels to support shipping decarbonisation under EU ETS , according to an industry appeal to EU lawmakers dated 12 October 2026. T he letter argues that the mechanism, introduced under the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) , could provide an estimated €15 billion in support between 2028 and 2040. However, its current design may not provide sufficient certainty to encourage shipping companies to enter into long-term offtake agreements with e-fuel producers. According to the signatories, securing such agreements is essential to unlocking investment in e-fuel production, which remains capital-intensive and will need to scale up significantly to meet the maritime sector’s long-term greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction targets. The appeal comes as negotiations on the ETS file continue, with industry stakeholders urging EU lawmakers to strengthen SMAP’s provisions to ensure the mechanism supports fuels capable of delivering long-term decarbonisation. The European Commission’s Sustainable Transport Investment Plan (STIP) indicates that 4.6 million tonnes of e-fuels could be needed within less than a decade to meet FuelEU Maritime targets. While the proposed SMAP mechanism provides for a higher level of price-difference coverage for e-fuels compared with other alternative fuels, the letter warns that this may not be enough to trigger a meaningful shift towards their adoption.
