https://safety4sea.com/from-lpg-to-lng-l.text: In a case study published by SEA-LNG in collaboration with its member Bernhard Schulte Shipmanagement (BSM), the two organizations examine the challenges of crewing and training for LNG bunker vessels. T he case study draws on BSM’s experience managing the LNG bunker vessel Kairos since 2018 and explores how the company addressed crewing challenges, developed specialised training and strengthened safe operating practices . It also examines the importance of retaining experienced crews and ensuring that receiving vessels are adequately prepared for LNG bunkering operations. When BSM took the Kairos into management in 2018, experienced LNG bunker vessel crew were scarce. The company addressed this gap by recruiting LPG-experienced seafarers and introducing mandatory training on LNG handling, pressure management and simultaneous operations (SIMOPS). This approach remains its primary recruitment strategy. BSM found that ship handling posed a greater challenge than cargo handling. LNG bunker vessels frequently manoeuvre in confined port waters, while azimuth thrusters require different skills from conventional propulsion systems. Drawing on its offshore vessel expertise, BSM developed an Azimuth Manoeuvring Manual, alongside simulator training and practical assessments, to ensure officers can handle vessels safely and independently. Frequent bunkering operations, short port calls and demanding schedules create workload and crew-rest challenges. BSM advocated for an additional navigational watch officer, allowing the chief officer to focus on cargo operations, safety and documentation.

https://safety4sea.com/singapore-prepare.text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) has announced new initiatives to advance alternative marine fuels and accelerate the adoption of electric harbour craft at the 24th Singapore International Bunkering Conference (SIBCON) 2026. O pened on 14 October by Murali Pillai, Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport, SIBCON is being held from 13 to 15 October under the theme “Charting a Resilient Multi-Fuel Future”. The biennial conference is expected to attract more than 2,000 maritime professionals from over 60 countries. Singapore is set to conduct its first ethanol bunkering operation at PSA’s Pasir Panjang Terminal later this week. The operation will involve Maersk, Golden Island Pte Ltd and PSA Singapore, with bioethanol transferred concurrently with cargo operations. The operation will use a mass flow meter (MFM) to measure the quantity transferred and assess whether Singapore’s existing methanol bunkering technical reference, TR 129, can be adapted for ethanol. It will also validate the use of MFM systems for ethanol bunkering, with the findings informing future technical and regulatory requirements. Previusly, Repsol had completed the first bioethanol bunkering operation for a Maersk container vessel at the Port of Barcelona, supplying 2,800 tons of bioethanol to the 16,000 TEU Antonia Maersk. MPA and Enterprise Singapore, through the Singapore Standards Council, have launched Technical Reference TR 148 for ammonia bunkering. The reference establishes requirements covering safety, bunkering procedures, custody transfer and personnel competencies.

https://safety4sea.com/korea-makes-billi.text: Credit: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries South Korea will invest more than 1.4 trillion won (approximately $1.05 billion) by 2030 to accelerate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across shipbuilding, targeting production efficiency, automation and technology transfer to smaller companies. A nnounced on 12 October by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, the initiative expands the existing Autonomous Ships M.AX Alliance into the Shipbuilding M.AX Alliance, bringing together major shipbuilders, smaller yards, equipment manufacturers and research institutions. The programme includes three flagship projects in Mokpo-Yeongam, Geoje-Busan and Gunsan, designed to address labour shortages, improve productivity and narrow the technology gap between major shipbuilders and smaller suppliers. Alongside the investment programme, the ministries unveiled South Korea’s first Basic Plan for the Development and Commercialisation of Autonomous Ships for 2026-2035. The roadmap targets the launch of fully autonomous ships corresponding to IMO Level 4 by 2035 , alongside the ambition to become the leading country in orders for fully autonomous vessels. Its priorities include core technology development, real-world trials, safe operations, workforce training and international standardisation.

https://safety4sea.com/cyber-extortion-g.text: Cyber extortion group n0n has listed 38 maritime and logistics organizations across 18 countries on its dark web leak site, raising concerns about potential vulnerabilities affecting interconnected shipping and port systems. A ccording to cybersecurity intelligence tracked by SOCRadar, the October 12, 2026, batch includes container terminals, shipping lines, port IT providers and logistics companies. Named organizations include Ocean Network Express, CULines, T.S. Lines, Santos Brasil, TTI Algeciras and Eurogate Tanger. South Korea accounts for 12 listings, including terminal operators, shipping companies and port IT providers. The concentration has raised questions about whether the alleged data exposures resulted from separate intrusions or a shared application or vulnerability. However, the available evidence does not establish a common entry point, and none of the maritime claims had been publicly confirmed by the listed organizations at the time of writing. The group, which emerged in September 2026, reportedly focuses on stealing data and threatening public disclosure rather than relying primarily on conventional ransomware deployment. Its latest listings threaten to publish the alleged stolen information on October 19, 2026, at 13:27 UTC, with reviewed ransom demands ranging from US$2.4 million to US$14 million. Separately, maritime cybersecurity company Cydome warned on October 14 that an alleged ransomware attack may have exposed operational and commercial information involving 37 maritime organizations.

https://safety4sea.com/malta-moves-seama.text: Seafarers serving on Malta-flagged commercial vessels will now have to apply for and access their Seaman’s Record Book digitally, following a move by the Merchant Shipping Directorate to replace the document’s physical format with an electronic version. W ith immediate effect, the Maltese Seaman’s Record Book will be issued exclusively in digital format, according to a notice from the Merchant Shipping Directorate. The document is available to seafarers employed, or due to be employed, on commercial vessels registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, as well as Maltese nationals and holders of Maltese Certificates of Competency. Applications must be submitted online through the Seafarer Portal at seafarers.transport.gov.mt. Seafarers can apply directly, or applications may be submitted by their representatives or employing companies. As stated, t he digital record can be verified by employers, Port State Control officers and relevant authorities using a QR code, while remaining accessible offline at sea. Each credential is cryptographically signed by the issuing authority and anchored on the Concordium blockchain, enabling independent verification and helping reduce the risk of document fraud. Seafarers also retain control over how their personal data is shared, with the service designed to comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Applicants must upload the required documentation through the relevant sections of the online portal. This includes a personal email address, a copy of a passport or national identity card, a passport-sized photograph against a white or light background, and a signature in black or blue ink on a plain white background.

https://safety4sea.com/abs-issues-guidan.text: The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) has published new guidance outlining a framework for evaluating the use of augmented reality (AR) in industrial operations, with a focus on improving task performance while maintaining safety and situational awareness. T he ABS Advisory on Assessing Augmented Reality for Industrial Operations examines how AR can support activities such as inspection, maintenance, navigation, training and remote assistance. While the technology has the potential to help industrial personnel work more efficiently and consistently, ABS emphasises that its wider adoption will depend on demonstrating measurable operational benefits without introducing additional safety risks. The guidance highlights the importance of assessing AR in real working conditions, rather than relying solely on its technical capabilities or the features it offers. Its suitability depends on how the technology affects human performance, decision-making and the ability of personnel to remain aware of their surroundings during task execution. Augmented reality could change how industrial work is performed, bringing expert guidance, operational data and digital workflows directly into the user’s field of view. To unlock that potential responsibly, industry needs a clear understanding of the safety and performance implications. This advisory provides the tools to evaluate the implications rigorously and consistently. AR can provide workers with digital information directly within their field of view, helping them identify equipment, access instructions and interpret operational data at the point of use. When appropriately designed and implemented, these capabilities can improve task execution and support safer, more consistent working practices. However, the same technology can also introduce challenges. The presentation of digital information may increase cognitive workload, divert attention from the surrounding environment or interfere with the visual scanning needed to identify potential hazards.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mid.text: Freight rates and charter fees for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that transport crude oil are soaring as the Hormuz Strait remains closed for an extended period due to the Middle East war and as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels attack Saudi Arabia. With the VLCC market booming, there is an outlook that shipping companies could increase new orders to replace aging vessels. According to the shipbuilding and shipping industries on the 14th, the average VLCC rate in the first week of Oct. was $665,000 per day, up nearly 10% from the previous week. It is a record high. Compared with the first week of March, immediately after the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, it rose 72%. The one-year charter rate for a VLCC rose to more than $210,000 per day from about $130,000 per day before the war. Amid the spillover effects of expanding armed clashes in the Middle East, available crude carriers have become even scarcer. According to a report released on the 2nd of this month by Clarksons Research, the volume of crude passing through the Hormuz Strait recently recovered to a daily average of 12 million barrels, or 80% of the pre-war level. However, shuttle transport repeatedly moving crude from the Gulf region to transshipment points and ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman have increased, and voyages have lengthened as ships detour around the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa, sharply reducing vessel turnaround. As a result, more VLCCs are needed and rates are rising.

https://www.marinelink.com/news/seven-mi.text: Rescuers were searching for seven missing crew on Thursday from one of two chemical tankers that caught fire overnight inside Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea, after Russian drones strayed into Romanian airspace, Romanian officials said. Romanian officials stopped short of explicitly linking the fires onboard the ships to the Russian drones. But the incidents follow drone strikes on at least five other cargo ships near the coasts of Romania and neighbouring fellow NATO member Bulgaria over the past 10 days. At least 23 sailors were lost from those strikes, which unlike the latest incidents took place just outside NATO's territorial waters. The two ships hit overnight were both anchored in the Black Sea near the mouth of the canal leading into the Danube River, a major shipping route used by Ukraine as Russia has attacked Ukraine's own Black Sea ports. Romania's naval authority said it received an emergency alert from the San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader. Seven of its 12 crew were missing and 5 were rescued. The interior ministry said it had sent two Black Hawk helicopters to the search and rescue mission, as well as two ships with medical staff on board. "At the moment, the rescue cannot be done safely because of very big waves," it said in a statement.

https://splash247.com/hormuz-claims-two-.text: Two ships have sunk near the Strait of Hormuz as fresh attacks on commercial shipping have hit three containerships linked to Abu Dhabi’s AD Ports Group. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride , a 2008-built, 2,824 teu feeder operated by Dubai-based Global Feeder Shipping (GFS), was struck by an unidentified projectile on Tuesday, caught fire and subsequently sank. Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) confirmed that all 21 crew members were evacuated without injury. Pakistan’s hydrographer issued a navigational warning on Wednesday after containers were reported floating in the water around four nautical miles northwest of Ras Shaykh Masud, off Oman, where the vessel went down. A second GFS boxship, the Singapore-flagged 4,400 teu GFS Giselle , sustained hull damage in a separate strike on Wednesday, Singapore time. The 2015-built vessel managed to reach a safe anchorage under its own power, with all 22 crew members unharmed. The attacks have hit a key part of AD Ports Group’s shipping business. The Abu Dhabi company increased its stake in GFS to 81% in June, while another of its feeder operators, Safeen Feeders, also had a vessel targeted in the latest wave. The Marshall Islands-flagged, 1,730 teu Al Saadiyat , operated by Safeen Feeders, was struck during an outbound transit but reportedly escaped serious damage. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) also recorded an attack on a tanker, identified by maritime security group Vanguard Tech as the Barbados-flagged, 38,842 dwt Alfonso. Its condition has not been independently confirmed.

https://splash247.com/natos-black-sea-fl.text: A chemical tanker has reported a suspected drone strike inside Romanian territorial waters. The Comoros-flagged Yara J was anchored approximately 10 nautical miles southeast of Sulina on Wednesday evening when its crew reported an explosion and fire onboard. The vessel, which was in ballast and reportedly preparing to enter the Danube, extinguished the fire without outside assistance. All crewmembers were reported safe. Romania’s defence minister Radu Miruță said an investigation was underway, stressing that military radar had not detected a drone approaching the ship. The tanker is expected to undergo an inspection in Constanța. Unlike the previous attacks in the exclusive economic zones of Romania and Bulgaria, both NATO members, Wednesday’s incident occurred inside Romanian territorial waters. The latest incident follows five reported drone attacks on merchant shipping off the two countries since October 5, with three vessels sinking.

https://splash247.com/us-shadow-fleet-pr.text: Asian shipping stocks took a beating on Thursday as reports that Washington is considering easing sanctions on shadow fleet tankers sent investors scrambling to reassess the extraordinary freight boom that has sent some spot segments into million-dollar territory for the first time in history. COSCO Shipping Energy plunged more than 13% in Hong Kong, while China Merchants Energy Shipping, COSCO Shipping Energy’s Shanghai-listed shares and China Merchants Nanjing Tanker hit their 10% daily downward limits in mainland trading.The sell-off also spread to other shipping sectors. The sharp reversal followed reports that the Trump administration is discussing exemptions allowing blacklisted tankers linked to Russia, Iran and Venezuela to carry oil and petroleum products not themselves subject to American sanctions. A US official told Reuters that companies would need Treasury approval to employ the vessels, with the initiative designed to release additional tanker capacity and bring down record freight rates. No formal easing has yet been announced. US energy secretary Chris Wright raised the possibility during a video address to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh this week, according to consultancy Energy Aspects. The proposal follows Washington’s decision last Friday to temporarily authorise Russian diesel trade until April 7, 2027, drawing criticism from Kyiv and US lawmakers.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: A brasileira Mary Hellen, condenada a nove anos e seis meses de prisão por tráfico de drogas na Tailândia , retornou ao Brasil em 5 de setembro, após cumprir a pena e receber o perdão real. De acordo com a defesa, a medida concedida pelas autoridades tailandesas possibilitou o retorno da brasileira ao país. Na nota, a defesa afirmou que acompanhou o caso e buscou oferecer suporte à brasileira ao longo do processo. A defesa também relata obstáculos no acompanhamento da situação, incluindo dificuldades de acesso e limitações na assistência consular prestada pela Embaixada do Brasil. O relato da advogada não detalha quais foram as dificuldades enfrentadas nem apresenta episódios específicos relacionados ao atendimento consular. Procurado, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores informou que a Embaixada do Brasil em Bangkok tomou conhecimento do caso em 2022 e prestou assistência consular à brasileira .

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A PF apreendeu um carro de R$ 2,3 milhões na casa do policial civil José Carlos, preso com outras cinco pessoas nesta quinta-feira (15). José Carlos é acusado de controlar de fato empresas que lavavam dinheiro em 96 postos de combustíveis e de usar a mulher como laranja. As prisões foram determinadas pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal em uma investigação sobre conexões entre agentes públicos e grupos criminosos.

A PF deflagrou nesta quinta-feira (15) a 8ª fase da Operação Unha e Carne. A ação prendeu o deputado Márcio Canella e o ex-secretário de Polícia Marcus Amim. A investigação mira um esquema que usava 96 postos de combustíveis para lavar dinheiro. O grupo movimentou mais de R$ 7,6 bilhões entre 2020 e 2026. Segundo as investigações, Márcio Canella atuava como articulador político do grupo. Ele teria recebido mais de R$ 2,59 milhões de origem não esclarecida. O ex-secretário Marcus Amim usava cargos públicos para dar proteção institucional ao grupo. Ele também é apontado como sócio oculto de um posto de combustíveis.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A professora Luziene Rosa Sobreira das Chagas, do Rio de Janeiro, venceu um prêmio nacional ao usar fantasias de super-heróis para alfabetizar seus alunos em Bangu. O projeto Alfabetização Divertida ajudou a alfabetizar 100% dos alunos em 2023 e 2025. A iniciativa beneficia inclusive estudantes neurodivergentes. A Rede Nacional de Ciência para Educação premiou o trabalho por unir a cultura pop ao desenvolvimento da consciência fonológica, com base científica. Com 26 anos de carreira, Luziene é graduada em Pedagogia e se inspirou em sua própria trajetória de melhora de vida pela educação.

A Polícia Militar faz buscas em Vargem Grande nesta quinta-feira (15) após tiroteio na Estrada dos Bandeirantes. Policiais apreenderam fuzis e roupas táticas. Policiais do 31º BPM cercaram os veículos dos criminosos após alerta no Túnel da Grota Funda. Houve confronto na Estrada dos Bandeirantes. Após baterem o carro, os bandidos fugiram pela mata da região. Foram apreendidos 1 pistola, 3 celulares e 2 veículos.

O deputado estadual Márcio Canella e o delegado Marcus Amim foram presos nesta quinta-feira (15) pela PF. A ação integra a Operação Unha e Carne 8. Segundo a PF, o grupo investigado usava uma rede de postos de combustíveis para lavagem de dinheiro. Eles responderão por corrupção e formação de cartel. Nesta quinta, agentes saíram para cumprir 6 mandados de prisão e 16 de busca e apreensão. As medidas são desdobramentos de investigações anteriores de julho. “Confio em Deus e na Justiça e tenho certeza de que tudo será esclarecido”, declarou Canella. A defesa de Amim informou que não vai se pronunciar até ter acesso aos autos. A TV Globo tenta contato com os demais investigados.

https://g1.globo.com/podcast/o-assunto/n.text: O plenário do Senado votou e aprovou nesta quarta-feira (14) a PEC que limita a jornada semanal de trabalho a 40 horas e estabelece uma escala de dois dias de descanso remunerado para cinco dias trabalhados: foram 75 votos a favor e 1 contra nos dois turnos.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: A PF prendeu o deputado Márcio Canella e o ex-chefe da Polícia Civil Marcus Amim nesta quinta-feira (15). Policiais acharam dinheiro na adega de um inspetor. Segundo a corporação, o grupo utilizava uma rede de postos de combustíveis para lavar dinheiro no Rio de Janeiro. A ação contou com o apoio da Corregedoria. As prisões foram ordenadas pelo ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do STF. A investigação aponta que o grupo movimentou R$ 7,6 bilhões em 6 anos. A Polícia Federal cumpriu 6 mandados de prisão e 16 de busca em 7 municípios fluminenses. O Supremo também determinou a suspensão de 112 empresas investigadas. Iniciada em dezembro de 2025, a operação investiga a relação de agentes públicos com facções criminosas. As defesas dos suspeitos informaram que não vão se pronunciar.

https://g1.globo.com/trabalho-e-carreira.text: O Senado aprovou a PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1, com dois dias de descanso remunerado e redução gradual da jornada semanal de 44 para 40 horas, sem redução salarial. As novas regras entram em vigor após a publicação da emenda, com transição para 42 horas semanais após dois meses e 40 horas após mais um ano. Setores como saúde, segurança, transporte e limpeza urbana poderão adotar escalas diferenciadas, conforme a regulamentação e as negociações coletivas. Autônomos, MEIs, PJs sem vínculo empregatício e trabalhadores informais não são diretamente abrangidos. Categorias que já têm jornadas reduzidas, como bancários e profissionais de telemarketing, podem ter impactos menores.

https://g1.globo.com/pop-arte/musica/not.text: U2 anuncia 'Carnaval de Luz', álbum que tem Rosalía e dueto póstumo com Dolly Parton — Foto: Viviane Sassen/Divulgação O U2 anunciou dois shows em São Paulo, no Brasil, em março de 2027. Os shows farão parte da turnê "The Greatest Show on Earth", para promover o disco "Carnaval de Luz".

https://g1.globo.com/pe/pernambuco/notic.text: A delegada do Pará Maria Virgínia Grimwood Pinto foi presa nesta quinta-feira (15). Ela é suspeita de repassar informações sigilosas à facção Primeiro Comando da Capital. A Operação Sinalagma foi deflagrada pela Polícia Civil de Pernambuco. A delegada foi detida em Brasília, e mandados também foram cumpridos em Belém, São Paulo e Recife. Investigações apontam que ela mantinha "laços de intimidade e confiança" com um integrante do grupo. https://g1.globo.com/ms/mato-grosso-do-s.text: A FICCO/MS deflagrou nesta quinta-feira (15) a Operação Capolinea contra o tráfico internacional de drogas. Entre os alvos estão chefes de facção e um vigilante da Polícia Federal. A ação cumpre 21 mandados de prisão e 20 de busca em 4 estados. A Justiça determinou o bloqueio de R$ 24 milhões em bens dos investigados. Segundo as investigações, o vigilante repassava informações sobre rotinas policiais e movimentações na delegacia. Ele também guardava drogas e participava do transporte de entorpecentes.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543708-su.text: Worley Rosenberg has secured a contract from Subsea7 to fabricate subsea structures and spools for the second phase of Norway's Northern Lights carbon capture and storage (CCS) development. The contract covers fabrication of key subsea infrastructure supporting the expansion of the carbon dioxide transportation and storage system beneath the North Sea. The award builds on Worley Rosenberg's involvement in the first phase of Northern Lights, for which it delivered comparable subsea structures and spools in 2023. The infrastructure will support the transportation of captured CO2 from industrial emitters to permanent geological storage beneath the seabed. “This award strengthens our position in the growing subsea market and further expands our role in delivering infrastructure that enables large-scale CO2 reduction,” said Jan Narvestad, Managing Director of Worley Rosenberg. Northern Lights is part of Norway's Longship CCS initiative and is designed to transport and permanently store captured industrial CO2.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543717-hy.text: HYDRA SUBSEA announced the execution of a commercial agreement with Shell Offshore Inc. for a standardized deepwater pipeline installation solution for selected short distance subsea tie-ins in the Gulf of America. Shell’s Appomattox gas lift line is the first project proposed, subject to project-specific approvals and requirements. Appomattox, located 80 miles off the coast of Louisiana, is operated by Shell (79%) with INEOS holding a 21% working interest. HYDRA is currently progressing through the program and preparations for reactivation of the Subsea Legend . The vessel is planned to receive new mission equipment, a 250-ton active heave-compensated subsea crane, a new propulsion system and an upgraded dynamic positioning system. The HYDRA Standard Solution combines repeatable engineering, standardized project configurations and dedicated regional installation capability. The approach is intended to reduce complexity and improve cost and schedule predictability for projects that fit the model and is specifically designed to support Gulf projects. The agreement establishes commercial and technical conditions under which the companies may progress qualifying opportunities. Each project remains subject to separate evaluation, approval and award.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Jadlog alcançou 5.500 pontos de atendimento no Brasil , somando franquias e estabelecimentos parceiros do modelo PUDO (Pick Up/Drop Off), voltado à postagem, retirada e devolução de encomendas. Com cobertura em todos os municípios brasileiros , a transportadora pretende agora ampliar a proximidade com os consumidores, com a meta de ter um ponto de atendimento a até 500 metros de cada pessoa. “Chegar a todo o território nacional foi uma etapa importante da construção da nossa malha. Agora, queremos que as pessoas tenham um ponto Jadlog cada vez mais perto de casa, do trabalho ou dos locais por onde circulam, tornando a postagem, a retirada e a devolução de encomendas mais simples e convenientes”, afirma Bruno Tortorello, CEO da companhia. Os pontos da rede Jadlog Pickup funcionam em estabelecimentos comerciais parceiros e oferecem alternativas à entrega e à coleta domiciliares. O modelo atende tanto grandes empresas quanto pessoas físicas que vendem pela internet, permitindo que consumidores retirem compras, enviem pacotes ou façam devoluções em locais próximos de suas rotinas, inclusive fora do horário comercial. A concentração de entregas e coletas em pontos parceiros também pode reduzir deslocamentos e a circulação de veículos nos centros urbanos, com potencial para diminuir as emissões de CO₂ e a poluição sonora. Segundo Tortorello, o serviço integra a estratégia de logística Out of Home, que busca oferecer mais flexibilidade aos usuários e eficiência às operações. “O Pickup é muito mais do que uma alternativa de entrega. É uma estratégia que impacta diretamente a jornada de compra do consumidor por oferecer mais conveniência e flexibilidade, e contribuir para uma operação logística mais eficiente e sustentável, com a consolidação de entregas e coletas em pontos próximos das pessoas”, destaca o executivo. A rede brasileira também está integrada ao modelo Pickup do grupo Geopost, ao qual a Jadlog pertence. Internacionalmente, a estrutura reúne mais de 150 mil pontos de retirada e postagem e armários inteligentes.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543705-se.text: SFL Corporation has won a Norwegian appeals court ruling in its contract dispute with Seadrill over the redelivery of the offshore drilling rig Hercules, with the court ordering Seadrill to pay approximately $55 million (NOK 525 million). The Borgarting Court of Appeal unanimously ruled that Seadrill breached its contractual obligations when returning the rig to SFL's rig-owning subsidiary in December 2022. The award includes compensation, late-payment interest and legal costs, with SFL receiving full reimbursement of its legal expenses for proceedings before both the Oslo District Court and the Borgarting Court of Appeal. The latest judgment largely upholds a February 2025 ruling by the Oslo District Court, with the total amount payable increasing because of accrued interest. According to Seadrill's financial disclosures for the six months ended June 30, 2026, the dispute began in March 2023, when SFL Hercules Ltd. filed a claim concerning the redelivery of Hercules, a 2008-built sixth-generation deepwater and harsh environment rig. The Oslo District Court initially ordered Seadrill to pay approximately $37 million, plus interest and legal costs of around $11 million, based on exchange rates at the time of the February 2025 judgment.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A J&T Express , operadora global de logística focada no e-commerce, inaugurou seu novo Centro de Distribuição em Guarulhos (SP) , com investimento de mais de R$ 75 milhões . O aporte está entre os principais feitos pela companhia em infraestrutura logística no Brasil em 2026 e é considerado estratégico para os planos de crescimento da empresa no País. Do total, R$ 71 milhões foram destinados exclusivamente à aquisição e instalação do novo sistema automatizado de triagem de pacotes (sorter) . O valor restante cobre infraestrutura, sistemas e demais gastos de implantação da unidade. Segundo a empresa, o CD de Guarulhos é hoje o mais moderno da J&T Express no Brasil . O sorter, de três andares , tem capacidade para processar mais de 2 milhões de encomendas por dia . A estrutura reúne 4.138 metros de esteiras transportadoras em uma área de mais de 20 mil m² , com 65 docas . “Este investimento representa um passo importante na expansão da J&T Express no Brasil. Estamos combinando escala, tecnologia e eficiência operacional para acompanhar o crescimento do e-commerce e oferecer aos nossos clientes uma infraestrutura cada vez mais preparada para suas necessidades”, afirma Linqun Gui, CEO da J&T Express no Brasil . O novo sorter automatiza etapas críticas da operação e reduz a necessidade de intervenção manual. Entre os principais recursos estão 21 equipamentos DWS ( Dimensioning, Weighing and Scanning ), que fazem a leitura de cinco faces das encomendas , e um sistema automatizado de triagem cross-belt . A unidade também conta com rastreabilidade por vídeo , que permite registrar e consultar o processo de triagem, ampliando a visibilidade e o controle sobre o fluxo de encomendas.

O grupo de transporte marítimo e logística CMA CGM e a empresa de energia ENGIE firmaram um acordo para desenvolver uma unidade de produção de biometano na zona industrial e portuária de Le Havre, na França. A instalação deverá fornecer 7 mil toneladas do combustível renovável por ano à frota da CMA CGM a partir de 2029 , volume equivalente a 100 GWh e com potencial estimado de evitar a emissão de 23 mil toneladas de CO₂ anualmente. A ENGIE será responsável pelo desenvolvimento do projeto, incluindo o planejamento técnico e o processo de licenciamento. A construção e a operação da unidade dependerão da decisão final de investimento. A CMA CGM participará como acionista minoritária, por meio do PULSE, fundo do grupo voltado a tecnologias e infraestruturas para descarbonizar suas atividades de transporte e logística. Prevista para entrar em operação entre 2029 e 2030, a instalação transformará resíduos pecuários, resíduos orgânicos domiciliares e resíduos agrícolas em biometano. O combustível será destinado à frota da CMA CGM por meio da rede europeia de gás, com rastreabilidade baseada em um sistema certificado de balanço de massa. Além do combustível, o processo deverá gerar 100 mil toneladas de digestato, material orgânico rico em nutrientes que poderá ser utilizado como fertilizante natural por agricultores da região. O projeto também prevê recuperar 13 mil toneladas de CO₂ de origem biogênica para comercialização. Segundo as empresas, o biometano pode reduzir em pelo menos 67% as emissões de gases de efeito estufa ao longo de seu ciclo de vida, em comparação com combustíveis marítimos convencionais. Outra vantagem é a possibilidade de utilização nos navios da CMA CGM movidos a gás natural liquefeito (GNL), sem necessidade de modificações nos motores ou na infraestrutura de abastecimento existente. “À medida que investimos juntos na produção de biometano na França, no maior porto de contêineres do país, avançamos em nossa visão de longo prazo de garantir acesso a combustíveis renováveis, contribuindo para a soberania energética da França e da Europa”, afirma Rodolphe Saadé, presidente e CEO do grupo CMA CGM.

https://www.gov.br/antaq/pt-br/noticias/.text: Brasília, 15/10/2026 – A Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (ANTAQ), o Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos (MPOR) e o Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA) realizarão, nos dias 21 e 22 de outubro, a oficina “Soluções baseadas na Natureza para adaptação climática no setor portuário”. O encontro acontecerá no Centro Cultural de Brasília (CCB), na Asa Norte, e contará com a colaboração da GIZ, por meio do Projeto ProAdapta, da Fundação Grupo Boticário e da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Educação, a Ciência e a Cultura (UNESCO). A oficina tem como objetivo promover a troca de experiências, identificar desafios e discutir caminhos para ampliar a adoção de Soluções baseadas na Natureza (SbN) como estratégia de adaptação dos portos brasileiros aos impactos das mudanças climáticas. O evento será presencial e voltado a representantes e instituições com atuação no setor portuário, tanto da esfera pública quanto da privada. Os interessados em participar devem preencher o formulário de inscrição . As Soluções baseadas na Natureza envolvem ações de conservação, restauração e gestão de ecossistemas naturais, como manguezais, restingas, dunas e áreas úmidas. Essas medidas podem contribuir para reduzir riscos associados à elevação do nível do mar, à erosão costeira e a eventos climáticos extremos, além de complementar soluções convencionais de engenharia e gerar benefícios ambientais e sociais. A oficina proporcionará um espaço de diálogo entre os participantes para identificar experiências já desenvolvidas no setor portuário, compreender os principais obstáculos à implementação dessas soluções e discutir oportunidades de integração às estratégias de planejamento, gestão e adaptação climática dos portos. A programação será dividida em dois dias, combinando apresentações técnicas, painéis temáticos e atividades participativas.

Romanian President Nicusor Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones but declined to say whether Russia was responsible, while a NATO military source said the drones came from Russia. “The drones that caused the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the NATO source said. https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: From “chokepoints” to “freedom of navigation,” the world’s headlines have been replete with maritime terms in recent years, and navigating that terminology has become a challenge for policymakers and maritime professionals alike, not to mention the general public. The maritime world is niche, with many archaic terms and concepts that have no terrestrial equivalent. Furthermore, it is often difficult to differentiate between terms that are colloquial versus technical. The term “shadow fleet,” for example, has graced newspapers around the world, but has no official definition and no legal significance. And while it may seem a pedantic or even trivial matter to try to clarify the terminology such that everybody is on the same page, there is an increasingly critical need to do so. As security threats, accidents at sea and climatic events disrupt maritime commerce in more frequent and significant ways, global supply chains of critical goods, including food and energy supplies, continue to break down. The resulting economic turbulence and life-threatening situations mean that maritime policy has become more important than ever. If leaders do not first understand how to articulate maritime matters in a way that is mutually intelligible to all actors, setting clear policy and resolving these critical issues (in some cases of existential concern) become all the more difficult, if not impossible. The time for a universal maritime lexicon with clear, commonly understood definitions has arrived. Four main challenges inhibit the ability of the maritime space to be governed in as clear a fashion as is currently necessary: - Diversity of understanding of issues and terms within the maritime world itself - The political appropriation of maritime terms to achieve non-maritime objectives All four of these issues encumber the ability of maritime professionals to be able to recognize and respond to the panoply of threats and challenges currently facing the domain that carries 90% of world trade, 99% of telephonic and internet communication, and more than 20% of our dietary protein intake. We need the maritime domain to function, so we need to be able to talk about it with clarity and precision.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: Romanian authorities are reporting an ongoing search and rescue effort in the Black Sea after two small product tankers were struck. Seven crewmembers from a San Marino-registered product tanker were reported missing while five others were evacuated. A second vessel reported no injuries and was said to be making its way to port under its own power as the increasing strikes are being discussed by NATO. The Maritime Coordination Center of the Romanian Naval Authority received the emergency call from the product tanker Wine Trader (6,259 dwt) at around 0700 on October 15. The vessel said it had been struck, and the crew was attempting to fight a fire. The first strike occurred in the area of the accommodation block and left several crewmembers unaccounted for and made a search difficult due to the intensity of the fire. A later report from the San Marino authorities said the captain reported the vessel was struck a second and possibly a third time. Damage to the water supply for the firefighting system forced them to suspend the efforts and evacuate. Romania was organizing a search for the missing crewmembers (Interior Ministry of Romania) The evacuation, however, was complicated by bad weather and high seas. A Romanian helicopter hoisted the injured crewmembers from the deck of the Wine Trader . Initial reports said there were four survivors, but the helicopter reported locating a fifth survivor. One person had suffered scalp burns, and another had mild smoke inhalation. A second helicopter team was dispatched to the vessel and was planning to board it to search for possible additional survivors. Seven crewmembers were listed as missing. The nationalities of the crew were reported as Beninese, Croatian, and Bosnian.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O marketplace global AliExpress e os Correios renovaram seu contrato de parceria para a entrega dos pedidos da plataforma no Brasil . A assinatura aconteceu em setembro, na sede do Alibaba Group, detentor da marca, em Hangzhou, na China. Além da renovação do contrato, as empresas assinaram um memorando de entendimentos (MoU) que estabelece ações conjuntas para acelerar as entregas no Brasil durante o peak season , período que inclui datas como o 11.11 e a Black Friday e tem maior volume de compras. O documento também formaliza o compromisso de aprimoramento contínuo do serviço pelas duas empresas. "Estamos preparados para o aumento do volume de encomendas previsto para o fim do ano, com uma logística robusta e integrada, que conecta o Brasil ao e-commerce global e garante mais agilidade aos consumidores", afirma o presidente dos Correios, Emmanuel Rondon. Briza Bueno, diretora-geral do AliExpress no Brasil , ressalta a alta capilaridade dos Correios, que atende todos os municípios do país, como peça estratégica da parceria. "A parceria com os Correios acompanha o AliExpress desde sempre no Brasil, e é muito importante para nossa operação no país. A capilaridade dos Correios leva o AliExpress ao Brasil inteiro, de ponta a ponta, das grandes capitais às cidades mais distantes do interior. Renovar esse contrato aqui, na casa do Alibaba Group, e assumir juntos novos compromissos mostra o quanto o consumidor brasileiro é prioridade para nós", comenta a executiva. A expansão das parcerias internacionais é um dos pilares do Plano de Reestruturação dos Correios. "A parceria com o AliExpress demonstra o reconhecimento da capacidade operacional dos Correios para atender, com excelência, um mercado em constante expansão. Ao fortalecer nossa atuação junto a grandes plataformas globais, ampliamos nossa capacidade de gerar receitas, atrair novos negócios e consolidar o papel dos Correios como protagonista da logística do comércio eletrônico", comenta Emmanuel Rondon. Participaram do encontro em Hangzhou, Hilton Rogério Maia Cardoso, diretor de Negócios dos Correios; José Marcos Gomes, diretor de Operações da estatal; Éverton Ferreira dos Santos membro do Conselho de Administração dos Correios; e Luiz Pavão, CEO da Infracommerce (MaisCorreios).

O Sistema Transporte participou da 43ª Assembleia Geral da CIT (Câmara Internacional de Logística e Transportes), realizada de 7 a 9 de outubro, em Santiago, no Chile . Representado pelo SEST SENAT , o Sistema apresentou a experiência brasileira na promoção da acessibilidade no transporte e defendeu uma agenda integrada que contemple usuários dos serviços, trabalhadores, empresas e instituições de formação profissional. Durante o encontro, a diretora executiva nacional do SEST SENAT, Nicole Goulart , apresentou o programa Rota da Acessibilidade e os resultados das ações desenvolvidas no Brasil. A iniciativa reúne medidas de qualificação profissional, inclusão no mercado de trabalho, acessibilidade física e digital, melhoria do atendimento e preparação das empresas para contratar, acolher e desenvolver profissionais com deficiência. A apresentação foi baseada em um levantamento sobre experiências adotadas por países das Américas. "As experiências de outros países nos ajudam a compreender que a acessibilidade precisa acompanhar toda a jornada da pessoa", afirmou Nicole. Segundo a diretora, além de garantir informações acessíveis, infraestrutura adequada, segurança no embarque e atendimento, é necessário assegurar condições para que pessoas com deficiência possam se qualificar, participar de processos seletivos, ingressar no mercado de trabalho e desenvolver suas carreiras no setor. Nicole destacou que, no Brasil, a legislação estabelece cotas para a contratação de pessoas com deficiência, mas o cumprimento dessa exigência não elimina, por si só, as barreiras enfrentadas por esses profissionais no mercado de trabalho. "Cumprir a cota não significa que o processo seletivo seja acessível e que a liderança esteja preparada para receber a pessoa com deficiência. É preciso que o profissional encontre oportunidades compatíveis com as suas competências e que tenha condições de crescer dentro da organização", disse. A diretora também apresentou o Estudo de Materialidade do Setor de Transporte Rodoviário, elaborado pelo SEST SENAT. O levantamento analisou 30 temas potencialmente relevantes para o setor e identificou dez prioritários para a agenda ESG (ambiental, social e de governança).

https://petronoticias.com.br/onze-mil-to.text: Iniciado em abril, o processamento de aço do casco dos navios Handymax no Estaleiro Rio Grande terá um importante reforço. Nesta quinta-feira chegou a Rio Grande uma embarcação vinda da Indonésia com 11 mil toneladas de aço, que começaram a ser descarregadas na parte da tarde. O material será utilizado na construção de quatro navios contratados pela Transpetro no âmbito do Programa Mar Aberto, iniciativa voltada à renovação e ampliação da frota própria do Sistema Petrobrás. As embarcações serão empregadas no transporte de derivados de petróleo pela costa brasileira. Pela manhã, houve a cerimônia de batimento de quilha reuniu trabalhadores e diretores das empresas. O batimento de quilha do primeiro navio Handymax encomendado pela Transpetro foi realizado seis meses após o início do processamento de aço do casco. A cerimônia, que reuniu trabalhadores do estaleiro e representantes da Transpetro, marca uma nova fase da construção das embarcações. Tradicional na indústria naval, o evento simboliza o início da construção de um navio. Do complexo naval sairão quatro navios do tipo Handymax contratados pela Transpetro no âmbito do Programa Mar Aberto, iniciativa voltada à renovação e ampliação da frota própria do Sistema Petrobrás. A quilha é como a “ espinha dorsal “, por onde a construção de um navio é iniciada. O ato de batimento é uma tradição secular considerada símbolo de proteção e boa sorte para a embarcação e seus tripulantes. O marco representa um novo passo para os trabalhos nos Handymax, que têm mobilizado mais de 500 profissionais ao longo deste ano no Estaleiro Rio Grande. Desde abril, o aço para o casco está sendo processado nas áreas fabris da Ecovix, de acordo com o cronograma alinhado com a Transpetro. “O dia de hoje concretiza a força e a capacidade do Estaleiro Rio Grande. É a consolidação de um trabalho responsável de todo o nosso time para a construção desses quatro navios – os primeiros de vários que entregaremos à Transpetro ao longo dos próximos anos”, afirma o CEO da Ecovix, Robson Passos. Os navios Handymax, que ampliarão a capacidade logística da Transpetro, terão 16.000 toneladas de porte bruto (TPB). As embarcações serão aptas ao transporte de produtos claros derivados de petróleo, como diesel marítimo, diesel S10, diesel S500 e gasolina de aviação. https://petronoticias.com.br/tmc-compres.text: A norueguesa TMC Compressors foi selecionada para fornecer um sistema de ar comprimido para o FPSO Maromba, que atualmente passa por modernização no o estaleiro COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry, na China, antes de ser instalado no campo de Maromba, operado pela BW Energy na Bacia de Campos. A TMC fornecerá um sistema marítimo de ar comprimido de alta capacidade, incluindo compressores de ar de serviço e de controle, secadores de ar, filtros e sistema de controle. O valor do contrato não foi divulgado. Segundo a empresa, sediada em Oslo, o compressor foi projetado para permitir que a própria tripulação realize a manutenção a bordo, sem a necessidade de um técnico de serviço externo. “ Há 20 anos, fornecemos o sistema marítimo de ar comprimido para o FPSO Polvo. Por isso, é um grande reconhecimento que tenham voltado a nos procurar para apoiar essa modernização. O FPSO Maromba exige tecnologias mais modernas e energeticamente eficientes, com capacidade ligeiramente superior. Estamos ansiosos para realizar essa entrega ”, afirma o diretor de vendas e desenvolvimento de negócios da TMC, Hans-Petter Tanum . Para lembrar, o casco da embarcação foi originalmente construído para um navio-tanque de transporte comercial. Em 2007, a unidade passou por sua primeira conversão para operar como FPSO no campo de Polvo, no Brasil, para a PRIO. Em abril de 2022, a BW Energy assinou um acordo para comprar o FPSO, que era de propriedade de outra empresa do conglomerado – a BW Offshore. A decisão final de investimento (FID, na sigla em inglês) para o desenvolvimento do campo de Maromba foi tomada em maio de 2025. O projeto tem como alvo um volume de 500 milhões de barris de petróleo in situ e prevê uma plataforma integrada de perfuração e cabeça de poço (WHP, na sigla em inglês), além do FPSO modernizado. O início da produção de petróleo no projeto brasileiro está previsto para o fim de 2027. A BW Energy estima que a produção atingirá um pico de 60 mil barris de petróleo por dia. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://gcaptain.com/by-the-numbers-u-s-.text: An image purportedly shows the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS PRIDE listing heavily and emitting thick black smoke following an attack in the Strait of Hormuz on October 13, 2026. The vessel subsequently sank, with all 21 crew members safely evacuated. The image has not been independently verified. U.S. Central Command says the United States and its regional partners control the Strait of Hormuz, citing more than 40 commercial ships moving through the waterway in the past 24 hours, even as maritime security officials warn that attacks on merchant vessels are increasing and the threat to shipping remains severe. The statement Thursday came as the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) released a new assessment documenting a series of attacks on commercial shipping, including the sinking of a containership, and warning that further strikes remain highly likely. “The United States and regional partners control the strait as commercial vessels continue to transit despite unwarranted IRGC aggression,” CENTCOM said in a statement rejecting three Iranian claims . But the military’s assertion of control comes against a markedly different picture of commercial shipping conditions. Traffic remains far below prewar levels, vessels continue to face attacks along established transit routes, and Iran is still attempting to influence how ships move through the strait. According to JMIC’s October 15 advisory , U.S.-facilitated traffic totaled 121 vessel transits between October 11 and 14, an average of approximately 30 ships per day. That compares with a historical average of roughly 138 daily transits in 2025, before the war.

https://gcaptain.com/trump-weighs-liftin.text: A U.S. military helicopter crew observes the sanctioned oil tanker Bertha during a right-of-visit boarding operation in the Indian Ocean. The interdiction marks the tenth vessel targeted in Washington’s expanding crackdown on shadow fleet oil shipments. Department of War photo WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) – The Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump’s fellow Republicans in the US Senate. Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine. The new talks center on the United States potentially allowing “legal oil” to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. That means crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by Washington rather than Russian and Iranian oil, which are under punitive measures. The goal is to get more refined products and crude out of the Gulf, the official said.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The U.S. Navy has confirmed that a midsize unmanned surface vessel has sailed with the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group, currently under way in the Pacific. It is the first time that a deployed CSG has been accompanied by an unmanned vessel too large to stow on a ship. Roosevelt got under way from San Diego on October 8, but preparations for integrating the USV into its escort force have been going on for some time. In September, the service released imagery of the destroyer USS Chafee practicing an astern refueling operation with the prototype USV Seahawk. Seahawk predates the drone-vessel designs now in production for the Navy's MUSV program. The prototype dates back to 2017, when the Navy awarded Leidos a contract to upgrade its existing Sea Hunter design using lessons learned from early trials. Leidos kept the trimaran hull form, but re-engineered the vessel's systems for minimal human intervention at sea, hoping to achieve truly unmanned, self-navigating operations. “We didn’t just put an autonomous navigation system onto an existing ship,” said defense executive Dan Brintzinghoffer, Leidos' Vice President for Maritime Solutions at the time of the USV's delivery(now with Austal USA). “Every mechanical and electrical system on Seahawk has unique configurations designed to run for months at a time without maintenance or a crew.” As delivered in 2021, Seahawk was an unarmed vessel, intended primarily to carry surveillance equipment and a sonar system for tracking submarines. Details of its configuration for the Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group deployment were not released; Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao suggested that it would be a useful addition. "This is a first carrier strike group to ever deploy with a large-size unmanned surface vessel, and this is a force multiplier. Imagine having more guns out there," Cao said at a U.S. Army conference this week.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: A wide-sweeping probe reaching from Norway to Germany and Romania has revealed a scheme of fraud and bribery for contracts to supply NATO ships. The first arrests were made on Wednesday in Bergen, Norway, with officials saying the scheme ran for at least four years and that they estimate the total losses are more than €1 million (US$1.12 million). The investigation began in April 2025 and was coordinated by Eurojust, the European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation, along with anti-corruption and prosecutor’s offices in Norway, Germany, Romania, and the United Kingdom. Eurojust reports the cross-border investigation is into alleged fraudulent invoices submitted to the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). The agency handles logistical support for military equipment and services, including the husbandry services that provide shore-based support to NATO warships. The Norwegian authority Økokrim said it believes the scheme ran for several years, between 2021 and 2025. It included over-invoicing NSPA for services provided to NATO ships in Norwegian ports, including Bergen. The fraud allegations Eurojust reports include bribery of foreign officials done by a suspected company through an intermediary, in return for favored support with their contractual dealings with NSPA. The cooperating agencies staged simultaneous raids in Norway, Germany, and Romania on Wednesday, searching homes and businesses. Økokrim reported that five individuals were taken into custody in the Bergen area. They have been charged with aggravated fraud against NSPA, or aiding and abetting such fraud. “Defence sector budgets are increasing worldwide, which entails an increased risk of economic crime,” said Marianne Bender, Senior Public Prosecutor at Økokrim. “It will take time to investigate this case as the charges cover several years and involve a very large number of ship calls.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: A British autonomous-boat startup has secured access to the fastest-moving R&D environment for naval USVs in the world: the Ukrainian attack-drone campaign in the Black Sea. Kraken Technology, based in Foreham, UK, has supplied its K3 Scout boats for use in at least one live strike on a Russian vessel, industry sources confirmed to Scottish paper The Times. A clearer footage of the moment of destruction of a Ukrainian unmanned surface vessel (USV) in the Russian port of Sochi earlier on Thursday. The USV was on its way to strike the NEFRIT multi-purpose offshore vessel (green hull) but was hit by Russian gunfire before being able to reach its target. At that time, the NEFRIT vessel was already damaged from the impact of another Ukrainian naval drone. On September 3, at least two USVs entered the port of Sochi, Russia and made an attack run on a Russian offshore construction vessel, the Nefrit . One strike USV penetrated the perimeter and damaged Nefrit's port side; a second made an attempt but detonated before reaching target, likely hit by defensive fire. "The unwavering British support for our Ukrainian allies continues and you can see why it is something the whole country cares so deeply about . . . British industry is a key pillar of the fight against Russian aggression and we support collaboration towards that effort," an industry source told The Times. An attack drone observed by bystanders during the Sochi strike, Sept. 3 (Russian social media) The K3 is a 28-foot boat with low-observable design and a top speed of about 55 knots. Its 600 kilogram maximum payload is enough to deliver a punch in a one-way attack role, and it can also be equipped to carry FPV drones. It has a range of about 650 nautical miles, enough to reach Sochi from Odesa, but there are additional ways to get it closer to target. In trials off the UK earlier this year, the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force repeatedly dropped a K3 out of the back of a cargo plane, parachuting it into open water for insertion in remote operating areas. The Scout survived four drops in a row, according to the Royal Navy.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: The tight global market for diesel fuel is likely to extend well into 2027, according to the latest analysis from the International Energy Agency, meaning that record prices may be here to stay through at least the first quarter of 2027 - and maybe longer, depending upon the conflicts in the Mideast and Ukraine. The disruption at the Strait of Hormuz, attacks on refineries in the GCC states, and Ukraine's concerted campaign of strikes on Russian energy infrastructure have all put downward pressure on diesel export volume. Increased exports from the U.S. Gulf Coast and (recently) China have helped offset the drop - but overall, the net global supply of diesel and gasoil has fallen by about 1.7 million barrels per day, according to the IEA. Demand for diesel is also down year-over-year, but only by about 0.75 million bpd in the third quarter. That picture could worsen in coming months because of deteriorating economics for refiners outside of the United States. The price of oil and the cost of tanker charters are both very high, and the net cost for making and shipping diesel is approaching unfavorable levels for some refiners in Asia and Europe. IEA forecasts that if their margins drop further, some of these overseas refiners could decide to make run cuts as a business decision, further tightening the market for middle distillates. The supply-demand mismatch means high prices. Diesel hit the $220 per barrel mark in the U.S. and in Europe last month, setting records, and average diesel retail prices in the American market are still about 75 percent more than they were this time last year. That added cost trickles down into inflation across all sectors, since diesel is the mobile energy supply of choice for trucking, construction, industry and agriculture. The shortfall in refinery output also requires suppliers to draw down on inventory. Global stocks of gasoil are down by five percent since before the conflict, according to IEA. Russian refineries are too damaged by previous Ukrainian strikes to make up the gap in the near term, IEA found, despite the White House's announced intention to bring more Russian diesel fuel to market.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: In the latest blow to Australia’s already struggling cruise industry, Carnival Cruise Line announced it will redeploy permanently to North America two of the four cruise ships it has had in the market. While Australia is the fourth largest overall cruise market, a coalition formed earlier this year highlighted that the market is sagging under rising costs and a lack of regulatory certainty. Carnival Cruise Line announced the Carnival Adventure (108,865 gross tons with accommodations for up to 3,150 passengers) will depart Sydney for its last cruise on March 20. 2028 and will not return as previously planned. Earlier in the year, Carnival had announced plans for the ship to split its year between the summer seasons in the northern and southern hemispheres. Carnival had recently announced that the ship, which had only joined the fleet in 2025, would start in May 2028, operate 7-day cruises from Seattle to Alaska, but planned for it to return to Australia in October 2028. The Carnival Luminosa (92,720 gross tons with accommodations for up to 2,800 passengers) had been operating seasonally between Australia and Alaska since the cruise industry restarted operations after the pandemic in 2022. Carnival reports it will depart from Brisbane for the final time on March 15, 2028. Carnival Cruise Line will continue to operate the sister ship Carnival Encounter (108,865 gross tons with accommodations for up to 3,150 passengers) from Brisbane. The Carnival Splendor (113,573 gross tons with accommodations for up to 3,012 passengers) will continue to operate from Sydney. “As the only cruise line with ships dedicated year-round to Australia, Carnival has greater exposure to changes in local market and operating conditions than cruise lines with a seasonal or more limited presence,” said Carnival Cruise Line Country Manager Peter Little, explaining the decision to redeploy the two ships. The line noted that Australia’s decision to extend the exemption for the cruise industry from Australia’s Coastal Trading Act was “a welcome but interim step while the long-term operating framework for the Australian cruise sector is developed over the next two years.” He said the company would continue to work with the Australian government.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: A.P. Moller Capital, the investment management arm of the A.P. Moller Group, is continuing to build its portfolio of port and logistics investments. In its latest move, the investment manager, which has approximately $2 billion in assets under management, announced it has agreed to acquire Singapore-based Portek International from Mitsui & Co. Portek is a cargo port terminal operator and engineering business with interests in seven port terminals across Africa, Asia and Europe. Founded in 1988, Portek operates a geographically diversified portfolio of multipurpose terminals serving local and international trade flows. Its terminal interests span Algeria, Gabon, Indonesia, Latvia, Malta and Vietnam. Portek also provides port engineering and operations and maintenance services, principally from Singapore and Indonesia. Its terminals handle around seven million tonnes of bulk cargo, 700,000 containers, and around 90,000 vehicles each year. Portek is a strong fit with our investment strategy and active owner philosophy,” said Semih Gökmen, Partner at A.P. Moller Capital. “It is an established business with a diversified portfolio of port operations serving important trade flows across three continents, supported by experienced local operating teams.” The investment gives A.P. Moller exposure to some of the fastest-growing cargo markets such as Vietnam, where Portek is an indirect shareholder in the owner/operator of the Vietnam International Container Terminal (VICT), the premier container port project in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It also manages a terminal in Latvia, Indonesia, and Malta, as well as locations in Algeria and two terminals in Gabon. Following completion of the acquisition, A.P. Moller Capital reports that it intends to work closely with Portek’s local operating teams to build on the company’s existing capabilities and support its next phase of development. It said there will be a focus on operational performance, governance, safety, capital discipline and environmental performance, including emissions-reduction planning.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: The Spirit of Toulouse , the first of three pioneering RoRos with wind-assisted propulsion, marked a milestone in its construction with the installation of its six wind rotors. The vessel, which is being built in China, becomes not only the largest RoRo vessel to be equipped with wind-assisted propulsion, but also has the largest number of mechanical sails fitted on a single vessel. " Spirit of Toulouse is much more than a new vessel. It is a tangible demonstration of how the maritime industry can accelerate its transition by combining innovation, operational expertise, and strong industrial partnerships,” said Samira Draoua, CEO of LD Armateurs, the owners of the vessels. The vessel, which is 19,000 gross tons, is being fitted with six Norsepower Rotor Sails. The six rotor sails each measure 35 meters by 5 meters (approximately 115 feet by 16.4 feet), and they are being paired with two dual-fuel main engines and two dual-fuel generator sets, capable of running on e-methanol, bio-methanol, or marine diesel oil. LD Armateurs, which is building the vessel for charter to Airbus, expects each vessel to deliver a 70 percent decrease in CO2 emissions, on an annual basis, compared with the two vessels it currently operates on the Atlantic for Airbus. Each of the ships has an overall length of approximately 168 meters (551 feet) and will be 5,300 dwt. They will have a service speed of 14 knots. The ships will be registered in France. Spirit of Toulouse is the largest RoRo with wind-assisted propulsion and has the largest number of mechanical sails on a vessel (LD Armateurs) “Completing installation of six Norsepower Rotor Sails on Spirit of Toulouse is a significant milestone for wind propulsion in the RoRo segment,” said Heikki Pöntynen, CEO of Norsepower. Wind-assisted propulsion continues to gain momentum with adoption ranging from tankers to bulkers and more RoRos and cruise ships.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: Georgia Port Authority has secured the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' approval for a massive new container terminal at the Port of Savannah, completing a three-year-long review process. The new terminal will be built on Hutchison Island on 350 acres, and will have a capacity of 3.5 million TEU. The extra room will allow Savannah to continue a decade-long growth boom, which started with the inauguration of the New Panama Canal and "all-water" routes from Asia to the U.S. East Coast back in 2016. At present, the port has a nameplate capacity of about 7.75 million TEU. It is also augmenting the Ocean Terminal, spending about $1.6 billion to increase its capacity from 200,000 TEU today to about 1.75 million TEU in 2028. The port authority, the state and the Corps of Engineers are working on additional projects to improve the harbor for larger vessel traffic and build out the shoreside infrastructure for intermodal transport. The work includes a large-scale dredging project for Savannah Harbor. The progress on permitting for the new terminal will be a capstone for the tenure of longtime CEO Griff Lynch, who has been at the helm of the Georgia Port Authority since 2011. Over the period, Savannah's container volume has nearly doubled, and GPA's overall revenues have more than tripled. "We have been blessed with talented, dedicated people at GPA and with business partners who defined our service levels, enabling our customers to succeed and grow. I’m proud of our people, thankful for our customers and confident in the port and inland infrastructure we’ve built. We’re never done growing," said Lynch in a statement.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543720-en.text: Italian energy firm Eni will start drilling up to six development wells from November that will feed gas to its new Coral North floating liquefied natural gas platform offshore Mozambique, a senior executive told Reuters on Thursday. The project is on track to start production by 2028, doubling the company's output to around 7 million metric tons per annum, Mario Bello, Eni's Head of sub-Saharan Africa said on the sidelines of an energy conference in Cape Town. "Mozambique actually is a premium gas source. I think geographically it's just perfectly located to fit the premium LNG market that is in the Far East without having a critical transit route," he said in reference to the Iran war that has choked off major gas and oil shipping routes. Bello said Eni, which previously said it was considering a third FLNG offshore Mozambique due to the country's abundant gas resources in the Rovuma Basin, was currently in the early pre-front-end engineering and design stage on the project. "And we are evaluating all aspects of the project," Bello said, adding the plan was for a larger platform higher than 5 MTPA. This process will pave the way towards taking a final investment decision, he said without providing a timeline.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543719-tu.text: Turkey will send its first floating gas production platform to the Black Sea on Saturday, a move expected to roughly double output from its largest domestic gas field, Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said on Thursday. The Osman Gazi platform is expected to begin production in early 2027, eventually raising daily output from the Sakarya gas field to 20 million cubic metres from the current 9.5 million, equivalent to 7.3 billion cubic metres (bcm) annually. The platform will operate around 170 km offshore and is expected to remain in service for 20 years, processing natural gas for delivery to Turkey's national grid. Turkey is one of Europe's largest gas markets, consuming 59 bcm last year. The country relies on imports for almost all its gas needs, with domestic production totalling 3.1 bcm last year, most of it from the Sakarya field.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ind.text: India has urged both Russia and Ukraine to ensure safe passage for commercial shipping through the Black Sea as attacks on merchant vessels put Indian seafarers at risk and threaten to disrupt vital food and energy supplies. “The targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways must be restored at the earliest,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said last week. India accounts for more than 12% of the global seafaring workforce, with 311,936 maritime professionals, according to a 2026 industry report. And attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea in recent months have highlighted the risks facing civilian crews. The Turkish-owned MV Royad Mammadov, a cargo ship carrying grain from Ukraine, caught fire and sank following an attack on Monday, killing two crew members. The three Indian nationals aboard the vessel survived, but sustained injuries and were taken to Romania to receive medical treatment. The Defense Ministry in Moscow separately said it had struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea but did not specifically identify the ships. The Liberian-flagged oil tanker Aframax Rio was also recently attacked by unmanned vessels off Russia’s Black Sea coast near Sochi, according to Russian authorities. The vessel was carrying 23 Indians, but all of them were rescued.

https://petronoticias.com.br/agencia-int.text: A Agência Internacional de Energia (AIE) vai acelerar a liberação dos cerca de 100 milhões de barris de petróleo restantes de uma ação coordenada entre seus países-membros, anunciada em março de 2026 em resposta à crise no Estreito de Ormuz. O plano inclui a disponibilização de mais de 20 milhões de barris de diesel o mais rapidamente possível, em meio à continuidade das restrições nos mercados globais de petróleo, especialmente no segmento de diesel. Em reunião realizada nesta quinta-feira (15), o Conselho de Administração da AIE reafirmou seu compromisso com a segurança energética internacional e sinalizou disposição para adotar novas medidas diante dos desafios nos mercados globais de energia, com base na declaração do G7 de 2 de outubro. Até o momento, aproximadamente 330 milhões de barris já foram liberados. Segundo a agência, o volume total poderá superar os 400 milhões de barris inicialmente previstos, uma vez que alguns países-membros liberaram quantidades superiores às prometidas em março e outros pretendem fazer o mesmo. O conselho também incentivou os países-membros com capacidade de produção e refino a ampliar a oferta de petróleo bruto e derivados, especialmente diesel, e ressaltou a importância da livre circulação do comércio internacional de energia. O secretariado da AIE continuará monitorando o avanço das liberações previstas na ação coletiva de março de 2026, em consonância com a declaração dos líderes do G7. A agência também atualizará suas avaliações do mercado de petróleo, com atenção especial ao diesel, para identificar a necessidade de novas medidas e manter os líderes do G7 e o conselho informados. © 2026 Petronotícias.
