https://gcaptain.com/fog-of-war-deepens-.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz near the beach of Bandar Abbas, Iran, September 28, 2026. Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA/via WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS Conflicting traffic figures and competing claims of control are making it increasingly difficult to establish what’s happening in the Strait of Hormuz, even as attacks on merchant shipping intensify. The true extent of attacks on merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz remains unclear, with a new report from UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) acknowledging that most vessels struck in the region are not reporting incidents directly to the maritime security organization. The admission comes as the United States and Iran offer sharply different accounts of who controls the vital waterway, while conflicting transit figures raise further questions about how much commercial shipping has actually recovered. In its weekly overview published Friday , UKMTO said it is struggling to establish the true number of attacks because the majority of vessels targeted are refusing to submit reports. UKMTO said it is aware of additional incidents through other sources but cannot include them in its reporting without sufficient verification.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/2-s.text: Romanian authorities have launched search and rescue operations in the Black Sea in a bid to find seven missing crew from a chemical tanker that caught fire overnight to Thursday. Another vessel, also a chemical tanker, was also set on fire in the same region some hours earlier, but all its crew is said to be safe. The fires occurred after Russian drones strayed into Romanian airspace, though Romanian officials have so far not explicitly said the unmanned aircraft caused the blazes. However, there have been drone strikes on at least five other cargo ships off the coasts of Romanian and neighboring Bulgaria — both NATO members — in the past 10 days, with at least 23 sailors lost in those incidents. Romanian President Nicusor Dan met with NATO chief Mark Rutte to address the situation. “This is unacceptable and it has to stop. Lives, global trade, and critical infrastructure are at stake,” Dan wrote on X after a meeting with NATO chief Mark Rutte to discuss a recent spate of such attacks.

https://gcaptain.com/supertanker-rates-f.text: LONDON, Oct 16 (Reuters) – The cost ?of shipping oil on the largest tankers fell this week from record highs as demand eased following a wave of attacks on vessels in the Middle East and as the US considered easing sanctions on the so-called shadow fleet. Freight rates ?for supertankers, also known as very large crude carriers (VLCCs), carrying oil ?from the Gulf of Oman to China fell to about 776 ?on the Worldscale basis, according to Baltic Exchange ?data. That was down from 841 last week, the highest since the rate was launched earlier this year, following gains since the outbreak of the Iran war. “Gulf of Oman VLCC rates dropped as demand on that route has softened since the fresh attacks, as higher Middle East Gulf freight rates and subsequently lower export volumes have reduced demand on this route,” said Kpler analyst Matthew Wright. Trump administration comments about potentially removing sanctions on some shadow-fleet tankers drove freight rates lower, Sparta Commodities analyst Michael Ryan said, adding a removal would increase the number of ships that can carry oil. Despite the drop, rates remain close to record highs. The US-Israeli war on Iran has increased the use of ship-to-ship transfers to move oil out of the Strait of Hormuz, boosting demand for tankers. If elevated shipping costs persist, they could add to inflationary pressures and raise costs for businesses and consumers.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards has carried out the keel-laying ceremony for the Canadian Coast Guard's next polar icebreaker, the future CCGS Imnaryuaq. It has been 15 years since the initial contract was awarded for Imnaryuaq, and the long-awaited vessel is now formally under way towards completion. Delivery is expected in 2032. At 520 feet long and 26,000 tonnes displacement, Imnaryuaq will be the largest icebreaker ever built in Canada. The ship will be constructed to Polar Class 2 standards for service in up to 10 feet of ice, with extra strengthening for severe duty in the High Arctic. With room for a science complement of up to 40 people, the vessel is ready for research missions as well as sovereign presence and SAR operations. "Today’s keel laying is an important step forward in the renewal of the Canadian Coast Guard fleet," said CCG Commissioner Kevin Brosseau in a statement. "The CCGS Imnaryuaq, named to honor Inuit placenames and culture, will be a world-class icebreaker that will protect Arctic sovereignty and serve Canadians and communities across Inuit Nunangat for generations to come." Imnaryuaq was initially scheduled to deliver in 2017, but construction was pushed back to make room for the Royal Canadian Navy's two Protecteur-class naval auxiliaries. Both are nearing completion at Seaspan and delivery is expected in the next several years. Canadian leaders also opted to buy another polar icebreaker from a different shipbuilder. Davie's Helsinki Shipyard is currently building the second vessel to a different design. The Helsinki Shipyard / Davie hull is slightly smaller, and is scheduled for delivery in 2030. Davie's vessel will cost US$2.3 billion, and Seaspan's CCGS Imnaryuaq is expected to cost US$3 billion. Seaspan has constructed multiple ice-classed vessels for the CCG already as part of the National Shipbuilding Strategy, and is also building 16 smaller multipurpose icebreakers for the Canadian Coast Guard.

The salvage and recycling operation for the wrecked containershp MSC Baltic III continues to make strong progress. The Canadian Coast Guard in its most recent update on the operation says that Resolve Marine has removed approximately 68 percent of the tonnage of the vessel, with the remaining sections being pulled toward shore. The latest figures compare with just over 6,000 tons that had been recovered as of the beginning of October. At that point, they said approximately 55 percent of the vessel’s tonnage had been recovered and sent for recycling. The latest calculation puts it at 7,445 tonnes recovered. The 207-meter (679-foot) vessel had blacked out and beached on the coast of Newfoundland in February 2025. The focus of the first phase of the salvage operation was to remove the fuel from the ship and other potential pollutants as well as the cargo. The second phase, which focused on the recycling of the vessel, began in May 2026 with a contract to Resolve Marine. After removing the accommodation block, most of the deck gear, and cargo hatches, the operation during the summer began cutting away the upper portion of the hull. By the end of July, the deconstruction of the upper portions of the hull was completed, and they began the pulling operation to move the remaining portion forward toward the shoreline for cutting and lifting. On September 9, a large portion of the bow section was removed from the MSC Baltic III . Remaining sections of the hull are being pulled forward with large chain pulls (Canadian Coast Guard) According to the latest report, the forward and midship section of the hull have now been moved forward a total of 170 meters (557 feet). Resolve Marine has also commenced pulling the stern section forward, having moved it a total of 78 meters (256 feet).

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: The Australian Defence Force is reporting that a person of interest has been identified and is cooperating with its investigation into a hidden camera that was found aboard one of its vessels. The camera located in a women’s bathroom on HMAS Leeuwin has turned into a national embarrassment and is being treated as an act of sexual violence. The video recording device was discovered aboard HMAS Leeuwin on October 11 while the ship was at its berth in Cairns, Queensland. The device had been planted in the shower facilities of female sailors. The Australian Defence Force, which described the discovery of the device as the “most despicable betrayal of trust,” said the ship’s program had been altered to enable a rapid and rigorous investigation by the Joint Military Police Unit working with civilian authorities. The Warrant Officer of the Navy was also in Cairns to support the ship’s company. Commissioned in 2000, the 71-meter HMAS Leeuwin is the lead ship of the Leeuwin-class of hydrographic survey vessels. The ship, which can accommodate 46 crew, is mainly deployed for hydrographic duties, although at times she’s called to carry out border protection operations. Together with her sister ship Melville, Leeuwin is equipped with multi-beam echo sounders and the ability to support a helicopter, and carry three nine-meter survey motor boats, all for survey operations. The surveys are designed to make the passage of vessels safer and help to protect Australia's ocean environment. Vice Admiral Matt Buckley, the Chief of the Navy, said, “The location of the recording device is the most despicable betrayal of trust and is fundamentally misaligned with the Navy’s values.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/s.text: South Korea’s HJ Heavy Industries completed a larger-than-planned overhaul and repair project for the Military Sealift Command supply ship USNS Amelia Earhart and redelivered the ship to the U.S. Navy. The project is in keeping with the U.S. Navy’s “Indo-Pacific Maintenance Capability Enhancement” policy, which is designed to undertake maintenance and overhaul work in the region to reduce the vessel’s time away from service and out of the region, while also reducing the amount of work on the already stretched shipyard facilities in the United States. While the U.S. had already sent several other ships from the Lewis and Clark dry cargo ship class for maintenance in South Korea, this project was the first time that a mid-sized Korean yard had won and successfully undertaken one of these projects. HJ Heavy Industries had assembled a team with other suppliers for the project, enabling it to compete with Korea’s largest shipbuilders. In the past, Hanwha Ocean and HD Hyundai had won the first overhaul assignments from the United States. USS Amelia Earhart is a 40,000-ton logistics support ship. It was placed in service in 2008. The ship measures 210 meters (689 feet) in length. It supplies up to 6,000 tons of ammunition, food, and cargo, as well as 2,400 tons of fuel to support the ships of the U.S. Navy. The contract for the vessel’s overhaul was awarded in December 2025, and it arrived at the Yeongdo Shipyard in Busan, South Korea, in January. It originally called for a three-month overhaul period. HJ Heavy Industries reports it undertook an inspection as part of the planned maintenance of the hull, major systems, and equipment. Numerous “defects” that were not included in the original contract, however, were identified, and HJ Heavy Industries also proposed improvements to the plan. The U.S. Navy accepted the proposal, and as a result, the scope was extended by six months. The handover was completed on October 14. The U.S. Navy provided a letter of appreciation to the yard and commended it for the work completed on the ship.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: The waters off the Horn of Africa are now the most dangerous for the merchant shipping industry owing to the resurgence of Somali piracy, a development that comes as global piracy and armed robbery incidents have plunged to their lowest levels in decades. In its quarterly report on violence against seafarers, the ICC International Maritime Bureau (IMB) highlighted the renewed threat from Somali pirates while saying vigilance needs to be maintained in all areas of the globe, The overall tone of the nine-month report from the IMB is that there have been major strides in the war against piracy and armed robberies. It points to declines in areas such as the Singapore Strait and a dramatic overall decline to levels last experienced in 1992, while also reporting that the threat of violence has increased. IMB reports that cases of piracy and armed robberies against ships now stand at historical lows after only 51 incidents were reported in the first nine months of this year. This was a significant decline from the 116 incidents reported over the same period last year. Despite the decline in incidents, threats of violence to seafarers remain a major concern. This emanates from the fact that 105 crewmembers were threatened or injured/killed in the first nine months of 2026, compared to 72 last year. Of the 105, 90 were taken hostage, six injured, five killed, three threatened, and one assaulted. Of more concern is that weapons were identified in 53 percent of the cases. The data shows that 36 vessels were boarded, eight hijacked, and our vessels were fired upon, while attempted boardings were reported in three vessels. In 86 percent of incidents, perpetrators successfully gained access to the vessel while either at anchor or steaming, with most boarding incidents occurring at night. Notably, bulk carriers continue to be the main targets for pirates and armed robbers, with 20 vessels targeted followed by tankers (11), containerships (10), and others (10). While piracy and armed robberies against merchant ships have declined in waters that have recently been dangerous, including the Singapore Straits and Gulf of Guinea, the Horn of Africa is again becoming the hotspot of piracy. Over the January to September period, eight hijacking cases were carried out by Somali pirates, who were also responsible for 94 percent of crew taken hostage worldwide. Cumulatively, IMB calculates a total of 15 ships came under attack by Somali pirates.

A Meta, responsável pelo Facebook, Instagram e Whatsapp, disse nesta sexta-feira (16), em nota, que a empresa "não toma partido nessa nem em nenhuma outra eleição", afirmou que a conta do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) chegou a ser suspensa "por engano" e que "incidentes técnicos recentes" afetaram as duas campanhas na internet. De acordo com o posicionamento, uma "lacuna" nas "proteções" da empresa fez com que a ferramenta de inteligência artificial da Meta elaborasse materiais de campanha que favoreciam o senador e também candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). "Nossos sistemas não classificam nem distribuem conteúdo com base em ideologia política, e nossas regras e sua aplicação valem igualmente para todos", declarou a empresa na nota. Na quinta-feira (15), o ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), determinou, que até o fim do segundo turno das eleições, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 500 mil, a Meta não interfira na distribuição de conteúdo político-eleitoral nem de Lula nem de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). A decisão foi dada em ação protocolada pela campanha de Lula, após dizer que a empresa "tem falhado, de forma reiterada e sistemática, na entrega de postagens da coligação". De acordo com a Meta, a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula (PT) foi desativada "por engano" e "não por razões políticas" em 23 de setembro . A suspensão, segundo a empresa, durou pouco mais de 1 hora - e a página oficial da campanha de Lula no Facebook e a conta no Instagram nunca foram bloqueadas.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: O Leblon registrou alta na criminalidade em 2026. Os dados foram divulgados após a arqueóloga Tania Andrade Lima ser baleada em assalto nesta quinta-feira (15). De janeiro a setembro de 2026, o roubo a transeunte subiu 47,8% no Leblon. O roubo após saque bancário aumentou de 1 para 5 casos. Tania teve ferimentos e foi transferida de hospital. A polícia identificou um suspeito do crime e recuperou a motocicleta utilizada no assalto.

Pacientes com câncer relatam a interrupção de tratamentos por falta de oncologistas no Hospital do Andaraí, no Rio. Consultas sucessivas foram canceladas. Relatos apontam que pacientes estão há 3 meses sem consultas ou quimioterapia. Os cancelamentos ocorreram após a saída de médicos. Municipalizado há 2 anos, o hospital recebeu R$ 100 milhões do Ministério da Saúde. A prefeitura relata dificuldades de contratação. A estrutura de leitos está abaixo da meta planejada de 450 vagas. Atualmente, o hospital possui 358 leitos, mas 42 estão indisponíveis. A prefeitura afirma ter contratado mais de 4.000 profissionais desde a municipalização. O atendimento dos pacientes citados será marcado na próxima semana.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mid.text: Brent crude’s price has remained elevated as more oil tankers and commercial vessels have come under attack while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. A containership came under attack within the Strait of Hormuz yesterday while conducting an inbound transit, sustaining minor damages, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency reported. A second container vessel was struck by an unknown projectile within the Strait of Hormuz yesterday, while conducting an outbound transit, also sustaining minor damages, the UKMTO said in a separate report. Between 11-14 October, the UKMTO reported at least 11 incidents within the Persian Gulf. About 10 vessels attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz yesterday – six inbound and four outbound, according to market intelligence provider Windward. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/att.text: India on Thursday (local time) strongly condemned attacks on maritime navigation and commercial shipping amid the wider escalating conflict in West Asia, reiterating that such strikes are “legally and morally indefensible” and calling for the protection of seafarers, including Indian nationals.India also underlined the international responsibility to safeguard the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Southern Red Sea amid the conflict in Yemen, involving the Houthis and its internationally recognised government and Saudi Arabia.Addressing the United Nations Security Council’s quarterly open debate on the situation in the Middle East, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, reaffirmed New Delhi’s commitment to the unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yemen and rejected any interference in its internal affairs. “We strongly condemn attacks on maritime navigation and on the seafarers, many of whom are Indian citizens. https://gcaptain.com/ship-fuel-crunch-to.text: Holding tanks are seen in an aerial photograph at Colonial Pipeline's Dorsey Junction Station in Woodbine, Maryland, U.S. May 10, 2021. REUTERS/Drone Base Oct 16, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Accelerating crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz aren’t translating into higher production of a dirty shipping fuel, according to a top Vitol Group executive, tightening supplies and sending prices soaring. The Middle East conflict has reduced fuel oil supply from the Persian Gulf, including from Iran, by 800,000 tons per month, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have cut supply by 1 million tons per month, Vitol’s Asia head Kieran Gallagher said at a conference in Singapore this week. “Many are looking to increased crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz as a silver bullet, but more crude does not necessarily mean more high-sulfur fuel oil,” Gallagher said at Sibcon . “Refining margins are exceptionally strong and refiners have been maximizing throughput to capture those returns,” he added, referring to refiners prioritizing other products such as diesel. The supply squeeze stemming from the two wars has driven prices of high-sulfur bunker fuel made with HSFO in Singapore to the highest level since April, according to data provider ClearLynx LLC. The city-state is the world’s biggest supplier of ship fuel. On Thursday, HSFO costs in Asia soared relative to crude, rising to a seven-month high, according to Bloomberg Fair Value data. Demand for HSFO as a refinery feedstock is adding to the squeeze. North Asian refiners are set to use more than 1 million tons of HSFO to feed upgrading units in November after disruptions to Saudi crude exports from the Red Sea, said Gallagher. Restoring medium and heavy oil supplies to those processors would reduce their reliance on fuel oil as a feedstock and release those barrels back into the bunker pool, he added.

https://gcaptain.com/iea-moves-to-accele.text: The International Energy Agency (IEA) has agreed to accelerate the release of approximately 100 million barrels of emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel, as the prolonged Strait of Hormuz crisis continues to strain global energy supplies. The decision, announced Thursday following a meeting of the agency’s Governing Board, comes amid mounting concerns over diesel shortages, high fuel prices and renewed attacks on commercial shipping in the Middle East. According to the IEA’s statement , member countries have already released approximately 330 million barrels under the emergency stock release agreed in March in response to the Iran war. The agency said it would take steps to accelerate the remaining releases, with more than 20 million barrels of diesel to be made available as soon as possible. The original agreement called for a record 400 million barrels of oil and petroleum products. However, some member countries have released more than initially pledged, while others plan to do the same, meaning the final total is expected to exceed 400 million barrels. The latest decision primarily speeds up previously committed releases rather than establishing an entirely new emergency stock drawdown. The IEA did not provide a specific timetable for completing the releases. The renewed push comes as the agency warns that the global diesel shortage could persist well into 2027.

https://gcaptain.com/wind-assisted-shipp.text: Caption: LD Armateurs’ Spirit of Toulouse, built for Airbus transatlantic transport operations, fitted with six 35-meter-tall Norsepower rotor sails at an outfitting site in Shanghai, China. Photo: LD Armateurs/Norsepower French shipowner LD Armateurs has completed the installation of six towering rotor sails aboard Spirit of Toulouse , a new roll-on/roll-off vessel being built to transport aircraft components for Airbus across the Atlantic. The installation, completed at a shipyard outfitting site in Shanghai, makes the 168-meter vessel the largest RoRo ship equipped with wind-assisted propulsion and gives it more mechanical sails than any other ship, according to LD Armateurs and Finnish wind propulsion specialist Norsepower. Each of the six rotor sails stands 35 meters tall and measures 5 meters in diameter. The rotating cylinders harness wind to generate additional thrust, reducing the workload on the ship’s main engines and, in turn, its fuel consumption. The vessel is also equipped with two dual-fuel main engines and two generator sets capable of operating on e-methanol, bio-methanol or marine diesel oil. The combination is intended to reduce fuel consumption and emissions without relying entirely on alternative fuels. Spirit of Toulouse is the first of three sister ships being built for LD Armateurs under charter to Airbus. The other two vessels, Spirit of Mobile and Spirit of Mirabel , will also receive six rotor sails each.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wha.text: Look at it from the viewpoint of a shipper moving goods by containership on the Asia-Europe route. The proportion of ships on this route which arrived on the scheduled day of arrival declined from 51% in May to just 31% in September (average of all ports and all carriers), according to the Drewry Container Capacity Insight. Even the Gemini alliance, which has a higher-than-average track record for on-time arrivals, managed just 34% in September. Shippers and forwarders are increasingly aware that, not only are the ships arriving late, but also a proportion of the intended sailings do not happen (so-called “blank sailings”). If we combine the 2 types of unpredicted changes and delays, then the proportion of performed and on-time sailings on the Asia-Europe route falls to about 29% in September. Not all carriers and alliances are the same. The Asia-Europe trade’s schedule reliability scores by carrier in September ranged between 19% and 38% and the proportion of sailings not cancelled ranged between 0% and 23%, according to Drewry’s analysis for this route. Informed and realistic shippers and forwarders, therefore, must conclude that the best they can do is to monitor and compare their providers’ shaky schedule adherence, switch to those who are above-average when possible… and build “buffer time” in their supply chains. This is because the cargo will, more often than not, arrive later than promised by the carrier at the time of booking. Peak season buffer time may need to be longer, too. If ocean carriers are under-performing on schedule adherence, they can still say that many ports and terminals, particularly in Asia, have been gridlocked during the summer, making it impossible to meet scheduled arrivals and departures for their ships.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/a-c.text: A port call is a stop a vessel makes along its route to load or unload cargo, take on supplies or let passengers go ashore. For a port authority it is a berth booking. For a ship agent it is a service opportunity. For a commodity analyst it is a data point that, repeated across months and years, can hint at where trade is heading. This guide covers what a port call is, who relies on port call data, and how to read port call activity as a trend rather than a list of events. It also sets out what port calls cannot tell you, which matters as much as what they can. What is a port call? A port call is a vessel’s visit to a port, bounded by an arrival and a departure. In between, a vessel may load or discharge cargo, embark or disembark passengers, bunker or undergo repairs. A single port call is a record of a vessel event. Structured over time, port calls become a time series of arrivals and departures that can be filtered by port, country, vessel type, flag, capacity, owner, operator or commercial manager. That shift, from individual events to the pattern they create, is what turns operational data into market intelligence. Every port call can be connected to a set of attributes that add context, such as: • Event data: including arrival and departure timestamps, port or terminal, and direction (inbound or outbound). • Vessel data: including vessel type, dimensions, deadweight, capacity fields such as TEU, CEU, liquid, gas, bale, grain or passenger capacity, flag, and fuel and engine characteristics. • Corporate data: including beneficial owner, registered owner, commercial manager, operator and technical manager. Several companies can be attached to the same vessel, and the legal owner is often not the party making deployment decisions. For questions about where a company is building market presence, the commercial operator or manager is usually the most relevant lens.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: Russia is clearly mounting a campaign in the Black Sea against merchant shipping, with the aim of reducing shipping volumes heading to and from Ukraine. There have been eight recorded attacks on merchant shipping in the western Black Sea in October, excluding attacks carried out directly on shipping and port facilities in Ukraine. Four vessels were attacked by drones in the sea area adjacent to the Romanian coastline. The San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader (IMO 8808707) and the Turkish-flagged cargo ship Royad Mammadov (IMO 9356969) were attacked while located in the Romanian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). The Comoros-flagged chemical/oil products tanker Yara J (IMO 9221803) and the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny (IMO 9454175) were struck in what the Romanian authorities acknowledged were the country's territorial waters, less than 12 nautical miles from shore. The remaining four, all cargo vessels, were attacked off the Bulgarian coast, apparently all in the Bulgarian EEZ. The Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity (IMO 9545912) was struck, leaving 11 sailors missing. The Maltese-flagged Chelsea-3 (IMO 9361392) was hit three times by drones, and the Palau-flagged Able/AEL (IMO 9001136) was also struck. Syrian authorities have lodged strong protests over the loss of the fourth cargo vessel, the Togo-flagged Alpha Watan (IMO 7510884), concerned that the search for 10 missing crew members – nine Syrians and one Egyptian – was called off too soon. Under the terms of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), a coastal state has no security responsibility for the safe passage of a vessel through its EEZ; that responsibility falls instead to the flag state. Likewise, a coastal state is not legally obligated to defend a foreign-flag vessel passing through its territorial seas - but the coastal state exercises full sovereignty over its own waters within the 12-nautical-mile limit, so an attack is considered in the same light as an attack on the soil of the state. NATO has not made any substantive response to the situation and would not be expected to do so unless a member state requested aid or assistance. Hitherto, ships traveling between the Bosporus and Ukraine, if following the most direct course, have tended to pass through the Bulgarian EEZ and thence into Romanian territorial waters. But since the upsurge in attacks, more ships have taken a longer course, hugging the Bulgarian coast and traveling through Bulgarian territorial waters in hopes of reducing their risk.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: In the United States, there is a long-running popular television game show called "The Price Is Right." Contestants compete in a variety of games to determine the prices of products that they may win. The contestant whose bid is closest to the actual retail price of the product without going over wins. As far as I know, secondhand oil tankers have never featured in this game show, but if they did, contestants would have a very difficult time determining the correct price. Especially at the moment. Unlike newbuilding prices, which are primarily cost-driven, secondhand prices are intensely market-driven. And in the current freight market, which has reached extreme levels due to the various geopolitical conflicts around the world, secondhand prices have gone through the roof. We'll discuss some of these developments and their underlying drivers in more detail, focusing on VLCCs because this is the highest-profile tanker segment with the most extreme price movements. However, similar developments are taking place in the other tanker sectors. In a "normal" market, the cost of a newbuilding acts as the upper benchmark for the pricing of a secondhand vessel. However, a newbuilding ordered today will not be delivered until 2029 at the earliest. So, in the current freight market, in which VLCCs can earn in excess of $1 million per day (see Chart 1), there is an extreme "prompt delivery premium. Secondhand vessels, which can be employed immediately in the current (red-hot) market, are much more valuable than newbuildings, for which you have to wait three years. This is reflected in the current prices for secondhand tonnage (Chart 2). According to Poten's Marine Project Report, you can order a newbuilding VLCC (forward delivery) for $130 million. However, a prompt resale (delivery today) is valued at $235 million, an 82% premium. If that is too expensive, you can try to buy a 5-year-old VLCC for $210 million or a 10-year-old for $180 million. Even a 15-year-old VLCC is priced higher than a newbuilding contract. There are no bargains in this market. It is also important to note that the market for secondhand tonnage is very illiquid. While the shipping press is full of rumored transactions, relatively few deals are actually concluded because the bid-ask spread is so wide. Shipowners with tonnage on the water make so much money that they are reluctant to sell their ships, and with prices rising so much, so quickly, nobody wants to sell too soon. After all, prices may be higher tomorrow and, in the meantime, owners are collecting record earnings. One way to deal with that conundrum is to sell a ship forward, i.e., agree on a price now for delivery in six months. https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Brazil's Estaleiro Rio Grande has formally begun construction on a 13-vessel order placed by Transpetro, the logistics arm of Petrobras. Rio Grande Shipyard has benefited greatly from its 13-vessel order. The latest attacks on two Singapore-flagged container ships have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping through one of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/tra.text: Trade Data Was Built for Commercial Visibility Cargo manifests, customs declarations, shipping records, and import and export filings exist to describe commerce. They do that well. How much crude moved through Yanbu last month? Which companies are shipping dry bulk into Rotterdam? What do the dominant trade flows look like across the Red Sea corridor this quarter? These are real questions with real answers, and the platforms built to answer them serve commodity traders, banks, and supply chain managers properly. Enforcement Asks a Different Set of Questions Which of the 15,000 containers arriving at this port today holds something that was not declared? Which vessel took a detour through a sanctioned port before arriving here? Which manifest is fraudulent? Which operator has a behavioral history that signals concealment? Trade data does not answer any of these, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of coverage or refresh rate. Trade data is a record of what parties declared. The enforcement problem begins at the point where the declaration stops being true. AIS does not close the gap either. A vessel running dark produces no AIS record to check. A vessel broadcasting manipulated positions produces a record that is worse than nothing, because it looks complete. In both cases, the vessel most worth examining is the one generating the least usable data. That is the shape of the enforcement problem. The subject of the investigation controls the inputs.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/jap.text: Japan is set to provide protection and indemnity cover and partially compensate cargo and hull insurance payments for the transportation of crude oil, oil products and LNG, as part of a bill approved by the Cabinet on Oct. 13, a senior official at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry said. The bill is one of three approved by the Japanese Cabinet earlier Oct. 13 to enhance the security of the country’s crude oil supply, among others, amid the conflict in the Middle East. “The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism will revise the existing specified tanker act. The current law covers crude oil, and the scope will be expanded to include petroleum products such as naphtha, as well as liquefied natural gas,” the METI official told a press briefing. METI will also introduce similar support measures for hull insurance and cargo insurance, the official added. In response to the Middle East situation and to ensure a stable supply of energy to Japan, METI said the government will establish a program under which it will partially compensate non-life insurance companies for the funds required to pay insurance claims under marine property insurance, such as cargo and hull insurance, covering the transportation of crude oil, oil products and LNG, even in cases where the provision of reinsurance is prohibited. “In the event foreign insurance companies become unable to provide reinsurance coverage, a situation could arise where the cargo is available but cannot be transported,” the official said. “To address such circumstances, the government will establish a mechanism to fill the gap left by the unavailable foreign reinsurance coverage.”

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/bim.text: As whales migrate into critical habitats, many authorities are activating seasonal and dynamic measures that can affect how should ships transit certain areas. We recommend you check if any of your ships are travelling through areas with mandatory and voluntary whale strike reduction measures and if you can use any digital tools to help you navigate more efficiently in whale sensitive areas. Measures Every year, whales migrate between feeding, breeding and calving zones, often passing through some of the world’s busiest shipping routes. To reduce the risk of collisions, governments, ports and conservation initiatives have set up a range of seasonal, dynamic and location specific measures. These can include speed reductions, routing recommendations, reporting requirements and areas to be avoided. In Canada, extensive protection measures for North Atlantic right whales remain in force throughout the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. The voluntary Cabot Strait slowdown has resumed and will remain in place until 15 November. This initiative is for ships over 13 metres in length and Transport Canada is requesting a voluntary maximum speed of 10 knots over ground within the designated Cabot Strait slowdown zone. This is a very important region due to bottlenecks which make the whales more vulnerable. The Shediac Valley restricted area is no longer in effect. On the western coast of Canada, in the Admiralty Inlet and North Puget Sound, a voluntary ship slowdown project to protect southern resident killer whales requests all ships to reduce speeds to 10 knots and will run until 31 January. The Quiet Sound provides fleet operations managers regular updates on their fleet’s participation throughout the slowdown and after the slowdown has concluded. The Mediterranean Sea remains an area of interest to the shipping industry and the conservation community as the region supports important populations of fin whales and sperm whales. Recent discussions have highlighted concerns regarding the approval of the operation of very high-speed passenger services within the Pelagos Sanctuary and the North-West Mediterranean Particularly Sensitive Sea Area (PSSA) protected areas. While speed reduction remains one of the most effective measures for reducing both collision risk and the severity of strikes, stakeholders continue to debate how best to balance transport needs with whale conservation objectives. The Mediterranean also remains one of the regions with the highest reported risks of ship strikes for large whales globally, underlining the importance of proactive voyage planning and whale awareness.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Vídeos de segurança registraram a briga familiar que terminou na morte de Thiago de Mattos Teixeira no último sábado (17). O fato ocorreu em Campo Grande. Israel Nascimento, de 21 anos, é suspeito de atirar no tio após presenciar a mãe sendo agredida. O jovem fugiu. A defesa diz que Israel agiu para defender a mãe, enquanto a esposa de Thiago nega agressões. O corpo foi enterrado nesta segunda-feira (19).

A PF prendeu a mãe e o irmão do rapper Oruam nesta segunda-feira (19). A Operação Backbone combate o monopólio de internet do Comando Vermelho. Ao todo, foram expedidos 23 mandados de prisão preventiva e 24 de busca e apreensão. O STF também determinou o bloqueio de R$ 558 milhões. Segundo a PF, criminosos cortam cabos e incendeiam caixas de operadoras para forçar a contratação do serviço do tráfico. Provedores autorizados pagam taxas à facção. A cobrança de internet representou mais de 40% da arrecadação da facção no Complexo da Penha. Os investigados responderão por crimes como domínio social estruturado.

A Polícia Penal apreendeu maconha e haxixe em feijão e carne assada no Presídio Nelson Hungria, em Bangu. A apreensão ocorreu no último sábado (17). Ao todo, 2 visitantes foram presos em flagrante com mais de 1,2 mil invólucros das substâncias. Eles visitariam parentes na unidade. A ação integra a Operação Illicitus, que combate facções em presídios. Desde agosto, a iniciativa já apreendeu mais de 32 quilos de drogas e prendeu 20 visitantes.

Um entregador morreu e outro ficou ferido em tiroteio no Morro do Cajueiro, Zona Norte do Rio, neste sábado (17). O conflito ocorreu durante disputa entre facções criminosas. O ferido Luís Cláudio Galisa dos Santos, de 26 anos, foi baleado no tórax enquanto realizava entregas. Ele segue internado com quadro de saúde estável. A vítima fatal foi identificada como Wendel Silva da Rocha. A Polícia Militar reforçou o policiamento na região e o caso foi registrado na 29ª DP.

A Polícia Civil iniciou, nesta segunda-feira (19), uma operação para prender o bandido que atirou na arqueóloga Tania Andrade Lima, de 80 anos, durante assalto no Leblon. O crime ocorreu na quinta-feira (15), quando a vítima reagiu a um assalto após sacar dinheiro. Ela foi atingida por 3 disparos. A arqueóloga foi internada com ferimentos no pescoço, ombro e mão. Ela é professora aposentada da UFRJ e descobriu o Cais do Valongo em 2011.

Camilly Duarte de Jesus, foragida há mais de 2 anos por tortura, foi presa no domingo (18) em um velório no Cemitério do Caju. Segundo a denúncia, o crime ocorreu por uma dívida de R$ 30 mil. A vítima foi atraída, espancada com madeira e teve o cabelo raspado pela suspeita. O companheiro dela, André Luiz, também é acusado e continua foragido. A investigada publicava fotos de lazer nas redes sociais enquanto estava foragida.

Rio deve ter tempo fechado ao longo da semana — Foto: Adilson Coutinho/ TV Globo O Rio de Janeiro começa a semana com céu nublado e chuva. Nesta segunda-feira (19), o tempo permanece fechado, com possibilidade de chuva a qualquer momento do dia. O tempo deve seguir fechado ao longo dos dias.

O ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), autorizou a prisão domiciliar do policial civil Christiano Gaspar Fernandes, preso na oitava fase da Operação Unha e Carne, na última quinta-feira (15). A decisão foi proferida no último sábado (17).

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Analysts use the best available information to try to determine how effective the United States' blockade of Iranian shipping has been in putting pressure on Tehran. But inevitably, they do not have the complete picture, particularly when there is unadvertised activity cloaked in secrecy. The Maritime Executive has tried to estimate how effective the U.S. naval blockade has been, based on the curtailment of Iranian imports and exports through the Strait of Hormuz and on calculations of when Iranian oil stocks held afloat off China and Malaysia will run dry as a revenue source. Iranian oil exports, 90% of which previously went to China, are likely to run out imminently as the last stocks held afloat are drained, with the last revenues received before the end of the year. (Estimate based primarily on Kpler data) But even before the Iranian regime loses the last of its revenue from the sale of its dwindling stock of oil held afloat, Admiral Brad Cooper has said that Central Command has evidence that the cash shortage is now affecting salary and pension payments in Iran's energy, oil, manufacturing, construction, aviation, steel and automotive sectors. Somewhat surprisingly, Cooper claimed, it is also extending to salary payments due to members of the regular military and the IRGC. The Basij internal security forces form part of the IRGC command structure and are the muscle on the streets used to suppress protests and disorder. The inability to export directly impacts government revenues. But so do the asset freezes and sanctions on financial networks orchestrated by the U.S. Treasury under Operation Economic Fury. The lack of imports also has an impact, creating shortages and thus driving up prices. These factors hurt ordinary Iranians – but increasingly also the regime's core supporters. The pressures being felt by the Iranian economy are reflected in two particularly sensitive indicators of the linkage between Iran and the outside world: the exchange rate has reached 2,695,000 rials to the dollar despite intervention by the Central Bank of Iran, and inflation has reached 70%. Both the exchange rate and the inflation rate are at all-time records.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/o.text: The Omani government says that it will not extend the current Salalah port concession to a Maersk-linked operator beyond the current lease expiration date in November 2028. Following a series of negotiations, Salalah Port Services Company (SAOG) has announced that it has received a notification from the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT), confirming the end of the concession. Further, the notification indicated that the decision is final and unconditional. MTCIT emphasized that normal port operations will continue uninterrupted for the remaining period. The government is expected to announce a new operator in due course. SAOG is led by APM Terminals, part of A.P Moller-Maersk Group, which holds a 30% stake. The Omani government through the national logistics company Asyad Group holds 20%. SAOG was granted 30-year concessions to run the Container and General Cargo Terminals back in 1998. The company also signed separate management agreements with APM Terminals for technical and operational support for the duration of the concessions. While the SAOG board is reviewing the impact of the decision on its business, the company said that it was hoping for an extension based on its track record. In the first quarter of 2025, the company completed a $300 million container terminal upgrade. This included improvements to all six existing berths, a new access road, expansion of reefer plugs and an upgraded electrical power substation.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Australian authorities have arrested two Greenpeace activists who briefly boarded an offshore gas platform off the coast of Western Australia. On Saturday morning, a group of Greenpeace activists sailed out to the Scarborough gas floating production unit (FPU), about 125 nautical miles off the coast of Exmouth, Western Australia. They climbed aboard without authorization and suspended banners from the FPU's hull, signaling their opposition and forcing operator Woodside to temporarily suspend pre-commissioning operations on the platform. The activists brought hanging tents with them so that they could stay for an extended period, and two members of the group remained aboard overnight Saturday and into Sunday. On Monday, the Australian Border Force announced the conclusion of an operation for the "safe removal" of the two remaining activists. According to the ABF, the Western Australia Police and the National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority (NOPSEMA), the two men were removed without injury and relocated to Western Australia for detention. The two men, aged 48 and 52, have been charged with "interfering with offshore petroleum installations or operations." If convicted, they could spend up to 10 years in prison, the ABF said. "Offshore petroleum facilities operate in inherently complex and potentially hazardous environments. Unauthorised access is unlawful and can place both trespassers and workers at significant risk," said ABF in a statement.

https://g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/notici.text: Motoristas de ônibus que atuavam na antiga Transwolff iniciaram uma paralisação na manhã desta segunda-feira (19), afetando 267 mil passageiros na Zona Sul de São Paulo. Os trabalhadores protestam contra supostos problemas trabalhistas e cobram a regularização dos recolhimentos do Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço (FGTS) e do INSS, além de melhorias nos benefícios. A paralisação atinge as linhas do lote D10, operadas por ônibus azuis. Desde dezembro de 2025, os serviços estão sob responsabilidade da SPTrans, após a Prefeitura decretar a caducidade do contrato com a Transwolff. Segundo a Prefeitura, o Plano de Apoio entre Empresas em Situação de Emergência (Paese) foi acionado para atender 34 linhas afetadas pela paralisação. A administração municipal também solicitou reforço policial para duas garagens. O lote D11 opera normalmente. Na manhã desta segunda, trabalhadores se concentraram em frente a uma das garagens da antiga Transwolff para protestar contra o que classificam como condições precárias de trabalho. https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: A Quaest divulgará nesta quarta-feira (21) a próxima pesquisa de intenção de voto para o segundo turno presidencial de 2026. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e O Globo. Na rodada anterior, Flávio tinha 46% contra 44% de Lula, em empate técnico dentro da margem de erro. O Datafolha divulgará nova pesquisa contratada pela Folha de S.Paulo na quinta-feira (22). Na anterior, Flávio Bolsonaro tinha 47% contra 45% de Lula, também em empate na margem de erro. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543761-oc.text: Abu Dhabi-based Ocean Oilfield Integrated Solutions has completed the acquisition and taken ownership of the former Noble Resolve jack-up drilling rig, now renamed Ocean MVM, from Noble Corporation. The GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC jack-up arrived in Malta on October 13, 2026, and is being marketed for immediate deployment on offshore drilling campaigns worldwide, subject to contractual arrangements and operational requirements, Ocean Oilfield said in an October 15 announcement. The acquisition follows a definitive agreement announced by Noble Corporation in December 2025, under which Ocean Oilfield Drilling agreed to acquire the Noble Resolve in a $64 million cash transaction. The transaction was initially expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, following completion of the rig's existing contract. The jack-up is based on the GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC design, developed for offshore drilling operations in challenging environmental and severe weather conditions. "This strategic acquisition strengthens our fleet and represents a significant step forward in our continued growth. It reinforces our operational capabilities and enhances our ability to support clients across key global markets," said Sameer M, CEO of Ocean Oilfield.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543760-fu.text: EirGrid has completed its 2026 marine and coastal survey campaign for Ireland's Powering Up Offshore – South Coast program, with Fugro carrying out investigations to support the development of grid infrastructure for approximately 900 MW of offshore renewable energy. The campaign involved almost 70,000 hours of survey work across 2,337 kilometers of maritime area, gathering environmental, geophysical and geotechnical data to inform future offshore energy infrastructure, according to announcements from EirGrid and Fugro. The surveys will support engineering, environmental and planning assessments for infrastructure associated with the Tonn Nua maritime area under Ireland's South Coast Designated Maritime Area Plan for Offshore Renewable Energy (SC-DMAP). Fugro said it carried out the investigations alongside its partners, helping establish a detailed understanding of marine and coastal conditions needed for the next phase of development. EirGrid is continuing a 12-week public consultation, running until December 8, on emerging infrastructure options for connecting the Tonn Nua maritime area to the national electricity grid. The consultation covers potential landfall locations, offshore cable corridors, offshore substations, grid connection points and onshore transmission cable routes in Cork and Wexford.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543758-eq.text: Equinor and its partners in Norway's Troll field have decided to complete the Troll West Electrification (TWEL) project without installing a second electric export compressor on the Troll C platform, a move expected to make an additional 2.3 billion standard cubic meters of gas available to Europe in 2027 and 2028. The decision revises the project's original 2021 development plan and follows an assessment of the impact that further installation work would have on production at the offshore field. The Troll license partnership has informed Norway's Ministry of Energy that TWEL will be completed following the commissioning of the first electric export compressor on Troll C. According to Equinor, installing the second compressor would require extensive modifications that could reduce production from Troll C for up to 21 months. The company said the assessment had changed since the project's approval in 2021, when temporary production losses at Troll C could be offset by increased output from Troll A. However, Troll has been operating at maximum capacity throughout the year since 2023, increasing the importance of maintaining available compressor capacity at Troll C.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543754-ei.text: Norwegian offshore vessel owner Eidesvik Offshore has secured a contract extension from Equinor for its platform supply vessel (PSV) Viking Avant, keeping the vessel under contract until the end of 2027. The extension follows directly from the current contract and includes an option for a further extension, according to Eidesvik. "Viking Avant has served Equinor since delivery in 2004, and we are pleased to extend our collaboration on current market terms. The extension reflects the consistent performance of the vessel and her crew," said Helga Cotgrove, CEO of Eidesvik Offshore. Built in 2004, Viking Avant has a deadweight capacity of 5,784 tonnes and a deck area of 1,010 square meters.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543752-ve.text: Venezuela expects nearly $76 billion in oil investment over the next five years under recently signed agreements, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday, adding that a bilateral accord with the US includes plans to drill 250 rigs. Since the January ouster of President Nicolas Maduro, the country has been reopening its energy sector to foreign investment with the backing of the administration of US President Donald Trump. The deals could help revive output in Venezuela, which has the world's largest proven crude oil reserves but produces well below levels seen a decade ago. Rodriguez said on national television the investments would bring direct benefits to Venezuela while also benefiting its partners, adding that the bilateral agreement with the US covers 17 oil fields and formed part of a broader package of 61 agreements signed by the parties. "Major investments are coming," she said. "We are talking about investment of almost $76 billion over five years. Those investments will translate into direct benefits for our country in a win-win partnership, because our partner will also benefit." There, production rose from 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 370,000 bpd, she said, adding it was expected to reach 400,000 bpd by the end of the year. She did not say over what period the increase occurred.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543753-gr.text: Woodside Energy has suspended pre-commissioning activities at its Scarborough gas project's floating production unit (FPU) offshore Western Australia following a Greenpeace protest that saw two activists occupy the facility for two days before being taken into police custody. Woodside suspended pre-commissioning work at the Scarborough FPU on Saturday following the activists' unauthorized entry, with operations still on hold as of Sunday, according to media reports citing a company spokesperson. The activists from Greenpeace Australia Pacific climbed onto the FPU, located more than 200 kilometers off the coast of Exmouth, at approximately 5:45 a.m. local time on Saturday, October 17. Using specialized climbing equipment, they attached themselves to the offshore facility and displayed banners reading "Stop Woodside's Dirty Gas. Save Scott Reef." The protest targeted Woodside's proposed Browse gas development at Scott Reef, rather than the Scarborough project itself. Specialist police personnel arrived at the Scarborough FPU by helicopter at approximately 11:30 a.m. on Sunday, according to Greenpeace.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543759-v-.text: Vår Energi and Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery at the Lakris prospect in the Norwegian Sea, with preliminary estimates indicating recoverable resources of between 1.3 million and 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe). The discovery was made in wildcat well 6407/5-3 S in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace, approximately 170 kilometers northwest of Kristiansund. The well was drilled by COSL's COSLProspector semi-submersible rig in production license 1002, operated by Vår Energi with a 42.3% working interest. Equinor holds the remaining 57.7%. According to the preliminary assessment, the discovery contains between 0.2 million and 0.9 million standard cubic meters of recoverable oil equivalent. The well was drilled to a measured depth of 2,986 meters and a vertical depth of 2,793 meters below sea level, terminating in the Lower Triassic Klappmyss Formation. Water depth at the drilling location is 406 meters. The well has been permanently plugged and abandoned following completion of drilling operations.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543751-se.text: Britain's Serica Energy flagged a further delay to the restart of its Triton production vessel on Monday, prompting the oil and gas firm to lower its annual production forecast. Triton production is expected to resume around the end of November. The planned maintenance began at the end of July and was set to end in about two months Serica expects 2026 production to average just below 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), compared with its previous forecast of above that level The company expects production rates of around 65,000 boepd by the end of the year once production resumes at Triton It reaffirmed its annual post-tax cash flow from operations and capital expenditure guidance, strengthened by current gas prices and expansion in the North Sea The company, which recently walked away from an offer for rival Pharos Energy PHARP.L, continues to look for merger and acquisition opportunities in the UK North Sea and overseas

https://www.rigzone.com/news/what_will_h.text: Analysts at BMI and Standard Chartered have outlined their thoughts on where the commodity is heading in the not-too-distant future in separate reports sent to Rigzone recently. In a BMI report sent to Rigzone by the Fitch Group on Friday, analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, highlighted that they had made a “significant upward revision” to their Brent forecast and now expect Brent futures to average $93 per barrel in 2026, up from $83 per barrel previously, and $81 per barrel in 2027, up from $71 per barrel previously. “This assumes growing, if fluctuating, price pressures over the coming three-to-six months, with Brent rising to an average of $107 per barrel in Q4 2026 and $112 per barrel in Q1 2027, up from $91 per barrel in Q3,” the analysts stated in the report. The analysts noted in the report that their price forecast revision principally reflects their evolving view of the U.S.-Iran war. “Whereas we had previously expected a preliminary agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in 2026, we now believe that a deal is unlikely before Q1 2027,” they revealed. “This has seen Brent remain under pressure heading into the fourth quarter, with Brent futures closing at $106.1 per barrel on October 14, significantly above the year-to-date average of $89 per barrel,” they pointed out.

https://safety4sea.com/xeneta-red-sea-re.text: Container shipping capacity scheduled to transit the Red Sea has doubled in six weeks, signaling an accelerating return to the region that could reshape global freight rates and services heading into 2027, according to Xeneta. O n 5 October, weekly scheduled capacity crossing Bab el-Mandeb in at least one direction reached 448,273 TEU, up from the levels recorded on 27 August. However, this remains 48% of the 930,679 TEU offered in August 2023, before vessels began diverting around the Cape of Good Hope. As explained by Emily Stausbøll, Xeneta Senior Shipping Analyst, the accelerated return could release capacity back into the global fleet, with potentially significant implications for freight rates and shipping services. While October is a typical period for volumes to ease following peak season, existing congestion across global ocean networks could absorb some of the released capacity in the short term. Stausbøll noted that carriers have not publicly explained what changes in their security assessments have supported the faster return to the Red Sea. She stressed that shippers should closely monitor developments, as the shift is likely to be one of the factors shaping the container shipping market in 2027. Spot rates from the Far East to the US remained broadly stable over the past month, but downward pressure is expected to intensify following the Golden Week period in China and as October progresses. Carriers are responding by withdrawing capacity from transpacific services. During the week covered by the update, 58,200 TEU was blanked on the Far East to US West Coast trade, while 35,500 TEU was removed from Far East to US East Coast services.

https://safety4sea.com/four-vessels-free.text: The European Union Naval Force (EUNAVFOR) Operation ATALANTA has closed four piracy cases involving vessels off the northern coast of Somalia, while the motor tanker Asana remains under the control of pirates in Somali territorial waters, according to an update issued on 16 October 2026. T he closed cases involve the motor tankers Honour 25, Eureka and Sibu 1, as well as the merchant vessel Sward. The incidents occurred between April and August 2026, with Operation ATALANTA coordinating with relevant authorities and companies to support the release of the vessels and their crews. Throughout the incidents, ATALANTA also issued maritime security warnings through the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean (MSCIO) to vessels sailing in the affected areas. The Honour 25 incident followed the hijacking of fishing vessel Alkhary 2 on 20 April. On 21 April, ATALANTA reported that Honour 25 had also been hijacked, with its last known position 28 nautical miles southeast of Alkhary 2. The fishing vessel was subsequently released with all crew members safe, while the pirate group remained aboard the tanker. On 29 September, Puntland Maritime Police Forces (PMPF) launched an operation to free Honour 25. Five crew members were killed and two were injured during the counter-piracy operation, according to official sources. The injured crew members disembarked at Bander Beyla on 30 September, while the remaining crew members were taken ashore in Bosaso on 4 October. ATALANTA’s flagship moved into the area to stand by to provide medical assistance and evacuate crew members if required.

https://safety4sea.com/fire-breaks-out-a.text: A fire broke out in the engine room of the Indonesia-flagged bulk carrier Prima Sentosa off the western coast of Sumatra on 16 October, forcing all 26 crew members to abandon the vessel. A ll crew were subsequently rescued in an operation involving Indonesia’s National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) and a nearby tanker. The fire reportedly started at around 7 pm local time, prompting the crew to evacuate the vessel. Basarnas received a distress call at approximately 8 pm and deployed a search and rescue (SAR) team, which arrived at the scene at around 2 am. All 26 crew members rescued Thirteen crew members managed to escape aboard a liferaft and were picked up by the passing tanker Seroja XX. The remaining 13 were located near Prima Sentosa and subsequently rescued by the SAR team, according to Basarnas. The 26 crew members, comprising 23 Indonesian nationals and three foreign nationals, were transported to Pulau Baai Port in Bengkulu for medical examinations. The incident once again highlights the importance of effective emergency preparedness and crew evacuation procedures, particularly when an engine-room fire threatens a vessel’s ability to operate safely.

https://safety4sea.com/britannia-pi-club.text: Life at sea offers seafarers a rewarding and often exhilarating career, but spending months away from home can also take an emotional toll. Long periods of separation from family and friends, combined with the isolation of life on board, can make homesickness a significant challenge. W hile returning home may seem like the obvious remedy, seafarers do not always have that option during long voyages. Britannia P&I Club highlights homesickness as a common experience among seafarers, with potential consequences for their mental well-being and life on board. Homesickness is a natural response to being separated from familiar surroundings and loved ones. For seafarers, however, the demands of life at sea can intensify these feelings in several ways. Isolation is one of the main contributing factors. Extended periods at sea can limit opportunities for social interaction outside the vessel, making it more difficult for seafarers to maintain their usual social connections and cope with feelings of loneliness. Separation from family and friends can also be particularly difficult. Although many people can manage short periods away from home, prolonged absences mean seafarers may miss birthdays, family gatherings and other important milestones in the lives of their loved ones. In addition, cultural differences and unfamiliar environments can add to the emotional strain. Adapting to different customs and social norms may be challenging, particularly when seafarers are already struggling with the distance from home.

https://safety4sea.com/uk-chamber-calls-.text: The UK Chamber of Shipping has called on the UK Government to ensure that a future maritime fuel standard is backed by reliable reporting systems, clear compliance rules and sufficient availability of low-carbon fuels, warning that regulatory complexity could increase costs and undermine shipping’s competitiveness. I n a new paper, Designing a Workable UK Maritime Fuel Standard: Lessons from the implementation of FuelEU Maritime , the industry body draws on the challenges encountered during the implementation of the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regulation, which entered into force on 1 January 2025. It argues that the UK has an opportunity to learn from the European experience before developing its own framework. The paper comes as the UK Government prepares to develop a domestic fuel standard as part of its wider maritime decarbonisation strategy, with a consultation expected in late 2026. The proposed framework is intended to encourage the uptake of lower- and zero-emission fuels, but the Chamber says its effectiveness will depend on how the rules are designed and implemented. The Chamber’s central message is that ambitious emissions targets must be matched by practical arrangements that allow shipowners, operators, fuel suppliers and verifiers to comply without unnecessary administrative burdens. Its assessment of FuelEU Maritime identifies several implementation difficulties, including complex reporting requirements, limited preparation time, evolving guidance and inconsistencies in how compliance calculations have been interpreted. In some cases, operators acting in good faith encountered difficulties meeting deadlines because procedures and supporting systems were not sufficiently clear or mature.

https://safety4sea.com/maersk-completes-.text: A.P. Moller–Maersk has completed its first ethanol bunkering operation on a retrofitted dual-fuel vessel, with Maersk Halifax receiving approximately 5,000 metric tonnes of ISCC-certified bioethanol in Singapore. T he operation, announced on 17 October, marks a new milestone in the efforts to explore alternative marine fuels and assess their potential role in reducing emissions from ocean transport. Conducted in collaboration with the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and other industry partners, the operation also provided an opportunity to evaluate the practical requirements of ethanol bunkering, including fuel sourcing, supply chain readiness, infrastructure and onboard operations. The operation took place alongside live cargo operations at PSA Singapore’s Pasir Panjang Terminal, under a simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) arrangement. Golden Island Pte Ltd supplied the fuel using a mass flow meter, marking Singapore’s first ethanol bunkering operation. Safety preparations included a hazard identification and hazard and operability study (HAZID/HAZOP) workshop involving the participating parties. The MPA also worked with stakeholders to ensure crew members received training in handling ethanol as a marine fuel and responding to potential emergencies, drawing on experience gained from methanol bunkering. The operation is expected to provide practical insights into how Singapore’s existing methanol bunkering experience and infrastructure could support the introduction of other alternative fuels. “This operation allows us to test how Singapore’s experience and existing infrastructure for methanol bunkering can support another emerging marine fuel,” said Ang Wee Keong, Chief Executive of the MPA. He added that the findings would help inform the development of standards and procedures for safe and efficient ethanol bunkering as Singapore prepares for a multi-fuel future.

https://safety4sea.com/imo-nzf-could-unl.text: The International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) Net Zero Framework (NZF) could help unlock investment in renewable electricity and support the electrification of shipping, according to a new report from the UCL Energy Institute’s Shipping and Oceans Research Group. T he report, Electrification investment from IMO’s Net Zero Framework: A case study on Grand Inga hydropower project , examines the potential for shore power in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and green ammonia production using electricity from the proposed Grand Inga hydropower project. Its findings indicate that the IMO framework could improve the economic case for electrification and help advance wider investment in renewable energy infrastructure. The study estimates that shore power at the DRC ports of Banana, Boma and Matadi could meet an annual electricity demand of approximately 20.99 GWh, based on 2018 vessel-call data. This could displace around 4,975 tonnes of heavy fuel oil (HFO) or 4,704 tonnes of marine gas oil (MGO), avoiding approximately 18,600 tonnes of CO₂-equivalent emissions annually on a well-to-wake basis. The report identifies shore power, also known as cold ironing, as a potentially cost-effective way for ships to reduce emissions while at berth and comply with the IMO NZF. However, the estimated electricity demand would account for less than 1% of the output of a fully developed Grand Inga project. While shore power alone would therefore be unlikely to provide a major anchor load for a project of this scale, it could support smaller renewable energy projects and investment in grid infrastructure.

https://safety4sea.com/watch-ship-retrof.text: Retrofitting existing vessels is emerging as a practical pathway for the maritime industry to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, improve energy efficiency and meet evolving environmental regulations, according to Lloyd’s Register (LR). A s shipowners and operators face growing pressure to decarbonise their fleets, upgrading existing vessels with energy-saving technologies and alternative fuel systems can help improve operational performance while reducing fuel consumption and emissions. LR highlights several retrofit options, including alternative fuel systems, wind-assisted propulsion, hull improvements, advanced propellers and carbon capture solutions, as ways to support maritime decarbonisation. Carbon capture can reduce emissions from vessels already in service by capturing CO2 from exhaust gases, while engine retrofits can enable ships to adopt alternative fuels and lower-carbon operations, LR notes in the video. The most suitable approach depends on fleet readiness, fuel availability, technology maturity and evolving regulations. In addition, hull optimisation is an established method of improving vessel efficiency by reducing resistance through the water, lowering fuel consumption throughout a ship’s operational life. Advances in propeller design can also deliver fuel savings while supporting compliance with international regulations. With much of the global fleet expected to remain in service well into the next decade, retrofit projects will play a critical role in shipping’s decarbonisation journey. The challenge is no longer identifying technologies, but understanding how those technologies can be safely, practically and economically integrated into existing ships while meeting increasingly demanding regulatory requirements

https://safety4sea.com/abs-annual-psc-re.text: Fire safety, International Safety Management (ISM) implementation and lifesaving appliance readiness remained among the main drivers of port State control (PSC) detentions in 2025, according to an analysis by the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS). T he findings of the Annual Port State Control Report by ABS highlight persistent weaknesses in onboard maintenance, corrective action follow-up, safety management systems and crew preparedness across the Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU and US Coast Guard (USCG) inspection regimes. In the Paris and Tokyo MoU regimes, inspections involving ABS-classed vessels and/or vessels for which ABS acted as a recognized organization (RO) totalled 6,812 in 2025. Of these, 3,070, or 45%, were completed without deficiencies. Across the ABS-related dataset, inspectors recorded 1,731 deficiencies and 565 detainable deficiencies, resulting in 150 detentions. ABS identified fire safety as the largest category of detainable deficiencies, accounting for 149 findings, followed by ISM with 69, lifesaving appliances with 59, emergency systems with 44, and safety of navigation with 39. The analysis found that detention exposure remained concentrated in recurring operational risk areas rather than emerging from a substantially new set of PSC concerns. Similar patterns were observed in 2023 and 2024, suggesting that maintenance discipline, system readiness and effective implementation of safety procedures remain critical to inspection outcomes. ISM was the most frequently recorded individual detainable deficiency in 2025, with 51 findings. Other leading deficiencies included fixed fire-extinguishing installations (25), fire doors and openings in fire-resisting divisions (19), lifeboats (17), and fire dampers (14).

https://www.marinelink.com/news/two-oil-.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Saturday that two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported. State media said both tankers were carrying about 2 million barrels of crude oil. IRNA reported that the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and attempted to use an unauthorised route through the strategic waterway. The second vessel was left immobilised after striking a mine, it added. State media earlier reported that the other tanker had also struck a mine while attempting to transit the strait via a route not authorised by Iran. The incidents come amid heightened tensions around the strait, a key oil shipping route. Disruptions to shipping in the waterway due to the US-Israeli war on Iran have boosted global energy prices and inflation. Maritime officials said on Wednesday that a container ship and a dry bulk carrier sank near the strait after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents.
