https://gcaptain.com/qatar-lng-cargo-mak.text: Oct 19, 2026, (Bloomberg) –A carrier loaded with Qatari liquefied natural gas is sailing north through the Red Sea, potentially speeding up delivery to European customers with a rare transit through waters vulnerable to renewed attacks from Houthi rebels. The tanker, which loaded an LNG cargo in Qatar in August, is signaling Poland as its next destination, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Poland’s Orlen SA has a long-term supply contract with QatarEnergy, though shipments under the deal were canceled after the exporter’s giant Ras Laffan plant was hit by drone strikes in March. The transit — which comes as European natural gas prices hit the highest level in almost four years — is unusual. Commercial vessels have increasingly tended to take long detours to avoid the Red Sea, typically sailing around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope to head to Europe, a route that can add almost two weeks and extra costs to a one-way journey. UK Maritime Trade Operations, a security outfit which links commercial shipping and military forces, reported on Saturday that an unnamed LNG tanker was approached southeast of the Yemeni port of Al Mukalla, in the Gulf of Aden, by a skiff that fired two shots. The tanker’s security team fired two shots in return. UKMTO did not provide further details, though ship-tracking data suggest the Poland-bound carrier was the only LNG tanker in the region at the time. The data suggests the vessel has since continued its journey. Continued disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has tightened global LNG supply for months, driving up prices and forcing Middle Eastern suppliers to look for workarounds.

https://splash247.com/hormuz-attacks-ove.text: The sheer volume of attacks on commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz has left Britain’s maritime security reporting centre struggling to keep track, with most vessels targeted in the increasingly dangerous waterway no longer reporting incidents directly. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) admitted in its latest weekly assessment that it is “struggling to accurately report true number of attacks”, warning that the majority of vessels attacked are refusing to report incidents. The organisation said it was aware of further attacks through other sources but could not include them in its figures without verification UKMTO has recorded 135 incidents related to the Iran-US conflict since hostilities began on February 28, including 114 reports of vessel damage and 76 people killed or injured. Twelve attacks were recorded in its latest weekly assessment, ten in Hormuz itself, one in the Arabian Gulf and another in the Gulf of Oman. Of the vessels involved, one was lost, two were disabled and three had unconfirmed outcomes. The violence has continued through the weekend, with attacks spreading well beyond the narrow confines of Hormuz. On Friday, the 302,977 dwt VLCC ST3 was struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 68 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia. The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker suffered an engine room fire and lost power, according to maritime security firm Vanguard. All 15 Indian seafarers aboard were safely evacuated to a nearby UAE-flagged containership. Later on Friday, another tanker was attacked approximately 78 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubail, this time by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat. The projectile damaged the vessel’s aft port quarter. All crewmembers were reported safe, although the full extent of the damage remains unclear.

https://splash247.com/norway-ends-one-of.text: Norway’s protracted offshore well services wage dispute has been settled through voluntary arbitration, even as a separate labour conflict has triggered a strike at subsea contractor Reach Subsea. An arbitration panel has ruled that wage and other provisions previously agreed under the Oil Services Agreement between employers’ organisation Offshore Norge and trade union Styrke will also apply to the Well Services Agreement between Offshore Norge and SAFE. The decision ends a dispute that sparked a month-long strike and lockout over the summer before the parties agreed on July 14 to refer the matter to arbitration. The ruling covers changes to wage rates and union funds, with the new terms taking effect retrospectively from July 14 and remaining in force until May 31, 2028. SAFE expressed disappointment that the panel rejected its demand to maintain a separate agreement for members employed by SLB. However, the union welcomed the decision to backdate wage adjustments and other payments rather than apply them only from the date of the ruling. Despite the settlement, industrial unrest continues elsewhere in Norway’s offshore services sector.

https://petronoticias.com.br/john-crane-.text: Com a perspectiva de novos investimentos em óleo e gás nos próximos cinco anos, a John Crane vê o Brasil como um dos mercados estratégicos para sua expansão global, impulsionado pela entrada das novas plataformas offshore no país, pela continuidade das atividades no Pré-Sal e pelas oportunidades na Margem Equatorial. Em entrevista ao Petronotícias, Rogério Quirino , gerente regional da John Crane, e Julian Diosa , diretor de vendas para a América Latina, destacaram as novas tecnologias da companhia, como o Selo Coaxial de Separação, que reduz em até 80% o consumo de nitrogênio, e as soluções de monitoramento de equipamentos críticos. Os executivos também ressaltaram o investimento da empresa em serviços especializados no Brasil e o potencial de crescimento nos segmentos offshore e onshore, incluindo projetos de expansão do refino. Rogério Quirino: Um dos principais destaques é o Selo Coaxial de Separação. Trata-se de uma tecnologia voltada para equipamentos que operam com sistemas críticos de selagem a gás. Em comparação com a tecnologia anterior, ela proporciona uma redução de até 80% no consumo de nitrogênio, além de proteger o sistema contra contaminações. Poderia detalhar o tipo de aplicação dessa tecnologia do Selo Coaxial? Onde ela é aplicada no setor onshore e offshore? Rogério Quirino: Ela possui aplicações tanto onshore quanto offshore. No segmento offshore, especificamente nas plataformas, praticamente todos os equipamentos voltados para a parte de compressão no topside podem utilizar esse tipo de tecnologia. É uma solução versátil, aplicável desde compressores centrífugos até compressores tipo parafuso, entre outros modelos. Como a John Crane atua na entrega de soluções de serviços e na extensão da vida útil dos equipamentos? Rogério Quirino: A John Crane possui uma atuação muito forte que vai além da entrega do produto em si; nós focamos na solução completa de serviço. Quando falamos em recuperação, não nos limitamos apenas a reparar o selo. Nós entregamos uma solução que engloba a análise de causa raiz, identificando o que está ocorrendo para que o equipamento consiga atingir seu desempenho máximo e estender sua vida útil nas operações de campo dos nossos clientes.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Rand released a report earlier this month entitled “Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment in the Coast Guard.” The report was mandated by the Fiscal Year 2024 Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, which directed the Secretary of Homeland Security to charter an independent and impartial review of the service’s efforts to reduce and respond to sexual assault and sexual harassment. Additionally, Congress directed that the review evaluate past and present climate and culture, preventative measures, accountability, transparency, victim support, and awareness; identify and evaluate completed and ongoing efforts and reforms undertaken to improve these areas; and make recommendations for additional efforts and reforms that should be undertaken to close remaining gaps. RAND researchers found a SASH policy environment characterized by distributed authority without centralized integration. Although individual programs address distinct forms of harm, the absence of a unifying framework limits the Coast Guard’s ability to monitor implementation, assess outcomes across programs, and ensure consistent experiences for victims and practitioners. They examined how these structural features influence prevention effectiveness, response quality, and accountability in practice. The RAND report noted that slow case timelines and limited transparency erodes trust. One of the Special Victims Counsel who spoke with researchers shared: "The biggest issue my clients face is that they make the decision to come forward and report, and then they’re stuck in limbo for a very long time. That uncertainty and feeling of powerlessness, because someone else is making a decision, eats away at them. They just want a decision made one way or another to get closure from these events. The lengthy time for prosecution in the Coast Guard negatively impacts victims." - The Coast Guard’s SASH efforts are constrained less by an absence of programs than by how those programs are structured, integrated, and resourced.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Ukraine’s Security Service and Prosecutor General’s Office reported they are proceeding with the case against a Russian captain accused of controlling a ship transporting stolen grain from Crimea. The captain was charged in absentia, with media reports noting it is the first time Ukraine has charged a captain with a war crime for their role in the export of grain. Several similar cases have been filed, and Ukraine has even seized a few smaller cargo ships on charges of entering the closed ports of occupied Crimea or transporting grain and other materials out of the region. Last month, they reported an investigation into the cargo ship Matros Pozynich (IMO 9573816) and the master, Mykola Telagin, age 54, a Russian citizen, who, it says, was controlling the vessel. “According to the investigation, the grain export was carried out by the decision of the top political leadership of the aggressor country. Such actions violate the Geneva Conventions, which prohibit the theft of property in occupied territories,” said the SBU. They said the investigation confirmed that the vessel, which is owned by a Russian company, had transported more than 54,000 tons of grain that they assert was taken from Ukrainian farmers. One shipment of over 27,000 tons was transported in November 2022, and the second load consisting of 27,300 tons was transported in January 2023. Both shipments were taken out of Crimea and delivered to Latakia in Syria. The SBU says the investigation indicated that the captain periodically turned off the AIS transmission system and transmitted inaccurate information about the vessel’s location. They assert the wheat was presented as if it had come from Russia. Investigators of the Security Service informed the captain in absentia of the charges on suspicion of a violation of the laws and customs of war and violation of the procedure for entering and leaving the temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine with the aim of causing harm to the interests of the state, committed by an organized group.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: German arms manufacturer Rheinmetall confirmed that it plans to acquire the Mangalia shipyard in Romania together with MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company. It reports the yard, which was once one of the largest shipbuilders in Europe, will serve roles for both civil and military shipbuilding. The court-appointed administrator for the shipyard confirmed 10 days ago that Rheinmetall had won the bidding in the fifth court-ordered auction for the yard. It placed a successful bid of €134 million ($154 million), promising to revitalize the yard’s operations. The yard had been driven into bankruptcy and administration after a dispute emerged between Damen and the Romanian government following legislative changes to how private partnerships were managed in the country. Damen was the largest creditor of the yard. Today’s announcement was the first confirmation that MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company had joined with Rheinmetall in the bid and would take ownership of a portion of the yard. Rheinmetall says the site, which is located south of Constanta, will be subdivided, but provided no details on how the operation would be managed. MSC had first been linked to the yard as a possible buyer in June 2025. Media reports said MSC had told the government of Romania it intends to consider the shipyard for the future construction of cruise ships, ro-pax, and tugboats. The company also said it was willing to pay in advance for ship repair work to provide the yard funds for hiring back employees. MSC has not publicly confirmed its role in the acquisition or its plans for the yard either as a repair facility or for new construction. Rheinmetall had said in May that it was exploring sharing the ownership with MSC. Rheinmetall says it will use the yard for an important role in the building of four naval vessels that have been commissioned by the Romanian government. The German company won the order, reportedly valued at €920 million in May 2026, promising a local component to the work. The contract calls for the construction of two 96-meter offshore patrol vessels as well as two 43-meter diver support vessels. The company says it plans to expand and upgrade the shipyard. They report that they intend for the Mangalia shipyard to serve as a hub for further military shipbuilding projects. They expect the deal to acquire Mangalia to be finalized in a few weeks.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/v.text: Passengers starting a week-long cruise aboard the cruise ship AIDAnova got to witness a rescue operation on Sunday afternoon, October 18. The German cruise ship was making its way from Kiel, Germany, to Norway when it was alerted to reports of smoke and then flames coming from a fishing vessel in the Skagerrak between Norway and Denmark. Norway’s Southern rescue force dispatched a helicopter to the scene and put out a call for vessels in the area to respond. The 183,858 gross ton cruise ship, which carries more than 5,200 passengers, was on the first day of a cruise from Germany to Bergen, Geiranger, Alesund, and Stavanger, Norway. The Color Line SuperSpeed 1 ferry heading toward Kristiansand, Norway, also changed course to standby. Passengers aboard the cruise posted videos and pictures of flames and smoke coming from the fishing boat as their ship was positioned nearby. It put down one of its fast launches, and the crew made their way to the burning boat. The four people aboard the fishing boat had already abandoned their ship and were in a liferaft. Danish authorities also placed a helicopter on standby to assist with the operation. They reported the unnamed fishing boat was registered in Denmark. The four people from the fishing boat were taken aboard the cruise ship and reported to be uninjured. After the rescue, the cruise ship resumed its trip to Norway with the four survivors aboard. There was no word as to what caused the fire aboard the fishing vessel.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: Merchant ships face serious risk of attack in and around the Strait of Hormuz, and not just tankers, bulkers and boxships. On Sunday, a tug was attacked and hit at a position to the east of the Musandam Peninsula, near the seaward entrance to the strait. The tug was moving southbound parallel to the peninsula when it was struck by two unknown projectiles, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). One crewmember suffered minor injuries. The vessel was able to continue its voyage despite damage. Vanguard Tech has identified the vessel in question as the Dutch-flagged tug JIF Barracuda (IMO: 9345506, ex name Smit Barracuda ). The vessel's AIS signal was last detected on the 17th, under way off Ras Al-Khaiman and headed in the direction of the strait's western entrance. The attack's location on the east side of the strait - about 20 nautical miles to the northeast of Khor Fakkan - is situated far from most of the recent kinetic activity associated with the Iranian campaign against GCC-linked shipping, but not all. In recent weeks, suspected Iranian attacks have been reported as far west as Qatar and Al Jubayl. On Friday, the master of a tanker reported that his ship was approached by unknown assailants in a small boat off Al Jubayl in the central Arabian Gulf. The occupants of the boat launched an RPG at the ship, damaging the port quarter. No harm to the crew was reported. The fast pace of Iranian attacks has not deterred tanker operators from moving crude through the waterway, despite the risks to their vessels and crewmembers. Analyst Tom Bike identified 11 vessels on the "Hormuz Shuttle" route in broad daylight satellite imaging on October 19, suggesting that the oil is still flowing out of the Gulf.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: The rescue of the crew from a burning containership took a tragic turn, according to reports from the Portuguese authorities. While the crew of the Singapore-registered containership Espirito Santo Express was safely recovered, the chief officer from the rescue ship, the Portuguese-flagged bulker Aeolian Arrow , was tragically lost as the rescue operation was being completed. A possible explosion followed by a fire aboard the 132,789 dwt containership was reported on October 15 in a location approximately 1,700 kilometers (1,056 miles) east of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, according to the Brazilian newspaper Reconecta. Tracking data shows the vessel was in a remote location midway between Rio de Janeiro and Tristan da Cunha, far from shore in the middle of the South Atlantic. The containership, which was built in 2018, has a capacity of 11,800 TEU and is managed by Seaspan. It had left Singapore on September 25, rounded the Cape of Good Hope on October 10, and slowed and then disappeared from AIS overnight on October 15. Tristan da Cunha has no airfield, but the Brazilian Air Force dispatched a radar-equipped Embraer KC-390 transport aircraft from Rio de Janeiro to overfly the rescue effort, one of few aircraft with the speed to get to the area quickly and with the necessary range to loiter in the rescue area. The Brazilian authorities issued NAVAREA V Warning 0648/26 covering the incident and coordinated the response. The bulker Aeolian Arrow responded to the distress call, and the situation was being managed by the MRCC Rio de Janeiro. According to the details released by Portugal’s Maritime Accident Investigation Office (GAMA), the bulker was able to rescue the 28 crewmembers from the containership. They had abandoned the vessel with 19 crewmembers in a lifeboat and nine in a life raft in difficult conditions with very high seas. The swell and current caused the rescue boat to move abruptly, GAMA reports. The chief officer of the Aeolian Arrow was thrown overboard from the rescue boat, and the rescue boat was subsequently swamped and lost. The chief officer was conscious after he fell into the water, and the crew of the bulker attempted to recover him. They used lifebuoys and a cargo net in an attempt to bring the chief officer aboard. The reports said the chief officer repeatedly lost the ability to hold onto the rescue equipment. He subsequently disappeared beneath the surface and could not be recovered.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O grupo Magalu anunciou uma parceria com a Shopee para vender seus produtos no marketplace. Com a novidade, a plataforma da Shopee vai passar a contar com eletroeletrônicos, eletroeletrônicos e móveis vendidos pelo grupo. A Magalu também vai participar das campanhas promocionais do marketplace, como 11.11 e Black Friday, com ofertas e benefícios para consumidores como cupons de desconto e frete grátis. Queremos transformar essa audiência adicional da Shopee em crescimento sustentável para o Magalu e para as marcas do nosso ecossistema", afirmou Fabrício Garcia, vice-presidente comercial e de operações do Magalu. A parceria acompanha o movimento de outras marcas do comércio eletrônico, como as Casas Bahia , que disponibilizaram seus produtos nas plataformas Amazon, Mercado Livre e Shopee. Esse modelo de parceria também viabiliza o acesso a soluções de social commerce da plataforma, como Shopee Lives, Shopee Vídeos e do alcance de mais de 10 milhões de criadores e afiliados no Brasil.

A redução da jornada semanal de trabalho de 44 para 40 horas, sem diminuição salarial, pode elevar os custos operacionais das transportadoras e exigir mudanças na organização das equipes. Estudo do Instituto Paulista do Transporte de Cargas (IPTC), realizado a pedido do Sindicato das Empresas de Transportes de Carga de São Paulo e Região (SETCESP), estima aumento de 10% no custo da hora trabalhada com a mudança. A entidade alerta para possíveis reflexos na formação do preço do frete. Para dimensionar o impacto, o IPTC simulou os custos de uma transportadora com 50 motoristas e 20 colaboradores operacionais. Em um cenário hipotético de aumento de 12% nas despesas com pessoal, considerando horas extras e ajustes para manter o mesmo volume de operação, o custo mensal da equipe passaria de R$ 372,3 mil para R$ 416,9 mil. A diferença representa aproximadamente R$ 536 mil por ano. Segundo o instituto, os valores são ilustrativos, e o impacto efetivo dependerá das características de cada operação. A mudança na jornada exigirá a revisão de escalas e da distribuição das horas de trabalho, especialmente nas operações de longa distância, que dependem do cumprimento de prazos e da continuidade dos serviços. De acordo com o SETCESP, a redução das horas disponíveis por trabalhador poderá levar à ampliação das equipes ou ao aumento do recurso a horas extras, em um setor que já enfrenta dificuldades para contratar e qualificar motoristas. “A redução da jornada vai impactar diretamente os custos e a organização das transportadoras. Estamos falando de um setor que precisa garantir entregas, cumprir prazos e manter o abastecimento. Com menos horas disponíveis por trabalhador, as empresas terão que reorganizar suas equipes e, em muitos casos, ampliar as contratações ou recorrer a horas extras. Isso vai pressionar os custos operacionais e terá reflexos na formação do preço do frete”, afirma Marcelo Rodrigues, presidente do SETCESP. A análise jurídica do sindicato aponta que a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 221/2019 não prevê tratamento diferenciado automático para transportadoras ou motoristas profissionais. A aplicação das novas regras precisará ser compatibilizada com a Lei 13.103/2015, conhecida como Lei do Motorista, e com as decisões do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) sobre jornadas, intervalos e repousos. A negociação coletiva continuará tendo papel na organização das escalas, respeitados os limites constitucionais. O IPTC ressalta que o aumento dos gastos com pessoal pode pressionar os preços do transporte, sobretudo nas operações que dependem de equipes de apoio, distribuição e movimentação de mercadorias. O repasse ao frete, porém, não é automático: dependerá das condições contratuais, da estrutura de custos e das margens de cada transportadora.

A JBS Terminais completou dois anos como operadora privada do terminal de contêineres e cargas do Porto de Itajaí (SC) com mais de 800 mil TEUs movimentados e quase R$ 250 milhões investidos destinados à retomada, modernização e ampliação da capacidade do terminal. A companhia anuncia um novo aporte de R$ 15,2 milhões para modernizar a inspeção de cargas e ampliar o fluxo de caminhões. De janeiro a setembro de 2026, o terminal movimentou quase 500 mil TEUs, volume 73% superior ao registrado no mesmo período de 2022, antes da paralisação das atividades. Com os investimentos realizados desde outubro de 2024, a capacidade operacional chegou a até 600 mil TEUs por ano. "Em dois anos, avançamos em movimentação, infraestrutura e conectividade. Fizemos investimentos para recuperar a capacidade operacional do terminal e, à medida que os volumes cresceram, seguimos ampliando e modernizando a estrutura. O objetivo é oferecer aos clientes eficiência, competitividade em custos e previsibilidade para suas operações", afirma Aristides Russi Junior, presidente da JBS Terminais . De acordo com a empresa, o novo ciclo de investimentos moderniza a inspeção de contêineres e aumenta a capacidade de processamento de caminhões no porto. Dentre as novidades, o terminal passou a operar um novo equipamento de inspeção por Raio-X , o Varex VXP6, que examina o interior dos contêineres sem abrir as unidades, com maior qualidade de imagem e precisão. Também está em andamento a ampliação de oito para 10 gates , com duas novas linhas de pesagem para ampliar o fluxo de veículos no acesso ao terminal. A demolição do antigo Armazém 3 e a incorporação da área C, em fase de conclusão, vão aumentar a área operacional do pátio em 25%, elevando a capacidade do terminal para 80 mil TEUs por ano . A mudança também permite melhor aproveitamento dos espaços alfandegados.

A Blips , empresa de tecnologia especializada em locação e financiamento de equipamentos produtivos para pequenas e médias empresas (PMEs), inaugurou um centro de distribuição em Cabreúva , no interior de São Paulo, com investimento de R$ 3 milhões . A nova estrutura tem 1.800 m² de área construída e amplia em 150% a área total de galpões da companhia , aumentando sua capacidade de armazenagem e distribuição de equipamentos. A localização foi escolhida pela proximidade com importantes corredores rodoviários, como as rodovias dos Bandeirantes e Anhanguera. O complexo tem capacidade para armazenar mais de mil toneladas e foi projetado para centralizar os estoques e o escoamento do portfólio da empresa. Com a nova unidade, a companhia prevê reduzir os prazos de entrega, otimizar os custos de frete e diminuir as despesas operacionais relacionadas à movimentação e à instalação dos equipamentos. A estrutura também deverá contribuir para a expansão nacional da empresa. “A inauguração do centro de distribuição em Cabreúva representa um marco na nossa trajetória de crescimento sustentável. O mercado de locação e financiamento de equipamentos produtivos para PMEs demanda uma cadeia logística extremamente precisa e ágil”, afirma Ricardo Rocha, cofundador da Blips. Segundo o executivo, a ampliação da infraestrutura busca reduzir custos e agilizar o atendimento aos clientes. A unidade paulista se junta aos centros de distribuição de Minas Gerais e do Espírito Santo. A integração entre as três unidades busca ampliar a eficiência da distribuição e atender diferentes regiões do país. “Ao unificar a gestão de estoque e a distribuição de bens produtivos entre as operações de São Paulo, Minas Gerais e Espírito Santo, estamos reduzindo a dependência de operadores logísticos terceirizados, garantindo maior controle sobre a integridade e manutenção dos equipamentos”, afirma Fernando Motta, diretor de Operações da Blips. A empresa atua na oferta de equipamentos produtivos por meio de modalidades de locação de longo prazo e financiamento, com suporte técnico. Segundo a companhia, sua estrutura inclui mais de 120 mil equipamentos instalados em todos os estados brasileiros e uma rede nacional com mais de 500 especialistas.

O Super Terminais iniciou as operações do Super Porto Verde, novo ativo portuário localizado em Itacoatiara (AM), com o transbordo de cerca de 27 mil toneladas de milho a granel destinadas ao Marrocos. Com investimento de R$ 250 milhões , o empreendimento, apresentado pela companhia como o maior sistema flutuante de transbordo de granéis das Américas , busca ampliar a infraestrutura para o escoamento da produção agrícola brasileira pelo Arco Norte e atender à movimentação de commodities e fertilizantes para exportação e importação. Localizado a cerca de 175 quilômetros de Manaus, o terminal ocupa uma área portuária de 300 mil m², com 240 metros de extensão e 18 metros de largura. A estrutura conta com três guindastes elétricos Sennebogen 895E, descritos pela empresa como os maiores do mundo na categoria e os primeiros em operação no hemisfério sul. Os equipamentos têm capacidade operacional de até 2.100 toneladas por hora. O Super Porto Verde permitirá a atracação simultânea de um navio Panamax de até 50 mil toneladas e seis barcaças, com previsão de realização da operação em até 36 horas. A configuração foi planejada para reduzir gargalos logísticos e aumentar a previsibilidade das operações para tradings e operadores do setor agrícola. “A realização do primeiro transbordo marca um novo capítulo na história do Super Terminais e da região Norte. O Super Porto Verde fortalece o papel do Amazonas na logística de exportação de commodities agrícolas e impulsiona a economia de Itacoatiara com a geração de novos postos de trabalho”, afirma Marcello Di Gregorio, diretor-geral do Super Terminais. A companhia também associa o empreendimento à sua estratégia de sustentabilidade, destacando o transporte hidroviário como alternativa de menor emissão de carbono para o deslocamento de grandes volumes de carga, especialmente em longas distâncias. “O Super Porto Verde representa um passo importante para fortalecer a competitividade logística do Brasil e consolidar a região amazônica como parte estratégica da conexão entre a produção nacional e os mercados internacionais, mantendo a sustentabilidade como parte fundamental desse desenvolvimento”, acrescenta Di Gregorio. O Super Terminais atua há 30 anos em Manaus e opera cargas conteinerizadas, cargas de projeto e cargas soltas, tanto nacionais quanto de importação. Entre seus projetos recentes estão a operação do porto de Itacoatiara, investimentos na modernização de ativos e uma parceria com o Governo do Amazonas para implantar uma usina de gás destinada ao abastecimento de equipamentos portuários, com o objetivo de ampliar o uso de energia mais limpa nas operações.

Como para os bancos importa manter o papel em carteira por longos períodos de tempo, as oscilações importam somente para agentes que atuam no mercado secundário, não impactando a decisão de bancos de ofertar capital Nos últimos meses os mercados financeiros globais vem desdobrando sua atenção aos eventos que tem afetado os mercados de óleo e gás. Afinal, os fenômenos e eventos ocorridos nessa indústria sempre geravam as principais fontes de variação de inflação, dólar global e juros dos bancos centrais. Passado o impacto inicial, na medida em que os agentes econômicos incorporaram os choques nas expectativas, o próprio setor experimenta agora uma nova janela de oportunidade a ser explorada. Neste final de 2026, a sensação entre os investidores é a de que há maior atração de investimentos para a indústria, sinalizando uma possível normalização dos ciclos de negócios. O contexto é de maior liquidez global, com aumento da oferta de crédito e capital dos bancos em busca de estabilidade, com maiores retornos esperados a longo prazo e redução do risco no setor. Pode-se argumentar que há duas causas na raiz dessa mudança de quadro. Uma causa estrutural e uma causa conjuntural. No aspecto estrutural, parece haver a consolidação do processo de "seleção natural" dos investidores no mercado. Durante a última década, notadamente do fim do último grande boom de petróleo até os choques da pandemia e das guerras na Ucrânia e no Irã, o setor experimentou um afastamento de investidores que, do pós crise de 2008 até o boom da virada da década de 2000/2010, entraram buscando retornos especulativos e de curto prazo. Essa não é uma característica do mercado de óleo e gás, marcado por longos períodos de maturação do investimento e riscos elevados. O resultado disto foi alguma distorção no mercado que recentemente verificou até posições em busca de hedge (proteção a algum evento adverso), o que definitivamente não é a natureza dos negócios em óleo e gás.

https://gcaptain.com/u-s-sets-first-deep.text: Polymetallic nodules, such as those shown here, can occur on the ocean floor and are of interest for the critical minerals they contain. Credit: NOAA. The Trump administration has scheduled the first offshore mineral lease sale in U.S. history, opening more than 31 million acres of seabed near American Samoa to companies seeking critical minerals from the deep ocean. The Department of the Interior’s Marine Minerals Administration (MMA) on Monday issued its Final Leasing Notice for the November 19 auction, clearing the final major administrative step before companies can bid on rights to explore and potentially develop mineral deposits on the U.S. Outer Continental Shelf. The sale, designated PACM-1, includes two lease areas covering approximately 31.5 million acres. The larger area encompasses 16.3 million acres, while the second covers 15.2 million acres. Under the final lease terms, each area carries a minimum bid of $3 million and a primary lease term of 20 years. Production royalties would begin at 2% for the first five years of commercial mining, increasing to 5% thereafter. The areas contain potential deposits of polymetallic nodules and ferromanganese crusts, which can hold valuable minerals including nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese. The Trump administration has made expanding domestic supplies of critical minerals a national security priority, particularly as it seeks to reduce reliance on China-dominated supply chains.

https://petronoticias.com.br/a-arabia-sa.text: A ofensiva da Arábia Saudita contra os Houthis visa assegurar o controle do Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, que está sufocando as exportações sauditas de petróleo. Enquanto os houthis ameaçam um importante corredor marítimo global, a Arábia Saudita intensifica o apoio militar às forças iemenitas que buscam repelir o grupo. No início de setembro, os houthis lançaram uma ofensiva rápida e inesperada ao longo da costa do Mar Vermelho no Iêmen. Capturaram o porto estrategicamente importante de Mocha e avançaram para o sul em direção ao Estreito de Bab Al-Mandeb, conquistando cerca de 150 km de litoral e ameaçando a entrada sul do Mar Vermelho. A ofensiva transformou Bab el-Mandeb em um segundo ponto de pressão marítima no conflito do Irã com os Estados Unidos. Antes disso, os recursos navais e militares dos EUA podiam se concentrar no Estreito de Ormuz, principal alavanca econômica do Irã. O avanço dos Houthis também colocou a rota do Mar Vermelho em jogo, dando ao Irã uma potencial vantagem, sobre os dois principais corredores de transporte da região. Os preços do petróleo são determinados pela margem, portanto, mesmo quando a perda real de produção é relativamente pequena, a mera ameaça de interrupção pode gerar um grande aumento de preço. Foi exatamente isso que aconteceu em setembro. O petróleo Brent, principal referência internacional para o preço do petróleo bruto, teve uma média de cerca de US$ 89 por barril durante a maior parte de 2026. Após a apreensão do poço Mocha, apesar de ainda não haver uma perda real equivalente na produção global de petróleo, seu preço ultrapassou os US$ 110. Atualmente, está um pouco mais abaixo fixando-se em US$ 108,65 na manhã de hoje (19). O ataque dos Houthis foi crucial demais para ficar sem resposta. Em 4 de outubro, o governo iemenita reconhecido internacionalmente, com o apoio da Arábia Saudita, lançou uma grande contraofensiva. Com substancial apoio aéreo e naval saudita, as forças governamentais atacaram as áreas recentemente conquistadas pelos Houthis. Em suas declarações públicas, o governo iemenita enfatizou que seu objetivo a longo prazo é a reunificação nacional. Consequentemente, quando Rashad al-Alimi, presidente do Conselho de Liderança Presidencial (PLC) do Iêmen, anunciou a operação em 5 de outubro, descreveu-a como um esforço para restaurar as instituições estatais, retomar Sanaa e derrotar o movimento Houthi. Provavelmente mais por esperança do que por expectativa, ele a denominou “ Operação Aurora do Iêmen”. O ex-embaixador dos EUA na Arábia Saudita, Michael Ratney, resumiu esse objetivo mais restrito de forma sucinta: “ Idealmente, seria uma operação bastante limitada para retomar as áreas costeiras e restabelecer o tráfego marítimo normal.” O esforço militar da coalizão é considerável. https://petronoticias.com.br/a-petrobras.text: A plataforma P-82 já está navegando para o Rio de Janeiro. Ela deixou o estaleiro Tuas Boulevard Yard , em Cingapura, rumo ao campo de Búzios, no pré-sal da Bacia de Santos, segundo informou a Petrobrás. A plataforma deixou o estaleiro dias depois da plataforma P-80, também para o campo de Búzios. O navio-plataforma (FPSO) terá capacidade de produzir 225 mil barris/dia de petróleo e processar 12 milhões de metros cúbicos por dia (m³/dia) de gás natural. A plataforma é uma das “ seis gigantes” da estatal que estavam em construção. Outra notícias importante foi o adiamento do acostamento da Plataforma P-35 no Estaleiro Inhaúma, onde fará manutenção e modernizações. Tudo estava sendo previsto para esta segunda-feira(19), mas o pessoal responsável da Petrobrás passou considerar o dia 1º de novembro. O dia seguinte será feriado e haverá mais margem de manobras para que o navio acoste no estaleiro, pelo que determinaram as pessoas responsáveis. Em relação a P-82 é importante dizer que ela tem 345,3 metros de comprimento, 60 metros de largura e pesa mais de 100 mil toneladas. Segundo a Petrobrás, a P-80 e a P-82 devem entrar em operação em 2027. Outras três plataformas semelhantes, P-83, P-84 e a P-85, irão, respectivamente, para os campos de Búzios, Atapu e Sépia, também no pré-sal da Bacia de Santos. Elas estão em construção, mas em etapas anteriores. A primeira das “seis gigantes ” foi a FPSO Almirante Tamandaré, que já alcançou produção de até 270 mil barris/dia. Ainda de acordo com a Petrobrás, os módulos de processo da P-82 foram fabricados no Brasil, no estaleiro Seatrium Aracruz, no Espírito Santo. A construção das P-82, assim como ocorreu com a P-80, foi contratada pela Petrobás pelo modelo EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning ), segundo o qual a empresa contratada é responsável pela engenharia, suprimentos, construção e comissionamento da unidade até sua entrega para operação no Brasil. © 2026 Petronotícias. https://splash247.com/emgs-lands-offshor.text: Norwegian geophysical services specialist Electromagnetic Geoservices (EMGS) has secured a letter of award from Pakistan’s Mari Energies for controlled-source electromagnetic surveys across multiple offshore exploration blocks. The Oslo-based company said the programme would combine CSEM-derived resistivity information with seismic and geological data to improve prospect evaluation, reduce exploration uncertainty and support decisions on future drilling targets. The survey is expected to take place in the first quarter of 2027. The agreement follows meetings between senior EMGS representatives, Mari Energies’ management and technical teams, and the Pakistani company’s offshore joint-venture partners, including Turkish Petroleum. Mari Energies said it intends to use electromagnetic technology to evaluate, rank and de-risk exploration prospects as it seeks to unlock Pakistan’s largely unexplored offshore hydrocarbon potential. In May, the country finalised agreements covering 23 offshore exploration blocks spanning approximately 54,600 sq km in the Indus and Makran basins, with initial investment commitments of $82m. Mari Energies emerged as the largest participant in the licensing round, securing operatorship of 18 blocks and non-operating interests in another five.

Para Marcello Di Gregorio, diretor-geral do Super Terminais, o primeiro transbordo abre um novo capítulo para a companhia e para a região. “O Super Porto Verde fortalece o papel do Amazonas na logística de exportação de commodities agrícolas e impulsiona a economia de Itacoatiara com a geração de novos postos de trabalho”, afirma. A estrutura fica a cerca de 175 quilômetros de Manaus e ocupa uma área portuária de 300 mil metros quadrados. O sistema tem 240 metros de extensão e 18 metros de largura e conta com três guindastes elétricos Sennebogen 895E, apontados como os maiores do mundo na categoria e os primeiros em operação no hemisfério sul. Cada equipamento tem capacidade operacional de até 2.100 toneladas por hora. O arranjo permite a atracação simultânea de um navio Panamax de até 50 mil toneladas e de seis barcaças, com previsão de operação em até 36 horas. A configuração busca reduzir gargalos logísticos e dar mais previsibilidade a tradings e operadores do setor agrícola, que dependem de janelas de embarque cada vez mais ajustadas. A infraestrutura também se conecta à estratégia de sustentabilidade da companhia. O transporte hidroviário está entre as alternativas de menor emissão de carbono para deslocar grandes volumes de carga, sobretudo em longas distâncias, o que aproxima o projeto da agenda de logística de baixo carbono.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: To maintain the global fleet to the required standards throughout a vessel’s lifecycle, shipowners and operators must comply with established Classification rules and regulations, ensuring vessels are equipped to meet new and future operational standards. Across the time available to survey a ship the surveyor has to utilise their expertise and experience to focus on the most important areas of the structure. New ‘remote’ technology, enabled by AI, can assist a survey, helping it be ever more comprehensive and effective. And, right now, remote surveys are also helping address operational challenges. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the Red Sea is placing extraordinary strain on global maritime operations. According to the International Maritime Organization (IMO) , which has condemned the latest attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, nearly 6,000 seafarers remain stranded on board vessels unable to depart the Persian Gulf safely. Amid this complex web of geopolitical volatility, one area of growing concern is the impact of sustained disruption on the health and condition of the global fleet, as vessels may begin to fall behind on their classification requirements. The impact of this ongoing disruption is evident. Diversion around the Cape of Good Hope adds 10 to 14 days of voyage time on average for Asia-Europe routes, placing additional strain on ships, which then leads to heightened maintenance requirements across shipowners' fleets. Port call delays at regional hubs have also increased significantly, at a time when surveyors face major restrictions on their ability to travel. Remote surveys can provide support when physical access is difficult, not safe or impossible. The case for smarter inspection is not only operational. Beyond the mounting pressures of cost, scheduling and fleet availability lies an ongoing concern: the safety of the people who carry out these surveys. Nowhere is that risk more acute than in the enclosed spaces that surveyors and crew may be required to enter. Despite decades of progress in the development of regulatory frameworks and training programmes, the hidden danger posed by enclosed spaces continues to claim lives. A recent report from the International Bulk Terminals Association (IBTA) outlines the scale of the threat: between 2000 and 2024, 1,010 ship and shore workers died in enclosed space-related incidents, which represents an average of 40 deaths per year; of those who died, some 69 percent were crew members. This trend is particularly relevant to survey engagements. Surveyors are regularly required to enter confined spaces that present a range of often hidden threats: extreme heat, with temperatures reaching 50 degrees Celsius in the Middle East, high humidity, and toxic gas pockets generat

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The Department of Justice filed last week with a U.S. District Court in Maryland, asking the court to remand the approval of the Construction and Operations Plan for the Maryland Offshore Wind for further review by the Department of the Interior. It is the second time in days that the federal government has attempted this tactic in its ongoing efforts to derail the offshore wind energy sector. The Trump administration, since taking office in 2025, has attempted multiple different tactics to stop the development of offshore wind energy projects, ranging from a review of the permitting process to stop-work orders and buying back leases. It has effectively stopped future development while also going after the five under-construction projects and others, such as Maryland Offshore Wind, which had gained approvals in the closing days of the Biden administration but have not yet reached construction. Maryland Offshore Wind’s lease dates to a 2014 offshore auction, which was won by US Wind. The company combined two leases into a single project in 2018 and started the review and approval process in 2020. In the summer of 2024, the Department of the Interior and the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management granted the final approvals for a plan that calls for up to 114 wind turbines, four offshore substations, four offshore export cables, and a 100-meter-tall meteorological tower placed in the lease area offshore from Ocean City, Maryland. It has not proposed specific turbine models, saying it was considering up to 18 MW models, while it has said in the past the total lease area had the potential for approximately 1.8 GW. The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM), an agency within the U.S. Department of the Interior, approved US Wind’s Construction and Operations Plan (COP) for Maryland Offshore Wind on December 3, 2024. The project, however, has continued to be mired in various lawsuits, including a 2024 case filed by the mayor and city council of Ocean City, Maryland. The Department of the Interior and US Wind are being sued with eight complaints each seeking to block the approval. The District Court has dismissed three counts, the violation of the procedural act, a claim involving migratory birds, and another against the Coastal Zone Management Act, while four are still pending. The Trump administration has found itself on both sides of the issue in the case of the claim against NOAA Fisheries that cited impacts on marine mammals. NOAA, during the approvals, said the impacts would be temporary and expected normal behavior to return after construction was completed. Department of Justice calls the count in the suit against NOAA “blatantly inaccurate” and says the court should grant a summary judgment on that one count.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/h.text: South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai and the U.S.-based venture-backed defense company Anduril are reporting a breakthrough with the first demonstration of autonomous ship technology in U.S. waters. The test was conducted as a demonstration for the U.S. Navy and is based on a two-year partnership between the companies to merge shipbuilding expertise with AI and autonomous technology. The test was conducted near Long Beach, California, and involved a 368-ton offshore support vessel formerly operated by the U.S. Navy. The demonstration lasted for approximately 3.5 hours and included the U.S. Navy, ABS (American Bureau of Shipping), the South Korean Navy, and South Korea’s Defense Acquisition Program Administration. The vessel was equipped with an autonomous navigation platform, VAOne, developed by HD Kosea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering, integrated with the Anduril Lattice software platform. The company reports that Lattice “delivers AI-enabled sensor fusion, mission autonomy, distributed network management, and command and control for robotic systems.” According to the statement released by the companies, the trial demonstrated autonomous navigation, changes in mission assignments, coordinated operations involving multiple vessels, and emergency responses to system failures. Shore-based control stations monitored the operations in real time. “The demonstration was meaningful because it confirmed the uncrewed vessel’s ability to carry out complex missions and respond to various real-world scenarios that could occur after deployment,” Chang Kwang-pil, senior executive vice president at HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering, said in a press statement describing the demonstration. HD Hyundai and Anduril announced a partnership two years ago focusing on autonomous military systems and weapons. Anduril, founded in 2017 by a group of tech entrepreneurs, has drawn favor with the Trump administration because of its integration of AI (Trump calls it Super Intelligence) into its platform. The company, which is also working on weapons systems, last week announced a major Pentagon contract and plans for a new manufacturing facility in Baltimore to develop components for the nuclear submarine program.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/g.text: The pro-Palestinian Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC) announced Saturday that it is suspending its current voyage to Gaza and will try again next year. This time, it was not blocked by Israeli interception, but by breakdowns, the organizers said in a statement. "Following mechanical difficulties and necessary repairs that delayed the voyage and narrowed the remaining sailing window . . . the FFC has decided to prepare for a renewed attempt to reach Gaza in 2027," the group said. The flotilla has been conducting shorter voyages around Europe to raise awareness and call for national governments to apply more pressure to Israel on the question of Palestinian rights. These shorter trips will continue while awaiting the next season of calm weather in 2027. The group still plans to return to the Eastern Mediterranean in order to protest the long-running Israeli naval blockade of the Gaza coastline. "We set out for Gaza, and it's painful to end this voyage without reaching it," said Frank Romano, a volunteer aboard one of the flotilla's vessels. "The commitment that brought us aboard remains as strong as ever." Various permutations of the Freedom Flotilla movement have been trying to breach the Gaza blockade for the past 16 years; early attempts in the 2010s had rhetorical support from Palestinian terrorist group Hamas. Each time, the vessels have been intercepted by Israeli commandos far from shore, usually in international waters (where no state has jurisdiction over foreign-flagged shipping). In the first, most controversial sailing, nine flotilla crewmembers were killed and ten Israeli soldiers were wounded in a boarding that turned confrontational. In many cases, flotilla members have been detained and brought to Israeli shores for processing. The largest recent attempt, the Global Sumud Flotilla of 2025, reported a suspected drone attack while at anchor off Malta. A fire occurred, but no injuries were reported, and the mission sailed onwards. All of its vessels were intercepted by Israeli forces by early October 2025.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: The Philippines' Bureau of Fire Protection has completed an initial investigation into the deadly fire aboard the ferry June Aster, which killed 77 off the coast of Palawan in September. The agency determined that faulty lashing may have allowed a chemical cargo to spill onto a shipment of solid asphalt, starting a vigorous fire. According to the BFP, June Aster was delayed for four days before departure and continued to take on additional cargo during the period. New additions in the ro/ro cargo bay included blocks of asphalt and drums of calcium hypochlorite, also known as bleaching powder, a chemically-reactive chlorinating agent used for water treatment. It is a powerful oxidizer and must be stowed away from organic materials and sources of heat for safety; according to IMDG Code guidance, it can start a fire by itself if it comes into contact with carbon-based materials. Once heated, it decomposes and releases oxygen gas, a powerful fire hazard, and chlorine gas, a deadly toxin. It is a well-known and notorious fire risk in merchant shipping. The hypchlorite and the asphalt blocks were stowed together aft on the cargo deck next to the engine room, BFP Superintendent Wilberto Rico Neil Ang Kwan Tiu told reporters on Friday. The cargo may have been exposed to above-ambient heat from the engine room at that location, Tiu said. On the evening of September 9, as the vessel was under way in the Strait of Coron, it encountered rough weather. The cargo of hypochlorite broke loose, mixed with the asphalt, caught fire and emitted large volumes of "highly toxic" smoke - the likely reason for the high number of fatalities. Some victims may have been killed before any consideration of evacuating the ship. "It’s possible that before they could even feel the heat, they had been suffocated. Given that it was 18:30, it was already dark and nighttime, they were likely in their bunks, which explains the high number of casualties — 77," said Tiu, per Balita.com. The vessel operator, members of the crew and port personnel face serious criminal charges in connection with the stowage of the cargo and the fatal outcome, Tiu said.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/int.text: InterManager has called for urgent industry action on enclosed space safety after its latest research highlighted persistent failures in procedures, training, leadership and accident prevention. The organisation has recorded 354 enclosed space accidents over the past 30 years, between 1996 and 2026, across tankers, bulkers, general cargo ships, passenger vessels, containerships and other vessel types. Its latest seafarer survey identifies a recurring gap between safety procedures and operational reality onboard. Over 900 respondents highlighted overly complex paperwork, inadequate time and manpower, commercial pressure, insufficient practical training and a reluctance to address underlying causes. The survey also highlights concerns that inspections can focus on superficial compliance rather than the effectiveness of actual safety practices. It also identifies opportunities to make greater use of real-time gas sensors, wearable technology, digital permits, hands-free communications and unmanned inspection tools to reduce human exposure. The organisation says its latest seafarer research points to two clear priorities. The need for continuous professional development, rather than one-off training, and for seafarers to be more directly engaged in the systems, ships and resources they are expected to operate safely. Current enclosed space training is often concentrated around a single exercise when people commence their careers. InterManager says this must now be enhanced to deliver competence, rather than just training, particularly as enclosed space entry training is being considered as part of the current review of STW requirements, with the International Chamber of Shipping leading industry input. InterManager will explore the survey findings and wider enclosed space safety concerns during a webinar, run in conjunction with The Nautical Institute, on 27 October 2026 at 10am GMT. The webinar will bring together industry experts, Captain Pradeep Chawla, CEO of Marie Pals, Captain Garry Hallett from InterManager and Richard Cowburn, human factors specialist, to discuss where the industry stands now on enclosed space safety, how seafarers and shore-based stakeholders feel about current practice, and what practical action is needed next.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/gol.text: Golden Island bunkered a Maersk ship with about 5,000 mt of ISCC-certified bio-ethanol in Singapore’s first operation of the kind. Golden Island’s IMO Type II chemical tanker Golden Centaurus supplied the dual-fuel container ship Maersk Halifax while the ship’s containers were being handled. A mass flow meter (MFM) was used in the operation. The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said it was the biggest volume of ethanol ever to be delivered in one bunker operation. The stem was nearly twice as large as the 2,800 mt of bio-ethanol that Repsol delivered to the Antonia Maersk in Barcelona in July. The MPA said the operation will provide data and learnings to assess how Singapore’s existing methanol bunker standards could be adapted for ethanol bunkering, and whether existing MFM systems can be used for future ethanol bunker operations. Before the operation, the companies involved ran a safety workshop. They used their experience in methanol bunkering to train crew members in handling ethanol and responding to emergencies. Source: By Nachiket Tekawade, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news

The US government is working with investors who buy idled sanctioned tankers, refurbish them and use the ships to transport non-sanctioned oil, Wright said Monday at a Citadel Securities event in New York. “We’re going to move some of the ships from what I call the ‘bad-guy fleet’ to the ‘good-guy fleet,’ ” Wright said. “They will not carry sanctioned oil anymore.” Wright’s comments represent the first detailed public explanation from the Trump administration about turning to sanctioned tankers as it seeks to expand the number of ships available to transport crude and boost supply disrupted by the war in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The Trump administration is undertaking an approval process to grant ships legitimate status, Wright said. He rejected the idea that the US was simply removing sanctions from tankers that carried crude from nations such as Russia or Iran.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/how.text: The rise is concentrated at the top end of the fleet. VLCC purchases climbed from 1 to 19, and Suezmax purchases from 2 to 7. Notable recent sales include the Vadin (308,000 DWT, Aug 2006, Mitsui Ichihara) that sold to Onex DMXX for USD 117 mil, adding to the additional seven VLCCs and Suezmaxes purchased by the company since the start of September. The Strait of Hormuz crisis is the clear driver of the purchase activity. Transit volumes through the Strait fell sharply after the ceasefire collapsed in early July, and the alternatives have come under pressure too. Drone strikes on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and Houthi threats around Bab el-Mandeb narrowed the options for moving Middle Eastern crude. As a result, fewer open market owners are willing to trade in the Gulf, and for producers and regional trading houses, buying tonnage outright has become a way of securing the ability to keep crude and money moving. There is a sellers angle too. For risk averse owners who will not trade in the region themselves, selling at elevated values offers a way to capture some of the gains created by the Middle East Gulf risk and rate environment, taking part in an extreme market without taking on the exposure. Positioning is key, with premiums most pronounced where delivery into the Gulf is a firm requirement. Earnings have added to the pull, with VLCC rates on the Middle East Gulf to China route pushing past 1,300,000 USD/day for the first time. Sale prices have followed, reaching record levels. For example, 15 YO VLCCs of 310,000 DWT have increased by 163.45% year-on-year from USD 55 mil to USD 144.9 mil. Whether these levels hold beyond this narrow pool of buyers will depend largely on how the disruption develops. Onex DMCC’s buying spree amid tight tonnage supply By Rebecca Galanopoulos Onex DMCC’s appetite has continued beyond the Pinios deal, with the trading house now linked to six VLCC and Suezmax purchases in recent weeks. Another VLCC, the Ashoka (302,600 DWT, Mar 2010, Universal), has also changed hands to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 130 mil. The deals rank among the highest ever seen for VLCC tonnage and highlight the breadth of regional demand for immediately available tonnage. Onex’s willingness to pay up for prompt tonnage has become a driving force behind current values, setting a new reference point for future sales.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/hyd.text: A review of fatal incidents submitted to the IMO shows that many seafarers were overcome by H₂S while carrying out routine maintenance and inspection activities outside enclosed spaces. Crew members have collapsed while opening tank manholes, dismantling pumps and pipelines, working near tank vents, and attempting to rescue colleagues. In many of these incidents, the victims had no intention of entering a tank. The findings highlight an important safety message: H₂S should not be viewed solely as an enclosed-space entry hazard. It is also a release hazard. Personnel can be exposed during everyday shipboard operations whenever a contaminated system is opened, disturbed or ventilated. More than half of fatalities happened outside According to IMO document CCC 12/INF.20 (10 July 2026), at least 29 of 56 identified H₂S-related fatalities occurred outside enclosed spaces. The victims were carrying out routine tasks when a sudden release of H₂S caused immediate collapse. These findings challenge the traditional perception that H₂S fatalities are primarily linked to enclosed-space entry. A hazardous gas release can also occur during normal shipboard operations, as the following case study illustrates. Case study: fatal exposure while opening a bilge water tank Before cleaning a bilge water tank on a drillship, a Second Engineer (2/E) and a Motorman opened the tank access hatch to allow for ventilation. Moments later, as he was climbing away from the hatch, the 2/E suddenly collapsed, and both men fell into the tank. Tragically, despite rescue efforts, both men lost their lives. The investigation found that the tank contained oily water and residue deposits capable of generating H₂S. Opening the hatch likely released accumulated gas into the surrounding pump room, exposing the workers before any tank entry had begun. The incident highlights a crucial point: simply opening a tank can release a potentially fatal concentration of H₂S. What is H₂S knockdown? H₂S knockdown refers to the sudden collapse and loss of consciousness that can occur following exposure to very high concentrations of hydrogen sulphide. H₂S is a colourless, highly toxic, and flammable gas. It is heavier than air and tends to accumulate in low-lying areas such as tank bottoms, bilges, pits, and poorly ventilated spaces.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/w.text: To address the historically-high cost of shipping oil on long-distance routes, the White House has announced that it will ease sanctions on shadow fleet tankers. But the details are different than simply a waiver process, Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Bloomberg on Monday: the U.S. sanctions designation will be removed when a "dirty" tanker is sold to a new owner and moved into a legitimate trade lane. The announcement is a new line of effort for the administration, and reflects the depth of the challenges that the Iran conflict has created. A concerted U.S.-backed effort to shuttle oil through the Strait of Hormuz has successfully restored much of the flow that disappeared early this year, at great financial and human cost. Despite Iran's frequent attacks on shipping, about 10 million barrels per day are getting through the strait. This is enough to bring Mideast crude export totals back up to about 80 percent of pre-conflict norms, according to The Wall Street Journal. The hard-won bounceback in volume would normally support a drop in oil prices, the Trump administration's greatest hope ahead of midterm elections. But even with flow restored, tanker availability remains constrained; in a tight market, day rates for large tankers are so high that shipping cost alone is sustaining benchmark crude oil prices at $100-plus per barrel. This tanker shortage is the motivator for removing sanctions on available vessels in the shadow fleet, the administration says. "We’re going to move some of the ships from what I call the 'bad-guy fleet' to the 'good-guy fleet,'" Wright said at a conference event Monday. "They will not carry sanctioned oil anymore." The arrangement Wright outlined suggested S&P transactions. Investors would buy sanctioned tankers, refit them, then use the tonnage to move legitimate cargo. "We are converting dark tankers to legitimate tankers," Wright told Bloomberg. "There is no removing of sanctions." Implicit in any purchase would be a transfer of funds to shadow fleet owners, and at favorable market timing. In a superheated charter market with immediate opportunities, an available used tanker can cost far more than a brand new one ordered for later delivery. Even a 15-year-old Suezmax - a typical shadow-fleet vessel - can fetch $100 million secondhand, per the latest brokerage figures, four times what it would have been worth in 2021. A sale on these commercial terms would net a large profit for shadow-fleet owners who bought older tonnage and deployed it in sanctioned trade lanes.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: On Monday, the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) - recently reconfigured as the Marine Minerals Administration (MMA) - announced that it will hold a mining lease sale for seabed acreage next to Rose Atoll, a protected marine sanctuary east of American Samoa. The area may hold a substantial quantity of polymetallic nodules, as well as the species and ecosystems that have evolved around them, and will be auctioned off on November 19. "Critical minerals are no longer just commodities; they are a vital strategic asset in global competition, essential for reaching our energy efficiency goals, strengthening our national defense, and securing domestic supply chains," said acting MMA Director Mike Olsen, pledging that environmental and cultural factors would be taken into account during planning and development. NOAA research vessel Okeanos Explorer surveyed the lease area earlier this summer, providing data that will help bidders in initial resource characterization. To begin leasing on a near-term timetable, MMA is leveraging a provision of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to hold a U.S.-only lease sale outside of the supervision of the International Seabed Authority (ISA), avoiding a thorny debate over whether ISA should license mining activity. The concept of commercial deep sea mining has opponents in environmental circles and in the oceanographic research community. Researchers' concerns include the possibility that the seabed habitats targeted for mining will not readily recover after extraction. Polymetallic nodules support ecosystems that are not well-studied, and if removed, the habitat is altered semi-permanently; the nodules take about two to three million years to regrow. The other possible risk, conservation advocates say, is that mining sediment containing heavy metals could be spilled into the water column. Once released it could spread and affect areas further from the site, blanketing the seabed or harming midwater species. Environmental NGO Oceana notes that the lease areas where the activity would occur are located next to Rose Atoll Marine National Monument, home to sea turtles, humpback whales and other species.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: The Port of Singapore has been at the forefront of harbor drone services since at least 2018, when it welcomed the first trials of a cargo-drone commercial delivery system for ships at anchor. While a friendly environment for R&D and commerce, it is also a leader in drone security regulation - a prudent step given the real-world risk of UAV-based sabotage or espionage. Seafarers who decide to launch a personal drone in Singapore's harbor - especially if they're close to Changi Airport - are at risk of hefty fines, and potentially a jail term for egregious offenses. The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) has strict rules for UAV use over land and water. Flights are not allowed over crowds, near roads, or near first-responders. Flights above 200 feet are prohibited, as are drone movements within five kilometers of an airport (without prior permission and a permit). The maximum penalty is a fine of up to US$39,000 or up to two years in prison. The five-kilometer exclusion zone around Changi Airport happens to cover multiple anchorage areas at the eastern end of Singapore's waterfront. Several seafarers have unwittingly found themselves on the wrong side of this regulation, according to a circular distributed to shipping interests by CAAS and the MPA last week. According to CAAS, two seafarers were caught operating recreational drones in the wrong areas over the summer. In June, a crewmember aboard a local bunker tanker decided to operate a drone at a height of about 140 feet, some three kilometers away from the airport at Eastern Petroleum Bravo Anchorage. The 46-year-old mariner lacked a permit, and was fined about US$4,000 - instead of a 10-day prison term. In July, a crewmember on a foreign-flagged tanker was caught running a recreational drone at an altitude of 240 feet - well above the statutory limit - in the Eastern Petroleum Charlie Anchorage, less than two kilometers from Changi Airport. The individual received a fine of US$2,300. On shore, tourists and members of the public get caught in drone-use violations at a rate of about 300 reported cases per year, according to the Straits Times . A small number of these cases are prosecuted, but for those that are, the court process can take weeks and real-world fines can be as high as US$10,000 or more.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543782-tr.text: Offshore drilling contractor Transocean has secured contracts worth approximately $550 million for two ultra-deepwater drillships in the U.S. Gulf, covering a combined 15 wells and adding to the company's firm contract backlog. The contracts involve the Deepwater Proteus and Deepwater Conqueror drillships, both awarded work by undisclosed operators, Transocean said in an October 19 announcement. The Deepwater Proteus secured a 10-well contract valued at approximately $325 million in backlog. The drilling campaign is expected to last around 700 days, starting in the first quarter of 2027 in direct continuation of the rig's existing U.S. Gulf contract. The Deepwater Conqueror was awarded a five-well contract expected to contribute approximately $225 million in backlog, excluding mobilization fees. The campaign is estimated to last 450 days and is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, directly following the drillship's existing program in Equatorial Guinea. https://www.oedigital.com/news/543777-no.text: Norway's combined oil and gas production missed an official forecast by 4% in September, data from the Norwegian Offshore Directorate (NOD) showed on Tuesday. Oil production was slightly ahead of projections while natural gas was lagging, the data showed. Norway is Europe's largest supplier of natural gas and a major producer of oil, but output varies from month to month depending on maintenance needs and other stoppages at its 100 offshore fields. Overall oil, condensate, natural gas liquids and gas output stood at 0.600 million standard cubic metres per day, equivalent to 3.77 million barrels of oil equivalent, a decrease of 2.3% year-on-year. Natural gas production in September rose to 298.4 million cubic metres (mcm) per day from 283.9 mcm a year earlier, but lagged a forecast of 319.9 mcm by 6.7%, the regulator said on its website. Crude oil output fell to 1.73 million barrels per day (bpd) in September from 1.89 million bpd in the same month last year, but came in above a forecast of 1.72 million bpd, NOD's preliminary data showed.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543778-ve.text: Oilfield service companies including Weatherford International, Baker Hughes, Halliburton and SLB are advertising dozens of jobs in Venezuela, according to company websites, an early sign that a Washington-backed plan to rebuild the country's energy industry is gaining traction.
