https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: Pittsburgh-based automated inspection company Gecko Robotics has won a $300 million IDIQ contract with the U.S. Navy to help fight the age-old enemy of corrosion with new high-tech tools. Gecko's robotic inspectors can crawl on steel structures of all kinds and detect flaws in minute detail, helping customers to plan maintenance in advance and build a digital record of asset health. For the Navy, the most valuable metric in sustainment is yard time: an understanding of the vessel's needs means better preparation for a yard period, which means more efficient utilization of both the yard capacity and the vessel. Tech tools can help get more vessels out of shipyard faster, a requirement to achieve the Navy's goal of maintaining 80% combat surge readiness at any given time. In a statement, Gecko said that its systems can help the Navy identify structural issues with its vessels up to 50 times faster than human methods can produce, and can complete digital inspections in mere days. Its proprietary technology can crawl along a flight deck and scan through thick nonskid coating. Combined with AI analysis, the technique generates a comprehensive map of corrosion. “With savings of millions of dollars per ship, months of inspections turning into days and warships returning to sea faster, the U.S. Navy is demonstrating to the world how to deploy technology at scale," said Gecko Robotics co-founder and CEO Jake Loosararian. The contract expands upon a previous $71 million award covering work on 18 ships in U.S. Pacific Fleet, announced in March. Gecko will also be involved in nondestructive testing of submarine components at Anduril's future manufacturing plants at Sparrows Point, Baltimore and Orange County, California, the firm says. The new Sparrows Point yard is expected to launch in 2030 and work at the OC site is already in progress.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: The Government of New South Wales and preservationists are battling over the fate of a historic little vessel, MV Cape Don , with the local government announcing on October 18 it had seized the vessel for immediate disposal. Local officials are calling their actions “the last resort,” as they contend the vessel’s condition continues to worsen, posing substantial risks to public safety and the environment. NSW Maritime asserts it has been monitoring the condition of the vessel as it has further deteriorated for the past several years. It highlights that the vessel has been issued two unsafe vessel notices, and they assert they met with the owners, a private foundation, nearly 50 times, raising concerns about the vessel’s condition and the immediate need for repairs to stabilize the vessel. “I want to make it clear that NSW Maritime has been working in good faith with the owners of the MV Cape Don for many years to help restore the vessel, but its condition has only worsened, and the likelihood of the owners being able to restore it back to its former glory has become untenable,” asserted NSW Minister for Roads, Jenny Aitchison. The government swooped in on Sunday, October 18, with media reports that the police searched the vessel to ensure there was no one aboard. They declared it had been seized for immediate disposal. Cape Don in her heyday - the foundation asserts she is a special piece of Australian history (Sea Heritage Foundation) The 2,100 gross ton vessel, which is 74 meters (244 feet) in length, was built in 1962 in Newcastle by the State Dockyard. It was purpose-built for the Commonwealth Lighthouse Service in order to build, supply, and maintain lighthouses and navigation aids around Australia. She, along with two sisterships, Cape Moreton and Cape Pillar , was also called on for other duties such as surveying and recovery work. Cape Don was involved in many high-profile scientific expeditions, including the salvage of two anchors from HMS Investigator , a Royal Navy sloop that between 1801 and 1803 became the first ship to circumnavigate Australia.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: On Monday, Mexican state oil company Pemex reported that it was fighting a fire on an unmanned satellite platform at a position about 60 nautical miles off the coast of Ciudad del Carmen in the Bay of Campeche. It is the latest in a long string of mishaps at the offshore-focused oil company's platforms. At about 1115 hours on Monday morning, Pemex announced an emergency at the Abkatun-H platform, an unmanned installation that is part of the larger Abkatun oilfield complex. Safety protocols were activated and vessels dispatched to fight the fire. As of Tuesday, Pemex has not released further details on the cause or status of the incident. The Abkatun field was one of six giant finds discovered in the late 1970s to early 1980s in Campeche Sound, the core of Mexico's offshore oil wealth. These maturing fields continue to deliver returns for Pemex today - Abkatun alone puts out 3.3 million barrels per year in 2024 - but the infrastructure is aging. Pemex has had a long string of fires and accidents this year, primarily in its onshore operations. The list includes a fire at the Olmeca refinery complex that killed five workers in March; another refinery accident that injured six in Salina Cruz in May; and a runaway well fire that burned for four months and polluted dozens of towns in Veracruz. In April, Pemex also acknowledged a significant oil spill from a pipeline at the Abkatun field that began in February. The crude fouled beaches around Campeche and threatened the earnings of local fisherman. Several company officials were dismissed for failing to disclose the leak sooner.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: New Zealand has moved quickly to open its first round for offshore renewable energy feasibility permit applications just weeks after it completed the enabling legislation. Government officials highlight that the country already has a high level of renewable electricity generation, while saying that offshore renewable energy has the potential to contribute to that while also helping New Zealand meet increasing demand for power. The notice for the round went into force on October 19 and runs until April 19, 2027. It opens two offshore areas, one near Taranaki and the other near Waikato/South Auckland, for proposals. Both zones are south of Auckland on the west coast of New Zealand, off the North Island. The process envisions a single permit in each area and requires the recipients to commence the ORE feasibility activities and provide annual update reports. “The winds off the South Taranaki coast are on a par with those of the North Sea, the most productive offshore wind region in the world, and because they blow so steadily, offshore turbines are expected to run at higher capacity than turbines on land,” said Energy Minister Simeon Brown earlier this year when the regulatory framework was adopted. New Zealand began the process in 2024 with the minister emphasizing that the absence of a regulatory framework had created uncertainty for potential developers of wind power as well as solar, wave, or tidal power. Parliament passed the Offshore Renewable Energy Bill on July 1, 2026, addressing the need for the regulatory framework. The legislation governing the construction, operation, and decommissioning of offshore renewable energy developments officially became law in early August. It established a two-stage permitting regime, which the government asserted would give potential developers greater certainty. It established the requirements for consultation, as well as requirements for decommissioning at the cost of the permit holder and transmission owners, and the safety rules.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/c.text: The court-appointed government administrator reports that it signed the final documents to conclude the sale of the Pula area shipbuilding facilities of Uljanik Brodogradnja 1856 to the Turkish-owned shipbuilder Kuzey Star. With a commitment from the buyer to retain the core shipbuilding activities at the facilities, including construction, repair, and overhaul, the Croatian officials said the deal marks a new chapter in the region’s long heritage in shipbuilding and restores a key industry. Uljanik had been a major employer and economic driver for the region before the yard fell on hard financial times starting in 2019. It had declined to about 250 employees with an equal number of subcontractors but went into bankruptcy proceedings. The creditors had attempted to sell, in 2023 and 2024, the approximately 55 percent stake of the company held privately before the government stepped in to take control of the company. The plan called for stabilizing and restructuring the operation while getting employees their back pay. Coratia’s Center for Restructuring and Sale (CERP) announced in June its plan to auction the shipbuilding company with a minimum price of €11.08 million. It said the four combined interests, which represented more than 97 percent ownership, had a combined value of more than €34 million. It was offering for sale the existing shipbuilding infrastructure and concession rights for the operation, but the government retains ownership of the land in the Bay of Pula. CERP reported that nine companies had requested the bidding packet, but only two proposals were received when the tender window closed in September. One offer, from Luxembourg-based Mira Finance Holding, was deemed invalid because CERP said it had not completed the bond requirements. Kuzey Star bid €12.05 million ($13.9 million) for the operations of Uljanik Brodogradnja 1856. CERP said it accepted the offer but noted that because the company was not within the European Union, it would be required to carry out a foreign investment screening procedure before the deal could be completed. “By signing this contract, Croatia is approaching the completion of the process of revitalizing the shipbuilding industry in the Pula area,” commented the Minister of the Economy, Ante Susnjar.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) deve enviar ao Congresso Nacional nesta quarta-feira (21) a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê tarifa zero para transporte coletivo aos finais de semana em todo o país. Lula anunciou a medida na semana passada, a dez dias das eleições do segundo turno, e afirmou que o custo da medida será compensado pela dinuição de emendas parlamentares. https://gcaptain.com/trumps-plan-to-revi.text: Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins (Bloomberg) — A US plan to rehabilitate sanctioned tankers to boost oil supply may attract only a sliver of the dark fleet , as existing contracts, complex compliance checks and sky-high freight rates reduce incentives for would-be sellers. The measure — detailed on Monday, just weeks ahead of the US midterm elections — is the latest in a string of efforts by the Trump administration to cool crude and fuel prices driven higher by months of war in the Persian Gulf and the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Soaring gasoline and diesel costs in particular have fueled affordability concerns among US voters. But with limited numbers of sanctioned supertankers actually available and would-be sellers unwilling to forgo lucrative crossings in the Middle East, industry analysts say the effort to revive so-called dark vessels may struggle to gain traction. “Sanctions relief does not equal immediately usable mainstream tanker capacity,” said Rahul Kapoor, global head of shipping analytics and research for S&P Global Energy. “The number of vessels that could realistically migrate back into mainstream trading would likely be materially smaller than the overall sanctioned fleet.” Under the US proposal, blacklisted vessels can be sold and rejoin the legitimate fleet, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Monday, adding the government would “convert” tankers to expand global availability but would not lift existing sanctions. He did not detail the sale process or potential investors.

East Asia Bunker operations at Zhoushan’s outer anchorages have been suspended since earlier today because of rough weather brought by Typhoon Champi, and disruptions are expected over the next few days, a source said. Availability remains strained despite low demand, with suppliers recommending lead times of around 11 days for VLSFO, LSMGO and HSFO. Supply conditions remain mixed across other Chinese ports. Suppliers are recommending lead times of 4-5 days for VLSFO, LSMGO and HSFO in Qingdao, Tianjin and Xiamen. In Nansha, VLSFO and LSMGO are available for delivery within 4-5 days. https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/por.text: Ports and terminals are no strangers to reinvention. Over the past 50 years, the industry has managed and adapted to the shift to containerization and ever-larger vessels, the move from paper manifests to electronic messaging and transactions, and the subsequent evolution to system-to-system integration with other parties in the shipping industries. But many port functions still run on clipboards, radio calls, or the gut instincts of a planner, who has watched the yard fill up and empty thousands of times. That is most visible at smaller terminals and in bulk ports. AI is the next wave, and this time it reaches the clipboard. It arrives as pressure builds from beyond the docks. The freight forwarders, logistics providers, and container liners that are a terminal’s customers are among the companies now investing heavily in AI, with spending across industries expected to increase over time. To assess how far the industry has come, BCG and TIC4.0 (an international nonprofit association of terminal operators and equipment and solution providers dedicated to the creation and promotion of digital standards for the cargo-handling industry) surveyed more than 100 leaders from across the container ports and terminals ecosystem. (See the sidebar, “Survey Demographics.”) AI is no longer an experiment at the edge of the business. On average, those we surveyed are already using or exploring the top 16 of the 43 use cases we assessed, from extracting data from shipping documents (62%) to predicting when a crane or straddle carrier will fail (48%). Survey Demographics In August 2026, BCG and the Terminal Industry Committee 4.0 (TIC4.0) surveyed the port and terminal ecosystem on the adoption of AI and generative AI, to establish where the industry sees the opportunity and where it sees the risk. Respondents were 103 experts across five continents, drawn from terminal operators, port authorities, container liners, and port vendors. They operate at regional, national, and global scale, and their companies are balanced across small (less than $1 billion in revenue), midsize ($1 billion to $8 billion), and large (more than $8 billion). The decision to adopt AI has been largely made across the industry. What it is worth has not been settled. The work now is to prove what it delivers, and to do it faster than the competition. https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: Norway has unveiled plans to procure up to 20 standardized government vessels that are designed to strengthen the capabilities of three allied nations, a development that comes amidst rising security threats - specifically from Russia. The novel procurement plan will put a Norwegian authority in charge of buying naval vessels for use by Lithuania and the UK. The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) said that it is looking to identify shipyards both from Norway and across Europe that could be awarded the contract for the 20 vessels. While FMA is hoping to attract interest from a wide range of yards, the agency intends to split the procurement into two separate contracts in order to foster competition, diversify its supplier base, and ensure that the program has enough capability behind it to scale up. In the planned shipbuilding project, FMA intends to procure the 20 vessels for Norway, the UK and Lithuania. Six of the vessels will be constructed for the Norwegian Coast Guard and four of the vessels for the country’s Navy. Six vessels that will be based on the naval variant will be built for the UK and four for Lithuania. While FMA said it intends to award the contracts in 2027 with the first delivery expected in 2030, the agency did not provide detailed specifications. “We have chosen to start with the large, ocean-going vessels to ensure progress while meeting the needs of our allies in the UK and Lithuania. At the same time, we will spend the necessary time on further developing the smaller vessels,” said Marte Gerhardsen, State Secretary. The agency said that it is reaching out early in the process because it wants to provide the industrial base with early insight into the shipbuilding contract, hoping to attract broad participation from shipyards and reduce procurement risk.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Commodity intelligence firm Kpler reports that oil flows out of the Arabian Gulf have rebounded so well that they now exceed levels seen before the start of the U.S.-Israel-Iran war. By Kpler's count, the GCC states are now moving about 24 million barrels per day out of the region, including volumes transported by overland pipeline. The resurgence can be attributed in large part to the U.S.-protected shipping lane through the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz, which is now moving about 14 million barrels per day of crude oil, despite the constant risk of Iranian attack. The hazard level is high, but day rates are as well, and strong earnings have attracted a growing number of tankers in the market despite regular drone and missile strikes. A "Hormuz Shuttle Service" of short-haul tankers provides the backbone, carrying Gulf crude to Fujairah for transfer to other vessels, but there are others as well; TankerTrackers.com counts several hundred ships engaged in various aspects of the trade. The restoration of Arabian Gulf exports has been done without Iran, which remains cut off by a U.S. Navy blockade. With no sign of progress in peace negotiations, that naval mission is expected to continue. The U.S. Navy flotilla in the Arabian Sea is getting reinforcement soon from the carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and her escorts, now under way from Japan to the Mideast, U.S. officials confirmed to Fox News' Liz Friden on Tuesday. The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group - comprised of amphibs USS Makin Island , USS Anchorage and USS John P. Murtha - is also under way from San Diego to join the task force near the Gulf of Oman. The arrival of more Navy assets could allow the ships on station to rotate out, putting less strain on the overall fleet, or provide more capacity for airstrikes after the midterm elections. Despite higher flows out of the Gulf, oil prices remain well above $100 per barrel, reflecting the extreme day rates for VLCCs and Suezmax tankers. The cost of delivering oil out of the Gulf to Asia now exceeds $35 per barrel, creating a market dynamic where transport cost effectively drives the price of crude. The Trump administration hopes to address this by boosting the availability of tanker tonnage: its plan is to create a path to resale and legitimacy for hundreds of "shadow fleet" tankers operating in sanctioned trades. But market watchers are skeptical whether this plan can scale: shadow fleet tankers are already quite profitable in their current role, and relatively few qualified candidates are available (and insurable), multiple analysts told Bloomberg this week.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/l.text: At a time of heightened tensions between the Philippines and China, the Independence-class LCS USS Charleston conducted a transit near Sabina Shoal, a contested reef within the boundaries of the Philippine exclusive economic zone and China's overlapping "nine dash line" claim. China's military interpreted the maneuver as a challenge to Beijing's sovereignty and issued a statement of protest. PLA Southern Theater Command spokesman Yin Gang said in a statement that USS Charleston had "illegally intruded" into waters next to Sabina Shoal, and that China's military had dispatched units to track and monitor the American ship. Zhang Junshe, a researcher at the PLA Naval Military Academic Research Institute and a frequent commentator in Chinese state media, told Global Times that Charleston's transit was calculated to show support for the Philippines and challenge "China's sovereignty in the South China Sea." He emphasized that the PLA has the capability to swiftly detect and track what it considers to be "unauthorized intrusions." The encounter comes amidst a diplomatic dustup over language used by the Chinese ambassador to Manila last week. In an interview on the 15th, Ambassador Jing Quan told Philippine media that China could "easily win" if it chose to use force to pursue its claims. "We should feel fortunate enough that you have a neighbor like China in this region. If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we’ll not use force. We love peace," Jing said. At least 10 Philippine lawmakers have called for Jing to be declared persona non grata and sent back to China. Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro summoned him on Monday to register the government's objections. "Secretary Lazaro told the Ambassador that the statement was provocative and unacceptable, and does not contribute to creating understanding," the ministry said in a statement.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543818-oe.text: OEG Marine Services has ordered three additional crew transfer vessels (CTVs) from Diverse Marine, expanding its offshore wind support fleet under a newbuilding program scheduled for delivery throughout 2027. The vessels will be built to the BREVITY SL Class design developed by Chartwell Marine, with each measuring 26 metres in overall length and having a load line length of less than 24 metres. All three CTVs will be constructed to the same specification, classed by Bureau Veritas and operated under the UK flag. The vessels will feature quad Volvo Penta IPS propulsion compliant with IMO Tier III emissions standards, alongside Hull Vane transom foils designed to improve fuel efficiency at cruising speeds. The contract marks the second collaboration between OEG and Diverse Marine, following the delivery of the OEG Fulmar in 2025. The three new vessels will support OEG's fleet renewal and expansion programme, with the company planning to deploy them in offshore wind operations from 2027.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543816-pe.text: Oil and gas company Perenco has restarted production at the Foukanda field offshore Congo following the installation of new infrastructure connecting the field directly to its own facilities. Production resumed on September 15 at a rate of 2,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), Perenco said. The restart follows a six-month infrastructure project involving the installation of a new 13-kilometre pipeline and a high-voltage power cable. According to Perenco, the project was completed safely, on schedule and within budget, with equipment redeployed from its operations in Congo and Gabon to accelerate execution. The Foukanda field, located approximately 52 kilometres offshore Pointe-Noire, was discovered in March 1998 and previously operated by Eni before Perenco acquired the asset in March 2024. Before the infrastructure upgrade, Foukanda relied on facilities operated by its previous operator to export production through the Kitina platform and a 14-inch pipeline connected to the Djeno terminal.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543815-te.text: TechnipFMC and BP have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore cooperation on the supply of high-pressure subsea production systems for BP's Paleogene oil developments in the U.S. Gulf. The agreement, announced on October 20, establishes a framework for the potential supply of subsea tree systems rated for pressures of up to 20,000 pounds per square inch (20K). Signed with BP Exploration & Production, a subsidiary of BP, the MoU will allow the companies to identify early project opportunities and collaborate on technology development. The cooperation is intended to improve project scheduling and delivery through the use of standardized 20K subsea equipment. "The MoU reflects our commitment to advancing the deployment of standardized 20K solutions. By combining proven technologies with repeatable and systematic project delivery, TechnipFMC can help improve predictability and performance across future developments," said Doug Pferdehirt, Chair and CEO of TechnipFMC. The agreement comes as BP advances two major Paleogene developments in the U.S. Gulf - Kaskida and Tiber-Guadalupe.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543817-no.text: Perenco UK has completed the decommissioning of the Leman South and Durango subsea assets in the UK Southern North Sea, using Petrodec's HAEVA jack-up vessel to plug and abandon the wells and remove associated subsea infrastructure. The two projects were executed under a single campaign framework in collaboration with Petrodec, a decommissioning specialist within the Dixstone group. The campaign covered the Leman South (53/02a-15Y) and Durango (48/21a-4z) subsea wells, including plugging and abandonment (P&A) operations and recovery of their associated subsea infrastructure. Perenco said the technically complex operations were completed safely and within the agreed timeframe. The work builds on previous subsea abandonment campaigns at the Gawain, Arthur and Davy assets, which were also carried out using Petrodec's HAEVA jack-up. "The Leman South and Durango campaigns were not routine P&A projects. They demonstrated Perenco's ability to deliver repeatable, large-scale, technically complex subsea well abandonment and infrastructure recovery using an innovative single campaign approach centred on Petrodec's HAEVA, rather than relying exclusively on high-cost drilling rigs and standalone offshore projects,” said Jo White, Perenco UK's Southern North Sea Managing Director.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543812-wo.text: Australia's Woodside Energy on Wednesday trimmed the top end of its annual production forecast and said it would scale back its investment in a lower-carbon ammonia project in the US due to slower demand. The country's top independent oil and gas producer now expects annual production of 174 to 181 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), down from its earlier forecast of 174 to 185 million boe. The scaled-back ammonia investment is the latest step back from clean energy at Woodside, which under CEO Liz Westcott has abandoned its longer-term emissions target and canned $5 billion in planned lower carbon spending. The Beaumont New Ammonia plant in Texas brought in lower-than-expected volumes for the quarter, with production constrained to 69% of capacity due to third-party feedstock availability and a 30-day shutdown following a safety incident. Woodside said it would reduce its investment in the plant after completing a strategic review that found customer demand was slower than expected. "The policy frameworks that were going to enable the lower carbon ammonia to be part of that market are also shifting," Westcott added.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543811-va.text: Norway's Vaar Energi raised its cash dividend for a second consecutive quarter on Wednesday and reported a doubling of its third-quarter operating profit from a year earlier, supported by higher oil and gas prices. The company reported its July-September earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) at $2.21 billion, up from $1.1 billion a year ago, slightly bellow the average $2.26 billion forecast in a company-compiled poll of 10 analysts. "We are pleased to report strong financial results in the third quarter of 2026, which is supported by high realised oil and gas prices," Vaar's CEO Nick Walker said in a statement. Vaar said it would pay $400 million in dividend in both the third and fourth quarters of 2026 with an "extraordinary component", up from $350 million for the second quarter and $300 million for the first quarter of 2026. Vaar maintained its long-term production guidance at 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boed) and maintained 2026 development capital spending guidance at $2.5 billion-$2.7 billion. Vaar said on October 12 it expected full-year 2026 production to be at 390,000 boepd, at the low end of its previous guidance of 390,000-410,000 boepd due to operational issues at several fields.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543814-ch.text: Egypt and Chevron have signed an agreement establishing the fiscal framework for developing and connecting Cyprus’ offshore Aphrodite gas to Egyptian gas infrastructure, marking another step towards transporting gas from the Eastern Mediterranean field to Egypt. The agreement, signed on October 20, forms part of efforts to finalize the financial, commercial and regulatory arrangements needed to advance the Aphrodite development and its connection to Egyptian gas facilities. It forms part of efforts to finalize the financial, commercial and regulatory arrangements needed to advance the Aphrodite development and its connection to Egyptian gas facilities. Under the proposed development, gas from Aphrodite would be transported to Egypt for domestic consumption or processing and liquefaction for export, depending on market demand and project economics. The agreement was initialled by Mohamed El-Bagoury, head of the Egyptian petroleum ministry's Central Administration for Legal Affairs, and Javier La Rosa, Chevron's President of Base Assets and Emerging Countries. Chevron operates the Aphrodite field with a 35% interest, alongside Shell with 35% and Israel's NewMed Energy with 30%.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543810-sh.text: The U.K. government has approved the Jackdaw offshore gas field operated by Adura, a joint venture between Shell and Equinor, clearing the way for the project to begin supplying gas within weeks. The decision, announced by Adura on October 21, follows a regulatory review by the Offshore Petroleum Regulator for Environment and Decommissioning (OPRED), including public consultation and an assessment of environmental evidence. Adura said the $2.8 billion (£2.1 billion) Jackdaw development could produce enough gas at peak output to heat the equivalent of approximately 1.4 million UK homes. The approval allows the project to move towards supplying gas to UK households, power stations and businesses, with the company expecting supplies to begin within weeks. "This decision is an important and positive step forward for Adura and for the future of UK energy. It provides certainty to the businesses and skilled workers already delivering the project and demonstrates the value of pragmatic, evidence-led decision-making," said Neil McCulloch, CEO of Adura. The company is also awaiting a regulatory decision on the Rosebank offshore development, which follows Jackdaw in the approval process.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/uk_greenlig.text: UK Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has greenlit the Jackdaw gas field, a statement posted on the UK government website today revealed. Jackdaw will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from the end of this month after Fahnbulleh agreed that the regulator - the North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) - can grant consent for gas to be produced at the field, according to the statement. The statement noted that the Jackdaw decision is expected to increase domestic gas production by around six percent at its peak, “supporting the UK’s gas supply over its lifespan of up to 11 years, boosting our energy security, protecting hundreds of jobs, and adding an estimated GBP 2.9 billion [$3.8 billion] to the UK economy”. This statement highlighted that recent events in the Middle East “have triggered global energy shocks and pushed up bills for families across the country”. It pointed out that, “at a time of global instability, homegrown energy can be a source of national strength”. Jackdaw’s green light comes as the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healy, announced a new Energy Wealth Fund, which the statement said will use tax revenues from North Sea oil and gas to invest in renewable and low carbon energy projects and “support the green transition”. “Reflecting our commitment to the North Sea, this will start with an initial GBP 2 billion [$2.6 billion] injection of funding, with future revenues from the North Sea flowing into the fund over time,” the statement revealed.

https://safety4sea.com/fire-breaks-out-o.text: A fire broke out aboard the Indonesian passenger ferry KMP Batumandi on October 20, 2026, as the vessel approached Merak Port in Cilegon, Banten, prompting an emergency evacuation and firefighting operation that continued into the following day. T he ferry was traveling from Bakauheni Port in Lampung to Merak when the fire was reported at approximately 16:15 local time, near Pulau Merak Besar. According to operator PT ASDP Indonesia Ferry, sparks were initially observed near the stern, on the upper vehicle deck, while the vessel was preparing to berth. The cause remains undetermined. The ferry was reportedly carrying 420 passengers, 40 crew members and 89 vehicles. All passengers and crew were safely evacuated, with no fatalities reported, although 11 people required medical treatment following the incident. Firefighting operations continued on October 21, with tugboats and patrol vessels spraying water onto the vessel as smoke continued to rise. Particular attention was given to cooling the vehicle deck, which contained cars, motorcycles, buses and trucks. A small fire reportedly reignited on Wednesday morning before being extinguished, while cooling operations continued to prevent further flare-ups. At least eight vessels participated in the response. Indonesia’s Ministry of Transportation confirmed that the National Transportation Safety Committee (KNKT) and police were investigating the circumstances of the incident.

https://safety4sea.com/new-energy-effici.text: The Global Centre for Maritime Decarbonisation (GCMD), AIM Horizon Investments and Eastern Pacific Shipping (EPS) have announced the first deployment of the Fund for Energy Efficiency Technologies (FEET), financing wind-assisted propulsion systems on two EPS vessels. F EET’s first deployment covers wind-assisted propulsion systems (WAPS) installed on MV Pacific Sentinel and MV Pacific Sunstone. Each vessel is equipped with three 22-meter suction sails, making them the first ships in the EPS fleet to adopt the technology. FEET is described as the world’s first fund to link verified fuel and regulatory savings from onboard energy efficiency technologies to a pay-as-you-save financing mechanism. The fund offers up to 100% upfront financing through a blended finance structure, seeking to reduce the initial investment burden for shipowners adopting energy-saving technologies. It is managed by AIM Horizon Investments, with GCMD serving as its decarbonization advisor. The initiative is supported by the Development Bank of Japan, DBS Bank and ING. The first deployment builds on an earlier collaboration between GCMD and EPS to develop a methodology for measuring fuel savings from the WAPS installed on MV Pacific Sentinel. To distinguish the technology’s contribution from changes in operational conditions, GCMD collected 276 million data points over four months of spot-market trading in the Americas, between mid-May and mid-September 2025.

https://safety4sea.com/ore-carrier-suffe.text: The Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Aquacharm, carrying 170,856 metric tons of iron ore from Australia, struck a wharf under construction at the Hoa Phat Dung Quat iron and steel complex in Vietnam’s Quang Ngai Province on October 18, 2026. T he 292-meter-long vessel, with a deadweight tonnage of 182,309 metric tons, collided with a 50-meter section connecting wharves No. 10 and No. 11 while maneuvering toward its assigned berth. The impact damaged both sides of the vessel’s bow, including a tear measuring approximately five meters, and caused damage to the wharf. All 22 crew members were reported safe, and no oil spill was detected, according to the Dung Quat Border Guard Station. Despite the collision, the vessel continued maneuvering and reached wharf No. 10 at approximately 6:30 pm. Its iron ore cargo was subsequently unloaded, while other port facilities remained operational and production at the complex continued normally. Preliminary information provided by the vessel’s captain and shipping agent suggests that difficulties controlling the vessel’s speed and communication errors involving the pilot may have contributed to the collision. However, the cause has not yet been established. Following the incident, the Quang Ngai Maritime Administration ordered additional safety measures due to adverse weather conditions, including a tropical depression and strong northeasterly monsoon winds.

https://safety4sea.com/singapore-warns-s.text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) has issued a notice reminding the maritime community of restrictions on unmanned aircraft operations over Singapore Port Waters, following two incidents in which crew members were fined for flying drones near Changi Airport without the required permits. I n Port Marine Notice No. 136 of 2026, dated October 14, the MPA referred shipping companies, harbor craft operators and pleasure craft users to an October 1 notification from the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), highlighting the aviation safety risks associated with unauthorized unmanned aircraft (UA) activities. The CAAS warning covers drones, radio-controlled aircraft and remote-controlled kites, emphasizing that operators must comply with applicable aviation regulations before conducting such activities over Singapore’s port waters. The CAAS notice details two enforcement cases involving seafarers operating drones for recreational purposes from tankers anchored within five kilometers of Changi Airport. In the first case, on June 8, 2026, a 46-year-old crew member aboard a locally registered bunker tanker was found operating a drone at an altitude of 42.7 meters in the Eastern Petroleum Bravo Anchorage, approximately 3.2 kilometers from Changi Airport. The crew member did not have the required permit and was subsequently convicted and fined SGD 5,000, with 10 days’ imprisonment stipulated in default of payment.

https://safety4sea.com/fleet-management-.text: Fleet Management has highlighted the need for maritime training to evolve alongside emerging technologies, alternative fuels and increasingly complex operational requirements, stressing that competence development must begin well before new vessels enter service. S peaking in connection with Seatrade Maritime Crew Connect Global 2026 , Capt. Somasundar Nair, Executive Director of Fleet Management Limited, emphasised that the ongoing STCW review provides an opportunity to strengthen training standards and prepare seafarers for future operational challenges. The challenge is no longer just attracting people into shipping. It is helping good people keep pace with the rate of change. Future readiness cannot begin when vessels are delivered. It has to start well ahead, with training and development, The ongoing comprehensive review of the STCW Convention and Code provides an opportunity to address evolving competence requirements, particularly as shipping adopts alternative fuels, digital systems and increasingly sophisticated onboard technologies. As previously reported by SAFETY4SEA , the IMO Sub-Committee on Human Element, Training and Watchkeeping (HTW 12) advanced the comprehensive STCW review in February 2026, moving into the second phase focused on developing amendments to address identified gaps. The review comes amid wider discussions about balancing new competence requirements with practical training needs. In a recent SAFETY4SEA opinion, Apo Belokas argued that the review should consider removing outdated or unnecessary requirements alongside introducing new ones.

https://safety4sea.com/bgn-strengthens-l.text: BGN has signed a contract with HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HD HHI) for four additional 93,000 cubic meter LPG dual-fuel Very Large Gas Carriers (VLGCs), expanding its owned fleet and investment in dual-fuel shipping. T he agreement was signed in Istanbul on October 14, 2026. The vessels will be constructed in South Korea, with delivery scheduled for January 2030. Once delivered, the newbuildings will increase BGN’s owned LPG VLGC fleet from 19 to 23 vessels. The company currently operates a fleet of more than 40 owned and chartered vessels. The latest contract brings BGN’s total orders for dual-fuel VLGCs placed with HD HHI during 2026 to 10 vessels. The orders include four 90,000 cbm VLGCs announced in April , followed by two 93,000 cbm vessels in June and the latest four 93,000 cbm vessels ordered in October. All four vessels covered by the latest agreement will feature dual-fuel propulsion systems, allowing them to operate on LPG alongside conventional marine fuels. According to BGN, this technology supports more efficient shipping operations and aligns with its broader commitment to maritime decarbonization. We are excited by the pace at which BGN is growing its shipping fleet. By accelerating investment in state-of-the-art vessels, we are building the capacity needed to support our strategic growth and diversify our global energy portfolio The latest agreement builds on BGN’s longstanding partnership with HD HHI and forms part of its strategy to expand its owned shipping capacity and support the growth of its global LPG trading operations.

https://safety4sea.com/new-framework-hel.text: As ports prepare to accommodate ships powered by alternative fuels, MissionGreenFuels has released a new guideline to support the safe introduction of methanol, ammonia and hydrogen into port operations. T he Guideline for Safe Storage, Bunkering and Usage of Green Fuels in Port Facilities is the final output of the SafeSBU project, developed by DBI, FORCE Technology and Aalborg University in collaboration with industry partners. It provides a common risk-based framework for port authorities, shipowners, bunker suppliers, terminal operators and emergency services, addressing safety throughout the fuel handling chain. The maritime industry is turning towards low-carbon fuels, and many ports are asking the same questions: What are the risks? How do we demonstrate that operations are safe? And how do we coordinate across the many organizations involved? This guideline provides a common language and a structured approach to answering those questions The guideline emphasizes that methanol, ammonia and hydrogen have different hazard profiles , requiring fuel-specific risk assessments and corresponding safety measures. It introduces an eight-layer safety framework covering hazard identification, risk evaluation, safety barriers, operational controls, emergency preparedness, competence, governance and public perception. Particular attention is given to bunkering operations, where coordination between vessels, suppliers and port facilities is essential. The publication addresses transfer equipment compatibility, emergency shutdown systems, leak detection, operating procedures and simultaneous operations (SIMOPS).

https://safety4sea.com/eu-unveils-new-ar.text: The European Commission has presented a new Arctic Strategy, placing maritime security, critical infrastructure protection and enhanced surveillance among its priorities as climate change and geopolitical competition reshape the region. U nveiled on 20 October 2026 by the European Commission and the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, the strategy establishes a new framework for cooperation with Arctic partners, focusing on security, climate change, economic prosperity and local communities. The initiative responds to significant changes in the Arctic since the EU’s previous policy was adopted in 2021. As the region warms nearly four times faster than the global average, retreating ice is opening access to new shipping routes and natural resources, while increasing strategic competition and military activity. According to the Commission, the evolving environment requires stronger preparedness, resilient infrastructure and closer cooperation to safeguard European interests and support Arctic communities. Today, we adopt our new Arctic Strategy. The Arctic is where the tectonic plates of geopolitics collide head-on. It requires us to change our strategic posture. And work with like-minded partners that share our values ↓ https://t.co/B6GvgUOCQk With our new Strategy, we are investing in stronger security, resilient infrastructure and economic opportunities. For the benefit of the people who call the Arctic home, and for our shared space

https://splash247.com/nato-boosts-black-.text: NATO is deploying additional maritime patrol aircraft, drones and radar systems to the Black Sea following a series of deadly attacks on merchant shipping off Romania and Bulgaria. The move follows a meeting of the alliance’s North Atlantic Council in Brussels on Tuesday, with members also sending intelligence personnel and explosives investigation teams to the region. NATO military spokesman colonel Martin O’Donnell said the additional assets would strengthen surveillance and reconnaissance, with the emphasis on improving intelligence sharing and identifying threats to shipping. Bulgaria has already confirmed that a US Navy P-8 Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft has begun reconnaissance flights over the Black Sea following its request for assistance from NATO. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev said allies had responded quickly to Sofia’s appeal, with further support expected. Four merchant ships have been attacked in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone over the past month, two of which sank. Allied specialists are also expected to help investigate the October 13 drone attack on the Malta-flagged general cargoship Chelsea 3 off Bulgaria. All 15 crewmembers were rescued, and investigators are examining recovered drone debris to establish the type of weapon used.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/su.text: Motoristas de ônibus que eram geridos pela empresa Transwolff, em São Paulo, afirmam que irão realizar uma nova paralisação a partir da meia-noite desta quarta-feira (21) . Porém, o advogado Emerson Silva, que representa os motoristas, confirmou, na manhã desta quarta, que ela a greve foi adiada para semana que vem. De acordo com Silva, o prefeito teria considerado a ação ilegal e informou que quem participasse da manifestação poderia sofrer "sanções". "Diante disso, para evitar maiores infortúnios, os trabalhadores resolveram adiar a greve para a semana que vem", concluiu Silva. Segundo o grupo, houve retaliação contra os funcionários, através de pelo menos três demissões por justa causa após a paralisação realizada na última segunda-feira (19), e falta de comprovação dos pagamentos do INSS. A SPTrans afirma, na manhã desta quarta, que todas as linhas operam normalmente e que não há informação de paralisação . A Transwolff opera sob intervenção da prefeitura desde dezembro do ano passado, após suspeitas de envolvimento da empresa com o PCC (Primeiro Comando da Capital) . Segundo Júnior Araújo, motorista e integrante da liderança da categoria, a SPTrans entregou um documento aos trabalhadores, mas o material não respondia a nenhuma das questões discutidas durante a greve .

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/br.text: A influenciadora digital Malévola Alves foi presa no Egito , junto com uma amiga, após uma investigação sobre vídeos que circulavam nas redes sociais. As imagens reveladas pelas autoridades do país mostram a dupla fazendo gestos e dançando. Ainda segundo o governo egípcio, a dupla brasileira fez supostos comentários insinuantes e 'assediando' pessoas no local. A informação foi divulgada pelo Ministério do Interior do Egito nesta terça-feira (20). Segundo as autoridades, as duas mulheres foram presas em Alexandria . País é conhecido por ações arbitrárias contra mulheres e comunidade LGBTQIA+ , segundo a ONU (Organização das Nações Unidas). Em uma publicação, o órgão também divulgou os vídeos que motivaram a investigação . Veja: Ainda de acordo com a pasta, durante o interrogatório, as duas confessaram os atos descritos e admitiram ter gravado e publicado os vídeos nas redes sociais com o objetivo de aumentar o número de visualizações. Em nota, a defesa da influenciadora, identificada como Mariana Alves Gadelha Pereira e conhecida publicamente como Malévola , informou que já está em contato com a Embaixada do Brasil no Cairo e com as autoridades e os órgãos competentes para garantir a integridade física das brasileiras . Os procedimentos legais foram iniciados, e o Ministério Público egípcio conduz a investigação . A CNN Brasil tenta contato com o Itamaraty, o espaço segue aberto.

https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/n.text: Por Betinho Casas Novas, Filipe Brasil , Lucas Soares , Rafael Nascimento , g1 Rio e TV Globo Câmeras e depoimentos reconstituem a perseguição que causou a morte do secretário de Queimados Jefferson da Silva, 51, na Avenida Brasil, nesta segunda-feira (19).

Um vídeo de segurança registrou uma perseguição policial e tiroteio que resultou na morte de um suspeito nesta quarta-feira (21), em Botafogo. O tiroteio ocorreu na Rua São Clemente. Policiais civis agiram para localizar um envolvido no ataque a uma arqueóloga de 80 anos no Leblon. O homem morto foi identificado como Luis Fernando Rodrigues dos Santos. Segundo investigações da Polícia Civil, ele possuía 27 passagens policiais. Agentes tentaram abordar o veículo, mas o motorista tentou atropelá-los e atirou. Policiais revidaram, matando o condutor e ferindo uma passageira com estilhaços. Por causa da ocorrência, uma faixa da via foi interditada. O trânsito registrou retenções e motoristas precisaram buscar rotas alternativas na região.

Uma perseguição policial terminou em tiroteio e acidentes em Botafogo nesta quarta-feira (21). Agentes buscavam um envolvido em tentativa de assalto no Leblon. O automóvel de Paulo Roberto foi atingido pelo veículo de Luis Fernando Rodrigues dos Santos, de 28 anos. Ele era perseguido por policiais civis. Após a batida, o motorista ouviu disparos e lutou para manter o controle do carro. Ele conseguiu parar em segurança e não se feriu.

Um transplante de coração nesta quarta-feira (21) mobilizou o Palácio Guanabara, sede do governo do RJ. Às 12h15, um helicóptero pousou no estádio do Olaria para buscar o órgão. Ele foi captado no Hospital Getúlio Vargas. O destino do órgão era o Instituto de Cardiologia Laranjeiras. O plano previa pousar no heliponto do Palácio Guanabara.

Luis Fernando Rodrigues dos Santos, de 28 anos, morreu após confronto com policiais civis em Botafogo nesta quarta-feira (21). O homem tinha 27 passagens pela polícia e era apontado como um dos chefes de uma quadrilha de roubos na Zona Sul. A investigação identificou Luis Fernando como envolvido na tentativa de latrocínio que baleou a arqueóloga Tania Andrade Lima, de 80 anos, no Leblon. Segundo a corporação, ele reagiu jogando o carro contra policiais e disparando, sendo atingido e morto durante a abordagem perto do Morro Santa Marta. Uma passageira ficou ferida por estilhaços e foi hospitalizada, enquanto a operação causou retenções no trânsito e interdição parcial na Rua São Clemente.

Segundo testemunhas, Jefferson estava em um BYD e teria desobedecido a uma ordem de parada policial. Ainda de acordo com os relatos, policiais dispararam contra o veículo. Em depoimento, quatro policiais admitiram ter efetuado disparos contra o carro.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (21) aponta que 44% dos eleitores temem a volta da família Bolsonaro. Outros 42% têm medo da reeleição de Lula. O medo de ambos os cenários subiu de 3% para 6%. Foram ouvidas 2.154 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais no levantamento. https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2026/.text: Especialistas da ONU cobraram nesta quarta-feira (21) que a Meta investigue se seus sistemas restringiram desproporcionalmente conteúdos na eleição do Brasil. A cobrança ocorreu após relatos de usuários de que a inteligência artificial do WhatsApp recusava criar imagens de Lula (PT), mas aceitava de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Cobrada pelo TSE, a empresa afirmou na terça-feira (20) ter cumprido as exigências da Corte para assegurar tratamento isonômico no 2º turno. Para os observadores, as plataformas digitais são "atores fundamentais no debate democrático". Restringir contas afeta o acesso à informação e a liberdade de associação.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: Por Márcio Falcão , Ana Flávia Castro , Isabela Camargo , TV Globo e g1 — Brasília O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques , e o vice-presidente da Corte, André Mendonça , discutiram com colegas a possibilidade de impor restrições a canais de WhatsApp com mais de 200 mil usuários nas 48 horas anteriores ao segundo turno das eleições, no próximo domingo (25). A proposta, que foi debatida nos últimos dias e dividiu a Corte, atingiria canais como o "Exército do Lula" , que conta com quase 8 milhões de seguidores, e o canal "Tropa do Flávio", que tem 2,7 milhões. Nas últimas semanas, o canal de mensagens liderado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) gerou embates no cenário político do segundo turno e virou alvo de disputas judiciais entre as campanhas (relembre mais abaixo).

https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2.text: A pesquisa Quaest mostra que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) seguem tecnicamente empatados na disputa pela Presidência a dias do 2º turno. O dado mais impressionante da pesquisa é aquele que abre o questionário: o voto espontâneo, avalia Felipe Nunes, diretor da Quaest e professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV). Neste ponto, Flávio e Lula têm o mesmo % de intenção de voto: 40%. Entre os independentes, a indecisão saiu de 13% para 31%. Sinalização clara de descontentamento com as opções e com a campanha negativa que vem sendo apresentada.

A nova pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (21) mostra que 47% dos entrevistados desaprovam o governo Lula, enquanto 46% aprovam. Em relação à pesquisa anterior, a desaprovação oscilou um ponto para baixo, e a aprovação, um ponto para cima. 38% têm avaliação negativa do governo (eram 40% na pesquisa anterior), 34% têm avalição positiva e 26% consideram o governo regular. O levantamento aponta também empate técnico na disputa pela Presidência. Flávio Bolsonaro registra 45% das intenções de voto e Lula tem 44%.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: O presidente Lula afirmou nesta quarta-feira (21) que pessoas pobres são boas pagadoras. A declaração ocorreu em evento sobre medidas para microempreendedores e transporte público. O presidente contrapôs o comportamento financeiro dos mais pobres ao dos ricos. Lula afirmou que "Tem muita gente rica que gosta de dever.". Ele justificou o perdão de dívidas de microempreendedores individuais. Segundo o presidente, o governo já avaliava que não receberia esses recursos. O presidente citou uma proposta de doação de R$ 5.000 para empreendedores iniciarem seus negócios. A medida ainda depende de aprovação do Congresso.

https://g1.globo.com/meio-ambiente/notic.text: As emissões de gases de efeito estufa do Brasil caíram 6% em 2025, atingindo o menor nível em 8 anos. O dado foi divulgado nesta terça-feira (20). As emissões líquidas recuaram 9%, somando 1,41 bilhão de toneladas. O volume ficou 6% acima da meta brasileira estabelecida no Acordo de Paris para 2025. Na agropecuária, as emissões registraram estabilidade, recuando 0,1%. O gado de corte responde por 66% das emissões diretas do setor agropecuário nacional.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543819-ma.text: Masirah Oil has started operations on the first well of its infill drilling campaign at the Yumna oil field offshore Oman, following several delays to the development program earlier in 2026. The company announced the start of operations on October 21, with production from the new well expected to begin in November 2026. "We expect production from the new well to start in November 2026," said Mike Hopkinson, General Manager of Masirah Oil. The drilling campaign is intended to increase oil production and extend the productive life of the Yumna field, located in offshore Block 50. The program had previously been scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2026 before being pushed back to May. In June, Masirah Oil said the start date would be revised again without providing a new timetable. The original development program comprised three production wells, with the company seeking to boost output and reserves from the offshore field.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A taxa de vacância dos condomínios logísticos de alto padrão no Brasil recuou para 4,2% no terceiro trimestre de 2026 , o menor índice da série histórica, segundo levantamento da Colliers. No mesmo período, a absorção bruta atingiu o recorde de 1,5 milhão de m², indicando a continuidade da demanda por espaços logísticos, mesmo com o aumento da oferta. Entre julho e setembro, foram entregues 819 mil m² de novos espaços, volume 60% superior ao registrado no segundo trimestre. Com as incorporações, o inventário nacional chegou a 33,6 milhões de m², alta de 10% em 12 meses. Ainda assim, a procura absorveu os novos empreendimentos e contribuiu para a redução da disponibilidade de áreas. O comércio eletrônico permaneceu entre os principais motores da demanda. Empresas do segmento responderam por seis das dez maiores locações realizadas no trimestre, movimento associado à expansão das operações de distribuição e à busca por instalações capazes de atender grandes volumes e prazos de entrega menores. A baixa vacância também se reflete nos preços. O valor médio pedido de locação no país se aproxima de R$ 33/m² por mês, mantendo a trajetória de alta observada ao longo de 2026. Para Ricardo Betancourt, CEO da Colliers, a absorção dos novos empreendimentos demonstra que a demanda segue sustentando a expansão do setor. “A baixa oferta de espaços em ativos de alto padrão construtivo nos principais centros consumidores tem intensificado a competição por imóveis bem localizados”, afirma. Segundo o executivo, a expectativa para os próximos trimestres é de manutenção da vacância em níveis reduzidos e continuidade da pressão de alta sobre os aluguéis, tanto nas novas negociações quanto nos reajustes contratuais.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: A A.P. Moller - Maersk anunciou o abastecimento bem-sucedido de etanol no Maersk Halifax, em Singapura. O navio é o primeiro de propulsão dual fuel adaptada da companhia, e a operação marca a primeira vez que o combustível foi usado em uma embarcação dessa categoria na frota. A operação foi realizada em colaboração com a Autoridade Marítima e Portuária de Singapura (MPA) e outros parceiros. Envolveu o abastecimento de aproximadamente 5.000 toneladas métricas de bioetanol com certificação ISCC. Segundo a Maersk, a iniciativa gerou experiência operacional e informações sobre infraestrutura, fornecimento, prontidão da cadeia de suprimentos e operação de navios relacionadas ao uso do etanol como combustível marítimo. São pontos centrais para que combustíveis alternativos ganhem escala no setor. A companhia afirma que a ação reforça seu compromisso de longa data com a busca por múltiplos caminhos de combustíveis e tecnologias para descarbonizar o transporte oceânico. Para a empresa, o etanol se destaca como combustível de transição pela disponibilidade global, pelas redes de produção e distribuição já estabelecidas e pela compatibilidade com tecnologias de motores movidos a álcool. A Maersk ressalta ainda que, quando certificado e obtido por rotas de baixo carbono, o etanol pode proporcionar reduções significativas nas emissões de gases de efeito estufa em relação aos combustíveis marítimos convencionais. Emma Mazhari, diretora de Mercados de Energia da Maersk, afirmou que a transição energética exige explorar e ampliar soluções capazes de gerar impacto real. Segundo ela, a companhia mantém uma estratégia multicombustível porque nenhum caminho isolado consegue descarbonizar sozinho o transporte marítimo global.

https://gcaptain.com/two-more-tankers-st.text: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 31, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer Two more tankers have been struck by unidentified projectiles in separate incidents near the Strait of Hormuz and in the northern Persian Gulf, adding to a growing series of attacks on commercial shipping as maritime security conditions across the region continue to deteriorate. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported Wednesday that a tanker was struck approximately 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman, at 0145 UTC on October 21. The impact sparked a fire aboard the vessel, which has since been extinguished. The tanker is now at anchor, with all crew members reported safe and no environmental damage reported. In a separate incident, the master of another tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile approximately 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq, at 1830 UTC on October 20. UKMTO received the report after the incident occurred. All crew members were reported safe, with no damage to the vessel or environmental impact reported.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: U.S. ambitions to mine the deep sea are rapidly expanding across the ocean, not only in the country’s own waters, but also on the high seas — the vast expanse of ocean outside any one country’s jurisdiction. In the Clarion-Clipperton Zone of the Pacific Ocean, a hotspot of mining interest in international waters, a Mongabay analysis shows that companies have either applied to the U.S. or already been granted rights to areas of the seabed equal to about half the expanse already designated for mining activities by the international community. Most of the applications to the U.S. occurred within the past year and a half, a fraction of the 25 years the multilateral U.N.-affiliated International Seabed Authority (ISA) has spent issuing seabed mining exploration licenses. U.S. applicants are not only seeking rights to explore the deep seabed, but some are also applying for commercial recovery permits. If approved by the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), these recovery permits would allow the companies to extract and eventually sell the minerals. While the ISA can also accept mining exploitation applications, no company has yet submitted one to the organization. No other country or institution is known to unilaterally accept applications to mine in international waters, and commercial-scale seabed mining has not yet begun anywhere in the world. Deep-sea mining companies are interested in many parts of the international seabed, but Mongabay’s analysis focused on the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), an extensive stretch of the Pacific Ocean between Mexico and Hawai‘i that holds vast quantities of polymetallic nodules — mineral-rich rocks that resemble burnt potatoes. Mongabay’s analysis also revealed overlaps between claims in the CCZ. U.S. applicants are seeking rights to seabed areas that overlap with areas the ISA has already contracted, as well as areas the ISA holds in reserve for future mining and to benefit developing countries. There are overlaps between ISA and U.S. applicants, and overlaps between U.S. applicants. The scale and locations of the U.S. claims, as well as the potential overlaps, are raising legal and regulatory questions about who has authority over the seabed in international waters, which are global commons beyond any nation’s sole jurisdiction. Some experts expressed concern that a U.S. move to unilaterally permit mining in the high seas could weaken or even topple multilateral systems that have long governed the oceans. Others said the U.S. push to mine might also trigger a premature start of commercial mining. Forty-six countries have called to put the brakes on the industry due to concerns about the potential damage to the marine environment, the need for further research, and a lack of international rules

https://maritime-executive.com/article/r.text: Russian officials are indicating the country is ready to begin its promised exports of diesel fuel, with the first tanker ready to sail as early as Thursday. It comes as the political debate continues over the deal between Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, while analysts continue to downplay the impact of the Russian supply on the American and global markets. Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Alexander Novak, said the tanker could depart on Thursday, October 22, according to a report from the Russian news agency TASS. Few details were provided other than that it would consist of 40,000 metric tons (the equivalent of 300,000 barrels according to Bloomberg). The report did not specify the name of the vessel or where it had loaded, possibly for security reasons, nor where it would be headed in the United States. Novak is quoted as saying the contract signing for the deal between the United States and Russia is “nearing completion,” and that Russia could restore its normal volumes of diesel exports by the end of the year. He highlighted that exports would be completed “to the extent of our capabilities,” while also saying Russia could restore natural gas exports if Europe was willing. He talked of the potential of repairing the Nord Stream pipelines while noting that one of the four lines is still operable. Separate reports are quoting Vladimir Putin also saying the first diesel shipment could happen in two or three days. He also referenced the need to complete the financial agreement. Putin had agreed with Trump to initially supply 300,000 metric tons of diesel, with Trump saying the volume would be increased to 500,000 metric tons in November and reach 1 million tons shortly thereafter. Russia’s Novak has said the goal would be to reach 3.5 million tons of diesel production by the end of 2026, noting Russia could also start supplying diesel to other countries. Trump continues to insist that the deal is part of his efforts to negotiate a peace deal with Russia. His envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Russia on Wednesday and thanked Putin for his efforts. Commentators also believe Trump is rushing the deal before the U.S. midterm elections. The U.S. Treasury suspended sanctions authorizing diesel transactions until April 2027, while Trump suspended the Congressional-imposed sanctions and tariffs just days after the legislation had become law. U.S. officials have said the deal would help to alleviate pressure on the U.S. market for diesel, where the price for road transport is averaging well over $6 per gallon, with many places reporting over $7 per gallon. Putin, in his comments, estimated Russia’s supply could lower global diesel prices by five to six percent.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: An overview of a series of separate developments suggests that a string of Asian nations facing pressure from China across maritime borders are cooperating more fully as a means of countering the threat. Exercise Keen Sword has commenced and is running until October 29. The exercise principally involves 45,000 Japanese and 12,000 US troops. But the exercise also involves seven other Asian and European nations, with participation for the first time in this recurring exercise by France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines. South Korea is participating as an observer, having trained with Japan and the United States on Exercise Freedom Edge last month. Keen Sword is focused on two geographical areas: Japan’s southwestern islands, where there is competition with China, and the Kuril Islands, ownership of which is disputed with Russia. With Japan-based carrier USS George Washington otherwise engaged in the Central Command area, the USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), the Ticonderoga Class guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin (CG 65) and the Arleigh Burke Class destroyer USS Decatur (DDG 73) have arrived at the US naval base in Yokusuka to join in the exercise. USS Theodore Roosevelt is the first non-forward-deployed carrier in four years to dock in Yokosuka. During the exercise, Japanese forces and US Marines will deploy (respectively) Type-25 land-to-ship missiles and the NMESIS ground-based missile system on the island of Yonaguni. With ranges of over 500 nautical miles, these missiles can reach large swathes of the Chinese mainland coastline, as well as the eastern and southern flanks of Taiwan. Japanese ownership of Yonaguni is disputed by China, which frequently intrudes into Japanese territorial waters around the island, and the island is also claimed by Taiwan. However, Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo has praised the Japanese and American exercise deployments on Yonaguni, regarding it not as an infringement of claimed sovereignty, but as support for Taiwan’s own defense. The Philippines is also deepening its ties with Taiwan, despite competing claims over certain islands in the South China Sea. Manila and Taipei have elected to make common cause against the claims made to these same islands by China. Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration is planning for a training ship with cadets aboard to make a port call in the Philippines in October next year, the first such visit since 1974. What the Taiwanese call Dunmu or Friendship Cruises normally consist of three vessels, and the cruise to the Philippines is likely to be led by the fast combat support ship Panshi (AOE-532).

https://maritime-executive.com/article/n.text: After the strikes on commercial vessels off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania, NATO has agreed to provide additional support to the region. The North Atlantic Council agreed on Tuesday, October 20, to the increased deployment after urging by Bulgarian and Romanian officials. NATO Allies had discussed the increase in Russia’s hybrid activities during a meeting in Bucharest, Romania, on October 15 and 16. According to the official reports, concerns had been raised about the increase in activity and the danger from hybrid activities, including sabotage, drone incidents, and cyber attacks. Romania reports that it has recorded 35 unauthorized drone incursions this year, compared to nine for all of 2025. Romanian officials said they had downed six of the drones, including two in recent days. Romania’s Defense Minister Radu Miruta said they were likely Russia’s latest-generation drones, noting they had been flying at speeds similar to jets. They were flying at approximately 280 mph, which the minister said indicated they were likely the Russian-made Geran-4 drones. “The situation remains serious, as commercial ships have been attacked and sunk close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria, and seafarers have been killed, injured, or are still missing,” said the President of Romania, Nicusor Dan. “These attacks are unacceptable and must stop.” Both Romania and Bulgaria have declined to speculate on the source of the attacks on seven commercial vessels in the past days, which killed at least 23 seafarers and sank several of the vessels. Bulgaria, however, reports it has been successful in finding fragments from one of the drone attacks, and it is analyzing the chemical residues. NATO officials said they would also provide intelligence agents and teams to conduct forensic analysis of the explosives. Bulgarian officials said several drone systems had already been put in place to increase the monitoring in the Black Sea. They also reported that U.S. Poseidon surveillance planes had already started patrols to provide increased early warning.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/i.text: An Iraqi-owned cargo ship departed the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates today, October 21, northbound in the Persian Gulf. What makes the departure so notable is that it signals Iraq’s efforts to resume commercial shipping after a more than 50-year hiatus. The country’s Ministry of Transport had announced at the beginning of the month the plan to restore commercial shipping. It cited the opportunities to increase the flow of goods in the Persian Gulf, along with supporting trade with the country’s neighbors. The report said the new initiative aligns with the strategic objectives to develop the country’s transport infrastructure and enhance its operational capabilities. While the initial reports had said the service would launch in mid-month, it may have been delayed by the recent escalations by Iran. In a report put out by UK Maritime Trade Operations on October 21, it said it had been informed by a master that a tanker had been struck by an unknown projectile. It called it a late report and said the incident had happened 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq. Iraqi officials have not confirmed the details. Experts note that most cargo has been flowing overland since the start of the war. Ports in the UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan, outside the Gulf, have reported increases in cargo volumes as shippers sought alternatives to move cargo in the region, but the road and rail networks are lacking and believed to be strained. Iraq has owned the cargo ship Basrah since it was built in 2014. The vessel is 17,787 dwt and measures 143 meters (469 feet) in length. Alphaliner reports it was outfitted to carry approximately 900 TEU. It is registered in Jordan. The vessel’s AIS signal shows its departure from Jebel Ali Port today. It is reporting a destination of Kuwait, with the Ministry reporting the shuttle service would also connect to Iraq’s southern port of Umm Qasr.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/a.text: IFM Investors, an Australia-based global fund manager with a focus on UK infrastructure, emerged as the winning bidder in the sale of Associated British Ports (ABP). The company, which was formed through a government privatization effort in the early 1980s, reportedly handles approximately a quarter of the UK’s seaborne trade. The Financial Times had first reported in February that the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and OMERS (Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System) were planning to sell their stakes, which collectively represent approximately 64 percent ownership of ABP. In August, Bloomberg reported the final round of bidding had been narrowed to three investment fund managers, Apollo Global Management, KKR, and IFM Investors. India’s Adani Group had reportedly also expressed interest but was not identified as one of the finalists. Terms of the deal were not reported, but Bloomberg cites sources saying ABP was valued at approximately £10 billion ($13.4 billion). Bloomberg calls the deal one of the largest in the UK this year. “This transaction represents an attractive opportunity to realize the value of our long-term investment and recycle capital into new opportunities,” said James Bryce, Managing Director, Head of Infrastructure, CPP Investments. ABP currently operates 19 ports around the UK, including in England, Scotland, and Wales. Its locations include Southampton, the UK’s third-largest container port, Humber, which is a major industrial area in the east around Hull and Immingham, and South Wales. In announcing the sale, OMERS also highlighted that ABP has continued to invest in its ports, support UK trade and develop new opportunities linked to the energy transition, including through major projects such as the Immingham Renewable Fuels Terminal, Green Port Hull, and Southampton's Horizon cruise terminal. The company was formed to take over the British Transport Docks Board during the wave of privatizations during the era of UK Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the early 1980s. It remained a public company until 2006, when a group of investors, including Goldman Sachs and OMERS, acquired the company for £2.8 billion. The Canadian Pension Plan acquired its stake in 2015. CPP held 33.9 percent while OMERS held 30 percent. Other investors include Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund and Kuwait Investment Authority’s Wren House Infrastructure.
