https://gcaptain.com/middle-east-oil-flo.text: The Soho Square, a crude oil tanker sailing under the flag of Liberia, is at anchor in the Galveston Bay as it makes it’s way to the Port of Houston shortly after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a 60-day waiver of the Jones Act shipping law, in Texas City, Texas, U.S. March 18, 2026. REUTERS/Antranik Tavitian By Julian Lee (Bloomberg) — Oil shipments from the Middle East are showing little sign of buckling in the face of Iran’s more frequent and damaging attacks on merchant ships in the region. Crude and condensate flows from the Persian Gulf hit a high of 24.6 million barrels a day in the week to Oct. 18, according to data provider Kpler. However, shipments are volatile and figures for the average of October to date remain below prewar levels. Loadings tend to happen in bunches, with ships traveling in convoys through the Strait of Hormuz , shuttling cargoes to tankers waiting outside the waterway before returning to reload. Figures from rival data firm Vortexa don’t show the same weekly surge, highlighting the difficulty of establishing export levels as most tankers are currently operating with their positioning signals turned off. It pegs flows over the same seven-day period at 18 million barrels a day. Both companies estimate flows before the conflict was at least 18.5 million barrels a day. The continued strong volumes despite the Iranian attacks show the desire for Middle Eastern producers to keep moving their barrels. Oil forms the backbone of the countries’ economies and they’ve been competing for customers in recent months to make up for billions of dollars of missed sales during the conflict. For October so far, Kpler pegs Middle East flows at 16.7 million barrels a day, while Vortexa puts it at 15.4 million. Kpler aggregates its numbers from Hormuz transits, net flows via ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, exports through Red Sea ports and those on the Gulf of Oman in the United Arab Emirates and Oman. The Vortexa numbers sum shipments from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Oman.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/us-.text: US sanctions relief on shadow-fleet tankers could redirect ships from Russian oil trades toward the Middle East, potentially raising Russian freight costs while easing some of the tanker shortages around the Strait of Hormuz, shipping analysts said. In recent public remarks, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the US will allow legitimate businesses to acquire sanctioned tankers for non-sanctioned trades to reduce shipping costs, though Washington has yet to announce a detailed relief proposal. The number of oil and LPG tankers sanctioned by Western authorities amounted to 1,226 as of the end of August, with the US having been particularly targeting VLCCs, according to S&P Global Energy Horizons research. But BRS Shipbrokers estimated only 148 tankers in deepsea trades, equivalent to 2.5% of the global total by vessel count, were sanctioned solely by the US Office of Foreign Assets Control as of Oct. 19. Of those, only 14 appeared to have been idle for more than three months based on location signals. The “overwhelming majority” of ships that could become candidates for mainstream employment were therefore already deployed in likely sanctioned trades, mainly carrying Russian clean petroleum products, BRS said. That means sanctions relief could redistribute existing tanker capacity rather than simply release large amounts of idle tonnage. “It may not drive looser oil or tanker market fundamentals,” BRS said in a research note. “It would instead see more mainstream oil carried at the expense of Russian or Iranian oil.”

https://gcaptain.com/russia-sees-first-d.text: FILE PHOTO: An employee holds a diesel fuel pump nozzle at a petrol station of Neftmagistral company in Moscow, Russia, September 8, 2023. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov/File Photo Oct 21, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A tanker loaded with Russian diesel will sail for the US on Thursday as Moscow starts to implement a fuel supply deal struck by Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, according to Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak. “The first tanker, as planned, will leave the port tomorrow,” Novak told reporters on Wednesday, according to Tass. “More batches will follow.” Novak didn’t identify the Russian port, the supplier or the tanker, but said the vessel has a capacity of 40,000 metric tons, according to Tass. That’s equivalent to about 300,000 barrels. In a phone call with Trump earlier this month, Putin agreed to relax diesel-export restrictions and send more fuel to the global market, including the US. The Russian government pledged to ship 500,000 tons of diesel in a first phase, but provided no exact timeframe. Trump is keen to lower diesel prices that are trading north of $200 a barrel just weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. But the pressure extends far beyond the US, spurring fears that energy inflation will force central bankers across the world to raise interest rates.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/new.text: Fifty-one vessels have been ordered for the first time at newbuild yards in 2026, up 34% from 38 in 2025, according to VesselsValue’s newbuild orderbook data. Eighteen more-established yards have now received their first Tanker orders in recent years, with more emerging; Anhui Zhongrun Heavy Industry received its first Tanker order of a Handy recently. Yards breaking into the Tanker market Perhaps the clearest illustration of this pace is Hengli Shipbuilding, which built its first vessel only in 2024 and has since become the top Asian yard by orderbook size with 495 vessels on order — across Bulkers, Tankers, and Containers — and a value of USD 46 bil. Its rapid ascent from newcomer to market leader in under two years underscores how quickly new entrants have been able to capture significant order share amid the current capacity crunch. Geographically, the trend is heavily concentrated in China, home to 11 of the 16 yards, though single entrants have also emerged in South Korea, Vietnam, Brazil, the US, and Philippines. By sub-type, Aframaxes and Handy Tankers account for the majority of first-time activity. VLCC and Suezmax entrants, by contrast, tend to be established heavy-industry groups or joint-venture facilities, such as Wison New Energies Nantong (VLCC) and Guangzhou CSSC Shipbuilding Industry (Aframax, Handy Tanker, Suezmax), rather than genuinely new builders, pointing to a size-based divide in owner willingness to commit to unproven yards. Yards continue to take on Tanker orders outside their usual remit: Anhui Zhongrun Heavy Industry received its first order for a Tanker, 2+3 MR1 units of 41,000 DWT, set for 2029 delivery, from a Greek owner, with a VV Value of USD 38.6 mil. This follows a similar pattern seen earlier this month at Haifeng Shipbuilding, which received its first Tanker orders from Yangzijiang Maritime Development for two LR2s and four MR2s. There has been no notable pricing differential at Haifeng despite its lack of Tanker-building history.

O desempenho faz parte de um crescimento observado ao longo do ano. Entre janeiro e setembro, a TCP movimentou 1,279 milhão de TEUs, volume 4% superior ao mesmo período de 2025. Nas operações terrestres, 489 mil transações de contêineres passaram pelos acessos rodoviários do terminal, avanço de 3% na comparação anual. Para empresa, o aumento reforça o papel de Paranaguá nas cadeias de exportação e importação e amplia a necessidade de que a eficiência alcançada dentro do terminal seja acompanhada por toda a estrutura responsável pela chegada e saída das mercadorias. Para as transportadoras, fatores como acessos rodoviários, agendamento, capacidade dos pátios, horários de atendimento e compartilhamento de informações interferem diretamente na produtividade das operações. Para Luiz Gustavo Nery, vice-presidente do Sindicato das Empresas de Transporte de Cargas no Estado do Paraná (SETCEPAR), o crescimento representa novas oportunidades para o setor, mas também exige maior coordenação entre os diferentes elos da cadeia. “ O recorde confirma a competitividade de Paranaguá e representa mais demanda e oportunidades para as transportadoras. Entre os pontos que precisam acompanhar esse novo patamar de movimentação, Nery destaca os sistemas de agendamento, os acessos rodoviários e a estrutura dos pátios de triagem. https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: The UK government has given the green light for the Jackdaw natural gas field development in the North Sea, a major win for the UK's declining offshore oil and gas industry. Once online, Jackdaw will provide about two percent of the UK's natural gas needs, offsetting imports. Work on the facility is already at an advanced stage, and its completion had only been prevented by court action. Now that it has its final government consent, it should be online and producing by this winter, Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said. "In the middle of an energy crisis, homegrown gas has a role to play in our energy security as we transition to net zero," said Fahnbuleh. "We’ll also invest North Sea revenues in renewables and other low-carbon projects." The project's advocates say that Jackdaw will actually reduce UK greenhouse gas emissions. If not for the field's production, Britain would import even more LNG from the United States, paying the extra emissions "price" of the liquefaction and transport of every cubic meter. Wood Mackenzie analyst Gail Anderson estimates that relying on American gas instead of Jackdaw's gas would mean a net emissions increase of another 3.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Perhaps even more importantly for policymakers, Jackdaw provides an incremental boost to the UK's energy security. "At a time of global instability, homegrown energy can be a source of national strength. A pragmatic approach to increasing gas production in the North Sea will make the UK more secure," said British ambassador to the United States Christian Turner in a statement.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/m.text: Three weeks after the training ship Empire State arrived in Virginia for preparations for a government mission, MARAD has notified the SUNY Maritime College at Fort Schuyler that it is releasing the ship. The school announced the change in plans to its community on October 21. “I am pleased to share an important update on Empire State VII . The federal activation plan has changed, and the ship is now expected to return to Fort Schuyler for academic use, ship work, and with watches resuming no later than the middle of November,” wrote Rear Admiral John A. Okon, who is president of SUNY Maritime College. He called the development “welcome news,” highlighting that the vessel is “an essential part of the maritime experience." Having the ship back at Fort Schuyler will allow us to resume the critical hands-on learning, shipboard activities, and sea time requirements for our USCG-approved program.” Details on the return to the campus are still to be announced, as well as the steps that will be required for the ship to resume its normal mission. News of the deployment had been released at the end of August, and the ship departed the New York campus on September 30, shifting the ship to Virginia. She was spotted at the General Dynamics NASSCO facility in Portsmouth sandwiched between Reserve Fleet vessels and a destroyer. The ship was scheduled to spend October in Virginia, being prepared for the mission. Details of the deployment had not been announced, but Okon had said MARAD was undertaking “certification of the flight deck.” Rumors had said the ship was going to sail to Diego Garcia. The vessel, which was delivered to SUNY in 2023 as the first of the new generation of training ships, was designed to support government missions. It was primarily anticipated that it would have a dual role for humanitarian support. The ship normally accommodates approximately 600 but can be equipped for up to approximately 1,000 and, as part of its humanitarian capabilities, has a full hospital aboard.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/u.text: On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury announced new sanctions on a Panama-based law firm and five of its staff for allegedly helping Iranian shipping interests. The action is intended to send a message to maritime service providers and further tighten the American net around Iranian international commerce. According to the Treasury, Karnakis and Karnakis was particularly active in its work on behalf of the Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh shipping network, which specialized in Iranian LPG exports. Emamjomeh's network was sanctioned last year; Treasury is effectively working its way upstream to target people who provided it with professional services. The department alleges that Karnakis and Karnakis helped clients to register corporate entities that own shadow fleet vessels in Iranian trades, thereby enabling the transport of Iranian petrochemicals, petroleum, steel and other commodities. Examples allegedly include the sanctioned shipping companies Skyros Maritime and Trading SA, Corfu Maritime and Trading SA, and Elias Shipping and Trading Group SA. Elias is the owner of the Ramona 1, a sanctioned tanker linked to oil sales on behalf of Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent in a statement. “We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Treasury also personally sanctioned the law firm's founders, along with three employees who had allegedly served as listed directors and officers of the holding companies that Karnakis and Karnakis created. Also sanctioned were shipping agency Amigoz Singapore, accused of providing bunkering and services for shadow fleet entities; and Whales Shipping Line, based in the UAE, for alleged involvement with Iranian petrochemical trading.

https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: U.S. ambitions to mine the deep sea are rapidly expanding across the ocean, not only in the country’s own waters, but also on the high seas — the vast expanse of ocean outside any one country’s jurisdiction. In the Clarion-Clipperton Zone of the Pacific Ocean, a hotspot of mining interest in international waters, a Mongabay analysis shows that companies have either applied to the U.S. or already been granted rights to areas of the seabed equal to about half the expanse already designated for mining activities by the international community. Most of the applications to the U.S. occurred within the past year and a half, a fraction of the 25 years the multilateral U.N.-affiliated International Seabed Authority (ISA) has spent issuing seabed mining exploration licenses. U.S. applicants are not only seeking rights to explore the deep seabed, but some are also applying for commercial recovery permits. If approved by the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), these recovery permits would allow the companies to extract and eventually sell the minerals. While the ISA can also accept mining exploitation applications, no company has yet submitted one to the organization. No other country or institution is known to unilaterally accept applications to mine in international waters, and commercial-scale seabed mining has not yet begun anywhere in the world. Deep-sea mining companies are interested in many parts of the international seabed, but Mongabay’s analysis focused on the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), an extensive stretch of the Pacific Ocean between Mexico and Hawai‘i that holds vast quantities of polymetallic nodules — mineral-rich rocks that resemble burnt potatoes. Mongabay’s analysis also revealed overlaps between claims in the CCZ. U.S. applicants are seeking rights to seabed areas that overlap with areas the ISA has already contracted, as well as areas the ISA holds in reserve for future mining and to benefit developing countries. There are overlaps between ISA and U.S. applicants, and overlaps between U.S. applicants. The scale and locations of the U.S. claims, as well as the potential overlaps, are raising legal and regulatory questions about who has authority over the seabed in international waters, which are global commons beyond any nation’s sole jurisdiction. Some experts expressed concern that a U.S. move to unilaterally permit mining in the high seas could weaken or even topple multilateral systems that have long governed the oceans. Others said the U.S. push to mine might also trigger a premature start of commercial mining. Forty-six countries have called to put the brakes on the industry due to concerns about the potential damage to the marine environment, the need for further research, and a lack of international rules

https://maritime-executive.com/article/t.text: In what is clearly emerging as a new tactic to derail the offshore wind energy sector, the Department of Justice filed for the fourth time in just a matter of days, asking a District Court to remand the prior approval of the Construction and Operations Plan of a proposed offshore wind farm. The latest target is New England Wind and is drawing angry criticism from environmentalists and elected officials. The Department of Justice filed a memorandum in support of the long-running case between an environmental group, Ack For Whales, which has been suing the Department of Commerce and Avangrid, the developer of a project known as New England Wind. In the now common tactic, DOJ asks the District Court for the District of Columbia to remand the approval of the Construction and Operations Plan back to the Department of the Interior so that it can reconsider the approval under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act. It writes in the memorandum that the approval, which was announced on July 1, 2024, “did not properly consider or explain how the COP ‘provides for’ the subsection’s identified factors.” It is the fourth time DOJ has used a similar tactic to target the permits for wind farms. It took the same approach to challenge the largely completed Revolution Wind project, which should complete commissioning by the end of this year, and then to challenge a series of projects that had gained approvals under the Biden administration but have not commenced construction. New England Wind is proposed by Avangrid, which is a division of Spain’s Iberdrola. It was proposed for a position approximately 20 nautical miles south of Martha’s Vineyard, Massachusetts, and about 24 nautical miles southwest of Nantucket, Massachusetts, in the same area as the now operating Vineyard Wind and near Revolution Wind. The lease dates from an April 2015 auction, but was assigned in 2021, and the project would straddle two areas. The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management announced its approval of the COP on July 1, 2024, encompassing the two phases of the project, which combined would have a total capacity of up to 2,600 MW. The approval encompassed up to 129 wind turbines and up to five offshore export cables. “Ooops, they did it again,” commented Pasha Feinberg, offshore wind strategist at NRDC (Natural Resources Defense Council). In a statement, the group highlighted that the administration has tried unsuccessfully to halt the under-construction projects and then resorted to buying back leases in exchange for investments in fossil fuel projects. “It's long past time for the Trump administration to realize its war on clean energy is backfiring,” said Feinberg. “Customers’ electricity bills keep rising, and our nation can’t meet its growing electricity demands because of these actions.”

https://maritime-executive.com/article/f.text: On Wednesday, the French navy issued an alert reporting an unlawful drone incursion - this time, during a military exercise. According to the Marine Nationale, several unauthorized drone flights were detected in restricted airspace during a series of exercises near Toulon. "To date, no sensitive infrastructure has been threatened. A judicial investigation has been opened," the Marine Nationale said. "For each incident, the planned security measures were activated by triggering anti-drone systems, coordinated with the internal security forces." French radio station Ici Provence, which first reported the incursions, said that the overflights occurred over Toulon's naval base - the largest naval station in Western Europe - along with the directorate of armaments building in Toulon and the base of the 54th Artillery Regiment in Hyeres. The source reported that the drones were "large machines," but the specific type and number were unknown. Electromagnetic jamming systems were used to counteract the incursion. The drones arrived during a joint French military exercise focused on the defense of harborside installations in Toulon, with military units working alongside internal security forces. Air traffic near the exercise was prohibited to allow for unencumbered military operations - including authorized drone operations. The Marine Nationale's report is the latest in a series of escalating drone disruptions, some attributed to Russian interference. The most dramatic example occurred in early August at Leipzig Airport, when drones armed with military-grade explosives approached Ukrainian transport aircraft on the tarmac. The attack was narrowly averted; German intelligence has identified the Russian sabotage unit likely responsible for the Leipzig incident as GRU Unit 29155, and specifically a team of agents led by Russian-Latvian dual national Oleg Levushkin.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/d.text: The Port of Coos Bay, Oregon has received a federal Department of Transportation grant for $205 million to upgrade the Coos Bay Rail Line, the short-line railway that links the small port to Class I rail services on the other side of Oregon's Coast Range. The grant was funded through DOT's Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program, and had support from Oregon's congressional delegation. Once completed, it will support the port's plans to build out a $2.3 billion container terminal with intermodal rail connections - the only saltwater facility of its kind between the Bay Area and Seattle. "The grant will bring us closer to the Port of Coos Bay becoming the first fully ship-to-rail port facility on the West Coast—a watershed moment for the region and our state,” said Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR). “The Port of Coos Bay project stands to create economic opportunities for working families by creating good-paying, local union jobs, and together, we’ll get this project over the finish line.” The funding augments an $11 million Port Infrastructure Development Program (PIDP) grant from DOT that was awarded for other work on the rail line earlier this year. The department's officials have recently emphasized the possibility of combining PIDP, CRISI and other funding streams to underwrite larger projects like Coos Bay's boxship terminal (in addition to incremental upgrades and repairs). If built, the proposed Pacific Coast Intermodal Port would be able to handle Neopanamax boxships up to 13,000 TEU in size. Sponsor NorthPoint says that the demand from large retail customers would support buildout of a pure container-to-rail box terminal for shipping to inland consumers. This would require about eight feet of vertical dredging (from 37 feet to 45 feet) and 150 feet of channel widening from the harbor entrance up to eight miles inland from the bar. The port would be positioned as an alternative to Prince Rupert, Vancouver, Seattle, Oakland or LA/Long Beach. It would also provide competition for Port of Portland's Terminal 6, Oregon's only existing container terminal. T6 (recently rebranded Oregon Container Terminal, or OCT) supports one weekly transpacific service provided by SM Line.

https://maritime-executive.com/article/p.text: Despite the challenges the Panama Canal has faced due to the drought and effects of El Niño, it completed a strong fiscal year, emphasizing its role in global trade. The canal authority cited a sustained recovery in demand, supported in part by shifts in international trade flows, while also reporting, with a recovery in water levels, it is now restoring the Last-Minute Reservation service to further support shipping. Speaking with the French news outlet AFP (Agence France-Presse) on Tuesday, officials highlighted a new record for the total volume of cargo moving through the canal. In the FY ending September 30, they report a total of 521 million tons (PC/UMS). That is a 6.5 percent increase versus the previous year and beats the 2022 record of 518 million tons. Detailing the performance for the year in a presentation today, Panama Canal Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta reported that the Panama Canal handled 13,951 transits in FY2026, up 4.1 percent from 13,404 in FY2025. Growth, they said, was driven by energy shipping segments and a strong containership performance. It contributed to a 16.6 percent increase in total revenues for the Panama Canal Authority. The strong demand was also in part driven by the disruptions in global patterns and the strong demand from Asia. Ships have been diverting away from the Suez Canal and Red Sea due to the dangers from the Houthis and then the disruption from the war in the Persian Gulf. The Panama Canal Authority highlighted growth in its share of larger-capacity vessels that were using the waterway. It notes that transits through the Neopanamax locks accounted for just over 52 percent of total tonnage. It said tonnage through the locks used by the largest ships increased over eight percent this year. The authority has worked to maintain the operations for the largest ships, with the officials noting they preserved a 50-foot draft throughout the dry season. They also highlighted to AFP that the canal increased the number of daily transits from 36 to 41 for a period of time to adjust for the uptick in demand.

https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/20.text: A Polícia Federal (PF) apura se o advogado Willer Tomaz, amigo do senador e candidato à Presidência da República, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), usou uma estrutura coordenada de empresas para ocultar ou dificultar a identificação de valores e o destino de eventuais pagamentos no mercado de loterias do Rio de Janeiro. Ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a PF afirma que "foram identificados elementos indicativos de vínculo de controle ou propriedade de fato de Willer Tomaz sobre a Rede Loto". A Rede Loto foi a primeira empresa a obter autorização da Loteria do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Loterj) para explorar apostas esportivas de quota fixa, com prazo inicial de até cinco anos. Para a PF, chama a atenção a relação de Willer com o ex-presidente da Loterj, Hazenclever Lopes Cançado, o ex-governador do Rio Cláudio Castro e a Pixs/Rio Pag. A Pixs/Rio Pag é a operadora de pagamentos de apostas de lotéricas e bets da Loterj. A análise está no pedido de abertura de inquérito feito pela PF ao STF que indica a suposta prática de lavagem de dinheiro, envolvendo Willer Tomaz e Flávio Bolsonaro . Os dois negam irregularidades (veja o posicionamento dos dois abaixo) .

A Polícia Federal encontrou uma suposta sala secreta em hangar do advogado Willer Tomaz, no Aeroporto de Brasília. O local guardava uma máquina de contar dinheiro. Os investigadores chegaram ao hangar em agosto após denúncia anônima. Uma porta blindada ficava oculta atrás de um painel de madeira, com prateleiras e malas. A defesa de Willer Tomaz confirmou a estrutura e afirmou tratar-se de uma "sala-cofre". A nota diz ser fantasiosa a insinuação de armazenamento de dinheiro ilícito. A busca ocorreu na operação Sem Desconto, que apura lavagem de dinheiro para o senador Weverton Rocha. Willer Tomaz teve 4 aviões apreendidos na ação.

https://gcaptain.com/u-s-sanctions-law-f.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent looks on as he speaks to the media at the World Bank on the day of a meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, in Washington, D.C., US, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Nathan Howard The United States has imposed a new round of sanctions targeting a law firm, shipping agents and nine vessels accused of helping Iran move oil and other commodities through international markets, expanding Washington’s crackdown on the networks supporting Tehran’s shadow fleet. The U.S. Treasury Department announced the measures Wednesday as part of Operation Economic Outcast, an ongoing campaign aimed at cutting off Iran’s remaining sources of revenue amid the continuing conflict in the Middle East. At the center of the latest action is Karnakis and Karnakis, a law firm operating in Panama and Greece that Treasury says has spent years establishing shell companies used to conceal the ownership of vessels transporting Iranian petroleum, petrochemicals and steel. According to Treasury, the firm helped register shipping companies responsible for moving hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian commodities, including vessels connected to previously sanctioned entities. The law firm also played a key role in establishing the corporate network behind Iranian liquefied petroleum gas magnate Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh, whose shipping operations have transported hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian LPG and crude oil.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543837-do.text: Norwegian offshore vessel owner DOF Group has secured a subsea installation contract in Africa, with its Skandi Acergy construction support vessel (CSV) scheduled to undertake the offshore campaign in early 2027. The contract, valued at between $15 million and $25 million, covers project management, engineering, logistics and offshore execution services for the transportation and installation of subsea production systems (SPS) at deepwater field developments. The offshore campaign is expected to begin in early first-quarter 2027 and last approximately 100 days. DOF's Atlantic region teams in Bergen and Aberdeen will handle project management, engineering and planning, while the Skandi Acergy will carry out the offshore installation work. The vessel is a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) construction support vessel designed to perform subsea operations across a range of water depths and environmental conditions. "We are pleased to secure this award and the trust placed in DOF by a leading operator. Deep-water SPS installation is a critical phase in the development of any field and requires careful planning, strong engineering and proven execution capability. Our priority will be to safeguard the installation, effectively manage project risks and deliver the work safely, efficiently and on schedule. We look forward to supporting our client in the successful delivery of this project," said Mons S. Aase, CEO of DOF Group.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543833-ch.text: Chevron is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the US Gulf, the company confirmed to Reuters, part of an effort to focus on high-growth developments in the region. The energy producer is in the early stages of a multi-month process that could see a number of assets offloaded, a Chevron spokesperson said in response to questions from Reuters about the sale effort. "We are initiating the process of marketing some of our mature Gulf of America producing assets, including Petronius, Tubular Bells, and Llano as well as working interest in several other operated and non-operated fields," the spokesperson said. The move is part of Chevron's efforts to ensure its portfolio aligns with the company's priorities, the spokesperson said, adding there was no guarantee that sales would take place. With Chevron targeting production from the US Gulf to grow to 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of this year, the portfolio-trimming efforts indicate Chevron is increasingly focused on newer projects and opportunities in the region. This would include Anchor, its first platform producing at ultra-high subsea pressure, and Ballymore, which began production last year. The company is also pursuing exploration to find oil and gas resources near existing facilities, and has been a top spender in recent sales of drilling rights in the US Gulf conducted by the Interior Department.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543836-on.text: OneSubsea has completed a joint industry project in Brazil with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP and Chevron to develop and qualify fully electric subsea production technologies for applications in water depths of up to 3,000 meters. The Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP), supported through the Brazilian National Petroleum Agency's (ANP) research and development regulation, focused on integrating electric subsea equipment, well completion technologies, topside controls and digital systems. The project qualified electric components and control systems for deepwater applications and demonstrated an integrated production architecture extending electrification beyond the subsea tree. Unlike conventional subsea production systems, which rely on hydraulic pressure to operate valves and chokes, all-electric systems use electric motors, eliminating the need for hydraulic fluids and associated distribution infrastructure. The project also demonstrated interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies. A purpose-built master control station connects subsea equipment with topside control and digital systems, allowing the different components to operate within an integrated architecture.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543838-te.text: Ttransmission system operator TenneT Netherlands and cable manufacturer NKT have completed a joint study examining the technical, environmental and economic aspects of decommissioning offshore power cables in the Netherlands and Germany. The study found that offshore cable decommissioning is technically feasible and could contribute to recycling and carbon emissions reduction, although the economic viability of individual projects depends on several factors. The research examined offshore cable end-of-life management from multiple perspectives, including recycling, biodiversity, carbon assessments, logistics, regulatory requirements and operational practices. The companies assessed how offshore cable infrastructure could be managed at the end of its operational life, with a focus on circularity and the potential recovery of materials. "The study highlighted the importance of considering end-of-life requirements from the earliest stages of infrastructure development, helping to create more sustainable solutions for future offshore projects. The study also demonstrated that offshore cable decommissioning is technically feasible and can support both circularity objectives and CO2 reduction. “The economic attractiveness may vary depending on factors such as the materials used, recycling value, processing costs and local market conditions. As a result, the most suitable approach must be assessed on a project-by-project basis," said Gwenn van der Schee, Sustainability Manager at TenneT Netherlands.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/uk_union_we.text: In a statement sent to Rigzone this week, UK union Unite welcomed the UK government’s decision to green light the Jackdaw gas field. Unite noted in its statement that it has long called for the development of Jackdaw, “in order to provide energy security and provide time to secure commensurate jobs for North Sea oil and gas workers”. The union highlighted in its statement that it has a longstanding North Sea campaign - No Ban without a Plan - which argues that the government must not allow a jobless transition for North Sea workers. Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham said in the statement, “in my conversations with the Prime Minister and the Chancellor, I have been very clear that whilst we of course support net zero, we cannot have a jobless transition, abandon our energy security, or offshore our carbon responsibilities”. “This gives us a bit more time to create and fund a concrete plan for commensurate jobs for workers currently working in the North Sea,” Graham continued. “Now we urgently need to use that and invest in industries like wind turbine manufacture and refining green jet fuel. We simply cannot let go of one rope until we have hold of another,” Graham went on to state.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: O Brasil utiliza economicamente 20,4 mil quilômetros de vias navegáveis interiores para o transporte de cargas, menos da metade dos 41,7 mil quilômetros previstos no Plano Nacional de Viação. Os dados fazem parte do Estudo sobre Regulação e Governança da Navegação Interior Brasileira , elaborado pela Pezco Economics e promovido pela Confederação Nacional do Transporte (CNT) , apresentado nesta quarta-feira (21). Segundo o levantamento, a navegação interior movimentou 91,3 milhões de toneladas em 2025, alta de 19,7% em relação ao ano anterior. Considerando também a parcela da cabotagem realizada em vias interiores, o volume transportado chega a aproximadamente 116 milhões de toneladas, de acordo com a Agência Nacional de Transportes Aquaviários (Antaq). Apesar da movimentação, o estudo identifica obstáculos à expansão do modal, como fragmentação da governança, insegurança regulatória, deficiências de infraestrutura e dificuldades de financiamento. Para enfrentar esses entraves, o documento propõe uma agenda de desenvolvimento com horizonte até 2046, dividida em medidas de curto, médio e longo prazos. As recomendações para o transporte de cargas estão organizadas em seis eixos: planejamento estratégico das hidrovias, governança e segurança regulatória, infraestrutura, capacitação profissional, segurança e financiamento. Entre as medidas sugeridas estão a criação de uma instância nacional de coordenação da política hidroviária, a elaboração de um Plano Setorial Hidroviário e o fortalecimento das ações de dragagem e manutenção das vias navegáveis. O estudo também recomenda garantir a continuidade do Programa de Operação e Manutenção de Eclusas (Proeclusas), planejar intervenções por corredores logísticos e aperfeiçoar mecanismos de financiamento, inclusive por meio de concessões. O levantamento destaca os efeitos das variações de navegabilidade sobre a logística, com base na seca que atingiu a região amazônica em 2023 e 2024. Segundo a publicação, cerca de 90% das embarcações no Amazonas operaram sob restrições naquele período. No corredor entre Porto Velho e Itacoatiara (AM), o tempo de viagem passou de oito para 20 dias, a capacidade de transporte caiu 60% e os custos de frete aumentaram em até 150%. Além disso, 23 municípios amazonenses tiveram o abastecimento de combustíveis comprometido por interrupções no transporte fluvial. O estudo defende que as decisões sobre investimentos considerem conjuntamente a demanda por transporte, as condições de navegação, os acessos terrestres, a disponibilidade de terminais e os custos de implantação e manutenção. A proposta é permitir que as hidrovias sejam avaliadas em conjunto com os demais modais, de acordo com as características de cada corredor logístico.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/dre.text: With regional security changing rapidly, Drewry’s Red Sea Diversion Tracker delivers timely intelligence to shippers, carriers, ports and other stakeholders on the evolving structure of carrier networks. This tracker page is updated fortnightly (every other Tuesday). Steady transit traffic via Suez During the week ended 18 Oct, 55 containership transited the Suez Canal (in either direction), up 120% when compared with the number in the same week of 2025, as carriers continued their gradual policy of returning to the Suez route. There have now been 3 weeks with more than 50 Suez transits a week, indicating a strong momentum in the return of containerships from the Cape of Good Hope route to the Suez route. The average number of transits via Suez was 57 in the latest 3 weeks, up 36% from the average in the previous three weeks. Source: Drewry

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/mae.text: Denmark-based shipping group A.P. Moller-Maersk expects all its shipping services to return to the Suez Canal by March 2027, according to a statement from the Suez Canal Authority (SCA). The outlook was unveiled during a videoconference between Ossama Rabiee, Chairman and Managing Director of the SCA, and Rabab Boulos, Maersk’s Chief Operating Officer and a member of its executive leadership team. The talks focused on strengthening cooperation and reviewing sailing plans and schedules to accelerate the return of services through the canal. Rabiee reported that Maersk-affiliated vessels made 276 transits through the canal between January and September 2026, with a combined net tonnage of 23.3 million tons. This compared with 146 transits totaling 7 million net tons during the same period in 2025. He described a substantial recovery in Maersk services using the waterway, attributing it to the strategic partnership and longstanding relationship between the two sides. Boulos also credited their cooperation with bringing back a significant number of services and identified the canal as Maersk’s preferred route. On preparations for further returns, Ahmed Hassan, a senior vice president at Maersk who also attended the meeting, said the group continued to revise its sailing schedules to enable more services to pass through the canal in the coming period. Hany El Nady, Maersk’s Chief Group Representative for the Middle East and North Africa, also participated in the talks and said the company was working to accelerate the restoration of all its services through the waterway. Rabiee highlighted the canal’s economic advantages, saying geopolitical developments and their impact on rising fuel prices and freight rates had reinforced its strategic importance. He said the route offered substantial cost savings for very large container ships and greater navigational safety than sailing around the Cape of Good Hope. Source: Zawya

https://splash247.com/maersk-tankers-lin.text: Danish shipowner Maersk Tankers has moved closer to converting four very large ammonia carriers to run on the cargo they transport after its retrofit proposal was selected for support under the European Union’s Innovation Fund. The project, known as RIPPLE, involves installing dual-fuel, two-stroke ammonia engines on four vessels in the company’s expanding gas carrier fleet. The European Commission has invited the project to begin grant agreement preparations, although the amount of funding has not yet been finalised. Crucially, Maersk Tankers said any decision to proceed would depend on securing commercial commitments from customers. The proposed conversions would allow the vessels to use ammonia as propulsion fuel rather than relying solely on conventional marine fuels. According to the Commission’s project description, RIPPLE would demonstrate the EU’s first dual-fuel ammonia retrofit on a VLAC.

https://splash247.com/tufton-rides-stron.text: London-listed Tufton Assets has secured higher-paying employment across its tanker and dry bulk fleet, with two MR product tankers extended for another year and further charter renewals in the pipeline. The charterer of the 2016-built Catherine Grace and Madelyn Grace exercised options in October to extend both vessels’ employment by 12 months at rates above their previous firm periods, the ship investment company said in its third-quarter update. The latest extensions add to a string of chartering moves during the third quarter, when the company secured improved terms for three vessels and fixed two handysize bulkers on new arrangements. Among the latest dry bulk fixtures, the ultramax African Inspiration has been extended for six to eight months from early October at a substantially higher rate, while the handysize Lucilia C has started a new seven- to nine-month charter following the expiry of its previous employment in September. https://www.marinelink.com/news/dof-gets.text: Norwegian offshore vessel owner DOF Group has secured a subsea installation contract in Africa, with its Skandi Acergy construction support vessel (CSV) scheduled to undertake the offshore campaign in early 2027. The contract, valued at between $15 million and $25 million, covers project management, engineering, logistics and offshore execution services for the transportation and installation of subsea production systems (SPS) at deepwater field developments. The offshore campaign is expected to begin in early first-quarter 2027 and last approximately 100 days. DOF's Atlantic region teams in Bergen and Aberdeen will handle project management, engineering and planning, while the Skandi Acergy will carry out the offshore installation work. The vessel is a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) construction support vessel designed to perform subsea operations across a range of water depths and environmental conditions. "We are pleased to secure this award and the trust placed in DOF by a leading operator. Deep-water SPS installation is a critical phase in the development of any field and requires careful planning, strong engineering and proven execution capability. Our priority will be to safeguard the installation, effectively manage project risks and deliver the work safely, efficiently and on schedule. We look forward to supporting our client in the successful delivery of this project," said Mons S. Aase, CEO of DOF Group.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/ira.text: Iraq’s deal with the US-based Excelerate Energy company to supply imported gas to its fuel-thirsty power facilities hinges on the end of the US-Iran conflict, experts say. The war has already disrupted the $450-million contract which had been due to be enforced in the second half of 2026 with the installation of an offshore regasification facility off Iraq’s southern Khor Al-Zubair port. Iraq has not revealed where it would get the liquefied natural gas (LNG) probably because the Texas-based company is responsible for importing LNG in line with the contract it signed with the Iraqi electricity ministry in late 2025. “I think Qatar is the likeliest candidate to supply LNG to Iraq given its location, large production and good relations with Iraq…but you cannot expect a supply agreement in the current circumstances,” Iraq energy analyst Walid Khaddouri said. In March, Excelerate said it has received a “force majeure” notice from the state-owned QatarEnergy related to its long-term LNG supply agreement following repeated Iranian and missile attacks. But it maintained that the long-term fundamentals supporting the project remain unchanged, driven by chronic power shortages and limited domestic gas processing capacity in Iraq, one of the world’s largest oil producers.

https://splash247.com/viridien-sharpens-.text: French geophysical company Viridien has launched the first phase of a major seismic reimaging programme offshore Guyana, targeting more than 10,000 sq km of existing 3D data in and around the country’s emerging shallow-water exploration acreage. The project covers the Kaieteur, Georgetown, Kanuku, and Corentyne legacy surveys and is intended to sharpen subsurface imaging updip of the prolific ExxonMobil-operated Stabroek block. Viridien said it would combine the reprocessed information with newly acquired 3D seismic to create a continuous regional dataset exceeding 14,000 sq km. Preliminary results are expected in the first quarter of 2027. The company, formerly known as CGG, holds exclusive access and commercialisation rights to the legacy datasets. It said the programme had attracted strong industry backing but did not disclose the value of the work or identify participating customers. The work comes against the backdrop of Guyana’s broader effort to expand exploration beyond Stabroek, where successive discoveries have transformed the country’s offshore oil sector. In March, Guyana’s natural resources ministry announced a wider multi-client 3D acquisition and imaging initiative with Viridien and Chinese geophysical company BGP, covering roughly 25,000 sq km of shallow-water acreage.

https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/gul.text: China’s non-Iranian Middle Eastern crude arrivals are set to reach their highest level since the war began, despite VLCC tightness and Hormuz ship-to-ship (STS) bottlenecks delaying cargo deliveries. As Iranian supplies dwindle, Gulf producers — particularly Saudi Arabia and Iraq — are well positioned to capture more of China’s crude demand. Meanwhile, Beijing’s fuel export policy remains closely tied to Middle Eastern crude availability, with tighter quotas limiting the scope for China to expand seaborne product exports in Q4. China’s Middle Eastern crude arrivals recover despite Hormuz bottlenecks Recent Middle Eastern crude arrivals into China have come entirely from the Middle East Gulf (MEG), rather than the Red Sea or Mediterranean, as China-bound loadings have shifted fully back to the MEG since late July. Although voyages from the MEG to China are taking longer because of STS transfers East of Hormuz or near India, non-Iranian Middle Eastern crude arrivals are still expected to reach around 4.5mbd in October, close to the 2025 average of 4.7mbd. Saudi Arabia and Iraq, China’s two largest non-sanctioned crude suppliers before the war, have led the month-on-month recovery. Saudi arrivals — all originating West of Hormuz — are expected to exceed 2mbd in October, compared with a 2025 average of 1.6mbd. Around 75% of these volumes are expected to be absorbed by China’s two largest oil majors, Sinopec and PetroChina. Iraqi arrivals are expected to remain around 1.1mbd, serving a broader range of buyers that includes Shandong’s teapot refiners. Together, Saudi Arabia and Iraq are set to account for more than two-thirds of China’s Middle Eastern crude imports and over 35% of its total seaborne crude imports in October.

https://splash247.com/global-shipbuildin.text: The global shipbuilding boom is gathering pace, with orderbooks surpassing their previous 2008 peak, Chinese yards tightening their grip on the market and tanker owners increasingly turning to inexperienced builders to secure delivery slots. New figures from BIMCO put the global orderbook at 203.2m compensated gross tonnes (cgt) at the start of September, up 13% year-on-year and just below May’s all-time high of 210.4m cgt. China captured 74% of new cgt contracted over the preceding 12 months, lifting its share of the global orderbook to 64%, against South Korea’s 19% and Japan’s 6%. Containerships account for 30% of tonnage on order and 68% of the past year’s growth. BIMCO calculates that Chinese yards hold orders equivalent to 4.2 years of recent peak annual production, compared with 1.9 years in South Korea and 1.7 in Japan. Chinese yards are scheduled to deliver a record 44m cgt in 2028, nearly twice the 22.7m cgt delivered in 2025 “Chinese yards are scheduled to deliver a record 44m cgt in 2028, nearly twice the 22.7m cgt delivered in 2025,” said BIMCO chief shipping analyst Niels Rasmussen, warning that the necessary capacity expansion risks leaving yards underutilised when contracting eventually slows.

https://splash247.com/a-new-world-order-.text: The world’s LNG trading map is undergoing its biggest upheaval in years, with the near-paralysis of Gulf exports redirecting cargoes across oceans, forcing Asian buyers towards alternative suppliers and pushing European gas prices to their highest levels since 2022. While gas prices approach $30 per million British thermal units, LNG carrier spot earnings remain remarkably weak, with the Baltic Exchange assessing the US Gulf-Europe route at just $21,200 a day last week. Nearly eight months into the Hormuz crisis, oil exporters have found ways around the chokepoint. Kpler estimates that non-Iranian Middle Eastern oil flows, including alternative routes, recovered to prewar levels last week. LNG remains a different proposition, with Qatar unable to replicate the pipelines and offshore transfers that have restored much of the region’s crude trade. Vortexa recorded just five confirmed LNG carrier transits of Hormuz last week, against a four-week average of 12. Only two were laden outbound voyages. Ras Laffan loaded five cargoes totalling 400,000 tonnes. Kpler identified 13 Qatari LNG loadings during October 1-13, but only four ships were broadcasting active AIS signals. The remaining nine were verified through satellite imagery, tug tracking and other intelligence. The Al Kharsaah, carrying Qatari LNG towards Poland via the Red Sea, came under fire from a small boat in the Gulf of Aden on October 17. Its armed security team returned warning shots, forcing the attackers to retreat. The voyage could deliver Europe’s first Qatari cargo since April.

https://www.guiamaritimo.com.br/noticias.text: O Tecon Imbituba, terminal de contêineres e carga geral operado pela Santos Brasil no sul de Santa Catarina, movimentou 131.263 TEUs entre janeiro e setembro de 2026. O volume já supera o maior resultado anual da unidade, de 123.681 TEUs, registrado em 2024, e foi alcançado com três meses de antecedência. A diferença é de cerca de 6% a mais em nove meses. O desempenho acompanha um ciclo de investimentos. Nos últimos 18 meses, a Santos Brasil aplicou R$ 36 milhões no terminal, sendo R$ 33 milhões apenas em 2026. A empresa prevê outros R$ 75 milhões até 2028, o que levaria o total a R$ 111 milhões em cerca de três anos. A principal novidade é a chegada, no dia 5, de um Mobile Harbor Crane (MHC), guindaste móvel portuário que se soma aos dois portêineres do tipo Ship-to-Shore (STS) já instalados. O equipamento aumenta a produtividade no cais e dá mais flexibilidade para atender tanto os serviços regulares quanto as demandas extraordinárias dos armadores. Também permitirá incluir um terceiro terno, o conjunto de equipamentos e trabalhadores dedicado à movimentação de contêineres, na operação de cada navio. O pacote de aquisições inclui ainda 12 chassis de caminhão, dois frames de içamento de contêineres, seis reach stackers e uma empilhadeira para contêineres vazios. A Santos Brasil também prevê a instalação de um novo scanner e a ampliação do número de tomadas para contêineres refrigerados (reefers). Na frente digital, o terminal implantou três frentes de modernização. O Centro de Controle Operacional (CCO), em funcionamento desde 2025, amplia o acompanhamento da operação em tempo real. O sistema OPUS-TOS, em uso desde julho, integra as operações de contêineres e os fluxos de pátio, gate e cais, além dos processos de documentação e automação ligados à movimentação de cargas e navios. A empresa afirma que a plataforma contribui para elevar produtividade e previsibilidade. A terceira frente é a atualização da rede wireless, que receberá tecnologia 5G. Além dos quatro serviços marítimos regulares, sendo três de longo curso e um de cabotagem, o terminal tem ampliado o atendimento a extra calls, escalas que não constam do planejamento da unidade. Foram 10 neste ano, o equivalente a 11% do volume total até setembro.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/economia/mo.text: O risco-país da Argentina voltou a superar os 700 pontos nesta semana e atingiu o maior nível em cerca de um ano. O movimento chama atenção, mas o número sozinho explica pouco sobre o que está acontecendo com os ativos argentinos. Por trás da piora está uma combinação de fatores externos, movimentos técnicos do mercado e uma discussão que deve ganhar cada vez mais espaço nos próximos meses: como a Argentina chegará a 2027, ano de eleição presidencial e de vencimentos relevantes da dívida em moeda estrangeira. São mais de US$ 30 bilhões em principal e juros no próximo ano , segundo levantamento do FMI (Fundo Monetário Internacional). A conta inclui compromissos com credores privados e organismos internacionais. O volume não é um problema imediato de pagamento. Hoje, o país mantém pouco mais de US$ 50 bilhões em reservas. Parte das obrigações pode ser refinanciada e outra parcela envolve o próprio FMI. O aumento do risco-país das últimas semanas, portanto, não deve ser explicado apenas por essa conta. Parte importante da alta recente veio de fora da Argentina, avalia Daniel Marcatto, sócio e analista da Exploritas. A abertura das taxas dos títulos norte-americanos e o fortalecimento do dólar pressionaram os mercados emergentes.

https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/nacional/ce.text: A Polícia Civil de Mato Grosso transferiu a detenta Angélica Saraiva de Sá, conhecida como “Angeliquinha”, na última terça-feira (20), para cumprir pena de maneira mais severa no modelo RDD (Regime Disciplinar Diferenciado). https://maritime-executive.com/editorial.text: Argentina is trying to stop a planned oil project near the Falkland Islands. On October 13, the government asked the International Tribunal for the Law of the Seas (Itlos), a court in Hamburg that deals with disputes over the sea, to halt the project. Argentina says the UK approved the drilling without its agreement and in breach of Argentina’s rights to the seabed. The project, called Sea Lion, is a joint venture between UK and Israeli companies, and has been licensed to produce oil by the Falkland Islands government. The Sea Lion field holds an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil, 500 million barrels of which is assessed as recoverable. Argentina began arbitration proceedings against the UK on September 28 and gave London 14 days to stop the project. That deadline expired on October 12. The Argentinian government has now called on Itlos to issue “provisional measures” – emergency orders to protect each side’s rights, or prevent serious harm to the marine environment. The UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has rejected Argentina’s claims, insisting the UK will “vigorously” contest jurisdiction. Itlos applies the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, which governs the sea – not land. Yet rights at sea flow from owning the coast, which means that whoever holds the Falklands holds the seabed – and the oil – around the islands. Tribunals under the convention have no power to decide who owns land, and can’t settle sovereignty disputes. Because rights at sea flow from land, every question about the oil in the dispute between Argentina and the UK has been dragged back into a near two-century argument over who owns the islands, as my colleague and I previously argued.

https://www.tecnologistica.com.br/notici.text: A Associação Brasileira de Transporte e Logística de Produtos Perigosos (ABTLP) conquistou duas certificações concedidas pela Câmara Internacional de Logística e Transportes (CIT) : a Certificação de Qualidade (CQCIT) e a CITGREEN, voltada à sustentabilidade. Os reconhecimentos foram concedidos após auditoria realizada entre julho e outubro de 2026 e têm validade até outubro de 2029. A CQCIT avalia aspectos da gestão institucional, como liderança, planejamento estratégico, relacionamento com clientes, gestão de pessoas, processos e resultados. Já a CITGREEN considera práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança (ESG), incluindo a contribuição da organização para os 17 Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS) e a implementação de iniciativas nessas áreas. Segundo a ABTLP, a conquista está relacionada ao aprimoramento de procedimentos internos, dos mecanismos de controle e registro documental e das práticas de governança e sustentabilidade. A entidade também participa da Comissão Estadual de São Paulo para a Segurança no Transporte Rodoviário de Produtos Perigosos, vinculada à Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística (SEMIL), e coordena o Grupo de Trabalho de Análise de Acidentes (GT01). Entre as iniciativas desenvolvidas estão parcerias com a Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT), por meio do programa ANTT Coopera, e com o SEST SENAT, voltadas à capacitação e à atualização técnica. A associação também promove o ABTLP 360, iniciativa que reúne transportadores, autoridades e especialistas para discutir questões regulatórias, operacionais e de segurança. Na área social, participou do projeto Juntos pelo Telhado, em benefício do Lar Nefesh. Para Oswaldo Caixeta, presidente da ABTLP, as certificações refletem a evolução dos processos internos da entidade. “A conquista das certificações CQCIT e CITGREEN representa um importante marco na trajetória institucional da ABTLP, pois reconhece o compromisso da associação com a excelência na gestão, a responsabilidade socioambiental, a transparência e a melhoria contínua de seus processos”, afirma. O reconhecimento ocorreu no mesmo período em que Caixeta recebeu a Medalha da Ordem do Mérito Interamericano dos Transportes, durante a 43ª Assembleia Geral Ordinária da CIT, realizada em Santiago, no Chile. O encontro reuniu representantes de diferentes países para discutir temas como segurança, sustentabilidade, inteligência artificial, escassez de motoristas, custos operacionais, integração logística e gestão de riscos.

Os gastos com logística no Brasil devem alcançar R$ 2,2 trilhões em 2026 , o equivalente a 16,1% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) , segundo estudo anual do Instituto de Logística e Supply Chain (ILOS). A estimativa indica que os custos de transporte, armazenagem e manutenção de estoques permanecem em um patamar superior ao registrado na década passada. A pesquisa realizada pelo instituto com mais de 100 grandes empresas industriais e varejistas, também aponta expectativa de aumento das despesas logísticas em 2027. O transporte representa cerca de 9% do PIB desde 2020, com oscilações ao longo do período. Já os custos de estoque apresentaram uma elevação mais acentuada: passaram de 2,9% do PIB em 2020 para 5% em 2022, atingiram 5,6% em 2023 e mantiveram esse nível em 2025. Segundo Maurício Lima, sócio-diretor do ILOS e responsável pelo levantamento, a alta está relacionada ao custo de manter capital imobilizado em mercadorias, influenciado pelo patamar elevado dos juros. Na análise dos custos dentro das empresas, a logística consome, em média, 9,5% da receita líquida das companhias pesquisadas. A participação varia conforme o setor: em material de construção, chega a 19,8%, enquanto em tecnologia e telecomunicações representa 3%. O levantamento foi realizado no primeiro semestre de 2026 e considera grandes empresas brasileiras em faturamento. As perspectivas para 2027 indicam pressão adicional sobre as operações. De acordo com a pesquisa, 69% das empresas esperam aumento nos custos de transporte, com alta média projetada de 9,6%. Na armazenagem, 44% preveem elevação, de 5,7% em média. Já 31% esperam aumento nos custos de estoque, com variação média de 7%. “O Brasil não está diante de um pico de custo logístico, mas de um novo patamar. O salto de 2022 se consolidou e, três anos depois, seguimos operando acima de 16% do PIB”, afirma Lima. Para o executivo, a expectativa de novas altas no transporte pode pressionar as margens das empresas, os preços ao consumidor e a competitividade do país. O ILOS acompanha os custos logísticos nacionais desde 2004, com frequência anual a partir de 2014. Os números relativos a 2026 são projeções do instituto, enquanto os indicadores de participação das despesas na receita líquida e as expectativas para 2027 têm como base a pesquisa realizada com mais de 100 empresas industriais e varejistas.

https://www.rigzone.com/news/oil_rises_i.text: In a market analysis sent to Rigzone on Thursday, Mahmoud Mashal, Senior Market Analyst at VT Markets Dubai, highlighted that both WTI and Brent oil prices were rising intraday “as escalating tensions in the Middle East revived concerns over Gulf supply”. At the time of writing, Brent was up more than three percent and WTI was up more than two percent from Wednesday settlements. “Friction between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has brought the kingdom’s energy infrastructure back into focus at a time when traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains restricted,” Mashal said in the analysis. “The U.S. decision to withdraw some diplomatic staff from Saudi Arabia, alongside troop movements in the region, has reinforced concerns that the conflict could broaden,” Mashal warned. “Shipping risks remain persistent, threatening operations that have helped exporters work around restrictions. Disruptions to alternative channels would make it harder for Gulf producers to maintain current export flows and could add significantly to supply concerns,” he added. Mashal went on to note in the analysis that several buffers are limiting the upside potential of oil prices.

https://safety4sea.com/bab-al-mandab-dis.text: Disruptions to shipping through the Bab al-Mandab Strait are increasing the risk of wider regional escalation, as Houthi attacks threaten one of the main alternative routes for Middle Eastern oil exports, according to analysis by W. Schreiner Parker, Partner and Head of Emerging Markets & NOCs at Rystad Energy. I n the analysis, “The Unbroken Glass: Bab al-Mandab and the Risk of Asymmetric Escalation” , Parker examines how actions by a non-state group can trigger disproportionate responses from regional powers, creating consequences for maritime trade, energy security and international shipping markets. The analysis highlights the growing vulnerability of alternative oil export routes following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz after the conflict began on February 28, 2026. Saudi crude loadings at Yanbu, on the Red Sea, increased from approximately 800,000 barrels per day (bpd) to around 5 million bpd in March, with roughly 80% of that volume initially moving south through Bab al-Mandab. However, the Houthi campaign launched in July placed this alternative route under increasing pressure. According to Parker, Houthi missile attacks against Israel in March developed into a wider campaign that ended the group’s four-year ceasefire with Saudi Arabia. On July 20, the Houthis announced an embargo targeting Saudi vessels while indicating that other commercial shipping could continue passing through Bab al-Mandab. Although most vessels reportedly continued transiting without incident, weekly passages through the strait declined from 354 to 269 during the first week of the embargo.

https://brasilenergia.com.br/petroleoega.text: O PDE simplificado, em forma de Relatório Síntese, será complementado com maior nível de aprofundamento por 10 Cadernos Temáticos que entram na rotina de publicação e de atualização pela EPE Está aberta no site do MME, desde o dia 8 de outubro e até o dia 6 de novembro próximo, a Consulta Pública 235 aberta pelo Ministério e pela EPE do Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia (PDE-2036).
