https://safety4sea.com/cm-skills-that-ma.text: How we respond to difficult situations can influence our relationships, decision-making and professional performance. Understanding our emotional reactions is an important step towards responding with greater awareness and confidence. E motional intelligence is the ability to recognise, understand and manage our emotions while remaining aware of how they affect others. In the demanding environment of a ship, where crews work and live together for extended periods, this skill can help seafarers navigate conflict, communicate effectively and make better decisions under pressure. However, when faced with criticism, disagreement, fatigue or stress, our immediate reactions are not always constructive. We may become defensive, avoid confrontation, feel overwhelmed or prioritise others’ expectations at the expense of our own needs. Recognising four common response patterns can help us respond more thoughtfully. When challenged or criticised, our instinctive response may be to argue, blame others or defend our position. Yet anger can sometimes mask frustration, fear or unmet expectations. For example, a crew member who feels unfairly criticised by a senior officer during a routine operation may respond defensively, turning feedback into confrontation.

https://safety4sea.com/lessons-learned-c.text: A crew member suffered second-degree chemical burns after a concentrated fuel biocide was incorrectly used to clean fuel oil strainers, according to a safety flash published by the International Marine Contractors Association (IMCA) on 22 October 2026. T he chemical penetrated the worker’s clothing, and the exposure continued when the contaminated coveralls were worn again the following day. The incident highlights how inappropriate chemical selection, inadequate protective equipment and delayed decontamination can turn routine maintenance into a serious injury. During maintenance work involving fuel oil strainers, a crew member used a concentrated fuel biocide as a soaking and rinsing agent. However, the substance was intended exclusively as a fuel additive and was not suitable for cleaning equipment. While carrying out the task, the worker wore standard cotton coveralls rather than the chemical-resistant protective clothing required for handling the substance. The chemical mixture soaked through the fabric, exposing the worker’s skin to its corrosive effects. Unaware of the chemical’s hazardous properties, the crew member did not immediately wash the affected skin. The situation was aggravated when the same contaminated coveralls were worn again the following day, extending the period of contact with the chemical. The worker subsequently developed second-degree chemical burns requiring hospital treatment.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543842-te.text: Norwegian engineering and technology company Techouse has agreed to acquire offshore potable water services specialist Ambio Water, expanding its water treatment business following a separate acquisition agreement announced earlier in October. Techouse said on October 22 it would acquire 100% of the shares in Ambio, a Stavanger-based company providing potable water system services to offshore installations and vessels. Ambio Water's customers include operators, drilling contractors and shipowners on the Norwegian continental shelf, with services covering fixed production platforms, floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessels, drilling rigs, subsea vessels and offshore support vessels. The company provides water quality risk assessments, contingency planning, inspections, audits, laboratory analyses, tank cleaning and disinfection, as well as engineering and technical support. Ambio Water also operates a proprietary digital platform for monitoring and compliance management of offshore water and fuel systems. Founded in 2000, Ambio Water employs 10 people and generated revenue of approximately NOK 28 million in 2025. It will continue operating under its existing management team as part of Techouse.

https://safety4sea.com/the-swedish-club-.text: Moving away from traditional command-and-control leadership toward an approach that encourages crew participation, independent thinking and shared responsibility can strengthen safety and decision-making aboard ships, according to leadership expert Jenny Jepsen. S peaking on The Swedish Club’s Knot Another Lesson podcast, hosted by Loss Prevention Manager Joakim Enström, Jepsen discussed how intent-based leadership can help maritime organizations create working environments where seafarers feel confident to speak up, challenge decisions and take responsibility for their actions. Jepsen, who works closely with David Marquet, author of Turn the Ship Around!, explained that the approach focuses on distributing decision-making to those with the relevant knowledge while ensuring that everyone understands the organization’s objectives and possesses the competence required to act safely. According to Jepsen, traditional leadership structures often require employees to seek approval before taking action, potentially placing excessive decision-making responsibility on a single individual. Intent-based leadership instead encourages personnel to communicate what they intend to do, demonstrating that they have considered the situation, understood the objectives and identified an appropriate course of action. When we shift to intent based language, it requires that we have thought through the problem, that we’ve looked at different perspectives, that we know from our own skills, ability, understanding of the direction or the vision, the goals, what to do. And now we are saying we’re sharing our intent to, and we take ownership of that action.

https://safety4sea.com/eu-seeks-stronger.text: The European Union is calling for stronger maritime security measures and the restoration of safe passage for commercial shipping in the Black Sea, following a series of suspected Russian drone attacks threatening vessels, seafarers and Ukrainian exports. A ddressing the European Parliament in Strasbourg on October 20, 2026, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas described six attacks in 10 days as a dangerous escalation. She said seven seafarers remained missing following a drone attack on two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast. Kallas also reported that Romanian F-16 fighter jets had intercepted two drones over Romanian territorial waters on October 17, highlighting the growing risks to European maritime security. According to Kallas, Russia has intensified attacks on Ukrainian export routes since mid-July, targeting Black Sea and Danube ports, agricultural infrastructure, vessels, shipping lanes, border crossings and grain storage facilities. The disruption is estimated to be costing Ukraine €60 million daily in lost export revenues. Kallas emphasized that approximately 90% of Ukraine’s agricultural exports move through the Black Sea corridor, making safe navigation essential to international food supplies. Today, HR/VP @kajakallas addressed the @Europarl_EN plenary on the escalation of Russian strikes in the EU, particularly attacks affecting Black Sea shipping routes. She stressed that diplomatic engagement must go hand in hand with sustained pressure on Moscow and continued support for Ukraine. Read the full speech here: https://t.co/1BXn3A7Uws

https://safety4sea.com/cm-the-future-of-.text: Wellness is no longer viewed simply as a healthy habit or an occasional activity. New findings from McKinsey suggest that it is becoming an integral part of everyday life, with growing emphasis on prevention, personalisation and overall quality of life. A ccording to a preview of McKinsey’s Future of Wellness Report 2026, based on research involving more than 9,000 consumers across the US, UK, Germany and China, 84% of respondents consider wellness important or a top priority in their daily lives. Yet only 13% report actually achieving their wellness goals. The findings highlight a significant gap between recognising the importance of wellbeing and putting healthy intentions into practice. McKinsey identifies six interconnected dimensions of wellness: health, sleep, nutrition, fitness, mindfulness and appearance. Rather than focusing on individual outcomes, consumers increasingly seek solutions that improve how they feel, perform, recover and age. For shipping, where demanding schedules, fatigue, isolation and limited access to services can affect daily life, several emerging trends deserve particular attention. Wellness is shifting from treating health problems towards preventing them and maintaining physical and mental capabilities over time.

https://www.oedigital.com/news/543845-ab.text: The National Ocean Industries Association (NOIA) has named the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Ørsted the winners of the 2026 NOIA Environmental, Social, & Governance (ESG) Excellence Awards. ABS is the winner of the Service, Supply & Support category, while Ørsted is the inaugural winner of the new Operators & Developers category. The NOIA ESG Excellence Award recognizes companies whose actions, design, or influence advance the ideals embodied by the NOIA ESG Principles. For the first time in 2026, NOIA expanded the competition to two categories, allowing companies throughout the offshore energy value chain to be evaluated alongside their industry peers.

https://safety4sea.com/rosatom-and-indon.text: Russia’s Rosatom and an Indonesian company have reached an agreement to deploy two floating nuclear power units to supply electricity in North Maluku, Indonesia. R osatom State Corporation and Indonesia’s PT Pembangkit Listrik Nuklir signed the agreement on October 16, 2026, during Russian Energy Week in Moscow. According to Rosatom, the project represents the first export agreement for electricity supplied by floating nuclear power units. Under the agreement, Rosatom plans to deploy two FPU-100 floating nuclear power units, each with a generating capacity of 100 MW, to supply electricity to the northern part of Halmahera Island in North Maluku, eastern Indonesia. The units will be equipped with RITM-200M marine nuclear reactors, developed from the RITM-series technology already used aboard Russia’s nuclear-powered icebreaker fleet. The FPU-100 design has been adapted for operation in warm climates, with Rosatom positioning the technology as a source of continuous, low-carbon electricity for remote coastal communities and industrial facilities. According to Rosatom, the floating units could begin supplying electricity within five years of the key terms of the electricity supply contract taking effect. Alexey Likhachev, Director General of Rosatom, described the agreement as a significant step in bilateral nuclear energy cooperation, emphasizing its potential to establish a long-term partnership between the two countries.

https://safety4sea.com/fueleu-pooling-bo.text: FuelEU Maritime’s pooling mechanism is supporting growing demand for liquefied biomethane (LBM/bio-LNG), while creating financial incentives for shipowners to exceed greenhouse gas emissions requirements, according to a new analysis by Titan Clean Fuels. I n its white paper, “FuelEU Maritime: The Methane Pathway is the Way to Compliance”, Titan, examines how LNG, LBM and e-methane can contribute to regulatory compliance, with particular attention to the commercial opportunities created by pooling arrangements. According to Titan, LBM increased from 6.5% to 19.1% of its total methane fuel deliveries between 2024 and 2025, largely supported by demand from operators seeking to generate surplus FuelEU compliance balances. The company also cites Port of Rotterdam figures indicating that LBM bunkering volumes increased sixfold in 2025 compared with the previous year. The findings suggest that FuelEU Maritime is influencing fuel purchasing decisions as operators seek to balance regulatory compliance, fuel costs and potential revenues from exceeding emissions targets. Under FuelEU Maritime, vessels must meet progressively tighter limits on the greenhouse gas intensity of energy used onboard, calculated on a well-to-wake basis. The regulation allows operators to combine the compliance balances of different vessels through pooling, enabling ships exceeding their emissions requirements to offset deficits elsewhere in the pool. This flexibility is available across different operators, allowing surplus compliance to be transferred under commercially negotiated arrangements.

https://safety4sea.com/shipping-lacks-da.text: Energy efficiency measures could account for nearly 40% of shipping’s cumulative emissions reductions through 2050, but gaps in data collection and monitoring are limiting the industry’s ability to assess their actual contribution, according to the Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping (MMMCZCS). I n its latest Countdown analysis, titled “How can we address energy efficiency’s untapped potential?” , the Center highlights the significant role of energy efficiency in maritime decarbonization while warning that the industry lacks reliable information on the installation, use and performance of available technologies. Drawing on the IMO’s Comprehensive Impact Assessment, the Center estimates that energy efficiency could contribute approximately 10% of modeled emissions reductions by 2030, increasing to 28% by 2040 and nearly 38% by 2050. These figures reflect the contribution of efficiency measures within a modeled decarbonization pathway rather than verified reductions achieved by the existing fleet. The analysis covers technical and operational measures, including hull and propeller improvements, waste heat recovery, air lubrication, speed optimization and more efficient voyage planning. According to the Center, one of the main obstacles to realizing energy efficiency’s potential is the absence of consistent information on how widely efficiency technologies and operational measures have been adopted across the global fleet.

https://safety4sea.com/lr-and-bpa-urge-p.text: Lloyd’s Register (LR) and the British Ports Association (BPA) are calling on ports to begin preparing for advanced nuclear technologies, highlighting the need to address maritime safety, regulatory alignment, emergency preparedness and liability before nuclear-powered merchant vessels become commercially widespread. I n a joint white paper published, titled “Advanced Nuclear Technology Use Within Port Environments” , the organizations argue that ports should approach nuclear technology as a long-term infrastructure and operational planning issue rather than simply another alternative marine fuel. The report examines three potential applications: nuclear-powered merchant vessels calling at commercial ports, floating or transportable nuclear power plants, and land-based small modular reactors (SMRs) or microreactors supporting port operations. According to LR and BPA, the principal challenges extend beyond technical development to include regulatory uncertainty, governance, insurance, workforce competence, emergency response capabilities and public confidence. The report emphasizes that nuclear-powered vessel calls would require additional safety arrangements, even though conventional operations such as pilotage, berthing, cargo handling and departure would remain broadly similar. Ports would need to establish procedures covering pre-arrival safety documentation, vessel authorization, berth suitability, radiation monitoring, access restrictions, security arrangements and emergency preparedness. Clear responsibilities would also be required between port operators, harbour authorities, maritime regulators, nuclear regulators and emergency services.

https://safety4sea.com/dnv-backed-resear.text: Credit: DNV / From left: Joakim Appelquist, Astrid Rusås Kristoffersen, John-Arne Røttingen, Leif Høegh, Camilla Stoltenberg and Jens Lundsgaard. Stiftelsen Det Norske Veritas has awarded NOK 96 million to 10 Nordic research projects addressing emerging technological and societal risks, including the safety of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) and human oversight. A nnounced by DNV on 22 October, the funding will support research at universities across Norway, Denmark, Sweden and Finland, with three projects specifically examining the challenges associated with increasingly autonomous AI systems. The research will investigate unexpected AI behavior, methods for assessing the safety of AI-controlled systems and the potential impact of AI-assisted decision-making on human expertise. A separate project will examine cascading risks affecting offshore wind energy and shipping under climate change. Three projects will focus on the safety and reliability of autonomous AI, particularly in environments where system failures could have significant consequences. At the University of Oslo, the EMERGE project will investigate how advanced AI systems develop unexpected behaviors, including situations involving interactions between multiple autonomous AI agents. The research aims to improve understanding of how potentially harmful behavior emerges and identify methods for detecting and addressing it.

https://safety4sea.com/ebl-adoption-reac.text: The adoption of electronic bills of lading (eBLs) has reached 51.1% among surveyed trade stakeholders, according to the FIT Alliance’s latest survey, which identifies interoperability and platform fragmentation as key challenges to wider digitalization. T he findings show that eBL adoption has increased from 49.2% in 2024 and 33% in 2022 – however, growth has slowed compared with the previous survey period, highlighting the need to address remaining barriers across the international trade ecosystem. The survey also found that 11.2% of respondents now use eBLs exclusively, compared with 7.5% in 2024, indicating a gradual transition away from paper-based documentation. Despite these developments, the FIT Alliance highlights the need to move beyond adoption within individual organizations toward the seamless exchange and acceptance of electronic documents across different platforms. According to the FIT Alliance, interoperability and platform fragmentation were the most frequently cited concerns among respondents, reflecting difficulties in exchanging electronic trade documents between different service providers and systems. While eBLs can streamline documentation within individual organizations, their wider effectiveness depends on the ability of carriers, shippers, freight forwarders, banks and other stakeholders to exchange, verify and transfer documents without being restricted to a particular platform.

https://splash247.com/marco-polo-marine-.text: Singapore-listed offshore vessel owner and shipyard group Marco Polo Marine has established a joint venture in South Korea with local partner NSEL, strengthening its presence in the country’s offshore vessel market. The new company, Baramgil Offshore, will focus on vessel operations, management and chartering, with NSEL holding a 51% stake and Baramgil Corporation taking the remaining 49%. Baramgil Corporation is 90% owned by Marco Polo Marine’s Taiwan-based affiliate PKR Offshore, in which the Singapore group holds an indirect 49% interest. The venture has been established with an initial paid-up capital of about $107,000, with Marco Polo Marine funding its investment through internal resources. The company said the move would have no material impact on its earnings or net tangible assets for the financial year ending September 2027. The latest move builds on an existing partnership between PKR Offshore and NSEL, established in 2023 to pursue opportunities in South Korea’s offshore wind sector. The partners made their first move into the Korean market in 2024, deploying a Korean-flagged crew transfer vessel (CTV) for offshore wind work. The MP Corus was among the vessels brought into the market to support wind farm construction activities off the country’s southwest coast.

https://petronoticias.com.br/288688-2/.text: Os terroristas Houthis apoiado pela Guarda Revolucionária do Irã voltaram a atacar o aeroporto de Riade, na Arábia saudita, enquanto o Irã e o presidente Trump trocam ameaças de grandes ataques. Os EUA e Israel planejam renovar os ataques ao Irã após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, marcadas para o dia 3 de novembro, com foco em ataques curtos e intensos. Segundo o relatório, os planos se concentram em uma operação militar curta e intensa que poderia durar aproximadamente três dias e incluir ataques às instalações nucleares do Irã. Os ataques seriam às instalações nucleares do Irã, à infraestrutura energética e às capacidades de mísseis e drones. Os dois países intensificaram os exercícios militares conjuntos, incluindo voos sobre o Iraque para ensaiar possíveis ataques. O secretário de Defesa dos EUA, Pete Hegseth , também discutiu os planos com o primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu durante sua visita a Israel esta semana. O preço do barril do Brent esta manhã reflete toda instabilidade no Oriente Médio: O barril está cotado em torno de US$ 111,81 e o WTI, 98,87. Ambos, muito alto. Os Estados Unidos e Israel estiveram perto de lançar um ataque no início deste mês, mas o presidente americano Donald Trump decidiu adiá-lo no último minuto. Trump ainda não aprovou uma nova operação militar, enquanto os esforços diplomáticos para chegar a um acordo com o Irã estão em andamento. Autoridades iranianas ameaçaram que qualquer novo ataque desencadearia uma resposta mais ampla, incluindo ataques a centros de dados e cabos de comunicação submarinos. Netanyahu pressionou por uma ofensiva em larga escala contra o Irã, com as Forças de Defesa de Israel (IDF) se preparando para uma campanha de bombardeio de vários dias. A operação não prosseguiu porque Trump se opôs à retomada das hostilidades antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. Esperava-se que os ataques fossem mais intensos do que os realizados por Israel e pelos EUA no início de sua campanha militar conjunta em fevereiro. Nem o primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, nem o ministro da Defesa Israel Katz , nem qualquer outro funcionário do governo instruiu as Forças de Defesa de Israel a se prepararem para atacar da maneira como essas ordens foram transmitidas antes dos conflitos com o Irã em junho de 2025 e início de 2026. Caças israelenses sobrevoaram a Síria e o Iraque em direção ao Irã durante um exercício realizado na madrugada de segunda para terça-feira. As aeronaves foram deslocadas para o leste durante o exercício. Caças israelenses foram avistados sobre o sul da Síria e, posteriormente, sobre a província de Muthanna, no sul do Iraque. Trump já havia deixado claro em 8 de outubro que os EUA não atacariam o Irã antes das eleições de meio de mandato. “ Estamos mantendo conversas produtivas
